inputs.description: The first image to be combined into the batch. It serves as the reference for the dimensions to which the second image will be adjusted if necessary.

inputs.name: image2
inputs.description: The second image to be combined into the batch. It is automatically rescaled to match the dimensions of the first image if they differ.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The combined batch of images, with the second image rescaled to match the first one's dimensions if needed.

ImageBlend.description: The ImageBlend node is designed to blend two images together based on a specified blending mode and blend factor. It supports various blending modes such as normal, multiply, screen, overlay, soft light, and difference, allowing for versatile image manipulation and compositing techniques. This node is essential for creating composite images by adjusting the visual interaction between two image layers.

inputs.name: image1
inputs.description: The first image to be blended. It serves as the base layer for the blending operation.

inputs.name: image2
inputs.description: The second image to be blended. Depending on the blend mode, it modifies the appearance of the first image.

inputs.name: blend_factor
inputs.description: Determines the weight of the second image in the blend. A higher blend factor gives more prominence to the second image in the resulting blend.

inputs.name: blend_mode
inputs.description: Specifies the method of blending the two images. Supports modes like normal, multiply, screen, overlay, soft light, and difference, each producing a unique visual effect.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The resulting image after blending the two input images according to the specified blend mode and factor.

ImageBlur.description: The ImageBlur node applies a Gaussian blur to an image, utilizing a specified blur radius and sigma value to control the extent and intensity of the blurring effect. This process can help in reducing image noise and detail, creating a smoother appearance.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be blurred, provided as a torch.Tensor. This image undergoes a Gaussian blur transformation based on the specified blur radius and sigma.

inputs.name: blur_radius
inputs.description: Specifies the radius of the blur effect. A larger radius results in a more pronounced blurring effect.

inputs.name: sigma
inputs.description: Determines the spread of the blur effect. A higher sigma value increases the extent of blurring, affecting the smoothness of the output image.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image after applying the Gaussian blur, returned as a torch.Tensor. This image will have a smoother appearance compared to the input.

ImageColorToMask.description: The ImageColorToMask node is designed to convert a specified color in an image to a mask. It processes an image and a target color, generating a mask where the specified color is highlighted, facilitating operations like color-based segmentation or object isolation.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The 'image' parameter represents the input image to be processed. It is crucial for determining the areas of the image that match the specified color to be converted into a mask.

inputs.name: color
inputs.description: The 'color' parameter specifies the target color in the image to be converted into a mask. It plays a key role in identifying the specific color areas to be highlighted in the resulting mask.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The output is a mask highlighting the areas of the input image that match the specified color. This mask can be used for further image processing tasks, such as segmentation or object isolation.

ImageCompositeMasked.description: The ImageCompositeMasked node is designed for compositing images, allowing for the overlay of a source image onto a destination image at specified coordinates, with optional resizing and masking.

inputs.name: destination
inputs.description: The destination image onto which the source image will be composited. It serves as the background for the composite operation.

inputs.name: source
inputs.description: The source image to be composited onto the destination image. This image can optionally be resized to fit the destination image's dimensions.

inputs.name: x
inputs.description: The x-coordinate in the destination image where the top-left corner of the source image will be placed.

inputs.name: y
inputs.description: The y-coordinate in the destination image where the top-left corner of the source image will be placed.

inputs.name: resize_source
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether the source image should be resized to match the destination image's dimensions.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: An optional mask that specifies which parts of the source image should be composited onto the destination image. This allows for more complex compositing operations, such as blending or partial overlays.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The resulting image after the compositing operation, which combines elements of both the source and destination images according to the specified parameters.

ImageCrop.description: The ImageCrop node is designed for cropping images to a specified width and height starting from a given x and y coordinate. This functionality is essential for focusing on specific regions of an image or for adjusting the image size to meet certain requirements.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be cropped. This parameter is crucial as it defines the source image from which a region will be extracted based on the specified dimensions and coordinates.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Specifies the width of the cropped image. This parameter determines how wide the resulting cropped image will be.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Specifies the height of the cropped image. This parameter determines the height of the resulting cropped image.

inputs.name: x
inputs.description: The x-coordinate of the top-left corner of the cropping area. This parameter sets the starting point for the width dimension of the crop.

inputs.name: y
inputs.description: The y-coordinate of the top-left corner of the cropping area. This parameter sets the starting point for the height dimension of the crop.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The cropped image as a result of the cropping operation. This output is significant for further processing or analysis of the specified image region.

ImageFromBatch.description: The ImageFromBatch node is designed to extract a specific segment of images from a larger batch based on a given index and length. This functionality is crucial for operations that require processing or analyzing subsets of images within a batch, enabling targeted manipulation or inspection of images.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The 'image' parameter represents the batch of images from which a subset will be extracted. It is crucial for specifying the source batch.

inputs.name: batch_index
inputs.description: The 'batch_index' parameter specifies the starting index within the batch from which the extraction begins, allowing for precise selection of the subset.

inputs.name: length
inputs.description: The 'length' parameter determines the number of images to extract from the specified starting index, enabling control over the size of the resulting subset.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is a subset of images extracted from the original batch, based on the specified 'batch_index' and 'length'.

ImageInvert.description: The ImageInvert node is designed to invert the colors of an image, effectively transforming each pixel's color value to its complementary color on the color wheel. This operation is useful for creating negative images or for visual effects that require color inversion.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The 'image' parameter represents the input image to be inverted. It is crucial for specifying the target image whose colors are to be inverted, affecting the node's execution and the visual outcome of the inversion process.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is an inverted version of the input image, with each pixel's color value transformed to its complementary color.

ImageOnlyCheckpointLoader.description: This node specializes in loading checkpoints specifically for image-based models within video generation workflows. It efficiently retrieves and configures the necessary components from a given checkpoint, focusing on image-related aspects of the model.

inputs.name: ckpt_name
inputs.description: Specifies the name of the checkpoint to load. This parameter is crucial for identifying and retrieving the correct checkpoint file from a predefined list of available checkpoints.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: Returns the main model loaded from the checkpoint, configured for image processing within video generation contexts.

outputs.name: clip_vision
outputs.description: Provides the CLIP vision component extracted from the checkpoint, tailored for image understanding and feature extraction.

outputs.name: vae
outputs.description: Delivers the Variational Autoencoder (VAE) component, essential for image manipulation and generation tasks.

ImageOnlyCheckpointSave.description: This node specializes in saving model checkpoints specifically for image-based applications, incorporating additional components like CLIP vision and VAE models. It allows for the customization of the checkpoint's filename prefix and optionally includes prompt and extra PNG information for enhanced flexibility and metadata storage.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The primary model whose state is to be saved as a checkpoint. It is central to the checkpoint creation process.

inputs.name: clip_vision
inputs.description: The CLIP vision model to be included in the checkpoint, enabling enhanced image understanding capabilities.

inputs.name: vae
inputs.description: The VAE model to be included in the checkpoint, facilitating image generation or manipulation tasks.

inputs.name: filename_prefix
inputs.description: A customizable prefix for the checkpoint filename, allowing for organized storage and easy identification.

ImagePadForOutpaint.description: This node is designed for preparing images for the outpainting process by adding padding around them. It adjusts the image dimensions to ensure compatibility with outpainting algorithms, facilitating the generation of extended image areas beyond the original boundaries.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The 'image' input is the primary image to be prepared for outpainting, serving as the base for padding operations.

inputs.name: left
inputs.description: Specifies the amount of padding to add to the left side of the image, influencing the expanded area for outpainting.

inputs.name: top
inputs.description: Determines the amount of padding to add to the top of the image, affecting the vertical expansion for outpainting.

inputs.name: right
inputs.description: Defines the amount of padding to add to the right side of the image, impacting the horizontal expansion for outpainting.

inputs.name: bottom
inputs.description: Indicates the amount of padding to add to the bottom of the image, contributing to the vertical expansion for outpainting.

inputs.name: feathering
inputs.description: Controls the smoothness of the transition between the original image and the added padding, enhancing the visual integration for outpainting.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output 'image' represents the padded image, ready for the outpainting process.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The output 'mask' indicates the areas of the original image and the added padding, useful for guiding the outpainting algorithms.

ImageQuantize.description: The ImageQuantize node is designed to reduce the number of colors in an image to a specified number, optionally applying dithering techniques to maintain visual quality. This process is useful for creating palette-based images or reducing the color complexity for certain applications.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image tensor to be quantized. It affects the node's execution by being the primary data upon which color reduction is performed.

inputs.name: colors
inputs.description: Specifies the number of colors to reduce the image to. It directly influences the quantization process by determining the color palette size.

inputs.name: dither
inputs.description: Determines the dithering technique to be applied during quantization, affecting the visual quality and appearance of the output image.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The quantized version of the input image, with reduced color complexity and optionally dithered to maintain visual quality.

ImageScale.description: The ImageScale node is designed for resizing images to specific dimensions, offering a selection of upscale methods and the ability to crop the resized image. It abstracts the complexity of image upscaling and cropping, providing a straightforward interface for modifying image dimensions according to user-defined parameters.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be upscaled. This parameter is central to the node's operation, serving as the primary data upon which resizing transformations are applied. The quality and dimensions of the output image are directly influenced by the original image's properties.

inputs.name: upscale_method
inputs.description: Specifies the method used for upscaling the image. The choice of method can affect the quality and characteristics of the upscaled image, influencing the visual fidelity and potential artifacts in the resized output.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: The target width for the upscaled image. This parameter directly influences the dimensions of the output image, determining the horizontal scale of the resizing operation.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: The target height for the upscaled image. This parameter directly influences the dimensions of the output image, determining the vertical scale of the resizing operation.

inputs.name: crop
inputs.description: Determines whether and how the upscaled image should be cropped, offering options for disabled cropping or center cropping. This affects the final composition of the image by potentially removing edges to fit the specified dimensions.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The upscaled (and optionally cropped) image, ready for further processing or visualization.

ImageScaleBy.description: The ImageScaleBy node is designed for upscaling images by a specified scale factor using various interpolation methods. It allows for the adjustment of the image size in a flexible manner, catering to different upscaling needs.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be upscaled. This parameter is crucial as it provides the base image that will undergo the upscaling process.

inputs.name: upscale_method
inputs.description: Specifies the interpolation method to be used for upscaling. The choice of method can affect the quality and characteristics of the upscaled image.

inputs.name: scale_by
inputs.description: The factor by which the image will be upscaled. This determines the increase in size of the output image relative to the input image.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The upscaled image, which is larger than the input image according to the specified scale factor and interpolation method.

ImageScaleToTotalPixels.description: The ImageScaleToTotalPixels node is designed for resizing images to a specified total number of pixels while maintaining the aspect ratio. It provides various methods for upscaling the image to achieve the desired pixel count.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be upscaled to the specified total number of pixels.

inputs.name: upscale_method
inputs.description: The method used for upscaling the image. It affects the quality and characteristics of the upscaled image.

inputs.name: megapixels
inputs.description: The target size of the image in megapixels. This determines the total number of pixels in the upscaled image.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The upscaled image with the specified total number of pixels, maintaining the original aspect ratio.

ImageSharpen.description: The ImageSharpen node enhances the clarity of an image by applying a sharpening filter. This process accentuates the edges and details within the image, making it appear more defined and crisp.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be sharpened. This tensor represents the image data that will undergo the sharpening process.

inputs.name: sharpen_radius
inputs.description: Defines the radius of the sharpening effect. A larger radius increases the area of influence around edges, enhancing the sharpening effect.

inputs.name: sigma
inputs.description: Determines the spread of the Gaussian kernel used in the sharpening process. A higher sigma value results in a smoother, less localized sharpening effect.

inputs.name: alpha
inputs.description: Controls the intensity of the sharpening. Higher alpha values result in a more pronounced sharpening effect.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The sharpened image. This output is the result of applying the sharpening filter to the input image, enhancing its edges and details.

ImageToMask.description: The ImageToMask node is designed to convert an image into a mask based on a specified color channel. It allows for the extraction of mask layers corresponding to the red, green, blue, or alpha channels of an image, facilitating operations that require channel-specific masking or processing.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The 'image' parameter represents the input image from which a mask will be generated based on the specified color channel. It plays a crucial role in determining the content and characteristics of the resulting mask.

inputs.name: channel
inputs.description: The 'channel' parameter specifies which color channel (red, green, blue, or alpha) of the input image should be used to generate the mask. This choice directly influences the mask's appearance and which parts of the image are highlighted or masked out.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The output 'mask' is a binary or grayscale representation of the specified color channel from the input image, useful for further image processing or masking operations.

ImageUpscaleWithModel.description: This node is designed to upscale images using a specified upscale model. It dynamically manages memory requirements based on the model and image size, performs the upscaling in a tiled manner to handle large images efficiently, and ensures the output image is clamped within a valid range.

inputs.name: upscale_model
inputs.description: The upscale model to be used for upscaling the image. It determines the upscaling algorithm and its parameters.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be upscaled. The image is processed and upscaled according to the specified upscale model.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The upscaled image, with pixel values clamped to the range [0, 1].

InpaintModelConditioning.description: This node is designed for conditioning in the context of inpainting tasks, where it likely processes and prepares inputs such as images and masks for inpainting, integrating with VAE models for generating or modifying image content. The node's specific functionality, including how it handles conditioning and interacts with other components like VAEs, remains undefined due to the lack of detailed information in the provided context.

inputs.name: positive
inputs.description: Represents the positive conditioning information required for the inpainting process, influencing the generation or modification of image content.

inputs.name: negative
inputs.description: Represents the negative conditioning information, which likely serves to guide the inpainting process by specifying undesired attributes or areas in the generated or modified image content.

inputs.name: vae
inputs.description: Specifies the VAE model used in the inpainting process, crucial for encoding or decoding image data.

inputs.name: pixels
inputs.description: The input image pixels that are subject to inpainting, serving as the primary content for the node's operation.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The mask indicating areas to inpaint, guiding the node in identifying which parts of the image require modification or generation.

outputs.name: positive
outputs.description: The processed positive conditioning output, ready for further steps in the inpainting pipeline.

outputs.name: negative
outputs.description: The processed negative conditioning output, indicating attributes or areas to avoid in the final image content.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The latent representation of the image, potentially modified or generated by the VAE model as part of the inpainting process.

InstructPixToPixConditioning.description: This node is designed for encoding images into a conditioning format suitable for the InstructPix2Pix model, incorporating both positive and negative conditioning alongside pixel data and a variational autoencoder (VAE).

inputs.name: positive
inputs.description: Positive conditioning data that influences the encoding process towards desired outcomes.

inputs.name: negative
inputs.description: Negative conditioning data that guides the encoding away from undesired outcomes.

inputs.name: vae
inputs.description: A variational autoencoder used to encode the pixel data into a latent space representation.

inputs.name: pixels
inputs.description: The pixel data of the image to be encoded, serving as the base for generating latent representations.

outputs.name: positive
outputs.description: Encoded positive conditioning data.

outputs.name: negative
outputs.description: Encoded negative conditioning data.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The latent space representation of the input image.

InvertMask.description: The InvertMask node is designed to invert the values of a given mask, effectively flipping the masked and unmasked areas. This operation is fundamental in image processing tasks where the focus of interest needs to be switched between the foreground and the background.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The 'mask' parameter represents the input mask to be inverted. It is crucial for determining the areas to be flipped in the inversion process.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The output is an inverted version of the input mask, with previously masked areas becoming unmasked and vice versa.

JoinImageWithAlpha.description: This node is designed for compositing operations, specifically to join an image with its corresponding alpha mask to produce a single output image. It effectively combines visual content with transparency information, enabling the creation of images where certain areas are transparent or semi-transparent.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The main visual content to be combined with an alpha mask. It represents the image without transparency information.

inputs.name: alpha
inputs.description: The alpha mask that defines the transparency of the corresponding image. It is used to determine which parts of the image should be transparent or semi-transparent.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is a single image that combines the input image with the alpha mask, incorporating transparency information into the visual content.

KarrasScheduler.description: The KarrasScheduler node is designed to generate a sequence of noise levels (sigmas) based on the Karras et al. (2022) noise schedule. It calculates these levels using specific parameters to control the noise intensity over a given number of steps, facilitating controlled diffusion processes in generative models.

inputs.name: steps
inputs.description: Specifies the number of noise levels to generate, controlling the granularity of the diffusion process.

inputs.name: sigma_max
inputs.description: Sets the maximum noise level, defining the upper bound of noise intensity.

inputs.name: sigma_min
inputs.description: Determines the minimum noise level, establishing the lower bound of noise intensity.

inputs.name: rho
inputs.description: A parameter influencing the shape of the noise schedule, affecting how noise levels progress from sigma_min to sigma_max.

outputs.name: sigmas
outputs.description: A sequence of calculated noise levels (sigmas) according to the Karras et al. (2022) noise schedule.

KSampler.description: The KSampler node is designed for advanced sampling operations within generative models, allowing for the customization of sampling processes through various parameters. It facilitates the generation of new data samples by manipulating latent space representations, leveraging conditioning, and adjusting noise levels.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: Specifies the generative model to be used for sampling, playing a crucial role in determining the characteristics of the generated samples.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: Controls the randomness of the sampling process, ensuring reproducibility of results when set to a specific value.

inputs.name: steps
inputs.description: Determines the number of steps to be taken in the sampling process, affecting the detail and quality of the generated samples.

inputs.name: cfg
inputs.description: Adjusts the conditioning factor, influencing the direction and strength of the conditioning applied during sampling.

inputs.name: sampler_name
inputs.description: Selects the specific sampling algorithm to be used, impacting the behavior and outcome of the sampling process.

inputs.name: scheduler
inputs.description: Chooses the scheduling algorithm for controlling the sampling process, affecting the progression and dynamics of sampling.

inputs.name: positive
inputs.description: Defines positive conditioning to guide the sampling towards desired attributes or features.

inputs.name: negative
inputs.description: Specifies negative conditioning to steer the sampling away from certain attributes or features.

inputs.name: latent_image
inputs.description: Provides a latent space representation to be used as a starting point or reference for the sampling process.

inputs.name: denoise
inputs.description: Controls the level of denoising applied to the samples, affecting the clarity and sharpness of the generated images.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: Represents the latent space output of the sampling process, encapsulating the generated samples.

KSamplerAdvanced.description: The KSamplerAdvanced node is designed to enhance the sampling process by providing advanced configurations and techniques. It aims to offer more sophisticated options for generating samples from a model, improving upon the basic KSampler functionalities.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: Specifies the model from which samples are to be generated, playing a crucial role in the sampling process.

inputs.name: add_noise
inputs.description: Determines whether noise should be added to the sampling process, affecting the diversity and quality of the generated samples.

inputs.name: noise_seed
inputs.description: Sets the seed for noise generation, ensuring reproducibility in the sampling process.

inputs.name: steps
inputs.description: Defines the number of steps to be taken in the sampling process, impacting the detail and quality of the output.

inputs.name: cfg
inputs.description: Controls the conditioning factor, influencing the direction and space of the sampling process.

inputs.name: sampler_name
inputs.description: Selects the specific sampler to be used, allowing for customization of the sampling technique.

inputs.name: scheduler
inputs.description: Chooses the scheduler for controlling the sampling process, affecting the progression and quality of samples.

inputs.name: positive
inputs.description: Specifies the positive conditioning to guide the sampling towards desired attributes.

inputs.name: negative
inputs.description: Specifies the negative conditioning to steer the sampling away from certain attributes.

inputs.name: latent_image
inputs.description: Provides the initial latent image to be used in the sampling process, serving as a starting point.

inputs.name: start_at_step
inputs.description: Determines the starting step of the sampling process, allowing for control over the sampling progression.

inputs.name: end_at_step
inputs.description: Sets the ending step of the sampling process, defining the scope of the sampling.

inputs.name: return_with_leftover_noise
inputs.description: Indicates whether to return the sample with leftover noise, affecting the final output's appearance.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The output represents the latent image generated from the model, reflecting the applied configurations and techniques.

KSamplerSelect.description: The KSamplerSelect node is designed to select a specific sampler based on the provided sampler name. It abstracts the complexity of sampler selection, allowing users to easily switch between different sampling strategies for their tasks.

inputs.name: sampler_name
inputs.description: Specifies the name of the sampler to be selected. This parameter determines which sampling strategy will be used, impacting the overall sampling behavior and results.

outputs.name: sampler
outputs.description: Returns the selected sampler object, ready to be used for sampling tasks.

LatentAdd.description: The LatentAdd node is designed for the addition of two latent representations. It facilitates the combination of features or characteristics encoded in these representations by performing element-wise addition.

inputs.name: samples1
inputs.description: The first set of latent samples to be added. It represents one of the inputs whose features are to be combined with another set of latent samples.

inputs.name: samples2
inputs.description: The second set of latent samples to be added. It serves as the other input whose features are combined with the first set of latent samples through element-wise addition.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The result of the element-wise addition of two latent samples, representing a new set of latent samples that combines the features of both inputs.

LatentBatch.description: The LatentBatch node is designed to merge two sets of latent samples into a single batch, potentially resizing one set to match the dimensions of the other before concatenation. This operation facilitates the combination of different latent representations for further processing or generation tasks.

inputs.name: samples1
inputs.description: The first set of latent samples to be merged. It plays a crucial role in determining the final shape of the merged batch.

inputs.name: samples2
inputs.description: The second set of latent samples to be merged. If its dimensions differ from the first set, it is resized to ensure compatibility before merging.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The merged set of latent samples, now combined into a single batch for further processing.

LatentBatchSeedBehavior.description: The LatentBatchSeedBehavior node is designed to modify the seed behavior of a batch of latent samples. It allows for either randomizing or fixing the seed across the batch, thereby influencing the generation process by either introducing variability or maintaining consistency in the generated outputs.

inputs.name: samples
inputs.description: The 'samples' parameter represents the batch of latent samples to be processed. Its modification depends on the seed behavior chosen, affecting the consistency or variability of the generated outputs.

inputs.name: seed_behavior
inputs.description: The 'seed_behavior' parameter dictates whether the seed for the batch of latent samples should be randomized or fixed. This choice significantly impacts the generation process by either introducing variability or ensuring consistency across the batch.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The output is a modified version of the input latent samples, with adjustments made based on the specified seed behavior. It either maintains or alters the batch index to reflect the chosen seed behavior.

LatentBlend.description: The LatentBlend node is designed to blend two sets of latent samples together, based on a specified blend factor and mode. It allows for the creation of new, hybrid samples by combining features from both input sets in a controlled manner.

inputs.name: samples1
inputs.description: The first set of latent samples to be blended. It serves as the base for the blending operation.

inputs.name: samples2
inputs.description: The second set of latent samples to be blended with the first set. It contributes to the new, hybrid samples created by the blend operation.

inputs.name: blend_factor
inputs.description: A float value that determines the proportion of the first set of samples in the final blend. A higher value gives more weight to the first set, while a lower value favors the second set.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The output is a set of blended latent samples, combining features from both input sets according to the blend factor and mode.

LatentComposite.description: The LatentComposite node is designed to blend or merge two latent representations into a single output. This process is essential for creating composite images or features by combining the characteristics of the input latents in a controlled manner.

inputs.name: samples_to
inputs.description: The 'samples_to' latent representation where the 'samples_from' will be composited onto. It serves as the base for the composite operation.

inputs.name: samples_from
inputs.description: The 'samples_from' latent representation to be composited onto the 'samples_to'. It contributes its features or characteristics to the final composite output.

inputs.name: x
inputs.description: The x-coordinate (horizontal position) where the 'samples_from' latent will be placed on the 'samples_to'. It determines the horizontal alignment of the composite.

inputs.name: y
inputs.description: The y-coordinate (vertical position) where the 'samples_from' latent will be placed on the 'samples_to'. It determines the vertical alignment of the composite.

inputs.name: feather
inputs.description: A boolean indicating whether the 'samples_from' latent should be resized to match the 'samples_to' before compositing. This can affect the scale and proportion of the composite result.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The output is a composite latent representation, blending the features of both 'samples_to' and 'samples_from' latents based on the specified coordinates and resizing option.

LatentCompositeMasked.description: The LatentCompositeMasked node is designed for blending two latent representations together at specified coordinates, optionally using a mask for more controlled compositing. This node enables the creation of complex latent images by overlaying parts of one image onto another, with the ability to resize the source image for a perfect fit.

inputs.name: destination
inputs.description: The latent representation onto which another latent representation will be composited. Acts as the base layer for the composite operation.

inputs.name: source
inputs.description: The latent representation to be composited onto the destination. This source layer can be resized and positioned according to the specified parameters.

inputs.name: x
inputs.description: The x-coordinate in the destination latent representation where the source will be placed. Allows for precise positioning of the source layer.

inputs.name: y
inputs.description: The y-coordinate in the destination latent representation where the source will be placed, enabling accurate overlay positioning.

inputs.name: resize_source
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether the source latent representation should be resized to match the destination's dimensions before compositing.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: An optional mask that can be used to control the blending of the source onto the destination. The mask defines which parts of the source will be visible in the final composite.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The resulting latent representation after compositing the source onto the destination, potentially using a mask for selective blending.

LatentCrop.description: The LatentCrop node is designed to perform cropping operations on latent representations of images. It allows for the specification of the crop dimensions and position, enabling targeted modifications of the latent space.

inputs.name: samples
inputs.description: The 'samples' parameter represents the latent representations to be cropped. It is crucial for defining the data on which the cropping operation will be performed.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Specifies the width of the crop area. It directly influences the dimensions of the output latent representation.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Specifies the height of the crop area, affecting the size of the resulting cropped latent representation.

inputs.name: x
inputs.description: Determines the starting x-coordinate of the crop area, influencing the position of the crop within the original latent representation.

inputs.name: y
inputs.description: Determines the starting y-coordinate of the crop area, setting the position of the crop within the original latent representation.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The output is a modified latent representation with the specified crop applied.

LatentFlip.description: The LatentFlip node is designed to manipulate latent representations by flipping them either vertically or horizontally. This operation allows for the transformation of the latent space, potentially uncovering new variations or perspectives within the data.

inputs.name: samples
inputs.description: The 'samples' parameter represents the latent representations to be flipped. The flipping operation alters these representations, either vertically or horizontally, depending on the 'flip_method' parameter, thus transforming the data in the latent space.

inputs.name: flip_method
inputs.description: The 'flip_method' parameter specifies the axis along which the latent samples will be flipped. It can be either 'x-axis: vertically' or 'y-axis: horizontally', determining the direction of the flip and thus the nature of the transformation applied to the latent representations.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The output is a modified version of the input latent representations, having been flipped according to the specified method. This transformation can introduce new variations within the latent space.

LatentFromBatch.description: This node is designed to extract a specific subset of latent samples from a given batch based on the specified batch index and length. It allows for selective processing of latent samples, facilitating operations on smaller segments of the batch for efficiency or targeted manipulation.

inputs.name: samples
inputs.description: The collection of latent samples from which a subset will be extracted. This parameter is crucial for determining the source batch of samples to be processed.

inputs.name: batch_index
inputs.description: Specifies the starting index within the batch from which the subset of samples will begin. This parameter enables targeted extraction of samples from specific positions in the batch.

inputs.name: length
inputs.description: Defines the number of samples to be extracted from the specified starting index. This parameter controls the size of the subset to be processed, allowing for flexible manipulation of batch segments.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The extracted subset of latent samples, now available for further processing or analysis.

LatentInterpolate.description: The LatentInterpolate node is designed to perform interpolation between two sets of latent samples based on a specified ratio, blending the characteristics of both sets to produce a new, intermediate set of latent samples.

inputs.name: samples1
inputs.description: The first set of latent samples to be interpolated. It serves as the starting point for the interpolation process.

inputs.name: samples2
inputs.description: The second set of latent samples to be interpolated. It serves as the endpoint for the interpolation process.

inputs.name: ratio
inputs.description: A floating-point value that determines the weight of each set of samples in the interpolated output. A ratio of 0 produces a copy of the first set, while a ratio of 1 produces a copy of the second set.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The output is a new set of latent samples that represent an interpolated state between the two input sets, based on the specified ratio.

LatentMultiply.description: The LatentMultiply node is designed to scale the latent representation of samples by a specified multiplier. This operation allows for the adjustment of the intensity or magnitude of features within the latent space, enabling fine-tuning of generated content or the exploration of variations within a given latent direction.

inputs.name: samples
inputs.description: The 'samples' parameter represents the latent representations to be scaled. It is crucial for defining the input data on which the multiplication operation will be performed.

inputs.name: multiplier
inputs.description: The 'multiplier' parameter specifies the scaling factor to be applied to the latent samples. It plays a key role in adjusting the magnitude of the latent features, allowing for nuanced control over the generated output.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The output is a modified version of the input latent samples, scaled by the specified multiplier. This allows for the exploration of variations within the latent space by adjusting the intensity of its features.

LatentRotate.description: The LatentRotate node is designed to rotate latent representations of images by specified angles. It abstracts the complexity of manipulating latent space to achieve rotation effects, enabling users to easily transform images in a generative model's latent space.

inputs.name: samples
inputs.description: The 'samples' parameter represents the latent representations of images to be rotated. It is crucial for determining the starting point of the rotation operation.

inputs.name: rotation
inputs.description: The 'rotation' parameter specifies the angle by which the latent images should be rotated. It directly influences the orientation of the resulting images.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The output is a modified version of the input latent representations, rotated by the specified angle.

LatentSubtract.description: The LatentSubtract node is designed for subtracting one latent representation from another. This operation can be used to manipulate or modify the characteristics of generative models' outputs by effectively removing features or attributes represented in one latent space from another.

inputs.name: samples1
inputs.description: The first set of latent samples to be subtracted from. It serves as the base for the subtraction operation.

inputs.name: samples2
inputs.description: The second set of latent samples that will be subtracted from the first set. This operation can alter the resulting generative model's output by removing attributes or features.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The result of subtracting the second set of latent samples from the first. This modified latent representation can be used for further generative tasks.

LatentUpscale.description: The LatentUpscale node is designed for upscaling latent representations of images. It allows for the adjustment of the output image's dimensions and the method of upscaling, providing flexibility in enhancing the resolution of latent images.

inputs.name: samples
inputs.description: The latent representation of an image to be upscaled. This parameter is crucial for determining the starting point of the upscaling process.

inputs.name: upscale_method
inputs.description: Specifies the method used for upscaling the latent image. Different methods can affect the quality and characteristics of the upscaled image.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: The desired width of the upscaled image. If set to 0, it will be calculated based on the height to maintain the aspect ratio.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: The desired height of the upscaled image. If set to 0, it will be calculated based on the width to maintain the aspect ratio.

inputs.name: crop
inputs.description: Determines how the upscaled image should be cropped, affecting the final appearance and dimensions of the output.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The upscaled latent representation of the image, ready for further processing or generation.

LatentUpscaleBy.description: The LatentUpscaleBy node is designed for upscaling latent representations of images. It allows for the adjustment of the scale factor and the method of upscaling, providing flexibility in enhancing the resolution of latent samples.

inputs.name: samples
inputs.description: The latent representation of images to be upscaled. This parameter is crucial for determining the input data that will undergo the upscaling process.

inputs.name: upscale_method
inputs.description: Specifies the method used for upscaling the latent samples. The choice of method can significantly affect the quality and characteristics of the upscaled output.

inputs.name: scale_by
inputs.description: Determines the factor by which the latent samples are scaled. This parameter directly influences the resolution of the output, allowing for precise control over the upscaling process.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The upscaled latent representation, ready for further processing or generation tasks. This output is essential for enhancing the resolution of generated images or for subsequent model operations.

LoadAudio.description: The LoadAudio node is designed for loading audio files from a specified directory, supporting a range of audio formats. It facilitates the process of reading audio data into a format suitable for further audio processing or analysis tasks.

inputs.name: audio
inputs.description: Specifies the audio file to be loaded. The choice of file affects the waveform and sample rate obtained, which are crucial for any subsequent audio processing or analysis.

outputs.name: audio
outputs.description: Returns a dictionary containing the waveform and sample rate of the loaded audio file, ready for further processing or analysis.

LoadImage.description: The LoadImage node is designed for loading and processing images from specified paths. It handles various image formats, applies necessary transformations like EXIF orientation correction, and converts images to a consistent format and tensor representation for further processing in machine learning pipelines.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The 'image' parameter specifies the image file to be loaded and processed from a predefined list of available files. It is crucial for determining the input for the node's operations, affecting the subsequent image manipulation and conversion steps.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: A tensor representing the loaded and processed image, ready for use in further processing or model inference.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: A tensor representing the mask associated with the input image, if applicable, indicating areas of interest or regions to ignore.

LoadImageMask.description: The LoadImageMask node is designed for loading and processing an image to generate a mask based on a specified color channel. It supports handling images with different formats and orientations, converting them to a standardized RGBA format if necessary, and extracting a specific channel (alpha, red, green, blue) to create a mask. This functionality is crucial for tasks that require image segmentation or specific channel manipulation.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: Specifies the image file to be loaded and processed. The selection is limited to the files available in a predefined input directory, facilitating the upload and handling of images for mask generation.

inputs.name: channel
inputs.description: Determines the color channel ('alpha', 'red', 'green', 'blue') of the image to be used for mask creation. This choice directly influences the resulting mask by selecting the relevant channel data.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The output is a mask generated from the specified color channel of the input image. This mask is useful for segmentation and other image processing tasks that require specific channel information.

LoadLatent.description: The LoadLatent node is designed for loading latent representations from files with a '.latent' extension. It adjusts the latent tensor based on its version and prepares it for further processing or generation tasks.

inputs.name: latent
inputs.description: Specifies the name of the latent file to be loaded. This file should be located in a predefined input directory and have a '.latent' extension.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: Provides the loaded and adjusted latent tensor, ready for further processing or generation tasks.

LoraLoader.description: The LoraLoader node is designed to dynamically load and apply LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) adjustments to models and CLIP instances based on specified parameters. It facilitates the customization of model behavior and performance without altering the original model architecture, enabling fine-tuned control over model and CLIP instance characteristics through LoRA parameters.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model to which LoRA adjustments will be applied. It is crucial for defining the base model that will be modified.

inputs.name: clip
inputs.description: The CLIP instance to which LoRA adjustments will be applied. This parameter allows for the modification of CLIP instances alongside models.

inputs.name: lora_name
inputs.description: The name of the LoRA file to be loaded. This determines which LoRA adjustments are applied to the model and CLIP instance.

inputs.name: strength_model
inputs.description: Defines the strength of LoRA adjustments applied to the model. This parameter allows for fine-tuning the impact of LoRA on the model.

inputs.name: strength_clip
inputs.description: Defines the strength of LoRA adjustments applied to the CLIP instance. This parameter allows for adjusting the influence of LoRA on the CLIP instance.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The modified model with LoRA adjustments applied.

outputs.name: clip
outputs.description: The modified CLIP instance with LoRA adjustments applied.

LoraLoaderModelOnly.description: The LoraLoaderModelOnly node is designed to load and apply LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) modifications to a given model, enhancing its capabilities or adapting it for specific tasks without altering the original model architecture. It focuses on applying these modifications solely to the model, disregarding any other components such as CLIP or additional inputs.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model to which LoRA modifications will be applied. This parameter is crucial as it determines the base model that will be enhanced with LoRA parameters.

inputs.name: lora_name
inputs.description: The name of the LoRA file to be applied to the model. This parameter specifies which LoRA modifications are to be loaded and applied, directly influencing the model's adaptation.

inputs.name: strength_model
inputs.description: A floating-point value that determines the strength of the LoRA modifications applied to the model. It allows for fine-tuning the impact of LoRA on the model's behavior.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The modified model with LoRA adaptations applied. This output showcases the enhanced capabilities or specific task adaptations of the original model through LoRA.

MaskComposite.description: This node specializes in combining two mask inputs through a variety of operations such as addition, subtraction, and logical operations, to produce a new, modified mask. It abstractly handles the manipulation of mask data to achieve complex masking effects, serving as a crucial component in mask-based image editing and processing workflows.

inputs.name: destination
inputs.description: The primary mask that will be modified based on the operation with the source mask. It plays a central role in the composite operation, acting as the base for modifications.

inputs.name: source
inputs.description: The secondary mask that will be used in conjunction with the destination mask to perform the specified operation, influencing the final output mask.

inputs.name: x
inputs.description: The horizontal offset at which the source mask will be applied to the destination mask, affecting the positioning of the composite result.

inputs.name: y
inputs.description: The vertical offset at which the source mask will be applied to the destination mask, affecting the positioning of the composite result.

inputs.name: operation
inputs.description: Specifies the type of operation to apply between the destination and source masks, such as 'add', 'subtract', or logical operations, determining the nature of the composite effect.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The resulting mask after applying the specified operation between the destination and source masks, representing the composite outcome.

MaskToImage.description: The `MaskToImage` node is designed to convert a mask into an image format. This transformation allows for the visualization and further processing of masks as images, facilitating a bridge between mask-based operations and image-based applications.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The mask input is essential for the conversion process, serving as the source data that will be transformed into an image format. This input dictates the shape and content of the resulting image.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is an image representation of the input mask, enabling visual inspection and further image-based manipulations.

ModelMergeAdd.description: The ModelMergeAdd node is designed for merging two models by adding key patches from one model to another. This process involves cloning the first model and then applying patches from the second model, allowing for the combination of features or behaviors from both models.

inputs.name: model1
inputs.description: The first model to be cloned and to which patches from the second model will be added. It serves as the base model for the merging process.

inputs.name: model2
inputs.description: The second model from which key patches are extracted and added to the first model. It contributes additional features or behaviors to the merged model.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The result of merging two models by adding key patches from the second model to the first. This merged model combines features or behaviors from both models.

ModelMergeBlocks.description: ModelMergeBlocks is designed for advanced model merging operations, allowing for the integration of two models with customizable blending ratios for different parts of the models. This node facilitates the creation of hybrid models by selectively merging components from two source models based on specified parameters.

inputs.name: model1
inputs.description: The first model to be merged. It serves as the base model onto which patches from the second model are applied.

inputs.name: model2
inputs.description: The second model from which patches are extracted and applied to the first model, based on the specified blending ratios.

inputs.name: input
inputs.description: Specifies the blending ratio for the input layer of the models. It determines how much of the second model's input layer is merged into the first model.

inputs.name: middle
inputs.description: Defines the blending ratio for the middle layers of the models. This parameter controls the integration level of the models' middle layers.

inputs.name: out
inputs.description: Determines the blending ratio for the output layer of the models. It affects the final output by adjusting the contribution of the second model's output layer.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The resulting merged model, which is a hybrid of the two input models with patches applied according to the specified blending ratios.

ModelMergeSD1.description: ModelMergeSD1 is designed for advanced model merging operations, specifically tailored to merge different aspects of two models into a single model. It allows for fine-grained control over the merging process by adjusting the influence of each model's components, such as input blocks, middle blocks, and output blocks, on the final merged model.

inputs.name: model1
inputs.description: The first model to be merged. It serves as the base model for the merging process.

inputs.name: model2
inputs.description: The second model to be merged. Its components are selectively integrated into the first model based on specified ratios.

inputs.name: time_embed.
inputs.description: Adjusts the influence of the time embedding components from both models in the merged model.

inputs.name: label_emb.
inputs.description: Adjusts the influence of the label embedding components from both models in the merged model.

inputs.name: input_blocks.i.
inputs.description: Adjusts the influence of the ith input block from both models in the merged model. The index i ranges from 0 to 11.

inputs.name: middle_block.i.
inputs.description: Adjusts the influence of the ith middle block from both models in the merged model. The index i ranges from 0 to 2.

inputs.name: output_blocks.i.
inputs.description: Adjusts the influence of the ith output block from both models in the merged model. The index i ranges from 0 to 11.

inputs.name: out.
inputs.description: Adjusts the influence of the final output components from both models in the merged model.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The result of the merging process, a single model that integrates selected components and adjustments from the two input models.

ModelMergeSD2.description: ModelMergeSD2 is designed for advanced model merging operations, specifically tailored to work with models that share the same block structures. It enables the precise blending of two models by adjusting the influence of each model's components across various blocks, such as input, middle, and output blocks, using specified blending ratios.

inputs.name: model1
inputs.description: The first model to be merged. It serves as the base model onto which patches from the second model are applied, influencing the final merged model's behavior.

inputs.name: model2
inputs.description: The second model to be merged. Key patches from this model are applied to the first model based on specified blending ratios, affecting the final outcome of the merged model.

inputs.name: time_embed.
inputs.description: Specifies the blending ratio for the time embedding blocks, influencing how temporal aspects of the models are combined.

inputs.name: label_emb.
inputs.description: Determines the blending ratio for the label embedding blocks, affecting how label information from both models is merged.

inputs.name: input_blocks.i.
inputs.description: Controls the blending ratio for the ith input block, allowing for detailed customization of how input-related features are merged. The index i ranges from 0 to 11.

inputs.name: middle_block.i.
inputs.description: Specifies the blending ratio for the ith middle block, enabling precise control over the merging of the models' intermediate processing stages. The index i ranges from 0 to 2.

inputs.name: output_blocks.i.
inputs.description: Sets the blending ratio for the ith output block, dictating how the final output features of the models are combined. The index i ranges from 0 to 11.

inputs.name: out.
inputs.description: Defines the blending ratio for the output blocks, influencing the final output characteristics of the merged model.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The result of the merging process, a single model that integrates the specified blending ratios and modifications from both input models.

ModelMergeSD3_2B.description: This node specializes in merging two models by adjusting their embedding and block parameters specifically for the SD3_2B architecture. It allows for fine-tuned control over the merging process by providing adjustable parameters for positional, context, and various embedder components, as well as for each of the joint blocks and the final layer, enabling a highly customized integration of model features.

inputs.name: model1
inputs.description: The first model to be merged. It serves as the base model for the merging process.

inputs.name: model2
inputs.description: The second model to be merged. Its features will be integrated into the first model based on the specified ratios.

inputs.name: pos_embed.
inputs.description: Adjusts the merging ratio for the positional embedding parameters, influencing how positional information is integrated from both models.

inputs.name: x_embedder.
inputs.description: Controls the merging ratio for the x embedder, affecting the integration of x-axis positional information.

inputs.name: context_embedder.
inputs.description: Determines the merging ratio for the context embedder, impacting how contextual information is blended between the two models.

inputs.name: y_embedder.
inputs.description: Sets the merging ratio for the y embedder, influencing the integration of y-axis positional information.

inputs.name: t_embedder.
inputs.description: Adjusts the merging ratio for the time embedder, affecting how temporal information is merged.

inputs.name: joint_blocks.i.
inputs.description: unknown

inputs.name: final_layer.
inputs.description: Controls the merging ratio for the final layer, determining how the final output features are combined.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The resulting model after merging, incorporating adjustments from both input models according to the specified ratios.

ModelMergeSDXL.description: ModelMergeSDXL is designed for advanced model merging operations, specifically tailored for handling large-scale models. It enables the precise blending of two models by adjusting the influence of each model's components across various blocks, including input, middle, and output blocks, as well as time embedding and label embedding features.

inputs.name: model1
inputs.description: The first model to be merged. It serves as the base model for the merging operation.

inputs.name: model2
inputs.description: The second model to be merged. Its components are selectively blended into the first model based on specified ratios.

inputs.name: time_embed.
inputs.description: Adjusts the blending ratio for the time embedding components of the models.

inputs.name: label_emb.
inputs.description: Adjusts the blending ratio for the label embedding components of the models.

inputs.name: input_blocks.i
inputs.description: Adjusts the blending ratio for the ith input block of the models. The index i ranges from 0 to 8.

inputs.name: middle_block.i
inputs.description: Adjusts the blending ratio for the ith middle block of the models. The index i ranges from 0 to 2.

inputs.name: output_blocks.i
inputs.description: Adjusts the blending ratio for the ith output block of the models. The index i ranges from 0 to 8.

inputs.name: out.
inputs.description: Adjusts the blending ratio for the output components of the models.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The result of merging two models, incorporating the specified blending ratios across various components.

ModelMergeSimple.description: The ModelMergeSimple node is designed for merging two models by blending their parameters based on a specified ratio. This node facilitates the creation of hybrid models that combine the strengths or characteristics of both input models.

inputs.name: model1
inputs.description: The first model to be merged. It serves as the base model onto which patches from the second model are applied.

inputs.name: model2
inputs.description: The second model whose patches are applied onto the first model, influenced by the specified ratio.

inputs.name: ratio
inputs.description: Determines the blend ratio between the two models' parameters, affecting the degree to which each model influences the merged output.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The resulting merged model, incorporating elements from both input models according to the specified ratio.

ModelMergeSubtract.description: This node is designed for advanced model merging operations, specifically to subtract the parameters of one model from another based on a specified multiplier. It enables the customization of model behaviors by adjusting the influence of one model's parameters over another, facilitating the creation of new, hybrid models.

inputs.name: model1
inputs.description: The base model from which parameters will be subtracted.

inputs.name: model2
inputs.description: The model whose parameters will be subtracted from the base model.

inputs.name: multiplier
inputs.description: A floating-point value that scales the subtraction effect on the base model's parameters.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The resulting model after subtracting the parameters of one model from another, scaled by the multiplier.

ModelSamplingContinuousEDM.description: The ModelSamplingContinuousEDM node is designed to configure and apply continuous, evenly distributed model sampling techniques within a deep learning model's architecture. It focuses on adjusting the model's sampling parameters based on provided configurations, enabling precise control over the diffusion process for generating or processing data.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model input represents the deep learning model to which the sampling techniques will be applied, serving as the foundation for configuring and adjusting sampling parameters.

inputs.name: sampling
inputs.description: Specifies the type of sampling technique to be applied, influencing the model's behavior and the characteristics of the generated or processed data.

inputs.name: sigma_max
inputs.description: Defines the maximum value of sigma for the sampling process, setting an upper limit on the diffusion scale.

inputs.name: sigma_min
inputs.description: Defines the minimum value of sigma for the sampling process, setting a lower limit on the diffusion scale.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The modified model with updated sampling parameters, reflecting the applied continuous, evenly distributed model sampling techniques.

ModelSamplingContinuousV.description: This node is designed to enhance a given model by applying a continuous variable (V) sampling technique, which involves cloning the original model and integrating a specialized sampling mechanism based on the 'v_prediction' method. It adjusts the model's behavior through dynamic sigma parameters, enabling refined control over the sampling process.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model to be enhanced with continuous variable sampling. It serves as the foundation for applying the sampling technique.

inputs.name: sampling
inputs.description: Specifies the sampling strategy to be used, which in this case is fixed to 'v_prediction', indicating the use of a prediction-based approach for continuous variable sampling.

inputs.name: sigma_max
inputs.description: The maximum sigma value for the sampling process, allowing for the adjustment of the sampling's upper bound.

inputs.name: sigma_min
inputs.description: The minimum sigma value for the sampling process, enabling the setting of the sampling's lower bound.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The enhanced model with the applied continuous variable (V) sampling technique, featuring the integrated specialized sampling mechanism.

ModelSamplingDiscrete.description: This node is designed to modify the sampling behavior of a model by applying a discrete sampling strategy. It allows for the selection of different sampling methods, such as epsilon, v_prediction, lcm, or x0, and optionally adjusts the model's noise reduction strategy based on the zero-shot noise ratio (zsnr) setting.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model to which the discrete sampling strategy will be applied. This parameter is crucial as it defines the base model that will undergo modification.

inputs.name: sampling
inputs.description: Specifies the discrete sampling method to be applied to the model. The choice of method affects how the model generates samples, offering different strategies for sampling.

inputs.name: zsnr
inputs.description: A boolean flag that, when enabled, adjusts the model's noise reduction strategy based on the zero-shot noise ratio. This can influence the quality and characteristics of the generated samples.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The modified model with the applied discrete sampling strategy. This model is now equipped to generate samples using the specified method and adjustments.

ModelSamplingSD3.description: This node introduces an advanced model sampling technique by applying a discrete flow-based modification to the input model. It enhances the model's sampling capabilities by integrating a shift parameter, allowing for refined control over the sampling process.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model to which the sampling technique will be applied. It serves as the foundation for the advanced sampling modifications.

inputs.name: shift
inputs.description: A parameter that adjusts the intensity of the sampling modification, offering a means to fine-tune the model's sampling behavior.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The modified model with enhanced sampling capabilities, incorporating the discrete flow-based adjustments.

ModelSamplingStableCascade.description: This node is designed to enhance the sampling process of models by applying a stable cascade patch. It clones the input model and integrates advanced sampling techniques, thereby potentially improving the model's performance or altering its behavior in a specified manner.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model to which the stable cascade sampling patch will be applied. This parameter is crucial as it determines the base model that will undergo modification.

inputs.name: shift
inputs.description: A floating-point value that specifies the degree of shift to be applied during the sampling process. This parameter influences how the model's behavior is altered by the patch.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The modified model with the stable cascade sampling patch applied. This output reflects the enhanced or altered version of the input model.

Morphology.description: The Morphology node provides a suite of image morphology operations, such as erosion, dilation, opening, closing, gradient, top hat, and bottom hat transformations. These operations are fundamental for image processing and analysis, allowing for the modification of the geometrical structure of images.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed. The choice of operation and kernel size will determine how the image's structure is modified.

inputs.name: operation
inputs.description: Specifies the morphological operation to be applied to the image. Options include 'erode', 'dilate', 'open', 'close', 'gradient', 'bottom_hat', and 'top_hat', each affecting the image's structure in unique ways.

inputs.name: kernel_size
inputs.description: Determines the size of the kernel used for the morphological operation. A larger kernel size will have a more pronounced effect on the image's structure.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image after applying the specified morphological operation. This image will have undergone structural modifications based on the operation and kernel size chosen.

PatchModelAddDownscale.description: The `PatchModelAddDownscale` node is designed to modify a given model by integrating downscaling and upscaling processes within its computation flow. This node specifically targets the manipulation of model's internal blocks based on specified parameters, enabling the adjustment of the model's behavior to incorporate downscaling at designated stages of processing. It aims to enhance model efficiency or alter its output characteristics by dynamically adjusting the resolution of intermediate representations.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model to be patched with downscaling and upscaling functionalities. It serves as the base for modifications applied by the node.

inputs.name: block_number
inputs.description: Specifies the block number within the model where the downscaling should be applied, targeting specific stages of the model's processing flow.

inputs.name: downscale_factor
inputs.description: The factor by which the model's intermediate representations are downscaled, affecting the resolution and potentially the computational efficiency.

inputs.name: start_percent
inputs.description: Defines the starting percentage of the sigma range for applying downscaling, determining the initial point within the model's processing where downscaling begins.

inputs.name: end_percent
inputs.description: Specifies the ending percentage of the sigma range for downscaling, marking the point within the model's processing where downscaling ceases.

inputs.name: downscale_after_skip
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether the downscaling should occur after skip connections within the model, affecting the placement and impact of downscaling operations.

inputs.name: downscale_method
inputs.description: The method used for downscaling the model's intermediate representations, influencing the quality and characteristics of the downscaling process.

inputs.name: upscale_method
inputs.description: The method used for upscaling the model's intermediate representations back to their original resolution, affecting the quality and characteristics of the upscaling process.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The modified model with integrated downscaling and upscaling functionalities, reflecting the adjustments made to its internal processing flow.

PerpNeg.description: The PerpNeg node is designed to adjust the conditioning of a model by applying a perpendicular negative guidance technique. This technique modifies the input conditioning vectors to enhance the generation of content that diverges from undesired directions, effectively guiding the model towards more desirable outputs.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model parameter represents the generative model to which the perpendicular negative guidance will be applied. It is crucial for determining the base behavior and capabilities of the node.

inputs.name: empty_conditioning
inputs.description: The empty_conditioning parameter is used to provide a baseline or neutral conditioning context, against which positive and negative deviations are calculated and adjusted.

inputs.name: neg_scale
inputs.description: The neg_scale parameter controls the intensity of the negative guidance applied, allowing for fine-tuning of the perpendicular negative effect on the model's output.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The output is a modified version of the input model, adjusted with perpendicular negative guidance to influence its generation process towards desired outcomes.

PerpNegGuider.description: The PerpNegGuider node is designed to guide the generation process by applying perpendicular negative conditioning. It adjusts the generation towards positive conditions while steering clear of specified negative conditions, utilizing a configurable scale for negative conditioning.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model parameter represents the generative model to which the guidance will be applied, serving as the foundation for the conditioning process.

inputs.name: positive
inputs.description: The positive parameter specifies the desired attributes or conditions that the generation should align with, guiding the model towards generating content that matches these positive conditions.

inputs.name: negative
inputs.description: The negative parameter defines the attributes or conditions that the generation should avoid, helping to steer the generated content away from these undesired aspects.

inputs.name: empty_conditioning
inputs.description: The empty_conditioning parameter is used to reset or provide a baseline for the conditioning, ensuring that the guidance starts from a neutral state.

inputs.name: cfg
inputs.description: The cfg parameter controls the overall strength of the conditioning, allowing for fine-tuning of how strongly the positive and negative conditions influence the generation.

inputs.name: neg_scale
inputs.description: The neg_scale parameter adjusts the scale of the negative conditioning, modifying the extent to which negative conditions are avoided in the generation process.

outputs.name: guider
outputs.description: The output is a configured guider object that applies perpendicular negative conditioning to guide the generative model.

PerturbedAttentionGuidance.description: The PerturbedAttentionGuidance node introduces a method to modify the attention mechanism within a given model by applying a perturbation function. This alteration aims to explore the effects of perturbed attention on the model's performance, potentially enhancing its ability to focus on relevant features by adjusting the attention weights.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model parameter represents the neural network model to which the perturbed attention guidance will be applied. It is crucial for defining the base architecture that will undergo the perturbation process.

inputs.name: scale
inputs.description: The scale parameter controls the intensity of the perturbation applied to the attention mechanism. It plays a significant role in determining the extent to which the original attention weights are modified.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: Returns a modified version of the input model, where the attention mechanism has been perturbed according to the specified scale.

PhotoMakerEncode.description: The PhotoMakerEncode node is designed to integrate visual information from images with textual embeddings, enhancing the latter with visual context. This process involves projecting image pixel values into an embedding space, merging these with existing text prompt embeddings, and applying a fusion module to effectively blend the visual and textual information.

inputs.name: photomaker
inputs.description: Specifies the photomaker model to be used for encoding the visual information from images into a format that can be integrated with text embeddings.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image input whose visual information is to be encoded and integrated with text embeddings.

inputs.name: clip
inputs.description: The CLIP model used for text tokenization and encoding, facilitating the integration of visual information with textual context.

inputs.name: text
