outputs.description: The selected image based on the input selector index. This output facilitates dynamic image selection in various applications.

ImageRepeat.description: The ImageRepeat node is designed to duplicate a given image a specified number of times, creating a batch of identical images. This functionality is useful for operations that require multiple instances of the same image for batch processing or augmentation purposes.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: Specifies the image to be repeated. It is crucial for defining the base image that will be duplicated across the batch.

inputs.name: amount
inputs.description: Determines the number of times the input image is repeated. It directly influences the size of the output batch, allowing for flexible batch creation.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is a batch of images, each identical to the input image, repeated according to the specified amount.

ImageScaleDown.description: The ImageScaleDown node is designed to reduce the dimensions of an image or a batch of images to a smaller size, maintaining the aspect ratio and optionally center-cropping to fit the specified dimensions. This operation is essential for optimizing image processing workflows, reducing computational load, and preparing images for further processing or display.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The input images to be scaled down. This parameter is crucial as it directly influences the output by determining which images undergo the scaling process.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: The target width for the scaled-down image(s). This parameter defines the horizontal dimension of the output images, affecting the scaling ratio.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: The target height for the scaled-down image(s). This parameter defines the vertical dimension of the output images, affecting the scaling ratio.

inputs.name: crop
inputs.description: A mode specifying if and how the images should be cropped after scaling to ensure they fit the target dimensions. This affects the final appearance of the scaled images.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The scaled-down images, potentially cropped to fit the specified dimensions. This output is the direct result of the scaling operation applied to the input images.

ImageScaleDownBy.description: The `ImageScaleDownBy` node is designed for scaling down images by a specified factor, maintaining the aspect ratio of the original images. It provides a straightforward way to reduce the resolution of images, which can be useful for optimizing performance or preparing images for specific display requirements.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The `images` parameter represents the images to be scaled down. It is crucial for defining the input images that will undergo the scaling process.

inputs.name: scale_by
inputs.description: The `scale_by` parameter specifies the factor by which the images will be scaled down. It directly influences the new dimensions of the output images, maintaining their aspect ratio.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is a scaled-down version of the input images, with dimensions adjusted according to the `scale_by` factor.

ImageScaleDownToSize.description: The `ImageScaleDownToSize` node is designed for resizing images to a specific size, scaling them down while maintaining their aspect ratio. It offers a mode to scale based on the maximum or minimum dimension, ensuring flexibility in how the image's dimensions are reduced.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The `images` parameter represents the collection of images to be scaled down. It is crucial for defining the input images that will undergo the resizing process.

inputs.name: size
inputs.description: The `size` parameter specifies the target size to which the images will be scaled down. It plays a pivotal role in determining the new dimensions of the images.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: The `mode` parameter determines whether the scaling should consider the maximum or minimum dimension of the images. This choice affects how the aspect ratio is preserved during scaling.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is a tensor of images that have been scaled down to the specified size, with their aspect ratio maintained.

ImageScaleToMegapixels.description: The node is designed to adjust the size of an image to meet a specified total number of megapixels, either by upscaling or downscaling. It incorporates various upscaling methods to achieve the desired image quality and size, ensuring the final image adheres to the specified megapixel count while maintaining aspect ratio.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The input images to be resized. This parameter is crucial as it serves as the base for the scaling operation, determining the starting point for any upscaling or downscaling to achieve the target megapixel size.

inputs.name: megapixels
inputs.description: Defines the target size of the image in megapixels, guiding the scaling process to either increase or decrease the image's dimensions to meet this specification.

inputs.name: upscale_model_opt
inputs.description: Optionally specifies the upscale model to be used for upscaling the image, allowing for advanced customization of the image quality and appearance post-scaling. This parameter influences the visual outcome of the resized image, especially when upscale is required beyond a certain threshold.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The resized image, adjusted to meet the specified megapixel count. This output is the direct result of the scaling operation, reflecting the changes in size and potentially quality based on the chosen upscaling method.

ISNetLoader.description: The ISNetLoader node is designed for loading ISNet models, allowing for the selection of a specific model by name or overriding it with an alternative model if specified. This functionality supports dynamic model loading for image segmentation tasks within the Art Venture/Segmentation category, enhancing flexibility in model management and deployment.

inputs.name: model_name
inputs.description: Specifies the name of the ISNet model to be loaded. This parameter enables the selection of a model from a predefined list of available ISNet models, facilitating targeted model loading based on specific requirements.

inputs.name: model_override
inputs.description: Allows for the specification of an alternative ISNet model to be loaded, overriding the default model selection. This parameter provides flexibility in model usage, accommodating changes or updates in model preferences without altering the core configuration.

outputs.name: isnet_model
outputs.description: Returns the loaded ISNet model, ready for use in image segmentation tasks. This output facilitates the direct application of the model to relevant image processing workflows.

ISNetSegment.description: ISNetSegment is designed for image segmentation using the ISNet model, providing functionality to process images through the model to generate segmented images and their corresponding masks. It supports conditional execution based on the model's availability and the option to specify device mode for computation.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The input images to be segmented. This is the primary data upon which segmentation is performed, determining the visual content to be analyzed and processed.

inputs.name: threshold
inputs.description: A threshold value for segmentation, influencing the sensitivity of the segmentation process. It determines the cut-off point for what is considered part of the segment versus the background.

inputs.name: device_mode
inputs.description: Specifies the computational device preference ('AUTO', 'Prefer GPU', 'CPU') for running the segmentation, affecting performance and resource utilization.

inputs.name: enabled
inputs.description: A boolean flag to enable or disable the segmentation process, allowing for conditional execution based on external criteria.

inputs.name: isnet_model
inputs.description: An optional ISNet model instance to be used for segmentation. If not provided, the system will attempt to load a default model.

outputs.name: segmented
outputs.description: The segmented images resulting from the application of the ISNet model on the input images.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The masks corresponding to the segmented images, indicating the segmented areas.

LaMaInpaint.description: The LaMaInpaint node is designed for object removal and image inpainting tasks, leveraging deep learning models to fill in missing or unwanted areas of an image with plausible textures and details. It processes images and corresponding masks to generate inpainted images, seamlessly blending the inpainted regions with the original image content.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image tensor that needs inpainting. It represents the visual data where certain regions are marked for removal or restoration.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The mask tensor indicating the areas to be inpainted. Pixels with non-zero values in the mask are treated as regions needing inpainting.

inputs.name: device_mode
inputs.description: Specifies the device (CPU or GPU) on which the inpainting operation is performed, allowing for flexibility in resource utilization.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output tensor containing the inpainted image, where the specified regions have been filled in with generated content matching the surrounding areas.

LoadImageAsMaskFromUrl.description: This node is designed to load images from URLs and convert them into masks based on a specified channel. It supports selecting from alpha, red, green, or blue channels to create the mask, making it versatile for various image processing tasks where masking based on color channels is required.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: A string containing the URL(s) of the image(s) to be loaded. If multiple URLs are provided, they should be separated by newlines. This parameter is essential for fetching the images from which masks will be created.

inputs.name: channel
inputs.description: Specifies the color channel ('alpha', 'red', 'green', 'blue') to be used for creating the mask. This choice determines which part of the image data will be converted into a mask, affecting the outcome significantly.

outputs.name: masks
outputs.description: The output is a tensor of masks created from the specified channel of the input images. These masks are suitable for further image processing tasks, such as compositing or inpainting.

LoadImageFromUrl.description: This node is designed to load images from URLs, supporting a variety of formats including direct links, file paths, and data URIs. It abstracts the complexities of fetching and decoding images from different sources, making it easier to integrate external images into workflows or applications.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image data directly provided for processing, allowing for flexibility in sourcing images beyond URLs.

inputs.name: keep_alpha_channel
inputs.description: Determines whether the alpha channel of the image should be preserved during processing, affecting the output image format.

inputs.name: output_mode
inputs.description: Specifies the desired format of the output image, influencing how the image is processed and returned.

inputs.name: url
inputs.description: The URL or path of the image to be loaded. It supports direct links, file paths, and data URIs, enabling the node to fetch and decode images from various sources.

outputs.name: images
outputs.description: The loaded images, processed according to the specified parameters such as alpha channel preservation and output mode.

outputs.name: masks
outputs.description: The masks generated for the images, if any, based on the processing options selected.

outputs.name: has_image
outputs.description: A flag indicating whether an image was successfully loaded and processed.

LoadJsonFromUrl.description: The node is designed to fetch JSON data from a specified URL, providing a straightforward way to load and integrate external data into the node's workflow.

inputs.name: url
inputs.description: The URL from which JSON data is to be fetched. It serves as the primary source for the node to retrieve data.

inputs.name: print_to_console
inputs.description: A flag to control whether the fetched JSON content should be printed to the console, aiding in debugging or verification.

outputs.name: json
outputs.description: The JSON data retrieved from the specified URL, ready for further processing or utilization within the node's workflow.

LoadVideoFromUrl.description: The LoadVideoFromUrl node is designed to facilitate the loading of video content from URLs into a usable format for further processing or analysis. It supports handling various URL schemes, including direct links to video files, local file paths, and specialized URLs with parameters for video retrieval. This node also includes functionality to manage video files by downloading or relocating them as needed, ensuring compatibility with the system's file structure.

inputs.name: video
inputs.description: The 'video' parameter is the URL or path of the video to be loaded. It plays a crucial role in determining the source from which the video will be fetched or loaded, directly influencing the node's processing logic and output.

inputs.name: force_rate
inputs.description: This parameter allows for the specification of a forced frame rate for the loaded video, affecting the temporal resolution and playback speed.

inputs.name: force_size
inputs.description: Allows setting a forced resolution for the loaded video, which can alter the spatial dimensions of the output frames.

inputs.name: custom_width
inputs.description: Specifies a custom width for the output video frames, overriding the default or source video's width.

inputs.name: custom_height
inputs.description: Specifies a custom height for the output video frames, overriding the default or source video's height.

inputs.name: frame_load_cap
inputs.description: Limits the number of frames to be loaded from the video, useful for reducing memory usage or focusing on specific segments.

inputs.name: skip_first_frames
inputs.description: Skips a specified number of frames from the beginning of the video, useful for bypassing unneeded content or intros.

inputs.name: select_every_nth
inputs.description: Loads every nth frame from the video, allowing for temporal downsampling and reduced dataset size.

inputs.name: meta_batch
inputs.description: A parameter for batch processing metadata, potentially used for optimizing load operations or handling multiple videos.

inputs.name: vae
inputs.description: An optional VAE model parameter for potential preprocessing or encoding of video frames.

outputs.name: frames
outputs.description: A list of loaded videos, each represented as a tensor. This output is crucial for subsequent video processing tasks.

outputs.name: frame_count
outputs.description: A list containing the number of frames for each video loaded. This information is essential for frame-based video analysis and processing.

outputs.name: has_video
outputs.description: A boolean indicating whether any video was successfully loaded. This flag can be used to trigger further processing or handle errors.

MergeModels.description: The MergeModels node is designed to blend two models together based on a specified ratio, effectively merging their characteristics and features. This process allows for the creation of hybrid models that combine the strengths or attributes of both input models.

inputs.name: model1
inputs.description: The first model to be merged. It serves as the base model onto which patches from the second model are applied, influenced by the specified ratio.

inputs.name: model2
inputs.description: The second model to be merged. Key patches from this model are applied to the first model, with the extent of their influence determined by the ratio.

inputs.name: ratio
inputs.description: A floating-point value that determines the balance between the two models in the merging process. A ratio closer to 1.0 gives more weight to the second model's characteristics.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The resulting model after merging the two input models according to the specified ratio.

NumberScaler.description: The NumberScaler node is designed to scale a numerical value within a specified range to a new range, effectively normalizing or denormalizing the value based on the provided minimum and maximum boundaries.

inputs.name: min
inputs.description: Specifies the minimum value of the original range. It sets the lower boundary for scaling the input value.

inputs.name: max
inputs.description: Defines the maximum value of the original range. It sets the upper boundary for scaling the input value.

inputs.name: scale_to_min
inputs.description: Determines the minimum value of the target scaling range. It influences the lower limit of the output scaled value.

inputs.name: scale_to_max
inputs.description: Sets the maximum value of the target scaling range. It influences the upper limit of the output scaled value.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: The numerical value to be scaled from its original range to the target range.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The scaled numerical value, adjusted to fit within the new specified range.

OverlayInpaintedImage.description: This node is designed to overlay an inpainted image onto another image, potentially within a specified crop region. It ensures that the overlay operation respects the dimensions and batch sizes of the input images, blending them seamlessly to produce a composite output.

inputs.name: inpainted
inputs.description: The inpainted image tensor to be overlaid onto the base image. It plays a crucial role in the overlay process by providing the content that fills in the missing or altered parts of the original image.

inputs.name: overlay_image
inputs.description: The base image tensor onto which the inpainted image will be overlaid. This image serves as the backdrop for the inpainted content, integrating both to create a cohesive visual output.

inputs.name: crop_region
inputs.description: A tensor specifying the region within the base image where the inpainted image should be overlaid. This allows for precise control over the placement and integration of the inpainted content within the larger image context.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The resulting image tensor after overlaying the inpainted image onto the base image, within the specified crop region if applicable. This image combines the visual elements of both inputs in a unified manner.

OverlayInpaintedLatent.description: The OverlayInpaintedLatent node is designed to blend original and inpainted latent representations based on a given mask, producing a seamless overlay where the inpainted content is integrated with the original content. This process is crucial for applications in art and image editing, where maintaining the integrity of the original image while incorporating new elements is essential.

inputs.name: original
inputs.description: The 'original' input represents the original latent representation before any inpainting has been applied. It serves as the base for the overlay process, ensuring that the inpainted content is integrated in a way that respects the original image's structure and content.

inputs.name: inpainted
inputs.description: The 'inpainted' input contains the latent representation of the inpainted areas. It is crucial for the overlay process, as it provides the new content that will be blended with the original latent representation based on the mask.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The 'mask' input specifies the areas of the original latent representation that should be replaced or blended with the inpainted content. It plays a key role in determining how the original and inpainted representations are combined during the overlay process.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The output is a latent representation that combines the original and inpainted content based on the provided mask, resulting in a seamless integration of both elements.

PrepareImageAndMaskForInpaint.description: This node prepares an image and its corresponding mask for the inpainting process by applying various preprocessing steps such as resizing, blurring, and adjusting the mask to ensure it is properly aligned and formatted for inpainting algorithms.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image tensor that needs inpainting, which is a crucial component for the inpainting process as it provides the visual context.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The mask tensor indicating areas to inpaint, essential for identifying the regions within the image that require restoration or modification.

inputs.name: mask_blur
inputs.description: An integer specifying the amount of blur to apply to the mask, which helps in smoothing the edges of the mask for a more natural inpainting result.

inputs.name: inpaint_masked
inputs.description: A boolean indicating whether to inpaint the masked areas, guiding the inpainting process on which regions to focus.

inputs.name: mask_padding
inputs.description: An integer defining the padding around the mask, which is used to adjust the focus area of the inpainting process.

outputs.name: inpaint_image
outputs.description: The inpainted image after applying the inpainting algorithm, showcasing the restored or modified regions.

outputs.name: inpaint_mask
outputs.description: The processed mask after applying the specified preprocessing steps, ready for use in the inpainting process.

outputs.name: overlay_image
outputs.description: An image that combines the original and inpainted images, providing a visual comparison between them.

outputs.name: crop_region
outputs.description: The region of the image that was selected for inpainting, indicating the focus area of the process.

QRCodeGenerator.description: The QRCodeGenerator node is designed to generate QR codes based on specified text inputs, offering customization options such as size, version, error correction level, box size, and border size. It encapsulates the process of QR code creation, making it accessible for various applications that require embedding information within a QR code format.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The 'text' parameter is the input string to be encoded into the QR code. It is crucial as it determines the content that the QR code will represent.

inputs.name: size
inputs.description: Specifies the final size of the generated QR code image in pixels. It affects the visibility and scannability of the QR code.

inputs.name: qr_version
inputs.description: Determines the version of the QR code, which indirectly controls the size and the amount of data that can be encoded.

inputs.name: error_correction
inputs.description: Sets the error correction level of the QR code, affecting its resilience to damage and the amount of data that can be restored.

inputs.name: box_size
inputs.description: Defines the size of each box (or pixel) in the QR code, influencing the overall size of the QR code.

inputs.name: border
inputs.description: Specifies the width of the border around the QR code. A larger border can improve scannability but increases the overall size of the QR code.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is an image of the generated QR code, ready for use in various applications.

RandomFloat.description: The RandomFloat node generates a random floating-point number within a specified range. It abstracts the complexity of random number generation using PyTorch's capabilities to provide a simple interface for obtaining a random float, which can be used in various applications requiring stochastic behavior.

inputs.name: min
inputs.description: Specifies the minimum value in the range from which the random float will be generated. It sets the lower bound for the random number, ensuring that the output is not less than this value.

inputs.name: max
inputs.description: Defines the maximum value in the range for the random float generation. It acts as the upper limit, guaranteeing that the generated number does not exceed this value.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The generated random floating-point number.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The string representation of the generated random floating-point number.

RandomInt.description: The `RandomInt` node generates a random integer within a specified range. It abstracts the complexity of random number generation, providing a simple interface for obtaining integers for various applications, such as random sampling or stochastic processes.

inputs.name: min
inputs.description: Specifies the minimum value in the range from which the random integer will be generated. It sets the lower bound for the random number generation.

inputs.name: max
inputs.description: Defines the maximum value in the range for the random integer generation. It establishes the upper limit, ensuring the generated number does not exceed this value.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: The generated random integer within the specified range.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: A string representation of the generated random integer, facilitating its use in contexts requiring textual data.

SAMEmbeddingToImage.description: The SAMEmbeddingToImage node is designed to convert SAM embeddings into visual representations, enabling the intuitive interpretation and manipulation of the embedded data. It abstracts the complex information contained within the embeddings into a more accessible image format.

inputs.name: embedding
inputs.description: The embedding input represents the SAM embedding to be transformed into an image. This embedding is crucial as it contains the encoded information that will be visualized as an image.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is an image generated from the SAM embedding, allowing for the visualization and further processing of the encoded information.

SDXLAspectRatioSelector.description: The SDXLAspectRatioSelector node is designed to select and adjust the aspect ratio for images, ensuring they fit specific dimensions while maintaining the original proportions. It provides a mechanism to scale images to a wide range of predefined aspect ratios, making it suitable for various display or processing requirements.

inputs.name: aspect_ratio
inputs.description: Specifies the desired aspect ratio for the image, chosen from a predefined list of ratios. This selection determines the dimensions to which the image will be scaled, affecting its final appearance.

outputs.name: ratio
outputs.description: The selected aspect ratio as a string, indicating the proportion between width and height of the image.

outputs.name: width
outputs.description: The calculated width of the image after scaling to the selected aspect ratio.

outputs.name: height
outputs.description: The calculated height of the image after scaling to the selected aspect ratio.

SeedSelector.description: The SeedSelector node is designed to select a seed value for procedural generation tasks, allowing users to switch between random and fixed seed modes. This flexibility enables both reproducibility of results with a fixed seed and the generation of varied outcomes with random seeds.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Determines whether the seed selection is random or fixed, impacting the reproducibility and variability of the generated outcomes.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: The seed value used when mode is set to random, influencing the procedural generation process.

inputs.name: fixed_seed
inputs.description: The seed value used when mode is set to fixed, ensuring reproducibility of the generated outcomes.

outputs.name: seed
outputs.description: The selected seed value, either fixed or randomly determined based on the mode, used for procedural generation.

StringToInt.description: Converts a string representation of a number into its integer form, providing a straightforward way to parse and utilize numerical data represented as text.

inputs.name: string
inputs.description: The string input represents the numerical data in text form that needs to be converted into an integer. This parameter is crucial for the conversion process, determining the numerical value that will be returned.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: The integer representation of the input string, allowing for numerical operations and processing within the system.

StringToNumber.description: The `StringToNumber` node converts a string representation of a number into its numerical form, offering options for rounding the result to the nearest integer, flooring it, or ceiling it. This functionality is essential for scenarios where numerical values are received as text and precise mathematical operations or comparisons are required.

inputs.name: string
inputs.description: The `string` parameter takes a string input that represents a number, which is then converted into a numerical form. This conversion is crucial for further numerical operations or analyses.

inputs.name: rounding
inputs.description: The `rounding` parameter specifies the method of rounding (nearest, floor, or ceil) to be applied to the converted number, affecting the final numerical output.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: The integer part of the converted number, after applying the specified rounding method.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The floating-point representation of the converted number, providing a precise numerical value.

It provides a sophisticated interface for applying custom modifications to the attention layers, enabling fine-tuned control over model behavior and performance.

Automatic CFG - Attention modifiers test.description: This node is designed to test and apply various attention modifier configurations to computational graph models, specifically focusing on enhancing or altering the attention mechanisms within these models. It aims to experiment with different attention modification strategies to optimize model performance or behavior.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: Specifies the seed for random number generation, ensuring reproducibility of the attention modifier application.

inputs.name: sigma_start
inputs.description: Defines the starting value of sigma for the attention modifier, indicating the beginning of the range within which the modifier is active.

inputs.name: sigma_end
inputs.description: Defines the ending value of sigma for the attention modifier, indicating the end of the range within which the modifier is active.

inputs.name: self_attn_mod_eval
inputs.description: Contains the evaluation code for self-attention modification, allowing for dynamic adjustment of attention mechanisms based on the model's requirements.

inputs.name: unet_block_id_input
inputs.description: Identifies the input block IDs where the attention modifier will be applied, enabling targeted modifications.

inputs.name: unet_block_id_middle
inputs.description: Identifies the middle block IDs where the attention modifier will be applied, enabling targeted modifications.

inputs.name: unet_block_id_output
inputs.description: Identifies the output block IDs where the attention modifier will be applied, enabling targeted modifications.

inputs.name: unet_attn
inputs.description: Specifies the type of attention (self, cross, or both) to be modified, allowing for precise control over the modification process.

inputs.name: join_parameters
inputs.description: Allows for the combination of attention modifier parameters from another source, enhancing the flexibility of attention modification.

outputs.name: Attention modifier
outputs.description: Outputs the modified attention parameters, reflecting the changes made to the model's attention mechanisms.

outputs.name: Parameters as string
outputs.description: Provides a string representation of the attention modifier parameters, facilitating easy review and documentation of the modifications.

Automatic CFG - Attention modifiers.description: This node encompasses a suite of functionalities aimed at modifying and enhancing the attention mechanisms within generative models. It provides a variety of methods to adjust attention parameters dynamically, apply custom attention patches, and manipulate attention layers for improved model performance and customization. The node's capabilities allow for experimental and targeted modifications to the model's attention mechanisms, facilitating advanced configuration and optimization of generative processes.

inputs.name: sigma_start
inputs.description: Defines the starting value of sigma for the attention modification process, determining the initial scope of modifications.

inputs.name: sigma_end
inputs.description: Sets the ending value of sigma for the attention modification process, marking the limit of the attention adjustments.

inputs.name: self_attn_mod_eval
inputs.description: Contains the evaluation code for self-attention modifications, allowing for dynamic and custom adjustments to the model's attention mechanism.

inputs.name: unet_block_id_input
inputs.description: Identifies the input UNet block IDs where the attention modifications will be applied, specifying the target areas within the model.

inputs.name: unet_block_id_middle
inputs.description: Specifies the middle UNet block IDs for applying attention modifications, targeting intermediate layers of the model.

inputs.name: unet_block_id_output
inputs.description: Indicates the output UNet block IDs for attention modifications, focusing on the final layers of the model.

inputs.name: unet_attn
inputs.description: Determines the type of attention (self, cross, or both) to be modified, guiding the application of attention adjustments.

inputs.name: join_parameters
inputs.description: Optional parameter for joining attention modifier parameters from different sources, enhancing the flexibility of attention modifications.

outputs.name: Attention modifier
outputs.description: The modified attention parameters or configurations resulting from the application of attention modifiers. This output is crucial for understanding the impact of modifications on the model's attention mechanisms.

outputs.name: Parameters as string
outputs.description: A string representation of the attention modification parameters, providing a clear and concise summary of the adjustments made.

Automatic CFG - Custom attentions.description: This node is designed to concatenate attention modifier parameters from two sources, creating a unified set of parameters for further processing. It serves as a utility within the context of configuring or enhancing model attention mechanisms, particularly in scenarios requiring the combination of distinct attention modification strategies.

Automatic CFG - Excellent attention.description: This node specializes in dynamically configuring a model's attention mechanism to enhance its performance. It applies a series of attention modifiers based on various conditions, including positive, negative, and global modifiers, to optimize the model's focus and processing capabilities. This customization allows for improved effectiveness in generating or interpreting data by adjusting the model's attention in response to specific scenarios.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model to which dynamic attention configuration modifications will be applied, serving as the foundation for optimizing attention mechanisms.

inputs.name: Auto_CFG
inputs.description: A flag indicating whether automatic configuration is enabled, allowing the node to dynamically adjust attention mechanisms based on predefined conditions.

inputs.name: patch_multiplier
inputs.description: A multiplier that adjusts the intensity of the attention modification, influencing the strength of the applied attention patches.

inputs.name: patch_cond
inputs.description: A condition that triggers the application of attention modifiers designed to enhance the model's focus under specific scenarios.

inputs.name: patch_uncond
inputs.description: A condition that triggers the application of attention modifiers regardless of specific scenarios, applying a uniform enhancement across the model.

inputs.name: light_patch
inputs.description: A flag that determines the application of lighter, less intensive attention modifiers, offering a subtler adjustment to the model's attention mechanism.

inputs.name: mute_self_input_layer_i_cond
inputs.description: A condition that mutes the self-attention inputs at a specified layer under certain conditions, reducing the model's internal focus at that layer.

inputs.name: mute_cross_input_layer_i_cond
inputs.description: A condition that mutes the cross-attention inputs at a specified layer under certain conditions, reducing the model's external focus at that layer.

inputs.name: mute_self_input_layer_i_uncond
inputs.description: A condition that unconditionally mutes the self-attention inputs at a specified layer, reducing the model's internal focus at that layer regardless of external conditions.

inputs.name: mute_cross_input_layer_i_uncond
inputs.description: A condition that unconditionally mutes the cross-attention inputs at a specified layer, reducing the model's external focus at that layer regardless of external conditions.

inputs.name: uncond_sigma_end
inputs.description: The ending value of sigma for unconditional attention modification, defining the lower bound of the modification's intensity.

inputs.name: bypass_layer_i_instead_of_mute
inputs.description: A flag that, when enabled, bypasses the attention mechanism at a specified layer instead of muting it, allowing for alternative processing pathways.

inputs.name: save_as_preset
inputs.description: A flag indicating whether to save the configured attention modifications as a preset for future use, facilitating easy replication of the configuration.

inputs.name: preset_name
inputs.description: The name under which the attention modification preset will be saved, allowing for easy identification and reuse.

inputs.name: attn_mod_for_positive_operation
inputs.description: Additional attention modifiers to be applied for positive operations, enhancing the model's focus on relevant aspects.

inputs.name: attn_mod_for_negative_operation
inputs.description: Additional attention modifiers to be applied for negative operations, mitigating the model's focus on less relevant aspects.

outputs.name: Model
outputs.description: unknown

outputs.name: Parameters as string
outputs.description: A string representation of the parameters used for the attention modifications, providing insight into the configuration applied.

Automatic CFG - Negative.description: This node is designed to modify the behavior of generative models by applying conditional fine-grained control, specifically targeting the enhancement or suppression of certain features or themes within the generated content. It leverages advanced dynamic configuration techniques to adjust the model's output based on specified negative conditions, aiming to refine the generation process and output quality.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The generative model to be modified. This parameter is crucial as it determines the base model on which the conditional fine-grained control will be applied, affecting the overall generation process and output.

inputs.name: boost
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether to skip unconditional generation steps, thereby focusing the model's generation capabilities more directly on the specified conditions. This can lead to more pronounced effects of the negative conditions on the generated content.

inputs.name: negative_strength
inputs.description: A floating-point value specifying the strength of the negative conditioning. This affects how strongly the specified negative conditions influence the model's output, allowing for fine-tuned control over the suppression of undesired features or themes.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The modified generative model, now capable of applying conditional fine-grained control based on the specified negative conditions. This model is expected to produce content that aligns more closely with the desired output characteristics by suppressing undesired features or themes.

Automatic CFG - Post rescale only.description: This node applies a post-conditional generative feedback (CFG) rescaling operation to adjust the balance between the original and degraded image features based on a scaling factor derived from the difference between the original and a secondary image (sag). It dynamically adjusts the scaling of the added CFG effect, aiming to enhance image restoration or modification tasks by recalibrating the intensity of changes applied to the original image, ensuring a more controlled and precise enhancement.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model to which the post-CFG rescaling operation will be applied, serving as the base for further adjustments.

inputs.name: subtract_latent_mean
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether to subtract the mean of the latent space representation.

inputs.name: subtract_latent_mean_sigma_start
inputs.description: The starting value of sigma for which subtracting the latent mean is applicable.

inputs.name: subtract_latent_mean_sigma_end
inputs.description: The ending value of sigma for which subtracting the latent mean is applicable.

inputs.name: latent_intensity_rescale
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether to apply intensity rescaling to the latent space representation.

inputs.name: latent_intensity_rescale_method
inputs.description: The method used for rescaling the intensity of the latent space representation.

inputs.name: latent_intensity_rescale_cfg
inputs.description: The configuration parameters for the latent intensity rescale operation.

inputs.name: latent_intensity_rescale_sigma_start
inputs.description: The starting value of sigma for which the latent intensity rescale is applicable.

inputs.name: latent_intensity_rescale_sigma_end
inputs.description: The ending value of sigma for which the latent intensity rescale is applicable.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The model after applying the dynamic rescaling of the CFG effect, reflecting a balanced enhancement.

Automatic CFG - Preset Loader.description: This node is designed to dynamically adjust the configuration of generative models by applying predefined or custom presets. It enhances model performance and flexibility by allowing users to modify model behavior based on specific presets, which can include adjustments to conditional and unconditional generation parameters, attention mechanisms, and other model-specific settings.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The generative model to which the preset configurations will be applied. This parameter is crucial as it determines the base model that will be modified according to the selected preset.

inputs.name: preset
inputs.description: The name of the preset to be applied to the model. Presets define a set of parameters and modifications that tailor the model's behavior for specific tasks or performance characteristics.

inputs.name: uncond_sigma_end
inputs.description: Specifies the end value for the unconditional sigma parameter, allowing for fine-tuning of the model's unconditional generation capabilities.

inputs.name: use_uncond_sigma_end_from_preset
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether to use the unconditional sigma end value specified in the preset or the value provided directly to the node.

inputs.name: automatic_cfg
inputs.description: Determines the mode of automatic configuration to be applied, which can range from preset-defined settings to custom configurations aimed at optimizing model performance.

inputs.name: join_global_parameters
inputs.description: Optional parameters that can be globally applied to the model, enhancing its capabilities or modifying its behavior in conjunction with the selected preset.

outputs.name: Model
outputs.description: unknown

outputs.name: Preset name
outputs.description: unknown

outputs.name: Parameters as string
outputs.description: A detailed string representation of the applied preset parameters, providing insight into the modifications made to the model.

Automatic CFG - Unpatch function.description: This node is designed to revert any previously applied configuration patches to a model, effectively restoring it to its original state without the specific adjustments made for automatic control flow graph (CFG) manipulation.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model to be unpatched. This input is crucial as it specifies the model from which the automatic CFG-related patches will be removed, ensuring the model is returned to its initial configuration.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The unpatched model, returned after removing specific automatic CFG-related patches, restoring it to its original, unmodified state.

Automatic CFG - Warp Drive.description: This node engages an advanced configuration for dynamic control flow graph (CFG) modification in a 'Warp Drive' mode, aimed at maximizing the speed and efficiency of model adjustments. It suggests settings for different levels of risk and performance, emphasizing speed and experimental adjustments for clearer subject prompts or general use.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model to be patched with advanced dynamic CFG settings for enhanced performance and speed.

inputs.name: uncond_sigma_start
inputs.description: Specifies the starting value of unconditional sigma for the dynamic CFG adjustments, influencing the model's behavior at the beginning of the patching process.

inputs.name: uncond_sigma_end
inputs.description: Defines the ending value of unconditional sigma for the dynamic CFG adjustments, affecting the model's behavior at the conclusion of the patching process.

inputs.name: fake_uncond_sigma_end
inputs.description: Determines the fake ending value of unconditional sigma used in the dynamic CFG adjustments, part of the advanced settings to tweak the model's performance.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The patched model with advanced dynamic CFG settings applied, optimized for speed and efficiency.

Automatic CFG.description: The Automatic CFG node is designed to dynamically modify the configuration of models to optimize their performance for specific tasks. It leverages advanced techniques to adjust model parameters and settings based on the input conditions, aiming to enhance model accuracy, speed, or other performance metrics.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The 'model' parameter represents the model to be modified. It is crucial for the node's operation as it serves as the base upon which modifications are applied to achieve the desired configuration.

inputs.name: hard_mode
inputs.description: The 'hard_mode' parameter dictates the strictness of the configuration adjustments. When set to True, it applies more rigorous modifications to the model, potentially leading to higher performance at the cost of flexibility.

inputs.name: boost
inputs.description: The 'boost' parameter enables or disables performance enhancements. When True, it activates additional modifications that can further improve the model's performance.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The modified model with optimized configuration settings. This output reflects the adjustments made based on the input parameters and the desired performance enhancements.

CADS.description: The CADS node is designed to apply conditional adaptive diffusion steps to a given model, enhancing its ability to generate or modify content based on specified conditions. It dynamically adjusts the diffusion process based on the progression of steps and conditions, aiming to improve the quality and relevance of the generated outputs.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model to which the CADS adjustments will be applied. It serves as the base for the adaptive diffusion process, determining the initial state and capabilities of the generation or modification task.

inputs.name: noise_scale
inputs.description: Defines the scale of noise to be added during the diffusion process. This parameter influences the degree of randomness and variation introduced at each step, affecting the diversity and novelty of the output.

inputs.name: t1
inputs.description: The lower threshold for the adaptive scaling factor, marking the beginning of the transition phase in the diffusion process. It helps in controlling the blend between original content and generated noise.

inputs.name: t2
inputs.description: The upper threshold for the adaptive scaling factor, indicating the end of the transition phase in the diffusion process. This parameter is crucial for fine-tuning the balance between preserving original details and introducing new elements.

inputs.name: rescale
inputs.description: Optional parameter that allows for the rescaling of the output after noise addition, aiming to maintain the overall distribution of the generated content. It can help in preserving the quality and consistency of the output.

inputs.name: start_step
inputs.description: Optional parameter that specifies the starting step of the adaptive diffusion process. It can be used to resume or customize the progression of the diffusion, tailoring it to specific needs or preferences.

inputs.name: total_steps
inputs.description: Optional parameter that defines the total number of steps in the diffusion process. It sets the boundary for the adaptation and progression, influencing the depth and thoroughness of the content generation or modification.

inputs.name: apply_to
inputs.description: Optional parameter that determines the specific part of the model to which the CADS adjustments are applied, such as conditioning or unconditioned components. It allows for targeted modifications, enhancing the relevance and effectiveness of the output.

inputs.name: key
inputs.description: Optional parameter that specifies the key for selecting the target component within the model for noise addition. It enables precise control over the diffusion process, focusing on specific areas or features.

inputs.name: noise_type
inputs.description: Optional parameter that defines the type of noise to be added during the diffusion process. It offers the ability to customize the nature of the introduced randomness, affecting the texture and characteristics of the output.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The modified model after applying the CADS adjustments. It represents the enhanced version of the original model, equipped with adaptive diffusion capabilities for improved content generation or modification.

CCSR_Model_Select.description: This node is designed to select and load a specific checkpoint for the CCSR model based on the provided checkpoint name. It initializes or updates the CCSR model in the system with the selected checkpoint, ensuring the model is ready for subsequent image processing tasks.

inputs.name: ckpt_name
inputs.description: The name of the checkpoint to load for the CCSR model. This parameter is crucial for identifying which specific model checkpoint to initialize or update the CCSR model with.

outputs.name: ccsr_model
outputs.description: The loaded CCSR model along with its data type, ready for use in image processing tasks. The dictionary contains the model itself and its data type, providing detailed information necessary for image processing applications.

CCSR_Upscale.description: The node is designed to upscale images or latent representations, leveraging custom scaling methods to enhance the resolution or detail of the input data. It focuses on applying advanced upscaling techniques to improve image quality or adjust the size of latent representations for further processing or visualization.

inputs.name: ccsr_model
inputs.description: Specifies the CCSR model to be used for upscaling, which determines the algorithm and approach for enhancing the image or latent representation.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: Represents the input image to be upscaled. The quality and characteristics of the input image directly influence the outcome of the upscaling process.

inputs.name: resize_method
inputs.description: Determines the method to be used for resizing during the upscaling process, offering a variety of algorithms such as lanczos among others.

inputs.name: scale_by
inputs.description: Defines the factor by which the image or latent representation is to be scaled. This value allows for precise control over the enlargement of the input data.

inputs.name: steps
inputs.description: Specifies the number of steps to be used in the upscaling process, affecting the detail and quality of the upscaled output.

inputs.name: t_max
inputs.description: The maximum threshold for the upscaling process, influencing the extent of detail enhancement.

inputs.name: t_min
inputs.description: The minimum threshold for the upscaling process, affecting the base level of detail to be enhanced.

inputs.name: sampling_method
inputs.description: Specifies the sampling method to be used in the upscaling process, affecting the algorithm's approach to enhancing detail and resolution.

inputs.name: tile_size
inputs.description: Defines the size of tiles to be used in the upscaling process, allowing for efficient processing of large images by breaking them into manageable pieces.

inputs.name: tile_stride
inputs.description: Determines the stride of tiling during the upscaling process, affecting the overlap and integration of upscaled tiles.

inputs.name: vae_tile_size_encode
inputs.description: Specifies the tile size for the encoding phase in the upscaling process, affecting the resolution and detail of the encoded representation.

inputs.name: vae_tile_size_decode
inputs.description: Specifies the tile size for the decoding phase in the upscaling process, affecting the resolution and detail of the decoded output.

inputs.name: color_fix_type
inputs.description: Determines the method for color correction during the upscaling process, offering options like 'adain' and 'wavelet' for enhanced visual fidelity.

inputs.name: keep_model_loaded
inputs.description: Indicates whether the CCSR model should remain loaded in memory after the upscaling process, affecting resource utilization and performance.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: Specifies the seed value for random number generation during the upscaling process, ensuring reproducibility of results.

outputs.name: upscaled_image
outputs.description: The result of the upscaling process, which is an enhanced-resolution version of the input samples. This output reflects the applied upscaling method and target dimensions.

DownloadAndLoadCCSRModel.description: This node is responsible for downloading and loading the CCSR model into memory, ensuring it is ready for use. It handles the model's retrieval, configuration, and initialization, adapting to the required precision (FP16 or FP32) based on the model's specifications.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: Specifies the model variant to be loaded, influencing the precision (FP16 or FP32) and the specific model configuration to be used.

outputs.name: ccsr_model
outputs.description: Provides the loaded CCSR model along with its data type, ready for further processing or inference.

Clarity AI Upscaler.description: The Clarity AI Upscaler node is designed to enhance image quality through upscaling, utilizing Clarity AI's API to process images based on various artistic and technical parameters. It allows for customization of the upscaling process through attributes like creativity, resemblance, dynamic, fractality, and style, aiming to produce higher-resolution images that meet specific aesthetic or technical requirements.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The primary image input for upscaling. This is a required parameter that defines the image to be processed and enhanced.

inputs.name: prompt
inputs.description: An optional text prompt that can guide the upscaling process, allowing for more creative or specific enhancements based on textual descriptions.

inputs.name: creativity
inputs.description: Adjusts the level of creative interpretation applied during the upscaling process. Affects how the AI interprets and enhances the image details.

inputs.name: resemblance
inputs.description: Controls the degree to which the upscaled image should resemble the original, balancing between fidelity and enhancement.

inputs.name: dynamic
inputs.description: Modifies the dynamic range of the upscaled image, potentially enhancing contrast and depth.

inputs.name: fractality
inputs.description: Influences the complexity and detail of textures in the upscaled image, adding more intricate patterns or smoothing out details.

inputs.name: style
inputs.description: Specifies the artistic style to be applied during upscaling, such as default, portrait, or anime, allowing for stylized enhancements.

inputs.name: scale_factor
inputs.description: Determines the factor by which the image will be upscaled, offering various predefined scaling options.

inputs.name: api_key_override
inputs.description: Allows for the use of a specific API key for the upscaling process, overriding the default key if necessary.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The enhanced, upscaled version of the input image, processed through Clarity AI's upscaling API.

EagleImageNode.description: The EagleImageNode is designed for processing and handling image sequences, particularly focusing on adjusting images to a uniform size, converting them to a consistent format, and preparing them for further processing or analysis. It emphasizes the manipulation of image data, including resizing, format conversion, and mask generation, to facilitate downstream tasks such as image composition or analysis.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: Specifies the image to be processed, essential for performing operations such as resizing, format conversion, and mask generation.

inputs.name: int_field
inputs.description: An integer parameter that influences the node's processing logic, such as defining the dimensions for resizing or the number of iterations for certain operations, directly impacting the output's characteristics.

inputs.name: float_field
inputs.description: A floating-point parameter that may adjust the intensity or threshold levels of certain image processing functions, affecting the visual outcome of the processed image.

inputs.name: print_to_screen
inputs.description: A boolean parameter that controls the verbosity of the node's operation, determining whether intermediate or final processing results are displayed to the user.

inputs.name: string_field
inputs.description: A string parameter that could specify file paths, format types, or other textual configurations relevant to the node's processing tasks.

SDXLPromptStyler.description: The SDXLPromptStyler node is designed to process and style text prompts based on specified styles and templates. It modifies the input positive and negative prompts by incorporating them into predefined templates, allowing for dynamic and context-aware text generation.

inputs.name: text_positive
inputs.description: The positive text input that will be styled according to the specified template and style. It plays a crucial role in shaping the output's positive sentiment.

inputs.name: text_negative
inputs.description: The negative text input that will be combined with the template's negative prompt, if present, to tailor the output's negative sentiment.

inputs.name: style
inputs.description: Specifies the styling template to be applied to the text inputs, influencing the thematic presentation of the generated prompts.

inputs.name: log_prompt
inputs.description: Controls whether the styling process details are logged, aiding in debugging and process transparency.

outputs.name: text_positive
outputs.description: The styled positive text, transformed according to the specified style and template.

outputs.name: text_negative
outputs.description: The styled negative text, adjusted to complement the positive text in accordance with the template's guidelines.

SDXLPromptStylerAdvanced.description: The SDXLPromptStylerAdvanced node is designed to process and style text prompts using advanced templates. It allows for the customization of positive and negative prompts with specific styles, and supports logging of the styled prompts for debugging or analysis purposes. This node is capable of handling more complex prompt styling scenarios, including the differentiation between global and local positive prompts, as well as the selective application of negative prompts.

inputs.name: text_positive_g
inputs.description: The global positive text to be styled. This text is intended for use across multiple prompts or contexts, providing a consistent positive message.

inputs.name: text_positive_l
inputs.description: The local positive text to be styled. This text is specific to a particular prompt or context, allowing for more targeted positive messaging.

inputs.name: text_negative
inputs.description: The negative text to be styled. This text is used to provide a contrasting or opposing viewpoint to the positive text, enhancing the prompt's effectiveness.

inputs.name: style
inputs.description: The style identifier used to select the template for styling the prompts. This allows for the customization of prompt appearance according to predefined styles.

inputs.name: negative_prompt_to
inputs.description: Determines the application scope of the negative prompt, whether it applies globally, locally, or both, influencing how the negative text is integrated into the styled prompts.

inputs.name: log_prompt
inputs.description: A flag indicating whether the styled prompts should be logged to the console. This is useful for debugging or analyzing the styling process.

outputs.name: text_positive_g
outputs.description: The styled global positive text, reflecting the application of the selected style.

outputs.name: text_positive_l
outputs.description: The styled local positive text, tailored to a specific context or prompt.

outputs.name: text_positive
outputs.description: The combined styled positive text, incorporating both global and local positive messages.

outputs.name: text_negative_g
outputs.description: The styled global negative text, applicable when the negative prompt is set to affect global context.

outputs.name: text_negative_l
outputs.description: The styled local negative text, applicable when the negative prompt is set to affect local context.

outputs.name: text_negative
outputs.description: The combined styled negative text, integrating both global and local negative messages.

SDXLResolutionPresets.description: The SDXLResolutionPresets node provides a selection of predefined image resolution presets for use in image generation tasks, allowing users to easily choose from a variety of common aspect ratios and dimensions.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: Specifies the desired image resolution from a predefined list of common resolutions, influencing the output image's dimensions.

outputs.name: width
outputs.description: The width component of the selected resolution preset.

outputs.name: height
outputs.description: The height component of the selected resolution preset.

CheckpointLoader_pysssss.description: This node is a specialized version of the CheckpointLoaderSimple, enhanced to handle images alongside checkpoint names. It facilitates the loading of model checkpoints with an emphasis on image-related configurations, making it suitable for scenarios where visual content is a primary concern.

inputs.name: ckpt_name
inputs.description: Specifies the name of the checkpoint to be loaded. This parameter is crucial as it determines which specific checkpoint the node will attempt to load, impacting the model's configuration and its subsequent performance.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The loaded model object, which is the primary output of the checkpoint loading process. It represents the model in its entirety, ready for further use or analysis.

outputs.name: clip
outputs.description: The CLIP model associated with the loaded checkpoint, if applicable. This is relevant for tasks involving text and image understanding or generation.

outputs.name: vae
outputs.description: The VAE (Variational Autoencoder) component loaded from the checkpoint. This is crucial for tasks involving image generation or manipulation.

ConstrainImageforVideo_pysssss.description: This node is designed to adjust the dimensions of an image to fit within specified maximum and minimum sizes, ensuring the aspect ratio is maintained. It offers the option to crop the image if necessary to meet the size constraints.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The images to be processed. They are adjusted to fit within the specified size constraints while maintaining their aspect ratio.

inputs.name: max_width
inputs.description: The maximum width allowed for the images. Images wider than this will be resized to this width.

inputs.name: max_height
inputs.description: The maximum height allowed for the images. Images taller than this will be resized to this height.

inputs.name: min_width
inputs.description: The minimum width allowed for the images. Images narrower than this will be resized to this width.

inputs.name: min_height
inputs.description: The minimum height allowed for the images. Images shorter than this will be resized to this height.

inputs.name: crop_if_required
inputs.description: Determines whether images should be cropped to meet the size constraints if resizing alone is insufficient.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: The processed images, resized and optionally cropped to fit within the specified size constraints.

ConstrainImage_pysssss.description: This node is designed to adjust the dimensions of an image to fit within specified maximum and minimum sizes, ensuring the image's aspect ratio is preserved. It can optionally crop the image if it exceeds the maximum dimensions.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The images to be constrained. This parameter is crucial as it directly influences the node's core functionality of resizing and potentially cropping images to meet the specified size constraints.

inputs.name: max_width
inputs.description: Specifies the maximum width the image can have after processing. It plays a key role in determining if and how the image needs to be resized.

inputs.name: max_height
inputs.description: Defines the maximum height the image can have after processing, influencing the resizing logic to ensure the image fits within the specified dimensions.

inputs.name: min_width
inputs.description: Sets the minimum width the image should have, ensuring the image is not resized below this width.

inputs.name: min_height
inputs.description: Determines the minimum height the image should have, preventing the image from being resized below this height.

inputs.name: crop_if_required
inputs.description: A flag indicating whether the image should be cropped if it exceeds the maximum dimensions, affecting the final output by potentially altering the image's composition.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The processed images, resized and optionally cropped to fit within the specified constraints.

LoadText_pysssss.description: The LoadText node is designed for loading text content from a specified file within a given directory. It facilitates the retrieval of text data, enabling further processing or display within a workflow.

inputs.name: root_dir
inputs.description: Specifies the directory from which the file will be loaded. It is crucial for locating the file and ensuring the correct path is used for file access.

inputs.name: file
inputs.description: The specific file to be loaded. This parameter is essential for identifying which text file's contents are to be retrieved and loaded.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: Returns the content of the specified text file as a string.

LoraLoader_pysssss.description: This node specializes in loading and applying LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) adjustments to models and clips, enhancing their capabilities or altering their behavior based on specified LoRA configurations. It extends the functionality of a base loader to also handle image-specific LoRA configurations, making it versatile for various multimedia applications.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model to which the LoRA adjustments will be applied. It's crucial for defining the base architecture that will be enhanced or modified through LoRA.

inputs.name: clip
inputs.description: The CLIP model to which the LoRA adjustments will be applied, allowing for enhanced or altered multimodal understanding and representation.

inputs.name: lora_name
inputs.description: Specifies the name of the LoRA configuration to be applied, determining the specific adjustments and enhancements to the model and clip.

inputs.name: strength_model
inputs.description: Defines the intensity of the LoRA adjustments applied to the model, allowing for fine-tuned control over the modifications.

inputs.name: strength_clip
inputs.description: Defines the intensity of the LoRA adjustments applied to the CLIP model, enabling precise control over the enhancements.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The model with applied LoRA adjustments, reflecting enhanced or altered capabilities.

outputs.name: clip
outputs.description: The CLIP model with applied LoRA adjustments, showcasing enhanced or altered multimodal understanding and representation.

MathExpression_pysssss.description: The MathExpression node evaluates mathematical expressions dynamically, supporting basic arithmetic, comparisons, and logical operations. It can handle variables and function calls within the expression, offering a flexible way to compute results based on input parameters.

inputs.name: expression
inputs.description: The mathematical expression to be evaluated. Supports arithmetic, comparisons, logical operations, and function calls, with the ability to include variables 'a', 'b', and 'c'.

inputs.name: a
inputs.description: An optional variable that can be used within the expression. Supports integers and floats.

inputs.name: b
inputs.description: An optional variable that can be used within the expression. Supports integers and floats.

inputs.name: c
inputs.description: An optional variable that can be used within the expression. Supports integers and floats.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: The integer part of the evaluated result, representing the outcome of the mathematical expression as an integer.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The floating-point part of the evaluated result, representing the outcome of the mathematical expression as a float.

PlaySound_pysssss.description: The PlaySound node is designed to play audio files with customizable settings such as volume and playback mode. It abstracts the complexity of audio playback, offering a simple interface for triggering sound effects or notifications within a workflow.

inputs.name: any
inputs.description: Acts as a wildcard input, allowing for flexible integration with various data types or structures without enforcing a specific format.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Determines the playback condition, either always playing the sound or only when the queue is empty, thus providing control over the sound's occurrence.

inputs.name: volume
inputs.description: Controls the audio volume on a scale from 0 to 1, enabling fine-tuned adjustments to the sound level.

inputs.name: file
inputs.description: Specifies the audio file to be played, with a default option provided, allowing for customization of the sound effect.

outputs.description: unknown

Repeater_pysssss.description: The Repeater node is designed to duplicate a given input source a specified number of times, with the ability to output either as a single node or multiple nodes based on the mode selected. It abstracts the functionality of repeating data, facilitating the creation of multiple instances of data or nodes within a workflow.

inputs.name: source
inputs.description: The source input represents the data to be repeated. Its role is crucial as it determines the base content that will be duplicated according to the specified repeat count.

inputs.name: repeats
inputs.description: Specifies the number of times the source input should be repeated. This parameter directly influences the output by determining the quantity of the duplicated data.

inputs.name: output
inputs.description: Determines whether the repeated data should be output as a single node or multiple nodes, affecting the structure of the output.

inputs.name: node_mode
inputs.description: Controls whether the repeated nodes are reused or newly created, impacting the way nodes are added to the graph when serialized.

outputs.description: The output is a list of repeated data, which can vary in structure based on the output and node_mode parameters.

ReroutePrimitive_pysssss.description: The ReroutePrimitive node is designed to pass through any given input without modification, acting as a universal connector in data flow architectures. It abstracts away the complexity of data types, allowing for flexible rerouting of data streams.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: The 'value' parameter serves as the universal input that the node will pass through unchanged. It is central to the node's functionality, enabling it to act as a versatile connector in various data processing scenarios.

outputs.description: The output is a tuple containing the unchanged input value, facilitating seamless data rerouting.

SaveText_pysssss.description: The SaveText node is designed for writing text to a file, with options to append to an existing file or create a new one. It abstracts file handling operations, allowing users to easily save text data without dealing with low-level file system details.

inputs.name: root_dir
inputs.description: Specifies the directory where the file will be saved. It's crucial for determining the file's path and ensuring the text is saved in the correct location.

inputs.name: file
inputs.description: The name of the file where the text will be saved. This parameter works in conjunction with 'root_dir' to define the full path of the target file.

inputs.name: append
inputs.description: Controls whether the text should be appended to an existing file or if a new file should be created. It supports options like 'append' and 'new only'.

inputs.name: insert
inputs.description: Determines if a newline should be inserted before appending text when the 'append' option is used.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The text content to be saved into the file. This is the primary data being written.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The output is the text that was successfully written to the file.

ShowText_pysssss.description: The ShowText node is designed to display text within a workflow, allowing for dynamic updates to UI elements based on input text. It can also modify widget values within the workflow if provided with specific metadata, enhancing interactive capabilities.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The primary text to be displayed or processed. This input is essential for the node's operation, serving as the main content for display or further action.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: unknown

StringFunction_pysssss.description: The String Function node provides utilities for manipulating strings, including appending multiple strings together, replacing parts of a string based on a pattern, and tidying up strings by removing extra spaces or adjusting tags. It's designed to offer a range of common string operations that can be dynamically applied based on the input parameters.

inputs.name: action
inputs.description: Specifies the string operation to perform, such as appending strings together or replacing parts of a string with another. This choice determines how the other inputs are used and the overall behavior of the node.

inputs.name: tidy_tags
inputs.description: Determines whether the output string should be tidied by removing extra spaces and adjusting tags, enhancing readability and consistency.

inputs.name: text_a
inputs.description: The primary text input for operations. It serves as the base string for append and replace actions.

inputs.name: text_b
inputs.description: Secondary text input that can be appended to 'text_a' or used as the search pattern for replacements.

inputs.name: text_c
inputs.description: In replace actions, this text replaces occurrences of 'text_b' in 'text_a'. In append actions, it's concatenated with 'text_a' and 'text_b'.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The result of the string manipulation operation, returned as a string.

SystemNotification_pysssss.description: The SystemNotification node is designed to facilitate the creation and management of system notifications, allowing for customizable messages and modes of operation. It abstracts the complexity of handling system alerts, providing a straightforward way to notify users based on specific conditions or system states.

inputs.name: message
inputs.description: Specifies the default message to be displayed in the notification. This parameter allows for customization of the notification content, tailoring it to specific needs or contexts.

inputs.name: any
inputs.description: Acts as a wildcard input, enabling flexible and dynamic handling of notifications without strict parameter constraints.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Determines the conditions under which the notification is triggered, offering options for always displaying or conditionally based on the system's state.

outputs.description: unknown

Analyze Palette [Dream].description: The 'Analyze Palette' node processes a palette to compute average metrics such as brightness, contrast, and color dominance (redness, greenness, blueness). It abstracts the color characteristics of the palette into numerical values that can be used for further image processing or analysis.

inputs.name: palette
inputs.description: The palette to be analyzed. It is a collection of colors from which the node calculates average brightness, contrast, and color dominance values.

outputs.name: brightness
outputs.description: The average brightness value of the analyzed palette.

outputs.name: contrast
outputs.description: The average contrast value of the analyzed palette.

outputs.name: redness
outputs.description: The average red dominance value of the analyzed palette.

outputs.name: greenness
outputs.description: The average green dominance value of the analyzed palette.

outputs.name: blueness
outputs.description: The average blue dominance value of the analyzed palette.

Beat Curve [Dream].description: The Beat Curve node generates animation curves based on musical beats, allowing for synchronization between visual animations and rhythmic elements of a soundtrack. It utilizes BPM (beats per minute), measure length, and optional accents to create dynamic, beat-aligned animations.

inputs.name: frame_counter
