inputs.description: Provides the current frame and timing information necessary for calculating the animation curve in relation to the music's beat.

inputs.name: bpm
inputs.description: Specifies the beats per minute of the music track, influencing the timing of the animation curve to match the rhythm.

inputs.name: time_offset
inputs.description: Adjusts the start time of the animation curve, allowing for precise synchronization with the music track.

inputs.name: measure_length
inputs.description: Defines the length of a musical measure in beats, used to calculate the timing of accents within the animation curve.

inputs.name: low_value
inputs.description: Sets the minimum value of the animation curve, defining the lower bound of the generated values.

inputs.name: high_value
inputs.description: Sets the maximum value of the animation curve, defining the upper bound of the generated values.

inputs.name: invert
inputs.description: Inverts the animation curve, flipping the generated values between the specified low and high values. This parameter accepts 'yes' or 'no' to indicate inversion.

inputs.name: power
inputs.description: Applies a power function to the animation curve, adjusting the intensity and dynamics of the curve's progression.

inputs.name: accent_i
inputs.description: Specifies an accent beat within a measure, enhancing the animation curve's response to musical rhythm. Accents range from 1 to the measure length, allowing for dynamic rhythm customization.

outputs.name: FLOAT
outputs.description: The floating-point value of the animation curve at the current frame, reflecting the rhythmic pattern.

outputs.name: INT
outputs.description: The integer-rounded value of the animation curve at the current frame, suitable for discrete animations.

Big Float Switch [Dream].description: The Big Float Switch node is designed to select a floating-point value from a set of inputs based on a specified condition. It facilitates dynamic decision-making in data flows by allowing the selection of values based on runtime conditions, enhancing flexibility and adaptability in processing numerical data.

inputs.name: select
inputs.description: Specifies the index of the input to be selected initially. The node will attempt to select this input, but may choose another based on the 'on_missing' strategy and the presence of valid data.

inputs.name: on_missing
inputs.description: Determines the node's behavior when the initially selected input does not meet the validation criteria. It can either move to the previous or next input until a valid one is found, ensuring a fallback mechanism is in place.

inputs.name: input_i
inputs.description: Represents one of the multiple floating-point inputs that can be selected by the node. Each 'input_i' stands for a potential value to be chosen based on the selection criteria, where 'i' can range from 0 to n, indicating the flexibility in the number of inputs.

outputs.name: selected
outputs.description: The floating-point value selected by the node based on the specified conditions and inputs.

Big Image Switch [Dream].description: This node is designed to switch between different image inputs based on a selection criterion, allowing for dynamic image selection within a workflow.

inputs.name: select
inputs.description: Determines which image input to select based on the provided criterion, enabling dynamic image selection.

inputs.name: on_missing
inputs.description: Specifies the action to take when the selected image input is missing, ensuring robustness in image selection.

inputs.name: input_i
inputs.description: Represents one of the multiple image inputs that can be selected. The index 'i' varies, indicating each distinct image input available for selection.

outputs.name: selected
outputs.description: The image that has been selected based on the provided criterion.

Big Int Switch [Dream].description: The Big Int Switch node is designed to selectively output an integer value based on a specified selection criterion. It facilitates dynamic decision-making within data flows by allowing the selection of an integer from a predefined set based on input conditions.

inputs.name: select
inputs.description: Specifies the index of the integer to be selected. It plays a crucial role in determining which integer value is output by the node, based on the selection logic implemented.

inputs.name: on_missing
inputs.description: Defines the behavior of the node when the selected integer is missing. This parameter ensures that the node can gracefully handle cases where the desired integer is not available, by specifying an alternative selection strategy.

inputs.name: input_i
inputs.description: Represents one of the potential integer values that can be selected. This parameter is part of a series (input_0 to input_9) that collectively define the set of integers from which the node can choose, based on the selection criteria.

outputs.name: selected
outputs.description: The integer value that has been selected based on the input criteria. This output reflects the decision made by the node in selecting one integer from the available options.

Big Latent Switch [Dream].description: The Big Latent Switch node is designed to dynamically select between multiple latent inputs based on a specified condition. It facilitates the flexible manipulation of latent representations in a computational graph, allowing for the conditional routing of data through different processing paths.

inputs.name: select
inputs.description: Specifies the index of the latent input to be selected. This parameter determines which of the multiple latent inputs will be actively passed through the node.

inputs.name: on_missing
inputs.description: Defines the behavior of the switch when the selected input is missing. It can either proceed to the next available input or revert to the previous one, ensuring continuous operation.

inputs.name: input_i
inputs.description: Represents one of the multiple latent inputs that can be selected by the switch. The node can handle an arbitrary number of these inputs, dynamically choosing among them based on the 'select' parameter.

outputs.name: selected
outputs.description: The output of the Big Latent Switch node, which is the latent representation selected based on the specified condition.

Big Palette Switch [Dream].description: The Big Palette Switch [Dream] node is designed to dynamically select between different color palettes based on input conditions. It facilitates the flexible manipulation of color schemes within a project by allowing the selection of a palette that best fits the given criteria or context.

inputs.name: select
inputs.description: Specifies the index of the palette to select. This parameter determines which of the potentially multiple input palettes is chosen based on its index, influencing the node's output directly.

inputs.name: on_missing
inputs.description: Defines the behavior of the node when the selected palette is missing. It can either move to the previous or next available palette, ensuring a seamless selection process even when some inputs are unavailable.

inputs.name: input_i
inputs.description: Represents one of the potential palette inputs from which one is selected. The index i ranges from 0 to 9, allowing for up to ten different palettes to be inputted, offering a wide range of choices.

outputs.name: selected
outputs.description: The palette that has been selected based on the input conditions. This output reflects the chosen palette after considering the 'select' and 'on_missing' parameters.

Big Text Switch [Dream].description: The Big Text Switch node is designed to dynamically select one of several text inputs based on a specified condition. It facilitates conditional logic within a flow, allowing for the selection of text values based on runtime criteria.

inputs.name: select
inputs.description: Specifies the index of the text input to be selected. It plays a crucial role in determining which text input is chosen based on the condition provided.

inputs.name: on_missing
inputs.description: Defines the behavior when the selected text input does not meet the specified condition, allowing for a fallback mechanism to either the previous or next valid input.

inputs.name: input_i
inputs.description: Represents one of the ten text inputs available for selection, where 'i' can range from 0 to 9. Each input can be individually set to a default value, ensuring a value is always available even if not explicitly provided. The index 'i' allows for dynamic selection among multiple inputs.

outputs.name: selected
outputs.description: The text value selected based on the specified condition and inputs. It represents the outcome of the conditional logic applied by the node.

Boolean To Float [Dream].description: Converts a boolean input to a float output, allowing for custom float values to be assigned to true and false boolean states. This node facilitates conditional logic and value transformation in data flows, enabling dynamic adjustments based on boolean conditions.

inputs.name: boolean
inputs.description: Determines the branch of execution: if true, the 'on_true' value is returned; if false, the 'on_false' value is selected. This boolean input thus directly influences the node's output.

inputs.name: on_true
inputs.description: Specifies the float value to return when the boolean input is true, enabling customization of the output for true conditions.

inputs.name: on_false
inputs.description: Defines the float value to return when the boolean input is false, allowing for tailored responses to false conditions.

outputs.name: result
outputs.description: The float value corresponding to the input boolean condition, determined by the 'on_true' or 'on_false' parameters.

Boolean To Int [Dream].description: The 'Boolean To Int' node converts a boolean input into an integer output, allowing for conditional logic to be applied in numerical contexts. It provides a straightforward way to translate true/false conditions into numerical representations for further processing or decision-making.

inputs.name: boolean
inputs.description: Determines the condition for the conversion. If true, the 'on_true' value is returned; otherwise, the 'on_false' value is selected.

inputs.name: on_true
inputs.description: The integer value to return when the 'boolean' input is true. This allows for customization of the true condition's numerical representation.

inputs.name: on_false
inputs.description: The integer value to return when the 'boolean' input is false. This enables the false condition to be represented by a specific numerical value.

outputs.name: result
outputs.description: The result of the boolean to integer conversion, reflecting either the 'on_true' or 'on_false' value based on the boolean input.

Build Prompt [Dream].description: The 'Build Prompt' node is designed for constructing and weighting textual prompts for generative tasks, allowing for the dynamic adjustment of prompt importance through weights.

inputs.name: added_prompt
inputs.description: Specifies the text to be added to the prompt, which can be dynamically adjusted in importance using the weight parameter.

inputs.name: weight
inputs.description: Determines the weight of the added prompt text, influencing its significance in the resulting prompt composition.

inputs.name: partial_prompt
inputs.description: An optional initial prompt structure that can be further modified by adding text with specified weight. If not provided, a new prompt structure is initialized.

outputs.name: partial_prompt
outputs.description: The modified or newly created prompt structure, incorporating the added text with its specified weight.

Calculation [Dream].description: The Calculation node is designed to dynamically evaluate mathematical expressions based on user-defined variables and constants. It allows for the flexible computation of results by interpreting and executing a given expression with the ability to incorporate both integer and floating-point numbers.

inputs.name: expression
inputs.description: Defines the mathematical expression to be evaluated. This expression can include variables and arithmetic operations, serving as the blueprint for the calculation.

inputs.name: a_int
inputs.description: Represents an integer variable 'a' that can be used within the expression. Its value influences the outcome of the calculation.

inputs.name: b_int
inputs.description: Represents an integer variable 'b' that can be used within the expression. Its value influences the outcome of the calculation.

inputs.name: c_int
inputs.description: Represents an integer variable 'c' that can be used within the expression. Its value influences the outcome of the calculation.

inputs.name: r_float
inputs.description: Represents a floating-point variable 'r' that can be used within the expression. Its value influences the outcome of the calculation.

inputs.name: s_float
inputs.description: Represents a floating-point variable 's' that can be used within the expression. Its value influences the outcome of the calculation.

inputs.name: t_float
inputs.description: Represents a floating-point variable 't' that can be used within the expression. Its value influences the outcome of the calculation.

outputs.name: FLOAT
outputs.description: The floating-point result of the evaluated expression.

outputs.name: INT
outputs.description: The integer result of the evaluated expression, obtained by rounding the floating-point result.

Common Frame Dimensions [Dream].description: The Common Frame Dimensions node provides a utility for calculating frame dimensions based on a set of input parameters including size, aspect ratio, orientation, divisor, and alignment. It abstracts the complexity of dimension calculations and alignment adjustments, offering a streamlined way to determine optimal frame sizes for various display requirements.

inputs.name: size
inputs.description: Specifies the desired frame size from a predefined list of resolutions. This choice influences the overall dimensions of the frame, serving as a base for further calculations.

inputs.name: aspect_ratio
inputs.description: Determines the frame's aspect ratio, affecting its width and height proportionally to ensure the specified ratio is maintained.

inputs.name: orientation
inputs.description: Indicates the frame's orientation (wide or tall), which influences the calculation of width and height based on the aspect ratio.

inputs.name: divisor
inputs.description: A factor used to divide the frame dimensions for finer control over size granularity, affecting the final dimensions.

inputs.name: alignment
inputs.description: Specifies the alignment value for dimension calculations, ensuring that the final dimensions are aligned to a certain boundary.

inputs.name: alignment_type
inputs.description: Determines how the final dimensions are rounded (up, down, or to the nearest) based on the alignment value.

outputs.name: width
outputs.description: The calculated width of the frame after considering all input parameters.

outputs.name: height
outputs.description: The calculated height of the frame after considering all input parameters.

outputs.name: final_width
outputs.description: The final width of the frame, adjusted according to the alignment and alignment type.

outputs.name: final_height
outputs.description: The final height of the frame, adjusted according to the alignment and alignment type.

Compare Palettes [Dream].description: The 'Compare Palettes' node is designed to compare two color palettes by calculating the average multipliers for brightness, contrast, and RGB color intensities between them. This comparison provides a quantitative measure of the differences in color characteristics between the two palettes.

inputs.name: a
inputs.description: The first RGB palette to be compared. It serves as the baseline for comparison against the second palette.

inputs.name: b
inputs.description: The second RGB palette to be compared against the first. This comparison yields multipliers indicating how much brighter, more contrasted, or differently colored the second palette is relative to the first.

outputs.name: brightness_multiplier
outputs.description: The average multiplier for brightness differences between the two palettes.

outputs.name: contrast_multiplier
outputs.description: The average multiplier for contrast differences between the two palettes.

outputs.name: red_multiplier
outputs.description: The average multiplier for red color intensity differences between the two palettes.

outputs.name: green_multiplier
outputs.description: The average multiplier for green color intensity differences between the two palettes.

CSV Curve [Dream].description: The CSV Curve node is designed to interpret and apply animation curves based on data extracted from CSV files. It allows for the dynamic generation of animation parameters through the parsing of CSV file content, supporting interpolation and customization of the CSV parsing process.

inputs.name: frame_counter
inputs.description: A counter tracking the current frame of the animation, essential for timing and synchronization of the animation curve with the overall animation sequence.

inputs.name: csvfile
inputs.description: Specifies the path to the CSV file to be used for generating the animation curve, enabling the node to dynamically interpret and apply the data contained within.

inputs.name: first_column_type
inputs.description: Determines whether the first column of the CSV file represents seconds or frames, affecting how the data is interpreted in the context of animation timing.

inputs.name: interpolate
inputs.description: Controls whether interpolation is applied between data points in the CSV file, allowing for smoother transitions in the generated animation curve.

inputs.name: csv_dialect
inputs.description: Specifies the dialect of the CSV file, enabling the node to accurately parse files with different formatting conventions.

outputs.name: FLOAT
outputs.description: The floating-point value generated by the CSV Curve node, representing a point on the animation curve.

outputs.name: INT
outputs.description: An integer representation of the generated animation curve point, providing an alternative precision level.

CSV Generator [Dream].description: The CSV Generator node is designed for creating and appending data to a CSV file, specifically tailored for animation curve data. It initializes or updates a CSV file with frame and value data, supporting custom CSV dialects for flexible file formatting.

inputs.name: frame_counter
inputs.description: Tracks the current frame in the animation, ensuring accurate timing data is recorded alongside values in the CSV.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: Specifies the numerical value to be recorded in the CSV file, playing a crucial role in the animation curve's data points.

inputs.name: csvfile
inputs.description: The path to the CSV file to be created or updated, serving as the primary storage for the animation curve data.

inputs.name: csv_dialect
inputs.description: Defines the formatting rules for the CSV file, allowing customization of the file's structure and syntax.

FFMPEG Video Encoder [Dream].description: The FFMPEG Video Encoder node is designed for encoding and compiling a sequence of images into a video file using FFMPEG. It allows for adjusting the framerate, optionally removing the source images after encoding, and handling file naming to avoid overwrites, thereby facilitating the creation of video content from individual frames.

inputs.name: sequence
inputs.description: Represents the sequence of images to be encoded into a video. It is crucial for defining the content and order of frames in the final video output.

inputs.name: name
inputs.description: Specifies the base name for the output video file, which can be further adjusted to avoid filename conflicts.

inputs.name: framerate_factor
inputs.description: A multiplier for the sequence's framerate, allowing for speed adjustments in the resulting video.

inputs.name: remove_images
inputs.description: Determines whether the source images should be deleted after encoding, helping in managing disk space.

outputs.name: log_entry
outputs.description: Provides a log entry detailing the encoding process and outcome, including any errors encountered.

File Count [Dream].description: This node counts the number of files in a specified directory that match given patterns, such as file extensions. It's designed to facilitate file management and organization tasks by providing a quick way to quantify relevant files within a project or dataset.

inputs.name: directory_path
inputs.description: Specifies the path to the directory where files will be counted. This path is essential for the node to locate and assess the files present in the desired location.

inputs.name: patterns
inputs.description: Defines the file patterns (e.g., '*.jpg', '*.png') to match against files in the directory. This allows for filtering and counting files of specific types, enhancing the node's utility in managing and organizing files.

outputs.name: TOTAL
outputs.description: The total count of files matching the specified patterns within the given directory. This output provides a straightforward metric for assessing the volume of relevant files.

Finalize Prompt [Dream].description: This node finalizes the construction of prompts by applying adjustments and clamping to ensure the prompt's components are within specified bounds. It's designed to refine and finalize the text for prompts, making them ready for use in generating content.

inputs.name: partial_prompt
inputs.description: Represents the initial or intermediate state of the prompt that is being finalized. It is crucial for determining the base content and structure of the final prompt.

inputs.name: adjustment
inputs.description: Specifies the method of adjustment to apply to the prompt's components, such as scaling by absolute maximum or sum, or leaving them raw. This affects the final distribution of weights in the prompt.

inputs.name: clamp
inputs.description: The maximum allowed value for any component's weight in the prompt, ensuring no single part dominates excessively.

inputs.name: adjustment_reference
inputs.description: A reference value used in scaling adjustments to balance the weights of the prompt's components.

outputs.name: positive
outputs.description: The finalized prompt with positive weights, ready for generating content that aligns with the desired attributes.

outputs.name: negative
outputs.description: The finalized prompt with negative weights, indicating content to avoid or minimize in generation.

Float Input [Dream].description: The Float Input node is designed to accept a floating-point number as input, providing a simple interface for users to input decimal values. It serves as a foundational element in user interfaces where numerical input is required, particularly for configurations that involve precise measurements or adjustments.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: Represents the floating-point number that the user inputs. It is the primary value the node operates on, serving as the basis for further processing or computation within the node's workflow.

outputs.name: FLOAT
outputs.description: Outputs the same floating-point number that was input, effectively acting as a pass-through for the value.

Float to Log Entry [Dream].description: The Float to Log Entry node is designed to convert floating-point numbers into log entries, facilitating the tracking and logging of numerical data within a system. It encapsulates the process of transforming a float value into a structured log format, making it easier to document and review numerical changes or states.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: Represents the floating-point number to be logged. Its inclusion is crucial for defining the numerical data that will be transformed into a log entry.

inputs.name: label
inputs.description: An optional label to prepend to the logged value, providing context or categorization for the numerical data being logged.

outputs.name: log_entry
outputs.description: The output is a structured log entry that encapsulates the provided floating-point value, optionally prefixed with a label, in a format suitable for logging and tracking.

Frame Count Calculator [Dream].description: The Frame Count Calculator node is designed to compute the total number of frames based on a given time duration and frame rate. It takes into account hours, minutes, seconds, and milliseconds to provide a precise frame count, making it essential for animation and video processing tasks where timing and synchronization are critical.

inputs.name: hours
inputs.description: Specifies the number of hours to be included in the total time duration for which frames are to be calculated. It directly influences the total frame count by contributing to the overall time.

inputs.name: minutes
inputs.description: Specifies the number of minutes to be included in the total time duration. This parameter, along with others, determines the total number of frames by contributing to the total time.

inputs.name: seconds
inputs.description: Defines the number of seconds to be considered in the total time duration. This is crucial for calculating the precise number of frames, especially in short clips or animations.

inputs.name: milliseconds
inputs.description: Includes milliseconds in the total time calculation, allowing for more precise frame count calculations in scenarios requiring high accuracy.

inputs.name: frames_per_second
inputs.description: Sets the frame rate per second, which is used to calculate the total number of frames based on the time duration provided. This parameter is essential for determining the animation or video's smoothness and quality.

outputs.name: TOTAL
outputs.description: The total number of frames calculated based on the input time duration and frame rate. This output is crucial for planning and synchronizing animations or video sequences.

Frame Counter (Directory) [Dream].description: This node is designed to count the number of frames based on images found in a specified directory, matching a given pattern, and ordered either numerically or alphabetically. It's particularly useful in animation projects where tracking the progression of frames is essential.

inputs.name: directory_path
inputs.description: Specifies the path to the directory containing the images to be counted. This path is crucial for locating and processing the images.

inputs.name: pattern
inputs.description: Defines the pattern (e.g., '*.jpg') to match files in the directory. This pattern determines which files are considered in the frame count.

inputs.name: indexing
inputs.description: Determines the order in which images are indexed and counted, either numerically or alphabetically. This affects the sequence of frame counting.

inputs.name: total_frames
inputs.description: Sets the maximum number of frames to count, providing a limit to the frame counting process.

inputs.name: frames_per_second
inputs.description: Specifies the frame rate, which is used to calculate the duration of the animation based on the number of frames.

outputs.name: frame_counter
outputs.description: Outputs a FrameCounter object, encapsulating the current frame count, total frames, and frames per second.

Frame Counter (Simple) [Dream].description: This node generates a frame counter based on the specified frame index, total number of frames, and frames per second. It is designed to facilitate animation processes by tracking and managing frame progression.

inputs.name: frame_index
inputs.description: Specifies the current frame index. It is crucial for determining the starting point of the frame counter.

inputs.name: total_frames
inputs.description: Defines the total number of frames in the animation sequence. It sets the upper limit for the frame counter.

inputs.name: frames_per_second
inputs.description: Determines the frame rate by specifying the number of frames to be played per second. This affects the timing and speed of the animation.

outputs.name: frame_counter
outputs.description: Outputs a FrameCounter object initialized with the current frame, total frames, and frames per second, facilitating further animation control.

Frame Counter Info [Dream].description: Provides detailed information about the current state of a frame counter in an animation context, including completed frames, total frames, and various time-based metrics.

inputs.name: frame_counter
inputs.description: The frame counter object that tracks the current frame, total frames, and timing information for an animation sequence.

outputs.name: frames_completed
outputs.description: The number of frames that have been completed.

outputs.name: total_frames
outputs.description: The total number of frames in the animation sequence.

outputs.name: first_frame
outputs.description: A boolean indicating if the current frame is the first frame.

outputs.name: last_frame
outputs.description: A boolean indicating if the current frame is the last frame.

outputs.name: elapsed_seconds
outputs.description: The elapsed time in seconds since the animation started.

outputs.name: remaining_seconds
outputs.description: The estimated remaining time in seconds until the animation completes.

outputs.name: total_seconds
outputs.description: The total time in seconds for the animation.

outputs.name: completion
outputs.description: The completion percentage of the animation.

Frame Counter Offset [Dream].description: The Frame Counter Offset node is designed to modify the frame counter by applying a specified offset value. This adjustment allows for the dynamic alteration of animation timelines, enabling the creation of shifted or delayed animation sequences based on the original frame count.

inputs.name: frame_counter
inputs.description: The frame counter input represents the current state of an animation's frame count, including information such as the current frame, total frames, and frames per second. The offset applied to this counter can shift the animation timeline forward or backward.

inputs.name: offset
inputs.description: The offset parameter specifies the number of frames by which the frame counter should be incremented or decremented. This allows for the adjustment of the animation's timeline, effectively shifting the sequence of frames.

outputs.name: frame_counter
outputs.description: The modified frame counter, which has been incremented or decremented by the specified offset, reflecting the new position in the animation timeline.

Frame Counter Time Offset [Dream].description: This node applies a time-based offset to a frame counter, effectively adjusting the current frame based on a specified duration in seconds. It's designed to facilitate animation timing adjustments by converting time into an equivalent frame count increment, using the frame rate for accurate synchronization.

inputs.name: frame_counter
inputs.description: The frame counter to be adjusted. It serves as the basis for applying the time offset, determining the new frame position.

inputs.name: offset_seconds
inputs.description: The duration in seconds to offset the frame counter. This value is multiplied by the frame rate to calculate the equivalent frame count to adjust.

outputs.name: frame_counter
outputs.description: The adjusted frame counter, incremented by the calculated frame count equivalent of the specified time offset.

Image Brightness Adjustment [Dream].description: This node adjusts the brightness of an image based on a specified factor, enhancing or dimming the image's overall luminance.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image to be processed for brightness adjustment. It serves as the primary input on which the brightness modification is performed.

inputs.name: factor
inputs.description: A multiplier for adjusting the brightness. Values greater than 1.0 increase brightness, while values less than 1.0 decrease it.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The resulting image after the brightness adjustment has been applied.

Image Color Shift [Dream].description: This node is designed to adjust the color balance of an image by applying multipliers to the red, green, and blue color channels, allowing for fine-tuned color correction or creative color adjustments.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be color-shifted. It serves as the base for applying color adjustments.

inputs.name: red_multiplier
inputs.description: A multiplier for the red channel, adjusting the intensity of red colors in the image.

inputs.name: green_multiplier
inputs.description: A multiplier for the green channel, adjusting the intensity of green colors in the image.

inputs.name: blue_multiplier
inputs.description: A multiplier for the blue channel, adjusting the intensity of blue colors in the image.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image after the color shift has been applied, reflecting the adjustments made to the color channels.

Image Contrast Adjustment [Dream].description: This node adjusts the contrast of an image based on a specified factor, enhancing or reducing the differences between the lightest and darkest parts of the image.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image to adjust the contrast for. This is the primary input on which the contrast adjustment operation is performed.

inputs.name: factor
inputs.description: A multiplier for adjusting the contrast. Values greater than 1.0 increase contrast, while values less than 1.0 decrease it.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The resulting image after the contrast adjustment has been applied.

Image Motion [Dream].description: The Image Motion node applies a series of transformations to an image to simulate motion, including zooming and translating in both x and y directions, along with applying overlap masks for more complex motion effects.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The primary image to which motion effects will be applied. It serves as the base for all subsequent transformations.

inputs.name: zoom
inputs.description: Defines the zoom level for the image, allowing for both zoom-in and zoom-out effects to simulate motion.

inputs.name: mask_i_feather
inputs.description: unknown

inputs.name: mask_i_overlap
inputs.description: unknown

inputs.name: x_translation
inputs.description: Controls the horizontal movement of the image, simulating lateral motion.

inputs.name: y_translation
inputs.description: Manages the vertical movement of the image, simulating upward or downward motion.

inputs.name: frame_counter
inputs.description: Tracks the number of frames processed, used for animations or effects that change over time.

inputs.name: noise
inputs.description: An optional image used to add noise to the motion effect, enhancing realism.

inputs.name: output_resize_width
inputs.description: Optionally resizes the output image's width, affecting the final image dimensions.

inputs.name: output_resize_height
inputs.description: Optionally resizes the output image's height, affecting the final image dimensions.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The transformed image with applied motion effects.

outputs.name: mask1
outputs.description: The first mask used in creating the motion effect, after transformations.

outputs.name: mask2
outputs.description: The second mask applied for enhanced motion effects, post-transformation.

outputs.name: mask3
outputs.description: The third mask contributing to the layered motion effect, following transformations.

Image Sequence Blend [Dream].description: This node blends animation sequences by applying fade-in and fade-out effects between frames over specified iterations, enhancing the visual transition and continuity within the sequence.

inputs.name: sequence
inputs.description: The animation sequence to be blended, serving as the primary input for the blending process.

inputs.name: fade_in
inputs.description: Specifies the intensity of the fade-in effect at the beginning of each frame transition, influencing the smoothness of the sequence's visual flow.

inputs.name: fade_out
inputs.description: Determines the intensity of the fade-out effect at the end of each frame transition, contributing to the seamless integration of consecutive frames.

inputs.name: iterations
inputs.description: Controls the number of times the blending process is applied, affecting the overall smoothness and continuity of the animation sequence.

outputs.name: sequence
outputs.description: The resulting animation sequence after applying the blend processing, featuring enhanced visual transitions between frames.

Image Sequence Loader [Dream].description: The Image Sequence Loader node is designed to load a sequence of images from a specified directory, applying a pattern and indexing method to select the images. It can also provide a default image as a fallback option if no images are found matching the criteria.

inputs.name: frame_counter
inputs.description: Represents the current frame counter, used to determine which image in the sequence to load based on its order.

inputs.name: directory_path
inputs.description: The path to the directory where the image sequence is stored. This allows the node to locate and load the images.

inputs.name: pattern
inputs.description: A pattern to match filenames within the directory, enabling selective loading of images based on their names.

inputs.name: indexing
inputs.description: Determines the method of indexing the images, either numerically or in alphabetical order, to establish the sequence order.

inputs.name: default_image
inputs.description: An optional default image to return if no images match the specified pattern and indexing in the directory.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The loaded image from the sequence based on the current frame counter, or the default image if no matching image is found.

outputs.name: frame_name
outputs.description: The name of the frame loaded from the sequence, providing context or identification for the image.

Image Sequence Saver [Dream].description: The Image Sequence Saver node is designed to save individual frames of an animation sequence to disk, supporting various file formats and configurations. It allows for detailed control over the output naming convention, directory structure, and file format, facilitating the creation of organized and accessible animation frame libraries.

inputs.name: frame_counter
inputs.description: Specifies the current frame in the animation sequence, used to determine the filename and whether the saving process should continue based on the 'at_end' parameter.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image to be saved for the current frame, representing a single snapshot in the animation sequence.

inputs.name: directory_path
inputs.description: The target directory path where the image file will be saved, allowing for organized storage of animation frames.

inputs.name: prefix
inputs.description: A prefix added to the filename of each saved image, aiding in the identification and organization of frames within the directory.

inputs.name: digits
inputs.description: The number of digits to use for zero-padding the frame number in the filename, ensuring a consistent file naming convention.

inputs.name: at_end
inputs.description: Determines the behavior when the end of the animation sequence is reached, offering options to stop output, raise an error, or keep going.

inputs.name: filetype
inputs.description: Specifies the file format for the saved image, including options for PNG with or without embedded workflow information, and JPG.

outputs.name: sequence
outputs.description: The updated animation sequence after saving the current frame, reflecting any changes or additions.

outputs.name: log_entry
outputs.description: A log entry detailing the outcome of the save operation, including success messages or error information.

Image Sequence Tweening [Dream].description: The node is designed to enhance animation sequences by interpolating additional frames between existing ones, effectively increasing the smoothness and fluidity of the animation. It utilizes a multiplier to determine the number of frames to be added between each original frame, allowing for customizable levels of tweening.

inputs.name: sequence
inputs.description: The animation sequence to be processed. It is the primary input that defines the frames to be tweened.

inputs.name: multiplier
inputs.description: Determines the number of interpolated frames to be added between each original frame in the sequence, allowing for control over the smoothness of the resulting animation.

outputs.name: sequence
outputs.description: The enhanced animation sequence with additional tweened frames inserted between the original frames.

Int Input [Dream].description: The 'Int Input' node allows users to input integer values into a system, providing a straightforward interface for numerical data entry. This node is essential for scenarios requiring precise numerical inputs, such as setting parameters or configurations that rely on integer values.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: Represents the integer value to be input by the user. It is crucial for defining the exact numerical input that the system will process.

outputs.name: INT
outputs.description: Outputs the integer value input by the user, facilitating its use in subsequent operations or calculations within the system.

Int to Log Entry [Dream].description: The 'Int to Log Entry' node is designed to convert an integer value along with an optional label into a log entry format. This functionality is essential for logging and tracking integer values within a system, providing a structured and readable log entry that can be easily interpreted and analyzed.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: The 'value' parameter represents the integer value to be logged. It is a crucial component of the log entry, serving as the primary data point around which the log entry is structured.

inputs.name: label
inputs.description: The 'label' parameter is an optional string that provides context or a descriptor for the integer value being logged. It enhances the readability and interpretability of the log entry by adding a textual description to the numerical value.

outputs.name: log_entry
outputs.description: The output 'log_entry' is a structured representation of the input integer value and optional label, formatted for logging purposes. It encapsulates the data in a log entry format, making it suitable for tracking and analysis within a logging system.

Laboratory [Dream].description: The Laboratory node is designed to generate and manipulate numerical values based on a variety of modes such as random uniform, random bell, ladder, and random walk. It allows for dynamic value generation within specified ranges, making it a versatile tool for experiments and simulations in creative projects.

inputs.name: frame_counter
inputs.description: A counter tracking the current frame within a sequence, essential for determining when to renew the generated value based on the specified policy.

inputs.name: key
inputs.description: A unique identifier for the generated value, supporting default randomization to ensure uniqueness. It plays a crucial role in value tracking and retrieval across frames.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: Determines the starting point of the random number generation, enabling reproducible results. It's essential for consistency in simulations or when re-generating values.

inputs.name: renew_policy
inputs.description: Defines the policy for renewing the generated value, affecting how often new values are produced based on frame changes or initial generation.

inputs.name: min_value
inputs.description: Sets the lower bound for the generated value, crucial for defining the value range and ensuring outputs fall within expected limits.

inputs.name: max_value
inputs.description: Establishes the upper limit for the generated value, essential for controlling the range and precision of the output.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Specifies the method of value generation, influencing the distribution and variation of the output values.

inputs.name: step_size
inputs.description: Determines the increment size between values in certain modes, impacting the granularity and smoothness of value transitions.

outputs.name: FLOAT
outputs.description: The primary generated float value, serving as the versatile output for various applications.

outputs.name: INT
outputs.description: An integer representation of the primary generated value, offering a discrete alternative for specific needs.

outputs.name: log_entry
outputs.description: A log entry detailing the generation or reuse of the value, providing insights and traceability for debugging and analysis.

Linear Curve [Dream].description: The Linear Curve node provides a linear interpolation between an initial and a final value over a sequence of frames, typically used to create smooth transitions or animations.

inputs.name: frame_counter
inputs.description: Tracks the progression of frames, dictating the current position in the interpolation process.

inputs.name: initial_value
inputs.description: Specifies the starting value of the linear interpolation, serving as the base for the animation or transition.

inputs.name: final_value
inputs.description: Defines the end value of the linear interpolation, determining the target of the animation or transition.

outputs.name: FLOAT
outputs.description: The interpolated float value at the current frame, reflecting the linear progression.

outputs.name: INT
outputs.description: The interpolated value rounded to the nearest integer, providing a discrete step in the progression.

Log Entry Joiner [Dream].description: The Log Entry Joiner node is designed to merge multiple log entries into a single, comprehensive log entry. It facilitates the consolidation of discrete log information, making it easier to manage and interpret log data as a unified entity.

inputs.name: entry_i
inputs.description: Represents a log entry to be merged. Each 'entry_i' allows for the sequential combination of log entries, enhancing the comprehensiveness of the resulting log. The index 'i' can range from 0 to 3, indicating the position of the log entry in the merge process.

outputs.name: log_entry
outputs.description: The resulting unified log entry, which combines the information from the individual log entries provided as input.

Log File [Dream].description: The Log File [Dream] node is designed for logging and organizing log entries related to frame counters and other specified inputs within a dream project. It supports conditional logging based on the active state, allows for customization of log file paths, and can output logs to both a file and stdout, facilitating both real-time monitoring and persistent record-keeping.

inputs.name: frame_counter
inputs.description: A required input that integrates frame counting into the logging process, enhancing the log's detail and utility for animation and timing analysis.

inputs.name: log_directory
inputs.description: Specifies the directory where the log file will be saved. This allows for flexible log management and organization within the file system.

inputs.name: log_filename
inputs.description: Defines the name of the log file where entries will be recorded. This enables easy identification and access to specific log files for review or analysis.

inputs.name: stdout
inputs.description: Determines whether log entries are also echoed to the standard output (stdout), enabling real-time monitoring of log messages.

inputs.name: active
inputs.description: Controls whether logging is active. If false, logging operations are bypassed, allowing for conditional logging based on runtime conditions.

inputs.name: clock_has_i_hours
inputs.description: Indicates whether the clock format for timestamps in log entries should be 24-hour. This affects the readability and standardization of time records in logs.

inputs.name: entry_i
inputs.description: Optional log entry inputs, allowing for the aggregation of multiple log entries into a single log file. Supports up to 8 entries, enhancing log detail and organization.

Noise from Area Palettes [Dream].description: The 'Noise from Area Palettes' node generates a noise-based image by blending colors from different area-specific palettes. It utilizes a unique area sharpness parameter to influence the randomness and distribution of colors across specified areas, creating a visually cohesive noise pattern.

inputs.name: area_sharpness
inputs.description: Controls the sharpness of the transitions between different area palettes, influencing how distinctly the areas are defined.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: The width of the generated image.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: The height of the generated image.

inputs.name: blur_amount
inputs.description: The amount of blur applied to the noise, affecting the smoothness of the color transitions.

inputs.name: density
inputs.description: Determines the density of the noise pattern, influencing the overall texture and complexity of the image.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: A seed value for random number generation, ensuring reproducibility of the noise pattern.

inputs.name: top_left_palette
inputs.description: Specifies the palette for the top-left area of the image, influencing the color scheme in that specific section.

inputs.name: top_center_palette
inputs.description: Defines the palette for the top-center area, affecting the color distribution and theme in this particular region.

inputs.name: top_right_palette
inputs.description: Determines the palette for the top-right area, impacting the color choices and overall aesthetic in that zone.

inputs.name: center_left_palette
inputs.description: Sets the palette for the center-left area, guiding the color scheme and visual harmony in this segment.

inputs.name: center_palette
inputs.description: Indicates the palette for the central area of the image, influencing the core color theme and distribution.

inputs.name: center_right_palette
inputs.description: Specifies the palette for the center-right area, affecting the color dynamics and visual appeal in this section.

inputs.name: bottom_left_palette
inputs.description: Determines the palette for the bottom-left area, impacting the color scheme and aesthetic consistency in this part.

inputs.name: bottom_center_palette
inputs.description: Sets the palette for the bottom-center area, guiding the color choices and thematic consistency in this region.

inputs.name: bottom_right_palette
inputs.description: Defines the palette for the bottom-right area, affecting the color distribution and visual impact in this zone.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The generated image, composed of noise patterns derived from the specified area palettes.

Noise from Palette [Dream].description: This node generates a noise pattern based on a given palette, allowing for the creation of textured images with specific color schemes. It utilizes parameters such as width, height, blur amount, density, and seed to customize the noise generation process, producing a unique and stylized noise image.

inputs.name: palette
inputs.description: The palette parameter defines the color scheme used for noise generation, influencing the overall appearance and color distribution of the resulting image.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Specifies the width of the generated noise image, determining its horizontal dimension.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Specifies the height of the generated noise image, determining its vertical dimension.

inputs.name: blur_amount
inputs.description: Controls the amount of blur applied to the noise, affecting the smoothness and blending of colors.

inputs.name: density
inputs.description: Adjusts the density of the noise pattern, influencing how closely packed the noise elements are.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: A seed value for random number generation, ensuring reproducibility of the noise pattern.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is a stylized noise image generated based on the input palette and other parameters.

Palette Color Align [Dream].description: This node is designed to align the colors of a given palette with a target palette based on a specified alignment factor. It adjusts the RGB values of the original palette's colors to more closely match those of the target palette, allowing for a controlled blending or matching of color schemes.

inputs.name: palette
inputs.description: The original color palette to be aligned. It serves as the base for color adjustments towards the target palette.

inputs.name: target_align
inputs.description: The target color palette that the original palette should align with. This palette acts as the reference for the desired color adjustments.

inputs.name: alignment_factor
inputs.description: A floating-point value that determines the degree of alignment between the original and target palettes. Higher values result in closer alignment to the target palette's colors.

outputs.name: palette
outputs.description: The adjusted color palette after alignment with the target palette, reflecting the applied color shifts.

Palette Color Shift [Dream].description: This node applies a color shift to a given palette by adjusting the red, green, and blue color components according to specified multipliers, optionally maintaining a fixed brightness level. It enables the customization of color palettes for images or visual elements, enhancing or altering their aesthetic appeal.

inputs.name: palette
inputs.description: The input palette to be modified. It represents a collection of colors that will undergo adjustments based on the provided multipliers.

inputs.name: red_multiplier
inputs.description: A multiplier for the red component of each color in the palette, allowing for the intensification or reduction of red hues.

inputs.name: green_multiplier
inputs.description: A multiplier for the green component of each color in the palette, enabling the adjustment of green hues.

inputs.name: blue_multiplier
inputs.description: A multiplier for the blue component of each color in the palette, facilitating the modification of blue hues.

inputs.name: fixed_brightness
inputs.description: Determines whether the brightness level of the palette should remain constant despite the color shifts.

outputs.name: palette
outputs.description: The modified palette after applying the specified red, green, and blue multipliers, potentially with fixed brightness.

Sample Image Area as Palette [Dream].description: This node samples colors from a specified area within an image to create a color palette. It allows for targeted palette generation by focusing on specific regions of an image, enhancing thematic consistency and relevance in the resulting palette.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image from which colors are sampled to create the palette. This parameter is crucial for defining the source of the color extraction.

inputs.name: samples
inputs.description: Specifies the number of color samples to extract from the designated area of the image, directly influencing the diversity and richness of the resulting palette.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: A seed for the random number generator, ensuring reproducibility of the palette by controlling the randomness in color sampling.

inputs.name: area
inputs.description: Defines the specific area of the image from which to sample colors, allowing for targeted palette creation based on predefined image regions.

outputs.name: palette
outputs.description: The generated color palette, comprising colors sampled from the specified area of the image.

Sample Image as Palette [Dream].description: This node samples colors from an image to create a palette, using a specified number of samples and a seed for randomization. It's designed to extract a diverse color palette from an image, which can then be used for various applications such as image editing, visualization, or as a basis for generating new images.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image from which to sample colors, serving as the source for palette creation.

inputs.name: samples
inputs.description: The number of color samples to extract from the image, determining the palette's richness and diversity.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: A seed value for randomization, ensuring reproducibility of the palette sampling process.

outputs.name: palette
outputs.description: The resulting color palette, composed of sampled colors from the input image.

Saw Curve [Dream].description: The Saw Curve node generates a linear ramp waveform that cycles over a specified period, allowing for the creation of sawtooth wave animations based on frame count and time. It supports customization through parameters like maximum and minimum values, periodicity, and phase adjustment.

inputs.name: frame_counter
inputs.description: Represents the current frame count and time, used as the basis for calculating the saw curve's position within its cycle.

inputs.name: max_value
inputs.description: The maximum value the saw curve can reach within its cycle, defining the peak of the waveform.

inputs.name: min_value
inputs.description: The minimum value the saw curve can reach, defining the base of the waveform.

inputs.name: periodicity_seconds
inputs.description: The duration of one complete cycle of the saw curve in seconds, determining its frequency.

inputs.name: phase
inputs.description: A phase shift for the saw curve, allowing the waveform to be advanced or delayed within its cycle.

outputs.name: FLOAT
outputs.description: The calculated float value of the saw curve at the current frame.

outputs.name: INT
outputs.description: An integer representation of the saw curve's current value, rounded from the float calculation.

Sine Curve [Dream].description: The 'Sine Curve' node generates a sine wave based on animation frame data, allowing for dynamic visual effects in animations. It utilizes parameters such as maximum and minimum values, periodicity, and phase to shape the sine wave's amplitude and frequency.

inputs.name: frame_counter
inputs.description: The frame counter tracks the current time in seconds based on the animation's frame rate, serving as the basis for calculating the sine wave's position.

inputs.name: max_value
inputs.description: Specifies the maximum amplitude of the sine wave, defining the peak value it can reach.

inputs.name: min_value
inputs.description: Determines the minimum amplitude of the sine wave, setting the lowest value it can descend to.

inputs.name: periodicity_seconds
inputs.description: Controls the period of the sine wave, affecting how quickly it completes a full cycle.

inputs.name: phase
inputs.description: Adjusts the phase of the sine wave, shifting its starting position within the cycle.

outputs.name: FLOAT
outputs.description: The calculated sine wave value at the current frame, as a floating-point number.

outputs.name: INT
outputs.description: The sine wave value rounded to the nearest integer, for discrete animations or effects.

Smooth Event Curve [Dream].description: The Smooth Event Curve node is designed to generate a smoothly transitioning curve based on a frame counter, facilitating the creation of animations with smooth starts and ends. It calculates values within a specified range and time frame, applying a smoothing algorithm to ensure a gradual transition.

inputs.name: frame_counter
inputs.description: The frame counter is essential for determining the current time in seconds, which is used to calculate the position on the curve. It affects the node's execution by dictating the timing of the curve's progression.

inputs.name: max_value
inputs.description: Specifies the maximum value the curve can reach, playing a crucial role in defining the curve's amplitude.

inputs.name: min_value
inputs.description: Defines the minimum value of the curve, setting the baseline from which the curve can start.

inputs.name: width_seconds
inputs.description: Determines the width of the curve in seconds, affecting the duration of the smooth transition.

inputs.name: center_seconds
inputs.description: Sets the center point of the curve in seconds, around which the smooth transition is centered.

outputs.name: FLOAT
outputs.description: The floating-point result of the curve calculation, representing the smoothed value at the current frame.

outputs.name: INT
outputs.description: An integer representation of the curve's calculated value, providing a discretized output for applications requiring integer values.

String Input [Dream].description: The String Input node is designed to capture and return a single-line string input from the user. It serves as a basic interface component within a larger system, allowing for the collection of textual data in a straightforward and user-friendly manner.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: Specifies the default value of the string input, which can be pre-populated or left empty. This parameter enables the initial configuration of the input field, catering to various use cases by providing a customizable starting point.

outputs.name: STRING
outputs.description: Returns the user-provided string input, facilitating the transfer of textual data within the system.

String to Log Entry [Dream].description: The 'String to Log Entry' node is designed to convert a given text string into a log entry, optionally prefixed with a label. This functionality is essential for logging and tracking purposes within a system, allowing for the structured recording of textual data.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The 'text' parameter is the primary content to be logged. It serves as the core information that will be recorded in the log entry.

inputs.name: label
inputs.description: The 'label' parameter is an optional prefix for the text content. When provided, it categorizes or provides context to the log entry, enhancing its informational value.

outputs.name: log_entry
outputs.description: The output 'log_entry' is a structured representation of the input text, potentially prefixed with a label, formatted as a log entry for recording or tracking purposes.

String Tokenizer [Dream].description: The String Tokenizer node is designed to split a given string into parts based on a specified separator and select one of these parts based on its index. This functionality is essential for parsing and manipulating text data, allowing for the extraction of specific segments of interest from larger text bodies.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The primary text input that will be split into parts. This parameter is crucial for defining the text to be tokenized.

inputs.name: separator
inputs.description: Defines the character or string used to split the text into parts. Its role is pivotal in determining how the text is divided.

inputs.name: selected
inputs.description: Determines which part of the split text to return, based on its index. This parameter is key for selecting the specific segment of interest.

outputs.name: token
outputs.description: The selected part of the text after splitting by the specified separator. This output is significant for text processing and manipulation tasks.

Text Input [Dream].description: Provides a user interface component for text input, allowing multiline text entry with a default value. It's designed for collecting textual data from users within a graphical interface.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: Represents the text value entered by the user. It supports multiline input and starts with an empty string by default, facilitating the collection of user-generated text.

outputs.name: STRING
outputs.description: Outputs the text entered by the user, directly reflecting the input without modification.

Triangle Curve [Dream].description: The Triangle Curve node generates a triangular waveform based on the current frame's time, allowing for the creation of animations with linear ascending and descending values within a specified periodicity and phase. This node is ideal for creating cyclic animations with a clear, predictable pattern.

inputs.name: frame_counter
inputs.description: Represents the current frame in the animation, used to calculate the current time in seconds for waveform generation.

inputs.name: max_value
inputs.description: The maximum value the triangle wave can reach, defining the peak of the waveform.

inputs.name: min_value
inputs.description: The minimum value the triangle wave can reach, defining the trough of the waveform.

inputs.name: periodicity_seconds
inputs.description: The duration in seconds for one complete cycle of the triangle wave, determining its frequency.

inputs.name: phase
inputs.description: Adjusts the starting point of the wave within its cycle, allowing for phase shifts in the waveform.

outputs.name: FLOAT
outputs.description: The calculated float value of the triangle wave at the current frame's time.

outputs.name: INT
outputs.description: The integer representation of the calculated triangle wave value, rounded to the nearest whole number.

Triangle Event Curve [Dream].description: The Triangle Event Curve node generates a triangular-shaped curve over time, designed for creating dynamic, event-driven animations. It calculates values based on a frame counter and parameters defining the curve's peak, width, and center, making it suitable for timed animations and transitions.

inputs.name: frame_counter
inputs.description: Represents the current frame in the animation, used to calculate the curve's value at any given time.

inputs.name: max_value
inputs.description: The peak value of the triangle curve, defining its maximum height.

inputs.name: min_value
inputs.description: The base value of the triangle curve, defining its minimum height.

inputs.name: width_seconds
inputs.description: The duration in seconds over which the peak of the triangle curve is reached from its base value.

inputs.name: center_seconds
inputs.description: The point in time (in seconds) at which the peak of the triangle curve occurs.

outputs.name: FLOAT
outputs.description: The calculated float value of the curve at the current frame.

outputs.name: INT
outputs.description: An integer representation of the calculated curve value at the current frame.

WAV Curve [Dream].description: The WAV Curve node dynamically generates animation curves based on the amplitude of audio data from a WAV file, allowing animations to be synchronized with audio. It scales the amplitude value for a given frame, providing both float and integer outputs for versatile use in animation scripting.

inputs.name: frame_counter
inputs.description: The frame counter is essential for determining the current point in the animation timeline, affecting which part of the WAV file's amplitude is used to generate the curve.

inputs.name: wav_path
inputs.description: Specifies the path to the WAV file whose audio data is used to generate the animation curve. A default path is provided, but can be customized.

inputs.name: scale
inputs.description: A multiplier for the amplitude value extracted from the WAV file, allowing for adjustment of the animation curve's intensity.

outputs.name: FLOAT
outputs.description: The scaled amplitude value from the WAV file as a floating-point number, suitable for precise animation adjustments.

outputs.name: INT
outputs.description: The scaled amplitude value from the WAV file, rounded to the nearest integer, for discrete animation steps.

dynamicThresholdingFull.description: The `dynamicThresholdingFull` node dynamically adjusts thresholding parameters for image processing tasks, leveraging inputs such as model, mimic scale, and threshold percentile. It employs dynamic thresholding to adaptively modify processing behavior, optimizing the balance between detail preservation and noise reduction.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: Specifies the model for dynamic thresholding, serving as the core component for threshold adjustments.

inputs.name: mimic_scale
inputs.description: Determines the scale at which the model mimics aspects of the input, influencing thresholding behavior.

inputs.name: threshold_percentile
inputs.description: Sets the percentile for threshold calculation, affecting the aggressiveness of thresholding.

inputs.name: mimic_mode
inputs.description: Defines the mode of mimicry, guiding how the mimic scale is applied.

inputs.name: mimic_scale_min
inputs.description: Establishes the minimum scale for mimicry, ensuring a baseline level of detail preservation.

inputs.name: cfg_mode
inputs.description: Specifies the configuration mode, altering thresholding behavior based on the model's configuration.

inputs.name: cfg_scale_min
inputs.description: Indicates the minimum scale for configuration, impacting the fineness of thresholding adjustments.

inputs.name: sched_val
inputs.description: A value to schedule or adjust the thresholding dynamically over time or iterations.

inputs.name: separate_feature_channels
inputs.description: Determines whether feature channels should be processed separately or together, affecting the thresholding process.

inputs.name: scaling_startpoint
inputs.description: Defines the starting point for scaling in the dynamic thresholding process.

inputs.name: variability_measure
inputs.description: Specifies the measure of variability to consider in the dynamic thresholding process.

inputs.name: interpolate_phi
inputs.description: A factor for interpolating the thresholding function, influencing the smoothness of the transition between thresholds.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: Produces a modified model with dynamically adjusted thresholding parameters, optimized for image processing.

easy a1111Loader.description: The easy a1111Loader node is designed to simplify the process of loading and configuring models for use in AI-driven applications. It abstracts the complexities involved in setting up models, including checkpoint loading, LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) adjustments, and optional control net stacking, making it easier for users to get started with their AI projects.

inputs.name: ckpt_name
inputs.description: Specifies the checkpoint name for the model to be loaded. It is crucial for identifying which pre-trained model to use, affecting the node's execution by determining the initial state of the model.

inputs.name: vae_name
inputs.description: Defines the name of the VAE (Variational Autoencoder) to be used alongside the model. This parameter influences the quality and characteristics of the generated content by specifying the underlying generative model.

inputs.name: clip_skip
inputs.description: Specifies the number of CLIP model layers to skip during processing, allowing for customization of the model's focus and performance.

inputs.name: lora_name
inputs.description: Indicates the name of the LoRA to apply to the model, allowing for fine-tuning and adaptation of the model's weights without extensive retraining. This parameter is key for customizing the model's behavior for specific tasks.

inputs.name: lora_model_strength
inputs.description: Determines the strength of the LoRA model adaptation, directly impacting the model's performance and output by adjusting the intensity of the applied modifications.

inputs.name: lora_clip_strength
inputs.description: Sets the strength of the LoRA clip adaptation, affecting the final output by modifying how strongly the clip adaptation influences the model's behavior.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: Specifies the resolution for the output, directly affecting the visual quality and detail of the generated images or content.

inputs.name: empty_latent_width
inputs.description: Defines the width of the empty latent space, influencing the dimensionality and potential complexity of the generated content.

inputs.name: empty_latent_height
inputs.description: Sets the height of the empty latent space, impacting the size and detail level of the generated outputs.

inputs.name: positive
inputs.description: A string input for positive prompts, guiding the model to emphasize or generate content that aligns with the specified attributes or themes.

inputs.name: negative
inputs.description: A string input for negative prompts, instructing the model to de-emphasize or avoid content related to the specified attributes or themes.

inputs.name: batch_size
inputs.description: Determines the number of instances to process in a single batch, affecting the efficiency and speed of model execution.

inputs.name: optional_lora_stack
inputs.description: Allows for the specification of an optional stack of LoRA adjustments, enabling more complex and layered model customizations.

inputs.name: optional_controlnet_stack
inputs.description: Enables the inclusion of an optional control net stack for further model customization and fine-tuning, offering advanced control over the model's behavior.

inputs.name: a1111_prompt_style

easy applyBrushNet.description: The `easy applyBrushNet` node integrates the functionality of BrushNet, a specialized neural network for image inpainting and enhancement, into a pipeline. It leverages BrushNet to apply sophisticated image processing techniques, enhancing or modifying images based on given masks and inputs. This node is designed to seamlessly incorporate BrushNet's capabilities into broader workflows, facilitating advanced image manipulation tasks.

easy applyFooocusInpaint.description: The `applyFooocusInpaint` node is designed to integrate inpainting capabilities into a model's pipeline by applying specific inpainting heads and patches. This process involves loading and applying pre-trained components to modify the model in a way that it can perform inpainting tasks, which is the process of filling in missing or corrupted parts of images.

easy applyInpaint.description: This node facilitates the application of various inpainting techniques to images, offering a flexible approach to restoring or modifying specific areas of an image based on the inpainting mode selected. It integrates seamlessly with different inpainting strategies, such as 'fooocus_inpaint', 'brushnet_random', and others, to accommodate diverse inpainting needs.

inputs.name: end_at

outputs.name: pipe

easy applyPowerPaint.description: The `easy applyPowerPaint` node is designed to facilitate advanced image manipulation tasks such as text-guided editing, shape-guided creation, object removal, context-aware adjustments, and image outpainting. It leverages a combination of models and techniques, including PowerPaint, to apply complex transformations and enhancements to images based on user-defined parameters.

easy boolean.description: This node provides a simplified interface for toggling boolean settings within a larger system, streamlining the process of enabling or disabling features or behaviors based on user input or predefined conditions.

easy cascadeKSampler.description: The easy cascadeKSampler node facilitates the generation of images through a cascading sampling process, leveraging a pipeline of models for enhanced detail and quality. It simplifies the complex setup typically required for cascading sampling, making it accessible for users to produce high-quality images with minimal configuration.

easy cascadeLoader.description: The `easy cascadeLoader` node is designed to facilitate the loading and management of cascading models, specifically focusing on integrating multiple model stages for enhanced processing capabilities. easy ckptNames.description: This node is designed to facilitate the selection and management of checkpoint names within a pipeline, allowing users to easily specify and retrieve the names of various checkpoints for use in model loading or other operations that require specific checkpoint identification.

easy cleanGpuUsed.description: The `cleanGpuUsed` node is designed to facilitate the release of GPU resources by clearing the GPU memory cache and unloading all models from memory. This operation is crucial for managing GPU memory efficiently, especially in environments where multiple models are loaded and unloaded dynamically.

It serves as a utility for resetting or refreshing the cache state within the system, ensuring that all cached data is removed to prevent stale or outdated information from being used.

It aims to manage and optimize cache usage by allowing the removal of outdated or unnecessary cache entries, thereby ensuring that the cache remains efficient and relevant.

easy comfyLoader.description: The `easy comfyLoader` node is designed to simplify the process of loading and configuring models for image generation tasks. It abstracts away the complexities involved in setting up models like Stable Diffusion, allowing users to easily specify model checkpoints, VAEs, and other parameters through a user-friendly interface. This node aims to make advanced image generation accessible to a wider audience by providing an easy-to-use loading mechanism.

easy controlnetLoader.description: The `easy controlnetLoader` node is designed to simplify the process of loading control networks within the ComfyUI framework. It abstracts the complexities involved in fetching and applying control networks to models, offering a streamlined interface for users to easily integrate control networks into their projects.

easy controlnetStack.description: This node is designed to dynamically stack control networks for image manipulation tasks. It allows for the flexible integration of multiple control networks into a single processing pipeline, enabling advanced image conditioning and transformation based on specified control parameters. The node supports varying levels of control intensity, start and end percentages for effect application, and the ability to scale soft weights, providing a comprehensive toolkit for precise image editing.

inputs.name: image_output

inputs.name: link_id
inputs.description: A unique identifier for the link in the sampling process, facilitating tracking and management of the generated output.

inputs.name: save_prefix
inputs.description: The prefix for saved files, allowing for organized storage of generated outputs.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: The seed value for the random number generator, ensuring reproducibility of the sampling process.

inputs.name: image_to_latent_c
inputs.description: Optional parameter for providing an image to be converted into a latent representation, enhancing the control over the generation process.

inputs.name: latent_c
inputs.description: Optional parameter for providing a latent representation directly, offering an advanced level of control over the generation process.

inputs.name: model_c

outputs.name: pipe

outputs.name: model_b

outputs.name: latent_b
