easy fullkSampler.description: The `easy fullkSampler` node is designed to facilitate the sampling process in generative models by providing a simplified interface for users. It abstracts the complexities involved in sampling configurations, allowing for easy experimentation with different models, seeds, steps, conditioning, and denoising parameters. This node aims to make the process of generating new samples more accessible and user-friendly, especially for those not deeply familiar with the underlying algorithms.

inputs.name: pipe
inputs.description: The pipeline configuration for the sampling process, integrating various nodes and operations for a comprehensive workflow.

inputs.name: steps
inputs.description: Defines the number of steps to be used in the sampling process. This parameter affects the detail and quality of the generated samples, with a higher number of steps potentially leading to more refined outputs.

inputs.name: cfg
inputs.description: Controls the conditioning factor, which influences the adherence of the generated samples to the specified conditions. This parameter allows for fine-tuning the balance between randomness and conditioning in the sampling output.

inputs.name: sampler_name
inputs.description: Selects the specific sampling algorithm to be used. This choice impacts the sampling behavior and the characteristics of the generated images, offering flexibility in exploring different sampling strategies.

inputs.name: scheduler
inputs.description: Chooses the scheduler for the sampling process, which determines how the sampling parameters are adjusted over time. This affects the progression and quality of the sampling process.

inputs.name: denoise
inputs.description: Sets the denoising strength used in the sampling process. Adjusting this parameter can help in controlling the level of detail and clarity in the generated samples.

inputs.name: image_output
inputs.description: Determines the output format for images, including options for file types and quality settings.

inputs.name: link_id
inputs.description: A unique identifier for linking the output with other processes or storage locations.

inputs.name: save_prefix
inputs.description: A prefix added to the filenames of saved images, allowing for organized storage and retrieval.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: Sets the initial seed for the random number generator used in the sampling process. This ensures reproducibility of results, allowing users to generate the same output given the same set of parameters.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: Specifies the generative model to be used for sampling. This parameter is crucial as it determines the base model from which samples will be generated, affecting the overall quality and characteristics of the output.

inputs.name: positive
inputs.description: Specifies positive conditioning to guide the sampling towards desired attributes or features in the generated output. This parameter helps in directing the model to produce samples that match certain criteria.

inputs.name: negative
inputs.description: Specifies negative conditioning to avoid certain attributes or features in the generated output. This parameter is useful for steering the sampling away from undesired characteristics.

inputs.name: latent
inputs.description: Provides an initial latent image to start the sampling from. This can be used for tasks like image editing or continuation, where the starting point is a pre-existing latent representation.

inputs.name: vae
inputs.description: Specifies the VAE model to be used in conjunction with the sampling process for tasks like encoding or decoding.

inputs.name: clip
inputs.description: Specifies the CLIP model for text or image conditioning, enhancing the relevance of the generated samples to given prompts or images.

inputs.name: xyPlot
inputs.description: An optional parameter for plotting or visualizing data related to the sampling process.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: An optional input image for tasks such as image editing or style transfer.

outputs.name: pipe
outputs.description: The output pipeline configuration, encapsulating the entire sampling process and its results.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The generated image or images as a result of the sampling process.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The model used in the sampling process, potentially modified or updated through the operation.

outputs.name: positive
outputs.description: The positive conditioning applied during the sampling, influencing the characteristics of the generated output.

outputs.name: negative
outputs.description: The negative conditioning applied to steer the sampling away from certain features or attributes.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The output latent representation of the generated sample. This can be used for further processing or conversion into an image, representing the final result of the sampling process.

outputs.name: vae
outputs.description: The VAE model involved in the sampling process, if applicable, including any encoding or decoding operations.

outputs.name: clip
outputs.description: The CLIP model used for conditioning, reflecting its role in shaping the output based on textual or visual prompts.

outputs.name: seed
outputs.description: The seed value used in the sampling process, indicating the role of randomness and reproducibility in generating the output.

easy fullLoader.description: The `easy fullLoader` node is designed to streamline the process of loading and initializing various models and components required for image generation tasks. It encapsulates the complexity of handling different model types, such as Stable Diffusion, control nets, and DIT loaders, providing a unified interface for easy integration and use within the ComfyUI framework. This node significantly simplifies the setup and configuration phase, enabling users to focus on the creative aspects of image generation.

inputs.name: ckpt_name
inputs.description: Specifies the checkpoint name for the model to be loaded. This parameter is crucial for identifying and retrieving the correct model version, affecting the quality and characteristics of the generated images.

inputs.name: config_name
inputs.description: Specifies the configuration name for further customization of the loading process, allowing for more tailored model initialization.

inputs.name: vae_name
inputs.description: Determines the VAE model to be used in conjunction with the primary model. The choice of VAE can influence the style and details of the generated images, making it an important aspect of the configuration.

inputs.name: clip_skip
inputs.description: Determines the number of layers to skip in the CLIP model, affecting the depth of text encoding.

inputs.name: lora_name
inputs.description: Identifies the LoRA model to be applied, if any. LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) allows for fine-tuning and adjusting model behaviors without extensive retraining, offering a way to customize the generation process.

inputs.name: lora_model_strength
inputs.description: Controls the intensity of the LoRA model's influence on the generation process. This parameter allows users to balance between the original model's output and the modifications introduced by LoRA.

inputs.name: lora_clip_strength
inputs.description: Adjusts the strength of LoRA's effect specifically on the CLIP model's outputs. This fine-tuning capability enables more precise control over the semantic alignment between text prompts and generated images.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: Sets the resolution for the generated images. Higher resolutions produce more detailed images but require more computational resources.

inputs.name: empty_latent_width
inputs.description: Specifies the width of the empty latent space to be used for image generation. This parameter is part of the setup for generating images from scratch or modifying existing ones.

inputs.name: empty_latent_height
inputs.description: Defines the height of the empty latent space, complementing the width setting to determine the overall dimensions of the generated images.

inputs.name: positive
inputs.description: A text prompt that guides the model towards generating images with desired attributes. Positive prompts encourage the inclusion of specific elements or themes in the output.

inputs.name: positive_token_normalization
inputs.description: Defines the method for normalizing positive prompt tokens, influencing the weighting of text prompts.

inputs.name: positive_weight_interpretation
inputs.description: Specifies how the weights of positive prompts are interpreted, affecting the emphasis on certain aspects of the image generation.

inputs.name: negative
inputs.description: A text prompt used to steer the model away from certain attributes or themes. Negative prompts help in excluding undesired elements from the generated images.

inputs.name: negative_token_normalization
inputs.description: Defines the method for normalizing negative prompt tokens, influencing the weighting of text prompts.

inputs.name: negative_weight_interpretation
inputs.description: Specifies how the weights of negative prompts are interpreted, affecting the emphasis on certain aspects of the image generation.

inputs.name: batch_size
inputs.description: Determines the number of images to be generated in a single batch. Adjusting the batch size can impact performance and resource utilization.

inputs.name: model_override
inputs.description: Allows for the override of the default model with a specified one, offering flexibility in model selection.

inputs.name: clip_override
inputs.description: Enables the override of the default CLIP model with a specified one, allowing for customization of text encoding.

inputs.name: vae_override
inputs.description: Permits the override of the default VAE model with a specified one, providing options for style and detail customization.

inputs.name: optional_lora_stack
inputs.description: Optional parameter to specify a stack of LoRA models for enhanced customization.

inputs.name: optional_controlnet_stack
inputs.description: Optional parameter to specify a stack of control net models for additional adjustments to the generation process.

inputs.name: a1111_prompt_style
inputs.description: Enables the use of a specific prompt style, offering further customization of the text-to-image translation process.

outputs.name: pipe
outputs.description: Outputs the configured pipeline necessary for generating images based on the provided settings.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: Returns the loaded model after configuration, ready for image generation.

outputs.name: vae
outputs.description: Returns the loaded VAE model, which influences the style and details of the generated images.

outputs.name: clip
outputs.description: Returns the loaded CLIP model, used for encoding text prompts into visual concepts.

outputs.name: positive
outputs.description: Outputs the positive embeddings generated from the text prompts, guiding the image generation towards desired attributes.

outputs.name: negative
outputs.description: Outputs the negative embeddings generated from the text prompts, steering the image generation away from certain attributes.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: Provides the latent space representation used for image generation, offering a foundation for creativity.

easy globalSeed.description: The `easy globalSeed` node is designed to manage and control the seed value used across various nodes in a workflow, allowing for consistent or varied randomization effects based on user-defined actions. It supports operations such as fixing, incrementing, decrementing, and randomizing the seed, as well as applying these actions globally or per node, to achieve controlled randomness in the generation process.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: Specifies the base seed value from which the seed management starts, serving as the foundation for subsequent operations like incrementing or randomizing.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Determines when the seed control should be applied, either before or after the generation process, allowing for precise timing in the application of seed values.

inputs.name: action
inputs.description: Defines the operation to be performed on the seed value, such as fixing, incrementing, decrementing, or randomizing, including variations for per-node actions.

inputs.name: last_seed
inputs.description: Optionally stores the last seed value used, facilitating tracking and reuse of seed values across sessions or nodes.

easy hiresFix.description: The `easy hiresFix` node is designed to enhance the resolution and detail of images, typically used as a post-processing step to refine and improve the visual quality of generated images. It focuses on fixing high-resolution aspects, making it suitable for applications requiring detailed and clear visual outputs.

inputs.name: model_name
inputs.description: Specifies the neural network model used for the upscale process, impacting the quality and method of enhancement.

inputs.name: rescale_after_model
inputs.description: Determines whether the image is rescaled after being processed by the model, affecting the final image size and detail.

inputs.name: rescale_method
inputs.description: Defines the method used for rescaling the image, influencing the quality and appearance of the final output.

inputs.name: rescale
inputs.description: Specifies how the image is rescaled, by percentage or to specific dimensions, directly impacting the output size.

inputs.name: percent
inputs.description: The percentage to rescale the image by when 'rescale' is set to 'by percentage', affecting the output image size.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: The target width of the image when 'rescale' is set to 'to Width/Height', determining the output dimensions.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: The target height of the image when 'rescale' is set to 'to Width/Height', determining the output dimensions.

inputs.name: longer_side
inputs.description: Specifies the longer side dimension for rescaling while maintaining aspect ratio, used when 'rescale' is set to 'to longer side - maintain aspect'.

inputs.name: crop
inputs.description: Indicates whether and how the image should be cropped, affecting the composition of the final output.

inputs.name: image_output
inputs.description: Determines the format of the output image, influencing how the result is saved or displayed.

inputs.name: link_id
inputs.description: A unique identifier for linking the processed image with other elements or processes, useful for tracking and organization.

inputs.name: save_prefix
inputs.description: A prefix added to the file name of the saved image, useful for organization and identification.

inputs.name: pipe
inputs.description: An optional pipeline of processes the image may go through before or after the upscale process, affecting the overall workflow.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be upscaled, serving as the direct subject of the enhancement process.

inputs.name: vae
inputs.description: An optional VAE model that can be used in conjunction with the upscale process for additional image processing.

outputs.name: pipe
outputs.description: The output pipeline, potentially including the upscaled image among other processed elements.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The upscaled image, showcasing improved resolution and detail.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: A latent representation of the image, useful for further processing or analysis.

easy humanSegmentation.description: This node is designed for segmenting human figures from images, utilizing a choice of pre-defined segmentation methods. It abstracts the complexity of human segmentation processes, offering an easy-to-use interface for extracting human figures with various levels of detail and precision.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be segmented. This parameter is crucial as it provides the raw data for the segmentation process.

inputs.name: method
inputs.description: Specifies the segmentation method to be used. This choice affects the segmentation's accuracy and detail, allowing for customization based on the user's needs.

inputs.name: confidence
inputs.description: Determines the confidence threshold for the segmentation process, influencing the precision of the human figure extraction.

inputs.name: crop_multi
inputs.description: Adjusts the cropping multiplier to control the extent of the area around the segmented human figure that is included in the output.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The segmented image with the human figure.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: A binary mask of the segmented human figure.

outputs.name: bbox
outputs.description: Bounding box coordinates of the segmented human figure.

easy hunyuanDiTLoader.description: This node is designed to load and configure the HunYuanDiT model for image generation tasks. It prepares the model by loading the necessary checkpoints, VAE, and CLIP components, and sets up the environment for generating images based on text prompts. The node facilitates the integration of the HunYuanDiT model into the workflow, ensuring that all components are correctly initialized and ready for use.

inputs.name: ckpt_name
inputs.description: Specifies the checkpoint name for loading the model, essential for initializing the HunYuanDiT model with the correct weights and configurations.

inputs.name: model_name
inputs.description: Defines the specific model configuration to use, allowing for customization and optimization of the image generation process.

inputs.name: vae_name
inputs.description: Indicates the VAE component to load, crucial for the image encoding and decoding processes within the HunYuanDiT model.

inputs.name: clip_name
inputs.description: Determines the CLIP model to integrate, used for processing text prompts and guiding the image generation.

inputs.name: mt5_name
inputs.description: Specifies the MT5 model for additional text processing capabilities, enhancing the model's understanding of text prompts.

inputs.name: device
inputs.description: Selects the computation device (e.g., CPU, GPU) for model execution, affecting performance and efficiency.

inputs.name: dtype
inputs.description: Sets the data type for model operations, ensuring compatibility and optimal performance.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: Defines the resolution of the generated images, allowing for control over image quality and detail.

inputs.name: empty_latent_width
inputs.description: Specifies the width of the empty latent space, important for initializing the image generation process.

inputs.name: empty_latent_height
inputs.description: Specifies the height of the empty latent space, important for initializing the image generation process.

inputs.name: positive
inputs.description: Contains positive text prompts that guide the image generation towards desired attributes.

inputs.name: negative
inputs.description: Contains negative text prompts that guide the image generation away from undesired attributes.

inputs.name: batch_size
inputs.description: Determines the number of images to generate in a single batch, impacting performance and output volume.

outputs.name: pipe
outputs.description: Returns the configured pipeline for image generation, including all necessary models and settings.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: Provides the loaded and configured model ready for image generation tasks.

outputs.name: vae
outputs.description: Returns the loaded VAE component, essential for the image encoding and decoding processes.

easy icLightApply.description: This node applies the ICLight model to enhance or modify the lighting of an image based on the specified mode. It leverages advanced image processing techniques to adjust the lighting conditions of the input image, making it suitable for various applications such as image editing, enhancement, and realistic rendering.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Specifies the lighting mode to apply to the image, offering options like left light, right light, top light, etc., to simulate different lighting conditions.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model to be used for the lighting adjustment process.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to which the lighting effects will be applied.

inputs.name: vae
inputs.description: A variational autoencoder used for encoding the image before applying the lighting effects.

inputs.name: lighting
inputs.description: Defines the specific lighting effect to be applied.

inputs.name: source
inputs.description: Specifies the source mode for generating the lighting image.

inputs.name: remove_bg
inputs.description: Indicates whether the background of the image should be removed before applying the lighting effects.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The model used after applying the lighting effects.

outputs.name: lighting_image
outputs.description: The output image with the applied lighting effects.

easy if.description: The 'easy if' node likely serves as a conditional logic gate within a pipeline, enabling the execution of different paths or operations based on specified conditions. This functionality is essential for creating dynamic and adaptable workflows that can respond to varying inputs or states.

inputs.name: any
inputs.description: Serves as a generic input that can be of any type, acting as the data or condition to be evaluated.

inputs.name: if
inputs.description: Defines the condition under which a certain path or operation should be executed.

inputs.name: else
inputs.description: Specifies an alternative path or operation to execute if the 'if' condition is not met.

outputs.description: The output can vary based on the evaluation of the 'if' condition, leading to different possible outcomes.

easy imageBatchToImageList.description: The node is designed to convert a batch of images into a list of individual images, facilitating operations that require handling images on a per-image basis rather than in batch form.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image batch to be split into individual images. This parameter is crucial for the node's operation as it directly influences the output list of images.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is a list of individual images that were originally part of the input image batch.

easy imageChooser.description: The `easy imageChooser` node enables users to select preferred images from a given set through an interactive interface. This node simplifies the process of image selection, making it an essential tool for workflows that require user engagement and decision-making in choosing specific images for further processing or analysis.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Specifies the selection mode, allowing users to define how the image selection process should be conducted. This parameter determines the behavior of the chooser, affecting the user's interaction and the selection criteria.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: A collection of images presented to the user for selection. This input is essential for providing the set of options from which the user can make their choice, directly influencing the selection process.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: Returns the selected image or images, reflecting the user's choices. This output is vital for further processing or analysis of the chosen images.

easy imageColorMatch.description: The 'easy imageColorMatch' node is designed to adjust the color scheme of a target image to match that of a reference image. It supports various color matching methods and allows for the customization of the output through saving options and prefixes. This node is particularly useful in scenarios where consistency in color tone across different images is desired, such as in photo editing, graphic design, and content creation.

inputs.name: image_ref
inputs.description: The reference image whose color scheme is to be matched. It serves as the standard for color adjustment of the target image.

inputs.name: image_target
inputs.description: The target image that will be adjusted to match the color scheme of the reference image.

inputs.name: method
inputs.description: Specifies the color matching method to be used. It determines the algorithm for adjusting the target image's colors.

inputs.name: image_output
inputs.description: Controls the output behavior of the node, allowing options such as hiding, previewing, or saving the processed image.

inputs.name: save_prefix
inputs.description: A prefix for the saved file name, providing a way to organize and identify processed images easily.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The processed image with its color scheme adjusted to match the reference image.

easy imageConcat.description: The `easy imageConcat` node is designed to concatenate two images either horizontally or vertically, with an option to match their sizes for seamless integration. This functionality is essential for tasks requiring the combination of images in a specific orientation, such as creating panoramic views or composite images.

inputs.name: image1
inputs.description: The first image to be concatenated. It serves as the base image to which the second image will be attached.

inputs.name: image2
inputs.description: The second image to be concatenated to the first one. This image can be resized to match the first image's dimensions if required.

inputs.name: direction
inputs.description: Specifies the direction of concatenation ('right', 'down', 'left', 'up'), determining how the second image is attached to the first.

inputs.name: match_image_size
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether the second image should be resized to match the first image's dimensions before concatenation.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The resulting image after concatenating the two input images according to the specified direction and size matching option.

easy imageCount.description: The `easy imageCount` node is designed to count the number of images in a given batch, providing a straightforward way to quantify image collections within a workflow.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The `images` parameter represents the batch of images to be counted. It is crucial for determining the total number of images present, affecting the node's output directly.

outputs.name: count
outputs.description: The `count` output represents the total number of images in the input batch, providing a simple integer count.

easy imageCropFromMask.description: The `imageCropFromMask` node is designed for cropping images based on a provided mask. It utilizes the mask to determine the relevant area of the image to retain, effectively isolating and extracting the portion of the image that corresponds to the mask's coverage.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The `image` parameter represents the image to be cropped. It is essential for determining the area of interest that will be retained after the cropping process, based on the mask's outline.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The `mask` parameter is crucial for defining the area of the image to be cropped. It acts as a guide for isolating the specific portion of the image that should be retained, based on the mask's coverage.

inputs.name: image_crop_multi
inputs.description: This parameter specifies the multiplier to adjust the crop size relative to the mask's bounding box, affecting the final cropped image size.

inputs.name: mask_crop_multi
inputs.description: This parameter adjusts the size of the mask used for cropping, influencing the area of the image that gets cropped.

inputs.name: bbox_smooth_alpha
inputs.description: This parameter controls the smoothing of bounding box size changes over time, affecting the consistency of the crop dimensions.

outputs.name: crop_image
outputs.description: The cropped portion of the original image, as determined by the mask and cropping parameters.

outputs.name: crop_mask
outputs.description: The cropped portion of the mask, corresponding to the cropped area of the image.

outputs.name: bbox
outputs.description: The bounding box coordinates of the cropped area within the original image.

easy imageDetailTransfer.description: This node specializes in transferring intricate details from a source image to a target image, enhancing the target with characteristics or styles found in the source. It operates by blending visual elements between images, potentially using various modes of blending to achieve the desired effect. The node is designed for applications requiring high fidelity in detail preservation or stylistic amalgamation, making it suitable for tasks like photo editing, artistic creation, and visual content enhancement.

inputs.name: target
inputs.description: The 'target' parameter represents the image that will receive the details or styles from the source image. It plays a crucial role in the operation by serving as the canvas on which the transferred details are applied, directly influencing the outcome of the detail transfer process.

inputs.name: source
inputs.description: The 'source' parameter specifies the image from which details or styles will be extracted and transferred to the target image. Its content significantly affects the detail transfer process, as it provides the visual elements to be blended into the target.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: The 'mode' parameter determines the blending technique used to transfer details from the source to the target image. It influences the visual outcome of the transfer, offering various options for how the details are integrated.

inputs.name: blur_sigma
inputs.description: Specifies the standard deviation for the Gaussian blur applied to the target image, affecting the smoothness of the detail transfer.

inputs.name: blend_factor
inputs.description: Controls the intensity of the blending between the source and target images, directly influencing the visibility of transferred details.

inputs.name: image_output
inputs.description: Determines how the output image is handled, whether it is hidden, previewed, saved, or a combination of these actions.

inputs.name: save_prefix
inputs.description: A prefix added to the filename when saving the output image, helping in organizing and identifying the results.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: An optional mask that can be applied to the target image, specifying areas where the detail transfer should or should not occur. This parameter allows for more precise control over the application of transferred details, enabling selective enhancement based on the mask's coverage.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The final image after the detail transfer process, incorporating the blended details from the source image into the target.

easy imageInsetCrop.description: The node provides functionality for cropping an image based on specified inset dimensions, adjusting the crop area according to the given measurements and ensuring the dimensions do not exceed the image's boundaries. It supports cropping by percentage or absolute values, with additional adjustments to align the crop area to a grid, enhancing compatibility with certain image processing operations.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image to be cropped, provided as a multi-dimensional array representing the image data.

inputs.name: measurement
inputs.description: Specifies the unit of measurement for the crop dimensions, allowing for either percentage-based or absolute value cropping, which influences how the crop boundaries are calculated.

inputs.name: left
inputs.description: The left boundary of the crop area, defined either as a percentage of the image's width or as an absolute value, depending on the measurement unit.

inputs.name: right
inputs.description: The right boundary of the crop area, similar to 'left', but for the right side of the image.

inputs.name: top
inputs.description: The top boundary of the crop area, defined in the same manner as 'left' and 'right', but for the top edge of the image.

inputs.name: bottom
inputs.description: The bottom boundary of the crop area, defined similarly to the other boundaries, for the bottom edge of the image.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The cropped image, returned as a multi-dimensional array with the same structure as the input image but with dimensions adjusted according to the specified crop boundaries.

easy imageInterrogator.description: The `easy imageInterrogator` node is designed to generate descriptive prompts based on input images, utilizing different modes to adjust the interrogation process according to the desired level of detail or speed. This functionality aids in creating textual representations of visual content, which can be used for further image generation or analysis tasks.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The `image` parameter is the visual content that the node will analyze to generate a descriptive prompt. It is central to the node's operation, as the output depends on the interpretation of this image.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: The `mode` parameter allows users to specify the interrogation process's detail level or speed, offering options like 'fast', 'classic', 'best', and 'negative'. This choice influences the prompt's quality and generation time.

inputs.name: use_lowvram
inputs.description: The `use_lowvram` parameter enables the node to operate in a low VRAM mode, optimizing resource usage for systems with limited graphics memory. This can affect the interrogation process's efficiency and results.

outputs.name: prompt
outputs.description: The output `prompt` is a textual description generated from the input image, reflecting the visual content's interpretation through the specified interrogation mode.

easy imageListToImageBatch.description: This node is designed to transform a list of images into a single image batch, effectively consolidating multiple images into a unified tensor structure for batch processing. It is particularly useful in scenarios where operations need to be applied to multiple images simultaneously, streamlining the workflow by handling images in a batched manner.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: Represents the list of images to be batched together. Each image in the list is processed and combined into a single batch, facilitating operations that require batch-level processing.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is a single tensor that combines all input images into a batch. This batched format is suitable for further processing or analysis that benefits from batched data handling.

easy imagePixelPerfect.description: This node is designed to enhance image quality by adjusting the pixel perfection of images. It focuses on optimizing the resolution and sharpness to achieve the best possible visual clarity without altering the original image's content.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed for pixel perfection. This parameter is essential for the node to perform its function of optimizing the image's resolution and sharpness.

inputs.name: resize_mode
inputs.description: Specifies the mode of resizing to be applied to the image, such as resizing to a specific dimension or scaling down while maintaining the aspect ratio. This parameter plays a crucial role in determining how the image's pixel perfection is enhanced.

outputs.name: resolution
outputs.description: The optimized resolution of the image after processing, indicating the enhanced pixel perfection.

easy imageRatio.description: The `easy imageRatio` node calculates the simplified width and height ratios of an image, providing both integer and floating-point representations. This functionality is essential for understanding the aspect ratio of images in a more digestible form, which can be particularly useful for resizing, scaling, or any form of image manipulation where maintaining aspect ratio is crucial.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image for which the width and height ratios are to be calculated. This image's dimensions are used to compute the greatest common divisor (GCD) and subsequently the simplified width and height ratios.

outputs.name: width_ratio_int
outputs.description: The simplified width ratio of the image as an integer.

outputs.name: height_ratio_int
outputs.description: The simplified height ratio of the image as an integer.

outputs.name: width_ratio_float
outputs.description: The simplified width ratio of the image as a floating-point number, identical to the integer ratio in this context.

outputs.name: height_ratio_float
outputs.description: The simplified height ratio of the image as a floating-point number, identical to the integer ratio in this context.

easy imageRemBg.description: This node specializes in removing backgrounds from images, offering a streamlined approach for image processing tasks that require isolating subjects from their backgrounds. It leverages specific removal modes to adapt the background removal process to various requirements, enhancing flexibility and utility in image manipulation workflows.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: Specifies the images from which backgrounds are to be removed. This parameter is crucial for defining the input images that the node will process, directly influencing the outcome of the background removal.

inputs.name: rem_mode
inputs.description: Determines the removal mode to be used, which can affect the method and quality of the background removal. This allows for customization of the background removal process based on specific needs or preferences.

inputs.name: image_output
inputs.description: Defines how the output image should be handled, whether it should be hidden, previewed, saved, or both hidden and saved. This parameter allows for flexible management of the output image.

inputs.name: save_prefix
inputs.description: Specifies the prefix for saved images, providing a way to organize and identify output files easily.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image with the background removed. This highlights the node's ability to isolate the subject from its background, providing a clean image ready for further processing or use.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The mask generated during the background removal process. This can be used for further image processing tasks, such as compositing or additional manipulations.

easy imageSave.description: The 'easy imageSave' node is designed to simplify the process of saving images. It abstracts the complexities involved in file handling and image encoding, providing a straightforward way for users to save images to disk with minimal configuration.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: Specifies the images to be saved. This parameter is crucial as it directly influences the output by determining which images are processed and stored.

inputs.name: filename_prefix
inputs.description: Defines the prefix for the saved image filenames, allowing users to organize their saved images more effectively by categorizing them under a common prefix.

inputs.name: only_preview
inputs.description: Determines if the node should only preview the images without saving them, offering an option to review images before committing to save.

easy imageScaleDown.description: The node 'easy imageScaleDown' is designed to reduce the resolution of an image according to specified downscaling options. It focuses on adjusting the image size while maintaining essential details through various downscaling methods, such as bicubic interpolation. This node is particularly useful in scenarios where image size reduction is required without significant loss of visual quality, optimizing images for various applications like faster web loading or efficient storage.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The 'images' parameter represents the input images to be downscaled. It is crucial for determining the starting point of the downscaling process.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: The 'width' parameter specifies the target width for the downscaled image. It directly influences the dimensions of the output image.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: The 'height' parameter specifies the target height for the downscaled image. It directly influences the dimensions of the output image.

inputs.name: crop
inputs.description: The 'crop' parameter determines how the image will be cropped during the downscaling process, affecting the final appearance and dimensions of the output image.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is the downscaled version of the input images, optimized in size while aiming to preserve as much of the original detail as possible.

easy imageScaleDownBy.description: The node is designed to scale down images by a specified factor, adjusting the dimensions of the image while maintaining its aspect ratio. It provides a straightforward way to reduce the resolution of images for various applications, such as optimizing for performance or adjusting for display sizes.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: Specifies the images to be scaled down. This parameter is crucial for defining the input images that will undergo the scaling process.

inputs.name: scale_by
inputs.description: Determines the factor by which the images will be scaled down. This parameter directly influences the output size of the images, allowing for precise control over the scaling process.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The scaled-down images, with dimensions adjusted according to the specified scale factor.

easy imageScaleDownToSize.description: This node provides functionality for scaling down images to a specified size while maintaining the aspect ratio. It allows users to choose between scaling down to the maximum or minimum dimension of the image, ensuring the final image dimensions do not exceed the specified size.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The input images to be scaled down. This parameter is crucial for defining the source images that the scaling operation will be applied to.

inputs.name: size
inputs.description: The target size to scale down the images to. This parameter determines the maximum dimension (width or height) of the output images, depending on the mode selected.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating the scaling mode: 'max' to scale down based on the larger dimension or 'min' to scale based on the smaller dimension. This affects how the aspect ratio is preserved during scaling.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output images after scaling down to the specified size, with aspect ratio maintained.

easy imageSize.description: The `easy imageSize` node is designed to calculate the dimensions of an image, returning the width and height as integers. This node simplifies the process of obtaining image size metrics, making it accessible for various image processing and analysis tasks.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The `image` parameter is the input image for which the dimensions are to be calculated. It plays a crucial role in the node's operation by providing the necessary data to determine the image's width and height.

outputs.name: width_int
outputs.description: The width of the input image in pixels, returned as an integer.

outputs.name: height_int
outputs.description: The height of the input image in pixels, returned as an integer.

easy imageSizeByLongerSide.description: This node is designed to determine the dimensions of an image by identifying and measuring the longer side. It simplifies the process of working with image dimensions in scenarios where the size of the longer side is crucial, offering a straightforward approach to image size adjustment while preserving the aspect ratio.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image input is essential for determining its dimensions, with a specific focus on measuring the longer side to accurately adjust the image size.

outputs.name: resolution
outputs.description: Outputs the resolution as an integer, representing the size of the longer side of the image.

easy imageSizeBySide.description: This node calculates the dimension of an image based on the specified side (longest or shortest), providing a simple way to obtain image resolution metrics.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image for which the dimension is to be calculated, affecting the output by determining the longest or shortest side based on the image's width and height.

inputs.name: side
inputs.description: Specifies whether to calculate the dimension based on the longest or shortest side of the image, directly influencing the result by selecting the appropriate dimension.

outputs.name: resolution
outputs.description: The calculated dimension (width or height) of the specified side (longest or shortest) of the image.

easy imageSplitGrid.description: The `easy imageSplitGrid` node is designed for splitting a single image into multiple smaller images based on specified grid dimensions. It allows for the division of an image into a grid of smaller, equally sized images, facilitating operations that require processing or analyzing parts of an image separately.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The input image to be split into a grid. This image is divided according to the specified row and column parameters, resulting in multiple smaller images.

inputs.name: row
inputs.description: Specifies the number of rows in the grid. This determines how many horizontal splits will be made on the input image.

inputs.name: column
inputs.description: Specifies the number of columns in the grid. This determines how many vertical splits will be made on the input image.

outputs.name: images
outputs.description: The output is a batch of images that have been split according to the specified grid dimensions. Each image in the batch represents a segment of the original image as defined by the grid.

easy imageSplitList.description: The node 'easy imageSplitList' is designed to split a given image into a list of smaller images, facilitating operations that require individual processing of segments or portions of the original image.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The 'images' parameter accepts an image or a batch of images to be split. It plays a crucial role in determining how the original image(s) will be divided into smaller segments.

outputs.name: images
outputs.description: The output 'images' consists of a list of smaller images that have been split from the original input. This allows for individual processing or analysis of each segment.

easy imagesSplitImage.description: The `easy imagesSplitImage` node is designed to split a single image tensor into multiple segments, distributing the original image's content across several new image tensors. This operation facilitates the manipulation and analysis of image data by breaking it down into more manageable pieces.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The `images` parameter represents the input image tensor that is to be split into multiple segments. This parameter is crucial for determining how the original image is divided and influences the resulting segmented images.

outputs.name: image1
outputs.description: Represents the first segment of the split image.

outputs.name: image2
outputs.description: Represents the second segment of the split image.

outputs.name: image3
outputs.description: Represents the third segment of the split image.

outputs.name: image4
outputs.description: Represents the fourth segment of the split image.

outputs.name: image5
outputs.description: Represents the fifth segment of the split image.

easy imageSwitch.description: The `easy imageSwitch` node provides a mechanism to switch between two images based on a boolean condition. It enables conditional image selection within a workflow, allowing for dynamic content generation based on specified criteria.

inputs.name: image_a
inputs.description: The first image option to choose from. It serves as the default or 'false' condition output.

inputs.name: image_b
inputs.description: The second image option to choose from. It is selected when the boolean condition is true.

inputs.name: boolean
inputs.description: A boolean value determining which image to output. If true, `image_b` is selected; otherwise, `image_a` is chosen.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is either `image_a` or `image_b`, depending on the boolean condition.

easy imageToBase64.description: The `easy imageToBase64` node is designed to convert images from a tensor format to a Base64-encoded string. This functionality is essential for web applications and APIs where images need to be transmitted over the internet in a text-based format.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The `image` parameter is the input tensor representing the image to be converted. It plays a crucial role in the conversion process, as it is the source image that will be transformed into a Base64-encoded string.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The output is a Base64-encoded string representation of the input image. This format is widely used for embedding images in HTML or CSS files, or for transmitting images over networks where binary data is not supported.

easy imageToMask.description: This node is designed to convert images into masks based on specific criteria or attributes. It encapsulates the functionality to process an image and extract a mask representation, which can be used for various applications such as image editing, compositing, or further image analysis.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image from which the mask will be generated. The image is processed to identify and isolate specific features or colors that define the mask.

inputs.name: channel
inputs.description: Specifies the color channel ('red', 'green', 'blue', 'alpha') used to generate the mask. This parameter determines which part of the image is used to create the mask, based on the selected color channel.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The output mask generated from the input image. This mask isolates specific features or colors from the original image, providing a binary or grayscale representation for further processing.

easy imageUncropFromBBOX.description: The `imageUncropFromBBOX` node is designed to reverse the cropping process of an image by using bounding box information. It restores the cropped image back to its original dimensions, optionally blending borders and adjusting for square masks, making it useful for tasks that require the original context of the image for further processing or visualization.

inputs.name: original_image
inputs.description: The original image before any cropping was applied. It serves as the reference for uncropping the cropped image back to its original dimensions.

inputs.name: crop_image
inputs.description: The cropped version of the original image that needs to be uncropped. This image will be adjusted based on the bounding box and other parameters to match the original image's dimensions.

inputs.name: bbox
inputs.description: The bounding box information used to crop the original image. This data is essential for accurately uncropping the image.

inputs.name: border_blending
inputs.description: A float value that determines the intensity of border blending when uncropping the image. It helps in smoothing the transition between the cropped and uncropped areas.

inputs.name: use_square_mask
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether a square mask should be applied during the uncropping process. This affects the shape of the uncropped area.

inputs.name: optional_mask
inputs.description: An optional mask that can be applied to the uncropped image for additional processing or visualization purposes.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The uncropped image, restored to its original dimensions with optional border blending and mask adjustments.

easy injectNoiseToLatent.description: The `injectNoiseToLatent` node is designed to modify latent representations by injecting noise, allowing for the generation of varied outputs from a given input. It supports operations such as averaging or scaling the noise before injection, normalization of the resulting noisy latent, and conditional application of noise based on a mask, facilitating nuanced control over the noise injection process.

inputs.name: strength
inputs.description: Specifies the strength of the noise to be injected into the latent space, affecting the intensity of the modification.

inputs.name: normalize
inputs.description: Determines whether the noised latent should be normalized, impacting the distribution of the resulting latent values.

inputs.name: average
inputs.description: Controls whether the original and noised latents are averaged, blending the input and noise for a potentially smoother result.

inputs.name: pipe_to_noise
inputs.description: An optional pipeline input that can provide noise settings and samples, offering an alternative source of noise.

inputs.name: image_to_latent
inputs.description: An optional image input that, if provided, will be converted to a latent representation for noise injection.

inputs.name: latent
inputs.description: The primary latent input to which noise will be added. If not provided, an attempt will be made to use an alternative source.

inputs.name: noise
inputs.description: The noise to be injected into the latent. This can be provided directly or sourced from the `pipe_to_noise` input.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: An optional mask that can be applied to selectively inject noise into parts of the latent space, allowing for localized modifications.

inputs.name: mix_randn_amount
inputs.description: Specifies the amount of random noise to mix into the noised latent, introducing additional randomness.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The modified latent representation after noise injection, which may exhibit variations depending on the applied noise and settings.

easy instantIDApply.description: This node facilitates the application of InstantID technology, integrating it with other models and processes within a pipeline to enhance identity verification and analysis capabilities. It leverages InstantID and InsightFace models, along with control network configurations, to process images for identity-related tasks.

inputs.name: pipe
inputs.description: Represents the pipeline configuration and state, serving as the foundation for applying InstantID technology.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image to be processed, acting as the primary input for identity verification and analysis.

inputs.name: instantid_file
inputs.description: Specifies the file path for the InstantID model, essential for loading and applying the model.

inputs.name: insightface
inputs.description: Indicates the InsightFace model to be used, enhancing the identity verification process with facial recognition capabilities.

inputs.name: control_net_name
inputs.description: Specifies the control network name to be used in the process, affecting the application of InstantID.

inputs.name: cn_strength
inputs.description: Determines the strength of the control network's influence on the process.

inputs.name: cn_soft_weights
inputs.description: Adjusts the soft weights for the control network, influencing its impact.

inputs.name: weight
inputs.description: Sets the overall weight of the InstantID application in the pipeline.

inputs.name: start_at
inputs.description: Defines the starting point of the InstantID application within the pipeline.

inputs.name: end_at
inputs.description: Specifies the endpoint of the InstantID application within the pipeline.

inputs.name: noise
inputs.description: Controls the level of noise to be considered in the InstantID process.

inputs.name: image_kps
inputs.description: Optional keypoints in the image, used for more precise identity verification.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: Optional mask to be applied on the image, used for focusing or excluding specific areas.

inputs.name: control_net
inputs.description: Optional control network settings, providing additional control over the InstantID application.

outputs.name: pipe
outputs.description: The updated pipeline configuration after applying InstantID, reflecting changes in the processing state.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The modified model incorporating InstantID features, ready for further processing or analysis.

outputs.name: positive
outputs.description: A positive outcome or feature extracted during the InstantID application, potentially used for further analysis.

outputs.name: negative
outputs.description: A negative outcome or feature extracted during the InstantID application, potentially used for identifying discrepancies or errors.

easy instantIDApplyADV.description: The `easy instantIDApplyADV` node is designed for advanced application of InstantID technology, integrating various models and parameters to enhance image processing capabilities. It focuses on applying sophisticated identity verification and analysis techniques to images, leveraging InstantID and InsightFace models along with control network adjustments for optimized results.

inputs.name: pipe
inputs.description: Represents the pipeline configuration, serving as the foundational structure for the node's processing sequence.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image to be processed, acting as the primary input for identity verification and analysis.

inputs.name: instantid_file
inputs.description: Specifies the file path for the InstantID model, enabling the node to load and apply the corresponding identity verification model.

inputs.name: insightface
inputs.description: Designates the InsightFace model to be used for facial analysis and recognition within the image processing workflow.

inputs.name: control_net_name
inputs.description: Identifies the control network to be applied, influencing how the InstantID and InsightFace models are integrated and utilized.

inputs.name: cn_strength
inputs.description: Controls the strength of the control network's influence, adjusting the intensity of model application.

inputs.name: cn_soft_weights
inputs.description: Determines the soft weighting for the control network, fine-tuning the balance between different model influences.

inputs.name: weight
inputs.description: Sets the overall weight of the InstantID application, impacting the prominence of identity verification features in the processed image.

inputs.name: start_at
inputs.description: Defines the starting point for model application within the processing sequence, allowing for phased integration of identity verification.

inputs.name: end_at
inputs.description: Specifies the endpoint for model application, concluding the identity verification and analysis phase.

inputs.name: noise
inputs.description: Adjusts the level of noise introduced during the processing, affecting the clarity and authenticity of the identity verification.

inputs.name: image_kps
inputs.description: Optional parameter for including key points of the image, enhancing the precision of facial analysis.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: Optional parameter for applying a mask to the image, focusing the identity verification on specific areas.

inputs.name: control_net
inputs.description: Optional parameter for directly specifying the control network configuration, offering advanced customization.

inputs.name: positive
inputs.description: Optional conditioning parameter to emphasize certain features or attributes in the identity verification process.

inputs.name: negative
inputs.description: Optional conditioning parameter to de-emphasize or exclude certain features from the identity verification process.

outputs.name: pipe
outputs.description: Returns the updated pipeline configuration, reflecting the applied identity verification and analysis.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: Outputs the enhanced model, incorporating the applied InstantID and InsightFace technologies.

outputs.name: positive
outputs.description: Outputs the conditioning parameters emphasizing desired features post-processing.

outputs.name: negative
outputs.description: Outputs the conditioning parameters de-emphasizing undesired features post-processing.

easy int.description: The `easy int` node is designed to simplify the process of generating and manipulating integer values within a user's workflow. It abstracts away the complexities associated with integer operations, offering a straightforward interface for creating, configuring, and utilizing integers in various computational tasks.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: Represents an integer value that can be configured by the user. It serves as the primary input for the node, allowing for the specification of integer-based parameters or values that influence the node's operation.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: Outputs an integer value as a result of the node's processing, reflecting the manipulation or generation of integer values based on the input provided.

easy ipadapterApply.description: This node facilitates the application of IPAdapter models to enhance or modify images within a given pipeline, leveraging predefined presets and optional parameters to tailor the adaptation process to specific needs.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The base model to which the IPAdapter will be applied, serving as the foundation for image enhancement or modification.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image to be processed or modified by the IPAdapter, acting as the primary subject of adaptation.

inputs.name: preset
inputs.description: A predefined configuration set that dictates how the IPAdapter modifies or enhances the image, allowing for standardized or custom adaptation processes.

inputs.name: lora_strength
inputs.description: Determines the intensity of the LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) applied during the adaptation process, enabling fine-tuning of the model's responsiveness to the IPAdapter's modifications.

inputs.name: provider
inputs.description: Specifies the computation provider for the IPAdapter, such as CPU or GPU, influencing the execution environment.

inputs.name: weight
inputs.description: A factor that influences the overall impact of the IPAdapter on the image, allowing for control over the adaptation intensity.

inputs.name: weight_faceidv2
inputs.description: Specifically adjusts the influence of the FaceID v2 feature within the IPAdapter, offering finer control over facial adaptations.

inputs.name: start_at
inputs.description: Defines the starting point of the adaptation effect, enabling phased or gradual application of the IPAdapter's modifications.

inputs.name: end_at
inputs.description: Sets the endpoint for the adaptation effect, allowing for precise control over the extent of modifications applied.

inputs.name: cache_mode
inputs.description: Determines the caching strategy for model components, affecting performance and resource utilization.

inputs.name: use_tiled
inputs.description: Indicates whether the adaptation should be applied in a tiled manner, potentially improving performance for large images.

inputs.name: attn_mask
inputs.description: An optional mask that can be applied to focus the IPAdapter's effect on specific areas of the image.

inputs.name: optional_ipadapter
inputs.description: Allows for the inclusion of an additional, optional IPAdapter to be used in conjunction with the primary one.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The enhanced or modified model after applying the IPAdapter, reflecting the adaptations made.

outputs.name: images
outputs.description: The resulting images after the adaptation process, showcasing the applied modifications or enhancements.

outputs.name: masks
outputs.description: Optional masks generated during the adaptation process, which may be used for further image processing or analysis.

outputs.name: ipadapter
outputs.description: The IPAdapter instance used in the adaptation process, encapsulating the specific modifications or enhancements applied.

easy ipadapterApplyADV.description: This node specializes in applying advanced IPAdapter configurations to models, enhancing their capabilities with custom style, composition, and embedding adjustments. It leverages a sophisticated set of parameters to fine-tune the integration of IPAdapter into the model's processing pipeline, offering a high degree of customization for generating or modifying images.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model to which the IPAdapter will be applied, serving as the foundation for the advanced customization and enhancements.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image to be processed, serving as the input for the IPAdapter's style and composition adjustments.

inputs.name: preset
inputs.description: Defines the preset configuration for the IPAdapter, guiding its application strategy.

inputs.name: lora_strength
inputs.description: Adjusts the strength of the LoRA adjustments within the IPAdapter, affecting the depth of customization.

inputs.name: provider
inputs.description: Specifies the provider for the model or service, influencing the selection of processing resources.

inputs.name: weight
inputs.description: The overall weight influencing the application of the IPAdapter, affecting the output's visual characteristics.

inputs.name: weight_faceidv2
inputs.description: Specific weight for FaceID v2 adjustments, tailoring the facial recognition enhancements.

inputs.name: weight_type
inputs.description: Determines the type of weighting applied, affecting the balance between different adjustment types.

inputs.name: combine_embeds
inputs.description: Determines whether embeddings should be combined, impacting the integration of multiple embeddings into the model.

inputs.name: start_at
inputs.description: Specifies the starting point within the model's layers for applying the IPAdapter, allowing for targeted enhancements.

inputs.name: end_at
inputs.description: Defines the end point within the model's layers for the application of the IPAdapter, enabling precise control over the extent of modifications.

inputs.name: embeds_scaling
inputs.description: Controls the scaling of embeddings, adjusting the impact of embeddings on the model's output.

inputs.name: cache_mode
inputs.description: Controls the caching strategy for the IPAdapter, optimizing performance and resource usage.

inputs.name: use_tiled
inputs.description: Indicates whether to apply the IPAdapter in a tiled manner, affecting the processing of large images.

inputs.name: use_batch
inputs.description: Specifies whether to process images in batches, improving efficiency for multiple inputs.

inputs.name: sharpening
inputs.description: Adjusts the sharpness of the output images, enhancing detail and clarity.

inputs.name: image_negative
inputs.description: unknown

inputs.name: attn_mask
inputs.description: An optional attention mask to focus the IPAdapter's adjustments on specific areas, enhancing the relevance of modifications.

inputs.name: clip_vision

inputs.name: optional_ipadapter
inputs.description: An optional IPAdapter parameter for additional customization and flexibility in the application process.

inputs.name: layer_weights

outputs.name: model

outputs.name: masks

outputs.name: ipadapter
outputs.description: The IPAdapter instance after application, encapsulating the advanced configurations and customizations.

easy ipadapterApplyEmbeds.description: The node 'easy ipadapterApplyEmbeds' is designed to apply embedding transformations to models using IPAdapter, facilitating the integration of positional and negative embeddings into the model's processing pipeline. It abstracts the complexity of embedding manipulation, offering a streamlined approach to enhance model performance with custom embeddings.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: Specifies the model to which embeddings will be applied, serving as the foundational structure for embedding integration.

inputs.name: clip_vision
inputs.description: Indicates whether to apply CLIP vision embeddings, influencing the model's visual understanding and processing.

inputs.name: ipadapter
inputs.description: The IPAdapter instance used for embedding transformations, central to the embedding application process.

inputs.name: pos_embed
inputs.description: The positive embeddings to be applied, enhancing the model's positive feature recognition.

inputs.name: weight
inputs.description: Defines the weight of the embeddings, influencing their impact on the model.

inputs.name: weight_type
inputs.description: Specifies the type of weight applied to the embeddings, affecting their integration into the model.

inputs.name: start_at
inputs.description: Determines the starting point for embedding application, allowing for precise control over when embeddings influence the model.

inputs.name: end_at
inputs.description: Sets the endpoint for embedding application, defining the scope of embedding influence on the model.

inputs.name: embeds_scaling
inputs.description: Defines the scaling method for embeddings, affecting how embeddings are integrated and weighted within the model.

inputs.name: neg_embed
inputs.description: The negative embeddings to be applied, enhancing the model's negative feature recognition.

inputs.name: attn_mask
inputs.description: An optional attention mask for more targeted embedding application, providing additional control over how embeddings affect the model.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The enhanced model with applied embeddings, reflecting the integration of positive and negative embeddings.

outputs.name: ipadapter
outputs.description: The IPAdapter instance after embedding application, indicating the successful integration of embeddings.

easy ipadapterApplyEncoder.description: The `easy ipadapterApplyEncoder` node is designed to encode images into positive and negative embeddings using an IPAdapter model. It processes multiple images, applying weights and masks to each, and combines the resulting embeddings according to a specified method. This node facilitates the integration of image features into models by generating embeddings that can be used to enhance or suppress certain aspects of the image in downstream tasks.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model parameter represents the base model to which the IPAdapter encoding process will be applied. It is crucial for ensuring that the encoding is compatible with the model's architecture and processing capabilities.

inputs.name: clip_vision
inputs.description: The clip_vision parameter is essential for providing vision-related features or models that the IPAdapter might utilize during the encoding process. It enhances the encoding by incorporating visual context.

inputs.name: image1
inputs.description: The first image to be encoded by the IPAdapter, contributing to the generation of positive and negative embeddings.

inputs.name: preset
inputs.description: Specifies the preset configuration for the IPAdapter encoding process, affecting how images are processed and encoded.

inputs.name: num_embeds
inputs.description: The number of embeddings to generate, dictating how many images will be processed by the IPAdapter.

inputs.name: image2
inputs.description: The second image to be encoded, if applicable, based on the num_embeds parameter.

inputs.name: image3
inputs.description: The third image to be encoded, used when num_embeds is greater than two.

inputs.name: image4
inputs.description: The fourth image to be encoded, used when num_embeds is four.

inputs.name: mask1
inputs.description: An optional mask for the first image, used to focus or exclude specific areas during encoding.

inputs.name: weight1
inputs.description: The weight applied to the first image's encoding, influencing the prominence of its features in the generated embeddings.

inputs.name: mask2
inputs.description: An optional mask for the second image, similar in purpose to mask1.

inputs.name: weight2
inputs.description: The weight applied to the second image's encoding.

inputs.name: mask3
inputs.description: An optional mask for the third image, following the same concept as the previous masks.

inputs.name: weight3
inputs.description: The weight applied to the third image's encoding.

inputs.name: mask4
inputs.description: An optional mask for the fourth image, used if num_embeds is four.

inputs.name: weight4

easy ipadapterStyleComposition.description: This node facilitates the application of style and composition adjustments to images using an IPAdapter. easy isSDXL.description: The `easy isSDXL` node is designed to determine if the current model configuration or environment is set to use the SDXL (Stable Diffusion XL) model. This node abstractly assesses the operational context to ensure compatibility or optimize settings for utilizing the SDXL model, facilitating seamless integration or transition between different model scales.

easy joinImageBatch.description: This node is designed to merge a batch of images into a single large image, either by stacking them horizontally or vertically based on the specified mode. It abstracts the complexity of image manipulation and resizing, providing a straightforward way to create composite images from multiple inputs.

easy kSampler.description: The `easy kSampler` node simplifies the sampling process in generative models by providing a streamlined interface for generating images. It abstracts complex sampling configurations and parameters, offering users an easier way to produce high-quality image outputs.

inputs.name: pipe

inputs.name: link_id

inputs.name: save_prefix

easy kSamplerDownscaleUnet.description: This node specializes in simplifying the process of image sampling by integrating Unet downscaling capabilities. It aims to enhance efficiency and performance in image generation tasks by applying a downscaling factor to the Unet model, which is particularly useful for handling high-resolution images or complex sampling scenarios. The node facilitates a streamlined workflow for image sampling with an emphasis on reducing computational load without compromising the quality of the generated images.

inputs.name: block_number

inputs.name: upscale_method

inputs.name: image_output

easy kSamplerInpainting.description: This node specializes in generating images by inpainting missing parts or modifying existing images. It leverages a variety of inpainting models and techniques to fill in gaps or replace sections of an image based on the surrounding context, allowing for creative and customized image manipulation.

easy kSamplerLayerDiffusion.description: This node integrates the concept of layer diffusion with the kSampler process in a simplified manner, aiming to enhance image generation by applying specialized diffusion techniques. easy kSamplerSDTurbo.description: The 'samplerSDTurbo' node is designed to facilitate the use of the SDTurbo sampler within a simplified interface, aiming to streamline the sampling process for users by abstracting the complexities involved in configuring and executing the SDTurbo sampling algorithm.

easy LLLiteLoader.description: The `easy LLLiteLoader` node is designed to simplify the process of loading and integrating LLLite models into a user's workflow. easy loadImageBase64.description: The node `easy loadImageBase64` is designed to load images encoded in Base64 format, converting them into a format suitable for further image processing or manipulation within the ComfyUI framework. easy loraStack.description: The `loraStack` node is designed to facilitate the dynamic integration and management of LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) layers into models.
