inputs.description: An optional input for providing a pre-blended image, used in conjunction with specific diffusion methods.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: An optional mask input, used to define areas of the image that should be treated differently during the diffusion process.

outputs.name: pipe
outputs.description: The modified pipeline configuration after applying the layer diffusion process, ready for further processing or generation steps.

easy preSamplingLayerDiffusionADDTL.description: This node is designed to apply layer diffusion techniques to pre-sample layers in a generative model, enhancing the quality and detail of generated images. It integrates advanced diffusion methods to manipulate layers based on specified methods, weights, and steps, allowing for fine-tuned control over the diffusion process.

inputs.name: pipe
inputs.description: unknown

inputs.name: foreground_prompt
inputs.description: The foreground prompt specifies additional textual input that influences the generative process, particularly focusing on the foreground elements of the image. It plays a crucial role in guiding the diffusion process to achieve desired visual outcomes in the foreground.

inputs.name: background_prompt
inputs.description: The background prompt provides textual input that targets the background elements of the image during the generative process. This parameter is essential for directing the diffusion effects specifically to the background, enabling more controlled and nuanced image generation.

inputs.name: blended_prompt
inputs.description: The blended prompt is used to specify textual input that affects the blending of foreground and background elements in the image. It is key to achieving a harmonious integration of elements through the diffusion process, impacting the overall aesthetic and coherence of the generated image.

inputs.name: optional_fg_cond
inputs.description: This optional parameter allows for the specification of additional conditions or modifiers for the foreground, providing a means to further customize and refine the foreground elements during the diffusion process.

inputs.name: optional_bg_cond
inputs.description: Similar to the optional foreground condition, this parameter enables the specification of additional conditions or modifiers for the background, offering enhanced control over the background's appearance and integration with the foreground.

inputs.name: optional_blended_cond
inputs.description: This parameter allows for the introduction of conditions or modifiers that specifically affect the blending of foreground and background elements. It is instrumental in fine-tuning the visual outcome of the blended areas, ensuring a seamless and aesthetically pleasing integration.

outputs.name: pipe
outputs.description: Returns the modified pipeline configuration after applying the layer diffusion, reflecting changes made to the generative model's layers.

easy preSamplingNoiseIn.description: This node is designed to inject noise into latent representations before the sampling process in a customizable manner. It allows for the adjustment of noise characteristics and the application of noise based on specific conditions or parameters, enhancing the flexibility and control over the noise injection process in generative models.

inputs.name: pipe
inputs.description: Represents the pipeline configuration and state, serving as the context for noise injection and other processing steps.

inputs.name: factor
inputs.description: Adjusts the intensity of the noise injected into the latent representation, allowing for finer control over the noise level.

inputs.name: steps
inputs.description: Determines the number of steps for the sampling process, impacting the intensity and granularity of noise injection.

inputs.name: cfg
inputs.description: Controls the configuration strength, influencing the balance between the original content and the generated aspects in the output.

inputs.name: sampler_name
inputs.description: Specifies the sampler to be used, allowing for different sampling strategies and their corresponding noise characteristics.

inputs.name: scheduler
inputs.description: Defines the scheduling strategy for noise injection, enabling precise control over the timing and sequence of noise application.

inputs.name: denoise
inputs.description: Adjusts the denoising factor, affecting the level of noise reduction applied to the latent representation.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: Sets the seed for random number generation, ensuring consistency and reproducibility in noise injection.

inputs.name: optional_noise_seed
inputs.description: An optional seed for generating noise, providing an additional layer of control over the randomness of the noise injected.

inputs.name: optional_latent
inputs.description: An optional latent representation that can be directly manipulated or injected with noise, offering more flexibility in the noise injection process.

outputs.name: pipe
outputs.description: The modified latent representation with noise injected, ready for further processing or sampling in the pipeline.

easy preSamplingSdTurbo.description: The `easy preSamplingSdTurbo` node is designed to facilitate the pre-sampling process for image generation tasks, leveraging the SDTurbo scheduler for efficient sampling. It integrates various components such as model selection, step configuration, and denoise settings to prepare and optimize the sampling pipeline, aiming to enhance the quality and efficiency of generated images.

inputs.name: pipe
inputs.description: Specifies the pipeline configuration to be used for pre-sampling, including model, sampling steps, and other relevant settings.

inputs.name: steps
inputs.description: Determines the number of steps to be used in the SDTurbo scheduler for the sampling process, affecting the detail and quality of the generated images.

inputs.name: cfg
inputs.description: Configures the conditioning factor for the sampling process, influencing the adherence to the input conditions and the overall image quality.

inputs.name: sampler_name
inputs.description: Selects the specific sampler to be used in conjunction with the SDTurbo scheduler, impacting the sampling strategy and output characteristics.

inputs.name: eta
inputs.description: Adjusts the eta parameter for the sampling process, influencing the randomness and variability of the generated images.

inputs.name: s_noise
inputs.description: Specifies the seed noise level for the sampling process, affecting the initial randomness of the generated images.

inputs.name: upscale_ratio
inputs.description: Determines the upscale ratio for image enhancement during the pre-sampling process, affecting the resolution and clarity of the output.

inputs.name: start_step
inputs.description: Specifies the starting step for the sampling process, allowing for finer control over the generation progression.

inputs.name: end_step
inputs.description: Defines the end step for the sampling process, setting the limit for the generation progression.

inputs.name: upscale_n_step
inputs.description: Sets the number of steps for the upscaling process, affecting the detail and quality of the upscaled images.

inputs.name: unsharp_kernel_size
inputs.description: Configures the kernel size for the unsharp mask applied during image enhancement, affecting the sharpness and clarity.

inputs.name: unsharp_sigma
inputs.description: Sets the sigma value for the unsharp mask, influencing the edge enhancement during the image upscaling process.

inputs.name: unsharp_strength
inputs.description: Adjusts the strength of the unsharp mask, fine-tuning the contrast and detail enhancement during upscaling.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: Sets the random seed for the sampling process, ensuring reproducibility of the generated images.

outputs.name: pipe
outputs.description: Outputs the modified pipeline configuration after the pre-sampling process, including updated model, sampling settings, and generated samples.

easy prompt.description: The `easy prompt` node is designed to facilitate the generation of text prompts by allowing users to input multiple strings and optionally combine them into a structured prompt. This node simplifies the process of creating complex or structured text inputs for further processing or generation tasks.

inputs.name: prompt
inputs.description: Accepts a string input to be used as part of a prompt, providing flexibility in generating text-based inputs.

inputs.name: main
inputs.description: Serves as the primary input for prompt generation, enabling the combination of multiple text elements.

inputs.name: lighting
inputs.description: Takes a string input to incorporate lighting conditions into the prompt, further expanding the possibilities for prompt customization.

outputs.name: prompt
outputs.description: Outputs a structured prompt, aggregating the input strings into a cohesive format.

easy promptConcat.description: The `promptConcat` node is designed to concatenate two text prompts with an optional separator, allowing for the dynamic creation of combined text strings. This functionality is particularly useful in scenarios where text from different sources needs to be merged into a single string, maintaining flexibility in how the texts are joined.

inputs.name: prompt1
inputs.description: The first text prompt to be concatenated. It serves as the initial part of the new combined text string.

inputs.name: prompt2
inputs.description: The second text prompt to be concatenated. It follows the first prompt in the new combined text string.

inputs.name: separator
inputs.description: An optional string used to separate the two prompts in the combined text string. If not specified, the prompts are concatenated directly without any separator.

outputs.name: prompt
outputs.description: The resulting text string after concatenating `prompt1` and `prompt2` with the optional `separator`. This output is useful for further text processing or output display.

easy promptLine.description: The `easy promptLine` node is designed to facilitate the manipulation and conditioning of textual prompts for generative models. It enables the dynamic integration and adjustment of negative conditioning phrases, ensuring that the generated content aligns with specified constraints and preferences. This node plays a crucial role in refining the input prompts to achieve desired outcomes in generative tasks, such as text generation or image synthesis, by allowing for precise control over the conditioning process.

inputs.name: prompt
inputs.description: Represents the primary textual content that the user inputs for processing. It serves as the base for any manipulations, additions, or exclusions applied by the node.

inputs.name: start_index
inputs.description: Specifies the starting index from which the node begins to process the input prompt, allowing for segmented or partial processing of the text.

inputs.name: max_rows
inputs.description: Defines the maximum number of rows or lines to be processed or generated from the input prompt, setting a limit on the output's extent.

outputs.name: STRING
outputs.description: The processed text output, which may include modifications, additions, or exclusions based on the node's functionality.

outputs.name: COMBO
outputs.description: A combination of processed text outputs, potentially including multiple variations or manipulations of the input prompt.

easy promptList.description: This node is designed to facilitate the generation of string lists from multiline prompts, with enhanced capabilities for processing prompts containing Chinese characters by converting them to English. It uniquely caters to workflows requiring specific starting points and row limitations in the output list, while also accommodating unique identifiers.

inputs.name: prompt_i
inputs.description: Represents a main text input from which the list of strings will be generated. Supports multiline input and is capable of handling multiple prompts sequentially numbered (e.g., prompt_1, prompt_2, etc.).

inputs.name: optional_prompt_list
inputs.description: An optional list parameter that allows for additional prompts to be included in the generation process.

outputs.name: prompt_list
outputs.description: The generated list of strings derived from the input prompts.

outputs.name: prompt_strings
outputs.description: A concatenated string of all input prompts, separated by a specified delimiter.

easy promptReplace.description: The `promptReplace` node is designed to dynamically modify text prompts based on a set of replacement rules. It allows for the customization of text by replacing specified phrases or words with alternatives, supporting a straightforward approach to text manipulation. This functionality is particularly useful for generating or altering text prompts in a flexible manner, accommodating a wide range of text manipulation needs.

inputs.name: prompt
inputs.description: The initial text prompt that will be modified based on the find and replace parameters provided.

inputs.name: find1
inputs.description: The first phrase or word to search for in the prompt for replacement.

inputs.name: replace1
inputs.description: The replacement text for the first search term found by `find1`.

inputs.name: find2
inputs.description: The second phrase or word to search for in the prompt for replacement.

inputs.name: replace2
inputs.description: The replacement text for the second search term found by `find2`.

inputs.name: find3
inputs.description: The third phrase or word to search for in the prompt for replacement.

inputs.name: replace3
inputs.description: The replacement text for the third search term found by `find3`.

outputs.name: prompt
outputs.description: The output is a modified version of the input text, with specified phrases or words replaced according to the defined rules.

easy pulIDApply.description: This node facilitates the application of the PulID model to images, enhancing them based on predefined or custom parameters. It integrates with other models like InsightFace for face analysis and Eva Clip for additional processing, aiming to improve image quality or modify images according to specific criteria.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The base model to which the PulID enhancements will be applied. It serves as the foundation for the image transformation process.

inputs.name: pulid_file
inputs.description: Specifies the file path to the PulID model to be used for the image enhancement. This parameter allows for the dynamic selection of different PulID models.

inputs.name: insightface
inputs.description: Defines the InsightFace model configuration to be used for face analysis within the image. This can be CPU, CUDA, or ROCM based, affecting the performance and accuracy of face detection.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image to be processed and enhanced by the PulID model. It is the primary input over which the transformations are applied.

inputs.name: method
inputs.description: unknown

inputs.name: weight
inputs.description: A floating-point value that adjusts the intensity of the PulID model's effect on the image. It allows for fine-tuning the strength of the enhancements.

inputs.name: start_at
inputs.description: Defines the starting point of the effect application in terms of image processing, allowing for partial enhancements.

inputs.name: end_at
inputs.description: Specifies the endpoint for the PulID model's effect application, enabling selective enhancement within the image.

inputs.name: attn_mask
inputs.description: An optional mask that can be applied to focus the PulID model's enhancements on specific areas of the image, providing more control over the output.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The enhanced model after applying the PulID transformations. It represents the output of the image enhancement process.

easy pulIDApplyADV.description: The `easy pulIDApplyADV` node is designed to enhance images by applying advanced PulID transformations. It leverages PulID models, InsightFace for facial analysis, and optionally EVA Clip for additional enhancements. This node is capable of adjusting images based on various parameters such as weight, projection, fidelity, and noise, offering a flexible approach to image manipulation.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model input is the base model onto which the PulID transformations will be applied. It is central to the node's operation, serving as the foundation for the enhancements.

inputs.name: pulid_file
inputs.description: Specifies the PulID file to be used for the transformation. It is crucial for defining the specific PulID model that will be applied to the input model.

inputs.name: insightface
inputs.description: Determines the InsightFace model to be used for facial analysis, supporting different computation backends. It plays a key role in facial feature detection and analysis within the image.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be enhanced. It is directly affected by the PulID transformations, with changes being applied based on the specified parameters.

inputs.name: weight
inputs.description: Controls the intensity of the PulID transformation applied to the image. It allows for fine-tuning the impact of the transformation on the final output.

inputs.name: projection
inputs.description: Defines the projection method used in the transformation process. It influences how the PulID model interprets and applies enhancements to the image.

inputs.name: fidelity
inputs.description: Adjusts the fidelity of the transformation, affecting the accuracy and detail preservation in the enhanced image.

inputs.name: noise
inputs.description: Specifies the level of noise to be added to the transformation. It can be used to introduce variability or texture into the enhanced image.

inputs.name: start_at
inputs.description: Determines the starting point of the transformation within the image. It allows for targeted application of the PulID enhancements.

inputs.name: end_at
inputs.description: Specifies the ending point of the transformation within the image, enabling precise control over the area affected by the PulID enhancements.

inputs.name: attn_mask
inputs.description: An optional attention mask that can be applied to focus the PulID transformation on specific areas of the image.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The enhanced model output, which has undergone the PulID transformation. It reflects the applied enhancements and adjustments.

easy rangeFloat.description: The `easy rangeFloat` node is designed to facilitate the manipulation and generation of floating-point numbers within a specified range. It abstracts the complexity of handling floating-point operations, providing a straightforward interface for generating, adjusting, and working with float values in a range defined by the user.

inputs.name: range_mode
inputs.description: Determines the mode of range calculation, either by specifying a step size or a total number of steps.

inputs.name: start
inputs.description: Specifies the starting value of the floating-point range.

inputs.name: stop
inputs.description: Defines the ending value of the floating-point range.

inputs.name: step
inputs.description: Sets the step size for the range when 'range_mode' is set to 'step'.

inputs.name: num_steps
inputs.description: Specifies the total number of steps in the range when 'range_mode' is set to 'num_steps'.

inputs.name: end_mode
inputs.description: Indicates whether the range should include ('Inclusive') or exclude ('Exclusive') the stop value.

outputs.name: range
outputs.description: The generated range of floating-point numbers based on the input parameters.

outputs.name: range_sizes
outputs.description: The size of the generated range, indicating how many floating-point numbers are included.

easy rangeInt.description: The 'build_range' node offers a versatile mechanism for generating a sequence of numbers, which can be either integers or floats, based on a comprehensive set of parameters including start, stop, step, and the number of steps. It supports different modes of operation and end conditions, making it highly adaptable for creating custom numerical ranges for a variety of applications.

inputs.name: range_mode
inputs.description: Determines the mode of range generation, either by specifying a step size or a fixed number of steps, which influences how the sequence is constructed.

inputs.name: start
inputs.description: Specifies the starting value of the range, setting the initial point for the sequence generation.

inputs.name: stop
inputs.description: Defines the ending value of the range, determining where the sequence will stop.

inputs.name: step
inputs.description: Indicates the increment between consecutive values in the range when 'range_mode' is set to 'step', allowing for control over the spacing of the sequence.

inputs.name: num_steps
inputs.description: Specifies the total number of steps in the range when 'range_mode' is set to 'num_steps', controlling the length of the sequence.

inputs.name: end_mode
inputs.description: Determines whether the ending value ('stop') is included in or excluded from the generated range, affecting the final sequence.

outputs.name: range
outputs.description: The generated sequence of numbers based on the input parameters, which can be tailored to include either a specific number of steps or a specific step size.

outputs.name: range_sizes
outputs.description: The size of the generated range, providing information on the total number of elements within the sequence.

easy removeLocalImage.description: The `easy removeLocalImage` node is designed to search for and delete a specified local image file. It operates by traversing directories to find a file that matches the given name, removing it if found, and providing feedback on the operation's success or failure.

inputs.name: any
inputs.description: This parameter is used internally for ensuring the node's compatibility with the system's requirements, without affecting the node's core functionality of searching and deleting files.

inputs.name: file_name
inputs.description: Specifies the name of the file to be searched and deleted. This parameter is crucial for identifying the target file within the local storage.

easy samLoaderPipe.description: The 'easy samLoaderPipe' node is designed to load and configure the SAM (Semantic Attention Model) for use in image processing pipelines. It facilitates the integration of SAM into custom workflows, enabling advanced image manipulation techniques such as semantic segmentation and attention-based image editing.

inputs.name: model_name
inputs.description: Specifies the name of the SAM model to be loaded. This parameter is crucial for determining which specific SAM model will be utilized in the processing pipeline.

inputs.name: device_mode
inputs.description: Determines the hardware (CPU/GPU) preference for running the SAM model, allowing for optimized performance based on the available resources.

inputs.name: sam_detection_hint
inputs.description: Guides the SAM model in focusing on specific areas or patterns within the image, enhancing the effectiveness of semantic segmentation.

inputs.name: sam_dilation
inputs.description: Adjusts the dilation of the detected semantic areas, enabling finer control over the segmentation boundaries.

inputs.name: sam_threshold
inputs.description: Sets the confidence threshold for semantic detection, filtering out less certain areas to improve segmentation accuracy.

inputs.name: sam_bbox_expansion
inputs.description: Controls the expansion of bounding boxes around detected areas, useful for ensuring complete coverage of relevant segments.

inputs.name: sam_mask_hint_threshold
inputs.description: Determines the threshold for mask hints, influencing how strongly the model should consider these hints in segmentation.

inputs.name: sam_mask_hint_use_negative
inputs.description: Configures the model's handling of negative mask hints, affecting the exclusion of certain areas from the segmentation.

outputs.name: sam_pipe
outputs.description: Outputs a configured SAM pipeline, ready for integration into further image processing stages.

easy seed.description: The `easy seed` node is designed to manage and control the seed value used in generation processes, allowing for the replication of results or the introduction of variability. It supports operations such as setting a fixed seed, incrementing, decrementing, or randomizing the seed for each node or globally across the workflow.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: The initial seed value, which serves as the basis for generation processes. It determines the starting point for any pseudo-random operations, affecting the reproducibility and variation of outputs.

outputs.name: seed
outputs.description: The seed value after being processed according to the specified action. This allows for controlled variation or consistency in generation processes.

easy showAnything.description: This node is designed to display any given input in a user-friendly manner, regardless of its original data type. It abstracts the complexity of data types, making it easier for users to visualize and understand the data presented within the ComfyUI environment.

inputs.name: anything
inputs.description: Accepts any data type as input, allowing for a wide range of data to be displayed. This flexibility ensures that users can visualize virtually any piece of data without concern for compatibility issues.

easy showLoaderSettingsNames.description: This node is designed to display the names of various loader settings, providing a straightforward way for users to understand and interact with the configuration options available for data loading processes.

inputs.name: pipe
inputs.description: Represents the pipeline configuration, crucial for determining the loader settings to be displayed.

inputs.name: names
inputs.description: Optional parameter allowing the specification of additional information or constraints on the names to be displayed.

outputs.name: ckpt_name
outputs.description: The name of the checkpoint file as determined by the loader settings.

outputs.name: vae_name
outputs.description: The name of the VAE model file as determined by the loader settings.

outputs.name: lora_name
outputs.description: The name of the LoRA model file as determined by the loader settings.

easy showSpentTime.description: The `showSpentTime` node is designed to display the time spent on a particular operation within a pipeline. It captures and reports the duration of specific tasks, aiding in performance analysis and optimization.

inputs.name: pipe
inputs.description: The `pipe` parameter represents the pipeline context, providing essential information about the current state and settings of the pipeline, including time-related data.

inputs.name: spent_time
inputs.description: The `spent_time` parameter optionally specifies the time spent on the operation. If not provided, the node will attempt to calculate or retrieve this information from the pipeline context.

easy showTensorShape.description: The `showTensorShape` node is designed to analyze and display the shape of tensor data structures within a given input. It abstracts the complexity of tensor operations, providing a straightforward way to visualize the dimensions and structure of tensors, which is crucial for debugging and understanding data flow in tensor-based computations.

inputs.name: tensor
inputs.description: The `tensor` parameter is the primary input for the `showTensorShape` node, representing the tensor whose shape is to be analyzed and displayed. This parameter is essential for the node's operation as it directly influences the output by determining the structure and dimensions of the tensor to be visualized.

easy sliderControl.description: The 'easy sliderControl' node provides a user-friendly interface for dynamically adjusting parameters within the ComfyUI environment. It simplifies the process of fine-tuning values through sliders, enhancing the user's ability to experiment with and control the behavior of various features or models in real-time.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Specifies the operational mode of the node, affecting how parameters are adjusted and applied within the ComfyUI environment.

inputs.name: model_type
inputs.description: Determines the type of model to which the adjustments will be applied, influencing the node's execution and the outcome of parameter modifications.

outputs.name: layer_weights
outputs.description: Outputs the adjusted layer weights as determined by the slider controls, reflecting the changes made to the model's parameters.

easy stableDiffusion3API.description: This node facilitates the generation of images using the Stable Diffusion model, allowing users to specify positive and negative prompts, select a model variant, define the aspect ratio, and adjust parameters such as seed and denoise level for customized image creation.

inputs.name: positive
inputs.description: The positive prompt guides the image generation towards desired themes or elements, influencing the model's output by specifying what to include.

inputs.name: negative
inputs.description: The negative prompt steers the image generation away from certain themes or elements, helping to avoid undesired aspects in the model's output.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: Specifies the variant of the Stable Diffusion model to be used, allowing for selection between standard and turbo modes.

inputs.name: aspect_ratio
inputs.description: Determines the aspect ratio of the generated image, offering a range of predefined ratios to fit various needs.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: Sets the seed for the random number generator, enabling reproducible results across image generations.

inputs.name: denoise
inputs.description: Adjusts the level of denoising applied to the generated image, with a range from 0 (no denoise) to 1 (full denoise), affecting the clarity and detail.

inputs.name: optional_image
inputs.description: An optional image input for tasks such as image-to-image translation or image enhancement, expanding the node's functionality.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: Outputs the generated image as a result of the image generation process, encapsulating the visual representation of the input prompts and parameters.

easy string.description: The 'easy string' node is designed to simplify the process of generating and manipulating strings within a computational context. It abstracts complex string operations, offering a user-friendly interface for tasks such as formatting, concatenation, and potentially parsing. This node aims to reduce the technical overhead associated with string manipulation, making it accessible to users with varying levels of programming expertise.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: The 'value' input is crucial for the node's operation as it represents the primary text or data that the node processes or manipulates. Its role is central to the functionality of the node, determining the nature of the string manipulation tasks performed, such as formatting or concatenation.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The 'string' output is the result of the node's processing or manipulation of the input text. It holds significant importance as it represents the final, processed form of the input data, ready for further use or display in the intended context.

easy styleAlignedBatchAlign.description: The `easy styleAlignedBatchAlign` node is designed to apply style alignment to a batch of models, adjusting their normalization and attention mechanisms based on shared parameters. This process enhances the consistency and harmony of styles across different models, facilitating more cohesive and aesthetically pleasing outputs.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model parameter represents the neural network model to which style alignment will be applied. It is crucial for defining the base structure that will undergo normalization and attention adjustments.

inputs.name: share_norm
inputs.description: This parameter specifies how normalization layers within the model should be shared or aligned, impacting the overall style consistency and coherence of the model's output.

inputs.name: share_attn
inputs.description: Determines the sharing strategy for attention mechanisms within the model, influencing how style elements are integrated and harmonized across different parts of the model.

inputs.name: scale
inputs.description: Affects the intensity of style application, allowing for fine-tuning of the style's impact on the model's output.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The output is a modified version of the input model, now with adjusted normalization and attention mechanisms for enhanced style alignment.

easy stylesSelector.description: The `easy stylesSelector` node is designed to facilitate the selection of styles for prompts in a user-friendly manner. It abstracts the complexity of choosing and applying styles by providing a simplified interface for users to select from predefined style options, enhancing the customization and creativity of prompt generation.

inputs.name: styles
inputs.description: This parameter allows users to select from a list of predefined styles, determining the visual and thematic presentation of the prompt.

inputs.name: positive
inputs.description: The positive prompt input where users can specify custom text to influence the style selection process positively.

inputs.name: negative
inputs.description: The negative prompt input where users can specify custom text to influence the style selection process negatively.

outputs.name: positive
outputs.description: The positive styled prompt, reflecting the user's style selection and customizations.

outputs.name: negative
outputs.description: The negative styled prompt, reflecting the user's style selection and customizations.

easy sv3dLoader.description: The `sv3DLoader` node is designed for loading and managing 3D model files specifically formatted for Stable Diffusion, facilitating the integration of 3D assets into generative AI workflows. It emphasizes ease of use and compatibility with a specific subset of 3D model files, aiming to streamline the process of incorporating 3D models into creative projects.

inputs.name: ckpt_name
inputs.description: Specifies the checkpoint name for loading the model, serving as a key identifier for selecting the appropriate 3D model files.

inputs.name: vae_name
inputs.description: Defines the VAE model name to be used in conjunction with the 3D models, ensuring compatibility and optimal performance within the generative workflow.

inputs.name: init_image
inputs.description: An initial image to start the generation process, providing a visual context or basis for further 3D model integration.

inputs.name: empty_latent_width
inputs.description: Sets the width for the latent space representation, defining the dimensions for the generated or manipulated 3D model output.

inputs.name: empty_latent_height
inputs.description: Sets the height for the latent space representation, similar to 'empty_latent_width', it defines the vertical dimension for the 3D model output.

inputs.name: batch_size
inputs.description: Determines the number of instances to process in a single batch, affecting the efficiency and speed of the 3D model loading operation.

inputs.name: interp_easing
inputs.description: Specifies the interpolation easing type to apply during the 3D model loading process, affecting the transition smoothness between models.

inputs.name: easing_mode
inputs.description: Defines the mode of easing to be applied, such as azimuth or elevation, providing control over the specific aspect of 3D model manipulation.

inputs.name: scheduler
inputs.description: An optional scheduler for managing the loading and processing tasks, offering advanced control over the execution flow.

outputs.name: pipe
outputs.description: The pipeline configuration resulting from the loaded 3D models, ready for further processing or generation tasks.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The specific 3D model loaded and prepared for integration into the generative workflow, encapsulated within the pipeline.

outputs.name: interp_log
outputs.description: A log of the interpolation and easing operations applied during the model loading process, providing insights into the manipulation effects.

easy svdLoader.description: The `easy svdLoader` node is designed to facilitate the loading of SVD (Singular Value Decomposition) models into the system. It streamlines the process of identifying and retrieving SVD model files from a specified directory, ensuring that only relevant files are selected for further processing. This node plays a crucial role in simplifying the integration and utilization of SVD models within the broader computational framework, making it easier for users to leverage SVD-based functionalities.

inputs.name: ckpt_name
inputs.description: The `ckpt_name` parameter specifies the checkpoint name for the SVD model to be loaded. It is crucial for identifying the specific model file to be used in the loading process, thereby enabling the precise application of SVD models within the system.

inputs.name: vae_name
inputs.description: The `vae_name` parameter identifies the VAE model to be used alongside the SVD model, facilitating a combined application of these models for enhanced processing capabilities.

inputs.name: clip_name
inputs.description: The `clip_name` parameter specifies the CLIP model to be used in conjunction with the SVD model, enabling advanced feature extraction and analysis.

inputs.name: init_image
inputs.description: The `init_image` parameter is used to provide an initial image for processing, serving as a starting point for model applications.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: The `resolution` parameter specifies the desired resolution for the output, impacting the quality and size of the generated content.

inputs.name: empty_latent_width
inputs.description: Specifies the width of the empty latent space to be used, affecting the dimensions of the generated content.

inputs.name: empty_latent_height
inputs.description: Specifies the height of the empty latent space, influencing the vertical dimension of the generated content.

inputs.name: video_frames
inputs.description: Determines the number of frames for video generation, directly affecting the video's length.

inputs.name: motion_bucket_id
inputs.description: Identifies the motion bucket to be used, influencing the motion characteristics of the generated video.

inputs.name: fps
inputs.description: Sets the frames per second for the video, impacting the playback speed and smoothness.

inputs.name: augmentation_level
inputs.description: Controls the level of augmentation applied, affecting the variety and intensity of visual modifications.

inputs.name: optional_positive
inputs.description: Optional positive conditioning text to guide the generation towards specific attributes.

inputs.name: optional_negative
inputs.description: Optional negative conditioning text to steer the generation away from certain attributes.

outputs.name: pipe
outputs.description: The `pipe` output represents the pipeline configuration resulting from the loaded models, integrating SVD, VAE, and possibly other models.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The `model` output refers to the specific SVD model that has been loaded and is ready for use within the pipeline.

outputs.name: vae
outputs.description: The `vae` output indicates the VAE model that has been loaded and integrated into the system for combined use with the SVD model.

easy textSwitch.description: The easy textSwitch node provides a mechanism to switch between two text inputs based on a boolean condition. It serves as a conditional operator, enabling dynamic text output selection within a flow.

inputs.name: input
inputs.description: A boolean value determining which of the two text inputs to output. If true, text1 is selected; otherwise, text2 is chosen.

inputs.name: text1
inputs.description: The first text option to choose from. This input is part of the conditional operation, selected when the boolean condition is true.

inputs.name: text2
inputs.description: The second text option to choose from. This input is part of the conditional operation, selected when the boolean condition is false.

outputs.name: STRING
outputs.description: The output text, selected based on the boolean condition. It dynamically switches between text1 and text2.

easy ultralyticsDetectorPipe.description: This node is designed to integrate Ultralytics object detection models into a pipeline, facilitating the detection of bounding boxes and segmentation masks for objects within images. It leverages Ultralytics' YOLO models to analyze image content and identify objects, providing detailed spatial information that can be used for further image processing or analysis.

inputs.name: model_name
inputs.description: Specifies the model to be used for detection, allowing for dynamic selection based on available Ultralytics YOLO models. This flexibility supports various detection needs by accommodating different model strengths and capabilities.

inputs.name: bbox_threshold
inputs.description: Determines the confidence threshold for bounding box detections, filtering out detections with confidence scores below this value to ensure result relevance and accuracy.

inputs.name: bbox_dilation
inputs.description: Adjusts the size of the detected bounding boxes by dilating or contracting them, enabling fine-tuning of object boundaries for subsequent processing steps.

inputs.name: bbox_crop_factor
inputs.description: Controls the extent to which the bounding box is enlarged or shrunk, providing a mechanism to include more or less context around detected objects.

outputs.name: bbox_segm_pipe
outputs.description: Outputs a pipeline configuration tailored for object detection, including model parameters and detection settings, ready for integration into broader image processing workflows.

easy unSampler.description: The `easy unSampler` node is designed for the reverse sampling process in generative models, allowing for the exploration of latent spaces and the refinement of generated images by stepping back through the model's layers. It provides a flexible interface for adjusting the sampling parameters and integrating with different sampler and scheduler types.

inputs.name: steps
inputs.description: Specifies the number of steps to take in the reverse sampling process, affecting the granularity of the exploration or refinement.

inputs.name: end_at_step
inputs.description: Determines the final step of the reverse sampling process, enabling partial reversals and targeted refinement.

inputs.name: cfg
inputs.description: Controls the conditioning factor, influencing the strength of conditioning on the input prompt or image features during reverse sampling.

inputs.name: sampler_name
inputs.description: Selects the specific sampler to use for the reverse sampling process, allowing for customization of the sampling strategy.

inputs.name: scheduler
inputs.description: Chooses the scheduler for controlling the sampling steps, impacting the progression and dynamics of the reverse sampling.

inputs.name: normalize
inputs.description: Enables or disables normalization, affecting the handling of input data and the stability of the reverse sampling process.

inputs.name: pipe
inputs.description: The pipeline configuration for the reverse sampling process, including model and conditioning settings.

inputs.name: optional_model
inputs.description: Optionally specifies a model to use for the reverse sampling, overriding the default.

inputs.name: optional_positive
inputs.description: Optionally adds positive conditioning to the reverse sampling process.

inputs.name: optional_negative
inputs.description: Optionally adds negative conditioning to the reverse sampling process.

inputs.name: optional_latent
inputs.description: Optionally specifies a latent representation to use as a starting point for the reverse sampling.

outputs.name: pipe
outputs.description: Returns the modified pipeline after the reverse sampling process, including any changes to the latent space or generated images.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: Outputs the latent representation obtained or modified during the reverse sampling process, providing insight into the model's internal state.

easy wildcards.description: The 'easy wildcards' node is designed to manage and process wildcards within strings, offering functionalities to define, normalize, read, and replace wildcards. It supports dynamic content generation by allowing the insertion of predefined or random elements into strings based on wildcard patterns. This node facilitates the customization and variability of text outputs, making it a versatile tool for generating dynamic content in applications.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: A string input that supports Lora Block Weight and wildcard functionality, allowing for dynamic content generation through the use of placeholders and predefined text patterns.

inputs.name: Select to add LoRA
inputs.description: Allows the selection of a LoRA to be added to the text, enhancing the input with additional, customizable layers of text transformation.

inputs.name: Select to add Wildcard
inputs.description: Enables the selection of a wildcard to be incorporated into the text, facilitating dynamic substitutions and content variability.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: An integer value used to seed random number generators for consistent wildcard replacements across different executions.

inputs.name: multiline_mode
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether the input text should be processed in multiline mode, affecting how wildcards and LoRAs are applied.

outputs.name: text
outputs.description: The original input text with wildcards and LoRAs processed and applied, reflecting the dynamic content generation.

outputs.name: populated_text
outputs.description: The text after processing, showing the result of wildcard and LoRA substitutions, providing a version of the text enriched with dynamic elements.

easy xyAny.description: The `easy xyAny` node is designed to facilitate the exploration and manipulation of data points or conditions across two dimensions, X and Y, within a customizable pipeline. It abstracts the complexity of handling various types of inputs and conditions, enabling users to easily plot, modify, or analyze data in a two-dimensional space, tailored to specific needs or experiments.

inputs.name: X
inputs.description: Specifies one of the dimensions in a two-dimensional space, serving as a basis for plotting, modifying, or analyzing data.

inputs.name: Y
inputs.description: Specifies the other dimension in a two-dimensional space, complementing X to enable a comprehensive analysis or visualization of data.

inputs.name: direction
inputs.description: Determines the orientation or sequence in which data points are processed or plotted, affecting the visualization or analysis outcome.

outputs.name: X
outputs.description: Outputs data points or conditions along the X axis, reflecting modifications or analyses performed by the node.

outputs.name: Y
outputs.description: Outputs data points or conditions along the Y axis, complementing the X output for a full two-dimensional perspective.

easy XYInputs_ CFG Scale.description: This node is designed to facilitate the exploration and manipulation of CFG (Conditional Free Guidance) scale values within generative models. It allows users to dynamically adjust the CFG scale, enabling fine-tuning of the model's conditional generation capabilities for enhanced control over the output quality and adherence to specified conditions.

inputs.name: batch_count
inputs.description: Specifies the number of batches for which the CFG scale adjustments will be applied. This parameter is crucial for understanding the scale of the operation and ensuring that the adjustments are applied uniformly across multiple instances.

inputs.name: first_cfg
inputs.description: Determines the starting value of the CFG scale adjustment. This allows for the initial setting of the conditional guidance's influence on the generative process.

inputs.name: last_cfg
inputs.description: Sets the ending value of the CFG scale adjustment. This parameter enables the fine-tuning of the CFG scale's influence on the generative process over a specified range, allowing for gradual adjustments.

outputs.name: X or Y
outputs.description: Returns the outcome of the CFG scale adjustments, which could be either a modified generative model or a specific set of generation results, depending on the context of the operation.

easy XYInputs_ Checkpoint.description: This node is designed to facilitate the manipulation and visualization of checkpoint data for models, specifically focusing on generating XY input values based on checkpoint names, clip skips, and VAE names. It abstracts the complexity of handling multiple checkpoints and their associated parameters, enabling users to easily configure and visualize the impact of different checkpoints on model behavior.

inputs.name: input_mode
inputs.description: Specifies the mode of input, determining how checkpoints, clip skips, and VAE names are processed and utilized within the node. It affects the node's execution path and the resulting XY values.

inputs.name: ckpt_count
inputs.description: Defines the number of checkpoints to process, influencing the size and composition of the output XY values. It determines how many sets of checkpoint-related parameters are considered in the operation.

inputs.name: ckpt_name_i
inputs.description: Represents the name of a checkpoint. Each 'i' in 'ckpt_name_i' ranges from 1 to the total number of checkpoints specified, allowing for individual specification of multiple checkpoints.

inputs.name: clip_skip_i
inputs.description: Indicates the clip skip value for each checkpoint. Each 'i' in 'clip_skip_i' ranges from 1 to the total number of checkpoints, specifying the clip skip value associated with each checkpoint.

inputs.name: vae_name_i
inputs.description: Specifies the VAE name associated with each checkpoint. Each 'i' in 'vae_name_i' ranges from 1 to the total number of checkpoints, allowing for the association of specific VAEs with individual checkpoints.

inputs.name: optional_lora_stack
inputs.description: An optional parameter that, if provided, adds a LORA stack to the processing of checkpoints, clip skips, and VAE names, potentially altering the resulting XY values.

outputs.name: X or Y
outputs.description: The output is a set of XY values derived from the processed checkpoints, clip skips, and VAE names, intended for visualization or further analysis.

easy XYInputs_ ControlNet.description: This node is designed to facilitate the application of control net parameters over a range of values, enabling dynamic adjustments to image processing based on control net strength and positioning. It aims to provide a versatile tool for experimenting with different control net configurations, enhancing the ability to fine-tune image generation or modification tasks.

inputs.name: control_net_name
inputs.description: Specifies the name of the control net to be applied. This parameter is crucial for identifying which control net configuration to use during the operation.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image to which the control net adjustments will be applied. This parameter is central to the node's functionality, serving as the base for subsequent control net manipulations.

inputs.name: target_parameter
inputs.description: Determines the specific control net parameter to vary, such as strength or positioning, guiding the node's processing and output generation.

inputs.name: batch_count
inputs.description: Defines the number of variations to generate, allowing for a range of control net adjustments to be explored in a single operation.

inputs.name: first_strength
inputs.description: Sets the starting strength value for the control net, marking the beginning of the range for strength adjustments.

inputs.name: last_strength
inputs.description: Sets the ending strength value for the control net, marking the end of the range for strength adjustments.

inputs.name: first_start_percent
inputs.description: Specifies the starting percentage for the control net's application, defining the initial point of effect along the image's axis.

inputs.name: last_start_percent
inputs.description: Specifies the ending percentage for the control net's application, defining the final point of effect along the image's axis.

inputs.name: first_end_percent
inputs.description: Determines the starting end percentage for the control net's effect, establishing the initial boundary of the control net's influence.

inputs.name: last_end_percent
inputs.description: Determines the ending end percentage for the control net's effect, establishing the final boundary of the control net's influence.

inputs.name: strength
inputs.description: The strength of the control net effect to be applied, influencing the intensity of the control net's impact on the image.

inputs.name: start_percent
inputs.description: The starting percentage of the control net's application, indicating the initial point of the control net's effect on the image.

inputs.name: end_percent
inputs.description: The ending percentage of the control net's application, indicating the final point of the control net's effect on the image.

outputs.name: X or Y
outputs.description: Outputs a range of values or configurations based on the specified control net parameters, facilitating exploration and fine-tuning of image processing tasks.

easy XYInputs_ Denoise.description: This node is designed to facilitate the exploration and visualization of denoising effects in generative models. It allows users to adjust denoising parameters over a batch of data, providing a graphical representation of the impact of different denoising levels on the generated outputs.

inputs.name: batch_count
inputs.description: Specifies the number of batches to process, allowing for the examination of denoising effects across multiple sets of data.

inputs.name: first_denoise
inputs.description: Sets the initial denoising level, marking the starting point for the exploration of denoising effects.

inputs.name: last_denoise
inputs.description: Defines the final denoising level, enabling users to observe how increasing or decreasing denoising intensity affects the output.

outputs.name: X or Y
outputs.description: Provides a graphical representation of the denoising process, illustrating the effects of different denoising levels on the data.

easy XYInputs_ Lora.description: This node is designed to facilitate the generation and manipulation of XY plot values based on Lora configurations. It dynamically adjusts model and clip strengths for each Lora, optionally incorporating weights and allowing for the extension of Lora configurations through an optional stack. The node aims to provide a flexible interface for visualizing and customizing Lora-based data representations.

inputs.name: input_mode
inputs.description: Specifies the mode of input, determining whether weights are included in the Lora configurations. It affects how the node processes and generates XY plot values.

inputs.name: lora_count
inputs.description: Defines the number of Loras to be considered for generating XY plot values. It directly influences the size and complexity of the output data.

inputs.name: model_strength
inputs.description: Sets a default or specific model strength for each Lora, used as a baseline unless overridden by individual Lora configurations.

inputs.name: clip_strength
inputs.description: Determines a default or specific clip strength for each Lora, serving as a baseline unless individual Lora configurations specify otherwise.

inputs.name: lora_name_i
inputs.description: Specifies the name of each Lora, allowing for individual identification and configuration within the XY plot generation process.

inputs.name: model_str_i
inputs.description: Sets the model strength for each Lora individually, overriding the default model strength if specified.

inputs.name: clip_str_i
inputs.description: Sets the clip strength for each Lora individually, overriding the default clip strength if specified.

inputs.name: optional_lora_stack
inputs.description: Allows for the extension of Lora configurations beyond the specified count, enabling more complex and customized data representations.

outputs.name: X or Y
outputs.description: Represents the generated XY plot values based on the provided Lora configurations, ready for visualization or further processing.

easy XYInputs_ ModelMergeBlocks.description: This node facilitates the merging of models by providing an easy-to-use interface for specifying the models to be merged and the parameters governing the merge process. It abstracts the complexities involved in model merging, making it accessible for users to combine different models to achieve enhanced or specific functionalities.

inputs.name: ckpt_name_i
inputs.description: Specifies the checkpoint name for the subsequent models to be merged. This parameter allows users to select additional model versions or states to combine, enabling the creation of a new, merged model.

inputs.name: vae_use
inputs.description: Determines which model's VAE (Variational Autoencoder) is to be used in the merged model or allows for the selection of a specific VAE from available options.

inputs.name: preset
inputs.description: Allows users to select a preset configuration for the model merging process, simplifying the setup by providing predefined parameter values.

inputs.name: values
inputs.description: Defines the specific values for the merge parameters, such as input, middle, and output block weights, allowing for detailed customization of the merge process.

outputs.name: X or Y
outputs.description: The output is a merged model, which could be either model X or Y depending on the merging parameters and conditions specified by the user.

easy XYInputs_ NegativeCond.description: The easy XYInputs: NegativeCond node is designed to process negative conditioning inputs for XY plotting. It dynamically generates values and conditions based on the specified negative inputs, facilitating the creation of plots that visually represent negative conditions.

inputs.name: negative_i
inputs.description: Specifies a negative condition to be considered in the XY plot. It plays a role in determining the plot's representation of negative conditions, where 'i' can range from 1 to 4, representing up to four negative conditions.

outputs.name: X or Y
outputs.description: Outputs the processed XY values and conditions, encapsulating the negative conditions into a format suitable for plotting.

easy XYInputs_ NegativeCondList.description: This node processes a list of negative conditions for XY plotting, transforming them into a structured format suitable for further processing or visualization. It abstracts the complexity of handling multiple negative conditions by encapsulating them into a unified representation.

inputs.name: negative
inputs.description: The 'negative' input accepts a list of conditions intended to be used for negative scenarios in XY plotting. It plays a crucial role in defining the conditions under which certain actions or events are considered negative, thereby influencing the outcome of the plotting process.

outputs.name: X or Y
outputs.description: Outputs a structured representation of the negative conditions, including their indices and corresponding conditions, formatted for easy integration with XY plotting functionalities.

easy XYInputs_ PositiveCond.description: This node is designed to process positive conditioning inputs for XY plotting, allowing users to specify conditions that influence the plotting axis and values based on positive scenarios. It abstracts the complexity of handling conditional logic for positive inputs, facilitating the creation of customized plots that reflect specific positive conditions.

inputs.name: positive_i
inputs.description: Represents a positive condition to be applied, where 'i' can range from 1 to 4. Each condition incrementally modifies the plot's axis and values, enhancing the plot's specificity and allowing for a layered approach to customizing the plot's appearance based on positive scenarios.

outputs.name: X or Y
outputs.description: Outputs the configured axis and values for the plot, reflecting the applied positive conditions. This output demonstrates the flexibility in choosing either the X or Y axis based on the conditions applied, providing a tailored plotting experience.

easy XYInputs_ PositiveCondList.description: The XYplot_Positive_Cond_List node is designed to process a list of positive conditions, transforming them into a structured format suitable for plotting or further analysis. It focuses on identifying and organizing the conditions based on their positive attributes, facilitating easy visualization or manipulation of data points in a 'positive' context.

inputs.name: positive
inputs.description: The 'positive' input accepts a list of conditions, each representing a positive attribute or criterion. This input is crucial for the node's operation, as it determines the conditions that will be processed and structured for output.

outputs.name: X or Y
outputs.description: Outputs a structured representation of the positive conditions, including their indices and corresponding conditions, ready for plotting or analysis.

easy XYInputs_ PromptSR.description: The PromptSR node specializes in processing textual prompts by adjusting or generating new prompts based on specified sentiments, positive or negative. It leverages search text, replacement text, and conditions to dynamically create or modify prompts, aiming for a more targeted and nuanced prompt engineering approach.

inputs.name: target_prompt
inputs.description: Determines the sentiment direction for prompt adjustment or generation, influencing the outcome towards either positive or negative sentiment.

inputs.name: search_txt
inputs.description: Text used for searching within prompts, enabling specific themes or content to be targeted for refinement or generation.

inputs.name: replace_all_text
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether all instances of the search text should be replaced in the prompt.

inputs.name: replace_count
inputs.description: Specifies the number of replacements to be made, allowing for controlled modifications of the prompt.

inputs.name: replace_i
inputs.description: Dynamic inputs for replacement text, where 'i' can range from 1 to the value specified by 'replace_count', facilitating specific text replacements.

outputs.name: X or Y
outputs.description: Generates a prompt categorized under 'X' or 'Y', based on the sentiment direction specified by the target prompt, with detailed modifications reflecting the input conditions.

easy XYInputs_ Sampler_Scheduler.description: This node is designed to integrate and manage the interaction between a sampler and a scheduler within a sampling process. It facilitates the configuration and execution of sampling strategies by allowing users to specify a sampler and a scheduler, along with their respective parameters, to generate or modify sample outputs effectively.

inputs.name: target_parameter
inputs.description: This parameter is crucial for defining the specific target or goal that the sampling process aims to achieve, directly influencing the outcome and effectiveness of the sampling strategy.

inputs.name: input_count
inputs.description: Determines the number of inputs to be processed, affecting the node's execution by scaling the sampling operation according to the provided input volume.

inputs.name: sampler_i
inputs.description: Specifies the index of the sampler to be used, selecting from a predefined list of available samplers. This choice impacts the sampling method and its characteristics.

inputs.name: scheduler_i
inputs.description: Indicates the index of the scheduler, chosen from a set of available scheduling algorithms. This selection influences the timing and adjustment of sampling parameters throughout the process.

outputs.name: X or Y
outputs.description: Outputs a result that is contingent upon the configuration and interaction of the sampler and scheduler. The exact nature of the output (X or Y) depends on the specific parameters and algorithms employed.

easy XYInputs_ Seeds++ Batch.description: This node is designed to generate a batch of seed values for plotting or other batch processing tasks, where each seed represents a unique starting point for the generation process. It allows for the specification of the batch size, providing flexibility in how many seeds are generated and used.

inputs.name: batch_count
inputs.description: Specifies the number of seeds to generate in the batch. This parameter allows the user to control the scale of the batch operation, affecting the total number of unique starting points available for generation.

outputs.name: X or Y
outputs.description: Outputs a dictionary containing the axis label and the batch of seed values, ready for use in plotting or further processing.

easy XYInputs_ Steps.description: This node is designed to facilitate the manipulation and visualization of step values within a given process, allowing users to specify and adjust the range of steps for operations. It abstracts the complexity of handling step intervals, making it easier for users to define and visualize step-based configurations in an intuitive manner.

inputs.name: target_parameter
inputs.description: Specifies the target parameter that the step values will adjust, such as 'steps', 'start_at_step', or 'end_at_step', influencing how the node calculates and presents step intervals.

inputs.name: batch_count
inputs.description: Determines the number of step values to generate, affecting the granularity of the step intervals presented.

inputs.name: first_step
inputs.description: The starting value of the step range, setting the lower bound for step calculations.

inputs.name: last_step
inputs.description: The ending value of the step range, setting the upper bound for step calculations.

inputs.name: first_start_step
inputs.description: Specifies the initial step value when 'start_at_step' is the target parameter, defining the starting point for this specific interval.

inputs.name: last_start_step
inputs.description: Specifies the final step value when 'start_at_step' is the target parameter, marking the end point for this specific interval.

inputs.name: first_end_step
inputs.description: Specifies the initial step value when 'end_at_step' is the target parameter, defining the starting point for this specific interval.

inputs.name: last_end_step
inputs.description: Specifies the final step value when 'end_at_step' is the target parameter, marking the end point for this specific interval.

outputs.name: X or Y
outputs.description: Outputs a structured representation of step values within the specified range, facilitating easy visualization and manipulation of steps in the given process.

easy XYPlot.description: The `easyXYPlot` node is designed to facilitate the creation and manipulation of XY plots, particularly in the context of visualizing and analyzing data points or conditions across two dimensions. It supports advanced features such as handling positive and negative conditions, integrating with control networks for specific adjustments, and customizing plot dynamics based on user-defined variables.

inputs.name: grid_spacing
inputs.description: Specifies the spacing between grid lines in the XY plot, affecting the plot's granularity and readability.

inputs.name: output_individuals
inputs.description: Determines whether individual data points should be outputted separately, allowing for detailed analysis of each point.

inputs.name: flip_xy
inputs.description: Controls whether the X and Y axes should be flipped, altering the plot's orientation and perspective.

inputs.name: x_axis
inputs.description: Defines the label or identifier for the X-axis, contributing to the plot's contextual understanding.

inputs.name: x_values
inputs.description: Represents the data points or conditions along the X-axis, directly influencing the plot's horizontal distribution.

inputs.name: y_axis
inputs.description: Defines the label or identifier for the Y-axis, contributing to the plot's contextual understanding.

inputs.name: y_values
inputs.description: Represents the data points or conditions along the Y-axis, directly influencing the plot's vertical distribution.

inputs.name: pipe
inputs.description: An optional pipeline parameter that can be used to pass additional information or settings for the plot generation process.

outputs.name: pipe
outputs.description: The modified or new pipeline configuration, including any changes or additions made through the plot settings.

easy XYPlotAdvanced.description: The `easy XYPlotAdvanced` node is designed for advanced plotting capabilities within a pipeline, allowing for the customization of plots based on various conditions and parameters. It integrates complex plotting logic with conditional processing to enhance visualization and analysis of data.

inputs.name: pipe
inputs.description: Represents the pipeline configuration to which the advanced XY plotting logic will be applied, serving as the foundation for plot customization and enhancement.

inputs.name: grid_spacing
inputs.description: Specifies the spacing between grid points in the plot, allowing for fine-tuned control over the plot's visual density and layout.

inputs.name: output_individuals
inputs.description: A boolean parameter that determines whether individual plot elements should be output separately, enabling detailed analysis of each component.

inputs.name: flip_xy
inputs.description: A boolean parameter that, when true, swaps the x and y axes of the plot, offering flexibility in how data is presented and analyzed.

inputs.name: X
inputs.description: Optional parameter representing the x-axis data and its configuration, allowing for dynamic adjustment of the plot's horizontal axis.

inputs.name: Y
inputs.description: Optional parameter representing the y-axis data and its configuration, allowing for dynamic adjustment of the plot's vertical axis.

outputs.name: pipe
outputs.description: Returns the modified pipeline configuration, now including the advanced XY plot settings, facilitating further processing or visualization.

easy zero123Loader.description: The easy zero123Loader node is designed to simplify the process of loading and configuring 3D models for use within the ComfyUI framework. It abstracts away the complexities involved in setting up 3D model parameters, making it easier for users to integrate 3D content into their applications.

inputs.name: ckpt_name
inputs.description: Identifies the checkpoint name for the model to be loaded, serving as a key identifier for selecting the specific 3D model configuration.

inputs.name: vae_name
inputs.description: Specifies the name of the VAE model to be used in conjunction with the 3D model, facilitating the generation or manipulation of 3D content.

inputs.name: init_image
inputs.description: Provides an initial image to guide the generation or manipulation process, acting as a starting point for the 3D model's output.

inputs.name: empty_latent_width
inputs.description: Defines the width of the latent space to be used for generating or manipulating 3D content, impacting the resolution and detail of the output.

inputs.name: empty_latent_height
inputs.description: Specifies the height of the latent space, influencing the vertical resolution and detail of the 3D model's output.

inputs.name: batch_size
inputs.description: Determines the number of instances to be processed in a single batch, affecting the efficiency and speed of the loading operation.

inputs.name: elevation
inputs.description: Sets the elevation angle for the 3D model's viewpoint, altering the vertical perspective of the rendered content.

inputs.name: azimuth
inputs.description: Defines the azimuth angle, adjusting the horizontal orientation and perspective of the 3D model's output.

outputs.name: pipe
outputs.description: The pipeline object configured with the specified 3D model and settings, ready for use in generating or manipulating 3D content.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The loaded 3D model object, prepared for integration and use within the ComfyUI framework.

outputs.name: vae
outputs.description: The VAE model associated with the 3D model, enabling advanced content generation and manipulation capabilities.

Fans Prompt Styler Negative.description: This node specializes in applying stylistic transformations to prompts based on predefined styles and structural positioning, enhancing the expressiveness and specificity of negative prompts.

inputs.name: style
inputs.description: Specifies the stylistic transformation to apply to the prompt, chosen from a predefined list of styles. It determines the thematic or stylistic overlay that will modify the original prompt.

inputs.name: structure
inputs.description: Determines the placement of the stylistic transformation in relation to the original prompt, either at the beginning or the end, affecting the prompt's overall structure and emphasis.

inputs.name: prompt
inputs.description: The original text prompt to which the stylistic and structural transformations will be applied, serving as the base content for modification.

outputs.name: result
outputs.description: The transformed prompt, incorporating the selected style and structural positioning to convey a negative sentiment or theme.

Fans Prompt Styler Positive.description: This node is designed to modify and enhance text prompts based on a selection of positive styles. It allows for the dynamic integration of stylistic elements into user-defined prompts, aiming to tailor the output text to specific aesthetic or thematic preferences.

inputs.name: style
inputs.description: The 'style' parameter allows users to select a specific style from a predefined list to apply to their prompt. This choice determines the stylistic transformation that the prompt will undergo, impacting the overall tone and presentation of the output.

inputs.name: prompt
inputs.description: The 'prompt' parameter accepts a user-defined text input that serves as the base content for stylistic enhancement. This input is crucial as it forms the foundation upon which the selected style is applied, directly influencing the final output.

outputs.name: result
outputs.description: The 'result' output is the transformed prompt text, incorporating the selected style to modify the original input according to the user's aesthetic or thematic preferences.

Fans Styler.description: The Fans Styler node is designed to apply specific styling options to input text, allowing for customization of text output based on predefined styles. It supports multiple styles that can be applied individually or in combination, enhancing the text's presentation or adapting it to various contexts.

inputs.name: with_comma_condition
inputs.description: Determines whether the styled text should be separated by commas, affecting the readability and format of the output.

inputs.name: style1
inputs.description: Selects a specific style to apply to the first segment of the input text, influencing its aesthetic or thematic presentation.

inputs.name: style2
inputs.description: Selects a specific style to apply to the second segment of the input text, influencing its aesthetic or thematic presentation.

inputs.name: style3

Fans Text Concatenate.description: This node is designed to concatenate multiple text inputs into a single string, optionally adding line breaks between each text segment. It allows for flexible text manipulation and aggregation, making it suitable for preparing text data for further processing or display.

inputs.name: linebreak_addition
inputs.description: Determines whether to add a line break between each concatenated text segment. A 'true' value inserts line breaks, while 'false' concatenates texts directly.

inputs.name: prompt
inputs.description: An initial piece of text to start the concatenation process. It serves as the base to which other texts are appended.

inputs.name: text_a
inputs.description: The first text to concatenate following the prompt, if provided.

inputs.name: text_b
inputs.description: The second text to concatenate following any previous texts.

inputs.name: text_c
inputs.description: The third text to concatenate, continuing the sequence of text aggregation.

inputs.name: text_d
inputs.description: The fourth text in the concatenation sequence.

inputs.name: text_e
inputs.description: The fifth text to be concatenated, further extending the text string.

inputs.name: text_f
inputs.description: The sixth text to be added to the concatenated string.

inputs.name: text_g
inputs.description: The seventh text in the concatenation order.

inputs.name: text_h
inputs.description: The eighth text to be concatenated, adding more content to the string.

inputs.name: text_i
inputs.description: The ninth text in the sequence, further extending the concatenated string.

inputs.name: text_j
inputs.description: The tenth and final text to be concatenated, completing the text aggregation process.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The final concatenated text string, composed of up to ten individual text inputs and optional line breaks.

DownloadAndLoadFlorence2Model.description: This node is designed to download and load a specified Florence2 model, applying the chosen precision and attention mechanism settings. It ensures the model is ready for use by initializing it with the appropriate device, data type, and attention implementation.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: Specifies the repository ID of the Florence2 model to be downloaded and loaded. It influences the model's capabilities and features.

inputs.name: precision
inputs.description: Determines the numerical precision (e.g., bf16, fp16, fp32) of the model's computations, affecting performance and memory usage.

inputs.name: attention
inputs.description: Selects the attention mechanism implementation to be used by the model, impacting its performance and accuracy.

outputs.name: florence2_model
outputs.description: A dictionary containing the loaded model, its processor, and the data type used for computations.

Florence2Run.description: The Florence2Run node is designed to process images and text inputs through the Florence2 model, executing a variety of tasks such as image captioning, object detection, and visual question answering. It leverages advanced deep learning techniques to understand and generate descriptions or answers based on the visual and textual context provided.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image to be processed. It is crucial for visual tasks and is used as the primary input for generating outputs based on visual content.

inputs.name: florence2_model
inputs.description: unknown

inputs.name: text_input
