inputs.description: Optional text input that provides context or queries for the model to consider alongside the image. It's essential for tasks requiring textual input like visual question answering.

inputs.name: task
inputs.description: Specifies the task to be performed, such as image captioning or object detection, guiding the model's processing and output generation.

inputs.name: fill_mask
inputs.description: A parameter used in certain tasks to control how the model fills in masked parts of the image or text.

inputs.name: keep_model_loaded
inputs.description: Determines whether the model remains loaded after processing, affecting resource utilization and performance for subsequent tasks.

inputs.name: max_new_tokens
inputs.description: Limits the number of new tokens the model can generate, impacting the length and detail of text outputs.

inputs.name: num_beams
inputs.description: Controls the beam search width during text generation, influencing the diversity and quality of the output.

inputs.name: do_sample
inputs.description: Enables or disables sampling in text generation, affecting the randomness and variety of the generated text.

inputs.name: output_mask_select
inputs.description: Allows selection of specific outputs or masks, providing finer control over the output data.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The processed image, potentially modified or annotated based on the task performed.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: A mask generated by the model, applicable for tasks involving segmentation or specific area highlighting.

outputs.name: caption
outputs.description: Generated text output by the model, such as captions, descriptions, or answers to queries, based on the task.

LDSRModelLoader.description: The LDSRModelLoader node is designed to load and prepare LDSR (Low-Dimensional Super-Resolution) models for use, specifically focusing on selecting and initializing models for image upscaling tasks.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: Specifies the model to be loaded for the upscaling task. The choice of model can influence the quality and characteristics of the upscaling result.

outputs.name: upscale_model
outputs.description: Returns the loaded and CPU-transferred LDSR model ready for image upscaling tasks.

LDSRUpscale.description: The LDSRUpscale node is designed to upscale images using a specified model, with options for pre and post downscaling, and a choice of downsample methods. It allows for detailed control over the upscaling process, including the number of steps and downscale factors, to enhance image resolution effectively.

inputs.name: upscale_model
inputs.description: Specifies the model to be used for upscaling the images. This choice determines the upscaling technique and quality.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: A collection of images to be upscaled. This input allows the node to process multiple images in a single operation.

inputs.name: steps
inputs.description: Defines the number of steps to be used in the upscaling process, affecting the detail and quality of the output.

inputs.name: pre_downscale
inputs.description: Optional pre-processing step to downscale images before upscaling, which can affect the upscaling quality and performance.

inputs.name: post_downscale
inputs.description: Optional post-processing step to adjust the size of the upscaled images, allowing for size customization or restoration to original dimensions.

inputs.name: downsample_method
inputs.description: The method used for downsampling during pre and post downscale steps, influencing the quality of the downscaled images.

outputs.name: images
outputs.description: The upscaled images, enhanced in resolution and detail through the specified upscaling process.

LDSRUpscaler.description: The LDSRUpscaler node is designed to upscale images using the LDSR model, providing a high-level interface for enhancing image resolution through deep learning techniques. It abstracts the complexities of the underlying LDSR model operations, offering a simplified method for users to improve image quality with options for pre and post downscaling and different downsample methods.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: Specifies the LDSR model to be used for upscaling. This model determines the upscaling technique and quality.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The images to be upscaled. This input allows for batch processing of multiple images, enhancing their resolution.

inputs.name: steps
inputs.description: Defines the number of steps for the upscaling process, affecting the quality and computation time of the upscaling.

inputs.name: pre_downscale
inputs.description: Optional pre-processing step to downscale images before upscaling, which can affect the final image quality and processing time.

inputs.name: post_downscale
inputs.description: Optional post-processing step to adjust the size of the upscaled images, allowing for customization of the output resolution.

inputs.name: downsample_method
inputs.description: The method used for downsampling during the pre and post downscale steps, influencing the quality of the downscaled images.

outputs.name: images
outputs.description: The upscaled images, enhanced in resolution through the LDSR upscaling process.

AMT VFI.description: The AMT_VFI node is designed for advanced motion transfer and frame interpolation in video processing. It leverages deep learning models to analyze and synthesize frames, achieving high-quality video frame interpolation by understanding and replicating the motion between consecutive frames.

inputs.name: ckpt_name
inputs.description: The checkpoint name for the model, selecting the specific pre-trained model for frame interpolation.

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: The sequence of frames to be interpolated, serving as the input for the frame interpolation process.

inputs.name: clear_cache_after_n_frames
inputs.description: Controls how often the cache is cleared during the frame interpolation process, optimizing memory usage.

inputs.name: multiplier
inputs.description: The factor by which the frame rate is increased, determining the number of frames generated between each pair of input frames.

inputs.name: optional_interpolation_states
inputs.description: Optional states for interpolation, allowing for customization of the interpolation process.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output interpolated frames, showcasing the node's capability in enhancing video fluidity and detail.

CAIN VFI.description: The CAIN VFI node is designed for video frame interpolation, leveraging deep learning models to predict intermediate frames between two consecutive frames in a video sequence. It utilizes the CAIN architecture, which focuses on capturing temporal and spatial details through an encoder-decoder structure, to enhance the smoothness and quality of video playback.

inputs.name: ckpt_name
inputs.description: The checkpoint name specifies the pre-trained model to be used for frame interpolation, enabling the node to load the appropriate weights for the CAIN model.

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: A tensor containing the consecutive frames of a video. These frames are the input to the CAIN model for generating intermediate frames.

inputs.name: clear_cache_after_n_frames
inputs.description: This parameter controls the cache clearing mechanism to manage memory usage during the frame interpolation process.

inputs.name: multiplier
inputs.description: Defines the number of intermediate frames to be generated between each pair of consecutive frames, dictating the smoothness of the output video.

inputs.name: optional_interpolation_states
inputs.description: Optional states that can be passed to influence the interpolation process, offering flexibility for different video processing scenarios and potentially affecting the selection of frames for interpolation.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is a tensor of interpolated frames, enhancing the video's fluidity by filling in the gaps between original frames.

FILM VFI.description: The FILM VFI node specializes in frame interpolation, leveraging deep learning models to generate intermediate frames between two given images. It aims to enhance video fluidity and detail by accurately predicting and synthesizing frames that could logically exist between the original frames, thus achieving smoother motion transitions and improved visual quality.

inputs.name: ckpt_name
inputs.description: Specifies the checkpoint name for the FILM VFI model, determining the specific pretrained model weights to be used for frame interpolation.

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: The sequence of images to be interpolated, serving as the input frames for generating intermediate frames.

inputs.name: clear_cache_after_n_frames
inputs.description: Controls how often the system's cache is cleared during the interpolation process to manage memory usage effectively.

inputs.name: multiplier
inputs.description: Defines the number of intermediate frames to be generated between each pair of input frames, affecting the smoothness of the output video.

inputs.name: optional_interpolation_states
inputs.description: Optional states that can influence the frame skipping logic during interpolation, allowing for more customized processing.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output images generated by the FILM VFI model, representing the interpolated frames that enhance the fluidity and detail of the original video sequence.

FLAVR VFI.description: The FLAVR_VFI node specializes in video frame interpolation, specifically designed to enhance video quality by interpolating frames to achieve a smoother motion at a 2x rate. It emphasizes the use of the FLAVR model for generating intermediate frames in a video sequence, ensuring a more fluid and visually appealing playback experience.

inputs.name: ckpt_name
inputs.description: The checkpoint name for loading the specific pretrained FLAVR model, facilitating the use of trained weights for interpolation.

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: The input video frames to be interpolated. These frames are processed to generate intermediate frames, enhancing the video's smoothness.

inputs.name: clear_cache_after_n_frames
inputs.description: Specifies the number of frames processed before clearing the CUDA cache to prevent memory overflow.

inputs.name: multiplier
inputs.description: Specifies the interpolation rate, with a strong recommendation for a 2x rate to align with FLAVR's optimal performance capabilities.

inputs.name: duplicate_first_last_frames
inputs.description: Indicates whether to duplicate the first and last frames in the output, potentially enhancing the visual continuity of the interpolated video.

inputs.name: optional_interpolation_states
inputs.description: Optional states that can be used to influence the interpolation process, providing flexibility in handling various video processing scenarios.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The interpolated frames produced by the FLAVR model, resulting in a smoother and more visually appealing video sequence.

GMFSS Fortuna VFI.description: The GMFSS Fortuna VFI node is designed for frame interpolation in video processing, leveraging deep learning models to predict intermediate frames between two given frames. It utilizes a specialized architecture to enhance the quality and accuracy of the interpolation, aiming to produce smooth and visually coherent transitions.

inputs.name: ckpt_name
inputs.description: The checkpoint name for the model, specifying which pretrained model to use for frame interpolation.

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: A tensor containing the sequence of frames for interpolation. It is the primary input from which intermediate frames are generated.

inputs.name: clear_cache_after_n_frames
inputs.description: Specifies after how many frames the CUDA cache should be cleared to prevent memory overflow.

inputs.name: multiplier
inputs.description: Determines the number of intermediate frames to be generated between each pair of input frames.

inputs.name: optional_interpolation_states
inputs.description: An optional parameter that allows for the skipping of frames based on certain conditions, potentially optimizing the interpolation process.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output of the interpolation process, consisting of the original frames along with the newly interpolated frames.

IFRNet VFI.description: The IFRNet VFI node specializes in video frame interpolation, utilizing deep learning models to predict and generate intermediate frames between existing frames in a video sequence. This process enhances video smoothness and can be used to increase the frame rate of videos.

inputs.name: ckpt_name
inputs.description: Specifies the checkpoint name for the model to be loaded, determining the specific pre-trained weights to use for frame interpolation.

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: A tensor containing the sequence of frames to be interpolated. This is the primary input on which the interpolation process is applied.

inputs.name: clear_cache_after_n_frames
inputs.description: Controls the cache clearing mechanism to manage memory usage during the interpolation process, by specifying after how many frames the cache should be cleared.

inputs.name: multiplier
inputs.description: Determines the number of intermediate frames to be generated between each pair of original frames, effectively controlling the output video's frame rate.

inputs.name: scale_factor
inputs.description: A scaling factor for adjusting the resolution of the interpolated frames relative to the original frames.

inputs.name: optional_interpolation_states
inputs.description: Optional states that can be used to influence the interpolation process, allowing for customization and optimization based on specific requirements.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output tensor containing the interpolated frames, enhancing the smoothness and frame rate of the input video sequence.

IFUnet VFI.description: The IFUnet_VFI node specializes in video frame interpolation, leveraging deep learning models to predict and generate intermediate frames between existing frames in a video sequence. This process enhances video fluidity and can be used to increase the frame rate of videos, improve slow-motion effects, or restore missing frames in damaged video files.

inputs.name: ckpt_name
inputs.description: Specifies the checkpoint name for the model to be used in the frame interpolation process, determining the specific pre-trained model configuration.

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: A sequence of images representing the video frames between which the interpolation will occur, serving as the input for generating intermediate frames.

inputs.name: clear_cache_after_n_frames
inputs.description: Controls the frequency of cache clearing to manage memory usage during the interpolation process, optimizing performance.

inputs.name: multiplier
inputs.description: Defines the factor by which the frame rate is to be increased, indicating the number of intermediate frames to be generated.

inputs.name: scale_factor
inputs.description: Determines the scaling factor applied to the frames during the interpolation process, affecting the resolution and size of the output frames.

inputs.name: ensemble
inputs.description: A boolean flag that enables or disables the use of ensemble methods for frame interpolation, potentially improving the quality of the output.

inputs.name: optional_interpolation_states
inputs.description: Optional states for managing the interpolation process, allowing for advanced control over frame selection and processing.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image sequence after interpolation, representing the enhanced video with additional frames inserted.

KSampler Gradually Adding More Denoise (.description: This node specializes in generating a sequence of samples by gradually increasing the denoising strength applied to a latent image. It leverages a common sampling function to produce a series of progressively denoised images, allowing for a controlled and incremental refinement of the generated content.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model parameter represents the neural network model used for the sampling process. It is crucial for determining the behavior and quality of the generated samples.

inputs.name: positive
inputs.description: Positive conditioning information that guides the generation towards desired attributes or features in the output.

inputs.name: negative
inputs.description: Negative conditioning information used to steer the generation away from certain attributes or features, complementing the positive conditioning.

inputs.name: latent_image
inputs.description: The initial latent representation of the image to be denoised. This serves as the starting point for the gradual denoising process.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: A seed value for random number generation, ensuring reproducibility of the sampling process.

inputs.name: steps
inputs.description: The number of steps to take in the sampling process, affecting the granularity of the denoising progression.

inputs.name: cfg
inputs.description: The CFG (Classifier-Free Guidance) scale, which adjusts the influence of conditioning information on the generation process.

inputs.name: sampler_name
inputs.description: The name of the sampler algorithm to use, which determines the specific approach to sampling and denoising.

inputs.name: scheduler
inputs.description: The scheduler determines the sequence of noise levels used throughout the sampling process, influencing the progression of denoising.

inputs.name: start_denoise
inputs.description: The initial denoising strength, setting the starting point for the gradual increase in denoising.

inputs.name: denoise_increment
inputs.description: The amount by which the denoising strength is increased at each step, controlling the pace of the denoising progression.

inputs.name: denoise_increment_steps
inputs.description: The total number of steps over which the denoising strength is increased, defining the length of the gradual denoising process.

inputs.name: optional_vae
inputs.description: An optional VAE (Variational Autoencoder) model that can be used in conjunction with the primary model for additional processing or refinement of the generated samples.

outputs.name: MODEL
outputs.description: The neural network model used for the sampling process, returned unchanged.

outputs.name: CONDITIONING+
outputs.description: The positive conditioning information, returned unchanged.

outputs.name: CONDITIONING-
outputs.description: The negative conditioning information, returned unchanged.

outputs.name: LATENT
outputs.description: The final latent representation of the image after the gradual denoising process.

outputs.name: VAE
outputs.description: The optional VAE model, if used, returned unchanged.

M2M VFI.description: The M2M VFI node is designed for video frame interpolation, utilizing deep learning models to predict intermediate frames between two consecutive frames in a video sequence. This process enhances video fluidity and can be used to increase the frame rate of videos.

inputs.name: ckpt_name
inputs.description: A checkpoint name specifying the model to be used for frame interpolation. It determines the specific pre-trained model weights to load, directly influencing the interpolation quality and performance.

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: A tensor containing the sequence of frames for which intermediate frames are to be generated. It is the primary input from which the model predicts the missing frames, affecting the overall video smoothness.

inputs.name: clear_cache_after_n_frames
inputs.description: Indicates after how many frames the cache should be cleared to prevent memory overflow. This parameter helps manage GPU memory usage efficiently during the interpolation process.

inputs.name: multiplier
inputs.description: Defines the number of intermediate frames to be generated between each pair of original frames, directly affecting the output video's frame rate.

inputs.name: optional_interpolation_states
inputs.description: An optional parameter that allows for the control of frame skipping and other interpolation behaviors, providing flexibility in the frame generation process.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output tensor containing the interpolated frames, which increases the frame rate and enhances the smoothness of the input video sequence.

Make Interpolation State List.description: This node is designed to generate a list of interpolation states based on provided frame indices and a skip list flag. It abstracts the process of preparing the necessary state information required for frame interpolation tasks, facilitating the setup for subsequent video frame interpolation operations.

inputs.name: frame_indices
inputs.description: Specifies the indices of frames to be included in the interpolation process. This string of comma-separated numbers is crucial for determining which frames are considered for interpolation.

inputs.name: is_skip_list
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether certain frames should be skipped in the interpolation process. This affects the selection of frames for interpolation, enabling more control over the output.

outputs.name: interpolation_states
outputs.description: The output is a list of states that represent the configuration for frame interpolation, including which frames to interpolate and whether to skip certain frames.

RIFE VFI.description: The RIFE_VFI node is designed for video frame interpolation, leveraging deep learning techniques to predict and generate intermediate frames between existing frames in a video sequence. This process enhances video fluidity and can be used for various applications such as slow-motion video generation, video restoration, and improving video frame rates.

inputs.name: ckpt_name
inputs.description: Specifies the checkpoint name for the model to use, which determines the pre-trained weights and potentially the model architecture for frame interpolation.

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: A sequence of images or frames that the node will process to generate interpolated frames. This is the core input that drives the interpolation process.

inputs.name: clear_cache_after_n_frames
inputs.description: Indicates after how many frames the node should clear its cache to manage memory usage efficiently during the interpolation process.

inputs.name: multiplier
inputs.description: Defines the number of intermediate frames to be generated between each pair of input frames, directly affecting the smoothness of the output video.

inputs.name: fast_mode
inputs.description: Enables a faster but potentially less accurate mode of frame interpolation, optimizing for speed over precision.

inputs.name: ensemble
inputs.description: Activates ensemble mode, which may use multiple models or techniques in tandem to improve the quality of the interpolated frames.

inputs.name: scale_factor
inputs.description: Adjusts the scale of the input frames before processing, which can influence the interpolation quality and performance.

inputs.name: optional_interpolation_states
inputs.description: Optional states that can control the interpolation process, allowing for advanced customization or optimization based on specific requirements.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output consists of a sequence of interpolated frames, enhancing the fluidity and frame rate of the input video sequence.

Sepconv VFI.description: The Sepconv VFI node is designed for video frame interpolation using separable convolutional networks. It enhances video quality by interpolating additional frames between existing ones, leveraging deep learning techniques to predict and generate intermediate frames with high accuracy and visual fidelity. This process is crucial for increasing the frame rate of videos, improving slow-motion effects, and enhancing the overall viewing experience.

inputs.name: ckpt_name
inputs.description: The checkpoint name for the model, specifying the pre-trained weights to be used for frame interpolation.

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: The sequence of frames to be interpolated, provided as a batch of images.

inputs.name: clear_cache_after_n_frames
inputs.description: Controls the cache clearing mechanism to manage memory usage, specifying after how many frames the cache should be cleared.

inputs.name: multiplier
inputs.description: Defines the frame rate multiplier, indicating how many intermediate frames should be generated between each pair of original frames.

inputs.name: optional_interpolation_states
inputs.description: Optional states for controlling the interpolation process, allowing for customization of the frame generation.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output interpolated frames, enhancing the original video by increasing its frame rate through the addition of generated intermediate frames.

STMFNet VFI.description: The STMFNet VFI node is designed for video frame interpolation, leveraging deep learning models to predict and generate intermediate frames between existing frames in a video sequence. It utilizes a combination of extraction, decoding, and refining processes to enhance the temporal resolution of videos by filling in missing frames with high accuracy and visual quality.

inputs.name: ckpt_name
inputs.description: Specifies the checkpoint name for the STMFNet model to be loaded, crucial for initializing the model with pre-trained weights.

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: The sequence of frames to be interpolated, serving as the input video data for frame interpolation.

inputs.name: clear_cache_after_n_frames
inputs.description: Determines after how many frames the CUDA cache should be cleared to manage memory usage effectively.

inputs.name: multiplier
inputs.description: Defines the factor by which the frame rate is increased, currently fixed to 2x interpolation.

inputs.name: duplicate_first_last_frames
inputs.description: A boolean flag to indicate whether the first and last frames should be duplicated, affecting the output frame sequence.

inputs.name: optional_interpolation_states
inputs.description: Optional states to manage frame skipping during interpolation, providing flexibility in handling specific frames.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output of the node, consisting of the interpolated video frames, enhancing the video's temporal resolution.

VFI FloatToInt.description: The VFI FloatToInt node is designed to convert floating-point numbers to integers. This conversion process is essential in scenarios where integer values are required for further processing or when interfacing with systems that only accept integers. The node can handle both single floating-point values and collections of values, offering flexibility in its application.

inputs.name: float
inputs.description: The floating-point number or collection of floating-point numbers to be converted to integer(s). This input is crucial for the conversion process, determining the output based on the value(s) provided.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: The converted integer or list of integers from the provided floating-point number(s). This output is significant for processes that require integer values.

Moondream Interrogator.description: The Moondream Interrogator node is designed to generate textual descriptions for images using a visual language model. It leverages the Moondream model to interpret and answer questions about the given images, providing a bridge between visual content and natural language descriptions.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image tensor to be described. It is crucial for generating the textual descriptions by interpreting the visual content.

inputs.name: prompt
inputs.description: A string or a list of strings representing the questions or prompts to guide the generation of descriptions for the image.

inputs.name: separator
inputs.description: A string used to separate multiple descriptions in the output, allowing for clear distinction between different pieces of generated text.

inputs.name: model_revision
inputs.description: Specifies the version of the Moondream model to use, enabling the selection of different model capabilities or updates.

inputs.name: temperature
inputs.description: Controls the randomness in the generation process, affecting the variability and creativity of the output descriptions.

inputs.name: device
inputs.description: Indicates whether to use CPU or GPU for computation, affecting performance and resource utilization.

inputs.name: trust_remote_code
inputs.description: A boolean flag that must be set to true to enable the use of this node, ensuring security and trust in the remote code executed.

outputs.name: description
outputs.description: The generated textual description for the input image, based on the provided prompts and questions.

BackgroundScaler.description: The BackgroundScaler node is designed to adjust the grayscale level of masked areas within an image, allowing for dynamic scaling based on specified parameters. It provides a method to selectively modify the appearance of background elements in images by applying a scale factor to the masked regions.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed. It serves as the primary canvas on which the grayscale scaling is applied to the masked areas.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: A mask that specifies the areas within the image to be scaled. The mask determines which parts of the image will undergo the grayscale adjustment.

inputs.name: scale
inputs.description: A scale factor that determines the intensity of the grayscale to be applied to the masked areas. It allows for fine-tuning the visual impact of the scaling on the image.

inputs.name: invert
inputs.description: A boolean flag that, when set to True, inverts the mask, thereby applying the scaling to the unmasked areas instead.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image with the masked areas adjusted in grayscale according to the specified scale factor.

CalculateNormalsFromImages.description: The CalculateNormalsFromImages node is designed to compute normal maps from a set of images representing different directional exposures. It processes batches of images to generate corresponding normal maps and optionally applies masks to refine the output, facilitating advanced image processing tasks such as lighting simulation or 3D reconstruction.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: A batch of images, expected to be in sets of four representing left, right, bottom, and top directional exposures. These images are used to calculate the normal maps.

inputs.name: sigma
inputs.description: A float value used to adjust the sharpness of the generated normal map. Higher values result in sharper details.

inputs.name: center_input_range
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether the input images should be normalized to a 0.5 center point before processing.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: An optional mask to apply to the images, used to isolate or highlight specific areas for normal map calculation.

outputs.name: normal
outputs.description: The generated normal map, representing the surface normals derived from the input images.

outputs.name: divided
outputs.description: An intermediate representation of the processed images, used internally for normalization and calculation.

DetailTransfer.description: The DetailTransfer node is designed to enhance the visual quality of images by transferring intricate details from one image to another. It focuses on improving the texture and depth of the target image, ensuring that the final output retains a high level of detail and realism.

inputs.name: target
inputs.description: The target image that will receive the detail enhancements, serving as the primary canvas for the detail transfer.

inputs.name: source
inputs.description: The source image from which details are extracted to be transferred to the target image, playing a key role in defining the transferred textures and details.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Specifies the blending mode used to combine the source and target images, influencing the final appearance of the detail transfer.

inputs.name: blur_sigma
inputs.description: Determines the amount of blur applied to the detail transfer, affecting the smoothness and subtlety of the detail integration.

inputs.name: blend_factor
inputs.description: Controls the intensity of the detail transfer, allowing for fine-tuning of how prominently the transferred details appear on the target image.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: An optional mask that can specify areas of the target image to be affected or excluded from the detail transfer, offering additional control over the outcome.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The enhanced image with transferred details, showcasing improved texture and depth for a more realistic and detailed appearance.

ICLightConditioning.description: The ICLightConditioning node is designed to prepare and condition inputs specifically for the IC-Light model, ensuring compatibility and optimal performance. It focuses on adjusting and validating input data, such as images and noise, to meet the model's requirements, facilitating enhanced image generation processes.

inputs.name: positive
inputs.description: A set of conditioning instructions intended to guide the image generation towards desired attributes or features, enhancing the positive aspects of the output.

inputs.name: negative
inputs.description: A set of conditioning instructions aimed at steering the image generation away from undesired attributes or features, minimizing the negative aspects of the output.

inputs.name: vae
inputs.description: The variational autoencoder used to encode images into a latent space, providing a compressed representation of the input images for further processing.

inputs.name: foreground
inputs.description: The latent representation of the foreground image to be used in the conditioning process, contributing to the generation of the final image.

inputs.name: multiplier
inputs.description: A scalar value that adjusts the intensity of the effect of the foreground latent representation on the conditioning process.

inputs.name: opt_background
inputs.description: An optional latent representation of the background image, which can be used to modify the background of the generated image.

outputs.name: positive
outputs.description: The modified set of positive conditioning instructions, incorporating the effects of the input latent representations and adjustments.

outputs.name: negative
outputs.description: The modified set of negative conditioning instructions, incorporating the effects of the input latent representations and adjustments.

outputs.name: empty_latent
outputs.description: A placeholder latent representation, typically used when no specific output latent is required for the operation.

LightSource.description: The LightSource node generates gradient images simulating various lighting effects based on specified parameters. It allows for the creation of dynamic lighting conditions in images, enhancing visual depth and realism.

inputs.name: light_position
inputs.description: Specifies the position of the simulated light source within the image, affecting the direction and spread of the light gradient.

inputs.name: multiplier
inputs.description: Adjusts the intensity and spread of the light gradient, enabling finer control over the lighting effect.

inputs.name: start_color
inputs.description: Defines the starting color of the light gradient, allowing for customization of the light's appearance.

inputs.name: end_color
inputs.description: Sets the ending color of the light gradient, facilitating the creation of varied lighting effects.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Determines the width of the generated gradient image, impacting the overall size of the light effect.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Specifies the height of the generated gradient image, influencing the scale of the light effect.

inputs.name: batch_size
inputs.description: Controls the number of gradient images generated in a batch, supporting batch processing of light effects.

inputs.name: prev_image
inputs.description: Optionally includes a previous image to be combined with the generated light gradient, enhancing composite image creation.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: Outputs a gradient image simulating the specified light source effect, ready for further processing or visualization.

LoadAndApplyICLightUnet.description: This node is designed to load and apply IC-Light Unet weights to a model, ensuring compatibility with specific model architectures by patching and converting state dictionaries as necessary. It focuses on enhancing models with IC-Light Unet's capabilities, facilitating the integration of advanced lighting effects into generated images.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model to which IC-Light Unet weights will be applied. It plays a crucial role in the node's operation by being the recipient of the enhanced lighting capabilities provided by IC-Light Unet.

inputs.name: model_path
inputs.description: The path to the IC-Light Unet weights file. This parameter is essential for locating and loading the specific weights to be applied to the model.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The model enhanced with IC-Light Unet weights. This output is crucial for utilizing the model with advanced lighting effects in generated images.

LoadHDRImage.description: The LoadHDRImage node is designed to load High Dynamic Range (HDR) images from a specified directory, process them to simulate different exposures, and convert them into a batch of Low Dynamic Range (LDR) images. This node facilitates the exploration of various exposure levels within an HDR image by generating multiple exposure-adjusted versions, thereby enabling enhanced image analysis and manipulation.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: Specifies the HDR image to be loaded and processed. The image is identified by its name within the input directory, and this parameter is crucial for determining which HDR image will undergo exposure adjustments.

inputs.name: exposures
inputs.description: A comma-separated string representing the exposure levels to apply to the HDR image. These values are used to simulate different lighting conditions by adjusting the brightness of the image, thereby generating multiple LDR versions.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: Represents the LDR images generated from the HDR image at specified exposure levels, facilitating further image processing or analysis.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: This output type is not directly mentioned in the provided context, indicating a potential misunderstanding or error in the original feedback.

IF_ChatPrompt.description: The IF_ChatPrompt node is designed to facilitate interactive chat experiences by generating responses based on user inputs and a variety of parameters. It supports customization of the chat experience through different engines, models, and prompts, and includes features for managing conversation history and context.

inputs.name: prompt
inputs.description: The initial prompt or question to start the conversation. It sets the context for the chatbot's response.

inputs.name: base_ip
inputs.description: The IP address of the server where the chat engine is hosted. It's crucial for establishing a connection to the engine.

inputs.name: port
inputs.description: The port number on the server to connect to the chat engine. It specifies the exact entry point for communication.

inputs.name: engine
inputs.description: Specifies the chat engine to use for generating responses. It allows for selection among various pre-defined engines, enabling flexibility in response generation.

inputs.name: selected_model
inputs.description: The specific model selected for generating responses. This parameter allows for further customization of the chat experience.

inputs.name: assistant
inputs.description: Defines the assistant's persona or role in the conversation, allowing for tailored responses based on the selected assistant.

inputs.name: context
inputs.description: The current context or state of the conversation. It's essential for generating coherent and contextually relevant responses.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: An image to be included in the chat context, allowing for responses that can incorporate visual elements.

inputs.name: max_tokens
inputs.description: The maximum number of tokens to generate for the response. It controls the length of the chatbot's replies.

inputs.name: temperature
inputs.description: Controls the randomness of the response generation, affecting the creativity and variability of the replies.

inputs.name: top_k
inputs.description: Limits the number of highest probability vocabulary tokens considered for each step, influencing the response's diversity.

inputs.name: top_p
inputs.description: Nucleus sampling parameter that controls the cumulative probability cutoff, shaping the response's unpredictability.

inputs.name: repeat_penalty
inputs.description: Adjusts the likelihood of repeating the same line, aiming to reduce redundancy in responses.

inputs.name: stop
inputs.description: A set of tokens that signal the end of a response, helping to delineate the chatbot's replies.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: A seed for the random number generator, ensuring reproducibility of responses under the same conditions.

inputs.name: random
inputs.description: Toggles between using a fixed seed or temperature for randomness, affecting the consistency of responses.

inputs.name: embellish_prompt
inputs.description: A prompt modifier that adds embellishment to the initial prompt, enhancing the creativity of the response.

inputs.name: style_prompt
inputs.description: A prompt modifier that applies a specific style to the response, allowing for stylistic customization.

inputs.name: neg_prompt
inputs.description: A prompt modifier that specifies content to avoid in the response, helping to tailor the chatbot's output.

inputs.name: clear_history
inputs.description: Controls whether to clear the chat history, affecting the continuity of the conversation.

inputs.name: history_steps
inputs.description: Specifies the number of recent messages to retain in the chat history, influencing the context available for generating responses.

inputs.name: keep_alive
inputs.description: Determines whether to keep the model loaded between requests, impacting response time and resource usage.

inputs.name: text_cleanup
inputs.description: unknown

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: unknown

outputs.name: Question
outputs.description: The original question or prompt provided to the chatbot.

outputs.name: Response
outputs.description: The generated response from the chatbot based on the input prompt and parameters.

outputs.name: Negative
outputs.description: A generated response that specifically avoids the content outlined in the neg_prompt parameter.

outputs.name: Context
outputs.description: The updated context of the conversation after the response, including any modifications made during processing.

IF_DisplayText.description: The IF_DisplayText node is designed for displaying text outputs within the ImpactFrames environment, providing a simple interface for visualizing text data.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The 'text' parameter is the primary input for the IF_DisplayText node, serving as the text content to be displayed. Its presence is crucial for the node's operation, dictating the textual output that will be visualized.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: unknown

IF_ImagePrompt.description: The IF_ImagePrompt node transforms visual inputs into textual prompts, leveraging user profiles and image characteristics to generate tailored text descriptions. It supports customization through various parameters, including style and embellishment options, to enhance the generated prompts.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image input can be a torch.Tensor, a PIL.Image, or a file path to an image. It serves as the primary visual content for generating the text prompt.

inputs.name: image_prompt
inputs.description: A textual description or directive provided by the user to guide the generation of the text prompt, influencing its thematic direction.

inputs.name: base_ip
inputs.description: The IP address of the server where the model engine is hosted, required for sending the image processing request.

inputs.name: port
inputs.description: The port number on the server for accessing the model engine, used in conjunction with the base IP address.

inputs.name: engine
inputs.description: The name of the engine (e.g., ollama, openai, anthropic) used for generating the text prompt, determining the underlying AI model.

inputs.name: selected_model
inputs.description: The specific model selected for generating the text prompt, chosen from the available models on the specified engine.

inputs.name: profile
inputs.description: A user profile identifier used to select specific settings or preferences for text generation, affecting the style and content of the generated prompts.

inputs.name: embellish_prompt
inputs.description: An optional parameter for adding embellishment to the generated text, enhancing its descriptive quality.

inputs.name: style_prompt
inputs.description: A parameter for specifying the style of the generated text, affecting its tone and presentation.

inputs.name: neg_prompt
inputs.description: A parameter for providing a negative or contrasting prompt, used to generate alternative text descriptions.

inputs.name: temperature
inputs.description: Controls the creativity of the generated text. A higher temperature results in more varied text.

inputs.name: max_tokens
inputs.description: The maximum number of tokens to generate for the text prompt, limiting its length.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: A seed value for the random number generator, ensuring reproducibility of the generated text.

inputs.name: random
inputs.description: A boolean parameter that, when true, uses a random seed for text generation, adding variability to the output.

inputs.name: keep_alive
inputs.description: A boolean parameter indicating whether to keep the model loaded between requests, affecting resource utilization.

outputs.name: Question
outputs.description: A system-generated message or question based on the image prompt and user profile.

outputs.name: Response
outputs.description: The main text description generated from the visual input, incorporating any specified style or embellishment.

outputs.name: Negative
outputs.description: A negative or alternative text prompt, possibly used for contrast or to provide different perspectives.

IF_PromptMkr.description: The IF_PromptMkr node is designed to transform an initial text prompt into a more detailed or stylistically altered prompt, leveraging various AI models and customizations. It enriches the input prompt with embellishments, styles, or negations based on user-selected options, aiming to generate more impactful or contextually appropriate prompts for further processing or creative generation.

inputs.name: input_prompt
inputs.description: The primary text prompt to be transformed. It serves as the base content for generating enriched or stylistically altered prompts.

inputs.name: base_ip
inputs.description: The IP address of the server where the AI model is hosted, used for sending requests to generate the enriched prompt.

inputs.name: port
inputs.description: The port number on the server for accessing the AI model, used in conjunction with the base IP address.

inputs.name: engine
inputs.description: Specifies the AI model engine to use for prompt generation, allowing selection from options like 'ollama', 'openai', or 'anthropic'.

inputs.name: selected_model
inputs.description: The specific AI model selected for generating the prompt, determined dynamically based on the engine, base IP, and port.

inputs.name: profile
inputs.description: The profile setting that influences the generation style or approach, selected from a predefined list of profiles.

inputs.name: embellish_prompt
inputs.description: A selection of embellishments to apply to the input prompt, enhancing its detail or thematic elements.

inputs.name: style_prompt
inputs.description: A selection of styles to apply to the input prompt, altering its presentation or tone.

inputs.name: neg_prompt
inputs.description: A selection of negations to apply to the input prompt, introducing contrast or oppositional elements.

inputs.name: temperature
inputs.description: Controls the creativity or randomness of the generated prompt, with a range from 0.0 (less random) to 1.0 (more random).

inputs.name: max_tokens
inputs.description: The maximum number of tokens to generate for the enriched prompt, setting an upper limit on its length.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: A seed value for the random number generator, ensuring reproducibility of the generated prompt when set.

inputs.name: random
inputs.description: A boolean flag that, when true, uses the seed value for generating the prompt, otherwise uses the temperature setting.

inputs.name: keep_alive
inputs.description: A boolean flag that, when true, keeps the AI model loaded between requests, potentially improving performance.

outputs.name: Question
outputs.description: The original input prompt, returned unchanged.

outputs.name: Response
outputs.description: The enriched or stylistically altered prompt generated based on the input and selected options.

outputs.name: Negative
outputs.description: The negated version of the input prompt, incorporating contrast or oppositional elements.

IF_SaveText.description: The IF_SaveText node is designed for processing and optionally saving text data related to interactions, such as questions, responses, and negative feedback, into various file formats. It encapsulates the functionality to generate unique identifiers for each interaction, format the interaction data, and save it to a file in a specified format and mode, enhancing data management and retrieval for further analysis or record-keeping.

inputs.name: question_input
inputs.description: The question part of the interaction, serving as a key input for generating the interaction record.

inputs.name: response_input
inputs.description: The response to the question, which is crucial for documenting the interaction.

inputs.name: negative_input
inputs.description: Negative feedback or input related to the interaction, providing additional context.

inputs.name: save_file
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether to save the interaction data to a file.

inputs.name: file_format
inputs.description: Specifies the format of the file (csv, txt, json) in which the interaction data will be saved.

inputs.name: save_mode
inputs.description: Determines how the file is saved: create a new file, overwrite an existing file, or append to an existing file.

outputs.name: Question
outputs.description: Returns the question part of the interaction.

outputs.name: Response
outputs.description: Returns the response part of the interaction.

outputs.name: Negative
outputs.description: Returns the negative feedback or input related to the interaction.

outputs.name: Turn
outputs.description: Returns a formatted string containing the interaction's unique identifier, question, response, and negative input.

IG Analyze SSIM.description: The IG Analyze SSIM node is designed to assess the similarity between consecutive images in a given folder using the Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM). It calculates SSIM values for pairs of consecutive images, potentially indicating changes or variations in visual content. Additionally, it visualizes these SSIM values through a plot, providing a graphical representation of similarity trends across the image sequence.

inputs.name: folder
inputs.description: The 'folder' parameter specifies the directory containing the images to be analyzed. It is crucial for determining the set of images on which SSIM calculations and comparisons are performed.

inputs.name: ymin
inputs.description: The 'ymin' parameter sets the minimum value on the y-axis of the SSIM plot, allowing for customization of the plot's vertical scale to better visualize the SSIM data.

inputs.name: ymax
inputs.description: The 'ymax' parameter sets the maximum value on the y-axis of the SSIM plot, enabling adjustment of the plot's vertical scale for optimal visualization of the SSIM trends.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is an image tensor representing the plotted SSIM data between consecutive images. This graphical output provides a visual summary of the structural similarity trends across the image sequence.

IG Cross Fade Images.description: The IG Cross Fade Images node is designed for creating a smooth transition between a sequence of images. It leverages crossfading techniques combined with easing functions to interpolate between images, allowing for customizable transitions in terms of duration and style. This node is particularly useful in generating animations or video effects where a seamless blend from one image to another is desired.

inputs.name: input_images
inputs.description: A list of image tensors to be crossfaded. This parameter is crucial for defining the sequence of images that will undergo the transition process.

inputs.name: interpolation
inputs.description: Determines the easing function applied to the transition, influencing the animation's dynamic and feel.

inputs.name: transitioning_frames
inputs.description: Specifies the number of frames to be used for transitioning between each pair of images, affecting the smoothness and duration of the crossfade effect.

inputs.name: repeat_count
inputs.description: Controls how many times each image is repeated before transitioning to the next, allowing for extended display of certain frames within the sequence.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: A tensor containing the sequence of crossfaded images, ready for visualization or further processing.

IG Explorer.description: The IG Explorer node is designed for navigating and analyzing latent space, facilitating the exploration and manipulation of parameters to generate or modify content.

inputs.name: folder
inputs.description: Specifies the directory containing the job queue and other relevant files for exploration, acting as the starting point for the node's operations.

inputs.name: precision
inputs.description: Determines the level of detail or accuracy in the exploration process, affecting how finely the node examines the latent space.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: Outputs a float value determined through exploration, indicating a specific point or configuration in latent space.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: Provides the filename of the image generated or identified during the exploration process, reflecting the current state of exploration.

IG Float List.description: The IG Float List node is designed for parsing and organizing lists of floating-point numbers from string inputs. It enables precise control over the representation of these numbers, including the selection of specific elements based on index and the formatting of the entire list to a specified number of decimal places. This functionality is essential for tasks that require manipulation and detailed examination of numerical data within a user interface.

inputs.name: index
inputs.description: Specifies the position in the float list from which a single float value will be returned. It plays a crucial role in selecting specific elements for further operations or display.

inputs.name: decimal_places
inputs.description: Determines the number of decimal places to which the float values in the list will be formatted. This allows for precise control over the numerical representation, affecting both the output's appearance and its numerical accuracy.

inputs.name: float_list
inputs.description: The string input containing the list of floats, separated by common delimiters. This input is parsed to create a list of float values, which are then processed according to the specified parameters.

outputs.name: current value
outputs.description: The float value at the specified index within the list. It provides direct access to individual elements, facilitating detailed numerical analysis.

outputs.name: list
outputs.description: The list of parsed float values. This output offers a structured representation of the input data, enabling further numerical operations or analysis.

outputs.name: list text
outputs.description: A list of strings representing the float values formatted to the specified number of decimal places. This output is useful for displaying numerical data in a user-friendly format.

IG Float.description: The IG Float node is designed to handle floating-point numbers within a specified range, allowing for precise numerical inputs in various computational tasks. It serves as a fundamental building block in operations requiring decimal values, facilitating accurate calculations and data manipulation.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: Specifies the floating-point number to be processed. This parameter is crucial for defining the numerical input that the node will handle, directly influencing the output based on the given value.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: Returns the processed floating-point number, which is the same as the input value. This output is essential for further numerical computations or as input to other nodes requiring decimal values.

IG Folder.description: The IG Folder node is designed to construct directory paths based on a specified parent directory and folder name. It abstracts the complexity of path manipulation, providing a straightforward way to generate paths for input or output operations within a file system.

inputs.name: folder_parent
inputs.description: Specifies the parent directory type, which can be either an input or output folder, influencing the base path for the resulting directory path.

inputs.name: folder_name
inputs.description: Defines the name of the folder to be appended to the parent directory path, allowing for dynamic directory creation.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: Returns the fully constructed directory path as a string, ready for use in file system operations.

IG Int.description: The IG Int node is designed to encapsulate and handle integer values within a node-based programming environment. It allows for the specification of an integer value, providing a straightforward way to work with integers in a visual programming context.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: Specifies the integer value to be used or manipulated by the node. This parameter is central to the node's operation, serving as the primary input that determines the node's output.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: Outputs the integer value specified by the input parameter, effectively passing the value through the node.

IG Interpolate.description: The IG Interpolate node is designed to facilitate the exploration of latent space by interpolating between embeddings of input images. It generates a sequence of in-between embeddings that smoothly transition from one image to the next, allowing for the creation of intermediate images that blend the features of the input images. This node is particularly useful for visualizing the path between points in latent space and understanding the underlying structure of the space.

inputs.name: ipadapter
inputs.description: The ipadapter parameter is an interface for integrating with external image processing adapters, essential for configuring the node's interaction with different image processing models.

inputs.name: clip_vision
inputs.description: The clip_vision parameter specifies the CLIP vision model to be used for encoding the input images into embeddings. This model plays a critical role in the interpolation process by providing the necessary embeddings for the input images.

inputs.name: transitioning_frames
inputs.description: The transitioning_frames parameter determines the number of frames to be generated between each pair of input images, directly affecting the smoothness and length of the interpolation sequence.

inputs.name: repeat_count
inputs.description: The repeat_count parameter controls the number of times each interpolated embedding is repeated in the output sequence, allowing for the adjustment of the pacing and duration of the visual transition between images.

inputs.name: interpolation
inputs.description: The interpolation parameter selects the method of interpolation (e.g., linear, ease_in, etc.) to be used for transitioning between embeddings, influencing the dynamics of the transition.

inputs.name: buffer
inputs.description: The buffer parameter specifies the number of repetitions for the first and last embeddings in the sequence, creating a 'buffer' period at the start and end of the interpolation. This helps in creating smoother transitions and more coherent visualizations of the interpolation path.

inputs.name: input_images1
inputs.description: The input_images1 parameter is the first set of images for which embeddings are to be interpolated, serving as one of the starting points for the interpolation process.

inputs.name: input_images2
inputs.description: The input_images2 parameter is the second set of images for which embeddings are to be interpolated, serving as another starting point for the interpolation process.

inputs.name: input_images3
inputs.description: The input_images3 parameter is the third set of images for which embeddings are to be interpolated, providing additional starting points for the interpolation process.

inputs.name: positive_prompts
inputs.description: The positive_prompts parameter is a collection of text prompts that describe desired attributes or features to be emphasized in the interpolated images.

inputs.name: negative_prompts
inputs.description: The negative_prompts parameter is a collection of text prompts that describe undesired attributes or features to be minimized in the interpolated images.

outputs.name: pos_embeds1
outputs.description: The pos_embeds1 output represents the interpolated embeddings corresponding to the first set of input images.

outputs.name: pos_embeds2
outputs.description: The pos_embeds2 output represents the interpolated embeddings corresponding to the second set of input images.

outputs.name: pos_embeds3
outputs.description: The pos_embeds3 output represents the interpolated embeddings corresponding to the third set of input images.

outputs.name: neg_embeds
outputs.description: The neg_embeds output represents the embeddings generated without conditioning on the input images, used for comparison or as a baseline in the interpolation process.

outputs.name: positive_string
outputs.description: The positive_string output is a formatted string of positive prompts, structured to facilitate their integration into the interpolation process.

outputs.name: negative_string
outputs.description: The negative_string output is a formatted string of negative prompts, structured to facilitate their integration into the interpolation process.

outputs.name: ipadapter
outputs.description: The ipadapter output returns the configured image processing adapter used in the node, providing context for the interpolation process.

outputs.name: BATCH_SIZE
outputs.description: The BATCH_SIZE output indicates the total number of embeddings generated during the interpolation process, reflecting the scale of the operation.

outputs.name: FRAMES_TO_DROP
outputs.description: The FRAMES_TO_DROP output lists specific frames that should be omitted from the final interpolated sequence to optimize the visual transition.

IG Load Image.description: The IG Load Image node is designed for loading images from a specified directory, providing functionality to handle image preprocessing such as orientation correction, conversion to a specific color mode, and normalization. It abstracts the complexities of image loading and preprocessing, making it easier to integrate image data into workflows.

inputs.name: image_path
inputs.description: The 'image_path' parameter specifies the path to the image to be loaded. It plays a crucial role in determining which image file will be processed, affecting the node's execution and the resulting image data.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The 'image' parameter represents the preprocessed image data, ready for further processing or analysis.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The 'mask' parameter provides a mask for the loaded image, useful for operations that require segmentation or specific area processing.

IG Load Images.description: The IG Load Images From Folder node is designed for efficiently loading multiple images from a specified folder, offering options to limit the number of images loaded, skip a certain number of initial images, and select images at a specified interval. This functionality is crucial for managing and preprocessing large datasets of images for further analysis or processing within a pipeline.

inputs.name: folder
inputs.description: Specifies the directory from which images are to be loaded. This is a required input that determines the source of the images.

inputs.name: image_load_cap
inputs.description: Limits the number of images to be loaded from the folder. If set to 0, there is no limit.

inputs.name: skip_first_images
inputs.description: Skips a specified number of images from the beginning of the folder. Useful for starting the loading process from a certain point.

inputs.name: select_every_nth
inputs.description: Loads every nth image from the folder, allowing for selective loading of images at regular intervals.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The loaded images from the specified folder.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The masks associated with the loaded images, if available.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: The total number of images loaded from the folder.

IG Multiply.description: The IG Multiply node performs multiplication of two floating-point values, providing a straightforward way to compute the product of two numbers within a graphical programming environment.

inputs.name: Value_A
inputs.description: Specifies the first floating-point value to be multiplied. Its range is virtually unlimited, allowing for a wide variety of numerical inputs.

inputs.name: Value_B
inputs.description: Determines the second floating-point value to be multiplied. Similar to Value_A, it supports a broad range of numerical inputs, enabling diverse multiplication scenarios.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The result of multiplying the input values Value_A and Value_B, returned as a floating-point number.

IG Path Join.description: The IG Path Join node is designed to concatenate two string paths into a single path string, facilitating file and directory path construction within a workflow.

inputs.name: first
inputs.description: Specifies the first part of the path to be joined. It forms the base to which the second part will be appended.

inputs.name: second
inputs.description: Defines the second part of the path to be joined to the first. This addition completes the construction of the full path.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The complete path string resulting from the concatenation of the first and second input strings.

IG String List.description: The IG String List node is designed to split a multiline string input into a list of strings based on newline characters and return a specific string from the list and the entire list itself. It allows for dynamic text manipulation and retrieval within a user-defined list, facilitating operations on collections of strings.

inputs.name: index
inputs.description: Specifies the position in the list of strings to retrieve the specific string. It determines which string to return based on its position in the list, enhancing the node's flexibility in accessing elements.

inputs.name: string_list
inputs.description: A multiline string input that the node splits into a list of strings based on newline characters. This input is essential for creating the string list that the node operates on, enabling dynamic text manipulation.

outputs.name: current value
outputs.description: Returns the string at the specified index from the list of strings, allowing for targeted retrieval of text.

outputs.name: list
outputs.description: Returns the entire list of strings derived from the input multiline string, providing access to all split text elements.

IG String.description: The IG String node is designed to handle string inputs, allowing users to input and pass through string values within a node-based processing environment. It serves as a fundamental building block for operations requiring textual data.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: This parameter accepts a string value, serving as the primary input for the node. It enables the node to process and pass through the input string without modification.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: Outputs the input string value unchanged, facilitating its use in subsequent nodes or operations.

IG ZFill.description: The IG ZFill node is designed to pad a given integer value with zeros up to a specified length. It is useful for formatting numbers to ensure they meet a certain string length requirement, enhancing readability or meeting specific data format standards.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: The integer value to be padded with leading zeros. This parameter determines the number to be formatted.

inputs.name: fill
inputs.description: Specifies the total length of the resulting string after padding with zeros. It determines how many leading zeros are added to the input value.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The formatted string with the input value padded with leading zeros to meet the specified total length.

AdainFilterLatent.description: The AdainFilterLatent node applies an adaptive instance normalization (AdaIN) technique to latent representations, using a reference latent to adjust the style of the input latent. It supports adjusting the intensity of the effect through a factor and allows for varying the filter size to control the granularity of the style transfer.

inputs.name: latents
inputs.description: The input latent representations to be stylized. This is the primary data that will undergo style adjustment based on the reference latent.

inputs.name: reference
inputs.description: The reference latent representation used to derive style characteristics that will be applied to the input latents.

inputs.name: filter_size
inputs.description: Determines the size of the filter used in the style transfer process, affecting the granularity of the applied style.

inputs.name: factor
inputs.description: Controls the intensity of the style transfer effect, allowing for blending between the original and stylized representations.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The stylized latent representations after applying the adaptive instance normalization process.

AdainImage.description: The AdainImage node applies the Adaptive Instance Normalization (AdaIN) technique to a batch of images, using a reference image to adjust the style of the input images. This process involves normalizing the input images based on the statistical properties (mean and standard deviation) of the reference image, allowing for style transfer at a given intensity level.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The input images to be stylized. These are the primary subjects for the style transfer process.

inputs.name: reference
inputs.description: The reference image used to derive style characteristics (mean and standard deviation) for the style transfer.

inputs.name: factor
inputs.description: A factor controlling the intensity of the style transfer, allowing for blending between the original and stylized images.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The stylized images, after applying the Adaptive Instance Normalization technique.

AdainLatent.description: AdainLatent is designed to perform adaptive instance normalization on latent representations by aligning the mean and standard deviation of a target latent space with those of a reference latent space, modulated by a specified factor. This process facilitates the transfer of style characteristics from the reference to the target latents, enabling style manipulation and consistency in generative models.

inputs.name: latents
inputs.description: The target latent representations to be normalized. This input is crucial for determining the base content or structure upon which style characteristics from the reference will be imposed.

inputs.name: reference
inputs.description: The reference latent representations providing the style characteristics to be transferred. This input is essential for defining the style attributes to be applied to the target latents.

inputs.name: factor
inputs.description: A modulation factor that controls the extent to which the style characteristics from the reference are applied to the target latents. It allows for fine-tuning the balance between preserving the original content and applying the new style.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The modified latent representations after applying adaptive instance normalization, reflecting the style characteristics of the reference with the original content of the target latents.

AlphaClean.description: The AlphaClean node is designed for image preprocessing, specifically targeting the enhancement and cleaning of image alpha channels. It employs techniques such as bilateral filtering, Gaussian blurring, and dynamic thresholding to refine the transparency and edges of images, making it particularly useful in graphics and image processing applications where precise alpha manipulation is required.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The input images to be processed, expected to have their alpha channels cleaned and enhanced.

inputs.name: radius
inputs.description: Specifies the radius for Gaussian blurring, affecting the smoothness of the alpha channel's edges.

inputs.name: fill_holes
inputs.description: Determines whether and how much to fill holes in the alpha channel, enhancing image completeness.

inputs.name: white_threshold
inputs.description: Sets the threshold for considering a pixel as white, aiding in the separation of foreground from background.

inputs.name: extra_clip
inputs.description: Applies an additional clipping factor to the image, adjusting the intensity of the cleaning effect.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The processed images with cleaned and enhanced alpha channels, ready for further use or display.

AlphaMatte.description: The AlphaMatte node is designed for advanced image processing, specifically focusing on extracting and refining the alpha matte of images. It utilizes deep learning techniques to accurately separate foreground from background, even in complex scenes, by analyzing images alongside their alpha trimaps. This node is capable of handling pre-blurring, adjusting black and white points, and performing iterative refinements to achieve high-quality matte extraction.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The input images for which the alpha matte needs to be extracted. This parameter is crucial as it directly influences the quality and accuracy of the matte extraction process.

inputs.name: alpha_trimap
inputs.description: A trimap providing an initial guess of the foreground, background, and unknown areas, which guides the matte extraction process.

inputs.name: preblur
inputs.description: Specifies the amount of pre-blurring applied to the trimap to smooth out hard edges and improve the matte extraction.

inputs.name: blackpoint
inputs.description: The black point value used to adjust the contrast of the trimap, aiding in clearer separation of the foreground from the background.

inputs.name: whitepoint
inputs.description: The white point value for adjusting the trimap's brightness, enhancing the distinction between foreground and background areas.

inputs.name: max_iterations
inputs.description: The maximum number of iterations allowed for refining the alpha matte, ensuring a balance between quality and computational efficiency.

inputs.name: estimate_fg
inputs.description: A flag indicating whether to estimate the foreground in addition to the alpha matte, providing a more complete separation of image elements.

outputs.name: alpha
outputs.description: The extracted alpha matte, representing the transparency levels of the foreground elements in the image.

outputs.name: fg
outputs.description: The estimated foreground of the image, obtained when the estimate_fg flag is true.

outputs.name: bg
outputs.description: The estimated background of the image, useful for compositing or further processing.

BatchAlign.description: The `BatchAlign` node is designed to align multiple batches of data, ensuring consistency and uniformity across different sets of inputs. It focuses on adjusting the alignment of data batches to facilitate more coherent processing or analysis downstream.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The images to be aligned, typically involving multiple frames or batches that require alignment for further processing.

inputs.name: ref_frame
inputs.description: A reference frame or image against which other images are aligned. This serves as the baseline for alignment adjustments.

inputs.name: direction
inputs.description: Specifies the direction of alignment, potentially influencing how images are adjusted relative to the reference frame.

inputs.name: blur
inputs.description: Determines the level of blur applied during the alignment process, affecting the smoothness or sharpness of the aligned images.

outputs.name: aligned
outputs.description: The result of aligning the input images, producing a coherent set of images aligned with the reference frame.

outputs.name: flow
outputs.description: A flow field or map indicating the transformation applied to each image for alignment, useful for understanding the alignment process.

BatchAverageImage.description: The BatchAverageImage node applies statistical averaging operations, such as mean or median, across a batch of images. This process is used to create a single representative image from a collection, either by calculating the mean or median pixel values across all images in the batch.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The collection of images to be processed. This parameter is crucial for determining the input data over which the averaging operation will be performed.

inputs.name: operation
inputs.description: Specifies the type of averaging operation to apply on the batch of images, such as 'mean' or 'median'. This choice directly influences the resulting output image.

outputs.name: image
