outputs.description: The output image after applying the specified averaging operation across the input batch of images. It represents a statistical summary of the input batch.

BatchAverageUnJittered.description: This node is designed to process a batch of images by applying an averaging or median operation to reduce jittering effects. It operates on sub-batches of images, applying the specified operation to create a smoother, more stable output image.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The batch of images to be processed. This input is crucial for determining the set of images on which the averaging or median operation will be applied.

inputs.name: operation
inputs.description: Specifies the operation ('mean' or 'median') to be applied across the images. This choice affects the method of jitter reduction and the final appearance of the output image.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The processed batch of images after applying the specified averaging or median operation to reduce jittering effects.

BatchNormalizeImage.description: The BatchNormalizeImage node is designed to normalize a batch of images based on a given factor, adjusting each image's pixel values to have a standard deviation and mean that aligns more closely with the batch's overall characteristics. This process enhances the consistency of image data, making it more suitable for further processing or analysis.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The 'images' parameter represents the batch of images to be normalized. It is crucial for the normalization process as it directly influences the computation of mean and standard deviation used for normalization.

inputs.name: factor
inputs.description: The 'factor' parameter controls the extent to which the original images are blended with their normalized versions. It plays a significant role in determining the final appearance of the normalized images.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is a batch of images that have been normalized according to the specified factor, potentially enhancing their suitability for further image processing tasks.

BatchNormalizeLatent.description: This node applies batch normalization to latent representations, adjusting each latent sample's distribution towards a standard distribution, thereby stabilizing and potentially improving the generative process.

inputs.name: latents
inputs.description: The latent representations to be normalized. This input is crucial for the normalization process as it directly modifies the distribution of these latents.

inputs.name: factor
inputs.description: A scaling factor that interpolates between the original and normalized latent representations, allowing for controlled adjustment of the normalization effect.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The normalized latent representations, adjusted according to the specified factor to potentially enhance generative model performance.

BetterFilmGrain.description: The BetterFilmGrain node enhances images by applying a customizable film grain effect, simulating the texture and appearance of traditional film photography. It allows for fine-tuning of the grain's scale, strength, saturation, and overall tone to achieve a desired aesthetic.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to which the film grain effect will be applied. It serves as the base for the grain texture overlay.

inputs.name: scale
inputs.description: Determines the scale of the grain particles, affecting their size relative to the image. A smaller scale results in finer grain.

inputs.name: strength
inputs.description: Controls the intensity of the grain effect, with higher values making the grain more pronounced.

inputs.name: saturation
inputs.description: Adjusts the color saturation of the grain effect, allowing for more or less colorful grain textures.

inputs.name: toe
inputs.description: Modifies the toe of the film response curve, affecting the shadow tones and overall contrast of the grain effect.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: A seed value for random number generation, ensuring reproducibility of the grain pattern.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image with the applied film grain effect, showcasing enhanced texture and a film-like aesthetic.

BilateralFilterImage.description: The BilateralFilterImage node applies a bilateral filter to images, a process that reduces noise while preserving edges. This technique is particularly useful for creating smoother images without blurring important features, making it ideal for enhancing image quality in a nuanced manner.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The images to be filtered. This input is crucial for defining the visual content that will undergo the bilateral filtering process.

inputs.name: size
inputs.description: Specifies the diameter of the pixel neighborhood used for the filter. A larger size can lead to more significant smoothing and noise reduction.

inputs.name: sigma_color
inputs.description: Controls the filter's sensitivity to color differences. Higher values allow more colors to be mixed within the pixel neighborhood.

inputs.name: sigma_space
inputs.description: Determines the spatial extent of the filter. Higher values mean that farther pixels will influence each other as long as their colors are close enough.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The filtered image, which has undergone bilateral filtering to reduce noise while preserving edges.

BlurImageFast.description: The BlurImageFast node provides a fast and efficient way to apply Gaussian blur to images. It is designed to blur images by specifying the radius of the blur in both the x and y directions, allowing for customizable blur effects.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The 'images' parameter represents the images to be blurred. It is crucial for defining the input images on which the Gaussian blur effect will be applied.

inputs.name: radius_x
inputs.description: The 'radius_x' parameter specifies the horizontal radius of the Gaussian blur. It determines the extent of blurring along the x-axis of the images.

inputs.name: radius_y
inputs.description: The 'radius_y' parameter specifies the vertical radius of the Gaussian blur. It determines the extent of blurring along the y-axis of the images.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is a blurred version of the input images, achieved through Gaussian blurring as specified by the radius_x and radius_y parameters.

BlurMaskFast.description: The BlurMaskFast node is designed to apply a Gaussian blur to masks, allowing for the softening of edges and the creation of a smoother mask appearance. This operation is particularly useful in image processing tasks where the harshness of mask boundaries needs to be reduced.

inputs.name: masks
inputs.description: Specifies the masks to be blurred. This input is crucial for defining the areas within the image where the blur effect will be applied.

inputs.name: radius_x
inputs.description: Determines the horizontal radius of the Gaussian blur. A larger radius results in a more pronounced blur effect horizontally.

inputs.name: radius_y
inputs.description: Determines the vertical radius of the Gaussian blur. A larger radius results in a more pronounced blur effect vertically.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The output is a mask that has been smoothed by the Gaussian blur process, with softer edges compared to the original.

ClampOutliers.description: The ClampOutliers node is designed to adjust the values of latent representations by clamping outliers based on a specified standard deviation threshold. This process aims to normalize the data, reducing the impact of extreme values on the overall distribution.

inputs.name: latents
inputs.description: The 'latents' parameter represents the latent representations to be adjusted. It is crucial for determining which data points are considered outliers and subsequently clamped.

inputs.name: std_dev
inputs.description: The 'std_dev' parameter specifies the threshold for clamping based on standard deviations from the mean. It controls the extent to which outliers are adjusted, impacting the normalization of the data.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: Returns the adjusted latent representations with outliers clamped according to the specified standard deviation threshold.

ColorMatchImage.description: The ColorMatchImage node is designed for advanced image processing, specifically focusing on matching the color distribution of one image to another. This process is essential for tasks that require the integration of images from different sources to ensure visual consistency across them. The node offers options for selecting the type and intensity of the blur applied during the color matching process, allowing for flexible adaptation to various image characteristics.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The input images whose color distribution needs to be matched to the reference image. This parameter is crucial for defining the source images on which color matching will be performed.

inputs.name: reference
inputs.description: The reference image to which the color distribution of the input images will be matched. It serves as the target for color matching, guiding the adjustment process.

inputs.name: blur_type
inputs.description: Specifies the type of blur to be applied during the color matching process, such as Gaussian blur or guided filter, affecting the smoothness and detail preservation.

inputs.name: blur_size
inputs.description: The size of the blur filter to be applied, determining the extent of blurring and its impact on the color matching process.

inputs.name: factor
inputs.description: A factor controlling the intensity of the color matching effect, allowing for fine-tuning the balance between the original and matched colors.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image with its color distribution matched to the reference image, integrating seamlessly with the target visual context.

ConvertNormals.description: The `ConvertNormals` node is designed to transform normal maps between different formats, adjust their scale, and optionally normalize or fill missing areas. It supports various input and output modes, allowing for flexible adaptation of normal maps to suit different rendering or processing requirements. This node is particularly useful in graphics and image processing pipelines where normal maps need to be converted or adjusted for specific uses.

inputs.name: normals
inputs.description: The input normal map tensor to be transformed. This parameter is central to the node's operation, as it undergoes various transformations based on the other input parameters.

inputs.name: input_mode
inputs.description: Specifies the format of the input normal map, influencing how it is initially processed. This parameter determines the initial adjustments made to the normal map before further transformations.

inputs.name: output_mode
inputs.description: Defines the desired format for the output normal map, guiding the final adjustments made to the tensor. This parameter ensures the transformed normal map meets specific format requirements.

inputs.name: scale_XY
inputs.description: A scaling factor applied to the X and Y components of the normal map, affecting its overall appearance. This parameter allows for fine-tuning the visual impact of the normal map on surfaces.

inputs.name: normalize
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether the normal map should be normalized after transformations. Normalization ensures the normal map's vectors are unit length, often required for consistent lighting effects.

inputs.name: fix_black
inputs.description: A boolean flag that, when enabled, applies a correction to black areas in the normal map, potentially filling these areas based on the `optional_fill` parameter. This is useful for repairing or enhancing normal maps with missing data.

inputs.name: optional_fill
inputs.description: An optional tensor used to fill black areas in the normal map if `fix_black` is enabled. This parameter allows for custom fill patterns or colors to be applied, enhancing the versatility of the node.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The transformed normal map tensor, adjusted according to the specified input and output modes, scaling, normalization, and optional filling. This output is ready for use in subsequent processing or rendering steps.

DifferenceChecker.description: The DifferenceChecker node is designed to compute the absolute difference between two images, scaled by a specified multiplier. This functionality is useful for highlighting differences or changes between two images, which can be applied in various image processing and analysis tasks.

inputs.name: images1
inputs.description: The first set of images to compare. This input is crucial for determining the baseline for comparison.

inputs.name: images2
inputs.description: The second set of images to compare against the first set. This input is essential for identifying the differences from the baseline.

inputs.name: multiplier
inputs.description: A scaling factor applied to the computed differences, allowing for adjustment of the difference intensity.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is an image or a set of images representing the scaled absolute difference between the input images.

DilateErodeMask.description: The DilateErodeMask node is designed to modify mask images by either dilating or eroding them, based on the specified radius and shape. This process adjusts the boundaries of objects within the mask, either expanding or contracting them to achieve the desired morphological effect.

inputs.name: masks
inputs.description: Specifies the mask images to be processed. The modification of these masks through dilation or erosion alters the boundaries of the objects they contain, depending on the operation's parameters.

inputs.name: radius
inputs.description: Determines the extent of the dilation or erosion effect. A positive radius dilates the mask, expanding object boundaries, while a negative radius erodes the mask, contracting them.

inputs.name: shape
inputs.description: Defines the shape of the structuring element used in the dilation or erosion process. This can be either a 'box' or a 'circle', influencing the morphological transformation's nature.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The modified mask image after applying the dilation or erosion operation, reflecting the adjusted boundaries of objects within the mask.

EnhanceDetail.description: The EnhanceDetail node is designed to improve the visual quality of images by applying a series of filters that enhance details, adjust sharpness, and potentially reduce noise. It operates by manipulating the image's details relative to its guided filter output, allowing for refined control over the enhancement process.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The input images to be enhanced. This parameter is crucial as it directly influences the enhancement process by serving as the base for all subsequent operations.

inputs.name: filter_radius
inputs.description: Specifies the radius of the filter applied during the enhancement process. A larger radius can lead to more pronounced detail enhancement but may also introduce more processing time.

inputs.name: sigma
inputs.description: Controls the sigma parameter of the guided filter, affecting the degree of smoothing and detail preservation.

inputs.name: denoise
inputs.description: Determines the strength of the denoising filter. A higher value can reduce noise but may also diminish fine details.

inputs.name: detail_mult
inputs.description: A multiplier for the detail enhancement. Adjusting this value allows for fine-tuning the intensity of the detail enhancement effect.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output of the node, which are the images after the enhancement process. These images are expected to have improved detail and potentially reduced noise.

ExposureAdjust.description: The ExposureAdjust node is designed to modify the exposure of images by adjusting their brightness levels. It supports different input and output color modes, and optionally applies tonemapping to adjust the dynamic range of the images.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The input images to be adjusted for exposure. This parameter is crucial for defining the visual content that will undergo exposure correction.

inputs.name: stops
inputs.description: Determines the exposure adjustment level. Positive values increase exposure (making the image brighter), while negative values decrease it (making the image darker).

inputs.name: input_mode
inputs.description: Specifies the color space of the input images, either 'sRGB' or 'linear', affecting how exposure adjustments are applied.

inputs.name: output_mode
inputs.description: Defines the color space for the output images, allowing for flexibility in integrating the adjusted images into various workflows.

inputs.name: use_tonemap
inputs.description: A boolean flag that indicates whether tonemapping should be applied to the images, useful for handling high dynamic range content.

inputs.name: tonemap_scale
inputs.description: Adjusts the scale of the tonemapping effect, providing control over the dynamic range compression of the images.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output images with adjusted exposure, potentially in a different color space and with optional tonemapping applied.

FrequencyCombine.description: The FrequencyCombine node is designed to blend high and low-frequency image components using specified mathematical operations. It enables the enhancement or modification of images by combining frequency elements in unique ways, offering a method to manipulate image textures and details.

inputs.name: high_frequency
inputs.description: The high-frequency component of an image, representing details such as edges and textures. It plays a crucial role in defining the sharpness and detail of the combined output.

inputs.name: low_frequency
inputs.description: The low-frequency component of an image, encapsulating broad features and color gradients. It forms the base upon which high-frequency details are added or modified.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Specifies the mathematical operation ('subtract' or 'divide') to combine high and low-frequency components, affecting the texture and detail enhancement of the output image.

inputs.name: eps
inputs.description: A small epsilon value used in the 'divide' mode to prevent division by zero, ensuring numerical stability.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The resulting image after combining high and low-frequency components, showcasing enhanced or altered textures and details.

FrequencySeparate.description: The FrequencySeparate node is designed for image processing, specifically to separate the high-frequency components from an image by either subtracting or dividing the low-frequency components. This operation is useful for tasks that require manipulation or analysis of an image's texture or fine details without affecting the overall structure.

inputs.name: original
inputs.description: The original image from which high-frequency components are to be extracted. It plays a crucial role in determining the texture and fine details to be separated.

inputs.name: low_frequency
inputs.description: The low-frequency component of the image, used as a basis for extracting high-frequency details by comparison with the original image.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Determines the method of separation (either 'subtract' or 'divide'), affecting how the high-frequency components are calculated from the original image.

inputs.name: eps
inputs.description: A small epsilon value to prevent division by zero when 'divide' mode is selected, ensuring numerical stability.

outputs.name: high_frequency
outputs.description: The high-frequency component of the image, representing the texture and fine details separated from the original image.

GameOfLife.description: The GameOfLife node simulates the Conway's Game of Life, a cellular automaton, over a specified number of steps. It evolves the state of a grid based on the rules of survival, death, and birth determined by the neighboring cells.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Specifies the width of the grid for the simulation, affecting the horizontal size of the cellular automaton.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Specifies the height of the grid for the simulation, affecting the vertical size of the cellular automaton.

inputs.name: cell_size
inputs.description: Determines the size of each cell in the grid, influencing the resolution of the simulation.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: A seed value for random number generation, ensuring reproducibility of the grid's initial state.

inputs.name: threshold
inputs.description: A threshold value to determine the initial state of each cell in the grid, based on random generation.

inputs.name: steps
inputs.description: The number of steps to simulate, dictating the duration of the Game of Life evolution.

inputs.name: optional_start
inputs.description: An optional parameter to specify the initial state of the grid, allowing for custom starting configurations.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The final state of the grid after the specified number of steps, represented as an image.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: A binary mask indicating the cells that changed state in the last step of the simulation.

outputs.name: off
outputs.description: A mask indicating cells that turned off in the last step of the simulation.

outputs.name: on
outputs.description: A mask indicating cells that turned on in the last step of the simulation.

GuidedFilterAlpha.description: The GuidedFilterAlpha node applies a guided filter to an image using a specified alpha mask. This process smooths the image while preserving edge details, guided by the alpha mask. It's designed for enhancing images or compositing tasks where maintaining edge integrity is crucial.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The input images to be filtered. This parameter is crucial for defining the visual content that will undergo the guided filtering process.

inputs.name: alpha
inputs.description: The alpha mask used to guide the filtering process. It influences how the filtering is applied, particularly around edges, to preserve details.

inputs.name: filter_radius
inputs.description: Defines the radius of the filter. A larger radius increases the area of influence for smoothing, affecting the level of detail preservation.

inputs.name: sigma
inputs.description: Controls the degree of smoothing. Higher values result in more aggressive smoothing, affecting the filter's sensitivity to edges.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The filtered image, where the guided filter has been applied according to the alpha mask and other parameters.

GuidedFilterImage.description: The GuidedFilterImage node applies a guided filter to a batch of images using a guide image to enhance the output images' details while preserving edges. This process involves adjusting the images based on the spatial correlations indicated by the guide image, making it suitable for tasks like smoothing, detail enhancement, or noise reduction.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The batch of images to be filtered. This input is crucial for determining the content that will undergo the guided filtering process.

inputs.name: guide
inputs.description: The guide image used to direct the filtering process. It plays a key role in determining how the filtering is applied across different regions of the input images.

inputs.name: size
inputs.description: Specifies the size of the kernel used for the guided filter. A larger size can lead to more pronounced smoothing and edge preservation.

inputs.name: sigma
inputs.description: Controls the degree of smoothing in the guided filtering process. Higher values result in stronger smoothing effects.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The filtered images, which have undergone guided filtering to enhance details while preserving edges.

ImageConstant.description: The ImageConstant node is designed to generate images of a constant color. It allows for the specification of the color in RGB format, along with the image dimensions and batch size, enabling the creation of multiple images with the same color specifications in a single operation.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Specifies the width of the generated images. It influences the horizontal dimension of the output images.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Determines the height of the generated images, affecting their vertical dimension.

inputs.name: batch_size
inputs.description: Indicates the number of images to generate in one batch, allowing for multiple images to be created at once.

inputs.name: red
inputs.description: Sets the red component of the constant color for the generated images.

inputs.name: green
inputs.description: Defines the green component of the constant color for the generated images.

inputs.name: blue
inputs.description: Specifies the blue component of the constant color for the generated images.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is an image or a batch of images with the specified constant color in RGB format.

ImageConstantHSV.description: The ImageConstantHSV node generates constant color images based on specified HSV (Hue, Saturation, Value) color values. It allows for the creation of uniform color images with adjustable color properties, enabling the generation of images with precise color tones.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Specifies the width of the generated image. It determines the horizontal dimension of the output image.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Specifies the height of the generated image. It determines the vertical dimension of the output image.

inputs.name: batch_size
inputs.description: Determines the number of images to generate in a single batch. This allows for the generation of multiple images with the same color properties simultaneously.

inputs.name: hue
inputs.description: Sets the hue component of the HSV color model for the image, defining the color tone.

inputs.name: saturation
inputs.description: Sets the saturation component of the HSV color model, controlling the intensity of the color.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: Sets the value component of the HSV color model, determining the brightness of the color.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The generated image(s) with constant color based on the specified HSV values.

InstructPixToPixConditioningAdvanced.description: This node is designed for advanced conditioning in Pix2Pix models, enabling the manipulation and transformation of image data through a sophisticated encoding process. It facilitates the integration of additional conditioning inputs and scales, allowing for more nuanced control over the generation process.

inputs.name: positive
inputs.description: Specifies the positive conditioning elements, influencing the encoding process to favor certain outcomes.

inputs.name: negative
inputs.description: Specifies the negative conditioning elements, influencing the encoding process to avoid certain outcomes.

inputs.name: new
inputs.description: Represents the new input data to be encoded, providing a basis for the generation.

inputs.name: new_scale
inputs.description: A scaling factor for the new input data, adjusting its influence in the encoding process.

inputs.name: original
inputs.description: Represents the original input data, serving as a reference or baseline in the encoding process.

inputs.name: original_scale
inputs.description: A scaling factor for the original input data, adjusting its influence in the encoding process.

outputs.name: cond1
outputs.description: Outputs the modified positive conditioning elements after encoding.

outputs.name: cond2
outputs.description: Outputs the modified negative conditioning elements after encoding.

outputs.name: negative
outputs.description: Outputs the unaltered negative conditioning elements, maintaining their original state post-encoding.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: Generates a new latent representation based on the encoded inputs and scales.

JitterImage.description: The `JitterImage` node applies a jitter effect to images, transforming them by applying a series of affine transformations to simulate camera or object movement. This effect can enhance the robustness of models to variations in input data or be used for data augmentation.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The input images to which the jitter effect will be applied. This parameter is crucial for defining the visual content that will undergo transformation.

inputs.name: jitter_scale
inputs.description: Defines the scale of the jitter effect, adjusting the intensity of the transformations applied to the images. This parameter allows for fine-tuning the extent of the jitter effect.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output images after the jitter effect has been applied, showcasing the transformed visual content.

Keyer.description: The Keyer node is designed for image processing, specifically to apply keying operations that selectively adjust the transparency of image areas based on color and brightness criteria. It allows for sophisticated manipulation of images, enabling the creation or modification of alpha channels to achieve effects like background removal or compositing.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The images to be processed, serving as the primary input for keying operations. This parameter is crucial for defining which images undergo the keying process.

inputs.name: operation
inputs.description: Specifies the keying operation to be performed, affecting how the images' colors and brightness levels are evaluated for transparency.

inputs.name: low
inputs.description: Defines the lower threshold for the keying operation, determining the minimum value for pixels to be considered transparent.

inputs.name: high
inputs.description: Sets the upper threshold for the keying operation, establishing the maximum value for pixels to be considered transparent.

inputs.name: gamma
inputs.description: Adjusts the gamma value for the keying operation, influencing the mid-tone contrast and overall appearance of the keyed image.

inputs.name: premult
inputs.description: Determines whether the output images should be pre-multiplied with their alpha channel, affecting the blending behavior in compositing workflows.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The processed image after the keying operation, with adjusted transparency based on the specified criteria.

outputs.name: alpha
outputs.description: The alpha channel generated or modified by the keying operation, representing the transparency levels of the processed image.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: A mask derived from the keying operation, indicating areas of transparency and opacity within the image.

LatentNormalizeShuffle.description: This node is designed to normalize and shuffle the latent representations of images, ensuring they are prepared for further processing or generation tasks. It adjusts the latent vectors to have a standard distribution and rearranges them to introduce variability, optimizing the input for diverse image generation outcomes.

inputs.name: latents
inputs.description: The 'latents' input represents the latent representations of images to be normalized and shuffled. This process ensures that the data is standardized and randomized, which is crucial for achieving varied and high-quality image generation results.

inputs.name: flatten
inputs.description: The 'flatten' input specifies whether the latent representations should be flattened as part of the normalization process, affecting the structure of the data for subsequent operations.

inputs.name: normalize
inputs.description: The 'normalize' input determines whether the latent representations undergo normalization, adjusting their scale and distribution for consistent processing.

inputs.name: shuffle
inputs.description: The 'shuffle' input indicates whether the latent representations should be shuffled, introducing randomness and variability into the dataset for enhanced diversity in generation.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The output 'latent' are the normalized and shuffled latent representations, ready for use in subsequent image generation tasks. This ensures that the input data is optimally prepared for producing diverse and high-quality images.

LatentStats.description: The LatentStats node is designed to analyze and report statistics of latent representations in a neural network model. It calculates and prints various statistical measures such as mean, standard deviation, minimum, and maximum values for different components of the latent space, providing insights into the characteristics of the data being processed.

inputs.name: latent
inputs.description: The 'latent' parameter represents the latent representations to be analyzed. It is crucial for the node's operation as it directly influences the statistical calculations and the resulting output.

outputs.name: stats
outputs.description: A string summarizing the statistical analysis of the latent representations, including batch size, dimensions, and statistics for each component.

outputs.name: c0_mean
outputs.description: The mean value of the first component in the latent representations.

outputs.name: c1_mean
outputs.description: The mean value of the second component in the latent representations.

outputs.name: c2_mean
outputs.description: The mean value of the third component in the latent representations.

outputs.name: c3_mean
outputs.description: The mean value of the fourth component in the latent representations.

MedianFilterImage.description: The MedianFilterImage node applies a median filter to a batch of images, smoothing them by replacing each pixel's value with the median value of the intensities in its neighborhood. This process is particularly effective at reducing salt-and-pepper noise while preserving edges, making it a valuable tool for image preprocessing and noise reduction.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The 'images' parameter represents the batch of images to be processed. It is crucial for defining the input data on which the median filtering operation will be performed, directly influencing the output's quality and effectiveness.

inputs.name: size
inputs.description: The 'size' parameter determines the size of the neighborhood used for calculating the median value for each pixel. It affects the degree of smoothing and noise reduction, with larger sizes leading to more pronounced filtering effects.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is a batch of images that have been smoothed using the median filter. This process reduces noise while preserving the essential structure and edges of the images.

NormalMapSimple.description: The NormalMapSimple node is designed to generate normal maps from images, applying a transformation that simulates the appearance of surface variations and depth based on lighting. It utilizes image gradients to create a texture that represents the orientation of the surface in three-dimensional space, enhancing the visual perception of depth in 2D images.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The 'images' input represents the source images for which normal maps are to be generated. This input is crucial for determining the texture and depth information that will be transformed into a normal map.

inputs.name: scale_XY
inputs.description: The 'scale_XY' parameter adjusts the intensity of the surface variation effect in the generated normal map. A higher value increases the perceived depth by scaling the x and y components of the normal vectors.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is a transformed version of the input images, represented as normal maps. These maps encode the surface orientation and depth information, enhancing the 3D appearance of the original 2D images.

OffsetLatentImage.description: The OffsetLatentImage node is designed to manipulate the latent space representation of images by applying specified offsets to each channel. This operation allows for the adjustment and fine-tuning of the generated image's characteristics at a low level, offering a means to explore variations in the image generation process.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Specifies the width of the latent image to be generated. This parameter directly influences the dimensions of the output latent representation.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Determines the height of the latent image. Similar to width, it affects the size of the latent output, enabling control over the generated image's aspect ratio.

inputs.name: batch_size
inputs.description: Controls the number of latent images to be generated in a single batch, facilitating batch processing for efficiency.

inputs.name: offset_i
inputs.description: Applies a specific offset to the ith channel of the latent representation, altering its characteristics. The index i ranges from 0 to 3, allowing for detailed customization of each channel in the latent space.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: Returns the modified latent representation of images with applied offsets, ready for further processing or image generation.

PrintSigmas.description: The `PrintSigmas` node is designed for utility purposes within a computational graph, specifically to print and return the values of sigma parameters. This functionality aids in debugging and monitoring the flow of sigma values through the graph, providing a simple yet effective means of outputting these values for inspection.

inputs.name: sigmas
inputs.description: The `sigmas` parameter represents the sigma values to be printed and returned. It plays a crucial role in the node's operation by serving as the data that is both outputted for user inspection and passed through the node for potential further use.

outputs.name: sigmas
outputs.description: Returns the same sigma values that were input, allowing for further processing or inspection elsewhere in the computational graph.

RelightSimple.description: The RelightSimple node is designed to adjust the lighting of an image based on provided normal maps and directional light parameters. It allows for dynamic relighting effects, simulating different lighting conditions by altering the direction and brightness of the light source.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be relit. It serves as the base for the lighting adjustments.

inputs.name: normals
inputs.description: Normal maps corresponding to the input image, used to calculate how light interacts with the surface.

inputs.name: x_dir
inputs.description: The x-direction component of the light source, influencing the direction from which the light appears to come.

inputs.name: y_dir
inputs.description: The y-direction component of the light source, affecting the vertical angle of the incoming light.

inputs.name: brightness
inputs.description: Controls the intensity of the light source, allowing for brighter or dimmer lighting effects.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image with adjusted lighting based on the provided normals and light direction parameters.

RestoreDetail.description: The RestoreDetail node is designed to enhance the visual quality of images by restoring details that may have been lost or obscured. It focuses on improving the clarity and sharpness of images, making them appear more vivid and lifelike.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The input images to be processed for detail restoration, aiming to enhance clarity and sharpness.

inputs.name: detail
inputs.description: A secondary image or detail layer that guides the restoration process, emphasizing specific details to be enhanced or recovered.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Specifies the operation mode (e.g., 'add' or 'multiply') to combine the input image with the detail layer, affecting the enhancement effect.

inputs.name: blur_type
inputs.description: Determines the type of blur (e.g., 'blur' or 'guidedFilter') applied as part of the detail restoration process.

inputs.name: blur_size
inputs.description: The size of the blur filter to be applied, influencing the smoothness or sharpness of the restored details.

inputs.name: factor
inputs.description: A scaling factor that adjusts the intensity of the detail restoration effect.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The enhanced image with restored details, reflecting the positive aspects described in the input.

SharpenFilterLatent.description: The SharpenFilterLatent node applies a sharpening filter to latent representations of images, enhancing their details by adjusting the contrast of edges within the latent space. This process involves blurring the latent image and then combining it with the original to accentuate edges, controlled by a specified factor and filter size.

inputs.name: latents
inputs.description: The latent representation of an image to be sharpened. This input is crucial for determining the base content that will undergo the sharpening process.

inputs.name: filter_size
inputs.description: Specifies the size of the filter used for blurring the latent image before sharpening. A larger size leads to a more pronounced blurring effect, which can affect the sharpness intensity.

inputs.name: factor
inputs.description: Controls the intensity of the sharpening effect applied to the latent image. A higher factor increases the contrast between edges and non-edges, making the image appear sharper.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The sharpened latent representation of the image, with enhanced edge details and contrast.

ShuffleChannels.description: The `ShuffleChannels` node is designed to manipulate the color channels of an image. It allows for the reassignment of color channels, including red, green, blue, and optionally alpha, to different color values or to a constant value. This functionality can be used to create various visual effects or to correct color channel misalignments in images.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed. This image will have its color channels shuffled according to the specified mappings.

inputs.name: red
inputs.description: Specifies the mapping for the red channel in the output image. It can be mapped to another color channel or set to a constant value.

inputs.name: green
inputs.description: Specifies the mapping for the green channel in the output image. It can be mapped to another color channel or set to a constant value.

inputs.name: blue
inputs.description: Specifies the mapping for the blue channel in the output image. It can be mapped to another color channel or set to a constant value.

inputs.name: alpha
inputs.description: Optionally specifies the mapping for the alpha (transparency) channel in the output image. It can be mapped to another channel, set to a constant value, or left unchanged.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image after the color channels have been shuffled according to the specified mappings.

Tonemap.description: The Tonemap node is designed to adjust the tonal range of images to make them suitable for display on different devices or for achieving specific visual effects. It supports conversion between linear and sRGB color spaces and allows for scaling of the tonemap effect.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The input images to be tonemapped. This is the primary data the node operates on, affecting the visual outcome based on the tonemap process.

inputs.name: input_mode
inputs.description: Specifies the color space of the input images, either linear or sRGB, determining the initial conversion step before tonemapping.

inputs.name: output_mode
inputs.description: Defines the color space for the output images, choosing between linear and sRGB, to ensure the images are in the desired format after tonemapping.

inputs.name: tonemap_scale
inputs.description: A scale factor that adjusts the intensity of the tonemap effect, allowing for finer control over the visual appearance of the output images.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output images after applying the tonemap process, adjusted for tonal range and color space as specified by the input parameters.

UnJitterImage.description: The UnJitterImage node is designed to reverse or mitigate the effects of jittering on images. It utilizes a predefined matrix to adjust the positioning of pixels in an image, aiming to restore the original or a more stable visual representation.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The input images to be processed for jitter correction. This parameter is crucial for determining the target images on which the un-jittering operation will be applied.

inputs.name: jitter_scale
inputs.description: Defines the scale of jitter correction to be applied. This parameter adjusts the intensity of the un-jittering effect, allowing for fine-tuning of the correction process.

inputs.name: oflow_align
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether optical flow alignment should be used as part of the un-jittering process. This can enhance the correction by aligning frames based on detected motion, offering a more dynamic approach to jitter correction.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image after the un-jittering process has been applied. This image is expected to have reduced or eliminated effects of jitter, presenting a more stable and visually coherent result.

UnTonemap.description: The UnTonemap node is designed to reverse the effects of tonemapping on images, converting them back from a tonemapped representation to their original linear or sRGB color space. This process is essential for restoring the original dynamic range and color fidelity of images that have undergone tonemapping.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The images to be untonemapped. This input is crucial for defining the set of images that will undergo the reverse tonemapping process.

inputs.name: input_mode
inputs.description: Specifies the color space of the input images, either 'sRGB' or 'linear', which determines the initial conversion step before untonemapping.

inputs.name: output_mode
inputs.description: Defines the desired color space of the output images, either 'linear' or 'sRGB', affecting the final conversion step after untonemapping.

inputs.name: tonemap_scale
inputs.description: A scaling factor applied during the untonemapping process to adjust the intensity of the effect.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The untonemapped images, returned in the specified output color space, either 'linear' or 'sRGB'.

VisualizeLatents.description: The VisualizeLatents node transforms latent space representations into visualizable images, adjusting their mean and standard deviation for better visual interpretation. It organizes the visualized latents into a grid layout based on the square root of the number of channels, facilitating the examination of latent space features.

inputs.name: latent
inputs.description: The 'latent' input is a dictionary containing the latent space samples to be visualized. It is crucial for generating the visual representation of the latent space, affecting the output image's appearance and layout.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is an image tensor representing the visualized latent space, adjusted for better visual interpretation and organized in a grid layout.

ImageDuplicator.description: The ImageDuplicator node is designed to duplicate each image in a given batch, effectively increasing the number of images by replicating them. This node serves the purpose of augmenting the dataset or preparing the data for processes that require multiple instances of the same image.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The images to be duplicated. This parameter is crucial as it directly influences the node's operation by specifying which images are to be processed and duplicated.

inputs.name: dup_times
inputs.description: Specifies the number of times each image should be duplicated. This parameter controls the extent of duplication, thereby determining the total number of images produced by the node.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output of the node, consisting of the original images along with their duplicates, effectively increasing the total number of images.

ImageSelector.description: The ImageSelector node is designed to filter and select specific images from a given set based on user-defined indexes. It supports selecting individual images or ranges of images, facilitating customized image processing and manipulation.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The 'images' parameter represents the set of images from which selections are made. It is crucial for determining the subset of images to be processed or analyzed.

inputs.name: selected_indexes
inputs.description: The 'selected_indexes' parameter specifies the indexes of images to be selected, supporting individual indexes and ranges for flexible image selection. This parameter is case-sensitive.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is a filtered set of images, selected according to the specified indexes.

LatentDuplicator.description: The LatentDuplicator node is designed to duplicate latent images a specified number of times, facilitating the generation of multiple copies of the same image for further processing or analysis.

inputs.name: latent_image
inputs.description: The input latent image to be duplicated. It serves as the base image from which multiple copies will be generated, based on the duplication count specified.

inputs.name: dup_times
inputs.description: Specifies the number of times the input latent image should be duplicated. This count determines how many copies of the base image will be produced.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The output consists of the duplicated latent images, concatenated into a single tensor, effectively multiplying the number of available images for subsequent operations.

LatentSelector.description: The LatentSelector node is designed to filter and select specific latent images from a given set based on user-defined indexes. It allows for the customization of the latent image dataset by enabling the selection of particular images, facilitating targeted manipulation or analysis of these images.

inputs.name: latent_image
inputs.description: The latent images to be filtered, provided as a mapping from string identifiers to tensors. This input is crucial for determining which images are available for selection and manipulation.

inputs.name: selected_indexes
inputs.description: A string specifying the indexes of the latent images to be selected. Supports individual indexes and ranges, allowing for flexible selection within the dataset.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The filtered set of latent images, returned as a subset of the input images based on the specified indexes.

AddMask.description: The AddMask node is designed to combine two mask inputs into a single mask output, effectively merging the areas covered by each input mask. This operation is useful in scenarios where the visual or logical integration of mask regions is required, such as in image processing tasks that involve layering or combining features from different sources.

inputs.name: mask1
inputs.description: The first mask input for the addition operation. It plays a crucial role in determining the initial areas to be combined with the second mask.

inputs.name: mask2
inputs.description: The second mask input for the addition operation. It specifies additional areas to be combined with the first mask, contributing to the final merged output.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The result of combining the two input masks. This output represents the merged area covered by both input masks, providing a unified mask that encompasses the features of both.

BasicPipeToDetailerPipe.description: This node is designed to transform a basic pipeline configuration into a more detailed pipeline configuration, enhancing its capabilities and allowing for more complex operations.

inputs.name: basic_pipe
inputs.description: The basic pipeline configuration to be transformed into a detailed pipeline configuration. It serves as the foundation for the enhancement process.

inputs.name: bbox_detector
inputs.description: A bounding box detector component to be included in the detailed pipeline configuration.

inputs.name: wildcard
inputs.description: A wildcard string that allows for dynamic customization of the detailed pipeline configuration.

inputs.name: Select to add LoRA
inputs.description: Allows the selection of a LoRA component to be added to the detailed pipeline configuration, enhancing its functionality.

inputs.name: Select to add Wildcard
inputs.description: Enables the selection of an additional wildcard component to be added to the detailed pipeline configuration for further customization.

inputs.name: sam_model_opt
inputs.description: An optional SAM model component that can be included in the detailed pipeline configuration for enhanced modeling capabilities.

inputs.name: segm_detector_opt
inputs.description: An optional segmentation detector component that can be included in the detailed pipeline configuration for improved segmentation capabilities.

inputs.name: detailer_hook
inputs.description: An optional hook component that can be included in the detailed pipeline configuration for customized processing and enhancements.

outputs.name: detailer_pipe
outputs.description: The resulting detailed pipeline configuration, which includes the basic pipeline components along with the specified enhancements.

BasicPipeToDetailerPipeSDXL.description: This node is designed to transform a basic pipeline configuration into a more detailed pipeline configuration specifically tailored for the SDXL model. It enriches the basic pipeline by incorporating additional models, clips, VAEs, and conditioning parameters, along with optional elements like SAM models and segmentation detectors, to enhance the detail and precision of the output.

inputs.name: base_basic_pipe
inputs.description: unknown

inputs.name: refiner_basic_pipe
inputs.description: unknown

inputs.name: bbox_detector
inputs.description: A bounding box detector model that identifies and locates objects within images, useful for targeted manipulations or enhancements.

inputs.name: wildcard
inputs.description: A flexible string input that can be used for dynamic prompts or additional instructions not covered by other parameters.

inputs.name: Select to add LoRA
inputs.description: Allows the selection of LoRA layers to be added to the text, enhancing the model's ability to adapt to specific tasks or domains.

inputs.name: Select to add Wildcard
inputs.description: Enables the selection of predefined wildcards to be added to the text, offering more control over the generation process.

inputs.name: sam_model_opt
inputs.description: An optional SAM model that can be used for sharpening and adjusting the focus of generated images, improving their clarity.

inputs.name: segm_detector_opt
inputs.description: An optional segmentation detector that can be used for identifying and segmenting specific parts of images, useful for detailed manipulations.

inputs.name: detailer_hook
inputs.description: An optional hook that allows for custom modifications or enhancements to the detailing process, providing flexibility in the pipeline's behavior.

outputs.name: detailer_pipe
outputs.description: The detailed pipeline configuration resulting from the transformation, tailored for the SDXL model.

BboxDetectorCombined_v2.description: This node combines bounding box detection with segmentation mask creation and optional dilation, providing a comprehensive solution for object detection and segmentation in images. It leverages a bounding box model to detect objects and generate segmentation masks, which can then be optionally dilated for improved coverage or specificity.

inputs.name: bbox_detector
inputs.description: Specifies the bounding box model to be used for object detection. It plays a crucial role in identifying objects within the image and generating initial bounding boxes.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image on which object detection and segmentation are to be performed. It serves as the primary data source for the detection process.

inputs.name: threshold
inputs.description: A threshold value to filter detected objects based on confidence scores. It helps in eliminating detections with low confidence.

inputs.name: dilation
inputs.description: Determines the extent to which the segmentation masks are dilated. This can enhance the mask's coverage over the detected objects.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The output segmentation mask representing detected objects. It combines all individual object masks into a single mask layer.

BboxDetectorSEGS.description: The BboxDetectorSEGS node is designed to detect bounding boxes around objects within images, leveraging segmentation techniques to enhance the accuracy and detail of the detection process. It combines the capabilities of bounding box detection with segmentation to provide a more comprehensive understanding of the objects' shapes and boundaries.

inputs.name: bbox_detector
inputs.description: Specifies the bounding box detector model to be used for detecting objects within the image. It plays a crucial role in the initial detection phase before segmentation is applied.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input images or frames on which object detection and segmentation are to be performed. This is the primary data that the node operates on.

inputs.name: threshold
inputs.description: A threshold value for bounding box detection, determining the sensitivity of the detector to potential objects within the image.

inputs.name: dilation
inputs.description: Specifies the dilation applied to the detected bounding boxes, allowing for adjustments in the size of the bounding area around detected objects.

inputs.name: crop_factor
inputs.description: Determines the extent to which the area around the detected object is included in the crop, affecting the context provided around the detected object.

inputs.name: drop_size
inputs.description: Sets the minimum size for detected objects, filtering out objects smaller than this size to focus on more significant detections.

inputs.name: labels
inputs.description: Optional labels to filter the detected objects, allowing for selective segmentation based on specified categories.

inputs.name: detailer_hook
inputs.description: An optional hook for detailed processing or modifications of the detection and segmentation process, providing a way to customize the output.

outputs.name: segs
outputs.description: The output of the node includes segmentation information derived from the detected bounding boxes, providing detailed insights into the objects' shapes and boundaries.

BitwiseAndMask.description: The BitwiseAndMask node performs a bitwise AND operation on two input masks, resulting in a single mask that represents the intersection of the input masks. This operation is useful for combining or overlaying masks to highlight areas of overlap between them.

inputs.name: mask1
inputs.description: The first input mask for the bitwise AND operation. It plays a crucial role in determining the areas of overlap with the second mask.

inputs.name: mask2
inputs.description: The second input mask for the bitwise AND operation. It is combined with the first mask to identify overlapping areas.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The result of the bitwise AND operation between the two input masks, highlighting the areas where both masks overlap.

BitwiseAndMaskForEach.description: The BitwiseAndMaskForEach node applies a bitwise AND operation between a base segmentation (or segments) and a mask for each segment, effectively combining the mask information with each segment. This operation is useful for refining segmentation results by incorporating additional mask constraints.

inputs.name: base_segs
inputs.description: The base segments to which the mask will be applied. This input is crucial for defining the scope of the operation and determining the segments that will be refined by the mask.

inputs.name: mask_segs
inputs.description: The mask segments to be applied to the base segments. These masks dictate the areas of interest within each segment and are essential for the bitwise AND operation.

outputs.name: segs
outputs.description: The resulting segments after applying the bitwise AND operation with the mask. This output reflects the refined segmentation, incorporating the constraints imposed by the mask.

CfgScheduleHookProvider.description: The CfgScheduleHookProvider node is designed to create configuration schedule hooks based on a specified iteration schedule and target configuration. It aims to dynamically adjust the configuration during the iteration process to achieve desired outcomes.

inputs.name: schedule_for_iteration
inputs.description: Specifies the iteration schedule to use for adjusting the configuration. It determines how the configuration changes over time.

inputs.name: target_cfg
inputs.description: The target configuration value to reach by the end of the iteration process. It influences the adjustment of the configuration over time.

outputs.name: pk_hook
outputs.description: Produces a hook that can be used to adjust the configuration during the iteration process.

CLIPSegDetectorProvider.description: The CLIPSegDetectorProvider node is designed to leverage the capabilities of CLIPSeg for object detection within images. It processes textual descriptions and image characteristics to identify and delineate objects, utilizing parameters such as blur, threshold, and dilation factor to refine the detection process.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The textual description of the object to be detected. This parameter is crucial for guiding the CLIPSeg model in identifying the relevant objects within the image.

inputs.name: blur
inputs.description: Specifies the level of blur applied to the image before detection. This can help in reducing noise and improving the accuracy of object detection.

inputs.name: threshold
inputs.description: A threshold value that determines the sensitivity of object detection. Higher values may result in fewer detections, while lower values can increase the detection of minor features.

inputs.name: dilation_factor
inputs.description: Determines the extent to which the detected object's boundaries are expanded or contracted. This can be useful in adjusting the preciseness of the object's outline.

outputs.name: bbox_detector
outputs.description: Provides an object detector based on the CLIPSeg model, capable of identifying and bounding objects within images based on textual descriptions.

CombineRegionalPrompts.description: The CombineRegionalPrompts node is designed to aggregate multiple regional prompts into a single, unified set. This functionality is crucial for scenarios where distinct regional inputs need to be combined to form a comprehensive prompt set for further processing or generation tasks.

inputs.name: regional_prompts1
inputs.description: Represents the initial set of regional prompts to be combined. This input is essential for the node's operation as it forms the basis for the aggregation process.

outputs.name: regional_prompts
outputs.description: The combined set of regional prompts, ready for use in subsequent processing or generation tasks.

CoreMLDetailerHookProvider.description: This node provides a mechanism to create and manage CoreML detailer hooks, which are specialized hooks designed to adjust and refine the details of generated images based on the specified mode. It encapsulates the complexity of configuring and applying these hooks, offering a streamlined interface for enhancing image quality.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Specifies the resolution mode for the CoreML detailer hook, determining the dimensions of the output image. This choice directly influences the detail level and aspect ratio of the generated image.

outputs.name: detailer_hook
outputs.description: Returns a CoreML detailer hook configured according to the specified mode, ready to be applied for image detail enhancement.

DenoiseScheduleHookProvider.description: The DenoiseScheduleHookProvider node is designed to create hooks that adjust denoising levels dynamically during the image generation process, based on a predefined schedule and target denoise value. It aims to enhance the quality of the generated images by fine-tuning the denoising parameter over the course of the generation.

inputs.name: schedule_for_iteration
inputs.description: Specifies the schedule to be used for adjusting the denoising level during the image generation process. The choice of schedule affects how the target denoising level is approached over time.

inputs.name: target_denoise
inputs.description: The target denoising level to be achieved by the end of the image generation process. This value influences the final clarity and detail of the generated image.

outputs.name: pk_hook
outputs.description: The output is a hook that can be applied to the image generation process to dynamically adjust the denoising level according to the specified schedule.

DenoiseSchedulerDetailerHookProvider.description: This node provides a mechanism to dynamically adjust denoising levels throughout the generation cycle based on a predefined schedule. It aims to enhance image detail and quality by fine-tuning denoise parameters at different stages of the image generation process.

inputs.name: schedule_for_cycle
inputs.description: Specifies the scheduling strategy for adjusting denoise levels throughout the generation cycle. It determines how denoise levels are modified over time to achieve optimal image quality.

inputs.name: target_denoise
inputs.description: The target denoise level to achieve by the end of the generation cycle. This parameter sets the goal for the dynamic adjustment of denoise levels, influencing the final image detail and quality.

outputs.name: detailer_hook
outputs.description: Produces a detailer hook that is used to dynamically adjust denoise levels throughout the image generation cycle, based on the specified schedule and target denoise level.

DetailerForEach.description: The `DetailerForEach` node is designed to apply detailed processing to each element in a given dataset or collection. It focuses on enhancing or modifying the details of each item, potentially for purposes such as improving visual quality, extracting features, or applying specific transformations based on the context of use.

DetailerForEachPipeForAnimateDiff.description: This node is designed to apply detailed animation effects to each frame or segment within a pipeline, enhancing the visual impact and dynamic elements of the content. It operates by iterating over each applicable segment or frame, applying a set of predefined or dynamically generated animation details to improve the overall aesthetic and engagement of the animation.

inputs.name: image_frames
inputs.description: The sequence of image frames to which animation effects will be applied. This input is crucial for determining the visual flow and continuity of the animation.

inputs.name: segs
inputs.description: Segmentation information for the image frames, used to identify and apply detailed effects to specific areas of the animation.

inputs.name: guide_size
inputs.description: Specifies the size guide for the animation detailing process, influencing the scale at which details are applied.

inputs.name: guide_size_for
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether the guide size applies to the bounding box or the crop region, affecting how details are scaled and applied.

inputs.name: max_size
inputs.description: The maximum size limit for the animation details, ensuring that the detailing process stays within computational and aesthetic bounds.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: A seed value for random number generation, providing consistency in the detailing effects applied across different runs.

inputs.name: steps
inputs.description: The number of steps to execute in the detailing process, affecting the depth and complexity of the applied effects.

inputs.name: cfg
inputs.description: Configuration parameter for the detailing process, allowing for fine-tuning of the animation effects.

inputs.name: sampler_name
inputs.description: Specifies the sampler to be used in the detailing process, influencing the variation and quality of the applied effects.

inputs.name: scheduler
inputs.description: Determines the scheduling algorithm for the detailing process, impacting the efficiency and outcome of the animation effects.

inputs.name: denoise
inputs.description: The denoising factor applied during the detailing process, affecting the clarity and quality of the animation.

inputs.name: feather
inputs.description: unknown

inputs.name: basic_pipe
inputs.description: The basic pipeline configuration for the animation detailing process, defining the core components and their interactions.

inputs.name: refiner_ratio
inputs.description: The ratio of refinement applied to the detailing process, adjusting the intensity of the effects for a more nuanced outcome.

inputs.name: detailer_hook
inputs.description: unknown

inputs.name: refiner_basic_pipe_opt
inputs.description: unknown

inputs.name: noise_mask_feather
inputs.description: unknown

inputs.name: scheduler_func_opt
inputs.description: unknown

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The enhanced image frames after applying animation effects, showcasing the improved visual impact.

outputs.name: segs
outputs.description: The updated segmentation information reflecting the detailed effects applied to specific areas of the animation.

outputs.name: basic_pipe
outputs.description: The basic pipeline configuration after the detailing process, potentially modified to incorporate new detailing components.

outputs.name: cnet_images
outputs.description: A collection of images generated during the detailing process, used for further refinement or as part of the animation.

DetailerHookCombine.description: The DetailerHookCombine node is designed to enhance the detail processing capabilities of image generation models by combining the functionalities of two distinct detailer hooks. This node sequentially applies the cycle_latent and post_detection methods of each hook to the input data, effectively integrating their individual effects to produce more refined and detailed outputs.

inputs.name: hook1
inputs.description: The first detailer hook to be combined. It contributes to the initial phase of detail enhancement by applying its cycle_latent and post_detection methods to the input data.

inputs.name: hook2
inputs.description: The second detailer hook to be combined. It further processes the data already enhanced by the first hook, applying its own cycle_latent and post_detection methods to achieve additional detail refinement.

outputs.name: detailer_hook
outputs.description: The output of the DetailerHookCombine node, which represents the enhanced and refined data after the combined effects of the two detailer hooks have been applied.

DetailerPipeToBasicPipe.description: This node transforms a detailer pipe configuration into two basic pipe configurations, one for the base model and another for the refiner model. It abstracts the complexity of handling different components within a detailer pipe and simplifies it into more manageable basic pipe structures.

inputs.name: detailer_pipe
inputs.description: The detailer pipe input is a comprehensive configuration that includes models, clips, VAEs, and conditioning information for both the base and refiner setups. It serves as the source from which the basic pipe configurations are derived.

outputs.name: base_basic_pipe
outputs.description: The base basic pipe configuration, derived from the input detailer pipe, containing the model, clip, VAE, and conditioning information for the base setup.

outputs.name: refiner_basic_pipe
outputs.description: The refiner basic pipe configuration, also derived from the input detailer pipe, but focusing on the refiner model's setup including its model, clip, VAE, and conditioning information.

EditBasicPipe.description: The EditBasicPipe node is designed to modify elements of a basic pipeline configuration, allowing for the customization of model, clip, VAE, and conditioning components.

inputs.name: basic_pipe
inputs.description: Represents the initial state of the basic pipeline components, which include model, clip, VAE, and conditioning elements. It is essential for determining the starting point for modifications.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: Optional parameter to replace the current model component of the basic pipe.

inputs.name: clip
inputs.description: Optional parameter to replace the current clip component of the basic pipe.

inputs.name: vae
inputs.description: Optional parameter to replace the current VAE component of the basic pipe.

inputs.name: positive
inputs.description: Optional parameter to add or replace the positive conditioning component of the basic pipe.

inputs.name: negative
inputs.description: Optional parameter to add or replace the negative conditioning component of the basic pipe.

outputs.name: basic_pipe
outputs.description: The modified basic pipeline configuration, reflecting any changes made to the model, clip, VAE, and conditioning components.

EditDetailerPipe.description: The EditDetailerPipe node is designed to enhance and detail the editing process by allowing the integration of various editing components such as LoRA, Wildcards, and models for refining the output. It serves as a foundational element in constructing detailed and customized editing pipelines.

inputs.name: detailer_pipe
inputs.description: Represents the core pipeline for detailing, serving as the primary input around which additional detailing components are integrated.

inputs.name: wildcard
inputs.description: Allows for the inclusion of dynamic, multiline text inputs, known as wildcards, to add flexibility and customization to the editing process.

inputs.name: Select to add LoRA
inputs.description: Enables the selection of LoRA (Locally Optimized Receptive Attention) components to be added to the text, enhancing its detail and specificity.

inputs.name: Select to add Wildcard
inputs.description: Facilitates the selection of predefined wildcards to be incorporated into the text, adding layers of customization.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: Specifies the model to be used in the detailing process, allowing for customization and refinement of outputs.

inputs.name: clip
inputs.description: Defines the CLIP model to be integrated into the detailing process for enhanced content understanding and generation.

inputs.name: vae
inputs.description: Specifies the VAE model to be used, enabling advanced image processing capabilities in the detailing process.

inputs.name: positive
inputs.description: Defines positive conditioning factors to guide the detailing process towards desired outcomes.

inputs.name: negative
inputs.description: Specifies negative conditioning factors to avoid certain outcomes in the detailing process.

inputs.name: bbox_detector
inputs.description: Integrates a bounding box detector for object localization in images, enhancing the detailing capabilities.

inputs.name: sam_model
inputs.description: Specifies the SAM model to be used, enabling advanced semantic understanding and manipulation.

inputs.name: segm_detector
inputs.description: Integrates a segmentation detector for detailed image segmentation, enhancing the editing capabilities.

inputs.name: detailer_hook
inputs.description: Allows for the integration of custom hooks into the detailing process, enabling further customization.

outputs.name: detailer_pipe
outputs.description: Outputs the enhanced detailer pipe, incorporating all specified modifications and integrations.

EditDetailerPipeSDXL.description: The EditDetailerPipeSDXL node is designed to enhance and refine the details of inputs through a sophisticated editing pipeline. It allows for the integration of various models and techniques, including LoRA and Wildcards, to achieve more precise and impactful modifications.

inputs.name: detailer_pipe
inputs.description: Represents the initial detailer pipeline to be enhanced or modified. It serves as the foundation for further refinements.

inputs.name: wildcard

inputs.name: Select to add LoRA

inputs.name: refiner_model

inputs.name: refiner_positive
inputs.description: Defines additional positive conditioning for the refinement process, enhancing desired attributes.

inputs.name: refiner_negative

inputs.name: sam_model

inputs.name: segm_detector
inputs.description: Defines a segmentation detector to be used for segmenting different parts or objects within the content.

inputs.name: detailer_hook
inputs.description: Provides a hook for custom detailer functions or modifications to be applied within the pipeline.

outputs.name: detailer_pipe
outputs.description: Outputs the enhanced detailer pipeline, incorporating all specified models, techniques, and modifications.

EmptySegs.description: The EmptySEGS node is designed to generate a base structure for segmentation data without any actual segments. It provides a foundational shape and an empty list to represent the absence of segments, serving as a starting point or placeholder in segmentation operations.

outputs.name: segs
outputs.description: Represents a tuple containing a shape and an empty list, indicating the absence of segmentation data.
