outputs.description: Returns the detailer hook component extracted from the detailer pipe.

outputs.name: refiner_model
outputs.description: Returns the refiner model component extracted from the detailer pipe.

outputs.name: refiner_clip
outputs.description: Returns the refiner clip component extracted from the detailer pipe.

outputs.name: refiner_positive
outputs.description: Returns the refiner positive conditioning element extracted from the detailer pipe.

outputs.name: refiner_negative
outputs.description: Returns the refiner negative conditioning element extracted from the detailer pipe.

FromDetailerPipe_v2.description: The `FromDetailerPipe_v2` node is designed to decompose a complex detailer pipe structure into its constituent components, facilitating the extraction and individual manipulation of each component for further processing or analysis.

inputs.name: detailer_pipe
inputs.description: Represents the complex structure of a detailer pipe, encapsulating various models and processing elements. It is essential for the node to dissect and provide access to individual components.

outputs.name: detailer_pipe
outputs.description: Returns the original detailer pipe structure, allowing for potential reassembly or further reference.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: Extracts the primary model component from the detailer pipe.

outputs.name: clip
outputs.description: Retrieves the CLIP model component, used for image-text matching and manipulation.

outputs.name: vae
outputs.description: Extracts the Variational Autoencoder (VAE) component, crucial for image generation and manipulation.

outputs.name: positive
outputs.description: Provides access to the positive conditioning component, essential for guiding the generation process.

outputs.name: negative
outputs.description: Provides access to the negative conditioning component, essential for guiding the generation process.

outputs.name: bbox_detector
outputs.description: Extracts the bounding box detector component, used for object detection within images.

outputs.name: sam_model_opt
outputs.description: Retrieves the optional SAM model component, enhancing image quality and detail.

outputs.name: segm_detector_opt
outputs.description: Extracts the optional segmentation detector component, used for detailed image segmentation.

outputs.name: detailer_hook
outputs.description: Provides access to the detailer hook component, allowing for custom modifications and enhancements.

GITSSchedulerFuncProvider.description: Provides a functionality to dynamically generate a noise schedule for image generation processes using the GITSScheduler. This node is designed to adjust the noise schedule based on given coefficients and denoise parameters, offering a flexible approach to controlling the diffusion process.

inputs.name: coeff
inputs.description: Specifies the coefficient factor for the GITSScheduler, influencing the overall noise schedule generation by adjusting the intensity of the applied noise.

inputs.name: denoise
inputs.description: Determines the amount of denoising to apply in the noise schedule, affecting the clarity and detail of the generated images.

outputs.name: scheduler_func
outputs.description: Returns a function capable of generating a dynamic noise schedule for use in image generation processes, tailored by the specified coefficients and denoise parameters.

ImageListToImageBatch.description: This node transforms a list of images into a single batched image tensor, ensuring all images have the same dimensions through upsampling if necessary. It's designed to facilitate operations that require batch processing of images by consolidating multiple images into a unified tensor format.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: A list of image tensors to be batched together. This input is crucial for the node's operation as it determines the composition of the resulting batched image tensor.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is a single batched image tensor, which is a consolidated version of the input images, potentially with upsampling applied to maintain dimension consistency.

ImageMaskSwitch.description: The ImageMaskSwitch node allows for the selection and output of a specific image and its associated mask from a set of up to four image-mask pairs based on a selection input. This functionality is useful for dynamically choosing between different visual elements and their masks within a workflow.

inputs.name: select
inputs.description: Determines which image-mask pair to output, allowing for dynamic selection from up to four options.

inputs.name: images1
inputs.description: The first image in the selection set.

inputs.name: mask1_opt
inputs.description: Optional mask associated with the first image.

inputs.name: images2_opt
inputs.description: The second optional image in the selection set.

inputs.name: mask2_opt
inputs.description: Optional mask associated with the second image.

inputs.name: images3_opt
inputs.description: The third optional image in the selection set.

inputs.name: mask3_opt
inputs.description: Optional mask associated with the third image.

inputs.name: images4_opt
inputs.description: The fourth optional image in the selection set.

inputs.name: mask4_opt
inputs.description: Optional mask associated with the fourth image.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The selected image based on the input selection.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The mask associated with the selected image, if provided.

ImageReceiver.description: The ImageReceiver node is designed to process and transform image data received in various formats, including base64-encoded strings. It decodes, transposes, and converts images to a standardized format for further processing or analysis, optionally applying a mask if transparency data is available. This node plays a crucial role in preparing image data for downstream tasks by ensuring images are in a consistent and usable state.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The 'image' parameter represents the image to be processed. It is crucial for the node's operation as it serves as the primary input upon which all transformations and analyses are performed.

inputs.name: link_id
inputs.description: The 'link_id' parameter is used to identify the specific processing task or workflow instance. It helps in tracking and managing the processed images within a larger system or application.

inputs.name: save_to_workflow
inputs.description: This boolean parameter determines whether the processed image should be saved to the workflow. Enabling this option triggers the image processing and transformation steps.

inputs.name: image_data
inputs.description: The 'image_data' parameter contains the image information, typically as a base64-encoded string. It is essential for decoding and converting the image into a format suitable for further processing.

inputs.name: trigger_always
inputs.description: This parameter controls whether the node's processing should be triggered unconditionally. It allows for flexibility in workflow execution, ensuring that image processing can occur as needed.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The processed image, transformed and standardized for further use.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: An optional mask generated based on the image's transparency data, useful for selective processing or analysis.

ImageSender.description: The ImageSender node is designed for sending images over a network to a specified destination, incorporating additional information such as a filename prefix and a link ID. It primarily serves the purpose of transmitting image data, potentially with extra metadata, to facilitate remote processing or storage.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: Specifies the images to be sent. This is the primary data that the node operates on, determining the content that will be transmitted.

inputs.name: filename_prefix
inputs.description: A prefix for the filename under which the images will be saved or identified. This helps in organizing or categorizing the images on the receiving end.

inputs.name: link_id
inputs.description: An identifier used to link the sent images to a specific context or session. This aids in tracking and managing images across different parts of a system.

ImpactAssembleSEGS.description: The ImpactAssembleSEGS node is designed to aggregate segment headers and segment elements into a unified structure, facilitating the organization and manipulation of segmented data within the ImpactPack framework.

inputs.name: seg_header
inputs.description: The 'seg_header' parameter represents the header information for a segment, serving as a crucial component in assembling the overall segmented structure.

inputs.name: seg_elt
inputs.description: The 'seg_elt' parameter signifies the individual segment elements, which are essential in constructing the complete segmented data structure.

outputs.name: segs
outputs.description: Produces a unified segmented data structure, combining the provided segment headers and elements.

ImpactCombineConditionings.description: The ImpactCombineConditionings node is designed to merge multiple conditioning inputs into a single, unified conditioning output. This process facilitates the combination of various conditioning elements, enhancing the flexibility and capability of conditioning-based operations within the ImpactPack suite.

inputs.name: conditioning1
inputs.description: The primary conditioning input to be combined. It serves as the foundational element for the combination process, allowing for the integration of additional conditioning inputs to enrich the overall context.

outputs.name: conditioning
outputs.description: The result of combining the input conditionings. This unified conditioning encapsulates the merged context and attributes of the inputs, ready for further processing.

ImpactCompare.description: The ImpactCompare node is designed to perform a variety of comparison operations between two input values. It supports basic comparison operations such as equality, inequality, greater than, less than, and their respective inclusive versions, as well as returning predefined true or false values. This functionality allows for dynamic decision-making processes within a workflow based on the comparison results.

inputs.name: cmp
inputs.description: Specifies the type of comparison to perform between the two input values. It includes operations like equality, inequality, greater than, less than, and their inclusive versions, as well as options to return true or false directly.

inputs.name: a
inputs.description: The first value to be compared. It can be of any type, allowing for flexibility in comparison operations.

inputs.name: b
inputs.description: The second value to be compared against the first. It can be of any type, enhancing the node's versatility in handling different comparison scenarios.

outputs.name: boolean
outputs.description: The result of the comparison operation, indicating whether the specified condition between the two input values is met.

ImpactConcatConditionings.description: The ImpactConcatConditionings node is designed to concatenate multiple conditioning inputs into a single conditioning output. This process is essential for combining various conditioning elements to enhance or specify the generation process further.

inputs.name: conditioning1
inputs.description: The primary conditioning input. This input serves as the base to which additional conditionings are concatenated, influencing the overall output by combining multiple conditioning aspects.

outputs.name: conditioning
outputs.description: The concatenated conditioning output, which combines the input conditionings into a unified form, enhancing the generation process.

ImpactConditionalBranch.description: This node provides a conditional branching mechanism, allowing for the execution of different logic or values based on a given condition. It serves as a fundamental building block for creating dynamic and conditional workflows within the ImpactPack.

inputs.name: cond
inputs.description: The condition upon which the branching logic is based. It determines which of the two provided values (true or false branch) is returned by the node.

inputs.name: tt_value
inputs.description: The value to be returned if the condition evaluates to True. This allows for dynamic selection of output based on the condition.

inputs.name: ff_value
inputs.description: The value to be returned if the condition evaluates to False. This enables the node to selectively output values based on the evaluated condition.

outputs.description: The output of this node is either the tt_value or ff_value, depending on the evaluation of the condition.

ImpactConditionalBranchSelMode.description: This node provides a conditional branching mechanism with a selection mode, allowing for dynamic control flow based on boolean conditions and selection preferences. It enables conditional execution paths in a workflow, enhancing decision-making capabilities.

inputs.name: cond
inputs.description: A boolean condition that determines the branch of execution. It is pivotal in deciding which value (true or false branch) to return based on its truthiness.

inputs.name: sel_mode
inputs.description: A boolean parameter that influences the selection mode, determining whether the selection is made on prompt or on execution. This adds an additional layer of control over the conditional branching behavior.

inputs.name: tt_value
inputs.description: The value to return if the condition is true. This parameter is optional and allows for flexibility in defining the true branch outcome.

inputs.name: ff_value
inputs.description: The value to return if the condition is false. This parameter is optional, providing flexibility in defining the false branch outcome.

outputs.description: The output is either the tt_value or ff_value based on the evaluation of the condition and the selection mode.

ImpactConditionalStopIteration.description: This node is designed to conditionally halt the iteration process within a workflow, based on a specified condition. It serves as a control mechanism to dynamically manage the flow of execution based on logical conditions.

inputs.name: cond
inputs.description: Determines whether the iteration should be stopped. If true, the iteration is halted.

ImpactControlBridge.description: The ImpactControlBridge node serves as a dynamic control mechanism for managing the state of other nodes within a network based on specific conditions. It can activate, mute, or bypass nodes based on the operational mode, thereby altering the flow of data or processing within the system.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: The input value that is passed through the node unchanged if none of the conditions for activation, muting, or bypassing are met. This value can be of any type, reflecting the diverse data that may flow through the system.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Determines if the node should activate other nodes. Activation is based on the presence of nodes in the 'should_be_active_nodes' list, which is a combination of nodes specified to be muted and bypassed.

inputs.name: behavior
inputs.description: Controls the muting of nodes. When set, nodes in the 'should_be_mute_nodes' list, which includes active and bypass nodes, are muted to prevent them from processing data.

outputs.name: value
outputs.description: The output value, which is the input value passed through unchanged unless the node's processing is interrupted by activating, muting, or bypassing other nodes.

ImpactControlNetApplyAdvancedSEGS.description: This node is designed to apply advanced segmentation (SEGS) adjustments using a control network. It enhances or modifies the segmentation data based on the control network's parameters, offering a way to fine-tune or dynamically adjust the segmentation output for more precise or varied results.

inputs.name: segs
inputs.description: The segmentation data to be processed. It serves as the primary input for the node, determining the base segmentation that will be adjusted.

inputs.name: control_net
inputs.description: The control network used to adjust the segmentation. It defines the transformation or adjustment logic applied to the segmentation data.

inputs.name: strength
inputs.description: A scalar value that determines the intensity of the control network's effect on the segmentation. Higher values result in more pronounced adjustments.

inputs.name: start_percent
inputs.description: The starting percentage of the effect's application range, allowing for gradual application of the control network's adjustments.

inputs.name: end_percent
inputs.description: The ending percentage of the effect's application range, enabling fine-tuning of where the adjustments taper off.

inputs.name: segs_preprocessor
inputs.description: An optional preprocessor for the segmentation data before applying the control network adjustments. It can be used for initial modifications or preparations of the SEGS.

inputs.name: control_image
inputs.description: An optional image that can influence the control network's adjustments, providing additional context or guidance for the transformations.

outputs.name: segs
outputs.description: The adjusted segmentation data after applying the control network's enhancements or modifications.

ImpactControlNetApplySEGS.description: This node applies a control network to segmentation elements (SEGS), modifying them based on the control network's parameters and potentially an additional control image. It's designed to adjust or enhance specific aspects of the segmentation elements, such as their appearance or structure, by leveraging the control network's capabilities.

inputs.name: segs
inputs.description: The segmentation elements to be modified. This is the primary input that the control network will be applied to.

inputs.name: control_net
inputs.description: The control network to be applied to each segmentation element. It defines the modifications or adjustments to be made.

inputs.name: strength
inputs.description: A scalar value that determines the intensity of the control network's effect on the segmentation elements.

inputs.name: segs_preprocessor
inputs.description: An optional preprocessor for the segmentation elements before applying the control network.

inputs.name: control_image
inputs.description: An optional image that can provide additional context or guidance for the control network's application.

outputs.name: segs
outputs.description: The modified segmentation elements after the control network has been applied.

ImpactControlNetClearSEGS.description: This node is designed to clear control networks from segmentation data, effectively resetting any modifications or enhancements previously applied. It operates by iterating over each segment in the provided segmentation data, creating a new segment with the original properties but without the control network information.

inputs.name: segs
inputs.description: The segmentation data to be processed. This input is essential for the node's operation as it defines the segments whose control networks will be cleared.

outputs.name: segs
outputs.description: The modified segmentation data with control networks cleared from each segment. This output is crucial for subsequent processing steps that require segmentation data without control network modifications.

ImpactConvertDataType.description: The ImpactConvertDataType node is designed to convert a given input value into multiple data types, including string, float, integer, and boolean, based on the input's nature and content. This conversion facilitates the handling and processing of data across different formats within the ImpactPack/Logic category.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: The 'value' parameter is the input that will be converted into multiple data types. Its nature and content determine the outcome of the conversion, affecting the node's execution and results.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: Represents the input value converted to a string format.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: Represents the input value converted to a float format, with numerical inputs directly converted and non-numerical inputs interpreted as boolean values before conversion.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: Represents the input value converted to an integer format, following the same conversion logic as for the float type.

outputs.name: boolean
outputs.description: Represents the input value converted to a boolean format, with numerical values interpreted based on their truthiness and non-numerical values based on specific string interpretations.

ImpactCount_Elts_in_SEGS.description: This node is designed to count the elements within a given SEGS data structure, providing a simple yet essential utility for quantifying the components of SEGS in the context of data processing or analysis.

inputs.name: segs
inputs.description: Represents the SEGS data structure whose elements are to be counted. It is crucial for determining the total number of elements contained within, impacting the node's output directly.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: The output is an integer representing the total number of elements within the provided SEGS data structure, serving as a quantitative measure of its content.

ImpactDecomposeSEGS.description: The ImpactDecomposeSEGS node is designed to decompose a given SEGS data structure into its constituent elements. This operation facilitates the manipulation and analysis of the segmented data by breaking it down into more manageable parts.

inputs.name: segs
inputs.description: Represents the SEGS data structure to be decomposed. This input is crucial for the operation as it provides the segmented data that will be broken down into its constituent elements.

outputs.name: segs_header
outputs.description: Represents the header information of the decomposed SEGS data structure.

outputs.name: seg_elt
outputs.description: Represents the individual elements of the decomposed SEGS data structure. This output is a list, allowing for the representation of multiple segmented elements.

ImpactDilateMask.description: The ImpactDilateMask node is designed to modify the spatial dimensions of a given mask by applying dilation or erosion. This process adjusts the mask's boundaries, either expanding or contracting them based on the specified dilation factor, thereby impacting the mask's coverage area.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The 'mask' parameter represents the input mask to be dilated or eroded. It is crucial for defining the area to be modified.

inputs.name: dilation
inputs.description: The 'dilation' parameter specifies the degree of dilation or erosion to apply to the mask. Positive values cause dilation (expansion), while negative values lead to erosion (contraction).

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The output is a modified mask with adjusted boundaries, either dilated or eroded based on the input parameters.

ImpactDilateMaskInSEGS.description: This node applies a dilation operation to the masks within a collection of segmentation elements (SEGS), potentially expanding their boundaries. It's designed to modify the spatial geometry of segmentation masks, making them larger or smaller based on the dilation parameter.

inputs.name: segs
inputs.description: Represents the collection of segmentation elements (SEGS) to which the dilation operation will be applied. It's crucial for defining the input segmentation masks that will undergo geometric transformation.

inputs.name: dilation
inputs.description: Specifies the intensity of the dilation operation. Positive values cause the masks to expand, while negative values lead to contraction. This parameter directly influences the geometric transformation of the segmentation masks.

outputs.name: segs
outputs.description: The output is a modified collection of segmentation elements (SEGS) where each mask has been dilated according to the specified dilation parameter.

ImpactDilate_Mask_SEG_ELT.description: This node is designed to apply dilation to the mask of a single segmentation element (SEG_ELT), allowing for the adjustment of the mask's boundaries. It is part of the ImpactPack/Util category and serves as a utility for modifying the spatial extent of segmentation masks, which can be crucial for various image processing and computer vision tasks.

inputs.name: seg_elt
inputs.description: Represents a single segmentation element (SEG_ELT) whose mask will be modified through dilation, depending on the dilation parameter value. This adjustment can be essential for refining segmentation results or preparing data for further processing.

inputs.name: dilation
inputs.description: Specifies the intensity of the mask modification. Positive values cause dilation (expanding the mask), allowing for flexible mask adjustments.

outputs.name: seg_elt
outputs.description: The output is a modified single segmentation element (SEG_ELT) with its mask dilated, based on the input parameters. This modification enables refined control over the segmentation mask's boundaries.

ImpactDummyInput.description: The ImpactDummyInput node is designed to generate a simple dummy output, primarily for testing or placeholder purposes within the ImpactPack/Debug category. It serves as a straightforward mechanism to introduce a constant or a placeholder value into the data flow.

outputs.description: Represents a generic output type, indicating that this node can produce a value of any type, serving as a versatile placeholder or test value.

ImpactEdit_SEG_ELT.description: The ImpactEdit_SEG_ELT node is designed for editing and manipulating segmentation elements (SEG_ELT) within the ImpactPack framework. It focuses on modifying the properties of segmentation elements to achieve desired alterations, such as adjusting their bounding boxes or applying transformations, thereby enabling more precise control over the segmentation output.

inputs.name: seg_elt
inputs.description: The 'seg_elt' parameter represents the segmentation element (SEG_ELT) to be edited. It is crucial for specifying the target segmentation element whose properties are to be modified.

inputs.name: cropped_image_opt
inputs.description: Optional parameter for providing an alternative cropped image for the segmentation element.

inputs.name: cropped_mask_opt
inputs.description: Optional parameter for providing an alternative cropped mask for the segmentation element.

inputs.name: crop_region_opt
inputs.description: Optional parameter for providing an alternative crop region for the segmentation element.

inputs.name: bbox_opt
inputs.description: Optional parameter for providing an alternative bounding box for the segmentation element.

inputs.name: control_net_wrapper_opt
inputs.description: Optional parameter for providing an alternative control net wrapper for the segmentation element.

inputs.name: confidence_opt
inputs.description: Optional parameter for specifying the confidence level of the segmentation element. It affects the processing and interpretation of the segmentation element.

inputs.name: label_opt
inputs.description: Optional parameter for specifying the label of the segmentation element. It affects the processing and categorization of the segmentation element.

outputs.name: seg_elt
outputs.description: Returns the modified segmentation element (SEG_ELT) after applying the specified edits, such as scaling the bounding box.

ImpactFloat.description: The ImpactFloat node is designed to process floating-point values, allowing for the manipulation and use of float data within a workflow. It serves as a fundamental building block in operations that require precise numerical computations.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: Specifies the floating-point value to be processed. This parameter is central to the node's operation, as it determines the exact float value that will be manipulated or utilized.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: Outputs the processed floating-point value. This is the result of any computations or manipulations performed on the input float value.

ImpactFrom_SEG_ELT.description: The `ImpactFrom_SEG_ELT` node is designed to process segmentation elements (SEG_ELT) by extracting and transforming relevant information such as cropped images, masks, and bounding boxes. It aims to facilitate further analysis or manipulation of these elements by providing detailed attributes including crop regions, bounding boxes, control network wrappers, confidence levels, and labels.

inputs.name: seg_elt
inputs.description: The segmentation element (SEG_ELT) input is crucial for extracting and transforming detailed attributes such as cropped images, masks, and bounding boxes. It serves as the foundation for the node's operation, enabling the analysis or manipulation of segmentation data.

outputs.name: seg_elt
outputs.description: Returns the original segmentation element (SEG_ELT) with potentially modified attributes.

outputs.name: cropped_image
outputs.description: Provides the cropped image extracted from the segmentation element.

outputs.name: cropped_mask
outputs.description: Provides the cropped mask associated with the segmentation element.

outputs.name: crop_region
outputs.description: Returns the crop region used to extract the cropped image and mask.

outputs.name: bbox
outputs.description: Returns the bounding box of the segmentation element.

outputs.name: control_net_wrapper
outputs.description: Provides the control network wrapper associated with the segmentation element.

outputs.name: confidence
outputs.description: Returns the confidence level of the segmentation element.

outputs.name: label
outputs.description: Provides the label assigned to the segmentation element.

ImpactFrom_SEG_ELT_bbox.description: This node is designed to extract the bounding box coordinates from a given segmentation element, providing a straightforward way to access the spatial boundaries of an object within an image.

inputs.name: bbox
inputs.description: The bounding box of a segmentation element, specifying the spatial boundaries of an object within an image. It is crucial for determining the area of interest.

outputs.name: left
outputs.description: The left coordinate of the bounding box.

outputs.name: top
outputs.description: The top coordinate of the bounding box.

outputs.name: right
outputs.description: The right coordinate of the bounding box.

outputs.name: bottom
outputs.description: The bottom coordinate of the bounding box.

ImpactFrom_SEG_ELT_crop_region.description: This node is designed to extract the bounding box coordinates from a given crop region of a segmented element. It serves as a utility within the ImpactPack to facilitate operations that require precise location information of a segment within an image.

inputs.name: crop_region
inputs.description: Specifies the crop region from which to extract the bounding box coordinates. This parameter is crucial for determining the exact area of interest within the segmented element.

outputs.name: left
outputs.description: The left coordinate of the bounding box extracted from the crop region.

outputs.name: top
outputs.description: The top coordinate of the bounding box extracted from the crop region.

outputs.name: right
outputs.description: The right coordinate of the bounding box extracted from the crop region.

outputs.name: bottom
outputs.description: The bottom coordinate of the bounding box extracted from the crop region.

ImpactGaussianBlurMask.description: The ImpactGaussianBlurMask node is designed to apply a Gaussian blur to a given mask, normalizing it to a 3-dimensional format if necessary. This process enhances the mask's smoothness and can be adjusted through kernel size and sigma parameters, making it suitable for applications requiring softened edges or gradients in mask representations.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The mask input represents the target mask for the Gaussian blur operation. It is crucial for defining the area to be smoothed.

inputs.name: kernel_size
inputs.description: Specifies the size of the Gaussian kernel used for blurring. Larger values increase the blur effect.

inputs.name: sigma
inputs.description: Determines the spread of the blur effect. Higher sigma values result in a more pronounced blur.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The output is a blurred version of the input mask, processed to enhance smoothness and visual quality.

ImpactGaussianBlurMaskInSEGS.description: This node applies a Gaussian blur to the masks within a collection of segmentation elements (SEGS), potentially enhancing the visual quality or aiding in the processing of these elements. It allows for the adjustment of the blur intensity and size, enabling fine-tuned control over the appearance of the segmentation masks.

inputs.name: segs
inputs.description: The collection of segmentation elements (SEGS) to which the Gaussian blur will be applied. This parameter is crucial for specifying the input data that will undergo the blurring process.

inputs.name: kernel_size
inputs.description: Specifies the size of the Gaussian kernel used for blurring. A larger kernel size results in a more pronounced blur effect, allowing for greater control over the visual outcome.

inputs.name: sigma
inputs.description: Determines the standard deviation of the Gaussian kernel. This parameter influences the spread of the blur; a higher sigma value leads to a softer, more diffuse blur effect.

outputs.name: segs
outputs.description: The modified collection of segmentation elements (SEGS) with the masks blurred using the specified Gaussian parameters. This output reflects the visual alteration performed on the input data.

ImpactHFTransformersClassifierProvider.description: Provides a classification pipeline for images using pre-trained models from Hugging Face Transformers. It allows selecting a model from a predefined list or specifying a custom model repository ID, and supports device mode configuration for performance optimization.

inputs.name: preset_repo_id
inputs.description: Specifies the pre-trained model to use for classification. It can be selected from a predefined list of model URLs or set to 'Manual repo id' for custom models, enabling flexibility in model choice.

inputs.name: manual_repo_id
inputs.description: The repository ID of a custom model to be used for classification when 'Manual repo id' is selected. This allows for the use of models outside the predefined list.

inputs.name: device_mode
inputs.description: Determines the device (CPU or GPU) on which the classification pipeline will run, optimizing for performance or resource availability.

outputs.name: transformers_classifier
outputs.description: The classification pipeline configured with the selected model, ready for image classification tasks.

ImpactIfNone.description: The ImpactIfNone node is designed to evaluate whether a given input is None and conditionally execute logic based on that evaluation. It abstracts the process of null-checking, allowing for streamlined decision-making in data flows where the presence or absence of data dictates subsequent actions.

inputs.name: signal
inputs.description: The 'signal' parameter is an optional input that the node can process alongside 'any_input' to determine the flow of logic based on the presence of data.

inputs.name: any_input
inputs.description: The 'any_input' parameter is evaluated to check if it is None. Its presence or absence influences the node's decision-making process and the output generated.

outputs.name: signal_opt
outputs.description: The 'signal_opt' output returns the 'signal' input if 'any_input' is not None, facilitating conditional logic flows.

outputs.name: bool
outputs.description: The 'bool' output indicates whether 'any_input' was None (False) or not (True), providing a boolean flag for further decision-making.

ImpactImageBatchToImageList.description: This node is designed to convert a batch of images into a list of individual images, facilitating operations that require handling images one at a time. It's particularly useful in workflows where images need to be processed or analyzed separately after being batch-processed.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input parameter 'image' represents the batch of images to be split into individual images. It plays a crucial role in the node's operation by providing the data that will be decomposed.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is a list of individual images, each extracted from the input batch. This allows for further individual processing or analysis of each image.

ImpactImageInfo.description: The ImpactImageInfo node is designed to extract and provide detailed information about an image within the context of enhancing or detailing images for visual impact. It focuses on analyzing image characteristics and metadata to support subsequent processing steps, such as detailing, segmentation, or enhancement, tailored to the specific needs of the image.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: The 'value' parameter represents the input image whose characteristics such as batch size, height, width, and channel count are to be analyzed and returned. This information is crucial for understanding the image's structure and for facilitating further image processing operations.

outputs.name: batch
outputs.description: The 'batch' output indicates the batch size of the input image tensor, which is essential for batch processing scenarios.

outputs.name: height
outputs.description: The 'height' output provides the height of the input image, which is crucial for understanding the image's dimensions.

outputs.name: width
outputs.description: The 'width' output provides the width of the input image, indicating its dimensions.

outputs.name: channel
outputs.description: The 'channel' output indicates the number of channels in the input image, such as RGB channels, which is essential for color image processing.

ImpactInt.description: The ImpactInt node is designed to process integer values within a specified range, allowing for the manipulation and validation of integer inputs in a workflow.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: Specifies the integer value to be processed. This parameter allows for the validation and manipulation of the input value within the defined range.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: Returns the processed integer value, ensuring it adheres to the specified constraints.

ImpactInversedSwitch.description: This node is designed to selectively invert the input signal based on a specified condition. It operates by examining the 'select' input and, depending on its value and type, either directly uses the input value or retrieves and uses a specific value from another node. This functionality allows for dynamic control flow and decision-making within a node network, enabling the inversion of signals based on runtime conditions.

inputs.name: select
inputs.description: The 'select' input determines the condition under which the input signal is inverted. It can be a direct value or a reference to another node's output, allowing for dynamic and conditional inversion based on the network's state.

inputs.name: input
inputs.description: The 'input' parameter represents the signal to be potentially inverted. The inversion is conditional, based on the evaluation of the 'select' parameter.

outputs.description: unknown

ImpactIPAdapterApplySEGS.description: This node applies an IP Adapter to SEGS (segmentation elements), enhancing or modifying them based on a set of parameters and a reference image. It allows for the dynamic adjustment of segmentation elements through image processing techniques and neural network models, facilitating complex image manipulation tasks.

inputs.name: segs
inputs.description: The segmentation elements to be processed, typically including information such as crop regions and masks.

inputs.name: ipadapter_pipe
inputs.description: A pipeline of models or functions that the IP Adapter will use to process the segmentation elements.

inputs.name: weight
inputs.description: A parameter controlling the influence of the IP Adapter on the segmentation elements.

inputs.name: noise
inputs.description: An optional noise parameter that can be applied for variability in the adaptation process.

inputs.name: weight_type
inputs.description: Specifies the type of weighting mechanism used in the adaptation process.

inputs.name: start_at
inputs.description: Defines the starting point within the pipeline for applying the IP Adapter.

inputs.name: end_at
inputs.description: Specifies the endpoint within the pipeline for the application of the IP Adapter.

inputs.name: unfold_batch
inputs.description: Determines whether the processing should unfold in batches for efficiency.

inputs.name: faceid_v2
inputs.description: An optional parameter for face identification, relevant in certain contexts.

inputs.name: weight_v2
inputs.description: A secondary weight parameter, potentially used for more nuanced control.

inputs.name: context_crop_factor
inputs.description: Adjusts the crop region in relation to the context, affecting how much of the surrounding area is considered in the adaptation.

inputs.name: reference_image
inputs.description: The reference image against which the segmentation elements are adapted or modified.

inputs.name: combine_embeds
inputs.description: Determines how embeddings are combined in the adaptation process, with options such as 'concat'.

inputs.name: neg_image
inputs.description: An optional negative image that can be used for contrast or as a counter-reference in the adaptation.

outputs.name: segs
outputs.description: The enhanced or modified segmentation elements after applying the IP Adapter.

ImpactIsNotEmptySEGS.description: This node checks if a given SEGS (segmentation data structure) is not empty. It is useful for determining whether segmentation results contain any segments, aiding in decision-making processes within workflows that involve image segmentation.

inputs.name: segs
inputs.description: The SEGS input represents the segmentation data structure to be checked for non-emptiness. It is crucial for determining the presence of segmentation results.

outputs.name: boolean
outputs.description: The output is a boolean indicating whether the input SEGS contains any segments. True means there are segments present, and False indicates an empty SEGS.

ImpactKSamplerAdvancedBasicPipe.description: This node provides an advanced sampling mechanism tailored for generating or modifying images through a sophisticated pipeline. It leverages a combination of models and custom sampling strategies to enhance the quality and control of the output images, focusing on achieving specific visual impacts or adjustments.

inputs.name: basic_pipe
inputs.description: Represents the core components required for sampling, including models and configurations, essential for the advanced sampling process.

inputs.name: add_noise
inputs.description: Indicates whether additional noise should be introduced in the sampling process.

inputs.name: noise_seed
inputs.description: Provides a seed for the random noise generation, ensuring reproducibility in the sampling outcomes.

inputs.name: steps
inputs.description: Determines the total number of steps in the sampling process, affecting the detail and quality of the generated images.

inputs.name: cfg
inputs.description: Specifies the classifier free guidance value, influencing the direction and strength of the sampling process.

inputs.name: sampler_name
inputs.description: Identifies the specific sampler to be used, allowing for customization of the sampling strategy.

inputs.name: scheduler
inputs.description: Defines the noise schedule to be applied during the sampling process, affecting the progression of noise addition or removal.

inputs.name: latent_image
inputs.description: The initial latent image to be modified or enhanced through the sampling process.

inputs.name: start_at_step
inputs.description: Specifies the starting step for the sampling process within the defined range of steps.

inputs.name: end_at_step
inputs.description: Defines the ending step for the sampling, allowing for partial application of the sampling process.

inputs.name: return_with_leftover_noise
inputs.description: Decides whether the output latent image should retain some of the introduced noise, affecting the final image texture.

inputs.name: scheduler_func_opt
inputs.description: [OPTIONAL] Specifies an alternative noise schedule generation function, offering flexibility beyond the predefined scheduler.

outputs.name: basic_pipe
outputs.description: The core components used in the sampling process, returned unchanged.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The resulting latent image after the sampling process, ready for further processing or conversion to an image.

outputs.name: vae
outputs.description: The VAE model used in the sampling process, facilitating transformations between latent and image spaces.

ImpactKSamplerBasicPipe.description: The ImpactKSamplerBasicPipe node is designed for advanced sampling techniques within the ComfyUI Impact Pack. It leverages a basic sampling pipeline to generate or modify latent images based on specified parameters, such as noise addition and classifier guidance, to achieve desired visual effects or enhancements.

inputs.name: basic_pipe
inputs.description: Represents the core components required for sampling, including models and configurations necessary for the operation.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: Used to initialize the random number generator for reproducible noise generation during sampling.

inputs.name: steps
inputs.description: Defines the total number of steps to perform during the sampling process.

inputs.name: cfg
inputs.description: Specifies the classifier free guidance value, influencing the direction and strength of the generated modifications.

inputs.name: sampler_name
inputs.description: Identifies the specific sampler to use, allowing for different sampling strategies.

inputs.name: scheduler
inputs.description: Determines the noise schedule to be applied throughout the sampling steps.

inputs.name: latent_image
inputs.description: The input latent image to be processed or modified through sampling.

inputs.name: denoise
inputs.description: Controls the amount of noise reduction, affecting the final output's clarity and detail.

inputs.name: scheduler_func_opt
inputs.description: Optional parameter for providing a custom noise schedule function, offering more control over the sampling process.

outputs.name: basic_pipe
outputs.description: Passes through the input basic_pipe, including all its components, unchanged.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The resulting latent image after applying the sampling process, reflecting the specified modifications.

outputs.name: vae
outputs.description: The VAE component from the input basic_pipe, included in the output for potential further processing.

ImpactLatentInfo.description: The ImpactLatentInfo node is designed to process latent representations, specifically by analyzing their shape and dimensions. It abstracts the complexity of handling latent spaces by providing a straightforward interface for extracting critical dimensional information.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: The 'value' parameter represents the latent representation to be analyzed. It is crucial for determining the shape and dimensions of the latent space, which are essential for further processing or manipulation.

outputs.name: batch
outputs.description: Represents the batch size of the input latent representation.

outputs.name: height
outputs.description: Indicates the modified height dimension of the latent representation.

outputs.name: width
outputs.description: Indicates the modified width dimension of the latent representation.

outputs.name: channel
outputs.description: Represents the channel dimension of the input latent representation.

ImpactLogger.description: The ImpactLogger node is designed for logging and debugging purposes within the ImpactPack framework. It captures and prints data, text, and additional information related to the execution of nodes, facilitating the monitoring and troubleshooting of workflows.

inputs.name: data
inputs.description: The primary data input for logging. This can be of any type and is central to what the logger will output, showcasing the node's flexibility in handling various data forms.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: A text input that allows for multiline strings, providing context or additional information to be logged alongside the data.

ImpactLogicalOperators.description: This node performs logical operations (AND, OR, XOR) on two boolean inputs, returning the result of the operation as a boolean value. It abstracts the complexity of logical decision-making processes into a simple interface, enabling conditional logic flows within a system.

inputs.name: operator
inputs.description: Specifies the logical operation to be performed: AND, OR, XOR. This determines how the two boolean inputs will be combined to produce the output.

inputs.name: bool_a
inputs.description: The first boolean input for the logical operation. Acts as one of the operands in the logical expression.

inputs.name: bool_b
inputs.description: The second boolean input for the logical operation. Acts as the other operand in the logical expression.

outputs.name: boolean
outputs.description: The result of the logical operation performed on the two input booleans.

ImpactMakeImageBatch.description: The ImpactMakeImageBatch node is designed to aggregate multiple images into a single batch. This process involves potentially resizing images to ensure uniform dimensions across the batch, facilitating operations that require consistent image sizes. The node serves as a utility within the Impact Pack, streamlining the handling of images for batch processing.

inputs.name: image1
inputs.description: The primary image to which subsequent images will be concatenated. It serves as the reference for resizing operations if other images differ in dimensions.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: A single tensor representing a batch of images, where each image has been resized as necessary to match the dimensions of the first image in the batch.

ImpactMakeImageList.description: The `ImpactMakeImageList` node is designed to aggregate multiple image inputs into a single list. This functionality is essential for scenarios where handling a collection of images as a unified entity is required, facilitating operations that span across multiple images.

inputs.name: image1
inputs.description: The primary image input for the node. It serves as the initial element in the resulting image list, setting the stage for additional images to be appended.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: A list of images aggregated from the input. This output is crucial for subsequent operations that require processing multiple images simultaneously.

ImpactMakeTileSEGS.description: The ImpactMakeTileSEGS node is designed for segmenting images into tiles based on specified bounding box sizes and overlap criteria. It applies various filters to include or exclude specific segments, adjusts tile sizes and overlaps to accommodate irregular masks, and ensures that the segmentation respects the image's dimensions and the specified constraints. This node is particularly useful in scenarios where image analysis or processing needs to be localized to smaller, manageable regions within larger images.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: Specifies the images to be segmented into tiles. This is the primary input that the node operates on, determining the scope of the segmentation process.

inputs.name: bbox_size
inputs.description: Specifies the size of the bounding box for each tile. It determines how large each segmented tile will be, directly affecting the granularity of the segmentation process.

inputs.name: crop_factor
inputs.description: Determines the factor by which the bounding box is enlarged or reduced, affecting the size of the segmented tiles. This parameter is crucial for adjusting the coverage area of each tile, ensuring that the segmentation process can be tailored to specific analysis needs or to accommodate varying image sizes.

inputs.name: min_overlap
inputs.description: Defines the minimum overlap between adjacent tiles. This parameter ensures that important features are not missed at the boundaries of tiles by providing a buffer zone where tiles overlap.

inputs.name: filter_segs_dilation
inputs.description: Specifies the dilation applied to the segments before filtering. This can alter the inclusion or exclusion of segments based on their expanded boundaries, directly influencing the segmentation outcome by modifying how segments are considered for tiling.

inputs.name: mask_irregularity
inputs.description: Specifies the degree of irregularity allowed for masks within the tiles. This parameter helps in fine-tuning the segmentation process to either include or exclude tiles based on the irregularity of their masks, affecting the overall quality and relevance of the segmented tiles.

inputs.name: irregular_mask_mode
inputs.description: Determines the mode of handling irregular masks, such as ignoring, including, or exclusively focusing on irregularly shaped segments. This affects the node's execution by guiding the segmentation process to prioritize or deprioritize certain types of segments based on their shape.

inputs.name: filter_in_segs_opt
inputs.description: Provides options for including specific segments based on predefined criteria. This influences the node's execution by allowing for the customization of the segmentation process to target or highlight particular features or areas within the images.

inputs.name: filter_out_segs_opt
inputs.description: Provides options for excluding specific segments based on predefined criteria. This parameter plays a critical role in refining the output by removing unwanted segments, thereby enhancing the focus and relevance of the segmented tiles.

outputs.name: segs
outputs.description: Outputs the segmented tiles along with their corresponding segments, facilitating further processing or analysis. This output is crucial for downstream tasks that require segmented image data.

ImpactMinMax.description: The ImpactMinMax node is designed to compare two input values and return either the maximum or minimum value based on a specified mode. This functionality is essential for operations requiring conditional selection between two values, such as optimizing performance or making decisions based on dynamic input.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Determines whether the maximum or minimum of the two inputs will be returned. When true, the maximum value is selected; otherwise, the minimum value is chosen.

inputs.name: a
inputs.description: One of the two values to be compared. This input, along with 'b', is essential for determining the output based on the selected mode.

inputs.name: b
inputs.description: The second of the two values to be compared. This input is crucial for the comparison operation alongside 'a'.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: The result of the comparison, either the maximum or minimum value between the two inputs, depending on the mode.

ImpactNeg.description: The ImpactNeg node is designed to invert the truth value of a given boolean input. It serves as a logical NOT operation, transforming true to false and vice versa, thus enabling conditional logic flows within a node network.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: The 'value' parameter represents the boolean input to be negated. Its inversion facilitates the execution of conditional logic based on the negated result.

outputs.name: boolean
outputs.description: The output is the negated boolean value of the input, enabling further conditional logic operations based on the result.

ImpactNodeSetMuteState.description: This node is designed to control the mute state of other nodes within a workflow. It sends a command to mute or activate specified nodes based on the provided state, enhancing the flexibility and control over the workflow's execution.

inputs.name: signal
inputs.description: A generic signal input that triggers the node's operation. It's essential for initiating the mute or activation process.

inputs.name: node_id
inputs.description: Specifies the unique identifier of the node whose mute state is to be controlled. It determines the target node for the mute or activation command.

inputs.name: set_state
inputs.description: A boolean value indicating the desired mute state. When true, the target node is activated; when false, it is muted.

outputs.name: signal_opt
outputs.description: Returns the original signal input, allowing for seamless integration into the workflow without altering the data flow.

ImpactQueueTrigger.description: The ImpactQueueTrigger node is designed to conditionally trigger an action within a queue system based on a boolean mode. It serves as a control mechanism to either proceed with or halt the execution of subsequent tasks in the queue.

inputs.name: signal
inputs.description: A generic input signal that triggers the node's operation. Its primary role is to initiate the execution flow.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: A boolean flag determining whether to trigger the subsequent action in the queue. When set to True, the action is triggered; otherwise, it is skipped.

outputs.name: signal_opt
outputs.description: The original input signal is passed through, allowing for the continuation of the execution flow.

ImpactQueueTriggerCountdown.description: This node is designed to manage a countdown mechanism within a queue system, triggering specific actions based on the countdown progress and conditional logic. It effectively integrates with external systems to update and control the flow of operations based on the countdown state.

inputs.name: count
inputs.description: Represents the current count in the countdown process, affecting the node's decision to trigger the next step or reset.

inputs.name: total
inputs.description: Defines the total count for the countdown, determining when the countdown should reset.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: A boolean flag that controls whether the countdown mechanism is active, influencing the node's behavior in triggering or not triggering actions.

inputs.name: signal
inputs.description: An optional input that can carry additional information or control signals through the node's operation.

outputs.name: signal_opt
outputs.description: Optionally returns the input signal, allowing for conditional data flow through the node.

outputs.name: count
outputs.description: Returns the updated count after the node's operation, reflecting the countdown's progress.

outputs.name: total
outputs.description: Returns the total count value, unchanged from the input, to maintain consistency in the data flow.

ImpactRemoteBoolean.description: The ImpactRemoteBoolean node is designed to interact with boolean widgets in a remote interface, allowing for the dynamic control of boolean values based on external inputs.

inputs.name: node_id
inputs.description: Specifies the unique identifier of the node whose widget is being controlled, playing a crucial role in targeting the correct widget for value updates.

inputs.name: widget_name
inputs.description: Identifies the specific widget within the node to be controlled, enabling precise manipulation of its boolean value.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: The boolean value to be set for the specified widget, dictating the widget's state as either true or false.

ImpactRemoteInt.description: The ImpactRemoteInt node is designed to remotely set integer values for specified widgets within a user interface. It facilitates dynamic interaction with UI components by allowing integer values to be programmatically assigned based on logic or user input.

inputs.name: node_id
inputs.description: Identifies the target node whose widget is to be updated. It ensures that the correct widget in the correct node receives the intended value, directly influencing which part of the UI is affected by the operation.

inputs.name: widget_name
inputs.description: Specifies the name of the widget within the target node that is to be updated. This allows for precise targeting of UI components for value updates, affecting the specific aspect of the user interface that will display the new value.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: The integer value to be set for the specified widget. This value dictates the new state or display of the widget, enabling dynamic UI updates. The chosen value directly impacts the visual feedback or functionality provided by the widget, making it a crucial aspect of UI interaction.

ImpactScaleBy_BBOX_SEG_ELT.description: This node scales the bounding box of a segmentation element by a specified factor, adjusting the segmentation mask accordingly. It ensures that the scaled bounding box and its corresponding mask are correctly aligned and sized, maintaining the integrity of the segmentation element.

inputs.name: seg
inputs.description: The segmentation element whose bounding box is to be scaled. It is crucial for determining the area of interest within the image.

inputs.name: scale_by
inputs.description: The factor by which the bounding box is to be scaled. This directly influences the size of the resulting bounding box and its associated mask.

outputs.name: seg_elt
outputs.description: The scaled segmentation element, including the adjusted bounding box and mask.

ImpactSchedulerAdapter.description: The ImpactSchedulerAdapter node is designed to adapt and select scheduling strategies for various tasks, allowing for dynamic adjustment of scheduling based on specific conditions or preferences.

inputs.name: scheduler
inputs.description: Specifies the primary scheduler to be used, with an option to default to a pre-defined input if no specific scheduler is provided.

inputs.name: extra_scheduler
inputs.description: Allows for the specification of an additional scheduler, offering options such as 'None', 'AYS SDXL', 'AYS SD1', 'AYS SVD', 'GITS[coeff=1.2]', to override the primary scheduler if needed.

outputs.name: scheduler
outputs.description: Outputs the selected scheduler, which could either be the primary scheduler or an overridden scheduler specified by the 'extra_scheduler' input.

ImpactSegsAndMask.description: The node applies a bitwise AND operation between segmentation masks and a given mask, modifying the segmentation data based on the overlap with the mask. This operation is useful for refining segmentation results by incorporating additional mask information, enhancing the accuracy and relevance of the segmented output.

inputs.name: segs
inputs.description: The segmentation data to be refined. It plays a crucial role in determining the final output by providing the initial set of segments to be modified.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The mask to apply to the segmentation data. It affects the operation by defining which parts of the segments will be retained or discarded based on the bitwise AND operation.

outputs.name: segs
outputs.description: The modified segmentation data after applying the bitwise AND operation with the given mask. It represents the refined set of segments that have been altered based on the mask's criteria.

ImpactSegsAndMaskForEach.description: This node applies a bitwise AND operation between each segmentation (seg) and its corresponding mask, effectively filtering the segments based on the mask. It's designed for batch processing, where each segment in a collection is paired with a mask to produce a modified set of segments that only include the areas covered by the masks.

inputs.name: segs
inputs.description: The collection of segments to be processed. Each segment represents a portion of an image that has been identified for further operations, such as filtering or modification.

inputs.name: masks
inputs.description: A collection of masks to be applied to the corresponding segments. Each mask defines the areas within a segment to retain, effectively filtering out the rest.

outputs.name: segs
outputs.description: The modified collection of segments after applying the bitwise AND operation with the corresponding masks. This output retains only the areas of each segment that overlap with the mask.

ImpactSEGSClassify.description: The ImpactSEGSClassify node is designed to classify segments (SEGS) based on specified criteria, comparing attributes or labels within each segment to filter and categorize them accordingly. This process involves evaluating conditions such as greater than, less than, or equal to, between attributes or label scores within the segments, facilitating advanced segmentation and classification tasks.

inputs.name: classifier
inputs.description: The 'classifier' input specifies the classification model to be used for evaluating the segments. It plays a crucial role in determining the classification outcomes based on the model's capabilities.

inputs.name: segs
inputs.description: The 'segs' input represents the segments to be classified, serving as the primary data upon which classification conditions are applied. It is crucial for determining which segments meet the specified criteria and which do not, affecting the node's execution and results.

inputs.name: preset_expr
inputs.description: The 'preset_expr' input allows for the selection of predefined classification expressions or the use of a manual expression. It defines the criteria for classification, impacting the filtering process.

inputs.name: manual_expr
inputs.description: The 'manual_expr' input is used when a custom classification expression is required, providing flexibility in defining specific conditions for segment classification.

inputs.name: ref_image_opt
inputs.description: The 'ref_image_opt' input is an optional parameter that specifies a reference image from which segments may be extracted or compared, enhancing the classification accuracy.

outputs.name: filtered_SEGS
outputs.description: The 'filtered_SEGS' output contains segments that meet the specified classification criteria, effectively separating them based on the comparison conditions applied.

outputs.name: remained_SEGS
outputs.description: The 'remained_SEGS' output includes segments that do not meet the classification criteria, allowing for further processing or exclusion from certain analyses.

outputs.name: detected_labels
outputs.description: The 'detected_labels' output lists all unique labels identified during the classification process, offering insights into the variety of labels present within the segments.

ImpactSEGSConcat.description: The ImpactSEGSConcat node is designed to concatenate multiple segmentation data structures (SEGS) into a single SEGS structure. It ensures that all concatenated segments have the same dimensions and combines them accordingly, handling discrepancies by ignoring incompatible segments.

inputs.name: segs1
inputs.description: Represents the first set of segmentation data structures to be concatenated. It is crucial for combining multiple SEGS into a single structure, ensuring they share the same dimensions for successful concatenation.

outputs.name: segs
outputs.description: The output is a single SEGS data structure that combines the input SEGS structures, ensuring they share the same dimensions. It may return an empty SEGS if no compatible segments are found.

ImpactSEGSLabelAssign.description: This node is designed to assign user-defined labels to segments (SEGS) within a dataset, enhancing data annotation and organization for further processing or analysis.

inputs.name: segs
inputs.description: The segments to which labels will be assigned. It is crucial for organizing and categorizing data segments for analysis.

inputs.name: labels
inputs.description: A list of labels to be assigned to the segments, provided as a comma-separated string. This parameter is essential for the customization and detailed categorization of the segments.

outputs.name: SEGS
outputs.description: The segments with newly assigned labels, facilitating enhanced data management and analysis.

ImpactSEGSLabelFilter.description: The ImpactSEGSLabelFilter node is designed to filter segments (SEGS) based on specified labels, allowing for the selective processing of image segments. It supports custom label lists, including special groupings like 'eyes' or 'eyebrows', to fine-tune the segments that are included or excluded from further processing.

inputs.name: segs
inputs.description: The 'segs' parameter represents the segments to be filtered. It is crucial for determining which segments of the image are subject to processing based on the labels provided.

inputs.name: preset
inputs.description: The 'preset' parameter allows for the selection of predefined label sets or custom labels for filtering. It plays a key role in defining the scope of segments to be processed.

inputs.name: labels
inputs.description: The 'labels' parameter specifies the list of labels based on which the segments are filtered. It directly influences which segments are included or excluded, enabling targeted segment processing.

outputs.name: filtered_SEGS
outputs.description: This output contains the segments that match the specified labels, ready for further processing.

outputs.name: remained_SEGS
outputs.description: This output includes the segments that did not match the specified labels, potentially for alternative processing or exclusion.

ImpactSEGSOrderedFilter.description: The ImpactSEGSOrderedFilter node is designed to filter and order segmentation elements (SEGS) based on specified criteria such as area, width, height, or position. It allows for the selection of a subset of SEGS by ordering them according to the specified criterion and then taking a specified range from the ordered list. This functionality is crucial for scenarios where prioritization or specific ordering of segmentation elements is needed based on their geometric properties or confidence levels.

inputs.name: segs
inputs.description: The segmentation elements (SEGS) to be filtered and ordered. This is the primary input on which the ordering and filtering operations are performed.

inputs.name: target
inputs.description: Specifies the criterion used for ordering the SEGS, such as area, width, height, or specific coordinates. This criterion determines how the SEGS will be sorted before selecting a subset.

inputs.name: order
inputs.description: Determines the order in which SEGS are sorted based on the target criterion. A boolean value where True indicates descending order and False indicates ascending order.

inputs.name: take_start
inputs.description: Specifies the starting index from which to begin selecting SEGS after they have been ordered. This allows for skipping a certain number of top elements.

inputs.name: take_count
inputs.description: Defines the number of SEGS to select starting from the take_start position. This determines the size of the subset of ordered SEGS to be returned.

outputs.name: filtered_SEGS
outputs.description: The subset of SEGS that have been filtered and ordered according to the specified criteria.

outputs.name: remained_SEGS
outputs.description: The SEGS that were not included in the filtered subset, remaining after the ordering and selection process.

ImpactSEGSPicker.description: The ImpactSEGSPicker node is designed for selecting specific segments from a collection based on user-defined criteria. It facilitates the generation of candidate images from the selected segments, enhancing the flexibility in processing and visualizing segment data.

inputs.name: picks
inputs.description: A comma-separated list of indices specifying which segments to pick from the collection. This parameter allows users to selectively process and output only the segments of interest.

inputs.name: segs
inputs.description: The collection of segments from which specific items are to be selected. This parameter is central to the node's operation, serving as the input data that will be filtered according to the 'picks' parameter.

inputs.name: fallback_image_opt
inputs.description: An optional image used to adjust the scale of segments to match its dimensions. This parameter is useful for ensuring consistency in segment sizes when necessary.

outputs.name: segs
outputs.description: The modified collection of segments after applying the selection and scaling operations, ready for further processing or visualization.

ImpactSEGSRangeFilter.description: The ImpactSEGSRangeFilter node is designed to filter segmentation elements (SEGS) based on specified criteria such as area, width, height, coordinates, or confidence level. It allows for the inclusion or exclusion of segments within a given range, enhancing the ability to focus on segments of interest within an image.

inputs.name: segs
inputs.description: The segmentation elements to be filtered. This is the primary data upon which the filtering operations are performed.

inputs.name: target
inputs.description: Specifies the attribute of the segmentation elements to be filtered, such as area, dimensions, or confidence level. This determines the basis on which segments are evaluated and filtered.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Determines the filtering mode, either including segments within the specified range ('inside') or excluding them ('outside'). This affects how segments are selected based on the target attribute's value.

inputs.name: min_value
inputs.description: The minimum value of the target attribute for a segment to be considered for inclusion or exclusion, depending on the mode.

inputs.name: max_value
inputs.description: The maximum value of the target attribute for a segment to be considered for inclusion or exclusion, depending on the mode.

outputs.name: filtered_SEGS
outputs.description: The segments that meet the filtering criteria based on the specified target and range.

outputs.name: remained_SEGS
outputs.description: The segments that do not meet the filtering criteria and are thus excluded based on the specified target and range.

ImpactSEGSToMaskBatch.description: This node is designed to convert a collection of segmentation data (SEGS) into a batch of masks. It processes the input segmentation data to generate a corresponding set of masks, which are then combined into a single batch. This operation facilitates the handling and manipulation of mask data at scale, streamlining workflows that involve the analysis or transformation of segmented images.

inputs.name: segs
inputs.description: The 'segs' input represents the segmentation data that will be converted into a batch of masks. This data is crucial for the node's operation as it forms the basis for the mask generation process.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The output is a batch of masks, where each mask corresponds to a segment from the input segmentation data. This batch format is useful for subsequent processing or analysis steps that require masks in a collective form.

ImpactSEGSToMaskList.description: This node is designed to convert segmentation data (SEGS) into a list of masks. It serves as a utility within the Impact Pack, facilitating the transformation of complex segmentation formats into a more universally applicable mask format, thereby enabling further image processing and analysis tasks.

inputs.name: segs
inputs.description: The 'segs' parameter represents the segmentation data to be converted into masks. It is crucial for the node's operation as it provides the raw segmentation information that will be transformed into a list of individual masks.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The output is a list of masks derived from the input segmentation data. Each mask corresponds to a segment in the input, allowing for detailed analysis and manipulation of individual segments.

ImpactSetWidgetValue.description: This node is designed to set the value of a widget within a node in a workflow, based on various types of input values such as boolean, integer, float, or string. It dynamically adjusts the widget's value and type according to the provided input, facilitating flexible and interactive adjustments within the workflow.

inputs.name: signal
inputs.description: A signal input that triggers the execution of the node, ensuring the node operates within the workflow's execution flow.

inputs.name: image_frames

inputs.name: bbox_threshold

inputs.name: bbox_dilation

inputs.name: crop_factor

inputs.name: drop_size

inputs.name: sub_threshold

inputs.name: sub_bbox_expansion

inputs.name: sam_mask_hint_threshold
inputs.description: A threshold value that influences the selection of segments for SAM (Segmentation-Aided Masking) model hints, guiding the model towards more relevant areas.

ImpactSleep.description: The ImpactSleep node introduces a delay in the execution flow by pausing for a specified number of seconds. This can be useful for timing operations or creating a pause in a sequence of actions.

outputs.name: signal_opt

ImpactStringSelector.description: The ImpactStringSelector node is designed to select a specific string or a set of strings from a given multiline string input based on user-defined criteria. It allows for the extraction of meaningful data or segments from larger text blocks, facilitating text manipulation and processing tasks within a workflow.

outputs.name: string

ImpactSwitch.description: The ImpactSwitch node is designed to dynamically select between multiple inputs based on a specified condition or index. It serves as a control mechanism within a workflow, allowing for the conditional routing of data streams based on runtime decisions.

inputs.description: Specifies the index of the input to be selected for output. This parameter determines which input path the node will follow, affecting the flow of data through the node.

outputs.name: selected_index

ImpactValueReceiver.description: The ImpactValueReceiver node is designed to receive and convert values based on their specified type. It supports a variety of types including strings, integers, floats, and booleans, allowing for flexible data handling within the ImpactPack/Logic category.

It serves as a conduit for sending data across different parts of the application, facilitating communication and data flow.

inputs.name: link_id

inputs.name: signal_opt

ImpactWildcardEncode.description: The ImpactWildcardEncode node is designed to dynamically encode text by replacing specified wildcard patterns with corresponding values or options. It leverages a comprehensive wildcard system to interpret and transform text inputs based on predefined or custom wildcard dictionaries, supporting complex pattern matching and replacement strategies to tailor text outputs for varied applications.

ImpactWildcardProcessor.description: The ImpactWildcardProcessor node is designed to enhance text inputs by dynamically populating them with predefined or custom wildcards. It leverages a comprehensive system for wildcard management, including loading, normalization, and replacement, to inject variability and specificity into text. This node supports both fixed and randomized text generation modes, allowing for controlled or stochastic text transformations based on the provided wildcards.
