inputs.description: The 'image' parameter is the input image for depth map generation, serving as the primary data for depth estimation.

inputs.name: a
inputs.description: The 'a' parameter influences the calculation of normals in the depth map, affecting the perception of depth and texture in the output.

inputs.name: bg_threshold
inputs.description: The 'bg_threshold' parameter sets the threshold for background separation in the depth map, enhancing the focus on foreground elements by filtering out background noise.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: The 'resolution' parameter specifies the resolution for the output depth map, affecting the level of detail and size of the generated depth map.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is a depth map image, providing a pixel-wise depth estimation of the input image.

Inference_Core_MiDaS-NormalMapPreprocess.description: This node is designed to preprocess images for normal map estimation using the MiDaS model. It adjusts images based on specified parameters to enhance the quality of normal map generation, facilitating improved depth perception in visual content.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed for normal map estimation.

inputs.name: a
inputs.description: The 'a' parameter influences the intensity of the normal map effect, allowing for fine-tuning of the depth estimation process.

inputs.name: bg_threshold
inputs.description: The 'bg_threshold' parameter sets the sensitivity for background detection, aiding in distinguishing foreground elements from the background in the depth estimation.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: Specifies the resolution for the output normal map, affecting the level of detail in the depth estimation.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: Produces an image that represents the estimated normal map, enhancing depth perception in visual content.

Inference_Core_ModelMergeBlockNumber.description: This node specializes in merging two models by blending their components based on specified blending ratios for different parts of the models. It allows for fine-tuned control over how elements from each model are combined, facilitating the creation of hybrid models that leverage strengths from both inputs.

inputs.name: model1
inputs.description: The first model to be merged. It serves as the base model onto which elements from the second model are blended.

inputs.name: model2
inputs.description: The second model to be merged. Elements from this model are blended into the first model based on the specified ratios.

inputs.name: time_embed.
inputs.description: Specifies the blending ratio for the time embedding components of the models.

inputs.name: label_emb.
inputs.description: Specifies the blending ratio for the label embedding components of the models.

inputs.name: input_blocks.i.
inputs.description: Specifies the blending ratio for the i-th input block of the models. The index i ranges from 0 to 11.

inputs.name: middle_block.i.
inputs.description: Specifies the blending ratio for the i-th middle block of the models. The index i ranges from 0 to 2.

inputs.name: output_blocks.i.
inputs.description: Specifies the blending ratio for the i-th output block of the models. The index i ranges from 0 to 11.

inputs.name: out.
inputs.description: Specifies the blending ratio for the output components of the models.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The merged model, which is a hybrid of the two input models with components blended according to the specified ratios.

Inference_Core_ModelMergeSDXL.description: The Inference_Core_ModelMergeSDXL node specializes in merging two distinct model architectures into a single cohesive model, focusing on integrating various components such as input, middle, and output blocks along with specific transformer elements. This process is designed to enhance model performance by leveraging the strengths of both original models.

inputs.name: model1
inputs.description: Represents the first model to be merged, playing a crucial role in the combined model's architecture and output.

inputs.name: model2
inputs.description: Denotes the second model to be merged, equally significant in shaping the final integrated model's capabilities.

inputs.name: time_embed.
inputs.description: Adjusts the time embedding layer's influence in the merged model, affecting temporal aspects of the model's processing. This parameter is critical for tuning how the model interprets time-related information, directly impacting the model's temporal processing capabilities.

inputs.name: label_emb.
inputs.description: Modifies the label embedding layer's impact, influencing how label information is integrated into the model. This parameter is key for adjusting the integration of label data, affecting how the model processes and utilizes label information.

inputs.name: input_blocks.i
inputs.description: Controls the blending of the i-th input block from both models, where i ranges from 0 to 8, determining the initial processing of inputs. Each index specifies a particular input block's contribution, directly influencing the initial stages of data processing.

inputs.name: middle_block.i
inputs.description: Affects the i-th middle block's contribution, where i ranges from 0 to 2, crucial for the model's intermediate computations. These parameters are essential for dictating the behavior of intermediate processing stages, impacting the model's overall computational flow.

inputs.name: output_blocks.i
inputs.description: Influences the i-th output block's role, where i ranges from 0 to 8, impacting the final output generation. Each index determines the specific output block's influence on the final model output, playing a significant role in the output characteristics.

inputs.name: out.
inputs.description: Adjusts the overall output layer's behavior, fine-tuning the final model output characteristics. This parameter is vital for the final adjustment of the model's output, allowing for precise control over the output features.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The merged model resulting from the integration of the two input models, embodying the combined features and capabilities of both. This output is a new, enhanced model that leverages the strengths of the input models to achieve improved performance.

Inference_Core_ModelMergeSDXLDetailedTra.description: This node specializes in merging two SDXL transformer models, incorporating detailed configuration options for transformer blocks within the model architecture. It enables precise adjustments and fine-tuning of transformer parameters across various sections of the input, middle, and output blocks, facilitating enhanced model integration and performance optimization.

inputs.description: The second model to be merged, serving as the secondary component in the merging process.

inputs.name: time_embed.
inputs.description: A parameter for adjusting the time embedding layers' weights in the merging process, affecting the temporal dynamics of the merged model.

inputs.name: label_emb.

Inference_Core_ModelMergeSDXLTransformer.description: This node specializes in merging two SDXL model architectures by blending their transformer blocks, allowing for the creation of hybrid models that leverage the strengths of both input models. It provides fine-grained control over the merging process through adjustable parameters for each transformer block component.

inputs.name: model1
inputs.description: The first SDXL model to be merged. It serves as one of the primary sources for the merging process, contributing its transformer blocks to the hybrid model.

inputs.name: model2
inputs.description: The second SDXL model to be merged. It complements the first model by providing additional transformer blocks, enriching the hybrid model's capabilities.

inputs.name: time_embed.
inputs.description: Adjustable parameters for the time embedding layers, allowing for customized integration of temporal aspects into the merged model.

inputs.name: label_emb.
inputs.description: Parameters for fine-tuning the label embedding layers, facilitating a nuanced incorporation of label information into the hybrid model.

inputs.name: input_blocks.i.j.
inputs.description: Adjustable parameters for the transformer blocks within the input section of the models, allowing for customized blending of the models' features. The indices i and j represent the block and sub-block levels, respectively, providing a hierarchical control mechanism.

inputs.name: input_blocks.i.j.transformer_blocks.k.
inputs.description: Parameters for fine-tuning individual transformer blocks within the input section's sub-blocks, offering precise control over the integration of transformer features. The indices i, j, and k denote the block, sub-block, and transformer block levels, respectively.

inputs.name: middle_block.i.
inputs.description: Controls for the transformer blocks in the middle section of the models, enabling a balanced integration of both models' characteristics. The index i represents the level within the middle block structure.

inputs.name: middle_block.i.transformer_blocks.j.
inputs.description: Parameters for adjusting the transformer blocks within the middle section's specific level, allowing for detailed customization of the merging process. The indices i and j indicate the middle block level and the transformer block level, respectively.

inputs.name: output_blocks.i.j.
inputs.description: Adjustable parameters for the transformer blocks within the output section of the models, facilitating precise control over the final model's output characteristics. The indices i and j represent the block and sub-block levels, respectively, in the output structure.

inputs.name: output_blocks.i.j.transformer_blocks.k.
inputs.description: Parameters for fine-tuning individual transformer blocks within the output section's sub-blocks, offering detailed control over the output characteristics. The indices i, j, and k denote the block, sub-block, and transformer block levels, respectively.

inputs.name: out.
inputs.description: Controls for the final output layer adjustments, enabling fine-tuning of the merged model's overall output characteristics.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The resulting merged model, incorporating elements from both input models according to the specified parameters.

Inference_Core_ModelSamplerTonemapNoiseT.description: This node applies a tonemapping technique to modify the noise prediction vector magnitude in a model's sampler, aiming to enhance image generation quality by adjusting the contrast and brightness based on the Reinhard tonemapping algorithm. It allows for dynamic adjustment of the effect through a multiplier, facilitating experimentation with different levels of tonemapping intensity.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model to which the tonemapping technique will be applied. This is crucial for modifying the model's internal sampler configuration to achieve the desired image generation enhancements.

inputs.name: multiplier
inputs.description: A scalar value used to adjust the intensity of the tonemapping effect applied to the noise prediction vector magnitude, allowing for fine-tuning of the image's contrast and brightness.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The modified model with an updated sampler configuration that incorporates the tonemapping technique, aimed at improving image generation quality.

Inference_Core_OneFormer-ADE20K-SemSegPr.description: This node is designed for semantic segmentation tasks using the OneFormer model specifically trained on the ADE20K dataset. It preprocesses images to facilitate semantic segmentation, leveraging a pretrained OneFormer model to analyze and segment the input image into different semantic categories based on the ADE20K dataset standards.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be semantically segmented. This image is processed and segmented into different semantic categories using the OneFormer model.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: Specifies the resolution for the output image after segmentation. This affects the level of detail and size of the segmented output.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output of the semantic segmentation process, which is an image segmented into different semantic categories.

Inference_Core_OneFormer-COCO-SemSegPrep.description: This node is designed for semantic segmentation tasks using the OneFormer model specifically trained on the COCO dataset. It preprocesses images to facilitate semantic segmentation, leveraging a pretrained OneFormer model to analyze and segment the input image into different semantic categories.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be semantically segmented. This image is processed by the OneFormer model to identify and categorize different semantic elements within the image.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: The resolution parameter specifies the desired output resolution of the segmented image. It affects the granularity and quality of the semantic segmentation performed by the OneFormer model.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is a semantically segmented image, where each pixel is classified into one of the semantic categories defined by the COCO dataset.

Inference_Core_OpenposePreprocessor.description: The OpenPose Preprocessor node is designed for estimating human poses from images. It leverages the OpenPose model to detect and annotate various keypoints of the human body, face, and hands, providing a comprehensive pose estimation.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image for pose estimation, serving as the primary data source for analysis.

inputs.name: detect_hand
inputs.description: Determines whether hand keypoints should be detected, enhancing the detail of the pose estimation.

inputs.name: detect_body
inputs.description: Controls the detection of body keypoints, forming the core of the pose estimation.

inputs.name: detect_face
inputs.description: Specifies if face keypoints should be identified, adding facial expressions to the pose analysis.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: Specifies the resolution for the pose estimation process, affecting the precision and scale of the output.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: Returns the pose image, visually representing the estimated poses.

outputs.name: pose_keypoint
outputs.description: Delivers the pose keypoints data, encapsulating detailed information about the estimated poses.

Inference_Core_PiDiNetPreprocessor.description: The PiDiNet Preprocessor node is designed for preprocessing images to extract soft-edge lines, utilizing the PiDiNet model for enhanced line detection. It supports configurable safety modes and resolution settings to adapt to various image processing needs.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed for line extraction. It is the primary data on which the PiDiNet model operates.

inputs.name: safe
inputs.description: A mode that enables or disables safety checks during image processing, affecting the execution path and potentially the output quality.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: The resolution to which the input image is resized before processing, impacting the detail level of the extracted lines.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The processed image with extracted lines, showcasing the capabilities of the PiDiNet model in enhancing line detection.

Inference_Core_PixelPerfectResolution.description: This node is designed to compute the optimal resolution for image generation tasks, ensuring pixel-perfect accuracy by adjusting the image size based on target dimensions and a specified resizing mode. It focuses on achieving the highest fidelity in visual output, tailored to the requirements of the target resolution.

inputs.name: original_image
inputs.description: The original image as a numpy array, which serves as the basis for computing the optimal resolution.

inputs.name: image_gen_width
inputs.description: The target width for the image, guiding the computation towards achieving this dimension.

inputs.name: image_gen_height
inputs.description: The target height for the image, guiding the computation towards achieving this dimension.

inputs.name: resize_mode
inputs.description: Specifies the mode of resizing (e.g., inner fit, outer fit) to determine how the image should be scaled to meet the target dimensions.

outputs.name: RESOLUTION (INT)
outputs.description: The computed optimal dimension (as an integer) for the image, ensuring pixel-perfect resolution.

Inference_Core_PromptExpansion.description: The Inference_Core_PromptExpansion node is designed to enhance and expand input prompts using a pre-trained language model. It automatically adjusts the input prompt based on a given seed, enriches it with additional context or variations, and outputs the expanded version. This process is aimed at improving the quality and relevance of the prompt for subsequent processing or generation tasks.

inputs.name: model_name
inputs.description: Specifies the model used for prompt expansion. It determines the linguistic style and capabilities of the expansion.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The initial text prompt to be expanded. It serves as the base content that will be enriched and extended to generate a more detailed or varied output.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: An integer seed that influences the variation in the expanded prompt. It ensures reproducibility of the expansion process, allowing for consistent results across different runs.

inputs.name: log_prompt
inputs.description: A boolean flag that controls the logging of the original and expanded prompts for debugging or analysis purposes.

outputs.name: expanded_prompt
outputs.description: The enriched and extended version of the original prompt, produced by incorporating additional context or variations based on the seed.

outputs.name: seed
outputs.description: The seed value used for the expansion process, returned for reference or further use.

Inference_Core_ReferenceOnlySimple.description: This node is designed to serve as a reference implementation within the ComfyUI Inference Core framework. It provides a simplified example of how to structure and implement inference nodes, focusing on demonstrating core concepts and practices without the complexity of full-featured nodes.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: Specifies the model to be used for inference, serving as the primary input for the node's processing.

inputs.name: reference
inputs.description: Provides a reference or context for the inference process, aiding in the generation or transformation of outputs.

inputs.name: batch_size
inputs.description: Determines the number of items to be processed in a single batch, affecting the throughput and performance of the inference.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: Represents the processed model data after inference, encapsulating the results in a structured format.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: Contains latent representations derived from the inference process, offering insights or modifications based on the model's output.

Inference_Core_RescaleClassifierFreeGuid.description: This node applies a custom patch to a given model, enhancing its inference capabilities by rescaling the classifier-free guidance process. It adjusts the balance between conditioned and unconditioned generation through a specified multiplier, aiming to improve the model's output quality.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model to be patched, which will have its classifier-free guidance process rescaled for improved inference performance.

inputs.name: multiplier
inputs.description: A scalar value that adjusts the balance between conditioned and unconditioned generation, influencing the final output quality of the model.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The patched model with an adjusted classifier-free guidance process for enhanced inference performance.

Inference_Core_SAMPreprocessor.description: The SAM Preprocessor node is designed for segmenting images using the SAM (Segment Anything Model) architecture. It leverages a pretrained SAM model to process images, adjusting their resolution as needed, and returns the segmented output.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be segmented. This is the primary data the SAM Preprocessor operates on, determining the areas of interest within the image.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: Specifies the resolution to which the input image should be scaled before segmentation. This affects the granularity and quality of the segmentation output.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The segmented version of the input image, highlighting different regions as determined by the SAM model.

Inference_Core_SavePoseKpsAsJsonFile.description: This node is designed to save pose keypoints data as a JSON file, incorporating a filename prefix customization feature. It facilitates the storage of pose keypoints information, enabling further analysis or visualization of pose data.

inputs.name: pose_kps
inputs.description: The pose keypoints to be saved. This data is crucial for capturing the spatial positions of various body parts in an image.

inputs.name: filename_prefix
inputs.description: An optional prefix for the filename, allowing for easier identification and organization of saved files.

Inference_Core_ScribblePreprocessor.description: The ScribblePreprocessor node is designed for preprocessing images to detect and extract scribble lines. It utilizes a specialized model to process the input image and enhance or isolate scribble-like features, making it suitable for applications requiring line extraction or artistic effect enhancements.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed for scribble line detection and extraction. This parameter is crucial for defining the visual content that the model will analyze and manipulate.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: Specifies the resolution to which the input image is scaled before processing. A higher resolution can lead to more detailed scribble line detection but may increase computation time.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The processed image with scribble lines detected and enhanced or isolated, suitable for further artistic or analytical applications.

Inference_Core_Scribble_XDoG_Preprocesso.description: This node is designed to preprocess images by applying a combination of Scribble and XDoG (eXtended Difference of Gaussians) techniques to extract stylized line drawings. It's part of the ControlNet Preprocessors/Line Extractors category, aimed at enhancing image analysis and processing tasks by emphasizing essential outlines and features.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed. It serves as the primary data for the line extraction process, where the node applies Scribble and XDoG techniques to highlight and stylize important features.

inputs.name: threshold
inputs.description: Defines the intensity threshold for the XDoG filter, affecting the contrast and visibility of the extracted lines. It allows for fine-tuning the line extraction to achieve the desired artistic effect.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: Specifies the resolution for the output image. It determines the level of detail and quality of the processed image, ensuring that the extracted lines are appropriately scaled.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is a processed image with stylized lines extracted using the Scribble and XDoG techniques. It highlights essential features and outlines, suitable for further image analysis or artistic applications.

Inference_Core_SemSegPreprocessor.description: The Inference_Core_SemSegPreprocessor node is designed to preprocess images for semantic segmentation tasks within a Detectron2 framework. It integrates custom modifications and configurations to adapt to specific segmentation needs, such as anime face segmentation, and ensures images are correctly formatted and enhanced for optimal segmentation performance.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image parameter is the primary input for the semantic segmentation preprocessing, representing the image to be processed. It is essential for the node to perform the necessary adjustments and enhancements to prepare the image for segmentation.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: The resolution parameter specifies the desired resolution for the image preprocessing. It plays a crucial role in adjusting the image size to meet the requirements of the segmentation model, impacting the quality and accuracy of the segmentation results.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The image output represents the preprocessed image, ready for semantic segmentation analysis. This output is the result of various preprocessing steps applied to enhance and format the image for optimal segmentation performance.

Inference_Core_ShufflePreprocessor.description: The Inference_Core_ShufflePreprocessor node is designed to preprocess images by applying a content shuffle operation. This operation aims to detect and potentially rearrange elements within an image to enhance or modify its content for further processing steps, particularly in tasks that require content manipulation or augmentation.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image to be processed. It is the primary input for the content shuffle operation, serving as the basis for detection and rearrangement of elements within the image.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: Specifies the resolution to which the image should be resized before processing. This affects the granularity of the shuffle operation, with higher resolutions allowing for more detailed manipulations.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: A seed for the random number generator used in the shuffle operation. This allows for reproducibility of the shuffle effect across different runs.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The processed image after the content shuffle operation has been applied. This output is ready for further processing or analysis.

Inference_Core_TEEDPreprocessor.description: The TEED Preprocessor node is designed for preprocessing images to extract soft-edge lines using the TEDDetector model. It adjusts the image processing based on the provided safety steps and resolution, optimizing for control net applications.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed for soft-edge line extraction.

inputs.name: safe_steps
inputs.description: Specifies the number of safety steps to use during preprocessing, affecting the thoroughness and potentially the quality of the line extraction.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: The resolution at which the image should be processed, influencing the detail level of the extracted lines.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is an image that has been processed to highlight soft-edge lines, suitable for further processing or analysis.

Inference_Core_TilePreprocessor.description: The Tile Preprocessor node is designed to enhance image inputs for further processing by applying a tiling mechanism. This involves detecting and adjusting image tiles to improve the quality and consistency of the input images for subsequent stages in a pipeline, particularly in control networks.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed and enhanced through the tiling mechanism. It serves as the primary data upon which the tile detection and adjustment operations are performed.

inputs.name: pyrUp_iters
inputs.description: Specifies the number of iterations for the pyramid upscaling process, affecting the granularity of the tile adjustment. This parameter plays a crucial role in determining the level of detail and the scale of adjustments applied to the input image.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: The target resolution for the output image, influencing the final size and detail level after processing. It determines how the image is resized as part of the preprocessing steps.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: Produces an enhanced version of the input image, where tiling adjustments have been applied to improve its suitability for further processing steps.

Inference_Core_TonemapNoiseWithRescaleCF.description: This node applies a tonemapping and noise rescaling configuration to a given model, enhancing its ability to handle conditional and unconditional inputs by adjusting their scale and contrast. It utilizes a combination of tonemapping techniques and rescaling factors to modify the model's sampling behavior, aiming to improve the quality and consistency of generated outputs.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model to which the tonemapping and noise rescaling configuration will be applied. This configuration adjusts the model's handling of inputs to enhance output quality.

inputs.name: tonemap_multiplier
inputs.description: A multiplier that adjusts the intensity of the tonemapping effect, influencing the contrast and brightness of the noise in the model's output.

inputs.name: rescale_multiplier
inputs.description: A multiplier that adjusts the scale of the conditional generation, affecting the balance between the original and modified noise predictions in the final output.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The modified model with an updated sampling behavior, incorporating the specified tonemapping and noise rescaling configurations.

Inference_Core_UniFormer-SemSegPreproces.description: This node is designed for semantic segmentation tasks, utilizing the UniFormer model to process images and generate semantic segmentation maps. It abstracts the complexity of model loading, image preprocessing, and inference into a streamlined operation, enabling efficient and accurate segmentation of images.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be semantically segmented. This parameter is crucial for determining the content and structure of the output segmentation map.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: Specifies the resolution to which the input image is resized before processing. This affects the granularity and quality of the segmentation output.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output semantic segmentation map of the input image, represented as a tensor.

Inference_Core_Unimatch_OptFlowPreproces.description: This node is designed for preprocessing optical flow data, specifically for enhancing and refining flow estimations through techniques such as upscaling, masking, and applying attention mechanisms. It leverages the Unimatch algorithm to process and improve the quality of optical flow predictions, making it suitable for tasks that require precise motion analysis between video frames.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The sequence of images for which optical flow needs to be estimated. This input is crucial for the node's operation as it directly influences the accuracy and quality of the flow predictions.

inputs.name: ckpt_name
inputs.description: The name of the checkpoint file for the Unimatch model. This determines the specific pre-trained model version used for flow estimation.

inputs.name: backward_flow
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether to estimate the backward optical flow. This affects the directionality of the flow estimation.

inputs.name: bidirectional_flow
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether to estimate bidirectional optical flow, enhancing motion analysis by considering both forward and backward flows.

outputs.name: OPTICAL_FLOW
outputs.description: The enhanced optical flow predictions, processed through the Unimatch algorithm to provide refined motion estimations between video frames.

outputs.name: PREVIEW_IMAGE
outputs.description: A visualization of the optical flow predictions, offering a visual representation of the motion between frames for easier interpretation and analysis.

Inference_Core_Zoe-DepthMapPreprocessor.description: The Zoe Depth Map Preprocessor node is designed to process images to estimate depth maps using the ZoeDepth model. It leverages pretrained models to generate depth estimations, enhancing the understanding of spatial relationships in images for various applications.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image for which the depth map is to be estimated. This image is processed by the ZoeDepth model to generate a depth estimation.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: The resolution parameter specifies the desired output resolution of the depth map. It allows for adjusting the detail level of the depth estimation.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is a depth map of the input image, providing a pixel-wise depth estimation.

Inference_Core_Zoe_DepthAnythingPreproce.description: This node preprocesses images for depth estimation by adapting them based on the specified environment (indoor or outdoor) using the Zoe Depth Anything Detector model. It aims to enhance depth estimation tasks by preprocessing images with a model specifically trained for different environments.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image to be processed for depth estimation. It serves as the primary input for the depth estimation preprocessing task.

inputs.name: environment
inputs.description: Specifies the environment context (indoor or outdoor) for the image, which influences the choice of pretrained model for depth estimation.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: The target resolution for the output image, affecting the detail level of the depth estimation.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The processed image with enhanced features for depth estimation, ready for further analysis or use.

INPAINT_ApplyFooocusInpaint.description: This node applies a specialized inpainting technique using the Fooocus method to enhance or modify images based on provided patches and latent information. It integrates seamlessly with the inpainting process, leveraging learned features and adjustments to achieve high-quality inpainting results.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model parameter represents the base model to which the inpainting patches and adjustments will be applied. It is crucial for defining the starting point of the inpainting process.

inputs.name: patch
inputs.description: This parameter consists of the inpainting head model and the LoRA patch information, which are essential for applying the specific inpainting adjustments to the base model.

inputs.name: latent
inputs.description: The latent parameter contains the latent representation and noise mask of the image to be inpainted, providing the necessary context for the inpainting operation.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: Returns a modified version of the base model with inpainting patches applied, ready for further inpainting tasks.

INPAINT_DenoiseToCompositingMask.description: This node is designed to transform a noisy mask into a cleaner, more usable mask for compositing purposes. It adjusts the mask based on provided offset and threshold parameters to enhance its quality for further image processing tasks.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The mask input is a key component for denoising, serving as the primary data that the node will process to produce a cleaner mask.

inputs.name: offset
inputs.description: The offset parameter allows for adjusting the starting point of the mask's intensity, aiding in the denoising process by setting a baseline for what is considered noise.

inputs.name: threshold
inputs.description: The threshold parameter defines the upper limit of mask intensity to be considered in the denoising process, helping to isolate the significant parts of the mask from noise.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The output is a denoised mask, optimized for compositing tasks by adjusting its values within a specified range.

INPAINT_ExpandMask.description: The ExpandMask node is designed for modifying the input mask by expanding its boundaries and applying a blur effect, making it suitable for inpainting tasks where adjusting the mask size and softness can help in achieving better results.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The 'mask' parameter represents the input mask to be expanded and blurred. It is crucial for defining the area to be inpainted.

inputs.name: grow
inputs.description: The 'grow' parameter specifies the amount by which the mask's boundaries should be expanded. It plays a key role in determining the new size of the mask.

inputs.name: blur
inputs.description: The 'blur' parameter controls the intensity of the blur effect applied to the expanded mask, affecting the softness of its edges.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The output is a modified mask with expanded boundaries and applied blur, ready for inpainting tasks.

INPAINT_InpaintWithModel.description: This node is designed to perform inpainting on images using a specified inpainting model. It takes an image and a mask as inputs, along with the inpainting model, and applies the model to the specified areas of the image to fill in or correct missing or undesired parts. The node supports optional upscaling of the inpainted image for enhanced detail and resolution.

inputs.name: inpaint_model
inputs.description: The inpainting model to be used for the inpainting process. This model dictates the inpainting technique and its underlying architecture, affecting the quality and style of the inpainting results.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image to be inpainted, provided as a tensor. This is the target image where the inpainting will be applied.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: A tensor representing the mask that indicates the areas of the image to be inpainted. The mask guides the inpainting process by specifying which parts of the image need correction or filling.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: An integer seed for random number generation, ensuring reproducibility of the inpainting results.

inputs.name: optional_upscale_model
inputs.description: An optional model for upscaling the inpainted image. This allows for enhancing the resolution and detail of the inpainted areas, improving the overall quality of the output.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The inpainted image, returned as a tensor. This output represents the final result of the inpainting process, with the specified areas corrected or filled in.

INPAINT_LoadFooocusInpaint.description: This node is designed to load specific inpainting models, focusing on initializing and preparing the models for the inpainting process. It abstracts the complexities of loading model weights and configurations, ensuring that the models are ready for use in subsequent inpainting tasks.

inputs.name: head
inputs.description: Specifies the filename of the head model to be loaded. It is crucial for initializing the inpainting head model with the correct weights for the inpainting process.

inputs.name: patch
inputs.description: Indicates the filename of the patch model to be loaded. This model is essential for applying localized adjustments or enhancements during the inpainting process.

outputs.name: inpaint_patch
outputs.description: Returns a tuple containing the initialized inpainting head model and the loaded patch model, ready for use in the inpainting process.

INPAINT_LoadInpaintModel.description: This node is designed to load an inpainting model based on the provided model name. It supports loading models stored in specific formats and prepares them for inpainting tasks by evaluating and configuring them accordingly.

inputs.name: model_name
inputs.description: The name of the model to be loaded for inpainting. This parameter is crucial for identifying and retrieving the correct model file from a predefined directory structure.

outputs.name: inpaint_model
outputs.description: The loaded and configured inpainting model ready for use in inpainting tasks.

INPAINT_MaskedBlur.description: The node applies a blurring effect to areas of an image specified by a mask, with adjustable intensity and falloff, blending the altered regions smoothly with the rest of the image. It's designed for inpainting tasks where selective blurring can help integrate edited areas more naturally.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed. The mask defines areas to blur, allowing for selective focus or smoothing within the image.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: A binary mask indicating areas of the image to apply the blur. It works in tandem with the image to selectively target regions for blurring.

inputs.name: blur
inputs.description: Specifies the intensity of the blur to be applied. Higher values result in more pronounced blurring, affecting the visual softness of the masked areas.

inputs.name: falloff
inputs.description: Determines the transition smoothness between blurred and unblurred areas, enabling a gradual blend that enhances the natural appearance of the image.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is the modified image where specified areas have been blurred according to the mask and blur settings, seamlessly integrating edits.

INPAINT_MaskedFill.description: The 'Fill Masked Area' node is designed to fill areas of an image that are masked, using either a neutral color fill or advanced inpainting techniques. It provides options for different fill methods, including a simple neutral fill or more complex methods leveraging OpenCV's inpainting algorithms, to seamlessly blend the filled area with the surrounding image content.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image tensor to be processed, where masked areas are to be filled. It serves as the primary input for the inpainting operation.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: A tensor representing the mask, indicating areas of the image to be filled. It plays a crucial role in determining which parts of the image are subject to inpainting.

inputs.name: fill
inputs.description: Specifies the method of filling: 'neutral' for a simple color fill, or 'telea'/'ns' for using OpenCV's inpainting algorithms. This choice affects the visual outcome of the filled areas.

inputs.name: falloff
inputs.description: An integer defining the falloff effect around the edges of the mask, enhancing the blending of filled areas with the rest of the image.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The image tensor after the masked areas have been filled, showcasing the result of the inpainting operation.

INPAINT_VAEEncodeInpaintConditioning.description: This node is designed for encoding and conditioning in the context of inpainting tasks, leveraging a Variational Autoencoder (VAE) to process and transform image pixels and masks into a format suitable for inpainting. It encapsulates the functionality to encode both positive and negative conditioning alongside generating latent representations for inpainting and sampling.

inputs.name: positive
inputs.description: Represents the positive conditioning input, crucial for guiding the inpainting process in a desired direction.

inputs.name: negative
inputs.description: Serves as the negative conditioning input, used to steer the inpainting away from undesired outcomes.

inputs.name: vae
inputs.description: The Variational Autoencoder (VAE) model used for encoding the image pixels into a latent space representation.

inputs.name: pixels
inputs.description: The image pixels to be inpainted, serving as the primary data for the encoding and conditioning process.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The mask indicating areas to inpaint, essential for focusing the inpainting process on specific regions of the image.

outputs.name: positive
outputs.description: The encoded and conditioned positive output, ready for inpainting.

outputs.name: negative
outputs.description: The encoded and conditioned negative output, prepared for the inpainting process.

outputs.name: latent_inpaint
outputs.description: A latent representation specifically tailored for inpainting, including samples and a noise mask.

outputs.name: latent_samples
outputs.description: The latent samples generated during the encoding process, useful for further inpainting tasks.

AnimeLineArt_Preprocessor_Provider_for_S.description: This node provides a preprocessor specifically tailored for anime line art within the SEGS framework, facilitating the preparation of images for further processing or analysis.

outputs.name: segs_preprocessor
outputs.description: Returns an instance of a preprocessor designed for anime line art, ready to be used in the SEGS framework.

ApplyRegionalIPAdapters __Inspire.description: This node is designed to apply a series of regional IP adapter transformations to a model, leveraging a pipeline of IP adapters and regional IP adapters to enhance or modify the model's capabilities based on regional information.

inputs.name: ipadapter_pipe
inputs.description: A tuple containing the main IP adapter, model, clip vision module, insightface module, and lora loader, which collectively form the pipeline through which the regional IP adapters are applied.

inputs.name: regional_ipadapter1
inputs.description: A regional IP adapter that is applied to the model as part of the transformation process.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The transformed model after applying the regional IP adapters.

BindImageListPromptList __Inspire.description: The BindImageListPromptList node is designed to integrate image lists with corresponding prompt lists, facilitating the creation of enriched visual-textual datasets. This node aims to streamline the process of binding images with their respective prompts, enabling more efficient and organized handling of visual and textual data for creative or analytical purposes.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The 'images' parameter accepts a list of images to be bound with prompts, serving as the visual component of the dataset.

inputs.name: zipped_prompts
inputs.description: The 'zipped_prompts' parameter takes a list of prompts (zipped format) to be associated with the images, acting as the textual component of the dataset.

inputs.name: default_positive
inputs.description: The 'default_positive' parameter specifies a default positive prompt to be used when the number of prompts is less than the number of images.

inputs.name: default_negative
inputs.description: The 'default_negative' parameter specifies a default negative prompt to be used in similar circumstances as the default positive, ensuring coverage for all images.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: Returns the original list of images, maintaining the visual data integrity.

outputs.name: positive
outputs.description: Returns a list of positive prompts, each corresponding to an image, enriching the dataset with positive textual annotations.

outputs.name: negative
outputs.description: Returns a list of negative prompts, complementing the positive prompts by providing contrasting textual annotations for each image.

outputs.name: prompt_label
outputs.description: Returns a list of labels for the prompts, offering additional context or categorization for the bound image-prompt pairs.

CacheBackendData __Inspire.description: The CacheBackendData node is designed to cache arbitrary data along with a unique key and a descriptive tag in a backend storage system. This functionality supports efficient data retrieval and management by allowing users to store and access data based on unique identifiers and descriptive tags.

inputs.name: key
inputs.description: The 'key' parameter serves as a unique identifier for the data being cached. It is crucial for retrieving the cached data at a later time.

inputs.name: tag
inputs.description: The 'tag' parameter provides a short description for the cached data, aiding in its identification and retrieval.

inputs.name: data
inputs.description: The 'data' parameter is the actual data to be cached. It can be of any type, making this node versatile in its application.

outputs.name: data opt
outputs.description: Returns the data that was cached, allowing for immediate verification or further processing.

CacheBackendDataList __Inspire.description: The CacheBackendDataList node is designed to cache lists of data in a backend storage system, allowing for efficient retrieval and management of data collections. It supports caching data with a unique key and tag, facilitating organized storage and easy access to grouped data items.

inputs.name: key
inputs.description: The 'key' parameter is used to uniquely identify the list of data being cached. It serves as a primary identifier for storing and retrieving the data from the cache.

inputs.name: tag
inputs.description: The 'tag' parameter provides a short description or label for the cached data, aiding in its categorization and retrieval.

inputs.name: data
inputs.description: The 'data' parameter represents the actual list of data items to be cached. It is crucial for the operation as it contains the content that will be stored in the backend.

outputs.name: data opt
outputs.description: Returns the list of data that was cached, confirming the successful storage of the provided data.

CacheBackendDataNumberKey __Inspire.description: This node is designed for caching data with numerical keys in the Inspire Pack backend. It allows for the storage and retrieval of data associated with a unique integer key and a descriptive tag, facilitating efficient data management and access within custom workflows.

inputs.name: key
inputs.description: The 'key' parameter is an integer that uniquely identifies the data to be cached. It serves as the primary identifier for storing and retrieving data.

inputs.name: tag
inputs.description: The 'tag' parameter is a string that provides a short description or label for the cached data, aiding in its identification and categorization.

inputs.name: data
inputs.description: The 'data' parameter represents the actual data to be cached. It can be of any type, allowing for versatile data storage options.

outputs.name: data opt
outputs.description: This output returns the same data that was input for caching, allowing for immediate verification or further processing.

CacheBackendDataNumberKeyList __Inspire.description: This node is designed to update a cache with data associated with a numeric key and a tag, supporting batch operations. It facilitates the storage and retrieval of backend data in a structured manner, allowing for efficient data management within the InspirePack backend framework.

inputs.name: key
inputs.description: The numeric key associated with the data to be cached. It serves as a unique identifier for the data within the cache.

inputs.name: tag
inputs.description: A short description or identifier for the data being cached. The tag helps in categorizing or describing the nature of the data for easier retrieval.

inputs.name: data
inputs.description: The actual data to be cached. This parameter allows for the storage of any type of data, making the node versatile in its application.

outputs.name: data opt
outputs.description: Returns the data that was passed in for caching, facilitating a confirmation of what data was processed.

Canny_Preprocessor_Provider_for_SEGS __I.description: This node provides a Canny edge detection preprocessor for SEGS (Semantic Edge Guided Synthesis), aimed at enhancing image edges for better segmentation and synthesis outcomes.

inputs.name: low_threshold
inputs.description: Specifies the lower bound for the hysteresis thresholding step in the Canny edge detection algorithm, influencing the detection of weaker edges.

inputs.name: high_threshold
inputs.description: Defines the upper bound for the hysteresis thresholding step, determining the detection of the most pronounced edges.

outputs.name: segs_preprocessor
outputs.description: Outputs a preprocessor object configured for Canny edge detection, ready to be used in SEGS workflows.

ChangeImageBatchSize __Inspire.description: The ChangeImageBatchSize node is designed to adjust the batch size of an image tensor to a specified size, using a simple mode to either expand or trim the batch based on the desired count. This functionality is crucial for ensuring that image data is correctly formatted for batch processing in various image manipulation and generation tasks.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image tensor to be resized. It's essential for batch processing where the batch size needs adjustment to meet specific requirements.

inputs.name: batch_size
inputs.description: Specifies the target batch size for the image tensor, determining how the tensor will be resized.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Defines the resizing mode, currently supporting a 'simple' method for expanding or trimming the tensor.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The resized image tensor with the adjusted batch size.

ChangeLatentBatchSize __Inspire.description: This node is designed to modify the batch size of a given latent representation. It achieves this by resizing the tensor associated with the latent samples according to the specified new batch size and mode, ensuring the latent's structure is maintained while adapting to the new batch size requirements.

inputs.name: latent
inputs.description: The latent representation to be resized. It is crucial for maintaining the integrity of the data while adjusting its batch size.

inputs.name: batch_size
inputs.description: Specifies the target batch size for the latent representation, directly influencing the resizing operation.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Determines the method of resizing, offering flexibility in how the batch size adjustment is performed.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The resized latent representation, now conforming to the specified batch size.

CheckpointLoaderSimpleShared __Inspire.description: The CheckpointLoaderSimpleShared node is designed to manage the loading and caching of model checkpoints in a shared manner. It allows for efficient reuse of loaded checkpoints by checking if a checkpoint is already cached before loading it from disk, supporting both read-only and override modes to accommodate different usage scenarios.

inputs.name: ckpt_name
inputs.description: The name of the checkpoint to load. This parameter is crucial for identifying which checkpoint file to retrieve and load.

inputs.name: key_opt
inputs.description: An optional key that can be used to uniquely identify the checkpoint in the cache. This allows for more flexible caching strategies, such as caching the same checkpoint under different keys.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Specifies the caching mode, such as 'Read Only' or 'Override Cache', which determines how the checkpoint should be handled in relation to the cache.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The loaded model from the checkpoint.

outputs.name: clip
outputs.description: The CLIP model associated with the checkpoint, if available.

outputs.name: vae
outputs.description: The VAE model associated with the checkpoint, if available.

outputs.name: cache key
outputs.description: The key under which the checkpoint is cached. This is useful for reference in subsequent operations.

CLIPTextEncodeWithWeight __Inspire.description: The CLIPTextEncodeWithWeight node is designed to encode text inputs using a CLIP model, applying specified strength and additional weight adjustments to the encoding process. This node allows for the customization of text encoding, enabling more nuanced control over the generated embeddings by adjusting their intensity and bias.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The text input to be encoded. It serves as the primary content for the encoding process, influencing the generated embeddings.

inputs.name: clip
inputs.description: The CLIP model used for encoding the text. It determines the method and quality of the encoding, impacting the final embeddings.

inputs.name: strength
inputs.description: A multiplier for the encoding strength. It adjusts the intensity of the text's representation in the embedding space.

inputs.name: add_weight
inputs.description: An additional weight applied to the encoding. It allows for fine-tuning the bias of the embeddings, offering a way to subtly alter their characteristics.

outputs.name: conditioning
outputs.description: The output is a conditioning object containing the encoded text along with any specified adjustments. It's ready for use in further processing or generation tasks.

ColorMapToMasks __Inspire.description: The `ColorMapToMasks` node is designed to process a color map image to identify and extract masks corresponding to the top colors present in the image. It aims to simplify the segmentation of images into distinct color-based regions, facilitating further image manipulation or analysis tasks.

inputs.name: color_map
inputs.description: The `color_map` parameter represents the input image from which masks will be generated based on the dominant colors. It plays a crucial role in determining the segmentation outcome.

inputs.name: min_pixels
inputs.description: The `min_pixels` parameter sets the minimum number of pixels a color must have within the color map to be considered for mask creation. This helps in filtering out less significant colors.

inputs.name: max_count
inputs.description: The `max_count` parameter limits the number of top colors to be considered for mask generation. This controls the granularity of the segmentation.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The output is a tensor of masks, each corresponding to one of the top colors identified in the input color map. These masks enable targeted manipulation or analysis of specific color regions within the image.

ColorMaskToDepthMask __Inspire.description: The `ColorMaskToDepthMask` node is designed to convert a color mask into a depth mask based on various specifications including color codes, base values, dilation, and flatten methods. This process involves analyzing the color mask to apply transformations that result in a depth representation, taking into account the specified parameters to adjust the depth effect.

inputs.name: color_mask
inputs.description: `color_mask` is the input tensor representing the color mask to be converted. It plays a crucial role in determining which pixels will be considered for conversion based on the specified mask color.

inputs.name: spec
inputs.description: `spec` defines the specifications for converting color codes into depth values, including the color code and its corresponding configuration.

inputs.name: base_value
inputs.description: `base_value` sets the initial depth value for the mask before applying any color-specific transformations.

inputs.name: dilation
inputs.description: `dilation` specifies the amount by which to dilate the mask, affecting the depth representation by expanding or contracting the mask areas.

inputs.name: flatten_method
inputs.description: `flatten_method` determines how multiple mask layers are combined into a single mask, with options such as 'override', 'max', and 'sum'.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The output is a depth mask tensor, representing the transformed depth mask derived from the original color mask and the specified transformations.

Color_Preprocessor_Provider_for_SEGS __I.description: The Color Preprocessor Provider for SEGS in the Inspire Pack is designed to preprocess images for segmentation tasks by applying color processing techniques. This node is part of the SEGS (Segmentation) category within the Inspire Pack and aims to enhance image data for better segmentation performance.

outputs.name: segs_preprocessor
outputs.description: Outputs a preprocessed image object tailored for segmentation tasks, encapsulating the necessary adjustments made during the color processing stage.

CompositeNoise __Inspire.description: The CompositeNoise node in the Inspire pack is designed to enhance the generation process by applying a composite noise strategy. It integrates various noise manipulation techniques to adjust and refine the generated outputs, aiming to improve the quality and diversity of the results. This node likely combines different types of noise and processing methods to achieve a more nuanced and controlled generation outcome, making it a versatile tool for creative and generative tasks.

inputs.name: destination
inputs.description: Specifies the destination for the noise application, indicating where the noise will be integrated within the generation process.

inputs.name: source
inputs.description: Identifies the source of the noise, which could be an external input or generated within the system, providing the basis for noise manipulation.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Determines the mode of noise application, such as additive or multiplicative, affecting how the noise interacts with the generation process.

inputs.name: x
inputs.description: Represents a specific parameter or variable related to the noise application, potentially influencing the direction or intensity of the noise.

inputs.name: y
inputs.description: Another parameter or variable that may affect the noise application process, offering additional control over the manipulation.

outputs.name: noise
outputs.description: The generated or modified noise after application, showcasing the effects of the composite noise manipulation strategies.

ConcatConditioningsWithMultiplier __Insp.description: This node is designed to concatenate multiple conditioning inputs, each potentially modified by a corresponding multiplier, into a single conditioning output. It primarily serves to enhance or modify the conditioning context for generative models by adjusting the strength of individual conditionings before combining them.

inputs.name: conditioning1
inputs.description: The primary conditioning input to which additional conditionings will be concatenated. This conditioning serves as the base for subsequent modifications and concatenations.

inputs.name: multiplier1
inputs.description: A multiplier to adjust the strength of the primary conditioning input. This allows for fine-tuning the influence of the primary conditioning on the overall output.

outputs.name: conditioning
outputs.description: The resulting conditioning after concatenating and adjusting the strength of multiple conditionings. It represents a modified or enhanced context for generative models.

ConditioningStretch __Inspire.description: The ConditioningStretch node is designed to modify the dimensions of conditioning areas within a given set of conditionings, adjusting them to new specified widths and heights. This node plays a crucial role in adapting conditionings to fit different resolutions or aspect ratios, ensuring that the conditioning effects are appropriately scaled and positioned.

inputs.name: conditioning
inputs.description: The 'conditioning' input specifies the set of conditionings to be stretched. It is essential for determining the base conditionings that will undergo dimensional adjustments.

inputs.name: resolutionX
inputs.description: Specifies the original width of the image or area to which the conditioning was applied. It's crucial for calculating the stretch ratio.

inputs.name: resolutionY
inputs.description: Specifies the original height of the image or area to which the conditioning was applied, essential for calculating the stretch ratio.

inputs.name: newWidth
inputs.description: The target width to stretch the conditioning areas to. It defines how much the original conditioning areas will be horizontally expanded or contracted.

inputs.name: newHeight
inputs.description: The target height to stretch the conditioning areas to. It defines how much the original conditioning areas will be vertically expanded or contracted.

outputs.name: conditioning
outputs.description: Returns the set of conditionings with their areas adjusted to the new specified dimensions, ensuring they are appropriately scaled and positioned.

ConditioningUpscale __Inspire.description: The ConditioningUpscale node is designed to upscale conditioning areas within a given set of conditionings, adjusting their dimensions based on specified scalar values. It focuses on modifying the 'area' attribute of each conditioning, scaling it to achieve a desired enlargement effect, which is crucial for applications requiring precise control over conditioning dimensions in generative tasks.

inputs.name: conditioning
inputs.description: The 'conditioning' input represents the set of conditionings to be upscaled. It is essential for determining the areas within the input that will undergo scaling, directly influencing the output's spatial characteristics.

inputs.name: scalar
inputs.description: The 'scalar' input specifies the factor by which the conditioning areas are to be upscaled. It plays a pivotal role in determining the extent of scaling applied to each conditioning area, affecting the overall dimensions of the output.

outputs.name: conditioning
outputs.description: The output is a modified version of the input conditionings, with each 'area' attribute scaled according to the specified scalar value. This is crucial for applications that require adjusted conditioning dimensions for enhanced generative performance.

DWPreprocessor_Provider_for_SEGS __Inspi.description: The DWPreprocessor Provider for SEGS is designed to preprocess images for segmentation tasks by detecting various elements such as hands, body, and face, and adjusting image resolution. It utilizes bounding box detectors and pose estimators to enhance the input data for better segmentation results.

inputs.name: detect_hand
inputs.description: Enables or disables hand detection in the preprocessing step, affecting the focus and accuracy of the segmentation.

inputs.name: detect_body
inputs.description: Enables or disables body detection, influencing the segmentation process by identifying body outlines.

inputs.name: detect_face
inputs.description: Activates or deactivates face detection, impacting the segmentation by highlighting facial features.

inputs.name: resolution_upscale_by
inputs.description: Adjusts the resolution of the input image by a specified upscale factor, enhancing the detail level for segmentation.

inputs.name: bbox_detector
inputs.description: Specifies the bounding box detector model to use, affecting the precision of element detection.

inputs.name: pose_estimator

FloatRange __Inspire.description: The FloatRange node generates a sequence of floating-point numbers starting from a specified value, stopping at another, and incrementing by a defined step. FromIPAdapterPipe __Inspire.description: The `FromIPAdapterPipe` node is designed to decompose a previously constructed IP adapter pipeline into its constituent components. This node facilitates the retrieval of individual elements such as the IP adapter, model, and additional features like CLIP vision and InsightFace from a bundled pipeline, enabling further manipulation or analysis of these components.

GlobalSampler __Inspire.description: The GlobalSampler __Inspire node is designed to integrate various advanced sampling techniques for image generation and manipulation within the Inspire Pack framework. GlobalSeed __Inspire.description: The GlobalSeed node in the Inspire pack is designed to manage and manipulate the global seed value used across various nodes in a workflow. It allows for the setting of a seed value, choosing an action to modify this seed (e.g., increment, decrement, randomize), and controlling the seed's application mode (before or after generation). This functionality is crucial for ensuring consistency, repeatability, and variation in the outputs of a generative process.

HEDPreprocessor_Provider_for_SEGS __Insp.description: This node provides a preprocessor for SEGS (semantic edge guided synthesis) using the HED (Holistically-Nested Edge Detection) algorithm. HyperTile __Inspire.description: The HyperTileInspire node is designed to enhance the functionality of models by applying a specialized tiling mechanism. ImageBatchSplitter __Inspire.description: The ImageBatchSplitter node is designed to split a batch of images into smaller batches or individual images, based on a specified split count. KSampler __Inspire.description: The KSampler __Inspire node is designed to perform sampling operations within the Inspire framework, leveraging advanced sampling techniques to generate or modify data based on specified conditions. LoadPromptsFromFile __Inspire.description: The LoadPromptsFromFile node is designed to read and parse prompt data from a specified file, extracting structured information based on predefined patterns. LoraLoaderBlockWeight __Inspire.description: The LoraLoaderBlockWeight node is designed to dynamically load and apply LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) adjustments to models based on specified parameters. RemoveBackendData __Inspire.description: The `RemoveBackendData` node in the Inspire Pack is designed to selectively clear data from a backend cache. RemoveControlNet __Inspire.description: This node is designed to remove control networks from regional prompts within a given dataset. ScheduledCFGGuider __Inspire.description: The ScheduledCFGGuider node in the Inspire pack is designed to dynamically adjust the guidance scale during the sampling process based on a predefined schedule. It allows for the customization of the guidance process by scheduling the guidance scale from a starting value to an ending value over the course of the sampling, enhancing the control over the generation quality and diversity.

inputs.name: negative

inputs.name: to_cfg

inputs.name: schedule
inputs.description: The schedule type for adjusting the guidance scale, such as linear, logarithmic, or exponential, providing flexibility in the guidance process. The choice of schedule affects how the guidance intensity changes over time.

outputs.name: guider

outputs.name: sigmas

inputs.description: Specifies the scale factor to be applied to the Fusers model, influencing the preparation and loading of the model to adjust its output according to the desired scale.

outputs.name: positionnet
outputs.description: Returns the loaded PositionNet model, prepared and ready for use in instance diffusion tasks.

outputs.name: fusers
outputs.description: Provides the loaded Fusers models as a list, adjusted according to the specified scale and ready for integration in instance diffusion processes.

outputs.name: scaleu
outputs.description: Delivers the loaded ScaleU models, making them available for use in enhancing the instance diffusion capabilities.

InstanceDiffusionTrackingPrompt.description: The InstanceDiffusionTrackingPrompt node is designed to integrate text-based prompts with instance tracking information, facilitating the generation of conditioned inputs for instance diffusion models. It extracts and encodes prompts related to specific instances or classes, combines these with spatial tracking data, and prepares them for further processing by instance diffusion mechanisms.

inputs.name: positive
inputs.description: The 'positive' parameter represents the initial conditioning data for positive instances, serving as a foundation for applying text-based conditions.

inputs.name: negative
inputs.description: Similar to 'positive', the 'negative' parameter holds the initial conditioning data for negative instances, which will be augmented with text-based conditions.

inputs.name: clip
inputs.description: The 'clip' parameter is a model used for encoding text prompts into embeddings, playing a crucial role in interpreting the textual information.

inputs.name: tracking
inputs.description: This parameter contains spatial tracking information for instances, crucial for aligning text prompts with their corresponding spatial locations.

inputs.name: positionnet
inputs.description: PositionNet is a model that, combined with fusers, is used to refine the spatial information of instances for better conditioning.

inputs.name: fusers
inputs.description: Fusers are mechanisms that integrate multiple sources of information, such as embeddings and spatial data, to enhance the conditioning process.

inputs.name: positive_text
inputs.description: A multiline string containing text prompts related to positive instances, which will be processed and encoded.

inputs.name: negative_text
inputs.description: A multiline string containing text prompts for negative instances, to be processed and encoded similarly to positive_text.

outputs.name: positive
outputs.description: The output is conditioned data for positive instances, now enriched with text-based prompts and spatial tracking information, ready for further processing in instance diffusion models.

outputs.name: negative
outputs.description: Similarly, this output is conditioned data for negative instances, enriched with text-based prompts and spatial tracking information.

LoadInstanceFusersNode.description: This node is designed to load and prepare instance fusers models from a specified directory, adjusting their scale according to the provided parameter. It facilitates the dynamic integration of fusers models into the instance diffusion process, enabling enhanced control over the fusion of instance-specific features.

inputs.name: model_filename
inputs.description: Specifies the filename of the model to be loaded. This parameter is crucial for identifying and retrieving the correct fuser model from the designated directory.

inputs.name: fusers_scale
inputs.description: Determines the scale factor to be applied to the fusers, affecting their influence on the instance fusion process. This allows for fine-tuning the impact of fusers on the generated instances.

outputs.name: fusers
outputs.description: Provides a list of loaded and scaled fuser models, ready for integration into the instance diffusion process.

LoadInstancePositionNetModel.description: This node is designed to load the PositionNet model, a component of the instance diffusion framework, by reading a specified model file and applying necessary configurations. It facilitates the initialization of PositionNet with predefined parameters and the option to include segmentation information, thereby preparing the model for subsequent instance-based processing tasks.

inputs.name: model_filename
inputs.description: Specifies the filename of the PositionNet model to be loaded. This parameter is crucial for identifying and retrieving the correct model file from a predefined directory.

inputs.name: use_segs
inputs.description: Determines whether segmentation information should be utilized in the PositionNet model configuration. This boolean flag allows for flexible adaptation of the model based on the presence of segmentation data.

outputs.name: positionnet
outputs.description: The loaded PositionNet model, ready for use in instance-based processing tasks. This output encapsulates the model initialized with the specified configurations.

outputs.name: fusers
outputs.description: The loaded fusers model, which is part of the instance diffusion framework, ready for integration with other components.

outputs.name: scaleu
outputs.description: The loaded ScaleU model, another component of the instance diffusion framework, prepared for use in scaling and processing instances.

LoadInstanceScaleUNode.description: This node is designed to load a specific instance of the ScaleU model from a given filename. It utilizes a checkpoint retrieval mechanism to load the model's state and prepares the ScaleU networks for subsequent use in the instance diffusion process.

inputs.name: model_filename
inputs.description: Specifies the filename of the model to be loaded. This parameter is crucial as it determines which specific ScaleU model instance is retrieved and loaded for use.

outputs.name: scaleu
outputs.description: Returns a dictionary containing a list of ScaleU model instances, ready for integration into the instance diffusion framework.

AddLabel.description: The AddLabel node is designed to add textual labels to images, allowing for customization of text position, size, color, and font. It supports various directions for label placement, including overlaying text directly on the image or positioning it around the image's edges, enhancing the image's informational content or aesthetic appeal.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to which the label will be added. This is the primary canvas for the label application.

inputs.name: text_x
inputs.description: The x-coordinate for the starting point of the text on the image. It determines the horizontal position of the label.

inputs.name: text_y
inputs.description: The y-coordinate for the starting point of the text on the image. It determines the vertical position of the label.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: The height of the label area in pixels. This can affect the overall size of the image if the label is not overlaid.

inputs.name: font_size
inputs.description: The size of the font used for the label text, impacting the readability and visual impact of the label.

inputs.name: font_color
inputs.description: The color of the font used for the label text, allowing for visual contrast or harmony with the image and label background.

inputs.name: label_color
inputs.description: The background color of the label area, which can be used to highlight the text or integrate with the image's color scheme.

inputs.name: font
inputs.description: The font used for the label text, selected from a predefined list of fonts. This choice influences the label's aesthetic and legibility.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The text content of the label to be added to the image. This defines what the label will say.

inputs.name: direction
inputs.description: The direction in which the label will be added relative to the image, including options like up, down, left, right, and overlay, affecting the label's placement and interaction with the image.

inputs.name: caption
inputs.description: An optional caption to include with the label, providing additional context or information.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The image with the added label, reflecting all specified customizations.

AppendInstanceDiffusionTracking.description: The AppendInstanceDiffusionTracking node is designed for integrating and enhancing tracking data within the InstanceDiffusion framework. It merges tracking information from two sources, ensuring that class data is combined without duplication, and concatenates prompts for enriched context. This node facilitates the creation of comprehensive tracking datasets for InstanceDiffusion applications, streamlining the process of data preparation for instance-based diffusion tasks.

inputs.name: tracking_i
inputs.description: unknown

inputs.name: prompt_i
inputs.description: unknown

outputs.name: tracking
outputs.description: The merged tracking data, combining class information and IDs from both input sources without duplication.

outputs.name: prompt
outputs.description: A concatenated string of the two input prompts, providing a unified context for the diffusion task.

BatchCLIPSeg.description: This node is designed for batch processing of images using the CLIPSeg model for image segmentation.
