It leverages the CLIPSegForImageSegmentation and CLIPSegProcessor from the transformers library to perform semantic segmentation on a collection of images, adapting the model and processor to the specific hardware configuration (CPU or GPU) and data type for efficient execution.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The input images to be processed for segmentation. This parameter is crucial for the node's operation as it directly affects the segmentation results.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The text prompt used to guide the segmentation process, influencing the areas of the image that will be segmented.

inputs.name: threshold
inputs.description: A threshold value for determining the segmentation cut-off, affecting the sensitivity of the segmentation process.

inputs.name: binary_mask
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether the output mask should be binary, affecting the format of the segmentation result.

inputs.name: combine_mask
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether to combine the output masks for batch processing, affecting the structure of the output.

inputs.name: use_cuda
inputs.description: A flag indicating whether to use CUDA for processing. This affects the execution speed and efficiency, especially for large batches of images.

inputs.name: blur_sigma
inputs.description: The sigma value for Gaussian blur to apply to the output mask, affecting the smoothness of the mask edges.

inputs.name: opt_model
inputs.description: An optional pre-loaded model and processor to use for segmentation, allowing for flexibility in model choice and potential reuse of resources.

inputs.name: prev_mask
inputs.description: An optional previous mask to be combined with the current segmentation, allowing for iterative segmentation refinement.

inputs.name: image_bg_level
inputs.description: The background level for the image, affecting the contrast and visibility of the segmentation.

inputs.name: invert
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether to invert the output mask, affecting the segmentation's focus area.

outputs.name: Mask
outputs.description: The output mask generated from the segmentation process, providing a binary or probabilistic map of the segmented areas.

outputs.name: Image
outputs.description: The original image overlaid with the segmentation mask, visually representing the segmentation results.

BatchCropFromMask.description: This node is designed to process a batch of masks and corresponding images, identifying and cropping out the relevant areas based on the masks. It calculates the optimal bounding box for each mask to ensure that the cropped images are centered and of uniform size, enhancing the consistency of the output. The node also handles cases of empty masks by segregating them, ensuring that only masks with content are processed.

inputs.name: original_images
inputs.description: A batch of original images corresponding to the masks. These images are cropped according to the calculated bounding boxes derived from the masks.

inputs.name: masks
inputs.description: A batch of masks to be processed. These masks are used to determine the areas of interest in the corresponding images, guiding the cropping process.

inputs.name: crop_size_mult
inputs.description: A multiplier that adjusts the size of the cropping area, allowing for flexibility in the size of the output images.

inputs.name: bbox_smooth_alpha
inputs.description: A smoothing factor applied to the bounding box dimensions to mitigate abrupt changes in size between different crops, ensuring a more uniform output size.

outputs.name: original_images
outputs.description: The original images provided for processing.

outputs.name: cropped_images
outputs.description: The images cropped according to the calculated bounding boxes from the masks.

outputs.name: bboxes
outputs.description: The bounding boxes calculated for each mask, used to crop the images.

outputs.name: width
outputs.description: The width of the largest bounding box calculated from the masks.

outputs.name: height
outputs.description: The height of the largest bounding box calculated from the masks.

BatchCropFromMaskAdvanced.description: This node is designed for advanced cropping operations on batches of images based on their associated masks. It calculates the optimal bounding box for each mask, applies smoothing to the bounding box sizes, and adjusts the crop size dynamically to ensure consistency across the batch. This process is aimed at enhancing the focus on relevant image areas while maintaining important aspects of the image composition.

inputs.name: original_images
inputs.description: The batch of original images that will be cropped according to the calculated bounding boxes derived from their corresponding masks.

inputs.name: masks
inputs.description: A batch of masks used to determine the areas of interest within the corresponding images. These masks guide the cropping process by identifying non-zero regions that signify important content.

inputs.name: crop_size_mult
inputs.description: A multiplier applied to the size of the bounding boxes to adjust the final crop size, allowing for flexibility in the cropping process.

inputs.name: bbox_smooth_alpha
inputs.description: A smoothing factor applied to the bounding box sizes to mitigate abrupt changes and ensure a smoother transition between crop sizes.

outputs.name: original_images
outputs.description: The original images provided as input, returned without modification.

outputs.name: cropped_images
outputs.description: The images after being cropped according to the calculated bounding boxes and applied adjustments.

outputs.name: cropped_masks
outputs.description: The masks after being cropped to match the dimensions of the cropped images.

outputs.name: combined_crop_image
outputs.description: A single image created by combining the cropped images, optimized for certain use cases.

outputs.name: combined_crop_masks
outputs.description: A single mask created by combining the cropped masks, corresponding to the combined cropped image.

outputs.name: bboxes
outputs.description: The bounding boxes calculated for each mask, used to determine the crop areas.

outputs.name: combined_bounding_box
outputs.description: The combined bounding box calculated from all masks, used for creating the combined cropped image and mask.

outputs.name: bbox_width
outputs.description: The width of the largest bounding box calculated across all masks, adjusted for crop size and smoothing.

outputs.name: bbox_height
outputs.description: The height of the largest bounding box calculated across all masks, adjusted for crop size and smoothing.

BatchUncrop.description: The BatchUncrop node is designed to reverse the cropping process on a batch of images. It takes previously cropped images along with their corresponding original images and other parameters to accurately restore them to their original context, adjusting for any specified borders and blending as needed. This node is essential for operations where the spatial integrity of images needs to be maintained after processing steps that involve cropping.

inputs.name: original_images
inputs.description: Original images before cropping, used as a reference for the uncropping process to restore the images to their original state.

inputs.name: cropped_images
inputs.description: Cropped images that need to be uncropped and restored to their original context.

inputs.name: bboxes
inputs.description: Bounding boxes specifying the cropped areas within the original images, used to accurately place the cropped images back into their original context.

inputs.name: border_blending
inputs.description: Controls the blending of the borders during the uncropping process to ensure a seamless transition between the cropped and original areas.

inputs.name: crop_rescale
inputs.description: Factor to rescale the cropped images before placing them back into the original images, allowing for adjustments in size if necessary.

inputs.name: border_top
inputs.description: Indicates whether a top border should be added during the uncropping process.

inputs.name: border_bottom
inputs.description: Indicates whether a bottom border should be added during the uncropping process.

inputs.name: border_left
inputs.description: Indicates whether a left border should be added during the uncropping process.

inputs.name: border_right
inputs.description: Indicates whether a right border should be added during the uncropping process.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The result of the uncropping process, where cropped images are integrated back into their original context, adjusted for borders and blending as specified.

BatchUncropAdvanced.description: The `BatchUncropAdvanced` node is designed for the advanced uncropping of images in a batch processing context. It integrates functionalities such as handling multiple images, applying border blending, rescaling crops, and utilizing combined or square masks to refine the uncropping process. This node aims to restore the original dimensions of cropped images while maintaining high fidelity to the original content, especially in scenarios where precise alignment and blending are crucial.

inputs.name: original_images
inputs.description: Specifies the original images before cropping. This input is crucial for the uncrop operation as it provides the reference for restoring the images to their original state.

inputs.name: cropped_images
inputs.description: Contains the images that have been cropped. These images are used alongside the original images to perform the uncropping process.

inputs.name: cropped_masks
inputs.description: Represents the masks of the cropped areas. These masks are essential for identifying the regions within the original images that need to be restored or blended during the uncropping.

inputs.name: combined_crop_mask
inputs.description: A single mask that combines all cropped areas. This mask is used to efficiently handle multiple cropped regions in a batch processing scenario.

inputs.name: bboxes
inputs.description: The bounding boxes that define the cropped areas within the original images. These are used to accurately place the cropped images back into their original context.

inputs.name: border_blending
inputs.description: Controls the blending of the borders during the uncropping process to ensure a seamless transition between the cropped and original image areas.

inputs.name: crop_rescale
inputs.description: Determines whether the cropped images should be rescaled to their original size during the uncropping process.

inputs.name: use_combined_mask
inputs.description: Indicates whether the combined crop mask should be used for the uncropping process, allowing for more complex uncropping scenarios.

inputs.name: use_square_mask
inputs.description: Specifies whether a square mask should be used for uncropping, which can be beneficial in certain contexts for maintaining uniformity.

inputs.name: combined_bounding_box
inputs.description: An optional parameter that defines a single bounding box encompassing all cropped areas, used for more advanced uncropping scenarios.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output images after the uncropping process, showcasing the result of the operation with restored or blended areas.

BboxToInt.description: The BboxToInt node is designed to convert bounding box coordinates from a list format to individual integer values, including the calculation of the center points. This functionality is essential for applications requiring precise spatial locations and dimensions of objects within images.

inputs.name: bboxes
inputs.description: The 'bboxes' parameter represents the list of bounding boxes to be processed. Each bounding box is expected to be a tuple or list containing the coordinates and dimensions of a rectangular area within an image.

inputs.name: index
inputs.description: The 'index' parameter specifies the position of the bounding box in the 'bboxes' list that should be converted to integer values. This allows for selective processing of bounding boxes.

outputs.name: x_min
outputs.description: The minimum x-coordinate of the selected bounding box.

outputs.name: y_min
outputs.description: The minimum y-coordinate of the selected bounding box.

outputs.name: width
outputs.description: The width of the selected bounding box.

outputs.name: height
outputs.description: The height of the selected bounding box.

outputs.name: center_x
outputs.description: The x-coordinate of the center point of the selected bounding box.

outputs.name: center_y
outputs.description: The y-coordinate of the center point of the selected bounding box.

BboxVisualize.description: The BboxVisualize node is designed to overlay bounding boxes on images, enhancing visual analysis by clearly delineating detected objects or areas of interest. It operates by drawing colored lines around specified regions, facilitating the evaluation of object detection models or the visualization of spatial data within images.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: A batch of images on which bounding boxes will be drawn. This input is essential for visualizing how well detected regions align with the objects or areas of interest in the images.

inputs.name: bboxes
inputs.description: A list of bounding box coordinates specifying the regions to be highlighted on the images. Each bounding box is defined by its top-left corner coordinates, width, and height, which are crucial for accurately drawing the boxes on the corresponding images.

inputs.name: line_width
inputs.description: Specifies the thickness of the lines used to draw the bounding boxes. Adjusting this parameter allows for customization of the visualization's appearance, making the bounding boxes more or less prominent.

outputs.name: images
outputs.description: A batch of images with bounding boxes drawn over them, facilitating visual inspection of detected regions or areas of interest.

CameraPoseVisualizer.description: The CameraPoseVisualizer node is designed to visualize camera poses in a 3D plot, either from a provided text file containing camera intrinsics and coordinates or directly from camera control poses. It supports customization of the visualization through parameters such as scale, base value adjustments, and the option to use exact focal lengths. This visualization aids in understanding and analyzing the spatial orientation and field of view of cameras in a given scene.

inputs.name: pose_file_path
inputs.description: Specifies the path to a text file containing camera poses or can be left empty to use camera control poses directly. It is essential for determining the source of camera poses to visualize.

inputs.name: base_xval
inputs.description: A base value for x-axis adjustments in the visualization, allowing for fine-tuning of the camera's position.

inputs.name: zval
inputs.description: A base value for z-axis adjustments, influencing the depth positioning in the visualization.

inputs.name: scale
inputs.description: Scales the entire visualization, affecting the size and spacing of visualized camera poses.

inputs.name: use_exact_fx
inputs.description: Determines whether to use exact focal lengths from the camera poses or a default value, impacting the accuracy of the visualization.

inputs.name: relative_c2w
inputs.description: Controls whether camera-to-world transformations are considered relative, affecting the positioning and orientation of cameras.

inputs.name: use_viewer
inputs.description: Enables or disables the use of an interactive viewer for the visualization, enhancing user interaction.

inputs.name: cameractrl_poses
inputs.description: Directly provides camera control poses for visualization, offering an alternative to loading poses from a file.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: Generates a 3D plot image visualizing the camera poses, providing a visual representation of camera orientations and positions.

CheckpointPerturbWeights.description: This node is designed to modify the weights of a model checkpoint in a controlled manner, allowing for the introduction of perturbations or adjustments to the model's parameters. Its purpose is to facilitate experiments with model behavior under slightly altered conditions, potentially improving performance or robustness through fine-tuning.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: Specifies the model whose weights are to be perturbed, serving as the foundation for the perturbation process.

inputs.name: joint_blocks
inputs.description: Determines the magnitude of perturbation applied to the weights of joint blocks within the model, influencing the extent of modification.

inputs.name: final_layer
inputs.description: Controls the perturbation level for the model's final layer weights, directly affecting the output characteristics.

inputs.name: rest_of_the_blocks
inputs.description: Sets the perturbation intensity for the weights of all other blocks in the model, excluding the final and joint blocks.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: Provides a seed value for random number generation, ensuring reproducibility of the perturbation effects.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: Returns the model with its weights perturbed according to the specified parameters, ready for further use or analysis.

ColorMatch.description: The ColorMatch node is designed for transferring color schemes between images, utilizing advanced color matching techniques. It supports multiple methods for color transfer, including histogram matching and various statistical approaches, to achieve high-quality color grading, correction, and harmonization across images.

inputs.name: image_ref
inputs.description: The reference image whose color palette is to be transferred. It plays a crucial role in determining the final appearance of the target image.

inputs.name: image_target
inputs.description: The target image that will receive the color palette from the reference image. This image is transformed to match the color scheme of the reference image.

inputs.name: method
inputs.description: Specifies the method used for color transfer. Different methods can produce varying effects, allowing for flexibility in achieving the desired color grading.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The resulting image after color transfer, with the color scheme of the reference image applied to the target image.

ColorToMask.description: The `ColorToMask` node is designed to convert specific RGB values within images into a binary mask, allowing for selective processing or analysis of those areas. It supports batch processing to handle multiple images simultaneously, offering customization through parameters like color selection, inversion, and thresholding for flexible mask generation.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: Specifies the images to be processed. This parameter is crucial for defining the input data on which the mask will be applied.

inputs.name: invert
inputs.description: Determines whether the mask should be inverted. Inverting the mask swaps the areas to be masked and preserved, affecting the final output.

inputs.name: red
inputs.description: Specifies the red component of the RGB value to be masked. This parameter is part of the color selection for mask generation.

inputs.name: green
inputs.description: Specifies the green component of the RGB value to be masked. Along with red and blue, it defines the specific color to target for masking.

inputs.name: blue
inputs.description: Specifies the blue component of the RGB value to be masked. It's a critical part of defining the exact color that will be converted into a mask.

inputs.name: threshold
inputs.description: Defines the tolerance for color matching. A higher threshold allows for a broader range of similar colors to be included in the mask.

inputs.name: per_batch
inputs.description: Controls the number of images processed in each batch. This parameter helps manage memory usage and processing speed when handling multiple images.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The output is a binary mask where the specified RGB color within the images has been converted to white (or black if inverted), and all other areas are the opposite color.

ConditioningMultiCombine.description: This node is designed to aggregate multiple conditioning inputs into a single, unified conditioning output. It leverages the capabilities of other conditioning nodes to sequentially combine conditioning data, facilitating complex conditioning scenarios in a streamlined manner.

inputs.name: inputcount
inputs.description: Specifies the number of conditioning inputs to be combined. It determines the execution flow by dictating how many conditioning inputs will be processed and merged.

inputs.name: conditioning_i
inputs.description: Represents a series of conditioning inputs to be combined, starting from 'conditioning_1' to 'conditioning_{inputcount}'. Each serves as an incremental addition to the combined conditioning output, facilitating a sequential combination process.

outputs.name: combined
outputs.description: The result of combining the specified conditioning inputs into a single conditioning output.

outputs.name: inputcount
outputs.description: Returns the number of conditioning inputs that were combined.

ConditioningSetMaskAndCombine.description: This node is designed to apply masks to conditioning data, adjusting the conditioning based on specified masks and their strengths. It combines the functionality of setting masks and combining conditioned data, allowing for the dynamic alteration of conditioning areas within a given dataset.

inputs.name: positive_i
inputs.description: Specifies a set of conditioning data to be positively influenced by the corresponding mask, playing a crucial role in tailoring the conditioning to specific areas or aspects of the data.

inputs.name: negative_i
inputs.description: Specifies a set of conditioning data to be negatively influenced by the corresponding mask, essential for excluding or diminishing certain areas or aspects from the conditioning.

inputs.name: mask_i
inputs.description: A mask to be applied to the corresponding conditioning data, determining the areas of influence for positive or negative conditioning adjustments.

inputs.name: mask_i_strength
inputs.description: Defines the strength of the mask's influence on the conditioning, allowing for fine-tuned control over how prominently the mask affects the conditioning.

inputs.name: set_cond_area
inputs.description: Determines whether to set the conditioning area to the bounds of the mask or use the default setting, impacting the scope and precision of conditioning adjustments.

outputs.name: combined_positive
outputs.description: The combined result of all positive conditioning data after mask application, reflecting the cumulative effect of positive adjustments.

outputs.name: combined_negative
outputs.description: The combined result of all negative conditioning data after mask application, reflecting the cumulative effect of negative adjustments.

ConditioningSetMaskAndCombine3.description: This node is designed to apply a set of masks to conditioning data, potentially modifying the conditioning area based on specified parameters, and then combine these conditioned elements into a single output. It focuses on enhancing or altering the conditioning process by applying multiple masks with varying strengths and areas, facilitating complex conditioning scenarios.

inputs.name: positive_i
inputs.description: Specifies a set of positive conditioning elements to be masked and combined. The strength and area of the mask applied to these elements can be adjusted, affecting the final conditioning output.

inputs.name: negative_i
inputs.description: Specifies a set of negative conditioning elements to be masked and combined. Similar to positive inputs, the mask's strength and area settings influence the conditioning outcome.

inputs.name: mask_i
inputs.description: The mask applied to the conditioning elements. It defines the area and intensity of the conditioning effect.

inputs.name: mask_i_strength
inputs.description: Defines the strength of the mask applied to the conditioning elements, affecting the intensity of the conditioning.

inputs.name: set_cond_area
inputs.description: Determines whether to set the conditioning area to the bounds of the mask or use a default setting, influencing how the mask is applied.

outputs.name: combined_positive
outputs.description: The combined result of positive conditioning elements after mask application and processing.

outputs.name: combined_negative
outputs.description: The combined result of negative conditioning elements after mask application and processing.

ConditioningSetMaskAndCombine4.description: This node is designed to apply a series of masks to conditioning data, combining them based on specified strengths and areas. It allows for the dynamic adjustment of conditioning areas through masks, enabling precise control over the conditioning process in a multi-step or complex conditioning scenario.

inputs.name: positive_i
inputs.description: Specifies the positive conditioning data to be combined with the corresponding mask. The strength and area of application are adjustable, allowing for nuanced conditioning effects.

inputs.name: negative_i
inputs.description: Specifies the negative conditioning data to be combined with the corresponding mask, allowing for the subtraction or negation of conditioning effects based on the mask's application.

inputs.name: mask_i
inputs.description: The mask to be applied to the conditioning data, defining the area and intensity of the conditioning effect.

inputs.name: mask_i_strength
inputs.description: Defines the strength of the conditioning effect for the corresponding mask, influencing the intensity of the applied conditioning.

inputs.name: set_cond_area
inputs.description: Determines whether the conditioning area is set to the bounds defined by the masks or uses a default setting, affecting how conditioning is applied.

outputs.name: combined_positive
outputs.description: The resulting positive conditioning data after applying the masks and combining them based on the specified parameters.

outputs.name: combined_negative
outputs.description: The resulting negative conditioning data, reflecting the subtractive or negating effects of the masks on the original conditioning.

ConditioningSetMaskAndCombine5.description: This node is designed to apply masks to conditioning data, combining multiple sets of conditioning and masks with varying strengths. It allows for the selective enhancement or suppression of features within the conditioning data based on the masks applied, facilitating complex conditioning scenarios for generative models.

inputs.name: positive_i
inputs.description: Specifies a set of positive conditioning data to be masked and combined. The strength of the mask applied affects how prominently these features will be represented.

inputs.name: negative_i
inputs.description: Specifies a set of negative conditioning data to be masked and combined. The strength of the mask applied affects how these features will be suppressed.

inputs.name: mask_i
inputs.description: The mask to be applied to the set of conditioning data, determining the areas of influence.

inputs.name: mask_i_strength
inputs.description: Defines the strength of the mask applied to the set of conditioning data, influencing the degree of feature enhancement or suppression.

inputs.name: set_cond_area
inputs.description: Determines whether to set the conditioning area to the bounds defined by the mask, allowing for more precise control over the conditioning effects.

outputs.name: combined_positive
outputs.description: The combined set of positive conditioning data after mask application, ready for use in further generative processes.

outputs.name: combined_negative
outputs.description: The combined set of negative conditioning data after mask application, indicating suppressed features for generative models.

CondPassThrough.description: The CondPassThrough node is designed to facilitate the direct passage of positive and negative conditioning data. It serves as a workaround to enable bypassing inputs in scenarios where the Set node's limitations would otherwise prevent such an operation.

inputs.name: positive
inputs.description: Represents the positive conditioning data to be passed through. It plays a crucial role in maintaining the integrity of the data flow, especially in bypass scenarios.

inputs.name: negative
inputs.description: Represents the negative conditioning data to be passed through. It ensures that negative conditioning data can also be seamlessly integrated into the workflow without alteration.

outputs.name: positive
outputs.description: Outputs the unmodified positive conditioning data, ensuring its availability for subsequent processing steps.

outputs.name: negative
outputs.description: Outputs the unmodified negative conditioning data, maintaining its original form for further use.

CreateAudioMask.description: The CreateAudioMask node is designed for generating audio-based visual masks by analyzing the amplitude of audio signals. It utilizes audio data to create dynamic masks that can visually represent the audio's intensity and rhythm, making it suitable for applications requiring audio-visual synchronization or enhancements.

inputs.name: invert
inputs.description: A boolean flag that, when set to true, inverts the color scheme of the generated masks, offering a visual contrast option.

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: Specifies the number of frames to generate for the mask, affecting the temporal resolution of the output.

inputs.name: scale
inputs.description: A scaling factor that adjusts the size of visual elements within the mask, allowing for customization of the mask's visual intensity.

inputs.name: audio_path
inputs.description: The file path to the audio file from which the mask will be generated, serving as the source for audio analysis.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Determines the width of each generated mask frame, impacting the spatial resolution of the visual representation.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Sets the height of each generated mask frame, influencing the vertical dimension of the mask's visual output.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is a series of images representing the audio mask, where each image corresponds to a frame of the mask generated based on the audio input.

CreateFadeMask.description: This node is designed to generate fade masks for images, allowing for the creation of transitions between different visual states. It provides the functionality to customize the fade effect through various parameters, enabling precise control over the appearance of the fade.

inputs.name: invert
inputs.description: A boolean flag that, when set, inverts the fade effect, creating a reverse transition.

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: Specifies the number of frames to generate for the fade mask, affecting the length of the transition.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Determines the width of the fade mask, impacting the horizontal dimension of the generated images.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Sets the height of the fade mask, influencing the vertical dimension of the generated images.

inputs.name: interpolation
inputs.description: Defines the method of interpolation used for the fade effect, allowing for smooth transitions.

inputs.name: start_level
inputs.description: The initial opacity level of the fade, setting the starting point of the transition.

inputs.name: midpoint_level
inputs.description: The opacity level at the midpoint of the transition, allowing for control over the fade's progression.

inputs.name: end_level
inputs.description: The final opacity level of the fade, determining the end point of the transition.

inputs.name: midpoint_frame
inputs.description: Specifies the frame at which the midpoint opacity level is reached, controlling the timing of the transition.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The generated fade mask, which can be used to create transitions between different visual states in images.

CreateFadeMaskAdvanced.description: The CreateFadeMaskAdvanced node is designed for generating sophisticated fade masks with customizable parameters, allowing for advanced control over the mask's appearance and behavior. This node enables the creation of dynamic masks that can be tailored to specific needs, incorporating features such as decay, alpha blending, and the ability to grow or shrink the mask with precision.

inputs.name: points_string
inputs.description: Specifies the sequence of points defining the fade effect over frames, allowing for complex mask transitions based on frame index and corresponding mask values.

inputs.name: invert
inputs.description: When enabled, inverts the final mask output, offering an alternative visual representation where masked areas are reversed.

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: Defines the total number of frames for the mask animation, setting the scope for how the fade effect progresses over time.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Sets the width of the mask, determining the horizontal dimension of the generated mask.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Sets the height of the mask, determining the vertical dimension of the generated mask.

inputs.name: interpolation
inputs.description: Determines the method of interpolation between points, affecting the smoothness and style of the fade transition.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The modified mask after applying the specified transformations, reflecting changes in size, shape, and appearance.

CreateFluidMask.description: The CreateFluidMask node is designed for generating dynamic fluid-based masks for images. It utilizes fluid dynamics to create visually complex and evolving masks that can be applied to frames, offering a unique way to enhance visual content with fluid effects.

inputs.name: invert
inputs.description: A boolean flag that, when set to True, inverts the colors of the generated fluid mask, offering an alternative visual style.

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: Specifies the number of frames for which the fluid mask will be generated, affecting the duration and evolution of the fluid effect.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Determines the width of the generated fluid mask, directly impacting the resolution and aspect ratio of the output.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Sets the height of the generated fluid mask, influencing the resolution and aspect ratio of the output.

inputs.name: inflow_count
inputs.description: Controls the number of inflow points within the fluid simulation, affecting the complexity and dynamics of the mask.

inputs.name: inflow_velocity
inputs.description: Determines the velocity of the inflow within the fluid simulation, influencing the speed and movement of the fluid effect.

inputs.name: inflow_radius
inputs.description: Specifies the radius of the inflow points in the fluid simulation, impacting the size and spread of the fluid effect.

inputs.name: inflow_padding
inputs.description: Sets the padding around the inflow points, ensuring there's a buffer zone within the simulation area.

inputs.name: inflow_duration
inputs.description: Defines the duration for which the inflow is active within the simulation, affecting the initial phase of the fluid effect.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The generated fluid mask applied to images, showcasing the dynamic fluid effects over the specified frames.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: A binary mask representing the areas affected by the fluid simulation, useful for further image processing or masking operations.

CreateGradientFromCoords.description: This node is designed to generate a gradient image based on specified start and end coordinates, colors, and a multiplier. It creates a visual transition between two colors across the image canvas, allowing for the creation of dynamic and customizable gradient backgrounds or elements.

inputs.name: coordinates
inputs.description: A string representing the start and end coordinates for the gradient. These coordinates dictate the direction and span of the gradient across the image.

inputs.name: frame_width
inputs.description: The width of the output image in pixels. It defines the horizontal dimension of the gradient image.

inputs.name: frame_height
inputs.description: The height of the output image in pixels. It defines the vertical dimension of the gradient image.

inputs.name: start_color
inputs.description: The color at the start of the gradient, specified as a string. This color marks the beginning of the gradient effect.

inputs.name: end_color
inputs.description: The color at the end of the gradient, specified as a string. This color marks the completion of the gradient effect.

inputs.name: multiplier
inputs.description: A float that adjusts the intensity of the gradient effect, allowing for finer control over the gradient's appearance.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The generated gradient image, returned as a tensor. This image visually represents the gradient created from the specified coordinates and colors.

CreateGradientMask.description: This node is designed to generate a series of gradient masks based on specified dimensions and frame count. It allows for the creation of dynamic, time-offset gradients that can be inverted, offering flexibility in mask generation for various visual effects.

inputs.name: invert
inputs.description: Determines whether the generated gradient mask should be inverted. Inverting the mask swaps the gradient direction, enabling more creative control over the visual output.

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: Specifies the number of frames (or images) to generate, each with a slightly offset gradient to create a dynamic, time-evolving effect.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Sets the width of the gradient mask, defining the horizontal dimension of the generated images.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Sets the height of the gradient mask, defining the vertical dimension of the generated images.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: Outputs a tensor representing the generated gradient mask(s), which can be used directly in image processing or visual effects pipelines.

CreateInstanceDiffusionTracking.description: This node is designed for creating tracking data to be utilized with InstanceDiffusion, a process that involves generating and managing instance-specific diffusion prompts and tracking information. It facilitates the structured organization of diffusion prompts based on class identifiers and names, enabling targeted image generation and manipulation.

inputs.name: coordinates
inputs.description: Specifies the coordinates for tracking, essential for defining the spatial location and boundaries of the instance to be tracked.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Defines the width of the tracking area, setting the horizontal scale for instance tracking.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Sets the height of the tracking area, determining the vertical scale for instance tracking.

inputs.name: bbox_width
inputs.description: Specifies the width of the bounding box for the instance, crucial for delineating the instance's horizontal boundaries.

inputs.name: bbox_height
inputs.description: Defines the height of the bounding box for the instance, essential for outlining the instance's vertical boundaries.

inputs.name: class_name
inputs.description: The name of the class for the instance being tracked, used for categorization and identification in the diffusion process.

inputs.name: class_id
inputs.description: A unique identifier for the class of the instance, facilitating differentiation and specific targeting in the diffusion process.

inputs.name: prompt
inputs.description: The diffusion prompt associated with the instance, guiding the generation process with specific textual cues.

inputs.name: size_multiplier
inputs.description: A multiplier for adjusting the size of the tracking area, allowing for flexible scaling based on specific needs.

inputs.name: fit_in_frame
inputs.description: A boolean indicating whether the instance should be adjusted to fit within the frame, ensuring visibility and proper placement.

outputs.name: tracking
outputs.description: The generated tracking data, structured for use with InstanceDiffusion, containing detailed instance-specific information.

outputs.name: prompt
outputs.description: A composite prompt string, derived from the class-specific prompts provided, for use in the diffusion process.

outputs.name: width
outputs.description: The width of the tracking area, as defined by the input parameters.

outputs.name: height
outputs.description: The height of the tracking area, as determined by the input parameters.

outputs.name: bbox_width
outputs.description: The width of the bounding box for the instance, as specified in the inputs.

outputs.name: bbox_height
outputs.description: The height of the bounding box for the instance, as outlined in the inputs.

CreateMagicMask.description: This node specializes in generating dynamic masks based on a combination of parameters such as frames, transitions, depth, distortion, and seed. It is designed to create visually complex and customizable masks for use in various multimedia applications, offering a unique way to enhance visual content with magical or mystical effects.

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: Specifies the number of frames for the mask animation, affecting the length and fluidity of the generated mask sequence.

inputs.name: depth
inputs.description: Determines the perceived depth of the mask, adding a sense of three-dimensionality to the generated visual effect.

inputs.name: distortion
inputs.description: Controls the level of distortion applied to the mask, allowing for the creation of more abstract or surreal visual effects.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: Sets a seed value for random number generation, ensuring reproducibility of the mask patterns.

inputs.name: transitions
inputs.description: Defines the types and characteristics of transitions between mask frames, contributing to the visual complexity and dynamism of the mask.

inputs.name: frame_width
inputs.description: Specifies the width of each frame in the mask animation, defining the horizontal dimension of the generated masks.

inputs.name: frame_height
inputs.description: Specifies the height of each frame in the mask animation, defining the vertical dimension of the generated masks.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The primary output mask generated by the node, offering a dynamic visual effect based on the input parameters.

outputs.name: mask_inverted
outputs.description: An inverted version of the primary mask, providing an alternative visual effect that can be used in various applications.

CreateShapeImageOnPath.description: This node is designed to generate images or a batch of images with specific shapes drawn on them. It allows for the creation of images with shapes such as circles, squares, and triangles at specified locations, sizes, and colors. The functionality extends to adjusting the shape's appearance through parameters like blur radius and intensity, enabling the creation of both sharp and soft-edged shapes on a customizable background.

inputs.name: shape
inputs.description: Specifies the shape to be drawn on the image. It can be a circle, square, or triangle, affecting the visual representation in the generated image.

inputs.name: coordinates
inputs.description: Defines the center location for the shape on the image. It is crucial for positioning the shape accurately within the frame.

inputs.name: frame_width
inputs.description: Sets the width of the frame for the image, determining the overall size of the generated image.

inputs.name: frame_height
inputs.description: Sets the height of the frame for the image, determining the overall size of the generated image.

inputs.name: shape_width
inputs.description: Determines the width of the shape to be drawn, allowing for size customization of the shape.

inputs.name: shape_height
inputs.description: Determines the height of the shape to be drawn, allowing for size customization of the shape.

inputs.name: shape_color
inputs.description: Defines the color of the shape, enabling visual customization.

inputs.name: bg_color
inputs.description: Sets the background color of the image, allowing for further customization of the image's appearance.

inputs.name: blur_radius
inputs.description: Applies a Gaussian blur to the shape, enabling the creation of soft edges. The radius affects the degree of blurriness.

inputs.name: intensity
inputs.description: Adjusts the intensity of the shape's color, affecting its visual prominence on the image.

inputs.name: size_multiplier
inputs.description: Modifies the size of the shape based on the multiplier, allowing for dynamic size adjustments in a batch of images.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The generated image with the specified shape drawn on it.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: A mask of the shape drawn on the image, useful for image processing and analysis.

CreateShapeMask.description: This node is designed to generate a series of masks or a single mask with a specified shape, allowing for dynamic creation of animated masks by adjusting the shape's size over a sequence of frames. It supports customization of the mask's dimensions, shape, and growth per frame, making it versatile for various masking applications.

inputs.name: shape
inputs.description: Specifies the geometric shape of the mask to be created. It determines the visual form of the mask, affecting its appearance and utility in masking operations.

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: Defines the number of frames (or masks) to generate. This allows for the creation of animated masks by specifying more than one frame.

inputs.name: location_x
inputs.description: The x-coordinate of the shape's center location within the mask. It determines where the shape will be positioned horizontally.

inputs.name: location_y
inputs.description: The y-coordinate of the shape's center location within the mask. It determines where the shape will be positioned vertically.

inputs.name: grow
inputs.description: Specifies the amount by which the shape's size should increase or decrease across frames, enabling dynamic resizing for animated effects.

inputs.name: frame_width
inputs.description: The width of the mask frame, defining the horizontal dimension of the mask.

inputs.name: frame_height
inputs.description: The height of the mask frame, defining the vertical dimension of the mask.

inputs.name: shape_width
inputs.description: The initial width of the shape within the mask, determining its size.

inputs.name: shape_height
inputs.description: The initial height of the shape within the mask, determining its size.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The generated mask with the specified shape and dimensions.

outputs.name: mask_inverted
outputs.description: An inverted version of the generated mask, where the shape is transparent and the rest of the mask is opaque.

CreateShapeMaskOnPath.description: This node is designed to generate shape-based masks along a specified path, enabling the creation of dynamic and complex mask patterns that can be applied to images or animations. It leverages shape parameters and path coordinates to craft masks that follow a designated trajectory, offering a versatile tool for creative and technical image manipulation tasks.

inputs.name: shape
inputs.description: Defines the type of shape to be used for the mask, such as circle, square, or triangle. This choice dictates the geometric form of the mask, contributing to its visual style.

inputs.name: coordinates
inputs.description: Specifies the center locations for the shape masks along the path. This parameter is crucial for determining the trajectory of the mask creation, impacting the overall design and flow of the generated masks.

inputs.name: frame_width
inputs.description: Defines the width of the frame for the mask. This parameter sets the boundary within which the mask is created, influencing the scale and visibility of the shape within the frame.

inputs.name: frame_height
inputs.description: Sets the height of the frame for the mask, establishing the vertical boundary and scale of the shape within the generated mask.

inputs.name: shape_width
inputs.description: Determines the width of the shape used in the mask. This parameter affects the size of the shape, allowing for customization of the mask's appearance.

inputs.name: shape_height
inputs.description: Specifies the height of the shape used in the mask, influencing the vertical dimension of the shape and thus the mask's overall appearance.

inputs.name: size_multiplier
inputs.description: A multiplier that adjusts the size of the shape, offering additional control over the mask's scale beyond the basic shape dimensions.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The primary output, a mask or a batch of masks, created based on the specified shape and path parameters.

outputs.name: mask_inverted
outputs.description: An inverted version of the primary mask, providing an alternative masking option where the shape's area is transparent and the surrounding area is opaque.

CreateTextMask.description: The CreateTextMask node is designed to generate text-based masks for images. It allows for the customization of text appearance and positioning within a specified frame, enabling the creation of dynamic and visually engaging masks based on textual content.

inputs.name: invert
inputs.description: Determines whether the text mask should be inverted. This affects the visual contrast between the text and the background in the generated mask.

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: Specifies the number of frames for the animation. This parameter is essential for creating animated masks, defining the total length of the animation.

inputs.name: text_x
inputs.description: Sets the horizontal position of the text within the frame. This parameter allows precise control over the text's location in the mask.

inputs.name: text_y
inputs.description: Sets the vertical position of the text within the frame. This parameter allows precise control over the text's location in the mask.

inputs.name: font_size
inputs.description: Determines the size of the font used for the text in the mask. This parameter allows for the adjustment of the text's visual impact within the mask.

inputs.name: font_color
inputs.description: Specifies the color of the text in the mask. This parameter enables the customization of the text's visual appearance to match the desired aesthetic.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: Defines the text to be displayed in the mask. This parameter allows for the input of custom text, making each mask uniquely tailored to the desired content.

inputs.name: font
inputs.description: Selects the font used for the text in the mask. This parameter enables customization of the text's appearance by choosing from a variety of fonts.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Sets the width of the frame in which the text mask will be generated. This parameter defines the horizontal bounds for the text placement.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Sets the height of the frame in which the text mask will be generated. This parameter defines the vertical bounds for the text placement.

inputs.name: start_rotation
inputs.description: Specifies the starting rotation angle for the text in the mask. This parameter is crucial for creating dynamic, rotating text effects in the mask.

inputs.name: end_rotation
inputs.description: Specifies the ending rotation angle for the text in the mask, enabling the creation of rotating text animations between the start and end angles.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The generated image with the text mask applied.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The mask created from the specified text.

CreateTextOnPath.description: This node is designed to create text along a specified path, allowing for dynamic text placement and styling in graphical applications. It enables the precise alignment and orientation of text to follow complex curves or shapes, enhancing the visual appeal and readability of text in graphical interfaces or designs.

inputs.name: coordinates
inputs.description: Specifies the path along which the text will be created. This is crucial for determining the trajectory of the text alignment and placement.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The text to be placed along the path. This input is crucial for defining the content that will be visually represented in the design.

inputs.name: frame_width
inputs.description: Defines the width of the frame within which the text is to be placed. It affects the scaling and positioning of the text relative to the path.

inputs.name: frame_height
inputs.description: Defines the height of the frame within which the text is to be placed. It affects the scaling and positioning of the text relative to the path.

inputs.name: font
inputs.description: Specifies the font used for the text. This input is essential for customizing the appearance of the text to match design requirements.

inputs.name: font_size
inputs.description: Determines the size of the font. This is key to ensuring the text is legible and aesthetically pleasing when placed along the path.

inputs.name: alignment
inputs.description: Defines the alignment of the text relative to the path. This is important for controlling how the text is positioned and oriented along the path.

inputs.name: text_color
inputs.description: Specifies the color of the text. This input allows for the customization of the text's visual appearance to fit the overall design.

inputs.name: size_multiplier
inputs.description: Affects the overall size of the text, allowing for dynamic scaling based on design needs.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The generated image with text placed along the specified path, adhering to the input style and content requirements.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: A mask representing the area of the image where text has been placed, useful for further image processing steps.

outputs.name: mask_inverted
outputs.description: An inverted mask of the text area, indicating where text has not been placed, which can be useful for additional processing or effects.

CreateVoronoiMask.description: The CreateVoronoiMask node is designed to generate dynamic Voronoi diagram-based masks. It utilizes parameters such as the number of points, line width, and speed to create evolving masks over a series of frames, allowing for the creation of complex and visually interesting patterns that can be used in various graphical applications.

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: Specifies the number of frames over which the Voronoi mask will evolve, creating a dynamic sequence of masks.

inputs.name: num_points
inputs.description: Determines the number of points used to generate the Voronoi diagram, directly affecting the complexity and appearance of the resulting mask.

inputs.name: line_width
inputs.description: Controls the thickness of the lines in the Voronoi diagram, influencing the visual style of the mask.

inputs.name: speed
inputs.description: Adjusts the rate at which the points in the Voronoi diagram move, affecting the dynamic evolution of the mask over the frames.

inputs.name: frame_width
inputs.description: Sets the width of the frame for the mask, defining the horizontal dimension of the output.

inputs.name: frame_height
inputs.description: Sets the height of the frame for the mask, defining the vertical dimension of the output.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The output is a tensor representing the generated Voronoi mask, suitable for use in graphical applications.

outputs.name: mask_inverted
outputs.description: The output is a tensor representing the inverted Voronoi mask, providing an alternative visual pattern for use in graphical applications.

CrossFadeImages.description: The CrossFadeImages node is designed to blend two sequences of images together over a specified number of frames, using a variety of easing functions to control the transition dynamics. This node allows for the creation of smooth transitions between images, making it ideal for generating animations or video effects where a gradual change from one image set to another is desired.

inputs.name: images_i
inputs.description: unknown

inputs.name: interpolation
inputs.description: Specifies the easing function to be used for the transition, allowing for various types of dynamic effects such as linear, ease-in, ease-out, and more complex functions like bounce or elastic.

inputs.name: transition_start_index
inputs.description: The index in the image sequences where the transition begins, allowing for precise control over the timing of the crossfade effect.

inputs.name: transitioning_frames
inputs.description: The number of frames over which the transition occurs, defining the length of the crossfade effect.

inputs.name: start_level
inputs.description: The initial alpha value for blending the images at the start of the transition, providing control over the beginning transparency level.

inputs.name: end_level
inputs.description: The final alpha value for blending the images at the end of the transition, allowing for adjustment of the ending transparency level.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The resulting sequence of images after applying the crossfade transition, combining elements of both input sequences into a single smooth animation.

CustomSigmas.description: The CustomSigmas node is designed to transform a list of float values into a tensor of sigmas, facilitating the manipulation and application of noise levels in generative models. It abstracts the process of converting numerical lists into a structured format that models can interpret for noise injection or adjustment.

inputs.name: sigmas_string
inputs.description: A string of comma-separated values representing sigma levels, which are converted into a tensor. This input is essential for defining the noise characteristics to be applied in generative processes.

inputs.name: interpolate_to_steps
inputs.description: An integer specifying the number of steps to which the sigma values should be interpolated. This parameter adjusts the length of the sigma tensor to match the desired number of steps in the generative process.

outputs.name: SIGMAS
outputs.description: A tensor of sigma values derived from the input list of floats, ready for use in noise application or adjustment within generative models.

DownloadAndLoadCLIPSeg.description: This node is designed to download and load a specific CLIPSeg model using the huggingface_hub library, making it available for image segmentation tasks within the ComfyUI framework. It abstracts the complexities of downloading, caching, and initializing the model, providing a streamlined way to integrate advanced segmentation capabilities into ComfyUI applications.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: Specifies the model to be downloaded and loaded for image segmentation. It supports specific CLIPSeg models available on huggingface_hub, with a default option provided for convenience.

outputs.name: clipseg_model
outputs.description: Returns a dictionary containing the loaded CLIPSeg model and its processor, ready for performing image segmentation tasks.

DrawInstanceDiffusionTracking.description: This node is designed for visualizing tracking data on images by drawing bounding boxes and optionally text annotations. It leverages tracking information generated by the CreateInstanceDiffusionTracking node to overlay visual cues on images, enhancing the interpretability of tracking data.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image on which tracking data will be visualized. It serves as the canvas for drawing bounding boxes and text annotations.

inputs.name: tracking
inputs.description: Tracking data containing information about detected objects, used to draw bounding boxes and text annotations on the image.

inputs.name: box_line_width
inputs.description: Specifies the thickness of the bounding boxes drawn around detected objects.

inputs.name: draw_text
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether to draw text annotations (class name and ID) above the bounding boxes.

inputs.name: font
inputs.description: The font used for text annotations, allowing customization of the visual appearance of text.

inputs.name: font_size
inputs.description: The size of the font used for text annotations, affecting the readability of text above bounding boxes.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The image with tracking data visualized through bounding boxes and optional text annotations.

DummyLatentOut.description: Provides a simple pass-through for latent data, facilitating the visualization of workflow outputs in the UI without necessitating data persistence on disk.

inputs.name: latent
inputs.description: The latent data to be passed through. This input is essential for the node's operation as it directly influences the output by being returned unchanged.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The unchanged latent data received as input, enabling direct visualization in the UI.

EmptyLatentImagePresets.description: This node is designed to generate presets for creating empty latent images with specific dimensions, offering options for inversion and batch processing. It abstracts the complexity of generating latent images by providing predefined dimension options and handling the inversion logic internally, making it easier to produce latent images tailored to specific requirements.

inputs.name: dimensions
inputs.description: Specifies the dimensions of the latent image to be generated. The selection of dimensions directly influences the size of the output latent image, with several predefined options available.

inputs.name: invert
inputs.description: Determines whether the dimensions of the latent image should be inverted. This option allows for flexibility in the orientation of the generated latent image.

inputs.name: batch_size
inputs.description: Defines the number of latent images to generate in a single batch. This allows for efficient generation of multiple latent images at once.

outputs.name: Latent
outputs.description: The generated latent image(s) based on the specified dimensions and inversion setting.

outputs.name: Width
outputs.description: The width of the generated latent image.

outputs.name: Height
outputs.description: The height of the generated latent image.

FilterZeroMasksAndCorrespondingImages.description: This node is designed to filter out all zero-value masks from a batch of masks and, optionally, filter out corresponding images based on the presence of non-zero masks. It aims to streamline the preprocessing of image and mask data by ensuring that only relevant, non-empty masks and their associated images are passed forward for further processing.

inputs.name: masks
inputs.description: A list of masks to be filtered, removing those that are entirely zero-valued. This parameter is essential for identifying relevant data for further processing.

inputs.name: original_images
inputs.description: An optional list of images corresponding to the masks. If provided, images associated with non-zero masks are retained, aligning image data with filtered mask data.

outputs.name: non_zero_masks_out
outputs.description: The filtered list of non-zero masks.

outputs.name: non_zero_mask_images_out
outputs.description: The list of images corresponding to the non-zero masks, if original images were provided.

outputs.name: zero_mask_images_out
outputs.description: The list of images corresponding to the zero masks, if original images were provided.

outputs.name: zero_mask_images_out_indexes
outputs.description: The indexes of images corresponding to the zero masks, useful for tracking which images were filtered out.

FlipSigmasAdjusted.description: The FlipSigmasAdjusted node is designed to manipulate a sequence of sigma values for use in diffusion models. It reverses the order of the sigma values, applies an offset, and optionally divides the entire sequence by the last sigma value or another specified divisor. This process is crucial for adjusting the noise levels in a controlled manner, ensuring that the diffusion process can be fine-tuned according to specific requirements.

inputs.name: sigmas
inputs.description: The sequence of sigma values to be adjusted. This sequence is reversed and potentially modified to meet certain conditions, such as avoiding zero values and applying offsets or divisions.

inputs.name: divide_by_last_sigma
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether the sigma values should be divided by the last sigma value in the sequence. This is used to normalize the sequence based on its final value.

inputs.name: divide_by
inputs.description: A scalar value by which the entire sequence of sigma values is divided. This allows for further adjustment of the noise level across the sequence.

inputs.name: offset_by
inputs.description: An integer indicating how many positions to offset the sigma values after reversing their order. This can be used to shift the noise levels applied at each step of the diffusion process.

outputs.name: SIGMAS
outputs.description: The adjusted sequence of sigma values, ready for use in diffusion processes. This output is a tensor of sigma values that have been reversed, offset, and potentially normalized or divided as specified.

outputs.name: sigmas_string
outputs.description: A string representation of the adjusted sigma values, formatted with a specified precision and separator for easy readability.

FloatConstant.description: The FloatConstant node provides a mechanism to define a constant floating-point value within a node-based processing environment. It allows for the specification of a float value with a wide range of possible values, enabling precise control over constants used in computations or data flows.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: Specifies the floating-point value to be used as a constant. This parameter allows for a wide range of values, enabling the node to serve various computational needs with precision.

outputs.name: value
outputs.description: Outputs the same floating-point value as defined by the input, serving as a constant throughout the node's usage.

FloatToMask.description: The `FloatToMask` node is designed to convert floating-point representations into mask formats, facilitating operations that require binary or discrete mask inputs. This node plays a crucial role in image processing and manipulation tasks where precise delineation of areas based on specific criteria is essential.

inputs.name: input_values
inputs.description: Represents the floating-point values to be converted into a mask. These values are typically thresholds or indicators that determine the mask's shape and boundaries.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Specifies the width of the output mask. This parameter determines the horizontal dimension of the mask generated from the input values.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Specifies the height of the output mask. This parameter determines the vertical dimension of the mask generated from the input values.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The output binary mask generated from the input floating-point values. This mask can be used for various image processing applications that require discrete delineation.

FloatToSigmas.description: Transforms a list of float values into a tensor of sigmas, facilitating the conversion of numerical data into a format suitable for noise generation and manipulation within neural networks.

inputs.name: float_list
inputs.description: A list of float values to be converted into a sigmas tensor. This input is crucial for defining the specific noise levels to be applied in the neural network's processing.

outputs.name: SIGMAS
outputs.description: A tensor of sigmas derived from the input list of float values, used for noise generation and manipulation in neural network operations.

GenerateNoise.description: The GenerateNoise node is designed to create noise patterns that can be used to augment or modify latent representations in generative models. It provides a flexible way to generate noise with specific characteristics, such as size, seed, and intensity, allowing for controlled variations in the generated content.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Determines the width of the generated noise pattern, enabling customization of the noise to fit specific dimensions.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Sets the height of the generated noise pattern, allowing for the generation of noise that matches the desired dimensions.

inputs.name: batch_size
inputs.description: Specifies the number of noise samples to generate, allowing for batch processing of multiple noise patterns simultaneously.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: Controls the randomness of the noise generation, ensuring reproducibility of the noise patterns when the same seed is used.

inputs.name: multiplier
inputs.description: Adjusts the intensity of the generated noise, providing a means to amplify or reduce the noise effect.

inputs.name: constant_batch_noise
inputs.description: When enabled, uses the same noise pattern across all samples in a batch, ensuring uniform noise characteristics.

inputs.name: normalize
inputs.description: Normalizes the generated noise, ensuring that its distribution has a standard deviation of 1.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: Optional parameter that, if provided, can influence the noise generation process based on the model's characteristics, such as adjusting the noise to align with specific model requirements or enhancing compatibility with the model's latent space.

inputs.name: sigmas
inputs.description: Optional parameter that allows for scaling the noise based on the difference between two sigma values, typically used in diffusion models. This scaling adjusts the intensity and variability of the noise, directly influencing the characteristics of the generated patterns.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The generated noise pattern, ready to be used in further processing or as part of a generative model's input.

GetImageRangeFromBatch.description: This node is designed to extract a specific range of images from a given batch based on a starting index and the number of frames desired. It can optionally handle masks associated with the images, ensuring that both images and their corresponding masks are selected in tandem.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The collection of images from which a range will be selected. This parameter is crucial for defining the subset of images to be extracted.

inputs.name: start_index
inputs.description: Specifies the starting index from which images will be selected in the batch. A special value of -1 indicates selection from the end.

inputs.name: num_frames
inputs.description: Determines the number of images to select from the starting index, defining the size of the output batch.

inputs.name: masks
inputs.description: An optional collection of masks corresponding to the input images. If provided, masks for the selected image range are also returned.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The selected range of images from the input batch.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The masks corresponding to the selected range of images, if masks were provided.

GetImagesFromBatchIndexed.description: This node is designed to select and return specific images from a given batch based on the provided indices. It allows for the dynamic extraction of a subset of images from a larger collection, facilitating operations that require targeted manipulation or analysis of image batches.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: Represents the batch of images from which specific items will be selected. It is crucial for determining the scope of images available for extraction.

inputs.name: indexes
inputs.description: A string of comma-separated indices indicating which images to extract from the batch. This parameter directly influences which images are selected and returned.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is a subset of images selected from the input batch based on the specified indices.

GetImageSizeAndCount.description: This node is designed to analyze an image to determine its width, height, and batch size, and then pass the image through unchanged. It serves the purpose of extracting dimensional and quantity information from a batch of images, which can be crucial for further processing steps that require knowledge of the image's size or the total number of images in a batch.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image or batch of images for which the size and count information is to be determined. This parameter is essential for the node to perform its analysis and return the dimensions and batch size of the image(s).

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The original image or batch of images passed through the node unchanged.

outputs.name: width
outputs.description: The width of the input image(s).

outputs.name: height
outputs.description: The height of the input image(s).

outputs.name: count
outputs.description: The total number of images in the batch.

GetLatentsFromBatchIndexed.description: This node is designed to select and return specific latents from a given batch based on provided indices. It facilitates the extraction of a subset of latents for further processing or analysis, making it a crucial component in workflows that require manipulation or inspection of individual or groups of latents within a larger batch.

inputs.name: latents
inputs.description: Represents the batch of latents from which specific items will be selected. It is essential for determining the scope of data the node will operate on.

inputs.name: indexes
inputs.description: A string of comma-separated indices indicating which latents to extract from the batch. This parameter allows for flexible selection of specific latents, enabling targeted manipulation or analysis.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The output is a modified version of the input latent batch, containing only the latents at the specified indices.

GetMaskSizeAndCount.description: This node is designed to analyze the dimensions and batch size of a given mask, returning its width, height, and count while passing the mask through unchanged. It serves as a utility for understanding and processing mask dimensions within a workflow.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The mask input is crucial for determining the dimensions and batch size of the mask. It directly influences the node's output by providing the necessary data for calculation.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The original mask passed through unchanged, facilitating further processing or analysis.

outputs.name: width
outputs.description: The width of the mask, providing insight into its dimensions.

outputs.name: height
outputs.description: The height of the mask, offering information on its size.

outputs.name: count
outputs.description: The batch size of the mask, indicating how many masks are processed.

GLIGENTextBoxApplyBatchCoords.description: The GLIGENTextBoxApplyBatchCoords node is designed for scheduling the positions of GLIGEN text boxes within a batch, specifically tailored for use with AnimateDiff-Evolved. It facilitates the integration of text box positioning with the Spline Editor node, enabling dynamic text placement in generated images. This node processes batched coordinates and text inputs to compute positioning parameters, enhancing the visual storytelling capabilities of GLIGEN-generated content.

inputs.name: conditioning_to
inputs.description: The target for applying the conditioning, typically a sequence of conditioning layers or parameters.

inputs.name: latents
inputs.description: Used to determine the batch size for processing, indicating the number of latent representations to be positioned.

inputs.name: clip
inputs.description: A standard text encoder used for encoding the text inputs, ensuring compatibility with the main prompt processing.

inputs.name: gligen_textbox_model
inputs.description: Connects to the GLIGEN Loader, enabling the application of GLIGEN-specific text box positioning logic.

inputs.name: coordinates
inputs.description: Accepts a JSON string of points for text box positioning, directly compatible with the Spline Editor node.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: Specifies the text content for which positions are being set within the GLIGEN bounding box.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Defines the width of the GLIGEN bounding box for text placement.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Specifies the height of the GLIGEN bounding box for text placement.

inputs.name: size_multiplier
inputs.description: A factor that scales the size of the GLIGEN bounding box, affecting the overall dimensions of the text placement area.

outputs.name: conditioning
outputs.description: Provides the conditioning parameters for the clip text encoder and sampler, facilitating the integration of positioned text into the generation process.

outputs.name: coord_preview
outputs.description: An optional output offering a visual preview of the text box coordinates and bounding boxes.

GradientToFloat.description: Transforms an image into a list of float values based on sampling along its width and height axes. This process is useful for extracting numerical representations of images for further analysis or processing.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image tensor to be sampled, where the sampling occurs along the width and height axes to generate float values.

inputs.name: steps
inputs.description: Defines the number of intervals to sample along the width and height axes of the image, affecting the resolution of the output float lists.

outputs.name: float_x
outputs.description: A list of float values representing the mean of the sampled points along the width of the image.

outputs.name: float_y
outputs.description: A list of float values representing the mean of the sampled points along the height of the image.

GrowMaskWithBlur.description: The GrowMaskWithBlur node is designed to manipulate masks by expanding or contracting them, optionally applying a blur effect, and performing various other transformations such as flipping, filling holes, and interpolating between frames. It provides a comprehensive set of operations for dynamic mask manipulation in image processing tasks, making it versatile for applications requiring precise control over mask geometry and appearance.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The input mask or batch of masks to be processed. It serves as the primary data upon which all transformations are applied, determining the base geometry for expansion, contraction, and other modifications.

inputs.name: expand
inputs.description: Specifies the amount by which the mask should be expanded or contracted. Positive values cause expansion, while negative values result in contraction, affecting the overall size and shape of the mask.
