inputs.name: incremental_expandrate
inputs.description: The rate at which the expand parameter is adjusted incrementally per frame, allowing for dynamic changes in mask size over a sequence of frames.

inputs.name: tapered_corners
inputs.description: A boolean flag that indicates whether to use tapered corners during mask manipulation, which can affect the smoothness and contour of the expanded or contracted mask.

inputs.name: flip_input
inputs.description: A boolean flag that determines whether the input mask should be flipped (inverted) before any other processing is done. This inversion can be useful for certain types of mask transformations.

inputs.name: blur_radius
inputs.description: The radius of the Gaussian blur to be applied to the mask. A value greater than 0 activates the blur effect, softening the edges and overall appearance of the mask.

inputs.name: lerp_alpha
inputs.description: The alpha value for linear interpolation between frames, enabling smooth transitions and blending of mask states across a sequence.

inputs.name: decay_factor
inputs.description: A factor that controls the decay of mask values over time, contributing to the fading or persistence of mask features in animated sequences.

inputs.name: fill_holes
inputs.description: A boolean flag that, when enabled, causes holes within the mask to be filled. This operation can enhance mask solidity but may be computationally intensive.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The modified mask after applying expansion, contraction, blur, and other transformations, ready for further processing or visualization.

outputs.name: mask_inverted
outputs.description: An inverted version of the modified mask, providing an alternative representation that can be useful in certain processing contexts.

ImageAddMulti.description: This node blends multiple images together using various blending modes such as add, subtract, multiply, and difference. It allows for dynamic input count adjustment, enabling the combination of a flexible number of images into a single output image.

inputs.name: inputcount
inputs.description: Specifies the number of images to blend together. It determines how many image inputs the node will process.

inputs.name: image_i
inputs.description: Represents an image to be blended. The index 'i' is dynamic, starting from 1 and increasing based on the 'inputcount'. This allows for a flexible number of images to be processed and blended together.

inputs.name: blending
inputs.description: Defines the blending mode to be used for combining the images. Supported modes are add, subtract, multiply, and difference.

outputs.name: images
outputs.description: The resulting image after blending the input images according to the specified blending mode.

ImageAndMaskPreview.description: This node is designed to generate a preview of an image with an optional mask applied. It supports adjusting the mask's opacity and color, and can handle cases where either the image, the mask, or both are provided. The node also offers functionality to pass through the generated preview without saving, or to save the preview with a specified filename prefix, incorporating additional PNG metadata if provided.

inputs.name: mask_opacity
inputs.description: Specifies the opacity level of the mask when both an image and a mask are provided, affecting the visibility of the mask overlay on the image.

inputs.name: mask_color
inputs.description: Defines the color of the mask in either RGB or hexadecimal format, which is applied when both an image and a mask are present, influencing the appearance of the mask overlay.

inputs.name: pass_through
inputs.description: A boolean flag that determines whether the generated preview is directly returned without being saved, allowing for immediate use or further processing.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image to be previewed, which can be optionally accompanied by a mask to create a composite preview.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The mask to be applied over the image, which can be adjusted in terms of opacity and color, or used alone to generate a mask-only preview.

outputs.name: composite
outputs.description: The generated preview of the image with the optional mask applied, which can be either passed through directly or saved to a file.

ImageBatchMulti.description: The ImageBatchMulti node is designed to create a batch of images from multiple individual images. It allows for dynamic input count adjustment, enabling the creation of a batch from a varying number of images based on the user's requirements.

inputs.name: inputcount
inputs.description: Specifies the number of images to be included in the batch. This parameter allows for dynamic adjustment of the batch size.

inputs.name: image_i
inputs.description: Represents an individual image to be included in the batch. The index i varies based on the input count, starting from 1 (e.g., image_1, image_2, etc.).

outputs.name: images
outputs.description: The resulting batch of images, combined from the individual inputs.

ImageBatchRepeatInterleaving.description: The ImageBatchRepeatInterleaving node is designed to expand a batch of images by repeating each image in the batch a specified number of times. This operation effectively increases the batch size by duplicating images, which can be useful for data augmentation or ensuring uniform batch processing sizes.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The 'images' parameter represents the batch of images to be repeated. It is crucial for defining the input data that will undergo the repetition process.

inputs.name: repeats
inputs.description: The 'repeats' parameter specifies the number of times each image in the batch should be repeated. It directly influences the resulting batch size by determining the duplication factor for each image.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is a new batch of images where each original image has been repeated according to the 'repeats' parameter, effectively enlarging the batch size.

ImageBatchTestPattern.description: The ImageBatchTestPattern node is designed to generate a batch of images, each containing a unique sequential number displayed in a randomly colored font. This functionality is useful for creating test patterns in image batches, where each image is customized with specific text, font, and size settings, and positioned according to given coordinates.

inputs.name: batch_size
inputs.description: Specifies the number of images to generate in the batch, affecting the output batch size.

inputs.name: start_from
inputs.description: The starting sequential number for the first image in the batch, setting the initial point for the sequence.

inputs.name: text_x
inputs.description: The x-coordinate for the position of the text within the images, determining where the text appears horizontally.

inputs.name: text_y
inputs.description: The y-coordinate for the position of the text within the images, determining where the text appears vertically.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: The width of the generated images, defining the horizontal dimension of each image in the batch.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: The height of the generated images, defining the vertical dimension of each image in the batch.

inputs.name: font
inputs.description: The name of the font to use for the text in the images, influencing the visual style of the numbers.

inputs.name: font_size
inputs.description: Determines the size of the font used for the text, directly impacting the appearance of the numbers in the images.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: A tensor representing the batch of generated images, each normalized and containing a unique sequential number in a randomly colored font.

ImageConcanate.description: The ImageConcatenate node is designed for combining two images into a single image along a specified direction. It supports matching the sizes of the input images and adjusting them to have the same batch size if necessary, allowing for flexible image concatenation operations.

inputs.name: image1
inputs.description: The first image tensor to be concatenated. It plays a crucial role in determining the final image's layout and size, especially when matching image sizes or batch sizes.

inputs.name: image2
inputs.description: The second image tensor to be concatenated with the first one. Its size and batch size can be adjusted to match the first image, ensuring seamless concatenation.

inputs.name: direction
inputs.description: Specifies the direction ('right', 'left', 'up', 'down') in which the second image should be concatenated to the first one, influencing the final image's orientation.

inputs.name: match_image_size
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether the sizes of the two images should be matched before concatenation, affecting the resizing operation if true.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The resulting tensor after concatenating the two input images along the specified direction.

ImageConcatMulti.description: The ImageConcatMulti node is designed to concatenate multiple images into a single image. It allows for the dynamic specification of the number of input images, the direction of concatenation, and whether to match the sizes of the images being concatenated. This functionality is useful for creating composite images or arranging multiple images in a specific layout.

inputs.name: inputcount
inputs.description: Specifies the number of images to concatenate. This allows for dynamic adjustment of the node's inputs based on user requirements.

inputs.name: image_i
inputs.description: Represents any of the images to be concatenated, allowing for a flexible number of image inputs beyond the first two specified. This accommodates the dynamic input count specified by the user.

inputs.name: direction
inputs.description: Determines the direction in which the images will be concatenated (right, down, left, up). This affects the final layout of the concatenated image.

inputs.name: match_image_size
inputs.description: Indicates whether the sizes of the images should be matched before concatenation. This ensures uniformity in the dimensions of the resulting image.

outputs.name: images
outputs.description: The resulting image after concatenation of the input images. This composite image reflects the specified direction and size matching settings.

ImageGrabPIL.description: The ImageGrabPIL node is designed for processing and transforming images into a standardized format suitable for further analysis or processing. It focuses on converting images to a consistent size, color mode, and numerical representation, ensuring they are ready for tasks such as machine learning model input or image manipulation operations.

inputs.name: x
inputs.description: The 'x' input specifies the starting x-coordinate for the region of the image to be captured. It is essential for defining the area of interest within the larger image context.

inputs.name: y
inputs.description: The 'y' input specifies the starting y-coordinate for the region of the image to be captured. It plays a critical role in pinpointing the area of interest on the vertical axis within the image.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: The 'width' parameter determines the width of the region to be captured from the source image. It is crucial for specifying the size of the area of interest horizontally.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: The 'height' parameter determines the height of the region to be captured from the source image. It is vital for defining the vertical size of the area of interest.

inputs.name: num_frames
inputs.description: The 'num_frames' parameter indicates the number of frames to capture in a sequence. It is essential for tasks requiring multiple, consecutive captures from the source image, such as creating animations or analyzing changes over time.

inputs.name: delay
inputs.description: The 'delay' parameter specifies the time delay between capturing consecutive frames. It is crucial for controlling the timing in sequences where multiple frames are captured, allowing for precise timing adjustments.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The 'image' output is the captured or processed portion of the input image, ready for further processing or analysis.

ImageGridComposite2x2.description: This node is designed to concatenate four input images into a 2x2 grid, effectively creating a composite image that showcases all inputs in a structured layout. It serves the purpose of visually aggregating multiple images into a single, cohesive unit for easier comparison, presentation, or further processing.

inputs.name: image1
inputs.description: The first image to be placed in the top-left corner of the 2x2 grid. It plays a crucial role in the overall composition by starting the visual sequence.

inputs.name: image2
inputs.description: The second image to be placed in the top-right corner of the 2x2 grid. It complements the first image, continuing the visual narrative.

inputs.name: image3
inputs.description: The third image to be placed in the bottom-left corner of the 2x2 grid. It adds to the visual diversity and complexity of the composite image.

inputs.name: image4
inputs.description: The fourth image to be placed in the bottom-right corner of the 2x2 grid. It completes the visual arrangement, providing a balanced and cohesive look.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The composite image resulting from concatenating the four input images into a 2x2 grid. This output is useful for visual analysis, presentation, or as input to further image processing tasks.

ImageGridComposite3x3.description: This node is designed to concatenate nine input images into a single 3x3 grid image. It's particularly useful for creating composite images or visual summaries where multiple images need to be displayed together in a structured format.

inputs.name: image1
inputs.description: The first image to be placed in the top-left corner of the 3x3 grid.

inputs.name: image2
inputs.description: The second image to be placed in the top row, middle position of the 3x3 grid.

inputs.name: image3
inputs.description: The third image to be placed in the top row, right position of the 3x3 grid.

inputs.name: image4
inputs.description: The fourth image to be placed in the middle row, left position of the 3x3 grid.

inputs.name: image5
inputs.description: The central image of the 3x3 grid.

inputs.name: image6
inputs.description: The sixth image to be placed in the middle row, right position of the 3x3 grid.

inputs.name: image7
inputs.description: The seventh image to be placed in the bottom row, left position of the 3x3 grid.

inputs.name: image8
inputs.description: The eighth image to be placed in the bottom row, middle position of the 3x3 grid.

inputs.name: image9
inputs.description: The ninth image to be placed in the bottom row, right position of the 3x3 grid.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is a single image that combines the nine input images into a 3x3 grid format.

ImageNormalize_Neg1_To_1.description: This node is designed to adjust the pixel values of images so that they fall within the range of -1 to 1, effectively normalizing them for further processing or analysis.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The images to be normalized. This input is crucial for the operation as it directly affects the normalization process by scaling the pixel values.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The normalized images, with pixel values adjusted to fall within the range of -1 to 1.

ImagePadForOutpaintMasked.description: This node is designed to adjust the dimensions of an image for outpainting tasks by applying padding to the specified sides of the image. It extends the functionality of outpainting by allowing for masked areas, enabling selective padding and processing based on the mask provided. This is particularly useful in scenarios where the image composition needs to be carefully controlled or when integrating new elements into existing images without affecting certain regions.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image to be processed and padded. It is the primary input on which the node operates, determining the base for padding adjustments.

inputs.name: left
inputs.description: The amount of padding to apply to the left side of the image. This parameter directly influences the horizontal expansion of the image.

inputs.name: top
inputs.description: The amount of padding to apply to the top side of the image. It affects the vertical expansion of the image, particularly on the top edge.

inputs.name: right
inputs.description: The calculated amount of padding to apply to the right side of the image, based on the target width, current width, and left padding. It adjusts the horizontal dimensions of the image.

inputs.name: bottom
inputs.description: The amount of padding to apply to the bottom side of the image. This parameter influences the vertical expansion of the image on the bottom edge.

inputs.name: feathering
inputs.description: The degree of feathering to apply along the edges of the padding. This parameter controls the smoothness of the transition between the original image and the padded areas.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: A scaled version of the mask that defines areas to be excluded or differently processed during the padding operation. It allows for selective padding adjustments.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is an image with applied padding according to the specified parameters and mask, ready for further processing or outpainting tasks.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The mask output reflects the areas that were selectively processed or excluded during the padding operation, maintaining the integrity of the original masked regions.

ImagePadForOutpaintTargetSize.description: This node is designed to adjust the dimensions of an image to meet a specified target size for outpainting purposes. It scales the image while maintaining its aspect ratio, calculates the necessary padding to reach the target dimensions, and optionally applies feathering to blend the edges smoothly. The node can also handle an associated mask, scaling and padding it in tandem with the image.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed for outpainting, which will be scaled and padded to meet the target dimensions.

inputs.name: target_width
inputs.description: The desired width of the output image after padding. This parameter determines how much the input image needs to be scaled and padded horizontally.

inputs.name: target_height
inputs.description: The desired height of the output image after padding. It influences the vertical scaling and padding required to achieve the target dimensions.

inputs.name: feathering
inputs.description: Specifies the intensity of the edge feathering applied to the padded areas, enhancing the visual integration of the padded regions with the original image.

inputs.name: upscale_method
inputs.description: The method used for upscaling the image during the scaling process, affecting the quality of the resized image.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: An optional mask that, if provided, is scaled and padded in parallel with the image, maintaining the alignment between the image and its mask.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The scaled and padded image, adjusted to match the target dimensions while preserving the original aspect ratio.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The scaled and padded mask corresponding to the processed image, if a mask was provided.

ImagePass.description: The ImagePass node is designed to facilitate the unaltered passage of an image through a processing pipeline. It serves as a neutral conduit, ensuring that the input image is passed through without any modifications, alterations, or enhancements.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The 'image' parameter is the primary input for the ImagePass node, representing the image to be passed through unmodified. It plays a crucial role in the node's operation by being the sole piece of data the node acts upon, ensuring the image's integrity is maintained throughout the process.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output 'image' parameter is identical to the input image, signifying that the image has been passed through the node without any modifications. It underscores the node's purpose of providing a direct, unaltered conduit for image data.

ImageResizeKJ.description: The ImageResizeKJ node is designed to resize images to specified dimensions, with options to maintain the original aspect ratio, upscale using various methods, and ensure the final dimensions are divisible by a given number. It provides flexibility in defining the target size either directly or based on the size of another image, catering to diverse image processing needs.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be resized. This parameter is crucial as it provides the source image for the resizing operation.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: The target width for the resized image. If keep_proportion is true and width is set, the height will be adjusted to maintain the aspect ratio.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: The target height for the resized image. Similar to width, if keep_proportion is true and height is set, the width will be adjusted accordingly.

inputs.name: upscale_method
inputs.description: Specifies the method to be used for upscaling the image, offering various algorithms to choose from.

inputs.name: keep_proportion
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether to maintain the original aspect ratio of the image during resizing.

inputs.name: divisible_by
inputs.description: Ensures the dimensions of the resized image are divisible by this value, useful for certain types of neural network inputs.

inputs.name: width_input
inputs.description: An optional width input that overrides the width parameter if provided, allowing for dynamic resizing based on external inputs.

inputs.name: height_input
inputs.description: An optional height input that overrides the height parameter if provided, similar to width_input.

inputs.name: get_image_size
inputs.description: An optional image input used to determine the target size for resizing, based on the dimensions of this image.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: unknown

outputs.name: width
outputs.description: The width of the resized image.

outputs.name: height
outputs.description: The height of the resized image.

ImageTransformByNormalizedAmplitude.description: This node applies a transformation to images based on normalized amplitude values, adjusting aspects such as zoom scale dynamically. It's designed to modify images in a batch by scaling their size according to audio-driven amplitude data, enabling creative visual-audio synchronization.

inputs.name: normalized_amp
inputs.description: An array of normalized amplitude values, each corresponding to an image in the batch, used to determine the scale of transformation.

inputs.name: zoom_scale
inputs.description: A scaling factor that determines how much the image is zoomed based on the amplitude value.

inputs.name: x_offset
inputs.description: The horizontal offset applied to the image after scaling, allowing for positional adjustments.

inputs.name: y_offset
inputs.description: The vertical offset applied to the image after scaling, allowing for positional adjustments.

inputs.name: cumulative
inputs.description: A boolean indicating whether the zoom effect should accumulate over the images in the batch.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The batch of images to be transformed, where each image's transformation is influenced by its corresponding amplitude value.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The transformed images, each adjusted according to its corresponding normalized amplitude value, zoom scale, and positional offsets.

ImageUpscaleWithModelBatched.description: This node is designed to upscale images using a specified model, with the added functionality of processing images in sub-batches. This approach helps in managing VRAM usage more efficiently, making it suitable for systems with limited memory resources.

inputs.name: upscale_model
inputs.description: The model used for upscaling images. It determines the quality and characteristics of the output images.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The batch of images to be upscaled. This input allows the node to process multiple images simultaneously, optimizing throughput.

inputs.name: per_batch
inputs.description: Defines the number of images to process in each sub-batch. This parameter helps in controlling VRAM usage by breaking down the batch into smaller, manageable chunks.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The upscaled images, returned as a batch. This output provides higher resolution versions of the input images.

InjectNoiseToLatent.description: The InjectNoiseToLatent node is designed to modify the latent representations by injecting noise into them. This process can include averaging the original and noise latents, scaling the noise by a strength factor, normalizing the resulting latent, applying a mask to selectively inject noise, and optionally mixing in random noise. The node aims to enhance or alter the characteristics of the latent space for various generative tasks, such as image synthesis or manipulation.

inputs.name: latents
inputs.description: The original latent representations to which noise will be added. This input is crucial for defining the base structure that the noise will modify.

inputs.name: strength
inputs.description: A factor that scales the noise before it is added to the latents, allowing for control over the intensity of the noise injection.

inputs.name: noise
inputs.description: The noise tensor to be injected into the latents, providing the variability or perturbation.

inputs.name: normalize
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether the noised latent should be normalized, affecting the distribution of the final output.

inputs.name: average
inputs.description: Determines if the noise should be averaged with the original latents, offering a method to blend rather than solely add noise.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: An optional mask to apply selective noise injection, allowing for targeted alterations in the latent space.

inputs.name: mix_randn_amount
inputs.description: The amount of random noise to mix into the noised latent, introducing additional randomness.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: An optional seed for generating random noise, ensuring reproducibility when desired.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The modified latent representations after noise injection, reflecting the applied changes.

InsertImageBatchByIndexes.description: The InsertImageBatchByIndexes node is designed for integrating a sequence of images into an existing batch of images at specified indices. It ensures that the newly inserted images are placed at the correct positions within the original batch, maintaining the original sequence order where possible. This node is particularly useful in workflows requiring dynamic modification or augmentation of image batches, such as in data preprocessing for machine learning models.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The original batch of images into which new images will be inserted. It serves as the base for the insertion operation.

inputs.name: images_to_insert
inputs.description: The images to be inserted into the original batch at specified indices. This parameter allows for dynamic content addition to the image batch.

inputs.name: insert_indexes
inputs.description: The indices within the original image batch where the new images should be inserted. These indices dictate the exact positions for insertion, aligning with the sequence of 'images_to_insert'.

outputs.name: images_after_insert
outputs.description: The updated batch of images after the insertion operation, maintaining the original sequence order with the new images integrated at specified positions.

InsertImagesToBatchIndexed.description: The InsertImagesToBatchIndexed node is designed for integrating specific images into a predefined batch of images at designated positions. It enables precise control over the composition of an image batch by allowing the insertion of new images at specified indices, thus modifying the original batch without altering its overall structure.

inputs.name: original_images
inputs.description: Specifies the original batch of images where new images will be inserted. It plays a crucial role in determining the base structure of the image batch.

inputs.name: images_to_insert
inputs.description: Defines the images to be inserted into the original batch. This parameter is essential for customizing the content of the image batch.

inputs.name: indexes
inputs.description: Indicates the specific positions within the original image batch where the new images should be inserted. This parameter allows for targeted modifications of the batch.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The modified image batch with the new images inserted at the specified indices.

INTConstant.description: The INTConstant node provides a mechanism to define a constant integer value within a node-based programming environment. It allows for the specification of a static integer value that can be used as a constant input across various computational graphs or pipelines.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: Specifies the integer value to be used as a constant. This value serves as a fixed input that influences the node's output by providing a predetermined integer.

outputs.name: value
outputs.description: Outputs the specified constant integer value. This output can be utilized as a fixed input in subsequent nodes or processes within the computational graph.

InterpolateCoords.description: The InterpolateCoords node is designed for interpolating a set of coordinates based on a specified curve. It processes input coordinates and an interpolation curve to generate a new set of coordinates that follow the given curve, effectively transforming the spatial layout of the original points.

inputs.name: coordinates
inputs.description: A string representing the original coordinates to be interpolated. This parameter is crucial for defining the starting point of the interpolation process.

inputs.name: interpolation_curve
inputs.description: A list of floating-point numbers representing the curve along which the coordinates will be interpolated. This parameter determines the shape and trajectory of the interpolation.

outputs.name: coordinates
outputs.description: A string representation of the interpolated coordinates, formatted as a list of dictionaries with 'x' and 'y' keys.

Intrinsic_lora_sampling.description: This node enables the application of intrinsic LoRAs (Low-Rank Adaptations) to models for specific tasks such as depth map generation, surface normal estimation, albedo, and shading. It leverages LoRAs to modify the behavior of pre-trained models without extensive retraining, focusing on enhancing or altering the model's output based on the task at hand.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model to which the intrinsic LoRA will be applied. It serves as the base for modifications and enhancements specific to the desired task.

inputs.name: lora_name
inputs.description: The name of the LoRA to be applied, selected from a predefined list of available intrinsic LoRAs.

inputs.name: task
inputs.description: Specifies the task for which the model's output is being adapted, such as depth map generation or surface normal estimation. The default task is depth map generation.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: A text prompt that guides the model's adaptation process for the specified task, enhancing the relevance of the output to the input text.

inputs.name: clip
inputs.description: A CLIP model used for encoding the text prompt into a format that guides the adaptation process.

inputs.name: vae
inputs.description: A VAE (Variational Autoencoder) model used for encoding or decoding the samples during the adaptation process.

inputs.name: per_batch
inputs.description: The number of samples processed per batch, affecting the efficiency and speed of the adaptation process.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: An optional input image that can be used as a basis for the adaptation process, providing a visual context.

inputs.name: optional_latent
inputs.description: An optional latent representation that can be used instead of generating one from an input image, offering a shortcut in the adaptation process.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image after applying the intrinsic LoRA, adapted for the specified task.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The latent representation of the output image, providing a deeper insight into the model's adaptation process.

JoinStringMulti.description: The JoinStringMulti node dynamically combines multiple input strings into a single string or a list of strings, based on user-defined parameters such as the number of inputs and a delimiter. It allows for flexible string manipulation within a flow, accommodating a variable number of string inputs.

inputs.name: inputcount
inputs.description: Specifies the number of input strings to be combined. This allows the node to dynamically adjust to the desired number of inputs.

inputs.name: string_i
inputs.description: Represents an input string to be combined. This serves as a generic placeholder for any string input beyond the first, facilitating the concatenation process with variable input counts.

inputs.name: delimiter
inputs.description: The delimiter used to separate the input strings in the final combined string.

inputs.name: return_list
inputs.description: Determines whether the output should be a single concatenated string or a list of the individual input strings.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The result of combining the input strings, either as a single concatenated string or a list of strings, depending on the return_list parameter.

JoinStrings.description: The JoinStrings node is designed to concatenate two input strings using a specified delimiter, producing a single output string. This functionality is essential for string manipulation tasks where combining pieces of text in a structured manner is required.

inputs.name: string1
inputs.description: The first string to be joined. It serves as the starting point of the concatenated result.

inputs.name: string2
inputs.description: The second string to be joined. It is appended to the first string, separated by the specified delimiter.

inputs.name: delimiter
inputs.description: A string used to separate the two input strings in the concatenated result. It defines the boundary between the joined strings.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The result of concatenating string1 and string2 with the delimiter in between.

LoadAndResizeImage.description: This node is designed to load images from a specified path and resize them according to given dimensions, maintaining the aspect ratio if required. It supports handling of image masks, allowing for simultaneous resizing and optional adjustment of the mask channel. The node is capable of processing single images or batches, adapting to various image formats and ensuring compatibility with further image processing tasks.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image or path to the image to be loaded and resized. It serves as the primary input for the node's operation, determining the content that will undergo resizing and potential mask adjustment.

inputs.name: resize
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether the image should be resized. This parameter influences the node's decision to alter the image dimensions or maintain the original size.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: The desired width of the output image. It plays a crucial role in determining the final dimensions of the resized image, especially when maintaining aspect ratio.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: The desired height of the output image. Similar to width, it affects the final dimensions of the resized image and is essential for aspect ratio calculations.

inputs.name: repeat
inputs.description: Indicates whether the image should be repeated to fill a larger canvas if necessary. This parameter is relevant for batch processing or specific layout requirements.

inputs.name: keep_proportion
inputs.description: A flag to maintain the original aspect ratio of the image during resizing. It ensures that the resized image retains its proportional dimensions, avoiding distortion.

inputs.name: divisible_by
inputs.description: Ensures the dimensions of the resized image are divisible by a specified number. This is often required for compatibility with certain image processing or machine learning models.

inputs.name: mask_channel
inputs.description: Specifies the channel of the image to be used as a mask, allowing for selective processing or adjustment in conjunction with the main image resizing.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The resized image, potentially alongside its mask, ready for further processing or analysis. This output is central to the node's purpose of preparing images for subsequent steps in a workflow.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The mask associated with the resized image, if applicable, providing additional data for selective processing or analysis.

outputs.name: width
outputs.description: The width of the resized image, reflecting the final dimensions after processing.

outputs.name: height
outputs.description: The height of the resized image, indicating the final dimensions post-resizing.

LoadResAdapterNormalization.description: This node is designed to enhance the adaptability and performance of a given model by loading and applying normalization weights from a ResAdapter. It aims to improve model accuracy and efficiency by integrating external normalization parameters, thereby optimizing the model's response to various inputs.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model to which the ResAdapter normalization weights will be applied. It is crucial for enhancing the model's adaptability and performance by integrating external normalization parameters.

inputs.name: resadapter_path
inputs.description: The file path to the ResAdapter normalization weights. This path is used to locate and load the normalization parameters that are essential for optimizing the model's performance.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: A clone of the original model with the ResAdapter normalization weights applied. This enhanced model is expected to exhibit improved accuracy and efficiency.

MaskBatchMulti.description: The `MaskBatchMulti` node is designed to create a batch of images by combining multiple masks. It allows for dynamic input count adjustment, enabling the combination of a variable number of masks into a single batch. This functionality is particularly useful in scenarios where the aggregation of mask data is required for further image processing or analysis.

inputs.name: inputcount
inputs.description: Specifies the number of input masks to be combined into a single batch. This parameter allows for dynamic adjustment of the node's input capacity, facilitating the aggregation of varying numbers of masks.

inputs.name: mask_i
inputs.description: Represents a mask to be included in the batch, where 'i' can range from 1 to the number specified by 'inputcount'. Each mask contributes to the aggregated batch, enabling complex mask combinations for advanced image processing tasks.

outputs.name: masks
outputs.description: The combined batch of masks resulting from the aggregation of the input masks. This output is useful for downstream image processing tasks that require batched mask data.

MaskOrImageToWeight.description: The MaskOrImageToWeight node is designed to calculate the mean value of either masks or images provided as input, but not both simultaneously. It supports converting these mean values into different output types, including lists, pandas series, or tensors, based on the specified output type. This functionality allows for flexible data handling and integration into broader data processing or machine learning workflows.

inputs.name: output_type
inputs.description: Specifies the desired format for the output data, which can be a list, pandas series, or tensor. This choice determines how the mean values calculated from the input masks or images are structured for subsequent use.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: An optional input consisting of images from which mean values are calculated if masks are not provided. This parameter allows the node to work with either image or mask data, but not both simultaneously.

inputs.name: masks
inputs.description: An optional input consisting of masks from which mean values are calculated if images are not provided. This parameter enables the node to process either mask or image inputs, ensuring flexibility in data handling.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The processed mean values of the input masks or images, formatted according to the specified output type. This output facilitates further data manipulation or analysis in subsequent steps of a pipeline.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: A list of the mean values calculated from the input, represented as strings. This provides an alternative view of the data for logging or display purposes.

MergeImageChannels.description: The MergeImageChannels node is designed for combining separate image channels (red, green, and blue) into a single composite image. It optionally supports the inclusion of an alpha channel for transparency, allowing for more complex image compositions.

inputs.name: red
inputs.description: The red channel of the image, which contributes to the overall color composition by defining the red intensity.

inputs.name: green
inputs.description: The green channel of the image, which contributes to the overall color composition by defining the green intensity.

inputs.name: blue
inputs.description: The blue channel of the image, which contributes to the overall color composition by defining the blue intensity.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: An optional alpha channel for adding transparency to the final image, enhancing its compositional complexity.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The resulting image after merging the red, green, and blue channels, optionally with an alpha channel for transparency.

ModelPassThrough.description: The ModelPassThrough node is designed to seamlessly forward a model input without any modifications. This functionality serves as a workaround for scenarios where bypassing inputs directly is not supported, ensuring that the model data can flow through the node unchanged.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model input represents the model data that will be passed through unchanged. It is crucial for maintaining the integrity of the model's structure and data throughout the node's operation.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The output model is identical to the input model, having been passed through the node without any alterations. This ensures the model's structure and data remain intact for subsequent operations.

NormalizedAmplitudeToFloatList.description: This node is designed to interface with the AudioScheduler nodes, converting normalized amplitude values into a list of floats. It ensures that the amplitude values are within a specific range before conversion, facilitating their use in audio processing workflows.

inputs.name: normalized_amp
inputs.description: Represents the normalized amplitude values to be converted. It is crucial for ensuring the amplitude values are within the acceptable range [0, 1] before conversion, affecting the node's execution and the accuracy of the output.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The output is a list of floats derived from the normalized amplitude values, suitable for further processing in audio-related applications.

NormalizedAmplitudeToMask.description: This node is designed to convert normalized amplitude values from audio signals into masks, applying a transformation that maps the amplitude range to a corresponding visual representation. It emphasizes the integration of audio data with visual elements, enabling dynamic adjustments to visual content based on audio input.

inputs.name: normalized_amp
inputs.description: The normalized amplitude values, expected to be in the range [0, 1], serve as the basis for generating masks. These values dictate the intensity and characteristics of the resulting visual masks, directly influencing the visual output.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Specifies the width of the output mask, allowing for customization of the mask's dimensions based on the requirements of the visual representation.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Determines the height of the output mask, enabling adjustment of the mask's size to fit specific visual contexts.

inputs.name: frame_offset
inputs.description: An integer value used to offset the amplitude values, providing a means to shift the visual representation of the mask in relation to the audio input.

inputs.name: location_x
inputs.description: The x-coordinate location where the mask will be applied, allowing for precise positioning of the visual effect within the larger image or scene.

inputs.name: location_y
inputs.description: The y-coordinate location for the mask application, facilitating accurate placement of the audio-induced visual effect.

inputs.name: size
inputs.description: Defines the size of the mask, offering control over the scale of the visual effect generated from the audio amplitude.

inputs.name: shape
inputs.description: Allows selection of the mask's shape, providing options such as 'none', 'circle', 'square', and 'triangle' to customize the visual outcome.

inputs.name: color
inputs.description: Chooses the color scheme of the mask, with options like 'white' and 'amplitude' to influence the visual appearance based on the audio input.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The output mask generated from the normalized amplitude values, where the amplitude information is visually encoded into the mask's structure.

OffsetMask.description: The OffsetMask node is designed to manipulate and transform masks by applying specified offsets, rotations, and potentially duplicating the mask to create a batch with varied transformations. This node allows for dynamic adjustments to mask positioning and orientation, enabling more complex mask-based operations and effects within image processing workflows.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The input mask or batch of masks to be transformed. It serves as the base for applying offsets, rotations, and duplications, directly influencing the output mask's appearance and arrangement.

inputs.name: x
inputs.description: Specifies the horizontal offset to apply to the mask. A positive value shifts the mask right, while a negative value shifts it left, affecting the mask's horizontal position.

inputs.name: y
inputs.description: Specifies the vertical offset to apply to the mask. A positive value shifts the mask down, while a negative value shifts it up, affecting the mask's vertical position.

inputs.name: angle
inputs.description: The rotation angle in degrees to apply to the mask. This transformation rotates the mask around its center, altering its orientation.

inputs.name: duplication_factor
inputs.description: The number of times the input mask is duplicated to form a batch. This parameter allows for the creation of multiple transformed copies of the mask.

inputs.name: roll
inputs.description: Determines whether edge wrapping (rolling) is applied during the offset. When true, the mask's edges wrap around, creating a continuous effect.

inputs.name: incremental
inputs.description: When set to true, applies the horizontal and vertical offsets incrementally across the mask batch, creating a progressive transformation effect.

inputs.name: padding_mode
inputs.description: Defines the padding mode used when applying offsets and rotations, affecting how the mask's edges are handled during transformation. Options include 'empty', 'border', and 'reflection'.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The transformed mask or batch of masks after applying the specified offsets, rotations, and duplications. It reflects the cumulative effect of all transformations.

OffsetMaskByNormalizedAmplitude.description: This node applies transformations to a mask based on the normalized amplitude of an audio signal. It adjusts the mask's orientation and position, leveraging the amplitude to dictate the degree of rotation and shift, thereby enabling dynamic visual effects synchronized with audio intensity.

inputs.name: normalized_amp
inputs.description: An array of normalized amplitude values from an audio signal, used to determine the extent of transformation.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The mask to be transformed, representing a visual element whose modifications are driven by audio amplitude.

inputs.name: x
inputs.description: The horizontal shift factor, influencing the mask's lateral movement in response to amplitude changes.

inputs.name: y
inputs.description: The vertical shift factor, affecting the mask's vertical displacement as dictated by the amplitude.

inputs.name: rotate
inputs.description: A boolean indicating whether the mask should be rotated based on the normalized amplitude.

inputs.name: angle_multiplier
inputs.description: A multiplier for the rotation angle, scaling the effect of the normalized amplitude on the mask's rotation.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The transformed mask after applying rotation and shift adjustments based on the audio's normalized amplitude.

PlotCoordinates.description: The PlotCoordinates node is designed to process and manipulate coordinate data for visualization purposes. It adjusts bounding box sizes based on a size multiplier, ensures coordinates fit within specified frame boundaries, and generates a tensor representation of the plotted coordinates. This node is essential for visualizing spatial data, such as object locations in an image, by dynamically adjusting and plotting the coordinates according to given parameters.

inputs.name: coordinates
inputs.description: A JSON string or list of dictionaries representing the coordinates to be plotted. Each dictionary should contain 'x' and 'y' keys with their respective values. This input is crucial for determining the spatial locations to be visualized.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: A text prompt or description associated with the coordinates. This parameter can be used for adding contextual information to the visualization.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: The width of the frame in which the coordinates are to be plotted. This parameter defines the horizontal boundary for the visualization.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: The height of the frame in which the coordinates are to be plotted. This parameter defines the vertical boundary for the visualization.

inputs.name: bbox_width
inputs.description: The base width of the bounding boxes before adjustment with the size multiplier. It sets the initial horizontal size for each plotted coordinate.

inputs.name: bbox_height
inputs.description: The base height of the bounding boxes before adjustment with the size multiplier. It sets the initial vertical size for each plotted coordinate.

inputs.name: size_multiplier
inputs.description: A list of multipliers to adjust the size of each bounding box based on the index. It allows for dynamic resizing of the bounding boxes for each coordinate, enhancing the visualization's adaptability.

outputs.name: images
outputs.description: A sequence of images representing the plotted coordinates within the specified frame. This output is essential for visualizing the adjusted and fitted coordinates.

outputs.name: width
outputs.description: The width of the output image frame.

outputs.name: height
outputs.description: The height of the output image frame.

outputs.name: bbox_width
outputs.description: The width of the bounding boxes in the output image.

outputs.name: bbox_height
outputs.description: The height of the bounding boxes in the output image.

PreviewAnimation.description: The PreviewAnimation node is designed to generate a preview animation from a sequence of images, optionally applying masks to each frame. It allows for the customization of the animation's frames per second (fps), enabling the creation of smooth transitions and dynamic visualizations tailored to specific requirements.

inputs.name: fps
inputs.description: Specifies the frames per second for the animation, controlling the speed at which the images are displayed.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: A list of images to be included in the animation. Each image in the sequence contributes to the overall animation.

inputs.name: masks
inputs.description: Optional masks to apply to each image in the sequence, allowing for selective visibility or effects on the animation frames.

RemapImageRange.description: The RemapImageRange node is designed to adjust the pixel value range of an input image to a specified new range. It supports optional clamping to ensure that the remapped image values stay within a desired interval, enhancing flexibility in image preprocessing for various applications.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be remapped. This parameter is crucial for defining the source image whose pixel values are to be adjusted.

inputs.name: min
inputs.description: Specifies the minimum value of the new range for the image pixel values. It plays a key role in defining the lower bound of the target range.

inputs.name: max
inputs.description: Defines the maximum value of the new range for the image pixel values, setting the upper limit of the target range.

inputs.name: clamp
inputs.description: A boolean flag that determines whether the remapped image values should be clamped to the [0.0, 1.0] range, ensuring that pixel values remain valid.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image with its pixel values remapped to the specified new range. This parameter signifies the transformed image ready for further processing or analysis.

RemapMaskRange.description: The `RemapMaskRange` node is designed to adjust the range of values within a mask to a specified new minimum and maximum. This operation is useful for normalizing mask values or adjusting their scale for further processing.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The input mask whose values are to be remapped. This mask serves as the basis for scaling to the new specified range.

inputs.name: min
inputs.description: The new minimum value to which the lowest value in the mask will be scaled. This parameter sets the lower bound of the new value range for the mask.

inputs.name: max
inputs.description: The new maximum value to which the highest value in the mask will be scaled. This parameter sets the upper bound of the new value range for the mask.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The output mask with its values remapped to the new specified range. This mask is scaled such that its values lie between the new minimum and maximum values.

ReplaceImagesInBatch.description: This node is designed to replace a subset of images within a batch with a new set of images, starting from a specified index. It facilitates the manipulation of image batches by allowing selective updating of images, which can be useful in various image processing and augmentation tasks.

inputs.name: original_images
inputs.description: The batch of original images that will be partially replaced. It plays a crucial role in the operation by serving as the base for the replacement process.

inputs.name: replacement_images
inputs.description: The images that will replace a portion of the original image batch. Their inclusion directly alters the content of the batch starting from the specified index.

inputs.name: start_index
inputs.description: The index within the original image batch from which the replacement should begin. It determines the starting point for the replacement operation.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The modified image batch after the replacement operation has been performed.

ResizeMask.description: The ResizeMask node is designed to adjust the dimensions of a given mask or a batch of masks to a specified width and height, optionally maintaining the original proportions. This functionality is crucial for tasks that require masks to match the dimensions of corresponding images or other layers within a graphical or machine learning pipeline.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The mask parameter represents the input mask or batch of masks that will be resized. It is central to the node's operation, determining the base data that will be transformed.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Specifies the target width for the resized mask. If keep_proportions is True and width is set to 0, the original width is maintained, adjusting only the height based on the aspect ratio.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Specifies the target height for the resized mask. Similar to width, if keep_proportions is True and height is set to 0, the original height is preserved, adjusting the width to maintain the aspect ratio.

inputs.name: keep_proportions
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether to maintain the original aspect ratio of the mask during resizing. When True, the mask is resized to fit within the specified dimensions without altering its aspect ratio.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The resized mask or batch of masks, adjusted to the specified dimensions.

outputs.name: width
outputs.description: The actual width of the resized mask, which may differ from the input width if keep_proportions is True.

outputs.name: height
outputs.description: The actual height of the resized mask, which may differ from the input height if keep_proportions is True.

ReverseImageBatch.description: The ReverseImageBatch node is designed to manipulate a batch of images by reversing their order. This functionality is useful in scenarios where the sequence of images needs to be processed or viewed in reverse order, providing flexibility in handling image data within a batch.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The 'images' parameter represents the batch of images to be reversed. It is crucial for determining the order in which the images will be processed, directly affecting the output by reversing this order.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is a batch of images with their order reversed from the input batch, allowing for reversed sequence processing or visualization.

RoundMask.description: The RoundMask node specializes in converting masks or batches of masks into binary masks by rounding their values. This operation is essential for tasks that require clear, binary distinctions within masks, such as separating foreground from background in image processing applications.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The mask input is the primary data that the RoundMask node processes. It rounds the values of this mask to produce a binary mask, which is crucial for applications needing distinct segmentation.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The output is a binary mask or a batch of binary masks, where each pixel value is rounded to the nearest integer, effectively converting the mask into a binary format.

SaveImageWithAlpha.description: This node is designed for saving images with an alpha channel, allowing for transparency effects. It processes a batch of images and their corresponding masks, applies the masks as alpha channels to the images, optionally adds metadata (such as prompts or additional PNG information), and saves the resulting images with transparency to a specified location.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: A batch of images to be processed and saved with alpha transparency. This input is crucial for defining the visual content of the output files.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: A batch of masks corresponding to the images, used to create the alpha channel for transparency effects. This input is essential for determining which parts of each image should be transparent.

inputs.name: filename_prefix
inputs.description: A prefix for the filenames of the saved images, allowing for organized storage and easy identification.

ScaleBatchPromptSchedule.description: This node is designed to adapt a batch schedule from Fizz' nodes BatchPromptSchedule to a different frame count, effectively scaling the schedule to fit a new timeline while preserving the original pattern.

inputs.name: input_str
inputs.description: The string representation of the original batch schedule, specifying frame numbers and their corresponding values. It's crucial for defining the base schedule to be scaled.

inputs.name: old_frame_count
inputs.description: The original frame count of the batch schedule, serving as the basis for scaling calculations.

inputs.name: new_frame_count
inputs.description: The target frame count to which the original schedule will be scaled, adjusting the timeline accordingly.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: A string representation of the scaled batch schedule, with adjusted frame numbers and values to match the new frame count.

Sleep.description: The Sleep node introduces a delay in the execution flow based on a specified amount of time, allowing for timed pauses in processing sequences.

inputs.name: input
inputs.description: Acts as a pass-through for any input data, ensuring that the data is returned after the sleep delay without modification.

inputs.name: minutes
inputs.description: Specifies the duration of the delay in whole minutes, contributing to the total sleep time.

inputs.name: seconds
inputs.description: Specifies the duration of the delay in fractional minutes (seconds), allowing for precise control over the total sleep time.

outputs.description: Returns the input data unchanged after the specified delay, maintaining data integrity through the sleep process.

SomethingToString.description: This node is designed to convert various data types into a string format, optionally allowing for the addition of a prefix or suffix to the resulting string. It abstracts the complexity of data type conversion and string manipulation, providing a straightforward way to generate string representations of diverse inputs.

inputs.name: input
inputs.description: The primary data that will be converted to a string. This input can be of any type, and its conversion is central to the node's functionality.

inputs.name: prefix
inputs.description: An optional string to prepend to the converted input, allowing for customization of the resulting string's format.

inputs.name: suffix
inputs.description: An optional string to append to the converted input, enhancing the flexibility in formatting the resulting string.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The output is the string representation of the input, potentially modified by the specified prefix and/or suffix.

SoundReactive.description: The SoundReactive node dynamically adjusts its output based on the sound level input, allowing for real-time audio-reactive applications. It is designed to work with browser-based sound input and supports real-time diffusion processes with autoqueue functionality.

inputs.name: sound_level
inputs.description: Specifies the sound level to react to. It is a key factor in determining the node's output, adjusting the response based on the input sound level.

inputs.name: start_range_hz
inputs.description: Defines the starting frequency range in Hertz for processing. It sets the lower bound of the frequency range of interest.

inputs.name: end_range_hz
inputs.description: Sets the ending frequency range in Hertz for processing. It determines the upper limit of the frequency spectrum to be considered.

inputs.name: multiplier
inputs.description: A multiplier applied to the sound level, allowing for amplification or attenuation of the input signal.

inputs.name: smoothing_factor
inputs.description: Controls the smoothing of the sound level input, providing a way to reduce abrupt changes and fluctuations.

inputs.name: normalize
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether the sound level should be normalized, affecting the scale of the output.

outputs.name: sound_level
outputs.description: The adjusted sound level after applying the node's processing, reflecting changes based on the input and node settings.

outputs.name: sound_level_int
outputs.description: An integer representation of the adjusted sound level, offering a discrete version of the output for certain applications.

SplineEditor.description: The SplineEditor node is a graphical tool designed for creating and editing splines that represent various schedules or mask batches. It provides a user-friendly interface for manipulating control points and curves, enabling the customization of values for different applications. This node is particularly useful for tasks that require precise control over the interpolation and distribution of values across a specified domain, such as animation scheduling or data visualization.

inputs.name: points_store
inputs.description: A storage mechanism for the control points. It plays a critical role in managing and accessing the points for spline generation and manipulation.

inputs.name: coordinates
inputs.description: A list of coordinates for control points. These points define the shape and trajectory of the spline, directly impacting its form and the interpolated values.

inputs.name: mask_width
inputs.description: Specifies the width of the mask to be generated. It determines the horizontal dimension of the output mask or batch, affecting the resolution and scale of the generated spline.

inputs.name: mask_height
inputs.description: Defines the height of the mask to be generated. It influences the vertical dimension of the output, playing a crucial role in determining the resolution and scale of the spline.

inputs.name: points_to_sample
inputs.description: Sets the number of sample points to be generated from the spline. This value determines the granularity of the output, impacting the precision and detail of the interpolated values.

inputs.name: sampling_method
inputs.description: Chooses the method for sampling points along the spline, either by time or path. This affects how values are distributed along the spline, catering to different use cases like schedules or coordinates.

inputs.name: interpolation
inputs.description: Specifies the method of interpolation between control points. This choice influences the smoothness and curvature of the spline, affecting its overall appearance and functionality.

inputs.name: tension
inputs.description: Controls the tension of the spline curve. Adjusting this parameter affects the curvature and tightness of the spline, allowing for finer control over its shape.

inputs.name: repeat_output
inputs.description: Determines whether the output should be repeated. This can be useful for creating looping animations or patterns that require a continuous sequence of values.

inputs.name: float_output_type
inputs.description: Determines the type of float values to be outputted, affecting the format and usability of the generated data for subsequent nodes or processes.

inputs.name: min_value
inputs.description: Sets the minimum value for the output range. This parameter ensures that the generated values do not fall below a certain threshold, maintaining consistency and control over the output.

inputs.name: max_value
inputs.description: Establishes the maximum value for the output range. It caps the generated values to prevent them from exceeding a specified limit, ensuring the output remains within desired parameters.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: Generates a batch of masks based on the defined spline. This output is suitable for nodes that require mask inputs for further processing.

outputs.name: coord_str
outputs.description: Produces a list of float values interpolated from the spline. These values can be used for weight adjustments or other numerical applications.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: Outputs a pandas series containing values derived from the spline. This format is convenient for data analysis and manipulation within pandas-supported environments.

outputs.name: count
outputs.description: Creates a torch tensor from the spline's interpolated values. This output is compatible with PyTorch-based models and operations, facilitating integration into deep learning workflows.

outputs.name: normalized_str
outputs.description: Provides a normalized string representation of the spline's interpolated values, useful for textual descriptions or further string-based processing.

SplitBboxes.description: Splits a list of bounding boxes (bboxes) at a specified index into two separate lists, facilitating operations that require segmenting bounding box data.

inputs.name: bboxes
inputs.description: The list of bounding boxes to be split. This parameter is crucial for determining how the bounding boxes are divided into two groups.

inputs.name: index
inputs.description: The index at which the list of bounding boxes is split. This parameter dictates the division point, affecting the composition of the resulting bounding box lists.

outputs.name: bboxes_a
outputs.description: The first sublist of bounding boxes, containing elements from the start of the original list up to (but not including) the specified index.

outputs.name: bboxes_b
outputs.description: The second sublist of bounding boxes, containing elements from the specified index to the end of the original list.

SplitImageChannels.description: The SplitImageChannels node is designed to separate the individual color channels of an image into distinct images, each channel being expanded across all channels of its respective output image, and additionally extracts the alpha channel as a separate mask. This process facilitates operations that require manipulation or analysis of specific color components within an image.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be split into its constituent color channels. This image is expected to have multiple channels, including an alpha channel for transparency.

outputs.name: red
outputs.description: The red channel of the input image, expanded across all three color channels of the output image.

outputs.name: green
outputs.description: The green channel of the input image, expanded across all three color channels of the output image.

outputs.name: blue
outputs.description: The blue channel of the input image, expanded across all three color channels of the output image.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The alpha channel of the input image, representing the transparency mask.

StabilityAPI_SD3.description: The StabilityAPI_SD3 node interfaces with the StabilityAI API to facilitate image generation or manipulation tasks. It leverages the StabilityAI platform's capabilities, allowing users to generate images based on textual descriptions or modify existing images. This node emphasizes the use of specific API keys for operation and warns against potential metadata storage issues when saving images through separate nodes.

inputs.name: prompt
inputs.description: The main textual description guiding the image generation or manipulation process, serving as the primary input for creating or altering images.

inputs.name: n_prompt
inputs.description: A negative textual description to guide the image generation process by specifying what to avoid, refining the output.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: A seed value for ensuring reproducibility of the generated images.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: Specifies the model used by StabilityAI for the image generation or manipulation task.

inputs.name: aspect_ratio
inputs.description: The desired aspect ratio for the output image, influencing its dimensions.

inputs.name: output_format
inputs.description: The format in which the generated image will be outputted, such as PNG or JPEG.

inputs.name: api_key
inputs.description: The API key required for accessing the StabilityAI platform's services.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: An existing image to be modified or used as a basis for generation in image-to-image tasks.

inputs.name: img2img_strength
inputs.description: Controls the influence of the input image on the generated output in image-to-image tasks.

inputs.name: disable_metadata
inputs.description: A flag to disable metadata storage, addressing privacy or data storage concerns.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The generated or manipulated image as a result of the process, aligning with the provided descriptions and parameters.

StableZero123_BatchSchedule.description: This node is designed to manage and schedule batch operations for the StableZero123 model, optimizing the processing of multiple inputs in a batched manner for efficiency and performance.

inputs.name: clip_vision
inputs.description: Represents the CLIP vision model input, used to provide visual context or features for processing.

inputs.name: init_image
inputs.description: Initial image input for the model to process or modify.

inputs.name: vae
inputs.description: The variational autoencoder used for encoding or decoding images in the model's processing pipeline.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Specifies the width of the output image, allowing for customization of the image dimensions.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Specifies the height of the output image, allowing for customization of the image dimensions.

inputs.name: batch_size
inputs.description: Determines the number of images processed in a single batch, affecting efficiency and performance.

inputs.name: interpolation
inputs.description: Defines the interpolation method used in image processing, affecting the smoothness and quality of the output.

inputs.name: azimuth_points_string
inputs.description: A string defining azimuth points for 3D model orientation, used in scheduling the model's view direction.

inputs.name: elevation_points_string
inputs.description: A string defining elevation points for 3D model orientation, used in scheduling the model's view direction.

outputs.name: positive
outputs.description: The positive conditioning output from the model, used for enhancing certain features or aspects in the generated content.

outputs.name: negative
outputs.description: The negative conditioning output from the model, used for suppressing certain features or aspects in the generated content.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: Represents the latent space encoding of the input, capturing the essential features for further processing or generation.

StringConstant.description: The StringConstant node is designed to pass through a string input without modification, serving as a constant string value within a flow.

inputs.name: string
inputs.description: Represents the string input to be passed through. This parameter allows for the input of a single-line string, with a default value of an empty string if none is provided.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: Outputs the same string that was input, effectively acting as a pass-through for the string value.

StringConstantMultiline.description: The StringConstantMultiline node is designed to process multiline string inputs, optionally stripping newline characters based on a boolean flag. It enables the manipulation of text data by allowing the preservation or removal of formatting, making it versatile for various text processing tasks.

inputs.name: string
inputs.description: The primary text input that the node processes. It accepts multiline strings, enabling the handling of text data that spans multiple lines.

inputs.name: strip_newlines
inputs.description: A boolean flag that determines whether newline characters in the input string should be removed. When set to true, it strips newline characters, flattening the text to a single line.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: Outputs the processed string, which may have newline characters removed based on the input flag. This allows for flexible text manipulation and formatting.

Superprompt.description: Superprompt is designed to enhance text prompts by upsampling them into more detailed descriptions using a T5 model fine-tuned on the SuperPrompt dataset. It serves as a pre-generation step to enrich prompts for text-to-image models, facilitating the creation of more detailed and accurate images.

inputs.name: instruction_prompt
inputs.description: A guiding instruction to shape the expansion of the prompt, setting the context for how the text should be detailed.

inputs.name: prompt
inputs.description: The initial text prompt to be expanded into a more detailed description.

inputs.name: max_new_tokens
inputs.description: Specifies the maximum number of new tokens to be generated, controlling the length of the expanded description.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The enhanced, detailed version of the original text prompt.

SV3D_BatchSchedule.description: The SV3D_BatchSchedule node is designed to facilitate the scheduling of azimuth and elevation conditions for SV3D, a video model. It allows for the dynamic adjustment of these conditions over the course of a video, enhancing the model's ability to generate more precise and contextually appropriate visual content.

inputs.name: clip_vision
inputs.description: Specifies the CLIP vision model to be used for conditioning the SV3D model, affecting the visual content generated.

inputs.name: init_image
inputs.description: Initial image to start the video generation process, setting the visual context for the SV3D model.

inputs.name: vae
inputs.description: The VAE model used for encoding and decoding images within the SV3D framework, crucial for the video generation process.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Defines the width of the generated video frames, allowing for customization of the video's resolution.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Sets the height of the generated video frames, enabling control over the video's aspect ratio and resolution.

inputs.name: batch_size
inputs.description: Determines the number of video frames to be processed in a single batch, impacting the efficiency of video generation.

inputs.name: interpolation
inputs.description: Specifies the interpolation method for transitioning between different azimuth and elevation points, affecting the smoothness of the video.

inputs.name: azimuth_points_string
inputs.description: A string defining key points for azimuth adjustment throughout the video, guiding the directional focus of the generated content.

inputs.name: elevation_points_string
inputs.description: A string detailing key points for elevation changes over the video, influencing the vertical angle of the generated visuals.

outputs.name: positive
outputs.description: The positive conditioning output, influencing the generation towards desired visual attributes.

outputs.name: negative
