outputs.description: The negative conditioning output, steering the generation away from undesired visual aspects.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The latent representation of the video, encapsulating the high-dimensional space that the model navigates during generation.

VRAM_Debug.description: The VRAM_Debug node is designed to monitor and manage the VRAM usage of models within a deep learning environment. It provides functionalities to clear the GPU cache, unload all models from memory, and perform garbage collection to free up VRAM. Additionally, it can return the amount of VRAM freed during its operation, aiding in debugging and optimizing memory usage.

inputs.name: empty_cache
inputs.description: Controls whether the GPU cache is cleared, which can help in freeing up unused memory.

inputs.name: gc_collect
inputs.description: Determines whether garbage collection is performed, potentially freeing up memory by removing unused objects.

inputs.name: unload_all_models
inputs.description: Specifies whether all models should be unloaded from memory, which can significantly reduce VRAM usage.

inputs.name: any_input
inputs.description: An optional input that can be passed through the node without modification, allowing for flexible usage.

inputs.name: image_pass
inputs.description: An optional image input that can be passed through the node without modification.

inputs.name: model_pass
inputs.description: An optional model input that can be passed through the node without modification.

outputs.name: any_output
outputs.description: Returns the inputs passed to the node along with the VRAM usage information before and after the operation.

outputs.name: image_pass
outputs.description: Returns the optional image input passed through the node without modification.

outputs.name: model_pass
outputs.description: Returns the optional model input passed through the node without modification.

outputs.name: freemem_before
outputs.description: Returns the amount of free VRAM before the operation.

outputs.name: freemem_after
outputs.description: Returns the amount of free VRAM after the operation.

WeightScheduleConvert.description: The WeightScheduleConvert node is designed for the conversion of value lists or series into different types, accommodating various data formats for further processing. It enables the transformation of input data to a specified output type, including options like matching the input format, converting to lists, pandas series, or tensors. This functionality is crucial for ensuring data compatibility and optimizing performance across different stages of a computational workflow.

inputs.name: input_values
inputs.description: Specifies the initial set of values to be converted. Its format and type are crucial for determining the appropriate conversion process and the resulting output type.

inputs.name: output_type
inputs.description: Determines the desired format of the output, allowing for conversion to formats such as 'match_input', 'list', 'pandas series', or 'tensor'. This choice affects how the input values are transformed and represented in the output.

inputs.name: invert
inputs.description: A boolean flag that, when set, may alter the conversion process by inverting certain aspects of the input data, depending on the specific implementation.

inputs.name: repeat
inputs.description: An integer specifying how many times the input values should be repeated in the output. This parameter can be used to expand the size of the output dataset.

inputs.name: remap_to_frames
inputs.description: An optional integer parameter that specifies if and how the input values should be remapped to a specific number of frames, affecting the temporal dimension of the output.

inputs.name: interpolation_curve
inputs.description: An optional floating-point parameter that defines the curve used for interpolating between input values, influencing the smoothness and dynamics of the conversion process.

inputs.name: remap_values
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether the input values should be remapped according to specified minimum and maximum values, enabling normalization or other forms of value adjustment.

inputs.name: remap_min
inputs.description: An optional floating-point parameter specifying the minimum value to which input values can be remapped, used in conjunction with 'remap_max' to define the range of the remapping process.

inputs.name: remap_max
inputs.description: An optional floating-point parameter specifying the maximum value to which input values can be remapped, used in conjunction with 'remap_min' to define the range of the remapping process.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The output can include floating-point numbers, representing transformed or converted values based on the specified output type.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The output may contain strings, particularly when the output type is set to formats like 'list' or 'pandas series' that involve textual representation.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: The output can include integers, which may result from certain types of conversions or processing applied to the input values.

WeightScheduleExtend.description: The WeightScheduleExtend node is designed to extend and convert weight schedules or value lists, supporting various output types for flexible integration into different model architectures. It allows for the manipulation of input values to match specific requirements, facilitating the customization of model behavior over time.

inputs.name: input_values_i
inputs.description: Represents the first set of input values for the operation, playing a crucial role in the extension or conversion process.

inputs.name: output_type
inputs.description: Specifies the desired output type of the operation, influencing the format of the extended or converted values.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The output of the operation, which can be a single float value or a collection of float values, depending on the specified output type.

WidgetToString.description: The get_widget_value node is designed to select a specific widget within a node and output its value as a string. It enables dynamic access to widget data based on node ID and widget name, with an option to return all widget values from a node if required. This functionality is crucial for customizing user interactions and data retrieval within a workflow.

inputs.name: id
inputs.description: Specifies the unique identifier of the node whose widget's value is to be retrieved, essential for pinpointing the exact node within a workflow.

inputs.name: widget_name
inputs.description: The name of the widget whose value is to be extracted as a string, critical for identifying the specific widget within the node.

inputs.name: return_all
inputs.description: A boolean flag that determines whether the node should return the values of all widgets as a string, offering flexibility in the amount of information extracted.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The extracted widget value(s) converted to a string, essential for presenting or further processing the widget data in text form.

LayeredDiffusionApply.description: The LayeredDiffusionApply node is designed to integrate and apply layered diffusion techniques to enhance image generation processes. It leverages multiple diffusion models to apply complex transformations and refinements to images, aiming to improve the quality and detail of the generated visuals.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model parameter represents the diffusion model to be patched and used for the layered diffusion process. It is crucial for defining the specific model behavior and characteristics that will be applied during the image generation.

inputs.name: config
inputs.description: The config parameter determines the configuration settings for the layered diffusion model, specifying how the model should be applied and operated.

inputs.name: weight
inputs.description: Weight defines the influence level of the layered diffusion process on the final image output, adjusting the intensity of the applied transformations.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The output model after applying the layered diffusion process, reflecting the transformations and refinements made to the original model.

LayeredDiffusionCondApply.description: This node specializes in applying conditional layered diffusion processes to models, leveraging specific conditions to guide the diffusion process. It integrates conditional inputs with the model's latent space, facilitating targeted modifications and enhancements in the generated outputs.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model to which the layered diffusion process will be applied, encapsulating the necessary architecture and parameters for the diffusion to take place.

inputs.name: cond
inputs.description: The conditional input that guides the diffusion process, influencing the direction and characteristics of the generated output.

inputs.name: uncond
inputs.description: An unconditional input that serves as a baseline or reference for the diffusion process, providing a contrast to the conditional input.

inputs.name: latent
inputs.description: The latent representation of the input, which is processed and integrated with the conditional and unconditional inputs during the diffusion process.

inputs.name: config
inputs.description: A configuration string that specifies the particular layered diffusion model to use, aligning with the model's version and capabilities.

inputs.name: weight
inputs.description: A weight factor that influences the extent to which the conditional input affects the diffusion process, allowing for fine-tuning of the output.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The modified model after the layered diffusion process, incorporating the conditional and unconditional inputs.

outputs.name: conditioning
outputs.description: The conditioning information used during the diffusion process, reflecting how the conditional inputs were integrated.

LayeredDiffusionCondJointApply.description: This node specializes in applying conditional and joint layered diffusion processes to generate or modify images based on specific conditions and joint configurations. It leverages advanced diffusion techniques to blend and refine images, ensuring high-quality outputs tailored to the given conditions.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model patcher used to apply the layered diffusion process, crucial for adapting the base model to specific configurations and conditions.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image to be processed, serving as a base for the diffusion effects and transformations.

inputs.name: config
inputs.description: Configuration string specifying the layered diffusion model to use, critical for selecting the appropriate processing approach.

inputs.name: cond
inputs.description: The conditional inputs guiding the diffusion process, essential for tailoring the output to specific requirements or contexts.

inputs.name: blended_cond
inputs.description: Blended conditional inputs, combining multiple conditions to enrich the diffusion process and enhance output quality.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The modified model after applying the layered diffusion process, reflecting the changes and enhancements made.

LayeredDiffusionDecode.description: This node is designed to decode images through a layered diffusion process, leveraging advanced techniques to enhance image quality and detail. It focuses on reconstructing or generating images by applying a series of diffusion steps, aimed at improving visual fidelity and achieving high-resolution outputs.

inputs.name: samples
inputs.description: Represents the input samples to be decoded, playing a crucial role in determining the characteristics and quality of the decoded images.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: A tensor of images to be processed, serving as the base for the diffusion decoding process. This parameter is essential for defining the initial state of the images before applying the diffusion steps.

inputs.name: sd_version
inputs.description: Indicates the version of the diffusion model to be used, impacting the decoding process's effectiveness and the final image quality.

inputs.name: sub_batch_size
inputs.description: Determines the size of sub-batches for processing, optimizing the decoding operation's efficiency and resource utilization.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The decoded image output, showcasing the result of the layered diffusion decoding process.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The alpha mask output, representing the transparency layer decoded alongside the image, enhancing the image's composition and detail.

LayeredDiffusionDecodeRGBA.description: The LayeredDiffusionDecodeRGBA node is designed to decode the alpha channel value from a given pixel value, transforming an RGB image input into an RGBA image output. This process involves adding an alpha channel to the existing RGB channels, thereby enabling the representation of transparency in the resulting image.

inputs.name: samples
inputs.description: The latent representation of the image to be decoded. It plays a crucial role in reconstructing the image with the added alpha channel for transparency.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The initial RGB images that are to be transformed into RGBA format by adding an alpha channel.

inputs.name: sd_version
inputs.description: Specifies the version of the Stable Diffusion model used for decoding, affecting the decoding process and the final image quality.

inputs.name: sub_batch_size
inputs.description: Determines the size of sub-batches for processing, impacting the efficiency and speed of the decoding operation.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image in RGBA format, where the alpha channel has been decoded and added to the original RGB image.

LayeredDiffusionDecodeSplit.description: The LayeredDiffusionDecodeSplit node is designed for the specialized task of decoding images in a layered diffusion process, specifically handling split layers. It modifies the sampling process to accommodate different frame rates or sequences, ensuring that each layer is processed appropriately for temporal consistency and visual quality.

inputs.name: samples
inputs.description: A collection of sample data that the node will process, typically representing different states or stages in the diffusion process. This input is crucial for determining how the images are decoded and split across frames.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: A tensor of images that are to be decoded and potentially modified by the node. This input is essential for applying the layered diffusion decoding process to each image in the sequence.

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: The number of frames to be processed, affecting how the samples are sliced and how images are decoded across the sequence. This parameter plays a key role in temporal segmentation of the diffusion process.

inputs.name: sd_version
inputs.description: Specifies the version of the stable diffusion model to be used, impacting the decoding behavior and the quality of the output images.

inputs.name: sub_batch_size
inputs.description: Determines the size of sub-batches for processing, influencing the efficiency and speed of the decoding operation. This parameter is important for managing computational resources.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output of the node, consisting of decoded images that have been processed through the layered diffusion technique. This includes modifications for split layers and adjustments for frame rates.

LayeredDiffusionDiffApply.description: This node applies a layered diffusion process to an input, leveraging a specific configuration and weight to modify the diffusion behavior. It is designed to integrate with a model patcher, facilitating the application of diffusion techniques in a controlled and customizable manner.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model patcher instance used to apply the layered diffusion. It serves as the primary interface for modifying the model's behavior based on the specified configuration and weight.

inputs.name: cond
inputs.description: The conditional input used to guide the diffusion process, providing context or constraints.

inputs.name: uncond
inputs.description: The unconditional input that represents the baseline or default state for the diffusion process.

inputs.name: blended_latent
inputs.description: A latent representation that combines elements of both conditional and unconditional inputs, used to influence the diffusion outcome.

inputs.name: latent
inputs.description: The initial latent representation of the input, serving as the starting point for the diffusion process.

inputs.name: config
inputs.description: A string identifier for the layered diffusion configuration to be applied. This determines the specific diffusion process and parameters to be used.

inputs.name: weight
inputs.description: A float value that adjusts the intensity of the diffusion effect. Higher values result in more pronounced diffusion effects.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The modified model after the layered diffusion process has been applied, reflecting the changes made.

outputs.name: conditioning
outputs.description: The conditioning information used during the diffusion process, which may include modified or additional context.

LayeredDiffusionJointApply.description: This node applies a joint layered diffusion process to generate or modify images, leveraging a combination of conditional and unconditional inputs to enhance the quality and relevance of the output. It integrates multiple diffusion models to process and blend latent representations, facilitating nuanced image synthesis or transformation.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model patcher that configures and applies the diffusion models, acting as the intermediary for executing the layered diffusion process.

inputs.name: config
inputs.description: Configuration string that specifies the particular diffusion model to be used, ensuring compatibility and optimal performance.

inputs.name: fg_cond
inputs.description: Foreground conditional inputs that guide the diffusion process towards generating images with specific foreground characteristics.

inputs.name: bg_cond
inputs.description: Background conditional inputs that influence the diffusion process to generate images with specific background characteristics.

inputs.name: blended_cond
inputs.description: Blended conditional inputs that combine foreground and background characteristics, enriching the diffusion process.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The modified model after applying the layered diffusion process, ready for further image generation or transformation tasks.

DownloadAndLoadLivePortraitModels.description: This node is responsible for downloading and loading the necessary models for the LivePortrait feature. It ensures that all components required for generating live portraits, such as appearance feature extractors, motion extractors, warping modules, and retargeting networks, are properly initialized and ready for use. The node dynamically adjusts model precision based on the execution environment and manages model dependencies to facilitate seamless live portrait generation.

inputs.name: precision
inputs.description: Specifies the desired precision for model computations, which can be set manually or determined automatically based on the device's capabilities. This affects the overall performance and accuracy of the live portrait generation process.

outputs.name: live_portrait_pipe
outputs.description: Returns a fully initialized pipeline configured for live portrait generation, including all necessary models and settings tailored to the specified precision. The specific type returned is a custom class instance that encapsulates the live portrait pipeline.

LivePortraitProcess.description: The LivePortraitProcess node is designed to transform static portrait images into animated versions by applying a series of image processing and deep learning techniques. It leverages facial landmarks, cropping, resizing, and feature extraction to prepare the source image. Subsequently, it utilizes keypoints information, rotation matrices, and 3D features to animate the portrait based on driving images, adjusting for eye and lip movements, and optionally stitching the results for a seamless animation.

inputs.name: pipeline
inputs.description: The processing pipeline that encapsulates the entire animation process, including cropping, feature extraction, and animation synthesis.

inputs.name: source_image
inputs.description: The source image to be animated. It serves as the base for the animation process, where facial features are detected and used to guide the transformation.

inputs.name: driving_images
inputs.description: A sequence of images that dictate the animation's movements. These images provide the dynamic expressions and orientations to be transferred to the source portrait.

inputs.name: dsize
inputs.description: The desired size for the output images, affecting how the source and driving images are cropped and resized.

inputs.name: scale
inputs.description: A scaling factor applied during the cropping process to adjust the emphasis on the central features of the portrait.

inputs.name: vx_ratio
inputs.description: The horizontal ratio used to fine-tune the cropping area, focusing on the central facial features.

inputs.name: vy_ratio
inputs.description: The vertical ratio used to fine-tune the cropping area, focusing on the central facial features.

inputs.name: lip_zero
inputs.description: A flag indicating whether to neutralize lip movements in the animation, keeping the lips static.

inputs.name: eye_retargeting
inputs.description: A flag to enable or disable eye movement retargeting in the animation, allowing for dynamic eye expressions.

inputs.name: eyes_retargeting_multiplier
inputs.description: A multiplier applied to the eye movement retargeting, allowing for exaggerated or subdued eye animations.

inputs.name: lip_retargeting
inputs.description: A flag to enable or disable lip movement retargeting in the animation, allowing for dynamic lip expressions.

inputs.name: lip_retargeting_multiplier
inputs.description: A multiplier applied to the lip movement retargeting, allowing for exaggerated or subdued lip animations.

inputs.name: stitching
inputs.description: A flag indicating whether to apply stitching to the animated frames, ensuring seamless transitions between expressions.

inputs.name: relative
inputs.description: A flag that determines whether the animation should be based on relative movements from the driving images or absolute positions.

inputs.name: onnx_device
inputs.description: Specifies the computation device (e.g., CUDA for GPU) for running the ONNX models involved in the animation process.

outputs.name: cropped_images
outputs.description: A list of cropped and processed images ready for animation, representing intermediate steps in the animation pipeline.

outputs.name: full_images
outputs.description: The final list of animated portraits, fully processed and ready for display or further use.

Bool-\ud83d\udd2c.description: The Bool node is designed to process boolean inputs, performing logical operations based on the provided boolean value.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: Represents the boolean input to the node, determining the logical operation to be performed.

outputs.name: BOOLEAN
outputs.description: Outputs the processed boolean value, reflecting the result of the logical operation.

Compare-\ud83d\udd2c.description: The Compare node is designed to evaluate the relationship between two inputs based on a specified comparison operation (e.g., equality, inequality, greater than, less than). It abstracts the logic of comparison into a simple interface, allowing users to dynamically assess the conditions between inputs and derive a boolean result indicative of the comparison's outcome.

inputs.name: a
inputs.description: The first input to be compared. It plays a crucial role in determining the outcome of the comparison operation.

inputs.name: b
inputs.description: The second input to be compared against the first. Its value is essential in evaluating the comparison operation.

inputs.name: comparison
inputs.description: Specifies the type of comparison to perform between the two inputs (e.g., '==', '!=', '<', '>', '<=', '>='). This parameter dictates the logic applied in the comparison.

outputs.name: B
outputs.description: unknown

DebugPrint-\ud83d\udd2c.description: The DebugPrint node is designed for logging purposes, specifically to print any given input to the console. This functionality aids in debugging by allowing the visualization of data flow through the node.

inputs.name: ANY
inputs.description: Represents any input that the node will log to the console. Its flexibility allows for a wide range of data types to be printed, aiding in debugging and data flow analysis.

Float-\ud83d\udd2c.description: The Float node is designed to process numerical floating-point values, allowing for precision adjustments and mathematical operations within a logic-based framework.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: Represents the floating-point number to be processed or manipulated. Its importance lies in being the primary data that the node operates on, affecting the outcome of the node's execution.

outputs.name: FLOAT
outputs.description: Outputs the processed or manipulated floating-point number, reflecting the result of the node's operations.

If ANY return A else B-\ud83d\udd2c.description: This node conditionally executes one of two provided operations based on a boolean input. It serves as a logical branch, allowing for dynamic flow control within a node network by executing the first operation if the condition is true, and the second operation if false.

inputs.name: ANY
inputs.description: Represents a boolean condition that determines which of the two operations, IF_TRUE or IF_FALSE, will be executed. Its evaluation to True or False directs the flow of execution accordingly.

inputs.name: IF_TRUE
inputs.description: The operation to be executed if the ANY input evaluates to True. This allows for conditional execution of node operations based on the provided boolean condition.

inputs.name: IF_FALSE
inputs.description: The operation to be executed if the ANY input evaluates to False, providing an alternative path for execution in the node's logic.

outputs.description: The output is either the result of IF_TRUE or IF_FALSE operation, depending on the evaluation of the ANY input.

Int-\ud83d\udd2c.description: The Int node is designed to process and output integer values. It serves as a fundamental logic unit within a system, enabling the manipulation and handling of integer data types for various computational and logical operations.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: Specifies the integer value to be processed by the node. This parameter is central to the node's operation, as it determines the exact integer data that will be manipulated or evaluated.

outputs.name: INT
outputs.description: Outputs the integer value that was input, after any processing. This demonstrates the node's ability to handle and return integer data, maintaining its integrity throughout the operation.

String-\ud83d\udd2c.description: The String node is designed to process and return string values. It encapsulates the functionality to accept a string input, potentially perform operations on it, and then output the processed string.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: Represents the string value to be processed by the node. It is the primary input upon which the node operates, allowing for potential manipulation or evaluation of string data.

outputs.name: STRING
outputs.description: Outputs the processed or original string value received as input, depending on the node's implementation.

ColorizeDepthmap.description: The ColorizeDepthmap node is designed to transform depth maps into colorized representations, enhancing visual interpretation by applying a colormap. This process facilitates easier understanding and analysis of depth information by converting grayscale depth maps into vibrant, color-coded images.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The depth map to be colorized, which can be either a torch.Tensor or a numpy.ndarray. This map represents the depth information of a scene as a 2D array.

inputs.name: colorize_method
inputs.description: The name of the matplotlib colormap to use for colorizing the depth map.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The colorized depth map, enhanced with a colormap for better visual interpretation. The output is in the same data type as the input depth map.

MarigoldDepthEstimation.description: The MarigoldDepthEstimation node is designed for diffusion-based monocular depth estimation, leveraging the Marigold model to generate depth maps from single images. This node focuses on enhancing the accuracy of depth perception in images by employing a series of denoising steps and iterations, allowing for the creation of ensembled depth maps that offer a more detailed and accurate representation of depth. It supports various configurations, including model selection and inversion of depth map colors, to cater to different use cases and preferences.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image for which the depth map is to be estimated. This is the primary input over which the depth estimation process is executed.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: A seed value for random number generation, ensuring reproducibility of the depth estimation process.

inputs.name: denoise_steps
inputs.description: Specifies the number of steps per depth map to enhance the accuracy of the depth estimation. Increasing this value results in more detailed depth maps at the cost of longer processing times.

inputs.name: n_repeat
inputs.description: Determines the amount of iterations to be ensembled into a single depth map, affecting the overall depth accuracy and detail.

inputs.name: regularizer_strength
inputs.description: Adjusts the strength of the regularization during the ensembling process, typically left at default settings.

inputs.name: reduction_method
inputs.description: Specifies the method used for reducing the ensemble of depth maps into a single map, impacting the final depth representation.

inputs.name: max_iter
inputs.description: Sets the maximum number of iterations for the ensembling process, controlling the depth map's refinement level.

inputs.name: tol
inputs.description: Defines the tolerance level for the ensembling process, determining when the process should terminate based on convergence criteria.

inputs.name: invert
inputs.description: Inverts the default depth map colors from black representing the front to the opposite, catering to specific application requirements.

inputs.name: keep_model_loaded
inputs.description: Indicates whether the Marigold model should remain loaded between invocations, improving performance at the expense of memory usage.

inputs.name: n_repeat_batch_size
inputs.description: Controls how many of the n_repeat iterations are processed in a batch, optimizing VRAM usage and processing speed based on available resources.

inputs.name: use_fp16
inputs.description: Determines whether to use fp16 precision for processing, affecting VRAM usage and potentially the depth map's quality.

inputs.name: scheduler
inputs.description: Chooses the scheduler for the denoising steps, affecting the depth map's final quality and characteristics.

inputs.name: normalize
inputs.description: Specifies whether the depth map should be normalized, affecting the range and distribution of depth values.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: Selects between the Marigold model and its LCM version for depth estimation, influencing the depth map's accuracy and appearance.

outputs.name: ensembled_image
outputs.description: The resulting depth map, ensembled from multiple iterations and denoising steps, providing a detailed representation of depth in the image.

MarigoldDepthEstimationVideo.description: The MarigoldDepthEstimationVideo node is designed for depth estimation in videos using a diffusion-based approach. It incorporates optical flow for enhanced frame consistency, aiming to produce more accurate and coherent depth maps across video sequences. This node is an experimental version that extends the capabilities of monocular depth estimation to video content, leveraging advanced techniques for improved depth perception and visual quality.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: A single image from a video sequence to be processed for depth estimation. The node uses this image along with optical flow to generate a depth map, ensuring consistency between frames.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: unknown

inputs.name: first_frame_denoise_steps
inputs.description: The number of denoising steps to apply specifically for the first frame in a video sequence, affecting the initial depth map's accuracy and processing time.

inputs.name: first_frame_n_repeat
inputs.description: Specifies the number of iterations to ensemble for the first frame's depth map, aiming to enhance the depth estimation accuracy for the video's starting point.

inputs.name: n_repeat_batch_size
inputs.description: Determines how many of the n_repeats are processed as a batch, allowing for adjustments based on available VRAM for potentially faster processing.

inputs.name: invert
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether to invert the depth map's color scheme, where the default setting has black representing the foreground.

inputs.name: keep_model_loaded
inputs.description: Indicates whether the Marigold model should remain loaded between frames to optimize processing time for video sequences.

inputs.name: scheduler
inputs.description: unknown

inputs.name: normalize
inputs.description: A boolean flag that specifies whether the output depth maps should be normalized, affecting the visual representation of depth.

inputs.name: denoise_steps
inputs.description: unknown

inputs.name: flow_warping
inputs.description: Enables the use of optical flow for warping depth maps between frames, enhancing the consistency and accuracy of depth estimation across the video.

inputs.name: flow_depth_mix
inputs.description: Determines the blending ratio between the depth map generated from the current frame and the warped depth map from the previous frame, affecting the smoothness and consistency of the video output.

inputs.name: noise_ratio
inputs.description: Specifies the ratio of noise to signal in the depth estimation process, influencing the model's behavior and the quality of the depth maps.

inputs.name: dtype
inputs.description: Defines the data type used during processing, such as fp16 or fp32, impacting VRAM usage and potentially the quality of the depth estimation.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: Specifies the Marigold model to be used for depth estimation, allowing selection between the standard and LCM versions of Marigold. This choice influences the depth estimation process and the quality of the output depth maps.

outputs.name: ensembled_image
outputs.description: The output ensembled depth map image, representing the combined result of depth estimation across multiple frames for enhanced accuracy and consistency.

MarigoldDepthEstimation_v2.description: The MarigoldDepthEstimation_v2 node is designed for diffusion-based monocular depth estimation, leveraging the Marigold model to generate depth maps from single images. This node focuses on enhancing the accuracy of depth predictions through iterative processing and ensemble techniques, offering customizable parameters for fine-tuning the depth estimation process.

inputs.name: marigold_model
inputs.description: Selects the specific Marigold model to be used for depth estimation, affecting the depth map's accuracy and appearance.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image for which the depth map is to be estimated, serving as the basis for the depth estimation process.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: Sets the seed for random number generation, ensuring reproducibility of the depth estimation.

inputs.name: denoise_steps
inputs.description: Specifies the number of steps per depth map, allowing users to balance between accuracy and processing time.

inputs.name: ensemble_size
inputs.description: Determines the number of depth maps to be ensembled into a single output, enhancing the depth estimation's accuracy.

inputs.name: processing_resolution
inputs.description: Defines the resolution at which the depth estimation process is performed, impacting the detail and quality of the depth map.

inputs.name: scheduler
inputs.description: Chooses the scheduler for the depth estimation process, influencing the final depth map's characteristics.

inputs.name: use_taesd_vae
inputs.description: Determines whether to use the TAESD VAE model for depth estimation, potentially improving the quality of the depth map.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: Produces a depth map image, representing the estimated depth of the scene from a single input image.

MarigoldDepthEstimation_v2_video.description: The MarigoldDepthEstimation_v2_video node is designed for depth estimation in videos using a diffusion-based approach. It incorporates optical flow to ensure consistency between video frames, enhancing the depth estimation process by leveraging temporal information. This node is an experimental version that aims to provide more accurate and visually coherent depth maps for video sequences.

inputs.name: marigold_model
inputs.description: Specifies the Marigold model to be used for depth estimation. This selection influences the accuracy and quality of the depth maps generated.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: A collection of images or a single image to be processed for depth estimation. The images serve as input for generating depth maps.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: A seed value for random number generation, ensuring reproducibility of the depth estimation results.

inputs.name: denoise_steps
inputs.description: The number of denoising steps to apply, affecting the clarity and detail of the generated depth maps.

inputs.name: processing_resolution
inputs.description: The resolution at which the images are processed, impacting the balance between processing speed and depth map quality.

inputs.name: scheduler
inputs.description: The scheduler type used for controlling the diffusion process, affecting the characteristics of the depth estimation.

inputs.name: blend_factor
inputs.description: Determines the blending ratio of the current frame with the previous frame's latent representation, enhancing temporal consistency in videos.

inputs.name: use_taesd_vae
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether to use the TAESD VAE model for improved depth estimation accuracy.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image after depth estimation, representing the depth map of the input image(s).

MarigoldModelLoader.description: This node is designed to load and initialize Marigold models for further processing. It prepares the model environment, ensuring that the necessary configurations and resources are in place for efficient execution of depth estimation or other related tasks.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: Specifies the model to be loaded. This parameter determines the type of Marigold model that will be initialized for use in subsequent processing steps, affecting the capabilities and performance of the node.

outputs.name: marigold_model
outputs.description: The loaded Marigold model, encapsulated within a dictionary that includes the pipeline and model type. This output is ready for use in depth estimation or other image processing tasks.

RemapDepth.description: The RemapDepth node is designed to adjust the depth values of an image within a specified range and optionally clamp these values for normalization. It operates by scaling the depth values linearly between a minimum and maximum value, enhancing the depth perception or preparing the image for further processing steps.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image whose depth values are to be remapped. This image is the primary subject of the node's operation, with its depth values being adjusted according to the other parameters.

inputs.name: min
inputs.description: The minimum value in the target range for depth remapping. It sets the lower bound for the depth values in the output image, playing a crucial role in defining the depth scale.

inputs.name: max
inputs.description: The maximum value in the target range for depth remapping. It sets the upper bound for the depth values in the output image, crucial for defining the scale and contrast of depth perception.

inputs.name: clamp
inputs.description: A boolean parameter that determines whether the remapped depth values should be clamped to the range [0.0, 1.0]. Clamping ensures that all depth values stay within a normalized range, enhancing compatibility with subsequent processing or visualization steps.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image with depth values remapped and optionally clamped. This image is ready for further processing or visualization, with enhanced depth perception or normalization.

SaveImageOpenEXR.description: This node specializes in saving images in the OpenEXR format, catering to the need for high dynamic range (HDR) imaging. It ensures that images are saved with enhanced luminance levels, accommodating a broader spectrum of light and color details. The node is designed to adapt to the system's available resources, ensuring that images are preserved in the desired format with high fidelity.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The images to be saved, expected to be in a NumPy array format. This input is crucial as it directly represents the data that will be processed and saved in the EXR format.

inputs.name: filename_prefix
inputs.description: A prefix for the filename under which the image will be saved. This allows for customizable naming of output files, facilitating better organization and retrieval of saved images.

outputs.name: file_url
outputs.description: The URL or path to the saved EXR file. This output provides a direct link to the saved image, enabling easy access and integration into further processing or storage solutions.

EmptyMotionData.description: The EmptyMotionData node is designed to generate a template for motion data with specified frame lengths. It primarily serves the purpose of creating a base structure for motion data that can be further processed or manipulated, providing a standardized format for initializing motion-related tasks within the MotionDiff framework.

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: Specifies the number of frames for the generated motion data. This parameter directly influences the shape of the motion tensor, thereby determining the temporal length of the motion data.

outputs.name: motion_data
outputs.description: Outputs a dictionary containing tensors for motion, motion mask, and motion length, establishing a foundational structure for motion data with zeroed motion values and appropriate masking.

ExportSMPLTo3DSoftware.description: This node is designed to facilitate the export of SMPL models to 3D software, streamlining the process of integrating these models into various 3D CGI workflows. It abstracts the complexities involved in the conversion and export process, making it easier for users to utilize SMPL models within their preferred 3D environments.

inputs.name: smpl
inputs.description: The smpl input specifies the SMPL models to be exported. This input is crucial for the node's operation, directly influencing its ability to process and prepare the models for export to 3D software, impacting the overall workflow and output quality.

inputs.name: foldername_prefix
inputs.description: The foldername_prefix input allows users to specify a prefix for the output folder where the exported models will be saved, providing a way to organize the exported files.

inputs.name: format
inputs.description: The format input determines the file format for the exported models, such as 'glb', allowing users to choose a format that is compatible with their 3D software environments.

Export_SMPLMultipleSubjects_To_3DSoftwar.description: This node is designed to facilitate the export of 3D models of multiple subjects in the SMPL format to various 3D software environments. It aims to streamline the process of integrating complex, multi-subject 3D models into professional 3D CGI applications, enhancing the workflow for 3D animators and visual effects artists.

inputs.name: smpl_multi_subjects
inputs.description: The dataset containing 3D models of multiple subjects in SMPL format, essential for exporting to 3D software. It plays a critical role in the node's operation by providing the necessary data for processing and conversion.

inputs.name: foldername_prefix
inputs.description: A prefix for the folder name where the exported files will be saved, allowing for organized storage and easy retrieval.

inputs.name: format
inputs.description: The format in which the 3D models will be exported, such as 'obj', 'fbx', or 'glb', determining the compatibility with various 3D software.

Human4D_Img2SMPL.description: The Human4D_Img2SMPL node is designed to transform 2D human images into 3D representations using the SMPL model. It leverages deep learning models to detect human figures in images, estimate their poses, and generate corresponding 3D mesh models, enabling advanced motion analysis and visualization.

inputs.name: human4d_model
inputs.description: The human4D model encapsulates the necessary configurations and models for detecting humans in images and generating their 3D SMPL representations. It plays a crucial role in the node's ability to accurately process and transform 2D images into 3D models.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image tensor containing human figures to be transformed into 3D SMPL models. This tensor is critical for the node to perform human detection and pose estimation.

inputs.name: det_confidence_thresh
inputs.description: The confidence threshold for human detection. This parameter helps in filtering out detections with low confidence, ensuring that only high-confidence human figures are processed for 3D modeling.

inputs.name: det_iou_thresh
inputs.description: The Intersection Over Union (IOU) threshold for human detection. It is used to manage the overlap between detected bounding boxes, improving the precision of human detection.

inputs.name: det_batch_size
inputs.description: The batch size for processing detections. This parameter affects the throughput and efficiency of the human detection process, balancing between speed and memory usage.

inputs.name: hmr_batch_size
inputs.description: The batch size for the HMR (Human Mesh Recovery) process. It determines how many human figures are processed simultaneously for 3D modeling, impacting the node's performance and resource utilization.

inputs.name: opt_scorehmr_refiner
inputs.description: An optional parameter for refining the scores from the HMR process. If provided, it enhances the accuracy of the 3D SMPL models generated by the node.

outputs.name: smpl_multiple_subjects
outputs.description: The output is a comprehensive 3D representation of multiple human subjects derived from 2D images, including mesh models, pose information, and additional metadata for advanced motion analysis.

Humans4DLoader.description: The Humans4DLoader node is designed to load and prepare 4D human models for further processing or analysis. It handles the downloading of necessary models and configurations, setting up the models for execution, and ensuring they are ready for use in tasks such as motion analysis or 3D reconstruction.

inputs.name: detector
inputs.description: Specifies the detector model to be used for identifying humans in images. The choice of detector can influence the accuracy and performance of human detection.

inputs.name: fp16
inputs.description: Indicates whether to use half-precision floating-point format (FP16) for the model, potentially improving performance on compatible hardware.

outputs.name: human4d_model
outputs.description: The output is a structured object containing the loaded 4D human model, its configuration, and the detector, ready for further processing.

mgpt_model_loader.description: This node is responsible for loading and initializing the MotionGPT model with a specified configuration and model weights. It ensures the model is ready for generating or processing motion data by setting up the necessary environment, including downloading the model if not locally available, and preparing it for inference.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: Specifies the model to be loaded and initialized for motion generation or processing. This parameter determines which specific MotionGPT model configuration and weights are used, impacting the quality and type of motion data the node can generate or process.

outputs.name: mgpt_model
outputs.description: The loaded and initialized MotionGPT model, ready for generating or processing motion data.

mgpt_t2m.description: The node transforms textual descriptions into motion data sequences using a MotionGPT model, enabling the generation of motion sequences based on natural language inputs.

inputs.name: mgpt_model
inputs.description: The MotionGPT model used for generating motion sequences from text. It's crucial for interpreting the textual input and producing corresponding motion data.

inputs.name: motion_length
inputs.description: Specifies the desired length of the generated motion sequence. It influences the granularity and extent of the motion details.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: A seed for random number generation, ensuring reproducibility of the motion sequences generated from the same inputs.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The textual description that guides the generation of the motion sequence, serving as the creative input for the motion synthesis.

outputs.name: motion_data
outputs.description: The generated motion data sequence, represented as joint positions over time, derived from the textual description.

MotionCLIPTextEncode.description: The MotionCLIPTextEncode node is designed to encode textual descriptions into a format suitable for motion generation tasks, leveraging a CLIP model and motion data to produce motion conditioning. This process facilitates the creation of motion sequences that are aligned with the given textual descriptions.

inputs.name: md_clip
inputs.description: The md_clip parameter represents a CLIP model tailored for motion data, crucial for interpreting and encoding the textual description in the context of motion.

inputs.name: motion_data
inputs.description: The motion_data parameter contains the motion information necessary for the encoding process, providing the context in which the text is to be interpreted.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The text parameter is the textual description to be encoded, serving as the input for generating motion-aligned sequences.

outputs.name: md_conditioning
outputs.description: The output is motion conditioning data, which is used to guide the generation of motion sequences that correspond to the input text.

MotionDataVisualizer.description: The MotionDataVisualizer node is designed to transform motion data into a visual representation, allowing for the visualization of motion through various parameters such as distance, elevation, and rotation. It supports different visualization styles and outputs the visualized motion as a sequence of tensor frames.

inputs.name: motion_data
inputs.description: The motion data to be visualized, which can include joints information or require conversion from motion format to joints. This input is crucial as it directly influences the visual output by determining the motion's structure and dynamics to be visualized.

inputs.name: visualization
inputs.description: Specifies the style of visualization to be applied to the motion data, affecting the visual appearance and interpretability of the output.

inputs.name: distance
inputs.description: The distance parameter controls the camera distance from the motion in the visualization, impacting the scale and perspective of the visualized motion.

inputs.name: elevation
inputs.description: The elevation parameter adjusts the camera elevation angle for the visualization, influencing the vertical angle and overall view of the motion.

inputs.name: rotation
inputs.description: The rotation parameter sets the camera rotation angle around the motion in the visualization, affecting the orientation and angle of the visualized motion.

inputs.name: poselinewidth
inputs.description: Defines the line width for the pose representation in the visualization, impacting the clarity and visual prominence of the motion's pose.

inputs.name: opt_title
inputs.description: An optional title for the visualization, which can enhance the context or provide additional information for the visualized motion.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The visualized motion output as an image.

MotionDiffLoader.description: The MotionDiffLoader node is designed to load and initialize the Motion Diffusion Model (MDM) and its associated CLIP wrapper based on a specified model dataset. This node plays a crucial role in preparing the motion generation models for subsequent processing or inference tasks, ensuring they are correctly configured with the necessary dataset information.

inputs.name: model_dataset
inputs.description: Specifies the dataset model to be loaded. This selection determines the configuration of the Motion Diffusion Model and its CLIP wrapper, impacting the behavior and performance of motion generation.

outputs.name: md_model
outputs.description: Returns a wrapped instance of the Motion Diffusion Model, ready for motion generation tasks.

outputs.name: md_clip
outputs.description: Returns a CLIP wrapper configured for the loaded Motion Diffusion Model, facilitating text-conditioned motion generation.

MotionDiffSimpleSampler.description: The MotionDiffSimpleSampler node is designed to facilitate the sampling process within a motion diffusion framework, specifically targeting the generation or transformation of motion data. It abstracts the complexities involved in selecting and applying different sampling strategies, such as uniform or loss-aware sampling, to produce or modify motion sequences based on given conditions and inputs.

inputs.name: sampler_name
inputs.description: Specifies the name of the sampling strategy to be used, affecting the choice of algorithm for generating or transforming motion data.

inputs.name: md_model
inputs.description: A wrapper around the motion diffusion model, providing the necessary interface for the sampling process.

inputs.name: md_clip
inputs.description: Represents the clip information required for motion generation or transformation, encapsulating the model and its associated data.

inputs.name: md_cond
inputs.description: The conditions under which the motion data is to be generated or transformed, guiding the sampling process. This includes text and motion data processed by the MotionCLIPTextEncode node.

inputs.name: motion_data
inputs.description: The input motion data that will be transformed or generated anew, depending on the sampling strategy. Includes motion, motion mask, and motion length.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: A seed value to ensure reproducibility of the generated or transformed motion data.

outputs.name: motion_data
outputs.description: The output motion data after sampling, including the generated or transformed motion sequence, motion mask, and motion length.

RenderMultipleSubjectsSMPLMesh.description: This node is designed to render multiple SMPL mesh subjects within a given scene. It leverages 3D mesh rendering techniques to visualize the motion and form of multiple subjects simultaneously, providing a comprehensive view of their spatial interactions and dynamics.

inputs.name: smpl_multi_subjects
inputs.description: This input is essential for rendering as it contains the SMPL models of multiple subjects, including their mesh data and possibly motion information. This dataset enables the node to accurately visualize each subject in the scene.

inputs.name: draw_platform
inputs.description: Specifies whether to draw a platform for the subjects to stand on, enhancing the visualization's realism.

inputs.name: depth_only
inputs.description: Determines whether to render only the depth map of the scene, which can be useful for certain types of visual analysis.

inputs.name: fx_offset
inputs.description: Horizontal offset for the camera's focal point, allowing for adjustments in the rendered scene's perspective.

inputs.name: fy_offset
inputs.description: Vertical offset for the camera's focal point, enabling fine-tuning of the scene's visual perspective.

inputs.name: move_x
inputs.description: Moves the camera along the x-axis, offering control over the scene's composition.

inputs.name: move_y
inputs.description: Moves the camera along the y-axis, allowing for adjustments in the scene's framing.

inputs.name: move_z
inputs.description: Moves the camera along the z-axis, providing the ability to alter the scene's depth.

inputs.name: rotate_x
inputs.description: Rotates the camera around the x-axis, enabling changes in the scene's vertical orientation.

inputs.name: rotate_y
inputs.description: Rotates the camera around the y-axis, allowing for alterations in the scene's horizontal orientation.

inputs.name: rotate_z
inputs.description: Rotates the camera around the z-axis, offering the possibility to adjust the scene's rotational perspective.

inputs.name: background_hex_color
inputs.description: Sets the background color of the scene using a hexadecimal color code, enhancing the visual appeal.

inputs.name: normals
inputs.description: Determines whether to render the normals of the mesh, which can provide additional detail for visual analysis.

inputs.name: remove_background
inputs.description: Specifies whether to remove the background from the rendered scene, focusing the visualization solely on the subjects.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: The output is a visual representation of multiple SMPL models, rendered as meshes within a scene. It provides a detailed view of the subjects' forms and motions.

outputs.name: DEPTH_MAP
outputs.description: The depth map of the rendered scene, offering insights into the spatial relationships and distances between subjects.

RenderSMPLMesh.description: This node is designed to render 3D meshes of human figures based on the SMPL model. It focuses on generating visual representations from SMPL parameters, enabling the visualization of human poses and shapes in a 3D environment.

inputs.name: smpl
inputs.description: The SMPL model parameters required for rendering the 3D mesh. This input is crucial for determining the pose and shape of the human figure to be visualized.

inputs.name: draw_platform
inputs.description: Specifies whether to draw a platform in the rendered image, affecting the visual context of the 3D mesh.

inputs.name: depth_only
inputs.description: Determines if only the depth map should be rendered, omitting the visual representation of the 3D mesh.

inputs.name: yfov
inputs.description: The field of view in the y-axis for the camera, influencing the perspective from which the mesh is rendered.

inputs.name: move_x
inputs.description: Horizontal movement of the camera, allowing for lateral adjustments in the rendering perspective.

inputs.name: move_y
inputs.description: Vertical movement of the camera, enabling adjustments in the vertical positioning of the rendering perspective.

inputs.name: move_z
inputs.description: Depth movement of the camera, affecting the distance between the camera and the 3D mesh.

inputs.name: rotate_x
inputs.description: Rotation of the camera around the x-axis, altering the tilt of the rendered image.

inputs.name: rotate_y
inputs.description: Rotation of the camera around the y-axis, changing the yaw of the rendered perspective.

inputs.name: rotate_z
inputs.description: Rotation of the camera around the z-axis, modifying the roll of the rendering perspective.

inputs.name: background_hex_color
inputs.description: The background color of the rendered image, specified as a hexadecimal color code.

inputs.name: frame_width
inputs.description: The width of the frame for the rendered image, defining the horizontal resolution.

inputs.name: frame_height
inputs.description: The height of the frame for the rendered image, defining the vertical resolution.

inputs.name: normals
inputs.description: Indicates whether normals should be included in the rendering, affecting the visual texture and lighting of the 3D mesh.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: The output is a visual representation (image) of the 3D mesh rendered from the SMPL parameters. This image showcases the human figure in various poses and shapes.

outputs.name: DEPTH_MAP
outputs.description: The depth map of the rendered 3D mesh, providing spatial depth information for each pixel in the image.

Render_OpenPose_From_SMPL_Mesh_Multiple_.description: This node is designed to render OpenPose keypoints from multiple SMPL mesh subjects, facilitating the visualization of human poses and movements in a standardized format. It emphasizes the conversion of 3D mesh data into 2D pose representations, enabling a more intuitive understanding of complex human interactions captured by the SMPL model.

inputs.name: smpl_multi_subjects
inputs.description: Represents multiple SMPL model subjects, serving as the input for generating OpenPose visualizations. This parameter is crucial for processing and rendering the poses of multiple individuals simultaneously.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is an image representation of OpenPose keypoints, providing a visual summary of human poses derived from the input SMPL meshes.

SaveSMPL.description: The SaveSMPL node is designed for saving SMPL model data, including thetas and metadata, to a specified output directory. It supports appending a custom prefix to the filename and saving the data in a structured format for further use or analysis.

inputs.name: smpl
inputs.description: The SMPL model data to be saved, including thetas and metadata, which are crucial for reconstructing the 3D model.

inputs.name: filename_prefix
inputs.description: A prefix for the filename to help organize and identify the saved SMPL model data files easily.

SmplifyMotionData.description: The SmplifyMotionData node is designed to convert motion data into a format compatible with the SMPL model, utilizing an iterative process to refine the representation of human motion. This conversion facilitates the use of motion data in applications requiring 3D human models, such as animation and simulation.

inputs.name: motion_data
inputs.description: The input motion data to be converted. This data is essential for generating a 3D representation of human motion using the SMPL model.

inputs.name: num_smplify_iters
inputs.description: Specifies the number of iterations for the SMPLify algorithm, affecting the accuracy and detail of the motion conversion.

inputs.name: smplify_step_size
inputs.description: Determines the step size for the SMPLify algorithm, influencing the convergence rate and precision of the motion representation.

inputs.name: smpl_model
inputs.description: The specific SMPL model to be used for motion conversion, dictating the gender and body proportions of the generated 3D human model.

outputs.name: smpl
outputs.description: The output includes the path to the SMPL model used, the SMPL model parameters representing the pose of the 3D human model across frames, and metadata related to the conversion process.

SMPLLoader.description: The SMPLLoader node is designed to load and process SMPL model data from specified files, facilitating the integration of SMPL models into motion analysis and synthesis workflows.

inputs.name: smpl
inputs.description: Specifies the file name of the SMPL model to be loaded. This file contains essential data for motion synthesis, including pose parameters.

inputs.name: smpl_model
inputs.description: Determines the specific SMPL model to be used, affecting the interpretation of the loaded SMPL data.

outputs.name: smpl
outputs.description: Outputs a tuple containing the path to the SMPL model, pose parameters (thetas), and metadata, ready for further processing or visualization.

SMPLShapeParameters.description: The SMPLShapeParameters node is designed to adjust the shape parameters of an SMPL model based on various anthropometric measurements. It encapsulates the functionality to modify an SMPL model's dimensions, such as size, thickness, and proportions of body parts, to achieve a desired appearance or match specific physical characteristics.

inputs.name: smpl
inputs.description: The SMPL model to be modified. This parameter is crucial as it serves as the base model whose shape parameters will be adjusted according to the provided measurements.

inputs.name: size
inputs.description: Represents the overall size of the SMPL model, affecting its scale.

inputs.name: thickness
inputs.description: Controls the thickness of the SMPL model, influencing its volume and bulk.

inputs.name: upper_body_height
inputs.description: Adjusts the height of the upper body, altering the torso length.

inputs.name: lower_body_height
inputs.description: Modifies the height of the lower body, affecting the leg length.

inputs.name: muscle_mass
inputs.description: Determines the muscle mass of the SMPL model, impacting its muscular definition.

inputs.name: legs
inputs.description: Adjusts the proportions of the legs, influencing their shape and length.

inputs.name: chest
inputs.description: Modifies the chest size, affecting the breadth and appearance of the torso.

inputs.name: waist_height
inputs.description: Controls the height of the waist, influencing the body's overall proportions.

inputs.name: waist_width
inputs.description: Adjusts the width of the waist, affecting the model's silhouette.

inputs.name: arms
inputs.description: Modifies the length and shape of the arms, influencing their appearance and proportion.

outputs.name: smpl
outputs.description: The modified SMPL model with updated shape parameters reflecting the input measurements.

SpectreFaceReconLoader.description: The SpectreFaceReconLoader node is designed to initialize and load the Spectre model along with a face tracker for facial recognition tasks. It prepares the model for subsequent operations by downloading necessary models and setting configuration parameters, ensuring the system is ready for face tracking and recognition within images or video streams.

inputs.name: fp16
inputs.description: Determines whether the model should be loaded in half-precision (FP16) format, which can reduce memory usage and potentially increase performance on compatible hardware.

outputs.name: spectre_model
outputs.description: Returns a tuple containing the initialized face tracker and Spectre model, ready for facial recognition tasks.

SpectreImg2SMPL.description: The SpectreImg2SMPL node is designed to transform images into 3D models using the Spectre model, focusing on generating SMPL (Skinned Multi-Person Linear) models from input images. It processes images to detect facial landmarks, crops and normalizes the images around the face, and then utilizes these preprocessed images to generate 3D representations, including vertices and camera parameters, suitable for further 3D rendering or analysis.

inputs.name: spectre_model
inputs.description: The spectre_model parameter is a tuple containing the face tracker and the Spectre model itself, essential for detecting facial landmarks and generating 3D models from input images.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image parameter represents the input image to be transformed into a 3D model. It undergoes preprocessing such as cropping around the face before being processed by the Spectre model.

inputs.name: chunk_size
inputs.description: The chunk_size parameter determines the number of images processed in a single batch, optimizing the performance and efficiency of the model's operation.

outputs.name: SMPL_MULTIPLE_SUBJECTS
outputs.description: The SMPL_MULTIPLE_SUBJECTS output contains the 3D vertices of the generated models, essential for constructing the 3D mesh.

outputs.name: CROPPED_FACE_IMAGE
outputs.description: The CROPPED_FACE_IMAGE output includes the preprocessed images that have been cropped and normalized, ready for further processing or visualization.

PortraitMaster.description: The PortraitMaster node is designed to dynamically generate detailed and customizable prompts for portrait creation, utilizing a wide range of parameters to fine-tune both the desired and undesired aspects of the final portrait. It allows for the manipulation of facial features, hair styles, expressions, and photorealism settings to craft comprehensive positive and negative prompts that guide the AI in generating more precise and realistic portraits.
