PreviewLatent.description: The PreviewLatent node provides a mechanism to generate visual previews of latent representations. It leverages a base model and optional parameters to produce images that visually represent the encoded information within a latent space.

inputs.name: latent
inputs.description: The latent representation to be visualized. This is the core input for generating the preview image.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: Returns the same latent input, allowing for potential further processing or analysis.

PreviewLatentAdvanced.description: This node is designed for advanced latent image preview generation, allowing for customization of the base model, preview method, and inclusion of additional metadata. It serves as a foundational component for generating previews of latent images with enhanced flexibility and control over the preview generation process.

inputs.name: latent
inputs.description: The latent representation of an image to be previewed. It is a crucial component for generating the image preview.

inputs.name: base_model
inputs.description: Specifies the base model to use for preview generation, offering options between 'SD15' and 'SDXL' to adjust the preview quality and characteristics.

inputs.name: preview_method
inputs.description: Determines the method used for converting the latent representation to an image preview, with options including 'auto', 'taesd', and 'latent2rgb' for varied preview styles.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: Returns the latent representation of the image, maintaining consistency with the input while potentially incorporating modifications from the preview process.

PreviewLatentXL.description: The PreviewLatentXL node specializes in generating previews of latent representations using the SDXL base model. It enhances the visualization of latent spaces by automatically determining the optimal preview method and incorporating additional information such as prompts and unique identifiers.

inputs.name: latent
inputs.description: The latent representation to be visualized. This is the core input for generating previews.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The modified latent representation, potentially adjusted during the preview generation process.

PromptComposerCustomLists.description: The PromptComposerCustomLists node is designed to integrate custom list selections into a prompt composition, allowing for dynamic and customizable text generation based on user-defined lists and weights.

inputs.name: lens_type
inputs.description: A required parameter representing a custom list for lens types, crucial for tailoring the prompt composition to specific visual perspectives.

inputs.name: lens_type_weight
inputs.description: Specifies the weight for the lens type selection, affecting the emphasis of the lens type in the final prompt composition.

inputs.name: photo_style
inputs.description: A required parameter for selecting a photo style from a custom list, essential for defining the visual style of the prompt.

inputs.name: photo_style_weight
inputs.description: Determines the weight of the photo style selection, influencing its prominence in the composed prompt.

inputs.name: effect
inputs.description: A required parameter for choosing an effect from a custom list, key to adding unique visual effects to the prompt.

inputs.name: effect_weight
inputs.description: Sets the weight for the chosen effect, modifying its impact on the overall prompt.

inputs.name: painting_style
inputs.description: A required parameter for selecting a painting style from a custom list, pivotal for incorporating artistic styles into the prompt.

inputs.name: painting_style_weight
inputs.description: Adjusts the weight of the painting style selection, affecting its influence on the final prompt.

inputs.name: active
inputs.description: A boolean parameter that activates or deactivates the inclusion of the custom list selections in the prompt composition.

inputs.name: text_in_opt
inputs.description: An optional initial text input that can be included at the beginning of the prompt composition, emphasizing the flexibility in starting the prompt with user-defined text.

outputs.name: text_out
outputs.description: The output is a single string that represents the composed prompt, dynamically generated based on the input custom lists and their associated weights.

PromptComposerEffect.description: The PromptComposerEffect node is designed to apply a specified effect with a given weight to an input text, enhancing the prompt composition process by allowing for dynamic customization based on the effect's intensity.

inputs.name: effect
inputs.description: Specifies the effect to be applied to the input text. This parameter determines the nature of the modification.

inputs.name: effect_weight
inputs.description: Defines the intensity of the applied effect, allowing for fine-tuned control over the modification's impact.

inputs.name: active
inputs.description: A boolean parameter that activates or deactivates the effect application, providing a way to enable or disable the effect dynamically.

inputs.name: text_in_opt
inputs.description: An optional input text to which an effect can be applied. It serves as the base text for further modification.

outputs.name: text_out
outputs.description: The output text with the specified effect applied, reflecting the modifications based on the effect's weight and activation status.

PromptComposerGrouping.description: The PromptComposerGrouping node is designed to modify and enhance input text based on specified weights and activity status, primarily focusing on grouping elements within prompts for AI-based applications.

inputs.name: text_in
inputs.description: The primary text input that serves as the base for grouping modifications.

inputs.name: weight
inputs.description: A numerical value that influences the degree of modification applied to the input text, with higher values indicating greater emphasis.

inputs.name: active
inputs.description: A boolean flag that determines whether the grouping modifications should be applied to the input text.

outputs.name: text_out
outputs.description: The modified text output after applying grouping logic, based on the input parameters.

PromptComposerMerge.description: The PromptComposerMerge node is designed to combine two text inputs into a single, concatenated output. This functionality is essential for merging distinct pieces of text to create a cohesive prompt, facilitating the generation of more complex and nuanced AI-generated content.

inputs.name: text_a
inputs.description: The first text input to be merged. It plays a crucial role in forming the beginning part of the merged output.

inputs.name: text_b
inputs.description: The second text input to be merged. It is concatenated to the first input, forming the latter part of the merged output.

outputs.name: text_out
outputs.description: The concatenated result of the two input texts, providing a merged text output for further processing or use.

PromptComposerStyler.description: The PromptComposerStyler node is designed to incorporate stylistic elements into text prompts based on specified styles and their associated weights. It enables the dynamic adjustment of text presentation by applying stylistic modifications, thereby enhancing the expressiveness and specificity of the generated prompts.

inputs.name: style
inputs.description: Specifies the style to be applied to the text. This parameter determines the aesthetic or thematic direction of the styling.

inputs.name: style_weight
inputs.description: Determines the intensity or degree of the applied style, allowing for nuanced control over the stylistic effect.

inputs.name: active
inputs.description: A boolean parameter that activates or deactivates the styling function. When false, the styling is not applied.

inputs.name: text_in_opt
inputs.description: An optional text input that, if provided, is included in the styled prompt. It serves as the base text to which the style is applied.

outputs.name: text_out
outputs.description: The output text with the specified style applied, reflecting the combined effect of the input text and the stylistic adjustments.

promptComposerTextMultiple.description: The `promptComposerTextMultiple` node is designed to compose a text prompt by combining multiple text inputs, each with an associated weight. This node allows for the dynamic creation of prompts by adjusting the significance of each text input through weights, enabling a flexible and weighted composition of text elements for various applications.

inputs.name: text_i
inputs.description: A text input to be included in the prompt composition. The index 'i' can range from 1 to 10, allowing for up to ten different text inputs.

inputs.name: weight_i
inputs.description: The weight associated with the corresponding text input, determining its significance in the composed prompt. The index 'i' matches that of 'text_i', allowing for individual weighting of up to ten text inputs.

inputs.name: active
inputs.description: A boolean input that activates or deactivates the composition of the prompt. When false, the node may ignore the text inputs and weights, resulting in an empty or default prompt.

inputs.name: text_in_opt
inputs.description: An optional initial text input that can be included in the prompt composition.

outputs.name: text_out
outputs.description: The composed text prompt, resulting from the combination and weighting of the provided text inputs.

PromptComposerTextSingle.description: The PromptComposerTextSingle node is designed for composing single text prompts with optional additional text and weight adjustments. It allows for the dynamic creation of prompts based on input text, optional text, and their respective weights, facilitating customized prompt generation for various applications.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The primary text input for the prompt. This text is the main focus of the prompt composition.

inputs.name: weight
inputs.description: A weight applied to the primary text to adjust its influence or importance in the final prompt composition.

inputs.name: active
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether the prompt composition should be active. If false, the composition may be bypassed or altered.

inputs.name: text_in_opt
inputs.description: An optional text input that, if provided, is prepended to the main text to form the prompt. It allows for the inclusion of additional context or information.

outputs.name: text_out
outputs.description: The output text resulting from the composition of the input texts and their weights, formatted as a single string.

ImageRGBA2RGB.description: The ImageRGBA2RGB node is designed to convert images from RGBA (Red, Green, Blue, Alpha) format to RGB format. This conversion process involves removing the alpha channel from the image, effectively transforming images with transparency information into standard RGB images without transparency.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The 'image' parameter represents the input image in RGBA format that needs to be converted to RGB. This parameter is crucial for the node's operation as it directly influences the conversion process and the resulting RGB image.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The 'image' output parameter represents the converted image in RGB format, after the alpha channel from the original RGBA image has been removed.

ReActorBuildFaceModel.description: This node is designed to construct a face model from a provided image, utilizing face detection and analysis to identify and extract facial features. It aims to create a detailed face model that can be used for various face manipulation tasks within the ReActor framework.

inputs.name: save_mode
inputs.description: Indicates whether the face model should be saved after creation, affecting the workflow of model handling and storage.

inputs.name: send_only
inputs.description: This parameter determines if only the face model's name should be sent back, without the actual model data, to optimize data transfer.

inputs.name: face_model_name
inputs.description: The name under which the face model will be saved. This parameter is essential for identifying and retrieving the model in subsequent operations.

inputs.name: compute_method
inputs.description: Defines the method used for computing the face model, allowing for flexibility in the face detection and analysis process.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: A batch of images from which to build face models, enabling the processing of multiple images in a single operation.

inputs.name: face_models
inputs.description: A collection of existing face models to be processed or analyzed further, providing a way to handle multiple models efficiently.

outputs.name: face_model
outputs.description: The constructed face model or an error message if the process fails.

ReActorFaceBoost.description: The ReActorFaceBoost node is designed to enhance the quality of facial images through advanced restoration techniques. It leverages deep learning models to upscale, denoise, and improve the overall visual fidelity of faces in images, making it suitable for applications requiring high-quality facial visuals.

inputs.name: enabled
inputs.description: Activates or deactivates the face restoration process, allowing users to control when face enhancement is applied.

inputs.name: boost_model
inputs.description: Specifies the deep learning model used for face restoration, affecting the quality and style of the output. Different models can be chosen based on desired resolution and restoration features.

inputs.name: interpolation
inputs.description: Determines the method used for resizing images during the restoration process, impacting the smoothness and clarity of the upscaled face.

inputs.name: visibility
inputs.description: Controls the blend between the original and restored face, allowing for fine-tuning of the restoration effect to achieve a natural-looking result.

inputs.name: codeformer_weight
inputs.description: Adjusts the influence of the CodeFormer model in the restoration process, allowing for customization of the restoration effect based on the model's weight.

inputs.name: restore_with_main_after
inputs.description: Determines whether additional restoration steps should be applied after the main restoration process, enabling further enhancement of the facial image.

outputs.name: face_boost
outputs.description: The enhanced facial image, with improvements in clarity, noise reduction, and resolution, as a result of the restoration process.

ReActorFaceSwap.description: The ReActorFaceSwap node specializes in performing fast face swaps within images, leveraging advanced algorithms to seamlessly replace faces in a given image with those from another source. This node is designed to handle the complexities of face swapping, including alignment, scaling, and blending, to produce natural-looking results.

inputs.name: enabled
inputs.description: Indicates if the face swap operation is currently enabled, controlling whether the swapping process should proceed.

inputs.name: input_image
inputs.description: The image that serves as either the source or target for the face swap operation, depending on the context of the swap.

inputs.name: swap_model
inputs.description: Specifies the model used for the face swapping process, determining the algorithm and parameters for the swap.

inputs.name: facedetection
inputs.description: unknown

inputs.name: face_restore_model
inputs.description: unknown

inputs.name: face_restore_visibility
inputs.description: unknown

inputs.name: codeformer_weight
inputs.description: unknown

inputs.name: detect_gender_input
inputs.description: unknown

inputs.name: detect_gender_source
inputs.description: unknown

inputs.name: input_faces_index
inputs.description: unknown

inputs.name: source_faces_index
inputs.description: unknown

inputs.name: console_log_level
inputs.description: unknown

inputs.name: source_image
inputs.description: unknown

inputs.name: face_model
inputs.description: unknown

inputs.name: face_boost
inputs.description: unknown

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The final image after the face swap operation has been completed, showcasing the seamless integration of the swapped face.

outputs.name: face_model
outputs.description: The model used for the face swap, providing details about the algorithm and parameters applied.

ReActorFaceSwapOpt.description: The ReActorFaceSwapOpt node offers an enhanced face swapping functionality with additional options for customization. It leverages advanced techniques to swap faces in images, providing users with the ability to fine-tune the process for improved results.

inputs.name: enabled
inputs.description: Indicates if the face swapping functionality is currently enabled, controlling whether the operation should proceed.

inputs.name: input_image
inputs.description: The image that will undergo the face swapping process, serving as the canvas for the operation.

inputs.name: swap_model
inputs.description: Specifies the model used for the face swapping process, affecting the accuracy and quality of the swap.

inputs.name: facedetection
inputs.description: Defines the method or model used for detecting faces within the images, crucial for identifying target faces for swapping.

inputs.name: face_restore_model
inputs.description: The model used for restoring or enhancing the quality of faces post-swap, contributing to more realistic outcomes.

inputs.name: face_restore_visibility
inputs.description: Controls the visibility level of the restored faces, allowing for fine-tuning of the final appearance.

inputs.name: codeformer_weight
inputs.description: Determines the weight of the CodeFormer model in the face restoration process, influencing the balance between original and enhanced features.

inputs.name: source_image
inputs.description: The source image providing the face to be swapped into the target image, key to the face swapping operation.

inputs.name: face_model
inputs.description: Specifies the face model used for the swapping process, impacting the swap's accuracy and compatibility with different face types.

inputs.name: options
inputs.description: A collection of additional options that can be configured to customize the face swapping process.

inputs.name: face_boost
inputs.description: Indicates whether an additional face enhancement feature is enabled, aiming to improve the quality of the swapped face.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The final image after the face swapping operation, showcasing the swapped and potentially enhanced face.

outputs.name: face_model
outputs.description: The face model used during the swapping process, potentially including modifications or enhancements applied.

ReActorImageDublicator.description: The ReActorImageDublicator node is designed to create duplicates of images, potentially in a list format, as part of the ReActor suite. This functionality is essential for operations that require multiple instances of the same image for processing or analysis, enhancing the workflow within image manipulation and augmentation tasks.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: Specifies the original image to be duplicated.

inputs.name: count
inputs.description: Determines the number of duplicates to be created from the original image.

outputs.name: IMAGES
outputs.description: Returns a list of duplicated images based on the specified count.

ReActorLoadFaceModel.description: The ReActorLoadFaceModel node is designed for loading face models into the ReActor system. It facilitates the retrieval and application of pre-trained face models, enabling the enhancement or modification of facial features in images.

inputs.name: face_model
inputs.description: Specifies the name of the face model to be loaded. This parameter is crucial for identifying and retrieving the correct model from a predefined set of available models, impacting the accuracy and effectiveness of face-related operations.

outputs.name: face_model
outputs.description: Returns the loaded face model, which can be utilized for further face manipulation tasks within the ReActor system.

ReActorMakeFaceModelBatch.description: The `ReActorMakeFaceModelBatch` node is designed for batch processing of face models within the ReActor framework. It facilitates the creation or manipulation of multiple face models simultaneously, streamlining workflows that require handling several face models, such as in batch face analysis, swapping, or restoration scenarios.

inputs.name: face_model1
inputs.description: The primary face model required for processing. It serves as the initial input for batch operations. Its presence is crucial as it sets the baseline for the batch process, influencing the execution by determining the starting point of the batch operation.

inputs.name: face_model2
inputs.description: An optional additional face model for processing, allowing for more complex or varied batch operations. Including this model can diversify the batch process, affecting the node's execution by introducing variability in the models being processed.

inputs.name: face_model3
inputs.description: An optional additional face model for processing, enabling the inclusion of multiple models in a single batch operation. This increases the complexity of the batch, potentially affecting the execution by requiring the node to handle a wider range of model characteristics.

inputs.name: face_model4
inputs.description: An optional additional face model for processing, further expanding the capacity for batch operations with multiple models. This expansion can influence the node's execution by increasing the volume of data processed, impacting performance and outcomes.

inputs.name: face_model5
inputs.description: An optional additional face model for processing, increasing the flexibility and scope of batch operations. Its inclusion can affect the node's execution by broadening the range of possible operations, allowing for more tailored batch processing.

inputs.name: face_model6
inputs.description: An optional additional face model for processing, enhancing the ability to handle a larger number of models in batch. This can significantly affect the node's execution by scaling the processing requirements and potentially the complexity of the batch operation.

inputs.name: face_model7
inputs.description: An optional additional face model for processing, allowing for an extended range of models to be included in batch operations. This can alter the node's execution by introducing more diversity in the models processed, which may require different handling or processing strategies.

inputs.name: face_model8
inputs.description: An optional additional face model for processing, enabling a broader inclusion of models for batch processing. This broadens the operational scope of the node, affecting its execution by potentially increasing the variety of processing needed for each model.

inputs.name: face_model9
inputs.description: An optional additional face model for processing, facilitating the inclusion of a wide array of models in a single batch. This inclusion can complicate the node's execution by adding more variables into the batch process, affecting how the batch is managed and executed.

inputs.name: face_model10
inputs.description: An optional additional face model for processing, maximizing the capacity for including numerous models in batch operations. This maximization affects the node's execution by pushing the limits of what the node can process in a single batch, impacting both performance and the complexity of the operation.

outputs.name: FACE_MODELS
outputs.description: The output is a collection of face models processed in the batch, ready for further use or analysis in various scenarios.

ReActorMaskHelper.description: The ReActorMaskHelper node is designed to assist in the process of masking within the ReActor framework. It likely involves operations such as combining, dilating, and possibly refining masks to be used in face swapping or restoration tasks, leveraging specific detection hints and mask manipulation techniques to optimize the masking process for better results.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The 'image' parameter is the primary input for mask-related operations, serving as the base for detection, manipulation, and transformation processes.

inputs.name: swapped_image
inputs.description: This parameter represents the image resulting from a face swap operation, which may require further masking or adjustments.

inputs.name: bbox_model_name
inputs.description: Specifies the name of the model used for bounding box detection, influencing the initial step of mask generation.

inputs.name: bbox_threshold
inputs.description: The threshold value for bounding box detection, determining the sensitivity of the model in identifying potential areas of interest.

inputs.name: bbox_dilation
inputs.description: Indicates the dilation factor applied to bounding boxes, potentially expanding the area considered for mask application.

inputs.name: bbox_crop_factor
inputs.description: Defines how much to crop around the detected bounding box, affecting the final mask's coverage area.

inputs.name: bbox_drop_size
inputs.description: The minimum size for bounding boxes to be considered, filtering out detections that are too small.

inputs.name: sam_model_name
inputs.description: The name of the model used for SAM (Semantic Attention Mask) prediction, crucial for refining mask details.

inputs.name: sam_dilation
inputs.description: Dilation factor specifically for SAM predictions, adjusting the mask's boundary for better fit or coverage.

inputs.name: sam_threshold
inputs.description: Threshold for SAM predictions, determining which masks are included based on confidence scores.

inputs.name: bbox_expansion
inputs.description: Specifies how much to expand the bounding box beyond its detected borders, affecting the area covered by the mask.

inputs.name: mask_hint_threshold
inputs.description: Threshold for generating mask hints, used in processes that require pre-identification of mask areas.

inputs.name: mask_hint_use_negative
inputs.description: Indicates whether to use negative hints (areas not to mask) in the mask generation process.

inputs.name: morphology_operation
inputs.description: Specifies the type of morphological operation (e.g., dilate, erode) to apply to the mask, affecting its shape and boundaries.

inputs.name: morphology_distance
inputs.description: The distance parameter for the morphological operation, determining the extent of the transformation.

inputs.name: blur_radius
inputs.description: Radius for blurring the mask, used to soften edges or blend the mask more seamlessly with the image.

inputs.name: sigma_factor
inputs.description: Factor for calculating the sigma value in Gaussian blur, affecting the smoothness of the mask's edges.

inputs.name: mask_optional
inputs.description: An optional mask input that can be used for additional mask operations or adjustments.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: The processed image with applied mask modifications, ready for further use or display.

outputs.name: MASK
outputs.description: The final mask generated or modified by the node, suitable for masking or compositing operations.

outputs.name: MASK_PREVIEW
outputs.description: A preview of the mask, typically used for visualization or debugging purposes.

outputs.name: SWAPPED_FACE
outputs.description: The image resulting from a face swap operation, potentially including mask adjustments for improved integration.

ReActorOptions.description: The ReActorOptions node provides a mechanism for configuring various options related to face swapping operations within the ReActor framework. It allows for the customization of face detection, gender detection, and logging levels to tailor the face swapping process to specific needs.

inputs.name: input_faces_order
inputs.description: Specifies the order in which input faces are processed, offering several strategies such as left-right, top-bottom, or based on size. This affects the selection and prioritization of faces for operations.

inputs.name: input_faces_index
inputs.description: Determines the index of the face to be processed in the input image, enabling targeted operations on specific faces.

inputs.name: detect_gender_input
inputs.description: Enables gender detection for the input faces, allowing for gender-specific processing or filtering.

inputs.name: source_faces_order
inputs.description: Defines the order for processing source faces, similar to input_faces_order, but applied to the source images.

inputs.name: source_faces_index
inputs.description: Specifies the index of the face in the source image to be used, facilitating precise control over the source face selection.

inputs.name: detect_gender_source
inputs.description: Activates gender detection for source faces, which can be used to apply gender-specific adjustments or selections.

inputs.name: console_log_level
inputs.description: Sets the verbosity level of console logging, allowing users to control the amount of log output generated during operations.

outputs.name: options
outputs.description: Outputs the configured options for face swapping operations, encapsulating settings like face and gender detection preferences.

ReActorRestoreFace.description: The ReActorRestoreFace node is designed for restoring faces in images using specified face restoration models. It adjusts the visibility of the restored face based on a given parameter, blending it with the original face to achieve a natural restoration effect.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image to be processed for face restoration. It serves as the base for detecting faces and applying restoration models.

inputs.name: facedetection
inputs.description: The face detection model used to identify faces within the input image, crucial for targeted restoration.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: Specifies the model to be used for face restoration, allowing for different restoration techniques to be applied.

inputs.name: visibility
inputs.description: Controls the blend level between the original and restored faces, determining the visibility of the restoration effect.

inputs.name: codeformer_weight
inputs.description: A weight parameter specific to the CodeFormer model, influencing the restoration outcome.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The result of the face restoration process, including the restored face image.

ReActorSaveFaceModel.description: This node is designed to save a face model after processing an image or a set of images. It involves analyzing faces within the provided images, selecting a specific face based on an index, and saving the analyzed face model to a specified location. The node supports operations such as building a face model from an image, selecting a face from the model, and saving the selected face model for future use.

inputs.name: save_mode
inputs.description: Indicates whether the face model should be saved. This affects the node's operation by either proceeding with saving the model or skipping this step.

inputs.name: face_model_name
inputs.description: The name under which the face model will be saved. This name is used to create the file name for the saved model.

inputs.name: select_face_index
inputs.description: The index of the face to select from the analyzed faces in the image. This allows for specific face selection within a group of detected faces.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image from which the face model will be built. This is optional if a pre-analyzed face model is provided.

inputs.name: face_model
inputs.description: A pre-analyzed face model that can be saved directly without further analysis. This is optional if an image is provided for analysis.

SALVTON_Apply.description: The SALVTON_Apply node is designed for applying the SAL-VTON (Virtual Try-On) process, enabling the overlay of a garment onto a person's image with the assistance of a garment mask. This node leverages deep learning models to achieve realistic try-on effects by considering the shape and fit of the garment relative to the person's body.

inputs.name: garment
inputs.description: The garment image to be overlaid onto the person's image. It plays a crucial role in the virtual try-on process by providing the specific item of clothing to be fitted.

inputs.name: person
inputs.description: The person's image onto which the garment will be applied. This image serves as the base for the virtual try-on, determining how the garment will be positioned and fitted.

inputs.name: garment_mask
inputs.description: A mask image for the garment, used to accurately overlay the garment onto the person's image by defining the garment's boundaries.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The resulting image after applying the virtual try-on process, showcasing the person with the garment realistically fitted onto them.

SV_random.description: The RandomImageFromDir node is designed to select a random image from a specified directory. This functionality is particularly useful for applications requiring variability and unpredictability in the selection of images, such as in data augmentation processes or when simulating diverse scenarios within a given context.

inputs.name: folder_path
inputs.description: Specifies the path to the directory from which a random image will be selected. This parameter is crucial for determining the pool of available images for random selection.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: Returns a randomly selected image from the specified directory. This output is essential for introducing variability and randomness in the selection of images for further processing or display.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: Provides a mask associated with the randomly selected image, if applicable, to facilitate further image processing tasks.

LCMScheduler.description: The LCMScheduler node is designed to compute and adjust the sigma values for a given model based on the specified number of steps and denoise factor. It aims to facilitate the customization of the sampling process in generative models by providing a tailored set of sigma values that can be used to control the level of noise introduced during the generation process.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The 'model' parameter specifies the generative model for which the sigma values are to be calculated. It plays a crucial role in determining the specific characteristics of the noise to be introduced during the sampling process.

inputs.name: steps
inputs.description: The 'steps' parameter defines the number of steps to be used in the sampling process. It directly influences the granularity of the noise adjustment, with a higher number of steps allowing for finer control over the generation.

inputs.name: denoise
inputs.description: The 'denoise' parameter allows for adjusting the intensity of the noise introduced during the sampling process. A lower value results in a higher number of total steps, enabling more precise control over the noise characteristics.

outputs.name: sigmas
outputs.description: This output represents the calculated sigma values for the specified model and parameters. These values are crucial for controlling the noise level in the generative process, directly impacting the quality and characteristics of the generated output.

SamplerLCMAlternative.description: This node provides a mechanism to generate samples using an alternative LCM (Least Common Multiple) approach, allowing for customization of the sampling process through parameters such as euler steps, ancestral influence, and noise multiplier. It aims to offer a flexible sampling strategy that can be tailored to specific needs or experimental setups.

inputs.name: euler_steps
inputs.description: Specifies the number of Euler integration steps to be used in the sampling process, influencing the granularity and potentially the quality of the generated samples.

inputs.name: ancestral
inputs.description: Determines the degree of ancestral sampling to be applied, affecting the diversity and characteristics of the samples by adjusting the influence of prior steps.

inputs.name: noise_mult
inputs.description: Adjusts the multiplier for the noise applied during sampling, allowing for control over the variance and exploration within the sample space.

outputs.name: sampler
outputs.description: Produces a sampler configured according to the specified parameters, ready for generating samples.

SamplerLCMCycle.description: The SamplerLCMCycle node is designed to generate a custom sampler based on the LCM (Least Common Multiple) cycle method, incorporating options for Euler steps, LCM steps, sigma tweaking, and ancestral sampling to tailor the sampling process.

inputs.name: euler_steps
inputs.description: Specifies the number of Euler steps to be used in the LCM cycle, affecting the granularity of the sampling process.

inputs.name: lcm_steps
inputs.description: Determines the number of LCM steps in the cycle, influencing the sampling's adherence to the LCM pattern.

inputs.name: tweak_sigmas
inputs.description: A boolean flag that, when enabled, tweaks the sigma values used in the sampling process for potentially enhanced results.

inputs.name: ancestral
inputs.description: Controls the ancestral sampling rate, offering a way to adjust the influence of previous generations on the current sample.

outputs.name: sampler
outputs.description: Produces a custom sampler configured according to the specified LCM cycle parameters.

SamplerLCMDualNoise.description: The SamplerLCMDualNoise node provides a mechanism for generating samples using a dual noise approach within a custom sampling framework. It leverages a combination of weights, normalization steps, and the option to reuse or parallelize noise generation to enhance the sampling process.

inputs.name: weight
inputs.description: Specifies the blending weight between two noise-induced samples, influencing the balance and variation in the sampling output.

inputs.name: normalize_steps
inputs.description: Determines the number of normalization steps to apply, affecting the smoothness and quality of the generated samples.

inputs.name: reuse_lcm_noise
inputs.description: Controls whether the same noise is reused across sampling steps, impacting the diversity and consistency of samples.

inputs.name: parallel
inputs.description: Enables parallel processing of noise generation, potentially speeding up the sampling process.

outputs.name: sampler
outputs.description: Produces a sampler configured with dual noise characteristics for generating samples.

CircularVAEDecode.description: The CircularVAEDecode node is designed to decode latent representations into images, with an added functionality to apply circular tiling effects. This node allows for the generation of seamless images by modifying the VAE model to support circular asymmetry in the tiling process.

inputs.name: samples
inputs.description: The latent representation to be decoded into an image. It is crucial for generating the final output image.

inputs.name: vae
inputs.description: The VAE model used for decoding the latent representation. It is essential for the transformation process.

inputs.name: tiling
inputs.description: Specifies the type of circular tiling to apply, enabling seamless image generation in various orientations.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The decoded image, potentially with circular tiling applied, based on the input latent representation and tiling settings.

MakeCircularVAE.description: This node is designed to modify a VAE (Variational Autoencoder) to support seamless tiling in generated images, either by making a copy of the VAE or modifying it in place. It adjusts the VAE's internal model to enable or disable circular (seamless) tiling along the x-axis, y-axis, or both, based on the specified tiling mode.

inputs.name: vae
inputs.description: The VAE to be modified for seamless tiling. This parameter is crucial as it determines the base model that will undergo modifications to support circular tiling.

inputs.name: tiling
inputs.description: Specifies the mode of tiling to be applied: enabling tiling on both axes, only on the x-axis, only on the y-axis, or disabling it. This affects how the VAE's internal model is adjusted for seamless image generation.

inputs.name: copy_vae
inputs.description: Determines whether to modify the original VAE in place or to make a copy before applying the tiling modifications. This choice impacts whether the original VAE remains unchanged.

outputs.name: vae
outputs.description: The modified VAE with seamless tiling capabilities enabled as specified. This VAE can then be used for generating images with seamless transitions.

OffsetImage.description: The OffsetImage node is designed to shift an image by a specified percentage of its width and height, effectively creating a seamless tiling effect. This operation is useful for generating patterns or textures that can be tiled without visible seams.

inputs.name: pixels
inputs.description: The input image to be offset. This parameter is crucial for determining the base image that will undergo the offset operation.

inputs.name: x_percent
inputs.description: The percentage of the image's width by which the image should be horizontally shifted. This parameter allows for horizontal adjustment of the image's position.

inputs.name: y_percent
inputs.description: The percentage of the image's height by which the image should be vertically shifted. This parameter allows for vertical adjustment of the image's position.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is the modified image after being offset both horizontally and vertically according to the specified percentages.

SeamlessTile.description: The SeamlessTile node enables the modification of a model to support seamless tiling in generated images. It can either modify the model in place or create a modified copy, depending on the user's choice, and supports different tiling modes including enabling tiling on both axes, only on the X-axis, or only on the Y-axis.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model to be modified for seamless tiling. It is the core component that will undergo modifications to support different tiling modes.

inputs.name: tiling
inputs.description: Specifies the tiling mode to apply to the model, which can be enabling tiling on both axes, only on the X-axis, or only on the Y-axis, or disabling it.

inputs.name: copy_model
inputs.description: Determines whether to modify the original model in place or to create and modify a copy, allowing for non-destructive edits.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The modified model with seamless tiling capabilities applied according to the specified tiling mode.

Deflicker (SuperBeasts.AI).description: The Deflicker node is designed to mitigate flickering in image sequences by adjusting the brightness of individual images based on the average brightness of their surrounding context. It incorporates additional image processing techniques such as noise reduction, gradient smoothing, and dithering to enhance the visual quality of the output.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: A sequence of images to be processed for flicker reduction. This input is crucial for determining the context and applying the necessary adjustments to each image.

inputs.name: context_length
inputs.description: Specifies the number of images around the current one to consider for calculating the average brightness, influencing the flicker correction intensity.

inputs.name: brightness_threshold
inputs.description: The minimum difference in brightness between the current image and the context average that triggers adjustment, controlling sensitivity to flicker.

inputs.name: blending_strength
inputs.description: Determines the intensity of blending between the original and processed images, affecting the subtlety of the deflickering effect.

inputs.name: noise_reduction_strength
inputs.description: Controls the degree of noise reduction applied to each image, enhancing clarity.

inputs.name: gradient_smoothing_strength
inputs.description: Adjusts the level of gradient smoothing to reduce visual noise and improve image coherence.

inputs.name: batch_size
inputs.description: The number of images processed at a time, affecting performance and memory usage.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The sequence of images after applying deflickering and additional image enhancements, ready for further processing or display.

HDR Effects (SuperBeasts.AI).description: The HDR Effects node enhances images by applying High Dynamic Range (HDR) effects, improving the visual quality through adjustments in contrast, color saturation, and brightness. It utilizes advanced image processing techniques to simulate HDR photography, making the images appear more vivid and lifelike.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be enhanced with HDR effects. It serves as the base for all subsequent HDR-related adjustments, including contrast, color saturation, and brightness enhancements.

inputs.name: hdr_intensity
inputs.description: Controls the overall intensity of the HDR effect applied to the image, affecting the depth and strength of shadows, highlights, and midtones adjustments.

inputs.name: shadow_intensity
inputs.description: Determines the intensity of shadows in the image, enhancing the depth and detail in darker areas.

inputs.name: highlight_intensity
inputs.description: Adjusts the brightness of highlights, enhancing the detail and visibility in brighter areas of the image.

inputs.name: gamma_intensity
inputs.description: Modifies the gamma levels of the image, affecting the midtone luminance and overall visual contrast.

inputs.name: contrast
inputs.description: Adjusts the contrast level of the image, making the darks darker and the lights lighter to enhance the overall dynamic range.

inputs.name: enhance_color
inputs.description: Increases the color saturation of the image, making the colors more vivid and enhancing the overall visual appeal.

outputs.name: result_img
outputs.description: The enhanced image with applied HDR effects, including improved contrast, color saturation, and brightness.

Image Batch Manager (SuperBeasts.AI).description: The Image Batch Manager node is designed to streamline the process of managing and processing batches of images within a workflow. It focuses on optimizing the handling, transformation, and preparation of large sets of images for further processing or analysis, ensuring efficient batch operations and enhancing overall workflow productivity.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: The 'width' parameter specifies the desired width for the output images after processing. It is essential for ensuring that all images in the batch conform to a uniform size, facilitating consistent analysis or further processing.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: The 'height' parameter defines the desired height for the output images after processing. Similar to 'width', it ensures uniformity in the size of images, which is critical for batch processing and subsequent analyses.

inputs.name: max_images
inputs.description: The 'max_images' parameter limits the number of images to be processed in the batch. This is crucial for controlling the batch size and ensuring efficient processing.

inputs.name: random_order
inputs.description: The 'random_order' parameter determines whether the images should be reordered randomly. This can be used to introduce variability in the processing sequence.

inputs.name: new_manual_order
inputs.description: The 'new_manual_order' parameter allows for the specification of a new order for the processed images. It enables custom sequencing of the input images, affecting the final arrangement and composition of the output.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: This output represents the processed batch of images, ready for further analysis or transformation. It encapsulates the results of the batch management operations, providing a streamlined dataset for subsequent processing stages.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: This output is a string representing the new order of the processed images, providing insight into the arrangement of the batch post-processing.

Make Resized Mask Batch (SuperBeasts.AI).description: This node is designed to process and combine multiple individual masks or mask batches into a single, resized mask batch. It adjusts the size of each mask to match specified dimensions, ensuring uniformity across the batch, and optionally reorders the masks based on a specified sequence. The node facilitates the creation of consistent mask batches for further image processing tasks.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Specifies the target width for the resized masks. This parameter determines the final width of each mask in the batch, ensuring they are resized uniformly.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Specifies the target height for the resized masks. This parameter affects the final height of each mask in the batch, ensuring they are resized to match the specified dimension.

inputs.name: mask1
inputs.description: An optional individual mask to be included in the batch. Masks are resized and optionally reordered to create a uniform batch.

inputs.name: mask2
inputs.description: An optional individual mask to be included in the batch. Masks are resized and optionally reordered to create a uniform batch.

inputs.name: mask3
inputs.description: An optional individual mask to be included in the batch. Masks are resized and optionally reordered to create a uniform batch.

inputs.name: mask4
inputs.description: An optional individual mask to be included in the batch. Masks are resized and optionally reordered to create a uniform batch.

inputs.name: mask5
inputs.description: An optional individual mask to be included in the batch. Masks are resized and optionally reordered to create a uniform batch.

inputs.name: mask6
inputs.description: An optional individual mask to be included in the batch. Masks are resized and optionally reordered to create a uniform batch.

inputs.name: mask7
inputs.description: An optional individual mask to be included in the batch. Masks are resized and optionally reordered to create a uniform batch.

inputs.name: mask8
inputs.description: An optional individual mask to be included in the batch. Masks are resized and optionally reordered to create a uniform batch.

inputs.name: mask9
inputs.description: An optional individual mask to be included in the batch. Masks are resized and optionally reordered to create a uniform batch.

inputs.name: mask10
inputs.description: An optional individual mask to be included in the batch. Masks are resized and optionally reordered to create a uniform batch.

inputs.name: mask11
inputs.description: An optional individual mask to be included in the batch. Masks are resized and optionally reordered to create a uniform batch.

inputs.name: mask12
inputs.description: An optional individual mask to be included in the batch. Masks are resized and optionally reordered to create a uniform batch.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The output is a single tensor representing a batch of resized masks, ready for further processing.

Mask Batch Manager (SuperBeasts.AI).description: The Mask Batch Manager node is designed to aggregate multiple individual masks or batches of masks into a single, processed batch. It adjusts the size and order of the input masks according to specified dimensions and optional ordering, ensuring the output is a unified batch suitable for further processing or analysis.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Specifies the desired width of the output masks, affecting how each input mask is resized or cropped to match this width.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Determines the desired height of the output masks, influencing the resizing and cropping operations to ensure each mask conforms to this height.

inputs.name: new_order
inputs.description: An optional parameter that allows specifying the order in which input masks should be arranged in the output batch, enabling custom sequencing of masks.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The aggregated output of processed masks, combined into a single batch for further use.

Pixel Deflicker (SuperBeasts.AI).description: The Pixel Deflicker node is designed to reduce flickering in sequences of images, enhancing visual consistency across frames. It employs a blend of temporal smoothing and adaptive blending techniques to mitigate rapid brightness variations, resulting in smoother transitions and improved image quality.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: A batch of images to be processed for flicker reduction. This input is crucial for identifying and mitigating flickering effects across the sequence.

inputs.name: window_size
inputs.description: Specifies the size of the window used for temporal smoothing, affecting the extent of flicker reduction across frames.

inputs.name: blending_strength
inputs.description: Controls the intensity of blending between original and smoothed frames, allowing for fine-tuning of the flicker mitigation effect.

inputs.name: batch_size
inputs.description: Determines the number of images processed at a time, impacting the node's execution efficiency.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output tensor containing the batch of images after flicker reduction, showcasing enhanced visual consistency.

String List Manager (SuperBeasts.AI).description: The String List Manager node is designed to reorder a list of strings based on a specified new order. It allows for dynamic reorganization of string elements, facilitating customized sequencing or prioritization of data within a list.

inputs.name: frames_per_image
inputs.description: Specifies the number of frames to be associated with each image, affecting the output string format by determining the numerical prefix for each string.

inputs.name: new_order
inputs.description: Defines a custom order for the strings to be rearranged. If provided, strings are reordered according to the indices specified in this parameter.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: Outputs a reordered list of strings, formatted with frame numbers as prefixes, based on the input order and frames per image.

SUPIR_conditioner.description: The SUPIR_conditioner node is designed to condition the generation process in the SUPIR model, utilizing positive and negative prompts along with optional captions to influence the generated output. It plays a crucial role in refining and directing the model's output towards the desired thematic or stylistic outcomes.

inputs.name: SUPIR_model
inputs.description: The SUPIR model instance to be conditioned. It is central to the operation as it provides the necessary context and parameters for conditioning.

inputs.name: latents
inputs.description: Latent representations that are to be conditioned. These play a key role in determining the final output by providing a base that is modified according to the prompts and captions.

inputs.name: positive_prompt
inputs.description: A positive prompt guiding the model towards desired features or themes in the output. It significantly influences the conditioning process by highlighting what to include.

inputs.name: negative_prompt
inputs.description: A negative prompt indicating what features or themes to avoid in the model's output. It helps in steering the generation away from undesired elements.

inputs.name: captions
inputs.description: Optional captions that can be added to the positive prompt for more specific conditioning. When provided, they enhance the contextual understanding of the desired output.

outputs.name: positive
outputs.description: Conditioned latent representations with the influence of positive prompts. These are ready for further processing or generation steps.

outputs.name: negative
outputs.description: Conditioned latent representations influenced by negative prompts, serving as a contrast to the positive conditioning.

SUPIR_decode.description: The SUPIR_decode node is designed for decoding latent representations into images using a specific VAE model within the SUPIR framework. It focuses on reconstructing images from their encoded state, potentially after modifications or processing in the latent space, thereby enabling the generation of images or the restoration of details from compressed or abstract representations.

inputs.name: SUPIR_VAE
inputs.description: The VAE model used for decoding. It is crucial for the decoding process as it defines the architecture and parameters that will be used to reconstruct the image from its latent representation.

inputs.name: latents
inputs.description: The latent representation of an image that is to be decoded. This input is essential for the reconstruction process, as it contains the compressed information that will be expanded back into an image.

inputs.name: use_tiled_vae
inputs.description: A flag indicating whether to use a tiled approach for the VAE decoding. This affects the decoding process by potentially improving the handling of large images or enhancing performance on certain hardware configurations.

inputs.name: decoder_tile_size
inputs.description: Specifies the size of the tiles when using a tiled VAE decoding approach. This parameter is critical for determining the resolution and detail in the reconstructed image, affecting the overall quality and efficiency of the decoding process.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The image resulting from the decoding process. It represents the final output where the latent representation has been transformed back into visual form, showcasing the reconstructed or generated image.

SUPIR_encode.description: The SUPIR_encode node is designed for encoding images into a latent space representation using a specified VAE model. It supports both standard and tiled encoding methods, allowing for flexible adaptation to different image sizes and computational constraints.

inputs.name: SUPIR_VAE
inputs.description: The VAE model used for encoding the image. This model dictates the encoding process and the structure of the generated latent space.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image to be encoded. This input is the primary data that the node processes to produce a latent representation.

inputs.name: use_tiled_vae
inputs.description: A flag indicating whether to use a tiled approach for VAE encoding, which can be beneficial for processing large images or for reducing memory usage.

inputs.name: encoder_tile_size
inputs.description: The size of the tiles used in the tiled VAE encoding process. This parameter is relevant only if 'use_tiled_vae' is True.

inputs.name: encoder_dtype
inputs.description: Specifies the data type for the encoder's output, allowing for control over the precision and size of the generated latent representation.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The latent space representation of the encoded image. This output is crucial for further processing or generation tasks within the VAE framework.

SUPIR_first_stage.description: The SUPIR_first_stage node is designed for the initial processing of images using the SUPIR model to address compression artifacts and other noise, often resulting in a slightly blurred image. This step is crucial for preparing the image for further enhancement or manipulation by reducing noise and refining details.

inputs.name: SUPIR_VAE
inputs.description: Specifies the SUPIR VAE model used for encoding and decoding in the denoising process.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed, targeted for noise reduction and detail refinement.

inputs.name: use_tiled_vae
inputs.description: Indicates whether to use a tiled approach for the VAE processing, affecting performance and outcome.

inputs.name: encoder_tile_size
inputs.description: The tile size for the encoder, influencing the granularity of processing.

inputs.name: decoder_tile_size
inputs.description: The tile size for the decoder, affecting the output image resolution and detail.

inputs.name: encoder_dtype
inputs.description: Defines the data type for the encoder, impacting processing precision and efficiency.

outputs.name: SUPIR_VAE
outputs.description: Returns the processed SUPIR VAE model, ready for further stages of image generation.

outputs.name: denoised_image
outputs.description: The output image after initial denoising, typically slightly blurred as part of the process.

outputs.name: denoised_latents
outputs.description: The latent representations of the denoised image, useful for further processing steps.

SUPIR_model_loader.description: This node is responsible for loading the SUPIR model, a key component in the SUPIR framework for image processing and enhancement. It handles the initialization and configuration of the model, ensuring it is ready for subsequent image processing tasks.

inputs.name: supir_model
inputs.description: Specifies the path to the SUPIR model's checkpoint files, crucial for loading the model's state for image processing tasks.

inputs.name: sdxl_model
inputs.description: Specifies the path to the SDXL model's checkpoint files, which are merged with the SUPIR model to enhance its capabilities.

inputs.name: fp8_unet
inputs.description: A flag to determine whether to cast the UNet weights to a lower precision format to save VRAM, with a slight impact on quality.

inputs.name: diffusion_dtype
inputs.description: Specifies the data type for diffusion operations, with options to optimize for performance or compatibility.

outputs.name: SUPIR_model
outputs.description: The loaded and configured SUPIR model, ready for image processing tasks.

outputs.name: SUPIR_VAE
outputs.description: The loaded VAE component of the SUPIR model, essential for certain image processing operations.

SUPIR_model_loader_v2.description: The SUPIR_model_loader_v2 node is designed to initialize and prepare the SUPIR model for use, specifically by loading the model's state from a specified path and optionally adjusting its precision for memory efficiency. This node plays a crucial role in setting up the SUPIR model for subsequent image processing tasks, ensuring that the model is correctly loaded and ready for operation.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: Specifies the main model configuration for the SUPIR model loader, integrating various components like CLIP and VAE for enhanced image processing.

inputs.name: clip
inputs.description: Specifies the CLIP model used in conjunction with the SUPIR model to enhance its capabilities, particularly for tasks involving image and text processing.

inputs.name: vae
inputs.description: Specifies the VAE model used alongside the SUPIR model, contributing to the overall image processing and generation capabilities.

inputs.name: supir_model
inputs.description: Specifies the file paths to the SUPIR model checkpoints, which are essential for loading the model's state for use in image processing tasks.

inputs.name: fp8_unet
inputs.description: A boolean flag that, when set, converts the model's weights to a lower precision format (torch.float8_e4m3fn) to save VRAM, with a slight impact on quality.

inputs.name: diffusion_dtype
inputs.description: Determines the data type for diffusion operations, offering options like fp16, bf16, fp32, or auto for automatic selection based on the execution environment.

inputs.name: high_vram
inputs.description: A boolean flag that, when enabled, uses a high VRAM mode for loading model weights, potentially improving model loading speed.

outputs.name: SUPIR_model
outputs.description: The loaded SUPIR model, ready for image processing tasks.

outputs.name: SUPIR_VAE
outputs.description: The loaded SUPIR VAE component, integral to the model's image processing capabilities.

SUPIR_model_loader_v2_clip.description: This node is designed for loading and integrating multiple models, specifically CLIP models and the SUPIR model, into a unified framework. It handles the complexities of loading state dictionaries, adjusting data types, and configuring models for use within a larger system, ensuring that each component is correctly initialized and ready for operation.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The primary model to be loaded, serving as the central component of the node's functionality.

inputs.name: clip_l
inputs.description: A CLIP model designated for local features, contributing to the nuanced understanding and processing of visual content.

inputs.name: clip_g
inputs.description: A CLIP model designated for global features, enhancing the node's ability to interpret and process visual information on a broader scale.

inputs.name: vae
inputs.description: The Variational Autoencoder (VAE) model, essential for generating and manipulating latent representations of images.

inputs.name: supir_model
inputs.description: The SUPIR model to be loaded, specialized in processing or enhancing images in specific ways.

inputs.name: fp8_unet
inputs.description: A flag indicating whether to cast the U-Net weights to a lower precision format to save VRAM, with a slight impact on quality.

inputs.name: diffusion_dtype
inputs.description: Specifies the data type for diffusion operations, with options to optimize performance or memory usage.

inputs.name: high_vram
inputs.description: A flag to enable high VRAM mode, which may speed up model loading times by using Accelerate to load weights to GPU.

outputs.name: SUPIR_model
outputs.description: The loaded SUPIR model, ready for integration and use within the system.

outputs.name: SUPIR_VAE
outputs.description: The loaded SUPIR VAE model, prepared for generating and manipulating latent representations in conjunction with the SUPIR model.

SUPIR_sample.description: The SUPIR_sample node is designed for sampling in the SUPIR model, utilizing various parameters to control the sampling process. It integrates model loading, latent manipulation, and conditional generation to produce samples based on the provided inputs.

inputs.name: SUPIR_model
inputs.description: The SUPIR model to be used for sampling. It is crucial for defining the generative process.

inputs.name: latents
inputs.description: Latent representations to be used as the basis for sampling. These play a key role in the generation process.

inputs.name: positive
inputs.description: Positive conditioning information, guiding the generation towards desired attributes.

inputs.name: negative
inputs.description: Negative conditioning information, used to steer the generation away from certain attributes.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: A seed for random number generation, ensuring reproducibility of the samples.

inputs.name: steps
inputs.description: The number of steps to perform in the sampling process. This parameter influences the quality and diversity of the generated samples.

inputs.name: cfg_scale_start
inputs.description: The initial scaling factor for CFG, affecting the conditioning strength at the beginning of the sampling process.

inputs.name: cfg_scale_end
inputs.description: The final scaling factor for CFG (Classifier Free Guidance), affecting the conditioning strength at the end of the sampling process.

inputs.name: EDM_s_churn
inputs.description: A parameter influencing the EDM sampling process, specifically related to churn.

inputs.name: s_noise
inputs.description: Noise level for the sampling process, affecting the randomness and variability of the generated samples.

inputs.name: DPMPP_eta
inputs.description: A parameter related to the DPM++ sampling method, influencing its behavior.

inputs.name: control_scale_start
inputs.description: The initial control scale, influencing the degree of control at the start of the sampling process.

inputs.name: control_scale_end
inputs.description: The final control scale, determining the degree of control at the end of the sampling process.

inputs.name: restore_cfg
inputs.description: A flag indicating whether to restore the CFG scale to its original value after sampling.

inputs.name: keep_model_loaded
inputs.description: A flag indicating whether to keep the model loaded in memory after sampling, which can improve performance for subsequent samples.

inputs.name: sampler
inputs.description: The specific sampler to be used for generating samples, which can vary based on the desired sampling technique.

inputs.name: sampler_tile_size
inputs.description: The size of tiles for the sampler, relevant when sampling is performed in a tiled manner.

inputs.name: sampler_tile_stride
inputs.description: The stride of tiles for the sampler, affecting how tiles are overlapped during the sampling process.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The latent representations generated as a result of the sampling process, which may include modifications from the original input latents.

SUPIR_tiles.description: This node is designed for generating a preview of image tiles, facilitating the visualization of how an image is segmented into smaller, manageable pieces for processing or analysis. It primarily serves in the context of image processing pipelines where handling images in tiles is advantageous for performance or algorithmic reasons.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be tiled. This parameter is crucial for determining how the image will be segmented into tiles, affecting the visualization output.

inputs.name: tile_size
inputs.description: Specifies the dimensions of each tile. This parameter directly influences the granularity of the tiling process, impacting both the number of tiles generated and their respective sizes.

inputs.name: tile_stride
inputs.description: Defines the stride for tiling the image. This parameter determines the overlap between tiles, affecting the total number of tiles generated and their arrangement.

outputs.name: image_tiles
outputs.description: A collection of image tiles derived from the input image. This output is significant for visualizing the segmentation and for further processing or analysis of individual tiles.

outputs.name: tile_size
outputs.description: The dimension of each tile, as specified in the input. This output is crucial for understanding the scale at which the image was segmented.

outputs.name: tile_stride
outputs.description: The stride used for tiling the image, as specified in the input. This output provides insight into the overlap and arrangement of the generated tiles.

SUPIR_Upscale.description: The SUPIR_Upscale node is designed to upscale images using the SUPIR model, enhancing image resolution while maintaining or improving image quality. This node is part of a suite of nodes aimed at image processing and enhancement, leveraging advanced deep learning techniques to achieve superior upscaling results.

inputs.name: supir_model
inputs.description: Specifies the SUPIR model to be used for upscaling, allowing for customization of the upscaling process.

inputs.name: sdxl_model
inputs.description: Determines the secondary model used in conjunction with the SUPIR model to enhance the upscaling process.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: Specifies the image to be upscaled, serving as the primary input for the upscaling process.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: Sets the seed for random number generation, ensuring reproducibility of the upscaling results.

inputs.name: resize_method
inputs.description: Determines the method used for resizing images during the upscaling process, affecting the texture and quality of the output.

inputs.name: scale_by
inputs.description: Specifies the factor by which the image will be upscaled, directly influencing the resolution of the output image.

inputs.name: steps
inputs.description: Defines the number of steps to be used in the upscaling process, impacting the detail and quality of the upscaled image.

inputs.name: restoration_scale
inputs.description: Adjusts the scale of restoration applied to the upscaled image, affecting the balance between detail enhancement and artifact reduction.

inputs.name: cfg_scale
inputs.description: Controls the configuration scale for the upscaling process, influencing the adherence to the input image's content and style.

inputs.name: a_prompt
inputs.description: Provides a positive textual description to guide the upscaling process, enhancing certain aspects of the image according to the specified attributes.

inputs.name: n_prompt
inputs.description: Provides a negative textual description to avoid certain aspects during the upscaling process, helping to steer the result away from undesired attributes.

inputs.name: s_churn
inputs.description: Specifies the churn rate in the sampling process, affecting the exploration of the latent space and the diversity of the upscaled results.

inputs.name: s_noise
inputs.description: Sets the noise level in the sampling process, influencing the amount of randomness and potentially the detail in the upscaled image.

inputs.name: control_scale
inputs.description: Adjusts the control scale for the upscaling process, affecting the overall control over the upscaling outcome.

inputs.name: cfg_scale_start
inputs.description: Specifies the starting configuration scale, allowing for dynamic adjustment of the cfg scale throughout the upscaling process.

inputs.name: control_scale_start
inputs.description: Specifies the starting control scale, enabling dynamic adjustment of control over the upscaling outcome throughout the process.

TiledDiffusion.description: The TiledDiffusion node specializes in applying diffusion processes to images in a tiled manner, optimizing for efficiency and scalability. It leverages a tiling strategy to manage and process large images or batches by breaking them down into smaller, manageable pieces, allowing for detailed and controlled diffusion effects across the entirety of the image.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model parameter represents the diffusion model to be applied. It is crucial for defining the diffusion behavior and processing the image data through the specified diffusion algorithm.

inputs.name: method
inputs.description: Specifies the diffusion method to be applied, such as 'Mixture of Diffusers' or other strategies, influencing the overall diffusion process and its outcomes.

inputs.name: tile_width
inputs.description: Determines the width of each tile in the tiling strategy, affecting the granularity of the diffusion process across the image.

inputs.name: tile_height
inputs.description: Sets the height of each tile, impacting how the image is segmented for the diffusion process and influencing the detail level achievable.

inputs.name: tile_overlap
inputs.description: Defines the overlap between tiles to ensure seamless diffusion effects across tile boundaries, enhancing the visual continuity of the processed image.

inputs.name: tile_batch_size
inputs.description: Controls the number of tiles processed simultaneously, balancing between computational efficiency and memory usage.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: Returns the modified model with the tiled diffusion process applied, ready for further use or analysis.

VAEDecodeTiled_TiledDiffusion.description: This node specializes in decoding latent representations into images using a tiled approach, enhancing the efficiency and quality of the decoding process, especially for large images. It leverages a variable tile size to optimize the decoding process, accommodating different computational constraints and image dimensions.

inputs.name: samples
inputs.description: The latent representation to be decoded into an image. This input is crucial for determining the content and quality of the output image.

inputs.name: vae
inputs.description: The variational autoencoder model used for the decoding process. This model is essential for transforming the latent representation back into pixel data.

inputs.name: tile_size
inputs.description: Specifies the size of the tiles used in the decoding process. Adjusting this parameter can optimize decoding performance and output quality.

inputs.name: fast
inputs.description: A boolean flag that, when enabled, accelerates the decoding process by potentially compromising on the output quality.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The decoded image, reconstructed from the latent representation using the specified VAE model and tile size.

VAEEncodeTiled_TiledDiffusion.description: This node is designed for encoding images into a latent space representation using a tiled VAE approach, optimizing for efficiency and flexibility in handling various image sizes through tiling.

inputs.name: pixels
inputs.description: The input image to be encoded. This parameter is crucial for determining the content that will be transformed into a latent representation.

inputs.name: vae
inputs.description: The VAE model used for encoding. It defines the architecture and parameters of the variational autoencoder that processes the image.

inputs.name: tile_size
inputs.description: Specifies the size of the tiles into which the image is divided for encoding. This affects the granularity of the encoding process and can be adjusted for performance or quality.

inputs.name: fast
inputs.description: A boolean flag that, when true, enables a faster but potentially less accurate encoding process.

inputs.name: color_fix
inputs.description: A boolean flag that, when true, applies a color correction step to the image before encoding. This can be useful for maintaining color consistency across tiles.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The encoded latent representation of the input image. This output captures the essential features of the image in a compressed form, suitable for various downstream tasks.

JWDatetimeString.description: This node generates a string representation of the current datetime, formatted according to a specified pattern. It abstracts the complexity of datetime formatting, providing a simple interface for obtaining formatted datetime strings.

inputs.name: format
inputs.description: Specifies the format in which the current datetime should be returned. This allows for customization of the output string according to the needs of the application.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The output is a string that represents the current datetime, formatted according to the specified pattern.

JWFloat.description: This node is designed to handle floating-point operations, providing a platform for performing calculations or manipulations involving float values. It focuses on enabling precise numerical computations and transformations within a given workflow.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: Represents the floating-point value to be processed or manipulated by the node. Its role is crucial for the execution of float-specific operations, directly influencing the outcome of the node's functionality.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The output is a floating-point value, which is the result of the node's operation on the input float. This output is essential for further numerical computations or analyses within the workflow.

JWFloatAbsolute.description: The JWFloatAbsolute node calculates the absolute value of a given float number, effectively removing any negative sign to ensure the result is non-negative.

inputs.name: value
