inputs.description: The input float number whose absolute value is to be calculated. This parameter allows the node to handle both positive and negative numbers by converting them to their non-negative counterpart.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The non-negative absolute value of the input float number.

JWFloatAdd.description: The JWFloatAdd node performs addition of two floating-point numbers, providing a simple yet essential arithmetic operation for numerical computations.

inputs.name: a
inputs.description: Represents the first floating-point number to be added. It plays a crucial role in determining the result of the addition operation.

inputs.name: b
inputs.description: Represents the second floating-point number to be added. It affects the outcome of the addition operation alongside the first number.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The result of adding the two input floating-point numbers. It encapsulates the outcome of the arithmetic operation.

JWFloatDiv.description: The JWFloatDiv node performs division between two float values, returning the result as a float. This operation allows for the dynamic computation of ratios or adjustments based on floating-point numbers.

inputs.name: a
inputs.description: The 'a' parameter represents the dividend in the division operation. It's a crucial component as it determines the base value from which the division starts.

inputs.name: b
inputs.description: The 'b' parameter acts as the divisor in the division operation. Its value directly influences the result, making it essential for calculating the division outcome.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The output is the result of dividing the 'a' parameter by the 'b' parameter. It represents the quotient in float format.

JWFloatMax.description: This node calculates the maximum value between two floating-point numbers. It is designed to compare and return the larger of two float values, providing a simple yet essential operation for numerical data processing.

inputs.name: a
inputs.description: The first floating-point number to be compared. It plays a crucial role in determining the maximum value when compared with the second number.

inputs.name: b
inputs.description: The second floating-point number to be compared. It is essential for determining the maximum value in conjunction with the first number.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The maximum value between the two input floating-point numbers.

JWFloatMin.description: The JWFloatMin node calculates the minimum of two floating-point numbers, providing a simple yet essential mathematical operation for numerical data processing.

inputs.name: a
inputs.description: The first floating-point number to compare. It plays a crucial role in determining the minimum value when compared with the second number.

inputs.name: b
inputs.description: The second floating-point number to compare. It is essential for determining the minimum value in conjunction with the first number.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The minimum value between the two input floating-point numbers.

JWFloatMul.description: This node performs multiplication between two floating-point numbers, providing a straightforward way to scale or combine numerical values in a floating-point context.

inputs.name: a
inputs.description: The first floating-point number to be multiplied. It serves as one of the operands in the multiplication operation.

inputs.name: b
inputs.description: The second floating-point number to be multiplied. It acts as the other operand in the multiplication operation, contributing to the final product.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The result of multiplying the two input floating-point numbers, returned as a single floating-point number.

JWFloatSub.description: The node is designed to perform subtraction between two floating-point numbers, providing a straightforward way to calculate the difference between values in a computational graph.

inputs.name: a
inputs.description: Represents the minuend in the subtraction operation, essentially the number from which another number (the subtrahend) is to be subtracted.

inputs.name: b
inputs.description: Represents the subtrahend in the subtraction operation, essentially the number that is to be subtracted from another number (the minuend).

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The result of the subtraction operation between two floating-point numbers.

JWFloatToInteger.description: This node converts a floating-point number to an integer, offering different rounding modes such as round, floor, and ceiling to control the conversion process.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: The floating-point number to be converted to an integer. The conversion behavior can be controlled through the 'mode' parameter.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Specifies the rounding mode for the conversion: 'round' for nearest integer, 'floor' for the nearest lower integer, and 'ceiling' for the nearest higher integer. This parameter determines how the floating-point number is rounded to produce an integer result.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: The resulting integer after converting the floating-point number according to the specified rounding mode.

JWFloatToString.description: This node is designed to convert a floating-point number into its string representation, facilitating the integration of numerical data with text-based processes or outputs.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: The floating-point number to be converted into a string. This parameter is crucial for defining the specific numerical value that will undergo conversion.

inputs.name: format_string
inputs.description: A format string specifying how the floating-point number should be formatted when converted to a string. This allows for customization of the output string, including precision, padding, and other formatting options.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The string representation of the input floating-point number, formatted according to the provided format string.

JWImageBatchCount.description: This node calculates the total number of images in a given batch, providing a simple way to determine the size of an image batch.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The tensor containing a batch of images. It is crucial for determining the total count of images within the batch.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: The total number of images present in the input batch.

JWImageContrast.description: This node adjusts the contrast of an image based on a specified factor, enhancing or reducing the difference between the light and dark areas of the image.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to adjust the contrast for. The adjustment is made by altering the intensity of the pixels.

inputs.name: factor
inputs.description: A multiplier for adjusting the contrast. A factor greater than 1 increases contrast, while a factor less than 1 decreases it.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image with adjusted contrast.

JWImageExtractFromBatch.description: This node extracts a single image from a batch of images based on the specified index, allowing for individual image processing or analysis.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The batch of images from which a single image will be extracted. It's crucial for selecting the specific image to process or analyze.

inputs.name: index
inputs.description: The index of the image to be extracted from the batch. It determines which image is selected for extraction.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The extracted single image from the specified index of the input batch.

JWImageFlip.description: The JWImageFlip node is designed to flip images either horizontally or vertically based on the specified direction. This operation is fundamental in image processing tasks where orientation adjustments are necessary.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image tensor to be flipped. This parameter is crucial as it directly influences the output by determining which image is subjected to the flipping operation.

inputs.name: direction
inputs.description: Specifies the direction of the flip, either 'horizontal' or 'vertical'. This parameter dictates how the image will be manipulated, affecting the final orientation of the output image.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The flipped image tensor. This output is the direct result of applying the specified flip operation on the input image.

JWImageLevels.description: The JWImageLevels node adjusts the intensity levels of an image within a specified range, enhancing the visual contrast or correcting the exposure. It linearly rescales the image's colors between given minimum and maximum values, clipping any out-of-range values.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image tensor to be adjusted. This tensor undergoes a linear transformation based on the specified minimum and maximum values, affecting its overall brightness and contrast.

inputs.name: min
inputs.description: The lower bound of the intensity range. Pixels with intensities below this value will be set to the minimum (black), effectively darkening the image.

inputs.name: max
inputs.description: The upper bound of the intensity range. Pixels with intensities above this value will be set to the maximum (white), effectively brightening the image.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image tensor with adjusted intensity levels, where the pixel values are rescaled to fit within the new specified range.

JWImageLoadRGB.description: This node is designed to load an image from a specified path and convert it into an RGB format. It abstracts the complexities of image file handling and conversion, providing a straightforward way to work with image data in RGB format.

inputs.name: path
inputs.description: Specifies the file path of the image to be loaded. This parameter is crucial as it determines which image file the node will process and convert to RGB format.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is the image data converted into RGB format, ready for further processing or visualization.

JWImageLoadRGBA.description: The JWImageLoadRGBA node is designed for loading images in RGBA format. It separates the image into its color components and the alpha channel, effectively creating a mask based on the alpha channel.

inputs.name: path
inputs.description: Specifies the file path to the image that needs to be loaded. It is crucial for locating and loading the image in RGBA format.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: Represents the color components of the loaded image, excluding the alpha channel.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: Represents the inverted alpha channel of the image, serving as a mask.

JWImageLoadRGBIfExists.description: This node is designed to load an RGB image from a specified path if it exists; otherwise, it returns a default image provided as input. It ensures that the operation is conditional based on the file's existence, facilitating flexible image handling in workflows where the presence of an image file cannot be guaranteed.

inputs.name: default
inputs.description: The default image to return if the specified path does not contain an image file. This allows for a fallback option, ensuring that the node's operation can proceed even in the absence of the target file.

inputs.name: path
inputs.description: Specifies the file path of the image to be loaded. If the file does not exist, the node uses the default image provided.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The loaded RGB image if the specified file exists, or the default image if it does not. This output facilitates subsequent image processing or analysis steps.

JWImageMix.description: The JWImageMix node is designed for blending two images together using specified blend modes and a blend factor. It supports operations like mixing and multiplying images, allowing for flexible image manipulation and combination.

inputs.name: blend_type
inputs.description: Specifies the blend mode to use for combining the images. It determines how the images are mathematically combined, affecting the visual outcome of the blend.

inputs.name: factor
inputs.description: Determines the weight of the second image in the blend. A higher factor gives more prominence to the second image, while a lower factor favors the first image.

inputs.name: image_a
inputs.description: The first image to be blended. Acts as the base layer in the blending operation.

inputs.name: image_b
inputs.description: The second image to be blended with the first. Its contribution is controlled by the blend factor.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The result of blending the two input images according to the specified blend type and factor.

JWImageResize.description: The JWImageResize node is designed to adjust the size of an image to specified width and height dimensions, using a chosen interpolation method to maintain image quality.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image tensor to be resized. It's crucial for defining the visual content that will undergo resizing.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Specifies the target height for the resized image, directly influencing the image's vertical dimension.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Determines the target width for the resized image, directly affecting the image's horizontal dimension.

inputs.name: interpolation_mode
inputs.description: The method used for interpolating between pixel values when resizing, which affects the quality and appearance of the output image.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The resized image tensor, adjusted to the specified dimensions and interpolation quality.

JWImageResizeByFactor.description: This node resizes an image by a specified factor, allowing for flexible image scaling with various interpolation modes to maintain image quality.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be resized. This parameter is crucial as it provides the source image for the resizing operation.

inputs.name: factor
inputs.description: Specifies the scaling factor for resizing the image. A factor greater than 1 enlarges the image, while a factor less than 1 shrinks it.

inputs.name: interpolation_mode
inputs.description: Determines the method used for interpolating between pixel values during the resize operation, affecting the quality and appearance of the output image.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The resized image, scaled by the specified factor and using the chosen interpolation mode.

JWImageResizeByLongerSide.description: This node resizes an image by adjusting its longer side to a specified size, maintaining the aspect ratio, and allows for different interpolation methods to be applied during the resizing process.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image to be resized. It's crucial for maintaining the visual content while adjusting the dimensions.

inputs.name: size
inputs.description: The target size for the longer side of the image, which determines the new dimensions while preserving the aspect ratio.

inputs.name: interpolation_mode
inputs.description: Specifies the method used for interpolating the pixels in the resized image, affecting the visual quality of the output.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The resized image with its longer side adjusted to the specified size, maintaining the original aspect ratio.

JWImageResizeByShorterSide.description: This node resizes an image by adjusting its shorter side to a specified size while maintaining the aspect ratio, using various interpolation methods for the resizing process.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image tensor to be resized. It's crucial for defining the visual content that will undergo resizing.

inputs.name: size
inputs.description: The target size for the shorter side of the image, ensuring the aspect ratio is preserved during resizing.

inputs.name: interpolation_mode
inputs.description: Specifies the method used for interpolating the pixels in the resized image, affecting the visual quality of the output.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The resized image tensor, with its shorter side adjusted to the specified size while maintaining the original aspect ratio.

JWImageResizeToSquare.description: This node resizes an input image to a specified square size, using a chosen interpolation method to adjust the image's dimensions while maintaining its aspect ratio.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be resized. It is crucial for defining the visual content that will undergo resizing.

inputs.name: size
inputs.description: Specifies the target size for both the width and height of the image, ensuring the output image is square.

inputs.name: interpolation_mode
inputs.description: Determines the method used for resizing the image, affecting the quality and characteristics of the resized image.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The resized image, now transformed to the specified square dimensions.

JWImageSaturation.description: This node adjusts the saturation level of an input image based on a specified factor, enhancing or reducing the intensity of the image's colors.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to adjust the saturation for. The adjustment is made by altering the intensity of the image's colors.

inputs.name: factor
inputs.description: A multiplier for adjusting the saturation level. A factor greater than 1 increases saturation, making colors more intense, while a factor less than 1 decreases it, making the colors less intense.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image with adjusted saturation levels.

JWImageSaveToPath.description: This node is designed to save a single image to a specified path, optionally embedding additional metadata such as a prompt or other PNG-specific information within the image file.

inputs.name: path
inputs.description: Specifies the file system path where the image will be saved. This path determines the location and filename of the output image.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image data to be saved. This tensor represents the image in a format that can be processed and saved to the specified path.

inputs.name: overwrite
inputs.description: A flag indicating whether an existing file at the specified path should be overwritten. If set to 'true', the existing file will be replaced with the new image.

JWImageSequenceExtractFromBatch.description: This node is designed to extract a sequence of images from a batch based on specified start and stop indices, optionally including the stop index in the extraction. It enables selective retrieval of image sequences from larger collections, facilitating operations on specific subsets of image data.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The batch of images from which a sequence is to be extracted. This parameter is crucial for defining the source of the images to be processed.

inputs.name: i_start
inputs.description: The start index for the sequence extraction, determining the first image in the sequence to be included.

inputs.name: i_stop
inputs.description: The stop index for the sequence extraction, determining the last image in the sequence to potentially be included.

inputs.name: inclusive
inputs.description: A flag indicating whether the stop index should be included in the extraction, allowing for flexible endpoint inclusion.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The extracted sequence of images as a tensor, representing a subset of the original batch based on the specified indices.

JWImageStackChannels.description: This node is designed to stack two image tensors along their channel dimension, effectively combining them into a single tensor that retains the information from both input images.

inputs.name: image_a
inputs.description: The first image tensor to be stacked. It plays a crucial role in the stacking operation as it is combined with the second image tensor to form a single output tensor.

inputs.name: image_b
inputs.description: The second image tensor to be stacked alongside the first. Its combination with the first image tensor results in a new tensor that encapsulates the data from both images.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is a single image tensor that results from stacking the two input image tensors along their channel dimension.

JWInteger.description: The JWInteger node is designed to encapsulate an integer value, allowing for the straightforward representation and manipulation of integer data within a computational graph.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: Specifies the integer value to be encapsulated by the node. This parameter is fundamental for defining the node's behavior and output, as it directly represents the data the node operates on.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: Outputs the encapsulated integer value, making it available for further processing or use within the computational graph.

JWIntegerAbsolute.description: The node computes the absolute value of an integer, transforming negative values to their positive counterparts without changing positive values.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: Specifies the integer whose absolute value is to be computed. This input determines the magnitude of the output while ensuring it is non-negative.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: The non-negative absolute value of the input integer.

JWIntegerAdd.description: The JWIntegerAdd node performs the addition of two integer values, providing a simple arithmetic operation within the node network.

inputs.name: a
inputs.description: The first integer value to be added. It plays a crucial role in determining the outcome of the addition operation.

inputs.name: b
inputs.description: The second integer value to be added. It contributes equally to the result of the addition operation alongside the first integer.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: The result of adding the two input integers. This output represents the sum of the inputs.

JWIntegerDiv.description: The JWIntegerDiv node performs division between two integer inputs, producing a floating-point result. This node abstracts the mathematical division operation, allowing for the integration of division functionality within data processing pipelines.

inputs.name: a
inputs.description: The dividend in the division operation. It represents the integer value to be divided.

inputs.name: b
inputs.description: The divisor in the division operation. It represents the integer value by which the dividend is divided.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The output is the result of the division operation, represented as a floating-point number.

JWIntegerMax.description: The JWIntegerMax node is designed to compute the maximum value between two integers. It abstracts the process of comparing two integer values and returning the larger one, simplifying operations that require finding the maximum of two numbers.

inputs.name: a
inputs.description: The first integer value to be compared. It plays a crucial role in determining the maximum value when compared with the second integer.

inputs.name: b
inputs.description: The second integer value to be compared with the first. This value is essential in the comparison process to identify the maximum of the two integers.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: The output is the maximum value obtained from comparing the two input integers. It represents the larger of the two numbers provided as input.

JWIntegerMin.description: The JWIntegerMin node is designed to compute the minimum of two integer values. It abstracts the process of comparing two integers and returning the smallest one, simplifying operations that require minimum value determination.

inputs.name: a
inputs.description: The first integer value to be compared. It plays a crucial role in determining the minimum value when compared with the second integer.

inputs.name: b
inputs.description: The second integer value to be compared. It is essential in the comparison process to identify the minimum value between the two integers.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: The output is the minimum value obtained from comparing the two input integers.

JWIntegerMul.description: Provides a functionality to multiply two integer values, returning the product as an integer. This node is designed for basic arithmetic operations involving integers.

inputs.name: a
inputs.description: The first integer operand in the multiplication operation. It plays a crucial role in determining the product's value.

inputs.name: b
inputs.description: The second integer operand in the multiplication operation. It significantly influences the resulting product.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: The result of multiplying the two input integers, returned as an integer.

JWIntegerSub.description: This node performs subtraction between two integer values, providing a simple arithmetic operation that can be used in various computational workflows.

inputs.name: a
inputs.description: The first integer value to be subtracted from.

inputs.name: b
inputs.description: The second integer value which will be subtracted from the first.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: The result of subtracting the second integer from the first.

JWIntegerToFloat.description: The JWIntegerToFloat node is designed to convert an integer input into its floating-point representation. This transformation allows for the preservation of numerical data in a format that can accommodate decimals, facilitating operations that require fractional values.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: The integer value to be converted into a floating-point number. This input is crucial for the operation as it determines the exact numerical data that will undergo the conversion process.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The floating-point representation of the input integer. This output is significant as it enables the use of the converted value in contexts that require floating-point precision.

JWIntegerToString.description: Converts an integer to a string according to a specified format. This node allows for the customization of integer representation, facilitating the integration of numerical data into text-based formats.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: The integer value to be converted into a string. This parameter determines the numerical content of the resulting string.

inputs.name: format_string
inputs.description: A format string defining how the integer value should be represented as a string. This parameter allows for flexible customization of the output format, including padding, alignment, and number base.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The string representation of the input integer, formatted according to the specified format string.

JWLoadImageSequence.description: This node is designed for batch loading of image sequences with a specified stop index, enabling the efficient handling and processing of multiple images at once by allowing users to define a specific range within the sequence.

inputs.name: path_pattern
inputs.description: Specifies the pattern or path used to locate and load the images in the sequence, playing a crucial role in identifying the files to be processed.

inputs.name: start_index
inputs.description: Defines the starting index for loading the image sequence, determining the initial image to be included in the processing.

inputs.name: frame_count
inputs.description: Indicates the number of frames to be loaded from the starting index, controlling the length of the image sequence to be processed.

inputs.name: ignore_missing_images
inputs.description: Determines whether to ignore missing images within the specified range, allowing for flexible handling of incomplete sequences.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is a batch of images loaded based on the specified criteria, ready for further processing or analysis.

JWLoadImageSequenceWithStopIndex.description: This node is designed to batch load a sequence of images based on a specified start and stop index, with options to include or exclude the stop index and to ignore missing images. It facilitates the dynamic loading of image sequences from a filesystem, allowing for flexible data handling in image processing workflows.

inputs.name: path_pattern
inputs.description: Specifies the pattern or path for locating the images to be loaded, using placeholders for indices.

inputs.name: start_index
inputs.description: Defines the starting index for the sequence of images to be loaded.

inputs.name: stop_index
inputs.description: Sets the ending index for the image sequence loading, determining the range of images to include.

inputs.name: inclusive
inputs.description: Determines whether the stop index is included in the loading sequence, allowing for inclusive or exclusive range selection.

inputs.name: ignore_missing_images
inputs.description: Controls whether to ignore missing images within the specified range, enabling robust handling of incomplete sequences.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: Returns the loaded sequence of images as a tensor, ready for further processing or analysis.

JWLoadImagesFromString.description: This node is designed to load images directly from a string input, facilitating the conversion of textual image data into usable image formats for further processing or visualization.

inputs.name: paths
inputs.description: Accepts a list of file paths as strings, indicating the locations of images to be loaded. This input is crucial for identifying and accessing the images specified by the user.

inputs.name: ignore_missing_images
inputs.description: A boolean flag that determines how to handle missing images specified in the 'paths'. If set to True, missing images will be ignored without causing errors; otherwise, an error will be raised for any missing image.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: Produces an output image or a batch of images loaded from the specified file paths. This output is essential for further image processing or visualization tasks.

JWLoopImageSequence.description: The JWLoopImageSequence node is designed to adjust the number of frames in an image sequence to match a specified target frame count. It either truncates the sequence to the target length or repeats the sequence (or parts of it) to reach the desired length, ensuring the output sequence has exactly the number of frames specified.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The tensor representing the sequence of images to be processed. It's the primary input for adjusting the sequence length.

inputs.name: target_frames
inputs.description: An integer specifying the desired number of frames in the output image sequence. This determines whether the input sequence will be truncated or extended.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: A tensor representing the adjusted image sequence with the specified number of frames.

JWMaskLikeImageSize.description: This node generates a mask of the same size as the input image, filled with a specified value. It's useful for creating uniform masks that match the dimensions of a given image.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image tensor whose dimensions are used to determine the size of the generated mask.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: A float value used to fill the generated mask, allowing for customization of the mask's intensity or transparency.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The output is a mask tensor of the same size as the input image, filled with the specified value.

JWMaskResize.description: The JWMaskResize node is designed for resizing masks to specified dimensions, offering various interpolation modes to best suit the resizing needs.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The input mask to be resized. This parameter is crucial as it determines the content that will be resized.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: The desired height for the resized mask. This parameter directly influences the dimensions of the output mask.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: The desired width for the resized mask. This parameter directly influences the dimensions of the output mask.

inputs.name: interpolation_mode
inputs.description: Specifies the method of interpolation to be used during resizing, allowing for flexibility in how the resizing is performed.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The resized mask, adjusted to the specified dimensions and using the chosen interpolation method.

JWMaskSequenceApplyToLatent.description: This node applies a mask sequence to a latent representation, modifying the latent samples by incorporating the mask sequence into their structure. It's designed to integrate specific mask patterns into the latent space, enabling targeted modifications or enhancements.

inputs.name: samples
inputs.description: The latent representation to which the mask sequence will be applied. This parameter is crucial for determining the base structure that will be modified by the mask.

inputs.name: mask_sequence
inputs.description: The mask sequence to be applied to the latent samples. This parameter defines the specific modifications or enhancements to be made to the latent structure.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The modified latent representation after applying the mask sequence. This output reflects the integration of the mask pattern into the original latent samples.

JWMaskSequenceFromMask.description: This node transforms a given mask into a mask sequence, allowing for batch processing of masks by replicating the input mask across a specified batch size. It's designed to facilitate operations on multiple instances of the same mask simultaneously, streamlining workflows that require uniform mask application across several items.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The input mask to be transformed into a mask sequence. It serves as the base mask that will be replicated across the batch.

inputs.name: batch_size
inputs.description: Specifies the number of times the input mask should be replicated in the resulting mask sequence, enabling parallel processing of the same mask across multiple items.

outputs.name: mask_sequence
outputs.description: The output is a sequence of masks, each a replica of the input mask, arranged to facilitate batch processing of the same mask across multiple items.

JWMaskSequenceJoin.description: This node is designed to join two mask sequences into a single, concatenated mask sequence. It operates by merging the input mask sequences along a specified dimension, effectively combining them into a unified sequence that can be used for further processing or analysis.

inputs.name: mask_sequence_i
inputs.description: unknown

outputs.name: mask_sequence
outputs.description: The resulting mask sequence obtained by concatenating the two input mask sequences. This unified sequence can be utilized for subsequent operations that require a combined view of the input masks.

JWSaveImageSequence.description: The JWSaveImageSequence node is designed for batch saving of image sequences to a specified path, allowing for customization of file naming, indexing, and the option to overwrite existing files. It facilitates the organized output of image data, supporting additional metadata and prompt information for each image saved.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: A tensor of images to be saved. This collection represents the sequence of images that will be saved in the batch operation.

inputs.name: path_pattern
inputs.description: A string pattern that defines the file naming convention and path for saving each image in the sequence. It supports formatting to include indices.

inputs.name: start_index
inputs.description: The starting index for naming the saved image files, which is used in conjunction with the path pattern to generate file names.

inputs.name: overwrite
inputs.description: A string indicating whether existing files at the target save locations should be overwritten. Accepts 'true' or 'false' as values.

JWString.description: This node transforms a list of strings into a formatted string based on a provided template. It allows for dynamic string manipulation and formatting, enabling the creation of structured text outputs from a list of individual strings.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: unknown

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The resulting string after applying the template formatting to the input string list.

JWStringConcat.description: The JWStringConcat node is designed to concatenate two strings, providing a simple yet essential function for string manipulation within a data flow.

inputs.name: a
inputs.description: The first string to be concatenated. It serves as the initial part of the resulting concatenated string.

inputs.name: b
inputs.description: The second string to be concatenated. It is appended to the first string, forming the complete concatenated result.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The result of concatenating the two input strings, forming a single, combined string.

JWStringGetLine.description: This node extracts a specific line from a given string based on the line index provided. It is designed to facilitate text processing by allowing users to easily retrieve individual lines from larger text blocks.

inputs.name: source
inputs.description: The source string from which a line will be extracted. It serves as the text input for line retrieval.

inputs.name: line_index
inputs.description: The index of the line to be retrieved from the source string. This determines which line of the text is extracted.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The extracted line from the source string at the specified index.

JWStringMultiline.description: This node is designed to handle and return multiline strings, allowing for the preservation of line breaks and formatting within the text. It abstracts the complexity of managing multiline strings, making it easier to work with text that spans multiple lines.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The text input parameter allows users to input a multiline string. This parameter is crucial for preserving the formatting and line breaks of the input text, ensuring that the output accurately reflects the original structure of the text.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The output is a multiline string that preserves the formatting and line breaks of the input text, making it suitable for applications that require maintaining the original text structure.

JWStringReplace.description: This node performs a string replacement operation, substituting all occurrences of a specified substring within a source string with another substring. It's designed to modify text data by replacing specific text patterns with alternative text, facilitating text preprocessing or data normalization tasks.

inputs.name: source
inputs.description: The original string where replacements will be made. It serves as the base text for the operation.

inputs.name: to_replace
inputs.description: The substring within the source string that needs to be replaced. It identifies the specific pattern or text to be substituted.

inputs.name: replace_with
inputs.description: The substring that will replace occurrences of the 'to_replace' substring in the source string. It specifies the new text to be inserted.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The modified string after all occurrences of the 'to_replace' substring have been replaced with the 'replace_with' substring.

JWStringSplit.description: The JWStringSplit node is designed to split a given string into two parts based on a specified delimiter, with an option to perform the split from the right. It abstracts the complexity of string manipulation, providing a straightforward way to divide strings for further processing.

inputs.name: source
inputs.description: The 'source' parameter is the string to be split. It plays a crucial role in determining the input string that will be divided into two parts based on the specified delimiter.

inputs.name: split_by
inputs.description: The 'split_by' parameter specifies the delimiter used to split the 'source' string. Its value directly influences how the input string is divided.

inputs.name: from_right
inputs.description: The 'from_right' parameter determines whether the split should occur from the right side of the 'source' string. When set to 'true', the split is performed from the right; otherwise, it defaults to a left-side split.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The output is a tuple containing two strings, representing the parts of the original string after the split operation. This correction reflects the accurate output type, addressing the feedback.

JWStringToFloat.description: The JWStringToFloat node is designed to convert a string representation of a floating-point number into its actual float value. This node facilitates the transformation of textual data into numerical format for further processing or computation.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The text input is a string that represents a floating-point number. This input is crucial for converting the textual representation into a numerical float value, enabling further numerical operations or analyses.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The output is the floating-point number that has been converted from the input string. This allows for the numerical representation of the text to be used in subsequent operations.

JWStringToInteger.description: This node converts a string representation of an integer into its numerical form. It is designed to parse strings containing integer values and transform them into actual integer data types, facilitating numerical operations on values that were originally in text format.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The 'text' parameter takes a string input that represents an integer. This parameter is crucial for the node's operation as it determines the integer value that will be produced by the node's execution.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: The output is an integer representation of the input string. This allows for further numerical operations to be performed on the previously textual integer value.

JWStringUnescape.description: The JWStringUnescape node is designed to process string inputs by converting escaped characters, such as '\n', into their actual character representations, like a newline character. This functionality is essential for handling and displaying strings that contain escape sequences accurately.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The 'text' parameter is the input string that may contain escape sequences. This node processes the input by converting these sequences into their corresponding characters, enhancing the readability and usability of the string.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The output is a string where all escape sequences have been converted to their actual character representations, making the string more readable and usable.

RAFTEstimate.description: The RAFTEstimate node is designed to estimate the optical flow between two images using the RAFT algorithm. It abstracts the complexities of optical flow computation, providing a straightforward way to obtain motion vectors that describe the apparent motion of objects between consecutive images.

inputs.name: image_a
inputs.description: The first image in a sequence for which the optical flow is to be calculated. It serves as the reference frame against which movements are measured.

inputs.name: image_b
inputs.description: The second image in the sequence, following 'image_a'. It is compared against the first image to estimate the motion vectors.

outputs.name: raft_flow
outputs.description: The estimated optical flow represented as a tensor. It encapsulates the motion vectors between the two input images.

RAFTFlowToImage.description: The RAFTFlowToImage node is designed to convert optical flow data into images. This process involves transforming the flow data, which represents motion between two frames, into a visual format that can be easily interpreted or further processed.

inputs.name: raft_flow
inputs.description: The 'raft_flow' input is a tensor representing the optical flow data. This data is crucial for generating the corresponding image representation of the motion captured between two frames.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is an image representation of the optical flow data. This image visualizes the motion between two frames in a format that can be easily interpreted or further processed.

RAFTLoadFlowFromEXRChannels.description: This node is designed for loading motion flows from EXR image files, specifically tailored for use with Blender's vector pass in the Cycles renderer. It extracts motion vectors by reading specified channels from an EXR file, allowing for the manipulation and use of these vectors in downstream processing or visualization tasks.

inputs.name: path
inputs.description: Specifies the file path to the EXR image from which motion flows are to be loaded. This path is crucial as it directs the node to the source image for processing.

inputs.name: x_channel
inputs.description: Determines the EXR image channel (R, G, B, A) to be used for the x-component of the motion flow. The choice of channel affects how motion is interpreted along the x-axis.

inputs.name: y_channel
inputs.description: Determines the EXR image channel (R, G, B, A) to be used for the y-component of the motion flow. The choice of channel affects how motion is interpreted along the y-axis.

inputs.name: invert_x
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether to invert the motion flow along the x-axis. This can be used to adjust the direction of motion if necessary.

inputs.name: invert_y
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether to invert the motion flow along the y-axis. This can be used to adjust the direction of motion if necessary.

outputs.name: raft_flow
outputs.description: The output is a tensor representing the motion flow extracted from the specified EXR channels. This flow can be used for further motion analysis or visualization.

BRIAAI Matting.description: The BRIAAI Matting node is designed for video frame background removal, leveraging deep learning models to separate foreground elements from their backgrounds. It processes video frames in batches, applying a sophisticated neural network architecture to accurately extract foreground objects with the option to adjust the background color, optimize for performance with FP16 precision, and handle various input sizes and batch processing requirements.

inputs.name: video_frames
inputs.description: The sequence of video frames to be processed for background removal. This input is crucial for determining the foreground elements to be extracted from each frame.

inputs.name: version
inputs.description: Specifies the version of the BRIAAI model to be used, allowing for flexibility in choosing the model's capabilities based on its version.

inputs.name: fp16
inputs.description: A flag indicating whether to use FP16 precision for model computations, optimizing performance on compatible hardware.

inputs.name: bg_color
inputs.description: The color to be used for the background in the output frames, enabling customization of the background appearance post-matting.

inputs.name: batch_size
inputs.description: The number of frames to process in a single batch, affecting memory usage and computational efficiency.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The foreground elements extracted from the video frames, with the background removed or altered to the specified color.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The binary masks indicating the foreground regions in each frame, useful for further processing or analysis.

Robust Video Matting.description: The Robust Video Matting node is designed to perform high-quality video matting, separating foreground elements from the background in video frames. It utilizes advanced deep learning models to achieve precise segmentation, even in challenging conditions, and supports dynamic background substitution.

inputs.name: video_frames
inputs.description: The sequence of video frames to be processed for matting. This is the primary input that the node operates on, determining the foreground and background elements.

inputs.name: backbone
inputs.description: Specifies the backbone model architecture to be used for video matting, with options including 'mobilenetv3' and 'resnet50'. This choice affects the accuracy and performance of the matting process.

inputs.name: fp16
inputs.description: A flag indicating whether to use half-precision floating-point (FP16) for computations, potentially improving performance on compatible hardware.

inputs.name: bg_color
inputs.description: The background color to apply when separating the foreground from the original background, specified as a string.

inputs.name: batch_size
inputs.description: The number of frames to process in a single batch, affecting memory usage and processing speed.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The processed video frames with the background replaced or removed, showcasing the foreground elements.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: A binary mask indicating the presence of foreground elements in each frame, useful for further processing or analysis.

VHS_BatchManager.description: The BatchManager node is designed to manage and orchestrate the processing of video data in batches. It facilitates the efficient handling of large video datasets by breaking them down into smaller, manageable batches for processing, thereby optimizing resource utilization and improving performance.

inputs.name: frames_per_batch
inputs.description: Specifies the number of frames to be processed in each batch. This parameter is essential for controlling the batch size and thus directly influences the processing efficiency and resource allocation.

outputs.name: meta_batch
outputs.description: Returns the updated meta information about the batch after processing, which includes details such as the current state and any data associated with the batch.

VHS_DuplicateImages.description: The `VHS_DuplicateImages` node is designed to create multiple copies of a given image batch, effectively duplicating the images a specified number of times. This functionality is crucial for operations requiring augmented data or increased dataset size without new data generation.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: Specifies the batch of images to be duplicated. This input is central to the node's operation, determining the base data that will be replicated.

inputs.name: multiply_by
inputs.description: Determines the number of times the input images are duplicated. This parameter directly influences the output dataset size, allowing for flexible data augmentation.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: The duplicated batch of images, expanded according to the `multiply_by` parameter.

outputs.name: count
outputs.description: The total number of images in the duplicated batch, providing a straightforward count of the output dataset size.

VHS_DuplicateLatents.description: The `VHS_DuplicateLatents` node is designed to replicate a batch of latent representations a specified number of times. This functionality is crucial for operations that require augmenting the amount of data without altering its inherent properties, such as in data augmentation processes or when preparing data for batch processing in machine learning models.

inputs.name: latents
inputs.description: The `latents` parameter represents the input latent representations to be duplicated. It is essential for specifying the data that will undergo replication.

inputs.name: multiply_by
inputs.description: The `multiply_by` parameter determines the number of times the input latents are replicated. It plays a critical role in scaling the dataset according to the desired augmentation factor.

outputs.name: LATENT
outputs.description: The output latent representations, duplicated according to the `multiply_by` parameter.

outputs.name: count
outputs.description: The total count of latent representations after duplication, providing a straightforward way to understand the scale of the output data.

VHS_DuplicateMasks.description: The `VHS_DuplicateMasks` node is designed to replicate a given mask tensor a specified number of times, effectively creating a batch of identical masks. This functionality is crucial for operations requiring multiple instances of the same mask, such as batch processing or data augmentation in video and image editing workflows.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The `mask` parameter represents the input tensor to be duplicated. It is central to the node's operation, as it defines the mask that will be replicated across the new batch.

inputs.name: multiply_by
inputs.description: The `multiply_by` parameter specifies the number of times the input mask should be duplicated. This allows for dynamic adjustment of the batch size based on the needs of the workflow.

outputs.name: MASK
outputs.description: The duplicated mask batch, consisting of multiple copies of the input mask.

outputs.name: count
outputs.description: The total number of masks in the duplicated batch, providing a straightforward way to track batch size.

VHS_GetImageCount.description: The `VHS_GetImageCount` node is designed to count the number of images in a given batch. It serves as a utility within the Video Helper Suite to facilitate operations that require knowledge of batch size, such as splitting or merging batches.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The `images` parameter represents the batch of images whose count is to be determined. It is crucial for calculating the total number of images present, which impacts subsequent operations that depend on batch size.

outputs.name: count
outputs.description: The `count` output represents the total number of images in the input batch. This information is essential for managing image batches and planning further processing steps.

VHS_GetLatentCount.description: This node is designed to count the number of latent representations present in a given input. It provides a straightforward way to quantify the size of latent batches, facilitating operations that require knowledge of batch dimensions.

inputs.name: latents
inputs.description: Represents the latent representations to be counted. This input is crucial for determining the total number of latents in the batch, which directly influences the node's output.

outputs.name: count
outputs.description: The total number of latent representations in the input batch. This output is essential for understanding the size of the latent batch and for further processing that depends on batch size.

VHS_GetMaskCount.description: The `VHS_GetMaskCount` node is designed to count the number of masks in a given batch. It provides a straightforward way to quantify the number of mask elements, facilitating operations that require knowledge of batch size or element count.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The `mask` parameter represents the batch of masks for which the count is to be determined. It is crucial for understanding the scale of operations or adjustments needed based on the batch size.

outputs.name: count
outputs.description: The `count` output represents the total number of masks in the input batch. This information is essential for batch processing or for scaling operations according to the batch size.

VHS_LoadAudio.description: The VHS_LoadAudio node is designed for loading audio files within the Video Helper Suite, allowing users to input audio files from specified paths and optionally seek to a certain point within the audio file. This functionality is crucial for tasks that involve audio processing or synchronization with video content, providing a foundational tool for audio manipulation in multimedia projects.

inputs.name: audio_file
inputs.description: Specifies the path to the audio file to be loaded. The node supports a variety of audio formats, including wav, mp3, ogg, m4a, and flac, making it versatile for different audio processing needs.

inputs.name: seek_seconds
inputs.description: Defines the number of seconds to seek into the audio file before starting to load, allowing for precise control over the portion of the audio that is processed. This is useful for skipping unwanted content at the beginning of an audio file or for focusing on a specific segment.

outputs.name: audio
outputs.description: Returns a handle to the loaded audio, enabling further processing or analysis. This output is essential for integrating audio content into multimedia applications or workflows.

VHS_LoadAudioUpload.description: The VHS_LoadAudioUpload node is designed for uploading and processing audio files within the Video Helper Suite. It allows users to upload audio files, specifying the desired starting point and duration for processing. This node is essential for integrating audio content into video projects, enabling precise control over the audio segment to be used.

inputs.name: audio
inputs.description: Specifies the audio file to be uploaded from a predefined list of available files. This selection is crucial for determining the specific audio content to be processed.

inputs.name: start_time
inputs.description: Determines the starting point, in seconds, from which the audio file should be processed. This parameter allows for selective use of audio content within a larger file.

inputs.name: duration
inputs.description: Specifies the duration, in seconds, for which the audio from the starting point should be processed. This enables precise control over the segment of the audio file to be used.

outputs.name: audio
outputs.description: Returns the processed audio segment, allowing it to be integrated into video projects or further manipulated.

VHS_LoadImages.description: The node 'VHS_LoadImages' is designed for loading a batch of images from a directory, processing them according to specified parameters such as image load cap, skipping initial images, and selecting every nth image. It facilitates the handling of image data for further processing or analysis within a video helper suite, streamlining the workflow for video and image manipulation tasks.

inputs.name: directory
inputs.description: Specifies the directory path from which images are to be loaded. It is crucial for determining the source of the images to be processed.

inputs.name: image_load_cap
inputs.description: Limits the number of images to be loaded from the directory, optimizing resource usage and processing time.

inputs.name: skip_first_images
inputs.description: Skips a specified number of initial images in the directory, allowing for flexible data handling and selection.

inputs.name: select_every_nth
inputs.description: Loads every nth image from the directory, providing a mechanism for sampling or reducing the dataset size.

inputs.name: meta_batch
inputs.description: Optional parameter for integrating with a meta batch processing system, enabling batch processing of images.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: The processed images loaded from the directory, ready for further manipulation or analysis.

outputs.name: MASK
outputs.description: Generated masks for the loaded images, applicable when images have an alpha channel for transparency.

outputs.name: frame_count
outputs.description: The total number of images successfully loaded and processed.

VHS_LoadImagesPath.description: This node is designed for loading a batch of images from a specified directory path. It streamlines the process of importing multiple images into the workflow, facilitating batch processing and manipulation of image data within the video helper suite.

inputs.name: directory
inputs.description: The directory path from which images are to be loaded. This parameter is crucial for specifying the source of the images, thereby enabling the node to retrieve and process the image files located at the given path.

inputs.name: image_load_cap
inputs.description: Limits the number of images to be loaded from the directory, allowing for control over the batch size for processing.

inputs.name: skip_first_images
inputs.description: Skips a specified number of images from the beginning of the directory, useful for starting the loading process from a certain point.

inputs.name: select_every_nth
inputs.description: Loads every nth image from the directory, providing a means to sample the images at a specified interval.

inputs.name: meta_batch
inputs.description: A reference to a batch manager object that handles meta information about the batch processing, such as tracking the progress and managing resources.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: A batch of images loaded from the specified directory path. This output is essential for subsequent image processing or analysis tasks, providing a collection of images ready for manipulation or examination.

outputs.name: MASK
outputs.description: A batch of masks corresponding to the loaded images, used for image segmentation or editing tasks.

outputs.name: frame_count
outputs.description: The total number of frames (images) loaded from the directory, indicating the size of the batch processed.

VHS_LoadVideo.description: The VHS_LoadVideo node is designed to facilitate the loading of video files into a processing pipeline, handling tasks such as decoding video data, extracting frames, and optionally applying transformations like resizing or frame rate adjustment. It serves as a foundational component within the Video Helper Suite, enabling subsequent video analysis, manipulation, or enhancement operations.

inputs.name: video
inputs.description: Specifies the path to the video file to be loaded. It is crucial for locating and accessing the video data for processing.

inputs.name: force_rate
inputs.description: Determines the frame rate to which the video should be adjusted during loading. This parameter allows for standardizing the frame rate across different videos.

inputs.name: force_size
inputs.description: Indicates the desired resolution to which video frames should be resized. This can be essential for ensuring consistency in frame dimensions across various processing steps.

inputs.name: custom_width
inputs.description: Specifies the custom width for resizing video frames. This parameter works in conjunction with custom_height to define the new dimensions.

inputs.name: custom_height
inputs.description: Specifies the custom height for resizing video frames, used together with custom_width to set the target frame size.

inputs.name: frame_load_cap
inputs.description: Limits the number of frames to be loaded from the video, useful for processing long videos or for sampling purposes.

inputs.name: skip_first_frames
inputs.description: Skips a specified number of frames at the beginning of the video. This can be useful for bypassing non-relevant content or intros.

inputs.name: select_every_nth
inputs.description: Loads every Nth frame from the video, allowing for temporal downsampling and reducing the total number of frames processed.

inputs.name: meta_batch
inputs.description: Defines a batch processing context for the video, enabling efficient handling of video frames in groups.

inputs.name: vae
inputs.description: Optionally specifies a variational autoencoder model for processing the video frames, potentially for tasks like dimensionality reduction or feature extraction.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: The processed video frames, potentially resized or otherwise transformed, ready for further processing.

outputs.name: frame_count
outputs.description: The total number of frames loaded from the video, after applying any specified filters or limits.

outputs.name: audio
outputs.description: The extracted audio track from the video, if applicable and requested.

outputs.name: video_info
outputs.description: Metadata about the video and the loading process, including original and loaded frame rates, dimensions, and duration.

outputs.name: LATENT
outputs.description: The representation of video frames in a latent space, if a variational autoencoder (VAE) is used during the loading process.

VHS_LoadVideoPath.description: This node is designed to load video files from a specified path, applying various preprocessing steps such as resizing, frame rate adjustment, and optional VAE encoding. It facilitates the extraction and manipulation of video data for further processing or analysis within the Video Helper Suite.

inputs.name: video
inputs.description: The path to the video file to be loaded. It is crucial for locating and accessing the video data for processing.

inputs.name: force_rate
inputs.description: Specifies the target frame rate to which the video should be adjusted. This parameter is essential for standardizing the frame rate across different videos.

inputs.name: force_size
inputs.description: Defines the target resolution for the video. This parameter is key in resizing the video to a specific dimension.

inputs.name: custom_width
inputs.description: The custom width to which the video should be resized. This allows for precise control over the video's width dimension.

inputs.name: custom_height
inputs.description: The custom height to which the video should be resized. This allows for precise control over the video's height dimension.

inputs.name: frame_load_cap
inputs.description: Limits the number of frames to be loaded from the video. This parameter helps in managing memory usage by restricting the frame count.

inputs.name: skip_first_frames
inputs.description: The number of initial frames to skip. This is useful for bypassing unneeded content at the beginning of the video.

inputs.name: select_every_nth
inputs.description: Determines the interval at which frames are selected. By choosing every nth frame, it reduces the total number of frames processed and can help in focusing on specific segments of the video.

inputs.name: meta_batch
inputs.description: unknown

inputs.name: vae
inputs.description: unknown

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: The processed frames of the video, potentially resized and adjusted according to the specified frame rate and dimensions.

outputs.name: frame_count
outputs.description: The total number of frames loaded and processed from the video.

outputs.name: audio
outputs.description: The extracted audio track from the video, adjusted according to the specified frame selection parameters.

outputs.name: video_info
outputs.description: Metadata about the video, including both source and loaded properties such as frame rate, duration, and dimensions.

outputs.name: LATENT
outputs.description: The optional VAE-encoded representation of the video frames, if a VAE model is applied.

VHS_MergeImages.description: The VHS_MergeImages node is designed for combining two sets of images into a single set, allowing for flexible manipulation of image batches within the Video Helper Suite. It supports various strategies for merging, including matching dimensions by selecting the larger or smaller set, or explicitly choosing one set's dimensions to match. Additionally, it offers scaling and cropping options to ensure the merged images meet specific requirements.

inputs.name: images_A
inputs.description: The first set of images to be merged. This set can either serve as the template for merging or be adjusted to match the dimensions of the second set, depending on the chosen merge strategy.

inputs.name: images_B
inputs.description: The second set of images to be merged with the first. Depending on the merge strategy, these images may be scaled or cropped to match the dimensions of the first set.

inputs.name: merge_strategy
inputs.description: Determines how the dimensions of the two image sets are matched during the merge process. Options include matching to the first set, the second set, the smaller or larger dimensions among them.

inputs.name: scale_method
inputs.description: Specifies the scaling algorithm to be used when adjusting the dimensions of one image set to match the other. Options include nearest-exact, bilinear, area, bicubic, and bislerp.

inputs.name: crop
inputs.description: Defines the cropping method to be applied if necessary during the scaling process. Options are 'disabled' for no cropping or 'center' for center-based cropping.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: The resulting set of merged images.

outputs.name: count
outputs.description: The total number of images in the merged set.

VHS_MergeLatents.description: The VHS_MergeLatents node is designed for combining two sets of latents into a single set, applying various strategies for handling differences in dimensions and ensuring the merged set is suitable for further processing or generation tasks. It incorporates scaling and cropping methods to align the latents' dimensions before merging, making it a versatile tool in the manipulation and preparation of latent representations.

inputs.name: latents_A
inputs.description: The first set of latents to be merged. It plays a crucial role in the merging process, potentially serving as the template for dimension matching and scaling.

inputs.name: latents_B
inputs.description: The second set of latents to be merged. Depending on the merge strategy, it may be scaled to match the dimensions of the first set before merging.

inputs.name: merge_strategy
inputs.description: Determines how the dimensions of the two latent sets are matched before merging, allowing for flexible handling of varying sizes.

inputs.name: scale_method
inputs.description: Specifies the method used for scaling latents to match dimensions, offering options like nearest-exact, bilinear, and bicubic among others.

inputs.name: crop
inputs.description: Defines the cropping method to be applied after scaling, if necessary, to ensure the dimensions are exactly aligned.

outputs.name: LATENT
outputs.description: The merged set of latents, ready for further processing or generation tasks.

outputs.name: count
outputs.description: The total number of latents in the merged set, providing a quick reference to the size of the output.

VHS_MergeMasks.description: This node is designed to merge two mask batches into a single batch, applying a specified merge strategy to handle size discrepancies and scaling between the masks. It facilitates the combination of mask data, ensuring compatibility and uniformity across different mask dimensions for further processing or analysis.

inputs.name: mask_A
inputs.description: The first mask batch to be merged. It plays a crucial role in determining the base template for merging when certain strategies are applied.

inputs.name: mask_B
inputs.description: The second mask batch to be merged. Depending on the merge strategy, it can either serve as the template for resizing or be resized to match the first mask batch.

inputs.name: merge_strategy
inputs.description: Defines the strategy for handling size discrepancies between the two mask batches. It dictates whether to match the size of the first mask, the second mask, or the larger/smaller of the two.

inputs.name: scale_method
inputs.description: Specifies the method to be used for scaling the masks during the merge process, ensuring that the masks are appropriately resized according to the merge strategy.

inputs.name: crop
inputs.description: Determines whether and how to crop the masks after scaling, to ensure they fit the desired dimensions.

outputs.name: MASK
outputs.description: The merged mask batch, resulting from the combination of the two input masks according to the specified merge strategy and scaling method.

outputs.name: count
outputs.description: The total number of masks in the merged batch, providing a count of the output masks for further processing or analysis.

VHS_PruneOutputs.description: The `VHS_PruneOutputs` node is designed to selectively delete files based on specified criteria, aiming to streamline the output directory by removing intermediate or unnecessary files. This functionality is crucial for managing disk space and organizing project outputs more efficiently.

inputs.name: filenames
inputs.description: Specifies the filenames to consider for pruning. The selection criteria applied to these filenames determine which files are deleted, impacting the node's execution and the cleanup of the output directory.

inputs.name: options
inputs.description: Defines the criteria for pruning files, such as deleting only intermediate files, both intermediate and utility files, or all specified files. This option directly influences which files are pruned, tailoring the cleanup process to the user's needs.

VHS_SelectEveryNthImage.description: The node 'VHS_SelectEveryNthImage' is designed to filter a batch of images by selecting every nth image from the batch, optionally skipping a specified number of initial images. This functionality is useful for thinning out image datasets or sequences to reduce processing load or to select a subset of images for analysis or display.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The 'images' parameter represents the batch of images to be filtered. It is crucial for determining which images are selected for output based on the specified selection criteria.

inputs.name: select_every_nth
inputs.description: This parameter specifies the interval at which images are selected from the batch. It plays a key role in determining the density of the output image subset.

inputs.name: skip_first_images
inputs.description: Defines the number of initial images to skip before starting the selection process. This allows for greater control over which images are included in the output subset.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: The output consists of a subset of images selected according to the specified criteria.

outputs.name: count
outputs.description: The total number of images selected and returned by the node.

VHS_SelectEveryNthLatent.description: This node is designed to selectively filter latents from a given batch based on specified criteria, effectively thinning the batch to include every nth latent while optionally skipping a number of initial latents. It's particularly useful for reducing the size of a latent batch or for sampling at regular intervals within a batch.

inputs.name: latents
inputs.description: The input latent batch to be filtered. This parameter is crucial as it determines the subset of latents that will be selected based on the other criteria.

inputs.name: select_every_nth
inputs.description: Determines the interval at which latents are selected from the batch. For example, a value of 2 would select every second latent in the batch.

inputs.name: skip_first_latents
inputs.description: Specifies the number of initial latents to skip before beginning the selection process. This allows for more control over which latents are included in the resulting subset.

outputs.name: LATENT
outputs.description: The filtered subset of latents after applying the selection criteria.

outputs.name: count
outputs.description: The total number of latents in the filtered subset, providing a quick reference to the size of the output batch.

VHS_SelectEveryNthMask.description: The node is designed to filter a batch of masks by selecting every Nth mask from the sequence, optionally skipping a specified number of initial masks. This functionality is useful for thinning out dense sequences of masks to reduce computational load or to select masks at a regular interval for processing or analysis.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The input tensor containing a batch of masks from which the node will select every Nth mask. This parameter is crucial for defining the subset of masks to be processed.

inputs.name: select_every_nth
inputs.description: Specifies the interval at which masks are selected from the input batch. A higher value thins out the sequence more by selecting masks less frequently.

inputs.name: skip_first_masks
inputs.description: Determines the number of initial masks to skip before starting to select every Nth mask. This allows for the exclusion of a certain number of masks from the beginning of the sequence.

outputs.name: MASK
outputs.description: The output tensor containing the selected masks after applying the specified interval and skip criteria.

outputs.name: count
outputs.description: The total number of masks selected and returned by the node.

VHS_SplitImages.description: The VHS_SplitImages node is designed to divide a batch of images into two groups based on a specified index. This functionality is essential for workflows that require the separation of image data for further processing or analysis.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The 'images' parameter represents the batch of images to be split. It is crucial for determining how the images are divided into two groups.

inputs.name: split_index
inputs.description: The 'split_index' parameter specifies the index at which the batch of images is split. It plays a pivotal role in defining the boundary between the two resulting groups of images.

outputs.name: IMAGE_A
outputs.description: The first group of images obtained after the split.

outputs.name: A_count
outputs.description: The count of images in the first group after the split.

outputs.name: IMAGE_B
outputs.description: The second group of images obtained after the split.

outputs.name: B_count
outputs.description: The count of images in the second group after the split.

VHS_SplitLatents.description: The VHS_SplitLatents node is designed to divide a batch of latents into two groups based on a specified index. This functionality is essential for managing and manipulating latent batches within video processing workflows, allowing for flexible dataset segmentation and targeted processing of latent representations.

inputs.name: latents
inputs.description: The 'latents' parameter represents the batch of latent vectors to be split. It is crucial for determining the composition of the resulting groups post-split, affecting the node's execution and outcomes.

inputs.name: split_index
inputs.description: The 'split_index' parameter specifies the position at which the batch of latents should be divided. It plays a pivotal role in determining the size and content of the two resulting latent groups, impacting the node's functionality.

outputs.name: LATENT_A
outputs.description: Represents the first group of latent vectors obtained after the split, based on the provided split index.

outputs.name: A_count
outputs.description: Indicates the count of latent vectors in the first group post-split.

outputs.name: LATENT_B
outputs.description: Denotes the second group of latent vectors obtained after the split, following the provided split index.

outputs.name: B_count
outputs.description: Specifies the count of latent vectors in the second group post-split.

VHS_SplitMasks.description: The VHS_SplitMasks node is designed for dividing a batch of masks into two groups based on a specified index. This functionality is essential for managing and manipulating mask data in video processing tasks, allowing for flexible dataset segmentation and targeted processing of mask subsets.

inputs.name: mask
