inputs.description: The 'mask' parameter represents the batch of masks to be split. It is crucial for determining how the masks are divided into two groups, affecting the node's execution and the composition of the output groups.

inputs.name: split_index
inputs.description: The 'split_index' parameter specifies the index at which the batch of masks is divided. It plays a pivotal role in determining the boundary between the two output groups, influencing the distribution of masks in the segmentation process.

outputs.name: MASK_A
outputs.description: The first group of masks obtained after splitting the original batch at the specified index.

outputs.name: A_count
outputs.description: The count of masks in the first group after the split.

outputs.name: MASK_B
outputs.description: The second group of masks obtained after splitting the original batch at the specified index.

outputs.name: B_count
outputs.description: The count of masks in the second group after the split.

VHS_VAEDecodeBatched.description: This node is designed for batch processing of latent representations to decode them into images using a Variational Autoencoder (VAE). It efficiently handles large sets of latent samples by decoding them in smaller, manageable batches, updating progress through a progress bar for better user experience.

inputs.name: samples
inputs.description: The latent representations to be decoded into images. This input is crucial for the node's operation as it specifies the data that will undergo the decoding process.

inputs.name: vae
inputs.description: The Variational Autoencoder model used for decoding the latent representations into images. It defines the specific VAE architecture and parameters to be used in the decoding process.

inputs.name: per_batch
inputs.description: Specifies the number of samples to be decoded in each batch. This allows for efficient memory management and processing speed by breaking down the workload into smaller chunks.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The decoded images from the latent representations. This output provides the visual content generated by the VAE model from the input latent samples.

VHS_VAEEncodeBatched.description: This node is designed for batch processing of images through a Variational Autoencoder (VAE) to encode them into a latent space representation. It efficiently handles large sets of images by dividing them into smaller batches, encoding each batch separately, and then aggregating the results. This approach optimizes resource utilization and accelerates the encoding process, making it suitable for applications requiring the transformation of images into their latent representations for further processing or analysis.

inputs.name: pixels
inputs.description: The 'pixels' parameter represents the images to be encoded into latent space. It is crucial for defining the input data that will undergo the encoding process, directly influencing the node's output by determining the characteristics of the generated latent representations.

inputs.name: vae
inputs.description: The 'vae' parameter specifies the Variational Autoencoder model to be used for encoding the images. It plays a pivotal role in the transformation process, as the model's architecture and trained parameters directly affect the quality and characteristics of the encoded latent space.

inputs.name: per_batch
inputs.description: The 'per_batch' parameter determines the number of images to be processed in each batch. It allows for flexible control over the batch size, balancing between computational efficiency and resource consumption.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The output is a latent space representation of the input images, encoded by the specified VAE model. This representation is crucial for downstream tasks that require a compressed yet informative version of the original data.

VHS_VideoCombine.description: The VHS_VideoCombine node is designed for creating animated videos or GIFs by combining multiple images or latent representations. It supports various customization options such as frame rate adjustment, looping, format selection, and the inclusion of audio. This node is part of the Video Helper Suite, aimed at facilitating video processing and generation tasks.

inputs.name: frame_rate
inputs.description: Specifies the frame rate for the video or GIF, affecting how smoothly the animation plays.

inputs.name: loop_count
inputs.description: Determines how many times the animation will loop, with support for infinite looping.

inputs.name: filename_prefix
inputs.description: The prefix for the output file name, allowing for easy identification of generated files.

inputs.name: format
inputs.description: The output format of the generated video or GIF, such as 'mp4' or 'gif'. Includes additional formats supported by ffmpeg.

inputs.name: pingpong
inputs.description: When enabled, the animation will play forwards and then backwards, creating a seamless looping effect.

inputs.name: save_output
inputs.description: Controls whether the generated video or GIF is saved to disk.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: An optional list of images to be combined into a video or GIF. If not provided, latents may be used instead.

inputs.name: audio
inputs.description: An optional audio file to be included in the video, enhancing the multimedia experience.

inputs.name: meta_batch
inputs.description: Metadata associated with the batch of images or latents being processed, useful for batch operations.

inputs.name: vae
inputs.description: The VAE model used for decoding latent representations into images, necessary when latents are provided.

inputs.name: latents
inputs.description: An optional list of latent representations to be converted into images for the video or GIF. Requires a VAE model to decode.

outputs.name: Filenames
outputs.description: The filenames of the generated videos or GIFs, indicating where the output files have been saved.

VHS_VideoInfo.description: The VHS_VideoInfo node is designed to extract and provide detailed information about a video file, focusing on key attributes that define its playback and visual characteristics. This node serves as a foundational element within the Video Helper Suite, enabling users to gain insights into video metadata essential for processing and manipulation tasks.

inputs.name: video_info
inputs.description: This parameter is essential as it carries the video metadata which the node uses to extract and analyze key video attributes, impacting the node's ability to provide comprehensive video information.

outputs.name: source_fps🟨
outputs.description: The frame rate of the source video, indicating how many frames are displayed per second.

outputs.name: source_frame_count🟨
outputs.description: The total number of frames in the source video.

outputs.name: source_duration🟨
outputs.description: The total duration of the source video in seconds.

outputs.name: source_width🟨
outputs.description: The width of the source video in pixels.

outputs.name: source_height🟨
outputs.description: The height of the source video in pixels.

outputs.name: loaded_fps🟦
outputs.description: The frame rate of the loaded video, indicating how many frames are displayed per second.

outputs.name: loaded_frame_count🟦
outputs.description: The total number of frames in the loaded video.

outputs.name: loaded_duration🟦
outputs.description: The total duration of the loaded video in seconds.

outputs.name: loaded_width🟦
outputs.description: The width of the loaded video in pixels.

outputs.name: loaded_height🟦
outputs.description: The height of the loaded video in pixels.

VHS_VideoInfoLoaded.description: The VHS_VideoInfoLoaded node is designed to extract and present detailed information about a video that has been loaded into the system. It focuses on providing metrics such as frame rate, frame count, video duration, and the dimensions of the video, facilitating a comprehensive understanding of the video's properties.

inputs.name: video_info
inputs.description: The 'video_info' parameter is crucial as it contains the loaded video's metadata, which is essential for extracting the video's detailed information such as fps, frame count, duration, width, and height. This metadata drives the node's execution and results.

outputs.name: fps🟦
outputs.description: Represents the frame rate of the loaded video.

outputs.name: frame_count🟦
outputs.description: Indicates the total number of frames in the loaded video.

outputs.name: duration🟦
outputs.description: The total duration of the loaded video, typically in seconds.

outputs.name: width🟦
outputs.description: The width of the loaded video in pixels.

outputs.name: height🟦
outputs.description: The height of the loaded video in pixels.

VHS_VideoInfoSource.description: The VHS_VideoInfoSource node is designed to extract and provide detailed information about the source video's characteristics, such as frame rate, frame count, duration, width, and height. It abstracts the complexity of video metadata extraction, offering a straightforward way to access essential video properties for further processing or analysis within the Video Helper Suite.

inputs.name: video_info
inputs.description: The 'video_info' parameter is essential for the operation of this node, as it contains the metadata of the source video from which information like fps, frame count, duration, width, and height are extracted. This metadata is crucial for accurately understanding and manipulating the video content.

outputs.name: fps🟨
outputs.description: Frames per second of the source video, indicating the video's playback speed.

outputs.name: frame_count🟨
outputs.description: Total number of frames in the source video.

outputs.name: duration🟨
outputs.description: Total duration of the source video, typically in seconds.

outputs.name: width🟨
outputs.description: Width of the video in pixels.

outputs.name: height🟨
outputs.description: Height of the video in pixels.

WD14Tagger_pysssss.description: The WD14Tagger node is designed to analyze images and generate tags based on their content, utilizing a model trained for this purpose. It supports customization of the tagging process through various parameters, allowing for tailored outputs that can include or exclude specific tags, adjust sensitivity thresholds, and format the output according to user preferences.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image to be analyzed and tagged. This is the primary input for the tagging process.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: Specifies the model to use for tagging. The node supports using different models, allowing for flexibility in the tagging process based on available models.

inputs.name: threshold
inputs.description: Sets the minimum confidence level for general tags to be included in the output. Helps filter out less relevant tags.

inputs.name: character_threshold
inputs.description: Sets the minimum confidence level for character-specific tags to be included in the output. This allows for more precise control over which character tags are considered relevant.

inputs.name: replace_underscore
inputs.description: Determines whether underscores in tags should be replaced with spaces, affecting the readability of the output tags.

inputs.name: trailing_comma
inputs.description: Controls whether a trailing comma is added to the tags in the output, influencing the formatting of the generated tag string.

inputs.name: exclude_tags
inputs.description: Allows specifying tags to be excluded from the output, enabling users to filter out unwanted or irrelevant tags.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The output type 'string' represents the formatted string of generated tags for the image, which was not explicitly listed but is implied by the node's functionality.

BNK_AddCLIPSDXLParams.description: This node is designed to augment the conditioning data with additional parameters related to image dimensions and cropping. It enriches the conditioning context by specifying width, height, crop width, crop height, target width, and target height, facilitating more precise control over the image generation process.

inputs.name: conditioning
inputs.description: The conditioning data to be augmented with image dimension and cropping parameters. It plays a crucial role in defining the context for image generation.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Specifies the width of the image. It affects the conditioning by setting a specific dimension for image generation.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Specifies the height of the image, contributing to the conditioning by defining a specific dimension for image generation.

inputs.name: crop_w
inputs.description: Determines the width of the crop area, allowing for more focused image generation based on the specified region.

inputs.name: crop_h
inputs.description: Determines the height of the crop area, enabling more targeted image generation based on the specified region.

inputs.name: target_width
inputs.description: Sets the target width for the image generation, influencing the final dimensions of the generated image.

inputs.name: target_height
inputs.description: Sets the target height for the image generation, impacting the final dimensions of the generated image.

outputs.name: conditioning
outputs.description: The augmented conditioning data, now including specific image dimensions and cropping parameters, ready for use in further processing.

BNK_AddCLIPSDXLRParams.description: This node is designed to enhance the conditioning data for image generation by incorporating additional parameters such as width, height, and an aesthetic score. It operates by iterating over a list of conditioning elements, modifying each with the specified dimensions and aesthetic score, thereby preparing the data for more tailored and aesthetically pleasing image generation.

inputs.name: conditioning
inputs.description: The base conditioning data for image generation, which this node modifies by adding width, height, and an aesthetic score to each element.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Specifies the width to be added to the conditioning data, influencing the dimensions of the generated image.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Specifies the height to be added to the conditioning data, influencing the dimensions of the generated image.

inputs.name: ascore
inputs.description: An aesthetic score to be added to the conditioning data, aiming to guide the image generation towards more visually appealing results.

outputs.name: conditioning
outputs.description: The enhanced conditioning data, now including specified width, height, and aesthetic score for each element.

BNK_CLIPTextEncodeAdvanced.description: This node specializes in generating advanced CLIP text embeddings by processing input text with options for token normalization and weight interpretation strategies. It aims to enhance text representation for conditioning in generative models.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The input text to be encoded. It supports multiline input, allowing for more complex and detailed text representations.

inputs.name: clip
inputs.description: A CLIP model instance used for text tokenization and embedding generation.

inputs.name: token_normalization
inputs.description: Specifies the method for normalizing token embeddings, offering options like none, mean, length, and length+mean to adjust the embedding process.

inputs.name: weight_interpretation
inputs.description: Defines the strategy for interpreting the weights of token embeddings, with options including comfy, A1111, compel, comfy++, and down_weight.

outputs.name: conditioning
outputs.description: The output is a conditioning format suitable for generative models, including the advanced CLIP text embeddings and optional pooled output.

BNK_CLIPTextEncodeSDXLAdvanced.description: This node specializes in generating advanced CLIP text embeddings for Stable Diffusion XL models, incorporating dual text inputs for local and global context, token normalization strategies, and weight interpretation methods to fine-tune the conditioning process.

inputs.name: text_l
inputs.description: The local context text input, allowing for detailed specification of parts of the image.

inputs.name: text_g
inputs.description: The global context text input, providing an overarching theme or setting for the image.

inputs.name: clip
inputs.description: A CLIP model instance used for text and image embeddings.

inputs.name: token_normalization
inputs.description: Specifies the method for normalizing token weights, affecting the emphasis of certain words or phrases.

inputs.name: weight_interpretation
inputs.description: Defines how weights are interpreted, influencing the final embedding by adjusting the significance of certain tokens.

inputs.name: balance
inputs.description: A float value determining the balance between local and global text embeddings in the final output.

outputs.name: conditioning
outputs.description: The output is a conditioning object containing the advanced CLIP text embeddings, tailored for Stable Diffusion XL models.

AdaptiveThresholding.description: The AdaptiveThresholding node applies adaptive thresholding techniques to images, dynamically adjusting the threshold value over different regions of the image based on local image characteristics. This method is particularly useful for images with varying lighting conditions, enhancing the ability to distinguish foreground from background.

inputs.name: src
inputs.description: The source image to be thresholded. It is crucial for defining the input on which the adaptive thresholding operation will be performed.

inputs.name: max_value
inputs.description: The maximum intensity value that a pixel can have after thresholding. It determines the brightness of the foreground region in the output image.

inputs.name: adaptive_method
inputs.description: Specifies the algorithm to use for calculating the threshold for a particular region of the image. It affects how the threshold values are computed across the image.

inputs.name: threshold_type
inputs.description: Determines the type of thresholding to be applied, influencing how pixels are classified into foreground and background.

inputs.name: block_size
inputs.description: The size of the neighborhood area used to calculate the threshold for each pixel. It influences the granularity of the thresholding.

inputs.name: c
inputs.description: A constant subtracted from the mean or weighted mean calculated. It allows fine-tuning of the thresholding process.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The result of applying adaptive thresholding to the input image, enhancing the distinction between regions of different intensities.

Add String To Many.description: This node is designed to either append or prepend a given string to a list of other strings, allowing for batch processing of string manipulation tasks. It supports a dynamic number of input strings and offers flexibility in how the string is added, catering to various use cases where string concatenation or modification is required.

inputs.name: to_add
inputs.description: Specifies the string to be appended or prepended to each input string, acting as the primary modifier in the concatenation process.

inputs.name: inputs_len
inputs.description: Determines the number of input strings to which the operation will be applied, allowing for dynamic adjustment based on user needs.

inputs.name: operation
inputs.description: Controls whether the specified string is appended or prepended to the input strings, offering versatility in string manipulation.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The modified strings after the specified string has been either appended or prepended, reflecting the result of the batch string manipulation.

AddAlpha.description: The `AddAlpha` node is designed to add an alpha channel to RGB images, allowing for the manipulation of image transparency. It supports optional inversion of the alpha channel, providing flexibility in handling transparency effects.

inputs.name: rgb_image
inputs.description: The RGB image to which an alpha channel will be added. This is the primary image input for transparency manipulation.

inputs.name: alpha
inputs.description: An optional alpha channel to be added to the RGB image. If provided, it specifies the transparency levels for the image.

inputs.name: method
inputs.description: An optional method specifying how the alpha channel should be applied. It can either add the alpha channel directly or invert it, affecting the transparency effect.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The resulting image with an alpha channel added, enabling transparency manipulation.

AdjustRect.description: The AdjustRect node is designed to modify the dimensions of a rectangle based on specified parameters, ensuring the new rectangle adheres to certain constraints like center alignment and size adjustments. It abstracts the complexity of geometric transformations, offering a straightforward way to recalibrate rectangle dimensions for various applications.

inputs.name: a
inputs.description: Represents one of the coordinates (x or y) of the rectangle, contributing to defining its initial position.

inputs.name: b
inputs.description: Represents another coordinate (x or y) of the rectangle, working alongside 'a' to specify the rectangle's starting dimensions.

inputs.name: c
inputs.description: Defines one of the dimensions (width or height) of the rectangle, influencing its size before adjustment.

inputs.name: d
inputs.description: Defines another dimension (width or height) of the rectangle, used in conjunction with 'c' to determine the initial size.

inputs.name: xm
inputs.description: Specifies the factor by which the rectangle's width is adjusted, ensuring the new width is a multiple of this value.

inputs.name: ym
inputs.description: Specifies the factor by which the rectangle's height is adjusted, ensuring the new height is a multiple of this value.

inputs.name: round_mode
inputs.description: Determines the rounding method used when adjusting the rectangle's dimensions, affecting the precision of the adjustment.

inputs.name: input_format
inputs.description: Indicates the format of the input rectangle coordinates, dictating how they should be interpreted and transformed.

inputs.name: output_format
inputs.description: Specifies the format for the output rectangle coordinates, determining how the adjusted dimensions are represented.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: Each element of the output tuple represents a coordinate or dimension of the adjusted rectangle, reflecting the modifications applied to the original dimensions. The output is a tuple of integers, each specifying a part of the rectangle's adjusted geometry.

AnyToAny.description: The AnyToAny node is designed to dynamically evaluate a user-defined function on its input, allowing for a wide range of operations from simple transformations to complex computations. This flexibility enables users to apply arbitrary logic to their data, making it a versatile tool for custom data manipulation and analysis.

inputs.name: v
inputs.description: Represents the input value on which the user-defined function will be applied. Its flexibility allows for any type of data to be processed, making the node adaptable to various use cases.

inputs.name: function
inputs.description: A string representing a user-defined function to be evaluated on the input. This function is defined in a lambda expression format, enabling dynamic and complex operations on the input data.

outputs.description: The output type is dynamic, determined by the result of the user-defined function applied to the input. This allows for a wide range of possible output types, reflecting the node's versatility.

BoundingRect (contours).description: This node calculates the bounding rectangle of a contour. It is designed to provide a simple way to obtain the smallest rectangle that can fully enclose a contour. This functionality is crucial for various computer vision tasks where understanding the spatial extent of objects within an image is necessary.

inputs.name: contour
inputs.description: A single contour for which the bounding rectangle will be calculated. This input is crucial for determining the spatial boundaries of the object represented by the contour.

inputs.name: return_mode
inputs.description: Specifies the mode of calculation for the bounding rectangle, affecting the format of the returned values.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: The coordinates of the top-left corner and the dimensions of the bounding rectangle (x, y, width, height). This output provides essential spatial information about the contour.

BuildColorRangeAdvanced (hsv).description: The `BuildColorRangeAdvanced (hsv)` node is designed to create a sophisticated range of colors in the HSV color space. It leverages advanced techniques to adjust and fix the bounds of hue, saturation, and value based on given parameters, enabling precise color selection and manipulation for various computer vision tasks.

inputs.name: samples
inputs.description: Specifies the HSV color samples from which to derive the color range. It is essential for determining the base colors for range calculation.

inputs.name: hue_exp
inputs.description: Defines the expression or method to adjust the hue component of the color range. It allows for dynamic hue range adjustments based on specific criteria or algorithms.

inputs.name: sat_exp
inputs.description: Specifies the expression or method to adjust the saturation component of the color range. It enables fine-tuning of the saturation levels within the generated color range.

inputs.name: val_exp
inputs.description: Indicates the expression or method to adjust the value (brightness) component of the color range. It facilitates the manipulation of brightness levels to achieve the desired color range.

outputs.name: hsv_color
outputs.description: Returns the calculated HSV color range based on the provided expressions and samples. It represents the final color range after all adjustments have been applied.

outputs.name: combo[string]
outputs.description: Provides additional information or results related to the color range calculation, potentially including details about the applied adjustments or methods.

BuildColorRangeHSV (hsv).description: This node is designed to establish a range of HSV (Hue, Saturation, Value) colors based on provided lower and upper bounds. It adjusts these bounds to ensure they are within acceptable limits and determines the optimal hue mode for color range construction.

inputs.name: samples
inputs.description: Specifies the HSV samples from which the color range is derived, influencing the determination of lower and upper bounds.

inputs.name: percentage_modifier
inputs.description: A modifier that affects the interpolation of the HSV color range, influencing how the bounds are adjusted.

inputs.name: interval_type
inputs.description: Determines the method used for calculating the color range, affecting the selection of lower and upper bounds and the hue mode.

outputs.name: hsv_color
outputs.description: The resulting HSV color range, including both lower and upper bounds, after adjustments.

outputs.name: combo[string]
outputs.description: The determined optimal hue mode for the color range construction, based on the adjusted bounds.

ChameleonMask.description: The ChameleonMask node is designed to adaptively blend or modify images or masks based on certain criteria or conditions. It aims to provide a flexible approach to image manipulation, allowing for dynamic adjustments that cater to the specific needs of the input data.

inputs.name: dst
inputs.description: Specifies the destination image over which the source image or mask will be applied, serving as the backdrop for the operation.

inputs.name: src
inputs.description: Defines the source image or mask to be blended or modified onto the destination image.

inputs.name: thresh_blur
inputs.description: Sets the threshold for blurring, affecting the smoothness of the mask edges.

inputs.name: close_dist
inputs.description: Determines the distance for the closing operation, impacting the closure of small holes in the mask.

inputs.name: open_dist
inputs.description: Specifies the distance for the opening operation, influencing the removal of small objects from the foreground of the mask.

inputs.name: size_dist
inputs.description: Controls the size distribution for filtering, affecting the scale of features retained in the mask.

inputs.name: mask_blur
inputs.description: Defines the blur level for the mask, impacting the overall softness and blending of edges.

inputs.name: contrast_adjust
inputs.description: Adjusts the contrast of the image, enhancing or reducing the visual differences between elements.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Selects the operational mode, determining the specific blending or modification technique used.

inputs.name: output_format
inputs.description: Chooses the output format of the image, affecting the visual style and compatibility.

inputs.name: optional_roi_mask
inputs.description: An optional mask defining regions of interest, focusing the operation on specific areas of the image.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The resulting image after adaptive blending or modification, showcasing the applied effects.

CheckpointLoader (dirty).description: This node is designed to load model checkpoints in a flexible manner, accommodating potentially mismatched or loosely specified checkpoint and configuration names. It utilizes utility functions to find the best match for given checkpoint and configuration names within a specified directory, thereby streamlining the process of loading models for further use or analysis.

inputs.name: config_name
inputs.description: Specifies the configuration name to be used in conjunction with the checkpoint. The node attempts to find a matching configuration file name, enhancing flexibility in specifying configurations.

inputs.name: ckpt_name
inputs.description: Indicates the checkpoint name to be loaded. The node employs utility functions to resolve the exact checkpoint file, allowing for a more lenient specification of checkpoint names.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: Returns the loaded model object, ready for use in downstream tasks or analyses.

outputs.name: clip
outputs.description: Returns the CLIP model associated with the loaded checkpoint, if applicable and requested.

outputs.name: vae
outputs.description: Returns the VAE model associated with the loaded checkpoint, if applicable and requested.

CheckpointLoaderSimple (dirty).description: This node simplifies the process of loading model checkpoints by automatically finding and loading the appropriate checkpoint file based on a given checkpoint name. It abstracts away the complexities of locating and verifying checkpoint files, making it easier to load models for further use or analysis.

inputs.name: ckpt_name
inputs.description: Specifies the name of the checkpoint file to load. This parameter is crucial for identifying and retrieving the correct checkpoint file from a predefined list of available checkpoints.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: Returns the loaded model from the specified checkpoint.

outputs.name: clip
outputs.description: Returns the CLIP model associated with the loaded checkpoint, if available.

outputs.name: vae
outputs.description: Returns the VAE model associated with the loaded checkpoint, if available.

CLAHE.description: The CLAHE node applies the Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization algorithm to enhance the contrast of images. It adjusts image intensities to enhance the contrast, particularly useful for images with poor lighting conditions or to bring out more detail in specific areas.

inputs.name: src
inputs.description: The source image to be processed. It is the primary input for the contrast enhancement operation.

inputs.name: clip_limit
inputs.description: Defines the threshold for contrast limiting. A higher value increases contrast but may also amplify noise.

inputs.name: tile_grid_x
inputs.description: Specifies the number of tiles in the horizontal direction for the adaptive histogram equalization. Affects the granularity of contrast enhancement.

inputs.name: tile_grid_y
inputs.description: Specifies the number of tiles in the vertical direction for the adaptive histogram equalization. Affects the granularity of contrast enhancement.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image after applying CLAHE, with enhanced contrast.

CLIPEncodeMultiple.description: The CLIPEncodeMultiple node is designed to encode multiple text inputs into a conditioning format using a CLIP model. It iterates over a specified number of inputs, encoding each one separately and aggregating the results into a list of conditionings. This node is useful for scenarios where multiple textual descriptions need to be encoded in parallel and then utilized for further processing or generation tasks.

inputs.name: clip
inputs.description: The CLIP model used for encoding the text inputs. It is crucial for the text encoding process, affecting the quality and relevance of the generated conditionings.

inputs.name: inputs_len
inputs.description: Specifies the number of text inputs to encode. It determines the iteration count for the encoding process, directly influencing the output list's length.

outputs.name: conditioning
outputs.description: A list of encoded text inputs, each transformed into a conditioning format suitable for further processing or generation tasks.

CLIPEncodeMultipleAdvanced.description: This node is designed for advanced text encoding using the CLIP model, capable of processing multiple inputs simultaneously. It extends the functionality of a standard CLIP text encoding by allowing for a customizable number of inputs, each potentially undergoing a unique encoding process based on token normalization and weight interpretation. The node is optimized for scenarios requiring batch processing of text inputs for conditioning generation models, making it a versatile tool in the generation of conditioned outputs.

inputs.name: clip
inputs.description: The CLIP model used for encoding the text inputs. It plays a crucial role in determining the quality and relevance of the encoded vectors.

inputs.name: token_normalization
inputs.description: A flag indicating whether or not to normalize the tokens during the encoding process. This affects the consistency and comparability of the encoded vectors.

inputs.name: weight_interpretation
inputs.description: A parameter that influences how the weights are interpreted during the encoding process, affecting the emphasis on different aspects of the input text.

inputs.name: inputs_len
inputs.description: Specifies the number of text inputs to be encoded. This allows for dynamic adjustment of batch sizes for encoding, accommodating a variable number of inputs.

outputs.name: conditioning
outputs.description: A list of conditioning vectors generated from the input texts, tailored for use in generation models requiring conditioned inputs.

Color (hexadecimal).description: This node is designed to convert hexadecimal color codes into a format that can be utilized within the system, ensuring compatibility and proper representation of colors as defined by their hex codes. It validates the hex code format and converts it to a recognized color format for further processing or display.

inputs.name: hex
inputs.description: The hexadecimal representation of a color, starting with a '#' followed by either 3 or 6 hexadecimal characters. This input is crucial for defining the specific color to be converted and validated.

outputs.name: color
outputs.description: The validated and possibly transformed color information, maintaining the integrity of the original hexadecimal input for use in color-related operations.

Color (RGB).description: This node is designed for creating a color representation from individual red, green, and blue components. It allows for the precise specification of colors in RGB format, facilitating their use in various image processing and visualization tasks.

inputs.name: r
inputs.description: Specifies the red component of the color, contributing to the overall hue when combined with green and blue components.

inputs.name: g
inputs.description: Specifies the green component of the color, contributing to the overall hue when combined with red and blue components.

inputs.name: b
inputs.description: Specifies the blue component of the color, contributing to the overall hue when combined with red and green components.

outputs.name: color
outputs.description: The RGB representation of the input components, allowing for its use in various image processing and visualization contexts.

Color Clip (advanced).description: The Color Clip (advanced) node is designed for advanced color manipulation within images, allowing for precise color clipping and replacement based on a set of advanced parameters. It extends basic color clipping capabilities by offering additional control over the color adjustment process, enabling users to specify alternative colors and adjust the leeway for color matching.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed for color clipping and manipulation.

inputs.name: target
inputs.description: Specifies the target operation for the primary color within the image, such as converting to black, white, or doing nothing.

inputs.name: complement
inputs.description: Defines the operation for colors in the image that do not match the primary color, including converting them or leaving them unchanged.

inputs.name: color
inputs.description: The primary color to be clipped or replaced in the image.

inputs.name: color_a
inputs.description: An optional color parameter that provides an alternative color option for the clipping process.

inputs.name: color_b
inputs.description: A second optional color parameter that offers another alternative color choice for the clipping process.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The image after applying the advanced color clipping and manipulation operations.

Color Clip ADE20k.description: The Color Clip ADE20k node is designed to modify the color palette of an image based on the ADE20K dataset, allowing for the clipping of image colors to a specific class color from the dataset. It extends the functionality of a base color clipping operation by incorporating ADE20K-specific color mappings, enabling targeted color transformations for image processing tasks.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed. This image will undergo color clipping based on the specified class name and target color operations.

inputs.name: target
inputs.description: Specifies the target operation for the color clipping, such as converting to black, white, or maintaining the color.

inputs.name: complement
inputs.description: Defines the complementary operation for the color clipping, providing additional control over the color transformation process.

inputs.name: class_name
inputs.description: The name of the class from the ADE20K dataset whose color will be used for clipping. This determines the specific color to which the image's colors will be clipped.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The processed image with colors clipped according to the specified class color from the ADE20K dataset.

Color Clip.description: The Color Clip node is designed to modify the colors within an image based on specific target and complement operations, optionally allowing for advanced color manipulation through additional color parameters. It leverages color theory principles to enhance or alter the visual appearance of images, making it a versatile tool for image processing tasks that require color adjustments.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image to be processed. It serves as the primary input for color clipping operations, determining the visual content that will undergo color modifications.

inputs.name: target
inputs.description: Specifies the target operation for color clipping, influencing how colors in the image are adjusted or replaced.

inputs.name: complement
inputs.description: Defines the complement operation for color clipping, determining the alternative color adjustments or replacements in the image.

inputs.name: color
inputs.description: The reference color used for clipping operations. It plays a crucial role in defining the color adjustments to be applied to the image.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The processed image with applied color clipping operations, showcasing the adjustments or alterations made to the original colors.

ColorDictionary (custom).description: This node allows for the creation of a custom color dictionary by mapping user-defined color names to their corresponding color values. It ensures that the number of color names matches the number of color values, adjusting the lists to match in length if necessary, before returning a dictionary that associates each color name with its color value.

inputs.name: color_names
inputs.description: A list of user-defined names for colors. These names are used as keys in the resulting color dictionary, allowing for easy identification and retrieval of color values.

inputs.name: colors
inputs.description: A list of color values (typically RGB tuples) that correspond to the user-defined color names. These values are used as the dictionary values in the resulting color dictionary, mapping each name to its respective color.

outputs.name: color_dict
outputs.description: The resulting custom color dictionary, mapping each user-defined color name to its corresponding color value.

ColorDictionary.description: The ColorDictionary node provides a predefined dictionary of color names to RGB values, allowing users to retrieve a subset of these colors based on a specified number. It simplifies the process of accessing common colors for various applications by offering a default set of colors and the ability to specify how many colors are needed.

inputs.name: number_of_colors
inputs.description: Specifies the number of colors to retrieve from the predefined color dictionary. It determines the size of the returned dictionary, allowing for flexible customization of the color selection.

outputs.name: color_dict
outputs.description: Returns a dictionary mapping color names to their corresponding RGB values, limited to the specified number of colors.

Conditioning Grid (cond).description: This node is designed to apply conditioning to a grid layout, where each cell within the grid can be individually conditioned based on text inputs. It automates the process of encoding text inputs using a CLIP model and then applying these encoded conditionings to specific areas within a grid, facilitating the generation of complex, grid-based visual layouts with varied content.

inputs.name: columns
inputs.description: Specifies the number of columns in the grid, determining the grid's horizontal layout and how many cells it contains.

inputs.name: rows
inputs.description: Specifies the number of rows in the grid, determining the grid's vertical layout and how many cells it contains.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: The width of each cell in the grid, in pixels. This affects the resolution and aspect ratio of the content within each cell.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: The height of each cell in the grid, in pixels. This affects the resolution and aspect ratio of the content within each cell.

inputs.name: strength
inputs.description: Controls the intensity of the applied conditioning, allowing for fine-tuning of how prominently the text inputs influence the generated content.

inputs.name: base
inputs.description: The base text input for the grid's overall theme or background. This input sets the foundational conditioning layer upon which additional cell-specific conditionings are applied.

outputs.name: conditioning
outputs.description: The resulting conditioning for the grid, ready to be used for generating content within each cell based on the provided text inputs.

Conditioning Grid (string) Advanced.description: This node enhances the functionality of ConditioningGridCond by incorporating an advanced text encoding step for each text input using AdvancedCLIPTextEncode. It automates the process of encoding text inputs into conditionings and then applies these conditionings to a grid's AreaConditioners, facilitating a more nuanced and customizable conditioning process for grid-based operations.

inputs.name: clip
inputs.description: The CLIP model used for encoding the text inputs. It plays a crucial role in determining the quality and relevance of the generated conditionings.

inputs.name: base
inputs.description: The base text input that is encoded and used as the foundational conditioning for the grid. It sets the initial context or theme for the grid's content.

inputs.name: columns
inputs.description: Specifies the number of columns in the grid. This determines the grid's horizontal dimension and how many conditionings are applied across it.

inputs.name: rows
inputs.description: Specifies the number of rows in the grid. This determines the grid's vertical dimension and how many conditionings are applied along it.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: The width of each grid cell. This affects the spatial resolution of the conditionings applied within the grid.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: The height of each grid cell. This affects the spatial resolution of the conditionings applied within the grid.

inputs.name: strength
inputs.description: Determines the intensity or influence of the conditioning on the grid. It modulates how strongly the encoded texts affect the grid's output.

inputs.name: token_normalization
inputs.description: Specifies the method for normalizing the tokens in the text encoding process, affecting the conditioning's consistency and balance.

inputs.name: weight_interpretation
inputs.description: Defines how the weights are interpreted in the text encoding process, influencing the emphasis and distribution of the conditioning across the grid.

outputs.name: conditioning
outputs.description: The resulting conditioning that combines the encoded base text and grid-specific conditionings, ready for further processing or application.

Conditioning Grid (string).description: This node automates the process of generating conditionings for a grid layout by encoding text inputs using ClipTextEncode and then applying these conditionings to the grid's AreaConditioners. It simplifies the creation of complex conditioning structures for grid-based layouts, making it easier to customize and generate content based on textual descriptions.

inputs.name: clip
inputs.description: The CLIP model used for encoding the text inputs. It's crucial for converting textual descriptions into a format that can be utilized for conditioning the grid.

inputs.name: base
inputs.description: A base text input that serves as the foundational conditioning for the entire grid. It's encoded and applied to set a baseline for further customization.

inputs.name: columns
inputs.description: Specifies the number of columns in the grid, determining its horizontal structure.

inputs.name: rows
inputs.description: Defines the number of rows in the grid, shaping its vertical layout.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: The width of each cell in the grid, affecting the resolution and detail of the conditioned content.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: The height of each cell in the grid, influencing the vertical resolution and detail of the conditioned content.

inputs.name: strength
inputs.description: Controls the intensity of the applied conditioning, allowing for fine-tuning of the grid's overall effect.

outputs.name: conditioning
outputs.description: The resulting conditioning structure for the grid, ready to be used for generating content based on the encoded text inputs.

Contour To Mask.description: The Contour To Mask node transforms a given contour into a mask on the specified image, allowing for the visualization or application of contours in image processing tasks. It supports customization of the output image format.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image on which the contour will be drawn to create a mask. It serves as the canvas for the contour transformation.

inputs.name: contour
inputs.description: The contour to be transformed into a mask on the image. This parameter defines the shape and location of the mask.

inputs.name: output_format
inputs.description: Specifies the desired output image format, allowing for flexibility in how the resulting masked image is encoded or saved.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is an image with the specified contour transformed into a mask, reflecting the shape and position of the contour on the original image.

Contours.description: The Contours node is designed to identify and extract contours from an image based on specified retrieval and approximation modes. It converts the input image to grayscale, applies thresholding if necessary, and utilizes OpenCV's findContours method to detect contours, providing a foundational step for further image analysis or manipulation.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image tensor that contours will be extracted from. It's crucial as the source for contour detection.

inputs.name: retrieval_mode
inputs.description: Specifies the contour retrieval mode, affecting how contours are organized and retrieved. It plays a key role in defining the hierarchy of the contours.

inputs.name: approximation_mode
inputs.description: Determines the method used to approximate the contours. This affects the level of detail of the extracted contours.

outputs.name: cv_contours
outputs.description: The detected contours as a list of points.

outputs.name: cv_contour
outputs.description: A single contour selected from the detected contours, if applicable.

outputs.name: cv_contours_hierarchy
outputs.description: The hierarchical information of the contours, providing details on the contour structure and relationships.

ControlNetHadamard (manual).description: This node applies a control network to a set of images and conditions, adjusting the influence of the control network on the images based on a specified strength. It is designed to modify image conditioning in a batch process, where each image's conditioning is individually adjusted according to the control network's parameters and the specified strength.

inputs.name: conds
inputs.description: Conditions to be applied to each image, serving as the basis for the control network's adjustments. These conditions dictate how the images are modified in conjunction with the control network.

inputs.name: control_net
inputs.description: The control network to be applied across the images, dictating the nature of the adjustments made to their conditioning. It plays a crucial role in how the images' conditions are modified.

inputs.name: strength
inputs.description: A scalar value determining the intensity of the control network's influence on the images, allowing for fine-tuned adjustments. This value scales the effect of the control network on the conditioning.

inputs.name: inputs_len
inputs.description: Specifies the number of images to be processed, indirectly indicating the batch size for the operation. It determines how many images the control network will be applied to.

outputs.name: conditioning
outputs.description: The modified conditions for each image after the application of the control network and the specified strength. It reflects the adjusted image conditioning post-processing.

ControlNetHadamard.description: This node applies a control network to a set of images and conditions, modulating the latter based on the control network's output and a specified strength. It's designed to integrate control network effects into image conditioning, allowing for dynamic adjustments to the conditioning process.

inputs.name: conds
inputs.description: The conditions to be modulated by the control network, representing the contextual or semantic guidance for image generation.

inputs.name: control_net
inputs.description: The control network to be applied, determining the nature and extent of modulation on the conditions.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The images to which the control network adjustments are applied, serving as the basis for condition modulation.

inputs.name: strength
inputs.description: A scalar value determining the intensity of the control network's effect on the conditions, allowing for fine-tuned control over the modulation.

outputs.name: conditioning
outputs.description: The modulated conditions, adjusted by the control network to reflect the desired changes.

ConvertImg.description: The ConvertImg node is designed for explicit image format conversion within a custom node environment, facilitating direct transformations between different image color spaces without resorting to workarounds.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The 'image' parameter represents the input image to be converted. Its role is crucial as it serves as the source image for the conversion process.

inputs.name: to
inputs.description: The 'to' parameter specifies the target color space format for the conversion, influencing the output image's color representation.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is an image that has been converted to the specified color space format, reflecting the changes in color representation as per the 'to' parameter.

CopyMakeBorder.description: The CopyMakeBorder node is designed to add a border around an image. It allows for the customization of the border size and type, excluding transparent borders, to enhance or modify the visual appearance of the image.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to which the border will be added. This is the primary data upon which the border operation is performed.

inputs.name: border_size
inputs.description: Specifies the size of the border to be added around the image. It affects the thickness of the border applied.

inputs.name: border_type
inputs.description: Determines the type of border to be applied to the image, excluding transparent types. This choice influences the visual style of the border.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image with the added border. This is the result of applying the specified border size and type to the input image.

CreateRequestMetadata.description: The CreateRequestMetadata node is designed for managing metadata related to request processing within a system. It facilitates the creation, update, and retrieval of request metadata, including the addition of resources to a request's metadata file. This node plays a crucial role in tracking the state and outputs of requests, ensuring that each request's information is accurately recorded and maintained throughout its lifecycle.

inputs.name: request_id
inputs.description: The unique identifier for a request. It is crucial for distinguishing between different requests and for tracking the specific metadata associated with each request.

DistanceTransform.description: The DistanceTransform node applies a distance transform to a binary image, converting it into a grayscale image where each pixel's intensity represents its distance to the nearest background pixel. It supports various distance types and mask sizes, allowing for customization of the distance calculation.

inputs.name: binary_image
inputs.description: The binary image to which the distance transform will be applied. It is crucial for identifying foreground and background pixels for distance calculations.

inputs.name: distance_type
inputs.description: Specifies the type of distance calculation to use, such as Euclidean (L2), Manhattan (L1), or Chebyshev (C). It affects the way distances are computed in the image.

inputs.name: mask_size
inputs.description: Determines the size of the mask used in the distance calculation, affecting the precision and computational cost of the transform.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output grayscale image where pixel intensities represent distances to the nearest background pixel.

Draw Contour(s).description: The DrawContours node is designed for visualizing contours on images by drawing them over the input image. It allows for selective contour visualization and customization of the contour appearance, such as color and thickness, enhancing the interpretability of contour-based analyses in computer vision tasks.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image on which contours will be drawn. It serves as the background for contour visualization.

inputs.name: contours
inputs.description: A collection of contours to be drawn on the image. Each contour is defined by a series of points.

inputs.name: index_to_draw
inputs.description: Specifies which contour from the contours list to draw. A value of -1 indicates that all contours should be drawn.

inputs.name: thickness
inputs.description: The thickness of the contour lines. A negative value fills the contour.

inputs.name: color
inputs.description: The color of the contour lines in RGB format.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image with the specified contours drawn over it.

EqualizeHistogram.description: The EqualizeHistogram node is designed to enhance the contrast of an image by equalizing its histogram. This process redistributes the intensity levels of the image, potentially improving its visual perception.

inputs.name: src
inputs.description: The source image to be processed for histogram equalization. This input is crucial as it directly influences the enhancement of the image's contrast.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is an enhanced image with equalized histogram, aimed at improving the contrast and visual quality.

ExtendColorList.description: The ExtendColorList node is designed to augment an existing list of colors by adding more color values to it. This functionality is essential in scenarios where a dynamic expansion of color selections is required, such as in image processing, design applications, or data visualization tasks, where a broader palette may enhance the output's aesthetic or informational value.

inputs.name: inputs_len
inputs.description: Specifies the number of color values to be added to the existing color list. This parameter determines the size of the expansion of the color palette.

outputs.name: color
outputs.description: The augmented list of colors, combining the original color list with the newly added color values. This output is significant for subsequent use in applications requiring a broader or modified color palette.

ExtendCondList.description: The ExtendCondList node is designed to extend a list of conditioning elements. It allows for the addition of new conditioning elements to an existing list, facilitating the dynamic expansion of conditioning data used in various computational models or processes.

inputs.name: inputs_len
inputs.description: The 'inputs_len' parameter represents the number of conditioning elements to be added to the existing list. It plays a crucial role in expanding the list's capacity and incorporating new conditioning data, which can significantly influence the execution and outcomes of the node.

outputs.name: conditioning
outputs.description: This node outputs an extended list of conditioning elements, incorporating the newly added samples into the existing list.

ExtendFloatList.description: The ExtendFloatList node is designed to concatenate multiple lists of floating-point numbers into a single, extended list. This functionality is particularly useful in scenarios where aggregation of data from various sources is required, allowing for a streamlined and efficient handling of numerical data collections.

inputs.name: inputs_len
inputs.description: Specifies the number of float lists to be concatenated. This parameter determines how many lists will be merged into the extended list, affecting the node's execution and the size of the resulting list.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The concatenated list of floating-point numbers, resulting from the aggregation of all input lists.

ExtendImageList.description: The ExtendImageList node is designed to extend an existing list of images with additional images. It focuses on aggregating multiple image resources into a single, comprehensive collection, facilitating operations that require bulk image data management.

inputs.name: inputs_len
inputs.description: The 'inputs_len' parameter is crucial for defining the starting point of the collection before new images are added. It represents the initial count of images to be extended, setting the foundation for the extension process.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The 'image' parameter represents the resultant collection of images after the extension process. It encompasses both the original and newly added images, providing a unified collection for further processing.

ExtendIntList.description: The ExtendIntList node is designed to concatenate multiple lists of integers into a single, extended list. This functionality is useful in scenarios where aggregation of integer data from various sources is required, enabling seamless data manipulation and analysis.

inputs.name: inputs_len
inputs.description: Specifies the number of integer lists to be concatenated. This parameter determines how many lists will be combined into the extended list.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: The concatenated list of integers, resulting from the aggregation of all input lists.

ExtendLatentList.description: The ExtendLatentList node is designed to extend a list of latent representations. It facilitates the aggregation of additional latent vectors into an existing collection, enabling the expansion of latent datasets for further processing or analysis.

inputs.name: inputs_len
inputs.description: The 'inputs_len' parameter represents the initial set of latent vectors to be extended. It plays a crucial role in determining the base collection to which new latent vectors will be appended, affecting the node's execution and the resulting extended list.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The 'latent' output parameter represents the extended list of latent vectors. It signifies the augmented collection of latent representations after the addition of new vectors.

ExtendMaskList.description: The ExtendMaskList node is designed to extend a list of masks, allowing for the aggregation of multiple mask elements into a single, comprehensive list. This functionality is crucial for operations that require the manipulation or analysis of multiple masks simultaneously, providing a streamlined approach to handling mask data in bulk.

inputs.name: inputs_len
inputs.description: The 'inputs_len' parameter represents the collection of mask elements to be extended. It plays a pivotal role in the node's operation by serving as the primary data input, which the node then processes to produce an extended list of masks.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The output is an extended list of mask elements, consolidated into a single entity for ease of further processing or analysis.

ExtendModelList.description: The ExtendModelList node is designed to aggregate multiple lists of models into a single, extended list. This functionality is crucial for scenarios where combining model lists is necessary to form a comprehensive collection of models for further processing or analysis.

inputs.name: inputs_len
inputs.description: Specifies the number of model lists to be combined. It determines how many lists will be aggregated into the extended list.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The combined list of models, aggregating all input model lists into a single, extended collection.

ExtendStringList.description: The ExtendStringList node is designed to concatenate multiple lists of strings into a single, extended list. This node is particularly useful in scenarios where aggregation of string data from various sources is required, facilitating operations that involve the manipulation or analysis of collective string datasets.

inputs.name: inputs_len
inputs.description: Specifies the number of string lists to be concatenated. This parameter determines how many string lists will be combined into the extended list.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The resulting list after concatenating all provided string lists. This list contains all strings from the input lists in their respective order.

FadeMaskEdges.description: This node is designed for refining the edges of masks in images, specifically targeting the enhancement of edge blending and smooth transitions. It focuses on premultiplying and alpha blending the edges of a subject to prevent the intrusion of outer pixels, which is particularly useful for stylized subjects or images requiring precise edge manipulation.

inputs.name: binary_image
inputs.description: Represents the mask image to be processed, where the edge modifications will be applied.

inputs.name: edge_size
inputs.description: Defines the size of the edge to be faded, impacting the extent of the edge modification.

inputs.name: edge_tightness
inputs.description: Controls the rate at which the edge fades to black, affecting the sharpness of the edge transition.

inputs.name: edge_exponent
inputs.description: Determines the nature of the fade, potentially softening small lines for a smoother transition.

inputs.name: smoothing_diameter
inputs.description: Specifies the diameter for optional smoothing applied after edge processing, to further refine the edge appearance.

inputs.name: paste_original_blacks
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether to paste original black values back into the image, preserving dark regions.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The processed image with enhanced and smoothly blended edges.

Filter Contour.description: The Filter Contour node is designed to process and filter contours based on a custom fitness function. It evaluates each contour in the context of an image and an auxiliary contour, allowing for dynamic selection and manipulation of contours according to specific criteria.

inputs.name: contours
inputs.description: A list of contours to be filtered. The fitness function evaluates each contour to determine its suitability.

inputs.name: fitness
inputs.description: A custom lambda function that defines the criteria for filtering contours. It is applied to each contour to compute a fitness score.

inputs.name: select
inputs.description: A selection mode that determines how the filtered contours are returned. It influences the output based on the fitness scores of the contours.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image in which the contours are found. It provides context for evaluating the fitness of each contour.

inputs.name: aux_contour
inputs.description: An auxiliary contour that can be used as additional context in the fitness function for filtering contours.

outputs.name: cv_contour
outputs.description: The primary contour selected based on the fitness function.

outputs.name: cv_contours
outputs.description: The filtered contours selected based on the fitness function.

FindComplementaryColor.description: This node is designed to find a complementary color within an image based on a given color dictionary and a specified power level. It can optionally use a mask to limit the search area within the image. The node aims to enhance or modify images by identifying and utilizing complementary colors, thereby supporting tasks related to color theory and image editing.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image on which the complementary color search is performed. It serves as the primary data for analysis.

inputs.name: color_dict
inputs.description: A dictionary mapping specific colors to their identifiers, used to determine the complementary color within the image.

inputs.name: power
inputs.description: Affects the intensity of the search for a complementary color, influencing how the complementary color is determined.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: An optional mask that can be applied to the image to restrict the search area for the complementary color.

outputs.name: color
outputs.description: The RGB values of the identified complementary color.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The identifier of the found complementary color from the provided color dictionary.

FindThreshold.description: The FindThreshold node is designed to dynamically determine an optimal threshold value for image processing tasks. It systematically searches through a specified range of threshold values, applying each to the source image and evaluating the result based on a user-defined condition. This approach allows for adaptive thresholding, enabling the selection of a threshold that best meets the criteria for a given image or set of images.

inputs.name: src
inputs.description: The source image on which thresholding operations are to be performed. It serves as the primary input for the threshold search process.

inputs.name: start_at
inputs.description: Specifies the starting point of the threshold value range to be considered in the search process.

inputs.name: end_at
inputs.description: Defines the end point of the threshold value range for the search, allowing the node to limit its evaluation to a specific range.

inputs.name: thresh_type
inputs.description: Determines the type of thresholding to be applied during the search process, influencing how the threshold values are evaluated against the source image.

inputs.name: downscale_factor
inputs.description: A factor by which the source image is downscaled before thresholding, optimizing the search process by reducing computational load.

inputs.name: condition
inputs.description: A user-defined condition (expressed as a string of Python code) that evaluates the effectiveness of each threshold value applied, guiding the selection of the optimal threshold.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image after applying the optimal threshold found through the search process.

FlatLatentsIntoSingleGrid.description: The FlatLatentsIntoSingleGrid node is designed to transform a batch of latent representations into a single, larger grid layout. This process involves rearranging individual latent samples into a grid pattern, effectively creating a single, unified latent representation that encapsulates the entire batch. This node is particularly useful in scenarios where spatial arrangement of latent samples is necessary for further processing or visualization.

inputs.name: latents
inputs.description: The 'latents' parameter represents the batch of latent representations to be transformed. It is crucial for the node's operation as it provides the raw material that will be rearranged into the grid layout. The transformation process relies on the structure and content of these latents to generate the unified grid.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The output is a single, unified latent representation in the form of a grid. This grid is composed of the input latent samples rearranged according to the specified grid dimensions, serving as a consolidated version of the input batch for further use.

Framed Mask Grab Cut 2.description: This node applies the GrabCut algorithm with an enhanced framing mechanism to segment the foreground from the background in images. It allows for more precise control over the segmentation process by incorporating options to ignore certain areas as probable background, thereby improving the accuracy of the mask generated.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image on which the GrabCut algorithm will be applied. This parameter is crucial for defining the area of interest for foreground segmentation.

inputs.name: thresh_maybe
inputs.description: Threshold values to identify probable foreground regions. This helps in refining the segmentation process by distinguishing between probable foreground and other areas.

inputs.name: thresh_sure
inputs.description: Threshold values to identify definite foreground regions. This parameter is essential for accurately segmenting the foreground from the background.

inputs.name: iterations
inputs.description: The number of iterations the GrabCut algorithm will run. More iterations can lead to more accurate segmentation but at the cost of increased computation time.

inputs.name: margin
inputs.description: Defines the margin size around the frame to be considered as definite background, aiding in better isolation of the foreground object.

inputs.name: frame_option
inputs.description: Specifies the framing options to include or exclude certain parts of the image from being considered as background, offering flexibility in foreground segmentation.

inputs.name: binary_threshold
inputs.description: The threshold value used to differentiate between probable foreground and background based on the 'thresh_maybe' and 'thresh_sure' parameters.

inputs.name: maybe_black_is_sure_background
inputs.description: A boolean parameter that, if true, treats pixels darker than the binary threshold as definite background, further refining the segmentation.

inputs.name: output_format
inputs.description: The desired output format of the result, which can influence how the segmented mask is utilized in subsequent processes or visualizations.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The segmented foreground mask generated by the GrabCut algorithm, highlighting the areas identified as foreground.

Framed Mask Grab Cut.description: The Framed Mask Grab Cut node is designed to apply the GrabCut algorithm with additional framing options to segment the foreground from the background in images. It allows for the specification of probable and sure foreground and background areas, and incorporates frame options to exclude certain margins from consideration, enhancing the flexibility and accuracy of the segmentation process.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image on which the GrabCut algorithm will be applied. It serves as the primary data for foreground-background segmentation.

inputs.name: thresh
inputs.description: A thresholded image indicating areas that might be the foreground or background. This parameter helps in refining the segmentation by marking uncertain areas.

inputs.name: iterations
inputs.description: The number of iterations the GrabCut algorithm should run, affecting the refinement of the segmentation.

inputs.name: margin
inputs.description: Specifies the margin size to be excluded from the frame options, allowing for more precise control over the area considered for segmentation.

inputs.name: frame_option
inputs.description: Defines the frame options to apply, such as ignoring certain margins, to tailor the segmentation process to specific requirements.

inputs.name: threshold_FGD
inputs.description: The threshold value used to classify pixels in 'thresh' image as foreground.

inputs.name: threshold_PR_FGD
inputs.description: The threshold value used to classify pixels in 'thresh' image as probable foreground.

inputs.name: output_format
inputs.description: The desired format for the output image, allowing for compatibility with different processing or display requirements.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The segmented image with the foreground isolated from the background, based on the GrabCut algorithm and additional framing options.

FromListGet1Color.description: The node is designed to retrieve a single color value from a list of colors based on a specified index. It abstracts the process of accessing list elements, allowing for direct retrieval of color information in a user-friendly manner.

inputs.name: list
inputs.description: This parameter represents the list of colors from which a single color will be retrieved. The list must contain color values, and the node will access one of these based on the provided index.

inputs.name: index
inputs.description: The index parameter specifies the position in the color list from which to retrieve the color. It supports both positive and negative indexing, enabling access to list elements from the beginning or end.

outputs.name: color
outputs.description: The output is a single color value retrieved from the specified position in the input list of colors.

FromListGet1Cond.description: This node is designed to extract a single conditioning element from a list based on a specified index. It enables selective access to conditioning data within a list, facilitating operations that require individual manipulation or inspection of conditioning elements.

inputs.name: list
inputs.description: The list from which a conditioning element is to be extracted. This parameter is crucial for specifying the source list.

inputs.name: index
inputs.description: The index at which the conditioning element is to be extracted from the list. Supports negative indexing for reverse access.

outputs.name: conditioning
outputs.description: The extracted conditioning element from the specified index in the list.

FromListGet1Float.description: The `FromListGet1Float` node is designed to retrieve a single float value from a list based on a specified index. It allows for random access within the list, including the use of negative indices to access elements in reverse order, thereby enhancing flexibility in data manipulation.

inputs.name: list
inputs.description: The list from which a float value is to be retrieved. This parameter is essential for specifying the source list.

inputs.name: index
inputs.description: The index at which the float value is to be retrieved from the list. Supports negative indexing for reverse access.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The float value retrieved from the specified index in the list.

FromListGet1Image.description: This node is designed to retrieve a single image from a list of images based on a specified index. It supports random access, including the use of negative indices to access elements from the end of the list, making it versatile for various image processing tasks.

inputs.name: list
inputs.description: The list of images from which a single image will be retrieved. This parameter is crucial for specifying the source of the images.

inputs.name: index
inputs.description: The index at which the image will be retrieved from the list. Supports negative indexing for reverse access.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The single image retrieved from the specified index in the list.

FromListGet1Int.description: This node is designed to retrieve a single integer value from a list based on a specified index. It allows for flexible access to list elements, including support for negative indexing to access elements from the end of the list.

inputs.name: list
inputs.description: The list from which an integer value is to be retrieved. It is essential for the operation as it provides the data source.

inputs.name: index
inputs.description: The index at which the integer value is to be retrieved from the list. Supports negative values for reverse access, affecting the selection of the output integer.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: The single integer value retrieved from the specified index of the list.
