FromListGet1Latent.description: This node is designed to extract a single latent representation from a list of latents. It simplifies the process of selecting a specific latent item for further operations or analysis, making it easier to work with collections of latent representations.

inputs.name: list
inputs.description: The list of latent representations from which a single latent is to be extracted. This parameter is crucial for specifying the source of the latent to be selected.

inputs.name: index
inputs.description: The index of the latent representation to be extracted from the list. This parameter determines which item in the list is selected.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The single latent representation extracted from the provided list. This output is essential for downstream tasks that require a specific latent item.

FromListGet1Mask.description: The node is designed to retrieve a specific item from a list of masks based on the provided index. It supports random access, including the use of negative indices to access items from the end of the list.

inputs.name: list
inputs.description: The list of masks from which an item will be retrieved. It is essential for specifying which list the operation should be performed on.

inputs.name: index
inputs.description: The index of the item to retrieve from the list. Supports negative values for reverse access.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The mask retrieved from the specified index in the list.

FromListGet1Model.description: The node 'FromListGet1Model' is designed to extract a single model from a list of models based on a specified index. It enables selective retrieval from a collection, facilitating focused operations on a particular model of interest.

inputs.name: list
inputs.description: The 'list' parameter represents the collection of models from which a single model is to be retrieved. It is crucial for specifying the dataset the node will operate on.

inputs.name: index
inputs.description: The 'index' parameter determines the position of the model to be retrieved from the list. It supports both positive and negative indexing, allowing for flexible access to the collection.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: This output represents the single model retrieved from the specified list. It is the focal point of the node's operation, enabling further individualized processing or analysis.

FromListGet1String.description: This node is designed to retrieve a single string element from a list based on a specified index. It allows for flexible access to list elements, including support for negative indexing to access elements from the end of the list.

inputs.name: list
inputs.description: The list from which a string element is to be retrieved. It is essential for specifying the source list.

inputs.name: index
inputs.description: The index at which the string element is to be retrieved from the list. Supports negative indexing for reverse access.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The string element retrieved from the specified index of the list.

FromListGetColors.description: This node is designed to extract color information from a list, facilitating the retrieval of color data for further processing or analysis.

inputs.name: list
inputs.description: The list from which color information is to be extracted. This parameter is crucial for specifying the source of color data the node will process.

outputs.name: color
outputs.description: A list of extracted color data from the input list. This output is significant for downstream tasks that require color information.

FromListGetConds.description: This node is designed to retrieve a single conditioning element from a list based on a specified index. It enables random access to the list elements, including the ability to use negative indices for reverse access, thereby enhancing flexibility in handling conditioning data.

inputs.name: list
inputs.description: The list from which a conditioning element is to be retrieved. It is essential for specifying the source of data.

outputs.name: conditioning
outputs.description: The retrieved conditioning element at the specified index.

FromListGetFloats.description: The `FromListGetFloats` node is designed to retrieve a specific float value from a list of floats based on the provided index. It enables random access within a list, including the ability to use negative indices for reverse access, thereby enhancing flexibility in data manipulation.

inputs.name: list
inputs.description: The list of floats from which a specific value is to be retrieved. It is essential for specifying the data set to be accessed.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The float value retrieved from the specified index in the list.

FromListGetImages.description: The node 'FromListGetImages' is designed to retrieve a specific image from a list of images based on a given index. It enables random access to the images in the list, including the ability to access images in reverse order by using negative indexes.

inputs.name: list
inputs.description: The 'list' parameter represents the list of images from which a specific image is to be retrieved. It is essential for specifying the source of the images.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: This output is the image retrieved from the specified position in the list.

FromListGetInts.description: The `FromListGetInts` node is designed to extract a single integer value from a list of integers based on a specified index. It enables random access within a list, allowing for both direct indexing and reverse access through negative indices, thereby facilitating flexible data retrieval from integer lists.

inputs.name: list
inputs.description: The list of integers from which a single integer value is to be retrieved. This parameter is essential for specifying the source list for extraction.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: The extracted integer value from the specified index within the list.

FromListGetLatents.description: The node 'FromListGetLatents' is designed to extract multiple latent representations from a provided list. It enables the selection and manipulation of latent data structures, facilitating operations such as retrieval, analysis, and transformation of latent vectors.

inputs.name: list
inputs.description: Specifies the list of latent representations from which to extract elements. This parameter is crucial for defining the source of latent data to be operated on.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The extracted latent representations from the specified list. This output is significant for further processing or analysis of the latent vectors.

FromListGetMasks.description: The `FromListGetMasks` node is designed to retrieve a specific mask from a list of masks based on a given index. It enables random access to the list elements, allowing for both forward and reverse indexing, thereby facilitating flexible manipulation and selection of masks within a list.

inputs.name: list
inputs.description: The list of masks from which a specific mask is to be retrieved. This parameter is crucial for specifying the source list.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The mask retrieved from the specified index in the list. This output is essential for further processing or manipulation of the selected mask.

FromListGetModels.description: The node is designed to extract a single model from a list of models based on a specified index. It enables selective retrieval of models from a collection, facilitating operations that require individual model processing.

inputs.name: list
inputs.description: The list of models from which a single model is to be retrieved. This parameter is crucial for specifying the source collection of models.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The model extracted from the specified index of the input list. This output is significant for subsequent operations that require a specific model.

FromListGetStrings.description: This node is designed to retrieve a specific string from a list of strings based on a given index. It abstracts the process of accessing list elements, allowing for both direct and reverse indexing, thereby enhancing the flexibility and ease of manipulating lists of strings within a workflow.

inputs.name: list
inputs.description: The list of strings from which a specific string is to be retrieved. It is essential for the operation of the node as it provides the data source.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The string retrieved from the specified index within the list. This output is crucial for further processing or utilization within the workflow.

Get Contour from list.description: This node is designed to retrieve a specific contour from a list of contours based on a given index. It abstracts the process of accessing contours within a collection, facilitating the extraction of individual contour data for further processing or analysis.

inputs.name: contours
inputs.description: The list of contours from which a specific contour is to be retrieved. It is essential for selecting the desired contour for further operations.

inputs.name: index
inputs.description: The index of the contour to be retrieved from the list. It determines which contour is selected for extraction, with a default value of 0.

outputs.name: cv_contour
outputs.description: unknown

Get Models.description: The Get Models node is designed to facilitate the retrieval and organization of various model-related files within a specified output directory. It supports a flexible selection mechanism, allowing users to specify which types of model files (e.g., checkpoints, configurations, embeddings) they wish to dump, either individually or collectively, into a structured JSON file. This functionality aids in managing and cataloging model assets for easier access and reference.

inputs.name: dump
inputs.description: Specifies the type of model-related files to retrieve. It allows for a broad selection, including options like 'all models' for a comprehensive dump or specific categories such as 'checkpoints' or 'embeddings', tailoring the output to user needs.

Get Prompt.description: The Get Prompt node is designed to process and modify a given prompt structure for execution or output purposes. It performs deep copying to avoid altering the original prompt, cleanses the prompt by removing unnecessary widget inputs, and supports outputting the modified prompt either to the console or to a file based on specified parameters. This node plays a crucial role in preparing prompts for execution by ensuring they are in the correct format and contain only the necessary information.

inputs.name: api_prompt
inputs.description: Specifies the output mode for the modified prompt, influencing how the prompt is processed and presented.

HypernetworkLoader (dirty).description: The HypernetworkLoader node is designed to enhance or modify the capabilities of a given model by applying a hypernetwork patch. This process involves loading a specified hypernetwork and applying it to the model with a certain strength, thereby potentially altering the model's behavior or performance based on the characteristics of the hypernetwork.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model to which the hypernetwork patch will be applied. This parameter is crucial as it determines the base model that will be enhanced or modified by the hypernetwork.

inputs.name: hypernetwork_name
inputs.description: The name of the hypernetwork to be loaded and applied. This parameter specifies which hypernetwork patch will be used to modify the model.

inputs.name: strength
inputs.description: The strength with which the hypernetwork patch will be applied to the model. This affects the intensity of the modification or enhancement.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The modified model after the hypernetwork patch has been applied. This output reflects the changes made to the original model by the hypernetwork.

ImageBatchToList.description: The node is designed to convert a batch of images into a list format, facilitating operations that require individual image processing or manipulation within a batch context. It abstracts the complexity of handling batches of images, making it easier to apply transformations or analyses on each image separately.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: Represents the batch of images to be converted into a list. This input is crucial for enabling the node to iterate over each image in the batch and apply necessary transformations or analyses individually.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is a list of images that were originally part of a single batch. This allows for individual image processing or manipulation post conversion.

Inpaint.description: The Inpaint node is designed to reconstruct the missing or damaged parts of images using a specified inpainting technique. It leverages computer vision algorithms to fill in gaps or remove unwanted objects from images, based on the surrounding pixel information.

inputs.name: img
inputs.description: The image to be inpainted. It serves as the primary input where missing parts or imperfections are identified and subsequently reconstructed.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: A mask image indicating the areas to be inpainted. Pixels marked in the mask are the targets for inpainting, guiding the algorithm on where to apply the reconstruction process.

inputs.name: radius
inputs.description: Defines the neighborhood size around each point to consider for inpainting. A larger radius uses more surrounding pixels for reconstruction, potentially leading to smoother results.

inputs.name: flag
inputs.description: Specifies the inpainting technique to use. Different methods can produce varying results based on the algorithm's approach to filling in missing data.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The inpainted image, where the specified areas have been reconstructed using the chosen inpainting technique.

Input_String to Int Array.description: This node is designed to convert input strings into arrays of integers, accommodating both direct array inputs and string representations of integer arrays separated by commas. It ensures flexibility in handling inputs by accepting polymorphic input types.

inputs.name: inStr
inputs.description: Accepts a string of integers separated by commas or an array of integers. This input flexibility allows for easy integration with various input sources.

outputs.name: int_array
outputs.description: Outputs an array of integers, either directly from the input array or by converting a comma-separated string into an integer array.

InRange (hsv).description: The InRangeHSV node is designed to filter an image based on a specified range of hue, saturation, and value (HSV) parameters. It allows for the dynamic selection of color ranges within an image, facilitating tasks such as color segmentation and object detection by identifying pixels that fall within the given HSV bounds.

inputs.name: rgb_image
inputs.description: The input RGB image to be processed and converted to HSV for filtering. This parameter is essential as it represents the data on which the HSV range filtering will be applied, affecting the node's execution and results.

inputs.name: color_a
inputs.description: The first color endpoint in HSV format, used in conjunction with color_b to determine the range of colors to be filtered. This parameter significantly influences the calculation of bounds for hue, saturation, and value.

inputs.name: color_b
inputs.description: The second color endpoint in HSV format, working alongside color_a to define the HSV range for filtering. It plays a key role in establishing the bounds for hue, saturation, and value filtering.

inputs.name: hue_mode
inputs.description: Specifies the method to be used for hue filtering, allowing for different strategies such as ignoring hue, using a single hue range, or splitting the hue range. This parameter determines how the color range is interpreted and applied during filtering.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image after applying the HSV range filtering. This parameter represents the result of the node's operation, showcasing the pixels that match the specified HSV range.

KMeansColor.description: This node applies the K-means clustering algorithm to an image to identify and extract a specified number of dominant colors. It leverages OpenCV's implementation of K-means for efficient color quantization, allowing for the simplification of the image's color palette.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed for color quantization. It serves as the basis for identifying dominant colors through clustering.

inputs.name: number_of_colors
inputs.description: Specifies the number of dominant colors to identify in the image. It determines the granularity of the color quantization.

inputs.name: max_iterations
inputs.description: The maximum number of iterations for the K-means algorithm to run, ensuring the process terminates.

inputs.name: eps
inputs.description: The epsilon value for convergence criteria in K-means, dictating the algorithm's precision and stopping condition.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The processed image with its colors quantized to the specified dominant colors.

Load 64 Encoded Image.description: This node is designed to decode and process a base64-encoded image, converting it into a tensor representation suitable for further image processing tasks. It emphasizes the transformation of encoded image data into a standardized format that can be seamlessly integrated into image analysis and manipulation workflows.

inputs.name: image_code
inputs.description: The base64-encoded string of the image to be loaded. This parameter is crucial for decoding the image and converting it into a tensor format for subsequent operations.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The decoded and processed image, represented as a tensor. This output is ready for use in various image processing and analysis tasks.

LoraLoader (dirty).description: The LoraLoader (dirty) node is designed to dynamically load LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) parameters into models and CLIP instances, allowing for the customization and fine-tuning of these components based on specified LoRA files and strength parameters. It serves as a bridge between static model states and adaptable, performance-enhanced versions tailored to specific tasks or datasets.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model parameter represents the pre-trained model into which LoRA parameters will be loaded. It is crucial for defining the base architecture that will be enhanced with LoRA adaptations.

inputs.name: clip
inputs.description: The clip parameter signifies the CLIP model instance that will be adjusted using LoRA parameters. It plays a key role in adapting the CLIP model for enhanced performance in specific tasks.

inputs.name: lora_name
inputs.description: The lora_name parameter specifies the filename of the LoRA parameters to be loaded. It determines which specific LoRA adaptations will be applied to the model and CLIP instances.

inputs.name: strength_model
inputs.description: This parameter controls the intensity of the LoRA adaptation applied to the model. It allows for fine-tuning the impact of LoRA parameters on the model's performance.

inputs.name: strength_clip
inputs.description: Similar to strength_model, this parameter adjusts the intensity of the LoRA adaptation on the CLIP model, enabling precise control over its influence.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The modified model with LoRA parameters applied, reflecting the adaptations made for enhanced performance or customization.

outputs.name: clip
outputs.description: The adjusted CLIP model with LoRA parameters incorporated, showcasing the enhancements made for improved task-specific performance.

MaskGrid N KSamplers Advanced.description: This node specializes in applying advanced sampling techniques to generate or modify latent images based on a grid pattern. It leverages mask-based operations to selectively apply changes to specific regions of the latent space, enabling complex image manipulations and enhancements.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model parameter specifies the generative model used for sampling operations within the specified regions of the latent space.

inputs.name: add_noise
inputs.description: Determines whether noise is added to the sampling process, enhancing the diversity of the generated images.

inputs.name: noise_seed
inputs.description: The seed for noise generation, ensuring reproducibility in the sampling process.

inputs.name: steps
inputs.description: The number of steps to perform in the sampling process, affecting the detail and quality of the generated images.

inputs.name: cfg
inputs.description: Configuration settings for the sampling process, allowing for customization of the generation.

inputs.name: sampler_name
inputs.description: The name of the sampler algorithm used for generating the latent images.

inputs.name: scheduler
inputs.description: The scheduler controls the sampling process, managing the progression of steps.

inputs.name: positive
inputs.description: Positive text prompts that guide the generation towards desired characteristics.

inputs.name: negative
inputs.description: Negative text prompts that steer the generation away from undesired characteristics.

inputs.name: latent_image
inputs.description: The latent_image parameter represents the initial state of the latent space that will undergo sampling. It is fundamental to the node's operation, serving as the canvas on which mask-based modifications are applied.

inputs.name: start_at_step
inputs.description: The initial step of the sampling process, allowing for control over the starting point.

inputs.name: end_at_step
inputs.description: The final step of the sampling process, defining the endpoint of generation.

inputs.name: return_with_leftover_noise
inputs.description: Indicates whether to include leftover noise in the output, providing additional control over the output's characteristics.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The mask parameter is crucial for defining the regions within the latent image that will be subjected to sampling operations. It plays a key role in determining which parts of the image are modified, ensuring targeted and precise adjustments.

inputs.name: rows
inputs.description: The number of rows in the grid pattern, defining the layout of the applied masks.

inputs.name: columns
inputs.description: The number of columns in the grid pattern, further specifying the layout of the applied masks.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: The mode of operation, determining how the sampling and mask application are conducted.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The latent output consists of a modified latent image reflecting the application of advanced sampling techniques within specified grid regions.

MaskOuterBlur.description: The MaskOuterBlur node is designed to selectively apply a blur effect to the outer regions of an image, utilizing a mask to distinguish between areas to be blurred and those to remain sharp. This technique is aimed at enhancing focus on specific parts of an image or creating a depth-of-field effect, making it particularly useful for image editing and post-processing applications.

inputs.name: src
inputs.description: The source image to which the blur effect will be applied. It serves as the primary input for determining the areas to be blurred based on the mask.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The mask used to differentiate between the areas of the image to be blurred and those to remain sharp. It plays a crucial role in guiding the selective blurring process.

inputs.name: kernel_size
inputs.description: Specifies the size of the blur kernel. A larger kernel size results in a more pronounced blur effect.

inputs.name: paste_src
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether the original source image should be pasted over the blurred areas, preserving detail in the non-blurred regions.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image after applying the selective blur effect, showcasing the enhanced focus or depth-of-field effect.

Merge Latent Batch Gridwise.description: This node is designed to merge a batch of latent representations into a single grid layout, utilizing specified rows and columns to organize the batch elements spatially. It aims to facilitate the visualization or further processing of batches by structuring them in a grid format, making it easier to handle and interpret the collective data.

inputs.name: batch
inputs.description: The batch of latent representations to be merged into a grid. It is the primary input that dictates the content and structure of the output grid.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: A mask image used to determine the dimensions of the grid cells. Although it is primarily for fetching sizes, it plays a crucial role in defining the spatial layout of the merged grid.

inputs.name: rows
inputs.description: Specifies the number of rows in the grid. It determines the vertical dimension of the grid layout.

inputs.name: columns
inputs.description: Specifies the number of columns in the grid. It determines the horizontal dimension of the grid layout.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The merged latent representations arranged in a grid format. This output facilitates the collective handling and visualization of the batch.

MonoMerge.description: The MonoMerge node is designed to merge two images into a monochromatic image based on a target color scheme (either towards white or black). This process involves comparing the luminance (L component) of corresponding pixels from both images and selecting the higher or lower value depending on the target, resulting in an image that emphasizes either the lighter or darker aspects of the combined images.

inputs.name: image1
inputs.description: The first image to be merged. It plays a crucial role in the merging process as its pixels are compared with those of the second image to determine the final image based on the target color scheme.

inputs.name: image2
inputs.description: The second image to be merged. It is compared against the first image to select the appropriate luminance values for the final monochromatic image, depending on the target color scheme.

inputs.name: target
inputs.description: Specifies the target color scheme for the merge, either 'white' or 'black'. This determines whether the merge will favor lighter or darker pixel values from the input images.

inputs.name: output_format
inputs.description: Defines the format of the output image, such as JPEG, PNG, etc. This affects how the final image is encoded and saved.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The resulting monochromatic image after merging the two input images based on the specified target color scheme.

MorphologicOperation.description: This node provides a comprehensive suite of morphological operations for image processing, including erode, dilate, open, close, gradient, top hat, and bottom hat transformations. It allows for the manipulation of the structure of images using different kernel shapes and sizes, enabling a wide range of effects from refining image features to extracting structural elements.

inputs.name: src
inputs.description: The source image to be processed. It serves as the primary input for applying morphological operations.

inputs.name: operation
inputs.description: Specifies the morphological operation to be applied to the source image. This determines the type of structural manipulation performed.

inputs.name: kernel_type
inputs.description: Defines the shape of the kernel used in the morphological operation, influencing the effect on the image's structure.

inputs.name: kernel_size_x
inputs.description: The horizontal size of the kernel. It affects the area of the image influenced by the operation.

inputs.name: kernel_size_y
inputs.description: The vertical size of the kernel. It affects the area of the image influenced by the operation.

inputs.name: iterations
inputs.description: The number of times the morphological operation is applied. Increasing this value intensifies the effect.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The result of applying the specified morphological operation to the source image, potentially altering its structure.

MorphologicSkeletoning.description: The MorphologicSkeletoning node is designed to perform skeletonization on binary images. It transforms the input image into its skeletal representation, reducing all objects to lines without changing the fundamental structure.

inputs.name: src
inputs.description: The source image to be skeletonized. It is crucial for the operation as it directly influences the skeletonization process.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The skeletal representation of the input image, highlighting its essential structure with minimal thickness.

NaiveAutoKMeansColor.description: This node is designed to automatically determine the optimal number of colors for K-means clustering on an image, and then apply the K-means algorithm to segment the image into these colors. It simplifies the process of color quantization by abstracting away the need for manual specification of the number of clusters, making it easier to use for tasks such as image simplification or color analysis.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image on which K-means clustering will be performed. This is the primary data the node operates on to determine the optimal number of colors.

inputs.name: max_k
inputs.description: The maximum number of colors (clusters) to consider for determining the optimal number through the algorithm. It sets an upper limit on the number of clusters to evaluate.

inputs.name: rc_threshold
inputs.description: A threshold for the relative compactness of clusters, used to help determine the optimal number of clusters by comparing the compactness of a cluster to the first computed compactness.

inputs.name: max_iterations
inputs.description: The maximum number of iterations the K-means algorithm will execute, providing a stopping criterion for convergence.

inputs.name: eps
inputs.description: The epsilon value for convergence criteria, specifying the minimum amount of change required for an iteration to be considered as making progress.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image after applying K-means clustering with the determined optimal number of colors, segmented into these colors.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: The optimal number of colors (clusters) determined by the algorithm for the input image.

OtsuThreshold.description: The OtsuThreshold node applies Otsu's thresholding method to an image to separate the foreground from the background. It optionally preprocesses the image with Gaussian blur to reduce noise and improve the thresholding result.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be thresholded. Otsu's method is applied to this image to determine the optimal threshold value for separating foreground and background.

inputs.name: threshold_type
inputs.description: Specifies the type of thresholding to apply in conjunction with Otsu's method, allowing for customization of the thresholding process.

inputs.name: gaussian_blur_x
inputs.description: The kernel width for the Gaussian blur applied to the image before thresholding. A larger value reduces noise but can blur edges.

inputs.name: gaussian_blur_y
inputs.description: The kernel height for the Gaussian blur applied to the image before thresholding. Works in conjunction with gaussian_blur_x to define the blur extent.

inputs.name: gaussian_border_type
inputs.description: Defines the border type used in the Gaussian blur process, affecting how image edges are handled during blurring.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image after applying Otsu's thresholding. The image is segmented into foreground and background, with noise reduced if Gaussian blur was applied.

Rect Grab Cut.description: The RectGrabCut node is designed for image segmentation using the GrabCut algorithm with a predefined rectangular area. It aims to separate the foreground from the background within the specified rectangle, enhancing image processing tasks by allowing for more precise object isolation.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be segmented. It plays a crucial role in determining the effectiveness of the foreground-background separation.

inputs.name: x1
inputs.description: The x-coordinate of the top left corner of the rectangle.

inputs.name: y1
inputs.description: The y-coordinate of the top left corner of the rectangle.

inputs.name: x2
inputs.description: The x-coordinate of the bottom right corner of the rectangle.

inputs.name: y2
inputs.description: The y-coordinate of the bottom right corner of the rectangle.

inputs.name: iterations
inputs.description: Specifies the number of iterations the GrabCut algorithm should run, affecting the accuracy and detail of the segmentation.

inputs.name: output_format
inputs.description: Defines the format of the output image, influencing how the segmented image is presented and utilized in subsequent processes.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The segmented image with the foreground isolated from the background, ready for further processing or analysis.

Remap.description: The `Remap` node serves as a foundational class for various image remapping operations, providing a base structure and common functionalities for specialized remapping transformations. It abstracts the core mechanisms needed to perform complex image geometry alterations, enabling derived classes to implement specific remapping effects such as distortion correction, perspective adjustments, and custom image warping techniques.

inputs.name: remap
inputs.description: Specifies the remapping function to be applied, which is a core component of the remapping process, determining how pixels from the source image are mapped to the destination image.

inputs.name: src
inputs.description: The source image to be remapped, serving as the input for the remapping operation.

inputs.name: interpolation
inputs.description: Defines the interpolation method used in the remapping process, affecting the quality and appearance of the output image.

inputs.name: src_mask
inputs.description: An optional mask that specifies which parts of the source image should be considered for remapping.

inputs.name: output_with_alpha
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether the output image should include an alpha channel, allowing for transparency effects.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The result of the remapping operation, which is a transformed version of the input image according to the specified remapping parameters.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: An optional output mask that corresponds to the remapped image, indicating areas of interest or exclusion.

RemapBarrelDistortion.description: This node is designed to apply barrel distortion to images, a common technique for correcting or introducing distortion based on lens characteristics. It can undistort images from camera and lens combinations or create specific types of distortion such as barrel, pincushion, or mustache distortion.

inputs.name: a
inputs.description: Coefficient 'a' influences the primary distortion effect on the image, playing a crucial role in the barrel distortion calculation.

inputs.name: b
inputs.description: Coefficient 'b' serves as a secondary factor in the distortion effect, modifying the curvature introduced by the primary coefficient.

inputs.name: c
inputs.description: Coefficient 'c' acts as a tertiary modifier for the distortion effect, fine-tuning the overall shape of the distortion.

inputs.name: use_inverse_variant
inputs.description: This boolean flag determines whether an alternative formula is used for computing the distortion, allowing for different distortion effects.

inputs.name: d
inputs.description: An optional coefficient that can further adjust the distortion effect when provided.

outputs.name: remap
outputs.description: The output is the result of applying the specified barrel distortion to the input image, which may include corrections or intentional distortions based on the provided coefficients.

RemapFromInsideParabolas.description: This node is designed to perform a remapping operation from the perspective of inside two parabolas, transforming an image based on specified width and height parameters. It utilizes a source mask defined by two parabolas to apply a unique geometric transformation, aiming to adjust the image's representation for specific visualization or processing needs.

inputs.name: src_mask_with_i_parabolas
inputs.description: Defines the source mask that contains two parabolas, which is crucial for determining the geometric transformation applied to the image.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Specifies the desired width of the output image after remapping, affecting the scale and aspect ratio of the transformation.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Determines the height of the output image, influencing the vertical scale and aspect ratio post-transformation.

outputs.name: remap
outputs.description: The result of the remapping operation, providing a transformed image based on the input parameters and the geometric characteristics of the source mask.

RemapFromQuadrilateral (homography).description: The RemapFromQuadrilateral node is designed for transforming images based on a source mask that defines a quadrilateral region. It primarily utilizes a homography transformation to map the specified quadrilateral region from the source image to a target rectangular shape, adjusting the image accordingly. This node is particularly useful for correcting or altering the perspective of an image region defined by four points.

inputs.name: src_mask_with_i_points
inputs.description: Specifies the source mask with four points defining the quadrilateral region to be transformed. This mask is crucial for determining the area of the image that will undergo the homography transformation.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Defines the width of the target image after the transformation. This parameter directly influences the dimensions of the output image, ensuring that the transformed quadrilateral fits within these specified bounds.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Specifies the height of the target image post-transformation. Similar to the width parameter, it determines the dimensions of the output image, ensuring the transformed area is appropriately scaled.

outputs.name: remap
outputs.description: The primary output of this node is the transformed image or 'remap', which results from applying the homography transformation to the specified quadrilateral region. This output is crucial for understanding the effect of the transformation on the original image.

RemapInsideParabolas.description: This node is designed for remapping images based on the geometry of two parabolas within a given mask. It adjusts the image's pixels to align or distort according to these parabolas, enabling advanced image transformation techniques that can simulate or correct specific optical effects.

inputs.name: dst_mask_with_i_parabolas
inputs.description: A mask image containing two parabolas. This mask is used to determine the transformation geometry for remapping the image.

outputs.name: remap
outputs.description: The output is a transformed version of the input image, where the pixel positions have been adjusted based on the specified parabolas within the mask.

RemapInsideParabolasAdvanced.description: This node specializes in adjusting the mapping of images based on the geometry of two parabolas within a given mask. It allows for fine-tuning the remapping process through curve and orthogonal adjustments, as well as the option to flip the orthogonal direction, enhancing flexibility in image processing tasks that require precise spatial transformations.

inputs.name: dst_mask_with_i_parabolas
inputs.description: unknown

inputs.name: curve_wise_adjust
inputs.description: Adjusts the curvature of the remapping process, allowing for finer control over the spatial transformation along the curve defined by the parabolas.

inputs.name: ortho_wise_adjust
inputs.description: Adjusts the orthogonal transformation relative to the parabolas' curve, enabling precise control over the image's spatial deformation.

inputs.name: flip_ortho
inputs.description: Determines whether the orthogonal direction of the remapping should be flipped, offering an additional degree of transformation customization.

outputs.name: remap
outputs.description: The output is a transformed image that has been remapped according to the specified parabolas and adjustments. This includes the spatially transformed image data, which is the result of applying the curve and orthogonal adjustments, as well as the optional flipping of the orthogonal direction.

RemapPinch.description: The RemapPinch node is designed to apply a pinch distortion effect to images, allowing for the adjustment of the distortion's power and center through specified parameters. It leverages a mathematical model to modify the image geometry, creating visually compelling effects that can enhance or alter the appearance of images in creative ways.

inputs.name: power_x
inputs.description: Specifies the horizontal distortion power. Higher values increase the pinch effect horizontally, affecting the image's geometry. This parameter is crucial for controlling the intensity of the distortion effect, directly influencing the degree to which the image is pinched horizontally.

inputs.name: power_y
inputs.description: Determines the vertical distortion power. Similar to power_x, but applies vertically, altering the image's vertical geometry. This parameter is essential for adjusting the vertical intensity of the distortion, impacting how much the image is pinched vertically.

inputs.name: center_x
inputs.description: Sets the horizontal center point of the pinch effect. Values range from 0 to 1, representing the relative position across the image width. Adjusting this parameter shifts the focal point of the distortion horizontally, affecting where the pinch effect is most pronounced.

inputs.name: center_y
inputs.description: Defines the vertical center point of the pinch effect. Values range from 0 to 1, indicating the position from top to bottom of the image. Modifying this parameter moves the distortion's focal point vertically, altering the central area of the pinch effect.

outputs.name: remap
outputs.description: The output is a remapped version of the input image, where the geometry has been altered based on the specified distortion parameters. This remapping results in a visually distorted image that exhibits the pinch effect, with the degree and center of distortion controlled by the input parameters.

RemapReverseBarrelDistortion.description: This node is designed to apply a reverse barrel distortion effect to images. It utilizes parameters to adjust the distortion effect, allowing for the correction of barrel distortion or the application of reverse effects based on the specified parameters.

inputs.name: a
inputs.description: Coefficient 'a' influences the primary distortion effect, playing a crucial role in the barrel distortion correction or application.

inputs.name: b
inputs.description: Coefficient 'b' serves to adjust the distortion effect further, complementing the primary coefficient 'a' in fine-tuning the distortion.

inputs.name: c
inputs.description: Coefficient 'c' is used alongside 'a' and 'b' to refine the distortion effect, offering additional control over the distortion characteristics.

inputs.name: use_inverse_variant
inputs.description: This boolean parameter determines whether to use an inverse variant of the distortion formula, affecting the overall distortion effect.

inputs.name: d
inputs.description: An optional coefficient that can be used to extend the distortion effect, providing even finer control over the distortion characteristics.

outputs.name: remap
outputs.description: The output is a remapped image with the reverse barrel distortion applied, based on the input parameters.

RemapStretch.description: The RemapStretch node is designed to apply a stretching transformation to images based on specified power factors along the x and y axes, and a center point around which the stretch is applied. This node allows for the dynamic adjustment of image geometry to simulate effects such as stretching or elongation, providing a versatile tool for image manipulation and enhancement.

inputs.name: power_x
inputs.description: Specifies the power factor for stretching along the x-axis. A higher value results in more pronounced stretching effect.

inputs.name: power_y
inputs.description: Specifies the power factor for stretching along the y-axis. Similar to `power_x`, a higher value intensifies the stretching effect.

inputs.name: center_x
inputs.description: Determines the x-coordinate of the center point around which the stretching effect is applied. This allows for targeted manipulation of the image geometry.

inputs.name: center_y
inputs.description: Determines the y-coordinate of the center point around which the stretching effect is applied, enabling precise control over the area of effect.

outputs.name: remap
outputs.description: Produces a transformed image where the specified stretching effects have been applied, altering the original geometry according to the input parameters.

RemapToInnerCylinder.description: The RemapToInnerCylinder node is designed to transform an image by mapping it onto an inner cylinder, adjusting the field of view and optionally swapping the x and y coordinates based on the provided parameters. This node is part of a suite of remapping functionalities that manipulate images to simulate various perspectives and distortions.

inputs.name: fov
inputs.description: The 'fov' parameter specifies the field of view in degrees, controlling the extent of the cylindrical projection. It determines how wide the view is on the resulting cylinder, affecting the distortion level of the remapped image.

inputs.name: swap_xy
inputs.description: The 'swap_xy' parameter indicates whether the x and y coordinates should be swapped in the remapping process. This can be used to change the orientation of the image on the cylindrical surface.

outputs.name: remap
outputs.description: The output 'remap' provides the transformed image data after applying the inner cylinder mapping. It encapsulates the result of the remapping process, reflecting the adjustments made to the field of view and the orientation of the image.

RemapToOuterCylinder.description: The RemapToOuterCylinder node is designed to transform an image by mapping it onto the surface of an imaginary outer cylinder. This transformation is based on the field of view and an optional swap of the x and y axes, aiming to simulate a perspective where the image wraps around the viewer in a cylindrical manner.

inputs.name: fov
inputs.description: The field of view in degrees, determining the extent of the cylindrical projection. It influences the curvature and the scale of the remapped image.

inputs.name: swap_xy
inputs.description: A boolean flag that, when true, swaps the x and y axes in the output mapping. This can be used to adjust the orientation of the remapped image based on specific requirements.

outputs.name: remap
outputs.description: The output of the RemapToOuterCylinder node is a transformed image that has been remapped to simulate being wrapped around an outer cylinder. This output is crucial for applications requiring cylindrical perspective transformations.

RemapToQuadrilateral.description: This node is designed to transform images by remapping them to fit within quadrilateral shapes, utilizing various methods including homography and edge pair interpolation. It abstracts complex geometric transformations, making it easier to apply perspective adjustments or corrections based on specified quadrilateral regions within images.

inputs.name: dst_mask_with_i_points
inputs.description: Specifies the destination mask with i points defining the quadrilateral to which the image will be remapped. This mask is crucial for determining the target shape and area for the remapping process.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Defines the method to be used for the remapping process, such as homography or length-wise interpolation, allowing for flexibility in how the image is transformed to fit the quadrilateral.

outputs.name: remap
outputs.description: The result of the remapping process, which includes the transformed image fitted within the specified quadrilateral shape.

RemapWarpPolar.description: The RemapWarpPolar node is designed to transform images by applying a warp polar transformation. This process involves converting images from a rectangular to a polar coordinate system, optionally applying logarithmic scaling, and performing inverse transformations. It supports adjustments to the transformation center, radius, and cropping of the result, making it versatile for various image processing tasks.

inputs.name: max_radius
inputs.description: Specifies the maximum radius for the warp polar transformation, affecting the extent of the transformation applied to the image.

inputs.name: radius_adjust
inputs.description: Adjusts the effective radius of the transformation, allowing for fine-tuning of the warp effect.

inputs.name: center_x_adjust
inputs.description: Adjusts the x-coordinate of the transformation center, enabling horizontal shifting of the warp effect's focal point.

inputs.name: center_y_adjust
inputs.description: Adjusts the y-coordinate of the transformation center, enabling vertical shifting of the warp effect's focal point.

inputs.name: log
inputs.description: Determines whether logarithmic scaling is applied, changing the nature of the warp from linear to logarithmic.

inputs.name: inverse
inputs.description: Controls whether the inverse warp polar transformation is applied, allowing for the reversal of the warp effect.

inputs.name: crop
inputs.description: Enables cropping of the transformed image to remove areas outside the specified radius, focusing on the central area.

outputs.name: remap
outputs.description: The result of the warp polar transformation, including any adjustments and cropping applied to the original image.

Repeat Into Grid (image).description: This node tiles input image samples into a grid of configurable dimensions, effectively repeating the input image across a specified number of rows and columns to create a larger, grid-like composite image.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be tiled across the grid. It determines the visual content that will be repeated in each cell of the grid.

inputs.name: columns
inputs.description: Specifies the number of columns in the grid. This determines how many times the input image is repeated horizontally.

inputs.name: rows
inputs.description: Specifies the number of rows in the grid. This determines how many times the input image is repeated vertically.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output composite image, consisting of the input image tiled according to the specified rows and columns.

Repeat Into Grid (latent).description: This node is designed to replicate and arrange input latent samples into a grid format based on specified dimensions. It enables the creation of a structured layout of latent representations, facilitating operations that require uniform spatial arrangements, such as visualization or further processing in grid-based models.

inputs.name: samples
inputs.description: The latent samples to be tiled into a grid. This input is crucial for determining the content that will be replicated across the grid.

inputs.name: columns
inputs.description: Specifies the number of columns in the grid. This parameter directly influences the grid's width and the arrangement of the replicated samples.

inputs.name: rows
inputs.description: Determines the number of rows in the grid. It affects the grid's height and how the samples are distributed vertically.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The output is a modified version of the input latent samples, now arranged into a grid as specified by the input dimensions.

RequestInputs.description: The RequestInputs node is designed to process a string of values, typically received as a JSON string, and convert them into a tuple of strings. This node is essential for handling and parsing input data received from web requests or other input sources, making it a key component in preparing data for further processing or analysis within a system.

inputs.name: values
inputs.description: The 'values' parameter accepts a JSON string representing the input values. It plays a crucial role in the node's operation by determining the data that will be parsed and converted into a tuple of strings for further processing.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: Each element in the output tuple represents a string value extracted and parsed from the input JSON string, facilitating the handling of multiple input values simultaneously.

RGB to HSV.description: The node converts RGB color values to HSV color space, facilitating color transformations and analysis by separating color hue, saturation, and value. This conversion is essential for tasks that require color space manipulation or analysis, such as image processing and computer vision applications.

inputs.name: rgb_color
inputs.description: The RGB color input that needs to be converted to HSV. This parameter is crucial for the conversion process, as it represents the color in RGB format that will be transformed into its HSV equivalent.

outputs.name: hsv_color
outputs.description: The output HSV color, represented as a tuple of hue, saturation, and value. This conversion is useful for applications that rely on the HSV color space for more intuitive handling of colors.

SampleColorHSV.description: This node is designed to sample pixels from an RGB image and convert these samples into the HSV color space. It aims to facilitate color analysis and processing by providing a representative subset of the image's color distribution in HSV format.

inputs.name: rgb_image
inputs.description: The RGB image from which pixels will be sampled. This image is the primary input for color sampling and subsequent conversion to HSV.

inputs.name: sample_size
inputs.description: Determines the number of pixels to be sampled from the RGB image. A larger sample size provides a more representative color distribution but requires more processing time.

inputs.name: sampling_seed
inputs.description: A seed value for the random number generator used in pixel sampling. This ensures reproducibility of the sample selection across different runs.

outputs.name: hsv_samples
outputs.description: The output is a collection of HSV color space samples derived from the sampled RGB image pixels. This facilitates further color analysis or processing.

Save Image (api).description: The Save Image node is designed to persist images to disk without including any metadata, using a unique hexdigest-based filename. It is typically used in workflows where the final output needs to be stored efficiently and metadata preservation is not required. The output from this node is often used to signal the completion of a request or task.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The primary input for the node, representing the images to be saved. This parameter is crucial for the node's operation as it directly influences the output by determining which images are stored.

inputs.name: resource_name
inputs.description: An optional parameter that specifies the base name for the saved images. It allows for a customizable naming convention that can be useful in organizing and retrieving saved images.

outputs.name: task_done
outputs.description: Indicates that the image saving task has been completed successfully.

SeamlessClone (simple).description: This node provides a simplified interface for performing seamless cloning operations on images, automatically determining the center of the source mask for the cloning process. It leverages the capabilities of a more complex seamless cloning node to offer an easier-to-use option for integrating one image into another with visually coherent results.

inputs.name: dst
inputs.description: The destination image onto which the source image will be cloned.

inputs.name: src
inputs.description: The source image to be cloned onto the destination image.

inputs.name: src_mask
inputs.description: A mask image indicating the region of the source image to be cloned.

inputs.name: flag
inputs.description: Specifies the cloning mode to be used, which can affect the blending behavior.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The result of the seamless cloning operation, with the source image integrated into the destination image.

SeamlessClone.description: The SeamlessClone node is designed for blending two images together in a seamless manner, using various cloning modes to achieve different visual effects. It allows for precise control over the blending process by specifying the source and destination images, a mask to define the blend area, and the position for blending, along with the choice of cloning mode.

inputs.name: dst
inputs.description: The destination image onto which the source image will be cloned. It serves as the backdrop for the cloning operation.

inputs.name: src
inputs.description: The source image to be cloned onto the destination image. This image will be blended into the destination based on the specified mask and cloning mode.

inputs.name: src_mask
inputs.description: A mask image that defines the area of the source image to be cloned. Only the parts of the source image covered by the mask will be blended into the destination.

inputs.name: flag
inputs.description: Specifies the cloning mode to be used for blending the images. The available modes are NORMAL, MIXED, and MONOCHROME_TRANSFER, each offering a different visual effect.

inputs.name: cx
inputs.description: The x-coordinate of the center point in the destination image where the source image will be cloned.

inputs.name: cy
inputs.description: The y-coordinate of the center point in the destination image where the source image will be cloned.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The result of the seamless cloning operation, which is a blend of the source and destination images according to the specified parameters.

SetRequestStateToComplete.description: This node is designed to mark the state of a request as 'complete' within the request metadata file, effectively signaling the successful completion of a task or set of tasks.

inputs.name: resource_i
inputs.description: unknown

String to Float.description: This node is designed to convert string representations of floating-point numbers into their float equivalents. It ensures that inputs, even if provided as strings, are accurately transformed to float values for further numerical processing.

inputs.name: inStr
inputs.description: Takes a string input that represents a floating-point number and converts it into a float. This allows for string-based numerical inputs to be accurately processed and utilized in calculations.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: Outputs the converted floating-point number from the string input, facilitating its use in numerical operations and calculations.

String to Integer.description: This node is designed to convert string representations of numbers into their integer equivalents. It ensures compatibility with both string and integer inputs, facilitating seamless data processing and integration within a pipeline that may receive inputs from various sources.

inputs.name: inStr
inputs.description: The input string to be converted into an integer. This parameter allows the node to accept both numerical strings and integer values, ensuring flexibility in handling different types of input.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: The integer representation of the input string or integer value.

String.description: The String node is designed to simply pass through the input string it receives without modification. This node serves as a straightforward utility within a larger processing pipeline, allowing for the direct transfer of string data from one node to another.

inputs.name: inStr
inputs.description: This parameter represents the input string that will be passed through the node. It is essential for the node's operation as it directly determines the output of the node.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The output of this node is the input string unchanged, facilitating the transfer of string data within a processing pipeline.

ToColorList.description: The `ToColorList` node is designed to transform a collection of color-related data into a structured list format, specifically tailored for handling color information. This node facilitates the organization and manipulation of color data, making it easier to process and utilize in various computational color analysis and manipulation tasks.

inputs.name: inputs_len
inputs.description: Represents the collection of color data to be transformed into a list. This parameter is crucial for the node's operation as it determines the content of the resulting color list, affecting subsequent processing and analysis.

outputs.name: color
outputs.description: The structured list of color data, organized for efficient processing and manipulation in further color-related computational tasks.

ToCondList.description: The ToCondList node is designed for creating lists of conditioning data from individual conditioning inputs. It streamlines the process of aggregating multiple conditioning elements into a single, organized list, facilitating easier manipulation and application in subsequent processes.

inputs.name: inputs_len
inputs.description: The 'inputs_len' parameter specifies the number of individual conditioning elements to be aggregated into a list. This parameter is essential for determining the size of the resulting list, thereby influencing the node's execution and the characteristics of the output.

outputs.name: conditioning
outputs.description: The output is a list of conditioning data, aggregated from the individual conditioning inputs provided to the node. This list is ready for use in processes that require conditioning data in a collective format.

ToFloatList.description: The `ToFloatList` node is designed to aggregate individual float values into a list, facilitating operations that require collective processing or manipulation of multiple float entries. This node serves as a utility for converting discrete float inputs into a structured list format, enabling more efficient handling and application in subsequent computational tasks.

inputs.name: inputs_len
inputs.description: Specifies the number of float inputs to be aggregated into the list. This parameter determines the size of the resulting float list, allowing for dynamic list creation based on the input count.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: Produces a list composed of the aggregated float inputs. This list serves as a structured collection of float values, ready for further processing or manipulation in subsequent operations.

ToImageList.description: The ToImageList node is designed to convert a collection of images into a standardized list format. This functionality is essential for processing multiple images in a uniform manner, enabling easier manipulation, analysis, and application of image-based operations across the entire collection.

inputs.name: inputs_len
inputs.description: The 'inputs_len' parameter represents the collection of images to be converted into a list. This input is crucial for the node's operation as it determines the set of images that will undergo the conversion process.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The 'image' output is a list of images that have been converted from the input collection. This standardized format facilitates further processing and manipulation of the images.

ToIntList.description: The `ToIntList` node is designed to aggregate multiple integer inputs into a single list. This functionality is essential for scenarios where a collection of integers needs to be processed or manipulated as a single entity, streamlining operations that involve multiple integer values.

inputs.name: inputs_len
inputs.description: Specifies the number of integer inputs to be aggregated into the list. This parameter determines the size of the resulting list and plays a crucial role in the node's operation by dictating how many integer values will be considered.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: The output is a list composed of the integer inputs provided to the node. This list serves as a consolidated collection of the individual integers, facilitating operations that require handling multiple integers as a unified structure.

ToLatentList.description: The `ToLatentList` node is designed to aggregate individual latent representations into a structured list format. This node facilitates the organization and manipulation of latent data by converting disparate latent samples into a cohesive list, making it easier to handle and process multiple latent samples collectively.

inputs.name: inputs_len
inputs.description: The `inputs_len` parameter represents the individual latent samples to be aggregated into a list. This parameter is crucial for collecting and structuring latent data into a format that is more manageable for further processing or analysis.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The `latent` output represents the aggregated list of latent samples. This structured format allows for easier manipulation and analysis of multiple latent samples as a collective unit.

ToMaskList.description: The ToMaskList node is designed to convert a collection of inputs into a list of masks. This node plays a crucial role in organizing and preparing mask data for further processing or manipulation within a pipeline, ensuring that data is in the correct format for subsequent nodes that require mask inputs.

inputs.name: inputs_len
inputs.description: The 'inputs_len' parameter represents the collection of inputs that are to be converted into a list of masks. This parameter is essential for the node's operation as it directly influences the composition of the output mask list, determining the data that will be available for further processing.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The output is a list of masks, structured to facilitate further operations that involve mask data within the pipeline.

ToModelList.description: The `ToModelList` node is designed to aggregate multiple model-related inputs into a single list. This functionality is essential for operations that require handling a collection of models simultaneously, such as batch processing or model comparison tasks. It abstracts away the complexity of managing multiple inputs by providing a streamlined way to group them together.

inputs.name: inputs_len
inputs.description: Specifies the number of model inputs to be aggregated into the list. This parameter determines the size of the resulting list and plays a crucial role in the node's execution by dictating how many model inputs will be considered.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The output is a list containing the aggregated model inputs. This list facilitates operations that need to process multiple models in a unified manner, enhancing flexibility and efficiency in handling model collections.

ToStringList.description: The ToStringList node is designed to aggregate multiple string inputs into a single list, facilitating operations that require collective handling of strings. It abstracts the complexity of handling individual strings, enabling efficient batch processing and manipulation.

inputs.name: inputs_len
inputs.description: Specifies the number of string inputs to be aggregated into the list. This parameter allows for dynamic adjustment of the list size based on the number of inputs provided.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: Outputs a list composed of the aggregated string inputs. This list enables further processing or manipulation as a collective entity.

UnGridify (image).description: The UnGridify (image) node is designed to deconstruct a grid of images into its individual tiles. It takes an image composed of a grid layout and separates it into distinct image tiles based on specified row and column parameters, facilitating the manipulation or analysis of each tile independently.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The composite image arranged in a grid format. This input is crucial for determining the structure from which individual tiles will be extracted.

inputs.name: columns
inputs.description: Specifies the number of columns in the grid. This parameter is essential for accurately dividing the image into the correct number of horizontal segments.

inputs.name: rows
inputs.description: Indicates the number of rows in the grid. It is vital for splitting the image into the appropriate number of vertical segments.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: A list of images, where each image represents a tile extracted from the original grid. This output allows for further individual processing or analysis of each tile.

VAEEncodeBatch.description: The VAEEncodeBatch node is designed to encode a batch of images into their latent representations using a Variational Autoencoder (VAE). It processes multiple images sequentially, leveraging a VAE model to transform each image into a latent space vector, and then concatenates these vectors to form a batch of latent representations.

inputs.name: inputs_len
inputs.description: Specifies the number of images to encode into their latent representations. It determines the size of the batch that will be processed by the node.

inputs.name: vae
inputs.description: The Variational Autoencoder (VAE) model used for encoding images into their latent representations. It is a crucial component that defines the encoding mechanism.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The latent representation of the encoded images. It is a batch of vectors in the latent space, representing the input images.

CR 8 Channel In.description: The CR 8 Channel In node is designed to facilitate the input of data across eight distinct channels within a pipeline, enabling complex data handling and manipulation for advanced processing tasks.

inputs.name: pipe
inputs.description: The 'pipe' parameter represents the pipeline through which data is inputted into the node, serving as the conduit for the eight distinct channels of data that are to be processed.

inputs.name: ch1
inputs.description: Represents one of the eight channels through which data can be inputted into the node, allowing for complex data handling and manipulation.

inputs.name: ch2
inputs.description: Represents one of the eight channels through which data can be inputted into the node, allowing for complex data handling and manipulation.

inputs.name: ch3
inputs.description: Represents one of the eight channels through which data can be inputted into the node, allowing for complex data handling and manipulation.

inputs.name: ch4
inputs.description: Represents one of the eight channels through which data can be inputted into the node, allowing for complex data handling and manipulation.

inputs.name: ch5
inputs.description: Represents one of the eight channels through which data can be inputted into the node, allowing for complex data handling and manipulation.

inputs.name: ch6
inputs.description: Represents one of the eight channels through which data can be inputted into the node, allowing for complex data handling and manipulation.

inputs.name: ch7
inputs.description: Represents one of the eight channels through which data can be inputted into the node, allowing for complex data handling and manipulation.

inputs.name: ch8
inputs.description: Represents one of the eight channels through which data can be inputted into the node, allowing for complex data handling and manipulation.

outputs.name: pipe
outputs.description: This output type signifies the continuation of the pipeline, carrying forward the data processed within the node to subsequent stages.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: Provides a link to helpful documentation or further information regarding the node's functionality.

CR 8 Channel Out.description: This node is designed to output data across eight channels from a pipeline, facilitating complex data manipulation and routing within a node-based processing environment. It serves as a critical component for distributing data to multiple downstream nodes, enhancing modularity and flexibility in data processing workflows.

inputs.name: pipe
inputs.description: The 'pipe' parameter represents the pipeline from which data is extracted and distributed across the eight output channels. It is essential for the node's operation as it sources the data to be processed and routed.

outputs.name: pipe
outputs.description: Represents the pipeline data structure, carrying data through the node for processing and output across multiple channels.

outputs.name: ch1
outputs.description: Outputs the first channel of data processed by the node.

outputs.name: ch2
outputs.description: Outputs the second channel of data processed by the node.

outputs.name: ch3
outputs.description: Outputs the third channel of data processed by the node.

outputs.name: ch4
outputs.description: Outputs the fourth channel of data processed by the node.

outputs.name: ch5
outputs.description: Outputs the fifth channel of data processed by the node.

outputs.name: ch6
outputs.description: Outputs the sixth channel of data processed by the node.

outputs.name: ch7
outputs.description: Outputs the seventh channel of data processed by the node.

outputs.name: ch8
outputs.description: Outputs the eighth channel of data processed by the node.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: Provides a URL to a help page, offering guidance on how to use the CR 8 Channel Out node effectively.

CR Apply ControlNet.description: This node applies a ControlNet to an image based on specified conditions, allowing for dynamic image manipulation through control networks. It optionally provides a mechanism to adjust the intensity of the effect and to enable or disable the application of the ControlNet.

inputs.name: conditioning
inputs.description: Represents the conditions under which the ControlNet is applied, affecting how the image is manipulated.

inputs.name: control_net
inputs.description: The ControlNet to be applied to the image, defining the specific transformations or effects.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image to which the ControlNet is applied, serving as the base for manipulation.

inputs.name: switch
inputs.description: A toggle to enable or disable the application of the ControlNet, allowing for conditional application.

inputs.name: strength
inputs.description: Adjusts the intensity of the ControlNet's effect on the image, providing control over the manipulation's strength.

outputs.name: CONDITIONING
outputs.description: The modified conditions after applying the ControlNet.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL to documentation or help related to the node's functionality.

CR Apply LoRA Stack.description: The CR_ApplyLoRAStack node is designed to apply a stack of LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) modifications to a given model and clip, enhancing or altering their functionalities based on the specified LoRA parameters. It allows for dynamic customization of models through LoRA, facilitating fine-tuned adjustments and optimizations.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model to which the LoRA modifications will be applied. It serves as the base for the adaptations, determining the initial state before any LoRA adjustments.

inputs.name: clip
inputs.description: The clip to which the LoRA modifications will be applied, alongside the model. It represents another aspect of the system that can be adjusted using LoRA parameters for enhanced performance or functionality.

inputs.name: lora_stack
inputs.description: A list of LoRA modifications to be applied to the model and clip. Each item in the list specifies a LoRA modification, including its name and the strength of its application to the model and clip.

outputs.name: MODEL
outputs.description: The model after the application of the LoRA stack, potentially altered or enhanced by the specified LoRA modifications.

outputs.name: CLIP
outputs.description: The clip after the application of the LoRA stack, potentially altered or enhanced alongside the model by the specified LoRA modifications.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL providing additional information and guidance on using the CR_ApplyLoRAStack node and its functionalities.

CR Apply Model Merge.description: This node is designed to merge multiple models and CLIPs based on specified ratios, normalization settings, and merge methods. It supports weighted merging and normalization of ratios to ensure the combined model accurately reflects the desired blend of input models.

inputs.name: model_stack
inputs.description: A stack of models to be merged, each accompanied by model and CLIP ratios. It's crucial for determining the composition of the final merged model.

inputs.name: merge_method
inputs.description: Specifies the method used for merging models, such as weighted merging, affecting how input models are combined.

inputs.name: normalise_ratios
inputs.description: Indicates whether the ratios of models and CLIPs should be normalized, ensuring their sum equals 1 for a balanced merge.

inputs.name: weight_factor
inputs.description: A factor used in weighted merging to adjust the influence of each model in the final merge.

outputs.name: MODEL
outputs.description: The final merged model resulting from the combination of input models according to specified methods and ratios.

outputs.name: CLIP
outputs.description: The final merged CLIP model resulting from the combination of input CLIP models according to specified methods and ratios.

outputs.name: model_mix_info
outputs.description: Information about the merged models, including names, ratios, and any normalization or weighting adjustments applied.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL providing additional help and documentation on how to use the node effectively.

CR Apply Multi Upscale.description: This node is designed to apply multiple upscaling models sequentially to an image, enhancing its resolution. It allows for the customization of the upscaling process through a stack of models and rescaling factors, providing flexibility in achieving the desired image quality.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be upscaled. It serves as the base for the sequential application of multiple upscaling models, each potentially enhancing the image's resolution further.

inputs.name: resampling_method
inputs.description: Specifies the method used for resampling during the upscaling process, affecting the quality and characteristics of the upscaled image.
