inputs.name: supersample
inputs.description: Determines whether supersampling is applied, which can enhance the quality of the upscaled image by reducing aliasing effects.

inputs.name: rounding_modulus
inputs.description: Used to round the dimensions of the upscaled image, ensuring they are multiples of a specified value, which can be important for compatibility with certain processing or display requirements.

inputs.name: upscale_stack
inputs.description: A list of tuples, each containing an upscaling model and a rescale factor. This stack defines the sequence and parameters of upscaling models applied to the image, allowing for complex and customized upscaling processes.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: The output of the node is the upscaled image, which has undergone sequential upscaling and potential resizing based on the provided stack of models and rescaling factors.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL providing additional information and guidance on the use of the node and its parameters.

CR Apply Multi-ControlNet.description: This node is designed to apply a stack of multiple ControlNets to a given set of conditioning data. It iterates through each ControlNet in the stack, applying them sequentially to modify the conditioning data based on the ControlNet's specifications and the provided image, strength, and percentage range. This allows for complex and layered modifications to the conditioning data, enabling more nuanced and controlled generation processes.

inputs.name: base_positive
inputs.description: The initial positive conditioning data to which the ControlNet stack will be applied. This data serves as the starting point for the sequential application of ControlNets.

inputs.name: base_negative
inputs.description: The initial negative conditioning data to which the ControlNet stack will be applied. Similar to 'base_positive', this data is modified sequentially by the ControlNet stack.

inputs.name: switch
inputs.description: A control switch to enable or disable the application of the ControlNet stack. If set to 'Off', the node will bypass the application process and return the original conditioning data.

inputs.name: controlnet_stack
inputs.description: A list of tuples, each representing a ControlNet to be applied. Each tuple contains the ControlNet's name or object, the image to use for control hints, the strength of application, and the start and end percentages for application range.

outputs.name: base_pos
outputs.description: unknown

outputs.name: base_neg
outputs.description: unknown

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL providing help and additional information about the node and its usage.

CR Aspect Ratio Banners.description: This node is designed to adjust the aspect ratio of banners, allowing for customization of width, height, and aspect ratio parameters. It supports operations such as swapping dimensions, upscaling, and prescaling, catering to various banner size requirements.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Specifies the desired width of the banner. It plays a crucial role in determining the final dimensions of the banner after aspect ratio adjustments.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Defines the desired height of the banner. This parameter is essential for calculating the banner's dimensions in accordance with the specified aspect ratio.

inputs.name: aspect_ratio
inputs.description: Determines the target aspect ratio for the banner. This parameter is key to achieving the desired proportion between width and height.

inputs.name: swap_dimensions
inputs.description: Allows for the swapping of width and height dimensions. This feature is useful for adapting the banner to different orientation requirements.

inputs.name: upscale_factor
inputs.description: Specifies the factor by which the banner's dimensions should be upscaled. This parameter enables the enlargement of banners while maintaining their aspect ratio.

inputs.name: prescale_factor
inputs.description: Indicates the factor by which the banner's dimensions should be prescaled before any other adjustments. This is useful for initial size modifications.

inputs.name: batch_size
inputs.description: Defines the number of banners to process in a single batch. This parameter helps in optimizing the processing of multiple banners simultaneously.

outputs.name: width
outputs.description: The adjusted width of the banner after applying the specified aspect ratio and other adjustments.

outputs.name: height
outputs.description: The adjusted height of the banner after applying the specified aspect ratio and other adjustments.

outputs.name: upscale_factor
outputs.description: The factor by which the banner's dimensions have been upscaled.

outputs.name: prescale_factor
outputs.description: The factor by which the banner's dimensions have been prescaled before any other adjustments.

outputs.name: batch_size
outputs.description: The number of banners processed in the batch.

outputs.name: empty_latent
outputs.description: A tensor representing the latent space of the processed banners.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL to the help documentation for using the aspect ratio node.

CR Aspect Ratio SDXL.description: This node dynamically adjusts the aspect ratio of images, supporting a variety of predefined aspect ratios for different media formats such as cinema, portrait, and landscape. It caters specifically to the requirements of SDXL models, facilitating the resizing and reshaping of images according to the selected aspect ratio.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: The 'width' parameter specifies the initial width of the image before aspect ratio adjustments. It's essential for calculating the new dimensions based on the selected aspect ratio.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: The 'height' parameter specifies the initial height of the image before aspect ratio adjustments. It's crucial for determining the new dimensions in line with the chosen aspect ratio.

inputs.name: aspect_ratio
inputs.description: This parameter allows selection from a range of predefined aspect ratios, influencing the final dimensions of the image to match specific media formats.

inputs.name: swap_dimensions
inputs.description: When enabled, this parameter swaps the width and height of the image, effectively rotating it 90 degrees.

inputs.name: upscale_factor1
inputs.description: This parameter specifies the first factor by which the image's dimensions are upscaled after adjusting the aspect ratio.

inputs.name: upscale_factor2
inputs.description: This parameter specifies the second factor by which the image's dimensions are upscaled, offering additional control over the final image size.

inputs.name: batch_size
inputs.description: Defines the number of images processed in a batch, affecting the computation and memory usage.

outputs.name: INT
outputs.description: The adjusted width of the image after applying the aspect ratio changes.

outputs.name: FLOAT
outputs.description: The adjusted height of the image after applying the aspect ratio changes.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL providing additional information and guidance on using the aspect ratio node.

CR Aspect Ratio Social Media.description: This node is designed to adjust the dimensions of images to fit specific aspect ratios tailored for social media platforms. It provides functionality to modify width and height based on predefined social media sizes, allowing for dimension swapping, scaling, and batch processing of images.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Specifies the initial width of the image. It's a crucial parameter as it serves as a base for calculating the new dimensions according to the selected aspect ratio.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Specifies the initial height of the image. Along with width, it forms the basis for the new dimensions calculation according to the selected aspect ratio.

inputs.name: aspect_ratio
inputs.description: Determines the target aspect ratio for the image, based on common social media platform requirements.

inputs.name: swap_dimensions
inputs.description: Allows for the swapping of width and height dimensions to accommodate different orientation needs.

inputs.name: upscale_factor
inputs.description: Defines the factor by which the image should be upscaled after adjusting to the target aspect ratio.

inputs.name: prescale_factor
inputs.description: Defines the factor by which the image should be prescaled before adjusting to the target aspect ratio.

inputs.name: batch_size
inputs.description: Specifies the number of images to process in a batch, facilitating batch processing.

outputs.name: width
outputs.description: The adjusted width of the image after applying the aspect ratio and scaling factors.

outputs.name: height
outputs.description: The adjusted height of the image after applying the aspect ratio and scaling factors.

outputs.name: upscale_factor
outputs.description: The factor by which the image has been upscaled.

outputs.name: prescale_factor
outputs.description: The factor by which the image has been prescaled.

outputs.name: batch_size
outputs.description: The number of images processed in the batch.

outputs.name: empty_latent
outputs.description: A tensor placeholder for further processing, representing the batch of images after resizing and scaling.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL providing additional help and documentation related to aspect ratio adjustments for social media.

CR Aspect Ratio.description: This node is designed to adjust the aspect ratio of images, ensuring they fit specific dimensions or standards. It's particularly useful in scenarios where maintaining the visual integrity of an image across different display sizes or formats is crucial.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Specifies the desired width of the output image. This parameter plays a crucial role in determining the final dimensions of the image after aspect ratio adjustments.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Specifies the desired height of the output image. Along with width, this parameter is essential for defining the final dimensions of the image post-adjustment.

inputs.name: aspect_ratio
inputs.description: Defines the aspect ratio to apply to the image. This parameter is key in ensuring the image fits the desired dimensions while maintaining its visual integrity.

inputs.name: swap_dimensions
inputs.description: Determines whether the width and height dimensions should be swapped. This is useful for rotating images or changing their orientation.

inputs.name: upscale_factor
inputs.description: Specifies the factor by which the image should be upscaled. This is important for enhancing image quality in larger displays.

inputs.name: prescale_factor
inputs.description: Specifies the factor by which the image should be prescaled before applying the aspect ratio adjustments. This helps in optimizing the processing for different image sizes.

inputs.name: batch_size
inputs.description: Defines the number of images to process in a single batch. This parameter is crucial for optimizing performance and resource utilization during batch processing.

outputs.name: width
outputs.description: The adjusted width of the image after applying the aspect ratio adjustments.

outputs.name: height
outputs.description: The adjusted height of the image after applying the aspect ratio adjustments.

outputs.name: upscale_factor
outputs.description: The factor by which the image has been upscaled during the aspect ratio adjustment process.

outputs.name: prescale_factor
outputs.description: The factor by which the image has been prescaled before applying the aspect ratio adjustments.

outputs.name: batch_size
outputs.description: The number of images processed in the batch.

outputs.name: empty_latent
outputs.description: A tensor representing the latent space of the processed images.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL to a help page with more information about aspect ratio adjustments.

CR Batch Images From List.description: This node is designed to transform a list of images into a batched format, facilitating operations that require batch processing. It also provides a help link for further guidance on list-related operations.

inputs.name: image_list
inputs.description: The list of images to be batched. This input is crucial for the node's operation as it directly influences the creation of the batched images output.

outputs.name: image_batch
outputs.description: The batched format of the input images, enabling efficient batch processing in subsequent operations.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL providing additional help and guidance on list-related operations within the ComfyUI ecosystem.

CR Batch Process Switch.description: The CR Batch Process Switch node is designed to selectively process images or image batches based on a specified input type. It facilitates the dynamic handling of either single images or batches of images, providing a flexible approach to image processing workflows.

inputs.name: Input
inputs.description: Determines whether a single image or a batch of images is processed, affecting the node's execution path and the resulting output.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The single image to be processed if 'Input' is set to 'image'.

inputs.name: image_batch
inputs.description: The batch of images to be processed if 'Input' is set to 'image batch'.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: The processed image or image batch, depending on the input type selected.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL providing additional help and documentation related to the node's functionality.

CR Binary Pattern.description: This node is designed to generate complex binary patterns, offering a creative tool for generating intricate designs and textures based on binary logic. It abstracts the complexity of creating binary patterns, making it accessible for users to incorporate these patterns into their graphics projects.

inputs.name: binary_pattern
inputs.description: Specifies the binary pattern as a multiline string, where each line represents a row in the pattern. This pattern determines the visual structure of the generated image.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Sets the width of the output image. It defines the horizontal dimension of the canvas on which the binary pattern will be drawn.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Sets the height of the output image. It defines the vertical dimension of the canvas on which the binary pattern will be drawn.

inputs.name: background_color
inputs.description: Determines the background color of the output image. It sets the color that will appear in the background of the binary pattern.

inputs.name: color_0
inputs.description: Specifies the color for the '0' bits in the binary pattern. This color will fill the squares corresponding to '0' bits.

inputs.name: color_1
inputs.description: Specifies the color for the '1' bits in the binary pattern. This color will fill the squares corresponding to '1' bits.

inputs.name: outline_thickness
inputs.description: Defines the thickness of the outline around each square in the pattern. A thickness of 0 means no outline.

inputs.name: outline_color
inputs.description: Sets the color of the outline around each square in the pattern.

inputs.name: jitter_distance
inputs.description: Specifies the maximum distance that squares in the pattern can be randomly displaced to create a jitter effect.

inputs.name: bias
inputs.description: Adjusts the probability of a square being colored with 'color_1' over 'color_0', allowing for more control over the pattern's appearance.

inputs.name: bg_color_hex
inputs.description: An optional hexadecimal value specifying the background color, providing an alternative to the 'background_color' input.

inputs.name: color0_hex
inputs.description: An optional hexadecimal value specifying the color for '0' bits, providing an alternative to the 'color_0' input.

inputs.name: color1_hex
inputs.description: An optional hexadecimal value specifying the color for '1' bits, providing an alternative to the 'color_1' input.

inputs.name: outline_color_hex
inputs.description: An optional hexadecimal value specifying the outline color, providing an alternative to the 'outline_color' input.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: The generated image based on the specified binary pattern and color settings.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL to a help page providing additional information and guidance on using the binary pattern node.

CR Binary To Bit List.description: The CR_BinaryToBitList node is designed to convert a binary string into a list of individual bits. It aims to facilitate the manipulation and analysis of binary data by breaking it down into its constituent bits.

inputs.name: bit_string
inputs.description: The 'bit_string' parameter represents the binary string to be converted into a list of bits. It is essential for specifying the binary data that the node will process.

outputs.name: STRING
outputs.description: This output is a list where each element represents an individual bit from the input binary string.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL providing access to additional information and documentation about the CR_BinaryToBitList node.

CR Bit Schedule.description: The CR Bit Schedule node is designed to generate a schedule based on a binary string, where each bit represents a state at a given interval over a specified number of loops. It abstracts the process of creating time-based sequences from binary data, facilitating the scheduling of animations or other time-sensitive operations.

inputs.name: binary_string
inputs.description: The binary string input represents a sequence of states (0 or 1) that are used to generate the schedule. Each bit in the string corresponds to a state at a specific time interval, playing a crucial role in defining the schedule's structure.

inputs.name: interval
inputs.description: The interval input specifies the time gap between each state in the schedule, determining the pace at which the binary string's states are processed and included in the schedule.

inputs.name: loops
inputs.description: The loops input defines how many times the binary string is repeated in the schedule, allowing for the extension or repetition of the sequence to meet the desired duration.

outputs.name: SCHEDULE
outputs.description: The SCHEDULE output is a string representation of the generated schedule, where each line corresponds to a time-stamped state derived from the binary string.

outputs.name: show_text
outputs.description: The show_text output provides a link to helpful documentation or additional information related to the node's functionality.

CR Central Schedule.description: This node serves as a central hub for managing and coordinating multiple animation schedules within a project. It allows for the integration and synchronization of various animation schedules, ensuring a cohesive animation flow across different elements or scenes.

inputs.name: schedule_1
inputs.description: Defines the first animation schedule to be managed, allowing for the specification of complex animation sequences.

inputs.name: schedule_type1
inputs.description: Specifies the type of the first animation schedule, categorizing it for appropriate processing and integration.

inputs.name: schedule_alias1
inputs.description: Provides an alias for the first animation schedule, facilitating easier reference and management within the node.

inputs.name: schedule_2
inputs.description: Defines the second animation schedule to be managed, extending the node's capability to coordinate multiple schedules.

inputs.name: schedule_type2
inputs.description: Specifies the type of the second animation schedule, enhancing the node's ability to categorize and process various schedules.

inputs.name: schedule_alias2
inputs.description: Provides an alias for the second animation schedule, aiding in its identification and management.

inputs.name: schedule_3
inputs.description: Defines the third animation schedule to be managed, further broadening the node's capacity to handle multiple animation sequences.

inputs.name: schedule_type3
inputs.description: Specifies the type of the third animation schedule, allowing for its proper categorization and integration.

inputs.name: schedule_alias3
inputs.description: Provides an alias for the third animation schedule, simplifying its reference and management.

inputs.name: schedule_format
inputs.description: Determines the format in which the schedules are to be processed, supporting different animation frameworks.

inputs.name: schedule
inputs.description: An optional schedule parameter that can be used to provide additional scheduling information.

outputs.name: SCHEDULE
outputs.description: The combined or processed animation schedule resulting from the node's operation, ready for use in the animation project.

outputs.name: show_text
outputs.description: Provides textual information or feedback about the processed schedule, aiding in debugging or further adjustments.

CR Checker Pattern.description: This node is designed to generate checkerboard patterns, allowing users to create visually appealing designs or backgrounds by specifying pattern parameters. It abstracts the complexity of generating such patterns programmatically, offering a simple interface for customization.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Specifies the mode of the checkerboard pattern generation, affecting the overall appearance and style of the output.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Determines the width of the generated checkerboard pattern, directly influencing the size of the output image.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Sets the height of the generated checkerboard pattern, directly influencing the size of the output image.

inputs.name: color_1
inputs.description: Defines the first color used in the checkerboard pattern, contributing to the visual aesthetics of the design.

inputs.name: color_2
inputs.description: Specifies the second color used in the checkerboard pattern, complementing the first color to create the checkerboard effect.

inputs.name: grid_frequency
inputs.description: Controls the frequency of the grid within the checkerboard pattern, affecting the density of the checkers.

inputs.name: step
inputs.description: Adjusts the step size between each checker in the pattern, allowing for customization of the checker spacing.

inputs.name: color1_hex
inputs.description: Provides an alternative way to specify the first color using hexadecimal color codes.

inputs.name: color2_hex
inputs.description: Provides an alternative way to specify the second color using hexadecimal color codes.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: The generated checkerboard pattern image, ready for use or further processing.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A link to additional documentation or help related to the checkerboard pattern generation.

CR Clamp Value.description: The CR Clamp Value node is designed to restrict a given value within a specified range, ensuring that the output value does not exceed the defined minimum and maximum limits. This functionality is crucial for maintaining data integrity and preventing errors in downstream processes that rely on bounded inputs.

inputs.name: a
inputs.description: The value to be clamped. It is the primary input whose final output is constrained within the specified range.

inputs.name: range_min
inputs.description: The minimum allowable value for the input. If 'a' is less than this value, 'a' is set to this minimum value.

inputs.name: range_max
inputs.description: The maximum allowable value for the input. If 'a' is greater than this value, 'a' is set to this maximum value.

outputs.name: a
outputs.description: The clamped value, adjusted to fall within the specified range.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL to the node's documentation, providing additional help and examples.

CR Clip Input Switch.description: This node allows for the dynamic selection between two clip inputs based on a specified integer input. It is designed to facilitate conditional logic within workflows, enabling the choice of clip to be used in subsequent operations.

inputs.name: Input
inputs.description: Determines which clip input to select. An input of 1 selects the first clip, while an input of 2 selects the second clip.

inputs.name: clip1
inputs.description: The first clip option that can be selected based on the input value.

inputs.name: clip2
inputs.description: The second clip option that can be selected based on the input value.

outputs.name: CLIP
outputs.description: The selected clip based on the input value.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL providing additional help and documentation for using the node.

CR Color Bars.description: The CR Color Bars node is designed to generate customizable color bar patterns. It allows users to specify various parameters such as color, orientation, and frequency to create visually appealing bar patterns on a canvas. This node leverages color mapping and geometric calculations to produce a wide range of artistic and design-oriented outputs.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: The 'mode' parameter determines the pattern style of the color bars, affecting the overall appearance of the generated image.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Specifies the width of the canvas for the color bars, influencing the size of the generated pattern.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Determines the height of the canvas, impacting the vertical scale of the color bar pattern.

inputs.name: color_1
inputs.description: Specifies the first color used in the color bar pattern, contributing to the visual appeal and theme of the output.

inputs.name: color_2
inputs.description: Specifies the second color used in the color bar pattern, complementing the first color to enhance the pattern's aesthetic.

inputs.name: orientation
inputs.description: Sets the orientation of the color bars (e.g., vertical, horizontal, diagonal), affecting the direction in which the bars are drawn.

inputs.name: bar_frequency
inputs.description: Controls the frequency of the color bars, influencing the density and spacing of the bars in the pattern.

inputs.name: offset
inputs.description: Determines the starting point of the color bars, allowing for adjustments in the pattern's alignment and positioning.

inputs.name: color1_hex
inputs.description: Provides a custom hexadecimal color value for the first color, offering enhanced customization for the color scheme.

inputs.name: color2_hex
inputs.description: Provides a custom hexadecimal color value for the second color, allowing for precise color matching in the pattern.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: The generated image data encapsulating the color bar pattern as per the specified parameters.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: Provides help or guidance related to the usage of the node and its parameters.

CR Color Gradient.description: The CR Color Gradient node is designed to generate a color gradient between two specified colors over a given canvas. It allows for customization of the gradient's orientation, transition style, and distance, enabling the creation of visually appealing backgrounds or elements with smooth color transitions.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: The width of the canvas on which the gradient will be applied, impacting the horizontal dimension of the gradient.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: The height of the canvas on which the gradient will be applied, affecting the vertical dimension of the gradient.

inputs.name: start_color
inputs.description: Specifies the starting color of the gradient. It can be a predefined color name or 'custom' to use a specific hex color code, influencing the gradient's initial color.

inputs.name: end_color
inputs.description: Defines the ending color of the gradient. Similar to 'start_color', it can be a predefined color name or 'custom' for a hex color code, determining the gradient's final color.

inputs.name: gradient_distance
inputs.description: Specifies the distance over which the gradient transition occurs, with a value between 0 and 1 representing the proportion of the canvas covered by the gradient.

inputs.name: linear_transition
inputs.description: A value between 0 and 1 indicating the position of the gradient transition's center point, with 0 being the start and 1 the end of the canvas.

inputs.name: orientation
inputs.description: Determines the orientation of the gradient (horizontal or vertical), influencing the direction in which the color transition occurs.

inputs.name: start_color_hex
inputs.description: The hex color code for the starting color, used when 'start_color' is set to 'custom'. It provides precise control over the gradient's initial color.

inputs.name: end_color_hex
inputs.description: The hex color code for the ending color, used when 'end_color' is set to 'custom'. It allows for exact specification of the gradient's final color.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: The resulting image with the applied color gradient, ready for display or further processing.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL to a help page providing additional information and guidance on using the CR Color Gradient node.

CR Color Panel.description: The CR_ColorPanel node is designed to generate a simple color panel image with customizable dimensions and fill color. It allows for the creation of a solid color background that can be used in various graphical layouts or as a base for further graphical manipulation.

inputs.name: panel_width
inputs.description: Specifies the width of the color panel. The width influences the size of the generated image, allowing for customization according to the user's needs.

inputs.name: panel_height
inputs.description: Determines the height of the color panel. Similar to the width, it affects the overall size of the output image, providing flexibility in the panel's dimensions.

inputs.name: fill_color
inputs.description: Defines the primary color used to fill the panel. This parameter is crucial for setting the visual appearance of the color panel.

inputs.name: fill_color_hex
inputs.description: An optional hexadecimal color code that can override the primary fill color, offering an alternative method for specifying the panel's color.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The generated color panel as an image, ready for use in various graphical contexts.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL providing additional help and documentation related to the CR_ColorPanel node.

CR Color Tint.description: The CR_ColorTint node applies a color tint to an image, allowing for the adjustment of the image's color tone based on a specified strength and color mode. It supports a variety of predefined color modes as well as custom color inputs, enabling a wide range of visual effects.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to which the color tint will be applied. This parameter is crucial as it serves as the base for the tinting process.

inputs.name: strength
inputs.description: Determines the intensity of the color tint applied to the image. A higher value results in a more pronounced color effect.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Specifies the color mode for the tint. This can be a predefined color mode such as 'sepia', 'red', or 'blue', or a custom color defined by 'tint_color_hex'.

inputs.name: tint_color_hex
inputs.description: The hexadecimal color code for the tint when 'mode' is set to 'custom'. This allows for precise control over the tint color.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: The image after the color tint has been applied, reflecting the specified strength and color mode.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL to the documentation or help page for the CR_ColorTint node.

CR Combine Prompt.description: The CR_CombinePrompt node is designed to concatenate multiple string inputs into a single string output, using a specified separator. This functionality is useful for dynamically constructing prompts or text sequences in a flexible manner.

inputs.name: part1
inputs.description: The first part of the prompt to be combined. It contributes to the beginning of the final concatenated string.

inputs.name: part2
inputs.description: The second part of the prompt to be combined. It is appended after the first part, separated by the specified separator.

inputs.name: part3
inputs.description: The third part of the prompt to be combined. It follows the second part, further extending the concatenated string.

inputs.name: part4
inputs.description: The fourth and final part of the prompt to be combined. It concludes the concatenated string.

inputs.name: separator
inputs.description: The string used to separate each part of the prompt in the final concatenated output.

outputs.name: prompt
outputs.description: The final concatenated string resulting from combining the specified parts with the separator.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL providing additional help and documentation related to the node's functionality.

CR Combine Schedules.description: The CR Combine Schedules node is designed to merge multiple animation schedules into a single comprehensive schedule. It facilitates the integration of various animation sequences by combining their schedules, enhancing the flexibility and complexity of animation planning.

inputs.name: schedule_1
inputs.description: Represents the first animation schedule to be combined. Its inclusion allows for the sequential integration of multiple schedules, contributing to the creation of a unified animation timeline.

inputs.name: schedule_2
inputs.description: Represents the second animation schedule to be combined, further enriching the unified animation timeline by adding its sequence.

inputs.name: schedule_3
inputs.description: Represents the third animation schedule to be combined, adding another layer of complexity to the unified animation timeline.

inputs.name: schedule_4
inputs.description: Represents the fourth animation schedule to be combined, completing the integration of multiple animation sequences into a single comprehensive schedule.

outputs.name: SCHEDULE
outputs.description: The combined list of schedules from all provided animation sequences.

outputs.name: show_text
outputs.description: A concatenated string representation of all schedules, intended for display or debugging purposes.

CR Comic Panel Templates.description: This node is designed to generate comic panel layouts based on predefined templates. It dynamically creates and arranges panels within a page, allowing for customization of panel sizes, colors, and border styles to fit various comic storytelling needs.

inputs.name: page_width
inputs.description: Specifies the width of the page on which the comic panels will be drawn, influencing the layout's scale and the size of individual panels.

inputs.name: page_height
inputs.description: Determines the height of the page, affecting the overall layout and the vertical size of the comic panels.

inputs.name: template
inputs.description: Defines the template used for the comic panel layout, which can be a predefined template or a custom layout specified by the user.

inputs.name: reading_direction
inputs.description: Indicates the direction in which the comic should be read, affecting the arrangement and flow of the panels.

inputs.name: border_thickness
inputs.description: Defines the thickness of the borders around each panel, contributing to the visual style of the comic.

inputs.name: outline_thickness
inputs.description: Sets the thickness of the outline around the page and panels, impacting the comic's aesthetic appeal.

inputs.name: outline_color
inputs.description: Specifies the color of the outline around the panels and page, adding to the visual design of the comic.

inputs.name: panel_color
inputs.description: Determines the color of the panel backgrounds, influencing the mood and style of the comic.

inputs.name: background_color
inputs.description: Sets the background color of the page, framing the panels and contributing to the overall visual theme.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: A collection of images to be placed within the comic panels. This parameter is crucial for populating the panels with visual content, significantly enhancing the storytelling aspect of the comic.

inputs.name: custom_panel_layout
inputs.description: Allows for the specification of a custom layout for the comic panels, offering flexibility in design beyond predefined templates.

inputs.name: outline_color_hex
inputs.description: Provides a hexadecimal color code for the outline color, offering precise color customization.

inputs.name: panel_color_hex
inputs.description: Gives a hexadecimal color code for the panel color, allowing for exact color selection.

inputs.name: bg_color_hex
inputs.description: Specifies a hexadecimal color code for the background color, enabling detailed color customization.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The final image output containing the generated comic panel layout.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A string output providing guidance or additional information related to the generated comic panel layout.

CR Composite Text.description: This node is designed for the advanced manipulation and combination of text elements within images, enabling users to create complex text overlays and compositions. It likely offers functionalities for adjusting text properties such as font, size, and alignment, as well as the ability to blend text with images in various creative ways.

inputs.name: image_text
inputs.description: The image onto which the text will be composited. This parameter is essential for integrating the text with the visual content.

inputs.name: image_background
inputs.description: The background image over which the text and foreground image will be composited, providing a backdrop for the composition.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The primary text content to be composited onto an image. This parameter is crucial for defining the textual element of the composition.

inputs.name: font_name
inputs.description: Specifies the font style to be used for the text, impacting the visual appearance of the text element within the composition.

inputs.name: font_size
inputs.description: Determines the size of the text, allowing for precise control over how the text fits within the overall image composition.

inputs.name: align
inputs.description: Controls the horizontal alignment of the text within the image, enabling users to position the text according to their compositional needs.

inputs.name: justify
inputs.description: Controls the vertical alignment and distribution of text lines within the image, further refining the text's placement and appearance.

inputs.name: margins
inputs.description: Defines the margins around the text, providing space between the text and the edges of the image or other compositional elements.

inputs.name: line_spacing
inputs.description: Adjusts the spacing between lines of text, allowing for better readability and aesthetic arrangement of the text content.

inputs.name: position_x
inputs.description: Specifies the x-coordinate for the position of the text within the image, enabling precise placement.

inputs.name: position_y
inputs.description: Specifies the y-coordinate for the position of the text within the image, enabling precise placement.

inputs.name: rotation_angle
inputs.description: Defines the angle at which the text will be rotated, allowing for dynamic and creative text orientations.

inputs.name: rotation_options
inputs.description: Provides additional options for text rotation, such as the point around which the text should rotate, enhancing the flexibility of text positioning.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: The resulting image after the text has been composited onto it. This output showcases the integration of text and image elements.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: Optional output that provides help or guidance related to the node's functionality or output.

CR Conditioning Input Switch.description: This node allows for the dynamic selection between two conditioning inputs based on a specified integer input. It facilitates conditional logic in data flow, enabling the choice of different conditioning paths within a workflow.

inputs.name: Input
inputs.description: Determines which conditioning input to pass through. An input of 1 selects the first conditioning option, while an input of 2 selects the second.

inputs.name: conditioning1
inputs.description: The first conditioning option that can be selected based on the input value.

inputs.name: conditioning2
inputs.description: The second conditioning option that can be selected based on the input value.

outputs.name: CONDITIONING
outputs.description: The selected conditioning input based on the provided integer input.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: Provides a URL to the help documentation for this node.

CR Conditioning Mixer.description: The CR Conditioning Mixer node is designed to blend or combine different conditioning inputs into a single, cohesive output. It supports various mixing methods such as combining, averaging, or concatenating conditioning inputs, allowing for flexible manipulation of conditioning data.

inputs.name: conditioning_1
inputs.description: The first set of conditioning inputs to be mixed. It serves as a base or starting point for the mixing process.

inputs.name: conditioning_2
inputs.description: The second set of conditioning inputs to be mixed with the first set. It adds or modifies the initial conditioning based on the mixing method.

inputs.name: mix_method
inputs.description: Specifies the method used for mixing the conditioning inputs. It affects how the inputs are blended together, offering options like 'Combine', 'Average', or 'Concatenate'.

inputs.name: average_strength
inputs.description: Determines the strength or weight of the second set of conditioning inputs when using the 'Average' mixing method. It controls the balance between the two sets of inputs.

outputs.name: CONDITIONING
outputs.description: The result of mixing the conditioning inputs according to the specified method. It represents the blended conditioning data.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: Provides a URL to a help page with more information about the CR Conditioning Mixer node and its usage.

CR ControlNet Input Switch.description: This node serves as a dynamic switch between two control networks based on a specified input. It allows for the selection of one of two control networks to be used in a workflow, enhancing flexibility and control in the processing pipeline.

inputs.name: Input
inputs.description: Determines which control network to select for use in the workflow. The choice affects the control flow and the resulting control network output.

inputs.name: control_net1
inputs.description: The first control network option that can be selected based on the input. Provides a pathway for control flow based on the selection.

inputs.name: control_net2
inputs.description: The second control network option that can be selected. Offers an alternative pathway for control flow, enhancing the node's flexibility.

inputs.name: control_net1
inputs.description: The first control network option that can be selected based on the input. Provides a pathway for control flow based on the selection.

inputs.name: control_net2
inputs.description: The second control network option that can be selected. Offers an alternative pathway for control flow, enhancing the node's flexibility.

outputs.name: CONTROL_NET
outputs.description: The control network selected based on the input. This output is used for further processing in the workflow.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL providing documentation and help for using the CR_ControlNetInputSwitch node.

CR Current Frame.description: The CR Current Frame node is designed to manage and optionally display the current frame index within an animation sequence. It allows for the adjustment of the frame index and provides an option to print the current frame index to the console, facilitating debugging and tracking of animation progress.

inputs.name: index
inputs.description: Specifies the current frame index. It is crucial for determining the specific frame being processed or displayed in the animation sequence.

inputs.name: print_to_console
inputs.description: Determines whether the current frame index should be printed to the console. This is useful for debugging purposes and tracking the progress of the animation.

outputs.name: index
outputs.description: Returns the current frame index. This is essential for tracking the progress of the animation and for further processing of the specific frame.

CR Cycle Images Simple.description: This node is designed to cycle through a simple list of images in a sequential manner, based on the current frame and a specified frame interval. It allows for the creation of simple animations by iterating over a collection of images a specified number of times (loops).

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Specifies the cycling mode, which determines how images are cycled through. For this node, 'Sequential' mode is used to cycle images in order.

inputs.name: frame_interval
inputs.description: Defines the number of frames to wait before transitioning to the next image in the sequence, allowing control over the animation speed.

inputs.name: loops
inputs.description: Determines how many times the list of images will be cycled through, enabling repeated animations.

inputs.name: current_frame
inputs.description: Indicates the current frame number in the animation sequence, used to calculate which image to display.

inputs.name: image_1
inputs.description: The first image in the sequence to be cycled through.

inputs.name: image_2
inputs.description: The second image in the sequence to be cycled through.

inputs.name: image_3
inputs.description: The third image in the sequence to be cycled through.

inputs.name: image_4
inputs.description: The fourth image in the sequence to be cycled through.

inputs.name: image_5
inputs.description: The fifth image in the sequence to be cycled through.

inputs.name: image_list_simple
inputs.description: An optional list of images to be cycled through, providing an alternative or additional set of images for the animation.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: The image to be displayed at the current frame of the animation.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL providing additional help and information about the node.

CR Cycle Images.description: This node is designed to cycle through a sequence of images based on specified parameters, allowing for the creation of animations or slideshows. It supports looping through the images multiple times and selecting images in a sequential order, providing a dynamic visual experience.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Specifies the cycling mode, which determines how images are selected during the animation. 'Sequential' mode cycles through images in the order they are provided.

inputs.name: image_list
inputs.description: A list of images to be cycled through. Each item in the list represents an image and its associated parameters, enabling complex animations.

inputs.name: frame_interval
inputs.description: The interval between frames, which controls the speed of the animation. A lower value results in a faster animation.

inputs.name: loops
inputs.description: Determines how many times the sequence of images is repeated, allowing for continuous animations.

inputs.name: current_frame
inputs.description: The current frame number in the animation sequence. It is used to calculate which image to display at any given time.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: The current image to be displayed based on the cycling logic. It changes over time as the animation progresses.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL to a help page providing additional information and guidance on using the node.

CR Cycle LoRAs.description: This node is designed to cycle through a predefined list of LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) parameters sequentially or based on a schedule, applying them to a model and clip at specified intervals. It enables dynamic modification of model behaviors over time or frames, enhancing the versatility and customization of generative processes.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: The 'mode' input determines the cycling strategy for applying LoRA parameters, either sequentially or based on a specific schedule, influencing the dynamic adaptation process.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The 'model' input represents the generative model to which the LoRA parameters will be applied, serving as a base for modifications.

inputs.name: clip
inputs.description: The 'clip' input signifies the CLIP model that will be modified alongside the generative model, using the specified LoRA parameters.

inputs.name: lora_list
inputs.description: The 'lora_list' input contains the predefined list of LoRA parameters to cycle through, dictating the specific adaptations to apply.

inputs.name: frame_interval
inputs.description: The 'frame_interval' input specifies the interval between each LoRA parameter application, controlling the pace of modifications.

inputs.name: loops
inputs.description: The 'loops' input indicates the number of times the cycling process should repeat, affecting the overall duration of the adaptation.

inputs.name: current_frame
inputs.description: The 'current_frame' input is used to determine the current position in the cycling schedule, guiding the selection of LoRA parameters.

outputs.name: MODEL
outputs.description: The 'MODEL' output refers to the modified generative model after the application of the current LoRA parameters.

outputs.name: CLIP
outputs.description: The 'CLIP' output signifies the modified CLIP model after the application of the current LoRA parameters.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: The 'show_help' output provides a URL to documentation or further information regarding the applied LoRA parameters.

CR Cycle Models.description: This node is designed to cycle through different models sequentially or maintain a single model based on the specified mode. It facilitates dynamic model switching during animation sequences, enhancing the versatility and creativity of the animation process.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Specifies the cycling mode, such as 'Off' for no cycling or 'Sequential' for cycling through models based on the current frame and interval settings.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The initial model to be used before any cycling occurs. It serves as the default model when the cycling mode is set to 'Off'.

inputs.name: clip
inputs.description: The initial CLIP model to be used alongside the main model, providing additional capabilities or enhancements.

inputs.name: model_list
inputs.description: A list of models to cycle through, each defined by its parameters including model alias and checkpoint name.

inputs.name: frame_interval
inputs.description: The interval between frames at which the model cycling occurs, determining the frequency of model switches.

inputs.name: loops
inputs.description: The number of times the model list is repeated, extending the sequence of models available for cycling.

inputs.name: current_frame
inputs.description: The current frame number in the animation sequence, used to determine the active model based on the cycling mode and frame interval.

outputs.name: MODEL
outputs.description: The current model after cycling, which may be different from the initial model depending on the cycling mode and frame progress.

outputs.name: CLIP
outputs.description: The current CLIP model after cycling, which may be different from the initial CLIP model depending on the cycling mode and frame progress.

outputs.name: VAE
outputs.description: The current VAE model after cycling, which may be different from the initial VAE model depending on the cycling mode and frame progress.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A help URL providing additional information about the cycling process.

CR Cycle Text Simple.description: This node is designed to cycle through a list of text strings in a specified mode, allowing for dynamic text animation within a sequence. It supports sequential cycling through texts based on frame intervals and loop counts, making it suitable for creating text-based animations or dynamic text displays in various applications.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Specifies the cycling mode, which determines how the text strings are cycled through. The mode 'Sequential' is supported, enabling the texts to be displayed one after another in order.

inputs.name: frame_interval
inputs.description: The interval, in frames, between each text change. This parameter controls the speed of the text cycling animation.

inputs.name: loops
inputs.description: The number of times the entire text list is repeated. This affects the total duration of the text cycling animation.

inputs.name: current_frame
inputs.description: The current frame number in the animation sequence. It is used to determine which text string should be displayed based on the frame interval and loops.

inputs.name: text_1
inputs.description: The first text string to be included in the cycling animation. If empty, it will be skipped.

inputs.name: text_2
inputs.description: The second text string to be included in the cycling animation. If empty, it will be skipped.

inputs.name: text_3
inputs.description: The third text string to be included in the cycling animation. If empty, it will be skipped.

inputs.name: text_4
inputs.description: The fourth text string to be included in the cycling animation. If empty, it will be skipped.

inputs.name: text_5
inputs.description: The fifth text string to be included in the cycling animation. If empty, it will be skipped.

inputs.name: text_list_simple
inputs.description: An optional list of text strings to be included in the cycling animation, in addition to the individual text inputs.

outputs.name: STRING
outputs.description: The text string that is currently selected to be displayed based on the mode, frame interval, loops, and current frame.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL to a help page providing additional information and guidance on using the CR Cycle Text Simple node.

CR Cycle Text.description: The CR Cycle Text node is designed to cycle through a list of text strings based on a specified mode, frame interval, and number of loops. It dynamically selects and outputs text strings for animation or display purposes, allowing for sequential or custom cycling patterns.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Specifies the cycling mode, such as 'Sequential', which determines how text strings are selected and cycled through during execution.

inputs.name: text_list
inputs.description: A list of text strings to be cycled through. This list forms the basis of the cycling operation, with each string potentially being displayed or used in sequence or according to the specified mode.

inputs.name: frame_interval
inputs.description: The interval between frames, used to calculate the current text string to display based on the current frame. This parameter influences the pace at which text strings are cycled through.

inputs.name: loops
inputs.description: The number of times the text list is looped through. This affects the total duration of the cycling operation.

inputs.name: current_frame
inputs.description: The current frame number, used in conjunction with the frame interval to determine the current text string to display.

outputs.name: STRING
outputs.description: The currently selected text string based on the cycling mode, frame interval, and current frame.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL to a help page providing additional information and guidance on using the CR Cycle Text node.

CR Data Bus In.description: The CR Data Bus In node is designed for loading and initializing data into a pipeline, allowing for optional inputs to be provided and utilized within the data flow. It serves as an entry point for data, facilitating the integration and manipulation of various data types as they enter the system.

inputs.name: pipe
inputs.description: Represents the primary data conduit into which data is loaded. It can optionally accept a tuple of any types, enabling the flexible integration of data into the pipeline.

inputs.name: any1
inputs.description: An optional input parameter that can be used to provide additional data or override the first element of the 'pipe' tuple if both are provided.

inputs.name: any2
inputs.description: Similar to 'any1', this optional input parameter allows for the provision or overriding of the second element in the 'pipe' tuple.

inputs.name: any3
inputs.description: This optional parameter enables the provision or overriding of the third element in the 'pipe' tuple, allowing for further customization of the data flow.

inputs.name: any4
inputs.description: Allows for the provision or overriding of the fourth element in the 'pipe' tuple, facilitating additional flexibility in how data is integrated into the pipeline.

outputs.name: pipe
outputs.description: Outputs a tuple representing the loaded data, potentially modified by the optional input parameters. This tuple serves as the processed data ready for further manipulation or analysis in subsequent nodes.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: Provides a URL to the documentation or help page for this node, offering users guidance and additional information on its usage.

CR Data Bus Out.description: The CR Data Bus Out node is designed to output data from a pipeline, allowing for the transfer of multiple data types through a single pipe. It also provides a link to documentation for further assistance.

inputs.name: pipe
inputs.description: The 'pipe' parameter is a tuple that carries the data to be outputted. It is essential for transferring the data through the pipeline.

outputs.name: pipe
outputs.description: Returns the modified or unmodified 'pipe' tuple, depending on the input parameters.

outputs.name: any1
outputs.description: Returns the first element of the 'pipe' tuple, potentially modified by the input parameter 'any1'.

outputs.name: any2
outputs.description: Returns the second element of the 'pipe' tuple, potentially modified by the input parameter 'any2'.

outputs.name: any3
outputs.description: Returns the third element of the 'pipe' tuple, potentially modified by the input parameter 'any3'.

outputs.name: any4
outputs.description: Returns the fourth element of the 'pipe' tuple, potentially modified by the input parameter 'any4'.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: Provides a URL to the documentation for further assistance with the node.

CR Debatch Frames.description: The CR_DebatchFrames node is designed to transform a batch of image frames into a list of individual frames, facilitating frame-by-frame processing or analysis within animation workflows.

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: The 'frames' parameter represents a batch of image frames to be debatched into individual frames. This is essential for operations that require handling each frame separately, such as animation frame processing.

outputs.name: debatched_frames
outputs.description: A list of individual image frames, each extracted from the input batch. This allows for frame-by-frame manipulation or analysis.

CR Diamond Panel.description: The CR_DiamondPanel node is designed to create and manipulate diamond-shaped panels within a graphical layout. It focuses on generating unique diamond patterns and layouts, offering a specialized tool for enhancing visual designs with geometric shapes.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The 'image' input specifies the base image on which the diamond panel pattern will be applied, serving as the foundation for the pattern generation.

inputs.name: pattern
inputs.description: The 'pattern' input defines the specific diamond pattern to be applied to the base image, dictating the arrangement and appearance of the diamond shapes within the layout.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The 'image' output provides the final image with the diamond panel pattern applied, showcasing the visual result of the node's processing.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: The 'show_help' output offers guidance and additional information about using the CR_DiamondPanel node, facilitating user understanding and application.

CR Draw Pie.description: The CR_DrawPie node is designed for creating pie-shaped graphics with customizable start and stop angles, colors, and positioning. It allows users to generate pie or partial pie shapes with specific dimensions, colors, and orientations, facilitating the creation of unique graphical representations.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Specifies the width of the canvas on which the pie shape will be drawn. It determines the horizontal dimension of the output image.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Specifies the height of the canvas on which the pie shape will be drawn. It determines the vertical dimension of the output image.

inputs.name: pie_start
inputs.description: Defines the starting angle of the pie shape. This angle sets the beginning point of the pie or partial pie segment.

inputs.name: pie_stop
inputs.description: Defines the stopping angle of the pie shape. This angle sets the end point of the pie or partial pie segment, completing its arc.

inputs.name: shape_color
inputs.description: Determines the color of the pie shape. This color fills the interior of the pie or partial pie segment.

inputs.name: back_color
inputs.description: Sets the background color of the canvas. It affects the overall appearance of the output image by providing a backdrop for the pie shape.

inputs.name: x_offset
inputs.description: Adjusts the horizontal position of the pie shape on the canvas. It allows for precise placement of the pie segment within the image.

inputs.name: y_offset
inputs.description: Adjusts the vertical position of the pie shape on the canvas. It allows for precise placement of the pie segment within the image.

inputs.name: zoom
inputs.description: Controls the zoom level of the pie shape. This parameter can enlarge or reduce the size of the pie segment, affecting its visual impact.

inputs.name: rotation
inputs.description: Rotates the pie shape around its center. This parameter can orient the pie segment at various angles, offering additional customization.

inputs.name: shape_color_hex
inputs.description: Specifies the hex code for the pie shape's color, offering an alternative to the predefined color options.

inputs.name: bg_color_hex
inputs.description: Specifies the hex code for the background color, offering an alternative to the predefined color options.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: Generates an image file containing the pie or partial pie shape as specified by the input parameters.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: Provides a string output that can offer guidance or additional information about the generated pie shape.

CR Draw Shape.description: The CR Draw Shape node is designed for drawing various geometric shapes on an image canvas. It supports a wide range of shapes including circles, ovals, diamonds, squares, triangles, hexagons, octagons, quarter circles, half circles, starbursts, stars, and crosses. This node allows for the customization of shape properties such as size, aspect ratio, and color, enabling the creation of complex graphics patterns.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Specifies the width of the image canvas. It determines the horizontal dimension of the canvas where the shapes will be drawn, affecting the overall layout and size of the geometric patterns.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Specifies the height of the image canvas. It determines the vertical dimension of the canvas where the shapes will be drawn, affecting the overall layout and size of the geometric patterns.

inputs.name: shape
inputs.description: Defines the type of geometric shape to be drawn on the canvas. The choice of shape affects the visual outcome and the complexity of the pattern created.

inputs.name: shape_color
inputs.description: Determines the color of the shape to be drawn. The color choice influences the visual appeal and contrast of the shape against the canvas background.

inputs.name: back_color
inputs.description: Specifies the background color of the image canvas. It sets the overall tone and mood of the image, providing a backdrop for the geometric shapes.

inputs.name: x_offset
inputs.description: Adjusts the horizontal position of the shape on the canvas. It allows for precise placement of the shape, enabling the creation of dynamic and varied patterns.

inputs.name: y_offset
inputs.description: Adjusts the vertical position of the shape on the canvas. It allows for precise placement of the shape, enabling the creation of dynamic and varied patterns.

inputs.name: zoom
inputs.description: Controls the scale of the shape relative to its original size. Zooming in or out can dramatically alter the visual impact of the shape on the canvas.

inputs.name: rotation
inputs.description: Specifies the rotation angle of the shape in degrees. Rotating the shape can add dynamism and complexity to the pattern.

inputs.name: shape_color_hex
inputs.description: Specifies the hexadecimal color code for the shape color, offering an alternative to the predefined color options.

inputs.name: bg_color_hex
inputs.description: Specifies the hexadecimal color code for the background color, offering an alternative to the predefined color options.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: The output image with the drawn shapes. It showcases the visual result of applying geometric patterns to the canvas, highlighting the node's capability to create complex graphics.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: Provides textual help or guidance related to the node's functionality or output. It can offer insights into the drawing process or tips for optimizing the use of the node.

CR Draw Text.description: This node is designed for drawing text onto images or graphics, allowing for customization of font properties, alignment, and positioning. It provides a versatile tool for adding textual elements to visual content, enhancing the ability to convey messages or labels within a graphical context.

inputs.name: image_width
inputs.description: Specifies the width of the image onto which the text will be drawn. This parameter sets the canvas size for the textual content.

inputs.name: image_height
inputs.description: Specifies the height of the image, defining the vertical dimension of the canvas for the text.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The text to be drawn onto the image. It allows for customization of the content and message conveyed through the graphical output.

inputs.name: font_name
inputs.description: Allows for the selection of the font used to render the text, impacting the style and readability.

inputs.name: font_size
inputs.description: Determines the size of the text, affecting visibility and emphasis within the image.

inputs.name: font_color
inputs.description: Specifies the color of the text, crucial for visibility against the background and overall visual appeal.

inputs.name: background_color
inputs.description: Defines the background color of the image, setting the visual context for the text.

inputs.name: align
inputs.description: Determines the alignment of the text within the image, affecting its positioning and overall layout.

inputs.name: justify
inputs.description: Determines the justification of the text, affecting its alignment relative to the specified position.

inputs.name: margins
inputs.description: Sets the margins around the text, aiding in its precise positioning within the image.

inputs.name: line_spacing
inputs.description: Controls the spacing between lines of text, affecting readability and text layout.

inputs.name: position_x
inputs.description: Specifies the horizontal position of the text within the image, allowing for accurate placement.

inputs.name: position_y
inputs.description: Specifies the vertical position of the text within the image, enabling precise alignment.

inputs.name: rotation_angle
inputs.description: Determines the angle at which the text is rotated, enabling dynamic text orientation.

inputs.name: rotation_options
inputs.description: Provides options for how the text rotation is applied, offering flexibility in text presentation.

inputs.name: font_color_hex
inputs.description: An optional hexadecimal value for the text color, offering an alternative to predefined color selections.

inputs.name: bg_color_hex
inputs.description: An optional hexadecimal value for the background color, providing additional customization options.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: The modified image after the text has been drawn onto it, showcasing the integration of textual and visual elements.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: Provides a link to additional documentation and help resources related to the node's functionality.

CR Encode Scheduled Prompts.description: This node is designed to encode scheduled prompts for animation sequences, converting them into a format suitable for further processing and animation generation. It focuses on organizing and preparing prompt data based on predefined schedules, ensuring that the animation prompts are correctly sequenced and formatted for optimal use.

inputs.name: clip
inputs.description: The clip input represents the animation clip for which the scheduled prompts are being encoded. It is crucial for determining the context and sequence of the animation.

inputs.name: current_prompt
inputs.description: The current prompt is the starting point of the animation sequence, setting the initial context for the animation.

inputs.name: next_prompt
inputs.description: The next prompt specifies the subsequent context in the animation sequence, allowing for a smooth transition between frames.

inputs.name: weight
inputs.description: The weight parameter influences the blending of prompts between frames, affecting the smoothness and transition quality of the animation.

outputs.name: CONDITIONING
outputs.description: The CONDITIONING output is a processed format of the input prompts, ready for animation generation.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL providing additional help and documentation related to the node's functionality.

CR Feathered Border.description: The CR Feathered Border node is designed to add a customizable feathered border around images. It allows for the adjustment of border thickness, color, and the degree of feathering to create visually appealing edges.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: A single image to which the feathered border will be applied. This parameter is crucial for defining the visual content that will be enhanced with the border.

inputs.name: top_thickness
inputs.description: Specifies the thickness of the top border. This parameter allows for the customization of the border's appearance by adjusting its size.

inputs.name: bottom_thickness
inputs.description: Specifies the thickness of the bottom border, enabling customization of the border's vertical dimensions.

inputs.name: left_thickness
inputs.description: Determines the thickness of the left side of the border, allowing for horizontal dimension customization.

inputs.name: right_thickness
inputs.description: Defines the thickness of the right side of the border, contributing to the customization of the border's horizontal dimensions.

inputs.name: border_color
inputs.description: The color of the border. This parameter is essential for defining the aesthetic appeal of the border.

inputs.name: feather_amount
inputs.description: The degree of feathering applied to the border edges, affecting the softness and visual effect of the border.

inputs.name: border_color_hex
inputs.description: An optional hexadecimal value for the border color, providing an alternative way to specify custom colors.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The resulting image with the applied feathered border, showcasing the enhanced visual appeal.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL providing additional information and guidance on using the CR Feathered Border node.

CR Float Range List.description: This node generates a list of floating-point numbers within a specified range, allowing for the creation of sequences with precise increments. It is designed to facilitate the creation of lists where each element is a float value, providing a tool for scenarios requiring detailed numerical sequences.

inputs.name: start
inputs.description: Defines the starting point of the float range. It sets the initial value from which the sequence begins, playing a crucial role in determining the range's scope.

inputs.name: end
inputs.description: Specifies the ending point of the float range. It determines the value at which the sequence stops, thus defining the extent of the range.

inputs.name: step
inputs.description: Determines the increment between each number in the range. This value affects the density of the sequence, allowing for finer control over the spacing between elements.

inputs.name: operation
inputs.description: Specifies the mathematical operation to apply to each element in the range, such as 'none', 'sin', 'cos', or 'tan', allowing for the transformation of the sequence based on trigonometric functions.

inputs.name: decimal_places
inputs.description: Determines the number of decimal places for each number in the range, allowing for precision control over the float values.

inputs.name: ignore_first_value
inputs.description: When true, the first value of the generated range is omitted from the output, allowing for sequences that start from the second value onwards.

inputs.name: max_values_per_loop
inputs.description: Limits the number of values generated per loop, providing control over the size of the output list within each iteration.

inputs.name: loops
inputs.description: Indicates how many times the range sequence should be repeated. This parameter can be used to extend the sequence by looping it multiple times.

inputs.name: ping_pong
inputs.description: A boolean flag that, when true, reverses the direction of the range on every other iteration, creating a back-and-forth pattern.

outputs.name: FLOAT
outputs.description: The generated list of floating-point numbers within the specified range.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL to a help page providing detailed information and guidance on using the CR Float Range List node.

CR Float To Integer.description: The node is designed to convert floating-point numbers to integers, providing a straightforward way to perform numerical type conversion within a workflow. Additionally, it offers a link to further documentation or help regarding its usage.

inputs.name: _float
inputs.description: This parameter accepts a floating-point number as input, which is then converted to an integer. The conversion process is essential for scenarios where integer values are required from floating-point inputs.

outputs.name: INT
outputs.description: The integer result obtained from converting the input floating-point number.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL string pointing to additional documentation or help related to the node's functionality.

CR Float To String.description: This node is designed to convert floating-point numbers into their string representation, facilitating the transition between numerical data types and text for further processing or display purposes.

inputs.name: float_
inputs.description: The floating-point number to be converted into a string. This input is essential for defining the numerical value that will undergo the conversion process.

outputs.name: STRING
outputs.description: The string representation of the input floating-point number.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL providing additional information and guidance on using the CR Float To String node.

CR Font File List.description: This node is designed to list TrueType font files (.ttf) from specified sources, including system fonts, Comfyroll's own font directory, or any user-specified folder. It aims to provide a convenient way to access and utilize font files for text rendering or design purposes within the Comfyroll environment.

inputs.name: source_folder
inputs.description: Specifies the source from which to list the font files. It can be the system's font directory, Comfyroll's internal font directory, or a custom folder path provided by the user. This choice dictates where the node searches for TrueType font files (.ttf).

inputs.name: start_index
inputs.description: Determines the starting index from which to begin listing the font files. This allows for pagination or selective listing of font files based on their order in the source directory.

inputs.name: max_rows
inputs.description: Specifies the maximum number of font files to list. This parameter can be used to limit the number of font files returned by the node, facilitating easier management and selection.

inputs.name: folder_path
inputs.description: When the source folder is set to 'from folder', this parameter specifies the custom folder path from which to list the font files. It enables the node to access and list font files from a user-defined directory.

outputs.name: LIST
outputs.description: A list of TrueType font files (.ttf) found in the specified source directory. This output can be used to select specific fonts for text rendering or design tasks within Comfyroll.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: Provides a URL to the documentation or help page for this node, offering additional information or guidance on its use.

CR Get Parameter From Prompt.description: This node is designed to extract specific parameters from a given prompt based on predefined criteria, such as the presence of certain strings or patterns. It aims to simplify the process of parameter extraction from text inputs, enhancing the efficiency and accuracy of data retrieval.

inputs.name: prompt
inputs.description: The 'prompt' parameter represents the text input from which the node attempts to extract specific parameters. It plays a crucial role in determining the node's execution and results, as the effectiveness of parameter extraction directly depends on the content and structure of the input text.

inputs.name: search_string
inputs.description: The 'search_string' parameter specifies the particular string or pattern the node is looking for within the prompt. Its presence and characteristics significantly influence the extraction process, guiding the node in identifying and retrieving the relevant parameters.

outputs.name: prompt
