outputs.description: The 'prompt' output parameter encapsulates the extracted parameters from the input text, providing a structured representation of the data retrieved. It is significant for downstream processes that require specific information extracted from textual inputs.

outputs.name: text
outputs.description: The 'text' output parameter contains the textual content extracted based on the 'search_string' criteria. It is crucial for further processing or analysis that requires the specific text identified within the prompt.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The 'float' output parameter represents numerical values extracted from the prompt, offering a quantifiable aspect of the data retrieved for subsequent operations.

outputs.name: boolean
outputs.description: The 'boolean' output parameter indicates the presence or absence of the 'search_string' within the prompt, providing a binary assessment of the extraction success.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: The 'show_help' output parameter offers guidance or additional information related to the node's operation, assisting users in understanding or troubleshooting the parameter extraction process.

CR Gradient Float.description: The CR_GradientFloat node is designed for creating smooth transitions between two float values over a specified number of frames, based on a given gradient profile. It calculates the interpolated float value for any given frame within the animation sequence, facilitating dynamic visual effects.

inputs.name: start_value
inputs.description: The starting float value of the gradient transition, marking the beginning of the interpolation.

inputs.name: end_value
inputs.description: The ending float value of the gradient transition, marking the end of the interpolation.

inputs.name: start_frame
inputs.description: The frame number at which the gradient transition begins.

inputs.name: frame_duration
inputs.description: The total number of frames over which the gradient transition occurs.

inputs.name: current_frame
inputs.description: The current frame number for which the interpolated value is being calculated.

inputs.name: gradient_profile
inputs.description: A profile defining the nature of the gradient transition, influencing the interpolation calculation.

outputs.name: FLOAT
outputs.description: The interpolated float value for the current frame, based on the gradient transition.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL to a help page providing additional information and guidance on using the gradient interpolation node.

CR Gradient Integer.description: The CR_GradientInteger node is designed to generate a gradient of integer values based on a specified start and end value, frame duration, and the current frame. It interpolates the value at the current frame within the gradient, providing a smooth transition between the start and end values over the specified duration.

inputs.name: start_value
inputs.description: The starting value of the gradient. It marks the beginning of the interpolation.

inputs.name: end_value
inputs.description: The ending value of the gradient. It marks the end point of the interpolation.

inputs.name: start_frame
inputs.description: The frame at which the gradient interpolation begins.

inputs.name: frame_duration
inputs.description: The total duration over which the gradient transitions from the start value to the end value.

inputs.name: current_frame
inputs.description: The current frame for which the interpolated value is calculated. It determines the specific point of interpolation within the gradient.

inputs.name: gradient_profile
inputs.description: A profile that defines the characteristics of the gradient, such as its type or method of interpolation.

outputs.name: INT
outputs.description: The interpolated integer value at the current frame within the gradient.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL to a help page providing more information about the CR_GradientInteger node.

CR Half Drop Panel.description: The CR Half Drop Panel node is designed to transform an input image into a patterned panel by applying half-drop, quarter-drop, or custom percentage drop techniques. This node enhances visual aesthetics by creating repetitive patterns that can be used in various design contexts.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be transformed into a patterned panel. This image serves as the base for creating the repetitive pattern.

inputs.name: pattern
inputs.description: Specifies the type of pattern to apply to the input image, such as 'half drop', 'quarter drop', or a 'custom drop %', determining the arrangement of the repeated image segments.

inputs.name: drop_percentage
inputs.description: Used when 'pattern' is set to 'custom drop %', it defines the percentage by which the image is dropped, allowing for customizable pattern repetition.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image after applying the specified drop pattern, showcasing the transformed panel with the repetitive design.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL to the documentation or help page for the CR Half Drop Panel node, providing additional information and guidance.

CR Halftone Filter.description: The CR Halftone Filter node applies a halftone effect to images, simulating the look of classic print media by transforming images into a pattern of dots. This node supports various customization options, including dot size, shape, and resolution, as well as color channel separation for more detailed control over the halftone effect.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to apply the halftone effect to. This node accepts both PIL Images and PyTorch tensors, automatically converting tensors to PIL Images if necessary.

inputs.name: dot_size
inputs.description: Specifies the size of the dots in the halftone pattern, allowing for control over the granularity of the effect.

inputs.name: dot_shape
inputs.description: Determines the shape of the dots in the halftone pattern, offering customization of the visual style of the halftone effect.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: Controls the resolution of the output image, with options for normal or high resolution, affecting the scale of the halftone effect.

inputs.name: angle_c
inputs.description: The angle of the cyan color channel in the CMYK color space, allowing for precise control over the orientation of the halftone dots.

inputs.name: angle_m
inputs.description: The angle of the magenta color channel in the CMYK color space, enabling adjustment of the halftone dot orientation for this color.

inputs.name: angle_y
inputs.description: The angle of the yellow color channel in the CMYK color space, used to set the orientation of the halftone dots for this color.

inputs.name: angle_k
inputs.description: The angle for the black (key) color channel in the CMYK color space, allowing for customization of the halftone dot orientation.

inputs.name: greyscale
inputs.description: A boolean indicating whether the image should be converted to greyscale before applying the halftone effect, simplifying the color palette.

inputs.name: antialias
inputs.description: A boolean indicating whether antialiasing should be applied, smoothing the edges of the halftone dots for a cleaner appearance.

inputs.name: antialias_scale
inputs.description: Defines the scale factor used during antialiasing to adjust the image size temporarily, enhancing the smoothness of the halftone dots.

inputs.name: border_blending
inputs.description: A boolean indicating whether border blending should be applied, potentially softening the transition between the halftone dots and the image background.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: The output image after applying the halftone effect, converted to RGB format regardless of the original color space.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL string providing additional help and documentation for the CR Halftone Filter node.

CR Halftone Grid.description: The CR Halftone Grid node is designed to generate a graphical representation of a halftone grid, a technique often used in printing to simulate continuous tone imagery through the use of dots. This node allows for customization of the grid's appearance, including dot style, frequency, and background color, enabling users to create visually appealing patterns and textures for various applications.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Specifies the width of the generated halftone grid image. It directly influences the size of the output image.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Determines the height of the generated halftone grid image, affecting the overall dimensions of the output.

inputs.name: dot_style
inputs.description: Defines the style of the dots in the halftone grid, allowing for creative control over the appearance of the pattern.

inputs.name: reverse_dot_style
inputs.description: When set to 'Yes', this reverses the dot style, adding an additional layer of customization to the halftone effect.

inputs.name: dot_frequency
inputs.description: Controls the frequency of dots in the halftone grid, impacting the density of the pattern.

inputs.name: background_color
inputs.description: Sets the background color of the halftone grid. It supports predefined colors or a custom color if specified.

inputs.name: x_pos
inputs.description: The x-coordinate position for the center of the dot pattern, influencing the distribution of dots.

inputs.name: y_pos
inputs.description: The y-coordinate position for the center of the dot pattern, affecting the placement of dots in the grid.

inputs.name: bg_color_hex
inputs.description: Specifies the hex code for a custom background color, offering precise control over the grid's background color.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: The output image of the halftone grid.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL providing additional help and documentation for the CR Halftone Grid node.

CR Hires Fix Process Switch.description: The CR_HiResFixProcessSwitch node is designed to selectively process high-resolution images or upscale latent representations based on the input provided. It facilitates the choice between two distinct processing paths, either focusing on image upscaling or latent space manipulation, thereby enabling a flexible approach to enhancing image quality or detail.

inputs.name: Input
inputs.description: Determines the processing path to be taken by the node, choosing between latent upscaling and image upscaling based on the input value.

inputs.name: latent_upscale
inputs.description: The latent representation to be upscaled if the 'Input' is set to 'latent_upscale'. This input directly influences the node's execution by determining the manipulation of the latent space, thereby affecting the detail and quality of the generated output.

inputs.name: image_upscale
inputs.description: The high-resolution image to be processed if the 'Input' is set to 'image_upscale'. This input determines the node's focus on enhancing the image's resolution or detail, directly impacting the visual quality of the output.

outputs.name: LATENT
outputs.description: The output of the node, which can be either the upscaled latent representation or the processed high-resolution image, based on the input path chosen.

outputs.name: STRING
outputs.description: A URL to a help page providing additional information and guidance on using the CR_HiResFixProcessSwitch node.

CR Image Border.description: This node is designed to add customizable borders around images. It allows for the adjustment of border thickness on all sides and the specification of border color, including the option to use a hex color code. Additionally, it supports the creation of feathered borders, providing a soft, blurred edge effect around the image.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image or images to which the border will be applied. This parameter is crucial for defining the visual content that will be enhanced with a border.

inputs.name: top_thickness
inputs.description: Specifies the thickness of the border at the top edge of the image. This parameter allows for the customization of the border's appearance by adjusting its size.

inputs.name: bottom_thickness
inputs.description: Specifies the thickness of the border at the bottom edge of the image. This parameter enables the user to customize the border's appearance by adjusting its size.

inputs.name: left_thickness
inputs.description: Specifies the thickness of the border at the left edge of the image. This parameter allows for the customization of the border's appearance by adjusting its size.

inputs.name: right_thickness
inputs.description: Specifies the thickness of the border at the right edge of the image. This parameter enables the user to customize the border's appearance by adjusting its size.

inputs.name: border_color
inputs.description: Defines the color of the border. This parameter allows for the customization of the border's appearance by choosing a specific color.

inputs.name: outline_thickness
inputs.description: Determines the thickness of the outline around the image, separate from the main border. This allows for an additional layer of customization.

inputs.name: outline_color
inputs.description: Specifies the color of the outline. This parameter works in conjunction with outline thickness to enhance the visual appeal of the image.

inputs.name: border_color_hex
inputs.description: An optional hex code to specify the border color, providing an alternative method for defining the border's color.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image with the applied borders. This includes any adjustments made to border thickness, color, feathering, and outline.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL providing additional information and guidance on using the CR Image Border node.

CR Image Grid Panel.description: This node is designed to create a visually organized grid panel of images, applying customizable borders, outlines, and arranging them into a specified number of columns. It aims to enhance the presentation of multiple images by structuring them in a coherent layout, making it easier to view and compare them side by side.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: A list of images to be arranged in a grid. These images are processed to apply borders and outlines, contributing to the overall aesthetic of the grid.

inputs.name: border_thickness
inputs.description: Specifies the thickness of the border around each image, playing a crucial role in the visual separation and emphasis of individual images within the grid.

inputs.name: border_color
inputs.description: Determines the color of the border around each image, allowing for customization of the grid's appearance to match thematic or aesthetic preferences.

inputs.name: outline_thickness
inputs.description: Defines the thickness of the outline around the entire grid, enhancing the grid's visual prominence and separation from the background.

inputs.name: outline_color
inputs.description: Sets the color of the outline around the entire grid, contributing to the visual identity and thematic consistency of the presentation.

inputs.name: max_columns
inputs.description: The maximum number of columns in the grid, dictating the layout and organization of images within the panel.

inputs.name: border_color_hex
inputs.description: Specifies the hexadecimal color code for the border, offering an alternative way to define the border color, especially for custom colors not predefined in the node.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The final processed image of the grid panel, ready for display or further use.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL providing additional information and guidance on using the node.

CR Image Input Switch (4 way).description: This node allows for the selection of one out of four possible image inputs based on a specified integer input. It is designed to facilitate dynamic image input selection within a workflow, providing flexibility in choosing which image to process or display next.

inputs.name: Input
inputs.description: Determines which of the four image inputs to select and return. The integer value ranges from 1 to 4, each corresponding to a different image input.

inputs.name: image1
inputs.description: The first image option that can be selected.

inputs.name: image2
inputs.description: The second image option that can be selected.

inputs.name: image3
inputs.description: The third image option that can be selected.

inputs.name: image4
inputs.description: The fourth image option that can be selected.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: The image selected based on the input integer value.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL providing help and documentation for using the node.

CR Image Input Switch.description: This node allows for the dynamic selection between two image inputs based on a specified integer input. It facilitates conditional image processing workflows by enabling the user to switch between different image sources.

inputs.name: Input
inputs.description: Determines which image input to use based on its integer value. It affects the node's execution by selecting one of the two possible image inputs for the workflow.

inputs.name: image1
inputs.description: The first optional image input that can be selected.

inputs.name: image2
inputs.description: The second optional image input that can be selected.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: The selected image based on the input integer value.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: Provides a URL to the help documentation for this node.

CR Image List Simple.description: The CR Image List Simple node is designed to create a simple list of images from a specified set of individual images. It allows for the aggregation of multiple image inputs into a single list, facilitating operations that require a collection of images as input.

inputs.name: image_1
inputs.description: Represents the first image to be included in the list. Its inclusion is optional but adds to the versatility of the list by allowing for a varied collection of images. Including this image can initiate or extend the list, affecting the node's execution by potentially increasing the diversity of images processed.

inputs.name: image_2
inputs.description: Represents the second image to be included in the list. Including this image expands the list and increases the potential for diverse image processing applications. It affects the node's execution by adding more variety to the list, which can influence subsequent image processing tasks.

inputs.name: image_3
inputs.description: Represents the third image to be included in the list. Its inclusion enhances the list's capacity for handling multiple images in sequence or batch operations. This can affect the node's execution by enabling more complex sequences or batches of images to be processed together.

inputs.name: image_4
inputs.description: Represents the fourth image to be included in the list. Adding this image further diversifies the list's content, enabling more complex image-based workflows. It influences the node's execution by contributing to the richness and complexity of the image collection.

inputs.name: image_5
inputs.description: Represents the fifth image to be included in the list. Its inclusion completes the list, offering a comprehensive set of images for processing or analysis. This affects the node's execution by potentially completing or rounding out the collection of images, which may be critical for certain analyses or processing tasks.

inputs.name: image_list_simple
inputs.description: An optional pre-existing list of images that can be extended with additional images specified by the other inputs. This parameter allows for the dynamic expansion of the image list based on varying requirements. Including or extending this list directly impacts the node's execution by modifying the initial set of images to be processed, thereby affecting the outcome.

outputs.name: IMAGE_LIST_SIMPLE
outputs.description: The compiled list of images, which may include a combination of individually specified images and those from an existing list. This list is ready for further processing or analysis.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: Provides a URL to the help documentation for this node, offering users guidance on its usage and capabilities.

CR Image List.description: The CR Image List node is designed to load and process a list of images from a specified directory, converting them into a format suitable for further manipulation or analysis. It focuses on organizing and preparing image data by ensuring the images are in a consistent format and facilitating their use in subsequent operations.

inputs.name: image_1
inputs.description: Specifies the first image to be processed. This parameter is part of a series that allows for the loading and processing of multiple images.

inputs.name: alias1
inputs.description: An alias for the first image, providing a means to reference it more conveniently in subsequent operations.

inputs.name: image_2
inputs.description: Specifies the second image to be processed, following the same pattern as the first.

inputs.name: alias2
inputs.description: An alias for the second image, aiding in its identification and use in later stages.

inputs.name: image_3
inputs.description: Specifies the third image to be processed, continuing the sequence of image inputs.

inputs.name: alias3
inputs.description: An alias for the third image, facilitating easier reference and manipulation.

inputs.name: image_4
inputs.description: Specifies the fourth image to be processed, extending the list of images to be handled.

inputs.name: alias4
inputs.description: An alias for the fourth image, simplifying its identification and subsequent processing.

inputs.name: image_5
inputs.description: Specifies the fifth image to be processed, completing the series of image inputs.

inputs.name: alias5
inputs.description: An alias for the fifth image, making it easier to refer to and work with in further operations.

inputs.name: image_list
inputs.description: A list parameter that allows for the bulk loading and processing of images, accommodating larger sets of image data.

outputs.name: IMAGE_LIST
outputs.description: A list of images that have been loaded and converted to a consistent format, ready for further processing or analysis.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: Provides a link to helpful documentation or resources related to the node's functionality.

CR Image Output.description: The CR Image Output node is designed to facilitate the output of images within a computational graph, providing a streamlined way to export, display, or further process images generated or modified by preceding nodes. It abstracts the complexities involved in handling image data, ensuring that images are appropriately formatted and ready for use or display.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The 'images' parameter represents the image data to be outputted. It plays a crucial role in determining the content and format of the output, affecting how images are processed and presented in the final output.

inputs.name: output_type
inputs.description: Specifies the type of output operation to perform with the images, such as saving to disk or displaying.

inputs.name: filename_prefix
inputs.description: A prefix to be added to the filenames of saved images, allowing for organized and identifiable output.

inputs.name: prefix_presets
inputs.description: Predefined prefix options that can be selected for convenience and standardization.

inputs.name: file_format
inputs.description: The format in which the images will be saved, such as PNG or JPEG.

inputs.name: trigger
inputs.description: A control signal that triggers the output operation, ensuring that images are processed and saved/displayed at the correct time.

outputs.name: trigger
outputs.description: Indicates the completion of the output operation, potentially used to trigger subsequent nodes in the computational graph.

CR Image Panel.description: The CR Image Panel node is designed to create a panel layout for images, allowing users to organize and display multiple images in a structured grid format. It provides customization options for borders, outlines, and the arrangement of images within the grid, enhancing the visual presentation of image collections.

inputs.name: image_1
inputs.description: The primary image to be included in the panel. This parameter is essential for initiating the layout of the image panel.

inputs.name: border_thickness
inputs.description: Specifies the thickness of the borders around each image in the panel, contributing to the visual separation and framing of the images.

inputs.name: border_color
inputs.description: Defines the color of the borders around each image. This parameter allows for visual customization and can enhance the aesthetic appeal of the panel.

inputs.name: outline_thickness
inputs.description: Determines the thickness of the outline around the entire panel, providing an additional layer of visual definition.

inputs.name: outline_color
inputs.description: Sets the color of the outline around the panel, further customizing the appearance and emphasizing the panel's boundaries.

inputs.name: layout_direction
inputs.description: Determines the arrangement direction of the images within the panel, either horizontally or vertically.

inputs.name: image_2
inputs.description: An optional second image to include in the panel, allowing for more complex layouts.

inputs.name: image_3
inputs.description: An optional third image to include in the panel, further expanding the layout possibilities.

inputs.name: image_4
inputs.description: An optional fourth image to include in the panel, maximizing the layout customization.

inputs.name: border_color_hex
inputs.description: An optional hexadecimal color code for the border color, offering an alternative way to specify the border color.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The final image output of the panel, combining all input images according to the specified layout and customization options.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL providing additional help and documentation for the CR Image Panel node.

CR Image Pipe Edit.description: This node is designed for editing the parameters of an image pipeline, allowing users to modify or replace the image and its attributes such as width, height, and upscale factor within the pipeline.

inputs.name: pipe
inputs.description: The current state of the image pipeline, encapsulating the image and its attributes that may be modified or replaced.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: An optional new image to replace the current one in the pipeline.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: An optional new width for the image, overriding the current width in the pipeline.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: An optional new height for the image, overriding the current height in the pipeline.

inputs.name: upscale_factor
inputs.description: An optional new upscale factor to apply to the image, overriding the current upscale factor in the pipeline.

outputs.name: pipe
outputs.description: The updated image pipeline, reflecting any modifications or replacements made to the image and its attributes.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL to the documentation or help page for this node.

CR Image Pipe In.description: This node is designed to initialize and configure an image processing pipeline, allowing for the specification of image properties such as dimensions and upscale factor. It serves as the entry point for images into a customizable processing flow, facilitating subsequent manipulations or analyses.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The initial image to be processed. It sets the starting point for the pipeline.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Specifies the desired width of the image. It affects the dimensions of the image as it moves through the pipeline.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Specifies the desired height of the image. It affects the dimensions of the image as it moves through the pipeline.

inputs.name: upscale_factor
inputs.description: Determines the factor by which the image should be upscaled. This parameter influences the resolution enhancement of the image.

outputs.name: pipe
outputs.description: A pipeline configuration encapsulating the image and its specified properties.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL providing detailed documentation and help for using the CR Image Pipe In node.

CR Image Pipe Out.description: The CR_ImagePipeOut node is designed for extracting and outputting image data and its associated parameters from a pipeline. It facilitates the retrieval of image properties such as dimensions and upscale factor, along with providing a help link for further guidance.

inputs.name: pipe
inputs.description: The 'pipe' parameter is a pipeline input that carries image data and its associated parameters such as width, height, and upscale factor. It is essential for the node's operation as it determines the image and its properties to be outputted.

outputs.name: pipe
outputs.description: Returns the original pipeline input, allowing for further processing or extraction of image data and parameters.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: Outputs the image data extracted from the pipeline.

outputs.name: width
outputs.description: Outputs the width of the image extracted from the pipeline.

outputs.name: height
outputs.description: Outputs the height of the image extracted from the pipeline.

outputs.name: upscale_factor
outputs.description: Outputs the upscale factor associated with the image extracted from the pipeline.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: Provides a link to a help page for further guidance on using the CR_ImagePipeOut node.

CR Image Size.description: The CR Image Size node is designed to adjust the dimensions of an image according to specified width, height, and upscale factor, providing a link to further help as part of its output. It serves as a utility for image preprocessing in creative projects, allowing for precise control over image size adjustments.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Specifies the desired width of the image. This parameter allows users to define the width dimension to which the image should be resized, playing a crucial role in determining the final image size.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Defines the desired height of the image. This parameter is essential for setting the height dimension for the image resizing process, directly influencing the aspect ratio and overall appearance of the final image.

inputs.name: upscale_factor
inputs.description: Determines the factor by which the image should be upscaled. This parameter is key to enhancing the resolution of the image without altering its original width and height proportions.

outputs.name: Width
outputs.description: unknown

outputs.name: Height
outputs.description: unknown

outputs.name: upscale_factor
outputs.description: The factor by which the image has been upscaled.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL providing additional help and documentation related to the CR Image Size node.

CR Img2Img Process Switch.description: The CR Img2Img Process Switch node is designed to dynamically select between two different processing paths based on the input mode, specifically targeting image-to-image transformations. It facilitates the flexible integration of distinct processing pipelines within a single workflow, enhancing the adaptability of image manipulation tasks.

inputs.name: Input
inputs.description: Determines the processing path to be taken, choosing between 'txt2img' and 'img2img' modes. This selection influences the subsequent processing steps and their outcomes.

inputs.name: txt2img
inputs.description: Specifies the latent representation to be used when the 'txt2img' mode is selected, enabling text-to-image conversion processes.

inputs.name: img2img
inputs.description: Specifies the latent representation to be used when the 'img2img' mode is selected, enabling image-to-image conversion processes.

outputs.name: LATENT
outputs.description: The latent representation resulting from the selected processing path, either from text-to-image or image-to-image conversion.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: Provides a URL to the help documentation for this node, offering additional information and guidance.

CR Increment Float.description: The CR_IncrementFloat node is designed to incrementally adjust floating-point values, facilitating the creation of sequences or gradients of numbers. This node is particularly useful in scenarios where gradual changes or interpolations are required.

inputs.name: start_value
inputs.description: Specifies the initial value from which the incrementation starts, setting the baseline for the sequence generation.

inputs.name: step
inputs.description: Determines the increment size for each step, directly influencing the pace and scale of the sequence progression.

inputs.name: start_frame
inputs.description: Defines the starting frame for the incrementation process, marking the point at which the sequence begins.

inputs.name: frame_duration
inputs.description: Specifies the duration in frames for each increment step, affecting the timing and pacing of the sequence.

inputs.name: current_frame
inputs.description: Indicates the current frame in the sequence, used to calculate the current value based on the starting point and step size.

outputs.name: FLOAT
outputs.description: Outputs the current incremented value, reflecting the progression of the sequence.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: Provides additional information or guidance related to the node's operation.

CR Increment Integer.description: This node is designed for the incremental adjustment of integer values over a sequence of frames, providing a means to dynamically alter numerical values based on frame progression within animations or simulations.

inputs.name: start_value
inputs.description: The initial integer value from which the increment operation begins. It serves as the foundational value for subsequent increments, influenced by the 'step' parameter across frames.

inputs.name: step
inputs.description: The fixed amount added to 'start_value' at each increment step, allowing for consistent or variable progression of the value across frames.

inputs.name: start_frame
inputs.description: The frame at which the increment operation commences, enabling synchronization of value changes with specific points in an animation timeline.

inputs.name: frame_duration
inputs.description: Defines the duration over which the increment operation is applied, allowing for controlled adjustments within a specified timeframe.

inputs.name: current_frame
inputs.description: The current frame being processed, determining if and how 'start_value' is incremented based on its relation to 'start_frame' and 'frame_duration'.

outputs.name: INT
outputs.description: The resulting integer value after applying the increment operation, reflecting the cumulative effect of the 'step' parameter over the specified frame range.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL providing access to additional help and documentation related to the node's functionality.

CR Index Increment.description: The CR Index Increment node is designed to modify an index value by incrementing it with a specified interval. It provides a simple yet effective way to iterate through sequences or collections by adjusting the index according to the defined interval.

inputs.name: index
inputs.description: The 'index' parameter represents the current position in a sequence or collection. It is the base value that will be incremented to move to the next position.

inputs.name: interval
inputs.description: The 'interval' parameter specifies the amount by which the 'index' should be incremented. This allows for flexible stepping through a sequence or collection.

outputs.name: index
outputs.description: The updated index after being incremented by the specified interval.

outputs.name: interval
outputs.description: The 'interval' parameter as it was input, unchanged by the operation.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL providing additional help and information about the CR Index Increment node.

CR Index Multiply.description: This node multiplies a given index by a specified factor, potentially altering the flow or behavior of subsequent operations based on the new index value. It's designed to dynamically adjust indices within a workflow, facilitating flexible data manipulation or access patterns.

inputs.name: index
inputs.description: The 'index' parameter represents the starting point or current state of an index that will be multiplied. It's crucial for determining the base value that will be adjusted by the multiplication, affecting the node's execution and results.

inputs.name: factor
inputs.description: The 'factor' parameter specifies the multiplier applied to the index. It defines how much the index will be scaled, playing a key role in the calculation and the resulting modified index value.

outputs.name: index
outputs.description: The modified index after multiplication, reflecting the new position or state as a result of the operation.

outputs.name: factor
outputs.description: The factor used in the multiplication, returned unchanged.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL providing additional help or documentation related to the index multiplication operation.

CR Index Reset.description: This node is designed to reset an index to a specified value, providing a simple way to control and reset counters or indices within a workflow.

inputs.name: index
inputs.description: The current value of the index. It is a required input that determines the starting point before the reset.

inputs.name: reset_to
inputs.description: The value to which the index will be reset. This allows for flexible resetting of the index to any specified value within the allowed range.

outputs.name: index
outputs.description: The reset value of the index, which is the same as the 'reset_to' input value.

outputs.name: reset_to
outputs.description: Echoes back the 'reset_to' input value, confirming the value to which the index was reset.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: Provides a URL to the help documentation for this node.

CR Index.description: The CR Index node is designed to manage and manipulate index values within a workflow, offering functionalities such as printing the current index to the console and providing a help link for further information.

inputs.name: index
inputs.description: Specifies the current index value. It is crucial for determining the position or order of elements in a sequence.

inputs.name: print_to_console
inputs.description: Determines whether the current index value should be printed to the console, aiding in debugging or monitoring the workflow.

outputs.name: INT
outputs.description: Returns the current index value after any modifications.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: Provides a URL to a help page for further information on the CR Index node.

CR Integer Multiple.description: The CR_IntegerMultipleOf node is designed to multiply an integer by a specified multiple, adjusting the integer's value accordingly. It provides a straightforward way to scale integers by a factor, with an option to access help documentation for further guidance.

inputs.name: integer
inputs.description: Specifies the integer to be multiplied. This parameter is central to the node's operation, determining the base value that will be scaled.

inputs.name: multiple
inputs.description: Defines the factor by which the integer will be multiplied. This parameter allows for the dynamic scaling of the integer's value.

outputs.name: INT
outputs.description: The result of multiplying the input integer by the specified multiple.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL providing access to additional documentation and help for using this node.

CR Integer Range List.description: The CR_IntegerRangeList node generates a list of integers within a specified range, potentially repeating and reversing the sequence based on the provided parameters. It's designed to create complex sequences of numbers for various applications, such as scheduling or iterative processes.

inputs.name: start
inputs.description: Defines the starting point of the integer range. It sets the initial value from which the range generation begins.

inputs.name: end
inputs.description: Specifies the endpoint of the integer range. It determines the value at which the range generation stops, not including this value itself.

inputs.name: step
inputs.description: Determines the increment between each integer in the range. It controls the difference between successive numbers in the sequence.

inputs.name: loops
inputs.description: Specifies the number of times the entire range sequence is repeated. It allows for the generation of longer sequences by repeating the basic range pattern.

inputs.name: ping_pong
inputs.description: A boolean parameter that, when true, reverses the direction of the range on every other iteration. It adds a back-and-forth pattern to the sequence.

outputs.name: INT
outputs.description: A list of integers generated based on the specified range, step, loops, and ping-pong parameters.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: Provides a URL to the documentation or help page related to the CR_IntegerRangeList node.

CR Integer To String.description: This node is designed to convert an integer value into its string representation. It aims to facilitate the conversion process within data processing pipelines, making it easier to handle numerical data as text for various applications.

inputs.name: int_
inputs.description: The integer value to be converted into a string. This parameter is crucial as it determines the exact numerical value that will be transformed into its textual form.

outputs.name: STRING
outputs.description: The string representation of the input integer value.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL providing additional help and documentation related to the integer to string conversion process.

CR Interpolate Latents.description: This node specializes in blending two latent representations based on a specified interpolation method, such as linear or spherical linear interpolation. It's designed to facilitate the creation of smooth transitions or animations between different states or frames within a generative model's latent space.

inputs.name: latent1
inputs.description: The first latent representation to be interpolated. It serves as the starting point for the interpolation process.

inputs.name: latent2
inputs.description: The second latent representation to be interpolated. It acts as the endpoint for the interpolation process.

inputs.name: weight
inputs.description: A scalar value that determines the interpolation ratio between the two latent representations.

inputs.name: method
inputs.description: Specifies the interpolation method to be used, such as 'lerp' for linear interpolation or 'slerp' for spherical linear interpolation.

outputs.name: LATENT
outputs.description: The resulting latent representation after applying the specified interpolation method.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL providing additional information and guidance on the interpolation methods available and their usage.

CR Intertwine Lists.description: The CR_IntertwineLists node is designed to intertwine two lists into a single list, combining elements from each input list into a new list structure. This node aims to facilitate the manipulation and combination of list data within a workflow, providing a straightforward method for merging list contents.

inputs.name: list1
inputs.description: The first list to be intertwined. It plays a crucial role in the combination process, contributing its elements to the formation of the new, combined list.

inputs.name: list2
inputs.description: The second list to be intertwined. It equally contributes to the new list's formation by merging its elements with those from the first list.

outputs.name: STRING
outputs.description: The resulting list after intertwining the elements of the two input lists.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL providing additional help and documentation related to the CR_IntertwineLists node.

CR Keyframe List.description: This node is designed to process and format a list of keyframes for animation purposes, providing a structured way to define animation sequences and their formats. It also offers a link to further help and documentation on how to use the node effectively.

inputs.name: keyframe_list
inputs.description: A multiline string representing a list of keyframes. This list is essential for defining the sequence of frames in an animation, where each keyframe specifies a significant point in the animation that will be interpolated between by the animation software.

inputs.name: keyframe_format
inputs.description: Specifies the format of the keyframes, allowing for different animation frameworks or custom formats to be used. This flexibility ensures compatibility with various animation tools and workflows.

outputs.name: keyframe_list
outputs.description: Returns the processed list of keyframes, ready for use in animation sequences.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: Provides a URL to further documentation and help for using the node, facilitating user understanding and effective utilization.

CR Latent Batch Size.description: This node is designed to adjust the batch size of latent representations by replicating the input samples to match the specified batch size. It facilitates the manipulation of data batch sizes for downstream processing or model inference.

inputs.name: latent
inputs.description: The latent representation of data, typically a tensor, that is to be adjusted in terms of batch size. This input is crucial for determining the structure and content of the data to be replicated.

inputs.name: batch_size
inputs.description: An integer specifying the desired batch size. This parameter dictates how many times the input samples are replicated to achieve the specified batch size.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The output latent representation with the adjusted batch size, achieved by replicating the input samples as specified.

CR Latent Input Switch.description: The CR_LatentInputSwitch node is designed to switch between two latent inputs based on a specified condition. It facilitates dynamic workflow paths in generative models by allowing the selection of different latent representations.

inputs.name: Input
inputs.description: Determines which latent input to select. A value of 1 selects the first latent input, while a value of 2 selects the second.

inputs.name: latent1
inputs.description: The first latent input option. This input is selected if the 'Input' parameter is set to 1.

inputs.name: latent2
inputs.description: The second latent input option. This input is selected if the 'Input' parameter is set to 2.

outputs.name: LATENT
outputs.description: The selected latent input based on the 'Input' parameter.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL providing additional information and guidance on using the CR_LatentInputSwitch node.

CR Load Animation Frames.description: This node is designed to load a sequence of animation frames from a specified directory, facilitating the processing and manipulation of animation data within a workflow.

inputs.name: image_sequence_folder
inputs.description: Specifies the directory containing the sequence of image folders to be loaded. Each folder represents a sequence of animation frames.

inputs.name: start_index
inputs.description: The index of the first frame to load from the sequence, allowing for control over the starting point of the animation.

inputs.name: max_frames
inputs.description: The maximum number of frames to load from the sequence, enabling limitation on the amount of data processed.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: The loaded sequence of animation frames, ready for further processing.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A string providing additional help or instructions related to the node's operation.

CR Load Flow Frames.description: The node is designed to load sequential image frames for animation purposes, handling the initial frame differently if no frames are skipped and preparing both the current and previous frames for further processing.

inputs.name: input_folder
inputs.description: The name of the folder from which the images will be loaded. This parameter is essential for identifying the specific directory containing the animation frames.

inputs.name: sort_by
inputs.description: Determines the order in which the files are sorted before loading. This affects the sequence in which frames are processed and displayed.

inputs.name: current_frame
inputs.description: Specifies the index of the current frame to be loaded, adjusting for any initial frames skipped. This index is crucial for determining the sequence of frames and ensuring the correct frame is processed next.

inputs.name: skip_start_frames
inputs.description: Indicates the number of initial frames to skip before starting the loading process. This parameter allows for flexibility in starting the animation from a specific frame.

inputs.name: input_path
inputs.description: An optional specific path to a directory or file to be loaded. Overrides the default path constructed from the input directory and folder name.

inputs.name: file_pattern
inputs.description: A pattern to match specific files within the directory. This allows for filtering and loading only the files that match the given pattern.

outputs.name: current_image
outputs.description: The current image frame loaded and processed for animation.

outputs.name: previous_image
outputs.description: The previous image frame loaded and processed, used for comparison or reference in animation.

outputs.name: current_frame
outputs.description: The index of the current frame that has been loaded.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL providing additional help and documentation related to the node.

CR Load GIF As List.description: This node is designed to load GIF images as a list, allowing for the manipulation and analysis of individual frames within the GIF. It provides functionality to specify the starting frame and the maximum number of frames to be loaded, making it a versatile tool for handling GIF animations in a granular manner.

inputs.name: input_folder
inputs.description: Specifies the folder containing the GIF file to be loaded. This parameter is crucial for locating the GIF file within the filesystem.

inputs.name: gif_filename
inputs.description: The name of the GIF file to be loaded. This parameter works in conjunction with `input_folder` to construct the full path to the GIF file.

inputs.name: start_frame
inputs.description: Determines the starting frame from which the GIF should be loaded. This allows for skipping initial frames and starting from a specific point in the animation.

inputs.name: max_frames
inputs.description: Limits the number of frames to be loaded from the GIF. This is useful for controlling the amount of data processed and focusing on a specific segment of the animation.

inputs.name: input_path
inputs.description: An optional parameter that directly specifies the path to the GIF file, bypassing the need for `input_folder` and `gif_filename`.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: A list of tensors representing the loaded frames of the GIF. Each tensor corresponds to an individual frame, allowing for frame-by-frame manipulation.

outputs.name: MASK
outputs.description: A list of tensors representing the alpha masks of the loaded frames. This is useful for operations that require knowledge of the transparency or opacity of each frame.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL to the help documentation for this node, providing additional information and guidance on its usage.

CR Load Image List Plus.description: The CR Load Image List Plus node is designed to load a list of images from a specified directory, along with additional information such as masks, indexes, filenames, and EXIF data. It aims to provide a comprehensive set of data for each image, facilitating advanced image processing and manipulation tasks.

inputs.name: input_folder
inputs.description: Specifies the directory from which images are to be loaded. It plays a crucial role in determining the source of the images and ensuring they are accessible for processing.

inputs.name: start_index
inputs.description: Determines the starting point within the list of images to begin loading, allowing for selective processing of images based on their order in the directory.

inputs.name: max_images
inputs.description: Limits the number of images to be loaded from the directory, enabling control over the volume of data processed at one time.

inputs.name: input_path
inputs.description: An optional path to a specific directory or file from which images are to be loaded, providing an alternative to the default input folder.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: A list of loaded images, each converted to a tensor format suitable for further processing.

outputs.name: MASK
outputs.description: A list of masks associated with the loaded images, providing additional data for image manipulation tasks.

outputs.name: index
outputs.description: A list of indexes corresponding to the loaded images, offering a reference for image identification and ordering.

outputs.name: filename
outputs.description: A list of filenames for the loaded images, aiding in tracking and referencing the images.

outputs.name: width
outputs.description: The width of the loaded images, providing dimensional data for processing.

outputs.name: height
outputs.description: The height of the loaded images, providing dimensional data for processing.

outputs.name: list_length
outputs.description: The total number of images loaded, offering insight into the dataset size.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A link to the help documentation for the node, offering additional information and guidance.

CR Load Image List.description: This node is designed to load a list of images from a specified directory, ensuring the images are in a format suitable for further processing or analysis. It focuses on organizing and converting images into a consistent format, facilitating their use in image-based workflows.

inputs.name: input_folder
inputs.description: Specifies the folder within the input directory from which images are to be loaded. It is essential for targeting a specific subset of images for processing.

inputs.name: start_index
inputs.description: Determines the starting index from which images in the directory are considered, allowing for selective processing of images based on their order.

inputs.name: max_images
inputs.description: Defines the maximum number of images to be loaded from the directory, enabling control over the volume of images processed.

inputs.name: input_path
inputs.description: Allows specifying a direct path to the folder from which images are to be loaded, offering an alternative to the default input directory.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: A list of images that have been loaded and converted to a consistent format, ready for further processing or analysis.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: Provides a URL to the help documentation for this node.

CR Load LoRA.description: This node is designed to dynamically load and apply Learning Rate Annealing (LoRA) adjustments to models and clips based on specified parameters or defaults. It supports conditional loading based on the presence of LoRA parameters, handling of default LoRAs, and iteration through a list of LoRAs to find a match for application. The node aims to enhance model performance or behavior by adjusting learning rates in a flexible and scheduled manner.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model to which the LoRA adjustments will be applied. It's crucial for defining the base upon which the LoRA modifications will take effect.

inputs.name: clip
inputs.description: The clip to which the LoRA adjustments will be applied, alongside the model. It plays a key role in the context of video or image processing tasks.

inputs.name: switch
inputs.description: A switch to enable or disable the application of LoRA adjustments. This allows for conditional application based on specific criteria.

inputs.name: lora_name
inputs.description: The name of the LoRA to be loaded and applied. This parameter is key to identifying which specific LoRA adjustments to apply.

inputs.name: strength_model
inputs.description: A floating-point value indicating the strength of the LoRA adjustments to be applied to the model. It affects the intensity of the learning rate modifications.

inputs.name: strength_clip
inputs.description: A floating-point value indicating the strength of the LoRA adjustments to be applied to the clip. It affects the intensity of the learning rate modifications.

outputs.name: MODEL
outputs.description: The model after the LoRA adjustments have been applied. It represents the modified version of the input model.

outputs.name: CLIP
outputs.description: The clip after the LoRA adjustments have been applied. It represents the modified version of the input clip.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL providing additional help and documentation regarding the LoRA adjustments and their application.

CR Load Schedule From File.description: This node is designed to load animation schedules from a specified file, enabling the dynamic control of animation parameters over time. It facilitates the integration of pre-defined animation timelines into the animation workflow, streamlining the process of applying complex animation schedules.

inputs.name: input_file_path
inputs.description: Specifies the directory path where the schedule file is located. This path is crucial for locating and loading the correct file.

inputs.name: file_name
inputs.description: The name of the file to be loaded. This name, combined with the file extension, is used to identify and access the specific schedule file.

inputs.name: file_extension
inputs.description: Defines the file format (e.g., 'txt', 'csv') of the schedule file. This information is essential for correctly parsing the file's content.

outputs.name: SCHEDULE
outputs.description: The loaded schedule, represented as a structured format suitable for further processing and application within the animation workflow.

outputs.name: show_text
outputs.description: Provides a textual representation of the loaded schedule, useful for debugging or informational purposes.

CR Load Scheduled LoRAs.description: This node is designed to dynamically load and apply LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) configurations based on a predefined schedule. It supports loading specific LoRAs for given frames, handling default LoRA settings, and operating in different modes such as 'Off' or 'Load default LoRA'. The node aims to enhance model performance or behavior for animation or image generation tasks by adjusting model and clip strengths according to the scheduled LoRA parameters.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Specifies the operational mode of the node, which can include 'Off', 'Load default LoRA', or dynamically loading LoRAs based on a schedule. This affects how and whether LoRAs are applied.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model to which the LoRA adjustments will be applied. It is a core component of the node's functionality.

inputs.name: clip
inputs.description: The clip to which the LoRA adjustments will be applied, alongside the model.

inputs.name: current_frame
inputs.description: The current frame number for which the node is determining which LoRA, if any, to apply. This is crucial for dynamic LoRA loading based on the schedule.

inputs.name: schedule_alias
inputs.description: An alias for the schedule, potentially used for identifying or categorizing the schedule in a more human-readable form.

inputs.name: default_lora
inputs.description: Specifies the default LoRA to be used when no specific LoRA is scheduled for the current frame or when operating in 'Load default LoRA' mode.

inputs.name: strength_model
inputs.description: The strength parameter for the model when loading the default LoRA or a scheduled LoRA. It influences the intensity of the applied LoRA on the model.

inputs.name: strength_clip
inputs.description: The strength parameter for the clip when loading the default LoRA or a scheduled LoRA. It influences the intensity of the applied LoRA on the clip.

inputs.name: schedule_format
inputs.description: Defines the format of the schedule used for loading LoRAs. It can vary, affecting how the schedule is interpreted and applied.

inputs.name: lora_list
inputs.description: A list of available LoRAs that can be scheduled. It provides the node with options for dynamic LoRA loading.

inputs.name: schedule
inputs.description: The schedule detailing which LoRA to load at specific frames. It is used when the node is in a mode that requires dynamic LoRA loading based on frame numbers.

outputs.name: MODEL
outputs.description: The model after potentially being modified by the application of a LoRA, based on the node's operational mode and schedule.

outputs.name: CLIP
outputs.description: The clip after potentially being modified by the application of a LoRA, based on the node's operational mode and schedule.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL providing help or documentation related to the node's functionality and usage.

CR Load Scheduled Models.description: This node is designed to dynamically load and switch between different models based on a predefined schedule for animation frames. It facilitates the use of various models at specific points in an animation sequence, enhancing the flexibility and diversity of the generated content.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Specifies the operational mode of the node, which determines how models are loaded and switched during the animation process.

inputs.name: current_frame
inputs.description: Indicates the current frame number in the animation sequence, used to determine the appropriate model to load based on the schedule.

inputs.name: schedule_alias
inputs.description: Serves as an identifier to match the schedule with the correct model, enabling the dynamic loading of models as per the animation frame requirements.

inputs.name: default_model
inputs.description: The default model to be used when no specific model is scheduled for the current frame.

inputs.name: schedule_format
inputs.description: Defines the format of the schedule, which influences how the schedule is interpreted and applied to model loading.

inputs.name: model_list
inputs.description: A list of models available for scheduling. This allows for the selection of different models to be loaded at specified frames.

inputs.name: schedule
inputs.description: Defines the timing and model selection for each frame in the animation, dictating which model to load at any given point.

outputs.name: MODEL
outputs.description: The model loaded as per the current frame and schedule.

outputs.name: CLIP
outputs.description: The CLIP model loaded, if specified in the schedule.

outputs.name: VAE
outputs.description: The VAE model loaded, if specified in the schedule.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: Provides help or guidance related to the scheduling and model loading process.

CR Load Text List.description: This node is designed to load and parse text lists from files with specific extensions, such as .txt or .csv, facilitating the handling and manipulation of textual data within a workflow.

inputs.name: input_file_path
inputs.description: Specifies the path to the directory containing the target file, playing a crucial role in locating the file for data extraction.

inputs.name: file_name
inputs.description: The name of the file (excluding its extension) to be loaded. This parameter is essential for identifying the specific file to be processed.

inputs.name: file_extension
inputs.description: Defines the file extension (e.g., 'txt', 'csv') of the target file, determining the method of parsing and loading the text list.

outputs.name: STRING
outputs.description: Returns a list of strings extracted from the specified file.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: Provides a URL offering additional help and guidance on using the node.

CR LoRA List.description: The CR LoRA List node is designed to compile and manage lists of LoRA (Layer-wise Relevance Propagation) configurations, facilitating the organization and application of multiple LoRA settings in animation projects. It supports the dynamic addition of LoRA configurations to an existing list, enabling users to efficiently manage and apply various LoRA effects based on specific animation requirements.

inputs.name: lora_name1
inputs.description: Specifies the first LoRA configuration name to be added to the list, playing a crucial role in defining the initial set of LoRA settings for the animation.

inputs.name: alias1
inputs.description: Provides an alias for the first LoRA configuration, offering a simplified reference to this specific set of LoRA settings.

inputs.name: model_strength_1
inputs.description: Determines the strength of the model's influence for the first LoRA configuration, affecting the overall impact of this LoRA setting on the animation.

inputs.name: clip_strength_1
inputs.description: Defines the clip strength for the first LoRA configuration, influencing how prominently this particular LoRA setting will affect the animation.

inputs.name: lora_name2
inputs.description: Specifies the second LoRA configuration name to be added to the list, allowing for the expansion of LoRA settings within the animation project.

inputs.name: alias2
inputs.description: Provides an alias for the second LoRA configuration, facilitating easier identification and application of this set of LoRA settings.

inputs.name: model_strength_2
inputs.description: Determines the strength of the model's influence for the second LoRA configuration, contributing to the diversity of LoRA effects available for the animation.

inputs.name: clip_strength_2
inputs.description: Defines the clip strength for the second LoRA configuration, adding another layer of LoRA effect to the animation.

inputs.name: lora_name3
inputs.description: Specifies the third LoRA configuration name to be added to the list, further broadening the range of LoRA settings for the animation.

inputs.name: alias3
inputs.description: Provides an alias for the third LoRA configuration, simplifying the management and application of a wider range of LoRA settings.

inputs.name: model_strength_3
inputs.description: Determines the strength of the model's influence for the third LoRA configuration, enhancing the animation with additional LoRA effects.

inputs.name: clip_strength_3
inputs.description: Defines the clip strength for the third LoRA configuration, contributing to the overall variety of LoRA settings in the animation.

inputs.name: lora_list
inputs.description: An existing list of LoRA configurations to which new settings can be added, enabling the dynamic management and application of multiple LoRA effects in the animation.

outputs.name: LORA_LIST
outputs.description: A compiled list of LoRA configurations, including any newly added settings, ready for application in animation projects.

outputs.name: show_text
outputs.description: A textual representation of the compiled LoRA configurations, providing an overview of the current LoRA settings for reference or documentation purposes.

CR LoRA Stack.description: The CR LoRA Stack node is designed to create and manage a stack of LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) modifications for models. It allows for the sequential application of multiple LoRA modifications to a model, enabling fine-tuned adjustments to model behavior and performance.

inputs.name: switch_1
inputs.description: Controls whether the first LoRA modification is applied. This switch enables selective application of modifications.

inputs.name: lora_name_1
inputs.description: Specifies the first LoRA modification to be applied. It is crucial for defining the initial step in the sequence of LoRA adjustments.

inputs.name: model_weight_1
inputs.description: Determines the weight of the first LoRA modification on the model. This weight influences the extent of the modification's impact.

inputs.name: clip_weight_1
inputs.description: Sets the weight of the first LoRA modification on the clip. This weight affects how significantly the clip is modified.

inputs.name: switch_2
inputs.description: Controls the application of the second LoRA modification, offering more granular control over the adjustments.

inputs.name: lora_name_2
inputs.description: Specifies the second LoRA modification in the sequence. It allows for further customization following the initial modification.

inputs.name: model_weight_2
inputs.description: Determines the weight of the second LoRA modification on the model, further adjusting its behavior.

inputs.name: clip_weight_2
inputs.description: Sets the weight of the second LoRA modification on the clip, modifying its characteristics further.

inputs.name: switch_3
inputs.description: Enables or disables the third LoRA modification, providing ultimate control over the stack.

inputs.name: lora_name_3
inputs.description: Defines the third LoRA modification in the stack, extending the customization capabilities.

inputs.name: model_weight_3
inputs.description: Specifies the weight of the third LoRA modification on the model, allowing for additional fine-tuning.

inputs.name: clip_weight_3
inputs.description: Determines the weight of the third LoRA modification on the clip, further influencing its output.

inputs.name: lora_stack
inputs.description: Allows for the inclusion of an existing LoRA stack to be extended with new modifications. This parameter facilitates the building of complex LoRA sequences.

outputs.name: LORA_STACK
outputs.description: Returns the compiled list of LoRA modifications, ready for application to a model and clip.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: Provides a URL to documentation or help related to the LoRA stack node, assisting users in understanding its use.

CR Mask Text.description: This node is designed to apply text masking operations within a graphical context, enabling the creation of text-based masks that can be used for various image manipulation and composition tasks. It abstracts the complexities involved in text rendering and mask generation, providing a straightforward way to integrate text into visual designs programmatically.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image over which the text mask will be applied. This forms the base layer for the text masking operation.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The text content to be used for creating the mask. This parameter allows users to specify the exact text that will be rendered into the mask.

inputs.name: font_name
inputs.description: Specifies the font to be used for rendering the text. This allows for customization of the text appearance in the mask.

inputs.name: font_size
inputs.description: Determines the size of the font used for the text. This affects how large the text appears within the mask.

inputs.name: background_color
inputs.description: The color of the background over which the text is rendered. This parameter is crucial for defining the visual contrast between the text and the background.

inputs.name: align
inputs.description: Specifies the alignment of the text within the mask. This can be left, center, or right, affecting the text's positioning relative to the specified margins.

inputs.name: justify
inputs.description: Determines whether the text is justified within the mask. This affects the distribution of space between words in each line.

inputs.name: margins
inputs.description: Specifies the margins around the text within the mask. This parameter helps in positioning the text properly within the mask.

inputs.name: line_spacing
inputs.description: Controls the spacing between lines of text. This is important for adjusting the readability of the text within the mask.

inputs.name: position_x
inputs.description: The horizontal position of the text within the mask. This parameter allows for precise placement of the text.

inputs.name: position_y
inputs.description: The vertical position of the text within the mask. Similar to position_x, it enables accurate placement of the text.

inputs.name: rotation_angle
inputs.description: The angle at which the text is rotated. This parameter allows for dynamic text orientations within the mask.

inputs.name: rotation_options
inputs.description: Additional options for controlling the rotation of the text. This provides further customization of the text's appearance.

inputs.name: bg_color_hex
inputs.description: Hexadecimal representation of the background color. Provides an alternative way to specify the background color.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: The resulting image after the text masking operation, showcasing the applied text mask over the original image.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: unknown

CR Math Operation.description: The CR_MathOperation node performs a variety of mathematical operations on a given input value, such as trigonometric functions, square root, exponentiation, logarithm, negation, and absolute value. It allows for the specification of the operation to be performed and the number of decimal places for the result, making it a versatile tool for mathematical manipulations within the node network.

inputs.name: a
inputs.description: The input value on which the mathematical operation will be performed. The choice of operation affects the node's execution and the nature of the result.

inputs.name: operation
inputs.description: Specifies the mathematical operation to be applied to the input value. This determines the mathematical transformation that the input will undergo.

inputs.name: decimal_places
inputs.description: Determines the number of decimal places to which the result will be rounded. This allows for control over the precision of the output.

outputs.name: a
outputs.description: The result of the specified mathematical operation performed on the input value, rounded to the specified number of decimal places.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL to a help page providing detailed information about the mathematical operations supported by this node.

CR Model Input Switch.description: This node allows for dynamic selection between two model inputs based on a specified integer input. It facilitates conditional model selection within a workflow, providing a link to further help and guidance.

inputs.name: Input
inputs.description: Determines which model input to select for the workflow based on its value. It plays a crucial role in conditional logic, affecting the node's execution path.

inputs.name: model1
inputs.description: The first model option that can be selected as input. It's one of the conditional choices available for the workflow.

inputs.name: model2
inputs.description: The second model option that can be selected as input. It offers an alternative choice for the workflow's conditional logic.

outputs.name: MODEL
outputs.description: The selected model input based on the 'Input' parameter. It's the outcome of the node's conditional logic.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: Provides a link to further documentation and help for using this node effectively.

CR Model List.description: The CR Model List node is designed to manage and organize models within a list structure, facilitating the selection and application of different models in a dynamic and flexible manner. It supports operations such as adding, removing, or selecting models from the list, enabling users to efficiently handle multiple models for various tasks or experiments.

inputs.name: ckpt_name1
inputs.description: Specifies the first checkpoint name for model selection. It plays a crucial role in defining the initial model to be included in the model list.

inputs.name: alias1
inputs.description: Provides an alias for the first checkpoint, allowing for easier identification and management within the model list.

inputs.name: ckpt_name2
inputs.description: Specifies the second checkpoint name for model selection, further expanding the model list.

inputs.name: alias2
inputs.description: Provides an alias for the second checkpoint, facilitating better organization and retrieval of models.

inputs.name: ckpt_name3
inputs.description: Specifies the third checkpoint name for model selection, adding to the diversity of the model list.

inputs.name: alias3
inputs.description: Provides an alias for the third checkpoint, enhancing the manageability of the model list.

inputs.name: ckpt_name4
inputs.description: Specifies the fourth checkpoint name for model selection, contributing to the comprehensive nature of the model list.

inputs.name: alias4
inputs.description: Provides an alias for the fourth checkpoint, aiding in the systematic organization of models.

inputs.name: ckpt_name5
inputs.description: Specifies the fifth checkpoint name for model selection, completing the set of primary models for the list.

inputs.name: alias5
inputs.description: Provides an alias for the fifth checkpoint, ensuring a well-structured and accessible model list.

inputs.name: model_list
inputs.description: This optional parameter allows users to input a pre-existing list of models to be managed within the node. It is crucial for integrating additional models into the node's functionality, directly affecting its operation.

outputs.name: MODEL_LIST
outputs.description: Outputs the list of models that are currently managed within the node, allowing for further manipulation or selection.

outputs.name: show_text
outputs.description: Provides textual information or feedback related to the operations performed on the model list, enhancing user interaction and understanding.

CR Model Merge Stack.description: This node is designed to facilitate the merging of multiple models into a single, cohesive model stack. It allows for the integration of various models by applying specified merging methods, normalization of ratios, and weighting factors to achieve a balanced and effective combination of model features.

inputs.name: switch_1
inputs.description: Activates or deactivates the inclusion of the first model in the merging process.

inputs.name: ckpt_name1
inputs.description: The name of the checkpoint file for the first model. This is used to identify and load the specific model to be merged.

inputs.name: model_ratio1
inputs.description: Specifies the contribution ratio of the first model in the merged output. This affects how prominently the model's features are represented.

inputs.name: clip_ratio1
