inputs.description: Determines the width of the generated image. The width influences the scale of the binary pattern, affecting its display size.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Sets the height of the generated image. Similar to width, height impacts the scale and display size of the binary pattern.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: The generated image based on the binary pattern input. This output is a visual representation of the binary design.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A string URL providing additional help and documentation related to binary pattern generation.

CR Simple Image Compare.description: The CR Simple Image Compare node is designed to facilitate the comparison of two images within a graphical interface. It abstracts the complexities involved in image comparison, providing a straightforward way for users to visually assess and contrast the differences or similarities between images.

inputs.name: text1
inputs.description: The first text input for comparison, allowing users to label or describe the first image.

inputs.name: text2
inputs.description: The second text input for comparison, enabling labeling or description of the second image for a clear contrast.

inputs.name: footer_height
inputs.description: Specifies the height of the footer area where additional information or labels can be displayed.

inputs.name: font_name
inputs.description: The name of the font used for text rendering in the comparison interface, allowing customization of text appearance.

inputs.name: font_size
inputs.description: Determines the size of the font used for text, affecting the readability and visual impact of text labels.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Defines the comparison mode, such as side-by-side or overlay, offering different ways to visualize the differences or similarities.

inputs.name: border_thickness
inputs.description: Specifies the thickness of the border around images, adding a visual separation that can enhance the comparison.

inputs.name: image1
inputs.description: The first image to be compared, serving as the baseline for visual assessment.

inputs.name: image2
inputs.description: The second image for comparison, allowing users to visually identify differences or similarities with the first image.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The resulting image after comparison, showcasing the differences or similarities identified between the two images.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A flag indicating whether help information about using the comparison tool should be displayed, aiding user understanding.

CR Simple List.description: The CR_SimpleList node is designed to process a list of string values, performing operations such as trimming and filtering empty strings, to produce a cleaned and streamlined list. It also provides a link to further documentation or help related to its functionality.

inputs.name: list_values
inputs.description: This parameter takes a multiline string input representing list values. Each line is considered a separate list item. The node processes these values to trim whitespace and filter out empty strings, effectively cleaning the list.

outputs.name: LIST
outputs.description: This output is a list of strings that have been cleaned by trimming whitespace and filtering out empty strings.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: Provides a URL to further documentation or help related to the CR_SimpleList node's functionality.

CR Simple Meme Template.description: This node is designed to facilitate the creation of simple meme templates, allowing users to easily generate memes by providing customizable text and image inputs. It abstracts the complexity of meme generation into a user-friendly interface, enabling quick and creative meme creation.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The 'image' input allows users to provide the base image on which the meme text will be overlaid. This is a crucial component for meme creation, setting the visual context for the text.

inputs.name: preset
inputs.description: The 'preset' input offers predefined meme formats that users can select to quickly generate popular meme styles, enhancing the ease of meme creation.

inputs.name: text_top
inputs.description: The 'text_top' input allows users to specify the text that appears at the top of the meme, enabling personalized messages or jokes.

inputs.name: text_bottom
inputs.description: The 'text_bottom' input allows users to specify the text that appears at the bottom of the meme, complementing the top text for a complete meme experience.

inputs.name: font_name
inputs.description: The 'font_name' input lets users choose the font style for the meme text, allowing for further customization of the meme's appearance.

inputs.name: max_font_size
inputs.description: The 'max_font_size' input determines the maximum size of the meme text, ensuring the text remains readable and visually appealing.

inputs.name: font_color
inputs.description: The 'font_color' input allows users to select the color of the meme text, enabling visual contrast and emphasis.

inputs.name: font_outline
inputs.description: The 'font_outline' input provides options for adding an outline to the meme text, enhancing readability against varied backgrounds.

inputs.name: bar_color
inputs.description: The 'bar_color' input enables users to choose the color of optional bars that can be added to the top and/or bottom of the meme for aesthetic or thematic purposes.

inputs.name: bar_options
inputs.description: The 'bar_options' input allows users to select the placement of optional bars in the meme, offering additional layout customization.

inputs.name: font_color_hex
inputs.description: The 'font_color_hex' input offers an alternative way to specify the meme text color using hexadecimal color codes, providing precise color customization.

inputs.name: bar_color_hex
inputs.description: The 'bar_color_hex' input offers an alternative way to specify the color of optional bars using hexadecimal color codes, allowing for precise color matching.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The 'image' output represents the final meme generated by the node, ready for sharing or further use.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: The 'show_help' output provides guidance or additional information about the meme generation process, assisting users in creating their desired memes.

CR Simple Prompt List Keyframes.description: This node is designed to generate a sequence of keyframes based on a list of simple prompts, intervals, and other animation parameters. It facilitates the creation of animated sequences by specifying how each prompt transitions over time, making it a crucial component for crafting dynamic visual narratives.

inputs.name: simple_prompt_list
inputs.description: A list of simple text prompts that describe each keyframe. This list is the foundation for generating the animated sequence, dictating the content and order of the animation.

inputs.name: keyframe_interval
inputs.description: Specifies the interval between each keyframe in the animation, determining the pacing and length of the animated sequence.

inputs.name: loops
inputs.description: Defines the number of times the animation sequence should loop, allowing for repeated cycles of the keyframe list.

inputs.name: transition_type
inputs.description: Determines the type of transition between keyframes, affecting the animation's visual flow.

inputs.name: transition_speed
inputs.description: Controls the speed of transitions between keyframes, influencing the animation's tempo.

inputs.name: transition_profile
inputs.description: Shapes the acceleration and deceleration of transitions, adding dynamism to the animation.

inputs.name: keyframe_format
inputs.description: Specifies the format for the keyframes, influencing how they are interpreted and rendered in the animation.

outputs.name: keyframe_list
outputs.description: The generated sequence of keyframes, ready for use in creating the animated sequence.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL to documentation or help related to this node, providing additional information and guidance.

CR Simple Prompt List.description: This node is designed to aggregate multiple text prompts into a single list, optionally incorporating an existing list of prompts. It's particularly useful for constructing comprehensive prompt lists for animation or text generation tasks, allowing for dynamic extension based on input prompts.

inputs.name: prompt_1
inputs.description: The first text prompt to be included in the prompt list. Its inclusion directly influences the beginning of the aggregated prompt list, setting the initial context or theme.

inputs.name: prompt_2
inputs.description: The second text prompt to be included in the prompt list. It adds to the diversity of the aggregated list, potentially introducing a new aspect or detail following the initial prompt.

inputs.name: prompt_3
inputs.description: The third text prompt to be included in the prompt list. It further diversifies the content of the list, adding depth or complexity to the combined narrative or instructions.

inputs.name: prompt_4
inputs.description: The fourth text prompt to be included in the prompt list. It contributes additional layers or nuances to the aggregated list, enriching the overall content.

inputs.name: prompt_5
inputs.description: The fifth text prompt to be included in the prompt list. It finalizes the input sequence, potentially capping the list with a conclusive or summarizing statement.

inputs.name: simple_prompt_list
inputs.description: An optional list of pre-existing prompts to be included in the final aggregated list. This allows for dynamic extension of the prompt list based on existing collections, effectively enriching the final output with a broader range of expressions or instructions.

outputs.name: SIMPLE_PROMPT_LIST
outputs.description: The aggregated list of text prompts, constructed from the input prompts and any existing prompt list provided. This list represents a comprehensive collection of instructions or themes for subsequent use.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL providing additional help and documentation for using the CR Simple Prompt List node.

CR Simple Prompt Scheduler.description: The CR_SimplePromptScheduler node is designed to manage and schedule animation prompts based on a simple scheduling logic. It processes a list of keyframes and, depending on the scheduling mode and format, prepares a sequence of prompts for animation frames. This node supports different scheduling modes, including default prompts and keyframe lists, and can handle format conversions for compatibility with different animation systems.

inputs.name: keyframe_list
inputs.description: The list of keyframes to be scheduled. It is crucial for defining the sequence and timing of animation prompts. The format and content of this list directly influence the scheduling outcome and the generation of animation prompts.

inputs.name: current_frame
inputs.description: The current frame number for which the prompt is being scheduled. It determines the relevant prompt and keyframe information for the current point in the animation sequence.

inputs.name: keyframe_format
inputs.description: Specifies the format of the keyframes, allowing for conversion between different animation systems' formats. This parameter ensures compatibility and correct interpretation of the keyframe list.

outputs.name: current_prompt
outputs.description: The prompt scheduled for the current frame, ready for use in generating the animation.

outputs.name: next_prompt
outputs.description: The prompt scheduled for the next frame, providing a lookahead for animation generation.

outputs.name: weight
outputs.description: A weight value indicating the relevance or influence of the current prompt in the context of animation blending or interpolation.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL to documentation or help resources related to the CR_SimplePromptScheduler node, offering guidance and additional information.

CR Simple Schedule.description: This node is designed to process and format animation schedules, simplifying the creation and management of animation timelines by allowing users to define schedules in a straightforward manner.

inputs.name: schedule
inputs.description: The 'schedule' parameter represents the animation schedule to be processed. It is crucial for defining the sequence and timing of animations, impacting the node's execution and the resulting animation timeline.

inputs.name: schedule_type
inputs.description: The 'schedule_type' parameter specifies the type of the schedule, influencing how the schedule is interpreted and processed by the node.

inputs.name: schedule_alias
inputs.description: The 'schedule_alias' parameter provides an alias for the schedule, facilitating easier identification and management of multiple schedules.

inputs.name: schedule_format
inputs.description: The 'schedule_format' parameter determines the format in which the schedule is to be processed, affecting the interpretation and output of the animation schedule.

outputs.name: SCHEDULE
outputs.description: A list of formatted schedule lines, ready for further processing or execution in animation workflows.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL providing additional help and documentation related to the node's functionality.

CR Simple Text Panel.description: This node is designed to create simple text panels within a graphical interface, allowing for the display of text in a visually appealing and customizable manner.

inputs.name: panel_width
inputs.description: Specifies the width of the text panel. It determines how wide the panel will be, affecting the layout and appearance of the displayed text.

inputs.name: panel_height
inputs.description: Defines the height of the text panel. It influences the vertical space available for text display, impacting the overall layout and design.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The text content to be displayed on the panel. This input allows for customization of the text message, playing a crucial role in the panel's purpose and appearance.

inputs.name: font_name
inputs.description: Selects the font used for the text. The choice of font can significantly affect the panel's aesthetic and readability.

inputs.name: font_color
inputs.description: Determines the color of the text, offering customization options for visual appeal and contrast against the panel background.

inputs.name: font_size
inputs.description: Sets the size of the text font. This parameter affects the text's visibility and how it fits within the panel's dimensions.

inputs.name: font_outline_thickness
inputs.description: Specifies the thickness of the text's outline, enhancing readability and visual distinction.

inputs.name: font_outline_color
inputs.description: Defines the color of the text's outline, which can enhance text visibility and aesthetic appeal.

inputs.name: background_color
inputs.description: Sets the panel's background color, affecting the overall look and feel of the text panel.

inputs.name: align
inputs.description: Controls the alignment of the text within the panel, affecting the layout and presentation of the content.

inputs.name: justify
inputs.description: Determines the justification of the text, impacting how the text is spaced and aligned horizontally.

inputs.name: font_color_hex
inputs.description: Specifies the hexadecimal color code for the text color, offering an alternative way to define text color.

inputs.name: bg_color_hex
inputs.description: Specifies the hexadecimal color code for the background color, providing an alternative way to define the panel's background color.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The generated image of the text panel, ready for display or further processing.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL providing additional help and documentation for using the text panel node.

CR Simple Text Scheduler.description: This node is designed to manage and schedule text animations within a user interface, allowing for dynamic text updates based on predefined schedules or conditions.

inputs.name: schedule
inputs.description: The 'schedule' parameter specifies the text and timing for each animation frame, serving as the blueprint for dynamic text updates.

inputs.name: current_frame
inputs.description: The 'current_frame' parameter indicates the current frame number in the animation sequence, determining which part of the schedule to execute.

outputs.name: STRING
outputs.description: This output represents the text scheduled for the current frame, ready for display or further processing.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: Provides a URL to documentation or help related to the scheduling process, offering guidance on how to use the scheduler effectively.

CR Simple Text Watermark.description: The CR Simple Text Watermark node is designed to overlay text onto images in a subtle manner, typically for the purpose of copyright or identification. It allows for the customization of text appearance and positioning, ensuring the watermark blends seamlessly with the underlying image while maintaining readability.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image onto which the watermark text will be applied. This is the primary canvas for the watermark operation.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The text to be used as the watermark. This allows for customization of the watermark content.

inputs.name: align
inputs.description: Controls the alignment of the watermark text within the image, aiding in precise placement.

inputs.name: opacity
inputs.description: Adjusts the opacity of the watermark text, ensuring it does not overpower the main content of the image.

inputs.name: font_name
inputs.description: Specifies the font used for the watermark text, enabling customization of the text appearance.

inputs.name: font_size
inputs.description: Determines the size of the font used for the watermark text, affecting its visibility and integration with the image.

inputs.name: font_color
inputs.description: Defines the color of the watermark text, allowing for visual customization to match or contrast with the image.

inputs.name: x_margin
inputs.description: The horizontal margin from the edge of the image to the start of the watermark text, providing control over its positioning.

inputs.name: y_margin
inputs.description: The vertical margin from the edge of the image to the start of the watermark text, providing control over its positioning.

inputs.name: font_color_hex
inputs.description: An optional hexadecimal color code for the watermark text, offering an alternative method for defining text color.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: Outputs the image with the applied watermark text.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: Provides additional information or guidance related to the watermarking process.

CR Simple Value Scheduler.description: This node is designed to manage and apply simple value-based scheduling for animations. It interprets a given schedule and the current frame to output appropriate integer and floating-point values, facilitating dynamic adjustments throughout the animation sequence.

inputs.name: schedule
inputs.description: The schedule string defines keyframes and their corresponding values for the animation, serving as the blueprint for value transitions across frames.

inputs.name: current_frame
inputs.description: Specifies the current frame in the animation sequence, determining which value from the schedule should be applied.

outputs.name: INT
outputs.description: The integer value corresponding to the current frame's schedule, rounded down from the floating-point representation.

outputs.name: FLOAT
outputs.description: The floating-point value directly derived from the schedule for the current frame.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL providing additional help and documentation on using the CR Simple Value Scheduler.

CR Split String.description: The CR Split String node is designed to split a given text string into multiple parts based on a specified delimiter, facilitating text manipulation and processing tasks.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The primary text string to be split. This parameter is crucial for determining the content that will be divided into parts.

inputs.name: delimiter
inputs.description: The character or sequence of characters used to divide the text string into parts. Its specification directly influences how the text is split.

outputs.name: string_1
outputs.description: The first part of the split text.

outputs.name: string_2
outputs.description: The second part of the split text.

outputs.name: string_3
outputs.description: The third part of the split text.

outputs.name: string_4
outputs.description: The fourth part of the split text.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL providing additional help and documentation for the node.

CR Starburst Colors.description: The CR Starburst Colors node is designed to generate starburst patterns with alternating colors. It utilizes matplotlib to set up a plot and draw triangles in a starburst formation, allowing for customization of the number of triangles, bounding box size, and color scheme. This node is ideal for creating visually striking backgrounds or elements in graphics projects.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Sets the width of the plot area for the starburst pattern, influencing the overall size of the generated graphic.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Determines the height of the plot area, working alongside 'width' to define the dimensions of the starburst pattern.

inputs.name: num_triangles
inputs.description: Specifies the number of triangles to draw in the starburst pattern, allowing for control over the pattern's complexity and density.

inputs.name: color_1
inputs.description: Specifies the first color in the alternating color scheme of the starburst pattern. This can be a predefined color or a custom hex value if 'custom' is selected.

inputs.name: color_2
inputs.description: Defines the second color in the alternating color scheme, complementing the first color. Like 'color_1', it supports predefined colors or custom hex values.

inputs.name: center_x
inputs.description: Sets the x-coordinate of the center point for the starburst pattern.

inputs.name: center_y
inputs.description: Sets the y-coordinate of the center point for the starburst pattern.

inputs.name: rotation
inputs.description: Determines the rotation angle of the starburst pattern, allowing for dynamic visual effects.

inputs.name: bbox_factor
inputs.description: Controls the size of the bounding box for the starburst pattern, affecting how tightly the triangles are packed together.

inputs.name: color1_hex
inputs.description: Specifies the hex value for the first color, used when 'color_1' is set to 'custom'.

inputs.name: color2_hex
inputs.description: Specifies the hex value for the second color, used when 'color_2' is set to 'custom'.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: Generates an image of the starburst pattern with the specified parameters.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: Provides a URL to documentation or help related to the starburst pattern generation.

CR Starburst Lines.description: This node is designed to generate a starburst pattern with lines radiating from a central point. It allows customization of various aspects such as the number of lines, their length, color, and rotation, enabling the creation of visually striking graphics.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Specifies the width of the canvas for the starburst pattern.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Specifies the height of the canvas for the starburst pattern.

inputs.name: num_lines
inputs.description: Specifies the number of lines in the starburst pattern. This determines how densely the lines are packed together, affecting the overall appearance of the starburst.

inputs.name: line_length
inputs.description: Defines the length of each line in the starburst pattern. Longer lines will extend further from the center, creating a more pronounced effect.

inputs.name: line_width
inputs.description: Sets the width of the lines in the starburst pattern. Thicker lines will make the starburst more visible and pronounced.

inputs.name: line_color
inputs.description: Determines the color of the lines in the starburst pattern. This can be a predefined color or a custom hex value, allowing for extensive customization.

inputs.name: background_color
inputs.description: Determines the background color of the canvas. This can be a predefined color or 'custom' to use a hex value specified in 'bg_color_hex'.

inputs.name: center_x
inputs.description: Specifies the x-coordinate of the center point from which the starburst lines radiate.

inputs.name: center_y
inputs.description: Specifies the y-coordinate of the center point from which the starburst lines radiate.

inputs.name: rotation
inputs.description: Specifies the rotation angle of the entire starburst pattern. This allows the pattern to be oriented in any direction.

inputs.name: line_color_hex
inputs.description: Specifies the custom hex color value for the lines if 'line_color' is set to 'custom'.

inputs.name: bg_color_hex
inputs.description: Specifies the custom hex color value for the background if 'background_color' is set to 'custom'.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: The generated image featuring the starburst pattern.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL to documentation or help page related to the starburst pattern generation.

CR String To Boolean.description: The CR String To Boolean node is designed to convert a string input into a boolean output based on predefined string values representing true or false. It also provides a link to further documentation or help related to its functionality.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The 'text' parameter accepts a string input that is evaluated to determine its boolean value. The conversion is based on specific string values representing true or false, making it crucial for controlling the node's output.

outputs.name: BOOLEAN
outputs.description: The BOOLEAN output represents the boolean value derived from the input string, indicating either true or false based on the input's content.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: The 'show_help' output provides a URL to further documentation or help related to the node's functionality.

CR String To Combo.description: The CR_StringToCombo node is designed to convert a string input into a combination or list based on specified delimiters, facilitating the manipulation and analysis of textual data in a structured format.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The 'text' parameter accepts a string input that the node will attempt to split into a combination or list based on commas. It plays a crucial role in determining the output structure and content.

outputs.name: any
outputs.description: The output is a list derived from the first element of the split input string, intended for further processing or analysis.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: Provides a URL to the help documentation for the CR_StringToCombo node, offering users guidance and additional information.

CR String To Number.description: This node is designed to convert a string representation of a number into its numerical form, offering options for rounding the result to the nearest integer, rounding up, or rounding down. It abstracts the complexity of handling numeric conversions and rounding decisions from the user, providing a straightforward interface for processing textual numeric data.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The text input is the string representation of a number that the node attempts to convert into a numerical form. Its correctness is crucial for the successful execution of the node.

inputs.name: round_integer
inputs.description: This parameter determines the rounding strategy (nearest, up, or down) to be applied to the converted number, affecting the final integer output.

outputs.name: INT
outputs.description: The integer output of the conversion process, affected by the chosen rounding strategy.

outputs.name: FLOAT
outputs.description: The floating-point representation of the input text, providing a non-rounded numerical version.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL to the node's documentation, offering additional help and examples.

CR Style Bars.description: The CR Style Bars node is designed to generate stylized bar patterns within a graphical context, utilizing various orientations and styles to create visually appealing designs. It leverages mathematical and graphical algorithms to produce patterns that can be customized in terms of orientation, color, and frequency, making it a versatile tool for creating background textures or decorative elements in a digital environment.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Specifies the mode of the bar pattern, such as color bars, sin wave, or gradient bars, defining the fundamental pattern type.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Determines the width of the output image in pixels, affecting the scale of the bar pattern.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Determines the height of the output image in pixels, affecting the scale of the bar pattern.

inputs.name: bar_style
inputs.description: Defines the style of the bars in the pattern, influencing the visual texture and complexity.

inputs.name: orientation
inputs.description: Sets the orientation of the bars, either vertical or horizontal, impacting the pattern's directionality.

inputs.name: bar_frequency
inputs.description: Controls the frequency of the bars within the pattern, adjusting the density and spacing of the bars.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: The generated stylized bar pattern as an image, showcasing the customized pattern based on the input parameters provided.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: Provides helpful information or guidance related to the use of the node and its functionalities.

CR Switch Model and CLIP.description: This node is designed to switch between two sets of models and CLIPs based on a given input. It facilitates dynamic selection within a workflow, allowing users to choose between alternative processing paths or resources.

inputs.name: Input
inputs.description: Determines which set of model and CLIP to use, enabling the selection between two predefined options.

inputs.name: model1
inputs.description: The first model option that can be selected.

inputs.name: clip1
inputs.description: The first CLIP option that can be selected alongside the first model.

inputs.name: model2
inputs.description: The second model option that can be selected.

inputs.name: clip2
inputs.description: The second CLIP option that can be selected alongside the second model.

outputs.name: MODEL
outputs.description: The selected model based on the input choice.

outputs.name: CLIP
outputs.description: The selected CLIP based on the input choice.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: Provides a link to further documentation or help related to this node.

CR Text Blacklist.description: This node is designed to filter and replace specific words in a given text with alternative text or an empty string, based on a user-defined blacklist. It's particularly useful for content moderation or customizing text output by removing unwanted words.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The input text to be processed. Words found in this text that match the blacklist will be replaced.

inputs.name: blacklist_words
inputs.description: A list of words to be filtered out from the input text. Each word should be separated by a newline.

inputs.name: replacement_text
inputs.description: The text to replace each blacklisted word with. If left empty, blacklisted words will be removed entirely.

outputs.name: STRING
outputs.description: The modified text after blacklisted words have been replaced or removed.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL to a help page providing additional information and guidance on using the CR Text Blacklist node.

CR Text Concatenate.description: The CR Text Concatenate node is designed to merge two text strings into a single string, optionally inserting a separator between them. This functionality is useful for combining pieces of text in a controlled manner, allowing for the creation of new strings from existing ones.

inputs.name: text1
inputs.description: The first text string to be concatenated. It serves as the starting point of the new string.

inputs.name: text2
inputs.description: The second text string to be concatenated. It is appended to the first string, optionally separated by a specified separator.

inputs.name: separator
inputs.description: A text string used as a separator between the first and second text strings during concatenation. If left empty, the texts are directly concatenated without any separation.

outputs.name: STRING
outputs.description: The concatenated text resulting from merging the first and second text strings with an optional separator.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL to the help documentation for the CR Text Concatenate node.

CR Text Cycler.description: The CR Text Cycler node is designed to repeat and loop through given text lines, creating a list of text items based on specified repetition and loop counts. It facilitates the generation of repetitive text sequences for various applications, such as animations or list manipulations.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The 'text' parameter takes a multiline string input, which is split into lines to be cycled through. It serves as the base content for repetition and looping, forming the core of the text sequences generated by the node.

inputs.name: repeats
inputs.description: The 'repeats' parameter specifies how many times each line of text is to be repeated within a single loop. It controls the density of repetition for each text item, affecting the overall length and composition of the output list.

inputs.name: loops
inputs.description: The 'loops' parameter determines the number of times the entire set of text lines (after applying the 'repeats' parameter) is looped over. It influences the final size of the output list by repeating the sequence of text items multiple times.

outputs.name: STRING
outputs.description: This output is a list of text items generated by cycling through the input text lines according to the specified 'repeats' and 'loops' parameters. It represents the repeated and looped text sequence.

outputs.name: show_text
outputs.description: A URL providing additional help and documentation for using the CR Text Cycler node.

CR Text Input Switch (4 way).description: This node allows for the selection of one out of four text inputs based on a given integer input, facilitating conditional text flow in a workflow.

inputs.name: Input
inputs.description: Determines which of the four text inputs to select and pass forward. The integer value ranges from 1 to 4, each corresponding to a different text input.

inputs.name: text1
inputs.description: The first text option that can be selected. It is one of the four possible text inputs that can be chosen based on the 'Input' value.

inputs.name: text2
inputs.description: The second text option that can be selected. It serves as one of the four possible choices, determined by the 'Input' parameter.

inputs.name: text3
inputs.description: The third text option available for selection. This input is part of the four choices that can be made based on the 'Input' value.

inputs.name: text4
inputs.description: The fourth and final text option that can be selected. It is included as one of the possible choices, contingent on the 'Input' parameter.

outputs.name: STRING
outputs.description: The selected text input based on the 'Input' parameter.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL providing help and documentation for using this node.

CR Text Input Switch.description: This node allows for the dynamic selection between two text inputs based on a specified integer input. It facilitates conditional text output in workflows, enhancing flexibility and decision-making capabilities.

inputs.name: Input
inputs.description: Determines which text input ('text1' or 'text2') to output based on its value (1 or 2).

inputs.name: text1
inputs.description: The first text option that can be outputted if 'Input' is 1.

inputs.name: text2
inputs.description: The second text option that can be outputted if 'Input' is 2.

outputs.name: STRING
outputs.description: The text output selected based on the 'Input' value.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL providing additional help and documentation for the node.

CR Text Length.description: This node calculates the length of a given text string and provides a link to further documentation or help related to the node.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The text string whose length is to be calculated. This input is essential for determining the output integer value representing the text's length.

outputs.name: INT
outputs.description: The length of the input text string, represented as an integer.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL string pointing to further documentation or help related to the CR Text Length node.

CR Text List Simple.description: This node is designed to create a simple list of texts from individual text inputs and an optional list of texts. It allows for the aggregation of up to five separate text inputs and an additional list of texts into a single list, facilitating the organization and manipulation of text data in a streamlined manner.

inputs.name: text_1
inputs.description: The first text input to be included in the list. It's a foundational element for constructing the list, contributing to the overall content.

inputs.name: text_2
inputs.description: The second text input to be included in the list. It adds to the list's content, following the first text input.

inputs.name: text_3
inputs.description: The third text input to be included in the list. It continues to build upon the list's content, following the second text input.

inputs.name: text_4
inputs.description: The fourth text input to be included in the list. It further enriches the list's content, following the third text input.

inputs.name: text_5
inputs.description: The fifth text input to be included in the list. It completes the initial set of individual text inputs, adding depth to the list's content.

inputs.name: text_list_simple
inputs.description: An optional list of texts that can be appended to the list. This parameter allows for the inclusion of pre-existing lists, enhancing the node's flexibility.

outputs.name: TEXT_LIST_SIMPLE
outputs.description: The compiled list of texts, combining individual text inputs and any provided list of texts into a unified collection.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL providing access to additional help and documentation related to the node.

CR Text List To String.description: This node is designed to convert a list of text items into a single string representation, potentially for display or further processing. It emphasizes the transformation of a collection of textual elements into a unified text format, facilitating operations that require a singular text entity.

inputs.name: text_list
inputs.description: The 'text_list' parameter represents the list of text items to be concatenated into a single string. It plays a crucial role in determining the content and structure of the resulting string.

outputs.name: STRING
outputs.description: The 'STRING' output is the concatenated result of the input text list, transformed into a single string for ease of use or display.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: Provides a URL to the documentation or help page related to this node's functionality.

CR Text List.description: This node is designed to transform a multiline text input into a list of strings, each representing a line of text, starting from a specified index and up to a maximum number of rows. It also provides a link to further help or documentation related to its functionality.

inputs.name: multiline_text
inputs.description: The multiline text to be split into a list. This input allows for the dynamic creation of lists based on textual content, enabling flexible list manipulation and processing.

inputs.name: start_index
inputs.description: Specifies the starting index from which to begin extracting lines from the multiline text. This allows for selective list creation, enhancing the node's versatility in handling text data.

inputs.name: max_rows
inputs.description: Defines the maximum number of rows to include in the output list, allowing for control over the list's size and content.

outputs.name: STRING
outputs.description: The output is a list of strings derived from the input multiline text, segmented according to the specified start index and maximum rows.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: Provides a URL to further help or documentation, aiding users in understanding and utilizing the node's functionality.

CR Text Operation.description: This node performs various text manipulation operations such as changing case, reversing, trimming, or removing spaces from the input text based on the specified operation.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The text to be manipulated. It is the primary input on which all operations are performed, affecting the node's execution and results.

inputs.name: operation
inputs.description: Specifies the text manipulation operation to be applied to the input text, such as uppercase, lowercase, capitalize, invert case, reverse, trim, or remove spaces.

outputs.name: STRING
outputs.description: The manipulated text after applying the specified operation.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL providing help and additional information about the text operation node.

CR Text Replace.description: This node allows for the replacement of specified substrings within a given text with new substrings. It supports up to three distinct find-and-replace operations within a single execution, making it a versatile tool for text manipulation and content editing.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The primary text in which the replacements will be made. It serves as the foundational content for the node's operation.

inputs.name: find1
inputs.description: The first substring to be searched for within the primary text. If found, it will be replaced with 'replace1'.

inputs.name: replace1
inputs.description: The replacement for the first found substring 'find1' within the primary text.

inputs.name: find2
inputs.description: The second substring to be searched for within the primary text. If found, it will be replaced with 'replace2'.

inputs.name: replace2
inputs.description: The replacement for the second found substring 'find2' within the primary text.

inputs.name: find3
inputs.description: The third substring to be searched for within the primary text. If found, it will be replaced with 'replace3'.

inputs.name: replace3
inputs.description: The replacement for the third found substring 'find3' within the primary text.

outputs.name: STRING
outputs.description: The modified text after all specified replacements have been made.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL providing additional information and documentation about the node.

CR Text Scheduler.description: The CR Text Scheduler node is designed to manage and schedule text outputs based on predefined schedules or default settings. It dynamically adjusts text outputs according to the current frame and specified scheduling parameters, facilitating the creation of animated text sequences in a user-friendly manner.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Specifies the scheduling mode, which can be either 'Default Text' or based on a 'Schedule', determining how text outputs are managed.

inputs.name: current_frame
inputs.description: Indicates the current frame number, used to determine the appropriate text output based on the schedule.

inputs.name: schedule_alias
inputs.description: An alias for the schedule, used for identification and reference within the scheduling process.

inputs.name: default_text
inputs.description: The default text to be used when no specific schedule is applied, ensuring a fallback text output.

inputs.name: schedule_format
inputs.description: Defines the format of the schedule, either 'CR' or 'Deforum', affecting how the schedule is interpreted.

inputs.name: schedule
inputs.description: The actual schedule data, optional, used when the mode is set to 'Schedule'.

outputs.name: STRING
outputs.description: The scheduled text output for the current frame.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL providing additional information or assistance related to text scheduling.

CR Text.description: This node is designed to handle multiline text input, providing a straightforward way to work with text data within the node's ecosystem. It simplifies the process of inputting and manipulating text, offering a link to further help and guidance on its usage.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The 'text' parameter allows users to input multiline text. This input is essential for the node's operation, serving as the primary data that the node processes and manipulates.

outputs.name: text
outputs.description: Returns the original text input by the user.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: Provides a URL to a help page for further information and guidance on using the node.

CR Thumbnail Preview.description: This node is designed to generate thumbnail previews of images, optionally rescaling them and arranging them in a grid layout. It supports both individual and batch processing of images, allowing for flexible adjustments to the thumbnail presentation. The node also integrates with a websocket server to send the generated thumbnails for display, providing a link to further documentation for user assistance.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image or a batch of images to be processed into thumbnails. This parameter is crucial for determining the content that will be transformed into a thumbnail preview.

inputs.name: rescale_factor
inputs.description: A factor by which the input images are rescaled. This affects the size of the resulting thumbnails, allowing for customization based on user preference or display requirements.

inputs.name: max_columns
inputs.description: Specifies the maximum number of columns in the grid layout for arranging the thumbnails. This parameter influences the overall layout and presentation of the thumbnails.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: Provides a link to further documentation for user assistance, enhancing the usability of the node.

CR Trigger.description: The CR Trigger node is designed to compare an input index against a specified trigger value, returning the index, a boolean indicating if the index matches the trigger value, and a URL for help documentation. This functionality is useful for conditional logic and flow control within node-based processing pipelines.

inputs.name: index
inputs.description: The index to compare against the trigger value. It determines the flow of execution based on its comparison with the trigger value.

inputs.name: trigger_value
inputs.description: The value against which the index is compared. This comparison dictates whether certain actions are triggered based on the match.

outputs.name: index
outputs.description: The original index value passed into the node.

outputs.name: trigger
outputs.description: A boolean indicating whether the index matches the trigger value.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL providing additional help and documentation for the CR Trigger node.

CR Upscale Image.description: This node is designed to upscale images using a specified model, with options for adjusting the scale, resizing, and resampling methods. It provides flexibility in image processing by allowing for multiple loops of upscaling, choice of resampling methods, and control over the final image size and quality.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be upscaled. This parameter is crucial as it determines the base image that will undergo the upscaling process.

inputs.name: upscale_model
inputs.description: Specifies the model to be used for upscaling the image. This choice impacts the quality and characteristics of the upscaled image.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Defines the method used for resizing the image, such as rescaling or cropping, affecting the final appearance.

inputs.name: rescale_factor
inputs.description: The factor by which the image is upscaled, directly influencing the increase in image dimensions.

inputs.name: resize_width
inputs.description: Sets a specific width for the upscaled image, overriding the default scaling behavior.

inputs.name: resampling_method
inputs.description: Specifies the algorithm used for resampling during resizing, influencing the smoothness and clarity of the upscaled image.

inputs.name: supersample
inputs.description: When enabled, applies supersampling for improved image quality, particularly in reducing aliasing effects.

inputs.name: rounding_modulus
inputs.description: Affects the final dimensions of the upscaled image by rounding them to the nearest multiple of this value, ensuring compatibility with certain processing or display requirements.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: The resulting tensor of upscaled images, potentially containing multiple images if loops are used.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL providing additional help and documentation for the upscaling process.

CR VAE Decode.description: The CR_VAEDecode node is designed to decode latent representations into images using a specified VAE model. It supports optional circular and tiled decoding modes to enhance the output image's visual characteristics.

inputs.name: samples
inputs.description: The 'samples' parameter represents the latent representations to be decoded into images. It plays a crucial role in determining the visual content of the output images.

inputs.name: vae
inputs.description: The 'vae' parameter specifies the VAE model used for decoding the latent representations into images. The choice of VAE model can significantly affect the quality and characteristics of the output images.

inputs.name: tiled
inputs.description: The 'tiled' parameter indicates whether tiled decoding should be used, which can help in generating larger images without running into memory constraints.

inputs.name: circular
inputs.description: The 'circular' parameter enables circular padding mode in convolutional layers of the VAE model, potentially enhancing the visual quality of the output images by avoiding edge artifacts.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: The output image generated from the decoded latent representation.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL providing additional help and documentation for the CR_VAEDecode node.

CR VAE Input Switch.description: This node allows for dynamic selection between two VAE inputs based on a specified condition, facilitating flexible workflow configurations and enabling users to switch between different VAE models or settings.

inputs.name: Input
inputs.description: Determines which VAE input to select, enabling conditional logic within the workflow.

inputs.name: VAE1
inputs.description: The first VAE input option. This input is optional and allows for the selection of a VAE model when the condition is met.

inputs.name: VAE2
inputs.description: The second VAE input option. This input is optional and provides an alternative VAE model selection based on the specified condition.

outputs.name: VAE
outputs.description: The selected VAE input based on the specified condition.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL providing documentation and help for using the CR VAE Input Switch node.

CR Value Cycler.description: The CR_ValueCycler node is designed to cycle through a list of values, repeating each value a specified number of times and looping through the entire list for a given number of iterations. It is capable of parsing numeric values from a multiline string, converting them into floats and integers, and outputting these numbers in separate lists.

inputs.name: values
inputs.description: A multiline string containing values to be cycled through. This input is crucial for defining the set of values the node will operate on.

inputs.name: repeats
inputs.description: Specifies how many times each value should be repeated in a single loop. This affects the length and repetition pattern of the output lists.

inputs.name: loops
inputs.description: Determines the number of times the entire set of values is cycled through. This influences the total number of iterations and the final size of the output lists.

outputs.name: FLOAT
outputs.description: A list of floating-point numbers parsed from the input values, repeated and looped according to the specified parameters.

outputs.name: INT
outputs.description: A list of integers converted from the floating-point numbers in the input values, following the same repetition and looping pattern.

outputs.name: show_text
outputs.description: A URL to a help page providing additional information and guidance on using the CR_ValueCycler node.

CR Value Scheduler.description: The CR Value Scheduler node is designed to manage the scheduling of numerical values across different frames in an animation sequence. It allows for the dynamic adjustment of values based on a predefined schedule, enhancing the flexibility and control over the animation's parameters.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Specifies the mode of operation, which can either use a default value or follow a custom schedule for value changes.

inputs.name: current_frame
inputs.description: Indicates the current frame number in the animation sequence, used to determine the appropriate value based on the schedule.

inputs.name: schedule_alias
inputs.description: A unique identifier for the schedule being applied, facilitating the management and reference of multiple schedules.

inputs.name: default_value
inputs.description: The fallback value to be used when the schedule is disabled or an appropriate scheduled value cannot be found.

inputs.name: schedule_format
inputs.description: Defines the format of the schedule, dictating how scheduled values are interpreted and applied.

inputs.name: schedule
inputs.description: The actual schedule containing the frame-wise values to be applied throughout the animation.

outputs.name: INT
outputs.description: The scheduled value converted to an integer, applicable for parameters requiring discrete values.

outputs.name: FLOAT
outputs.description: The scheduled value in its original floating-point format, suitable for parameters requiring continuous values.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL providing additional information and guidance on using the CR Value Scheduler.

CR Value.description: The CR Value node is designed to convert a given value into multiple formats, specifically float, integer, and string, and provide a link to further documentation. It serves as a utility node for format conversion and information retrieval.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: The 'value' parameter is the input that the node will convert into different formats. It plays a crucial role in determining the output formats (float, integer) and the information link provided.

outputs.name: FLOAT
outputs.description: A floating-point representation of the input value.

outputs.name: INT
outputs.description: An integer representation of the input value.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL string pointing to further documentation about the CR Value node.

CR Vignette Filter.description: The CR Vignette Filter node applies a vignette effect to images, allowing for customization of the vignette's shape, intensity, and position. This node enhances visual aesthetics by softly fading the image edges into a specified color, typically to focus attention towards the central area of the image.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The 'image' input specifies the single image to which the vignette effect will be applied. This input is essential for determining the visual output of the node, as it directly influences the appearance and intensity of the vignette effect on the image.

inputs.name: vignette_shape
inputs.description: Specifies the shape of the vignette effect applied to the image. Options include 'circle', 'oval', 'square', and 'diamond', allowing for versatile visual styling.

inputs.name: feather_amount
inputs.description: Determines the softness of the vignette's edges by specifying the amount of feathering. A higher value results in softer, more blended edges.

inputs.name: x_offset
inputs.description: Adjusts the horizontal position of the vignette effect, allowing for custom alignment relative to the image's center.

inputs.name: y_offset
inputs.description: Adjusts the vertical position of the vignette effect, enabling precise placement in relation to the image's central point.

inputs.name: zoom
inputs.description: Controls the size of the vignette effect relative to the image size. A higher zoom value decreases the vignette's size, focusing the effect more centrally.

inputs.name: reverse
inputs.description: Determines whether the vignette effect is applied inside or outside the specified shape. Choosing 'yes' reverses the effect, highlighting the edges instead of the center.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: The processed image with the applied vignette effect, showcasing the enhanced focus and aesthetic appeal.

outputs.name: MASK
outputs.description: The mask used to create the vignette effect, useful for further image processing or analysis.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A string output that provides helpful information or guidance related to the vignette effect's application.

CR XY From Folder.description: The CR XY From Folder node is designed to automate the process of loading and processing a sequence of images from a specified folder, converting them into a format suitable for further manipulation or analysis. This node streamlines the task of handling multiple images, facilitating operations such as annotation and organization into a grid layout based on their filenames.

inputs.name: image_folder
inputs.description: Specifies the list of subfolders within the specified directory from which images are to be loaded. This allows for targeted processing of images grouped in specific folders.

inputs.name: start_index
inputs.description: Defines the starting index for processing images within the folder. This allows for selective processing of images, starting from a specific point in the sequence.

inputs.name: end_index
inputs.description: Specifies the ending index for image processing, enabling selective processing of images within a defined range.

inputs.name: max_columns
inputs.description: Sets the maximum number of columns for organizing the images into a grid layout. This parameter helps in structuring the output in a visually coherent manner.

inputs.name: x_annotation
inputs.description: Provides the annotations for the x-axis of the grid, allowing for descriptive labeling of columns.

inputs.name: y_annotation
inputs.description: Supplies the annotations for the y-axis of the grid, enabling descriptive labeling of rows.

inputs.name: font_size
inputs.description: Determines the font size used for annotating the images. This parameter is crucial for ensuring that annotations are legible and appropriately scaled.

inputs.name: gap
inputs.description: Specifies the gap between images in the grid layout. This parameter allows for adjusting the spacing to achieve the desired layout appearance.

inputs.name: trigger
inputs.description: Acts as a control mechanism to initiate the node's operation. When set to True, the node proceeds with loading and processing the images from the specified folder.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: The processed images organized into a grid layout, ready for further manipulation or analysis.

outputs.name: trigger
outputs.description: Indicates whether the node's operation was initiated.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: Provides helpful information or guidance related to the node's functionality.

CR XY Index.description: The CR XY Index node is designed to calculate the X and Y positions in a grid based on a given index. It facilitates the organization and navigation of elements within a grid structure by converting a linear index into two-dimensional coordinates.

inputs.name: x_columns
inputs.description: Specifies the number of columns in the grid. It determines how the index is translated into the X coordinate, affecting the grid's horizontal layout.

inputs.name: y_rows
inputs.description: Defines the number of rows in the grid. It influences the calculation of the Y coordinate from the index, impacting the grid's vertical structure.

inputs.name: index
inputs.description: The linear index to be converted into X and Y coordinates. This index helps in locating a specific element within the grid structure.

outputs.name: x
outputs.description: The calculated X coordinate in the grid, derived from the provided index.

outputs.name: y
outputs.description: The Y coordinate in the grid, calculated based on the index and the grid dimensions.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL to a help page providing detailed information and guidance on using the CR XY Index node.

CR XY Interpolate.description: The CR XY Interpolate node is designed for interpolating between two points or sets of points on an XY grid, facilitating the creation of smooth transitions or animations within a two-dimensional space. This node is particularly useful in scenarios where visual continuity or gradual changes between states are desired.

inputs.name: x_columns
inputs.description: Specifies the number of columns in the X dimension for the grid. It defines the horizontal spread of points to be interpolated.

inputs.name: x_start_value
inputs.description: The starting value for the X dimension, indicating the initial point or state from which interpolation begins.

inputs.name: x_step
inputs.description: The step size for the X dimension, determining the increment between each point in the grid along the X axis.

inputs.name: x_annotation_prepend
inputs.description: A prefix for annotating the X dimension, used for labeling or identifying points along the X axis.

inputs.name: y_rows
inputs.description: Specifies the number of rows in the Y dimension for the grid. It defines the vertical spread of points to be interpolated.

inputs.name: y_start_value
inputs.description: The starting value for the Y dimension, indicating the initial point or state from which interpolation begins.

inputs.name: y_step
inputs.description: The step size for the Y dimension, determining the increment between each point in the grid along the Y axis.

inputs.name: y_annotation_prepend
inputs.description: A prefix for annotating the Y dimension, used for labeling or identifying points along the Y axis.

inputs.name: index
inputs.description: An index to specify a particular interpolation operation or sequence. It can be used to manage multiple interpolations within the same grid.

inputs.name: gradient_profile
inputs.description: Specifies the gradient profile to be used for interpolation, affecting the transition smoothness between points.

outputs.name: X
outputs.description: The interpolated values along the X dimension, representing a blend of the input states based on the specified parameters.

outputs.name: Y
outputs.description: The interpolated values along the Y dimension, representing a blend of the input states based on the specified parameters.

outputs.name: x_annotation
outputs.description: Generated annotations for the X dimension based on the 'x_annotation_prepend' input and interpolation parameters.

outputs.name: y_annotation
outputs.description: Generated annotations for the Y dimension based on the 'y_annotation_prepend' input and interpolation parameters.

outputs.name: trigger
outputs.description: A trigger output that can be used to initiate further actions or processes once the interpolation is complete.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: Provides a link to additional documentation or help related to the node and its usage.

CR XY List.description: The CR XY List node is designed to generate a pair of outputs based on the Cartesian product of two input lists, with additional functionality to prepend and append custom text to each element. It also provides annotations for the last iteration of the Cartesian product, facilitating complex list manipulations and grid-based operations.

inputs.name: index
inputs.description: The index to select a specific pair from the Cartesian product. Indexing starts from 1.

inputs.name: list1
inputs.description: The first list to participate in the Cartesian product. Elements from this list are combined with elements from the second list to generate the output pairs.

inputs.name: x_prepend
inputs.description: Text to prepend to each element of the first list in the output pairs.

inputs.name: x_append
inputs.description: Text to append to each element of the first list in the output pairs.

inputs.name: x_annotation_prepend
inputs.description: Text to prepend to the annotation of each element of the first list.

inputs.name: list2
inputs.description: The second list to participate in the Cartesian product. It is combined with elements from the first list to generate the output pairs.

inputs.name: y_prepend
inputs.description: Text to prepend to each element of the second list in the output pairs.

inputs.name: y_append
inputs.description: Text to append to each element of the second list in the output pairs.

inputs.name: y_annotation_prepend
inputs.description: Text to prepend to the annotation of each element of the second list.

outputs.name: X
outputs.description: The processed output from the first list after applying prepend and append operations.

outputs.name: Y
outputs.description: The processed output from the second list after applying prepend and append operations.

outputs.name: x_annotation
outputs.description: The annotation for all elements of the first list after the last iteration of the Cartesian product.

outputs.name: y_annotation
outputs.description: The annotation for all elements of the second list after the last iteration of the Cartesian product.

outputs.name: trigger
outputs.description: A boolean flag indicating if the current iteration is the last one in the Cartesian product.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL to the help documentation for the CR XY List node.

CR XY Product.description: The CR XY Product node performs a Cartesian product operation on two lists of text inputs, generating a new list that combines each element of the first list with every element of the second list. This node is useful for creating combinations of different text elements, facilitating operations that require exhaustive pairing of input elements.

inputs.name: text_x
inputs.description: Represents the first list of text inputs. Each line is considered a separate element in the list, and the node combines each of these elements with every element of the second list to form the Cartesian product.

inputs.name: text_y
inputs.description: Represents the second list of text inputs. Similar to 'text_x', each line is treated as a separate element, and is combined with elements from the first list to generate the Cartesian product.

outputs.name: x_values
outputs.description: A list containing the first elements of each pair in the Cartesian product.

outputs.name: y_values
outputs.description: A list containing the second elements of each pair in the Cartesian product.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: A URL providing additional help and documentation for the CR XY Product node.

CR XY Save Grid Image.description: This node is designed to save a grid of images to a specified output path, optionally adding annotations to the images. It supports various file formats and allows for customization of image saving parameters such as compression level and quality. The node can operate in different modes, such as saving for output or generating a temporary preview, and provides a UI component for previewing the saved images.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Specifies the operation mode of the node, which can be either 'Save' for saving images to a permanent location or 'Preview' for generating temporary images for preview purposes. This affects the type of path used for saving and the metadata associated with the saved images.

inputs.name: output_folder
inputs.description: The name of the folder where the images will be saved. This folder is created inside a predefined output directory.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image or images to be saved. This can be a single image or a list of images to be arranged in a grid.

inputs.name: filename_prefix
inputs.description: A prefix added to the filename of the saved images, useful for organizing and identifying images.

inputs.name: file_format
inputs.description: The file format in which the images will be saved. Supports common formats like PNG, JPG, WEBP, and TIFF.

inputs.name: output_path
inputs.description: An optional custom path where the images will be saved. If provided, it overrides the default output folder path.

inputs.name: trigger
inputs.description: A boolean flag that must be set to True to activate the image saving process. If False, the node does not perform any action.

CR_Aspect Ratio For Print.description: This node is designed to adjust the aspect ratio of images specifically for print purposes. It modifies image dimensions to fit standard print sizes, ensuring that the output is optimized for physical media.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Specifies the initial width of the image. This value is adjusted based on the selected aspect ratio and other parameters to fit standard print sizes.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Specifies the initial height of the image. Similar to 'width', this value is adjusted to match the desired aspect ratio for print.

inputs.name: aspect_ratio
inputs.description: Defines the target aspect ratio for the image, selected from a predefined list of standard print sizes. This choice determines the final dimensions of the image.

inputs.name: swap_dimensions
inputs.description: Allows for the swapping of width and height dimensions, accommodating different orientation needs without altering the aspect ratio.

inputs.name: upscale_factor
inputs.description: A multiplier for scaling the image's dimensions up, allowing for higher resolution prints.

inputs.name: prescale_factor
inputs.description: A multiplier for scaling the image's dimensions before applying the aspect ratio adjustments. This can be used for initial size adjustments.

inputs.name: batch_size
inputs.description: Determines the number of images processed in a single batch, allowing for efficient bulk processing of images.

outputs.name: width
outputs.description: The adjusted width of the image, optimized for the selected print aspect ratio.

outputs.name: height
outputs.description: The adjusted height of the image, reflecting the chosen aspect ratio for print purposes.

outputs.name: upscale_factor
outputs.description: The factor by which the image's dimensions have been scaled up, applicable if an upscale was performed.

outputs.name: prescale_factor
outputs.description: The factor by which the image's dimensions were scaled before aspect ratio adjustments, applicable if a prescale was performed.

outputs.name: batch_size
outputs.description: The number of images processed, reflecting the input batch size.

outputs.name: empty_latent
outputs.description: A tensor placeholder for the processed images, structured to accommodate the adjusted dimensions.

outputs.name: show_help
outputs.description: Provides a link to additional help and documentation regarding aspect ratio adjustments for print.

AIO_Preprocessor.description: The AIO_Preprocessor node is designed to dynamically select and apply a specified auxiliary preprocessing operation on an image, based on the preprocessor type chosen. It supports a variety of preprocessing options, automatically configuring and executing the appropriate auxiliary preprocessor to modify the image according to the selected preprocessor's requirements.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be preprocessed. This image is directly passed to the selected auxiliary preprocessor for modification.

inputs.name: preprocessor
inputs.description: Specifies the type of preprocessing to apply to the image. This selection determines which auxiliary preprocessor's logic will be executed, impacting the final preprocessing outcome on the image.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: The resolution for the preprocessing operation, which may be used by certain preprocessors to adjust the processing detail level or output resolution.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The preprocessed image, as modified by the selected auxiliary preprocessor.

AnimalPosePreprocessor.description: The AnimalPosePreprocessor node is designed for detecting and analyzing animal poses within images. It utilizes advanced pose estimation techniques to identify and process animal figures, aiming to provide detailed pose information that can be used for further analysis or processing.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed for animal pose detection. This is the primary input for the pose estimation process.

inputs.name: bbox_detector
inputs.description: Specifies the bounding box detector model used to identify the regions of interest within the image where animals are present. This step is crucial for narrowing down the areas for pose estimation.

inputs.name: pose_estimator
inputs.description: Defines the pose estimation model to be used for analyzing the detected animal figures within the image. This parameter determines the accuracy and effectiveness of the pose detection.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: Sets the resolution for the pose detection process. Higher resolutions can lead to more detailed pose estimations but may require more computational resources.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: Returns the processed image with detected animal poses highlighted, facilitating visual inspection and analysis of the pose estimation results.

outputs.name: pose_keypoint
outputs.description: Outputs the key points of detected animal poses, providing detailed information about the pose structure for further analysis or processing.

AnimeFace_SemSegPreprocessor.description: This node is designed for preprocessing images for semantic segmentation tasks specifically tailored to anime faces. It leverages a specialized model to segment anime faces from the background, optionally removing the background based on the provided settings, and prepares the image and mask for further processing.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed for anime face segmentation. This image is the primary subject for the segmentation task.

inputs.name: remove_background_using_abg
inputs.description: A flag to determine whether the background should be removed from the image during the segmentation process. This affects the output mask and segmented image.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: The resolution to which the input image is resized before processing. This ensures consistency in the segmentation output across different image sizes.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: The segmented image with anime faces, optionally with the background removed based on the input flag.

outputs.name: ABG_CHARACTER_MASK (MASK)
outputs.description: The mask indicating the segmented areas of the anime faces in the image. Useful for further image manipulation or processing.

AnimeLineArtPreprocessor.description: The AnimeLineArtPreprocessor node is designed for extracting line art from anime images. It utilizes a specialized model to process images and enhance their line art features, making it suitable for applications that require clean and distinct line drawings.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed for line art extraction. This parameter is crucial as it determines the quality and characteristics of the output line art.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: Specifies the resolution of the output image. A higher resolution can lead to more detailed line art but may increase processing time.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The processed image with enhanced line art features. This output is ideal for further artistic or analytical applications.

AnyLineArtPreprocessor_aux.description: This node is designed to preprocess images by applying a line art extraction process, which can be customized to merge with different line art styles such as standard, realistic, anime, or manga. It enhances images for further processing or visualization by extracting prominent lines and adjusting them according to the selected line art style, making it versatile for various artistic and design applications.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed for line art extraction. It serves as the primary data on which the line art preprocessing is performed, determining the visual output of the node.

inputs.name: merge_with_lineart
inputs.description: Specifies the line art style to merge with during the preprocessing, such as 'lineart_standard', 'lineart_realistic', 'lineart_anime', or 'manga_line'. This choice influences the aesthetic and stylistic outcome of the processed image.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: Defines the resolution for the output image, affecting the detail and quality of the extracted line art.

inputs.name: lineart_lower_bound
inputs.description: Sets the lower bound for line art extraction, influencing the minimum intensity of lines to be included in the output.

inputs.name: lineart_upper_bound
inputs.description: Sets the upper bound for line art extraction, influencing the maximum intensity of lines to be included in the output.

inputs.name: object_min_size
inputs.description: Determines the minimum size of objects to be considered in the line art extraction, affecting the granularity of the output.

inputs.name: object_connectivity
inputs.description: Specifies the connectivity criteria for objects in the line art extraction, impacting how individual lines and shapes are interpreted and connected in the output.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The processed image with extracted line art, presented in a format suitable for visualization or further artistic processing.
