BAE-NormalMapPreprocessor.description: The BAE-NormalMapPreprocessor node is designed for preprocessing images to generate normal maps using the BAE (Boundary Aware Encoder) model. It enhances images for further processing or visualization by estimating surface normals.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed for normal map generation.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: The resolution to which the input image is resized before processing. It affects the detail level of the generated normal map.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output normal map generated from the input image, providing an estimation of surface normals.

BinaryPreprocessor.description: The BinaryPreprocessor node is designed for preprocessing images by applying a binary thresholding technique. This method converts images into binary images (black and white) based on a specified threshold, which is useful for highlighting certain features or simplifying the image for further processing.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The 'image' parameter is the input image to be processed. It is the primary data on which the binary thresholding operation is performed.

inputs.name: bin_threshold
inputs.description: The 'bin_threshold' parameter specifies the cutoff value for converting pixel values in the image to either black or white. Pixels with values above this threshold are turned white, and those below are turned black, aiding in the extraction of prominent features from the image.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: The 'resolution' parameter specifies the resolution to which the input image is resized before applying the binary thresholding. This allows for consistent processing across images of varying original resolutions.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is a binary (black and white) version of the input image, where the conversion is based on the specified bin_threshold value.

CannyEdgePreprocessor.description: The CannyEdgePreprocessor node is designed for edge detection in images using the Canny algorithm. It preprocesses images by applying a Canny edge detector to highlight the edges within the image, making it suitable for further image processing or analysis tasks.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image parameter is the input image on which edge detection will be performed using the Canny algorithm.

inputs.name: low_threshold
inputs.description: The low_threshold parameter sets the lower bound for the hysteresis thresholding step in the Canny edge detection algorithm. It helps in identifying the weak edges in the image.

inputs.name: high_threshold
inputs.description: The high_threshold parameter sets the upper bound for the hysteresis thresholding step in the Canny edge detection algorithm. It is crucial for distinguishing strong edges in the image.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: The resolution parameter specifies the resolution to which the input image will be resized before applying the Canny edge detection algorithm.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is an image where the edges have been highlighted using the Canny edge detection algorithm.

ColorPreprocessor.description: The ColorPreprocessor node is designed to process images by detecting and annotating colors within them, utilizing a specialized color detection model. This preprocessing step is crucial for tasks that require color analysis or modification before further processing.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed for color detection and annotation.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: Specifies the resolution to which the input image should be resized before processing. This parameter influences the precision and performance of color detection.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The processed image with color detection and annotation applied.

ControlNetPreprocessorSelector.description: The ControlNetPreprocessorSelector node is designed to select a specific preprocessor for use in ControlNet operations, allowing for dynamic adaptation of preprocessing strategies based on user input.

inputs.name: preprocessor
inputs.description: Specifies the preprocessor to be selected for the operation, enabling dynamic adaptation to various preprocessing needs.

outputs.name: preprocessor
outputs.description: Returns the selected preprocessor, facilitating its application in subsequent ControlNet operations.

DensePosePreprocessor.description: The DensePosePreprocessor node is designed to estimate dense human body poses from images. It preprocesses images using a selected DensePose model and color map to generate detailed body pose estimations.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed for dense pose estimation. This image is the primary input on which the pose estimation is performed.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: Specifies the DensePose model to be used for pose estimation. The choice of model can affect the accuracy and performance of the pose estimation.

inputs.name: cmap
inputs.description: Determines the color map used for visualizing the pose estimation results. Different color maps can provide varying visual clarity and aesthetic appeal.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: The resolution to which the input image is resized before processing. A higher resolution can lead to more detailed pose estimations but may increase processing time.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: Produces an image with the dense pose estimation visualized according to the selected color map.

DepthAnythingPreprocessor.description: The DepthAnythingPreprocessor node is designed to preprocess images for depth estimation tasks by utilizing different pretrained models based on the checkpoint name provided. It abstracts the complexity of model selection and preprocessing steps, offering a streamlined way to generate depth maps from input images.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed for depth estimation. This image is transformed and fed into the selected model to generate a depth map.

inputs.name: ckpt_name
inputs.description: Specifies the pretrained model checkpoint to use for depth estimation. The choice of checkpoint affects the model's performance and accuracy.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: The resolution to which the input image is resized before processing. This parameter can influence the detail level of the resulting depth map.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is a depth map of the input image, providing a pixel-wise estimation of depth.

DepthAnythingV2Preprocessor.description: This node is designed to preprocess images for depth estimation, utilizing a selection of pretrained models to generate depth maps. It allows for the customization of the model checkpoint and resolution, catering to different levels of detail and accuracy in depth estimation.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed for depth estimation. It is the primary data upon which the depth map will be generated.

inputs.name: ckpt_name
inputs.description: The name of the checkpoint file for the pretrained model to be used in depth estimation. This selection enables the use of different model architectures or training datasets for varied depth estimation needs.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: The resolution at which the depth map should be generated. Higher resolutions can provide more detailed depth estimations but may require more computational resources.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output depth map image, providing a visual representation of the estimated depths across the input image.

DiffusionEdge_Preprocessor.description: The DiffusionEdge_Preprocessor node is designed for preprocessing images to extract edge maps using a diffusion-based edge detection model. It supports environment-specific model loading and adjustable patch processing for optimized performance.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed for edge detection.

inputs.name: environment
inputs.description: Specifies the environment context ('indoor', 'urban', 'natural') for the edge detection model, influencing the model's behavior and output.

inputs.name: patch_batch_size
inputs.description: Determines the batch size for processing image patches, affecting the speed and VRAM usage of the edge detection operation.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: The resolution to which the input image is resized before edge detection, affecting the detail level of the output.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is an image representing the detected edges within the input image, suitable for further processing or visualization.

DSINE-NormalMapPreprocessor.description: The DSINE Normal Map Preprocessor node is designed to preprocess images for normal map generation using the DSINE model. It adjusts the field of view and iteration parameters to optimize the model's performance for generating detailed normal maps from input images.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image input is the target for normal map generation, serving as the base for the model to apply its processing and generate the normal map.

inputs.name: fov
inputs.description: The field of view parameter adjusts the perspective from which the normal map is generated, affecting the depth perception and detail in the resulting image.

inputs.name: iterations
inputs.description: The iterations parameter controls the number of refinement steps the model performs, impacting the accuracy and detail of the generated normal map.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: The resolution parameter specifies the output resolution of the generated normal map, affecting the level of detail and clarity.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is a normal map image, which visually represents surface normals as colors, providing detailed information about the surface geometry of the input image.

DWPreprocessor.description: The DWPreprocessor node is designed for preprocessing input data specifically for the DWPose estimation tasks. It transforms input data into a format suitable for pose estimation, enhancing the performance of pose estimation models by optimizing the input data's structure and format.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed for pose estimation.

inputs.name: detect_hand
inputs.description: Enables or disables hand detection in the pose estimation process, affecting the comprehensiveness of the pose analysis.

inputs.name: detect_body
inputs.description: Enables or disables body detection, determining whether body keypoints are included in the pose estimation.

inputs.name: detect_face
inputs.description: Controls the inclusion of face detection in the pose estimation, influencing the detail level of facial keypoints.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: The resolution to which the input image is resized, affecting the detail level of the pose estimation.

inputs.name: bbox_detector
inputs.description: Specifies the bounding box detector model to use, impacting the initial detection phase of pose estimation.

inputs.name: pose_estimator
inputs.description: Determines the pose estimation model, directly affecting the accuracy and performance of pose keypoint detection.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The processed image after pose estimation, ready for further analysis or visualization.

outputs.name: pose_keypoint
outputs.description: The detected pose keypoints, providing detailed positional information for body parts.

FacialPartColoringFromPoseKps.description: This node is designed to colorize specific facial parts in pose keypoints data, allowing for visual differentiation and analysis of facial features based on pose estimation. It utilizes facial keypoints to draw or fill specified parts with colors, supporting customization of part colors and rendering modes.

inputs.name: pose_kps
inputs.description: The pose keypoints data, which includes positions of various facial and body keypoints for one or more individuals. This data is essential for determining the facial parts to be colorized.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Specifies the rendering mode for the facial parts, either as points or filled polygons, affecting the visual representation of the colorized keypoints.

inputs.name: skin
inputs.description: Specifies the color for the skin facial part.

inputs.name: left_eye
inputs.description: Specifies the color for the left eye facial part.

inputs.name: right_eye
inputs.description: Specifies the color for the right eye facial part.

inputs.name: nose
inputs.description: Specifies the color for the nose facial part.

inputs.name: upper_lip
inputs.description: Specifies the color for the upper lip facial part.

inputs.name: inner_mouth
inputs.description: Specifies the color for the inner mouth facial part.

inputs.name: lower_lip
inputs.description: Specifies the color for the lower lip facial part.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The processed image(s) with facial parts colorized according to the provided specifications.

FakeScribblePreprocessor.description: The FakeScribblePreprocessor node is designed for preprocessing images to simulate scribble lines, leveraging a modified HED (Holistically-Nested Edge Detection) model. This node aims to produce images with scribble-like lines, which can be useful in various image processing and computer vision tasks, especially in contexts where the stylization of edges as scribbles is desired.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed for scribble line simulation.

inputs.name: safe
inputs.description: A mode that, when enabled, applies a safety mechanism to the preprocessing, potentially altering the processing to avoid undesirable effects.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: The resolution at which the image processing should be executed. This parameter allows for adjusting the detail level of the output image.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image with simulated scribble lines, processed from the input image.

HEDPreprocessor.description: The HEDPreprocessor node is designed for extracting soft-edge lines from images using the HED (Holistically-Nested Edge Detection) model. It preprocesses images to enhance or isolate their line features, making it suitable for tasks that require detailed edge or line detection.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed for edge detection.

inputs.name: safe
inputs.description: A toggle to enable or disable safety checks during processing, potentially affecting the output's fidelity.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: The resolution to which the input image is resized before processing. Higher resolutions may improve detail at the cost of increased computation.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The processed image with enhanced or isolated soft-edge lines.

HintImageEnchance.description: This node is designed to enhance and resize hint images for image generation tasks. It supports multiple resizing modes to fit the generated image's dimensions, ensuring the hint images are appropriately scaled and processed for optimal use in the generation process.

inputs.name: hint_image
inputs.description: The collection of hint images to be enhanced and resized. These images serve as guidance for the image generation process, influencing the output's appearance.

inputs.name: image_gen_width
inputs.description: The target width for the generated images. This parameter determines how the hint images are resized horizontally.

inputs.name: image_gen_height
inputs.description: The target height for the generated images. This parameter influences the vertical resizing of the hint images.

inputs.name: resize_mode
inputs.description: Specifies the mode of resizing to be applied to the hint images, such as fitting within or stretching to the target dimensions.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The enhanced and resized hint images, ready for use in the image generation process.

ImageGenResolutionFromImage.description: This node is designed to compute the generation resolution from an input image. It analyzes the dimensions of the provided image and calculates the width and height that should be used for image generation, ensuring the output resolution is directly derived from the input image's size.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image for which the generation resolution is to be calculated. This parameter is crucial as it directly influences the output resolution by analyzing the image's dimensions.

outputs.name: IMAGE_GEN_WIDTH (INT)
outputs.description: The calculated width for image generation, derived from the input image's dimensions.

outputs.name: IMAGE_GEN_HEIGHT (INT)
outputs.description: The calculated height for image generation, derived from the input image's dimensions.

ImageGenResolutionFromLatent.description: This node is designed to calculate the generation resolution for images based on the dimensions of a given latent representation. It extracts the height and width from the latent's shape and scales them to determine the appropriate resolution for image generation.

inputs.name: latent
inputs.description: The latent representation from which the image generation resolution will be derived. The latent's shape is used to calculate the desired output dimensions by scaling its height and width.

outputs.name: IMAGE_GEN_WIDTH (INT)
outputs.description: The calculated width for image generation, derived from the latent's dimensions and scaled appropriately.

outputs.name: IMAGE_GEN_HEIGHT (INT)
outputs.description: The calculated height for image generation, derived from the latent's dimensions and scaled appropriately.

ImageIntensityDetector.description: The ImageIntensityDetector node is designed for preprocessing images by adjusting their intensity levels. This adjustment is achieved through gamma correction, enhancing the image's overall visibility and contrast before further processing.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed for intensity adjustment through gamma correction.

inputs.name: gamma_correction
inputs.description: Specifies the gamma correction factor to adjust the image's intensity. A higher value brightens the image, while a lower value darkens it, significantly impacting the visual quality of the output.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: The resolution to which the image is resized before applying the intensity adjustment, affecting the detail level of the output.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is an image with adjusted intensity levels, suitable for visual analysis or further image processing tasks.

ImageLuminanceDetector.description: The ImageLuminanceDetector node is designed to analyze and adjust the luminance of images based on gamma correction. It utilizes the Recolorizer from the controlnet_aux library to modify the image's luminance, aiming to enhance image quality or achieve specific visual effects.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed for luminance adjustment.

inputs.name: gamma_correction
inputs.description: Specifies the gamma correction factor to adjust the image's luminance. A higher value brightens the image, while a lower value darkens it, affecting the overall visual output.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: The resolution to which the image is resized before applying the luminance adjustment, affecting the detail level of the output.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: Outputs the modified image with adjusted luminance levels, enhancing or altering the visual appearance based on the gamma correction applied.

InpaintPreprocessor.description: The InpaintPreprocessor node is designed for preparing images for inpainting tasks by applying a mask to the input image. It modifies the image by marking specified areas (as defined by the mask) as needing inpainting, effectively setting up the image for further processing where these areas can be filled or corrected.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The 'image' parameter represents the input image that needs inpainting. It is crucial for defining the areas that will remain unchanged during the inpainting process.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The 'mask' parameter specifies the areas within the image that require inpainting. It plays a key role in identifying which parts of the image should be processed or filled by the inpainting algorithm.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is a modified version of the input image, where areas specified by the mask are marked for inpainting, ready for further processing.

LeReS-DepthMapPreprocessor.description: The LeReS Depth Map Preprocessor node is designed for enhancing depth map estimations from images. It utilizes the LeReS model to preprocess images, offering options to remove nearest objects and background, and an optional boost mode for improved depth estimation.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image for which the depth map will be estimated and enhanced.

inputs.name: rm_nearest
inputs.description: Specifies the threshold for removing the nearest objects from the depth map, enhancing focus on more distant elements.

inputs.name: rm_background
inputs.description: Defines the threshold for background removal in the depth map, aiding in the isolation of primary subjects.

inputs.name: boost
inputs.description: Enables an enhanced depth estimation mode, known as 'boost', for potentially improved depth map quality.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: Specifies the resolution at which the depth map estimation should be performed. Higher resolutions may improve detail but require more computational resources.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: Produces an enhanced depth map image, with options for nearest object and background removal, and an enhanced mode for improved depth estimation.

LineArtPreprocessor.description: The LineArtPreprocessor node is designed for extracting line art from images, specifically focusing on creating realistic line art representations. It utilizes a specialized model to process images and optionally allows for the adjustment of the line art's coarseness.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed for line art extraction.

inputs.name: coarse
inputs.description: This parameter allows users to toggle the coarseness of the line art extraction, enabling a choice between a more detailed or a more generalized representation.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: Specifies the resolution at which the image should be processed, affecting the detail level of the extracted line art.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is an image that has been processed to extract realistic line art, suitable for various artistic and design applications.

LineartStandardPreprocessor.description: The LineartStandardPreprocessor node is designed for extracting line art from images using a standard approach. It preprocesses images to highlight and refine line details, making it suitable for applications requiring clear line delineation, such as digital art and animation.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed for line art extraction.

inputs.name: guassian_sigma
inputs.description: Specifies the sigma value for the Gaussian blur applied to the image, affecting the smoothness of the lines extracted.

inputs.name: intensity_threshold
inputs.description: Determines the threshold for intensity differentiation, influencing the distinction between line art and the background.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: The resolution to which the input image is resized before processing, affecting the detail level of the extracted line art.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: Produces an image with enhanced and refined line art, suitable for further processing or direct use in various applications.

M-LSDPreprocessor.description: The M-LSDPreprocessor node is designed for extracting line segments from images using the M-LSD (Multiple Line Segment Detector) model. It processes images to detect and delineate line structures, which can be crucial for various computer vision tasks that require understanding of geometric shapes and boundaries.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed for line segment detection.

inputs.name: score_threshold
inputs.description: Defines the threshold for line segment detection confidence. Higher values result in fewer, but more confident line detections.

inputs.name: dist_threshold
inputs.description: Sets the distance threshold for separating line segments. Smaller values lead to finer segmentation of closely spaced lines.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: Specifies the resolution to which the input image is resized before processing. Affects the scale of detected line segments.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: Outputs an image with detected line segments superimposed or highlighted, facilitating further processing or analysis.

Manga2Anime_LineArt_Preprocessor.description: This node is designed to preprocess images by extracting line art from manga images, transforming them into a format suitable for anime-style rendering. It utilizes a specialized model to detect and highlight the line art, ensuring the output is optimized for further processing or direct use in anime-style visual projects.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed for manga line art extraction. This image is transformed to highlight the line art, making it suitable for anime-style rendering.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: Specifies the resolution to which the input image is scaled before line art extraction. This parameter ensures the output is optimized for the desired visual quality.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The processed image with manga line art extracted, presented in a format optimized for anime-style rendering.

MaskOptFlow.description: The MaskOptFlow node applies a mask to an optical flow input, effectively filtering the optical flow data based on the mask provided. This operation is crucial for isolating relevant motion information from specific regions of interest within the optical flow data.

inputs.name: optical_flow
inputs.description: The optical flow input represents the motion between two consecutive frames. It is essential for understanding the dynamics within the scene.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The mask input is used to filter the optical flow data, allowing only the motion information from regions of interest to be retained.

outputs.name: OPTICAL_FLOW
outputs.description: The filtered optical flow data, where motion information is retained only for the regions specified by the mask.

outputs.name: PREVIEW_IMAGE
outputs.description: A visualization of the filtered optical flow, providing a visual representation of the motion information retained by the mask.

MediaPipe-FaceMeshPreprocessor.description: The MediaPipe Face Mesh Preprocessor node is designed for detecting and processing facial features in images using the MediaPipe library. It focuses on identifying faces and their key landmarks with configurable accuracy and performance settings, making it suitable for applications requiring facial analysis.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed for face detection and landmark annotation. This parameter is essential for the node to perform its facial analysis tasks.

inputs.name: max_faces
inputs.description: Specifies the maximum number of faces to detect in an image. This parameter allows for control over the detection process, ensuring that the algorithm focuses on a manageable number of faces for further processing.

inputs.name: min_confidence
inputs.description: Determines the minimum confidence level for a face to be considered detected. This threshold helps in filtering out detections that are less likely to be accurate, ensuring that only faces with a high probability of being correctly identified are processed.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: The resolution at which the input image is processed. This parameter can affect the detection accuracy and performance of the face mesh preprocessor.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is an image annotated with detected facial landmarks. This includes key points and contours for facial features such as eyes, eyebrows, nose, and mouth, enabling detailed facial analysis.

MeshGraphormer+ImpactDetector-DepthMapPr.description: This node integrates an external impact detector with the MeshGraphormer model to preprocess images for depth map and mask generation. It enhances the depth map preprocessing by incorporating detection of specific features (e.g., hands) in the images, refining the depth map and mask outputs based on detected regions.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed for depth map and mask generation, serving as the primary data for the node's operations.

inputs.name: bbox_detector
inputs.description: Specifies the bounding box detector to be used for identifying regions of interest within the images, crucial for the subsequent depth map and mask generation.

inputs.name: bbox_threshold
inputs.description: The threshold value for bounding box detection, controlling the sensitivity of the external impact detector in identifying regions of interest.

inputs.name: bbox_dilation
inputs.description: The dilation factor applied to bounding boxes, adjusting the area around detected features for depth map generation.

inputs.name: bbox_crop_factor
inputs.description: The factor by which the bounding box is cropped, focusing the depth map generation on more precise areas of interest.

inputs.name: drop_size
inputs.description: The minimum size of detected features to be considered, filtering out smaller detections to focus on significant regions.

inputs.name: mask_bbox_padding
inputs.description: The padding added around the bounding box when generating masks, allowing for more flexible mask creation around detected features.

inputs.name: mask_type
inputs.description: Defines the method used for mask generation, whether based on depth information, tight bounding boxes, or the original detection method.

inputs.name: mask_expand
inputs.description: The expansion factor for masks, adjusting the area covered by the mask beyond the detected features.

inputs.name: rand_seed
inputs.description: The random seed used for deterministic operations within the model, ensuring consistent results across runs.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: Specifies the resolution at which the depth map and mask are generated, impacting the detail and quality of the output.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: The generated depth maps corresponding to the input images, refined based on detected features and regions of interest.

outputs.name: INPAINTING_MASK
outputs.description: The masks indicating the areas of interest within the images, generated based on the depth map preprocessing and feature detection.

MeshGraphormer-DepthMapPreprocessor.description: This node is designed to preprocess images for depth map generation, specifically tailored for hand gestures. It utilizes a MeshGraphormer model to refine depth maps and masks of hands within images, enhancing the accuracy of depth perception for each detected hand region.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed for hand gesture depth map generation. It serves as the primary data for detecting hand landmarks and generating corresponding depth maps and masks.

inputs.name: mask_bbox_padding
inputs.description: Specifies the padding around the bounding box of detected hands, affecting the area considered for depth map generation. It helps in adjusting the focus area around the hands.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: The resolution to which the input images are resized before processing. This parameter directly impacts the model's performance and the quality of the output depth maps.

inputs.name: mask_type
inputs.description: Determines the type of mask to be generated, such as based on depth values or tight bounding boxes, influencing how hand regions are isolated from the background.

inputs.name: mask_expand
inputs.description: Defines the expansion or contraction of the mask boundaries, allowing for finer control over the size of the hand region to be processed.

inputs.name: rand_seed
inputs.description: A seed value for random number generation, ensuring reproducibility of the depth maps and masks across multiple runs.

inputs.name: detect_thr
inputs.description: The detection threshold for the MeshGraphormer model, determining the sensitivity of hand detection within the images.

inputs.name: presence_thr
inputs.description: The presence threshold for the MeshGraphormer model, affecting the likelihood of a hand's presence being recognized in the processed area.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: The refined depth maps for each hand region detected in the input images. These maps provide detailed depth information, crucial for subsequent processing steps.

outputs.name: INPAINTING_MASK
outputs.description: Binary masks corresponding to the hand regions within the input images. These masks are essential for isolating hand gestures from the background.

Metric3D-DepthMapPreprocessor.description: This node preprocesses images for depth map estimation using a 3D metric model. It leverages a configurable backbone architecture and camera intrinsic parameters to enhance the depth estimation process, aiming to provide a detailed depth map for each input image.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed for depth map estimation. The quality and characteristics of the image can significantly impact the accuracy and detail of the resulting depth map, making it a crucial factor in the node's execution.

inputs.name: backbone
inputs.description: Specifies the backbone model architecture used for depth estimation. The choice of backbone can significantly influence the accuracy and performance of the depth map generation.

inputs.name: fx
inputs.description: Represents the focal length of the camera along the x-axis. It is a critical parameter for accurately mapping 2D images to 3D space, affecting the scale and perspective of the depth map.

inputs.name: fy
inputs.description: Represents the focal length of the camera along the y-axis, essential for correct depth perception and 3D reconstruction from 2D images.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: The desired resolution for the output depth map, affecting the level of detail and size of the output image. Higher resolutions can provide more detailed depth maps but may require more computational resources.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is a depth map image, providing a pixel-wise depth estimation for the input image.

Metric3D-NormalMapPreprocessor.description: This node preprocesses images for normal map estimation using a 3D metric model. It leverages a pre-trained Metric3DDetector model, configurable with different backbone architectures and intrinsic camera parameters, to compute normal maps from input images. The node aims to enhance depth and normal estimation tasks by providing detailed normal maps, which are crucial for accurate 3D reconstruction and analysis.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed for normal map estimation.

inputs.name: backbone
inputs.description: Specifies the backbone architecture for the Metric3DDetector model. Different backbones offer varying levels of detail and accuracy in the normal map estimation.

inputs.name: fx
inputs.description: The focal length of the camera in the x-axis, used to calibrate the Metric3DDetector model for accurate normal map estimation.

inputs.name: fy
inputs.description: The focal length of the camera in the y-axis, essential for calibrating the model to accurately estimate normal maps.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: The resolution to which the input image is scaled before processing. This parameter can affect the detail level of the estimated normal map.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is an image representing the estimated normal map, which visualizes the orientation of surfaces in the scene.

MiDaS-DepthMapPreprocessor.description: This node preprocesses images to generate depth maps using the MiDaS model, enhancing the perception of depth in images for further processing or visualization.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The 'image' parameter is the input image to be processed for depth map generation, serving as the primary data for depth estimation.

inputs.name: a
inputs.description: The 'a' parameter adjusts the depth estimation sensitivity, influencing the depth map's perception of distance and depth.

inputs.name: bg_threshold
inputs.description: The 'bg_threshold' parameter sets the threshold for background separation, aiding in distinguishing between foreground and background elements in the depth map.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: The 'resolution' parameter specifies the resolution at which the depth map should be generated, affecting the detail and quality of the output.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is an image representing the depth map, where pixel intensity corresponds to the estimated depth from the camera perspective.

MiDaS-NormalMapPreprocessor.description: The MiDaS-NormalMapPreprocessor node is designed for generating normal maps from images using the MiDaS model. It preprocesses images to enhance depth estimation, facilitating the creation of detailed normal maps that can be used for various applications such as 3D modeling and augmented reality.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The 'image' parameter is the input image for which the normal map will be generated, serving as the basis for depth estimation and normal map creation.

inputs.name: a
inputs.description: The 'a' parameter adjusts the intensity of the depth estimation, influencing the contrast and detail in the generated normal map.

inputs.name: bg_threshold
inputs.description: The 'bg_threshold' parameter sets the threshold for background separation, helping to isolate the subject from the background in the depth estimation process.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: The 'resolution' parameter specifies the resolution at which the depth estimation and normal map generation will be performed, affecting the detail level of the output.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is an image representing the normal map generated from the input image, providing detailed surface orientation information.

OneFormer-ADE20K-SemSegPreprocessor.description: This node is designed for semantic segmentation tasks using the OneFormer model pre-trained on the ADE20K dataset. It processes images to segment them semantically, identifying and categorizing each pixel into a predefined class based on the ADE20K dataset.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be semantically segmented. This image is processed by the OneFormer model to identify and categorize each pixel.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: The resolution to which the input image is resized before processing. This affects the detail level of the segmentation output.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output of the semantic segmentation process. It is an image where each pixel is categorized into a class based on the ADE20K dataset.

OneFormer-COCO-SemSegPreprocessor.description: This node utilizes a pre-trained OneFormer model specifically trained on the COCO dataset to perform semantic segmentation on images. It aims to identify and delineate each semantic object within an image, enhancing the understanding of its content at a pixel level.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be semantically segmented. This parameter is crucial as it directly influences the segmentation output, determining the objects and their boundaries within the image.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: Specifies the resolution to which the input image is resized before segmentation. This parameter affects the detail level of the segmentation output, with higher resolutions potentially leading to more precise segmentations.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output of the semantic segmentation process, represented as an image where each pixel's value corresponds to a semantic class.

OpenposePreprocessor.description: The OpenPose Preprocessor node is designed for estimating human poses from images. It leverages the OpenPose model to detect and annotate various keypoints on the human body, face, and hands, providing a comprehensive pose estimation.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image for pose estimation. This is the primary data on which the pose detection algorithms operate.

inputs.name: detect_hand
inputs.description: Determines whether hand keypoints should be detected in the pose estimation process. Enabling this option allows for detailed hand pose analysis.

inputs.name: detect_body
inputs.description: Controls the detection of body keypoints in the pose estimation. Enabling this feature enables the analysis of overall body posture and movements.

inputs.name: detect_face
inputs.description: Specifies whether facial keypoints should be detected, enabling detailed facial expressions and orientation analysis in the pose estimation.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: The resolution to which the input image is resized before processing. Higher resolutions may improve detection accuracy at the cost of increased computational load.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image with annotated keypoints, visually representing the pose estimation.

outputs.name: pose_keypoint
outputs.description: A dictionary containing the detected keypoints for body, face, and hands, enabling detailed pose analysis.

PiDiNetPreprocessor.description: The PiDiNetPreprocessor node is designed for preprocessing images to extract soft-edge lines, utilizing the PiDiNet model. It aims to enhance image analysis and processing tasks by providing a refined input for further processing or analysis.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed for soft-edge line extraction. It's the primary data the node operates on, aiming to enhance its features for subsequent analysis.

inputs.name: safe
inputs.description: A mode selector that determines whether to perform the operation in a safe mode. Enabling 'safe' mode ensures that the preprocessing adheres to safety constraints, potentially affecting the output's fidelity and detail in favor of reducing risks during processing.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: Specifies the resolution at which the image should be processed. A higher resolution leads to more detailed extraction of soft-edge lines, while a lower resolution might speed up the process at the cost of detail.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The processed image with extracted soft-edge lines, ready for further analysis or processing steps.

PixelPerfectResolution.description: The PixelPerfectResolution node is designed to calculate the optimal resolution for resizing an image to achieve pixel-perfect clarity. It considers the original and target dimensions of the image, along with the specified resizing mode, to compute the most suitable resolution that maintains the image's visual integrity.

inputs.name: original_image
inputs.description: The original image to be resized. It's crucial for determining the base dimensions before applying the resizing operation.

inputs.name: image_gen_width
inputs.description: The target width for the image generation. It influences the scaling factor and the final resolution calculation.

inputs.name: image_gen_height
inputs.description: The target height for the image generation. Similar to image_gen_width, it affects the scaling factor and the final resolution outcome.

inputs.name: resize_mode
inputs.description: Specifies the mode of resizing (e.g., OUTER_FIT, INNER_FIT) which directly impacts how the final resolution is computed.

outputs.name: RESOLUTION (INT)
outputs.description: The computed optimal resolution for resizing the image, ensuring pixel-perfect clarity.

RenderAnimalKps.description: The RenderAnimalKps node is designed to process pose keypoints data for animals, converting it into a visual representation. It decodes the input keypoints, applies pose rendering to generate an image of the animal's pose, and returns the image as a numpy array.

inputs.name: kps
inputs.description: The 'kps' parameter represents the pose keypoints data for an animal. It is crucial for rendering the visual representation of the animal's pose, as it contains the spatial information needed to accurately depict the pose.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is an image representation of the animal's pose, provided as a numpy array.

RenderPeopleKps.description: This node is designed for rendering human pose keypoints into images. It processes pose keypoints data, applying options to render body, hand, and face details, and outputs the rendered image as a numpy array.

inputs.name: kps
inputs.description: The pose keypoints data to be rendered. It is crucial for determining the positions and orientations of different body parts in the rendered image.

inputs.name: render_body
inputs.description: A boolean flag to indicate whether to render the body keypoints. It affects the visual representation of the body in the output image.

inputs.name: render_hand
inputs.description: A boolean flag to indicate whether to render the hand keypoints. It influences the inclusion of hand details in the rendered image.

inputs.name: render_face
inputs.description: A boolean flag to indicate whether to render the face keypoints. It determines the depiction of facial features in the output image.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is a rendered image of human pose keypoints, represented as a numpy array.

SAMPreprocessor.description: The SAMPreprocessor node is designed to segment images using the SAM (Segment Anything Model) method. It preprocesses images to enhance them for further processing or analysis, specifically focusing on segmentation tasks.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be segmented. This is the primary data the SAMPreprocessor operates on, aiming to identify and segment various elements within.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: Specifies the resolution to which the input image should be resized before processing. This parameter can influence the segmentation accuracy and performance.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is a segmented version of the input image, where different segments are identified and separated.

SavePoseKpsAsJsonFile.description: This node is designed to save pose keypoints data as a JSON file. It takes pose keypoints and an optional filename prefix as inputs, appending a unique identifier to the filename before saving. This functionality is crucial for persisting pose data for further analysis or processing.

inputs.name: pose_kps
inputs.description: The pose keypoints to be saved. This data is essential for capturing the spatial positions of various body parts in an image or a sequence of images.

inputs.name: filename_prefix
inputs.description: An optional prefix for the filename under which the pose keypoints will be saved. This allows for easier identification and organization of saved files.

ScribblePreprocessor.description: The ScribblePreprocessor node is designed for preprocessing images to detect scribble lines. It utilizes a specific model to analyze and process the input image, aiming to highlight or extract scribble-like patterns.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed for scribble line detection. This parameter is crucial as it provides the visual data on which the scribble detection model operates.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: Specifies the resolution to which the input image is resized before processing. This affects the detail level of the scribble line detection.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The processed image with scribble lines detected or highlighted. This output is useful for further processing or visualization of scribble patterns.

Scribble_PiDiNet_Preprocessor.description: This node preprocesses images to extract scribble lines using the PiDiNet model, enhancing them for further processing or visualization. It focuses on generating clear, scribble-like lines from input images, making it suitable for applications requiring stylized line drawings or sketches.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed for scribble line extraction.

inputs.name: safe
inputs.description: A mode that, when enabled, applies additional safety checks or constraints during the processing to ensure robustness.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: The resolution to which the input image is scaled before processing. This affects the detail level of the extracted lines.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The processed image with enhanced scribble lines, suitable for visualization or further processing.

Scribble_XDoG_Preprocessor.description: The Scribble_XDoG_Preprocessor node is designed for extracting stylized line drawings from images using a combination of scribble detection and XDoG (eXtended Difference of Gaussians) filtering techniques. It preprocesses images to highlight important edges and details, making them suitable for further artistic or analytical processing.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed for line extraction. It serves as the primary data for the node to apply scribble detection and XDoG filtering techniques.

inputs.name: threshold
inputs.description: Determines the sensitivity of the XDoG filter in detecting edges. A lower threshold value results in finer details being captured, while a higher value emphasizes more prominent edges.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: Specifies the resolution at which the image should be processed. It affects the level of detail captured in the extracted lines.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is a processed image with stylized line drawings, emphasizing edges and details extracted using the Scribble_XDoG technique.

SemSegPreprocessor.description: The SemSegPreprocessor node is designed for preprocessing images for semantic segmentation tasks. It utilizes the UniFormer model to perform semantic segmentation, transforming input images into segmented outputs that categorize each pixel according to its semantic class. This node serves as a crucial step in preparing images for further analysis or model training within the domain of semantic segmentation.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed for semantic segmentation. This parameter is crucial as it represents the raw data that will be transformed into a semantically segmented image, enabling further analysis or model training.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: Specifies the resolution to which the input image is resized before semantic segmentation. This parameter affects the granularity of the segmentation output, with higher resolutions potentially leading to more detailed segmentations.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output of the semantic segmentation process. This is a segmented version of the input image, where each pixel is categorized according to its semantic class.

ShufflePreprocessor.description: The ShufflePreprocessor node is designed to preprocess images by applying a content shuffle detection algorithm. This preprocessing step is crucial for tasks that require the identification or manipulation of shuffled content within images, enhancing the model's ability to recognize and handle such patterns effectively.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed. It is the primary data on which the content shuffle detection algorithm is applied.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: Specifies the resolution to which the input image is resized before processing. This parameter can influence the detection accuracy and performance.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: A seed value for random number generation, ensuring reproducibility of the shuffle detection process.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The processed image after applying the content shuffle detection algorithm. It represents the detected shuffled content within the original image.

TEEDPreprocessor.description: The TEEDPreprocessor node is designed for preprocessing images to extract soft-edge lines using the TEED (TEDDetector) model. It enhances the input image by applying a specialized line extraction technique, making it suitable for further processing or analysis.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed for soft-edge line extraction.

inputs.name: safe_steps
inputs.description: Defines the number of safe steps to take during the line extraction process, affecting the robustness and sensitivity of the detection.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: Specifies the resolution at which the image should be processed, impacting the detail level of the extracted lines.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is an image that has undergone line extraction to highlight soft edges, making it more suitable for tasks requiring detailed line information.

TilePreprocessor.description: The TilePreprocessor node is designed for preprocessing images to enhance or modify their features for better analysis or further processing. It specifically focuses on manipulating the image's resolution and structure through pyramid upscaling iterations, making it suitable for tasks that require refined image details.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed. It serves as the primary data for the node's operation, influencing the outcome of the preprocessing.

inputs.name: pyrUp_iters
inputs.description: Specifies the number of pyramid upscaling iterations to apply to the image. This parameter directly affects the level of detail enhancement in the processed image.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: Defines the target resolution for the image after processing. This parameter helps in adjusting the image's size and detail level to suit specific requirements.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The processed image after pyramid upscaling iterations. It reflects the modifications made to the original image, with potentially enhanced detail and resolution.

TTPlanet_TileGF_Preprocessor.description: This node preprocesses images for tile detection by applying a guided filter technique, enhancing the image's features relevant for tile detection. It adjusts the image based on scale factor, blur strength, radius, and epsilon values to prepare it for further processing or analysis.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed. It is the primary data on which the guided filter and other preprocessing steps are applied.

inputs.name: scale_factor
inputs.description: Determines the scaling of the image, affecting its resolution and the granularity of details to be preserved or enhanced.

inputs.name: blur_strength
inputs.description: Controls the intensity of the blur applied to the image, which can help in reducing noise and improving the effectiveness of the guided filter.

inputs.name: radius
inputs.description: Specifies the radius of the guided filter, influencing the size of the local region around each pixel considered during filtering.

inputs.name: eps
inputs.description: Epsilon value for the guided filter, determining the degree of smoothing and edge preservation.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The processed image, enhanced and ready for further tile detection steps.

TTPlanet_TileSimple_Preprocessor.description: This node is designed for preprocessing images by applying a simple tiling effect, which involves scaling and blurring to enhance or modify the image's appearance for further processing or analysis.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed. It serves as the primary data for the tiling effect application.

inputs.name: scale_factor
inputs.description: Determines the scaling factor for the image, affecting the size of the tiles in the processed image.

inputs.name: blur_strength
inputs.description: Adjusts the strength of the blur applied to the image, influencing the smoothness of the tile edges.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The processed image with the applied tiling effect, ready for further processing or analysis.

UniFormer-SemSegPreprocessor.description: The UniFormer-SemSegPreprocessor node is designed for semantic segmentation tasks within the ControlNet Preprocessors/Semantic Segmentation category. It utilizes the UniformerSegmentor model to process images, aiming to understand and segment them into different semantic regions based on learned representations.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be semantically segmented. This parameter is crucial as it is the primary data the model operates on to perform segmentation.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: Specifies the resolution to which the input image is resized before processing. This affects the detail level of the segmentation output.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output of the semantic segmentation process, which is an image segmented into different semantic regions.

Unimatch_OptFlowPreprocessor.description: This node is designed to preprocess optical flow data for further processing or analysis, specifically within the context of Unimatch, a system for estimating and manipulating optical flows in video sequences. It abstracts the complexities involved in preparing optical flow data, ensuring it is in the correct format and resolution for Unimatch's algorithms to operate effectively.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The sequence of images to be processed for optical flow estimation. This input is essential for generating optical flow data between consecutive frames in a video sequence, serving as the foundation for flow analysis or manipulation.

inputs.name: ckpt_name
inputs.description: The name of the checkpoint file for the Unimatch model. This parameter allows for the selection of specific pre-trained models, influencing the accuracy and quality of the optical flow estimation.

inputs.name: backward_flow
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether to estimate the backward optical flow. This option enables bidirectional flow estimation, enhancing the analysis of motion between frames.

inputs.name: bidirectional_flow
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether to estimate bidirectional flow. This enhances the motion analysis by considering both forward and backward movements between frames.

outputs.name: OPTICAL_FLOW
outputs.description: The preprocessed optical flow data, ready for further analysis or visualization. This output is optimized for accuracy and efficiency in subsequent processing steps.

outputs.name: PREVIEW_IMAGE
outputs.description: A visual representation of the optical flow data, often used for previewing the motion or for debugging purposes. This image can help in understanding the flow's characteristics and in verifying the preprocessing's effectiveness.

UpperBodyTrackingFromPoseKps.description: This node is designed to process pose keypoints for upper body tracking, extracting and formatting specific body parts such as the torso, arms, and face from pose detection results. It enhances the keypoints data by appending additional points for completeness and accuracy, particularly for facial features, and compiles the results into structured pose results for further analysis or visualization.

inputs.name: pose_kps
inputs.description: The input pose keypoints, which are essential for identifying and tracking the upper body parts in images or video frames. This data includes body, hands, and face keypoints along with their scores.

inputs.name: id_include
inputs.description: An optional string to include specific IDs in the tracking process, allowing for targeted analysis of pose keypoints.

inputs.name: Head_width_height
inputs.description: Specifies the width and height for the head part, used in calculating dimensions for tracking.

inputs.name: Neck_width_height
inputs.description: Specifies the width and height for the neck part, used in calculating dimensions for tracking.

inputs.name: Shoulder_width_height
inputs.description: Specifies the width and height for the shoulder part, used in calculating dimensions for tracking.

inputs.name: Torso_width_height
inputs.description: Specifies the width and height for the torso part, used in calculating dimensions for tracking.

inputs.name: RArm_width_height
inputs.description: Specifies the width and height for the right arm part, used in calculating dimensions for tracking.

inputs.name: RForearm_width_height
inputs.description: Specifies the width and height for the right forearm part, used in calculating dimensions for tracking.

inputs.name: LArm_width_height
inputs.description: Specifies the width and height for the left arm part, used in calculating dimensions for tracking.

inputs.name: LForearm_width_height
inputs.description: Specifies the width and height for the left forearm part, used in calculating dimensions for tracking.

outputs.name: tracking
outputs.description: Structured data representing the tracking of upper body parts, including detailed information about body keypoints, hands, and face, along with their respective scores.

outputs.name: prompt
outputs.description: A textual prompt or summary generated based on the tracking results, providing insights or conclusions from the analysis.

Zoe-DepthMapPreprocessor.description: This node is designed to preprocess images for depth map estimation using the Zoe Detector model. It adjusts the input image's resolution and processes it through the model to generate a depth map, which can be utilized for various applications such as 3D modeling and scene understanding.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed for depth map estimation. This image is the primary input for the Zoe Detector model to analyze and generate the corresponding depth map.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: Specifies the resolution to which the input image should be resized before processing. This parameter allows for standardizing the input size for consistent depth map estimation across different images.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output depth map generated from the input image. This depth map provides a per-pixel estimation of depth, useful for understanding the scene's spatial layout.

Zoe_DepthAnythingPreprocessor.description: This node preprocesses images for depth estimation by selecting and applying a depth estimation model based on the specified environment (indoor or outdoor). It leverages the ZoeDepthAnythingDetector model to generate depth maps, enhancing the understanding of spatial relationships in images.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed for depth estimation.

inputs.name: environment
inputs.description: Determines the choice of pretrained model for depth estimation, selecting between indoor and outdoor environments to optimize depth map accuracy.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: Specifies the resolution at which the depth estimation should be performed. Affects the output depth map's resolution.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is a depth map of the input image, providing a pixel-wise estimation of depth values.

ImageDirIterator.description: The ImageDirIterator node is designed to iterate through images in a specified directory, providing functionality to access and manipulate image files based on directory structure and file properties. This node is likely to facilitate operations such as image retrieval, sorting, and processing, aiming to streamline workflows that involve handling multiple images stored in a directory.

inputs.name: directory_path
inputs.description: Specifies the path to the directory containing images. This path is used to locate and iterate through the image files for processing.

inputs.name: image_index
inputs.description: An index to specify which image to retrieve from the sorted list of images in the directory. This allows for sequential or specific access to images.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The image retrieved from the directory at the specified index, processed and returned as a tensor.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The filename of the retrieved image, without its extension, providing a means to identify or reference the image.

Modelscopet2v.description: The Modelscopet2v node is designed for transforming text inputs into visual outputs, leveraging advanced models to interpret and visualize textual descriptions in a visual format. This node encapsulates the process of text-to-visual conversion, enabling the creation of images or visual representations based on textual input.

inputs.name: prompt
inputs.description: The 'prompt' parameter specifies the textual input that describes the desired visual output. It plays a key role in guiding the model towards generating images that align with the given description, directly influencing the thematic and stylistic aspects of the generated visual content.

inputs.name: negative_prompt
inputs.description: The 'negative_prompt' parameter provides textual input that describes undesired aspects of the visual output. It helps in refining the generated images by steering the model away from unwanted characteristics, thus fine-tuning the final visual representation.

inputs.name: model_path
inputs.description: Specifies the path to the model used for generating visual content. This parameter allows for the selection of different models, potentially offering various styles or capabilities.

inputs.name: num_inference_steps
inputs.description: Determines the number of steps the model will take during the inference process. A higher number of steps can lead to more detailed and coherent visual outputs.

inputs.name: guidance_scale
inputs.description: Controls the degree to which the model adheres to the prompt. A higher guidance scale can result in images that more closely match the provided description.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: Sets the random seed for generating visual content, ensuring reproducibility of results.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Specifies the width of the generated visual content in pixels.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Specifies the height of the generated visual content in pixels.

inputs.name: num_frames
inputs.description: Determines the number of frames to be generated for video content, defining the length of the output video.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: This output represents the generated visual content based on the textual descriptions provided as input. It encapsulates the text-to-visual conversion logic, producing images or video frames.

Modelscopev2v.description: The Modelscopev2v node is designed to transform visual content from one domain to another, leveraging advanced models to understand and manipulate visual data at a high level. It focuses on enabling complex visual transformations and enhancements, making it suitable for tasks that require deep understanding and modification of visual information.

inputs.name: video_frames
inputs.description: Specifies the video frames to be transformed. Essential for defining the visual content that will undergo transformation.

inputs.name: prompt
inputs.description: A textual description of the desired transformation or outcome, guiding the model's understanding and manipulation of the visual content.

inputs.name: negative_prompt
inputs.description: A textual description of undesired elements or outcomes, helping to steer the model away from certain transformations.

inputs.name: model_path
inputs.description: The path to the model used for the transformation, determining the specific capabilities and characteristics of the transformation process.

inputs.name: strength
inputs.description: Controls the intensity of the transformation, allowing for fine-tuning of the visual output's adherence to the prompt.

inputs.name: num_inference_steps
inputs.description: Determines the number of steps the model takes to perform the transformation, affecting the quality and detail of the output.

inputs.name: guidance_scale
inputs.description: Adjusts the influence of the prompt on the transformation, balancing between fidelity to the prompt and the original content.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: A seed value for random number generation, ensuring reproducibility of the transformation.

inputs.name: enable_forward_chunking
inputs.description: Enables or disables forward chunking, potentially improving performance for large video frames.

inputs.name: enable_vae_slicing
inputs.description: Enables or disables VAE slicing, which can affect the model's efficiency and output quality.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The transformed video frames, representing the visual content after undergoing the specified transformation.

RemapRange.description: The RemapRange node is designed to adjust a given value from one range to another, optionally clamping the output within the target range. This functionality is essential for normalizing data or adapting values to fit within specific bounds, making it a versatile tool for data preprocessing and transformation.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: Specifies the value to be remapped. Its role is crucial as it determines the base value that will undergo transformation according to the specified input and output ranges.

inputs.name: input_min
inputs.description: Defines the lower bound of the original range. It sets the starting point from which the value will be scaled.

inputs.name: input_max
inputs.description: Sets the upper limit of the original range. This parameter, in conjunction with input_min, establishes the range within which the value currently resides.

inputs.name: output_min
inputs.description: Determines the lower boundary of the target range. It marks the minimum value to which the original value can be scaled.

inputs.name: output_max
inputs.description: Specifies the upper boundary of the target range. This parameter defines the maximum potential value after remapping.

inputs.name: clamp
inputs.description: A boolean flag that, when true, clamps the remapped value within the output range, ensuring it does not exceed the specified bounds.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The result of the remapping process. It represents the original value adjusted to fit within the new specified range.

TextFileLineIterator.description: The TextFileLineIterator node is designed to read and return a specific line from a text file, based on a given line index. It abstracts the process of file handling, reading, and line selection, making it easier to extract text data programmatically.

inputs.name: file_path
inputs.description: Specifies the path to the text file from which a line will be read. It is crucial for locating and accessing the file's content.

inputs.name: line_index
inputs.description: Determines the index of the line to be retrieved from the text file. The index is wrapped around using modulo to ensure it falls within the file's line count, allowing cyclic access.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: Returns the text of the specified line from the text file, stripped of any surrounding whitespace.

VidDirIterator.description: The VidDirIterator node is designed to navigate through directories containing video files, allowing for the retrieval of video file paths based on their index. This functionality facilitates the organization and selection of video content within a specified directory, streamlining the process of accessing and utilizing video files in various applications.

inputs.name: directory_path
inputs.description: Specifies the path to the directory containing video files. This path is crucial for the node to locate and list the video files for further operations.

inputs.name: video_index
inputs.description: Determines the index of the video file to retrieve from the sorted list of video files in the directory. This index is used to select a specific video file, enabling targeted access to video content.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: Returns the path to the video file at the specified index within the directory. This output facilitates direct access to the selected video file for further processing or playback.

ArgosTranslateCLIPTextEncodeNode.description: This node is designed for translating text from one language to another and encoding the translated text using the CLIP model for further processing or conditioning in AI models. It supports a variety of languages and leverages the CLIP model to provide a rich, contextual representation of the translated text.

inputs.name: from_translate
inputs.description: Specifies the source language from which the text will be translated. It determines the starting point of the translation process.

inputs.name: to_translate
inputs.description: Defines the target language to which the text will be translated. It affects the final output of the translation process by setting the desired language.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The text to be translated. This input is crucial as it provides the content that will undergo translation and subsequent encoding.

inputs.name: clip
inputs.description: A CLIP model instance used for encoding the translated text. It plays a key role in generating contextual embeddings for the text.

outputs.name: conditioning
outputs.description: Provides the conditioning information derived from the CLIP model's encoding of the translated text.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The translated text, serving as a direct output of the translation process.

ArgosTranslateTextNode.description: This node specializes in translating text from one language to another, leveraging the Argos Translate library. It modifies the input types inherited from its parent class to exclude the 'clip' parameter, focusing solely on text translation without the need for additional conditioning inputs.

inputs.name: from_translate
inputs.description: Specifies the source language code from which the text will be translated. It plays a crucial role in determining the translation process by identifying the original language of the input text.

inputs.name: to_translate
inputs.description: Defines the target language code to which the text will be translated. This parameter is essential for guiding the translation engine towards the desired output language.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The text to be translated. This parameter is central to the node's functionality, as it provides the content that will undergo the translation process.

outputs.name: text
outputs.description: The translated text. This output is the direct result of the translation process, providing users with text that has been converted from the source to the target language.

ColorsCorrectNode.description: The ColorsCorrectNode is designed for image color correction, allowing adjustments to brightness, contrast, saturation, gamma, and hue. It supports optional color tinting using a specified hex color value, providing a comprehensive suite of image enhancement tools.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be corrected. It serves as the base for all subsequent color and enhancement operations.

inputs.name: brightness
inputs.description: Adjusts the brightness of the image. A higher value increases brightness.

inputs.name: contrast
inputs.description: Adjusts the contrast of the image. A higher value increases contrast.

inputs.name: saturation
inputs.description: Adjusts the saturation of the image, enhancing or muting the colors.

inputs.name: gamma
inputs.description: Adjusts the gamma of the image, affecting the luminance of mid-tones.

inputs.name: hue_degrees
inputs.description: Adjusts the hue of the image in degrees. This shifts all colors in the image.

inputs.name: use_color
inputs.description: A boolean flag that determines whether to apply a color tint to the image based on the specified hex color.

inputs.name: hex_color
inputs.description: The hex color code used for tinting the image if use_color is True. It allows for custom color adjustments.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The corrected image after applying the specified adjustments.

DeepTranslatorCLIPTextEncodeNode.description: This node is designed to encode text inputs using a deep translation mechanism combined with CLIP text encoding, facilitating the translation of text into different languages before encoding it into a format suitable for conditioning models. It serves as a foundational component for nodes that require text translation and encoding capabilities for further processing or model conditioning.

inputs.name: from_translate
inputs.description: Specifies the source language of the text to be translated. It plays a crucial role in determining the initial language from which the text will be translated, affecting the accuracy and relevance of the translation.

inputs.name: to_translate
inputs.description: Defines the target language to which the text will be translated. This parameter is essential for guiding the translation process towards the desired language, impacting the final output's applicability for specific linguistic contexts.

inputs.name: add_proxies
inputs.description: Indicates whether proxies should be added to the translation request, enabling the bypass of potential network restrictions.

inputs.name: proxies
inputs.description: Specifies the proxy settings to be used if 'add_proxies' is true, facilitating the translation request through specified network paths.

inputs.name: auth_data
inputs.description: Authentication data required for accessing the translation service, ensuring secure and authorized translation requests.

inputs.name: service
inputs.description: The translation service to be used, such as 'GoogleTranslator' or another supported service, determining the translation mechanism and capabilities.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The text input to be translated and encoded. This parameter is central to the node's functionality, as it provides the raw content for translation and subsequent encoding.

inputs.name: clip
inputs.description: A CLIP model instance used for text encoding. It is crucial for converting the translated text into a format compatible with conditioning models, enhancing the text's utility for model inputs.

outputs.name: conditioning
