outputs.description: The encoded representation of the translated text, suitable for use as conditioning input in various models. It includes both the conditioning vectors and pooled output for comprehensive model conditioning.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The translated text, providing a direct linguistic output of the translation process. It serves as a readable representation of the text after translation, useful for verification or further processing.

DeepTranslatorTextNode.description: The DeepTranslatorTextNode is designed for advanced text translation tasks, leveraging deep learning models to enhance translation accuracy and support for multiple languages. It extends the capabilities of a standard translation node by incorporating deep learning techniques to improve the quality of translations, especially in complex or nuanced text scenarios.

inputs.name: from_translate
inputs.description: Specifies the source language from which the text will be translated, crucial for determining the translation context and accuracy.

inputs.name: to_translate
inputs.description: Specifies the target language to which the text will be translated, essential for ensuring the translation meets the desired linguistic and cultural nuances.

inputs.name: add_proxies
inputs.description: Indicates whether proxies should be added to the translation request, affecting the node's ability to bypass geo-restrictions or network limitations.

inputs.name: proxies
inputs.description: Provides proxy details for the translation request, enabling the node to operate in environments with restricted internet access.

inputs.name: auth_data
inputs.description: Contains authentication data required by certain translation services, ensuring secure access to premium translation features.

inputs.name: service
inputs.description: Specifies the translation service to be used, impacting the translation's quality, speed, and language support.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The text input to be translated, highlighting the node's core functionality in processing and translating textual content.

outputs.name: text
outputs.description: The translated text, demonstrating the node's ability to accurately convey the original message in a different language.

GoogleTranslateCLIPTextEncodeNode.description: This node leverages the Google Translate API to translate text from one language to another and then encodes the translated text using the CLIP model for further processing or analysis. It supports automatic language detection, manual translation control, and integrates CLIP's powerful text and image understanding capabilities to produce conditioning vectors and pooled outputs for downstream tasks.

inputs.name: from_translate
inputs.description: Specifies the source language for translation or 'auto' for automatic language detection. It plays a crucial role in guiding the translation process.

inputs.name: to_translate
inputs.description: Defines the target language for the translation, with 'en' (English) as the default. This parameter determines the language into which the text will be translated.

inputs.name: manual_translate
inputs.description: A boolean flag that, when set to True, bypasses the translation process and uses the original text for CLIP encoding. This allows for optional use of the translation feature.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The text to be translated and/or encoded. This is the primary input for the translation and encoding process.

inputs.name: clip
inputs.description: A CLIP model instance used for encoding the translated text into vectors. This enables the integration of text understanding and image recognition capabilities.

outputs.name: conditioning
outputs.description: A vector representation of the translated text, suitable for conditioning models or further analysis.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The translated text, providing the outcome of the translation process.

GoogleTranslateTextNode.description: This node is designed to translate text from one language to another, offering an option for manual translation bypass. It leverages the Google Translate API or a manual override to return the translated text, streamlining the process of language translation within workflows.

inputs.name: from_translate
inputs.description: Specifies the source language of the text to be translated, or 'auto' to automatically detect the language. This parameter is crucial for determining the starting point of translation.

inputs.name: to_translate
inputs.description: Defines the target language for the translation, guiding the node to convert the input text into the desired language.

inputs.name: manual_translate
inputs.description: A boolean flag that, when set to True, bypasses the translation process and returns the original text. This allows for optional manual control over the translation.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The text to be translated, serving as the primary input for the translation process.

outputs.name: text
outputs.description: The translated text, either through the Google Translate API or as manually inputted, depending on the manual_translate flag.

HexToHueNode.description: The HexToHueNode is designed to convert hexadecimal color values to their corresponding hue values, providing both the hue in degrees and normalized hue as outputs. It serves as a utility for color manipulation, enabling the transformation of color specifications from a web-friendly format to a format that can be used for more detailed color analysis and adjustments.

inputs.name: color_hex
inputs.description: The hexadecimal representation of a color, which the node converts into hue values. This input is essential for determining the specific color's hue characteristics.

outputs.name: string_hex
outputs.description: The original hexadecimal color value inputted to the node.

outputs.name: float_hue_degrees
outputs.description: The hue of the color in degrees, providing a measure of the color's position on the color wheel.

outputs.name: float_hue_norm
outputs.description: The normalized hue value, scaled between -0.5 and 0.5, offering a standardized measure of hue.

outputs.name: string_hue_degrees
outputs.description: The hue value in degrees, represented as a string.

outputs.name: string_hue_norm
outputs.description: The normalized hue value, represented as a string, for ease of use in contexts where a string format is preferred.

PainterNode.description: The PainterNode is designed to facilitate image processing and manipulation within a custom node environment. It enables the dynamic updating of images based on user input, supports asynchronous communication with a server for image updates, and manages node-specific settings for personalized image processing workflows.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The primary image input for processing. It serves as the base for any transformations or updates applied by the node.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: An optional list of images to be processed or updated. These images can be used for batch processing or as additional inputs for the node's operations.

inputs.name: update_node
inputs.description: A flag indicating whether the node should update its internal state based on the provided images. This affects how images are processed and integrated into the node's workflow.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The processed image after applying the node's operations, ready for further use or display.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: An optional mask generated during the image processing, which can be used for further image manipulation or analysis.

PoseNode.description: The PoseNode is designed to process images by converting them into a tensor format suitable for pose estimation tasks. It emphasizes the preparation of image data for further analysis or model inference, focusing on the transformation of images from their original format into a normalized tensor representation.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The 'image' parameter represents the name of the image file to be processed. It is crucial for locating and loading the image from a temporary directory, where it undergoes conversion and normalization for pose analysis.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is a tensor representation of the input image, prepared for pose estimation tasks. This tensor is normalized and ready for further processing or model inference.

PreviewTextNode.description: The PreviewTextNode is designed to generate a preview of text inputs, allowing users to visualize how their text will appear. It primarily serves as a user interface component within a larger system, enhancing the user experience by providing immediate feedback on text input.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The primary text input for which a preview is generated. It is essential for the node's operation, determining the content of the preview.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: unknown

ELLATextEncode.description: The ELLATextEncode node is designed for encoding text inputs using the ELLA model, incorporating an additional layer of processing through a T5 text embedder. This node aims to generate conditioned embeddings suitable for further processing or generation tasks, leveraging the capabilities of both ELLA and T5 models to enhance the text encoding process.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The 'text' input is the primary textual data for encoding. It plays a crucial role in determining the output embeddings by serving as the direct input for the T5 text embedder, which is then processed by the ELLA model.

inputs.name: sigma
inputs.description: The 'sigma' parameter specifies the timesteps for the ELLA model, affecting the temporal aspect of the encoding process. It influences how the ELLA model interprets the conditioning over time, thereby impacting the final embeddings.

inputs.name: ella
inputs.description: The 'ella' input provides the necessary ELLA model components, including the ELLA model itself and the T5 text embedder, for the text encoding process. It is essential for enabling the node to perform its encoding function.

outputs.name: conditioning
outputs.description: The output is a conditioned embedding, tailored for further generative tasks. It includes the embeddings from the ELLA model, enriched with additional information such as pooled output, designed to enhance downstream processing.

GetSigma.description: The GetSigma node is designed to calculate a specific sigma value based on a given model, sampler, scheduler, and step parameters. It abstracts the complexity of interacting with different samplers and schedulers to provide a straightforward way to obtain a sigma value, which is crucial for controlling the noise level in generative models.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model parameter specifies the generative model to be used for sigma calculation. It is crucial for determining the appropriate noise level based on the model's characteristics and configurations.

inputs.name: sampler_name
inputs.description: The sampler_name parameter identifies the specific sampling strategy to be employed. This choice affects how sigma values are computed and applied, tailoring the noise injection process to the selected sampler's methodology.

inputs.name: scheduler
inputs.description: The scheduler parameter determines the scheduling algorithm for adjusting noise levels throughout the generative process. It plays a key role in fine-tuning the progression of sigma values over specified steps.

inputs.name: steps
inputs.description: Specifies the total number of steps to consider for sigma calculation. It defines the scope within which the start and end steps are evaluated, impacting the final sigma value.

inputs.name: start_at_step
inputs.description: The starting step from which to begin calculating sigma. This parameter allows for flexibility in determining the initial noise level, influencing the early stages of the generative process.

inputs.name: end_at_step
inputs.description: The ending step at which to stop calculating sigma. It sets the final point for noise adjustment, affecting the outcome of the generative model's output.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: Returns the calculated sigma value, which is a measure of the noise level to be applied. This value is critical for controlling the generative process's fidelity and diversity.

LoadElla.description: The LoadElla node is designed to initialize and load the ELLA model along with a specified T5 model into the system, setting them up for further text encoding and processing tasks. It encapsulates the functionality to load model state dictionaries and configure the models for operation on the designated device and data type.

inputs.name: ella_model
inputs.description: Specifies the directory path to the ELLA model to be loaded. This path is crucial for locating and initializing the ELLA model for subsequent operations.

inputs.name: t5_model
inputs.description: Indicates the directory path to the T5 model to be loaded alongside ELLA. The T5 model is essential for text embedding processes that precede ELLA's conditioning tasks.

outputs.name: ella
outputs.description: Returns a dictionary containing the initialized ELLA and T5 models, ready for text encoding and processing tasks.

ApplyCLIPSeg+.description: This node applies CLIPSeg, a segmentation model, to an image based on a given prompt, threshold, and optional smoothing, dilation, and blurring parameters. It processes the image to segment it according to the semantics of the prompt, allowing for fine-tuned control over the segmentation output through post-processing steps.

inputs.name: clip_seg
inputs.description: A tuple containing the CLIPSeg processor and model, used for processing the image and prompt to generate segmentation masks.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be segmented. It is processed and segmented according to the given prompt and threshold.

inputs.name: prompt
inputs.description: The text prompt that guides the segmentation process, influencing the areas of the image to be segmented.

inputs.name: threshold
inputs.description: The threshold value for converting the model's output into a binary mask, determining the segmentation boundary.

inputs.name: smooth
inputs.description: An optional parameter for applying Gaussian blur to smooth the edges of the segmented areas, enhancing the visual quality.

inputs.name: dilate
inputs.description: An optional parameter for dilating the segmented areas, allowing for adjustments to the segmentation boundary.

inputs.name: blur
inputs.description: An optional parameter for further blurring the segmented areas, useful for creating softer edges.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The segmented output as a tensor, where each pixel's value indicates whether it belongs to the segment defined by the prompt.

BatchCount+.description: The `BatchCount` node is designed to calculate the total number of elements within a given batch. It supports various data structures such as tensors, dictionaries, and lists, adapting its counting mechanism based on the structure's characteristics to accurately determine the batch size.

inputs.name: batch
inputs.description: The `batch` parameter is the primary input for the node, representing the data collection whose size is to be determined. It plays a crucial role in the node's functionality by allowing it to adapt its counting mechanism to the input's structure.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: This output represents the total count of elements within the input batch, providing a single integer value as the result.

CLIPTextEncodeSDXL+.description: This node is designed to encode text inputs using a CLIP model, specifically tailored for the Stable Diffusion XL framework. It processes text inputs to generate conditioning vectors and pooled outputs that are optimized for image generation tasks, incorporating additional parameters such as aesthetic scores and dimensions to fine-tune the generated images.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Defines the width of the target image in pixels, affecting the aspect ratio and resolution of the generated image.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Sets the height of the target image in pixels, impacting the aspect ratio and resolution of the generated image.

inputs.name: size_cond_factor
inputs.description: Specifies the factor by which the dimensions of the target image are scaled, affecting the detail and scale of the generated image.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The text input to be encoded, serving as the basis for generating the conditioning vector and influencing the content of the generated image.

inputs.name: clip
inputs.description: The CLIP model used for text tokenization and encoding, central to generating the conditioning vectors.

outputs.name: conditioning
outputs.description: Outputs a conditioning vector and associated metadata, including the aesthetic score and image dimensions, tailored for image generation.

ConditioningCombineMultiple+.description: This node is designed to combine multiple conditioning inputs into a single conditioning output. It allows for the flexible integration of up to five separate conditioning inputs, making it ideal for scenarios where multiple conditioning factors need to be merged to guide the generation process effectively.

inputs.name: conditioning_i
inputs.description: unknown

outputs.name: conditioning
outputs.description: The resulting combined conditioning output, integrating up to five separate conditioning inputs into a single, cohesive conditioning factor.

ConsoleDebug+.description: The ConsoleDebug node is designed for debugging purposes, allowing users to print values to the console with an optional prefix. It facilitates the observation of data flow and values within a node network by providing a simple way to output information to the standard output in a visually distinguishable format.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: The primary data or value to be printed. This parameter is essential for the node's operation as it determines what information will be displayed in the console.

inputs.name: prefix
inputs.description: An optional string that precedes the printed value, helping to contextualize or label the output. Its default value is 'Value:'.

DebugTensorShape+.description: The DebugTensorShape node is designed for debugging purposes, specifically to inspect and print the shapes of tensors within a data structure. It recursively traverses through nested tensors, including those within dictionaries and lists, to collect and display their shapes, aiding in the understanding of data flow and structure in tensor-based computations.

inputs.name: tensor
inputs.description: The 'tensor' parameter is the primary input for the DebugTensorShape node. Its purpose is to enable the inspection of tensor shapes within complex data structures, facilitating debugging and analysis.

DrawText+.description: The DrawText+ node is designed to render text onto images with customizable options such as font, size, color, and alignment. It supports adding shadows to text, adjusting text position with offsets, and can work with existing images or create new ones based on text dimensions.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The text to be rendered. It can span multiple lines and affects the overall size and layout of the resulting image.

inputs.name: font
inputs.description: Specifies the font type used for rendering the text. The choice of font impacts the text's appearance and style.

inputs.name: size
inputs.description: Determines the font size for the text, directly influencing its visibility and fit within the image.

inputs.name: color
inputs.description: The color of the text, defined in a format that specifies its appearance on the image.

inputs.name: background_color
inputs.description: The background color of the image, which can be transparent or any solid color, setting the scene for the text.

inputs.name: shadow_distance
inputs.description: The distance of the shadow from the text, enabling a depth effect. A value of 0 means no shadow.

inputs.name: shadow_blur
inputs.description: The blur radius for the text shadow, contributing to the softness and spread of the shadow effect.

inputs.name: shadow_color
inputs.description: Color of the shadow, enhancing the text's readability or aesthetic appeal against the background.

inputs.name: horizontal_align
inputs.description: Alignment of the text horizontally within the image, affecting its placement relative to the image's width.

inputs.name: vertical_align
inputs.description: Vertical alignment of the text within the image, impacting its position relative to the image's height.

inputs.name: offset_x
inputs.description: Horizontal offset for the text position, allowing fine-tuning of its exact location on the image.

inputs.name: offset_y
inputs.description: Vertical offset for the text position, enabling precise adjustment of its placement.

inputs.name: img_composite
inputs.description: An optional existing image to render the text onto. If not provided, a new image is created based on text dimensions.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The final image with the rendered text and applied customizations, including background and shadow effects if specified.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: A mask representing the alpha channel of the final image, useful for further image processing or compositing.

GetImageSize+.description: The GetImageSize node is designed to extract the dimensions of an image, providing essential information such as width, height, and the number of channels or depth. This node is fundamental in image processing tasks where understanding the size and scale of images is crucial for further manipulations or analyses.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The 'image' parameter represents the input image from which the size information is to be extracted. It is crucial for determining the dimensions and depth of the image, which are essential for various image processing applications.

outputs.name: width
outputs.description: Represents the width of the input image.

outputs.name: height
outputs.description: Represents the height of the input image.

outputs.name: count
outputs.description: Represents the number of channels or depth of the input image.

ImageApplyLUT+.description: This node applies a Look-Up Table (LUT) to an image or a batch of images to modify their appearance based on the LUT's defined transformations. It supports optional gamma correction, clipping of LUT values, and blending the transformed image with the original based on a specified strength. This process allows for sophisticated color grading and image effect applications.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image or batch of images to which the LUT will be applied. This is the primary input that undergoes transformation.

inputs.name: lut_file
inputs.description: The filename of the Look-Up Table (LUT) to be applied. This determines the specific color transformation to be executed.

inputs.name: gamma_correction
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether gamma correction should be applied to the image before and after LUT application, enhancing the visual quality.

inputs.name: clip_values
inputs.description: A boolean flag that, when true, clips the LUT values to ensure they stay within the defined domain, preventing potential color distortion.

inputs.name: strength
inputs.description: A float value between 0 and 1 indicating the blend strength of the LUT-applied image with the original image, allowing for subtle to full application of the LUT effect.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The transformed image or batch of images after the LUT has been applied, optionally gamma-corrected and blended with the original based on the specified strength.

ImageBatchMultiple+.description: The node 'ImageBatchMultiple+' is designed to handle multiple images simultaneously, applying operations that involve combining, transforming, or otherwise processing these images in a batch-oriented manner. It abstracts the complexity of dealing with image dimensions and formats, providing a streamlined approach to batch image manipulation.

inputs.name: image_i
inputs.description: Specifies the input images to be processed. It is central to the node's operation, as it determines the images that will undergo manipulation.

inputs.name: method
inputs.description: Specifies the approach for resizing or manipulating the images, such as stretching or cropping, which affects the final appearance.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The manipulated images after processing according to the specified parameters.

ImageCASharpening+.description: The ImageCASharpening+ node applies contrast adaptive sharpening to images, enhancing their clarity and detail without significantly altering the overall composition. This process adjusts the sharpness of an image based on its local contrast, making it particularly effective for images that may appear soft or slightly out of focus.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be sharpened. This is the primary data upon which the contrast adaptive sharpening algorithm operates.

inputs.name: amount
inputs.description: A floating-point value that determines the intensity of the sharpening effect. Higher values result in more pronounced sharpening, allowing for fine-tuning based on the specific needs of the image or application.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image after applying contrast adaptive sharpening. This image will have enhanced sharpness and detail, particularly in areas of varying contrast.

ImageColorMatch+.description: This node is designed to adjust the colors of an image to match those of a reference image, utilizing color space conversions and histogram matching techniques to achieve a visually harmonious result. It leverages advanced image processing algorithms to ensure that the output image closely mirrors the color distribution and tone of the target, making it ideal for applications requiring color consistency across different images.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be color-matched. This image will undergo color space conversion and histogram matching to align its color profile with that of the reference image.

inputs.name: reference
inputs.description: The reference image whose color profile is to be matched. This image serves as the target for the color matching process, guiding the adjustments made to the input image.

inputs.name: color_space
inputs.description: The color space to be used for the color matching process. This determines how the colors are interpreted and adjusted during the matching operation.

inputs.name: factor
inputs.description: A factor that blends the matched image with the original input image to control the intensity of the color matching.

inputs.name: device
inputs.description: Specifies the device (CPU, GPU, or auto) on which the color matching operation is performed.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image after color matching. This image has been adjusted to closely match the color profile of the reference image, ensuring color consistency.

ImageCompositeFromMaskBatch+.description: This node is designed for image manipulation tasks, specifically for creating composite images from two source images based on a mask. It blends parts of the 'image_from' and 'image_to' images according to the mask, allowing for sophisticated image editing and composition techniques.

inputs.name: image_from
inputs.description: The source image from which pixels are taken when the mask is not applied. It plays a crucial role in determining the final composite image's appearance.

inputs.name: image_to
inputs.description: The target image to which pixels are added based on the mask. It significantly influences the outcome of the composite image.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: A binary or grayscale mask that determines how pixels from 'image_from' and 'image_to' are blended together. The mask's values dictate the blending process, affecting the composite image's visual result.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The resulting composite image, created by blending 'image_from' and 'image_to' according to the mask. It showcases the combined visual elements of both source images.

ImageCrop+.description: The ImageCrop+ node is designed for cropping images to a specified width and height starting from a given x and y coordinate. It allows for precise control over the portion of the image to be extracted, making it a fundamental tool for image manipulation and preprocessing tasks.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be cropped. This parameter is crucial as it defines the source image from which a specific region will be extracted.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Specifies the width of the cropped image. It determines how wide the resulting image will be after cropping.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Specifies the height of the cropped image. It determines the vertical size of the resulting image after cropping.

inputs.name: position
inputs.description: Defines the starting position for the crop operation, offering predefined options for alignment.

inputs.name: x_offset
inputs.description: The horizontal offset from the specified position for additional control over the cropping area.

inputs.name: y_offset
inputs.description: The vertical offset from the specified position for additional control over the cropping area.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: The cropped portion of the input image. This output is the direct result of the cropping operation, representing the specified region of the original image.

outputs.name: x
outputs.description: The x-coordinate of the top-left corner of the cropped image.

outputs.name: y
outputs.description: The y-coordinate of the top-left corner of the cropped image.

ImageDesaturate+.description: The ImageDesaturate node is designed for adjusting the saturation level of an image, allowing for partial to full desaturation based on a specified method and factor. It supports different methods of calculating grayscale values, enabling nuanced control over the desaturation process.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be desaturated. It serves as the primary data for the desaturation process.

inputs.name: factor
inputs.description: A value between 0 and 1 that determines the intensity of the desaturation effect. A factor of 1 results in full desaturation, while 0 leaves the image unchanged.

inputs.name: method
inputs.description: The method used to calculate the grayscale values during desaturation. Options include luminance (Rec.709), luminance (Rec.601), average, and lightness, each affecting the output image's appearance differently.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The desaturated image, with its saturation level adjusted according to the specified factor and method.

ImageEnhanceDifference+.description: This node is designed to enhance and highlight the differences between two images by applying a power transformation. It is useful for visualizing changes or discrepancies between two images in a more pronounced manner.

inputs.name: image1
inputs.description: The first image to compare. It serves as the baseline for the comparison.

inputs.name: image2
inputs.description: The second image to compare against the first. This image is adjusted to match the dimensions of the first image if necessary.

inputs.name: exponent
inputs.description: A factor that controls the intensity of the enhancement. Higher values increase the contrast of the differences.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The enhanced difference image, highlighting discrepancies between the input images.

ImageExpandBatch+.description: This node is designed to facilitate the manipulation of image batches within a graphical interface, specifically focusing on expanding a given batch of images. It abstracts the complexities involved in handling multiple images simultaneously, providing a streamlined approach to either augment the existing batch size or modify the batch in a way that accommodates additional image processing operations.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The primary image or batch of images to be expanded. This parameter is the basis for the expansion operation, determining the initial set of images to be modified or augmented.

inputs.name: size
inputs.description: Specifies the target size for the batch expansion. This could dictate the number of times the image(s) are repeated or the new size of the batch after expansion.

inputs.name: method
inputs.description: Defines the method of expansion, such as repeating the entire batch, repeating only the first or last image, or expanding the batch size in another specified manner.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is an expanded batch of images, modified according to the specified size and method. This facilitates further batch-level image processing or analysis.

ImageFlip+.description: The ImageFlip node provides functionality for flipping images along specified axes. It supports flipping images horizontally, vertically, or both, allowing for versatile image manipulation and orientation adjustments.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image to be flipped. This parameter is crucial for defining the visual content that will undergo the flipping transformation.

inputs.name: axis
inputs.description: Specifies the axis or axes along which the image will be flipped. Accepting values 'x', 'y', or 'xy', it determines the direction of the flip, affecting the final appearance of the image.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The flipped image. This output represents the visual result of applying the specified flip transformation to the input image.

ImageFromBatch+.description: This node is designed to extract a specific segment from a batch of images based on the starting index and the length of the segment desired. It enables selective retrieval of images from a larger batch, facilitating operations that require processing or analysis of subsets of image collections.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The batch of images from which a segment is to be extracted. It serves as the primary input for determining the subset of images to be processed.

inputs.name: start
inputs.description: The starting index from which the image segment extraction begins. It defines the initial position in the batch from which images are to be retrieved, allowing for targeted selection within the batch.

inputs.name: length
inputs.description: Specifies the number of images to extract from the batch, starting from the 'start' index. It determines the size of the image segment to be retrieved, enabling precise control over the subset size.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The extracted segment of images from the specified batch. This output facilitates further processing or analysis of the selected subset of images.

ImageHistogramMatch+.description: This node is designed to perform histogram matching on images, a process that adjusts the pixel values of an image so its histogram matches that of a reference image. This technique is useful for color correction and achieving consistent visual styles across different images.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image to be processed and adjusted to match the histogram of the reference image. It plays a pivotal role in the histogram matching operation, determining the final appearance of the adjusted image.

inputs.name: reference
inputs.description: The reference image providing the desired histogram distribution for the histogram matching process. It establishes the target histogram characteristics for the image adjustment.

inputs.name: method
inputs.description: Specifies the method to be used for histogram matching. This parameter allows for the selection between different histogram matching techniques, influencing the approach and potentially the quality of the result.

inputs.name: factor
inputs.description: A blending factor that determines the degree to which the matched histogram influences the final image, allowing for partial adjustments.

inputs.name: device
inputs.description: Indicates the computational device ('cpu', 'gpu', or 'auto') where the histogram matching process will be executed, affecting performance and resource utilization.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image after applying histogram matching, reflecting the adjusted pixel values to match the histogram of the reference image.

ImageListToBatch+.description: This node is designed to convert a list of images into a single batched tensor, ensuring that all images conform to the same dimensions through optional resizing and cropping. It's particularly useful for preparing a collection of images for batch processing in machine learning models, where uniform input sizes are often required.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The list of images to be batched together. Each image in the list is processed to match the dimensions of the first image, using bicubic upsampling and center cropping if necessary.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: A single tensor containing all input images batched together. This tensor is suitable for direct use in models that require batched input.

ImagePosterize+.description: The ImagePosterize node is designed for image processing tasks, specifically to posterize images. It simplifies the color palette of an image based on a threshold, effectively reducing the number of colors to create a stylized effect. This node operates on the principle of comparing pixel values against a threshold and adjusting them accordingly to achieve the posterization effect.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The 'image' parameter represents the input image to be posterized. It is crucial for defining the visual content that will undergo the posterization process.

inputs.name: threshold
inputs.description: The 'threshold' parameter determines the cutoff value for posterization. Pixels above this threshold will be treated differently from those below it, playing a key role in defining the posterization effect's intensity and appearance.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is a posterized version of the input image, where the color palette has been simplified according to the specified threshold.

ImagePreviewFromLatent+.description: This node is designed to generate a preview image from a given latent representation. It leverages specific decoding techniques to transform latent vectors into visual previews, facilitating a visual understanding of the latent space.

inputs.name: latent
inputs.description: The latent representation to be transformed into a preview image. This input is crucial for visualizing the encoded information in a human-interpretable format.

inputs.name: vae
inputs.description: The variational autoencoder model used for decoding the latent representation into an image.

inputs.name: tile_size
inputs.description: Specifies the size of the tiles used in the decoding process, affecting the resolution of the output image.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: An optional input image that can be used in conjunction with the latent representation for generating the preview.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: The generated preview image, offering a visual interpretation of the latent representation.

outputs.name: MASK
outputs.description: An optional mask that may be generated alongside the preview image, depending on the node's implementation.

outputs.name: width
outputs.description: The width of the generated preview image.

outputs.name: height
outputs.description: The height of the generated preview image.

ImageRandomTransform+.description: This node applies a series of random transformations to an image, including perspective distortion, rotation, color jitter (brightness, contrast, saturation, hue), horizontal flipping, and random cropping. These transformations introduce variability and can be used to augment images for training or to generate diverse variations of a given image.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be transformed. It serves as the base for applying the random transformations, affecting the visual appearance and geometry of the output image.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: A seed value for the random number generator to ensure reproducibility of the transformations applied to the image.

inputs.name: repeat
inputs.description: Specifies how many times the input image should be repeated before applying the transformations, effectively controlling the number of transformed images generated.

inputs.name: variation
inputs.description: A scalar that modulates the intensity of the transformations applied, influencing the degree of variation in the output images.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The transformed images, each having undergone a unique set of random transformations based on the specified parameters.

ImageRemoveAlpha+.description: This node is designed to process images by removing the alpha channel, effectively converting images with transparency into a standard RGB format. It ensures that images are compatible with operations or environments that do not support or require transparency.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image with a potential alpha channel. This parameter is crucial for the operation as it determines whether the alpha channel, if present, needs to be removed to convert the image into RGB format.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image after the alpha channel has been removed, provided in standard RGB format.

ImageRemoveBackground+.description: This node is designed for removing the background from images using the rembg library. It processes each image in the input, applies the background removal algorithm, and returns the foreground image along with a mask indicating the areas of the image that were kept.

inputs.name: rembg_session
inputs.description: The session object for the rembg library, used to manage settings and configurations for the background removal process.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image or images to have their background removed. The node supports batch processing of multiple images.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The foreground of the input image(s) after background removal, with the background areas made transparent or removed.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: A binary mask indicating the areas of the image that were kept during the background removal process.

ImageResize+.description: This node is designed for resizing images to a specified width and height, offering a straightforward way to adjust image dimensions for various applications. It abstracts the complexities of image processing, providing an easy-to-use interface for resizing operations.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be resized. This parameter is crucial as it determines the source image that will undergo the resizing process.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Specifies the desired width of the resized image. This parameter directly influences the output image's dimensions.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Specifies the desired height of the resized image. This parameter directly influences the output image's dimensions.

inputs.name: interpolation
inputs.description: Defines the method used for interpolating pixels in the resizing process, affecting the quality and appearance of the resized image.

inputs.name: method
inputs.description: Determines how the image is resized, influencing whether and how the aspect ratio is preserved or altered.

inputs.name: condition
inputs.description: Specifies under what conditions the resizing should occur, allowing for conditional resizing based on the original and target dimensions.

inputs.name: multiple_of
inputs.description: Ensures the dimensions of the resized image are multiples of this value, useful for certain processing or model input requirements.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: The resized image. This output reflects the changes in dimensions specified by the width and height parameters.

outputs.name: width
outputs.description: The actual width of the resized image, which may differ from the requested width due to constraints like maintaining aspect ratio or alignment to a multiple.

outputs.name: height
outputs.description: The actual height of the resized image, which may differ from the requested height due to constraints like maintaining aspect ratio or alignment to a multiple.

ImageSeamCarving+.description: This node specializes in dynamically resizing images while preserving the content's essential features, utilizing the seam carving technique. It intelligently removes or adds pixels in paths (seams) of least importance, allowing for aspect ratio changes, content amplification, or object removal without noticeable distortion.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed. It is the primary subject for seam carving, where the algorithm will apply modifications based on the specified parameters.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: The target width for the output image. This parameter dictates the new width the input image should be resized to, either by removing or adding seams.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: The target height for the output image. Similar to width, it determines the new height by adjusting the number of seams.

inputs.name: energy
inputs.description: Defines the energy calculation mode to identify seams. Higher energy values indicate areas of higher importance, guiding the seam carving process.

inputs.name: order
inputs.description: Specifies the order of seam removal or addition, which can be either width-first or height-first, influencing the direction of the carving process.

inputs.name: keep_mask
inputs.description: An optional mask to protect certain areas from being altered. Regions covered by the keep mask are treated as high importance, preserving them during seam carving.

inputs.name: drop_mask
inputs.description: An optional mask to designate areas for removal. The drop mask marks regions as less important, making them prime candidates for seam elimination.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image after seam carving. It reflects the specified dimensions and modifications while aiming to preserve the visual content's integrity.

ImageTile+.description: The ImageTile node is designed for slicing an image into smaller, overlapping or non-overlapping tiles based on specified rows and columns. This functionality is essential for processing large images in manageable segments or for extracting specific regions of interest with controlled overlap for detailed analysis or further manipulation.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be tiled. This parameter is crucial as it defines the source image from which tiles will be generated.

inputs.name: rows
inputs.description: Specifies the number of rows to divide the image into. This affects the vertical segmentation of the image, influencing the height of each tile.

inputs.name: cols
inputs.description: Determines the number of columns to divide the image into. This parameter influences the horizontal segmentation, affecting the width of each tile.

inputs.name: overlap
inputs.description: Defines the percentage of overlap between adjacent tiles. This parameter allows for a seamless transition between tiles, especially useful in certain analysis or reconstruction tasks.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output consists of a tensor containing the generated image tiles, ready for further processing or analysis.

ImageToDevice+.description: The ImageToDevice node is designed for transferring images to a specified computing device, such as GPU or CPU, within a deep learning environment. It supports dynamic device selection based on user input, enabling optimized computation by leveraging the appropriate hardware resources.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image to be transferred to the specified device. It plays a crucial role in ensuring that the image is processed on the correct hardware, affecting performance and efficiency.

inputs.name: device
inputs.description: Specifies the target device for the image transfer. It can be set to 'auto', 'cpu', or 'gpu', allowing for flexible execution across different hardware configurations.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The image after being transferred to the specified device, ready for further processing or analysis.

KSamplerVariationsStochastic+.description: This node specializes in generating stochastic variations of latent images using a specific sampling technique. It leverages randomness and a defined stochastic process to introduce variations, aiming to enhance the diversity of generated images while maintaining their core characteristics.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model parameter specifies the generative model used for sampling. It plays a crucial role in determining the quality and characteristics of the generated variations.

inputs.name: latent_image
inputs.description: The latent_image parameter represents the initial latent representation of an image. It serves as the starting point for generating variations, influencing the final outcome.

inputs.name: noise_seed
inputs.description: The noise_seed parameter controls the randomness of the variation noise. It ensures reproducibility of the variations by initializing the random noise generator.

inputs.name: steps
inputs.description: The steps parameter defines the number of sampling steps. It affects the degree of variation and the quality of the generated images.

inputs.name: cfg
inputs.description: The cfg parameter adjusts the conditioning factor, influencing the strength of the applied variations.

inputs.name: sampler
inputs.description: The sampler parameter selects the specific sampling algorithm used for generating variations.

inputs.name: scheduler
inputs.description: The scheduler parameter determines the scheduling algorithm for the sampling process, affecting the progression of variations.

inputs.name: positive
inputs.description: The positive parameter provides positive conditioning to guide the variation generation towards desired attributes.

inputs.name: negative
inputs.description: The negative parameter provides negative conditioning to steer the variation generation away from undesired attributes.

inputs.name: variation_seed
inputs.description: The variation_seed parameter specifically controls the randomness of the variation process, distinct from the initial noise seed.

inputs.name: variation_strength
inputs.description: The variation_strength parameter adjusts the intensity of the applied variations, affecting the distinctiveness of the generated images.

inputs.name: cfg_scale
inputs.description: The cfg_scale parameter scales the conditioning factor for the variation process, modifying the impact of conditioning on the variations.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: This output represents the latent image after applying stochastic variations, reflecting the enhanced diversity and creativity of the sampling process.

KSamplerVariationsWithNoise+.description: This node introduces a two-stage sampling process with noise injection to generate variations of an input latent image. Initially, it applies a composition sampler to the input, optionally adding or fully denoising the result based on the variation strength. Subsequently, it employs a variation sampler that further processes the output of the first stage, adjusting the configuration based on the variation strength and cfg scale, to produce diverse and nuanced variations of the original image.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model parameter specifies the generative model used for sampling, playing a crucial role in determining the characteristics and quality of the generated variations.

inputs.name: latent_image
inputs.description: The latent_image parameter represents the input latent representation of an image, serving as the starting point for the sampling process to generate variations.

inputs.name: main_seed
inputs.description: The main_seed parameter is used to initialize the random noise generation for the base noise, influencing the stochastic aspects of the sampling process.

inputs.name: steps
inputs.description: The steps parameter defines the number of sampling steps to be performed, affecting the detail and quality of the generated image variations.

inputs.name: cfg
inputs.description: The cfg parameter adjusts the conditioning factor, influencing the generation process by modulating the influence of the conditioning on the output.

inputs.name: sampler_name
inputs.description: The sampler_name parameter specifies the sampling strategy used in the first stage of the process, determining the approach for generating the initial variation.

inputs.name: scheduler
inputs.description: The scheduler parameter determines the scheduling strategy for the sampling process, affecting the progression of noise reduction and detail refinement.

inputs.name: positive
inputs.description: The positive parameter provides positive textual guidance for the sampling process, steering the generation towards desired attributes or themes.

inputs.name: negative
inputs.description: The negative parameter provides negative textual guidance, instructing the model to avoid certain attributes or themes in the generated variations.

inputs.name: variation_strength
inputs.description: The variation_strength parameter controls the degree of variation introduced between the two stages, affecting the diversity of the generated images.

inputs.name: variation_seed
inputs.description: The variation_seed parameter is used to seed the variation process in the second stage, ensuring reproducibility and control over the variation generation.

inputs.name: denoise
inputs.description: The denoise parameter determines the level of denoising applied during the sampling process, affecting the clarity and detail of the generated image variations.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The output latent represents the final varied latent representation of the image after the two-stage sampling process with noise injection.

LoadCLIPSegModels+.description: This node is designed to load the CLIPSeg models for image segmentation, specifically initializing and returning the CLIPSeg processor and model pre-trained on a specific dataset. It abstracts the complexity of model loading, providing an easy-to-use interface for obtaining the necessary components for CLIPSeg-based segmentation tasks.

outputs.name: clip_seg
outputs.description: The output is a tuple containing the CLIPSeg processor and model, ready for use in image segmentation tasks.

MaskBatch+.description: The MaskBatch+ node is designed for batch processing of mask images, specifically for combining two mask images into a single batch. It ensures compatibility between mask sizes through resizing operations if necessary, facilitating the integration of masks from different sources or dimensions into a unified batch format.

inputs.name: mask1
inputs.description: The first mask image to be combined into the batch. Its dimensions are checked against the second mask to ensure compatibility.

inputs.name: mask2
inputs.description: The second mask image to be combined with the first. If its dimensions differ from the first mask, it is resized to match, ensuring uniformity in the batch.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The combined batch of the two input masks, returned as a single tensor. This facilitates further processing or analysis of the masks as a unified entity.

MaskBlur+.description: The `MaskBlur+` node applies a Gaussian blur to a given mask, optionally adjusting the intensity of the blur and accommodating different computational devices. It's designed to smooth out the edges or details of a mask, which can be useful in various image processing tasks where softer transitions or less pronounced features are desired.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The mask to be blurred. This is the primary input on which the Gaussian blur operation is performed.

inputs.name: amount
inputs.description: Specifies the intensity of the blur. A higher value results in a more pronounced blurring effect.

inputs.name: device
inputs.description: Determines the computational device ('auto', 'cpu', or 'gpu') on which the blurring operation is executed, allowing for flexibility in resource utilization.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The blurred version of the input mask, with potentially softened features or transitions.

MaskBoundingBox+.description: This node is designed for processing masks to identify and extract bounding box coordinates, facilitating tasks that require spatial localization within images. It can be used for cropping, object detection, and area-specific processing, enhancing the utility of masks by providing precise location data.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The input mask for which the bounding box is to be computed, representing a specific area within an image. The node calculates the bounding box that tightly encloses this area, providing spatial localization.

inputs.name: padding
inputs.description: An optional parameter that specifies the amount of padding to add to the bounding box, allowing for adjustments to the size of the extracted area.

inputs.name: blur
inputs.description: An optional parameter that applies a blur to the mask before computing the bounding box, potentially smoothing the edges and affecting the final bounding box coordinates.

inputs.name: image_optional
inputs.description: An optional image input that, if provided, can be used in conjunction with the mask to refine the bounding box calculation based on the image content.

outputs.name: MASK
outputs.description: The mask adjusted to the bounding box, potentially including padding and modifications from the blur parameter.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: An optional output image cropped to the bounding box of the mask, provided if an image input was given.

outputs.name: x
outputs.description: The x-coordinate of the top-left corner of the bounding box.

outputs.name: y
outputs.description: The y-coordinate of the top-left corner of the bounding box.

outputs.name: width
outputs.description: The width of the bounding box.

outputs.name: height
outputs.description: The height of the bounding box.

MaskExpandBatch+.description: This node is designed to expand a given mask to a specified size using a chosen method, such as repeating or expanding the mask in various ways. It abstracts the complexity of manipulating mask dimensions and provides a straightforward way to adjust mask sizes for batch processing.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The mask input represents the initial mask that will be expanded. It is crucial for determining the base pattern or shape that will be manipulated according to the specified size and method.

inputs.name: size
inputs.description: The size parameter specifies the target size to which the mask will be expanded. It plays a key role in determining the final dimensions of the output mask.

inputs.name: method
inputs.description: The method parameter dictates the technique used to expand the mask, offering options like 'expand', 'repeat all', 'repeat first', and 'repeat last'. This choice significantly influences the pattern and distribution of the expanded mask.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The output is an expanded mask that has been adjusted to the specified size using the chosen method, suitable for further processing or application in batch operations.

MaskFix+.description: The MaskFix node is designed to correct or adjust masks within images, focusing on refining mask boundaries, shapes, or overall mask integrity. It aims to enhance the quality and accuracy of masks used in image processing tasks, ensuring they accurately represent the intended areas or objects.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The 'mask' parameter is the primary input for the MaskFix node, representing the mask to be corrected or adjusted. It plays a crucial role in determining the areas of the image that require refinement.

inputs.name: erode_dilate
inputs.description: Specifies the degree to which the mask should be eroded or dilated, affecting the mask's boundaries and overall shape.

inputs.name: fill_holes
inputs.description: Determines whether and to what extent holes within the mask should be filled, enhancing mask integrity.

inputs.name: remove_isolated_pixels
inputs.description: Controls the removal of isolated pixels, improving the mask's overall appearance and accuracy.

inputs.name: smooth
inputs.description: Adjusts the smoothness of the mask's edges, refining its boundaries for a more precise representation.

inputs.name: blur
inputs.description: Defines the level of blur applied to the mask, aiding in softening edges and improving visual quality.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The output is a refined or adjusted mask, improved in terms of boundary definition, shape, and overall integrity.

MaskFlip+.description: The MaskFlip+ node is designed for flipping masks along specified axes. It provides functionality to manipulate the orientation of mask data, allowing for horizontal, vertical, or both flips, enhancing flexibility in mask manipulation for various image processing tasks.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The 'mask' parameter represents the input mask to be flipped. It is crucial for determining the spatial data that will undergo orientation changes.

inputs.name: axis
inputs.description: The 'axis' parameter specifies the axes along which the mask will be flipped. It plays a key role in defining the direction of the flip operation, affecting the final output.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The output is a flipped version of the input mask, modified according to the specified axis or axes of flipping.

MaskFromBatch+.description: The MaskFromBatch+ node is designed for extracting a specific segment from a batch of masks based on the provided start index and length. It enables selective focus on particular portions of mask data for further processing or analysis.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The 'mask' parameter represents the batch of masks from which a segment will be extracted. It is crucial for specifying the data subset to be operated on.

inputs.name: start
inputs.description: The 'start' parameter determines the starting index from which the mask segment will be extracted, allowing for precise control over the selection of the data subset.

inputs.name: length
inputs.description: The 'length' parameter specifies the number of masks to be extracted from the batch, enabling the extraction of a specific range of data for focused analysis or processing.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: Returns a segment of the mask batch, extracted based on the specified start index and length, facilitating targeted manipulation or examination of mask data.

MaskFromColor+.description: This node generates a mask from an image based on specified color values and a threshold. It allows for the selective isolation of parts of an image that match the given color within a certain tolerance, enabling targeted image manipulation or analysis.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image from which the mask will be generated. It serves as the basis for identifying areas that match the specified color criteria.

inputs.name: red
inputs.description: The red component of the target color. It defines the red value that the node will use to generate the mask.

inputs.name: green
inputs.description: The green component of the target color. It defines the green value that the node will use to generate the mask.

inputs.name: blue
inputs.description: The blue component of the target color. It defines the blue value that the node will use to generate the mask.

inputs.name: threshold
inputs.description: The tolerance for color matching. It specifies how closely the colors in the image must match the target color to be included in the mask.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The output mask indicating areas of the image that match the specified color within the given threshold.

MaskFromList+.description: The MaskFromList+ node generates a mask based on a list of values, allowing for the creation of custom masks with specified dimensions and values. It supports both numerical and string inputs for mask values, providing flexibility in defining the mask's content.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Specifies the width of the generated mask. It determines the horizontal dimension of the mask.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Specifies the height of the generated mask. It determines the vertical dimension of the mask.

inputs.name: values
inputs.description: A list of numerical values (integers or floats) or a single numerical value used to populate the mask. This input allows for the customization of the mask's intensity or transparency.

inputs.name: str_values
inputs.description: A string representation of numerical values, separated by commas, used to populate the mask. This provides an alternative method for defining the mask's content.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The output is a mask created from the provided list of values, with the specified dimensions and value intensities.

MaskFromRGBCMYBW+.description: The MaskFromRGBCMYBW node is designed to generate masks based on specific RGB, CMY, and BW (black and white) thresholds applied to an input image. It allows for the creation of multiple masks corresponding to the primary and secondary colors, as well as black and white, based on the defined thresholds, enabling precise control over color-based segmentation for various image processing tasks.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed for mask generation based on RGB, CMY, and BW thresholds.

inputs.name: threshold_r
inputs.description: The threshold value for the red component, used to determine the boundaries for red, cyan, magenta, and black/white masks.

inputs.name: threshold_g
inputs.description: The threshold value for the green component, used to determine the boundaries for green, cyan, yellow, and black/white masks.

inputs.name: threshold_b
inputs.description: The threshold value for the blue component, used to determine the boundaries for blue, magenta, yellow, and black/white masks.

outputs.name: red
outputs.description: The mask generated for the red color based on the threshold.

outputs.name: green
outputs.description: The mask generated for the green color based on the threshold.

outputs.name: blue
outputs.description: The mask generated for the blue color based on the threshold.

outputs.name: cyan
outputs.description: The mask generated for the cyan color based on the threshold.

outputs.name: magenta
outputs.description: The mask generated for the magenta color based on the threshold.

outputs.name: yellow
outputs.description: The mask generated for the yellow color based on the threshold.

outputs.name: black
outputs.description: The mask generated for black based on the threshold.

outputs.name: white
outputs.description: The mask generated for white based on the threshold.

MaskFromSegmentation+.description: This node is designed to generate masks from image segmentation, effectively converting segmented areas into distinct mask layers. It allows for advanced image editing and manipulation by isolating specific segments of an image for targeted operations.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be segmented into masks. It serves as the basis for generating distinct mask layers for each segmented area.

inputs.name: segments
inputs.description: The number of segments to divide the image into. This parameter controls the granularity of the segmentation, with higher values resulting in more detailed masks.

inputs.name: remove_isolated_pixels
inputs.description: A threshold for removing isolated pixels within a mask to clean up noise and improve mask quality.

inputs.name: remove_small_masks
inputs.description: A threshold for removing small masks deemed to be noise, ensuring only significant segments are retained.

inputs.name: fill_holes
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether to fill holes within the generated masks, enhancing their completeness and usability.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The output consists of a stack of masks corresponding to the segmented areas of the input image, ready for further processing or application.

MaskPreview+.description: The MaskPreview node is designed for generating a preview image from a given mask. It reshapes and expands the mask to fit the image format, then saves the resulting image with a specified prefix, optionally incorporating additional PNG metadata and a prompt.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The mask input is the primary data used for generating the preview image. It dictates the shape and content of the output image.

MaskSmooth+.description: This node applies a Gaussian blur to a given mask to smooth its edges, with the amount of smoothing determined by the input parameter. It's designed to refine mask outlines, making them less jagged and more visually appealing for further processing or application.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The mask to be smoothed. It represents the area or object of interest that will undergo the smoothing process.

inputs.name: amount
inputs.description: Determines the intensity of the smoothing effect. A higher value results in more blurring, thus a smoother mask.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The smoothed version of the input mask, with edges blurred to the specified degree.

ModelCompile+.description: The ModelCompile node is designed for optimizing and compiling models for improved execution performance. It allows for dynamic adjustments and fine-tuning of the compilation process based on the model's needs and the desired optimization level, enhancing efficiency and potentially reducing overhead.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model to be compiled. This parameter is crucial as it determines the base model that will undergo the compilation process for optimization.

inputs.name: fullgraph
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether to compile the model using a full graph approach. This affects the depth and extent of the compilation, potentially leading to more thorough optimization.

inputs.name: dynamic
inputs.description: A boolean flag that enables dynamic compilation, allowing for more flexibility in how the model is optimized during the compilation process.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Specifies the mode of compilation, which can range from default settings to modes focused on reducing overhead or maximizing autotuning for performance optimization.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The compiled and optimized model, ready for enhanced performance during execution.

PixelOEPixelize+.description: The PixelOEPixelize node focuses on transforming images by applying a pixelization effect. It abstracts the complexity of manipulating pixel data to achieve a stylized reduction in image resolution, often used for aesthetic purposes or to anonymize sensitive information in images.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be pixelized. This image undergoes a transformation where its resolution is reduced in a stylized manner, effectively 'pixelizing' the image.

inputs.name: downscale_mode
inputs.description: Specifies the method used for downscaling the image as part of the pixelization process. Different modes can affect the visual outcome of the pixelization.

inputs.name: target_size
inputs.description: Defines the target size for the pixelization process, determining the final dimensions of the pixelized image.

inputs.name: patch_size
inputs.description: The size of each 'pixel' in the pixelized image, affecting the granularity of the pixelization effect.

inputs.name: thickness
inputs.description: Controls the thickness of the grid lines in the pixelized image, adding to the stylized effect.

inputs.name: color_matching
inputs.description: Determines how colors are matched during the pixelization process, influencing the color accuracy of the pixelized image.

inputs.name: upscale
inputs.description: A flag indicating whether the pixelized image should be upscaled back to its original resolution, affecting the final appearance.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The resulting image after applying the pixelization effect, which may be upscaled to match the original image's resolution.

RemBGSession+.description: The RemBGSession node is designed for background removal from images, utilizing various models to cater to different purposes such as general image segmentation, human segmentation, and cloth parsing. It supports execution on multiple hardware providers, allowing for flexible deployment.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: Specifies the model to be used for background removal, offering a range of options for different segmentation tasks.

inputs.name: providers
inputs.description: Determines the hardware provider for executing the model, supporting a variety of platforms including CPU, CUDA, and more.

outputs.name: rembg_session
outputs.description: Produces a session configured for background removal, ready to process images according to the specified model and provider.

RemoveLatentMask+.description: This node is designed to remove the noise mask from a given set of latent samples. It ensures that the latent samples are cleaned of any previously applied noise masks, maintaining the integrity of the original latent representation.

inputs.name: samples
inputs.description: The latent samples from which the noise mask is to be removed. This operation is crucial for processes that require the original, unaltered state of the latent samples.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The cleaned latent samples, with the noise mask removed, ready for further processing or generation tasks.

SD3NegativeConditioning+.description: This node specializes in modifying the conditioning input for generative models by applying a negative conditioning technique. It zeroes out the initial conditioning and then selectively applies conditioning within a specified timestep range, effectively allowing for more controlled and nuanced generation outcomes.

inputs.name: conditioning
inputs.description: The conditioning input represents the initial set of conditions or parameters that guide the generative model's output. Modifying this input allows for targeted adjustments to the generation process.

inputs.name: end
inputs.description: Specifies the end of the timestep range within which conditioning is applied. A value of 0 indicates no conditioning, while values greater than 0 adjust the extent of conditioning applied, influencing the generative model's output.

outputs.name: conditioning
outputs.description: The modified conditioning output, which has been adjusted within the specified timestep range to influence the generative model's behavior.

SDXLEmptyLatentSizePicker+.description: This node is designed to select an appropriate latent size for a given resolution and batch size, specifically tailored for the SDXL model. It calculates the dimensions of the latent space required to accommodate the specified resolution and batch size, ensuring compatibility with the model's architecture.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: Specifies the desired output resolution from a predefined list of resolutions, each associated with a scaling factor. This parameter is crucial for determining the dimensions of the generated latent space, directly influencing the quality and detail of the generated content.

inputs.name: batch_size
inputs.description: Defines the number of latent samples to generate in one batch. This parameter is essential for managing the computational load and memory usage, impacting the efficiency of the generation process.

outputs.name: LATENT
outputs.description: A tensor representing the generated latent space, structured to match the SDXL model's expected input dimensions.

outputs.name: width
outputs.description: The width of the latent space, derived from the specified resolution.

outputs.name: height
outputs.description: The height of the latent space, derived from the specified resolution.

SimpleMath+.description: SimpleMath is a node designed to evaluate mathematical expressions dynamically. It interprets and computes expressions from abstract syntax trees (AST), supporting basic arithmetic operations, variable resolution, custom function calls, and array indexing.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: The mathematical expression to be evaluated, represented as a string. It is parsed into an abstract syntax tree (AST) for evaluation, supporting operations like addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, and more complex expressions involving variables and functions.

inputs.name: a
inputs.description: An optional variable 'a' that can be used within the mathematical expression. Its value affects the computation if 'a' is referenced in the expression.

inputs.name: b
inputs.description: An optional variable 'b' that can be used within the mathematical expression. Its value affects the computation if 'b' is referenced in the expression.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: The rounded integer result of the evaluated mathematical expression.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The exact floating-point result of the evaluated mathematical expression.

TransitionMask+.description: The TransitionMask+ node specializes in generating dynamic transition effects within masks, offering a range of transition styles and timing functions to create complex visual transitions between frames or states. This node simplifies the creation of animated or static transition effects, making it easier for users to apply sophisticated mask transitions in their projects.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Defines the width of the mask to be generated, setting the horizontal dimension of the transition effect.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Sets the height of the mask, determining the vertical dimension of the transition effect.

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: Specifies the total number of frames in the transition animation, controlling the length of the transition effect.

inputs.name: start_frame
inputs.description: Indicates the starting frame number for the transition effect, allowing for control over the animation's beginning.

inputs.name: end_frame
inputs.description: Determines the ending frame number for the transition, enabling customization of the animation's duration.

inputs.name: transition_type
inputs.description: Selects the type of transition effect to be applied, such as slides, bars, boxes, or fades, offering a variety of visual styles.

inputs.name: timing_function
inputs.description: Chooses the timing function for the transition effect, such as linear or ease-in-out, affecting the pacing of the transition.
