outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: Produces a mask that represents the transition effect, which can be used to apply or visualize the transition within an image or a series of images.

ModelMergeBlockNumber.description: This node specializes in merging two models by blending their components based on specified ratios for different parts of the models. It allows for fine-grained control over the merging process by enabling the adjustment of blend ratios for various blocks within the models.

inputs.name: model1
inputs.description: The first model to be merged. It serves as the base model onto which patches from the second model are applied.

inputs.name: model2
inputs.description: The second model to be merged. Key patches from this model are applied to the first model based on specified ratios.

inputs.name: time_embed.
inputs.description: Specifies the blend ratio for the time embedding components of the models.

inputs.name: label_emb.
inputs.description: Specifies the blend ratio for the label embedding components of the models.

inputs.name: input_blocks.i.
inputs.description: Specifies the blend ratio for each of the input blocks. The index 'i' ranges from 0 to 11, allowing for individual adjustment of 12 input blocks.

inputs.name: middle_block.i.
inputs.description: Specifies the blend ratio for each of the middle blocks. The index 'i' ranges from 0 to 2, targeting 3 middle blocks for adjustment.

inputs.name: output_blocks.i.
inputs.description: Specifies the blend ratio for each of the output blocks. The index 'i' ranges from 0 to 11, enabling individual adjustment of 12 output blocks.

inputs.name: out.
inputs.description: Specifies the blend ratio for the final output components of the models.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The result of merging two models based on the specified blend ratios for various components.

ModelMergeSDXLDetailedTransformers.description: This node specializes in merging two models with a focus on detailed transformer block adjustments. It allows for fine-tuning of the merging process by providing extensive control over transformer block parameters, enabling precise model customization and optimization.

inputs.name: model1
inputs.description: The first model to be merged. It serves as the base model for the merging process.

inputs.name: model2
inputs.description: The second model to be merged. Its parameters are used to augment or modify the first model based on the specified merging strategy.

inputs.name: time_embed.
inputs.description: Adjusts the time embedding layer's contribution to the merged model, allowing for temporal aspects of the models to be fine-tuned.

inputs.name: label_emb.
inputs.description: Adjusts the label embedding layer's contribution to the merged model, enabling customization of how label information influences the merged model.

inputs.description: unknown

inputs.name: output_blocks.i.j.transformer_blocks.k.attn2.to_v
inputs.description: unknown

inputs.name: output_blocks.i.j.transformer_blocks.k.attn2.to_out
inputs.description: unknown

inputs.name: output_blocks.i.j.transformer_blocks.k.norm3
inputs.description: unknown

inputs.name: out.
inputs.description: Adjusts the final output layer's contribution to the merged model, enabling customization of the model's final output characteristics.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The resulting model after merging, incorporating adjustments from both input models and specified transformer block parameters.

ModelMergeSDXLTransformers.description: This node specializes in merging the transformer blocks of two SDXL models, allowing for intricate customization of model behavior by adjusting the influence of specific transformer components across the models.

inputs.name: model1
inputs.description: The first SDXL model to be merged. It serves as the base model for the merging process.

inputs.name: model2
inputs.description: The second SDXL model to be merged. Its transformer blocks can be selectively blended into the first model.

inputs.name: time_embed.
inputs.description: Adjusts the influence of the time embedding component in the merging process.

inputs.name: label_emb.
inputs.description: Adjusts the influence of the label embedding component in the merging process.

inputs.name: input_blocks.i.j.
inputs.description: unknown

inputs.name: input_blocks.i.j.transformer_blocks.k.
inputs.description: unknown

inputs.name: middle_block.i.
inputs.description: Adjusts the influence of the i-th middle block in the merging process. The index i ranges from 0 to 2.

inputs.name: middle_block.i.transformer_blocks.j.
inputs.description: unknown

inputs.name: output_blocks.i.j.
inputs.description: unknown

inputs.name: output_blocks.i.j.transformer_blocks.k.
inputs.description: unknown

inputs.name: out.
inputs.description: Adjusts the final output of the merging process.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The resulting model after merging the specified components of the two SDXL models.

ModelSamplerTonemapNoiseTest.description: This node applies a tonemapping technique to modify the noise prediction in a model's sampling process, aiming to enhance image generation by adjusting the noise's intensity and distribution. It utilizes the Reinhard tonemapping method to scale the noise prediction vector magnitude, thereby influencing the final image output based on a specified multiplier.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model to which the tonemapping noise adjustment will be applied. This parameter is crucial for defining the base model that will undergo the noise modification process.

inputs.name: multiplier
inputs.description: A scalar value that influences the intensity of the tonemapping effect on the noise prediction, directly affecting the visual characteristics of the generated images.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The modified model with the tonemapping noise adjustment applied, ready for further image generation tasks.

ReferenceOnlySimple.description: This node is designed to manipulate and extend model references for batch processing. It clones a given model, applies a custom attention mechanism to blend reference samples with generated latent samples, and adjusts noise masks for the output. The node's functionality is crucial for scenarios requiring the integration of reference data into the model's processing pipeline, enhancing the model's ability to handle diverse batch inputs effectively.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model to be cloned and modified. This parameter is essential as it serves as the base for the subsequent operations, including the application of a custom attention mechanism.

inputs.name: reference
inputs.description: A dictionary containing reference samples. These samples are used alongside generated latent samples to create a blended output, playing a key role in the node's batch processing capabilities.

inputs.name: batch_size
inputs.description: Specifies the number of samples to generate in the batch. This parameter directly influences the size of the generated latent samples and the overall batch processing.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The cloned and modified model with a custom attention mechanism applied.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: A dictionary containing the blended output of reference and generated latent samples, along with adjusted noise masks.

RescaleClassifierFreeGuidanceTest.description: This node applies a custom patch to a given model, modifying its classifier-free guidance sampling function. The patch rescales the guidance scale factor dynamically based on the standard deviation of the conditional and unconditional inputs, aiming to maintain a consistent scale of features across different guidance strengths.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model to which the patch will be applied. This patch modifies the model's classifier-free guidance sampling function to dynamically adjust the guidance scale.

inputs.name: multiplier
inputs.description: A scaling factor that blends the original and rescaled guidance signals, controlling the strength of the rescaling effect on the model's output.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The patched model with an updated classifier-free guidance sampling function that incorporates dynamic rescaling based on input standard deviations.

TonemapNoiseWithRescaleCFG.description: This node applies a tonemapping and noise rescaling technique to a given model's configuration, enhancing its ability to generate images by adjusting the contrast and scale of generated features. It utilizes a combination of tonemapping and rescaling operations to modify the model's output, aiming to improve visual quality and detail in the generated images.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model to which the tonemapping and noise rescaling configuration will be applied. This parameter is crucial as it defines the base model that will be enhanced with the specified techniques.

inputs.name: tonemap_multiplier
inputs.description: A multiplier that adjusts the intensity of the tonemapping effect. This parameter allows for fine-tuning of the contrast enhancement applied to the generated images.

inputs.name: rescale_multiplier
inputs.description: A multiplier that adjusts the intensity of the rescaling effect. This parameter allows for fine-tuning of the scale adjustment applied to the generated images, affecting their overall visual quality.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The enhanced model with applied tonemapping and noise rescaling configuration. This output represents the model after the adjustments have been made, ready for generating improved images.

FaceAlign.description: The FaceAlign node is designed for aligning faces within images based on facial keypoints. It adjusts the orientation of a face in an input image to match the orientation of a face in a target image or to a standard alignment if no target is provided, enhancing the consistency of facial analysis or recognition tasks.

inputs.name: analysis_models
inputs.description: Specifies the models used for facial analysis, particularly for detecting facial keypoints. Its role is crucial in determining the orientation and alignment of faces within images.

inputs.name: image_from
inputs.description: The source image containing the face to be aligned. This image is processed to detect facial keypoints and adjust its orientation based on these points.

inputs.name: image_to
inputs.description: An optional target image used to align the source image's face orientation with the target's face orientation. If provided, the alignment is adjusted to match the target face's orientation.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The aligned image with the face orientation adjusted either to match the target image or to a standard alignment if no target is provided.

FaceAnalysisModels.description: The FaceAnalysisModels node is designed to load and manage face analysis models based on specified libraries and providers. It dynamically supports different face analysis libraries and hardware acceleration options, facilitating the flexible integration of face analysis capabilities into applications.

inputs.name: library
inputs.description: Specifies the face analysis library to use. The choice of library affects the underlying model and algorithms for face analysis.

inputs.name: provider
inputs.description: Determines the hardware acceleration provider for the face analysis model, enabling optimized performance on various platforms.

outputs.name: analysis_models
outputs.description: Returns an instance of the loaded face analysis model, ready for performing face analysis tasks.

FaceBoundingBox.description: The FaceBoundingBox node is designed to detect and extract bounding boxes around faces in images. It utilizes analysis models to identify the location and dimensions of faces, applying optional padding and selecting specific faces based on an index. This functionality is crucial for tasks that require precise face detection and cropping, such as facial recognition or analysis applications.

inputs.name: analysis_models
inputs.description: Specifies the models used for face detection and analysis. It's crucial for determining the accuracy and efficiency of face detection within images.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image or images in which faces need to be detected. It serves as the primary data for face detection.

inputs.name: padding
inputs.description: An optional parameter that adds a fixed padding to the detected face bounding boxes, allowing for more context around the faces.

inputs.name: padding_percent
inputs.description: Similar to padding, but adds a percentage-based padding around the detected face bounding boxes, offering flexible context inclusion.

inputs.name: index
inputs.description: Specifies the index of the face to focus on when multiple faces are detected. A negative index indicates no specific focus, utilizing all detected faces.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: The cropped images of detected faces, potentially adjusted by padding and index selection.

outputs.name: x
outputs.description: The x-coordinate of the top-left corner of each face bounding box.

outputs.name: y
outputs.description: The y-coordinate of the top-left corner of each face bounding box.

outputs.name: width
outputs.description: The width of each face bounding box.

outputs.name: height
outputs.description: The height of each face bounding box.

FaceEmbedDistance.description: The FaceEmbedDistance node calculates the distance between facial embeddings using cosine or Euclidean (L2) metrics. It supports normalization of embeddings for distance calculation, enabling a versatile approach to measuring facial similarity or dissimilarity.

inputs.name: analysis_models
inputs.description: Specifies the face analysis models to be used for generating embeddings from the input images. It plays a critical role in the accuracy of the distance measurements.

inputs.name: reference
inputs.description: The reference image against which other images are compared. This image is used to generate a facial embedding for similarity comparison.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image to be compared against the reference. It is used to generate a facial embedding for calculating the distance to the reference embedding.

inputs.name: similarity_metric
inputs.description: Defines the metric used for calculating the distance between embeddings. Options include 'L2_norm', 'cosine', and 'euclidean', affecting the comparison's sensitivity and outcome.

inputs.name: filter_thresh
inputs.description: A threshold for filtering out distances above a certain value, enhancing the focus on closer matches.

inputs.name: filter_best
inputs.description: Limits the number of results to the best matches below the specified threshold, optimizing the search for similarity.

inputs.name: generate_image_overlay
inputs.description: A boolean indicating whether to overlay the reference image on top of the comparison image, visually representing the similarity measurement.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: The image result of overlaying the reference image on the comparison image, if enabled, providing a visual representation of the similarity.

outputs.name: distance
outputs.description: The calculated distance between the facial embeddings of the reference and comparison images, quantifying their similarity.

FaceSegmentation.description: The FaceSegmentation node is designed to process images by segmenting faces based on provided parameters. It utilizes advanced image processing techniques to refine the segmentation mask through expansion, tapering, and blurring, ultimately extracting and modifying the face segment within the image for further analysis or visualization.

inputs.name: analysis_models
inputs.description: A collection of models used for analyzing the image, crucial for determining the initial segmentation mask before refinement.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed, serving as the basis for face segmentation.

inputs.name: area
inputs.description: Specifies the area of interest within the image for segmentation, guiding the initial mask creation. This parameter allows selection from predefined areas such as the face, eyes, or mouth, influencing the focus of the segmentation process.

inputs.name: grow
inputs.description: Determines how much to expand the segmentation mask, allowing for more inclusive face coverage.

inputs.name: grow_tapered
inputs.description: Indicates whether the mask expansion should taper off, providing a more natural transition at the edges.

inputs.name: blur
inputs.description: The intensity of blur applied to the segmentation mask, enhancing the mask's smoothness and blending.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The refined segmentation mask after processing.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The original image modified by the segmentation mask, highlighting the segmented area.

outputs.name: seg_mask
outputs.description: A mask representing the precise segment of the face extracted from the image.

outputs.name: seg_image
outputs.description: The extracted segment of the face from the original image.

outputs.name: x
outputs.description: The minimum x-coordinate of the face segment within the image.

outputs.name: y
outputs.description: The minimum y-coordinate of the face segment within the image.

outputs.name: width
outputs.description: The width of the face segment extracted from the image.

outputs.name: height
outputs.description: The height of the face segment extracted from the image.

FaceWarp.description: The FaceWarp node is designed to perform facial warping between two images by utilizing facial landmarks to align features from a source image to a target image. This process involves calculating a transformation matrix based on the landmarks, applying the transformation to warp the source image and its mask to match the target image's geometry, and blending the images for a seamless transition.

inputs.name: analysis_models
inputs.description: A collection of models used for analyzing facial features, including landmark detection and other preprocessing tasks. It plays a crucial role in determining the transformation matrix for warping.

inputs.name: image_from
inputs.description: The source image from which facial features will be warped.

inputs.name: image_to
inputs.description: The target image to which the source image's facial features will be aligned.

inputs.name: keypoints
inputs.description: Specifies the set of facial landmarks to be used for the warping process, influencing the precision and areas of alignment.

inputs.name: grow
inputs.description: A parameter that controls the expansion of the mask around the detected facial landmarks, affecting the area of the image to be warped.

inputs.name: blur
inputs.description: Determines the level of blurring applied to the edges of the warped image and mask, enhancing the blending effect.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The resulting image after applying the warping and blending processes, where the source image's features have been aligned to the target image.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The mask generated during the warping process, indicating the areas of the source image that have been transformed and blended into the target image.

FL_Ascii.description: The FL_Ascii node transforms images into ASCII art by resizing the input image based on specified spacing and then mapping pixel brightness values to characters. This process creates a text-based visual representation of the image, utilizing a specified font size, font name, and character set.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be transformed into ASCII art. It serves as the canvas for the ASCII art effect.

inputs.name: spacing
inputs.description: Determines the spacing between characters in the ASCII art, effectively controlling the resolution of the output.

inputs.name: font_size
inputs.description: Specifies the font size used for the characters in the ASCII art, impacting the detail and readability of the output.

inputs.name: font_name
inputs.description: The name of the font used to render characters in the ASCII art, influencing the style and appearance of the output.

inputs.name: characters
inputs.description: A string of characters used to represent different brightness levels in the ASCII art, where each character's position in the string corresponds to a specific range of brightness.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The resulting ASCII art as an image, where the original image is represented by a matrix of characters.

FL_AudioConverter.description: The FL_AudioConverter node is designed to transform audio data into a format that simulates the characteristics of VHS audio quality. It processes audio inputs by adjusting their sample rate and converting them into a byte stream that represents the audio in a VHS-like quality.

inputs.name: audio
inputs.description: The 'audio' input represents the raw audio data that will be processed and converted into VHS audio quality. It is crucial for defining the audio content that will undergo transformation.

inputs.name: sample_rate
inputs.description: The 'sample_rate' input specifies the sample rate of the audio data. It plays a significant role in the conversion process by determining the resolution of the audio output.

outputs.name: audio
outputs.description: The output is a lambda function that, when called, returns the audio data bytes simulating VHS audio quality.

FL_AudioFrameCalculator.description: The FL_AudioFrameCalculator node is designed to process audio files by calculating the number of frames within specified bars of the audio, based on the beats per minute (BPM), frame rate, and other parameters. It utilizes audio processing libraries to extract and manipulate audio data, providing insights into the audio's structure and timing for further processing or analysis.

inputs.name: audio_file_path
inputs.description: Specifies the absolute path to the audio file to be processed. It is crucial for locating and loading the audio data for analysis.

inputs.name: start_bar
inputs.description: Determines the starting bar from which the audio analysis begins, allowing for targeted processing within the audio file.

inputs.name: bar_count
inputs.description: Defines the number of bars to analyze, enabling the calculation of frames over a specific section of the audio.

inputs.name: fps
inputs.description: Frames per second setting, which influences the calculation of the total number of frames within the specified audio segment.

outputs.name: AUDIO
outputs.description: The processed audio segment, suitable for further audio manipulation or analysis.

outputs.name: Frame Count
outputs.description: The total number of frames calculated within the specified audio segment.

outputs.name: BPM
outputs.description: The beats per minute of the audio, determined during processing.

outputs.name: FPS
outputs.description: The frames per second parameter, as specified in the input, returned for reference.

FL_AudioPreview.description: The FL_AudioPreview node is designed to play audio segments, allowing users to preview audio data within their workflow. It supports both mono and stereo audio formats and can handle audio data provided as either PyTorch tensors or numpy arrays.

inputs.name: audio_segment
inputs.description: A tuple containing the audio data and its sample rate. This input is crucial for determining the audio content to be played and its playback speed.

FL_CodeNode.description: The FL_CodeNode allows for dynamic execution of user-provided code within a predefined execution environment, enabling custom processing and manipulation of inputs to generate outputs. It abstracts the complexity of executing arbitrary code snippets safely and efficiently, providing a flexible interface for user-defined logic.

inputs.name: code_input
inputs.description: The primary input for the node, accepting a multiline string of code that the user wishes to execute. This code can interact with optional inputs and define the logic for output generation.

inputs.name: input_i
inputs.description: A series of optional input parameters (up to four) that can be used within the user-provided code for custom logic and processing. These inputs are dynamically accepted and can vary in type based on the user's code.

outputs.name: output_0
outputs.description: An output parameter that is the result of the executed user-provided code.

outputs.name: output_1
outputs.description: An output parameter that is the result of the executed user-provided code.

outputs.name: output_2
outputs.description: An output parameter that is the result of the executed user-provided code.

outputs.name: output_3
outputs.description: An output parameter that is the result of the executed user-provided code.

FL_DirectoryCrawl.description: The FL_DirectoryCrawl node is designed to scan a specified directory and its subdirectories for image files, supporting a range of common image formats. It then loads these images, applies necessary orientation corrections, converts them to a uniform RGB format, and finally aggregates them into a batch of tensors. This process facilitates the bulk processing of images located within a filesystem for further image-based operations or analyses.

inputs.name: directory_path
inputs.description: Specifies the path to the directory that the node will scan for image files. This path is crucial as it determines the root location from which the search for image files will begin, affecting which images are loaded and processed.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: A batch of images that have been loaded, oriented correctly, converted to RGB, and normalized, encapsulated within a tensor. This output facilitates further processing or analysis in image-based machine learning workflows.

FL_Glitch.description: The FL_Glitch node applies a digital glitch effect to images, optionally incorporating color offsets and controlled by a seed for reproducibility. It processes a batch of images, applying a glitch effect that distorts the visual content in a stylistic manner, and provides progress updates during processing.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The 'images' parameter is a collection of images to which the glitch effect will be applied. It is essential for defining the input data that will undergo the glitch transformation process.

inputs.name: glitch_amount
inputs.description: The 'glitch_amount' parameter controls the intensity of the glitch effect applied to the images. It plays a crucial role in determining the extent of visual distortion.

inputs.name: color_offset
inputs.description: The 'color_offset' parameter enables or disables color offsetting in the glitch effect, adding an additional layer of visual manipulation.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: The 'seed' parameter ensures the reproducibility of the glitch effects applied to the images, allowing for consistent results across different runs.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is a tensor of images that have been processed to include a digital glitch effect, potentially with color offsets, depending on the input parameters.

FL_HexagonalPattern.description: The FL_HexagonalPattern node is designed to transform a collection of images into a hexagonal pattern, adjusting the size of hexagons based on the image dimensions and applying optional shadow effects for enhanced visual depth. It allows for customization of the hexagonal pattern through parameters such as hexagon size, shadow properties, and background color, enabling a versatile approach to image styling.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: A collection of images to be transformed into a hexagonal pattern. This parameter is essential for the node's operation, serving as the primary input around which the hexagonal pattern is generated.

inputs.name: hexagon_size
inputs.description: Specifies the desired size of the hexagons in the pattern, affecting the overall appearance and granularity of the hexagonal tiling.

inputs.name: shadow_offset
inputs.description: Determines the offset distance for the shadow effect applied to each hexagon, enhancing the pattern's visual depth.

inputs.name: shadow_color
inputs.description: Defines the color of the shadow effect, allowing for customization of the shadow's appearance.

inputs.name: background_color
inputs.description: Sets the background color of the output image, providing a base for the hexagonal pattern.

inputs.name: rotation
inputs.description: Controls the rotation angle of each hexagon in the pattern, offering an additional dimension of stylistic customization.

inputs.name: spacing
inputs.description: Adjusts the spacing between individual hexagons in the pattern, influencing the pattern's density and overall aesthetic.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The transformed image with the applied hexagonal pattern, incorporating any specified shadow effects and background color.

FL_ImageCaptionSaver.description: The FL_ImageCaptionSaver node is designed to save a batch of images along with their corresponding captions into specified directory, with options for file naming and overwrite control. It facilitates the organization and storage of generated images and textual descriptions, enhancing accessibility and management of visual content.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: A batch of images to be saved. This input is crucial for determining the content that will be stored, directly affecting the output files created.

inputs.name: folder_name
inputs.description: The name of the folder where images and captions will be saved. It serves as the destination path for the output, influencing the organization of saved files.

inputs.name: caption_text
inputs.description: The text caption to be saved alongside each image. This input provides contextual or descriptive information about the images, enriching the content's value.

inputs.name: overwrite
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether existing files with the same name should be overwritten. This affects how the node handles file naming conflicts and storage management.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: A confirmation message detailing the number of images and captions saved and the directory where they are stored. It provides feedback on the operation's success.

FL_ImageDimensionDisplay.description: This node is designed to calculate and display the dimensions of an image, supporting both individual images and batches of images in various formats. It abstracts the complexity of handling different image representations, providing a straightforward way to obtain image dimensions.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image input is crucial for determining the dimensions of the provided image. It supports both tensor and PIL image formats, adapting its processing based on the input type to accurately return the image dimensions.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: Outputs the dimensions of the provided image as a string, formatted to include both width and height.

FL_ImageDurationSync.description: The FL_ImageDurationSync node is designed to synchronize the duration of a sequence of images with a specific musical beat per minute (BPM), frame count, and bars, adjusting the number of frames each image is held to match the desired total duration. This functionality is particularly useful in creating visuals that align with audio tracks, ensuring that the visual elements progress in harmony with the music's tempo.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The sequence of images to be synchronized with the audio duration. This input is crucial for determining the base visual content that will be adjusted in duration.

inputs.name: frame_count
inputs.description: Specifies the total number of frames for the output sequence, influencing how the images are stretched or compressed to fit the desired duration.

inputs.name: bpm
inputs.description: The beats per minute of the audio track, which is used to calculate the duration of each bar and, consequently, the total duration of the image sequence.

inputs.name: fps
inputs.description: The frames per second rate at which the images will be displayed, affecting the calculation of how long each image is held.

inputs.name: bars
inputs.description: The number of musical bars over which the images will be synchronized, directly impacting the total duration of the visual sequence.

outputs.name: output_images
outputs.description: The sequence of images adjusted to match the desired duration, ensuring synchronization with the audio track.

outputs.name: hold_frames
outputs.description: The number of frames each image is held, calculated based on the BPM, bars, and FPS to achieve the desired synchronization.

FL_ImagePixelator.description: The FL_ImagePixelator node applies pixelation effects to images, supporting both individual images and batches. It can process images represented as tensors or PIL images, applying a scale factor to pixelate the image and a kernel size for additional processing, enhancing the pixelation effect.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image to be pixelated. This can be a single image or a batch of images, in either torch.Tensor or PIL.Image format. It's the primary input for pixelation.

inputs.name: scale_factor
inputs.description: Determines the intensity of the pixelation effect by scaling the image's resolution down before scaling it back up.

inputs.name: kernel_size
inputs.description: Specifies the size of the kernel used in the additional processing step after pixelation, affecting the final appearance of the pixelated image.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The pixelated image, processed according to the specified scale factor and kernel size. It can be a single image or a batch of images, in the same format as the input.

FL_ImageRandomizer.description: The FL_ImageRandomizer node is designed to select and process images from a specified directory, offering options for random selection or sequential access. It enhances image handling in workflows by providing a flexible way to work with image datasets, including randomization features for varied outputs.

inputs.name: directory_path
inputs.description: Specifies the filesystem path to the directory containing images. It is essential for locating and loading the images to be processed.

inputs.name: randomize
inputs.description: A boolean toggle that determines whether images are selected randomly or sequentially. This affects the diversity and unpredictability of the output.

inputs.name: run_trigger
inputs.description: A dummy input used to trigger the node's execution, helping to circumvent caching issues.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The processed image, returned as a tensor, suitable for further image processing or visualization tasks.

outputs.name: path
outputs.description: The filesystem path of the selected image, providing context or for use in subsequent operations.

FL_PixelSort.description: The FL_PixelSort node applies a pixel sorting effect to images based on their hue values, allowing for artistic manipulation of image textures. It supports customization through parameters such as direction, threshold, smoothing, and rotation to achieve various visual effects.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: A collection of images to be processed. The images are sorted based on their hue values, allowing for creative retexturing and manipulation.

inputs.name: direction
inputs.description: Specifies the direction of the pixel sorting process, either 'Horizontal' or 'Vertical'. This affects the orientation of the sorting effect on the images.

inputs.name: threshold
inputs.description: A value that determines the sensitivity of hue changes required to trigger sorting. A lower threshold results in more aggressive sorting based on smaller hue differences.

inputs.name: smoothing
inputs.description: Controls the smoothness of the transitions between sorted and unsorted regions, with higher values resulting in smoother transitions.

inputs.name: rotation
inputs.description: Applies a rotation to the image before sorting, with possible values indicating the number of 90-degree rotations.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The processed images with the pixel sorting effect applied, based on the specified parameters.

FL_Ripple.description: The FL_Ripple node applies a ripple effect to a collection of images, transforming each image by simulating a ripple pattern. This effect is achieved through mathematical manipulation of the image pixels, based on specified parameters such as amplitude, frequency, and phase, to create visually dynamic results.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: A collection of images to which the ripple effect will be applied. This parameter is essential for determining the input images that will undergo the transformation.

inputs.name: amplitude
inputs.description: Defines the height of the ripple waves. A higher amplitude results in more pronounced ripples.

inputs.name: frequency
inputs.description: Determines the number of ripples in the image. Higher frequencies result in more ripples within a given space.

inputs.name: phase
inputs.description: Adjusts the starting point of the ripple effect, allowing for phase shifts in the wave pattern.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is an image with the ripple effect applied, represented as a tensor.

AbsCosWave.description: The AbsCosWave node generates a wave pattern based on the absolute value of a cosine function, modulated by parameters such as phase, amplitude, x_translation, and max_value. It's designed to create dynamic, visually interesting waveforms for various applications.

inputs.name: phase
inputs.description: The phase parameter controls the periodicity of the wave, affecting how frequently the wave pattern repeats over a given interval.

inputs.name: amplitude
inputs.description: Amplitude determines the height of the wave peaks, influencing the overall intensity of the wave pattern.

inputs.name: x_translation
inputs.description: X_translation shifts the wave pattern along the horizontal axis, allowing for adjustments in the wave's starting position.

inputs.name: max_value
inputs.description: Max_value sets the upper limit for the wave's value, capping the peak height and affecting the wave's amplitude.

inputs.name: current_frame
inputs.description: Current_frame represents a specific point in time or sequence, used to calculate the wave's position and shape at that moment.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The first element of the output tuple, representing the calculated wave value in its precise form.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: The second element of the output tuple, providing an integer approximation of the wave's current state.

AbsSinWave.description: The AbsSinWave node generates a sine wave where the sine function's output is modified by the absolute value, creating a unique wave pattern. This transformation is applied to model wave-like behaviors with a distinctive mathematical alteration.

inputs.name: phase
inputs.description: The 'phase' parameter controls the period of the sine wave, affecting how quickly the wave cycles through its pattern.

inputs.name: amplitude
inputs.description: The 'amplitude' parameter determines the height of the wave peaks, influencing the wave's overall intensity.

inputs.name: x_translation
inputs.description: The 'x_translation' parameter shifts the wave along the x-axis, allowing for adjustments in the wave's starting position.

inputs.name: max_value
inputs.description: The 'max_value' parameter sets the maximum value the wave can reach, influencing the wave's peak.

inputs.name: current_frame
inputs.description: The 'current_frame' parameter specifies the current point in time or frame for which the wave's value is being calculated, playing a crucial role in the wave's progression.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The first output is the calculated wave value as a float, reflecting the wave's current state.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: The second output is the integer representation of the calculated wave value, providing a discrete measure of the wave's state.

BatchPromptSchedule.description: The BatchPromptSchedule node is designed to process animation prompts by cleaning up input text, splitting it into positive and negative prompts based on predefined weights, and then applying a series of transformations to interpolate and condition these prompts for animation sequences. This node facilitates the generation of dynamic, frame-specific animation content by leveraging prompt scheduling techniques to adjust the influence of various prompts over the course of an animation.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The text parameter includes the input text for animation prompts, which is processed to remove whitespace and newlines before being split into positive and negative prompts.

inputs.name: clip
inputs.description: The clip parameter represents the animation clip to which the prompt scheduling and conditioning will be applied. It is essential for aligning the generated prompts with the specific frames and dynamics of the animation.

inputs.name: max_frames
inputs.description: This parameter specifies the maximum number of frames for the animation, used to determine the scheduling and interpolation of prompts across the animation sequence.

inputs.name: print_output
inputs.description: A boolean parameter indicating whether to print the output of the prompt processing for debugging or informational purposes.

inputs.name: pre_text
inputs.description: Pre-text to be added before each prompt, used to modify or enhance the original prompt text before processing.

inputs.name: app_text
inputs.description: Appended text to be added after each prompt, serving to further customize or refine the prompt text.

inputs.name: start_frame
inputs.description: Specifies the starting frame number for the animation, used in conjunction with end_frame to define the range of frames affected by the prompt scheduling.

inputs.name: end_frame
inputs.description: Defines the ending frame number for the animation, setting the boundary for prompt processing and application.

inputs.name: pw_a
inputs.description: Parameter weight A, part of a set of weights used to adjust the influence of various prompts or conditions within the animation.

inputs.name: pw_b
inputs.description: Parameter weight B, another weight in the set for fine-tuning the prompt conditioning and scheduling.

inputs.name: pw_c
inputs.description: Parameter weight C, used alongside other weights to customize the prompt's impact on the animation.

inputs.name: pw_d
inputs.description: Parameter weight D, the last of the set of weights for adjusting prompt influence, contributing to the dynamic generation of animation content.

outputs.name: POS
outputs.description: The output 'POS' represents the conditioned positive prompts, ready for use in generating or influencing animation frames.

outputs.name: NEG
outputs.description: The output 'NEG' represents the conditioned negative prompts, similarly prepared for influencing animation frames in contrast to the positive prompts.

BatchPromptScheduleEncodeSDXL.description: This node is designed to process and encode batch prompts for Stable Diffusion XL models, allowing for the scheduling of G and L clips separately before tokenization. It integrates a weighted addition process to generate a batch of conditionings tailored for animation or dynamic content creation.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Specifies the width of the output image or frame, impacting the aspect ratio and detail level of the generated content.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Determines the height of the output image or frame, affecting the aspect ratio and overall composition of the generated content.

inputs.name: crop_w
inputs.description: Defines the width of the cropping area, used to focus on or exclude specific parts of the generated content.

inputs.name: crop_h
inputs.description: Specifies the height of the cropping area, enabling precise control over the content's framing and focus areas.

inputs.name: target_width
inputs.description: The desired width for resizing the output, allowing for adjustments to the content's dimensions without altering its aspect ratio.

inputs.name: target_height
inputs.description: The target height for resizing the output, facilitating dimension adjustments while maintaining the original aspect ratio.

inputs.name: text_g
inputs.description: Represents the global text prompts that guide the overall theme and content generation, serving as a foundational element for the animation or dynamic content.

inputs.name: clip
inputs.description: Refers to the clip model used for conditioning the prompts, playing a critical role in the interpretation and processing of the text inputs.

inputs.name: text_l
inputs.description: Denotes the local text prompts that provide detailed guidance for specific parts of the content, complementing the global prompts to refine the output.

inputs.name: max_frames
inputs.description: Indicates the maximum number of frames to be generated, defining the length and scope of the animation or dynamic content.

inputs.name: print_output
inputs.description: A flag to enable or disable the printing of output for debugging or transparency purposes during the content generation process.

inputs.name: pre_text_G
inputs.description: Prepended text for global prompts, used to add context or modify the tone of the global text inputs before processing.

inputs.name: app_text_G
inputs.description: Appended text for global prompts, allowing for additional details or thematic elements to be included after the main global text.

inputs.name: pre_text_L
inputs.description: Prepended text for local prompts, used to introduce or alter the context of the local text inputs, enhancing specificity and focus.

inputs.name: app_text_L
inputs.description: Appended text for local prompts, providing a means to extend or refine the local text inputs with further details or thematic elements.

inputs.name: pw_a
inputs.description: Weight parameter A, part of a set of weights used to adjust the influence of different components in the prompt processing and conditioning.

inputs.name: pw_b
inputs.description: Weight parameter B, contributing to the fine-tuning of prompt influence and conditioning in the generation process.

inputs.name: pw_c
inputs.description: Weight parameter C, involved in balancing the effects of various prompt components on the content output.

inputs.name: pw_d
inputs.description: Weight parameter D, used to adjust the relative impact of prompt elements, aiding in the customization of the generation process.

outputs.name: POS
outputs.description: The enhanced positive conditioning output, reflecting the emphasized aspects of the original prompt after processing.

outputs.name: NEG
outputs.description: The adjusted negative conditioning output, indicating the de-emphasized elements of the original prompt following processing.

BatchPromptScheduleLatentInput.description: This node is designed to process animation prompts for generating scheduled latent inputs. It sequences the user's formatted prompt into current and next prompts along with their conditioning strengths, evaluates expressions within the prompts, and applies a scheduling algorithm to produce a batch of conditionings tailored to the input latent. The node's functionality facilitates the creation of dynamic, time-sequenced visual content by manipulating latent space representations in accordance with the specified prompt schedule.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The user's input prompt intended for animation, which is processed to generate positive and negative prompts for content generation. This input is crucial for defining the thematic and narrative direction of the generated content.

inputs.name: clip
inputs.description: A representation of the clip model used for conditioning the input prompt, playing a key role in the generation process by influencing the visual characteristics of the output.

inputs.name: num_latents
inputs.description: Specifies the number of latent vectors to be used in the generation process, directly impacting the diversity and variation of the generated content.

inputs.name: print_output
inputs.description: A boolean flag that, when set, enables the printing of output for debugging purposes, aiding in the analysis and refinement of the generation process.

inputs.name: pre_text
inputs.description: Pre-text added to the animation prompts before processing, influencing the initial context and direction of the generated content.

inputs.name: app_text
inputs.description: Appended text to the animation prompts, modifying the final output by adding specific details or themes to the generated content.

inputs.name: start_frame
inputs.description: Defines the starting frame for the animation, setting the initial point for the prompt scheduling process.

inputs.name: end_frame
inputs.description: Specifies the ending frame for the animation, marking the conclusion of the prompt scheduling.

inputs.name: pw_a
inputs.description: A parameter weight influencing the conditioning strength of the animation, affecting the intensity of the generated content's attributes.

inputs.name: pw_b
inputs.description: A parameter weight that adjusts the balance between different attributes in the generated content, impacting the overall visual outcome.

inputs.name: pw_c
inputs.description: A parameter weight used to fine-tune the conditioning process, allowing for precise control over the generated content's characteristics.

inputs.name: pw_d
inputs.description: A parameter weight that affects the temporal dynamics of the animation, influencing how attributes evolve over time.

outputs.name: POS
outputs.description: The processed and scheduled positive conditioning, ready for use in generating content that emphasizes desired attributes.

outputs.name: NEG
outputs.description: The processed and scheduled negative conditioning, aimed at minimizing or avoiding certain attributes in the generated content.

outputs.name: INPUT_LATENTS
outputs.description: The original input latents passed through the node, potentially modified or unchanged, depending on the node's internal logic.

BatchPromptScheduleSDXLLatentInput.description: This node is designed to process animation prompts for both G and L clips, applying a scheduling algorithm that separates, tokenizes, and then recombines these prompts with weighted adjustments before finally applying a batch of conditionings. It uniquely handles latent inputs, allowing for the dynamic adjustment of animation parameters based on the provided latents.

inputs.name: width

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: The height of the clip or frame in pixels.

inputs.name: crop_w
inputs.description: The width of the crop area in pixels.

inputs.name: crop_h
inputs.description: The height of the crop area in pixels.

inputs.name: target_width
inputs.description: The target width of the clip or frame after processing.

inputs.name: target_height
inputs.description: The target height of the clip or frame after processing.

inputs.name: text_g
inputs.description: The text prompt for G clips, which will be processed, tokenized, and adjusted according to the scheduling algorithm.

inputs.name: clip
inputs.description: Represents the clip information or parameters that are used in conjunction with the text prompts to apply the scheduling algorithm.

inputs.name: text_l
inputs.description: The text prompt for L clips, similar to text_g, it will be processed, tokenized, and adjusted for scheduling.

inputs.name: num_latents
inputs.description: The number of latent inputs that are used to dynamically adjust the animation parameters during the scheduling process.

inputs.name: print_output
inputs.description: A flag indicating whether to print the output of the scheduling process.

inputs.name: pre_text_G
inputs.description: Pre-text to be added to the G clip's text prompt before processing.

inputs.name: app_text_G
inputs.description: App-text to be appended to the G clip's text prompt after processing.

inputs.name: pre_text_L
inputs.description: Pre-text to be added to the L clip's text prompt before processing.

inputs.name: app_text_L
inputs.description: App-text to be appended to the L clip's text prompt after processing.

inputs.name: pw_a
inputs.description: Weight parameter a, used in the scheduling algorithm for adjusting prompts.

inputs.name: pw_b
inputs.description: Weight parameter b, used in the scheduling algorithm for adjusting prompts.

inputs.name: pw_c
inputs.description: Weight parameter c, used in the scheduling algorithm for adjusting prompts.

inputs.name: pw_d
inputs.description: Weight parameter d, used in the scheduling algorithm for adjusting prompts.

outputs.name: POS
outputs.description: The positive conditioning batch resulting from the applied scheduling and animation adjustments.

outputs.name: NEG
outputs.description: The negative conditioning batch resulting from the applied scheduling and animation adjustments.

outputs.name: POS_CUR
