BatchStringSchedule.description: The `BatchStringSchedule` node processes animation prompts by splitting them into positive and negative prompts, interpolating these prompts over a series of frames, and returning them as a batch of strings. This node is designed to handle the temporal dynamics of animation prompts, facilitating the generation of text sequences that vary over time.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The text input represents the base animation prompt that will be split into positive and negative prompts, serving as the foundation for the temporal interpolation process.

inputs.name: max_frames
inputs.description: Specifies the maximum number of frames for which the prompts will be interpolated, defining the temporal extent of the animation sequence.

inputs.name: print_output
inputs.description: A flag indicating whether the output should be printed, affecting the node's output behavior.

inputs.name: pre_text
inputs.description: Text to be prepended to each animation prompt, modifying the initial content of the prompts before they are split and interpolated.

inputs.name: app_text
inputs.description: Text to be appended to each animation prompt, modifying the final content of the prompts before they are split and interpolated.

inputs.name: pw_a
inputs.description: Weight parameter A for interpolation, influencing how the positive and negative prompts are blended over time.

inputs.name: pw_b
inputs.description: Weight parameter B for interpolation, further influencing the blending of prompts over the animation sequence.

inputs.name: pw_c
inputs.description: Weight parameter C for interpolation, adjusting the influence of certain aspects of the prompt interpolation.

inputs.name: pw_d
inputs.description: Weight parameter D for interpolation, adjusting the influence of certain aspects of the prompt interpolation.

outputs.name: POS
outputs.description: The interpolated positive prompt for the current frame, as part of the batch of strings.

outputs.name: NEG
outputs.description: The interpolated negative prompt for the current frame, as part of the batch of strings.

BatchValueSchedule.description: The BatchValueSchedule node is designed to process a batch of text inputs, applying a scheduling algorithm to generate a sequence of values based on the text's key frames over a specified number of frames. It supports batch processing for efficiency and can optionally print the output for debugging purposes.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The text input containing key frames for value generation. It supports multiline input and plays a crucial role in determining the sequence of generated values.

inputs.name: max_frames
inputs.description: Specifies the maximum number of frames for which values will be generated. It defines the length of the output sequence.

inputs.name: print_output
inputs.description: A boolean flag that, when set to True, enables printing of the output for debugging purposes.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The first element of the output tuple, representing the generated values as floating-point numbers.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: The second element of the output tuple, representing the generated values converted to integers.

BatchValueScheduleLatentInput.description: The BatchValueScheduleLatentInput node is designed to process latent inputs in the context of batch scheduling. It focuses on handling and transforming latent data according to a value schedule, enabling dynamic adjustments and manipulations of latent vectors based on specified scheduling parameters.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The 'text' parameter is a string that specifies the key frames and their corresponding values for the value schedule. It plays a crucial role in determining how the latent inputs are transformed over time.

inputs.name: num_latents
inputs.description: The 'num_latents' parameter represents the latent inputs to be processed. It is essential for defining the latent vectors that will be adjusted according to the value schedule.

inputs.name: print_output
inputs.description: The 'print_output' parameter controls whether the scheduling results are printed. It allows for optional debugging or visualization of the value schedule's effect on the latent inputs.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: This output represents the scheduled values as a floating-point number, reflecting the dynamic adjustments made to the latent inputs.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: This output provides the integer representation of the scheduled values, offering an alternative numerical perspective on the adjustments.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: This output includes the transformed latent inputs, showcasing the result of the scheduling process on the latent vectors.

CalculateFrameOffset.description: This node is designed to calculate the offset for frame numbers in a sequence, facilitating the management of frame-based operations in animations or simulations. It computes the starting frame number based on the current frame, maximum number of frames, number of latent inputs, and an index, ensuring seamless transitions and looping in frame sequences.

inputs.name: current_frame
inputs.description: Specifies the current frame in the sequence. It is crucial for determining the starting point for the offset calculation.

inputs.name: max_frames
inputs.description: Defines the maximum number of frames in the sequence. It is essential for ensuring the calculated frame number loops correctly within the sequence limits.

inputs.name: num_latent_inputs
inputs.description: Indicates the number of latent inputs used in the frame sequence. This parameter influences the calculation of the frame offset by adjusting the spacing between frames.

inputs.name: index
inputs.description: Represents an index used in the calculation of the frame offset. It affects the final computed frame number, contributing to the determination of the starting frame.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: Returns the calculated frame offset as an integer, facilitating the determination of the next frame in the sequence.

ConcatStringSingle.description: The ConcatStringSingle node is designed to concatenate two strings into a single string. It focuses on combining textual inputs, providing a straightforward way to merge text data.

inputs.name: string_a
inputs.description: The first string to be concatenated. It serves as the initial part of the new combined string.

inputs.name: string_b
inputs.description: The second string to be concatenated. It is appended to the end of the first string, completing the new combined string.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The concatenated result of the two input strings, returned as a single string.

convertKeyframeKeysToBatchKeys.description: The `convertKeyframeKeysToBatchKeys` node is designed to transform individual frame keys into a format suitable for batch processing, specifically by calculating a new key value that aligns with the batch's indexing requirements. This transformation facilitates the integration of frame-specific data into batch-oriented workflows, ensuring that each frame's data is correctly positioned within the batch structure.

inputs.name: input
inputs.description: Represents the individual frame key to be transformed. This parameter is crucial for identifying the specific frame whose data needs to be integrated into a batch process.

inputs.name: num_latents
inputs.description: Specifies the total number of latent variables or elements in the batch. This parameter is essential for correctly calculating the new key value, ensuring that the frame's data aligns with the batch's indexing structure.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: The transformed key value, ready for use in batch processing. This output is critical for aligning the frame's data with the batch's indexing requirements, facilitating efficient batch operations.

CosWave.description: The CosWave node generates a cosine wave based on various parameters such as phase, amplitude, and translations. It abstracts the mathematical complexity involved in creating a cosine wave, providing a simple interface for generating these waves for various applications.

inputs.name: phase
inputs.description: The 'phase' parameter adjusts the phase shift of the cosine wave, affecting its starting position on the x-axis. This allows for fine-tuning the wave's alignment with other elements or waves.

inputs.name: amplitude
inputs.description: The 'amplitude' parameter controls the height of the cosine wave, determining how far it extends above and below its central axis. This is crucial for adjusting the wave's intensity or impact.

inputs.name: x_translation
inputs.description: The 'x_translation' parameter shifts the entire wave along the x-axis, allowing for precise positioning of the wave in relation to other graphical or wave elements.

inputs.name: y_translation
inputs.description: The 'y_translation' parameter shifts the wave vertically, enabling the adjustment of the wave's baseline position on the y-axis.

inputs.name: current_frame
inputs.description: The 'current_frame' parameter specifies the current frame or point in time for which the wave's value is being calculated, enabling the generation of dynamic, moving waves.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The first element of the output tuple, representing the calculated wave value as a float.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: The second element of the output tuple, providing the integer representation of the wave's calculated value.

FizzFrame.description: The FizzFrame node is designed for creating and managing frames within a narrative or sequence, allowing for the dynamic generation of content based on positive and negative textual inputs. It leverages conditioning and pooling techniques to encode textual information, facilitating the creation of nuanced and contextually relevant frames.

inputs.name: frame
inputs.description: Specifies the identifier for the frame being created or manipulated. It serves as a key to organize and access frames within the sequence.

inputs.name: previous_frame
inputs.description: An optional reference to a previous frame, allowing for the inheritance of certain attributes and ensuring continuity within the sequence.

inputs.name: positive_text
inputs.description: The primary textual content intended to convey a positive aspect or sentiment within the frame. It forms the basis of the frame's positive conditioning.

inputs.name: negative_text
inputs.description: Optional textual content intended to convey a negative aspect or sentiment within the frame. It complements the positive text to provide a balanced perspective.

outputs.name: fizzframe
outputs.description: The newly created or updated frame, encapsulating the positive and negative conditioning along with any inherited or specified attributes.

outputs.name: conditioning
outputs.description: The conditioning information derived from the textual inputs, including both the condition and pooled output for positive and negative texts.

FizzFrameConcatenate.description: The FizzFrameConcatenate node is designed to concatenate frame-related information, specifically focusing on combining text and frame data to construct a comprehensive frame narrative. It operates by merging positive and negative textual content with frame identifiers, facilitating the creation of a structured and detailed frame representation.

inputs.name: frame
inputs.description: The frame input serves as the central data structure around which the concatenation process revolves, containing all necessary information for constructing the narrative.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: A concatenated string of frame identifiers and their associated texts, structured to represent a comprehensive narrative across multiple frames.

ImagesFromBatchSchedule.description: This node is designed to generate a batch of images based on a predefined schedule. It leverages a batch value schedule list to select and export images from an input batch, facilitating the creation of image sequences or animations. The node's functionality is rooted in the ability to process and manipulate image batches according to specified scheduling criteria, making it a valuable tool for dynamic image generation and manipulation tasks.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: Specifies the input batch of images to be processed and scheduled for output. This parameter is crucial for defining the source images that will be manipulated and organized according to the batch schedule.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: Defines the scheduling criteria or instructions as a text input, used to determine how images are selected and organized in the output batch.

inputs.name: current_frame
inputs.description: Indicates the current frame number in the sequence, used to track progression and manage image selection according to the schedule.

inputs.name: max_frames
inputs.description: Sets the maximum number of frames to be included in the output batch, limiting the sequence length according to this threshold.

inputs.name: print_output
inputs.description: A boolean flag that, when set to True, enables the printing of output information for debugging or informational purposes.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is a batch of images that have been selected and organized according to the specified schedule, ready for further processing or visualization.

Init FizzFrame.description: The Init FizzFrame node is designed to initialize the frame environment for further operations, setting up a foundational structure for managing and manipulating frame data within the FizzNodes framework.

inputs.name: frame
inputs.description: The 'frame' parameter is crucial as it serves as the primary identifier for the frame being initialized, dictating the starting point for frame-related operations.

inputs.name: positive_text
inputs.description: The 'positive_text' parameter allows for the specification of positive aspects or attributes associated with the frame, contributing to the frame's overall positive context.

inputs.name: negative_text
inputs.description: The 'negative_text' parameter enables the inclusion of negative aspects or attributes for the frame, adding to the frame's overall negative context.

inputs.name: general_positive
inputs.description: This parameter specifies general positive context that can be applied across frames, enhancing the positive aspect of the frame environment.

inputs.name: general_negative
inputs.description: Similar to 'general_positive', this parameter adds a general negative context applicable across frames, contributing to the frame environment's negative aspect.

inputs.name: previous_frame
inputs.description: The 'previous_frame' parameter is used to reference a prior frame, allowing for the continuation or modification of its context in the current frame initialization.

inputs.name: clip
inputs.description: The 'clip' parameter is intended for including CLIP model information, which can be utilized for further processing or conditioning of the frame data.

outputs.name: fizzframe
outputs.description: Returns a FizzFrame object, representing the initialized frame with its specified attributes and contexts.

outputs.name: conditioning
outputs.description: Provides conditioning information derived from the frame's positive and negative texts, facilitating further contextual processing.

InvCosWave.description: The InvCosWave node generates an inverse cosine wave based on specified parameters, such as phase, amplitude, and translations. It's designed to create complex wave patterns by applying the inverse cosine function to the input values, offering a unique approach to wave generation.

inputs.name: phase
inputs.description: The 'phase' parameter controls the period of the wave, affecting how stretched or compressed the wave appears over its cycle. A larger phase value results in a more stretched wave, impacting the frequency of the wave pattern generated.

inputs.name: amplitude
inputs.description: The 'amplitude' parameter determines the height of the wave's peaks, influencing the wave's overall intensity. Higher amplitude values produce waves with greater peak-to-trough distances, affecting the visual and numerical amplitude of the wave.

inputs.name: x_translation
inputs.description: The 'x_translation' parameter shifts the wave along the x-axis, allowing for adjustments in the wave's starting position. This shift can alter the phase of the wave, affecting where the wave begins within its cycle.

inputs.name: y_translation
inputs.description: The 'y_translation' parameter shifts the wave along the y-axis, adjusting the baseline level of the wave. This influences the vertical positioning of the wave, affecting its alignment relative to the y-axis.

inputs.name: current_frame
inputs.description: The 'current_frame' parameter specifies the current point in the wave's cycle, used to calculate the wave's value at that specific moment. This parameter is crucial for animating the wave over time, determining the wave's position at each frame.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The first element of the output is the calculated wave value as a float, representing the precise wave value.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: The second element of the output is the integer representation of the wave value, providing a rounded wave value.

InvSinWave.description: The InvSinWave node generates an inverse sine wave pattern, modifying the wave's amplitude based on the absolute value of the cosine function. It's designed for creating dynamic, wave-like animations or effects by adjusting parameters such as phase, amplitude, x translation, and y translation over a series of frames.

inputs.name: phase
inputs.description: Defines the period of the wave, affecting how many units it takes for the wave to complete one full cycle. A crucial parameter for controlling the wave's speed and spacing.

inputs.name: amplitude
inputs.description: Determines the height of the wave's peaks. This parameter influences the wave's intensity and the range of its vertical movement.

inputs.name: x_translation
inputs.description: Shifts the wave along the x-axis, allowing for horizontal positioning adjustments.

inputs.name: y_translation
inputs.description: Adjusts the wave's vertical positioning, allowing for vertical positioning adjustments.

inputs.name: current_frame
inputs.description: Specifies the current frame in the animation sequence, enabling the wave pattern to evolve over time.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: Outputs the calculated wave value, useful for precise wave calculations.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: Outputs the integer representation of the wave value, useful for scenarios requiring discrete values.

Lerp.description: The Lerp node linearly interpolates between two values based on a given strength and the current frame within a specified number of images. It's designed to smoothly transition or blend values across a sequence, making it useful for animations or gradual changes.

inputs.name: num_Images
inputs.description: Specifies the total number of images in the sequence. It determines the interpolation step size, affecting the smoothness of the transition.

inputs.name: strength
inputs.description: Defines the interpolation strength. It influences the range of output values, affecting how significantly the output changes across frames.

inputs.name: current_frame
inputs.description: Indicates the current frame number in the sequence. It's used to calculate the specific interpolation value for that frame, determining the output at each step.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The floating-point result of the linear interpolation, representing the interpolated value at the current frame.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: The integer representation of the interpolated value, providing a discretized output for scenarios requiring whole numbers.

PromptSchedule.description: The PromptSchedule node sequences user-formatted prompts, evaluates expressions within these prompts, and applies a scheduling mechanism to generate a batch of conditionings. This process involves sequencing the current and next prompts along with their conditioning strengths, ultimately producing a tailored output that incorporates the scheduled prompt adjustments.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: Represents the user's formatted prompt, serving as the primary input for generating conditionings. It is crucial for defining the content and structure of the desired output.

inputs.name: clip
inputs.description: A model or mechanism used for conditioning, influencing the generation process based on the input prompts.

inputs.name: max_frames
inputs.description: Specifies the maximum number of frames to be considered for the scheduling process, affecting the temporal scope of the generated outputs.

inputs.name: current_frame
inputs.description: Indicates the current frame in the sequence, used to determine the specific point of evaluation within the scheduling process.

inputs.name: print_output
inputs.description: unknown

inputs.name: pre_text
inputs.description: Optional pre-text added before the main prompt text, used to prepend additional context or instructions.

inputs.name: app_text
inputs.description: Optional appended text added after the main prompt text, used to append additional context or instructions.

inputs.name: pw_a
inputs.description: A weight parameter influencing the scheduling process, part of a set of parameters (pw_a, pw_b, pw_c, pw_d) for fine-tuning the output.

inputs.name: pw_b
inputs.description: A weight parameter influencing the scheduling process, part of a set of parameters (pw_a, pw_b, pw_c, pw_d) for fine-tuning the output.

inputs.name: pw_c
inputs.description: A weight parameter influencing the scheduling process, part of a set of parameters (pw_a, pw_b, pw_c, pw_d) for fine-tuning the output.

inputs.name: pw_d
inputs.description: A weight parameter influencing the scheduling process, part of a set of parameters (pw_a, pw_b, pw_c, pw_d) for fine-tuning the output.

outputs.name: POS
outputs.description: The positive conditioning output, reflecting the applied prompt schedule and targeted adjustments.

outputs.name: NEG
outputs.description: The negative conditioning output, reflecting the applied prompt schedule and targeted counteractions.

PromptScheduleEncodeSDXL.description: This node is designed to schedule and encode prompts specifically for the SDXL model, handling the process of tokenization, applying weighted combinations of prompts, and returning the conditioned output for either the current, next, or an averaged state. It focuses on enhancing the flexibility and precision of prompt conditioning in generative models.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Specifies the width of the image for which the prompt is being scheduled, affecting the spatial dimensions of the generated output.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Specifies the height of the image for which the prompt is being scheduled, affecting the spatial dimensions of the generated output.

inputs.name: crop_w
inputs.description: Defines the width of the crop area, which is used to refine the focus of the generated output within the specified width.

inputs.name: crop_h
inputs.description: Defines the height of the crop area, which is used to refine the focus of the generated output within the specified height.

inputs.name: target_width
inputs.description: The target width after processing, which may involve resizing or cropping to fit specific output requirements.

inputs.name: target_height
inputs.description: The target height after processing, which may involve resizing or cropping to fit specific output requirements.

inputs.name: text_g
inputs.description: Represents the global textual content to be scheduled and encoded, serving as a foundational element for generating prompts within the SDXL model.

inputs.name: clip
inputs.description: Specifies the clip model to be used in conjunction with the prompt for generating or refining outputs, integrating visual context or constraints into the prompt scheduling process.

inputs.name: text_l
inputs.description: unknown

inputs.name: max_frames
inputs.description: The maximum number of frames to be considered for scheduling, defining the temporal boundary of the animation or video output.

inputs.name: current_frame
inputs.description: The current frame number in the sequence, used to determine the specific state of prompt conditioning at any given time.

inputs.name: print_output
inputs.description: unknown

inputs.name: pre_text_G
inputs.description: Pre-text for global prompts, used to prepend additional context or instructions to the global text, enhancing the specificity of the generated output.

inputs.name: app_text_G
inputs.description: Append text for global prompts, used to add concluding remarks or instructions to the global text, further refining the output.

inputs.name: pre_text_L
inputs.description: Pre-text for local prompts, similar to global pre-text but applied to local or specific areas of interest within the generated output.

inputs.name: app_text_L
inputs.description: Append text for local prompts, similar to global append text but focused on enhancing local or specific areas within the output.

inputs.name: pw_a
inputs.description: Weight parameter A, part of a set of parameters used to adjust the influence of different prompts or aspects of the prompt on the final output.

inputs.name: pw_b
inputs.description: Weight parameter B, works in conjunction with other weight parameters to fine-tune the balance between various elements of the prompt.

inputs.name: pw_c
inputs.description: Weight parameter C, another factor in the complex equation of prompt weighting, contributing to the nuanced control over the generated output.

inputs.name: pw_d
inputs.description: Weight parameter D, completes the set of weight parameters, ensuring a comprehensive approach to prompt conditioning.

outputs.name: POS
outputs.description: The enhanced positive prompt, conditioned and ready for use in generating desired outputs with the SDXL model.

outputs.name: NEG
outputs.description: The adjusted negative prompt, conditioned to minimize its influence on the generated outputs.

PromptScheduleNodeFlow.description: This node is designed to dynamically construct and manipulate JSON strings based on input text and numerical parameters, facilitating the scheduling of content in a structured format. It primarily serves to augment input text with additional context or parameters, thereby enabling more complex or conditional content generation workflows.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The primary text input that will be included in the constructed JSON string, serving as the main content or subject of the scheduling operation.

inputs.name: num_frames
inputs.description: A numerical parameter that specifies the starting point for the scheduling operation, affecting the key under which the new content will be placed in the JSON structure.

inputs.name: in_text
inputs.description: An optional initial JSON string to which the new content will be appended, allowing for incremental construction of complex JSON structures.

inputs.name: max_frames
inputs.description: A numerical parameter that, when combined with 'num_frames', determines the key for the new content in the JSON structure, influencing the scheduling sequence.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: The new maximum frame count, derived from the input 'num_frames' and 'max_frames', indicating the next available key in the JSON structure.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The newly constructed JSON string, containing the scheduled content with keys based on the input parameters.

PromptScheduleNodeFlowEnd.description: This node represents the final step in a scheduling node flow, designed to evaluate and finalize the JSON structure produced by preceding nodes. It focuses on ensuring the integrity of the JSON output, making adjustments as necessary to fit the expected format for downstream processing.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The JSON text to be evaluated and potentially modified for format correctness. It plays a crucial role in the node's operation by serving as the primary data that will be adjusted to meet the expected output structure.

inputs.name: clip
inputs.description: A clip parameter that influences the animation and scheduling process, affecting the final output based on the clip's characteristics.

inputs.name: max_frames
inputs.description: Specifies the maximum number of frames to be considered in the scheduling process. It affects how the JSON text is evaluated, particularly in terms of frame-related adjustments.

inputs.name: print_output
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether the output should be printed, affecting the node's execution by potentially adding a debugging or logging step.

inputs.name: current_frame
inputs.description: Indicates the current frame being processed. This parameter is crucial for determining the specific adjustments needed for the JSON text based on the frame's context.

inputs.name: pre_text
inputs.description: Optional pre-text that can be prepended to the input text, affecting the context or framing of the animation.

inputs.name: app_text
inputs.description: Optional appended text that can be added to the input text, modifying the final animation's context or narrative.

inputs.name: pw_a
inputs.description: A weight parameter influencing the animation's dynamics or characteristics in a specific manner.

inputs.name: pw_b
inputs.description: A weight parameter influencing the animation's dynamics or characteristics in a specific manner.

inputs.name: pw_c
inputs.description: A weight parameter influencing the animation's dynamics or characteristics in a specific manner.

inputs.name: pw_d
inputs.description: A weight parameter influencing the animation's dynamics or characteristics in a specific manner.

outputs.name: POS
outputs.description: Represents the positive conditioning output, which is part of the final evaluated and adjusted JSON structure, contributing to the animation's positive aspects.

outputs.name: NEG
outputs.description: Represents the negative conditioning output, which is part of the final evaluated and adjusted JSON structure, contributing to the animation's negative aspects.

SawtoothWave.description: The SawtoothWave node is designed for generating and manipulating sawtooth waveforms, which are characterized by a linear rise and sharp fall. This node facilitates the creation of these periodic functions, allowing for their use in various applications that require such wave patterns.

inputs.name: phase
inputs.description: Defines the period of the sawtooth wave, affecting its repetition rate.

inputs.name: step_increment
inputs.description: Determines the incremental steps in the sawtooth wave's progression.

inputs.name: x_translation
inputs.description: Adjusts the horizontal positioning of the sawtooth wave.

inputs.name: start_value
inputs.description: Sets the starting value of the sawtooth wave, establishing its initial position.

inputs.name: current_frame
inputs.description: Indicates the current point in time for the wave's calculation, crucial for its dynamic progression.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The calculated wave value as a floating-point number.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: The integer representation of the calculated wave value.

SinWave.description: The SinWave node generates a sinusoidal wave based on various parameters such as phase, amplitude, and translations along the x and y axes. It is designed to produce a sine wave output that can be adjusted dynamically for different effects in visual or audio applications.

inputs.name: phase
inputs.description: The 'phase' parameter controls the phase shift of the sine wave, affecting where the wave starts along the x-axis. It is crucial for adjusting the wave's position relative to its cycle.

inputs.name: amplitude
inputs.description: The 'amplitude' parameter determines the height of the sine wave peaks, allowing for the adjustment of the wave's intensity or loudness in applications.

inputs.name: x_translation
inputs.description: The 'x_translation' parameter shifts the sine wave along the x-axis, enabling the wave to be moved horizontally.

inputs.name: y_translation
inputs.description: The 'y_translation' parameter shifts the sine wave vertically along the y-axis, allowing for the adjustment of the wave's baseline position.

inputs.name: current_frame
inputs.description: The 'current_frame' parameter specifies the current frame or point in time for which the wave's value is being calculated, essential for animating the wave over time.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The first output is the calculated sine wave value, representing the wave's current amplitude at the specified frame.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: The second output is the integer representation of the sine wave value, useful for applications requiring discrete values.

SquareWave.description: The SquareWave node generates a square wave pattern based on specified parameters such as phase, amplitude, and translations. It's designed to create distinct, square-shaped oscillations for various applications in signal processing and waveform generation.

inputs.name: phase
inputs.description: Defines the period of the square wave. A higher value results in a longer period between wave peaks.

inputs.name: amplitude
inputs.description: Determines the height of the square wave peaks. A larger amplitude results in taller peaks.

inputs.name: x_translation
inputs.description: Shifts the wave along the X-axis. This can be used to adjust the starting point of the wave.

inputs.name: y_translation
inputs.description: Shifts the wave along the Y-axis, adjusting the baseline level of the wave.

inputs.name: current_frame
inputs.description: Specifies the current frame or point in time for which the wave value is being calculated. This allows for dynamic wave generation over time.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The primary output of the wave calculation, representing the wave's value at the current frame.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: An integer representation of the wave's value at the current frame.

StringConcatenate.description: The `StringConcatenate` node is designed to merge multiple pairs of text and frame identifiers into a single string representation. This node is crucial for scenarios requiring the aggregation of textual data associated with specific frames, facilitating the creation of a structured text list that maps frame identifiers to their corresponding text.

inputs.name: text_a
inputs.description: `text_a` is the initial piece of text to be concatenated. Its inclusion is essential for starting the construction of the text list, serving as the foundation upon which additional text-frame pairs can be appended.

inputs.name: frame_a
inputs.description: `frame_a` represents the frame identifier associated with `text_a`. It is crucial for mapping `text_a` to a specific frame in the resulting text list, thereby organizing the text in a structured manner.

inputs.name: text_b
inputs.description: `text_b` is the second piece of text to be concatenated. It is appended to `text_a`, contributing to the expansion of the text list with more text-frame mappings.

inputs.name: frame_b
inputs.description: `frame_b` represents the frame identifier associated with `text_b`. Its inclusion further structures the text list by mapping `text_b` to another specific frame.

inputs.name: text_c
inputs.description: `text_c` is an optional third piece of text that can be concatenated if provided. It allows for the inclusion of additional text-frame pairs, enhancing the comprehensiveness of the text list.

inputs.name: frame_c
inputs.description: `frame_c`, if provided, represents the frame identifier for `text_c`. Including this parameter allows for the mapping of `text_c` to a specific frame, further enriching the text list.

inputs.name: text_d
inputs.description: `text_d` is an optional fourth piece of text for concatenation. Its provision enables the extension of the text list with more detailed text-frame associations.

inputs.name: frame_d
inputs.description: `frame_d` represents the frame identifier for `text_d` if provided. It plays a key role in associating `text_d` with a specific frame, adding more structure to the text list.

inputs.name: text_e
inputs.description: `text_e` is an optional fifth piece of text for concatenation. Including this text allows for a broader representation of text-frame pairs in the text list.

inputs.name: frame_e
inputs.description: `frame_e` represents the frame identifier for `text_e` if provided. It is important for mapping `text_e` to a specific frame, contributing to the detailed structuring of the text list.

inputs.name: text_f
inputs.description: `text_f` is an optional sixth piece of text for concatenation. Its inclusion further expands the text list with additional text-frame mappings.

inputs.name: frame_f
inputs.description: `frame_f` represents the frame identifier for `text_f` if provided. Including this parameter enhances the text list by associating `text_f` with a specific frame.

inputs.name: text_g
inputs.description: `text_g` is an optional seventh piece of text for concatenation. It allows for the inclusion of more text-frame pairs, maximizing the comprehensiveness of the text list.

inputs.name: frame_g
inputs.description: `frame_g` represents the frame identifier for `text_g` if provided. Its inclusion is crucial for mapping `text_g` to a specific frame, thereby completing the structured text list.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The output is a structured string that maps frame identifiers to their corresponding texts. This output is significant as it provides a comprehensive and organized representation of text associated with specific frames, facilitating further processing or analysis.

StringSchedule.description: This node is designed for scheduling and animating text and other elements within a given frame range. It supports dynamic text updates, conditional formatting based on frame-specific parameters, and the integration of various inputs to create complex animation sequences. The node facilitates the creation of animated visual content by interpolating between values or states across frames, enabling the development of engaging and dynamic presentations.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The primary text input for animation, serving as the base content or narrative to be animated or modified across frames.

inputs.name: max_frames
inputs.description: Specifies the maximum number of frames for the animation, defining the length of the animation sequence.

inputs.name: current_frame
inputs.description: Indicates the current frame number within the animation sequence, used to determine the specific modifications or animations to apply.

inputs.name: print_output
inputs.description: A boolean flag to enable or disable printing of the animation output for debugging or preview purposes.

inputs.name: pre_text
inputs.description: Optional text input that precedes the main text, used for adding introductory or contextual content to the animation.

inputs.name: app_text
inputs.description: Optional text input that appends to the main text, used for adding concluding or additional content to the animation.

inputs.name: pw_a
inputs.description: A parameter weight used for adjusting or influencing the animation or text modification process.

inputs.name: pw_b
inputs.description: A parameter weight used for adjusting or influencing the animation or text modification process.

inputs.name: pw_c
inputs.description: A parameter weight used for adjusting or influencing the animation or text modification process.

inputs.name: pw_d
inputs.description: A parameter weight used for adjusting or influencing the animation or text modification process.

outputs.name: POS
outputs.description: Outputs the positive conditioning or formatted text for the current frame, reflecting dynamic changes or emphasis.

outputs.name: NEG
outputs.description: Outputs the negative conditioning or formatted text for the current frame, providing contrast or alternative emphasis.

TriangleWave.description: The TriangleWave node generates a triangular wave pattern based on the provided parameters. It manipulates the wave's phase, amplitude, and translations along the x and y axes, as well as the current frame to produce a unique wave output.

inputs.name: phase
inputs.description: The 'phase' parameter determines the period of the triangular wave, affecting how frequently the wave pattern repeats over a given interval.

inputs.name: amplitude
inputs.description: The 'amplitude' parameter specifies the height of the triangular wave, influencing the peak values the wave can reach.

inputs.name: x_translation
inputs.description: The 'x_translation' parameter shifts the wave along the x-axis, allowing for horizontal adjustment of the wave's position.

inputs.name: y_translation
inputs.description: The 'y_translation' parameter shifts the wave along the y-axis, providing vertical adjustment to the base level of the wave.

inputs.name: current_frame
inputs.description: The 'current_frame' parameter indicates the specific point in time for which the wave's value is being calculated, playing a crucial role in the wave's progression.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The first element of the output tuple, representing the calculated wave value as a float.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: The second element of the output tuple, which is the integer representation of the calculated wave value.

ValueSchedule.description: The ValueSchedule node is designed to animate values over a sequence of frames based on keyframes defined in a text input. It modulates the current frame within the maximum frame range and computes interpolated values to provide dynamic, frame-specific outputs.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: A multiline string containing keyframes for animation, serving as the blueprint for generating interpolated values across frames.

inputs.name: max_frames
inputs.description: The maximum number of frames for the animation, setting an upper limit for frame modulation and interpolation.

inputs.name: current_frame
inputs.description: The current frame number, used to determine the specific value to be output based on the animation's progression.

inputs.name: print_output
inputs.description: A boolean flag that, when true, prints the current frame and its corresponding value for debugging purposes.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The interpolated value for the current frame as a floating-point number.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: The interpolated value for the current frame, cast to an integer.

ApplyInstantID.description: The ApplyInstantID node is designed to integrate InstantID technology into images, leveraging facial analysis and control networks to enhance or modify the image based on specified conditions. It utilizes a combination of model inputs and image processing techniques to apply identity-preserving transformations, ensuring the output aligns with user-defined positive and negative conditioning.

inputs.name: instantid
inputs.description: Represents the InstantID model configuration and weights, crucial for the identity transformation process.

inputs.name: insightface
inputs.description: Facial analysis model used to extract facial features from the image, essential for guiding the InstantID transformation.

inputs.name: control_net
inputs.description: Control network model that influences the strength and direction of the applied transformations.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed and transformed by the InstantID technology.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The underlying model used for generating the transformations.

inputs.name: positive
inputs.description: Positive conditioning phrases that guide the transformation towards desired attributes.

inputs.name: negative
inputs.description: Negative conditioning phrases that guide the transformation away from undesired attributes.

inputs.name: weight
inputs.description: Overall weight of the transformation, affecting the intensity of the applied changes.

inputs.name: start_at
inputs.description: Defines the starting point of the transformation process, allowing for gradual application.

inputs.name: end_at
inputs.description: Defines the ending point of the transformation process, ensuring the transformation is applied within a specific range.

inputs.name: image_kps
inputs.description: Optional keypoints image for more precise facial feature alignment.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: Optional mask to limit the transformation to specific areas of the image.

outputs.name: MODEL
outputs.description: The modified model after applying the InstantID transformations.

outputs.name: positive
outputs.description: Updated positive conditioning reflecting the applied transformations.

outputs.name: negative
outputs.description: Updated negative conditioning reflecting the applied transformations.

ApplyInstantIDAdvanced.description: The ApplyInstantIDAdvanced node is designed to enhance image generation with specific identity features by applying advanced conditioning techniques. It utilizes a combination of InstantID, insight face analysis, control net adjustments, and additional parameters to fine-tune the identity preservation and control in the generated images.

inputs.name: instantid
inputs.description: The InstantID parameter is crucial for providing the identity-specific features to be preserved or emphasized in the generated image.

inputs.name: insightface
inputs.description: Insightface parameter is used for face analysis, providing critical facial feature information that aids in the identity preservation process.

inputs.name: control_net
inputs.description: Control net parameter allows for fine-tuning and control over the generation process, ensuring the identity features are accurately applied.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image parameter serves as the base for identity application, where the identity features are to be preserved or emphasized.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: Model parameter specifies the generative model to be used in conjunction with identity features for image generation.

inputs.name: positive
inputs.description: Positive conditioning to emphasize certain identity features in the generated image.

inputs.name: negative
inputs.description: Negative conditioning to de-emphasize certain identity features in the generated image.

inputs.name: ip_weight
inputs.description: IP weight parameter adjusts the influence of identity preservation in the generation process.

inputs.name: cn_strength
inputs.description: CN strength parameter controls the strength of the control net adjustments in the identity application process.

inputs.name: start_at
inputs.description: Start at parameter defines the beginning point of identity feature application in the generation process.

inputs.name: end_at
inputs.description: End at parameter defines the end point of identity feature application in the generation process.

inputs.name: noise
inputs.description: Noise parameter introduces variability in the identity features application, enhancing the naturalness of the generated image.

inputs.name: combine_embeds
inputs.description: Combine embeds parameter determines the method of combining multiple identity embeddings for application in the image generation.

inputs.name: image_kps
inputs.description: Image keypoints parameter provides additional facial feature information for enhanced identity preservation.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: Mask parameter allows for selective application of identity features in the generated image, enhancing control over the preservation process.

outputs.name: MODEL
outputs.description: The output model after applying InstantIDAdvanced, incorporating the identity features and adjustments made through the input parameters.

outputs.name: positive
outputs.description: The enhanced positive conditioning output, reflecting the emphasized identity features in the generated image.

outputs.name: negative
outputs.description: The enhanced negative conditioning output, reflecting the de-emphasized identity features in the generated image.

ApplyInstantIDControlNet.description: This node is designed to apply a control network to modify facial embeddings based on specified conditions, leveraging insights from facial analysis and control network parameters to achieve targeted modifications in facial representations.

inputs.name: face_embeds
inputs.description: Facial embeddings that represent the key features of a face, serving as the input for targeted modifications.

inputs.name: control_net
inputs.description: The control network model used to apply modifications to the facial embeddings.

inputs.name: image_kps
inputs.description: Key points from the image that are used to guide the modifications applied by the control network.

inputs.name: positive
inputs.description: Positive conditioning phrases or keywords that guide the direction of the modifications.

inputs.name: negative
inputs.description: Negative conditioning phrases or keywords that specify undesired attributes to be avoided in the modifications.

inputs.name: strength
inputs.description: The intensity of the modifications applied by the control network.

inputs.name: start_at
inputs.description: The starting point in the process where modifications begin to be applied.

inputs.name: end_at
inputs.description: The ending point in the process where modifications cease to be applied.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: An optional mask that can be used to localize the modifications applied by the control network.

outputs.name: positive
outputs.description: The modified positive conditioning after applying the control network, reflecting the targeted modifications.

outputs.name: negative
outputs.description: The modified negative conditioning after applying the control network, reflecting the avoidance of specified undesired attributes.

FaceKeypointsPreprocessor.description: The FaceKeypointsPreprocessor node is designed to preprocess images by extracting facial keypoints. This process involves analyzing the input image to detect faces and compute their keypoints, which are essential for various facial analysis tasks.

inputs.name: faceanalysis
inputs.description: The 'faceanalysis' parameter is a model that has been loaded and prepared for face analysis. It is crucial for detecting faces within the image and extracting their keypoints, which are then used for further processing.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The 'image' parameter represents the input image to be processed. It is analyzed by the face analysis model to detect faces and extract their keypoints, which are essential for the preprocessing task.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is an image with facial keypoints extracted. This processed image is essential for tasks that require facial feature analysis, such as facial recognition or emotion detection.

InstantIDAttentionPatch.description: The InstantIDAttentionPatch node is designed to enhance the attention mechanism within a model by applying specialized patches. These patches adjust the model's attention based on various factors such as image embeddings, noise levels, and specific conditions, aiming to improve the model's focus and performance on tasks related to image and face recognition.

inputs.name: instantid
inputs.description: The instantid parameter represents the core configuration or model that the attention patching will be applied to, serving as the foundation for the modifications.

inputs.name: insightface
inputs.description: The insightface parameter is used for face analysis and feature extraction, providing critical data that influences how the attention patches are applied.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image parameter is the input image on which face analysis and feature extraction are performed, directly impacting the attention patching process.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model parameter refers to the neural network model that will be modified by the attention patches, affecting its attention mechanism.

inputs.name: weight
inputs.description: The weight parameter controls the influence of the attention patches on the model, allowing for fine-tuning of the patching effect.

inputs.name: start_at
inputs.description: The start_at parameter specifies the beginning point in the model's processing where the attention patches start to take effect, marking the initial phase of modification.

inputs.name: end_at
inputs.description: The end_at parameter defines the endpoint in the model's processing where the attention patches conclude their effect, delineating the final phase of modification.

inputs.name: noise
inputs.description: The noise parameter introduces randomness into the attention patching process, potentially enhancing the model's robustness and ability to generalize.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The mask parameter allows for selective application of the attention patches, targeting specific areas or features within the image for focused modification.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: This output type represents the modified model after the application of attention patches, reflecting the adjustments made to its attention mechanism.

outputs.name: face_embeds
outputs.description: This output type represents the face embeddings generated or utilized during the patching process, which are critical for the targeted modifications.

InstantIDFaceAnalysis.description: The InstantIDFaceAnalysis node is designed to load and prepare a face analysis model for further processing. It focuses on initializing the model with the specified provider (CPU, CUDA, ROCM) and setting it up for face detection and analysis tasks.

inputs.name: provider
inputs.description: Specifies the computation provider for the face analysis model, affecting where the model's computations are executed (e.g., on CPU, CUDA, or ROCM).

outputs.name: faceanalysis
outputs.description: Represents the initialized and prepared face analysis model ready for performing face detection and analysis.

InstantIDModelLoader.description: The InstantIDModelLoader node is designed to load and initialize the InstantID model from a specified file path. It prepares the model for further processing or analysis by loading its checkpoint and configuring it based on the file type, ensuring compatibility and readiness for InstantID operations.

inputs.name: instantid_file
inputs.description: Specifies the file path to the InstantID model to be loaded. This parameter is crucial for locating and loading the model's checkpoint for initialization and further use.

outputs.name: instantid
outputs.description: Returns the loaded and initialized InstantID model, ready for further processing or analysis within the InstantID framework.

IPAAdapterFaceIDBatch.description: IPAAdapterFaceIDBatch extends the capabilities of IPAdapterFaceID by introducing batch processing functionality, allowing for the efficient handling of multiple inputs simultaneously. This node is designed to enhance the adaptability and performance of image processing tasks, particularly those involving facial identification and manipulation, by leveraging batch operations.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: Specifies the model to be used for processing, serving as a core component of the node's operation.

inputs.name: ipadapter
inputs.description: Defines the IPAdapter to be utilized, indicating the specific adapter configuration for image processing.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: Represents the image input for processing, central to the node's functionality in handling visual data.

inputs.name: weight
inputs.description: Determines the weighting factor for the processing, influencing the outcome based on the specified value.

inputs.name: weight_faceidv2
inputs.description: Specifies the weighting factor for FaceID v2 processing, adjusting the influence of this specific feature on the overall processing.

inputs.name: weight_type
inputs.description: Indicates the type of weighting to be applied, affecting how weights are interpreted and utilized in processing.

inputs.name: combine_embeds
inputs.description: Defines the method for combining embeddings, which plays a crucial role in the integration and manipulation of image features.

inputs.name: start_at
inputs.description: Sets the starting point for processing, allowing for fine-tuned control over the operation's initiation.

inputs.name: end_at
inputs.description: Determines the ending point for processing, providing a mechanism to precisely define the scope of the operation.

inputs.name: embeds_scaling
inputs.description: Specifies the scaling approach for embeddings, impacting how image features are adjusted and integrated.

inputs.name: image_negative
inputs.description: Optional. Represents a negative image input, used for contrast or as a counterpoint in processing.

inputs.name: attn_mask
inputs.description: Optional. Defines an attention mask, enhancing the focus and specificity of processing on certain image areas.

inputs.name: clip_vision
inputs.description: Optional. Specifies the use of CLIP vision features, enriching the processing with advanced visual understanding capabilities.

inputs.name: insightface
inputs.description: Optional. Indicates the use of the InsightFace model, crucial for advanced facial identification tasks.

outputs.name: MODEL
outputs.description: Returns the processed model, reflecting the modifications and enhancements made during the operation.

outputs.name: face_image
outputs.description: Outputs the processed face image, showcasing the results of the facial identification and manipulation tasks.

IPAdapter.description: The IPAdapter node serves as a modular component designed to adapt and apply various image processing techniques to models within the ComfyUI framework. It enables the customization and enhancement of image generation processes through a diverse set of parameters and methods, facilitating a wide range of artistic and technical manipulations.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model parameter represents the neural network model to which the IPAdapter will apply its image processing techniques, serving as the foundation for the adaptations and enhancements performed by the node.

inputs.name: ipadapter
inputs.description: This parameter specifies the particular IPAdapter configuration or method to be applied, dictating the specific image processing techniques and customizations that will be executed on the model.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image parameter is the input image to be processed or manipulated by the IPAdapter, serving as the primary subject for the node's image processing techniques.

inputs.name: weight
inputs.description: Specifies the weight of the adaptation effect, allowing for fine-tuning of the intensity of the applied image processing techniques.

inputs.name: start_at
inputs.description: Defines the starting point of the effect application in a process, enabling phased or gradual application of image processing techniques.

inputs.name: end_at
inputs.description: Determines the endpoint of the effect application, allowing for precise control over how the image processing techniques conclude.

inputs.name: weight_type
inputs.description: Indicates the type of weighting method to be used, affecting how the adaptation effect is applied over the process.

inputs.name: attn_mask
inputs.description: An optional parameter that provides an attention mask to focus or exclude specific areas from the image processing effects.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The modified model after applying the specified IPAdapter techniques and parameters, showcasing the adaptations and enhancements.

IPAdapterAdvanced.description: The IPAdapterAdvanced node is designed to enhance image processing capabilities by applying advanced image processing techniques. It extends the functionality of simpler IP adapters, offering more sophisticated options for image manipulation and enhancement.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model parameter specifies the neural network model to be used for image processing. It plays a crucial role in determining the quality and type of image enhancements applied.

inputs.name: ipadapter
inputs.description: This parameter represents the specific IP adapter to be applied, dictating the nature of the image processing technique used.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed, serving as the base for all applied enhancements.

inputs.name: weight
inputs.description: Controls the intensity of the applied image processing effect, offering flexibility in the final image output.

inputs.name: weight_type
inputs.description: Specifies the method used to calculate the weight of the image processing effect, affecting how the effect is applied over time.

inputs.name: combine_embeds
inputs.description: Determines how multiple embeddings are combined during the image processing, impacting the final image's characteristics.

inputs.name: start_at
inputs.description: Defines the starting point of the effect applied by the IP adapter, allowing for fine-tuned control over the image processing.

inputs.name: end_at
inputs.description: Specifies the endpoint of the effect applied, enabling precise manipulation of the image enhancement process.

inputs.name: embeds_scaling
inputs.description: Specifies the scaling method for embeddings, affecting the influence of different components in the image processing.

inputs.name: image_negative
inputs.description: An optional image used to specify negative effects, enabling the exclusion of certain aspects from the final output.

inputs.name: attn_mask

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: Represents the images to be processed, allowing for batch processing of multiple images in a single operation.

inputs.name: weight
inputs.description: Determines the influence of the adapter's effect on the images, with the ability to adjust the intensity of the applied transformations.

inputs.name: weight_type

inputs.name: start_at

inputs.name: end_at

inputs.name: embeds_scaling

IPAdapterCombineEmbeds.description: The IPAdapterCombineEmbeds node is designed to merge multiple embedding vectors into a single, unified representation. This process enhances the ability to manipulate and generate images by combining various aspects of input embeddings, thereby enabling more complex and nuanced image synthesis.

inputs.name: embed1
inputs.description: The 'embed1' parameter represents the primary embedding vector to be combined with others. It serves as the foundational vector for the combination process, influencing the final, unified embedding output.

inputs.name: method
inputs.description: The 'method' parameter specifies the technique used to combine the embedding vectors, such as 'concat', 'add', 'subtract', 'average', 'norm average', 'max', or 'min'. This choice determines how the embeddings are merged, affecting the characteristics of the resulting vector.

inputs.name: embed2
inputs.description: The 'embed2' parameter represents an optional additional embedding vector to be combined with 'embed1'. It contributes to the diversity and richness of the final embedding output.

inputs.name: embed3
inputs.description: The 'embed3' parameter is another optional embedding vector that can be combined with 'embed1' and potentially 'embed2', further enriching the final embedding output.

inputs.name: embed4
inputs.description: The 'embed4' parameter provides an option to include yet another embedding vector in the combination process, adding to the complexity and detail of the resulting unified embedding.

inputs.name: embed5
inputs.description: The 'embed5' parameter allows for the inclusion of a fifth embedding vector, maximizing the potential for creating a highly nuanced and detailed final embedding output.

outputs.name: embeds
outputs.description: The output 'embeds' represents the unified embedding vector resulting from the combination of input embeddings according to the specified method. This combined embedding can be used for advanced image manipulation and generation tasks.

IPAdapterCombineParams.description: This node is designed to combine multiple sets of parameters for IP adapters, allowing for the flexible integration of various input parameters into a single, unified set. It supports the aggregation of images, attention masks, weights, weight types, and start and end points from up to five different parameter sets, facilitating complex parameter management and customization in image processing tasks.

inputs.name: params_i
inputs.description: A set of parameters to be combined. This generalized parameter name represents any of the up to five sets of parameters (params_1 to params_5) that can be provided. Each set contributes to the overall aggregation, enriching the combined parameters with its values. The index 'i' ranges from 1 to 5, indicating the position of the parameter set in the combination process.

outputs.name: ipadapter_params
outputs.description: The resulting combined set of parameters, encompassing aggregated values from up to five input parameter sets. This unified parameter set is ready for use in further image processing tasks.

IPAdapterCombineWeights.description: The IPAdapterCombineWeights node is designed to aggregate and combine weight values from two different sources, providing a unified set of weights and their count. This functionality is essential for operations that require the blending or merging of weight parameters from distinct inputs, facilitating more nuanced control over weight-based computations or adjustments.

inputs.name: weights_i
inputs.description: unknown

outputs.name: weights
outputs.description: The combined list of weights resulting from merging weights_1 and weights_2, reflecting the aggregate influence of both inputs.

outputs.name: count
outputs.description: The total number of weights in the combined list, providing a quantitative measure of the outcome of the combination process.

IPAdapterEncoder.description: The IPAdapterEncoder node is designed to encode images with specific adaptations, leveraging additional parameters such as weight and mask to fine-tune the encoding process. It aims to enhance image processing tasks by integrating clip vision capabilities and custom adaptations.

inputs.name: weight
inputs.description: A weight factor that influences the encoding process, allowing for fine-tuning of the adaptation effects on the image.

inputs.name: mask

inputs.name: clip_vision

IPAdapterFaceID.description: The IPAdapterFaceID node is designed to enhance image processing capabilities by integrating face identification features. It leverages advanced IPAdapter functionalities to apply face-specific adjustments and embeddings, aiming to improve the quality and relevance of generated images based on facial recognition.

inputs.name: model

inputs.name: ipadapter

inputs.name: weight_faceidv2
inputs.description: A float value specifically for adjusting the influence of FaceID v2 features, offering finer control over the face identification process.

inputs.name: weight_type

inputs.name: combine_embeds

inputs.name: end_at

inputs.name: embeds_scaling

IPAdapterNoise.description: The IPAdapterNoise node specializes in adding noise to images, offering customizable noise types, strengths, and blur levels. It can optionally work with existing images to enhance or modify their appearance with noise, providing a versatile tool for image processing tasks that require noise injection for effects or testing purposes.

inputs.name: type
inputs.description: Specifies the type of noise to be added to the image, affecting the visual characteristics of the noise applied.

inputs.name: strength
inputs.description: Determines the intensity of the noise added to the image, allowing for control over how pronounced the noise effect will be.

inputs.name: blur
inputs.description: Applies a Gaussian blur to the noise, with the ability to adjust the level of blur for a smoother or more subtle noise effect.

inputs.name: image_optional

IPAdapterPreciseStyleTransfer.description: The IPAdapterPreciseStyleTransfer node is designed for executing precise style transfer operations on images within a given model's framework. It leverages advanced image processing techniques to blend and transfer styles between images, offering fine-grained control over the style transfer process through a comprehensive set of parameters.

inputs.name: image

inputs.name: weight
inputs.description: Controls the intensity of the style transfer, allowing for adjustable influence of the style on the target image.

inputs.name: style_boost
inputs.description: Amplifies the effect of the style being transferred, providing an additional layer of control over the style's impact.

inputs.name: combine_embeds
inputs.description: Determines the method for combining embeddings from different sources, influencing the final outcome of the style transfer.

inputs.name: start_at
inputs.description: Defines the starting point of the style transfer effect within the model's processing layers, offering control over the depth of style application.

inputs.name: end_at
inputs.description: Sets the endpoint for the style transfer effect, allowing for precision in how deeply the style is integrated into the target image.

inputs.name: embeds_scaling
inputs.description: Specifies the approach for scaling embeddings, affecting the balance between key and value components in the style transfer.

inputs.name: image_negative

inputs.name: attn_mask
inputs.description: An optional attention mask that can be applied to focus or restrict the style transfer to specific regions of the image.

inputs.name: clip_vision
inputs.description: Optionally integrates CLIP vision models to enhance the style transfer with semantic understanding from textual or visual cues.

IPAdapterPreciseStyleTransferBatch.description: This node specializes in applying precise style transfer techniques to images in batch mode, leveraging advanced image processing algorithms to blend styles from one image to another with high fidelity. inputs.description: Adjusts the intensity of the style enhancement, enabling more pronounced style features in the transferred style.

IPAdapterPromptScheduleFromWeightsStrate.description: This node generates a prompt schedule based on a given weights strategy, dynamically adjusting the prompt sequence to align with the specified frame count and incorporating optional starting and ending frames. It's designed to tailor the prompt delivery in image processing tasks, ensuring that prompts are optimally distributed across the desired number of frames.

inputs.name: weights_strategy
inputs.description: A strategy dictating the distribution of weights across frames, including the total number of frames, and whether to add starting or ending frames. This strategy influences how the prompt schedule is generated, ensuring alignment with the frame-based processing requirements.

inputs.name: prompt
inputs.description: A multiline string input that represents the base prompt to be scheduled. This input is split and adjusted according to the weights strategy to fit the frame count, enhancing the relevance of the prompt at each frame.

outputs.name: prompt_schedule
outputs.description: A string representation of the scheduled prompts, formatted to align with the frame distribution specified by the weights strategy. This schedule is ready for use in frame-based image processing tasks.

IPAdapterRegionalConditioning.description: This node specializes in applying regional conditioning to images within the IPAdapter framework. This functionality is crucial for tasks requiring targeted adjustments or enhancements, such as modifying specific image regions without affecting the overall composition.
