It aims to provide a more nuanced and effective approach to prompt engineering, leveraging additional parameters and methods to fine-tune the interaction with the generative model.

inputs.name: handling
inputs.description: Specifies the method for handling and combining the positive and negative prompts, offering various strategies to tailor the prompt processing according to specific needs.

inputs.name: pos_g
inputs.description: Represents the global positive prompt input that the node will process, playing a crucial role in guiding the generative model towards producing desired outcomes.

inputs.name: pos_l
inputs.description: Serves as the local positive prompt input, providing additional context or emphasis to refine the output further.

outputs.name: pos_g
outputs.description: The processed global positive prompt, optimized for clarity and effectiveness in guiding the generative model.

outputs.name: pos_l
outputs.description: The refined local positive prompt, tailored to add specific context or emphasis to the generated output.

SDXL Prompt Styler (JPS).description: The SDXL Prompt Styler node is designed to enhance and stylize text prompts for image generation tasks. It processes and combines user-defined positive and negative prompts with predefined templates, incorporating additional stylistic elements such as artist and movie references, to create more detailed and focused prompts for generating images.

inputs.name: text_positive_g
inputs.description: The primary positive prompt to be stylized and enhanced. It serves as the main subject or theme for the image generation.

inputs.name: text_positive_l
inputs.description: A secondary positive prompt that can be combined with the primary prompt for additional detail or emphasis in the image generation process.

inputs.name: text_negative
inputs.description: A negative prompt that specifies undesired elements or themes to be excluded from the generated image.

inputs.name: artist
inputs.description: An artist's name to infuse the generated image with a style reminiscent of that artist's work.

inputs.name: movie
inputs.description: A movie reference to imbue the generated image with thematic elements or stylistic cues associated with that movie.

inputs.name: style
inputs.description: A general stylistic direction or theme to apply to the generated image, enhancing its aesthetic appeal.

inputs.name: fooocus_enhance
inputs.description: An optional parameter to further enhance the focus on certain elements within the generated image.

inputs.name: fooocus_negative
inputs.description: An optional parameter to specify elements that should be de-emphasized or excluded from the focus of the generated image.

inputs.name: universal_negative
inputs.description: A global negative prompt to exclude certain themes or elements from all generated images, regardless of other specified prompts.

outputs.name: text_positive_g
outputs.description: unknown

outputs.name: text_positive_l
outputs.description: unknown

outputs.name: text_positive
outputs.description: unknown

outputs.name: text_negative
outputs.description: unknown

SDXL Recommended Resolution Calc (JPS).description: This node calculates the recommended resolution for SDXL (Stable Diffusion XL) based on a target width and height, aiming to find the closest matching aspect ratio from a predefined set. It considers horizontal, vertical, and square aspect ratios to determine the most suitable resolution for generating images with the desired dimensions.

inputs.name: target_width
inputs.description: Specifies the desired width of the image. It plays a crucial role in determining the closest matching aspect ratio for the recommended resolution.

inputs.name: target_height
inputs.description: Specifies the desired height of the image. It is used alongside the target width to calculate the closest matching aspect ratio for the recommended resolution.

outputs.name: SDXL_width
outputs.description: The recommended width for the SDXL image, based on the closest matching aspect ratio.

outputs.name: SDXL_height
outputs.description: The recommended height for the SDXL image, based on the closest matching aspect ratio.

SDXL Resolutions (JPS).description: This node is designed to calculate and return the width and height dimensions based on a predefined set of resolutions. It supports various aspect ratios and resolutions, facilitating the selection of appropriate dimensions for different image orientations and sizes.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: Specifies the desired resolution from a predefined list, influencing the output dimensions of width and height. This selection determines the aspect ratio and size of the resulting image.

outputs.name: width
outputs.description: The calculated width dimension based on the selected resolution.

outputs.name: height
outputs.description: The calculated height dimension based on the selected resolution.

SDXL Settings (JPS).description: The SDXL Settings (JPS) node is designed to configure and provide essential settings for image generation processes, including resolution factors, sampler and scheduler types, and other parameters critical for controlling the output quality and characteristics of generated images.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: Specifies the resolution setting for the image generation, influencing the dimensions of the output image.

inputs.name: res_factor
inputs.description: Determines the resolution factor, affecting the detail level and quality of the generated image.

inputs.name: sampler_name
inputs.description: Selects the sampler to be used, impacting the sampling method for the image generation process.

inputs.name: scheduler
inputs.description: Chooses the scheduler type, influencing the scheduling strategy for the image generation steps.

inputs.name: steps
inputs.description: Defines the total number of steps in the image generation process, affecting the refinement of the output image.

inputs.name: cfg
inputs.description: Sets the configuration value, which adjusts the generation process's behavior and output characteristics.

inputs.name: cfg_rescale
inputs.description: Specifies the rescale value for the configuration, modifying how the configuration influences the generation process.

inputs.name: clip_skip
inputs.description: Indicates the number of clips to skip, affecting the processing of the image generation.

inputs.name: filename
inputs.description: The filename for the generated image, determining the output file's name.

outputs.name: sdxl_settings
outputs.description: Encapsulates a comprehensive set of settings used for the SDXL image generation process, including resolution, sampler, scheduler, and other configurations.

SDXL Settings Pipe (JPS).description: The SDXL Settings Pipe node is designed to process and return a comprehensive set of settings for image generation, including resolution, sampling, scheduling, and other configuration parameters. It abstracts the complexity of configuring various aspects of image generation into a simple interface, enabling users to easily specify and retrieve detailed settings for their image generation tasks.

inputs.name: sdxl_settings
inputs.description: Serves as the comprehensive input encapsulating all necessary settings for the SDXL image generation process. It is essential for determining the configuration and resultant behavior of the image generation.

outputs.name: image_res
outputs.description: The resolution of the generated image.

outputs.name: width
outputs.description: The width of the generated image in pixels.

outputs.name: height
outputs.description: The height of the generated image in pixels.

outputs.name: res_factor
outputs.description: A factor influencing the resolution of the generated image.

outputs.name: sampler_name
outputs.description: The name of the sampling method used for image generation.

outputs.name: scheduler
outputs.description: The scheduling method used during the image generation process.

outputs.name: steps
outputs.description: The number of steps to be taken in the image generation process.

outputs.name: cfg
outputs.description: A configuration parameter affecting the generation process.

outputs.name: cfg_rescale
outputs.description: A parameter for rescaling the configuration during the generation process.

outputs.name: clip_skip
outputs.description: Indicates the number of clipping steps to skip during the generation process.

outputs.name: filename
outputs.description: The name of the file where the generated image will be saved.

Substract Int Int (JPS).description: This node performs subtraction between two integer inputs, providing both integer and floating-point representations of the result. It is designed to facilitate mathematical operations within the JPS Nodes/Math category, offering a straightforward way to compute the difference between two numbers.

inputs.name: int_a
inputs.description: The first integer input for the subtraction operation. It serves as the minuend in the subtraction.

inputs.name: int_b
inputs.description: The second integer input for the subtraction operation. It acts as the subtrahend, being subtracted from the first input.

outputs.name: int_substract
outputs.description: The result of the subtraction operation as an integer.

outputs.name: float_substract
outputs.description: The result of the subtraction operation represented as a floating-point number, providing precision flexibility.

Text Concatenate (JPS).description: The Text Concatenate node is designed to merge multiple text inputs into a single string, using a specified delimiter to separate the texts. This functionality is essential for creating concatenated strings from various inputs, allowing for flexible text manipulation and aggregation.

inputs.name: delimiter
inputs.description: Specifies the type of delimiter to use between text inputs, such as a space or comma, influencing how the concatenated text is formatted.

inputs.name: text1
inputs.description: The first text input to be concatenated.

inputs.name: text2
inputs.description: The second text input to be concatenated, appended to the first input with the specified delimiter in between.

inputs.name: text3
inputs.description: The third text input to be concatenated, appended to the previous inputs with the specified delimiter in between.

inputs.name: text4
inputs.description: The fourth text input to be concatenated, appended to the previous inputs with the specified delimiter in between.

inputs.name: text5
inputs.description: The fifth text input to be concatenated, appended to the previous inputs with the specified delimiter in between.

outputs.name: text
outputs.description: The resulting string after concatenating the given text inputs with the specified delimiter.

Text Prompt (JPS).description: The Text Prompt (JPS) node is designed to receive a textual input and return it unchanged. It serves as a straightforward mechanism for inputting and outputting text within a workflow, essentially acting as a pass-through for text data.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: This parameter accepts a multiline string input, serving as the prompt text. It allows for dynamic prompts, enabling users to input text that can be dynamically processed or utilized within the node's workflow.

outputs.name: text
outputs.description: Outputs the same text string that was input, effectively acting as a pass-through for the text data.

Text Prompt Combo (JPS).description: The Text Prompt Combo node is designed to accept two distinct text inputs, typically representing positive and negative prompt texts, and returns them as is. This node facilitates the combination or juxtaposition of different textual inputs for further processing or generation tasks.

inputs.name: pos
inputs.description: Represents the positive prompt text, allowing for multiline input and dynamic prompt generation. It plays a crucial role in defining the positive aspect of the content to be generated or processed.

inputs.name: neg
inputs.description: Represents the negative prompt text, also allowing for multiline input and dynamic prompt generation. It is essential for specifying the negative aspect or elements to be excluded in the content generation or processing.

outputs.name: pos
outputs.description: Returns the positive prompt text as provided in the input, facilitating further content generation or processing tasks.

outputs.name: neg
outputs.description: Returns the negative prompt text as provided in the input, enabling the exclusion or negation of certain elements in content generation or processing.

Time Seed (JPS).description: The Time Seed node generates a unique seed value based on the current time, optionally allowing for a fixed seed to be specified. This functionality is crucial for ensuring reproducibility in processes that require randomization, by providing a way to initialize random number generators with a consistent starting point.

inputs.name: fixed_seed
inputs.description: Specifies a fixed seed value to be used instead of generating one based on the current time. If set to 0, a time-based seed is generated, ensuring variability with each execution.

outputs.name: seed
outputs.description: The generated seed value, which is either based on the current time or the specified fixed seed, used for initializing random number generators.

VAE Switch (JPS).description: The VAE Switch node is designed to select and output one of several provided Variational Autoencoder (VAE) models based on an integer selection input. It facilitates dynamic switching between different VAE models within a pipeline, allowing for flexible model selection during runtime.

inputs.name: select
inputs.description: Determines which VAE model to output, with each integer value corresponding to a specific VAE model input.

inputs.name: vae_i
inputs.description: Represents a generic VAE model input that can be selected for output. The index 'i' can range from 1 to 5, allowing for dynamic selection among multiple VAE models.

outputs.name: vae_out
outputs.description: The selected VAE model based on the 'select' input.

LayerColor_ AutoAdjust.description: The AutoAdjust node provides automated adjustments to the color properties of an image, including brightness, contrast, saturation, and individual color channels. It aims to enhance the image's overall appearance or correct its color balance based on specified parameters.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be adjusted. This parameter is crucial as it serves as the base for all subsequent color corrections and enhancements.

inputs.name: strength
inputs.description: Determines the intensity of the automatic adjustments applied to the image, affecting the overall impact of the correction.

inputs.name: brightness
inputs.description: Adjusts the brightness level of the image, influencing its lightness or darkness.

inputs.name: contrast
inputs.description: Modifies the contrast of the image, enhancing or reducing the difference between its light and dark areas.

inputs.name: saturation
inputs.description: Alters the saturation level, adjusting the intensity of the image's colors.

inputs.name: red
inputs.description: Adjusts the red color channel, allowing for fine-tuning of the image's red hues.

inputs.name: green
inputs.description: Adjusts the green color channel, enabling modifications to the image's green tones.

inputs.name: blue
inputs.description: Adjusts the blue color channel, facilitating adjustments to the blue hues in the image.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image after applying the auto adjustments, reflecting changes in color properties such as brightness, contrast, saturation, and color channels.

LayerColor_ AutoBrightness.description: The AutoBrightness node automatically adjusts the brightness of an image based on specified strength and saturation levels, optionally considering a mask to apply the adjustment selectively.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image to be processed for auto brightness adjustment. It serves as the primary input for the node's operation.

inputs.name: strength
inputs.description: Determines the intensity of the brightness adjustment. A higher value results in a more pronounced change.

inputs.name: saturation
inputs.description: Adjusts the saturation level of the image alongside brightness, allowing for a balanced color correction.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: An optional mask that can be applied to restrict the brightness adjustment to specific areas of the image.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image after auto brightness adjustment, reflecting changes in brightness and saturation.

LayerColor_ Brightness & Contrast.description: This node is designed to adjust the brightness, contrast, and saturation of images. It processes each image individually, allowing for fine-tuned enhancements to image aesthetics by modifying these three key visual parameters.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image or images to be processed. This parameter is crucial for the node's operation as it directly influences the visual output by applying the specified adjustments.

inputs.name: brightness
inputs.description: Determines the level of brightness adjustment to be applied to the input images. A pivotal parameter for altering the image's luminance.

inputs.name: contrast
inputs.description: Specifies the degree of contrast adjustment. This parameter is essential for enhancing or reducing the difference between the darkest and lightest tones in the image.

inputs.name: saturation
inputs.description: Controls the saturation level, affecting the intensity of the image's colors. It plays a significant role in the visual impact of the image.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output images after applying brightness, contrast, and saturation adjustments. This reflects the visual modifications made to the input images, showcasing the node's capability to enhance image aesthetics.

LayerColor_ Color of Shadow & Highlight.description: This node is designed to adjust the color properties of shadows and highlights within an image. It allows for the fine-tuning of brightness, saturation, and hue for both shadows and highlights, enabling users to achieve a desired visual effect or correct color imbalances.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed for shadow and highlight color correction.

inputs.name: shadow_brightness
inputs.description: Specifies the brightness level for shadows, affecting the overall darkness or lightness of shadow areas in the image.

inputs.name: shadow_saturation
inputs.description: Determines the saturation level for shadows, influencing the intensity of colors in shadowed regions.

inputs.name: shadow_hue
inputs.description: Adjusts the hue for shadows, allowing for the alteration of color tones in shadow areas.

inputs.name: shadow_level_offset
inputs.description: Offsets the level of shadows, modifying the threshold at which shadows are defined.

inputs.name: shadow_range
inputs.description: Defines the range of shadow levels, affecting the breadth of tones considered as shadows.

inputs.name: highlight_brightness
inputs.description: Defines the brightness level for highlights, impacting the luminosity of highlighted areas in the image.

inputs.name: highlight_saturation
inputs.description: Sets the saturation level for highlights, affecting the vibrancy of colors in highlighted regions.

inputs.name: highlight_hue
inputs.description: Modifies the hue for highlights, enabling changes in color tones within highlighted areas.

inputs.name: highlight_level_offset
inputs.description: Offsets the level of highlights, modifying the threshold at which highlights are defined.

inputs.name: highlight_range
inputs.description: Defines the range of highlight levels, affecting the breadth of tones considered as highlights.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: An optional mask to specify areas of the image to apply the shadow and highlight adjustments.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image after applying shadow and highlight color corrections.

LayerColor_ ColorAdapter.description: The ColorAdapter node is designed to adapt the color of an image to match a reference image's color scheme, applying a specified opacity level to blend the adapted image. It processes each image in a batch, adjusting colors to closely resemble the reference, and supports images with transparency by maintaining the alpha channel.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image or images to be color adapted. This parameter is crucial for defining the source images whose colors need to be adjusted to match the reference image.

inputs.name: color_ref_image
inputs.description: The reference image or images used to adapt the color scheme of the input images. It plays a key role in determining the target color profile for the adaptation process.

inputs.name: opacity
inputs.description: The opacity level applied to the blended image, affecting the intensity of the color adaptation. It allows for fine-tuning the strength of the color match between the input and reference images.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The batch of images after color adaptation, blended with the original images at the specified opacity level. It represents the final output where each image's color has been adjusted to match the reference.

LayerColor_ ColorBalance.description: The ColorBalance node is designed to adjust the color balance of images by modifying the cyan-red, magenta-green, and yellow-blue channels. It allows for fine-tuning of color hues to achieve a desired visual effect, enhancing or correcting the color composition of images.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image or images to be processed for color balance adjustment. This parameter is crucial for defining the visual content that will undergo color correction.

inputs.name: cyan_red
inputs.description: Adjusts the balance between cyan and red hues in the image, affecting the overall color temperature.

inputs.name: magenta_green
inputs.description: Adjusts the balance between magenta and green hues, influencing the color harmony and contrast.

inputs.name: yellow_blue
inputs.description: Modifies the balance between yellow and blue hues, impacting the image's warmth or coolness.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image or images after applying the color balance adjustments, reflecting the changes in color hues.

LayerColor_ ColorTemperature.description: This node adjusts the color temperature of an image, simulating warmer or cooler lighting conditions. It modifies the image's RGB values based on the specified temperature, enhancing the visual warmth or coolness.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed. Adjusting its color temperature simulates different lighting conditions.

inputs.name: temperature
inputs.description: The temperature value to adjust the image's color temperature. Positive values simulate warmer lighting, while negative values simulate cooler lighting.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The image with adjusted color temperature, reflecting the simulated lighting condition.

LayerColor_ Exposure.description: The Exposure node is designed to adjust the exposure level of images, allowing for the brightening or darkening of the image based on the specified exposure value. This node applies a mathematical transformation to the pixel values to simulate the effect of changing the camera's exposure setting, enhancing or reducing the image's overall luminance.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The 'image' parameter represents the input image(s) to be adjusted. It is crucial for determining the base visual content that will undergo exposure correction, directly influencing the outcome of the node's processing.

inputs.name: exposure
inputs.description: The 'exposure' parameter specifies the degree to which the image's exposure is adjusted. A positive value increases brightness, while a negative value decreases it, significantly affecting the visual result of the image processing.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output 'image' is the result of applying the exposure correction to the input image(s), reflecting the adjustments made based on the specified exposure level.

LayerColor_ Gamma.description: The Gamma node is designed for color correction by applying gamma correction to images. It adjusts the luminance of the images based on the gamma value provided, enhancing the visual quality of images by making them appear more natural or stylized according to the gamma setting.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image(s) to which gamma correction will be applied. This parameter is crucial for defining the visual content that will undergo the adjustment process.

inputs.name: gamma
inputs.description: The gamma value determines the intensity of the luminance adjustment. A higher gamma value darkens the image, while a lower value brightens it, playing a key role in achieving the desired visual effect.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image(s) after applying gamma correction, showcasing the adjusted luminance levels.

LayerColor_ HSV.description: This node is designed for color correction in the HSV color space, allowing adjustments to the hue, saturation, and value (brightness) of an image. It enables fine-tuning of image colors to achieve desired visual effects or correct color imbalances.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be color corrected. This parameter is crucial as it determines the base for all subsequent HSV adjustments.

inputs.name: H
inputs.description: Specifies the hue adjustment. Positive values shift the hue right, while negative values shift it left, enabling the modification of the image's overall color tone.

inputs.name: S
inputs.description: Determines the saturation level adjustment. Positive values increase saturation, making colors more vivid, while negative values decrease it, leading to a more muted color palette.

inputs.name: V
inputs.description: Controls the value (brightness) adjustment. Positive values make the image brighter, whereas negative values make it darker, affecting the image's lightness or darkness.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image after applying HSV color corrections. This reflects the adjustments made to hue, saturation, and value, showcasing the color-corrected version of the input image.

LayerColor_ LAB.description: The LayerColor: LAB node is designed for color correction in the LAB color space. It adjusts the L, A, and B channels of an image, allowing for precise control over the lightness, green-red, and blue-yellow components, respectively.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be color corrected. It serves as the base for applying LAB color space adjustments.

inputs.name: L
inputs.description: Adjusts the lightness of the image. A positive value increases lightness, while a negative value decreases it.

inputs.name: A
inputs.description: Modifies the green-red axis of the image. Positive values shift towards red, negative values towards green.

inputs.name: B
inputs.description: Alters the blue-yellow axis of the image. Positive values shift towards yellow, negative values towards blue.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The color-corrected image in the LAB color space, reflecting adjustments made to the L, A, and B channels.

LayerColor_ Levels.description: The 'LayerColor: Levels' node is designed for advanced color correction of images. It allows users to adjust the intensity levels of specific color channels, including black point, white point, and midtones (gray point), as well as to set the output range for these adjustments. This functionality is crucial for enhancing image contrast or correcting the color balance in images to achieve a desired aesthetic or to correct photographic errors.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed. This is the primary data on which color correction levels will be applied.

inputs.name: channel
inputs.description: Specifies the color channel(s) (RGB, red, green, blue) to be adjusted. This allows for targeted color correction on specific channels, enhancing flexibility in image editing.

inputs.name: black_point
inputs.description: Sets the black point threshold for the selected channel(s). Adjusting this value can alter the darkest parts of the image, affecting overall contrast and detail in shadows.

inputs.name: white_point
inputs.description: Defines the white point threshold for the selected channel(s). Modifying this value impacts the brightest parts of the image, influencing highlights and overall image brightness.

inputs.name: gray_point
inputs.description: Adjusts the midtone (gray point) level for the selected channel(s). This is crucial for fine-tuning the balance between shadows and highlights, affecting the image's overall tonal range.

inputs.name: output_black_point
inputs.description: Sets the output range's black point, allowing for further refinement of the image's contrast and depth.

inputs.name: output_white_point
inputs.description: Determines the output range's white point, enabling adjustments to the image's brightness and contrast levels.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image after applying the specified color correction levels. This image reflects the adjustments made to the intensity levels of the selected color channels.

LayerColor_ LUT Apply.description: The node applies a Look-Up Table (LUT) to images for color correction, supporting different color spaces. It enables the transformation of the color palette of images according to predefined LUT files, facilitating advanced color grading and adjustments.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image(s) to which the LUT will be applied. This is crucial for defining the visual content that will undergo color transformation.

inputs.name: LUT
inputs.description: Specifies the LUT file to be used for color correction. This determines the specific color transformation that will be applied to the input images.

inputs.name: color_space
inputs.description: Defines the color space of the input image(s), such as 'linear' or 'log', affecting how the LUT is applied and the final color correction outcome.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image(s) after applying the LUT, showcasing the result of the color correction process.

LayerColor_ RGB.description: This node is designed for color correction in RGB color space, allowing adjustments to the red, green, and blue channels of an image. It enables fine-tuning of the image's color balance by applying specific offsets to each color channel, enhancing or modifying the image's overall coloration.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be color corrected. It serves as the base for applying RGB adjustments, impacting the visual outcome of the color correction process.

inputs.name: R
inputs.description: The offset value for the red channel, which adjusts the intensity of red colors in the image. This parameter directly influences the image's red hues, allowing for nuanced color correction.

inputs.name: G
inputs.description: The offset value for the green channel, which adjusts the intensity of green colors in the image. This parameter is crucial for modifying the image's green hues, enabling detailed color adjustments.

inputs.name: B
inputs.description: The offset value for the blue channel, which adjusts the intensity of blue colors in the image. By altering this parameter, users can fine-tune the blue hues within the image, achieving desired color effects.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The color-corrected image, with adjustments applied to the red, green, and blue channels. This output reflects the cumulative effect of the RGB offsets on the original image, showcasing the enhanced or altered coloration.

LayerColor_ YUV.description: The node 'LayerColor: YUV' is designed for color correction in the YUV color space. It adjusts the Y (luminance), U (chrominance), and V (chrominance) components of an image to achieve desired color effects or corrections.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The 'image' parameter represents the input image(s) to be processed. It is crucial for the color correction operation, serving as the base upon which YUV adjustments are applied.

inputs.name: Y
inputs.description: The 'Y' parameter adjusts the luminance component of the image. Its modification affects the brightness and contrast of the image.

inputs.name: U
inputs.description: The 'U' parameter modifies the chrominance component related to blue color projection. Altering this value impacts the blue-yellow balance of the image.

inputs.name: V
inputs.description: The 'V' parameter adjusts the chrominance component associated with red color projection, influencing the red-green balance of the image.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output 'image' is the result of applying YUV color corrections to the input image(s), reflecting the adjustments made to luminance and chrominance components.

LayerFilter_ AddGrain.description: The AddGrain node is designed to apply a grain effect to images, enhancing their texture by adding a layer of visual noise. This process aims to simulate the grainy appearance often found in film photography, thereby adding a stylistic or aesthetic quality to digital images.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image(s) to which the grain effect will be applied. This parameter is crucial for defining the base upon which the grain effect will be overlaid, directly influencing the node's output. The choice of images determines the initial visual context for the grain effect, impacting both the aesthetic and technical aspects of the final output.

inputs.name: grain_power
inputs.description: Determines the intensity of the grain effect applied to the image, with higher values resulting in a more pronounced grain texture. This parameter allows for fine-tuning the visual impact of the grain on the image, significantly affecting the texture's visibility and overall feel of the processed image.

inputs.name: grain_scale
inputs.description: Controls the scale of the grain particles, affecting their size and distribution across the image. This parameter enables customization of the grain effect to achieve desired visual outcomes, influencing how natural or pronounced the grain appears in relation to the image's content.

inputs.name: grain_sat
inputs.description: Adjusts the saturation of the grain effect, influencing the color intensity of the grain particles. This parameter allows for the modulation of the grain's color characteristics to match the aesthetic needs of the image, affecting the colorfulness and vibrancy of the grain effect.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image(s) with the grain effect applied. This parameter represents the transformation of the input image(s) through the addition of grain, enhancing their texture and visual appeal.

LayerFilter_ ChannelShake.description: The ChannelShake node applies a unique visual effect to images by shifting the color channels (RGB) in specified directions and distances. This manipulation creates a shaking or displacement effect on the image, offering a creative way to alter the visual appearance based on angle and distance parameters.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to apply the channel shake effect. This parameter is crucial for defining the base image on which the effect will be applied.

inputs.name: distance
inputs.description: Specifies the distance of the channel shift. This parameter influences the intensity of the shaking effect, with larger values resulting in more pronounced shifts.

inputs.name: angle
inputs.description: Determines the angle at which the channels will be shifted. This affects the direction of the shake effect, allowing for a wide range of visual distortions.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Defines the order in which the RGB channels are shifted. This selection alters the visual outcome of the effect, offering various combinations for creative experimentation.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image after applying the channel shake effect. This image showcases the visual transformation achieved through the specified channel shifts.

LayerFilter_ ColorMap.description: The ColorMap node applies a specified color map to an image, optionally adjusting its opacity, to transform the visual appearance of the image. This node supports a variety of color maps, allowing for a wide range of aesthetic effects.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to which the color map will be applied. This is the primary data the node operates on, determining the visual output.

inputs.name: color_map
inputs.description: Specifies the color map to apply to the input image. The choice of color map affects the aesthetic and thematic presentation of the image.

inputs.name: opacity
inputs.description: Determines the opacity level of the color map applied to the image, allowing for fine-tuning of the visual effect.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image after the color map and opacity adjustments have been applied, showcasing the transformed visual appearance.

LayerFilter_ Film.description: The Film node applies a cinematic film effect to images, enhancing them with a specific aesthetic that emulates the look and feel of traditional film photography. This node is designed to transform digital images by applying various film-like attributes, such as color grading, grain, and contrast adjustments, to achieve a visually appealing, filmic quality.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The primary input for the Film node, representing the image to which the film effect will be applied. This parameter is crucial as it determines the base upon which all film-like transformations are performed.

inputs.name: center_x
inputs.description: Specifies the horizontal center of the effect focus, influencing how certain effects like blur and vignette are centered on the image.

inputs.name: center_y
inputs.description: Determines the vertical center of the effect focus, affecting the positioning of effects such as blur and vignette on the image.

inputs.name: saturation
inputs.description: Controls the intensity of the image's colors, allowing for either a more vivid or subdued color palette.

inputs.name: vignette_intensity
inputs.description: Adjusts the strength of the vignette effect, adding a darkened border that can focus attention towards the center of the image.

inputs.name: grain_power
inputs.description: Sets the intensity of the film grain effect, adding a textured, analog feel to the image.

inputs.name: grain_scale
inputs.description: Determines the scale of the grain effect, affecting how large or fine the grain particles appear.

inputs.name: grain_sat
inputs.description: Adjusts the saturation of the grain effect, influencing how pronounced the grain appears in color.

inputs.name: grain_shadows
inputs.description: Controls the visibility of grain in the darker areas of the image, allowing for more or less texture in shadows.

inputs.name: grain_highs
inputs.description: Adjusts the grain effect in the highlights, modifying how grain affects brighter areas of the image.

inputs.name: blur_strength
inputs.description: Sets the intensity of the blur effect, which can simulate depth of field or focus effects.

inputs.name: blur_focus_spread
inputs.description: Controls the spread of the blur effect around the focus point, affecting the transition between focused and blurred areas.

inputs.name: focal_depth
inputs.description: Determines the depth of the focal area, influencing how much of the image appears in focus.

inputs.name: depth_map
inputs.description: An optional parameter that provides a depth map for more advanced depth-based effects like variable blur.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output of the Film node is an image that has been processed to emulate the appearance of film, incorporating adjustments to color, grain, and contrast to enhance its cinematic quality.

LayerFilter_ FilmV2.description: The FilmV2 node applies a sophisticated film layer filter to images, enhancing them with a cinematic quality. It leverages advanced image processing techniques to simulate the aesthetic and characteristics of film photography, offering users a unique way to stylize their visuals.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The 'image' input type represents the image data to which the FilmV2 filter will be applied. It is crucial for defining the visual content that will undergo the transformation, serving as the foundation for the filter's effects.

inputs.name: center_x
inputs.description: Specifies the horizontal center of the effect focus area, influencing how certain effects like blur are centered on the image. It plays a key role in the placement of visual enhancements.

inputs.name: center_y
inputs.description: Defines the vertical center of the effect focus area, affecting the positioning of effects such as blur. Essential for tailoring the filter's impact to specific areas of the image.

inputs.name: saturation
inputs.description: Controls the intensity of the image's colors. Adjusting saturation can dramatically alter the mood and visual style of the output, making it a key parameter for customization.

inputs.name: vignette_intensity
inputs.description: Determines the strength of the vignette effect applied to the edges of the image, contributing to the cinematic feel by darkening the periphery.

inputs.name: grain_method
inputs.description: Selects the algorithm used to add grain to the image, offering options to customize the texture and appearance of the film effect. The choice between 'fastgrain' and 'filmgrainer' methods affects the texture and visual quality of the grain, with each method providing a distinct style and impact on the final image.

inputs.name: grain_power
inputs.description: Adjusts the intensity of the grain effect, allowing for fine-tuning the level of perceived film grain and texture.

inputs.name: grain_scale
inputs.description: Modifies the scale of the grain particles, affecting their size and visibility on the image. This parameter helps in achieving the desired level of detail and texture.

inputs.name: grain_sat
inputs.description: Sets the saturation level of the grain effect, influencing how colorfully the grain appears on the image.

inputs.name: filmgrainer_shadows
inputs.description: Controls the visibility of grain in the darker areas of the image, enabling more precise customization of the film effect in shadows.

inputs.name: filmgrainer_highs
inputs.description: Adjusts the grain effect in the highlights, allowing for nuanced control over the appearance of grain in brighter image areas.

inputs.name: blur_strength
inputs.description: Determines the intensity of the blur effect, which can be used to simulate depth of field or focus effects.

inputs.name: blur_focus_spread
inputs.description: Controls the spread of the blur effect around the focus point, affecting how gradually the image transitions from sharp to blurred.

inputs.name: focal_depth
inputs.description: Sets the depth at which the focus effect is centered, crucial for achieving realistic depth of field simulations.

inputs.name: depth_map
inputs.description: An optional input that provides a depth map for more advanced depth-based effects, such as variable blur based on distance from the camera. Including a depth map enables the node to apply blur effects more accurately by simulating the depth of field based on the map, thus enhancing the realism of the film effect.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output 'image' type is the transformed version of the input image, now bearing the distinctive qualities of the FilmV2 filter. It signifies the culmination of the filter's application, showcasing the enhanced cinematic effect.

LayerFilter_ GaussianBlur.description: The GaussianBlur node applies a Gaussian blur filter to images, effectively smoothing them by reducing high-frequency noise and details. This node is part of the LayerFilter category, focusing on enhancing or modifying the visual appearance of images through blurring techniques.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The 'image' parameter represents the input image(s) to be blurred. It is crucial for defining the visual content that will undergo the Gaussian blur transformation.

inputs.name: blur
inputs.description: The 'blur' parameter specifies the intensity of the Gaussian blur effect. A higher value results in a more pronounced blurring effect, directly influencing the smoothness of the output image.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output 'image' parameter is the result of applying the Gaussian blur filter to the input image(s), showcasing the transformed visual content with reduced noise and details.

LayerFilter_ HDREffects.description: The HDR Effects node is designed to enhance images by applying High Dynamic Range (HDR) effects, improving contrast, brightness, and color depth to simulate the HDR photography technique. This node aims to make images appear more vivid and closer to what the human eye perceives in real life, by adjusting various parameters such as shadow, highlight, and gamma intensity.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to which HDR effects will be applied. This is the primary input for the node, serving as the basis for all subsequent HDR enhancements.

inputs.name: hdr_intensity
inputs.description: Controls the overall intensity of the HDR effect, affecting how pronounced the HDR enhancements are on the image.

inputs.name: shadow_intensity
inputs.description: Adjusts the intensity of shadows in the image, making them lighter or darker to enhance depth and detail.

inputs.name: highlight_intensity
inputs.description: Adjusts the intensity of highlights in the image, enhancing brightness in lighter areas for a more dynamic range.

inputs.name: gamma_intensity
inputs.description: Controls the gamma correction level, affecting the mid-tones and overall brightness of the image.

inputs.name: contrast
inputs.description: Adjusts the contrast level of the image, enhancing the difference between light and dark areas.

inputs.name: enhance_color
inputs.description: Enhances the saturation and vibrancy of colors in the image, making them more vivid and pronounced.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image after applying HDR effects, showcasing enhanced contrast, brightness, and color depth.

LayerFilter_ LightLeak.description: The LightLeak node applies a light leak effect to images, simulating the accidental exposure of film to light, enhancing the visual appeal with a vintage or artistic flair. It allows customization of the light leak's appearance, including its position, hue, saturation, and opacity, to achieve a variety of visual effects.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to which the light leak effect will be applied. This is the primary canvas for the effect.

inputs.name: light
inputs.description: Specifies the type of light leak effect to apply, which can be a specific light pattern or a random selection from a predefined set.

inputs.name: corner
inputs.description: Determines the corner of the image where the light leak effect will be primarily applied, allowing for directional control of the effect.

inputs.name: hue
inputs.description: Adjusts the hue of the light leak effect, enabling color customization to match or contrast with the image.

inputs.name: saturation
inputs.description: Modifies the saturation of the light leak effect, allowing for more vivid or subdued color intensity.

inputs.name: opacity
inputs.description: Controls the opacity of the light leak effect, affecting its prominence and blend with the image.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image with the applied light leak effect, showcasing the enhanced visual appeal.

LayerFilter_ MotionBlur.description: The MotionBlur node applies a directional blur effect to images, simulating the appearance of movement or speed. It allows for the adjustment of the blur's angle and intensity, enabling the creation of dynamic visual effects that convey motion.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to which the motion blur effect will be applied. This parameter is crucial for defining the visual content that will undergo transformation.

inputs.name: angle
inputs.description: Specifies the angle of the motion blur, allowing for the simulation of movement in various directions. This parameter is key to customizing the directionality of the perceived motion.

inputs.name: blur
inputs.description: Determines the intensity of the motion blur effect, enabling control over how pronounced the motion appears in the image.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image with the motion blur effect applied, showcasing the simulated movement.

LayerFilter_ Sharp & Soft.description: The 'Sharp & Soft' node applies varying degrees of sharpness or softness to images, allowing for detailed enhancement or smoothing effects based on the selected mode. It dynamically adjusts filter parameters to achieve the desired level of image clarity or softness, enhancing visual quality or creating a more subtle, softened appearance.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The input images to be processed. This parameter is crucial as it directly influences the outcome by serving as the base for the sharpness or softness enhancement.

inputs.name: enhance
inputs.description: Specifies the degree of sharpness or softness to apply to the images, ranging from 'very sharp' to 'very soft'. This choice determines the intensity of the effect and directly impacts the visual characteristics of the output images.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The processed images, enhanced with the specified level of sharpness or softness. This output reflects the visual modifications applied to the input images, showcasing the effect of the chosen enhancement mode.

LayerFilter_ SkinBeauty.description: The SkinBeauty node enhances the visual quality of skin in images by applying smoothing, adjusting brightness, and improving overall skin texture. It utilizes advanced image processing techniques to selectively blur, adjust thresholds, and manage opacity to achieve a more aesthetically pleasing and natural-looking skin appearance.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image or images to be processed for skin beauty enhancement. This is the primary data on which the skin beauty effects will be applied.

inputs.name: smooth
inputs.description: Determines the degree of skin smoothing applied to the image. Higher values result in smoother skin.

inputs.name: threshold
inputs.description: Adjusts the brightness threshold for highlighting effects. This parameter helps in enhancing the skin's high points by making them brighter or more subdued.

inputs.name: opacity
inputs.description: Controls the opacity of the applied skin beauty effects, allowing for fine-tuning of the final image's look by blending the processed layer with the original.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The processed image with enhanced skin beauty effects applied.

outputs.name: beauty_mask
outputs.description: A mask that highlights the areas of the image where skin beauty effects have been applied.

LayerFilter_ SoftLight.description: The SoftLight node applies a soft lighting effect to images, enhancing their visual appeal by blending them with various lighting conditions. It utilizes advanced image processing techniques to adjust the brightness, contrast, and detail of images to simulate the effect of soft light, making it ideal for creating mood or atmosphere in visual content.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The primary image to which the soft light effect will be applied. This image serves as the base for the lighting adjustments.

inputs.name: soft
inputs.description: Controls the intensity of the soft light effect, allowing for fine-tuning of the blur amount applied to the image.

inputs.name: threshold
inputs.description: Determines the threshold for highlighting, affecting how light or dark areas are enhanced or subdued in the image.

inputs.name: opacity
inputs.description: Adjusts the opacity of the soft light effect, enabling control over how strongly the effect is applied to the image.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The image after the soft light effect has been applied, showcasing enhanced lighting and visual appeal.

LayerFilter_ WaterColor.description: The WaterColor node applies a watercolor effect to images, transforming their appearance with customizable line density and opacity levels to simulate the look of watercolor paintings.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to which the watercolor effect will be applied. This parameter is crucial for defining the base image that will undergo the transformation.

inputs.name: line_density
inputs.description: Controls the density of the lines in the watercolor effect, affecting the overall texture and detail of the resulting image.

inputs.name: opacity
inputs.description: Determines the opacity of the watercolor effect, allowing for fine-tuning of the visual impact on the original image.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image with the watercolor effect applied, showcasing the transformation from the original input.

LayerMask_ BiRefNetUltra.description: The BiRefNetUltra node is designed for advanced image processing, specifically focusing on background removal and refinement of layer masks. It leverages the BiRefNet architecture to achieve high-quality segmentation and mask generation, catering to applications requiring precise foreground-background separation.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The primary image input for processing, which the node uses to generate and refine masks based on the background and foreground segmentation.

inputs.name: detail_method
inputs.description: Specifies the method used for enhancing the detail of the mask, including options like 'VITMatte', 'VITMatte(local)', 'PyMatting', and 'GuidedFilter', to adjust the mask's precision and quality.

inputs.name: detail_erode
inputs.description: Determines the erosion level applied to the mask, affecting the mask's edge by reducing its size to remove small, unwanted foreground elements.

inputs.name: detail_dilate
inputs.description: Determines the dilation level applied to the mask, affecting the mask's edge by expanding its size to include additional foreground elements that might have been missed.

inputs.name: black_point
inputs.description: Sets the black point for histogram remapping, influencing the darkest areas of the mask to refine shadow details and contrast.

inputs.name: white_point
inputs.description: Sets the white point for histogram remapping, influencing the brightest areas of the mask to enhance highlights and details.

inputs.name: process_detail
inputs.description: A boolean flag that indicates whether to apply detailed processing to the mask, affecting the overall quality and precision of the mask refinement.

inputs.name: device
inputs.description: Specifies the computing device ('cuda' or 'cpu') used for processing, affecting performance and efficiency.

inputs.name: max_megapixels
inputs.description: Limits the maximum size of the image in megapixels to optimize processing time and resource usage, affecting the resolution of the processed image and mask.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The processed image with refined foreground-background separation, suitable for further use or visualization.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The generated mask that highlights the foreground by separating it from the background, ready for use in compositing or further processing.

LayerMask_ BlendIf Mask.description: The `BlendIfMask` node provides functionality for blending images based on specific color channel thresholds, allowing for complex masking operations that can dynamically adjust the visibility of layers or effects based on the underlying color values.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The primary image to be processed, serving as the base for the blend if operation.

inputs.name: invert_mask
inputs.description: Determines whether the mask should be inverted, affecting how the blend conditions are applied.

inputs.name: blend_if
inputs.description: Specifies the color channel (gray, red, green, blue) to be used for the blend if condition, dictating how the blending is controlled.

inputs.name: black_point
inputs.description: The threshold below which pixels are fully transparent in the blending operation, allowing for fine-tuning of dark areas.

inputs.name: black_range
inputs.description: Defines the range over which the transparency effect fades from fully transparent to fully opaque, offering control over the blend transition in dark areas.

inputs.name: white_point
inputs.description: The threshold above which pixels are fully opaque, enabling precise control over bright areas in the blend.

inputs.name: white_range
inputs.description: Determines the range over which the opacity effect transitions from fully opaque to fully transparent, facilitating smooth blending in bright areas.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: An optional mask that can be applied to further refine the blending operation, providing additional control over which parts of the image are affected.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The resulting mask after applying the blend if conditions, which can be used to selectively apply effects or layer visibility.

LayerMask_ CreateGradientMask.description: This node is designed to create gradient masks with customizable dimensions, gradient direction, scale, offset, and opacity. It allows for the creation of nuanced layer masks that can be applied to images for various effects, such as fading or blending.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Specifies the width of the gradient mask to be created. It determines the horizontal dimension of the resulting mask.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Specifies the height of the gradient mask to be created. It determines the vertical dimension of the resulting mask.

inputs.name: gradient_side
inputs.description: Determines the side from which the gradient starts. This affects the direction of the gradient applied to the mask.

inputs.name: gradient_scale
inputs.description: Controls the scale of the gradient effect within the mask, affecting how gradual or steep the gradient appears.

inputs.name: gradient_offset
inputs.description: Adjusts the starting point of the gradient within the mask, allowing for shifted gradient effects.

inputs.name: opacity
inputs.description: Sets the opacity level of the gradient mask, enabling transparency effects.

inputs.name: size_as
inputs.description: Optionally specifies another object's size to match for the gradient mask, providing flexibility in mask dimensions.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The resulting gradient mask, ready for application to images or layers for various visual effects.

LayerMask_ ImageToMask.description: The `LayerMask: ImageToMask` node is designed to transform images into masks, focusing on extracting and processing mask layers from given images. It utilizes image processing techniques to create or modify mask layers, which can be used for further image manipulation or analysis.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The `image` parameter specifies the input image from which the mask will be generated. It is the primary source for mask creation.

inputs.name: channel
inputs.description: The `channel` parameter selects the specific color channel or image property to be used for mask generation, such as luminance or specific color channels, influencing the mask's characteristics.

inputs.name: black_point
inputs.description: The `black_point` parameter sets the lower threshold for mask generation, converting pixels darker than this value to black in the resulting mask.

inputs.name: white_point
inputs.description: The `white_point` parameter sets the upper threshold for mask generation, converting pixels lighter than this value to white in the resulting mask.

inputs.name: gray_point
inputs.description: The `gray_point` parameter adjusts the mid-tone levels in the mask, affecting the contrast and detail of the mask.

inputs.name: invert_output_mask
inputs.description: The `invert_output_mask` parameter allows for the inversion of the generated mask, swapping its black and white areas.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The `mask` parameter, when provided, specifies an existing mask to be modified or combined with the newly generated mask from the image.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The output `mask` is the transformed or newly created mask layer, which has been processed according to the specified parameters. It can be used for further image manipulation or analysis.

LayerMask_ MaskBoxDetect.description: The node 'LayerMask: MaskBoxDetect' is designed to analyze and process image masks to detect and adjust bounding boxes. It supports various detection modes, including minimum bounding rectangle, maximum inscribed rectangle, and mask area detection. Additionally, it allows for adjustments in scale and position, providing flexibility in handling mask-based spatial data for image editing or analysis tasks.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The 'mask' parameter represents the input image mask for which the bounding box needs to be detected. It plays a crucial role in determining the area of interest within the image.

inputs.name: detect
inputs.description: The 'detect' parameter specifies the method to be used for bounding box detection, offering options like minimum bounding rectangle, maximum inscribed rectangle, or mask area detection. This choice affects the algorithm's approach to analyzing the mask.

inputs.name: x_adjust
inputs.description: The 'x_adjust' parameter allows for horizontal adjustment of the detected bounding box, enabling fine-tuning of its position relative to the original mask.

inputs.name: y_adjust
inputs.description: The 'y_adjust' parameter enables vertical adjustment of the detected bounding box, allowing for precise positioning adjustments.

inputs.name: scale_adjust
inputs.description: The 'scale_adjust' parameter modifies the scale of the detected bounding box, offering the ability to resize it according to specific requirements.

outputs.name: box_preview
outputs.description: An image with the detected bounding box drawn over the original mask, providing a visual preview of the detection result.

outputs.name: x_percent
outputs.description: The horizontal center position of the detected bounding box, expressed as a percentage of the mask's width.

outputs.name: y_percent
outputs.description: The vertical center position of the detected bounding box, expressed as a percentage of the mask's height.

outputs.name: width
outputs.description: The width of the detected bounding box.

outputs.name: height
outputs.description: The height of the detected bounding box.

outputs.name: x
outputs.description: The x-coordinate of the top-left corner of the detected bounding box.

outputs.name: y
outputs.description: The y-coordinate of the top-left corner of the detected bounding box.

LayerMask_ MaskByColor.description: The MaskByColor node is designed to generate masks based on specific color criteria within images. It allows for the creation of layer masks by isolating areas that match a given color, with options to adjust the threshold for color matching, invert the mask, and apply gap fixing to improve mask quality.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image on which the mask generation is based. This image is analyzed to identify areas that match the specified color criteria.

inputs.name: color
inputs.description: Specifies the target color for mask generation. This parameter is crucial for determining which areas of the image will be isolated to create the mask.

inputs.name: color_in_HEX
inputs.description: A hexadecimal string representing the target color for mask generation. This provides an alternative method for specifying the color, offering flexibility in defining the color criteria.

inputs.name: threshold
inputs.description: Determines the sensitivity of color matching. A lower threshold results in a more inclusive selection of matching colors, while a higher threshold restricts the match to colors more closely resembling the specified target color.

inputs.name: fix_gap
inputs.description: Activates gap fixing in the mask to close small holes or gaps. This parameter can enhance the mask's quality by ensuring more continuous and coherent masked areas.

inputs.name: fix_threshold
inputs.description: Sets the threshold for gap fixing, controlling the size of gaps to be filled. This parameter works in conjunction with 'fix_gap' to refine the mask's details and overall appearance.

inputs.name: invert_mask
inputs.description: When enabled, inverts the generated mask, swapping the masked and unmasked areas. This option allows for flexibility in selecting either the matching areas or their complements.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: unknown

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: Returns a tensor of the generated mask, isolating areas matching the specified color criteria, adjusted for threshold, inversion, and gap fixing settings.

LayerMask_ MaskByDifferent.description: This node is designed to create a mask based on differences between two images, enabling the identification and isolation of unique elements. It facilitates dynamic segmentation by analyzing and contrasting the visual characteristics present in each layer.

inputs.name: image_i
inputs.description: The first and second images to be compared, serving as reference points for identifying differences. These images are used to detect variations and unique features, enabling the creation of a mask that highlights these differences.

inputs.name: gain
inputs.description: Adjusts the sensitivity of the difference detection, influencing the intensity of the identified changes.

inputs.name: fix_gap
inputs.description: Defines the tolerance for gap fixing in the generated mask, helping to smooth and refine the mask's edges.

inputs.name: fix_threshold
inputs.description: Sets the threshold for fixing gaps within the mask, further enhancing mask accuracy by refining edge details.

inputs.name: main_subject_detect
inputs.description: A boolean flag that, when enabled, focuses the difference detection on the main subject of the images, potentially improving the relevance of the generated mask.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The resulting mask that highlights the differences between the two input images, isolating unique elements and features.

LayerMask_ MaskEdgeShrink.description: The MaskEdgeShrink node is designed to process image masks by shrinking their edges, optionally inverting the masks, and applying a level of softness to the edge transitions. It allows for detailed control over the edge modification process, including the ability to preserve certain edge details while reducing others, making it suitable for creating stylized or more precise mask boundaries in image editing and compositing tasks.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The input mask to be processed. It serves as the primary data for edge modification, determining the areas of the image where edge shrinking will be applied.

inputs.name: invert_mask
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether the input mask should be inverted before processing. Inversion can be useful for operations targeting the area outside the original mask.

inputs.name: shrink_level
inputs.description: Specifies the intensity of the edge shrinking operation. Higher values result in more significant edge reduction.

inputs.name: soft
inputs.description: Determines the softness of the edge transitions after shrinking, allowing for smoother or more abrupt changes at the mask edges.

inputs.name: edge_shrink
inputs.description: Controls the amount of edge that is specifically targeted for shrinking, enabling precise manipulation of edge width.

inputs.name: edge_reserve
inputs.description: Defines the extent to which original edge details are preserved during the shrinking process, allowing for a balance between edge reduction and detail retention.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The processed mask with shrunken edges, returned as a tensor. This output reflects the modifications applied to the original mask, including any inversion, softening, and detail preservation specified.

LayerMask_ MaskEdgeUltraDetail V2.description: This node specializes in enhancing the detail and precision of mask edges in layer masks, utilizing advanced techniques to refine edges for improved visual clarity and accuracy. It offers a sophisticated approach to mask edge processing, catering to needs for high-detail and precision in image editing tasks.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image(s) to be processed. This parameter is crucial for determining the areas where mask edge refinement is applied, directly influencing the outcome of the node's operation.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The mask(s) corresponding to the input image(s), indicating areas of interest for edge refinement. The precision of mask edges is enhanced based on this parameter, making it essential for targeted detail improvement.

inputs.name: method
inputs.description: Specifies the technique used for mask edge refinement, affecting the level of detail and precision achieved in the processed mask edges.

inputs.name: mask_grow
inputs.description: Determines the extent to which mask edges are expanded, playing a key role in the overall edge refinement process.

inputs.name: fix_gap
inputs.description: Controls the gap filling in mask edges, aiding in creating smoother and more continuous edges.

inputs.name: fix_threshold
inputs.description: Sets the threshold for fixing gaps in mask edges, contributing to the refinement of edge detail and continuity.

inputs.name: edge_erode
inputs.description: Defines the amount of erosion applied to mask edges, crucial for achieving the desired level of edge detail and precision.

inputs.name: edte_dilate
inputs.description: Specifies the dilation applied to mask edges after erosion, balancing the edge refinement process by restoring some of the eroded details.

inputs.name: black_point
inputs.description: Adjusts the black point in the image, affecting the contrast and visibility of mask edges.

inputs.name: white_point
inputs.description: Adjusts the white point in the image, influencing the brightness and clarity of mask edges.

inputs.name: device
inputs.description: Indicates the computing device (CPU or GPU) used for processing, affecting the performance and efficiency of the node.

inputs.name: max_megapixels
inputs.description: Limits the maximum size of images processed, ensuring efficient memory usage and performance.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The processed image(s) with refined mask edges, showcasing enhanced detail and precision.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The refined mask(s) with improved edge detail, corresponding to the processed image(s).

LayerMask_ MaskEdgeUltraDetail.description: This node specializes in enhancing the detail and precision of edges in layer masks. It applies advanced image processing techniques to refine mask edges, making them ultra-detailed and precise for improved visual quality in layered compositions.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed. This image serves as the base for mask edge enhancement, determining the areas where detail and precision are to be improved.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The mask that outlines the areas of the image to be detailed. It acts as a guide for the node to apply edge enhancement, defining the regions where ultra-detailing is necessary.

inputs.name: method
inputs.description: Specifies the technique used for mask edge detailing. This parameter influences the approach taken to enhance the mask edges, affecting the outcome's precision and detail.

inputs.name: mask_grow
inputs.description: Controls the expansion of the mask edges. This parameter adjusts how much the mask edges are grown to achieve the desired level of detail.

inputs.name: fix_gap
inputs.description: Determines whether to fill gaps in the mask edges. This option helps in creating a more continuous and precise edge by bridging small gaps.

inputs.name: fix_threshold
inputs.description: Sets the threshold for fixing gaps in the mask edges. It defines the sensitivity of gap detection and filling, impacting the smoothness of the final edge.

inputs.name: detail_range
inputs.description: Defines the range of edge detailing. This parameter sets the extent to which the mask edges are enhanced, affecting the level of detail achieved.

inputs.name: black_point
inputs.description: Adjusts the black point for edge detailing. This setting modifies the darkest areas of the mask, influencing the contrast and depth of the edge detail.

inputs.name: white_point
inputs.description: Adjusts the white point for edge detailing. This setting modifies the lightest areas of the mask, influencing the brightness and highlight of the edge detail.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The processed image with enhanced mask edges. This output reflects the improvements in edge detail and precision, showcasing the node's effect on the original image.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The enhanced mask with ultra-detailed edges. This output demonstrates the refined precision and detail achieved through the node's processing.

LayerMask_ MaskGradient.description: The `MaskGradient` node is designed to apply gradient effects to masks, enhancing visual aesthetics or highlighting specific areas. It leverages gradient parameters to dynamically adjust the appearance of input masks, offering a versatile tool for image manipulation and layer styling within graphical interfaces.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The mask input represents the target image mask to which the gradient effect will be applied. It is crucial for defining the area of effect and the base for gradient application.

inputs.name: invert_mask
inputs.description: This parameter determines whether the input mask should be inverted before applying the gradient effect, allowing for flexibility in targeting either the masked area or its inverse.

inputs.name: gradient_side
inputs.description: Specifies the side of the mask where the gradient effect begins, enabling directional control over the gradient application.

inputs.name: gradient_scale
inputs.description: Controls the scale of the gradient effect, affecting how the gradient transitions across the mask area.

inputs.name: gradient_offset
inputs.description: Adjusts the starting point of the gradient effect within the mask, offering additional customization for the gradient's positioning.

inputs.name: opacity
inputs.description: Sets the opacity level of the gradient effect, allowing for fine-tuning of the visual impact on the mask.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The output is a tensor containing the modified mask(s) with the applied gradient effect, showcasing the visual transformation.

LayerMask_ MaskGrain.description: The MaskGrain node applies a grain effect to a given mask, optionally inverting the mask and adjusting the grain intensity for a more textured appearance. It's designed to enhance or modify the visual texture of layer masks in image processing workflows, providing a tool for creative and detailed mask manipulation.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The 'mask' parameter represents the input mask to which the grain effect will be applied. It is crucial for defining the area of the image that will be affected by the grain texture.

inputs.name: grain
inputs.description: The 'grain' parameter determines the intensity of the grain effect applied to the mask. A higher value results in a more pronounced grain texture, allowing for customizable visual effects.

inputs.name: invert_mask
inputs.description: The 'invert_mask' parameter allows for the inversion of the input mask before applying the grain effect, enabling flexibility in how the grain texture is applied to the image.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The output is a modified mask with the grain effect applied, potentially inverted based on the input parameters. It's suitable for further image processing or as a final textured mask in creative projects.

LayerMask_ MaskGrow.description: The MaskGrow node is designed to modify image masks by inverting, growing, and blurring them to achieve a desired visual effect. This node allows for the dynamic adjustment of mask boundaries and texture, facilitating more nuanced and flexible image manipulation.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The 'mask' parameter represents the image mask to be processed. It is the primary input for transformations, determining the base form on which the node operates.

inputs.name: invert_mask
inputs.description: The 'invert_mask' parameter controls whether the input mask should be inverted before processing. This inversion can be crucial for achieving specific visual effects or mask manipulations.

inputs.name: grow
inputs.description: The 'grow' parameter specifies the amount by which the mask's boundaries should be expanded or contracted, allowing for dynamic resizing of the mask area.

inputs.name: blur
inputs.description: The 'blur' parameter determines the intensity of the blur effect applied to the mask's edges, enabling the creation of softer or more pronounced boundaries.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The output 'mask' is the transformed version of the input mask, after applying the specified inversion, growth, and blur operations.

LayerMask_ MaskInvert.description: The MaskInvert node is designed to invert the values of a given mask, transforming white areas to black and vice versa. This operation is essential for tasks that require the opposite representation of mask areas, such as highlighting regions of interest in image processing or computer vision applications.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The 'mask' input is the primary data the node operates on, representing the areas to be inverted. It plays a crucial role in determining the output, as the inversion process directly transforms this mask.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The output 'mask' is the result of inverting the input mask, with all originally white areas turned black and vice versa, ready for further processing or analysis.

LayerMask_ MaskMotionBlur.description: The MaskMotionBlur node applies a motion blur effect to a mask, optionally inverting the mask before processing. It allows for the customization of the blur intensity and direction, enabling dynamic visual effects on mask elements.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The mask to which the motion blur effect will be applied. It serves as the primary input for the transformation.

inputs.name: invert_mask
