inputs.description: A boolean flag that determines whether the input mask should be inverted before applying the motion blur effect. Inversion can highlight or alter areas of interest.

inputs.name: blur
inputs.description: Specifies the intensity of the motion blur effect. Higher values result in a more pronounced blur, simulating faster motion.

inputs.name: angle
inputs.description: Defines the angle of the motion blur effect, allowing for directional blurring that simulates motion in a specific direction.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The resulting mask after applying the motion blur effect, potentially inverted based on the input flag.

LayerMask_ MaskPreview.description: The MaskPreview node is designed to generate a visual preview of a mask by transforming it into an image format suitable for visualization. It extends the functionality of saving images by specifically handling mask data, ensuring that masks can be easily reviewed and verified within a workflow.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The 'mask' input is crucial for generating a preview of the mask. It represents the mask data that will be transformed into a visual format. The processing of this input directly influences the appearance of the generated preview, making it essential for visual verification of mask conditions.

LayerMask_ MaskStroke.description: The MaskStroke node is designed to process image masks by applying transformations such as inversion, growth, width adjustment, and blurring to create stylized stroke effects around the mask's edges. It's aimed at enhancing visual elements by dynamically modifying mask boundaries for artistic or design purposes.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The 'mask' parameter represents the input image mask to be transformed. It is crucial for defining the area where stroke effects will be applied, serving as the base for subsequent modifications.

inputs.name: invert_mask
inputs.description: The 'invert_mask' parameter allows for the inversion of the input mask, flipping the areas to be considered as the foreground and background. This inversion is essential for achieving desired visual effects based on the mask's context.

inputs.name: stroke_grow
inputs.description: Specifies the growth or shrinkage of the stroke's inner boundary, adjusting the mask's coverage area before applying the stroke width. It's key for fine-tuning the effect's intensity and reach.

inputs.name: stroke_width
inputs.description: Determines the thickness of the stroke applied around the mask's edges, directly influencing the visual prominence of the stroke effect.

inputs.name: blur
inputs.description: Controls the level of blur applied to the stroke, smoothing the edges for a more refined or subtle effect.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The transformed mask with the applied stroke effect, showcasing the adjustments made to the original mask through inversion, growth, width modification, and blurring.

LayerMask_ MediapipeFacialSegment.description: This node leverages the Mediapipe library to perform facial feature segmentation on images. It extracts specific facial features based on user input, such as eyes, eyebrows, lips, and teeth, and generates corresponding masks for each feature.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image on which facial feature segmentation is to be performed. It is essential for identifying and extracting the facial features.

inputs.name: left_eye
inputs.description: A boolean indicating whether to include the left eye in the facial feature segmentation. This affects the output mask by including or excluding the left eye region.

inputs.name: left_eyebrow
inputs.description: A boolean indicating whether to include the left eyebrow in the segmentation. This choice influences the resulting mask by determining if the left eyebrow area is segmented.

inputs.name: right_eye
inputs.description: A boolean parameter that controls whether the right eye's region is included in the segmentation output. It affects the mask generation process by including or excluding the right eye.

inputs.name: right_eyebrow
inputs.description: Determines whether the right eyebrow is included in the facial feature segmentation. This parameter influences the mask creation by specifying if the right eyebrow area should be segmented.

inputs.name: lips
inputs.description: Indicates whether the lips should be segmented in the facial feature extraction. This parameter affects the output by including or excluding the lips in the generated mask.

inputs.name: tooth
inputs.description: Controls whether the teeth are included in the segmentation. This affects the final mask by determining if the teeth area is segmented.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The original image with facial features segmented based on the input parameters.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: A mask image highlighting the segmented facial features. Each feature segmented based on the input parameters is represented in the mask.

LayerMask_ PersonMaskUltra V2.description: This node specializes in generating a precise mask for individuals within an image, leveraging advanced segmentation techniques to accurately distinguish human figures from the background. LayerMask_ PixelSpread.description: The PixelSpread node is designed to apply a pixel spreading effect to images, potentially using a mask to guide the effect. It can adjust the spread based on the mask's properties, allowing for dynamic image manipulation that can enhance visual effects or achieve specific artistic styles.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The primary image to which the pixel spread effect will be applied. It serves as the canvas for the effect, determining the overall visual outcome.

inputs.name: invert_mask
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether the mask should be inverted before applying the pixel spread effect, affecting which parts of the image are manipulated.

inputs.name: mask_grow
inputs.description: An integer specifying the amount by which to grow the mask before applying the pixel spread, influencing the extent of the effect.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: An optional mask image that guides the pixel spread effect, allowing for selective application of the effect to specific areas of the image. The presence or absence of the mask can significantly alter the node's behavior, enabling more precise control over which parts of the image are affected by the pixel spread, thus directly impacting the visual outcome.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The processed image with the pixel spread effect applied, showcasing the visual transformation.

LayerMask_ RemBgUltra.description: The `LayerMask: RemBgUltra` node specializes in removing backgrounds from images with an emphasis on high detail preservation. It leverages advanced techniques to ensure that even fine details like hair or fur edges are retained after background removal, making it ideal for tasks requiring precise foreground extraction.

inputs.name: detail_range

inputs.name: white_point

It processes images to extract foreground elements by applying advanced techniques to improve edge definition and reduce artifacts, making it suitable for complex image compositions.

inputs.name: black_point

LayerMask_ SegmentAnythingUltra V2.description: This node specializes in segmenting various objects within an image, leveraging advanced algorithms to accurately distinguish and isolate different elements. It's designed to enhance layer-based editing by providing precise segmentation capabilities, making it a valuable tool for complex image manipulation tasks.

inputs.name: threshold
inputs.description: Sets the threshold for segmentation, defining the sensitivity of the algorithm in distinguishing between different elements within the image.

inputs.name: detail_method
inputs.description: Chooses the method for enhancing detail in the segmentation, allowing for finer control over the clarity and precision of the segmented elements.

inputs.name: detail_erode
inputs.description: Specifies the amount of erosion to apply to the details in the segmentation, helping to refine the edges and boundaries of segmented elements.

inputs.name: detail_dilate
inputs.description: Determines the amount of dilation for the details, enhancing the visibility and prominence of segmented elements.

inputs.name: black_point
inputs.description: Sets the black point for the segmentation, adjusting the darkest areas of the image for better contrast and visibility of elements.

inputs.name: white_point
inputs.description: Defines the white point, modifying the brightest areas of the image to improve the segmentation's overall appearance and clarity.

inputs.name: process_detail

inputs.name: prompt

LayerMask_ Shadow & Highlight Mask.description: This node is designed to generate shadow and highlight masks for images, allowing for detailed manipulation of lighting effects in image processing tasks. It processes images to extract or enhance shadows and highlights based on specified level offsets and ranges, supporting both aesthetic adjustments and functional analysis.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The primary image input for which shadow and highlight masks are to be generated. It plays a crucial role in determining the areas of shadow and highlight to be enhanced or extracted.

inputs.name: shadow_level_offset
inputs.description: Specifies the offset for shadow levels, adjusting the intensity of shadows in the image. This parameter fine-tunes the shadow mask generation process.

inputs.name: shadow_range
inputs.description: Defines the range of shadow levels to be considered, affecting the breadth of shadows captured in the mask. It helps in customizing the depth and extent of shadows.

inputs.name: highlight_level_offset
inputs.description: Specifies the offset for highlight levels, adjusting the brightness of highlights in the image. This parameter fine-tunes the highlight mask generation process.

inputs.name: highlight_range
inputs.description: Defines the range of highlight levels to be considered, affecting the breadth of highlights captured in the mask. It helps in customizing the intensity and extent of highlights.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: An optional mask that can be applied to the image to focus the shadow and highlight mask generation on specific areas, enhancing processing efficiency and precision.

outputs.name: shadow_mask
outputs.description: The generated mask that emphasizes shadows in the image, useful for further image manipulation or analysis.

outputs.name: highlight_mask
outputs.description: The generated mask that emphasizes highlights in the image, useful for further image manipulation or analysis.

LayerMask_ YoloV8Detect.description: The YoloV8Detect node is designed for object detection within images, utilizing the YOLOv8 model to identify and segment objects. It supports the generation of masks for detected objects, allowing for selective application or removal of effects based on the presence of specific objects within an image. This node can handle multiple images, merge detected object masks according to specified criteria, and return both the original images with detected objects highlighted and the corresponding masks.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image on which object detection and segmentation are to be performed. It is crucial for identifying and segmenting objects within the image using the YOLOv8 model.

inputs.name: yolo_model
inputs.description: Specifies the YOLOv8 model to be used for object detection. This parameter is essential for configuring the detection process according to the model's capabilities and requirements.

inputs.name: mask_merge
inputs.description: Determines how detected object masks should be merged. It can either merge all masks into one or merge a specified number of masks, affecting the final mask output.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The final merged mask for all processed images, suitable for further processing or visualization.

outputs.name: yolo_plot_image
outputs.description: Images with detected objects highlighted, useful for visualizing the detection results.

outputs.name: yolo_masks
outputs.description: Individual masks for detected objects, before any merging is applied. Useful for detailed analysis or selective processing.

LayerStyle_ ColorOverlay V2.description: The ColorOverlay V2 node applies a color overlay to an image, allowing for the adjustment of blend mode, opacity, and color to achieve various visual effects. It supports the inversion of a mask for more complex layering and styling options.

inputs.description: Specifies the background image over which the color overlay will be applied. It is a foundational element for the overlay effect.

inputs.name: layer_image
inputs.description: Defines the layer image to which the color overlay effect will be applied, enabling the creation of layered visual effects.

inputs.name: invert_mask

inputs.description: Optional mask that can be applied to the layer image for more precise control over the overlay effect.

LayerStyle_ ColorOverlay.description: The ColorOverlay node applies a color overlay to an image, allowing for the adjustment of blend mode, opacity, and color to achieve various visual effects. It supports the use of an optional layer mask for more precise control over the overlay application.

inputs.description: An optional mask that can be applied to the overlay, offering enhanced control over the areas affected by the color overlay.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The resulting image after applying the color overlay, incorporating all specified adjustments.

LayerStyle_ DropShadow V2.description: The DropShadow V2 node applies an advanced drop shadow effect to images, enhancing visual depth and realism. It processes input images by adding a customizable shadow based on parameters such as distance, blur, and color, effectively simulating the appearance of a shadow cast by the layer onto its background.

inputs.name: background_image
inputs.description: The background image over which the shadow and layer will be composited. It serves as the canvas for the drop shadow effect, providing context and depth to the layered image.

inputs.name: layer_image
inputs.description: The image of the layer to which the drop shadow effect will be applied. This image is composited over the background image, with the shadow effect enhancing its visual separation and depth.

inputs.name: invert_mask
inputs.description: A boolean flag that indicates whether the mask should be inverted. This affects how the shadow is applied relative to the mask, allowing for more flexible shadow effects.

inputs.name: blend_mode
inputs.description: Specifies the blending mode to be used when applying the shadow, affecting how the shadow merges with the layer and background images.

inputs.name: opacity
inputs.description: The opacity level of the shadow, determining how transparent the shadow appears over the background. It allows for fine-tuning the intensity of the shadow effect.

inputs.name: distance_x
inputs.description: The horizontal distance by which the shadow is offset from the layer, simulating the direction and distance of the light source relative to the layer.

inputs.name: distance_y
inputs.description: The vertical distance by which the shadow is offset from the layer, further contributing to the realism of the shadow effect by simulating elevation.

inputs.name: grow
inputs.description: Determines the extent to which the shadow expands beyond the original boundaries of the layer, simulating the diffusing effect of light.

inputs.name: blur
inputs.description: The level of blur applied to the shadow, simulating the softness of the shadow's edges. This parameter affects the shadow's realism and how it blends with the background.

inputs.name: shadow_color
inputs.description: The color of the shadow, allowing for customization of the shadow effect to match the aesthetic of the image or scene.

inputs.name: layer_mask
inputs.description: An optional mask that defines the area of the layer image where the drop shadow should be applied. It helps in fine-tuning the shadow effect by specifying which parts of the layer image should cast a shadow.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The resulting image after applying the drop shadow effect, combining the background, layer images, and the generated shadow into a single composited image.

LayerStyle_ DropShadow.description: The DropShadow node applies a drop shadow effect to an image layer, enhancing its visual depth by simulating a shadow cast behind it. This node processes input images to add shadows based on specified parameters such as distance, direction, color, and blur, effectively creating a more dynamic and visually appealing composition.

inputs.name: layer_image

inputs.name: distance_y

inputs.name: grow
inputs.description: The amount by which the shadow expands beyond the original boundaries of the layer, making the shadow appear larger or smaller.

inputs.name: blur

inputs.description: The color of the drop shadow, allowing customization to match the aesthetic of the composition.

inputs.name: layer_mask
inputs.description: An optional mask that defines the area of the layer image where the drop shadow effect should be applied. It helps in fine-tuning the shadow effect by restricting it to specific parts of the layer image.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The resulting image after applying the drop shadow effect, combining the background, layer, and the generated shadow into a single image.

LayerStyle_ GradientOverlay V2.description: This node applies a version 2 gradient overlay effect to images, allowing for enhanced visual styling through the manipulation of gradient colors, blend modes, and opacity settings. It is designed to process multiple images, applying the gradient overlay to each based on specified parameters, and supports handling of mask mismatches by dropping incompatible masks, ensuring the final composition maintains visual consistency.

inputs.name: background_image
inputs.description: The background image over which the gradient overlay will be applied. It serves as the base layer for the overlay effect, determining the underlying visual context.

inputs.name: layer_image
inputs.description: The layer image to which the gradient overlay effect will be applied. This image is composited over the background image using specified gradient parameters and blending options.

inputs.name: invert_mask
inputs.description: A boolean flag to indicate whether the mask should be inverted, affecting how the overlay applies to masked areas.

inputs.name: blend_mode
inputs.description: Specifies the blending mode to be used when applying the gradient overlay, influencing the final visual effect.

inputs.name: opacity
inputs.description: Defines the opacity level of the gradient overlay, allowing for control over the transparency of the applied effect.

inputs.name: start_color
inputs.description: The starting color of the gradient, marking the beginning of the gradient effect.

inputs.name: start_alpha
inputs.description: The alpha value (transparency) for the start color of the gradient, affecting the beginning of the gradient effect's transparency.

inputs.name: end_color
inputs.description: The ending color of the gradient, marking the end of the gradient effect.

inputs.name: end_alpha
inputs.description: The alpha value (transparency) for the end color of the gradient, affecting the end of the gradient effect's transparency.

inputs.name: angle
inputs.description: The angle at which the gradient is applied, determining the direction of the gradient effect across the image.

inputs.name: layer_mask
inputs.description: An optional mask that defines the area of the layer image to be affected by the gradient overlay. If provided, it allows for more precise control over where the gradient effect is applied.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The resulting image after the application of the gradient overlay effect, incorporating the specified styling enhancements.

LayerStyle_ GradientOverlay.description: The GradientOverlay node applies a gradient overlay effect to images, allowing for the blending of layer images with background images using specified gradients, blend modes, and opacity settings. It provides a way to enhance visual aesthetics or achieve specific design goals by modifying the appearance of images.

inputs.name: background_image
inputs.description: The background image over which the gradient overlay will be applied. It serves as the base layer for the overlay effect.

inputs.name: layer_image
inputs.description: The layer image to which the gradient overlay effect will be applied. This image is blended with the background image according to the specified gradient and blend mode.

inputs.name: invert_mask
inputs.description: A boolean flag to indicate whether the mask should be inverted. This affects which parts of the layer image the gradient overlay will be applied to.

inputs.name: blend_mode
inputs.description: The blend mode used to combine the layer image with the background image under the gradient overlay effect.

inputs.name: opacity
inputs.description: The opacity level of the gradient overlay, determining how transparent the overlay appears over the background image.

inputs.name: start_color
inputs.description: The starting color of the gradient overlay. It defines the initial color of the gradient effect applied to the layer image.

inputs.name: start_alpha
inputs.description: The starting opacity of the gradient overlay, affecting the transparency of the start color.

inputs.name: end_color
inputs.description: The ending color of the gradient overlay. It specifies the final color in the gradient transition applied to the layer image.

inputs.name: end_alpha
inputs.description: The ending opacity of the gradient overlay, affecting the transparency of the end color.

inputs.name: angle
inputs.description: The angle at which the gradient is applied, affecting the direction of the color transition on the layer image.

inputs.name: layer_mask
inputs.description: An optional mask that can be used to limit the area of the layer image affected by the gradient overlay. If provided, it specifies the exact areas where the gradient effect should be applied.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The resulting image after applying the gradient overlay effect, combining the background and layer images with the specified gradient, blend mode, and opacity settings.

LayerStyle_ InnerGlow V2.description: The InnerGlow V2 node is designed to apply an inner glow effect to images, enhancing their visual appeal by adding a soft light from within. This node focuses on creating a more vibrant and dynamic look for graphical elements by simulating the effect of light emanating from the inside out.

inputs.name: background_image
inputs.description: The base image over which the inner glow effect will be applied, serving as the backdrop for the effect.

inputs.name: layer_image
inputs.description: The image layer to which the inner glow effect will be applied, directly influencing the appearance of the glow.

inputs.name: invert_mask
inputs.description: A boolean flag to invert the mask applied to the layer image, affecting the areas where the glow effect is visible.

inputs.name: blend_mode
inputs.description: Specifies the blending mode used to combine the glow effect with the layer image, impacting the overall look of the effect.

inputs.name: opacity
inputs.description: Controls the opacity level of the inner glow effect, allowing for fine-tuning of its visibility.

inputs.name: brightness
inputs.description: Adjusts the brightness of the inner glow effect, influencing its intensity and spread.

inputs.name: glow_range
inputs.description: Defines the range of the glow effect, determining how far the glow extends from the layer image.

inputs.name: blur
inputs.description: Sets the blur amount for the glow effect, contributing to its softness and diffusion.

inputs.name: light_color
inputs.description: The color at the center of the glow effect, setting the tone for the light source.

inputs.name: glow_color
inputs.description: The color at the outer edge of the glow effect, defining the peripheral color transition.

inputs.name: layer_mask
inputs.description: An optional mask that can be applied to the layer image, dictating the specific areas where the glow effect is applied.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The resulting image after applying the inner glow effect, showcasing the enhanced visual appeal with a soft, emanating light.

LayerStyle_ InnerGlow.description: The InnerGlow node applies an inner glow effect to images, enhancing visuals by adding a soft light from within the subject. This effect can be used to create depth or highlight elements in a composition, contributing to the overall aesthetic appeal.

inputs.name: background_image
inputs.description: The 'background_image' input serves as the base layer onto which the inner glow effect is applied, providing the context and foundation for the effect.

inputs.name: layer_image
inputs.description: The 'layer_image' input specifies the target layer within the background image to which the inner glow effect will be applied, allowing for precise control over the effect's placement.

inputs.name: invert_mask
inputs.description: The 'invert_mask' input determines whether the mask applied to the layer image should be inverted, affecting how the inner glow effect interacts with the image's transparency.

inputs.name: blend_mode
inputs.description: The 'blend_mode' input allows for the selection of blending modes that determine how the inner glow effect combines with the underlying images, offering various visual outcomes.

inputs.name: opacity
inputs.description: The 'opacity' input controls the transparency level of the inner glow effect, enabling fine-tuning of its visual impact on the final image.

inputs.name: brightness
inputs.description: The 'brightness' input adjusts the intensity of the inner glow effect, influencing the overall luminosity and visibility of the effect.

inputs.name: glow_range
inputs.description: The 'glow_range' input specifies the spread of the inner glow effect, determining how far the effect extends from the edges of the layer image.

inputs.name: blur
inputs.description: The 'blur' input defines the level of blur applied to the inner glow effect, contributing to the softness and diffusion of the light.

inputs.name: light_color
inputs.description: The 'light_color' input sets the color of the light at the center of the inner glow effect, allowing for customization of the effect's hue.

inputs.name: glow_color
inputs.description: The 'glow_color' input determines the color of the outer edge of the inner glow effect, enabling the creation of a gradient or solid color glow.

inputs.name: layer_mask
inputs.description: The 'layer_mask' input (optional) provides an additional masking layer to further refine where the inner glow effect is applied, enhancing the precision of the effect's application.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output 'image' showcases the enhanced visual appeal of the background image with the applied inner glow effect, reflecting the successful integration of the effect.

LayerStyle_ InnerShadow V2.description: The InnerShadow V2 node is designed to apply an inner shadow effect to a given layer image, enhancing visual depth and dimensionality. It processes images by applying a shadow inside the layer boundaries based on specified parameters such as shadow color, distance, blur, and opacity, ensuring a more dynamic and visually appealing result.

inputs.name: background_image
inputs.description: The background image over which the layer image will be placed. It serves as the canvas for the inner shadow effect, ensuring that the shadow blends seamlessly with the background.

inputs.name: layer_image
inputs.description: The layer image to which the inner shadow effect will be applied. This image is modified to include the shadow, creating a sense of depth within the layer itself.

inputs.name: invert_mask
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether the mask should be inverted. This affects how the shadow effect is applied relative to the masked areas.

inputs.name: blend_mode
inputs.description: The blending mode used to combine the shadow with the layer, affecting how the shadow merges with the layer's colors and textures.

inputs.name: opacity
inputs.description: The opacity of the inner shadow, controlling the transparency of the shadow effect for subtler or more pronounced visual impact.

inputs.name: distance_x
inputs.description: The horizontal displacement of the shadow within the layer, allowing for the customization of the shadow's position relative to the layer.

inputs.name: distance_y
inputs.description: The vertical displacement of the shadow within the layer, enabling the adjustment of the shadow's vertical position for a more tailored effect.

inputs.name: grow
inputs.description: The amount by which the shadow's size is increased beyond the original layer boundaries, contributing to a more pronounced shadow effect.

inputs.name: blur
inputs.description: The level of blur applied to the shadow, determining the softness of the shadow edges for a more natural and integrated appearance.

inputs.name: shadow_color
inputs.description: The color of the inner shadow, allowing for the customization of the shadow to match or contrast with the layer and background for desired visual effects.

inputs.name: layer_mask
inputs.description: An optional mask that defines the area of the layer image where the inner shadow effect should be applied, providing additional control over the effect's application.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The resulting image after applying the inner shadow effect, showcasing the enhanced visual depth and dimensionality of the layer.

LayerStyle_ InnerShadow.description: The InnerShadow node applies an inner shadow effect to a layer within an image, enhancing depth and visual interest by simulating shadows within the boundaries of the layer. It allows for customization of shadow properties such as direction, blur, and color, catering to various stylistic needs.

inputs.name: background_image
inputs.description: Serves as the canvas for the inner shadow effect, providing context and depth to the layer.

inputs.name: layer_image
inputs.description: The target layer image for the inner shadow effect, enhancing its visual appearance by simulating shadows within its boundaries.

inputs.name: invert_mask
inputs.description: Determines whether the layer mask should be inverted, affecting the area where the inner shadow effect is applied.

inputs.name: blend_mode
inputs.description: Determines how the shadow's color interacts with the layer through the blending mode, influencing the final visual effect.

inputs.name: opacity
inputs.description: Controls the shadow's visibility and impact on the layer image by adjusting its opacity level.

inputs.name: distance_x
inputs.description: The horizontal displacement of the shadow effect, affecting the shadow's direction and perceived depth within the layer.

inputs.name: distance_y
inputs.description: The vertical displacement of the shadow effect, similar to distance_x, it influences the shadow's direction and depth perception.

inputs.name: grow
inputs.description: Adjusts the shadow's spread by increasing its size, affecting its softness and the overall depth effect.

inputs.name: blur
inputs.description: The blur radius applied to the shadow, softening its edges and contributing to the realism of the effect.

inputs.name: shadow_color
inputs.description: Allows customization of the shadow's color to complement or contrast with the layer image.

inputs.name: layer_mask
inputs.description: Defines the specific regions of the layer image where the inner shadow effect should be applied, ensuring precision in the effect's placement.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The resulting image after applying the inner shadow effect, showcasing the enhanced layer with the shadow.

LayerStyle_ OuterGlow V2.description: The OuterGlow V2 node is designed to enhance images by applying a sophisticated outer glow effect. This node allows for detailed customization of the glow through various parameters, enabling users to adjust aspects such as intensity, spread, and color to achieve the desired visual effect.

inputs.name: background_image
inputs.description: The base image over which the outer glow effect will be applied. It serves as the canvas for the glow effect.

inputs.name: layer_image
inputs.description: The image layer to which the outer glow effect will be applied. This layer is the primary focus of the glow enhancement.

inputs.name: invert_mask
inputs.description: A boolean parameter that determines whether the mask applied to the layer image should be inverted, affecting the area of the glow effect.

inputs.name: blend_mode
inputs.description: Specifies the blending mode to be used for combining the glow effect with the layer image, influencing the overall appearance of the effect.

inputs.name: opacity
inputs.description: Controls the opacity of the outer glow effect, allowing for fine-tuning of its visibility.

inputs.name: brightness
inputs.description: Adjusts the brightness of the glow effect, affecting its intensity and visibility.

inputs.name: glow_range
inputs.description: Defines the range of the glow effect, determining how far the glow extends from the layer image.

inputs.name: blur
inputs.description: Sets the level of blur applied to the glow effect, contributing to its softness and diffusion.

inputs.name: light_color
inputs.description: The color of the light source at the center of the glow effect, contributing to the effect's overall color scheme.

inputs.name: glow_color
inputs.description: The color of the outermost part of the glow effect, defining its peripheral appearance.

inputs.name: layer_mask
inputs.description: An optional mask that can be applied to the layer image to control the application of the glow effect to specific areas.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The resulting image after the outer glow effect has been applied, showcasing the enhanced visual appeal.

LayerStyle_ OuterGlow.description: The OuterGlow node applies an outer glow effect to images, enhancing their visual appeal by adding a soft, diffused light around their borders. This node is designed to stylize images by simulating the effect of a light source illuminating the outer edges, creating a distinctive glow that can be customized to fit various aesthetic requirements.

inputs.name: background_image
inputs.description: The 'background_image' input specifies the base image to which the outer glow effect will be applied. It serves as the foundational layer for the effect.

inputs.name: layer_image
inputs.description: The 'layer_image' input represents the image layer that will receive the outer glow effect. This layer is superimposed on the background image to create the glow effect.

inputs.name: invert_mask
inputs.description: The 'invert_mask' input determines whether the mask applied to the layer image should be inverted, affecting how the glow effect is masked around the image.

inputs.name: blend_mode
inputs.description: The 'blend_mode' input specifies the blending mode used to combine the layer image with the outer glow, influencing the overall appearance of the effect.

inputs.name: opacity
inputs.description: The 'opacity' input controls the transparency of the outer glow effect, allowing for fine-tuning of its visibility against the background image.

inputs.name: brightness
inputs.description: The 'brightness' input adjusts the intensity of the glow effect, affecting how brightly the glow appears around the layer image.

inputs.name: glow_range
inputs.description: The 'glow_range' input defines the spread of the outer glow effect, determining how far the glow extends from the edges of the layer image.

inputs.name: blur
inputs.description: The 'blur' input sets the level of blur applied to the outer glow, softening the edges of the glow for a more diffused appearance.

inputs.name: light_color
inputs.description: The 'light_color' input specifies the color at the center of the glow effect, contributing to the overall color scheme of the glow.

inputs.name: glow_color
inputs.description: The 'glow_color' input determines the color of the outer edges of the glow, allowing for a gradient effect from the center to the outskirts of the glow.

inputs.name: layer_mask
inputs.description: The 'layer_mask' input allows for an additional masking layer to be applied to the layer image, providing further control over how the glow effect is applied and integrated with the image.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The 'image' output type represents the final image with the applied outer glow effect, showcasing the enhanced visual appeal with a soft, diffused light around its borders.

LayerStyle_ Stroke V2.description: The Stroke V2 node is designed to apply advanced stroke effects to images within a layer-based design system. It enhances visual aesthetics by allowing for detailed customization of stroke properties such as color, width, and blending modes.

inputs.name: background_image
inputs.description: The background image over which the stroke effect will be applied. It serves as the canvas for the stroke enhancements.

inputs.name: layer_image
inputs.description: The layer image to which the stroke effect will be directly applied. This image is modified based on the stroke settings.

inputs.name: invert_mask
inputs.description: A boolean parameter that determines whether the mask applied to the layer image should be inverted, affecting the area where the stroke is applied.

inputs.name: blend_mode
inputs.description: Specifies the blending mode used to combine the stroke effect with the layer image, influencing the final visual outcome.

inputs.name: opacity
inputs.description: Controls the opacity level of the stroke effect, allowing for fine-tuning of its visibility on the layer image.

inputs.name: stroke_grow
inputs.description: Determines the growth or shrinkage of the stroke effect relative to the original layer boundaries, enabling more precise control over the effect's spread.

inputs.name: stroke_width
inputs.description: Sets the width of the stroke effect, defining the thickness of the applied stroke around the layer image.

inputs.name: blur
inputs.description: Adjusts the blur intensity of the stroke effect, offering the ability to soften or sharpen the edges of the stroke.

inputs.name: stroke_color
inputs.description: Defines the color of the stroke effect, allowing for customization to match the design's color scheme.

inputs.name: layer_mask
inputs.description: An optional mask that can be applied to the layer image, defining specific areas where the stroke effect should or should not be applied.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The resulting image after applying the stroke V2 effect, showcasing the enhanced visual layer with the specified stroke properties.

LayerStyle_ Stroke.description: The `LayerStyle: Stroke` node is designed to apply a stroke effect to a layer image, allowing for customization of the stroke's appearance through various parameters such as color, width, and opacity. It operates by blending the layer image with a background image, optionally using a mask for more precise control over the effect's application.

inputs.name: background_image
inputs.description: The background image over which the layer image will be placed. It serves as the canvas for the stroke effect.

inputs.name: layer_image
inputs.description: The layer image to which the stroke effect will be applied. This image is blended with the background based on the specified parameters.

inputs.name: invert_mask
inputs.description: A boolean parameter that determines whether the mask applied to the layer image should be inverted, affecting the areas where the stroke effect is applied.

inputs.name: blend_mode
inputs.description: Defines the blending mode used to combine the layer image with the background, influencing the visual outcome of the stroke effect.

inputs.name: opacity
inputs.description: The opacity level of the stroke effect, allowing for adjustments in transparency from fully opaque to fully transparent.

inputs.name: stroke_grow
inputs.description: The amount by which the stroke effect grows or shrinks the layer image, enabling the adjustment of the effect's spread.

inputs.name: stroke_width
inputs.description: Specifies the width of the stroke effect, determining how thick or thin the stroke appears around the layer image.

inputs.name: blur
inputs.description: The level of blur applied to the stroke effect, which can soften the edges of the stroke for a more subtle appearance.

inputs.name: stroke_color
inputs.description: The color of the stroke effect, allowing for customization of the stroke's appearance to match the desired aesthetic.

inputs.name: layer_mask
inputs.description: An optional mask that can be applied to the layer image, providing more control over where the stroke effect is applied.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The resulting image after applying the stroke effect, combining the layer and background images with the specified stroke parameters.

LayerUtility_ AddBlindWaterMark.description: This node is designed to embed a blind watermark into an image, utilizing a method that allows the watermark to be later extracted or detected without altering the visible characteristics of the original image significantly. It operates by manipulating the image's channels to encode the watermark invisibly.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The primary image(s) into which the watermark is to be embedded. This parameter is crucial for determining the base content that will carry the hidden watermark.

inputs.name: watermark_image
inputs.description: The image(s) to be used as the watermark. This parameter is essential for defining the content of the watermark that will be invisibly embedded into the primary image(s).

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The resulting image(s) after the watermark has been embedded. This output is significant as it represents the original image(s) altered to include the invisible watermark, ready for use or further processing.

LayerUtility_ BatchSelector.description: The BatchSelector node is designed to selectively process and return subsets of images and masks based on specified indices. It enables dynamic selection and manipulation of image batches, facilitating customized processing flows within image editing or generation pipelines.

inputs.name: select
inputs.description: Specifies the indices of images and masks to be selected for processing. This parameter is crucial for determining which elements of the input batches are operated on, allowing for targeted manipulation or analysis.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: An optional batch of images to be selectively processed based on the indices provided in 'select'. This parameter enables the node to work with varying sets of images, adapting to the needs of the workflow.

inputs.name: masks
inputs.description: An optional batch of masks to be selectively processed alongside images, based on the indices provided in 'select'. This allows for parallel manipulation of images and their corresponding masks, enhancing workflow flexibility.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The processed batch of images, selectively compiled based on the specified indices. This output facilitates further image processing or analysis steps within the pipeline.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The processed batch of masks, selectively compiled alongside images, based on the specified indices. This output supports tasks requiring synchronized manipulation of images and masks.

LayerUtility_ Boolean.description: The Boolean node is designed to encapsulate and convert a boolean value into a boolean and string representation. It serves as a fundamental utility within data processing pipelines, allowing for the straightforward manipulation and interpretation of boolean logic.

inputs.name: bool_value
inputs.description: Determines the boolean value to be processed by the node. It is crucial for defining the logical state that will be converted and represented in both boolean and string formats.

outputs.name: boolean
outputs.description: The boolean representation of the input value.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The string representation of the boolean input value.

LayerUtility_ BooleanOperator.description: This node performs a variety of boolean operations between two inputs based on a specified operator. It abstracts the complexity of conditional logic into a simple interface, allowing users to easily implement logical conditions and comparisons within their data flows.

inputs.name: a
inputs.description: The first input for the boolean operation. Its role varies based on the chosen operator, acting either as a standalone value for unary operations or one of the operands for binary operations.

inputs.name: b
inputs.description: The second input for the boolean operation, serving as the other operand in binary operations. It is not used in unary operations like 'not(a)'.

inputs.name: operator
inputs.description: Specifies the boolean operation to be performed. It supports a range of operators including comparison, logical, and bitwise operations, directly influencing the outcome of the node.

outputs.name: output
outputs.description: The result of the boolean operation, indicating the truth value of the applied condition.

LayerUtility_ BooleanOperatorV2.description: This node performs a variety of boolean operations between two values, supporting both direct value inputs and string representations of numbers. It can execute standard comparisons, logical operations, and even min/max calculations, making it versatile for conditional logic and decision-making processes within data flows.

inputs.name: a_value
inputs.description: A string representation of the first value, which will be converted to a number if possible. It serves as the primary operand for the boolean operation.

inputs.name: b_value
inputs.description: A string representation of the second value, which will be converted to a number if possible. It acts as the secondary operand for the boolean operation.

inputs.name: operator
inputs.description: Specifies the boolean operation to perform, such as comparison, logical operation, or min/max calculation.

inputs.name: a
inputs.description: An optional direct numeric input for the first value, providing an alternative to 'a_value' if a direct number is preferred.

inputs.name: b
inputs.description: An optional direct numeric input for the second value, providing an alternative to 'b_value' if a direct number is preferred.

outputs.name: output
outputs.description: The boolean result of the specified operation.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The string representation of the boolean result, facilitating easy integration and readability in various contexts.

LayerUtility_ CheckMask.description: The CheckMask node is designed to evaluate the effectiveness of a given mask by determining if the area of the mask that meets certain criteria (e.g., white point value) exceeds a specified percentage. This functionality is crucial for filtering out ineffective masks in image processing workflows, ensuring that subsequent operations are performed on valid data.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The mask input is the primary data on which the node operates, used to determine if the mask is effective based on its white point value and area coverage.

inputs.name: white_point
inputs.description: The white point parameter sets the threshold value for considering a pixel as part of the effective area of the mask, playing a critical role in the mask's evaluation.

inputs.name: area_percent
inputs.description: The area percent parameter specifies the minimum percentage of the mask that must be considered effective, based on the white point criteria, for the mask to be deemed valid.

outputs.name: bool
outputs.description: Indicates whether the mask is considered effective based on the white point and area percentage criteria.

LayerUtility_ ColorImage V2.description: This node is designed to generate a solid color image based on specified dimensions and color. It abstracts the process of creating an image filled with a single color, facilitating the creation of background layers or color-based placeholders in graphic projects.

inputs.name: size
inputs.description: Determines the size of the generated image, allowing for predefined or custom dimensions. It enables flexibility in defining the image's overall dimensions.

inputs.name: custom_width
inputs.description: Specifies the custom width for the image when 'size' is set to 'custom'. It defines the width of the image in pixels.

inputs.name: custom_height
inputs.description: Specifies the custom height for the image when 'size' is set to 'custom'. It defines the height of the image in pixels.

inputs.name: color
inputs.description: Defines the color of the generated image. This parameter allows for customization of the image's appearance, enabling the creation of images with any desired solid color.

inputs.name: size_as
inputs.description: Optionally specifies an image to match its size. If provided, the generated image will match the dimensions of this reference image.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is a solid color image with the specified dimensions and color. It serves as a versatile element for various graphic design and layering tasks.

LayerUtility_ ColorImage.description: The ColorImage node generates a solid color image based on specified dimensions and color. It serves as a utility for creating background layers or color fills in image processing workflows.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Specifies the width of the generated image. It determines how wide the image will be.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Specifies the height of the generated image. It determines the height of the image.

inputs.name: color
inputs.description: Defines the color of the generated image. The color is specified in a string format, typically as a hex code.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is a solid color image with the specified dimensions and color.

LayerUtility_ ColorPicker.description: The ColorPicker node provides functionality for selecting colors and converting them between different formats, such as hexadecimal and decimal color codes. It allows users to input a color in a specified format and convert it to another, facilitating easy integration and manipulation of color data within a design or visualization workflow.

inputs.name: color
inputs.description: Specifies the color to be converted or selected. It serves as the primary input for the node, determining the base color for conversion or selection.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Determines the output format of the color conversion, allowing users to choose between hexadecimal ('HEX') and decimal ('DEC') representations.

outputs.name: value
outputs.description: The converted or selected color value, outputted in the format specified by the 'mode' input.

LayerUtility_ CreateQRCode.description: This node generates QR codes based on specified text inputs, allowing for the creation of customizable QR codes with defined sizes and border thicknesses. It encapsulates the process of QR code generation, offering a straightforward way to integrate QR code creation into workflows or applications.

inputs.name: size
inputs.description: Specifies the size of the generated QR code image. A larger size means the QR code will be bigger, affecting its visibility and scannability.

inputs.name: border
inputs.description: Determines the thickness of the border around the QR code. A thicker border can help distinguish the QR code from its surroundings, potentially improving its readability.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The text to be encoded into the QR code. This can be any string, such as a URL or a message, which will be converted into a QR code format.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The generated QR code as an image. This output can be used directly in UIs or further processed as needed.

LayerUtility_ CropBoxResolve.description: The CropBoxResolve node is designed to calculate the dimensions of a new, adjusted bounding box based on the coordinates of an existing crop box. It transforms the original coordinates into a format suitable for further image processing tasks, such as cropping or resizing.

inputs.name: crop_box
inputs.description: The 'crop_box' parameter represents the original bounding box coordinates. It is essential for determining the starting point and size of the area to be processed, affecting the output dimensions directly.

outputs.name: x
outputs.description: The 'x' output represents the starting x-coordinate of the new bounding box.

outputs.name: y
outputs.description: The 'y' output represents the starting y-coordinate of the new bounding box.

outputs.name: width
outputs.description: The 'width' output specifies the width of the new bounding box.

outputs.name: height
outputs.description: The 'height' output specifies the height of the new bounding box.

LayerUtility_ CropByMask V2.description: This node provides advanced image cropping capabilities based on a mask. It allows for dynamic cropping of images by applying a mask to identify the relevant area, with options for adjusting the crop area through parameters such as detection method, border reserves, and rounding to multiples. It's designed to offer flexibility in image processing tasks where precise control over the cropping area is required.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image to be cropped. This parameter is crucial as it provides the visual content that will be processed and cropped according to the mask and other specified parameters.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The mask used to determine the cropping area. This parameter is essential for identifying the relevant portion of the image to be cropped, based on the mask's shape and area.

inputs.name: invert_mask
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether the mask should be inverted before processing. This affects which part of the image is considered relevant for cropping, allowing for greater flexibility in handling different types of masks.

inputs.name: detect
inputs.description: Specifies the method used to detect the cropping area within the mask. This can include methods like 'min_bounding_rect' or 'max_inscribed_rect', influencing how the crop area is calculated.

inputs.name: top_reserve
inputs.description: The amount of padding to reserve at the top of the crop area. This allows for fine-tuning of the crop boundary, ensuring that important image details are not lost.

inputs.name: bottom_reserve
inputs.description: The amount of padding to reserve at the bottom of the crop area. Similar to top_reserve, this parameter helps in adjusting the crop boundary to include essential image details.

inputs.name: left_reserve
inputs.description: The amount of padding to reserve on the left side of the crop area. It enables precise control over the crop boundary, ensuring the inclusion of important image elements.

inputs.name: right_reserve
inputs.description: The amount of padding to reserve on the right side of the crop area. This parameter is used to adjust the crop boundary for including necessary image details.

inputs.name: round_to_multiple
inputs.description: An optional parameter that rounds the dimensions of the crop area to the nearest multiple of a specified number. This is useful for ensuring that the cropped image meets certain size requirements.

inputs.name: crop_box
inputs.description: An optional parameter specifying a predefined crop box. If provided, the cropping operation will use these coordinates instead of calculating them based on the mask and detection method.

outputs.name: croped_image
outputs.description: The image resulting from the cropping operation. This output is essential for visualizing the effect of the applied mask and cropping parameters on the original image.

outputs.name: croped_mask
outputs.description: The mask corresponding to the cropped area of the image. This output is crucial for further processing or analysis that requires the mask of the cropped image.

outputs.name: crop_box
outputs.description: The coordinates of the crop box determined based on the mask and additional parameters. This output is crucial for understanding the exact area of the image that has been cropped.

outputs.name: box_preview
outputs.description: A preview image showing the crop box applied on the original image. This is useful for visual verification of the cropping area before proceeding with further image processing steps.

LayerUtility_ CropByMask.description: This node is designed to crop images based on a specified mask, adjusting the crop area dynamically to fit the mask's shape. It provides functionality to visually preview the crop area on the original image, allowing for precise adjustments based on the mask's boundaries.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image to be cropped, serving as the primary input for the cropping operation.

inputs.name: mask_for_crop
inputs.description: The mask based on which the image will be cropped. It determines the area of the image that will be retained after cropping.

inputs.name: invert_mask
inputs.description: A boolean flag to invert the mask before cropping, allowing for flexibility in selecting the area to be cropped.

inputs.name: detect
inputs.description: The method used to determine the cropping area based on the mask. Options include 'min_bounding_rect', 'max_inscribed_rect', and 'mask_area'.

inputs.name: top_reserve
inputs.description: The amount of padding to add to the top edge of the crop area, allowing for adjustments beyond the mask's boundaries.

inputs.name: bottom_reserve
inputs.description: The amount of padding to add to the bottom edge of the crop area, enabling adjustments beyond the mask's boundaries.

inputs.name: left_reserve
inputs.description: The amount of padding to add to the left edge of the crop area, facilitating adjustments beyond the mask's boundaries.

inputs.name: right_reserve
inputs.description: The amount of padding to add to the right edge of the crop area, allowing for adjustments beyond the mask's boundaries.

outputs.name: croped_image
outputs.description: unknown

outputs.name: croped_mask
outputs.description: unknown

outputs.name: crop_box
outputs.description: The coordinates of the crop box used in the cropping operation, providing details on the area selected for cropping.

outputs.name: box_preview
outputs.description: A preview image showing the crop box overlaid on the original image, aiding in visualizing the crop area.

LayerUtility_ DecodeQRCode.description: The DecodeQRCode node is designed to interpret QR codes from images, applying optional preprocessing to enhance readability before decoding. It aims to extract textual information encoded within QR codes, offering a means to retrieve embedded data from visual inputs.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image input represents the visual source from which QR codes are to be decoded. It plays a crucial role in the node's operation by providing the raw data necessary for QR code interpretation.

inputs.name: pre_blur
inputs.description: The pre_blur parameter allows for optional preprocessing of the image to improve QR code readability by applying a Gaussian blur. This can enhance the node's ability to accurately decode QR codes from images that may be noisy or of low quality.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The output is a string or a list of strings representing the decoded textual information from the QR codes found within the input images.

LayerUtility_ ExtendCanvas.description: This node is designed to extend the canvas of an image, allowing for adjustments in size and dimensions without altering the original content. It provides a way to add space around an image, which can be useful for layout, design, or preparation for further processing.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The primary image to be extended. This parameter is crucial as it defines the base upon which the canvas will be extended.

inputs.name: invert_mask
inputs.description: Determines whether the mask should be inverted during the process. This can affect how the mask is applied in relation to the canvas extension.

inputs.name: top
inputs.description: Specifies the amount of space to add to the top of the canvas. It affects the vertical expansion of the image's canvas.

inputs.name: bottom
inputs.description: Determines the amount of space to add to the bottom of the canvas, contributing to the vertical expansion.

inputs.name: left
inputs.description: Indicates the amount of space to add to the left side of the canvas, affecting the horizontal expansion.

inputs.name: right
inputs.description: Specifies the amount of space to add to the right side of the canvas, also affecting the horizontal expansion.

inputs.name: color
inputs.description: Defines the color to fill the newly added space around the image, ensuring the extension blends seamlessly or contrasts as desired.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: An optional mask that can be applied to the image during the canvas extension process. It allows for more precise control over how the extension affects specific parts of the image.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The resulting image after the canvas has been extended. It showcases the original image with added space around it as specified by the input parameters.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The mask corresponding to the extended canvas, which can be used for further image processing or manipulation.

LayerUtility_ ExtendCanvasV2.description: The ExtendCanvasV2 node is designed to enhance the functionality of image manipulation by providing advanced capabilities for extending the canvas of an image. This node aims to offer more sophisticated options and flexibility compared to its predecessor, allowing for more precise and creative adjustments in image composition.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: Specifies the original image to be manipulated. It is the primary input on which the canvas extension operations are performed.

inputs.name: invert_mask
inputs.description: A boolean parameter that determines whether the mask applied to the image should be inverted, affecting how the canvas extension is applied in relation to the mask.

inputs.name: top
inputs.description: Defines the number of pixels to extend the canvas at the top edge of the image.

inputs.name: bottom
inputs.description: Specifies the number of pixels to extend the canvas at the bottom edge of the image.

inputs.name: left
inputs.description: Indicates the number of pixels to extend the canvas on the left side of the image.

inputs.name: right
inputs.description: Determines the number of pixels to extend the canvas on the right side of the image.

inputs.name: color
inputs.description: Specifies the color to fill the extended canvas area, allowing for aesthetic customization of the added canvas space.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: An optional mask that can be applied to the image, influencing the areas of the canvas extension.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The resulting image after the canvas has been extended, reflecting the specified adjustments.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The mask applied to the extended canvas, if any, indicating areas of interest or exclusion in the extended space.

LayerUtility_ Float.description: The Float node is designed to process floating-point numbers, allowing for the manipulation and conversion of float values within a given range. It provides functionality to input a float value, perform any necessary processing, and output the processed value along with its string representation.

inputs.name: float_value
inputs.description: Specifies the floating-point number to be processed. This parameter is crucial for determining the node's operation and output, as it directly influences the manipulation and conversion of the float value.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The processed floating-point number after the node's operation.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The string representation of the processed floating-point number.

LayerUtility_ GetColorTone.description: This node is designed to analyze an image and determine its dominant or average color tone, returning the result in both HEX and HSV formats. It provides a straightforward way for users to extract color information from images, which can be useful in various applications such as theming, design, and visual analysis.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image to analyze for color tone. This is the primary input on which the color analysis is performed.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Specifies the method of color analysis: 'main_color' for dominant color or 'average' for average color of the image. This choice affects the outcome of the color tone analysis.

outputs.name: RGB color in HEX
outputs.description: The dominant or average color of the image represented as a HEX code.

outputs.name: HSV color in list
outputs.description: The dominant or average color of the image represented in HSV format, provided as a list.

LayerUtility_ GetColorToneV2.description: The GetColorToneV2 node is designed to analyze and manipulate the color tone of images. It offers advanced features for removing backgrounds, adjusting masks, and determining the main or average color tone of specific image areas, such as the entire image, the background, or the subject. This node is an enhancement over its predecessor, providing more control over the image processing and color analysis.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed for color tone analysis. This parameter is crucial as it serves as the base for all subsequent operations within the node.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Specifies the method of color tone analysis: either determining the main color or calculating the average color of the image. This choice affects the algorithm used for color extraction.

inputs.name: color_of
inputs.description: Determines the area of the image to analyze: the entire image, just the background, or only the subject. This parameter allows for targeted color analysis based on the specified area.

inputs.name: remove_bkgd_method
inputs.description: The method used for background removal from the image, offering options like 'BiRefNet' or 'RMBG 1.4'. This is essential for isolating the subject or background for accurate color analysis.

inputs.name: invert_mask
inputs.description: A boolean flag to invert the mask applied during image processing, which can alter the area of interest for color analysis.

inputs.name: mask_grow
inputs.description: Specifies the amount to grow or shrink the mask around the subject or background, allowing for finer control over the area being analyzed.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: An optional mask that can be applied to the image for more precise control over the areas to be analyzed for color tone.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The processed image with applied color tone adjustments or background removal effects.

outputs.name: color_in_hex
outputs.description: The determined color of the specified image area in HEX format, providing a precise color representation.

outputs.name: HSV color in list
outputs.description: The HSV (Hue, Saturation, Value) representation of the determined color, offering an alternative color space for analysis.

LayerUtility_ GetImageSize.description: This node is designed to determine the dimensions of an image, returning its width, height, and original size in a structured format. It abstracts the complexity of image processing to provide straightforward metrics that can be used for further image manipulation or analysis.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The 'image' parameter is the input image tensor for which the size is to be determined. It plays a crucial role in the node's operation by being the source from which the dimensions are extracted.

outputs.name: width
outputs.description: The width of the input image as determined by the node.

outputs.name: height
outputs.description: The height of the input image as determined by the node.

outputs.name: original_size
outputs.description: A tuple containing the original width and height of the input image, providing a compact representation of its dimensions.

LayerUtility_ GradientImage V2.description: This node is designed to generate gradient images with enhanced features and options compared to its predecessor. It focuses on creating customizable gradient backgrounds or layers by specifying dimensions, colors, and gradient direction, leveraging advanced image processing techniques to achieve more dynamic and visually appealing results.

inputs.name: size
inputs.description: Specifies the predefined or custom size for the gradient image, allowing for standard or user-defined dimensions.

inputs.name: custom_width
inputs.description: Specifies the width of the gradient image when a custom size is selected, affecting the horizontal dimension of the output image.

inputs.name: custom_height
inputs.description: Specifies the height of the gradient image when a custom size is selected, affecting the vertical dimension of the output image.

inputs.name: angle
inputs.description: Determines the angle of the gradient, influencing the direction and spread of the color transition in the generated image.

inputs.name: start_color
inputs.description: Defines the starting color of the gradient, marking the beginning of the color transition.

inputs.name: end_color
inputs.description: Defines the ending color of the gradient, marking the end of the color transition.

inputs.name: size_as
inputs.description: Optionally specifies an image tensor to use its dimensions as the size for the gradient image, overriding 'size', 'custom_width', and 'custom_height' if provided.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The generated gradient image, showcasing a smooth transition between the specified start and end colors.

LayerUtility_ GradientImage.description: This node generates a gradient image based on specified dimensions, angle, and color range. It abstracts the complexity of creating smooth transitions between colors over a defined area, providing a versatile tool for generating backgrounds or layer effects in image processing tasks.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Specifies the width of the gradient image to be generated. It determines the horizontal dimension of the resulting image.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Specifies the height of the gradient image to be generated. It determines the vertical dimension of the resulting image.

inputs.name: angle
inputs.description: Defines the angle of the gradient direction. This affects how the color transition appears across the image.

inputs.name: start_color
inputs.description: The starting color of the gradient. It marks the beginning of the color transition.

inputs.name: end_color
inputs.description: The ending color of the gradient. It marks the end of the color transition.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The generated gradient image as a result of the specified parameters.

LayerUtility_ HLFrequencyDetailRestore.description: The HLFrequencyDetailRestore node is designed to enhance image details by restoring high and low frequency components. It allows for the manipulation of image textures and details through frequency-based adjustments, providing a means to fine-tune the visual quality of images in a layer-wise manner.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The primary image to which frequency detail restoration will be applied. It serves as the base layer for the operation.

inputs.name: detail_image
inputs.description: An image containing the details to be restored into the primary image. This image is used to extract high-frequency components.

inputs.name: keep_high_freq
inputs.description: Determines the intensity of high-frequency details to be preserved in the detail image.

inputs.name: erase_low_freq
inputs.description: Specifies the level of low-frequency details to be erased from the primary image before merging with high-frequency details.

inputs.name: mask_blur
inputs.description: Applies a blur to the mask, if provided, to smooth the edges of the applied details.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: An optional mask to specify areas of the image where detail restoration should be applied.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The resulting image after applying high and low frequency detail restoration.

LayerUtility_ HSV Value.description: The 'LayerUtility: HSV Value' node is designed to convert color values into their corresponding HSV (Hue, Saturation, Value) components. It supports input in both hexadecimal string and RGB tuple formats, facilitating the transformation of color representations into a format that's widely used for color manipulation and analysis.

inputs.name: color_value
inputs.description: The 'color_value' parameter accepts a color in either hexadecimal string format or RGB tuple format. It is crucial for determining the output HSV values, as the node converts this input into its HSV components.

outputs.name: H
outputs.description: Represents the Hue component of the color in the HSV color space, as an integer.

outputs.name: S
outputs.description: Represents the Saturation component of the color in the HSV color space, as an integer.

outputs.name: V
outputs.description: Represents the Value component of the color in the HSV color space, as an integer.

LayerUtility_ If.description: This node provides conditional logic execution within a workflow, allowing for branching paths based on specified conditions. It evaluates a given condition and directs the flow accordingly, enabling dynamic decision-making in processing pipelines.

inputs.name: if_condition
inputs.description: Determines the branch of execution based on its truth value. A true condition leads to the execution of the 'when_TRUE' path, while a false condition leads to the 'when_FALSE' path.

inputs.name: when_TRUE
inputs.description: The path or operation to execute if the 'if_condition' evaluates to true. This allows for dynamic control over the workflow based on conditions.

inputs.name: when_FALSE
inputs.description: The path or operation to execute if the 'if_condition' evaluates to false. This provides an alternative execution path, ensuring flexibility in handling various scenarios.

outputs.description: The result of the executed path, which could be from either the 'when_TRUE' or 'when_FALSE' branch, depending on the evaluation of the 'if_condition'. This output type name is represented by a placeholder '?', indicating the flexibility in the output based on conditional logic.

LayerUtility_ ImageAutoCrop V2.description: This node automatically crops images based on their content, enhancing focus and composition by removing unnecessary background. It utilizes advanced algorithms to detect and retain the main subject of the image while discarding the extraneous parts, providing a cleaner, more focused visual output.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be auto-cropped. This parameter is crucial as it determines the area of focus and the parts to be eliminated based on the content and composition of the image.

inputs.name: fill_background
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether to fill the background after cropping. If true, the area outside the cropped region will be filled with the specified background color.

inputs.name: background_color
inputs.description: The color used to fill the background if fill_background is set to true. This parameter allows customization of the background color post-cropping.

inputs.name: aspect_ratio
inputs.description: Specifies the desired aspect ratio for the cropped image. This can be set to 'custom', 'original', 'detect_mask', or a specific ratio like '16:9', guiding the cropping process to maintain the specified aspect ratio.

inputs.name: proportional_width
inputs.description: When aspect_ratio is set to 'custom', this parameter defines the width component of the custom aspect ratio.

inputs.name: proportional_height
inputs.description: When aspect_ratio is set to 'custom', this parameter defines the height component of the custom aspect ratio.

inputs.name: scale_to_side
inputs.description: A boolean flag that, when true, scales the image to fit the longest side to the specified scale_to_length, maintaining the aspect ratio.

inputs.name: scale_to_length
inputs.description: Specifies the length to which the longest side of the image should be scaled when scale_to_side is true.

inputs.name: detect
inputs.description: Determines the method used to detect the cropping area. Options include 'min_bounding_rect', 'max_inscribed_rect', and 'mask_area', each affecting how the crop area is calculated.

inputs.name: border_reserve
inputs.description: An additional border added around the detected crop area to ensure important parts of the image are not cut off. Specified in pixels.

inputs.name: ultra_detail_range
inputs.description: Specifies the range for enhancing detail in the cropped area, useful for fine-tuning the focus on specific parts of the image.

inputs.name: matting_method
inputs.description: The method used for image matting, which helps in separating the foreground from the background. Options include 'SegmentAnything' and other matting techniques.

inputs.name: sam_model
inputs.description: Specifies the model used for the 'SegmentAnything' matting method, affecting the quality and accuracy of the foreground extraction.

inputs.name: grounding_dino_model
inputs.description: Specifies the DINO model used for grounding, which assists in better foreground segmentation when using 'SegmentAnything'.

inputs.name: sam_threshold
inputs.description: The threshold value for the 'SegmentAnything' method, determining the sensitivity of the segmentation process.

inputs.name: sam_prompt
inputs.description: The prompt used for the 'SegmentAnything' method, guiding the model in understanding what part of the image to focus on during segmentation.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: An optional mask that can be provided to guide the cropping process. It helps in specifying the areas of the image that should be retained or removed, enhancing the accuracy of the auto-cropping algorithm.

outputs.name: cropped_image
outputs.description: The result of the auto-cropping process, which is a version of the original image with unnecessary background removed, focusing on the main subject.

outputs.name: box_preview
outputs.description: A visual preview of the bounding box used for cropping the image. It helps in understanding how the image was cropped and the area that was focused on.

outputs.name: cropped_mask
