inputs.description: A boolean indicating whether to log the prompt styling process. Enabling this option provides transparency and insight into the styling decisions made by the node.

outputs.name: text_positive
outputs.description: The artistically styled positive text output, reflecting the application of the selected artistic style to the original positive input.

outputs.name: text_negative
outputs.description: The artistically styled negative text output, reflecting the application of the selected artistic style to the original negative input.

ArtistStylerAdvanced.description: The ArtistStylerAdvanced node dynamically subclasses from SDXLPromptStylerAdvanced to apply advanced styling options to text prompts based on artist-specific styles. It leverages a comprehensive dataset of style templates to transform input prompts into artistically styled versions, enhancing creativity and specificity in text generation tasks.

inputs.name: text_positive_g
inputs.description: The global positive text prompt to be styled, serving as a foundational element for artistic transformation.

inputs.name: text_positive_l
inputs.description: The local positive text prompt to be styled, allowing for more detailed and nuanced artistic transformations.

inputs.name: text_negative
inputs.description: The negative text prompt to be styled, providing a basis for contrastive or negating artistic transformations.

inputs.name: artist
inputs.description: unknown

inputs.name: negative_prompt_to
inputs.description: Specifies the scope of the negative styling transformation, allowing choices between global, local, or both styling applications.

inputs.name: log_prompt
inputs.description: A boolean flag to enable or disable logging of the prompt styling process, offering insights into the styling decisions and outcomes.

outputs.name: text_positive_g
outputs.description: The final styled global positive text prompt.

outputs.name: text_positive_l
outputs.description: The final styled local positive text prompt.

outputs.name: text_positive
outputs.description: The combined final styled positive text prompt, incorporating both global and local artistic transformations.

outputs.name: text_negative_g
outputs.description: The final styled global negative text prompt.

outputs.name: text_negative_l
outputs.description: The final styled local negative text prompt.

outputs.name: text_negative
outputs.description: The combined final styled negative text prompt, reflecting both global and local artistic nuances.

AzazealStylesStyler.description: The AzazealStylesStyler node dynamically applies a specific aesthetic or thematic style to text prompts based on a selection from predefined styles. It enhances the original text prompts by incorporating stylistic elements, aiming to achieve a more targeted or nuanced expression.

inputs.name: text_positive
inputs.description: The original positive text prompt to be styled. It serves as the base content that will be enhanced with the selected style.

inputs.name: text_negative
inputs.description: The original negative text prompt to be styled. It acts as a counterpoint to the positive prompt, both of which will be modified according to the chosen style.

inputs.name: Azazeal Styles
inputs.description: Specifies the particular style to apply to the text prompts, chosen from a predefined list of styles. This selection determines the stylistic adjustments made to the prompts.

inputs.name: log_prompt
inputs.description: A boolean flag that, when true, enables logging of the prompt styling process for debugging or verification purposes.

outputs.name: text_positive
outputs.description: The positive text prompt after being styled, reflecting the intended thematic enhancements.

outputs.name: text_negative
outputs.description: The negative text prompt after styling, showcasing the applied aesthetic or thematic elements.

AzazealStylesStylerAdvanced.description: The AzazealStylesStylerAdvanced node is designed to apply advanced styling to text prompts based on a selection of styles from the Azazeal styles menu. It enhances text inputs with stylistic modifications, aiming to tailor the output to specific aesthetic or thematic preferences.

inputs.name: text_positive_g
inputs.description: The global positive text prompt to be styled. It serves as the base content for applying global stylistic transformations.

inputs.name: text_positive_l
inputs.description: The local positive text prompt to be styled. It is used for applying local stylistic adjustments, complementing the global styling.

inputs.name: text_negative
inputs.description: The negative text prompt to be styled. This input is modified to reflect the selected styles in a manner that negates or contrasts with the positive prompts.

inputs.name: Azazeal Styles
inputs.description: unknown

inputs.name: negative_prompt_to
inputs.description: Specifies the scope of negative styling application, allowing for targeted adjustments to either global, local, or both types of prompts.

inputs.name: log_prompt
inputs.description: A boolean flag that, when enabled, logs the input and output prompts along with the selected styles for debugging or review purposes.

outputs.name: text_positive_g
outputs.description: The styled global positive text prompt, reflecting the applied Azazeal styles.

outputs.name: text_positive_l
outputs.description: The styled local positive text prompt, showcasing the local stylistic enhancements.

outputs.name: text_positive
outputs.description: A composite styled positive text prompt, integrating both global and local stylistic modifications.

outputs.name: text_negative_g
outputs.description: The styled global negative text prompt, altered to contrast with the styled positive prompts.

outputs.name: text_negative_l
outputs.description: The styled local negative text prompt, providing a nuanced contrast to the positive styling.

PrepositionStyler.description: The PrepositionStyler node dynamically generates styling options for text prompts based on predefined templates and user selections. It enhances text prompts by applying stylistic modifications according to the selected options, aiming to refine the prompts for more targeted and effective generative tasks.

SubjectStyler.description: The SubjectStyler node dynamically applies thematic styling to text prompts based on a predefined set of styles related to 'subject' themes. It enhances text prompts by incorporating subject-specific stylistic elements, aiming to achieve a more targeted and refined generation of content.

NNLatentUpscale.description: The NNLatentUpscale node specializes in enhancing the resolution of SDXL latent representations using a neural network approach. It dynamically adjusts its internal model based on the specified version and upscale factor, ensuring optimized upscaling of latent samples to achieve higher fidelity outputs.

inputs.name: latent
inputs.description: The latent representation to be upscaled. It is crucial for defining the starting point of the upscaling process.

inputs.name: version
inputs.description: Specifies the version of the model to use for upscaling, allowing for flexibility and optimization based on the latent's characteristics.

inputs.name: upscale
inputs.description: The factor by which to upscale the latent representation, directly influencing the output's resolution and detail.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The upscaled latent representation, enhanced in resolution and detail.

BNK_GetSigma.description: The `BNK_GetSigma` node is designed to calculate a specific sigma value based on the provided model, sampler name, scheduler, and step parameters. It focuses on determining the appropriate noise level for latent space manipulation, facilitating the generation of variations or adjustments in generated images or data. This node plays a crucial role in controlling the noise injection process, which is essential for fine-tuning the details and quality of generative models' outputs.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The `model` parameter specifies the generative model to be used for calculating sigma. It is crucial for determining the appropriate noise level based on the model's characteristics and latent space.

inputs.name: sampler_name
inputs.description: The `sampler_name` parameter identifies the sampling strategy to be employed. It affects how the noise levels are calculated and applied, influencing the variation and quality of the generated outputs.

inputs.name: scheduler
inputs.description: The `scheduler` parameter defines the scheduling strategy for noise level adjustment over steps. It plays a key role in the temporal dynamics of noise injection, affecting the smoothness and progression of generated variations.

inputs.name: steps
inputs.description: Specifies the total number of steps for the noise calculation process. It determines the granularity and range of sigma values to be considered.

inputs.name: start_at_step
inputs.description: Defines the starting step for sigma calculation, allowing for targeted noise level adjustments from a specific point in the generation process.

inputs.name: end_at_step
inputs.description: Marks the ending step for sigma calculation, enabling precise control over the extent of noise adjustments in the generative process.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The output is a floating-point number representing the calculated sigma value. This value is crucial for adjusting the noise level in the latent space, directly influencing the detail and quality of the generated outputs.

BNK_InjectNoise.description: The `InjectNoise` node is designed to augment latent representations with noise, offering a mechanism to introduce variability and potentially enhance the generation quality of models. It supports the injection of custom noise and the application of a mask to selectively apply noise, thereby providing a versatile tool for manipulating latent spaces.

inputs.name: latents
inputs.description: The primary latent representation to which noise will be added. This parameter is crucial for defining the base structure that the noise will modify.

inputs.name: strength
inputs.description: Determines the intensity of the noise applied to the latents. A higher value results in more pronounced noise effects.

inputs.name: noise
inputs.description: An optional parameter allowing for the injection of custom noise into the latent representation.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: An optional mask that can be applied to selectively introduce noise to specific areas of the latent representation.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The modified latent representation after noise injection, potentially with selective application based on an optional mask.

BNK_NoisyLatentImage.description: The Noisy Latent Image node generates a tensor of random noise as latent images, configurable by dimensions and batch size, and intended for use in generative models where noise serves as a foundational element for image synthesis.

inputs.name: source
inputs.description: Specifies the computational resource (CPU or GPU) to be used for generating the noise, affecting the execution speed and efficiency.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: Determines the initialization value for random number generation, ensuring reproducibility of the noise patterns.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Sets the width of the generated latent images, influencing the dimensions of the output noise tensor.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Sets the height of the generated latent images, influencing the dimensions of the output noise tensor.

inputs.name: batch_size
inputs.description: Defines the number of latent images to generate in a single batch, allowing for batch processing of noise generation.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The generated tensor of random noise, structured as latent images for further processing or model input.

BNK_SlerpLatent.description: The BNK_SlerpLatent node performs spherical linear interpolation (SLERP) between two latent spaces, allowing for smooth transitions and interpolations between different latent representations. It can optionally apply a mask to selectively interpolate parts of the latent spaces.

inputs.name: latents1
inputs.description: The first set of latent representations to interpolate from. It serves as the starting point for the interpolation process.

inputs.name: factor
inputs.description: A scalar factor determining the interpolation's progress between the two latent spaces. A factor of 0 returns the first latent space, while a factor of 1 returns the second.

inputs.name: latents2
inputs.description: The second set of latent representations to interpolate towards. This optional parameter allows for interpolation between two distinct latent spaces.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: An optional mask to apply during interpolation, enabling selective blending of the latent spaces based on the mask's pattern.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The interpolated latent representation, smoothly blending between the two input latent spaces according to the specified factor and optional mask.

BNK_Unsampler.description: The Unsampler node is designed to reverse the sampling process in generative models, allowing for the manipulation or refinement of latent images through specific configurations and steps. It integrates with various sampling and scheduling strategies to achieve desired outcomes.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: Specifies the generative model to be used for the unsampling process, central to determining the transformation applied to the latent image.

inputs.name: steps
inputs.description: Defines the number of steps to execute in the unsampling process, directly impacting the extent of transformation.

inputs.name: end_at_step
inputs.description: Specifies the final step at which the unsampling should conclude, allowing for partial unsampling sequences.

inputs.name: cfg
inputs.description: Configuration parameter influencing the unsampling behavior, potentially adjusting aspects like strength or direction of the process.

inputs.name: sampler_name
inputs.description: Determines the sampling strategy to be employed, affecting how the latent image is processed during unsampling.

inputs.name: scheduler
inputs.description: Selects the scheduling algorithm to control the progression of steps in the unsampling process.

inputs.name: normalize
inputs.description: Indicates whether to apply normalization to the latent image during unsampling, affecting the output's characteristics.

inputs.name: positive
inputs.description: Positive conditioning text to guide the unsampling towards generating specific features or themes in the output.

inputs.name: negative
inputs.description: Negative conditioning text to steer the unsampling away from certain features or themes, refining the output.

inputs.name: latent_image
inputs.description: The initial latent image to be transformed through the unsampling process, serving as the starting point.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The transformed latent image resulting from the unsampling process, reflecting the applied configurations and steps.

GroundingDinoModelLoader (segment anythi.description: This node is designed to load a specific GroundingDINO model based on the provided model name. It facilitates the utilization of GroundingDINO models for segmentation tasks by preparing the model for inference.

inputs.name: model_name
inputs.description: Specifies the name of the GroundingDINO model to be loaded. This parameter is crucial as it determines which model will be prepared for the segmentation task.

outputs.name: grounding_dino_model
outputs.description: The loaded GroundingDINO model, ready for performing segmentation tasks.

GroundingDinoSAMSegment (segment anythin.description: The GroundingDinoSAMSegment node is designed to leverage the capabilities of the GroundingDINO model for segmenting various objects within an image. It utilizes advanced neural network architectures, including transformers and Swin Transformers, to accurately identify and segment objects by understanding their context and relationships within the image.

inputs.name: sam_model
inputs.description: Specifies the SAM model to be used in conjunction with the GroundingDINO model for the segmentation task. This model assists in refining the segmentation results obtained from GroundingDINO.

inputs.name: grounding_dino_model
inputs.description: Specifies the GroundingDINO model to be used for initial object detection within the image. This model identifies potential objects of interest based on the provided prompt.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed. The GroundingDINO model first identifies objects within this image, which are then segmented by the SAM model.

inputs.name: prompt
inputs.description: A text prompt that guides the GroundingDINO model in identifying objects of interest within the image. This prompt helps focus the model's attention on relevant objects.

inputs.name: threshold
inputs.description: A threshold value that determines the sensitivity of object detection by the GroundingDINO model. Objects with confidence scores above this threshold are considered for segmentation.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The segmented images obtained after processing. Each segmented object is returned as a separate image.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The segmentation masks corresponding to each segmented object in the image. These masks indicate the precise area of each object within the original image.

InvertMask (segment anything).description: The InvertMask node is designed for the inversion of mask values, effectively flipping the masked and unmasked areas. This operation is fundamental in image processing tasks where the focus of interest needs to be switched between the foreground and background.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The 'mask' parameter represents the input mask whose values are to be inverted. This inversion process is crucial for tasks that require toggling the areas of interest within an image.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The output is a mask with inverted values, where previously masked areas are now unmasked and vice versa, facilitating operations that require the opposite area of interest.

IsMaskEmpty.description: The IsMaskEmptyNode node is designed to determine if a given mask is entirely empty, meaning it contains no marked areas. It provides a simple yet essential functionality for mask analysis within the context of segmentation tasks, enabling the identification of masks that lack any significant content.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The 'mask' parameter represents the input mask to be analyzed. It is crucial for determining whether the mask is empty or contains any marked areas, directly influencing the node's output.

outputs.name: boolean_number
outputs.description: The output is a boolean value represented as a number (0 for false, meaning the mask is not empty, and 1 for true, indicating the mask is empty), indicating whether the input mask is entirely devoid of marked areas.

SAMModelLoader (segment anything).description: The SAMModelLoader node is designed to load and prepare SAM (Segment Anything Model) models for use in image segmentation tasks. It handles the retrieval and initialization of various SAM models, ensuring they are ready for segmentation operations.

inputs.name: model_name
inputs.description: Specifies the name of the SAM model to be loaded. This parameter is crucial for determining which specific model is retrieved and initialized for segmentation tasks.

outputs.name: sam_model
outputs.description: The loaded and initialized SAM model, ready for segmentation tasks.

ttN advanced xyPlot.description: The `ttN advanced xyPlot` node is designed for advanced plotting capabilities, focusing on generating and manipulating XY plots. It enables the creation of plots based on X, Y, and optionally Z coordinates, with features such as flipping the X and Y axes, adjusting grid spacing, and saving individual plots. This node is tailored for visualizing complex data relationships through customizable 2D and 3D plots.

inputs.name: grid_spacing
inputs.description: Specifies the spacing between grid lines in the plot, affecting the plot's resolution and visual density.

inputs.name: save_individuals
inputs.description: Determines whether to save each plotted point as an individual file, enabling detailed analysis of specific data points.

inputs.name: flip_xy
inputs.description: Controls whether the X and Y axes should be swapped, allowing for alternative data perspective visualization.

inputs.name: x_plot
inputs.description: The X coordinates for plotting, defining the horizontal positioning of data points.

inputs.name: y_plot
inputs.description: The Y coordinates for plotting, defining the vertical positioning of data points.

inputs.name: z_plot
inputs.description: The Z coordinates for plotting, adding a third dimension to the visualization when applicable.

outputs.name: adv_xyPlot
outputs.description: The generated XY plot data, including coordinates and configuration settings for visualization.

ttN advPlot combo.description: The node ttN_advPlot_combo is designed for generating advanced plot text outputs based on a combination of input parameters such as node identifiers, widget types, and mode selections. It dynamically constructs plot text by mapping values to specified labels and formatting them for display, supporting customization of plot elements through various configurations including range and selection modes.

inputs.name: node
inputs.description: Specifies the node identifier used in the plot text, essential for linking the plot elements to their respective nodes.

inputs.name: widget
inputs.description: Defines the widget type associated with the plot values, playing a crucial role in how values are presented and interacted with in the plot.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Determines the mode of value selection for plotting, such as 'all', 'range', or 'select', affecting how values are gathered and displayed.

inputs.name: start_from
inputs.description: Specifies the starting point for 'range' mode, indicating the beginning of the value range to be plotted.

inputs.name: end_with
inputs.description: Defines the end point for 'range' mode, marking the conclusion of the value range to be plotted.

inputs.name: select
inputs.description: Indicates the widget used for 'select' mode, allowing specific values to be chosen for plotting.

inputs.name: selection
inputs.description: Contains the selected values for plotting in 'select' mode, serving as a direct input of plot data.

inputs.name: label_type
inputs.description: Determines the labeling scheme for the plot elements, influencing the textual representation and organization of plot data.

outputs.name: plot_text
outputs.description: The generated plot text, encapsulating the formatted plot elements based on the input parameters.

ttN advPlot range.description: The node ttN_advPlot_range is designed to generate a range of values for plotting purposes, providing a flexible way to create customized plot labels and values based on specified parameters. It supports different modes of range generation, including step-based and numerical step intervals, and allows for the inclusion of custom labels, making it suitable for a wide array of plotting scenarios.

inputs.name: node
inputs.description: Connects to an xyPlot node, determining the context and options for the range generation.

inputs.name: widget
inputs.description: Selects a specific widget from the connected node to apply the range generation, influencing the plot's output.

inputs.name: range_mode
inputs.description: Defines the method of range generation, such as step-based or numerical steps, affecting how values are calculated.

inputs.name: start
inputs.description: Specifies the starting value of the range, serving as the initial point from which the range generation begins.

inputs.name: step
inputs.description: Determines the increment between each value in the range, allowing for precise control over the distribution of values.

inputs.name: stop
inputs.description: Defines the ending value of the range, marking the limit up to which values are generated.

inputs.name: include_stop
inputs.description: Determines whether the stop value is included in the range, allowing for precise control over the range's boundaries.

inputs.name: num_steps
inputs.description: Indicates the number of steps or intervals within the specified range, enabling detailed customization of the range's granularity.

inputs.name: label_type
inputs.description: Specifies the type of label to be used for each value in the range, offering options for different levels of detail in labeling.

outputs.name: plot_text
outputs.description: Generates a textual representation of the range values with labels, suitable for display or further processing.

ttN advPlot string.description: This node is designed to generate advanced plotting strings based on specified parameters, including node identification, widget interaction, and value formatting. It dynamically constructs plot text elements that can be used to visualize data or control elements in a UI context, emphasizing flexibility in label presentation and numerical value adjustment.

inputs.name: node
inputs.description: Identifies the node to which the plot string will be associated, enabling dynamic interaction with xyPlot options.

inputs.name: widget
inputs.description: Specifies the widget to interact with, allowing for dynamic selection of options based on the node's configuration.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The text input that will be split and formatted according to the delimiter to generate plot values.

inputs.name: delimiter
inputs.description: Defines the character or sequence used to split the text input into individual plot values.

inputs.name: label_type
inputs.description: Determines the type of label to be used for each plot value, affecting the presentation and information included.

outputs.name: plot_text
outputs.description: The generated plot text, ready for use in visualization or UI control.

ttN concat.description: The ttN concat node is designed for concatenating text strings, providing a simple yet flexible way to merge multiple text inputs into a single string. This functionality is essential in text processing workflows where combining pieces of text in various configurations is required.

inputs.name: text1
inputs.description: The first text string to be concatenated. It serves as the initial part of the final concatenated text.

inputs.name: text2
inputs.description: The second text string to be concatenated. It follows the first text in the final concatenated output.

inputs.name: text3
inputs.description: The third text string to be concatenated. It is added after the first and second texts in the final output.

inputs.name: delimiter
inputs.description: A string used to separate the concatenated texts. It defines how the texts are joined together in the final output.

outputs.name: concat
outputs.description: The result of concatenating the input texts separated by the specified delimiter.

ttN conditioning.description: The node focuses on applying conditioning transformations to input data, leveraging advanced encoding techniques to enhance or modify the data based on specified conditions. It abstracts complex conditioning logic into a more accessible interface for users, aiming to streamline the process of data manipulation and enrichment.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: Specifies the model to be used for conditioning, playing a central role in how the input data is processed and transformed.

inputs.name: clip
inputs.description: Defines the CLIP model parameters to be used in conjunction with the main model for conditioning, affecting the outcome of the transformation.

inputs.name: loras
inputs.description: Specifies the LoRA configurations to be applied, influencing the conditioning process by adjusting the model's behavior.

inputs.name: positive
inputs.description: The positive text input for conditioning, used to guide the model towards desired attributes or outcomes.

inputs.name: positive_token_normalization
inputs.description: Normalization method for the positive text, affecting how the text is processed before conditioning.

inputs.name: positive_weight_interpretation
inputs.description: Determines how the positive text's weight is interpreted during the conditioning process, influencing the model's adjustments.

inputs.name: negative
inputs.description: The negative text input for conditioning, used to steer the model away from undesired attributes or outcomes.

inputs.name: negative_token_normalization
inputs.description: Normalization method for the negative text, affecting how the text is processed before conditioning.

inputs.name: negative_weight_interpretation
inputs.description: Determines how the negative text's weight is interpreted during the conditioning process, influencing the model's adjustments.

inputs.name: optional_lora_stack
inputs.description: An optional stack of LoRA configurations to be applied, providing additional customization to the conditioning process.

inputs.name: prepend_positive
inputs.description: Text to prepend to the positive input, further customizing the conditioning process.

inputs.name: prepend_negative
inputs.description: Text to prepend to the negative input, further customizing the conditioning process.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: Returns the conditioned model after applying the specified transformations.

outputs.name: positive
outputs.description: Outputs the positive conditioning effects applied to the model.

outputs.name: negative
outputs.description: Outputs the negative conditioning effects applied to the model.

outputs.name: clip
outputs.description: Returns the CLIP model parameters used during the conditioning process.

outputs.name: pos_string
outputs.description: Outputs the final positive string after conditioning, reflecting the combined and processed input.

outputs.name: neg_string
outputs.description: Outputs the final negative string after conditioning, reflecting the combined and processed input.

ttN debugInput.description: The node is designed for debugging purposes, allowing users to input various parameters and observe their effects in a controlled environment. It primarily focuses on capturing and displaying input values to facilitate troubleshooting and analysis of data flow within the system.

inputs.name: print_to_console
inputs.description: Determines whether the debug information should be printed to the console, enabling or disabling console output.

inputs.name: console_title
inputs.description: Specifies the title to be displayed on the console during debugging, serving as an identifier for the debug session.

inputs.name: console_color
inputs.description: Specifies the color in which the console text is displayed, allowing for visual differentiation of debug outputs.

inputs.name: debug
inputs.description: An optional parameter for additional debugging information, enhancing the granularity of the debug output.

ttN float.description: The `ttN float` node is designed to perform conversions involving floating-point numbers. It takes a floating-point number as input and outputs the same number in three different formats: as a float, as an integer by truncating the decimal part, and as a string representation of the float. This node is useful in scenarios where different representations of a floating-point number are needed for further processing or display purposes.

inputs.name: float
inputs.description: The `float` parameter is the primary input for the `ttN float` node, representing the floating-point number to be converted. It is crucial for determining the output in three different formats: float, integer, and string. The precision and value of this input directly affect the conversion results.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The original floating-point number inputted to the node, unchanged.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: The integer part of the input floating-point number, obtained by truncating the decimal part.

outputs.name: text
outputs.description: The string representation of the input floating-point number, preserving its decimal part.

ttN hiresfixScale.description: The ttN hiresfixScale node specializes in enhancing image resolution through various upscale methods, including model-based and algorithmic approaches. It provides options for rescaling images after model application, adjusting the scale by percentage or to specific dimensions while maintaining aspect ratios, and optionally outputting the result in latent space. This node is designed to improve image quality and detail, catering to both standard and custom upscale needs.

inputs.name: model_name
inputs.description: Specifies the name of the upscale model to be used for enhancing the image resolution. It's essential for selecting the appropriate model-based upscale method.

inputs.name: vae
inputs.description: The variational autoencoder used for decoding or encoding images when required, playing a crucial role in the upscale process.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be upscaled. This parameter is the starting point of the upscale process and determines the initial quality and resolution.

inputs.name: rescale_after_model
inputs.description: Indicates whether the image should be rescaled after being processed by the upscale model, affecting the final image size and resolution.

inputs.name: rescale_method
inputs.description: Defines the method used for rescaling the image after model upscaling, influencing the final appearance and dimensions of the image.

inputs.name: rescale
inputs.description: Specifies how the image should be rescaled, offering options like by percentage, to specific width/height, or to maintain aspect ratio by adjusting the longer side.

inputs.name: percent
inputs.description: The percentage by which the image should be rescaled, relevant when the 'rescale' parameter is set to 'by percentage'. It directly impacts the final image size.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: The target width for the image after rescaling, applicable when the 'rescale' parameter is set to 'to Width/Height'. It determines the final width of the image.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: The target height for the image after rescaling, applicable when the 'rescale' parameter is set to 'to Width/Height'. It determines the final height of the image.

inputs.name: longer_side
inputs.description: The target size for the longer side of the image when maintaining aspect ratio, affecting the final dimensions while preserving the image's original proportions.

inputs.name: crop
inputs.description: Determines if and how the upscaled image should be cropped, offering options like disabled or center cropping. This affects the final composition of the image.

inputs.name: image_output
inputs.description: Controls how the upscaled image is outputted, with options for hiding, previewing, saving, or a combination of hiding and saving. This affects how users interact with and access the final image.

inputs.name: save_prefix
inputs.description: The prefix added to the filename when saving the upscaled image, allowing for easy identification and organization of output files.

inputs.name: output_latent
inputs.description: Indicates whether the result should also include the upscaled image in latent space, enabling further manipulation or analysis in this format.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The upscaled image in latent space, available when output_latent is set to True, allowing for further manipulation or analysis.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The final upscaled image, showcasing the improved resolution and detail achieved through the upscale process.

ttN imageOutput.description: The `ttN_imageOutput` node is designed for image processing and output management within the ComfyUI tinyterraNodes framework. It encapsulates functionality for handling image outputs, including saving images with specific configurations, adjusting image visibility based on user-defined parameters, and potentially transforming images for further use. This node plays a crucial role in the workflow by providing flexible output options and integrating with other components for image manipulation and storage.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed or managed by the node, serving as the primary data for output operations.

inputs.name: image_output
inputs.description: Specifies the desired output behavior for images, such as whether to display, hide, or save the images, influencing how the node processes and returns image data.

inputs.name: output_path
inputs.description: The file path where the image should be saved if the saving option is selected, providing a location for output storage.

inputs.name: save_prefix
inputs.description: A prefix added to the saved image filename, allowing for organized naming conventions.

inputs.name: number_padding
inputs.description: Determines the padding for numbering saved images, facilitating ordered file naming.

inputs.name: file_type
inputs.description: The file type for the saved image, such as PNG or JPEG, defining the format of the output file.

inputs.name: overwrite_existing
inputs.description: A boolean indicating whether existing files with the same name should be overwritten, controlling file management behavior.

inputs.name: embed_workflow
inputs.description: Indicates whether the workflow metadata should be embedded within the image file, enhancing traceability.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The processed image, returned based on the specified image output behavior.

ttN imageREMBG.description: The node is designed to remove the background from images using the REMBG library, converting images to a format suitable for further processing or visualization. It emphasizes the extraction of the main subject by eliminating the background, potentially enhancing the focus on the subject matter for subsequent operations.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed for background removal. This parameter is crucial as it directly influences the effectiveness of the background removal process.

inputs.name: image_output
inputs.description: Determines how the output image is handled, offering options such as hiding, previewing, saving, or a combination of hiding and saving. This parameter affects the output format and visibility of the processed image.

inputs.name: save_prefix
inputs.description: Specifies the prefix for saving the processed image, indicating how the output file names should begin. This parameter is essential when the image output is set to save, guiding the naming convention of the saved files.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The processed image tensor with the background removed, ready for further use.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: A mask tensor indicating the areas of the image where the background was removed.

ttN int.description: The `ttN int` node is designed for integer manipulation within the tinyterra utility category, offering functionality to convert an integer input into multiple formats.

inputs.name: int
inputs.description: Specifies the integer value to be converted. This parameter is central to the node's operation, as it determines the base value that will be transformed into different formats.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: Returns the original integer input without modification.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: Converts and returns the input integer as a float.

outputs.name: text
outputs.description: Converts and returns the input integer as a string.

ttN KSampler_v2.description: The ttN KSampler_v2 node is designed for advanced sampling in generative models, offering a flexible interface to control the sampling process. It integrates various sampling and scheduling strategies, noise control mechanisms, and optional conditioning inputs to generate or refine images based on latent representations. This node is tailored for customization and experimentation in image generation workflows, enabling users to fine-tune the balance between fidelity and diversity in the generated outputs.

ttN multiModelMerge.description: The `ttN_multiModelMerge` node specializes in combining multiple models or CLIPs through various interpolation methods, enabling the creation of hybrid models that leverage the strengths of each input model. It supports a range of interpolation strategies, such as weighted sum and addition of differences, to fine-tune the merging process according to specific requirements.

inputs.name: ckpt_A_name
inputs.description: Specifies the checkpoint name for model A, used as an input for model merging.

inputs.name: config_A_name
inputs.description: Specifies the configuration name for model A, used alongside the checkpoint name to load the model.

inputs.name: ckpt_B_name
inputs.description: Specifies the checkpoint name for model B, used as an input for model merging.

inputs.name: config_B_name
inputs.description: Specifies the configuration name for model B, used alongside the checkpoint name to load the model.

inputs.name: ckpt_C_name
inputs.description: Specifies the checkpoint name for model C, used as an input for model merging.

inputs.name: config_C_name
inputs.description: Specifies the configuration name for model C, used alongside the checkpoint name to load the model.

inputs.name: model_interpolation
inputs.description: Defines the interpolation method to be used for merging models.

inputs.name: model_multiplier
inputs.description: The multiplier factor used in the interpolation of models.

inputs.name: clip_interpolation
inputs.description: Defines the interpolation method to be used for merging CLIP models.

inputs.name: clip_multiplier
inputs.description: The multiplier factor used in the interpolation of CLIP models.

inputs.name: model_A_override
inputs.description: Overrides the model A with a specified model, bypassing the need for a checkpoint.

inputs.name: model_B_override
inputs.description: Overrides the model B with a specified model, bypassing the need for a checkpoint.

inputs.name: model_C_override
inputs.description: Overrides the model C with a specified model, bypassing the need for a checkpoint.

inputs.name: clip_A_override

inputs.name: clip_B_override
inputs.description: Overrides the CLIP model B with a specified CLIP, bypassing the need for a checkpoint.

inputs.name: clip_C_override

outputs.name: clip

ttN pipe2BASIC.description: The ttN pipe2BASIC node is designed to simplify and streamline the processing pipeline by converting a complex input pipeline into a basic form. This node extracts essential components from the input pipeline, focusing on core elements such as model, clip, vae, and conditioning parameters, to facilitate further processing or analysis.

inputs.name: pipe
inputs.description: The 'pipe' parameter represents the complex input pipeline that is to be simplified. It is essential for the operation as it contains all the data and settings that will be streamlined into a basic form.

outputs.name: basic_pipe
outputs.description: The 'basic_pipe' output contains the simplified version of the input pipeline, focusing on essential components for further processing.

outputs.name: pipe
outputs.description: Returns the original input pipeline, allowing for reference or further modifications.

ttN pipe2DETAILER.description: The ttN pipe2DETAILER node is designed to enhance and detail the data pipeline by integrating additional processing steps. It focuses on refining and enriching the pipeline's output, making it more detailed and tailored for subsequent operations or analyses.

inputs.name: pipe
inputs.description: The 'pipe' input is the primary data structure that carries the flow of data through the node. It is essential for the node's operation, serving as the basis for the detailing process.

inputs.name: bbox_detector
inputs.description: The 'bbox_detector' input specifies the bounding box detector to be used for identifying regions of interest within the data. This is crucial for the detailing process, as it allows for targeted enhancements.

inputs.name: wildcard
inputs.description: The 'wildcard' input allows for flexible specification of additional conditions or parameters that can be applied during the detailing process. It enables customization and fine-tuning of the output.

inputs.name: sam_model_opt

inputs.name: segm_detector_opt

inputs.name: detailer_hook
inputs.description: An optional input that allows for the integration of custom detailing functions or hooks. This enables the node to perform highly customized detailing operations based on specific requirements.

outputs.name: detailer_pipe

outputs.name: pipe

ttN pipeEDIT.description: The ttN pipeEDIT node is designed for editing and refining the parameters and settings of a pipeline, allowing for the customization and optimization of the pipeline's behavior and output. It focuses on enhancing the flexibility and control over the pipeline's execution by enabling adjustments to its components and configurations.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: Specifies the model component of the pipeline, allowing for its selection or modification.

inputs.name: pos
inputs.description: Defines the positive conditioning aspect of the pipeline, enabling its specification or alteration.

inputs.name: neg
inputs.description: Specifies the negative conditioning component, allowing for adjustments to how the pipeline handles negative inputs.

inputs.name: latent
inputs.description: Represents the latent space configuration of the pipeline, permitting adjustments to its handling of latent variables.

inputs.name: vae
inputs.description: Specifies the VAE (Variational Autoencoder) component, enabling its selection or modification within the pipeline.

inputs.name: clip
inputs.description: Defines the CLIP model component of the pipeline, allowing for its specification or alteration.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: Specifies the image component of the pipeline, enabling adjustments to how images are handled.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: Represents the seed value for random number generation within the pipeline, allowing for its specification to ensure reproducibility.

outputs.name: neg
outputs.description: Outputs the adjusted negative conditioning component of the pipeline.

outputs.name: latent

outputs.name: vae

ttN pipeEncodeConcat.description: The ttN pipeEncodeConcat node is designed for advanced text processing within a pipeline, focusing on encoding and concatenating text inputs based on specific conditioning. It leverages token normalization and weight interpretation to refine the input text, aiming to enhance the overall quality and relevance of the generated content.

ttN pipeIN.description: The ttN pipeIN node is designed for initializing and configuring pipelines within the tinyterra ecosystem, specifically tailored for legacy applications. It focuses on setting up the initial parameters required for a pipeline, including models, conditioning, latent space, VAE, CLIP, and seed values, along with optional image inputs.

ttN pipeLoraStack.description: The node is designed to integrate and manage LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) models within a processing pipeline, enabling the dynamic adjustment of model and clip strengths based on specified LoRA configurations. It facilitates the customization of AI model behavior for specific tasks or datasets by applying LoRA modifications to the underlying models.

inputs.description: A boolean toggle to enable or disable the application of LoRA models within the pipeline.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Specifies the operation mode, either 'simple' or 'advanced', determining the complexity of LoRA model adjustments.

inputs.name: num_loras
inputs.description: The number of LoRA models to be applied, allowing for multiple adaptations.

inputs.name: optional_pipe
inputs.description: An optional pipeline configuration that can be modified by the LoRA adjustments.

inputs.name: model_override
inputs.description: Allows for overriding the default model with a specified one for further customization.

inputs.name: clip_override
inputs.description: Enables the override of the default clip model, facilitating custom clip adaptations.

inputs.name: optional_lora_stack

inputs.name: lora_i_name
inputs.description: Specifies the name of the ith LoRA model to be applied, determining the specific adaptation for each model.

inputs.name: lora_i_strength
inputs.description: Defines the strength of the ith LoRA model adaptation, influencing the degree of modification.

inputs.name: lora_i_model_strength

inputs.name: lora_i_clip_strength

outputs.name: lora_stack

ttN pipeOUT.description: The ttN pipeOUT node is designed for the final stage of a pipeline in the tinyterra legacy system, where it extracts and returns various components of a given pipeline such as models, conditioning data, latent representations, and more. This node serves as a crucial endpoint for retrieving processed data from the pipeline.

outputs.name: neg

outputs.name: vae

outputs.name: seed

ttN seed.description: The ttN seed node is designed to manage and apply seed values for generating or manipulating data within the TinyTerra ecosystem. It integrates with various components such as models, conditioning parameters, and latent spaces to ensure consistent and controlled outcomes. This node plays a crucial role in the procedural generation or transformation of content, allowing for reproducibility and customization through seed manipulation.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: The seed parameter is used to initialize the random number generator, ensuring that the generation or manipulation of data can be reproducible. It is crucial for achieving consistent results across different runs.

outputs.name: seed
outputs.description: The seed value used in the process, ensuring reproducibility and consistency of the results.

ttN text.description: The `ttN text` node is designed for text manipulation within the tinyterra ecosystem, offering functionalities to process and transform text data based on dynamic prompts. It encapsulates the ability to handle multiline text inputs, allowing for versatile text processing operations.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The `text` parameter is the primary input for text manipulation, accepting multiline strings. It supports dynamic prompts, enabling flexible and context-aware text processing.

outputs.name: text
outputs.description: The output is a transformed or processed version of the input text, maintaining the string data type.

ttN text3BOX_3WAYconcat.description: This node is designed to concatenate three input strings in various combinations, allowing for flexible string manipulation and concatenation strategies. It supports custom delimiters and can generate multiple output strings, including each input string individually, pairs of input strings concatenated together, and all three input strings concatenated.

inputs.name: text1
inputs.description: The first text string to be concatenated. It plays a crucial role in the concatenation process, affecting the output by being part of multiple concatenation combinations.

inputs.name: text2
inputs.description: The second text string to be concatenated. It is essential for creating concatenated pairs with the first and third strings, as well as contributing to the overall three-string concatenation.

inputs.name: text3
inputs.description: The third text string to be concatenated. This string is combined with the first and second strings in various ways to produce the node's output.

inputs.name: delimiter
inputs.description: A string used as the delimiter in the concatenation process. It defines the separator between the concatenated strings, impacting the format and readability of the output.

outputs.name: text1
outputs.description: Returns the first input text string as is, without any concatenation.

outputs.name: text2
outputs.description: Returns the second input text string as is, without any concatenation.

outputs.name: text3
outputs.description: Returns the third input text string as is, without any concatenation.
The concatenation of the first and second input text strings, separated by the specified delimiter.
The concatenation of the first and third input text strings, separated by the specified delimiter.
The concatenation of the second and third input text strings, separated by the specified delimiter.

outputs.name: concat
outputs.description: The concatenation of all three input text strings, separated by the specified delimiter.

ttN text7BOX_concat.description: This node is designed to concatenate up to seven text strings, allowing for flexible text manipulation and combination. It supports custom delimiters, including new lines, to format the concatenated result according to specific requirements.

inputs.name: text1

inputs.name: text2

inputs.name: text3
inputs.description: The third text string to be concatenated, further extending the combined text output.

inputs.name: text4
inputs.description: The fourth text string to be concatenated, contributing to the growing list of combined texts.

inputs.name: text5
inputs.description: The fifth text string to be concatenated, adding more content to the concatenation.

inputs.name: text6
inputs.description: The sixth text string to be concatenated, continuing to build upon the concatenated text.

inputs.name: text7
inputs.description: The seventh and final text string to be concatenated, completing the concatenation process.

inputs.name: delimiter
inputs.description: The delimiter used to separate each text string in the concatenation. It can significantly affect the formatting of the output.

outputs.name: text1
outputs.description: Returns the first input text string, unchanged.

outputs.name: text2
outputs.description: Returns the second input text string, unchanged.

outputs.name: text3
outputs.description: Returns the third input text string, unchanged.

outputs.name: text4
outputs.description: Returns the fourth input text string, unchanged.

outputs.name: text5
outputs.description: Returns the fifth input text string, unchanged.

outputs.name: text6
outputs.description: Returns the sixth input text string, unchanged.

outputs.name: text7
outputs.description: Returns the seventh input text string, unchanged.

outputs.name: concat
outputs.description: Returns the concatenated result of all seven input text strings, separated by the specified delimiter.

ttN textCycleLine.description: The ttN textCycleLine node is designed for cycling through lines of text based on a given index and control method. It allows for dynamic text manipulation by selecting specific lines from a larger text body, supporting operations like increment, decrement, random selection, or fixed position access.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The 'text' parameter is the input text from which lines will be cycled through. It plays a crucial role in determining the content available for cycling and directly impacts the output based on the selected line.

inputs.name: index
inputs.description: The 'index' parameter specifies the starting point or specific line to access within the input text. Its value influences which line is selected during the cycling process.

inputs.name: index_control
inputs.description: The 'index_control' parameter determines the method of cycling through lines, such as incrementing, decrementing, randomizing, or fixing the index. This affects how the next line is selected from the input text.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: unknown

ttN textDebug.description: The ttN textDebug node is designed for debugging purposes within the tinyterra text processing framework. It allows for the inspection and manipulation of text data, providing a means to evaluate and refine text processing workflows.

inputs.name: print_to_console
inputs.description: Determines whether the debugged text data should be printed to the console, facilitating real-time inspection.

inputs.name: execute
inputs.description: Controls when the node executes, with options like 'Always' or 'On Change', to optimize debugging efficiency.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The 'text' input is essential for providing the text data to be debugged. It supports multiline input and dynamic prompts, enabling flexible and interactive debugging sessions.

outputs.name: text
outputs.description: The output 'text' is the processed or inspected text data, allowing for direct observation of the debugging results.

ttN tinyLoader.description: The ttN tinyLoader node is designed for loading and initializing tiny models within the ComfyUI framework, facilitating the integration and management of lightweight models for efficient processing and analysis.

ttN xyPlot.description: The ttN xyPlot node is designed for generating and manipulating XY plots, including the ability to flip axes, manage plot points for X, Y, and optionally Z dimensions, and configure plot appearance and behavior. It supports advanced plotting features such as grid spacing and saving individual plot elements, catering to customized visualization needs.

inputs.name: latent_id

inputs.name: output_individuals
inputs.description: Determines whether individual plot elements should be outputted, enabling detailed analysis and customization of plot components.

inputs.name: flip_xy
inputs.description: Controls whether the X and Y axes should be swapped, allowing for flexible orientation of the plot based on data or preference.

inputs.name: x_axis

inputs.name: x_values

inputs.name: y_axis

inputs.name: y_values

outputs.name: xyPlot

UltimateSDUpscale.description: The UltimateSDUpscale node integrates advanced upscaling techniques to enhance image resolution and quality within the ComfyUI framework, leveraging the Ultimate SD Upscale by Coyote-A. It utilizes deep learning models and custom algorithms to upscale images, apply seam fixing, and redraw images for improved visual fidelity, supporting various modes and configurations for tailored image processing.

inputs.description: The input image tensor to be upscaled. It plays a crucial role in determining the final output quality and resolution, as the node applies deep learning-based upscaling techniques to enhance the image.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The deep learning model used for processing the image. It is essential for the upscaling and enhancement process, influencing the quality of the output.

inputs.name: positive

inputs.name: negative

inputs.name: vae
inputs.description: The variational autoencoder used for image manipulation, playing a key role in the image's quality and detail enhancement.

inputs.name: upscale_by
inputs.description: The factor by which the image will be upscaled. This directly influences the size and detail level of the output image, enabling precise control over the upscaling process.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: A seed value for random number generation, ensuring reproducibility of the upscaling process.

inputs.name: steps
inputs.description: The number of steps to perform in the upscaling process, affecting the detail and quality of the output image.

inputs.name: cfg
inputs.description: Configuration parameter influencing the generation process, allowing for fine-tuning of the upscaling results.

inputs.name: sampler_name
inputs.description: The name of the sampler used in the processing, affecting the randomness and variation in the upscaling process.

inputs.name: scheduler
inputs.description: The scheduler used for managing the upscaling process, contributing to the efficiency and outcome of the image enhancement.

inputs.name: denoise
inputs.description: The denoising factor applied during upscaling, aiming to reduce noise and improve image clarity.

inputs.name: upscale_model
inputs.description: The specific upscaling model used, determining the technique and quality of the upscaling process.

inputs.name: mode_type
inputs.description: Specifies the upscaling mode to be used, affecting the upscaling technique and final image appearance. This parameter allows for customization of the upscaling process to suit different image types and desired outcomes.

inputs.name: tile_width
inputs.description: The width of the tiles used in the upscaling process, affecting the granularity and detail of the upscaled image.

inputs.name: tile_height
inputs.description: The height of the tiles used in the upscaling process, affecting the granularity and detail of the upscaled image.

inputs.name: mask_blur
inputs.description: The amount of blur applied to the mask during upscaling, affecting the smoothness and blending of the upscaled image.

inputs.name: tile_padding
inputs.description: The padding around each tile during upscaling, affecting the overlap and blending between tiles.

inputs.name: seam_fix_mode
inputs.description: Determines the seam fixing strategy to be applied after upscaling, aiming to improve the visual coherence of the upscaled image by addressing potential artifacts at tile boundaries.

inputs.name: seam_fix_denoise

inputs.name: seam_fix_padding
inputs.description: The padding applied during seam fixing, affecting the area of influence for seam corrections.

inputs.name: force_uniform_tiles
inputs.description: A boolean indicating whether to force uniform tile sizes during upscaling, affecting the consistency and layout of the upscaled image.

inputs.name: tiled_decode

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image tensor representing the upscaled image. This tensor encapsulates the enhanced resolution and quality achieved through the upscaling process, ready for further processing or display.

UltimateSDUpscaleCustomSample.description: This node specializes in enhancing image quality through upscaling, leveraging advanced techniques to refine image details and textures. inputs.name: mask_blur
inputs.description: The level of blur applied to the mask used in tiled upscaling, affecting the blending of tiles.

inputs.name: tile_padding

inputs.name: seam_fix_mode

inputs.name: seam_fix_denoise
inputs.description: The degree of denoising applied specifically for seam fixing, affecting the smoothness of seams.

inputs.name: seam_fix_width
inputs.description: The width of the area affected by seam fixing, influencing the extent of seam correction.

inputs.name: seam_fix_mask_blur
inputs.description: The amount of blur applied to the seam fix mask, affecting the smoothness of seam corrections.

inputs.name: seam_fix_padding
inputs.description: Padding added around the seam fix area, affecting the blending of corrected seams.

inputs.name: force_uniform_tiles
inputs.description: A flag indicating whether to force uniform tile sizes during processing, affecting the consistency of processing across the image.

inputs.name: tiled_decode
inputs.description: Indicates whether decoding is performed in a tiled manner, affecting the method of image reconstruction.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: Returns the processed image, which has undergone enhancements and conditioning as per the specified inputs but retains its original size.

Empty Images.description: This node is designed to generate a batch of empty images with specified dimensions and color. It serves as a foundational tool for creating placeholder or background images in various image processing and generation tasks.

inputs.name: num_images
inputs.description: Specifies the total number of images to generate. This parameter can be used to control the overall output volume when generating images.

inputs.name: splits
inputs.description: Defines how the total number of images should be divided into separate batches or groups. This can be used to create varied sets of images within the overall batch.

inputs.name: batch_size
inputs.description: Determines the number of images to generate in a single batch. This allows for the creation of multiple images at once, optimizing processing time.

outputs.name: Image
outputs.description: The output is a batch of images with the specified dimensions and color.

ImageListLoader.description: The ImageListLoader node is designed to load a list of images from a specified source, facilitating the handling and manipulation of multiple images in a batch processing or image analysis workflow.

inputs.name: folder_path
inputs.description: Specifies the directory path from which images will be loaded. This input is essential for locating the source of images that the node will process.

inputs.name: file_filter
inputs.description: Defines the file pattern to filter the images to be loaded, such as '*.png'. This allows for selective loading of images based on their file type or naming convention.

inputs.name: sort_method
inputs.description: Determines the sorting method for the loaded images, either 'numerical' or 'alphabetical'. This affects the order in which images are processed and is crucial for workflows requiring a specific sequence.

outputs.name: Images
outputs.description: Outputs the loaded images as a list, making them available for further processing or analysis. This is essential for workflows that require manipulation of multiple images simultaneously.

Join Float Lists.description: This node is designed to merge two lists of floating-point numbers into a single list, maintaining the order of elements as they appear in the input lists. It facilitates operations that require the concatenation of numerical data, such as combining datasets or aggregating results from different sources.

inputs.name: In1
inputs.description: Represents the first list of floating-point numbers to be joined. Its elements are combined with those of 'In2' to form a single, concatenated list.

inputs.name: In2
inputs.description: Denotes the second list of floating-point numbers to be merged with 'In1'. The order of elements in 'In2' follows those of 'In1' in the concatenated output list.

outputs.name: Joined
outputs.description: The concatenated list of floating-point numbers derived from 'In1' and 'In2'. This output preserves the order of elements as they appear in the input lists.

Join Image Lists.description: The Join Image Lists node is designed to merge multiple lists of images into a single list, while also providing the sizes of the original lists. This functionality is essential for operations that require the consolidation of image data from various sources, ensuring seamless integration and manipulation of image collections.

inputs.name: In1
inputs.description: Represents the first list of images to be joined. It is a required input that plays a crucial role in initiating the merging process.

inputs.name: In2
inputs.description: Represents the second list of images to be joined. It is a required input that contributes to the merging process alongside the first list.

inputs.name: In3
inputs.description: An optional list of images that can be included in the merging process, providing flexibility in handling varying numbers of image lists.

inputs.name: In4
inputs.description: An optional list of images that can be included in the merging process, providing flexibility in handling varying numbers of image lists.

inputs.name: In5
inputs.description: An optional list of images that can be included in the merging process, providing flexibility in handling varying numbers of image lists.

outputs.name: Joined
outputs.description: The combined list of images from all input lists.

outputs.name: Sizes
outputs.description: A list of integers representing the sizes of the original input lists.

KepStringList.description: The KepStringList node is designed to aggregate and process multiple string inputs into a list format, accommodating both required and optional text inputs. It effectively combines various textual elements, providing a flexible mechanism for handling and organizing string data within a list structure.

inputs.name: Text1
inputs.description: A required string input that contributes to the formation of the string list.

inputs.name: Text2
inputs.description: Another required string input that is included in the string list.

inputs.name: Text3
inputs.description: An optional string input that can be included in the string list if provided.

inputs.name: Text4
inputs.description: An optional string input that can be included in the string list if provided.

inputs.name: Text5
inputs.description: An optional string input that can be included in the string list if provided.

inputs.name: Text6
inputs.description: An optional string input that can be included in the string list if provided.

inputs.name: Text7
inputs.description: An optional string input that can be included in the string list if provided.

outputs.name: Strings
outputs.description: The list of strings aggregated from the input texts.

outputs.name: Num Strings
outputs.description: The number of strings included in the output list, indicating the list's length.

KepStringListFromNewline.description: This node is designed to convert a multiline string into a list of strings, each representing a line from the original string. It also calculates the number of strings generated.

inputs.name: Text
inputs.description: The 'Text' parameter takes a multiline string as input, which is then split into individual strings based on newline characters. This parameter is essential for determining the content and structure of the output list.

outputs.name: Strings
outputs.description: A list of strings, each representing a line from the input multiline string.

outputs.name: Num Strings
outputs.description: The number of strings generated from splitting the input multiline string.

Kep_JoinListAny.description: The `Kep_JoinListAny` node is designed to merge multiple lists into a single list, regardless of the element types contained within those lists. This node facilitates the combination of diverse lists, enhancing flexibility in list manipulation.

inputs.name: In1
inputs.description: Represents the first input list to be joined. Its elements can be of any type, contributing to the flexibility of the node.

inputs.name: In2
inputs.description: Represents the second input list to be joined, similar to `In1` in that it can contain elements of any type.

inputs.name: In3
inputs.description: An optional third input list that can be joined with the previous lists. It can contain elements of any type.

inputs.name: In4
inputs.description: An optional fourth input list for joining. It can contain elements of any type, further extending the node's merging capabilities.

inputs.name: In5
inputs.description: An optional fifth input list that can be joined, allowing for even more extensive list merging operations.

outputs.name: Joined
outputs.description: The merged list resulting from the combination of all input lists.

Kep_RepeatList.description: The Kep_RepeatList node is designed to replicate a given list a specified number of times, effectively extending the list by repeating its elements. This node is part of the 'List Stuff' category, emphasizing its utility in manipulating list structures within a data processing pipeline.

inputs.name: In
inputs.description: The input list to be repeated. It serves as the base list whose elements will be replicated according to the specified count.

inputs.name: Count
inputs.description: Specifies the number of times the input list should be repeated. This parameter determines the final length of the output list by multiplying the original list's length.

outputs.name: Extended
outputs.description: The output list resulting from repeating the input list elements a specified number of times. It represents the extended version of the original list.

Kep_ReverseList.description: The Kep_ReverseList node is designed for reversing the order of elements in a list. It takes a list as input and returns a new list with the elements in reverse order, maintaining the original data types of the elements.

inputs.name: In
inputs.description: The input list to be reversed. This parameter is essential for the operation as it determines the sequence of elements that will be reversed.

outputs.name: Reversed
outputs.description: The output list with its elements in reverse order compared to the input list.

Kep_VariableImageBuilder.description: The VariableImageBuilder node is designed for generating a batch of images with specified RGBA color values and dimensions. It allows for the creation of uniform color images, which can be used for various purposes such as placeholders, backgrounds, or testing.

inputs.name: r
inputs.description: Specifies the red component of the RGBA color for the image. It influences the overall color of the generated images.

inputs.name: g
inputs.description: Specifies the green component of the RGBA color for the image. It affects the overall color of the generated images.

inputs.name: b
inputs.description: Specifies the blue component of the RGBA color for the image. It impacts the overall color of the generated images.

inputs.name: a
inputs.description: Specifies the alpha (transparency) component of the RGBA color for the image. It determines the opacity of the generated images.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Determines the width of the generated images. It defines the horizontal dimension of the images.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Determines the height of the generated images. It defines the vertical dimension of the images.

inputs.name: batch_size
inputs.description: Specifies the number of images to generate in a batch. It controls the total output volume of images.

outputs.name: Image
outputs.description: The output is a batch of images with the specified RGBA color values and dimensions.

List Length.description: The List Length node is designed to calculate the length of a given list. It abstracts the process of determining how many elements are contained within a list, providing a straightforward way to obtain this information.

inputs.name: In
inputs.description: Represents the input list whose length is to be calculated. The length of this list directly determines the output of the node.

outputs.name: Length
outputs.description: The output is the length of the input list, indicating how many elements it contains.

Range(Num Steps) - Float.description: This node generates a range of floating-point numbers based on specified start and stop values, and a number of steps. It allows for the creation of evenly spaced sequences of numbers, which can be used for various applications such as generating sample points or defining intervals.

inputs.name: start
inputs.description: Specifies the starting value of the range. It sets the initial point from which the sequence of floating-point numbers will begin.

inputs.name: stop
inputs.description: Defines the ending value of the range. It determines the final point up to which the sequence of floating-point numbers will extend.

inputs.name: num_steps
inputs.description: Determines the total number of steps or intervals within the specified range. This affects the spacing between each number in the sequence.

outputs.name: range
outputs.description: A list of floating-point numbers representing the generated range based on the input parameters.

outputs.name: range_sizes
outputs.description: A list containing the size of each generated range, indicating how many numbers are in each sequence.

Range(Num Steps) - Int.description: This node generates a range of integer values based on specified start and stop points, a number of steps, and an end mode. It allows for the creation of evenly or unevenly spaced sequences of integers, with options to include or exclude the stop point in the final range.

inputs.name: start
inputs.description: Defines the starting point of the range. It sets the initial value from which the range begins.

inputs.name: stop
inputs.description: Sets the ending point of the range. This value can be included or excluded from the final range based on the end mode.

inputs.name: num_steps
inputs.description: Specifies the number of steps (or values) to generate within the range. It determines how many integers will be included in the sequence.

inputs.name: end_mode
inputs.description: Determines whether the stop point is included ('Inclusive') or excluded ('Exclusive') from the generated range.

inputs.name: allow_uneven_steps
inputs.description: Indicates whether to allow steps that result in uneven spacing between the integers in the range.

outputs.name: range
outputs.description: The generated sequence of integers within the specified range.

outputs.name: range_sizes
outputs.description: The size of each generated range, indicating how many integers are in each sequence.

Range(Step) - Float.description: This node generates a sequence of floating-point numbers within a specified range, allowing for precise control over the start, stop, and step values. It is designed to facilitate operations that require iterating over a range of floats with specific increments, making it ideal for scenarios where uniform spacing between values is necessary.

inputs.name: start
inputs.description: Specifies the starting value of the range. It sets the lower bound for the sequence of generated numbers.

inputs.name: stop
inputs.description: Defines the ending value of the range. It sets the upper limit for the sequence of generated numbers.

inputs.name: step
inputs.description: Determines the increment between each number in the range. This value controls the spacing between consecutive numbers in the generated sequence.

inputs.name: end_mode
inputs.description: Indicates whether the stop value is inclusive or exclusive in the range. This parameter affects whether the final number in the sequence reaches or excludes the stop value.

outputs.name: range
outputs.description: The generated sequence of floating-point numbers within the specified range.

outputs.name: range_sizes
outputs.description: The size of each generated range, indicating the number of elements in each sequence.

Range(Step) - Int.description: This node generates a sequence of integers within a specified range, allowing for control over the start, stop, and step values. It is designed to facilitate the creation of integer lists based on customizable intervals and endpoints, supporting both inclusive and exclusive end modes.

inputs.name: start
inputs.description: Specifies the starting value of the range. This parameter sets the initial point from which the integer sequence begins.

inputs.name: stop
inputs.description: Determines the stopping value of the range. This parameter defines the endpoint for the integer sequence, which can be inclusive or exclusive based on the end_mode.

inputs.name: step
inputs.description: Defines the interval between each number in the range. This parameter controls the step size for the sequence generation.

inputs.name: end_mode
inputs.description: Indicates whether the stop value is inclusive or exclusive. This parameter allows for flexibility in defining the bounds of the integer sequence.

outputs.name: range
outputs.description: The generated sequence of integers within the specified range.

outputs.name: range_sizes
