outputs.description: The size of each generated integer sequence, providing insight into the number of elements within each range.

Stack Images.description: The Stack Images node is designed to aggregate multiple images into a single composite image. It supports various stacking modes and configurations, including the ability to handle batches of images, apply specific stacking directions, and incorporate optional labels for both horizontal and vertical orientations. This functionality is particularly useful for visualizing collections of images in a structured and coherent manner.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: A list of images to be stacked together. This parameter is crucial for defining the set of images that will be processed and combined into a single composite image.

inputs.name: splits
inputs.description: Defines how the images are split into batches or groups for stacking. This parameter influences the organization of images within the final composite image.

inputs.name: stack_mode
inputs.description: Specifies the direction (horizontal or vertical) in which the images within a batch are stacked. This affects the layout of the composite image.

inputs.name: batch_stack_mode
inputs.description: Determines the stacking direction of batches of images. This parameter is essential for defining the overall structure of the composite image.

inputs.name: horizontal_labels
inputs.description: Optional labels for the horizontal axis, used when the stacking direction allows for horizontal labeling. Enhances the interpretability of the composite image.

inputs.name: vertical_labels
inputs.description: Optional labels for the vertical axis, used when the stacking direction allows for vertical labeling. Enhances the interpretability of the composite image.

outputs.name: Image
outputs.description: The resulting composite image after stacking.

XYAny.description: The XYAny node is designed to generate combinations of X and Y values, optionally incorporating a third dimension, Z, to extend these combinations. It facilitates the creation and labeling of these combinations, providing fallback labels and the ability to specify custom labels. This node is particularly useful for data manipulation and preparation tasks where the relationships or interactions between different sets of data points need to be explored or visualized.

inputs.name: X
inputs.description: The primary set of values to be combined. Acts as one axis in the generation of value pairs.

inputs.name: Y
inputs.description: The secondary set of values to be combined with the X values. Acts as the other axis in the generation of value pairs.

inputs.name: X_Label_Fallback
inputs.description: Fallback labels for the X values, used when specific labels are not provided. Ensures that each X value has an associated label.

inputs.name: Y_Label_Fallback
inputs.description: Fallback labels for the Y values, used when specific labels are not provided. Ensures that each Y value has an associated label.

inputs.name: Z_Label_Fallback
inputs.description: Fallback labels for the Z values, used when specific labels are not provided. This allows for a third dimension of data to be labeled.

inputs.name: Z
inputs.description: An optional third set of values to be combined with the X and Y values, adding a third dimension to the combinations.

inputs.name: X_Labels
inputs.description: Custom labels for the X values, overriding the fallback labels if provided.

inputs.name: Y_Labels
inputs.description: Custom labels for the Y values, overriding the fallback labels if provided.

inputs.name: Z_Labels
inputs.description: Custom labels for the Z values, overriding the fallback labels if provided.

outputs.name: X Values
outputs.description: The combined X values resulting from the combinations generated by the node.

outputs.name: X Labels
outputs.description: The labels associated with the combined X values.

outputs.name: Y Values
outputs.description: The combined Y values resulting from the combinations generated by the node.

outputs.name: Y Labels
outputs.description: The labels associated with the combined Y values.

outputs.name: Z Values
outputs.description: The combined Z values resulting from the combinations generated by the node, if Z values were provided.

outputs.name: Z Labels
outputs.description: The labels associated with the combined Z values, if Z values were provided.

outputs.name: Total Images
outputs.description: The total number of combinations generated by the node.

outputs.name: Split Every
outputs.description: The interval at which the combinations are split, based on the length of the Y values.

XYImage.description: The XYImage node is designed for the complex task of generating and manipulating images based on specified parameters, including splitting, flipping, and stacking images in batches. It supports the addition of labels on different axes and the ability to handle images in a multi-dimensional (z-axis enabled) context, making it versatile for various image processing and visualization needs.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: A list of images to be processed. This parameter is crucial as it serves as the primary data that the node will manipulate through splitting, flipping, and stacking operations.

inputs.name: splits
inputs.description: Defines how the images should be split. This parameter directly influences the structure and layout of the output image, affecting its segmentation and organization.

inputs.name: flip_axis
inputs.description: Specifies the axes along which the images should be flipped. This parameter allows for the adjustment of image orientation, enhancing the flexibility in image presentation and analysis.

inputs.name: batch_stack_mode
inputs.description: Determines how images are stacked together in batches. This parameter is essential for defining the overall structure and layout of the combined image output.

inputs.name: z_enabled
inputs.description: Indicates whether the z-axis is enabled for image processing. This parameter enables multi-dimensional image handling, allowing for more complex image manipulations and visualizations.

inputs.name: x_main_label
inputs.description: The main label for the x-axis. This optional parameter allows for the addition of descriptive labels to the x-axis, enhancing the interpretability of the image.

inputs.name: y_main_label
inputs.description: The main label for the y-axis. Similar to the x_main_label, this enhances the image's interpretability by adding descriptive labels to the y-axis.

inputs.name: z_main_label
inputs.description: The main label for the z-axis, used when z_enabled is True. This enhances the multi-dimensional image's interpretability by adding descriptive labels to the z-axis.

inputs.name: x_labels
inputs.description: Labels for each segment along the x-axis. This parameter adds detailed descriptions to segments of the image, aiding in its analysis and understanding.

inputs.name: y_labels
inputs.description: Labels for each segment along the y-axis, providing detailed descriptions for segments of the image similar to x_labels.

inputs.name: z_labels
inputs.description: Labels for each segment along the z-axis, used when z_enabled is True. This adds detailed descriptions to segments of the multi-dimensional image.

outputs.name: Image
outputs.description: The processed image after applying operations such as splitting, flipping, and stacking. This output is significant as it represents the culmination of the node's image manipulation capabilities, ready for further use or analysis.

Add To Playlist (mtb).description: This node facilitates the addition of videos to a specified playlist, allowing for the dynamic creation and updating of playlists based on user-defined parameters. It supports both relative and absolute path specifications for videos, and can handle persistent storage of playlists across sessions.

inputs.name: relative_paths
inputs.description: Determines whether the paths of videos added to the playlist should be relative to the output directory. This affects how the paths are stored and interpreted, facilitating easier relocation of the playlist and its contents.

inputs.name: persistant_playlist
inputs.description: Indicates whether the playlist should be stored persistently across sessions. A persistent playlist is saved in a common directory, while a non-persistent one is saved in a session-specific directory.

inputs.name: playlist_name
inputs.description: The name of the playlist, which can include formatting options such as an index. This allows for dynamic naming based on the playlist's contents or order.

inputs.name: index
inputs.description: An integer used to format the playlist name, enabling the creation of sequentially named playlists or the organization of playlists by index.

Animation Builder (mtb).description: The MTB_AnimationBuilder node is designed to facilitate the creation of animations by managing frame sequencing, scaling, and looping. It provides a structured approach to generating animations through a set of parameters that control the total number of frames, their scaling, and the number of loops, thereby enabling the creation of complex animation sequences with ease.

inputs.name: total_frames
inputs.description: Specifies the total number of frames to be generated for the animation. This parameter directly influences the length of the animation sequence.

inputs.name: scale_float
inputs.description: A scaling factor applied to the normalized current value, which is a float between 0 and 1, to adjust the animation's scaling over its duration.

inputs.name: loop_count
inputs.description: Determines the number of times the animation sequence is looped, allowing for repeated cycles of the animation.

inputs.name: raw_iteration
inputs.description: An internal counter used to track the current iteration within the animation loop, facilitating frame sequencing.

inputs.name: raw_loop
inputs.description: An internal counter used to track the current loop iteration, supporting the looping functionality of the animation.

outputs.name: frame
outputs.description: The current frame number in the animation sequence.

outputs.name: 0-1 (scaled)
outputs.description: The scaled value of the current frame, normalized between 0 and 1, adjusted by the scale factor.

outputs.name: count
outputs.description: The current count of loops that have been completed in the animation.

outputs.name: loop_ended
outputs.description: A boolean indicating whether the current loop of the animation has ended.

Any To String (mtb).description: This node is designed to convert various types of inputs into their string representations, aiming to provide a versatile solution for handling and displaying different data types as strings.

inputs.name: input
inputs.description: Accepts a wide range of input types, including strings, tensors, images, numpy arrays, and dictionaries, converting them into a string format that describes their characteristics.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: Outputs a string representation of the input, detailing its type and key characteristics.

Apply Text Template (mtb).description: This node is designed for dynamic string interpolation, allowing users to insert variables into a template string. It provides a flexible way to generate customized text outputs by replacing placeholders within a template with actual values.

inputs.name: template
inputs.description: The template string with placeholders for variables, which will be dynamically replaced with actual values during execution. This parameter is essential for defining the structure and content of the output text.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The resulting string after all placeholders in the template have been replaced with their corresponding values.

Auto Pan Equilateral (mtb).description: This node is designed to generate a 360-degree panning video from an equilateral image by transforming the image based on specified field of view (FOV) parameters, elevation, and frame count to create a seamless panoramic experience.

inputs.name: equilateral_image
inputs.description: The equilateral image to be transformed into a 360-degree panning video. It serves as the base for generating the panoramic frames.

inputs.name: fovX
inputs.description: Specifies the horizontal field of view for the panoramic transformation. It influences the breadth of view in each frame of the video.

inputs.name: fovY
inputs.description: Specifies the vertical field of view for the panoramic transformation. It affects the height of the view in each frame of the video.

inputs.name: elevation
inputs.description: Determines the elevation angle at which the panoramic frames are generated, affecting the vertical angle of the camera.

inputs.name: frame_count
inputs.description: The total number of frames to generate for the 360-degree panning video, determining the video's length.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: The width of each frame in the generated video, affecting the resolution.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: The height of each frame in the generated video, influencing the resolution.

inputs.name: floats_fovX
inputs.description: An optional list of FOVX values to specify a varying horizontal field of view across frames, allowing for dynamic panning effects.

inputs.name: floats_fovY
inputs.description: An optional list of FOVY values to specify a varying vertical field of view across frames, enabling dynamic panning effects.

inputs.name: floats_elevation
inputs.description: An optional list of elevation values to specify varying camera angles across frames, enhancing the panoramic effect.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The resulting image after applying the 360-degree panning transformation, represented as a sequence of frames.

Batch Float (mtb).description: Generates a batch of float values with interpolation, offering customization through various parameters such as interpolation mode, count, and range. This node is essential for creating sequences of floats based on specified mathematical easing functions, enabling precise control over the generation of float batches for simulations, animations, or data analysis.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Specifies the interpolation mode for generating float values, with options like 'Single' or 'Steps' to define how values are interpolated.

inputs.name: count
inputs.description: Determines the number of float values to generate, allowing for control over the size of the output batch.

inputs.name: min
inputs.description: Sets the minimum value in the range of generated floats, providing a lower bound for interpolation.

inputs.name: max
inputs.description: Defines the maximum value in the range of generated floats, setting an upper limit for interpolation.

inputs.name: easing
inputs.description: Selects the easing function to apply during interpolation, such as 'Linear', 'Sine In/Out', or 'Elastic In', affecting the distribution of generated values.

outputs.name: floats
outputs.description: The generated batch of interpolated float values, ready for further processing or analysis.

Batch Float Assemble (mtb).description: The MTB_BatchFloatAssemble node is designed to aggregate multiple batches of floating-point numbers into a single, unified batch. This process allows for the efficient combination of data streams, optionally reversing the order of the batches before assembly, to suit various data processing and analysis needs.

inputs.name: reverse
inputs.description: Determines whether the batches of floats should be assembled in reverse order. Setting this to true reverses the order, which can be useful for certain data processing scenarios where the sequence of data matters.

outputs.name: floats
outputs.description: The output is a single, consolidated list of floating-point numbers, assembled from the input batches. This unified batch can be used for further processing or analysis.

Batch Float Fill (mtb).description: This node is designed to extend a batch of floating-point numbers to a specified length by filling it with a given value, either at the beginning or the end of the batch, depending on the specified direction.

inputs.name: floats
inputs.description: The list of floating-point numbers to be extended. It serves as the base batch that will be filled to reach the target length.

inputs.name: direction
inputs.description: Specifies whether the filling should occur at the beginning ('head') or the end ('tail') of the batch, influencing the order in which the batch is extended.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: The floating-point number used to fill the batch, allowing customization of the fill value.

inputs.name: count
inputs.description: The target length for the batch after filling, determining how many times the fill value will be added.

outputs.name: floats
outputs.description: The resulting batch of floating-point numbers after being filled to the target length.

Batch Float Fit (mtb).description: This node is designed to adjust the range of a batch of float values, optionally clamping them within a new target range and applying an easing function for smooth transitions. It can automatically compute the source range based on the input values or use a specified range, making it versatile for various data normalization and transformation tasks.

inputs.name: values
inputs.description: A list of float values to be transformed. The transformation adjusts these values from their original range to a new target range, potentially with clamping and easing for smooth transitions.

inputs.name: clamp
inputs.description: A boolean indicating whether to clamp the transformed values to the target range, ensuring no values fall outside this range.

inputs.name: auto_compute_source
inputs.description: A boolean that, when true, automatically computes the source range from the minimum and maximum of the input values, instead of using the provided source_min and source_max.

inputs.name: source_min
inputs.description: The minimum value of the source range, used as the starting point for transformation if auto_compute_source is false.

inputs.name: source_max
inputs.description: The maximum value of the source range, used as the ending point for transformation if auto_compute_source is false.

inputs.name: target_min
inputs.description: The minimum value of the target range to which the input values are transformed.

inputs.name: target_max
inputs.description: The maximum value of the target range to which the input values are transformed.

inputs.name: easing
inputs.description: The name of the easing function to apply during the transformation, allowing for smooth transitions between ranges.

outputs.name: floats
outputs.description: The list of transformed float values, adjusted to the new target range with optional clamping and easing applied.

Batch Float Math (mtb).description: Provides mathematical operations on batches of floating-point numbers, enabling complex computations and manipulations of data sets in a batch processing manner.

inputs.name: reverse
inputs.description: Determines the order in which the batches of floats are processed. When set to true, the batches are processed in reverse order, affecting the outcome of the operation.

inputs.name: operation
inputs.description: Specifies the mathematical operation to be applied to the batches of floats, such as addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, power, or absolute value. This choice directly influences the result of the computation.

outputs.name: floats
outputs.description: The result of applying the specified mathematical operation on the input batch of floats.

Batch Float Normalize (mtb).description: This node normalizes a list of float values, adjusting them to a common scale without distorting differences in the range of values. It's designed to standardize the data, making it easier to compare and process.

inputs.name: floats
inputs.description: A list of float values to be normalized. This input is crucial for the normalization process, as it directly influences the output by scaling the input values to a range between 0 and 1.

outputs.name: normalized_floats
outputs.description: The output is a list of normalized float values, scaled to a range between 0 and 1, maintaining the proportional differences of the original list.

Batch Make (mtb).description: The MTB_BatchMake node is designed to create batches from individual data points or smaller batches, facilitating the processing of data in bulk. This node is essential for optimizing data handling and processing efficiency in machine learning workflows, especially when dealing with large datasets or when performing operations that benefit from batch processing.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: This input type is used for specifying images that are to be batched together, playing a crucial role in the batch creation process for visual data.

inputs.name: count
inputs.description: The 'count' input type specifies the number of images or data points to include in each batch, directly affecting the size and composition of the created batches.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: This output type represents batches of images, ready for further processing or analysis in downstream tasks.

Batch Merge (mtb).description: The MTB_BatchMerge node is designed to merge multiple image batches into a single batch, adjusting for different frame counts among the batches and applying a specified fusion method to combine images.

inputs.name: fusion_mode
inputs.description: Specifies the method for merging images from different batches. It affects how the final merged image is created, with options including adding, multiplying, or averaging the images.

inputs.name: fill
inputs.description: Determines how to fill the frame count discrepancy in batches, either by repeating the first (head) or last (tail) frame of the batch.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is a single image batch that results from merging and adjusting the input image batches according to the specified fusion mode and fill method.

Batch Shake (mtb).description: The Batch Shake node applies a dynamic shaking effect to a batch of images, utilizing parameters such as position, rotation, and frequency to simulate motion or instability effects.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The batch of images to be processed. This input is crucial for defining the visual content that will undergo the shaking effect.

inputs.name: position_amount_x
inputs.description: Determines the horizontal intensity of the shaking effect, affecting how far images can move along the x-axis.

inputs.name: position_amount_y
inputs.description: Determines the vertical intensity of the shaking effect, affecting how far images can move along the y-axis.

inputs.name: rotation_amount
inputs.description: Controls the amount of rotation applied to the images, simulating a twisting motion.

inputs.name: frequency
inputs.description: Defines the frequency of the shaking effect, influencing the speed of motion changes.

inputs.name: frequency_divider
inputs.description: Modifies the base frequency, allowing for finer control over the shaking effect's speed.

inputs.name: octaves
inputs.description: Adjusts the complexity of the shaking pattern, adding layers of motion for a more nuanced effect.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: Sets the initial seed for random number generation, ensuring reproducible shaking patterns.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The processed image after applying the shaking effect.

outputs.name: pos_x
outputs.description: The horizontal translation values applied to each image in the batch.

outputs.name: pos_y
outputs.description: The vertical translation values applied to each image in the batch.

outputs.name: rot
outputs.description: The rotation values applied to each image in the batch, reflecting the degree of twist.

Batch Shape (mtb).description: Generates a batch of 2D shapes with optional shading, offering a creative tool for experimental design and visualization. This node allows for the customization of shape, size, color, and shading within generated images, making it ideal for creating diverse datasets or unique visual content.

inputs.name: count
inputs.description: Specifies the number of shapes to generate in the batch, affecting the overall output volume.

inputs.name: shape
inputs.description: Determines the type of shape to generate, such as Box, Circle, Diamond, or Tube, providing a variety of geometric forms for creation.

inputs.name: image_width
inputs.description: Sets the width of the generated image, defining the canvas size.

inputs.name: image_height
inputs.description: Sets the height of the generated image, defining the canvas size.

inputs.name: shape_size
inputs.description: Controls the size of the generated shapes, allowing for customization of the visual scale.

inputs.name: color
inputs.description: Specifies the color of the shapes, offering aesthetic customization.

inputs.name: bg_color
inputs.description: Determines the background color of the image, enabling contrast and visibility adjustments.

inputs.name: shade_color
inputs.description: Sets the color used for shading, adding depth and dimension to the shapes.

inputs.name: thickness
inputs.description: Defines the line thickness of the shapes, impacting visual prominence.

inputs.name: shadex
inputs.description: Adjusts the horizontal shading offset, influencing the shading direction.

inputs.name: shadey
inputs.description: Adjusts the vertical shading offset, influencing the shading direction.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: Produces an image or a batch of images containing the specified 2D shapes with optional shading effects.

Batch Time Wrap (mtb).description: The Batch Time Wrap (mtb) node is designed to remap a batch of images according to a specified time curve, effectively allowing for the dynamic adjustment of image sequences based on temporal data.

inputs.name: target_count
inputs.description: Specifies the desired number of images in the output batch, allowing for dynamic adjustment of the batch size.

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: The input batch of images to be remapped according to the time curve.

inputs.name: curve
inputs.description: A sequence of floating-point values defining the time curve along which the input images are remapped.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output batch of images that have been remapped according to the specified time curve.

outputs.name: interpolated_floats
outputs.description: A sequence of floating-point values representing the interpolated positions of the input images along the time curve.

Batch2d Transform (mtb).description: The Batch2d Transform node is designed to apply a series of 2D transformations to batches of images, including translation, rotation, zoom, and shear adjustments. It leverages mathematical and graphical operations to modify image data for various applications such as data augmentation, animation, and visual effects.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image tensor to be transformed. It serves as the base for applying the 2D transformations, affecting the visual outcome of the operation.

inputs.name: border_handling
inputs.description: Specifies the method for handling image borders during transformation, influencing how the image is extended or cropped.

inputs.name: constant_color
inputs.description: Defines the color used to fill any new areas of the image created as a result of the transformation, ensuring visual consistency.

inputs.name: x
inputs.description: A list of floats representing the translation values along the x-axis for each image in the batch, dictating horizontal movement.

inputs.name: y
inputs.description: A list of floats representing the translation values along the y-axis for each image in the batch, dictating vertical movement.

inputs.name: zoom
inputs.description: A list of floats indicating the zoom levels to be applied to each image in the batch, affecting the image scale.

inputs.name: angle
inputs.description: A list of floats specifying the rotation angles for each image in the batch, determining the orientation change.

inputs.name: shear
inputs.description: A list of floats representing the shear values to be applied to each image in the batch, altering the shape through skewing.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The transformed image tensor, resulting from the application of specified 2D transformations to the input images.

Bbox (mtb).description: The Bbox (mtb) node is designed to generate a bounding box (bbox) based on specified dimensions. It abstracts the process of defining a rectangular area within an image or a frame, facilitating operations like cropping or region of interest (ROI) identification.

inputs.name: x
inputs.description: Specifies the x-coordinate of the top-left corner of the bounding box, serving as a starting point for the rectangle's horizontal dimension.

inputs.name: y
inputs.description: Specifies the y-coordinate of the top-left corner of the bounding box, serving as a starting point for the rectangle's vertical dimension.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Defines the width of the bounding box, determining how far it extends horizontally from the x-coordinate.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Defines the height of the bounding box, determining how far it extends vertically from the y-coordinate.

outputs.name: bbox
outputs.description: The output is a tuple representing the bounding box, structured as (x, y, width, height), which can be used for further image processing tasks.

Bbox From Mask (mtb).description: The `Bbox From Mask` node is designed to extract a bounding box from a given mask, optionally inverting the mask and considering an image for size compatibility. It aims to identify the minimal bounding area that encapsulates the non-zero elements of the mask, providing a foundational tool for image cropping and processing tasks.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The mask tensor from which the bounding box is to be extracted. It plays a crucial role in determining the area of interest within an image or a set of images.

inputs.name: invert
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether the mask should be inverted before extracting the bounding box. This inversion can alter the focus area within the mask, affecting the resulting bounding box.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: An optional image tensor that, if provided, ensures the extracted bounding box is compatible with the image's dimensions. It's used for additional validation and processing when both mask and image are provided.

outputs.name: bbox
outputs.description: The bounding box extracted from the mask, represented as a tuple of coordinates and dimensions (x, y, width, height).

outputs.name: image (optional)
outputs.description: unknown

Blur (mtb).description: The Blur node applies a Gaussian blur to an image, allowing for both uniform and variable blurring across the image. This process can be used to reduce image noise and detail, simulating the effect of shooting in a lower resolution or with a softer focus lens.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be blurred. This is the primary data upon which the blur effect is applied, serving as the foundation for the operation.

inputs.name: sigmaX
inputs.description: Specifies the standard deviation in the x-direction for the Gaussian kernel. This parameter controls the amount of blur horizontally.

inputs.name: sigmaY
inputs.description: Specifies the standard deviation in the y-direction for the Gaussian kernel. This parameter controls the amount of blur vertically.

inputs.name: sigmasX
inputs.description: An optional list of standard deviations in the x-direction for applying variable blur across different parts of the image.

inputs.name: sigmasY
inputs.description: An optional list of standard deviations in the y-direction for applying variable blur across different parts of the image.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image after applying the Gaussian blur. This image will have reduced noise and detail, with a softer appearance.

Color Correct (mtb).description: Provides a suite of color correction capabilities for images, allowing adjustments to gamma, contrast, exposure, offset, hue, saturation, and value to enhance or modify the image's appearance.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be color corrected. This is the primary data upon which all color correction operations are applied.

inputs.name: clamp
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether the color values should be clamped. Clamping ensures that the color values do not exceed the allowable range, maintaining image integrity.

inputs.name: gamma
inputs.description: Adjusts the gamma value of the image, affecting the luminance to either darken or lighten the image.

inputs.name: contrast
inputs.description: Modifies the contrast level of the image, enhancing the difference between the light and dark areas.

inputs.name: exposure
inputs.description: Alters the exposure level, simulating the effect of changing the amount of light the image is exposed to.

inputs.name: offset
inputs.description: Applies an offset to the color values, shifting all colors by a fixed amount.

inputs.name: hue
inputs.description: Changes the hue of the image, adjusting the overall color tone.

inputs.name: saturation
inputs.description: Adjusts the saturation level, affecting the intensity of the colors in the image.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: Modifies the value (brightness) of the image, making it brighter or darker.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The color-corrected image, with adjustments applied as per the input parameters.

Colored Image (mtb).description: The Colored Image node is designed to apply color transformations to images, enabling the enhancement or alteration of their visual appearance through various color adjustment techniques.

inputs.name: color
inputs.description: The 'color' parameter defines the primary color to be applied to the image, influencing its overall hue and tone.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: The 'width' parameter specifies the desired width of the output image, allowing for size customization.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: The 'height' parameter sets the desired height of the output image, enabling size adjustments to fit specific requirements.

inputs.name: foreground_image
inputs.description: The 'foreground_image' parameter allows for the overlay of an image atop the colored background, adding complexity to the visual output.

inputs.name: foreground_mask
inputs.description: The 'foreground_mask' parameter specifies an alpha mask for the foreground image, determining transparency and blending with the background.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is an image that has been transformed by applying the specified color and background to the given mask.

Concat Images (mtb).description: The Concat Images node is designed to merge multiple images into a single batch, allowing for efficient processing and manipulation of image collections. It provides flexibility in handling size mismatches through customizable strategies.

inputs.name: reverse
inputs.description: Determines the order in which images are concatenated. When set to True, images are concatenated in reverse order.

inputs.name: on_mismatch
inputs.description: Specifies the strategy to adopt when there is a size mismatch between images being concatenated. Options include 'Error', 'Smallest', and 'Largest', with 'Smallest' being the default.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is a single batched tensor containing all the concatenated images, ready for further processing.

Constant (mtb).description: The MTB_Constant node is designed to output a constant value. It serves as a utility within a graph to provide a fixed value that can be used as input to other nodes, facilitating the creation of static or dynamic flows based on predefined constants.

inputs.name: Value
inputs.description: Represents the constant value to be output by the node. This parameter is essential for defining the static data that will be passed through the graph, affecting subsequent operations.

outputs.name: output
outputs.description: The output of the MTB_Constant node, which is the constant value defined by the input parameter. This value is passed through the graph for use in subsequent nodes.

Crop (mtb).description: The Crop node in the MTB (Mask to Bounding Box) suite is designed to perform image cropping operations based on specified parameters such as bounding boxes or masks. It allows for precise extraction of image regions, supporting functionalities like border blending for seamless integration of cropped areas into new contexts.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be cropped. This is the primary data upon which the cropping operation is performed, determining the area of focus for the operation.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: An optional mask that can be used to define the cropping area more precisely, allowing for more complex shapes beyond simple rectangular regions.

inputs.name: x
inputs.description: The x-coordinate of the top-left corner of the cropping area.

inputs.name: y
inputs.description: The y-coordinate of the top-left corner of the cropping area.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: The width of the cropping area.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: The height of the cropping area.

inputs.name: bbox
inputs.description: An optional bounding box that specifies the cropping area. If provided, it overrides the x, y, width, and height parameters.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The resulting image after the cropping operation.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The mask corresponding to the cropped area, if a mask was provided as input.

outputs.name: bbox
outputs.description: The coordinates and dimensions of the cropping area.

Curve (mtb).description: The MTB_Curve node is designed to process FLOAT_CURVE inputs, maintaining the integrity of the curve's structure. It primarily serves to ensure that curve data, whether received as a string or in a structured format, is correctly serialized or deserialized for further processing within the system.

inputs.name: curve
inputs.description: The 'curve' parameter represents the FLOAT_CURVE input that the node operates on. It is essential for the node's functionality, as it dictates the curve data that will be serialized or deserialized for further processing.

outputs.name: float_curve
outputs.description: The output is a float_curve, which is either the original curve data or its serialized string representation, depending on the input's format.

Curve To Float (mtb).description: This node specializes in transforming a FLOAT_CURVE into a FLOAT or FLOATS. It abstractly focuses on the conversion process, leveraging the curve's structure to produce either a singular value or a sequence of values, tailored to the interpolation requirements.

inputs.name: curve
inputs.description: Represents a curve defined by a series of points, each with X and Y coordinates, serving as the primary data structure for generating FLOAT or FLOATS output through interpolation.

inputs.name: steps
inputs.description: Specifies the number of intervals for interpolating Y values along the curve, affecting the granularity of the FLOATS output or the precision of the FLOAT output.

outputs.name: floats
outputs.description: A list of interpolated FLOAT values derived from the input FLOAT_CURVE, based on the specified number of steps.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: A single interpolated FLOAT value from the input FLOAT_CURVE, suitable for scenarios requiring a singular value.

Debug (mtb).description: The MTB_Debug node is designed for experimental debugging of various Comfy values, with plans to support additional types and widgets in the future. It allows for the inspection and logging of data passed through it, facilitating the debugging process by providing insights into the data's structure and content.

inputs.name: output_to_console
inputs.description: Determines whether the debug output should be printed to the console. Enabling this option allows for immediate visual inspection of the data being debugged, aiding in the debugging process.

Deep Bump (mtb).description: The Deep Bump node is designed for generating normal and height maps from single images, offering a versatile approach to texture processing by converting color images to normal maps, normal maps to curvature maps, or normal maps to height maps, depending on the selected mode. It utilizes advanced image processing techniques to achieve detailed and accurate representations of surface textures.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image for which the normal or height map will be generated. It serves as the foundational data from which the node derives texture maps.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Specifies the operation mode of the node, which can be converting color images to normal maps, normal maps to curvature maps, or normal maps to height maps, affecting the type of texture map produced.

inputs.name: color_to_normals_overlap
inputs.description: Determines the overlap size when converting color images to normal maps, influencing the smoothness and continuity of the generated normal map.

inputs.name: normals_to_curvature_blur_radius
inputs.description: Specifies the blur radius when converting normal maps to curvature maps, affecting the level of detail and smoothness in the curvature map.

inputs.name: normals_to_height_seamless
inputs.description: A boolean indicating whether the conversion from normal maps to height maps should be seamless, impacting the continuity and uniformity of the height map.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is either a normal map, curvature map, or height map based on the selected mode, representing the processed texture of the input image.

Export With Ffmpeg (mtb).description: The Export With Ffmpeg (mtb) node provides functionality for exporting media files using FFmpeg, supporting various formats and codecs. It allows for the conversion of image sequences or playlists into video files, with customizable frame rates, formats, and codecs, catering to different requirements for video production.

inputs.name: fps
inputs.description: Specifies the frames per second for the video export, affecting the playback speed and smoothness of the resulting video.

inputs.name: prefix
inputs.description: A prefix for the output file name, aiding in the organization and identification of exported files.

inputs.name: format
inputs.description: Determines the video file format (e.g., mov, mp4, mkv), influencing compatibility with different players and platforms.

inputs.name: codec
inputs.description: Selects the codec used for encoding the video, impacting the balance between quality and file size.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: An optional tensor of images to be exported as a video, enabling the creation of video content from individual frames.

inputs.name: playlist
inputs.description: An optional list of video file paths for concatenation, facilitating the compilation of multiple videos into a single file.

outputs.name: video
outputs.description: The path to the exported video file, indicating the successful creation of the video.

Face Swap (mtb).description: Performs face swapping between a source and a target image using deep learning models, specifically designed to handle complex scenarios involving multiple faces and preserving facial features accurately.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image tensor where the face(s) will be swapped onto. It serves as the canvas for the operation, determining the final output's visual context.

inputs.name: reference
inputs.description: The reference image tensor providing the face(s) to be swapped into the target image. It acts as the source of facial features for the swap.

inputs.name: faces_index
inputs.description: A string specifying the indices of faces in the target image to be swapped. It allows selective swapping, enhancing control over the output.

inputs.name: faceanalysis_model
inputs.description: The model used for analyzing faces within images, crucial for identifying and extracting facial features accurately.

inputs.name: faceswap_model
inputs.description: The model responsible for the actual face swapping process, leveraging deep learning to ensure realistic and seamless swaps.

inputs.name: preserve_alpha
inputs.description: A boolean indicating whether to preserve the alpha channel of the image, allowing for transparency handling in images with RGBA format.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The resulting image after the face swap has been performed, showcasing the swapped faces within the original image's context.

Film Interpolation (mtb).description: The Film Interpolation (mtb) node utilizes Google Research's FILM technology for frame interpolation, specifically designed to handle large motion between frames. It provides a method to interpolate additional frames between a sequence of images, enhancing the fluidity and smoothness of motion in video content.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: A tensor of images to be interpolated. This input is crucial for determining the frames between which the interpolation will occur, directly influencing the output's visual continuity.

inputs.name: interpolate
inputs.description: An integer specifying the number of frames to interpolate between each pair of input frames. This parameter directly affects the smoothness and duration of the resulting motion.

inputs.name: film_model
inputs.description: An instance of the FILM model used for interpolation. This model is responsible for the actual computation of the interpolated frames, leveraging advanced techniques to manage large motions effectively.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is a tensor of interpolated images, enriched with additional frames to create a smoother transition between the original images.

Filter Z (mtb).description: The MTB_FilterZ node applies a depth-based filtering to an image, allowing for selective visibility based on depth values. It supports operations such as converting specified depth regions to black or adjusting their transparency, with options for thresholding and inversion.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be filtered based on depth values. It plays a crucial role in determining the final output by providing the visual content to be manipulated.

inputs.name: depth
inputs.description: The depth map associated with the input image, used to determine which parts of the image are affected by the filtering process.

inputs.name: to_black
inputs.description: A boolean flag that determines whether the filtered areas are turned to black or made transparent.

inputs.name: threshold
inputs.description: A float value that sets the depth threshold for filtering, controlling which parts of the image are affected based on their depth values.

inputs.name: invert
inputs.description: A boolean flag that inverts the filtering effect, changing which parts of the image are affected based on the threshold.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The filtered image, which has been modified based on the depth map and filtering parameters.

Fit Number (mtb).description: The Fit Number node is designed to adjust a single numerical value to fit within a specified target range. It supports clamping to ensure the value stays within the target range and allows for the application of easing functions to modify the distribution of the transformed value.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: A single numerical value to be transformed. The node adjusts this value to fit within the specified target range, potentially altering its distribution based on the easing function applied.

inputs.name: clamp
inputs.description: A boolean indicating whether to clamp the transformed value to the target range, ensuring it does not fall outside the specified limits.

inputs.name: source_min
inputs.description: The minimum value of the source range. It is used as the lower bound when transforming the value.

inputs.name: source_max
inputs.description: The maximum value of the source range. It serves as the upper bound for the transformation of the value.

inputs.name: target_min
inputs.description: The minimum value of the target range. This is the lower limit to which the input value is scaled.

inputs.name: target_max
inputs.description: The maximum value of the target range. This defines the upper limit to which the input value is adjusted.

inputs.name: easing
inputs.description: A string representing the easing function applied to the distribution of the transformed value, affecting how it is scaled between the source and target ranges.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The input value transformed to fit within the specified target range, potentially altered in distribution by the easing function.

Float To Floats (mtb).description: This node serves as a conversion utility designed to transform a single floating-point number into a tuple of floating-point numbers, facilitating compatibility with other extensions that use a list format to represent multiple float values.

inputs.name: float
inputs.description: The single floating-point number to be converted into a tuple. This input is essential for the node's operation, enabling the conversion from a singular float value to a list format.

outputs.name: floats
outputs.description: The tuple of floating-point numbers resulting from the conversion of the input single float. This output facilitates compatibility with other extensions requiring a list format.

Float To Number (mtb).description: This node is designed to convert floating-point numbers into a more general number format, facilitating compatibility and data exchange within the WAS Suite ecosystem.

inputs.name: float
inputs.description: The floating-point number to be converted into a general number format. This input is crucial for the node's operation as it directly influences the output number.

outputs.name: number
outputs.description: The converted general number format from the input floating-point number.

Floats To Float (mtb).description: Provides a conversion utility to transform a list of floats into a single float value, facilitating compatibility with other extensions that use a single float to represent multiple values.

inputs.name: floats
inputs.description: The list of floats to be converted into a single float value. This input is crucial for the conversion process, determining the output of the node.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The single float value resulting from the conversion of the input list of floats.

Floats To Ints (mtb).description: Provides a conversion utility specifically designed for frame interpolation by converting a list of float values into integers. This node is essential for scenarios requiring integer representations of floating-point numbers, such as pixel values in image processing or discrete steps in animations.

inputs.name: floats
inputs.description: Accepts a list of floating-point numbers to be converted into integers. This input is crucial for the conversion process, enabling the node to process and transform each float value into its integer counterpart.

outputs.name: ints
outputs.description: Outputs a list of integers, each derived from the corresponding float input. This is useful for applications that require integer values for further processing or analysis.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: Additionally provides a single integer value, typically representing a specific or aggregated result derived from the input floats.

Get Batch From History (mtb).description: The MTB_GetBatchFromHistory node is designed to retrieve a batch of data from a historical dataset based on specified parameters. It enables conditional fetching of data, allowing for dynamic data loading and manipulation within a pipeline.

inputs.name: enable
inputs.description: Determines whether the node should attempt to load data from history. If disabled, it can pass through an alternative image if provided.

inputs.name: count
inputs.description: Specifies the number of historical data entries to retrieve. A count of 0 disables data loading.

inputs.name: offset
inputs.description: Defines the starting point within the historical dataset from which to begin data retrieval, allowing for pagination or skipping entries.

inputs.name: internal_count
inputs.description: A hacky parameter used to invalidate the node's cache, forcing a reload under certain conditions.

inputs.name: passthrough_image
inputs.description: An optional image to pass through when data loading is disabled or the count is 0, providing a fallback mechanism.

outputs.name: images
outputs.description: The batch of images retrieved from history, or a zero tensor if no data is found or loading is disabled.

Image Compare (mtb).description: This node compares two images using different modes such as difference, blend, or checkerboard, and returns a new image highlighting the differences or combinations based on the selected mode.

inputs.name: imageA
inputs.description: The first image to compare, represented as a torch.Tensor. It is one of the primary inputs for the comparison operation.

inputs.name: imageB
inputs.description: The second image to compare, also represented as a torch.Tensor. This image is compared against the first to identify differences or create a blend/checkerboard effect.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: A string indicating the comparison mode: 'checkerboard', 'diff', or 'blend'. The mode determines how the two images are compared and combined.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The resulting image after comparison, highlighting differences or combinations based on the selected mode.

Image Premultiply (mtb).description: The MTB_ImagePremultiply node is designed to premultiply an image with a mask, optionally inverting the mask. This operation is commonly used in image processing to combine an image with a transparency mask, affecting the image's transparency according to the mask's values.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The 'image' parameter represents the image to be premultiplied with the mask. It plays a crucial role in the node's operation by serving as the primary visual content to be processed.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The 'mask' parameter is used to define the transparency mask that will be applied to the image. Its values determine the transparency of the corresponding areas in the image, significantly influencing the output.

inputs.name: invert
inputs.description: The 'invert' parameter allows for the inversion of the mask's values before applying it to the image. This inversion can alter the visual outcome by changing which parts of the image are transparent.

outputs.name: RGBA
outputs.description: The output is an image that has been premultiplied with the mask, reflecting the combined visual effect of the image and mask transparency.

Image Remove Background Rembg (mtb).description: This node specializes in removing the background from images using the Rembg tool, enhancing the focus on the primary subject by isolating it from its surroundings.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image from which the background is to be removed. It is the primary data on which the background removal process is executed.

inputs.name: alpha_matting
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether alpha matting is to be applied for finer edge handling in the background removal process.

inputs.name: alpha_matting_foreground_threshold
inputs.description: Defines the threshold for foreground selection in the alpha matting process, affecting the precision of the subject's edges.

inputs.name: alpha_matting_background_threshold
inputs.description: Sets the threshold for background selection in the alpha matting process, influencing the accuracy of background removal.

inputs.name: alpha_matting_erode_size
inputs.description: Determines the erode size in the alpha matting process, impacting the smoothness of the subject's edges.

inputs.name: post_process_mask
inputs.description: A boolean flag that enables post-processing of the mask to refine the background removal results.

inputs.name: bgcolor
inputs.description: Specifies the background color to be applied post-removal, allowing for customization of the resulting image's backdrop.

outputs.name: Image (rgba)
outputs.description: The resulting image with the background removed, presented in RGBA format to include transparency information.

outputs.name: Mask
outputs.description: The mask generated during the background removal process, indicating areas of foreground and background.

outputs.name: Image
outputs.description: The final image after background removal, without the alpha channel, suitable for use in contexts where transparency is not required.

Image Resize Factor (mtb).description: This node is designed to resize images based on a specified scaling factor, optionally applying supersampling for higher quality resizing. It supports different resampling strategies to accommodate various image processing needs.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image tensor to be resized. This tensor's dimensions are checked to ensure they meet the expected format for processing.

inputs.name: factor
inputs.description: The scaling factor to resize the image by. This determines the new dimensions of the output image.

inputs.name: supersample
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether supersampling should be applied during resizing for enhanced image quality.

inputs.name: resampling
inputs.description: The method of resampling to use when resizing the image. This affects the quality and characteristics of the output image.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: An optional mask that can be applied during the resizing process. If provided, it is used in conjunction with the image data.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The resized image tensor, potentially supersampled for enhanced quality, and resized according to the specified factor and resampling method.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The mask tensor, if provided, resized to match the dimensions of the output image tensor.

Image Tile Offset (mtb).description: The Image Tile Offset (mtb) node is designed to adjust the positioning of tiles within an image, allowing for the customization of tile offsets. This functionality is crucial for tasks that require precise alignment of image segments, such as in image stitching or texture mapping.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed for tile offset adjustment. This parameter is essential for defining the base image on which the tile offset operation will be performed.

inputs.name: tilesX
inputs.description: Specifies the number of horizontal tiles into which the image is divided. This parameter is crucial for determining the horizontal segmentation of the image for tile adjustment.

inputs.name: tilesY
inputs.description: Specifies the number of vertical tiles into which the image is divided. This parameter is crucial for determining the vertical segmentation of the image for tile adjustment.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image after applying the tile offset adjustments. This image reflects the changes made to the tile positioning, showcasing the alignment modifications.

Int To Bool (mtb).description: This node performs a basic conversion of an integer to a boolean value, abstracting the process of interpreting numerical inputs as binary truth values.

inputs.name: int
inputs.description: The integer input that will be converted to a boolean. A non-zero value is considered true, while zero is considered false.

outputs.name: boolean
outputs.description: The boolean result of the conversion, where non-zero integers are true and zero is false.

Int To Number (mtb).description: Converts an integer to a number within a specified range, ensuring compatibility with the WAS Suite's numerical data types.

inputs.name: int
inputs.description: The integer input to be converted to a number. This parameter is crucial for defining the exact value that will undergo conversion.

outputs.name: number
outputs.description: The output number, directly corresponding to the input integer.

Interpolate Clip Sequential (mtb).description: This node is designed for sequential interpolation of text encodings within a given base text, using specified replacements and an interpolation strength parameter. It aims to modify the base text by interpolating new text encodings, thereby achieving a seamless transition between the original and the new text content.

inputs.name: base_text
inputs.description: The original text content that serves as the starting point for interpolation.

inputs.name: text_to_replace
inputs.description: The specific portion of the base text that is targeted for replacement through interpolation.

inputs.name: clip
inputs.description: A parameter that influences the degree to which the original text is modified, controlling the blend between the original and new text encodings.

inputs.name: interpolation_strength
inputs.description: Defines the intensity of the interpolation effect, adjusting how prominently the new text encodings are integrated into the base text.

outputs.name: conditioning
outputs.description: The result of the interpolation process, represented as a conditioning object that encapsulates the blended text encodings.

Latent Lerp (mtb).description: Performs linear interpolation between two latent vectors, blending them based on a specified ratio to create a new latent vector.

inputs.name: A
inputs.description: The first latent vector to be interpolated.

inputs.name: B
inputs.description: The second latent vector to be interpolated.

inputs.name: t
inputs.description: The interpolation ratio, determining the blend between the two latent vectors.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The resulting latent vector after interpolation.

Load Face Analysis Model (mtb).description: This node is designed to load a face analysis model, facilitating the analysis of facial features and characteristics within images. It supports the selection of different model types to accommodate various analysis needs.

inputs.name: faceswap_model
inputs.description: Specifies the model to be used for face analysis. The choice of model affects the accuracy and type of analysis performed.

outputs.name: face_analysis_model
outputs.description: The loaded face analysis model, ready for performing facial feature analysis.

Load Face Enhance Model (mtb).description: This node is designed to load and prepare a face enhancement model, specifically targeting GFPGan or RestoreFormer models, to enhance the quality of facial images. It facilitates the selection of the model and optionally integrates background upsampling for improved image results.

inputs.name: model_name
inputs.description: Specifies the name of the face enhancement model to load, influencing the enhancement technique and the quality of the output.

inputs.name: upscale
inputs.description: Sets the upscale factor for the face enhancement process, aiming to improve the resolution of the enhanced image.

inputs.name: bg_upsampler
inputs.description: An optional parameter for a background upsampler model to further refine the background in the enhanced images.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The loaded face enhancement model, ready to be utilized for improving facial image quality.

Load Face Swap Model (mtb).description: This node is responsible for loading a faceswap model from a specified path, ensuring the model is available for face swapping operations. It dynamically lists available models based on the files present in a designated directory, offering flexibility in model selection.

inputs.name: faceswap_model
inputs.description: Specifies the name of the faceswap model to load. The selection is dynamically generated based on the available model files in the insightface directory, allowing for a flexible and up-to-date choice of models.

outputs.name: faceswap_model
outputs.description: Returns an instance of the faceswap model, ready for use in face swapping operations. This enables the application of the model to input images for generating swapped face images.

Load Film Model (mtb).description: The MTB_LoadFilmModel node is designed to load FILM models for frame interpolation tasks, supporting a variety of model formats and ensuring the model is correctly loaded for further processing.

inputs.name: film_model
inputs.description: Specifies the FILM model to be loaded, affecting which specific model file is accessed and utilized in frame interpolation tasks.

outputs.name: film_model
outputs.description: Returns an instance of the loaded FILM model, ready for frame interpolation operations.

Load Image From Url (mtb).description: This node is designed to load an image from a specified URL, handling the retrieval and processing necessary to convert the image into a format suitable for further manipulation or analysis.

inputs.name: url
inputs.description: The URL from which the image will be loaded. This parameter is crucial as it determines the source of the image to be processed.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The loaded image, processed and converted into a tensor format, ready for further image processing tasks.

Load Image Sequence (mtb).description: The Load Image Sequence node is designed for loading sequences of images from a specified directory, allowing for the dynamic retrieval of individual frames or batches of frames based on the current frame index or a specified range. It supports loading all frames at once or fetching specific frames, making it versatile for applications requiring sequential image processing or animation.

inputs.name: path
inputs.description: Specifies the directory path where the image sequence is stored. This path is crucial for locating and loading the desired images.

inputs.name: current_frame
inputs.description: Determines the specific frame to load from the sequence. Setting this to -1 instructs the node to load all frames available, facilitating batch processing or full sequence retrieval.

inputs.name: range
inputs.description: Defines a specific range of frames to load from the sequence, offering fine-grained control over which images are retrieved for processing.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The loaded image or images from the specified sequence. This output can be a single frame or a batch of frames, depending on the input parameters.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The corresponding mask or masks for the loaded image(s), providing additional data for processing or analysis.

outputs.name: current_frame
outputs.description: The index of the current frame that was loaded, useful for tracking progress through a sequence.

outputs.name: total_frames
outputs.description: The total number of frames loaded, which can be used to understand the scope of the sequence being processed.

Mask To Image (mtb).description: This node transforms a mask into an RGB image, expanding the mask's single channel into a three-channel RGB format, effectively converting binary or grayscale mask data into a visual, color image representation.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The mask input represents the binary or grayscale mask data that will be converted into an RGB image. This transformation allows for the visualization of the mask as a color image, enhancing interpretability.

inputs.name: color
inputs.description: The color input specifies the color to be applied to the non-transparent parts of the mask, contributing to the visual representation of the output image.

inputs.name: background
inputs.description: The background input defines the color used for the background of the output image, allowing for customization of the image's backdrop.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is an RGB image generated from the input mask, where the mask's data is expanded across three channels to form a visual representation.

Match Dimensions (mtb).description: The MTB_MatchDimensions node is designed to adjust the dimensions of source images to match those of reference images along a specified dimension (height or width), ensuring the aspect ratio is preserved. This functionality is crucial for tasks requiring uniform image dimensions without distorting the image content.

inputs.name: source
inputs.description: The source image whose dimensions are to be adjusted. It plays a critical role in determining the new dimensions while preserving the aspect ratio.

inputs.name: reference
inputs.description: The reference image provides the target dimensions to match. It sets the benchmark for adjusting the source image, ensuring consistency in dimensions across images.

inputs.name: match
inputs.description: Specifies the dimension (height or width) along which the source image's dimensions should be matched to the reference image. It guides the adjustment process, ensuring the aspect ratio is preserved.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The adjusted image with dimensions matched to the reference image, preserving the aspect ratio.

outputs.name: new_width
outputs.description: The new width of the adjusted image after matching dimensions.

outputs.name: new_height
outputs.description: The new height of the adjusted image after matching dimensions.

Math Expression (mtb).description: This node is designed to evaluate simple math expressions provided as strings, incorporating the ability to replace placeholders within the expression with specified values. It aims to offer a straightforward method for dynamically calculating numerical results based on input expressions.

inputs.name: expression
inputs.description: The math expression string to be evaluated. This string can include placeholders for dynamic substitution and supports basic math operations.

outputs.name: result (float)
outputs.description: The evaluated result of the math expression as a floating-point number.

outputs.name: result (int)
outputs.description: The evaluated result of the math expression, explicitly cast to an integer.

Model Patch Seamless (mtb).description: This node is designed to seamlessly patch models within the MTB framework, enhancing their functionality or performance without altering their core structure. It focuses on integrating modifications in a way that is transparent to the user, ensuring that the original model's capabilities are extended or optimized while maintaining its original workflow and outputs.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model to be patched, aiming to enhance its functionality or performance seamlessly within the MTB framework.

inputs.name: startStep
inputs.description: Defines the starting step for the patching process, allowing for targeted modifications within the model's operation.

inputs.name: stopStep
inputs.description: Specifies the stopping step for the patching process, enabling precise control over the extent of model modifications.

inputs.name: tilingX
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether tiling should be applied along the X-axis, affecting the model's processing of images.

inputs.name: tilingY
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether tiling should be applied along the Y-axis, impacting the model's image processing capabilities.

outputs.name: Original Model (passthrough)
outputs.description: The original model passed through without modifications, serving as a baseline for comparison.

outputs.name: Patched Model
outputs.description: The modified version of the original model, enhanced with seamless patching to improve functionality or performance.

Model Pruner (mtb).description: The MTB_ModelPruner node is designed for optimizing and pruning machine learning models to enhance performance and efficiency. It supports operations such as precision conversion, removal of unnecessary components, and conditional execution based on model characteristics.

inputs.name: save_separately
inputs.description: Determines whether model components should be saved separately, affecting the organization of the output files.

inputs.name: save_folder
inputs.description: Specifies the directory where the pruned model and its components will be saved.

inputs.name: fix_clip
inputs.description: Indicates whether to apply fixes to the CLIP model component, potentially improving compatibility or performance.

inputs.name: remove_junk
inputs.description: Controls the removal of unnecessary or redundant parts of the model to streamline and optimize.

inputs.name: ema_mode
inputs.description: Defines the mode for Exponential Moving Average (EMA) handling within the model, affecting model stability and performance.

inputs.name: precision_unet
inputs.description: Sets the precision level for the U-Net model component, impacting memory usage and computational efficiency.

inputs.name: operation_unet
inputs.description: Specifies the operation to be performed on the U-Net model component, such as pruning or optimization.

inputs.name: precision_clip
inputs.description: Sets the precision level for the CLIP model component, impacting memory usage and computational efficiency.

inputs.name: operation_clip
inputs.description: Specifies the operation to be performed on the CLIP model component, such as pruning or optimization.

inputs.name: precision_vae
inputs.description: Sets the precision level for the VAE model component, impacting memory usage and computational efficiency.

inputs.name: operation_vae
inputs.description: Specifies the operation to be performed on the VAE model component, such as pruning or optimization.

inputs.name: unet
inputs.description: Optional U-Net model component to be pruned or optimized, provided as a dictionary of tensors.

inputs.name: clip
inputs.description: Optional CLIP model component to be pruned or optimized, provided as a dictionary of tensors.

inputs.name: vae
inputs.description: Optional VAE model component to be pruned or optimized, provided as a dictionary of tensors.

Pick From Batch (mtb).description: The MTB_PickFromBatch node allows for the selection of a specific number of images from a batch, based on a specified direction (either from the start or the end of the batch). This functionality is useful for operations that require a subset of images from a larger collection, enabling targeted manipulation or analysis.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The batch of images from which a subset will be selected. This parameter is crucial as it determines the pool of available images for selection.

inputs.name: from_direction
inputs.description: Specifies the direction from which images are selected within the batch, either from the 'end' or the 'start'. This affects the subset of images chosen for output.

inputs.name: count
inputs.description: The number of images to select from the batch. This determines the size of the output subset.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The selected subset of images from the batch, based on the specified count and direction.

Plot Batch Float (mtb).description: The MTB_PlotBatchFloat node is designed for visualizing batches of floating-point numbers as images. It generates plots based on the provided float values, allowing for a graphical representation of data distributions or patterns.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Specifies the width of the generated plot image. Affects the resolution and size of the output image.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Specifies the height of the generated plot image. Influences the resolution and size of the output visualization.

inputs.name: point_size
inputs.description: Determines the size of each point in the plot. Larger values produce bigger points, enhancing visibility but potentially reducing clarity in dense areas.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: A seed value for random number generation, ensuring reproducibility of the plot's layout when using random elements.

inputs.name: start_at_zero
inputs.description: A boolean flag that, when true, forces the plot's axis to start at zero, potentially altering the plot's scale and appearance.

outputs.name: plot
outputs.description: The generated plot image, visualizing the input float values as a graphical representation.

Qr Code (mtb).description: This node generates QR codes based on provided parameters such as URL, size, error correction level, and color inversion. It's designed for creating customizable QR codes that can be further adjusted in terms of dimensions, error resilience, and aesthetic preferences.

inputs.name: url
inputs.description: The URL to be encoded into the QR code. This is the primary content of the QR code.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: The width of the generated QR code image in pixels. This determines the size of the QR code on the horizontal axis.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: The height of the generated QR code image in pixels. This determines the size of the QR code on the vertical axis.

inputs.name: error_correct
inputs.description: The level of error correction applied to the QR code, which can be one of 'L', 'M', 'Q', 'H'. Higher levels increase the QR code's resilience to damage.

inputs.name: box_size
inputs.description: The size of each box in the QR code grid, affecting the granularity of the QR code.

inputs.name: border
inputs.description: The width of the border around the QR code, measured in boxes, not pixels.

inputs.name: invert
inputs.description: A boolean indicating whether the QR code's colors should be inverted, swapping the foreground and background colors.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The generated QR code as an image tensor, ready for further processing or saving.

Read Playlist (mtb).description: The Read Playlist node is designed to facilitate the reading of playlists from a specified path, allowing for the retrieval of playlist contents based on the provided name and index. It supports conditional execution and persistence options to enhance flexibility in playlist management.

inputs.name: enable
inputs.description: Determines whether the reading of the playlist is enabled or not, acting as a conditional execution flag.

inputs.name: persistant_playlist
inputs.description: Indicates whether the playlist should be read from a persistent storage location, affecting the path from which the playlist is loaded.

inputs.name: playlist_name
inputs.description: The name of the playlist to read, which can include formatting for dynamic naming based on the index.

inputs.name: index
inputs.description: An integer used to format the playlist name dynamically, allowing for indexed playlist management.

outputs.name: playlist
outputs.description: The contents of the read playlist, returned as a list of playlist items.

Restore Face (mtb).description: The Restore Face node leverages advanced face restoration techniques to enhance and restore faces in images. It utilizes models like GFPGan to improve the quality of facial features, making it suitable for applications requiring high-quality face images.

inputs.name: image
