inputs.description: The input image tensor containing faces to be restored. It plays a crucial role in the restoration process by serving as the primary data on which enhancement operations are performed.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The face enhancement model used for restoring faces. This model dictates the restoration technique and its effectiveness.

inputs.name: aligned
inputs.description: A boolean indicating whether the input faces are aligned. This affects the restoration process by determining how the model approaches face enhancement.

inputs.name: only_center_face
inputs.description: A boolean that specifies whether to only restore the center face in the image. This is useful for focusing the enhancement on the primary subject.

inputs.name: weight
inputs.description: A float value representing the weight of the restoration effect. It allows for fine-tuning the intensity of the face enhancement.

inputs.name: save_tmp_steps
inputs.description: A boolean indicating whether to save intermediate steps of the restoration process. This can be useful for debugging or for detailed analysis of the enhancement process.

inputs.name: preserve_alpha
inputs.description: A boolean that determines whether to preserve the alpha channel of the input image during restoration. This is important for maintaining transparency in images where applicable.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output tensor containing the enhanced and restored faces. It represents the final result of the face restoration process.

Save Gif (mtb).description: This node is designed to save a sequence of images as a GIF file, offering customization options such as frame rate, size adjustment, optimization, and the choice between a standard saving method or using FFmpeg for potentially enhanced performance.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The sequence of images to be saved as a GIF. This is the primary input that dictates the content of the resulting GIF file.

inputs.name: fps
inputs.description: Specifies the frames per second for the GIF, controlling how fast the images in the sequence are played back.

inputs.name: resize_by
inputs.description: A scaling factor to adjust the size of the images in the GIF, with 1.0 meaning no scaling.

inputs.name: optimize
inputs.description: A boolean indicating whether to apply optimization to the GIF, which can reduce file size at the cost of potentially longer processing times.

inputs.name: pingpong
inputs.description: When enabled, the GIF animation will play forwards and then backwards, creating a seamless loop effect.

inputs.name: resample_filter
inputs.description: The resampling filter to use when resizing images, affecting the quality of the resized images.

inputs.name: use_ffmpeg
inputs.description: A boolean indicating whether to use FFmpeg for GIF creation, which can offer more efficient processing for certain types of content.

Save Image Grid (mtb).description: The Save Image Grid node is designed to compile a collection of images into a single, cohesive grid layout. This functionality is particularly useful for visualizing multiple images in a structured format, allowing for easier comparison and analysis of visual data.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: A batch of images to be compiled into a grid. This collection is essential for determining the composition and overall appearance of the final image grid.

inputs.name: filename_prefix
inputs.description: A prefix for the filename under which the grid image will be saved. This parameter allows for customizable naming of the output file, aiding in organization and retrieval.

inputs.name: save_intermediate
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether intermediate images should be saved during the grid compilation process. This option provides flexibility in saving individual images before they are combined into the final grid.

Save Image Sequence (mtb).description: The Save Image Sequence node is designed to save a sequence of images to a specified directory, allowing for the inclusion of additional metadata such as prompts and custom PNG information. It facilitates the organization and storage of generated image sequences, making it easier to retrieve and utilize them for further processing or presentation.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The sequence of images to be saved. This parameter is crucial as it directly influences the node's primary function of storing these images in a specified format and location.

inputs.name: filename_prefix
inputs.description: A prefix for the filename under which the images will be saved. This allows for easy identification and organization of saved images within the output directory.

inputs.name: current_frame
inputs.description: Indicates the starting point or current frame number for the sequence of images being saved. This helps in organizing the sequence and maintaining continuity if the sequence is being updated over time.

Save Tensors (mtb).description: The Save Tensors node is designed for saving torch tensors, such as images, masks, or latent representations, to disk. This functionality is particularly useful for debugging purposes outside of the Comfy environment, allowing for the inspection and analysis of tensor data generated within custom workflows.

inputs.name: filename_prefix
inputs.description: Specifies the prefix for the filename under which the tensor will be saved. This parameter helps in organizing and identifying saved tensors for debugging purposes.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: An optional image tensor that can be saved to disk. This allows for the storage and later inspection of image data.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: An optional mask tensor that can be saved to disk. Useful for debugging and analyzing mask data applied in image processing.

inputs.name: latent
inputs.description: An optional latent tensor that can be saved to disk. Facilitates the debugging and examination of latent representations in models.

Sharpen (mtb).description: The Sharpen node enhances the visual clarity of images by applying a sharpening effect, utilizing a Gaussian kernel to accentuate edges and details.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be sharpened. This is the primary data upon which the sharpening process is applied, affecting the overall visual outcome.

inputs.name: sharpen_radius
inputs.description: Defines the radius of the sharpening effect. A larger radius increases the area of influence around edges, contributing to a more pronounced sharpening effect.

inputs.name: sigma_x
inputs.description: The horizontal standard deviation of the Gaussian kernel. It influences the spread of the sharpening effect horizontally across the image.

inputs.name: sigma_y
inputs.description: The vertical standard deviation of the Gaussian kernel. It influences the spread of the sharpening effect vertically across the image.

inputs.name: alpha
inputs.description: Controls the intensity of the sharpening effect. A higher alpha value results in a more aggressive sharpening.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image after the sharpening process has been applied, showcasing enhanced edges and details.

Smart Step (mtb).description: The MTB_SmartStep node is designed to manage the progression of steps within the KAdvancedSampler by calculating start and end points based on specified percentages. This utility facilitates dynamic step control, allowing for more precise and efficient sampling processes.

inputs.name: step
inputs.description: The 'step' parameter specifies the current step count, which is used to calculate the starting and ending points of the sampling process based on percentage values.

inputs.name: start_percent
inputs.description: The 'start_percent' parameter determines the percentage at which the sampling process should start, relative to the total number of steps.

inputs.name: end_percent
inputs.description: The 'end_percent' parameter sets the percentage at which the sampling process should end, enabling fine-tuned control over the sampling range.

outputs.name: step
outputs.description: Returns the original step count as provided.

outputs.name: start
outputs.description: Calculates and returns the starting point of the sampling process as an integer value.

outputs.name: end
outputs.description: Calculates and returns the ending point of the sampling process as an integer value.

Stack Images (mtb).description: This node is designed to stack multiple input images either vertically or horizontally, based on the specified orientation. It ensures that all images are normalized to the same size and RGBA format before stacking, allowing for consistent and seamless image composition.

inputs.name: vertical
inputs.description: Determines the orientation of the stacking process. When true, images are stacked vertically, requiring uniform width across all images. When false, images are stacked horizontally, necessitating uniform height.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is a single image tensor that represents the stacked composition of the input images, arranged according to the specified orientation.

String Replace (mtb).description: Provides a basic string replacement functionality, allowing for the substitution of a specified substring with another within a given string. This node is designed to facilitate text manipulation by enabling users to easily replace parts of strings.

inputs.name: string
inputs.description: The original string where replacements will be made. It serves as the base text for the operation.

inputs.name: old
inputs.description: The substring to be replaced. This parameter specifies the part of the original string that should be substituted.

inputs.name: new
inputs.description: The replacement substring. This parameter defines the new text that will replace the specified 'old' substring in the original string.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The modified string after the specified replacements have been made.

Styles Loader (mtb).description: The MTB_StylesLoader node is designed to manage and provide access to various styles for conditioning, enabling the selection and application of predefined styles to modify or enhance content generation processes.

inputs.name: style_name
inputs.description: Specifies the name of the style to be loaded. This parameter is crucial for identifying and retrieving the specific style's attributes from a collection of available styles.

outputs.name: positive
outputs.description: Returns the positive aspect of the selected style, which is part of the style's characteristics.

outputs.name: negative
outputs.description: Returns the negative aspect of the selected style, which is another part of the style's characteristics.

Text To Image (mtb).description: The Text To Image node is designed to convert text into an image using specified fonts. It searches for font files within a specified directory and utilizes these fonts to render the given text into an image format. This functionality allows for dynamic text visualization with various font styles, supporting a range of font file formats.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The text string to be converted into an image. This parameter is crucial as it defines the content that will be visually represented in the resulting image.

inputs.name: font
inputs.description: Specifies the font to be used for rendering the text into an image. This parameter allows for customization of the text's appearance, enhancing the visual appeal of the output.

inputs.name: wrap
inputs.description: Determines whether the text should wrap to fit within the specified width of the image. This parameter is important for ensuring the text fits neatly within the image boundaries without being cut off.

inputs.name: trim
inputs.description: Indicates whether whitespace around the text should be trimmed in the final image. This parameter helps in creating a cleaner, more focused visual representation of the text.

inputs.name: line_height
inputs.description: Controls the spacing between lines of text when the text wraps. This parameter is essential for maintaining readability and aesthetic spacing in multi-line text images.

inputs.name: font_size
inputs.description: The size of the font used to render the text. This parameter directly affects the readability and visual impact of the text in the image.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: The desired width of the output image. This parameter defines the horizontal dimension of the image canvas.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: The desired height of the output image. This parameter defines the vertical dimension of the image canvas.

inputs.name: color
inputs.description: The color of the text in the image. This parameter allows for customization of the text color, enabling contrast and visibility against the background.

inputs.name: background
inputs.description: The background color of the image. This parameter is crucial for setting the overall tone and contrast of the image, affecting the visibility of the text.

inputs.name: h_align
inputs.description: Horizontal alignment of the text within the image. This parameter controls the text's positioning along the horizontal axis, affecting the layout and balance of the image.

inputs.name: v_align
inputs.description: Vertical alignment of the text within the image. This parameter controls the text's positioning along the vertical axis, affecting the layout and balance of the image.

inputs.name: h_offset
inputs.description: Horizontal offset for the text position from its aligned location. This parameter allows for fine-tuning of the text's placement within the image, enabling precise layout adjustments.

inputs.name: v_offset
inputs.description: Vertical offset for the text position from its aligned location. This parameter allows for fine-tuning of the text's placement within the image, enabling precise layout adjustments.

inputs.name: h_coverage
inputs.description: Specifies the percentage of the image width that the text should cover. This parameter is important for controlling the text's spread across the image, affecting the visual density and readability.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is an image with the specified text rendered using the chosen font and settings. This image represents the visual interpretation of the input text, customized according to the provided parameters.

To Device (mtb).description: The `MTB_ToDevice` node is designed to transfer image or mask tensors to a specified computing device, such as CPU, GPU, or MPS (Apple Silicon), enhancing computational efficiency and flexibility in data processing pipelines.

inputs.name: ignore_errors
inputs.description: Determines whether to proceed without throwing an error if both image and mask inputs are absent, allowing for more flexible error handling.

inputs.name: device
inputs.description: Specifies the computing device to which the tensors will be transferred. It dynamically includes available options like CPU, GPU, and MPS, adapting to the system's capabilities.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: An optional image tensor that, if provided, will be transferred to the specified device.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: An optional mask tensor that, if provided, will be transferred to the specified device.

outputs.name: images
outputs.description: The image tensor after being transferred to the specified device.

outputs.name: masks
outputs.description: The mask tensor after being transferred to the specified device.

Transform Image (mtb).description: The Transform Image (mtb) node is designed to apply a series of affine transformations to an image, including translation, rotation, scaling (zoom), and shearing. It allows for flexible image manipulation with options for border handling and filling with a constant color, making it suitable for a wide range of image processing tasks.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image tensor to be transformed. It serves as the primary data on which the affine transformations are applied, affecting the visual outcome of the operation.

inputs.name: x
inputs.description: The horizontal translation distance. It shifts the image left or right, influencing the image's position.

inputs.name: y
inputs.description: The vertical translation distance. It shifts the image up or down, affecting the image's vertical positioning.

inputs.name: zoom
inputs.description: The scaling factor. It enlarges or reduces the image size, impacting the level of detail visible in the transformed image.

inputs.name: angle
inputs.description: The rotation angle in degrees. It rotates the image around its center, changing its orientation.

inputs.name: shear
inputs.description: The shear intensity. It distorts the image by slanting it, modifying the shape and angles within the image.

inputs.name: border_handling
inputs.description: The method used for handling image borders during transformation. It determines how the edges of the image are treated, affecting the appearance of the image's periphery.

inputs.name: constant_color
inputs.description: The color used to fill in new areas when the image is transformed. It specifies the fill color for areas that become exposed as a result of the transformation.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The transformed image tensor, reflecting the applied affine transformations.

Uncrop (mtb).description: The Uncrop (mtb) node is designed to reverse the cropping process on images, restoring them to their original dimensions or to a specified larger context. This node is essential for operations where the spatial context of an image needs to be preserved or reconstructed after it has been cropped for analysis or processing.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The original image that will serve as the background for the uncropping process. It defines the spatial context into which the cropped image will be placed.

inputs.name: crop_image
inputs.description: The cropped image to be integrated back into the original image's context. This image is essential for the node's operation as it contains the content that needs to be restored.

inputs.name: bbox
inputs.description: The bounding box specifying where the cropped image should be placed within the original image. This parameter is crucial for positioning the cropped content accurately.

inputs.name: border_blending
inputs.description: A parameter that controls the blending of the borders between the cropped image and the original image to ensure a seamless transition.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The image after the uncropping process has been applied, showing the cropped content seamlessly integrated into the original image's context.

Unsplash Image (mtb).description: The MTB_UnsplashImage node is designed to fetch and return an image from Unsplash based on specified dimensions and optional keywords. It utilizes the Unsplash API to dynamically source images, which can be tailored by the user through parameters such as image size and thematic keywords.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Specifies the desired width of the image to be fetched. This dimension directly influences the resolution of the returned image, impacting its clarity and detail.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Determines the height of the image to be fetched. Similar to width, this parameter affects the resolution and aspect ratio of the resulting image.

inputs.name: random_seed
inputs.description: A seed value to introduce randomness in the image selection process, ensuring that requests for images are not deterministic and can vary with each call.

inputs.name: keyword
inputs.description: An optional parameter that allows the user to specify a keyword to narrow down the image search, making the results more relevant to the desired theme or context.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The image retrieved from Unsplash, converted into a tensor format suitable for further processing or display within the node's operational context.

Vae Decode (mtb).description: This node is designed to decode latent representations into images using a VAE model, with options for seamless decoding or tiled decoding to handle larger images efficiently.

inputs.name: samples
inputs.description: The latent representations to be decoded into images. These samples are the input that the VAE model decodes, directly influencing the output images.

inputs.name: vae
inputs.description: The VAE model used for decoding the latent representations into images. It is central to the node's functionality, determining the decoding process and the quality of the output images.

inputs.name: seamless_model
inputs.description: A flag indicating whether to use seamless mode for decoding, which adjusts the padding mode of convolutional layers for seamless image generation.

inputs.name: use_tiling_decoder
inputs.description: A flag that determines whether to use a tiling decoder for image generation, enabling efficient handling of larger images by processing them in tiles.

inputs.name: tile_size
inputs.description: The size of the tiles used in tiling decoder mode, affecting the granularity of the decoding process and the handling of larger images.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The decoded image or images from the latent representations, produced by the VAE model.

DF_Absolute_value.description: The DF_Absolute_value node provides a functionality to compute the absolute value of a given input. It can optionally return the negative absolute value based on a specified condition, allowing for flexible numerical transformations within data processing pipelines.

inputs.name: Value
inputs.description: The primary input for the node, representing the value for which the absolute (or negative absolute) value is to be computed. Its role is crucial in determining the output of the node.

inputs.name: negative_out
inputs.description: A boolean flag that determines whether the output should be the negative absolute value of the input. This parameter allows for conditional output, enhancing the node's versatility in numerical operations.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The output of the node, which is either the absolute value or the negative absolute value of the input, depending on the 'negative_out' parameter.

DF_Ceil.description: The DF_Ceil node rounds up a given floating-point number to the nearest integer, effectively implementing the mathematical ceiling function.

inputs.name: Value
inputs.description: Specifies the floating-point number to be rounded up to its nearest integer value. This input is crucial for determining the output of the node.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: Represents the integer result of rounding up the input floating-point number.

DF_Conditioning_area_scale_by_ratio.description: This node is designed to adjust the scale of conditioning areas based on a specified ratio, modifying both the dimensions and strength of the conditioning to achieve a desired effect. It allows for dynamic resizing of conditioning areas, making it suitable for applications requiring precise control over the conditioning's influence on generated content.

inputs.name: conditioning
inputs.description: The conditioning input represents the current state of conditioning areas that will be scaled. It is crucial for determining the base dimensions and strength that will be modified.

inputs.name: modifier
inputs.description: The modifier is a scaling factor that directly influences the size of the conditioning areas, allowing for proportional resizing.

inputs.name: strength_modifier
inputs.description: This parameter adjusts the strength of the conditioning, enabling fine-tuning of its impact on the generation process.

outputs.name: conditioning
outputs.description: Returns the conditioning with adjusted area sizes and strength, reflecting the applied scaling modifications.

DF_Cosines.description: The Cosines node calculates the cosine of a given angle, with the option to compute the arc cosine instead. It supports angles in both degrees and radians, allowing for flexible trigonometric calculations.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: The numerical value of the angle for which the cosine (or arc cosine) is to be calculated. This value determines the specific angle involved in the trigonometric operation.

inputs.name: type_
inputs.description: Specifies the unit of the input angle: radians ('RAD') or degrees ('DEG'). This affects how the angle is interpreted for the trigonometric calculation.

inputs.name: arcCos
inputs.description: A boolean flag that, when set to True, changes the operation from calculating the cosine to calculating the arc cosine of the given angle.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The result of the cosine (or arc cosine) calculation for the given angle.

DF_Divide.description: The DivideNode facilitates the division of two numerical values, providing a straightforward way to perform arithmetic division operations within a node-based programming environment.

inputs.name: Numerator
inputs.description: Specifies the dividend in the division operation, determining the value to be divided.

inputs.name: Denominator
inputs.description: Determines the divisor in the division operation, affecting the outcome by dividing the numerator.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The result of dividing the Numerator by the Denominator, expressed as a floating-point number.

DF_DynamicPrompts_Text_Box.description: This node specializes in processing text input with dynamic prompts, allowing for a more interactive and flexible user input experience. It captures and returns the input text as is, supporting multiline and dynamically generated prompts.

inputs.name: Text
inputs.description: The 'Text' parameter accepts multiline text input with dynamic prompts, enhancing the node's ability to handle varied and contextually rich user inputs.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: Outputs the input text unchanged, encapsulating it within a tuple to maintain consistency with the node's return type expectations.

DF_Float.description: The DF_Float node is designed to directly pass through floating-point values without modification, serving as a fundamental building block for numerical data manipulation within the node network.

inputs.name: Value
inputs.description: Accepts a floating-point value as input, which is directly passed through without any modification. This parameter is essential for the node's operation as it determines the exact value that will be output.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: Outputs the same floating-point value as received in the input, ensuring a direct pass-through of numerical data.

DF_Floor.description: The DF_Floor node is designed to round down the input floating-point number to its nearest lower integer. This operation is commonly known as 'flooring' a number.

inputs.name: Value
inputs.description: The 'Value' parameter represents the floating-point number that is to be rounded down. It is crucial for determining the output of the node, as it directly influences the floor operation.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: The output is the nearest lower integer value of the input floating-point number, achieved through the floor operation.

DF_Get_image_size.description: This node is designed to calculate and return the dimensions of an image, specifically its width and height. It abstracts the complexity of handling image data structures to provide a straightforward way to obtain image size information.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The 'image' parameter is crucial as it represents the image data from which the size will be determined. This parameter directly influences the node's ability to calculate and return the correct dimensions of the image.

outputs.name: WIDTH
outputs.description: Represents the width of the image in pixels.

outputs.name: HEIGHT
outputs.description: Represents the height of the image in pixels.

DF_Get_latent_size.description: The node `DF_Get_latent_size` is designed to calculate and return the dimensions of a latent representation, either in its original size or scaled. It abstracts the complexity of handling latent data structures to provide straightforward access to their size attributes.

inputs.name: latent
inputs.description: The latent input represents the data structure for which the size is being calculated. It is crucial for determining the dimensions based on the latent's current state.

inputs.name: original
inputs.description: This boolean parameter dictates whether the original size of the latent is returned or if it is scaled. It affects the calculation by potentially altering the dimensions returned.

outputs.name: WIDTH
outputs.description: Represents the width dimension of the latent's size.

outputs.name: HEIGHT
outputs.description: Represents the height dimension of the latent's size.

DF_Image_scale_by_ratio.description: This node is designed to upscale an image by a specified ratio, applying a chosen upscale method and optionally cropping the image. It focuses on adjusting the image's dimensions based on a scaling factor, enhancing the image quality or fitting it into a desired size while maintaining its aspect ratio.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image to be upscaled. It is central to the node's operation as it determines the base for scaling and the subject of the upscale process.

inputs.name: upscale_by
inputs.description: The factor by which the image's dimensions should be increased. This value directly influences the final size of the upscaled image.

inputs.name: upscale_method
inputs.description: The method used for upscaling the image. Different methods can affect the quality and characteristics of the upscaled image.

inputs.name: crop
inputs.description: Determines if and how the upscaled image should be cropped, affecting the final composition and aspect ratio of the output.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The upscaled version of the input image, potentially cropped according to the specified method.

DF_Image_scale_to_side.description: This node is designed to upscale an image to a specified side length while maintaining the aspect ratio. It allows for the selection of which side (width, height, longest, or shortest) to scale to, the method of upscaling, and whether to apply cropping, providing flexibility in image processing tasks.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be upscaled. It serves as the base for the upscaling process, determining the initial dimensions and aspect ratio that will be adjusted.

inputs.name: side_length
inputs.description: Specifies the target length of the side (width or height) to which the image will be scaled. This value directly influences the final dimensions of the upscaled image.

inputs.name: side
inputs.description: Determines which side of the image (width, height, longest, or shortest) will be scaled to the specified side length, affecting the upscaling direction and final aspect ratio.

inputs.name: upscale_method
inputs.description: The method used for upscaling the image, which affects the quality and characteristics of the output image.

inputs.name: crop
inputs.description: Indicates whether and how the upscaled image should be cropped, affecting the final composition and dimensions.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The upscaled image, adjusted to the specified side length while maintaining the original aspect ratio.

DF_Integer.description: The DF_Integer node is designed to convert floating-point numbers to integers by rounding them down to the nearest whole number. It serves as a fundamental tool for operations requiring integer values, such as indexing or discrete mathematics, by ensuring numerical inputs are appropriately formatted for such contexts.

inputs.name: Value
inputs.description: The 'Value' parameter accepts a floating-point number and rounds it down to the nearest integer, facilitating operations that require whole numbers.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: The output is an integer representation of the input floating-point number, rounded down to the nearest whole number.

DF_Int_to_Float.description: The DF_Int_to_Float node is designed to convert integer values to floating-point numbers, facilitating operations that require decimal precision.

inputs.name: Value
inputs.description: The 'Value' parameter represents the integer input that will be converted to a floating-point number. This conversion is essential for enabling precise calculations that integers alone cannot accommodate.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The output is a floating-point representation of the input integer, allowing for decimal precision in subsequent operations.

DF_Latent_Scale_by_ratio.description: This node is designed to scale latent representations of images by a specified ratio, adjusting their dimensions while maintaining the integrity of the latent space. It supports various scaling and cropping methods to fine-tune the output.

inputs.name: latent
inputs.description: The latent representation of an image to be scaled. It is crucial for determining the base dimensions that will be modified according to the scaling ratio.

inputs.name: modifier
inputs.description: A scaling factor that determines how much the latent dimensions should be increased or decreased.

inputs.name: scale_method
inputs.description: Specifies the method used for scaling the latent image, such as nearest-exact, bilinear, etc., affecting the quality and characteristics of the output.

inputs.name: crop
inputs.description: Defines the cropping method to be applied after scaling, allowing for adjustments in the latent's aspect ratio or size.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The scaled latent representation, adjusted according to the specified modifier, scale method, and cropping preference.

DF_Latent_Scale_to_side.description: This node is designed to upscale or modify the dimensions of a latent representation based on a specified side length and side (Width, Height, Longest, Shortest). It adjusts the latent's dimensions while maintaining its aspect ratio, using various scaling methods and optional cropping.

inputs.name: latent
inputs.description: The latent representation to be scaled. It is the core input that undergoes transformation based on the specified parameters.

inputs.name: side_length
inputs.description: Specifies the target length for the chosen side (Width, Height, Longest, Shortest) of the latent, dictating the scale to which the latent will be adjusted.

inputs.name: side
inputs.description: Determines which side of the latent (Width, Height, Longest, Shortest) the side_length applies to, guiding the scaling process.

inputs.name: scale_method
inputs.description: The method used for scaling the latent's dimensions. It affects the quality and characteristics of the output.

inputs.name: crop
inputs.description: Optional parameter that specifies if and how the scaled latent should be cropped, affecting the final output's dimensions.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The scaled latent representation, adjusted according to the specified side length, side, scale method, and cropping option.

DF_Logic_node.description: The LogicNode facilitates the execution of basic logical operations such as comparisons (greater than, less than, equal to) and boolean operations (AND, OR, XOR) between input values. It abstractly supports decision-making processes by evaluating conditions and determining outcomes based on the specified logic.

inputs.name: Operation
inputs.description: Specifies the logical operation to be performed, including comparisons and boolean operations, which dictates the logic applied between CompareValue_A and CompareValue_B.

inputs.name: CompareValue_A
inputs.description: The primary value for comparison or logical operation.

inputs.name: CompareValue_B
inputs.description: The secondary value for comparison or logical operation, used in conjunction with CompareValue_A to evaluate the specified Operation.

inputs.name: OnTrue
inputs.description: The value to return if the logical operation evaluates to true.

inputs.name: OnFalse
inputs.description: The value to return if the logical operation evaluates to false.

outputs.description: The result of the logical operation, which can be either the OnTrue or OnFalse value based on the operation's outcome.

DF_Multiply.description: The `DF_Multiply` node performs multiplication of two floating-point numbers, providing a straightforward way to calculate the product of two values within a mathematical or computational workflow.

inputs.name: Value_A
inputs.description: `Value_A` represents the first floating-point number to be multiplied. It plays a crucial role in determining the overall result of the multiplication operation.

inputs.name: Value_B
inputs.description: `Value_B` is the second floating-point number involved in the multiplication. Its value directly influences the product outcome, making it an essential component of the operation.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The output is a floating-point number representing the product of the two input values, `Value_A` and `Value_B`. It encapsulates the result of the multiplication operation.

DF_Power.description: The `DF_Power` node performs exponentiation, raising a base value to the power of a specified exponent. It abstracts the mathematical operation of exponentiation, enabling the dynamic computation of powers within a workflow.

inputs.name: Value
inputs.description: The base value for the exponentiation operation. It determines the number being raised to the power of the exponent.

inputs.name: Exponent
inputs.description: The exponent value in the exponentiation operation. It specifies the power to which the base value is raised.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The result of raising the base value to the power of the exponent, computed as a floating-point number.

DF_Random.description: The `DF_Random` node generates a random floating-point number within a specified range. It utilizes a seed for reproducible randomness, allowing for consistent results across multiple executions.

inputs.name: Value_A
inputs.description: Specifies the lower bound of the random number range. It influences the minimum value that the random number generator can produce.

inputs.name: Value_B
inputs.description: Defines the upper bound of the random number range. It sets the maximum value that the random number generator can output.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: A seed value for the random number generator to ensure reproducibility of results. It determines the sequence of numbers generated, allowing for consistent randomness across runs.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The output is a random floating-point number within the specified range, determined by the input bounds and seed.

DF_Search_In_Text.description: The `DF_Search_In_Text` node is designed to search for a specified pattern within a given text. It supports both strict and regular expression (RegEx) modes for pattern matching, and can optionally consider case sensitivity. This node provides a way to determine if the pattern exists in the text and to count the number of occurrences, offering flexibility for text analysis and processing tasks.

inputs.name: Text
inputs.description: The text in which to search for the specified pattern. It serves as the primary input for the search operation.

inputs.name: Pattern
inputs.description: The pattern to search for within the text. This can be a literal string in strict mode or a regular expression in RegEx mode.

inputs.name: ConsiderRegister
inputs.description: A boolean indicating whether to consider case sensitivity in the search. When false, the search is case-insensitive.

inputs.name: Mode
inputs.description: Specifies the mode of pattern matching: 'Strict' for literal string matching or 'RegEx' for regular expression matching.

outputs.name: BOOLEAN
outputs.description: Indicates whether the specified pattern was found in the text.

outputs.name: OCCURRENCES
outputs.description: The number of times the specified pattern was found in the text.

DF_Sinus.description: The Sinus node calculates the sine of a given angle, which can be specified in either radians or degrees. It also offers the option to compute the arcsine of the input value, allowing for flexibility in trigonometric calculations.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: The angle for which the sine value is to be calculated. This can be in radians or degrees, based on the 'type_' parameter.

inputs.name: type_
inputs.description: Specifies the unit of the input angle: 'RAD' for radians or 'DEG' for degrees, affecting how the input value is interpreted before calculation.

inputs.name: arcSin
inputs.description: A boolean flag that, when true, changes the operation from sine to arcsine, allowing for inverse trigonometric calculations.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The result of the sine or arcsine calculation, depending on the input parameters.

DF_Square_root.description: The SquareRootNode provides a mathematical operation to calculate the square root of a given value, returning both the positive and negative square root values.

inputs.name: Value
inputs.description: The input value for which the square root is to be calculated. This value determines the magnitude of the output.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The positive and negative square root values of the input.

DF_String_Concatenate.description: The DF_String_Concatenate node is designed to concatenate two strings with an optional delimiter. It enables the creation of a new string by appending one string to another, separated by a specified delimiter, thus facilitating string manipulation and formatting tasks.

inputs.name: Prepend
inputs.description: The string to be placed at the beginning of the new concatenated string. It serves as the base to which the other string is appended, playing a crucial role in the concatenation process.

inputs.name: Append
inputs.description: The string to be appended to the end of the 'Prepend' string. This parameter is essential for extending the base string with additional content, contributing to the formation of the concatenated result.

inputs.name: Delimiter
inputs.description: An optional string used to separate the 'Prepend' and 'Append' strings in the concatenated result. It defines the character or sequence of characters that will be inserted between the two strings, affecting the overall format and readability of the output.

outputs.name: TEXT
outputs.description: The resulting string after concatenation. It represents the combined output of the 'Prepend' and 'Append' strings, optionally separated by the 'Delimiter', showcasing the node's ability to merge strings effectively.

DF_String_Replace.description: The `DF_String_Replace` node is designed to modify strings by replacing specified patterns with a new string. It supports both strict replacements and regular expression-based substitutions, allowing for flexible text manipulation within a given text input.

inputs.name: Text
inputs.description: The original text in which replacements will be made. It serves as the base for modifications.

inputs.name: Pattern
inputs.description: The pattern to be replaced in the text. This can be a literal string (in strict mode) or a regular expression pattern.

inputs.name: Replace_With
inputs.description: The string that will replace occurrences of the pattern in the text.

inputs.name: Mode
inputs.description: Determines whether the replacement will be done using strict matching or regular expressions, offering flexibility in how patterns are identified and replaced.

outputs.name: TEXT
outputs.description: The modified text after the specified patterns have been replaced.

DF_Subtract.description: The DF_Subtract node is designed to perform subtraction between two input values, returning the difference as its output. This node abstracts the mathematical operation of subtraction, allowing for the dynamic computation of differences between numerical values within a data flow.

inputs.name: Value_A
inputs.description: Value_A represents the minuend in the subtraction operation. It is the initial value from which Value_B will be subtracted, playing a crucial role in determining the outcome of the node's computation.

inputs.name: Value_B
inputs.description: Value_B serves as the subtrahend in the subtraction operation. Its value is subtracted from Value_A, directly influencing the resulting difference output by the node.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The output is the numerical difference resulting from subtracting Value_B from Value_A, encapsulating the subtraction operation's result.

DF_Sum.description: The SumNode is designed to perform arithmetic addition, taking two float inputs and returning their sum as a float output. This node simplifies the process of adding numbers within a mathematical or computational context, facilitating operations that require summation.

inputs.name: Value_A
inputs.description: Represents one of the two values to be added together. Its role is crucial as it directly influences the sum calculation.

inputs.name: Value_B
inputs.description: Serves as the second value to be added to the first. Its importance lies in its contribution to the overall sum, affecting the node's output.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The result of adding the two input values. It signifies the computed sum, encapsulating the node's primary function.

DF_Tangent.description: The DF_Tangent node calculates the tangent or arctangent of a given value, with the option to specify the angle measurement unit (degrees or radians). This functionality allows for the transformation and analysis of angular data within mathematical and trigonometric computations.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: The numerical value for which the tangent or arctangent is to be calculated. This input is crucial for determining the specific angle or its tangent value.

inputs.name: type_
inputs.description: Specifies the angle measurement unit for the input value, either as radians (RAD) or degrees (DEG), affecting how the value is interpreted and processed.

inputs.name: arcTan
inputs.description: A boolean flag that determines whether to calculate the arctangent (True) or tangent (False) of the input value, allowing for flexibility in trigonometric calculations.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The calculated tangent or arctangent of the input value, provided as a floating-point number.

DF_Text.description: The `DF_Text` node is designed to capture and process textual input, allowing for the manipulation and transformation of strings within a workflow. It emphasizes the handling of text data, providing a straightforward interface for inputting and outputting text in various forms.

inputs.name: Text
inputs.description: This parameter accepts a string input, serving as the primary data for the node's operation. It plays a crucial role in the text processing and manipulation capabilities of the node.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: Outputs the processed text as a string, reflecting any transformations or manipulations applied within the node.

DF_Text_Box.description: The DF_Text_Box node is designed to capture and process multiline text input, allowing for the handling of extended text data within a node-based programming environment.

inputs.name: Text
inputs.description: This parameter accepts multiline text input, enabling the node to process and manipulate text data that spans multiple lines.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: Outputs the processed text as a string, maintaining its multiline format.

DF_To_text_(Debug).description: The `DF_To_text_(Debug)` node is designed for debugging purposes, allowing users to log and inspect any data passed through it. It converts the input data to a string format, logs the original and string-converted data for debugging, and handles exceptions by logging them. This node facilitates the observation and troubleshooting of data flow within node-based processing pipelines.

inputs.name: ANY
inputs.description: Accepts any type of data for debugging purposes. It logs the input data in its original form and after conversion to a string, aiding in the inspection and troubleshooting of data flow.

outputs.name: SAME AS INPUT
outputs.description: Returns the original input data, allowing it to be passed through for further processing or inspection.

outputs.name: STRING
outputs.description: Returns the input data converted to a string, or an error message if an exception occurs, facilitating debugging and error tracking.

Apply ControlNet Stack.description: The Apply ControlNet Stack node is designed to enhance the conditioning of positive and negative prompts by applying a stack of control networks. This process allows for the dynamic adjustment of the prompts based on specified control networks, images, and strength parameters, thereby refining the conditioning for more targeted and effective generation outcomes.

inputs.name: positive
inputs.description: The positive prompt to be conditioned. It serves as the initial input for the control network stack application, influencing the generation towards desired attributes or themes.

inputs.name: negative
inputs.description: The negative prompt to be conditioned. It acts as a counterpart to the positive prompt, guiding the generation away from undesired attributes or themes.

inputs.name: cnet_stack
inputs.description: An optional stack of control networks and associated parameters that are applied sequentially to the positive and negative prompts. This stack enables complex, layered adjustments to the conditioning.

outputs.name: CONDITIONING+
outputs.description: The conditioned positive prompt after the application of the control network stack.

outputs.name: CONDITIONING-
outputs.description: The conditioned negative prompt after the application of the control network stack.

Control Net Stacker.description: The TSC Control Net Stacker node is designed to aggregate control networks along with their associated images, strengths, and percentage ranges into a stack. This functionality is crucial for managing and applying multiple control networks in a sequential or layered manner, enhancing the flexibility and efficiency of image manipulation processes.

inputs.name: control_net
inputs.description: The control network to be added to the stack. It plays a central role in defining the manipulation or adjustment to be applied to the image.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image associated with the control network. This image serves as a reference or target for the control network's application.

inputs.name: strength
inputs.description: Defines the intensity of the control network's effect on the image, allowing for fine-tuned adjustments.

inputs.name: start_percent
inputs.description: Specifies the starting point of the control network's effect in terms of the image's generation process, enabling precise control over the application timing.

inputs.name: end_percent
inputs.description: Determines the ending point of the control network's effect, further refining the application's temporal precision.

inputs.name: cnet_stack
inputs.description: An existing stack of control networks to which the new control network will be added, facilitating the accumulation of multiple networks.

outputs.name: CNET_STACK
outputs.description: The updated stack of control networks, each associated with specific images, strengths, and percentage ranges, ready for sequential or layered application.

Eff. Loader SDXL.description: The Eff. Loader SDXL node is designed to efficiently load and prepare models and data for the SDXL (Super Diffusion XL) process. It handles the initialization and configuration of base and refiner models, clip skipping, aesthetic scoring, and various other parameters to optimize the loading process for enhanced performance and efficiency in generative tasks.

inputs.name: base_ckpt_name
inputs.description: Specifies the checkpoint name for the base model, crucial for initializing the model with pre-trained weights.

inputs.name: base_clip_skip
inputs.description: Determines the number of clip layers to skip in the base model, affecting the model's performance and output quality.

inputs.name: refiner_ckpt_name
inputs.description: Defines the checkpoint name for the refiner model, enabling the enhancement of generated outputs through refinement.

inputs.name: refiner_clip_skip
inputs.description: Indicates the number of clip layers to skip in the refiner model, optimizing the refinement process.

inputs.name: positive_ascore
inputs.description: The aesthetic score for positive feedback, used to guide the model towards generating more appealing outputs.

inputs.name: negative_ascore
inputs.description: The aesthetic score for negative feedback, helping to steer the model away from less desirable outputs.

inputs.name: vae_name
inputs.description: The name of the VAE used in the process, essential for the model's data encoding and decoding.

inputs.name: positive
inputs.description: Positive input data or conditions, used to direct the model towards specific generative goals.

inputs.name: negative
inputs.description: Negative input data or conditions, used to avoid certain patterns or themes in the generated outputs.

inputs.name: token_normalization
inputs.description: Controls the normalization of tokens, impacting the model's interpretation and processing of input data.

inputs.name: weight_interpretation
inputs.description: Adjusts how the model interprets the weighting of different inputs, affecting the balance between positive and negative feedback.

inputs.name: empty_latent_width
inputs.description: Specifies the width of the empty latent space, configuring the dimensions for model initialization.

inputs.name: empty_latent_height
inputs.description: Defines the height of the empty latent space, setting up the spatial dimensions for the generative process.

inputs.name: batch_size
inputs.description: The number of samples to process in a single batch, influencing the efficiency and speed of the loading operation.

inputs.name: lora_stack
inputs.description: Optional LoRA stack configuration, enhancing model performance with LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) techniques.

inputs.name: cnet_stack
inputs.description: Optional ControlNet stack configuration, further refining the model's output through controlled network adjustments.

outputs.name: SDXL_TUPLE
outputs.description: A tuple containing the base and refiner models, clips, and encoded positive and negative feedback, ready for the SDXL process.

outputs.name: LATENT
outputs.description: The latent space samples generated by the VAE, essential for the generative process.

outputs.name: VAE
outputs.description: The VAE model used in the process, crucial for encoding and decoding data.

outputs.name: DEPENDENCIES
outputs.description: A collection of dependencies required for the operation, including model names, clip information, and configuration parameters.

Efficient Loader.description: The Efficient Loader node is designed to streamline the process of loading and initializing models, VAEs, and other dependencies for generative tasks. It efficiently manages resources by selectively caching and reusing components, and supports customization through parameters like checkpoint names, LoRA configurations, and batch sizes. This node aims to optimize the setup phase for generative workflows, reducing overhead and facilitating quicker iterations.

inputs.name: ckpt_name
inputs.description: Specifies the checkpoint name for the model to be loaded, serving as a key identifier for retrieving model parameters and configurations.

inputs.name: vae_name
inputs.description: Identifies the VAE to be used in the generative process, crucial for defining the visual encoding and decoding mechanisms.

inputs.name: clip_skip
inputs.description: Specifies the intervals at which CLIP layers are skipped, optimizing the model's performance for specific tasks.

inputs.name: lora_name
inputs.description: Specifies the name of the LoRA model to be loaded, if applicable, enabling dynamic adjustments to model parameters without full retraining.

inputs.name: lora_model_strength
inputs.description: Defines the strength of the LoRA model adjustments, allowing for fine-tuning of the model's behavior.

inputs.name: lora_clip_strength
inputs.description: Determines the strength of the CLIP adjustments when LoRA is applied, affecting the text-image alignment.

inputs.name: positive
inputs.description: The positive conditioning text, guiding the generative model towards desired attributes in the output.

inputs.name: negative
inputs.description: The negative conditioning text, instructing the generative model to avoid certain attributes in the output.

inputs.name: token_normalization
inputs.description: Defines the method for normalizing tokens, affecting how text inputs are processed and interpreted by the model.

inputs.name: weight_interpretation
inputs.description: Determines how weights are interpreted, allowing for customization of the model's learning and adaptation processes.

inputs.name: empty_latent_width
inputs.description: Specifies the width of the empty latent space, setting the dimensions for the initial generative canvas.

inputs.name: empty_latent_height
inputs.description: Specifies the height of the empty latent space, setting the dimensions for the initial generative canvas.

inputs.name: batch_size
inputs.description: Determines the number of samples to be processed in parallel, directly impacting memory usage and computational efficiency.

inputs.name: lora_stack
inputs.description: A stack of LoRA models to be applied, enabling complex model adjustments through multiple layers.

inputs.name: cnet_stack
inputs.description: A stack of ControlNet models to be applied, facilitating advanced control over the generative process.

outputs.name: MODEL
outputs.description: The main model loaded and prepared for generative tasks, including any applied modifications like LoRA.

outputs.name: CONDITIONING+
outputs.description: Processed positive conditioning information, ready for use in guiding the generative process.

outputs.name: CONDITIONING-
outputs.description: Processed negative conditioning information, ready for use in avoiding undesired attributes.

outputs.name: LATENT
outputs.description: An empty latent space tensor, prepared based on specified dimensions, serving as a starting point for generation.

outputs.name: VAE
outputs.description: The loaded VAE model, essential for encoding and decoding visual information in the generative process.

outputs.name: CLIP
outputs.description: The CLIP model loaded and configured based on the specified skip intervals, facilitating text-image alignment.

outputs.name: DEPENDENCIES
outputs.description: A collection of dependencies including model names, configurations, and parameters, ensuring all necessary components are loaded.

Evaluate Floats.description: The `TSC_EvaluateFloats` node is designed to evaluate mathematical expressions involving floats, converting the results into multiple formats (integer, float, and string) for further use. It supports dynamic input through variables and can optionally print the evaluation results to the console for debugging or informational purposes.

inputs.name: python_expression
inputs.description: The mathematical expression to be evaluated, allowing for dynamic computation involving floats. It plays a crucial role in determining the node's output by dictating the operation to be performed.

inputs.name: print_to_console
inputs.description: A flag indicating whether the evaluation result should be printed to the console, aiding in debugging or providing immediate visual feedback of the operation's outcome.

inputs.name: a
inputs.description: An optional variable 'a' that can be used within the python_expression for dynamic evaluation.

inputs.name: b
inputs.description: An optional variable 'b' that can be used within the python_expression for dynamic evaluation.

inputs.name: c
inputs.description: An optional variable 'c' that can be used within the python_expression for dynamic evaluation.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: The integer representation of the evaluated expression's result.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The float representation of the evaluated expression's result.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The string representation of the evaluated expression's result.

Evaluate Integers.description: The node 'Evaluate Integers' dynamically evaluates mathematical expressions involving integers, using variables 'a', 'b', and 'c' as inputs. It supports basic arithmetic operations and returns the result in multiple formats (integer, float, and string), optionally printing the outcome to the console.

inputs.name: python_expression
inputs.description: Specifies the mathematical expression to be evaluated. It can include variables 'a', 'b', and 'c' and supports basic arithmetic operations.

inputs.name: print_to_console
inputs.description: Controls whether the evaluation result is printed to the console. Useful for debugging or direct output visualization.

inputs.name: a
inputs.description: Represents the first integer variable that can be used in the python_expression.

inputs.name: b
inputs.description: Represents the second integer variable that can be used in the python_expression.

inputs.name: c
inputs.description: Represents the third integer variable that can be used in the python_expression.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: The evaluated result of the python_expression as an integer.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The evaluated result of the python_expression as a float.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The evaluated result of the python_expression as a string.

Evaluate Strings.description: The `Evaluate Strings` node is designed to dynamically evaluate Python expressions using string variables. It allows for the execution of simple arithmetic or functional expressions by substituting string values for variables within the expression. This node is particularly useful for generating or manipulating string data based on dynamic inputs.

inputs.name: python_expression
inputs.description: Specifies the Python expression to be evaluated. This expression can include arithmetic operations or functions, with variables that will be replaced by their corresponding string values provided in other inputs. The choice of expression directly influences the node's behavior and output, as it determines the operations performed on the input strings.

inputs.name: print_to_console
inputs.description: Controls whether the evaluation result and variable values are printed to the console. This option is crucial for debugging or when visual confirmation of the process is needed, as it affects how the results are presented to the user.

inputs.name: a
inputs.description: Represents the string value to substitute for variable 'a' in the Python expression. Altering this value changes the outcome of the expression, demonstrating its direct impact on the node's execution and results.

inputs.name: b
inputs.description: Represents the string value to substitute for variable 'b' in the Python expression. This input plays a key role in the evaluation process by affecting the final result, based on how the expression utilizes this variable.

inputs.name: c
inputs.description: Represents the string value to substitute for variable 'c' in the Python expression. The value of 'c' significantly influences the evaluation outcome, showcasing its importance in the node's overall functionality.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The result of the evaluated Python expression, converted to a string. This output reflects the culmination of the node's processing, providing a string representation of the evaluation.

HighRes-Fix Script.description: The HighRes-Fix Script node is designed to enhance image resolution and quality in a customizable manner. It leverages various upscaling techniques, control nets, and preprocessing steps to refine images, offering options for seed consistency, denoising, and iterative refinement. This node integrates with animation and control net scripts, adapting to specific high-resolution enhancement needs while maintaining the flexibility to work with different upscaling models and preprocessors.

inputs.name: upscale_type
inputs.description: Specifies the method of upscaling to be used, affecting the quality and approach of the high-resolution output.

inputs.name: hires_ckpt_name
inputs.description: The checkpoint name for the high-resolution model, indicating the specific model version or configuration to use for upscaling.

inputs.name: latent_upscaler
inputs.description: Identifies the latent space upscaling method, which enhances image detail at a foundational level before pixel-level adjustments.

inputs.name: pixel_upscaler
inputs.description: Defines the pixel-level upscaling method, refining image details after latent space enhancements.

inputs.name: upscale_by
inputs.description: Determines the scaling factor for the upscaling process, directly influencing the final image size and detail.

inputs.name: use_same_seed
inputs.description: Controls whether the same seed is used throughout the upscaling process, ensuring consistency in random elements.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: The initial seed value for random processes, providing a starting point for reproducibility and variation control.

inputs.name: hires_steps
inputs.description: Specifies the number of steps to perform in the high-resolution enhancement process, affecting the depth of refinement.

inputs.name: denoise
inputs.description: Indicates whether denoising is applied during the upscaling process, improving image clarity by reducing noise.

inputs.name: iterations
inputs.description: The number of iterations to run the upscaling process, allowing for multiple passes of refinement.

inputs.name: use_controlnet
inputs.description: Determines whether a control net is used for guided upscaling, influencing the direction and quality of enhancements.

inputs.name: control_net_name
inputs.description: The name of the control net to be used, specifying the model for guided upscaling.

inputs.name: strength
inputs.description: The strength of the control net's influence on the upscaling process, adjusting the level of guidance.

inputs.name: preprocessor
inputs.description: The preprocessor method used to prepare images for upscaling, affecting initial quality and compatibility.

inputs.name: preprocessor_imgs
inputs.description: Preprocessed images ready for upscaling, serving as the input to the enhancement process.

inputs.name: script
inputs.description: An optional script containing additional parameters or configurations for the upscaling process.

outputs.name: script
outputs.description: The resulting script configuration after applying the high-resolution fix, encapsulating all specified parameters and adjustments made during the process.

Image Overlay.description: The ImageOverlay node is designed to overlay one image onto another with various customization options such as resizing, rotation, opacity adjustment, and optional masking. This node enables the creation of composite images by applying transformations and blending techniques to the overlay image before merging it with the base image.

inputs.name: base_image
inputs.description: The base image onto which the overlay image will be applied. It serves as the background for the composite image.

inputs.name: overlay_image
inputs.description: The image to be overlaid onto the base image. This image can be resized, rotated, and its opacity adjusted before overlaying.

inputs.name: overlay_resize
inputs.description: Specifies how the overlay image should be resized to fit the base image, with options including fitting to dimensions, rescaling by a factor, or resizing to specific width and height.

inputs.name: resize_method
inputs.description: The method used for resizing the overlay image, affecting the quality and appearance of the resized image.

inputs.name: rescale_factor
inputs.description: The factor by which the overlay image is rescaled when the 'Resize by rescale_factor' option is selected.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: The width to which the overlay image is resized when the 'Resize to width & height' option is selected.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: The height to which the overlay image is resized when the 'Resize to width & height' option is selected.

inputs.name: x_offset
inputs.description: The horizontal offset at which the overlay image is placed over the base image.

inputs.name: y_offset
inputs.description: The vertical offset at which the overlay image is placed over the base image.

inputs.name: rotation
inputs.description: The angle in degrees to rotate the overlay image before applying it to the base image.

inputs.name: opacity
inputs.description: The opacity level of the overlay image, allowing for transparent overlays.

inputs.name: optional_mask
inputs.description: An optional mask that can be applied to the overlay image, controlling the transparency of different parts of the overlay.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The base image after the overlay has been applied, reflecting all specified transformations and adjustments.

Join XY Inputs of Same Type.description: This node is designed to merge two XY inputs of the same type into a single output, handling different types of XY data with specific merging strategies for each type. It ensures that the input types match before proceeding with the merge, providing a unified XY output that combines the input data in a manner appropriate to their type.

inputs.name: XY_i
inputs.description: Represents one of the XY inputs to be merged. Its type and values are crucial for determining the merge strategy and ensuring compatibility with the other XY input.

outputs.name: X or Y
outputs.description: The merged output of the two XY inputs, which combines their data according to their type and the specific merging logic implemented for each type.

KSampler (Efficient).description: The KSampler (Efficient) node is designed to efficiently sample latent images using a variety of sampling strategies, including regular and advanced methods. It leverages the Comfy KSampler nodes to generate or refine latent images based on specified conditions, aiming to optimize the sampling process for speed and resource usage.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: Specifies the model to be used for sampling. It is crucial for determining the sampling behavior and the quality of the generated images.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: Determines the random seed for sampling, ensuring reproducibility of results. It affects the randomness of the generated latent images.

inputs.name: steps
inputs.description: Defines the number of steps to perform during sampling. It influences the detail and quality of the generated images.

inputs.name: cfg
inputs.description: Controls the conditioning-free guidance (CFG) scale, affecting the adherence to the specified conditions.

inputs.name: sampler_name
inputs.description: Identifies the specific sampler algorithm to use, impacting the sampling method and results.

inputs.name: scheduler
inputs.description: Specifies the scheduler for controlling the sampling process, affecting the progression of image generation.

inputs.name: positive
inputs.description: The positive conditioning text to guide the image generation towards desired attributes.

inputs.name: negative
inputs.description: The negative conditioning text to steer the image generation away from undesired attributes.

inputs.name: latent_image
inputs.description: The initial latent image to refine or generate from, if provided. It influences the starting point of the sampling process.

inputs.name: denoise
inputs.description: Adjusts the level of denoising applied during sampling, affecting the clarity and quality of the generated images.

inputs.name: preview_method
inputs.description: unknown

inputs.name: vae_decode
inputs.description: unknown

inputs.name: optional_vae
inputs.description: unknown

inputs.name: script
inputs.description: unknown

outputs.name: MODEL
outputs.description: unknown

outputs.name: CONDITIONING+
outputs.description: Positive conditioning information that has been applied or generated during the sampling process.

outputs.name: CONDITIONING-
outputs.description: Negative conditioning information that has been applied or generated during the sampling process.

outputs.name: LATENT
outputs.description: The sampled or refined latent image, representing the result of the sampling process.

outputs.name: VAE
outputs.description: VAE-related output, potentially including encoded or decoded information as part of the sampling process.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: The final image output, representing the visual result of the sampling and conditioning process.

KSampler Adv. (Efficient).description: This node specializes in advanced sampling techniques for generating or refining images based on given inputs. It leverages a more sophisticated approach compared to regular samplers, allowing for enhanced control over the sampling process, including noise addition and stepwise refinement, to produce high-quality outputs.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model parameter specifies the generative model to be used for sampling. It is crucial for determining the behavior and quality of the generated images.

inputs.name: add_noise
inputs.description: Determines whether noise should be added to the sampling process, allowing for more variability and realism in the generated images.

inputs.name: noise_seed
inputs.description: Seed for the noise generation, ensuring control over the randomness in the added noise for reproducibility.

inputs.name: steps
inputs.description: Specifies the number of steps to perform in the sampling process, affecting the detail and quality of the output.

inputs.name: cfg
inputs.description: The CFG scale used to balance between fidelity to the prompt and the randomness of the generation, influencing the output's creativity.

inputs.name: sampler_name
inputs.description: The name of the sampler to use, defining the specific sampling algorithm and its characteristics.

inputs.name: scheduler
inputs.description: Specifies the scheduler for controlling the sampling process, affecting how the steps are executed over time.

inputs.name: positive
inputs.description: Positive conditioning to guide the generation towards desired attributes or features.

inputs.name: negative
inputs.description: Negative conditioning to steer the generation away from certain attributes or features.

inputs.name: latent_image
inputs.description: The initial latent image to start the sampling process from, setting the basis for generation or refinement.

inputs.name: start_at_step
inputs.description: The step number to start the sampling process, allowing for mid-process interventions or adjustments.

inputs.name: end_at_step
inputs.description: The final step number in the sampling process, defining the endpoint for generation or refinement.

inputs.name: return_with_leftover_noise
inputs.description: Indicates whether to return the sampled image with leftover noise, offering a choice between a cleaner or more raw output.

inputs.name: preview_method
inputs.description: unknown

inputs.name: vae_decode
inputs.description: unknown

inputs.name: optional_vae
inputs.description: unknown

inputs.name: script
inputs.description: unknown

outputs.name: MODEL
outputs.description: The output includes the model used in the sampling process, potentially modified or updated.

outputs.name: CONDITIONING+
outputs.description: Output conditioning that positively influences the generation towards desired characteristics.

outputs.name: CONDITIONING-
outputs.description: Output conditioning that negatively influences the generation, steering it away from undesired characteristics.

outputs.name: LATENT
outputs.description: The latent representation of the image after the sampling process, ready for further processing or conversion to image form.

outputs.name: VAE
outputs.description: The VAE model used or affected during the sampling process, if applicable.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: The final image output after the sampling process, reflecting the combined effects of conditioning, noise, and model parameters.

KSampler SDXL (Eff.).description: This node specializes in sampling images using a sophisticated version of the KSampler algorithm, optimized for efficiency and tailored for use with the SDXL model. It incorporates advanced features such as noise addition, step refinement, and optional VAE decoding, making it suitable for generating high-quality images with fine-tuned control over the generation process.

inputs.name: sdxl_tuple
inputs.description: Represents the model used for sampling, encapsulating the necessary parameters and configurations specific to the SDXL model.

inputs.name: noise_seed
inputs.description: The seed used for generating noise, ensuring reproducibility and consistency in the sampling process.

inputs.name: steps
inputs.description: The number of steps to iterate the sampling process, affecting the detail and quality of the generated images.

inputs.name: cfg
inputs.description: The conditioning factor guiding the sampling process, influencing the adherence to the provided prompts or images.

inputs.name: sampler_name
inputs.description: The identifier for the specific KSampler variant used, in this case, tailored for the SDXL model.

inputs.name: scheduler
inputs.description: The scheduling algorithm applied to control the sampling process, optimizing the balance between speed and quality.

inputs.name: latent_image
inputs.description: The initial latent image to be refined or altered through the sampling process, serving as a starting point.

inputs.name: start_at_step
inputs.description: The step at which to begin the sampling process, allowing for mid-process intervention or refinement.

inputs.name: refine_at_step
inputs.description: Specifies the step at which to apply refinement operations, enhancing the final image quality.

inputs.name: preview_method
inputs.description: The method used for generating previews during the sampling process, aiding in visualization and adjustment.

inputs.name: vae_decode
inputs.description: Indicates whether to use a VAE decoder for post-processing the sampled images, affecting the final image style.

inputs.name: optional_vae
inputs.description: An optional VAE model for further processing the sampled images, offering an additional layer of customization.

inputs.name: script
inputs.description: A script for further customizing the sampling process, enabling complex generation scenarios.

outputs.name: SDXL_TUPLE
outputs.description: The SDXL model tuple, encapsulating the model and its configurations used in the sampling process.

outputs.name: LATENT
outputs.description: The latent representation of the sampled image, serving as an intermediate step in the image generation process.

outputs.name: VAE
