outputs.description: The optional VAE model used for further processing the sampled images, enhancing their quality and style.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: The final output image generated by the sampling process, showcasing the result of the applied configurations and models.

LoRA Stack to String converter.description: The LoRA Stack to String converter node is designed to transform a list of LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) model configurations, each represented as a tuple, into a single, space-separated string. This conversion facilitates the efficient representation and communication of LoRA model parameters for various applications, including model configuration and debugging.

inputs.name: lora_stack
inputs.description: Represents a list of tuples, each containing a model identifier and two numerical values, which are to be converted into a formatted string. This input is crucial for generating a compact representation of LoRA model configurations.

outputs.name: LoRA string
outputs.description: A single string that concatenates all the input tuples into a formatted, space-separated sequence, enabling easy interpretation and use of LoRA model configurations.

LoRA Stacker.description: The LoRA Stacker node is designed to aggregate and configure LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) parameters into a structured format, facilitating the manipulation and application of LoRA adjustments across different model components. It supports dynamic configuration through input parameters, allowing for the customization of LoRA parameters based on specific requirements.

inputs.name: input_mode
inputs.description: Specifies the mode of input processing, determining how LoRA parameters are aggregated and structured. It affects the configuration and representation of LoRA parameters in the output.

inputs.name: lora_count
inputs.description: Defines the number of LoRA adjustments to be considered, dictating the scale of aggregation and the number of parameters to be processed.

inputs.name: lora_name_i
inputs.description: Specifies the name of each LoRA parameter, allowing for the identification and configuration of individual LoRA adjustments.

inputs.name: lora_wt_i
inputs.description: Determines the weight of each LoRA parameter, influencing the impact of the adjustment on the model.

inputs.name: model_str_i
inputs.description: Specifies the strength of the model adjustment for each LoRA parameter, affecting the model's behavior.

inputs.name: clip_str_i
inputs.description: Defines the clipping strength for each LoRA parameter, controlling the extent of adjustment applied.

inputs.name: lora_stack
inputs.description: An optional stack of pre-configured LoRA parameters that can be extended or modified with the current configuration, enhancing flexibility in LoRA parameter management.

outputs.name: LORA_STACK
outputs.description: Returns a structured representation of LoRA parameters, ready for further processing or application within model components.

Manual XY Entry Info.description: This node is designed to provide detailed information about manual entries for XY plots within a specific system. It focuses on extracting and presenting key details that are crucial for understanding and utilizing manual XY entries effectively.

inputs.name: notes
inputs.description: Captures detailed notes or annotations related to manual XY entries, facilitating a deeper understanding and more effective use of XY plot data.

Noise Control Script.description: The TSC_Noise_Control_Script node is designed to integrate and manage noise sources and seed variations within the ComfyUI framework. It allows for the customization of noise generation and seed manipulation, enhancing the control over the randomness and variability in generated outputs. This node serves as a pivotal element in adjusting the noise characteristics and seed behavior, thereby offering a nuanced approach to managing the stochastic elements of the generation process.

inputs.name: rng_source
inputs.description: Specifies the source of randomness for noise generation, allowing selection from CPU, GPU, or NV options. This choice influences the computational backend for noise generation, impacting performance and compatibility.

inputs.name: cfg_denoiser
inputs.description: A boolean flag that enables or disables the configuration denoiser, affecting the noise filtering process during generation.

inputs.name: add_seed_noise
inputs.description: Determines whether additional noise based on a seed value should be introduced, adding another layer of variability to the output.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: The seed value for noise generation, providing a basis for reproducibility and variation in the noise applied.

inputs.name: weight
inputs.description: Defines the weight of the seed noise, adjusting the intensity of the noise effect on the output.

inputs.name: script
inputs.description: An optional script parameter that can be modified or extended with noise settings, offering flexibility in script-based customization.

outputs.name: SCRIPT
outputs.description: Returns a modified or extended script with applied noise settings, facilitating customized noise control within the generation process.

Pack SDXL Tuple.description: The Pack SDXL Tuple node is designed to aggregate multiple model and conditioning parameters into a single, structured tuple. This facilitates the efficient handling and transfer of a comprehensive set of parameters between different stages of a generative AI pipeline, particularly in scenarios involving base and refiner models along with their respective conditioning inputs.

inputs.name: base_model
inputs.description: Represents the base generative model to be included in the tuple, playing a crucial role in the initial stages of generation.

inputs.name: base_clip
inputs.description: Specifies the base CLIP model used for guiding the generation towards the desired outcome.

inputs.name: base_positive
inputs.description: Defines positive conditioning inputs for the base model, influencing the direction of content generation.

inputs.name: base_negative
inputs.description: Describes negative conditioning inputs for the base model, used to steer away from undesired content.

inputs.name: refiner_model
inputs.description: Represents the refiner model that fine-tunes or enhances the output of the base model.

inputs.name: refiner_clip
inputs.description: Specifies the refiner CLIP model used for additional guidance in the refining stage.

inputs.name: refiner_positive
inputs.description: Defines positive conditioning inputs for the refiner model, further directing the refinement process.

inputs.name: refiner_negative
inputs.description: Describes negative conditioning inputs for the refiner model, helping to eliminate undesired aspects in the refinement stage.

outputs.name: SDXL_TUPLE
outputs.description: The structured tuple containing all specified models and conditioning inputs, ready for use in subsequent processing stages.

Simple Eval Examples.description: This node provides a mechanism to load and display example inputs for simple evaluation tasks, facilitating the understanding and testing of evaluation functionalities within the system.

inputs.name: models_text
inputs.description: Defines the default text examples for simple evaluation tasks, loaded from a file. This text aids in illustrating the usage and potential inputs for evaluation purposes.

Tiled Upscaler Script.description: The Tiled Upscaler Script node is designed to enhance image resolution through a process of tiled sampling and upscaling. It leverages various upscaling strategies, including latent and pixel-based methods, to improve image quality while maintaining efficiency. This node is capable of handling different tiling strategies, applying denoise filters, and optionally utilizing control nets for more precise upscaling results.

inputs.name: upscale_by
inputs.description: Specifies the factor by which the image should be upscaled. It affects the overall resolution enhancement of the image.

inputs.name: tile_size
inputs.description: Determines the size of the tiles used in the upscaling process, impacting the granularity of the upscaling and potentially the performance.

inputs.name: tiling_strategy
inputs.description: Defines the approach for tiling during the upscaling process, influencing how the image is segmented and processed.

inputs.name: tiling_steps
inputs.description: Indicates the number of steps or iterations to perform during the tiling process, affecting the depth of the upscaling operation.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: Provides a seed for random number generation, ensuring reproducibility of the upscaling process.

inputs.name: denoise
inputs.description: Enables or disables the application of a denoise filter during the upscaling process, affecting image clarity.

inputs.name: use_controlnet
inputs.description: Determines whether a control net is used in the upscaling process, allowing for more precise adjustments.

inputs.name: tile_controlnet
inputs.description: Specifies the control net to be applied if use_controlnet is true, guiding the upscaling process.

inputs.name: strength
inputs.description: Adjusts the intensity of the upscaling effect, allowing for finer control over the final image appearance.

inputs.name: script
inputs.description: Optional script parameters that can be used to customize the upscaling process further.

outputs.name: script
outputs.description: Returns the modified script with upscaling parameters included, ready for further processing.

Unpack SDXL Tuple.description: The 'Unpack SDXL Tuple' node is designed to decompose a complex tuple structure into its constituent components, specifically tailored for handling data related to models, clips, and conditioning elements in an efficient manner. It facilitates the separation and individual handling of base and refiner elements, enhancing modularity and flexibility in processing SDXL tuples.

inputs.name: sdxl_tuple
inputs.description: The SDXL tuple to be unpacked, containing combined model, clip, and conditioning information for both base and refiner stages.

outputs.name: BASE_MODEL
outputs.description: The base model component extracted from the SDXL tuple.

outputs.name: BASE_CLIP
outputs.description: The base clip component extracted from the SDXL tuple.

outputs.name: BASE_CONDITIONING+
outputs.description: The positive base conditioning component extracted from the SDXL tuple.

outputs.name: BASE_CONDITIONING-
outputs.description: The negative base conditioning component extracted from the SDXL tuple.

outputs.name: REFINER_MODEL
outputs.description: The refiner model component extracted from the SDXL tuple.

outputs.name: REFINER_CLIP
outputs.description: The refiner clip component extracted from the SDXL tuple.

outputs.name: REFINER_CONDITIONING+
outputs.description: The positive refiner conditioning component extracted from the SDXL tuple.

outputs.name: REFINER_CONDITIONING-
outputs.description: The negative refiner conditioning component extracted from the SDXL tuple.

XY Input_ Add_Return Noise.description: The node TSC_XYplot_AddReturnNoise is designed to handle XY input types specifically for adding or returning noise within a given process. It maps input types to their corresponding noise actions, enabling or disabling noise based on the specified type.

inputs.name: XY_type
inputs.description: Specifies the type of noise action to be performed, either adding noise or returning with leftover noise, which determines how the node processes the input.

outputs.name: X or Y
outputs.description: unknown

XY Input_ Aesthetic Score.description: This node is designed to generate aesthetic score values for XY plotting, allowing users to visualize and analyze the aesthetic quality of images or outputs based on specified criteria. It supports both positive and negative aesthetic scores, enabling a comprehensive assessment of aesthetic attributes.

inputs.name: target_ascore
inputs.description: Specifies the target aesthetic score type, either 'positive' or 'negative', to determine the nature of the aesthetic evaluation.

inputs.name: batch_count
inputs.description: Determines the number of aesthetic score values to generate, facilitating batch processing for efficiency and scalability.

inputs.name: first_ascore
inputs.description: Sets the starting point of the aesthetic score range, enabling customization of the evaluation scope.

inputs.name: last_ascore
inputs.description: Defines the end point of the aesthetic score range, allowing for precise control over the evaluation interval.

outputs.name: X or Y
outputs.description: Outputs the generated aesthetic score values, categorized as either 'AScore+' for positive or 'AScore-' for negative, suitable for XY plotting.

XY Input_ CFG Scale.description: The node 'XY Input: CFG Scale' is designed to process and generate configuration scale (CFG Scale) values for XY plotting purposes within an efficiency-focused context. It aims to facilitate the visualization and analysis of CFG Scale values by generating a range of floating-point numbers based on input parameters, ensuring these values adhere to specified bounds. This node is integral for tasks that require precise CFG Scale adjustments and visual representation, contributing to the optimization and efficiency analysis of various processes.

inputs.name: batch_count
inputs.description: Specifies the number of CFG Scale values to generate. It influences the node's execution by determining the size of the output array of CFG Scale values.

inputs.name: first_cfg
inputs.description: Defines the starting point of the CFG Scale range. It affects the lower bound of the generated CFG Scale values, ensuring the output starts from this specified value.

inputs.name: last_cfg
inputs.description: Sets the ending point of the CFG Scale range. It impacts the upper bound of the generated CFG Scale values, ensuring the output ends at this specified value.

outputs.name: X or Y
outputs.description: unknown

XY Input_ Checkpoint.description: The TSC_XYplot_Checkpoint node is designed to process XY plot data related to model checkpoints, focusing on validating and handling checkpoint values and clip skip values for efficiency analysis in model training and refinement processes.

inputs.name: target_ckpt
inputs.description: Specifies the target checkpoint type, either 'Base' or 'Refiner', to determine the context of the XY plot data processing.

inputs.name: input_mode
inputs.description: Determines the mode of input which affects how checkpoint data is processed and visualized in the XY plot.

inputs.name: batch_path
inputs.description: The file path to the batch data used for generating the XY plot, influencing the source of data analysis.

inputs.name: subdirectories
inputs.description: A boolean indicating whether to include subdirectories in the batch data search, expanding the scope of data analysis.

inputs.name: batch_sort
inputs.description: Specifies the sorting order of batch data, either 'ascending' or 'descending', to organize the data for analysis.

inputs.name: batch_max
inputs.description: Defines the maximum number of batches to consider for the XY plot, setting an upper limit on the data analysis.

inputs.name: ckpt_count
inputs.description: Indicates the number of checkpoints to include in the analysis, directly impacting the comprehensiveness of the XY plot.

inputs.name: ckpt_name_i
inputs.description: Specifies the name of the i-th checkpoint, allowing for detailed customization of checkpoint data included in the XY plot.

inputs.name: clip_skip_i
inputs.description: Determines the clip skip value for the i-th checkpoint, affecting the granularity of data analysis for each checkpoint.

inputs.name: vae_name_i
inputs.description: Identifies the name of the i-th VAE model, enabling the inclusion of VAE-specific data in the XY plot analysis.

outputs.name: X or Y
outputs.description: Outputs the type of XY plot data generated ('Clip Skip' or 'Clip Skip (Refiner)') along with the corresponding values, facilitating efficiency analysis.

XY Input_ Clip Skip.description: This node is designed to process and validate clip skip values for efficiency in generating XY plots. It focuses on adjusting clip skip values within specified bounds and ensuring they are appropriate for the target checkpoint, either 'Base' or 'Refiner'. The node plays a crucial role in optimizing the generation process by fine-tuning the clip skip parameters, which are essential for controlling the granularity of the plot data.

inputs.name: target_ckpt
inputs.description: Specifies the target checkpoint for which the clip skip values are being adjusted. It determines the context ('Base' or 'Refiner') in which the clip skip values are applied, affecting the output XY plot's granularity.

inputs.name: batch_count
inputs.description: Defines the number of batches for which clip skip values are generated. It influences the volume of data processed and the detail level in the resulting XY plot.

inputs.name: first_clip_skip
inputs.description: The starting point of the clip skip range. It sets the lower limit for clip skip adjustments, impacting the plot's detail level.

inputs.name: last_clip_skip
inputs.description: The ending point of the clip skip range. It sets the upper limit for clip skip adjustments, impacting the plot's detail level.

outputs.name: X or Y
outputs.description: unknown

XY Input_ Control Net Plot.description: This node is designed to generate a series of values for plotting based on the control network's parameters over a specified range. It dynamically adjusts the input parameters such as strength, start percent, and end percent to create a dataset suitable for XY plotting, facilitating the visualization of how changes in these parameters affect the control network's output.

inputs.name: control_net
inputs.description: Represents the control network whose parameters are being adjusted for plotting. It is central to determining the output values for the XY plot.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image input that, along with the control net, influences the generated values for the XY plot.

inputs.name: plot_type
inputs.description: Specifies the type of plot to generate, indicating how X and Y values are derived and related to each other.

inputs.name: strength
inputs.description: The strength parameter applied to the control net, affecting the output values for the plot.

inputs.name: start_percent
inputs.description: The starting percentage value, indicating the initial point of the range for the plot's X or Y axis.

inputs.name: end_percent
inputs.description: The ending percentage value, indicating the final point of the range for the plot's X or Y axis.

inputs.name: X_batch_count
inputs.description: Specifies the number of data points to generate for the X axis of the plot, affecting its granularity.

inputs.name: X_first_value
inputs.description: The starting value for the X axis of the plot, marking the beginning of the range to be visualized.

inputs.name: X_last_value
inputs.description: The ending value for the X axis of the plot, marking the end of the range to be visualized.

inputs.name: Y_batch_count
inputs.description: Specifies the number of data points to generate for the Y axis of the plot, affecting its granularity.

inputs.name: Y_first_value
inputs.description: The starting value for the Y axis of the plot, marking the beginning of the range to be visualized.

inputs.name: Y_last_value
inputs.description: The ending value for the Y axis of the plot, marking the end of the range to be visualized.

inputs.name: cnet_stack
inputs.description: An optional stack of additional parameters that can be appended to each data point, allowing for more complex or detailed plots.

outputs.name: X
outputs.description: Represents the X values generated for the plot, based on the specified input parameters and adjustments.

outputs.name: Y
outputs.description: Represents the Y values generated for the plot, based on the specified input parameters and adjustments.

XY Input_ Control Net.description: The node is designed to generate and manipulate XY input data for control networks, facilitating the exploration of different control parameters (such as strength, start percent, and end percent) across batches of images. It dynamically adjusts control net parameters to optimize image generation, supporting complex conditioning scenarios and enabling detailed analysis and visualization of control net effects.

inputs.name: control_net
inputs.description: The control network configuration to be applied or manipulated across the image batch, central to determining the influence on the generated images.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image or batch of images to which the control net parameters are applied, serving as the basis for the control net's effect analysis.

inputs.name: target_parameter
inputs.description: The specific control net parameter to be varied across the batch, such as strength, start percent, or end percent, guiding the generation process.

inputs.name: batch_count
inputs.description: Specifies the number of variations to generate for the given control parameter, enabling a detailed exploration of its impact.

inputs.name: first_strength
inputs.description: The initial strength value for the control net parameter variation.

inputs.name: last_strength
inputs.description: The final strength value for the control net parameter variation, allowing for a range of adjustments.

inputs.name: first_start_percent
inputs.description: The initial start percent value for the control net parameter variation.

inputs.name: last_start_percent
inputs.description: The final start percent value for the control net parameter variation.

inputs.name: first_end_percent
inputs.description: The initial end percent value for the control net parameter variation.

inputs.name: last_end_percent
inputs.description: The final end percent value for the control net parameter variation.

inputs.name: strength
inputs.description: The strength level applied to the control net, affecting the intensity of its influence.

inputs.name: start_percent
inputs.description: The starting percentage of the control net's effect, determining its initial influence.

inputs.name: end_percent
inputs.description: The ending percentage of the control net's effect, determining its final influence.

inputs.name: cnet_stack
inputs.description: An optional stack of additional control net configurations, allowing for layered or sequential application of multiple control nets.

outputs.name: X or Y
outputs.description: The generated values for either the X or Y axis, based on the control net parameters, structured for integration into visualization or analysis tools.

XY Input_ Denoise.description: This node is designed to generate a set of floating-point values representing denoising levels for a batch of data. It abstracts the process of calculating denoise values across a specified range, facilitating the visualization or analysis of denoising effects in a computational efficiency context.

inputs.name: batch_count
inputs.description: Specifies the number of denoise values to generate, allowing for control over the granularity of the denoising analysis.

inputs.name: first_denoise
inputs.description: Defines the starting point of the denoise range, enabling customization of the denoising process's lower bound.

inputs.name: last_denoise
inputs.description: Sets the endpoint of the denoise range, allowing for the adjustment of the upper limit in the denoising analysis.

outputs.name: X or Y
outputs.description: Outputs a tuple containing the type of values ('Denoise') and the generated floating-point denoise values, suitable for plotting or further analysis.

XY Input_ LoRA Plot.description: This node is designed to generate XY plot data specifically for LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) parameters, facilitating the visualization of relationships between different LoRA configurations and their impacts. It dynamically handles various LoRA-related inputs to produce coordinated X and Y values for plotting, accommodating a range of LoRA parameters such as batch, weight, model strength, and clip strength.

inputs.name: input_mode
inputs.description: Specifies the mode of input, determining which LoRA parameters (e.g., batch, weight, model strength, clip strength) are considered for generating the plot. This affects how the node processes and interprets the provided data.

inputs.name: lora_name
inputs.description: The name of the LoRA configuration being visualized, which is crucial for identifying and differentiating between various LoRA setups in the plot.

inputs.name: model_strength
inputs.description: The strength of the model adaptation applied, relevant when visualizing the impact of model strength on LoRA's effectiveness.

inputs.name: clip_strength
inputs.description: The strength of the clipping applied, relevant when assessing the impact of clip strength on LoRA's performance.

inputs.name: X_batch_count
inputs.description: Specifies the number of batches to be considered for the X-axis values, influencing the granularity of the plot.

inputs.name: X_batch_path
inputs.description: The file path to the batch data for the X-axis, essential for locating and processing the specific LoRA data to be visualized.

inputs.name: X_subdirectories
inputs.description: Indicates whether subdirectories should be included when searching for batch data, affecting the scope of data considered for the X-axis.

inputs.name: X_batch_sort
inputs.description: Determines the sorting order of batch data for the X-axis, which can influence the plot's representation of temporal or ordinal relationships.

inputs.name: X_first_value
inputs.description: The starting value for generating a range of model strengths or clip strengths for the X-axis, setting the lower bound of the plot.

inputs.name: X_last_value
inputs.description: The ending value for generating a range of model strengths or clip strengths for the X-axis, setting the upper bound of the plot.

inputs.name: Y_batch_count
inputs.description: Specifies the number of batches to be considered for the Y-axis values, influencing the granularity of the plot.

inputs.name: Y_first_value
inputs.description: The starting value for generating a range of model strengths or clip strengths for the Y-axis, setting the lower bound of the plot.

inputs.name: Y_last_value
inputs.description: The ending value for generating a range of model strengths or clip strengths for the Y-axis, setting the upper bound of the plot.

inputs.name: lora_stack
inputs.description: An optional stack of LoRA configurations that can be included in the plot, allowing for the visualization of multiple LoRA setups within a single plot.

outputs.name: X
outputs.description: The data represented on the X-axis, including the type and values derived from the specified LoRA parameters.

outputs.name: Y
outputs.description: The data represented on the Y-axis, including the type and values derived from the specified LoRA parameters.

XY Input_ LoRA Stacks.description: This node is designed to process and visualize XY plot data specifically for LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) stacks, enabling the analysis and comparison of different LoRA configurations and their impacts on model efficiency and performance.

inputs.name: node_state
inputs.description: Indicates whether the node is active or not, affecting whether the LoRA stacks are processed for XY plotting.

inputs.name: lora_stack_i
inputs.description: Represents a LoRA stack configuration to be included in the XY plot analysis. The index 'i' can range from 1 to 5, allowing for multiple LoRA stack configurations to be analyzed.

outputs.name: X or Y
outputs.description: Outputs the XY plot data for the given LoRA stacks, facilitating visualization and comparison. The output can represent either 'X' or 'Y' data based on the processing of LoRA stacks.

XY Input_ LoRA.description: This node is designed to process and manipulate LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) parameters for generating XY plot inputs. It handles various LoRA-related inputs, such as batch information, model and clip strengths, and weights, to produce structured data suitable for visualization or further analysis. The node dynamically adjusts to different LoRA configurations, ensuring compatibility and flexibility for diverse analytical needs.

inputs.name: input_mode
inputs.description: Specifies the operational mode of the node, affecting how LoRA parameters are processed and interpreted for XY plotting.

inputs.name: batch_path
inputs.description: Defines the file path for batch processing of LoRA parameters, enabling the node to handle multiple inputs simultaneously for XY plotting.

inputs.name: subdirectories
inputs.description: Indicates whether subdirectories should be considered in the batch processing of LoRA parameters, affecting the scope of data inclusion for XY plotting.

inputs.name: batch_sort
inputs.description: Determines the sorting order of batch-processed LoRA parameters, influencing the organization of data for XY plotting.

inputs.name: batch_max
inputs.description: Sets the maximum number of batches to be processed, limiting the volume of LoRA parameters considered for XY plotting.

inputs.name: lora_count
inputs.description: Specifies the number of LoRA parameters to be processed, directly impacting the composition of data for XY plotting.

inputs.name: model_strength
inputs.description: Defines the strength of the model adjustment for LoRA parameters, influencing the intensity of modifications applied for XY plotting.

inputs.name: clip_strength
inputs.description: Sets the clip strength for LoRA parameters, affecting the extent of clipping applied during the processing for XY plotting.

inputs.name: lora_name_i
inputs.description: Identifies individual LoRA parameters by name, allowing for specific selection and manipulation within the XY plotting process.

inputs.name: model_str_i
inputs.description: Specifies the model strength for individual LoRA parameters, enabling fine-tuned control over the adjustment intensity for each.

inputs.name: clip_str_i
inputs.description: Determines the clip strength for individual LoRA parameters, allowing for precise clipping adjustments on a per-parameter basis.

inputs.name: lora_stack
inputs.description: Represents an optional stack of LoRA parameters, contributing to the aggregated LoRA data for XY plotting.

outputs.name: X or Y
outputs.description: Outputs structured LoRA data for XY plotting, encapsulating various LoRA configurations and parameters in either the X or Y axis.

XY Input_ Manual XY Entry.description: This node facilitates the manual entry of X and Y values for plotting, allowing users to directly input or modify the data points that will be visualized. It serves as a foundational tool for customizing and generating specific XY plots within a user interface, emphasizing user control and flexibility in data presentation.

inputs.name: plot_type
inputs.description: Specifies the type of plot to be generated, guiding the selection of data and the configuration of the plot. This parameter is crucial for determining the overall structure and appearance of the plot.

inputs.name: plot_value
inputs.description: Defines the specific values to be used in the plot, directly influencing the visual representation of the data. This parameter allows for precise control over the data points displayed in the plot.

outputs.name: X or Y
outputs.description: Outputs either X or Y values based on the input configuration, providing the data necessary for constructing the plot.

XY Input_ Prompt S_R.description: This node is designed to facilitate the search and replace functionality within prompts, specifically targeting the enhancement or modification of text inputs for efficiency in processing. It operates by dynamically adjusting the content of prompts based on specified search and replace criteria, thereby optimizing the generation or refinement of text outputs.

inputs.name: target_prompt
inputs.description: Specifies whether the prompt to be modified is positive or negative, directly influencing the type of modification applied to the text.

inputs.name: search_txt
inputs.description: The text string to be searched for within the prompt, serving as the basis for the replacement operation.

inputs.name: replace_count
inputs.description: Indicates the number of times the search text should be replaced, affecting the extent of modification.

inputs.name: replace_i
inputs.description: Dynamic inputs representing the replacement text for each occurrence of the search text, allowing for varied modifications across multiple instances.

outputs.name: X or Y
outputs.description: Outputs the modified prompt text, reflecting either positive or negative modifications as specified by the input criteria.

XY Input_ Refiner On_Off.description: The node is designed to refine the XY plot inputs based on a specified percentage, enabling dynamic adjustment of the refinement process to optimize efficiency and accuracy in data visualization or processing tasks.

inputs.name: refine_at_percent
inputs.description: Specifies the percentage at which the refinement process should be initiated, allowing for precise control over when the refinement adjustments are applied to the XY plot.

outputs.name: X or Y
outputs.description: Outputs a tuple containing the type of refinement ('Refiner On/Off') and the corresponding XY values after applying the refinement at the specified percentage. This output aligns with the expected 'X or Y' designation, indicating either X or Y values are refined.

XY Input_ Sampler_Scheduler.description: This node is designed to process and validate combinations of samplers and schedulers for use in sampling operations. It ensures that the provided sampler and scheduler names are valid within the system's defined bounds, potentially adjusting or providing feedback if invalid options are encountered. The node's functionality is crucial for configuring and optimizing sampling processes, facilitating the selection of appropriate sampling and scheduling strategies based on user input or system requirements.

inputs.name: target_parameter
inputs.description: Specifies the target parameter for optimization, such as 'sampler', 'scheduler', or a combination of both. It determines the focus of the node's processing and directly influences the selection and validation process, guiding the optimization of sampling operations.

inputs.name: input_count
inputs.description: Defines the number of inputs to be considered for the target parameter. This count affects the node's execution by determining how many sampler or scheduler options are evaluated, influencing the comprehensiveness of the validation process.

inputs.name: sampler_i
inputs.description: Represents one of potentially multiple sampler names to be validated. The index 'i' varies, indicating each sampler's position in the sequence for evaluation. This parameter is crucial for assessing the suitability of various samplers within the specified sampling strategy.

inputs.name: scheduler_i
inputs.description: Denotes one of potentially multiple scheduler names to be validated, with 'i' indicating the scheduler's position in the sequence. It plays a key role in evaluating the compatibility and efficiency of different scheduling algorithms for the sampling process.

outputs.name: X or Y
outputs.description: This output represents the result of the validation process, either confirming the suitability of a sampler or scheduler ('X') or providing an alternative recommendation ('Y'). It ensures that the chosen strategies are optimal for the intended sampling operation.

XY Input_ Seeds++ Batch.description: This node is designed to generate a sequence of values representing a batch of seeds, which can be used to control the initialization or variation of processes in a batched manner. It allows for the specification of the batch size and outputs a structured representation of seed values for batch processing.

inputs.name: batch_count
inputs.description: Specifies the number of seeds to generate for the batch. This count directly influences the size of the output seed sequence, enabling control over the batch size for processing.

outputs.name: X or Y
outputs.description: Outputs a tuple containing the type of batch ('Seeds++ Batch') and a list of integers representing the seed values for each batch entry.

XY Input_ Steps.description: The node is designed to generate a sequence of values based on specified step parameters within a given range, tailored for batch processing or iterative operations. It abstracts the complexity of generating step sequences, facilitating efficient data manipulation and visualization in XY plots.

inputs.name: target_parameter
inputs.description: Specifies the parameter to target for generating step values, influencing the sequence generation process.

inputs.name: batch_count
inputs.description: Determines the number of values to generate, directly affecting the length of the output sequence.

inputs.name: first_step
inputs.description: The starting value of the step sequence, setting the initial point for generation.

inputs.name: last_step
inputs.description: The ending value of the step sequence, defining the final point in the generated sequence.

inputs.name: first_start_step
inputs.description: Defines the initial step value for the start_at_step parameter, influencing the starting point of the sequence.

inputs.name: last_start_step
inputs.description: Specifies the final step value for the start_at_step parameter, affecting the sequence's commencement point.

inputs.name: first_end_step
inputs.description: Sets the beginning step value for the end_at_step parameter, impacting the sequence's termination point.

inputs.name: last_end_step
inputs.description: Determines the concluding step value for the end_at_step parameter, defining the end point of the sequence.

inputs.name: first_refine_step
inputs.description: Indicates the initial step value for the refine_at_step parameter, affecting the refinement start point of the sequence.

inputs.name: last_refine_step
inputs.description: Specifies the last step value for the refine_at_step parameter, influencing the refinement end point of the sequence.

outputs.name: X or Y
outputs.description: A tuple containing the type of step sequence generated (X or Y) and the sequence itself, facilitating further processing or visualization.

XY Input_ VAE.description: The node is designed to facilitate the integration and manipulation of VAE (Variational Autoencoder) models within a generative art pipeline, specifically tailored for generating or transforming images based on VAE characteristics. It abstracts the complexities of handling VAE models, including loading, encoding, and decoding operations, to streamline the creation of visual content.

inputs.name: input_mode
inputs.description: Specifies the mode of input, determining whether VAE models are loaded individually or in batches, which influences how the VAE files are processed and utilized in the pipeline.

inputs.name: batch_path
inputs.description: The filesystem path to a directory containing batch VAE files, used when 'input_mode' is set to batch processing, enabling the node to locate and operate on multiple VAE models.

inputs.name: subdirectories
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether to include VAE files from subdirectories within 'batch_path' during batch processing, expanding the scope of VAE models to be considered.

inputs.name: batch_sort
inputs.description: Determines the order in which VAE files are processed in batch mode, supporting ascending or descending sort orders to influence the sequence of VAE model utilization.

inputs.name: batch_max
inputs.description: Sets a limit on the number of VAE files to be processed in batch mode, allowing for control over the maximum number of VAE models to be included in the operation.

inputs.name: vae_count
inputs.description: Specifies the number of individual VAE models to be loaded and processed when not in batch mode, guiding the node in how many VAE models to expect and handle.

inputs.name: vae_name_i
inputs.description: Identifies each individual VAE model by name when not using batch mode, allowing for specific VAE models to be selected and loaded for processing.

outputs.name: X or Y
outputs.description: The output represents either 'X' or 'Y' values processed or generated by the node, typically related to the VAE models' data or characteristics.

XY Plot.description: The XY Plot node is designed to generate and manipulate XY plots based on various parameters and conditions. It supports operations such as flipping axes, adjusting label orientations, caching models, and handling unique identifiers for plot generation. This node is versatile in processing and visualizing data in a structured XY plot format, accommodating different types of plot inputs and configurations.

inputs.name: grid_spacing
inputs.description: Specifies the spacing between grid lines in the plot, affecting the plot's granularity and visual density.

inputs.name: XY_flip
inputs.description: A boolean parameter that determines whether the X and Y axes should be flipped, altering the plot's orientation.

inputs.name: Y_label_orientation
inputs.description: Controls the orientation of Y-axis labels, enhancing readability based on the plot's layout and presentation.

inputs.name: cache_models
inputs.description: Indicates whether to cache model data for efficiency, reducing load times for repeated plot generations.

inputs.name: ksampler_output_image
inputs.description: The output image from the ksampler, which is used as a reference or base for the XY plot.

inputs.name: dependencies
inputs.description: Optional dependencies required for the plot generation, such as additional data sources or configurations.

inputs.name: X
inputs.description: The X-axis values or data points for the plot, which can be a tuple unpacked if connected.

inputs.name: Y
inputs.description: The Y-axis values or data points for the plot, similar to X, can be a tuple unpacked if connected.

outputs.name: SCRIPT
outputs.description: Returns a dictionary containing the script configuration for the XY plot, including plot parameters and data points.

CropFace.description: The CropFace node is designed for processing images by detecting faces, cropping them, and then applying a face restoration model to enhance or restore the cropped face images. It utilizes face detection to identify faces within an image, crops these faces, and then processes each cropped face through a face restoration model to improve image quality or restore facial details.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed for face detection and restoration.

inputs.name: facedetection
inputs.description: The face detection model used to identify and locate faces within the input image.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is a tensor of the cropped and restored faces, ready for further processing or visualization.

FaceRestoreCFWithModel.description: This node is designed to restore faces in images using a face restoration model. It leverages advanced deep learning techniques to enhance the quality of faces in images, addressing issues such as blurriness, noise, and artifacts. The node operates by detecting faces, processing each face individually with the restoration model, and then integrating the enhanced faces back into the original image.

inputs.name: facerestore_model
inputs.description: The face restoration model used for enhancing the quality of faces in images. It plays a crucial role in the node's ability to improve image clarity and detail.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image containing faces to be restored. This image is processed to detect and enhance faces individually.

inputs.name: facedetection
inputs.description: The face detection model used to identify faces within the input image. It ensures that each face is accurately detected before restoration.

inputs.name: codeformer_fidelity
inputs.description: A parameter controlling the fidelity of the restoration process. It adjusts the balance between enhancing details and preserving the original appearance.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image with faces restored. It showcases the enhanced clarity and detail of faces after processing.

FaceRestoreModelLoader.description: The FaceRestoreModelLoader node is designed to load and manage face restoration models, facilitating the initialization and configuration of models required for face restoration tasks. It acts as a central hub for accessing different face restoration and detection models, streamlining the process of model selection and loading for subsequent face restoration operations.

inputs.name: model_name
inputs.description: Specifies the name of the face restoration model to be loaded. This parameter is crucial for identifying and retrieving the correct model from a predefined list of available models.

outputs.name: facerestore_model
outputs.description: Returns the loaded face restoration model, ready for use in face restoration tasks.

Any Converter.description: The Any Converter node is designed to facilitate type conversion and processing of various input types, including integers, floats, numbers, strings, and seeds. It primarily serves to normalize and convert input data into multiple formats, ensuring compatibility and utility across different processing scenarios. This node is particularly useful in scenarios where dynamic type handling and conversion are required, providing a versatile tool for data manipulation and preparation.

inputs.name: int_
inputs.description: An optional integer input that, if provided, is directly used as the value for conversion. It plays a crucial role in determining the output when present, overriding other inputs except for 'str_' if it is valid.

inputs.name: float_
inputs.description: An optional floating-point input that is used for conversion if 'int_' is not provided. It allows for decimal values to be included in the conversion process, adding flexibility in handling numerical data.

inputs.name: number_
inputs.description: A generic numerical input that is used for conversion if neither 'int_' nor 'float_' are provided. It offers a broader range of numerical input handling, accommodating various formats.

inputs.name: string_
inputs.description: An optional string input that, if valid, is converted into multiple formats including integer, float, and seed. This input significantly expands the node's versatility by allowing text-based numerical conversion.

inputs.name: seed_
inputs.description: An optional seed input provided as a dictionary, used for conversion if no other inputs are valid. It extracts the 'seed' value for conversion, demonstrating the node's capability to handle structured input.

inputs.name: str_
inputs.description: An alternative string input that can be used for conversion, similar to 'string_'. If valid, it takes precedence over other inputs except for 'int_', showcasing the node's flexibility in input prioritization.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: The converted integer value from the input.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The converted floating-point value from the input, provided twice for compatibility.

outputs.name: number
outputs.description: The converted numerical value from the input, identical to 'float' for consistency.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The original or converted string representation of the input.

outputs.name: seed
outputs.description: A dictionary containing the converted integer value under the key 'seed', demonstrating the node's ability to output structured data.

outputs.name: str
outputs.description: The original or converted string input, ensuring textual data is preserved or transformed as needed.

Calculate Upscale.description: The Calculate Upscale node is designed to compute the necessary upscale factor and tile size for an image given a target height and the number of tiles in the horizontal direction. It aims to facilitate image processing tasks by determining how much an image needs to be upscaled to meet specific dimensions, thereby assisting in optimizing image manipulation and rendering processes.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image parameter represents the input image to be processed. It is crucial for determining the current dimensions of the image, which are necessary to calculate the upscale factor and tile size.

inputs.name: target_height
inputs.description: The target_height parameter specifies the desired height of the image after upscaling. It plays a key role in calculating the upscale factor by comparing it with the current height of the image.

inputs.name: tiles_in_x
inputs.description: The tiles_in_x parameter indicates the number of horizontal tiles the upscaled image should be divided into. This is essential for calculating the width of each tile after the image has been upscaled.

outputs.name: tile_size
outputs.description: The tile_size output represents the width of each tile in the upscaled image. It is calculated based on the upscaled width of the image and the number of tiles in the horizontal direction.

outputs.name: upscale
outputs.description: The upscale output indicates the factor by which the image needs to be upscaled to achieve the target height. It is a crucial metric for resizing images in image processing tasks.

Image Resize To Height.description: This node is designed to resize an image to a specified target height while maintaining its aspect ratio. It calculates the necessary scaling factor based on the target height and the original height of the image, then applies a Lanczos filter for high-quality resizing.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image to be resized. It is crucial for determining the new dimensions of the image after resizing to the target height.

inputs.name: target_height
inputs.description: The desired height of the image after resizing. This parameter directly influences the scaling factor used to adjust the image's height.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The resized image with the specified target height, maintaining the original aspect ratio.

Image Resize To Width.description: The node is designed to resize an image to a specific width while maintaining its aspect ratio, using a specified upscale method to ensure quality preservation.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image to be resized. This parameter is crucial as it provides the source image that will undergo resizing to match the target width.

inputs.name: target_width
inputs.description: The target width to which the image will be resized. This parameter determines the scale of the resizing operation and directly affects the output image's dimensions.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The resized image with the specified target width, maintaining the original aspect ratio.

Image size to string.description: The node converts the dimensions of an image into a string representation, indicating the image's width and height in a concise format. It abstracts the process of extracting image dimensions and formatting them into a human-readable string.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image whose dimensions are to be converted into a string. This parameter is crucial for determining the size of the image to be represented as a string.

outputs.name: size
outputs.description: A string representing the dimensions of the input image, formatted as 'widthxheight'.

Load Random Image.description: This node is designed to load a random image from a specified directory, optionally including subdirectories. It aims to facilitate the random selection and loading of images for various applications, such as data augmentation, testing, or providing variability in input data for machine learning models.

inputs.name: directory
inputs.description: Specifies the directory from which to load a random image. The node can optionally search through subdirectories if instructed, enhancing its flexibility in handling file structures.

inputs.name: subdirectories
inputs.description: Determines whether the node should include subdirectories in its search for an image file, allowing for a more comprehensive search across a nested directory structure.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: A seed value for the random number generator, ensuring reproducibility of the random image selection when the same seed is used.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The randomly selected image, loaded as a tensor, suitable for further processing or analysis in machine learning workflows.

outputs.name: file name
outputs.description: unknown

Load Text.description: The Load Text node is designed to read and process text data from a specified file path, filtering out any lines that start with a comment symbol. It abstracts the file reading and preprocessing steps, providing a clean text output for further use.

inputs.name: file_path
inputs.description: Specifies the path to the text file to be loaded. This parameter is essential for locating and reading the file's contents.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: Returns the processed text from the file, with comments removed and lines cleaned up.

Multi Text Merge.description: The Multi Text Merge node is designed to concatenate multiple text inputs into a single string, using a specified delimiter to separate each input. It allows for the flexible combination of up to six text strings, making it useful for generating composite text outputs from various sources.

inputs.name: delimiter
inputs.description: Specifies the string used to separate each text input in the concatenated output. This parameter allows for customization of the output format, enabling the use of different separators such as commas, spaces, or custom strings.

inputs.name: s1
inputs.description: The first optional text input to be concatenated. It supports multiline input and is forced to be included in the node's UI.

inputs.name: s2
inputs.description: The second optional text input to be concatenated. It supports multiline input and is forced to be included in the node's UI.

inputs.name: s3
inputs.description: The third optional text input to be concatenated. It supports multiline input and is forced to be included in the node's UI.

inputs.name: s4
inputs.description: The fourth optional text input to be concatenated. It supports multiline input and is forced to be included in the node's UI.

inputs.name: s5
inputs.description: The fifth optional text input to be concatenated. It supports multiline input and is forced to be included in the node's UI.

inputs.name: s6
inputs.description: The sixth optional text input to be concatenated. It supports multiline input and is forced to be included in the node's UI.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The concatenated result of the input texts, separated by the specified delimiter.

Prompt Parser.description: The Prompt Parser node is designed to process and transform text prompts based on a set of rules and conditions. It can parse input prompts to extract and format specific pieces of information, apply random selection to parts of the text based on predefined conditions, and integrate external tags into the prompt. This node is essential for dynamically generating or modifying text prompts in a controlled manner, allowing for customized and context-aware text output.

inputs.name: prompt
inputs.description: The main text input that the node will process. It serves as the base content for parsing and applying transformations.

inputs.name: tags_file
inputs.description: A file path to a text file containing tags that can be used to replace placeholders within the prompt. This allows for dynamic content insertion based on external data.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: A seed value for random number generation, ensuring reproducibility of the random selections made within the prompt processing.

inputs.name: extra1
inputs.description: An optional text input for additional content that can be inserted into the prompt at a specified placeholder.

inputs.name: extra2
inputs.description: Another optional text input for extra content, similar to 'extra1', providing further customization capability for the prompt.

inputs.name: tags
inputs.description: Directly provides tags as text input for replacing placeholders in the prompt, offering an alternative to using a tags file.

outputs.name: positive
outputs.description: The processed text output containing elements designated as positive or desirable.

outputs.name: negative
outputs.description: The processed text output containing elements designated as negative or undesirable.

outputs.name: debug
outputs.description: A detailed log of the parsing process, including seed values, extra inputs, and the raw prompt before processing, useful for debugging and analysis.

Random Line 4.description: The Random Line 4 node is designed to select a random line from each of up to four provided text inputs based on a given seed, concatenate these lines with a specified delimiter, and return the concatenated string. This node enables the generation of unique and varied text outputs by randomly sampling from the provided inputs.

inputs.name: text1
inputs.description: A multiline text input from which a random line will be selected. It contributes to the node's output by potentially being one of the sources for a random line.

inputs.name: text2
inputs.description: A multiline text input, serving as another potential source for a random line selection.

inputs.name: text3
inputs.description: Serves as a potential source for the random line selection, similar to the other text inputs.

inputs.name: text4
inputs.description: Another multiline text input that can contribute a random line to the node's output.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: The seed for the random number generator, ensuring reproducibility of the output across runs.

inputs.name: delimiter
inputs.description: The delimiter used to concatenate the selected random lines from the text inputs.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The concatenated string formed by joining selected random lines from the provided text inputs with the specified delimiter.

Random Line.description: The Random Line node is designed to select a random line from a given text input based on a specified seed. This functionality allows for the introduction of randomness and variability in text processing tasks, ensuring that outputs can vary even with the same input under different seeds.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The 'text' parameter is the input text from which a random line will be selected. It supports multiline input, allowing for a broader range of text to be processed.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: The 'seed' parameter determines the randomness of the line selection, ensuring reproducibility of results when the same seed is used.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: Returns a randomly selected line from the input text, ensuring variability in the output based on the provided seed.

concat.description: The `concat` node is designed to concatenate strings, potentially including an optional additional string, following specific guidelines. It abstracts the process of string concatenation, ensuring that the operation adheres to predefined formatting rules, such as adding spaces between concatenated strings for readability and coherence.

inputs.name: string_a
inputs.description: The primary string to be concatenated. It serves as the base string to which other strings are appended.

inputs.name: string_b
inputs.description: The second string to be concatenated to the primary string, enhancing the base content.

inputs.name: string_c
inputs.description: An optional third string that can be concatenated to the primary and second strings, providing additional flexibility in the concatenation process.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The result of concatenating up to three strings, with optional spaces between non-empty strings for proper formatting.

Filter.description: The Filter node is designed to selectively process data based on specific criteria, allowing for the refinement and extraction of relevant information from a dataset. It focuses on evaluating and filtering input data to meet defined conditions, thereby enabling targeted data analysis and manipulation.

inputs.name: in_question
inputs.description: Serves as the primary query or condition for filtering, determining the focus of data processing.

inputs.name: wordlist
inputs.description: A list of words or terms used as criteria for filtering the data, aiding in the refinement of results.

inputs.name: safeword
inputs.description: A specific term or flag that ensures certain data is preserved or excluded from filtering, enhancing control over the output.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The result of the filtering process, typically a subset of the input data that meets the defined criteria.

Florence2Captions2IPA.description: The Florence2Captions2IPA node is designed to format input captions into a standardized string format. It accepts captions in various forms, including single strings or lists, and processes them into a unified string representation. This functionality is essential for preparing text data for further processing or analysis, ensuring consistency in input format.

inputs.name: caption_input
inputs.description: The 'caption_input' parameter can accept captions in multiple formats, including single strings or lists of strings. It plays a crucial role in determining how the input text is formatted for further processing, directly impacting the node's output.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The output is a formatted string, which may be a concatenation of multiple input strings or a single input string, depending on the input type. This standardized output is suitable for subsequent text processing or analysis tasks.

PresentString.description: The PresentString node is designed to display a given string within a user interface context, effectively parsing and presenting the input text as is.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The 'text' parameter is the primary input for the PresentString node, requiring a string to be displayed. Its role is crucial as it directly influences the content that will be presented to the user.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: unknown

SingleString.description: The SingleString node is designed to pass through a single string input without modification, serving as a straightforward conduit for string data within a pipeline.

inputs.name: string
inputs.description: Represents the string input to be passed through. It is essential for the node's operation as it directly influences the output by being returned unchanged.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The output is the unaltered input string, demonstrating the node's function as a simple pass-through mechanism.

SizeSelector.description: The SizeSelector node provides a mechanism for selecting a specific size configuration (width and height) based on a predefined list of sizes. It abstracts the complexity of handling different resolution requirements by allowing users to select from a human-readable list of size options, which are then translated into the corresponding numerical width and height values.

inputs.name: size_selected
inputs.description: This parameter allows the user to select a size from a predefined list of size options. Each option corresponds to a specific resolution, and the selection determines the output width and height of the node.

outputs.name: width
outputs.description: The width component of the selected size configuration, expressed as an integer.

outputs.name: height
outputs.description: The height component of the selected size configuration, expressed as an integer.

YellowBus.description: YellowBus is designed to facilitate the transfer of various types of data, including models, VAEs, conditioning prompts, and latent embeddings, without modification. It acts as a conduit, allowing these elements to flow seamlessly from input to output, thereby enabling the preservation and straightforward exchange of information between different stages of a processing pipeline.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: Represents a model input, allowing for the transfer of model data through the node.

inputs.name: vae
inputs.description: Represents a VAE (Variational Autoencoder) input, facilitating the transfer of VAE data through the node.

inputs.name: pos_prompt
inputs.description: Represents a positive conditioning prompt, enabling the transfer of specific conditioning information intended to positively influence the outcome.

inputs.name: neg_prompt
inputs.description: Represents a negative conditioning prompt, enabling the transfer of specific conditioning information intended to negatively influence the outcome.

inputs.name: latent
inputs.description: Represents latent embeddings input, allowing for the transfer of latent space representations through the node.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: Outputs the model data received as input, unchanged.

outputs.name: vae
outputs.description: Outputs the VAE (Variational Autoencoder) data received as input, unchanged.

outputs.name: pos_prompt
outputs.description: Outputs the positive conditioning prompt received as input, unchanged.

outputs.name: neg_prompt
outputs.description: Outputs the negative conditioning prompt received as input, unchanged.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: Outputs the latent embeddings received as input, unchanged.

ImageFromURL.description: The ImageFromURL node is designed to fetch and process an image from a given URL, converting it into a tensor format suitable for further image processing or machine learning tasks.

inputs.name: url
inputs.description: The URL of the image to be fetched. This parameter is crucial for the node's operation as it specifies the source of the image to be processed.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The processed image in tensor format, ready for further processing or analysis.

LoraInfo.description: The LoraInfo node is designed to retrieve and provide detailed information about a specific LoRa (Low-Power, Long-Range) configuration, including its output characteristics, trigger words, example prompts, and the base model it is associated with. This node serves as a bridge to access pre-stored or dynamically generated LoRa metadata, facilitating the integration and utilization of LoRa configurations within applications.

inputs.name: lora_name
inputs.description: The name of the LoRa configuration for which information is being requested. It is crucial for identifying the specific LoRa setup and retrieving its associated data.

outputs.name: trigger_words
outputs.description: The trigger words associated with the specified LoRa configuration, providing insights into its usage.

outputs.name: example_prompt
outputs.description: An example prompt associated with the specified LoRa configuration, offering a glimpse into how it can be utilized.

Blur.description: The Blur node applies a Gaussian blur to an image, allowing for the adjustment of the blur's intensity and spread through parameters. This process can soften the image or reduce noise and detail, making it useful for post-processing effects or preparing images for further processing steps.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be blurred. This is the primary data upon which the blur effect is applied, affecting the visual clarity and detail of the image.

inputs.name: radius
inputs.description: Determines the radius of the blur effect. A larger radius results in a more pronounced blur, affecting the overall softness of the image.

inputs.name: sigma_factor
inputs.description: Controls the spread of the blur effect. A higher sigma value increases the spread of the blur, contributing to the intensity and softness of the effect.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The blurred image, which has undergone a Gaussian blur transformation to reduce detail and soften the image.

Change Channel Count.description: The Change Channel Count node is designed to modify the number of channels in an image tensor. It supports changing an image to a mask, RGB, or RGBA format, depending on the specified kind. This functionality is crucial for image processing tasks where the channel count of an image needs to be adjusted for compatibility with different models or outputs.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image tensor whose channel count is to be changed. This parameter is essential for determining the structure and content of the output image.

inputs.name: kind
inputs.description: Specifies the desired output format of the image, which can be a mask, RGB, or RGBA. This choice directly influences the transformation applied to the input image.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The transformed image tensor with the specified number of channels.

Combine Masks.description: The Combine Masks node is designed to perform various operations on two input masks, such as union, intersection, difference, and others, to produce a single output mask. It allows for flexible manipulation of masks, enabling the creation of complex mask shapes and patterns by combining simpler ones.

inputs.name: image1
inputs.description: The first input mask for the operation. It plays a crucial role in determining the base of the operation, such as the starting point for union, intersection, or difference calculations.

inputs.name: image2
inputs.description: The second input mask that is combined with the first mask according to the specified operation. It contributes to the final shape and content of the output mask.

inputs.name: op
inputs.description: Specifies the type of operation to perform on the input masks, such as union, intersection, difference, etc. This determines how the masks are combined to produce the output.

inputs.name: clamp_result
inputs.description: Determines whether the resulting mask values should be clamped between 0 and 1, ensuring valid mask values.

inputs.name: round_result
inputs.description: Indicates whether the values in the resulting mask should be rounded to the nearest integer, potentially simplifying the mask.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The resulting mask after applying the specified operation on the input masks. It represents the combined effect of the inputs according to the operation.

Constant Mask.description: The Constant Mask node is designed to create a uniform mask with a specified constant value across all its elements. It can generate masks of explicit dimensions or replicate the dimensions of a provided image, offering flexibility in mask creation for various image processing tasks.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: Specifies the constant value to fill the mask with, allowing for control over the mask's intensity or transparency.

inputs.name: explicit_height
inputs.description: Defines the explicit height of the generated mask, used when not replicating the size of an existing image.

inputs.name: explicit_width
inputs.description: Defines the explicit width of the generated mask, used when not replicating the size of an existing image.

inputs.name: copy_image_size
inputs.description: An optional image parameter whose dimensions are used to determine the size of the generated mask, overriding explicit dimensions if provided.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is a mask filled with the specified constant value, potentially matching the dimensions of an input image if provided.

Convert Color Space.description: The ConvertColorSpace node is designed to transform the color space of an image from one format to another, such as from RGB to HSV or HSL, and vice versa. This node facilitates the manipulation and analysis of images by allowing them to be represented in different color models, which can be more suitable for specific tasks or visual effects.

inputs.name: in_space
inputs.description: Specifies the original color space of the input image. This parameter determines how the image's color data is interpreted before conversion.

inputs.name: out_space
inputs.description: Defines the target color space to which the image will be converted. This parameter sets the desired color model format for the output image.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be converted. This parameter is the actual image data that will undergo the color space transformation.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image after the color space conversion. This image will be in the target color space specified by the 'out_space' parameter.

Create QR Code.description: This node generates a QR code from provided text, allowing customization of size, version, error correction level, box size, and border. It outputs the QR code as an image tensor, suitable for further processing or visualization.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The text to be encoded into the QR code. This is the primary data the QR code will represent.

inputs.name: size
inputs.description: Specifies the size of the generated QR code image in pixels.

inputs.name: qr_version
inputs.description: Determines the version of the QR code, which affects the amount of data that can be stored.

inputs.name: error_correction
inputs.description: Sets the error correction level of the QR code, influencing its resilience to damage.

inputs.name: box_size
inputs.description: Defines the size of each box in the QR code grid.

inputs.name: border
inputs.description: Specifies the width of the border around the QR code.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The generated QR code as an image tensor, ready for use or display.

Create Rect Mask.description: The Create Rect Mask node is designed to generate rectangular masks based on specified dimensions and origin points. It supports creating masks in either percentage or pixel modes, allowing for flexible mask creation relative to the image size. This node can also adapt the mask size automatically if a reference image is provided, ensuring the mask aligns perfectly with the image dimensions.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Specifies the mode of dimension calculation for the mask, either as a percentage of the image size or in absolute pixels, affecting how the mask's dimensions are interpreted.

inputs.name: origin
inputs.description: Determines the starting point of the mask within the image, which can be any of the four corners, influencing the mask's position.

inputs.name: x
inputs.description: The x-coordinate of the mask's origin, which sets the horizontal starting point of the mask.

inputs.name: y
inputs.description: The y-coordinate of the mask's origin, which sets the vertical starting point of the mask.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: The width of the mask, which can be defined in pixels or as a percentage of the image width, depending on the mode.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: The height of the mask, which can be defined in pixels or as a percentage of the image height, depending on the mode.

inputs.name: image_width
inputs.description: The width of the image to which the mask will be applied. This parameter is ignored if copy_image_size is provided.

inputs.name: image_height
inputs.description: The height of the image to which the mask will be applied. This parameter is ignored if copy_image_size is provided.

inputs.name: copy_image_size
inputs.description: An optional image parameter. If provided, the mask dimensions will be automatically adjusted to match the size of this reference image, overriding the image_width and image_height parameters.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: Outputs a rectangular mask as a tensor, with dimensions and position based on the input parameters.

Cut By Mask.description: The 'Cut By Mask' node is designed to precisely extract or isolate parts of an image based on a specified mask. It allows for the resizing of the cut-out image to specific dimensions, optionally handling multiple image segments in a batch when provided with mask mappings from a 'Separate Mask Components' node.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed. It serves as the primary canvas from which parts will be cut out based on the mask.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The mask that defines the areas of the input image to be cut out. It acts as a stencil, specifying which parts of the image are to be extracted or isolated.

inputs.name: force_resize_width
inputs.description: An optional width to which the cut-out image(s) will be resized. If specified, it overrides the natural size of the cut-out segments, enabling uniformity in output dimensions.

inputs.name: force_resize_height
inputs.description: An optional height to which the cut-out image(s) will be resized. Similar to force_resize_width, it allows for the standardization of output sizes across different cut-outs.

inputs.name: mask_mapping_optional
inputs.description: An optional mapping of mask components, typically provided by a 'Separate Mask Components' node. It enables the cutting of multiple image segments in a single operation, based on distinct mask parts.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image(s) after being cut by the mask. This can be a single image or multiple images, depending on whether mask mapping was used, resized as specified.

Get Image Size.description: This node is designed to determine the dimensions of an image, specifically its width and height, by analyzing the image's size attributes.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image for which the size is to be determined. This input is crucial as it directly influences the output by providing the necessary data to calculate the image's dimensions.

outputs.name: width
outputs.description: The width of the input image, calculated based on the image's size attributes.

outputs.name: height
outputs.description: The height of the input image, calculated based on the image's size attributes.

Image To Mask.description: The Image To Mask node is designed to convert images into masks based on specified criteria. It supports different methods of conversion, allowing for flexibility in how the mask is generated from the image.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be converted into a mask. This parameter is crucial as it provides the source material from which the mask will be generated.

inputs.name: method
inputs.description: Specifies the method of conversion to be used for generating the mask from the image. This affects how the mask is derived, offering options such as intensity-based or alpha channel-based conversions.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The output is a mask derived from the input image according to the specified conversion method.

Make Image Batch.description: The Make Image Batch node is designed to aggregate multiple individual images or smaller batches of images into a larger batch. This functionality is crucial for processing multiple images in parallel, enhancing efficiency in batch operations.

inputs.name: image1
