inputs.description: The primary image to start the batch. It is a required input that serves as the base to which additional images can be appended.

inputs.name: image2
inputs.description: An optional image that can be appended to the initial image to form a larger batch.

inputs.name: image3
inputs.description: An optional image that can be appended to the growing batch, further increasing its size.

inputs.name: image4
inputs.description: An optional image that can be appended to the batch, contributing to the batch's expansion.

inputs.name: image5
inputs.description: An optional image that can be appended, further enlarging the batch size.

inputs.name: image6
inputs.description: An optional image that can be appended, maximizing the batch's capacity.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The resulting larger batch of images, aggregated from the individual inputs.

Mask By Text.description: This node automatically generates masks based on textual prompts, allowing for the creation of image masks that are aligned with the semantic content of the provided text. It utilizes natural language processing to interpret the prompts and generate corresponding masks, facilitating targeted image editing and manipulation.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image for which the mask will be generated, serving as the canvas for the text-based mask creation.

inputs.name: prompt
inputs.description: The positive text prompt that guides the mask generation, focusing on what should be included or highlighted in the generated mask.

inputs.name: negative_prompt
inputs.description: The negative text prompt that guides the mask generation by specifying what should be excluded from the generated mask, helping to refine the mask's focus.

inputs.name: precision
inputs.description: Specifies the precision of the mask generation, allowing for control over the mask's sensitivity to the text prompts.

inputs.name: normalize
inputs.description: Determines whether the mask should be normalized, affecting the scale and distribution of the mask values.

outputs.name: thresholded_mask
outputs.description: The mask generated based on the text prompts, thresholded to distinguish between the areas of interest and the background.

outputs.name: raw_mask
outputs.description: The raw mask generated from the text prompts before any thresholding, providing a more nuanced view of the mask's response to the text.

Mask Morphology.description: The Mask Morphology node specializes in altering the shape of masks through morphological operations such as dilation, erosion, opening, and closing. These operations enable the refinement or modification of mask boundaries, facilitating more precise control over mask shapes for various image processing tasks.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The 'image' parameter represents the mask to be processed. It is the primary input for morphological transformations, determining the initial shape and structure that will undergo modification.

inputs.name: distance
inputs.description: The 'distance' parameter specifies the extent of the morphological operation. It affects the size of the transformation applied, influencing how much the mask expands or contracts during processing.

inputs.name: op
inputs.description: The 'op' parameter selects the specific morphological operation to apply to the mask. Options include 'dilate', 'erode', 'open', and 'close', each altering the mask in distinct ways to achieve desired shape modifications.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is a modified mask, resulting from the applied morphological operation. It reflects changes in the mask's shape and boundaries, tailored by the specified operation and parameters.

Mask To Region.description: The 'Mask To Region' node is designed to transform a given mask into a rectangular region that encompasses the mask, adhering to specified constraints such as padding, aspect ratio, and minimum dimensions. This node facilitates the extraction of meaningful regions from masks for further processing or analysis.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The 'mask' parameter represents the input mask image that the node will process to identify and extract the rectangular region.

inputs.name: padding
inputs.description: The 'padding' parameter allows specifying additional space around the identified region, enhancing flexibility in region extraction.

inputs.name: constraints
inputs.description: The 'constraints' parameter defines the rules for adjusting the extracted region's dimensions, including keeping aspect ratios and size multiples.

inputs.name: constraint_x
inputs.description: The 'constraint_x' parameter sets a constraint on the region's width, ensuring it adheres to specified requirements.

inputs.name: constraint_y
inputs.description: The 'constraint_y' parameter sets a constraint on the region's height, ensuring it adheres to specified requirements.

inputs.name: min_width
inputs.description: The 'min_width' parameter establishes a minimum width for the extracted region, ensuring it meets a certain size threshold.

inputs.name: min_height
inputs.description: The 'min_height' parameter establishes a minimum height for the extracted region, ensuring it meets a certain size threshold.

inputs.name: batch_behavior
inputs.description: The 'batch_behavior' parameter dictates how the node should handle multiple masks in a batch, focusing on matching aspect ratios or sizes.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is an image of the rectangular region extracted from the input mask, conforming to the specified constraints.

MasqueradeIncrementer.description: The MasqueradeIncrementer node is designed to perform a simple arithmetic operation on a given seed value, incrementing it within a specified maximum value. This node abstracts the concept of modular arithmetic, providing a straightforward way to cycle through a range of numbers starting from a seed value.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: The 'seed' parameter serves as the starting point for the increment operation. It determines the initial value from which the incrementing begins, playing a crucial role in the node's execution and the resulting output.

inputs.name: max_value
inputs.description: The 'max_value' parameter sets the upper limit for the increment operation. It defines the range within which the seed value can be incremented, ensuring that the result cycles within a specified boundary.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: The output is an integer representing the incremented value of the seed, modulo the specified maximum value.

Mix Color By Mask.description: The Mix Color By Mask node blends a specified color into an image based on a provided mask, allowing for selective colorization or recoloring of parts of the image.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The original image to be processed. The mask determines which parts of this image will be blended with the specified color.

inputs.name: r
inputs.description: The red component of the color to blend into the image, scaled from 0 to 255. It influences the final color's red intensity in the masked areas.

inputs.name: g
inputs.description: The green component of the color to blend into the image, scaled from 0 to 255. It affects the final color's green intensity in the masked areas.

inputs.name: b
inputs.description: The blue component of the color to blend into the image, scaled from 0 to 255. It impacts the final color's blue intensity in the masked areas.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The mask used to determine where the specified color should be blended into the original image. Areas of the mask with higher values will have more of the color applied.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The resulting image after blending the specified color into the original image based on the mask.

Mix Images By Mask.description: The Mix Images By Mask node blends two images together based on a provided mask, creating a composite image where parts of each input image are visible according to the mask's values. This node is essential for tasks that require the dynamic combination of images, such as creating effects or merging images in a context-sensitive manner.

inputs.name: image1
inputs.description: The first image to be mixed. It serves as one of the base layers for the blending operation.

inputs.name: image2
inputs.description: The second image to be mixed. It acts as the other base layer in the blending process.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: A mask that determines how the two images are blended together. Areas of the mask with higher values allow more of the second image to show through.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The resulting image after blending the two input images according to the mask.

Paste By Mask.description: The Paste By Mask node enables the pasting of one image onto another using a specified mask to define the paste location. It supports various resizing behaviors to ensure the pasted image fits the mask area appropriately, and optionally allows for mask mapping to control the pasting process more granularly.

inputs.name: image_base
inputs.description: The base image onto which another image will be pasted. It serves as the background for the operation.

inputs.name: image_to_paste
inputs.description: The image to be pasted onto the base image. This image is manipulated according to the mask and resize behavior to fit appropriately.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: A mask that defines where on the base image the pasting should occur. The mask's shape and values determine the pasting area.

inputs.name: resize_behavior
inputs.description: Specifies how the image to paste should be resized to fit the mask area, with options like keeping the ratio, filling the area, or matching the source size.

inputs.name: mask_mapping_optional
inputs.description: Optionally used to control which part of the pasting image goes onto which part of the base image, based on a mask mapping obtained from a separate operation.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The result of pasting an image onto another with the specified mask, producing a new image that combines elements of both according to the defined parameters.

Prune By Mask.description: The Prune By Mask node is designed to filter out images from a batch based on the associated mask's average pixel value, ensuring only images with sufficiently defined masks are processed further.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image input represents the batch of images to be filtered based on their associated mask's average pixel value.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The mask input is used to determine which images in the batch meet the criteria for having an average pixel value of at least 0.5, acting as a filter criterion.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: This output consists of the filtered batch of images that have passed the mask's average pixel value criterion.

Separate Mask Components.description: This node is designed to process a given mask by separating it into multiple contiguous components, effectively breaking down a complex mask into simpler, individual parts. It returns these separated components along with a mapping that can be utilized in subsequent operations, particularly useful in batch processing scenarios.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The mask input is a crucial component for the operation of this node, as it represents the complex mask that needs to be broken down into simpler, contiguous components. The processing of this mask determines the output of separated mask components and their mapping.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The output masks represent the separated contiguous components derived from the original complex mask input.

outputs.name: mask_mappings
outputs.description: The mask mappings provide a reference to the original mask from which each separated component was derived, facilitating further processing or analysis.

Unary Image Op.description: This node applies a specified unary operation on an image, such as inversion, averaging, rounding, clamping, or taking the absolute value. It's designed to manipulate the pixel values of an image according to the chosen operation, enabling various image preprocessing tasks.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image to be processed. It serves as the primary input for the operation, determining the visual content that will undergo the specified unary transformation.

inputs.name: op
inputs.description: Specifies the unary operation to apply to the image. Options include 'invert', 'average', 'round', 'clamp', and 'abs', each affecting the image's pixel values in a unique way.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The processed image, after applying the specified unary operation. It reflects the visual changes made to the original image based on the operation performed.

Unary Mask Op.description: The Unary Mask Op node applies a specified unary operation to a given mask image, transforming it according to the operation chosen. This node supports operations such as inverting, averaging, rounding, clamping, and taking the absolute value of the mask, enabling various forms of mask manipulation.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The 'image' parameter represents the mask image to be transformed. It is crucial for determining the base data on which the unary operation will be applied, directly influencing the outcome of the transformation.

inputs.name: op
inputs.description: The 'op' parameter specifies the unary operation to apply to the mask image, such as invert, average, round, clamp, or abs. This choice dictates the nature of the transformation performed on the mask.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The transformed mask image, resulting from the application of the specified unary operation.

AddMetaData.description: The AddMetaData node is designed to embed metadata into images by associating specific labels and text values with them. This process enriches the image data with additional, descriptive information that can be utilized for various purposes, such as categorization, identification, or further processing.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image to which metadata will be added. It serves as the primary input for the metadata embedding process.

inputs.name: label
inputs.description: A label that categorizes or identifies the metadata being added. It acts as a key in the metadata dictionary.

inputs.name: text_value
inputs.description: The actual text to be added as metadata under the specified label. This value enriches the image with descriptive or identifying information.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The image with the newly added metadata, allowing for enriched data representation and usage.

Batch Crop Image.description: The BatchCropImage node is designed for processing a batch of images by cropping them based on a specified amount. It operates on a directory of images, applying a uniform crop operation to each image to reduce their dimensions by a certain percentage, thereby preparing the images for further processing or analysis.

inputs.name: image_directory
inputs.description: Specifies the directory containing the images to be processed. It is crucial for locating and accessing the batch of images for cropping.

inputs.name: crop_amount
inputs.description: Determines the percentage of the image to be cropped from each side. This parameter directly influences the final size of the cropped images, affecting both their width and height.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The cropped images are returned as a list, with each element representing a cropped version of the original images found in the specified directory.

Batch Crop Resize Inplace.description: This node is designed to perform in-place cropping and resizing operations on a batch of images. It aims to modify the dimensions of each image in the batch according to specified parameters, optimizing the images for further processing or analysis.

inputs.name: image_directory
inputs.description: Specifies the directory containing the images to be processed. This parameter is crucial for locating and loading the images for subsequent cropping and resizing operations.

inputs.name: subdirectories
inputs.description: Indicates whether to include subdirectories within the specified image directory for processing. This parameter allows for more comprehensive image selection.

inputs.name: replace_original
inputs.description: Determines whether the original images should be replaced with the processed versions. This parameter affects how the output images are saved.

inputs.name: replace_suffix
inputs.description: Specifies the suffix to be added to the filenames of processed images when not replacing the original images. This parameter helps in identifying the modified images.

inputs.name: upscale_method
inputs.description: Defines the method to be used for upscaling the images during the resizing process. This parameter influences the quality and dimensions of the output images.

inputs.name: crop
inputs.description: Specifies the cropping method to be applied to the images. This parameter determines how the images are cropped before resizing.

inputs.name: crop_amount
inputs.description: Determines the proportion of the image to be cropped. This parameter directly influences the final dimensions of the images, playing a key role in the resizing process.

outputs.name: job_done
outputs.description: The output is a string message indicating the completion of the processing job, including the number of images processed. This provides a summary of the operation's outcome.

Batch Load Images.description: This node is designed to load a batch of images from a specified directory, optionally including images from subdirectories. It supports various image formats and converts them into a tensor format suitable for further processing or model input.

inputs.name: image_directory
inputs.description: Specifies the directory path where images are stored. This path is essential for locating and loading the images into the node.

inputs.name: subdirectories
inputs.description: Determines whether to include images from subdirectories within the specified image directory. This allows for more comprehensive image loading.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: Outputs a list of images loaded and converted into tensor format, ready for further processing or as input to models.

Batch Resize Image for SDXL.description: This node is designed for batch processing of images, specifically resizing them according to specified upscale and crop methods. It allows for the efficient handling of multiple images within a directory, applying the same resizing parameters to each image.

inputs.name: image_directory
inputs.description: Specifies the directory containing the images to be processed. This parameter is crucial for locating and iterating over the images to apply the resizing operations.

inputs.name: upscale_method
inputs.description: Determines the method used for upscaling the images during the resizing process. The choice of method can affect the quality and characteristics of the resized images.

inputs.name: crop
inputs.description: Defines the cropping method to be applied to the images before resizing. This parameter allows for the adjustment of image dimensions and focus prior to upscaling.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is a list of images that have been resized according to the specified upscale and crop methods.

Checkpoint Loader Simple Mikey.description: This node is designed to simplify the process of loading model checkpoints for further use in machine learning tasks. It abstracts away the complexities involved in locating, loading, and configuring checkpoints, making it easier for users to integrate pre-trained models into their workflows.

inputs.name: ckpt_name
inputs.description: Specifies the name of the checkpoint to be loaded. This parameter is crucial as it determines which checkpoint file is accessed and loaded for use.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The loaded model object, ready for use in various machine learning tasks.

outputs.name: clip
outputs.description: The CLIP model associated with the loaded checkpoint, if applicable and requested.

outputs.name: vae
outputs.description: The VAE model associated with the loaded checkpoint, if applicable and requested.

outputs.name: ckpt_name
outputs.description: The name of the loaded checkpoint, useful for reference or further processing.

outputs.name: ckpt_hash
outputs.description: A hash value representing the loaded checkpoint, useful for verification or identification purposes.

CheckpointHash.description: The CheckpointHash node is designed to generate a hash value for a given checkpoint file. It identifies the file within a specified directory, computes its hash, and updates a prompt dictionary with the hash and checkpoint name. This functionality is crucial for ensuring the integrity and uniqueness of checkpoint files in machine learning workflows.

inputs.name: ckpt_name
inputs.description: The name of the checkpoint file for which the hash is to be generated. This parameter is essential for locating the file within the directory and computing its hash.

outputs.name: ckpt_hash
outputs.description: The computed hash value of the checkpoint file, ensuring its integrity and uniqueness.

CinematicLook.description: The CinematicLook node is designed to transform images by applying a cinematic look, combining techniques from ImageOverlay and HALDClut. It enhances visuals to evoke a film-like aesthetic, incorporating various styles such as modern, retro, and black and white, among others.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image parameter represents the visual content to be transformed. It serves as the base for applying the cinematic look, determining the final aesthetic outcome.

inputs.name: look
inputs.description: The look parameter specifies the desired cinematic style to be applied to the image, such as 'modern', 'retro', or 'black and white'. It influences the visual characteristics and mood of the output.

outputs.name: result_img
outputs.description: The output is a transformed image with the applied cinematic look, reflecting the specified style and enhancing the visual appeal.

Empty Latent Ratio Custom SDXL.description: This node is designed to generate a custom-sized latent representation based on specified width and height dimensions, tailored for the SDXL latent format. It utilizes predefined ratios to adjust the dimensions if they match known ratios, or calculates the appropriate size otherwise, ensuring the generated latent space is optimized for subsequent image generation tasks.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Specifies the desired width of the latent representation. This dimension is used to determine the final size of the latent space, potentially adjusted based on predefined ratios or calculated to fit the SDXL format.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Specifies the desired height of the latent representation. Similar to width, this dimension influences the final size of the latent space, adjusted according to predefined ratios or calculated for optimal compatibility with the SDXL format.

inputs.name: batch_size
inputs.description: Determines the number of latent representations to generate in a single batch. This allows for the generation of multiple latents simultaneously, enhancing efficiency.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The generated latent representation, optimized for the SDXL format. It is a tensor structured to facilitate subsequent image synthesis processes.

Empty Latent Ratio Select SDXL.description: This node is designed to generate a tensor representing an empty latent space based on a selected ratio from predefined options. It facilitates the creation of a latent space with specific dimensions that adhere to a user-selected aspect ratio, enabling the generation of content with desired proportions.

inputs.name: ratio_selected
inputs.description: Specifies the aspect ratio for the latent space to be generated. It determines the dimensions of the resulting latent space, ensuring that the generated content aligns with the selected proportions.

inputs.name: batch_size
inputs.description: Determines the number of latent spaces to generate in a single batch. It allows for the efficient creation of multiple latent spaces with the same dimensions in one operation.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The generated tensor representing the empty latent space. It is structured to match the dimensions dictated by the selected aspect ratio and batch size.

EvalFloats.description: EvalFloats is designed to dynamically evaluate mathematical expressions provided by the user. It takes two float inputs and a formula as a string, processes the formula by substituting the inputs, and returns the result in multiple formats.

inputs.name: a
inputs.description: Represents the first float input for the mathematical formula. Its value is crucial as it directly influences the outcome of the evaluated expression.

inputs.name: b
inputs.description: Serves as the second float input for the mathematical formula. Similar to 'a', its value significantly affects the result of the expression.

inputs.name: formula
inputs.description: A string input representing the mathematical formula to be evaluated. This formula should include placeholders for 'a' and 'b' which are replaced by their respective input values during processing.

outputs.name: result_float
outputs.description: The floating-point result of the evaluated mathematical formula.

FaceFixerOpenCV.description: FaceFixerOpenCV is designed to enhance and modify facial features within images using OpenCV. It employs face detection algorithms to identify faces in images and applies various transformations to improve or alter the appearance of these faces, such as resizing, denoising, and blending with other facial features.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image tensor where faces need to be detected and fixed. It serves as the primary input for face detection and subsequent modifications.

inputs.name: base_model
inputs.description: The base model used for generating new facial features or enhancing existing ones.

inputs.name: vae
inputs.description: The variational autoencoder used for encoding and decoding facial features.

inputs.name: positive_cond_base
inputs.description: Base conditioning for positive attributes to enhance or generate in the face.

inputs.name: negative_cond_base
inputs.description: Base conditioning for negative attributes to reduce or eliminate in the face.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: A seed value for random number generation, ensuring reproducibility of results.

inputs.name: face_img_resolution
inputs.description: The resolution to which the face images are scaled before processing.

inputs.name: padding
inputs.description: Padding added to the detected face region before processing to include a broader context.

inputs.name: scale_factor
inputs.description: A parameter that influences the detection process by specifying how much the image size is reduced at each image scale.

inputs.name: min_neighbors
inputs.description: A threshold for determining which detected faces are retained. It represents the minimum number of neighbors each candidate rectangle should have to qualify as a face.

inputs.name: denoise
inputs.description: The degree of denoising applied to the face images during processing.

inputs.name: classifier
inputs.description: Specifies the classifier model to be used for face detection. It determines the type of faces (e.g., anime, frontal, profile) the node is looking for within the image.

inputs.name: sampler_name
inputs.description: Specifies the sampling method used for generating or enhancing facial features.

inputs.name: scheduler
inputs.description: The scheduler used for controlling the sampling process.

inputs.name: cfg
inputs.description: Configuration settings for the face fixing process.

inputs.name: steps
inputs.description: The number of steps in the face fixing process.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The modified image tensor with enhanced or altered facial features.

FileNamePrefix.description: This node is designed to generate a prefix for filenames based on various conditions such as the current date, a custom directory, and custom text. It allows for dynamic filename customization by incorporating date formatting and custom text replacement, ensuring filenames are structured and organized according to user-defined parameters.

inputs.name: date
inputs.description: Indicates whether the current date should be included in the filename prefix. When set to 'true', the date is formatted and appended to the prefix, contributing to a time-stamped file organization.

inputs.name: date_directory
inputs.description: Determines if the current date should be used to create a directory structure within the filename prefix. If 'true', a date-based directory is prepended to the prefix, aiding in chronological sorting of files.

inputs.name: custom_directory
inputs.description: Specifies a custom directory path to be included in the filename prefix. This path is dynamically generated based on additional information provided, allowing for customized file organization within specific directories.

inputs.name: custom_text
inputs.description: Custom text to be appended to the filename prefix. This text can be dynamically generated and is sanitized to remove invalid filename characters, enabling personalized file naming.

outputs.name: filename_prefix
outputs.description: The generated filename prefix, constructed based on the input parameters and conditions. It is sanitized and structured to ensure valid and organized filenames.

FileNamePrefixDateDirFirst.description: This node is designed to generate a filename prefix based on a combination of date, custom directory, and custom text inputs. It dynamically constructs the prefix by incorporating current date information, user-defined directory structures, and custom text, ensuring the generated prefix is unique and organized according to the specified parameters.

inputs.name: date
inputs.description: Indicates whether the current date should be included in the filename prefix. Including the date helps in organizing files chronologically and makes the prefix more informative.

inputs.name: date_directory
inputs.description: Determines if the current date should be used as a directory in the file path. This is useful for organizing files into date-based directories for better file management.

inputs.name: custom_directory
inputs.description: Allows for the specification of a custom directory path to be included in the filename prefix. This enables users to organize their files within custom directory structures.

inputs.name: custom_text
inputs.description: Specifies custom text to be appended to the filename prefix. This allows for further customization and identification of files.

outputs.name: filename_prefix
outputs.description: The generated filename prefix, which is a string that combines date information, custom directory paths, and custom text according to the specified inputs.

Float to String.description: The FLOATtoSTRING node is designed to convert floating-point numbers into their string representation, optionally formatting the output with commas for readability. This node serves as a utility for transforming numerical data into a text format that can be easily displayed or processed further.

inputs.name: float_
inputs.description: The floating-point number to be converted into a string. This parameter is central to the node's operation, determining the numerical value that will be transformed.

inputs.name: use_commas
inputs.description: A flag indicating whether to format the resulting string with commas for thousands, millions, etc., enhancing readability.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The string representation of the input floating-point number, formatted according to the 'use_commas' parameter.

GetSubdirectories.description: This node is designed to retrieve all subdirectories within a specified directory, effectively scanning a directory path to list its immediate child directories. It serves as a utility for directory management and organization, facilitating the exploration and manipulation of filesystem structures.

inputs.name: directory
inputs.description: Specifies the directory path to scan for subdirectories. It is the starting point for the search operation, determining where the node begins its directory traversal.

outputs.name: subdirectories
outputs.description: Returns a list of paths representing the subdirectories found within the specified directory. This output enables further processing or inspection of these directories.

HaldCLUT.description: The HaldCLUT node applies a color lookup table (CLUT) to an image, optionally performing gamma correction, to achieve various color grading effects. This process allows for the transformation of the image's color palette based on predefined CLUT files, enhancing or altering its aesthetic according to the selected CLUT.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to which the color lookup table will be applied. This image undergoes color transformation based on the selected HaldCLUT file and gamma correction settings.

inputs.name: hald_clut
inputs.description: The name of the HaldCLUT file to be used for color transformation. This selection determines the specific color grading effect to be applied to the input image.

inputs.name: gamma_correction
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether gamma correction should be applied to the input image before color transformation. This can affect the image's brightness and contrast.

outputs.name: i
outputs.description: The output image after applying the selected color lookup table and optional gamma correction. This image reflects the color grading effect determined by the HaldCLUT file.

Image Caption.description: The Image Caption node is designed to add textual captions to images. It processes an image tensor, formats and wraps the provided text to fit the image dimensions, and then overlays the caption onto the image, optionally incorporating additional metadata into the image's PNG info.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image tensor to which the caption will be added. It serves as the visual base for the caption overlay.

inputs.name: font
inputs.description: Specifies the font to be used for the caption text, influencing the aesthetic presentation of the caption.

inputs.name: caption
inputs.description: The text content of the caption to be added to the image, which will be formatted and wrapped to fit within the image's dimensions.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The modified image with the caption overlayed, potentially including additional PNG metadata.

ImageBorder.description: The ImageBorder node is designed to add a decorative or functional border around an image. It supports various border styles, including checkerboard patterns, blurred edges, and solid colors, allowing for a wide range of visual effects to enhance the image's appearance.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to which the border will be applied. This parameter is crucial as it defines the base image that will be modified by adding a border.

inputs.name: border_width
inputs.description: Specifies the width of the border to be added around the image. This parameter directly influences the thickness of the border, affecting the overall visual impact of the border on the image.

inputs.name: border_color
inputs.description: Determines the color or style of the border. It can be a solid color, a checkerboard pattern, or a blurred effect, offering flexibility in the border's appearance.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image with the applied border. This image includes the original content with the added border, enhancing its visual appeal.

ImageOverlay.description: The ImageOverlay node is designed to seamlessly overlay a foreground image onto a background image. It automatically adjusts the foreground image by filling, cropping, or resizing it to match the dimensions of the background image, ensuring a harmonious blend between the two.

inputs.name: background_image
inputs.description: The background image onto which the foreground image will be overlaid. It serves as the base layer in the overlay process.

inputs.name: foreground_image
inputs.description: The foreground image to be overlaid onto the background image. This image is adjusted to match the size of the background image for a seamless overlay.

inputs.name: opacity
inputs.description: Determines the transparency level of the foreground image when overlaid onto the background image. A higher value results in a less transparent foreground, making it more prominent in the final image.

outputs.name: result_img
outputs.description: The resulting image after overlaying the foreground image onto the background image, with adjustments made for size and transparency.

ImagePaste.description: The ImagePaste node is designed to overlay a foreground image with transparency onto a background image, effectively merging them into a single composite image. This process allows for the creation of complex images by combining multiple layers.

inputs.name: background_image
inputs.description: The background image over which the foreground image will be pasted. It serves as the base layer for the composite image.

inputs.name: foreground_image
inputs.description: The foreground image to be pasted over the background image. This image should have transparency areas to blend seamlessly with the background.

inputs.name: x_position
inputs.description: The horizontal position (x-coordinate) where the top-left corner of the foreground image will be placed on the background image.

inputs.name: y_position
inputs.description: The vertical position (y-coordinate) where the top-left corner of the foreground image will be placed on the background image.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The composite image resulting from pasting the foreground image over the background, converted back to a tensor format.

Int to String.description: The IntToString node is designed to convert integer values into their string representation, optionally formatting the output with commas for readability. This node serves as a utility for transforming numerical data into a text format suitable for display or further text-based processing.

inputs.name: int_
inputs.description: The integer value to be converted into a string. This parameter is the primary input for the conversion process.

inputs.name: use_commas
inputs.description: A flag indicating whether to format the output string with commas for thousands, millions, etc., enhancing readability.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The string representation of the input integer, formatted according to the 'use_commas' parameter.

LMStudioPrompt.description: LMStudioPrompt is designed to interface with the LM Studio API, offering a streamlined way to generate prompts by leveraging the capabilities of this specific API. It mirrors the functionality of a similar node but specifically utilizes LM Studio's services for prompt generation, emphasizing its integration with LM Studio's unique features and API structure.

inputs.name: input_prompt
inputs.description: The 'input_prompt' parameter represents the initial prompt or question provided by the user, serving as the basis for generating contextually relevant responses through the LM Studio API.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: The 'mode' parameter determines the operational mode of the LM Studio API, potentially affecting the style or approach of the generated responses.

inputs.name: custom_history
inputs.description: The 'custom_history' parameter allows for the inclusion of a custom interaction history, enhancing the context for the generated response by the LM Studio API.

inputs.name: server_address
inputs.description: The 'server_address' parameter specifies the network address of the LM Studio server, required for API communication.

inputs.name: server_port
inputs.description: The 'server_port' parameter indicates the network port of the LM Studio server, essential for establishing a connection.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: The 'seed' parameter is used to initialize the random number generator within the LM Studio API, ensuring reproducibility of the generated responses.

outputs.name: text
outputs.description: The output 'text' contains the generated prompt from the LM Studio API, encapsulating the result of the prompt generation process.

Load Image Based on Number.description: The node loads an image from a specified directory based on a given index (seed). It is designed to handle large indices by wrapping around the list of image files in the directory, ensuring a valid image is always returned regardless of the seed value.

inputs.name: image_directory
inputs.description: Specifies the directory from which to load the image. It is crucial for locating and accessing the desired images.

inputs.name: seed

It dynamically modifies model and clip parameters based on the LoRA specifications found within the text, enabling customized model behavior and output generation.

Mikey Sampler Tiled Base Only.description: This node specializes in generating tiled samples based solely on base conditions, optimizing for scenarios where a straightforward, tile-based approach is preferred. inputs.name: samples

inputs.name: positive_cond_base

inputs.name: negative_cond_base

inputs.name: vae

Mikey Sampler Tiled.description: The Mikey Sampler Tiled node is designed for generating tiled samples in a structured manner, leveraging advanced sampling techniques to ensure consistency and quality across tiles. It focuses on creating seamless and coherent outputs by efficiently managing the sampling process across different sections of an image or pattern.

inputs.name: base_model

inputs.name: refiner_model
inputs.description: Defines the model used for refining the initial samples. The refiner model enhances the details and coherence of the tiles, ensuring a seamless integration across the tiled output.

inputs.name: samples
inputs.description: Represents the latent representations of the initial samples. These latents are the starting point for the sampling process, serving as the basis for generating and refining the tiles.

inputs.name: positive_cond_base
inputs.description: The positive conditioning applied to the base model. This conditioning guides the base model towards generating samples that align with the desired attributes.

inputs.name: negative_cond_base
inputs.description: The negative conditioning applied to the base model. It steers the base model away from generating samples with undesired attributes, ensuring the quality of the initial tiles.

inputs.name: positive_cond_refiner
inputs.description: The positive conditioning for the refiner model. It influences the refinement process, encouraging the model to enhance the tiles in a way that aligns with the desired outcomes.

inputs.name: negative_cond_refiner
inputs.description: The negative conditioning for the refiner model. It helps in avoiding the enhancement of undesired attributes during the refinement process, maintaining the integrity of the tiles.

outputs.name: tiled_image

outputs.name: upscaled_image
outputs.description: The upscaled version of the tiled image. This output showcases the enhanced resolution and detail achieved through the upscaling process.

Mikey Sampler.description: The Mikey Sampler node is designed for sampling operations within the Mikey framework, focusing on generating or manipulating data samples. It abstracts complex sampling processes, providing a streamlined interface for various sampling techniques.

inputs.name: refiner_model

inputs.name: samples

inputs.name: positive_cond_base

inputs.name: negative_cond_base

inputs.name: positive_cond_refiner

inputs.name: negative_cond_refiner

inputs.name: top

OobaPrompt.description: The OobaPrompt node is designed to facilitate the generation of text prompts by processing and transforming input text according to specific syntax rules. inputs.name: custom_history
inputs.description: The 'custom_history' parameter allows for the inclusion of a custom history file in JSON format, which can be used to influence the generation process by providing additional context or data.

It processes input prompts by stripping existing style syntax, matching them with available styles, and then reformatting them according to the selected style, including handling of special syntax and wildcards. This node aims to provide a versatile tool for generating styled prompts that can be further customized or used directly in various text-based applications.

Prompt With Style.description: The PromptWithStyle node is designed to process textual prompts by applying specific styles, removing or replacing certain syntax, and incorporating user-defined styles. It aims to enhance the expressiveness and specificity of prompts through stylistic modifications and the integration of dynamic elements based on input parameters.

inputs.name: positive_prompt
inputs.description: Represents the positive aspect of the textual content to which styles and modifications will be applied. It is crucial for generating the enhanced positive output prompt.

inputs.name: negative_prompt
inputs.description: Represents the negative aspect of the textual content to which styles and modifications will be applied. It is essential for generating the enhanced negative output prompt.

inputs.name: style
inputs.description: Specifies the style to be applied to both positive and negative prompts. It determines the stylistic adjustments and enhancements made to the prompts.

inputs.name: ratio_selected
inputs.description: Determines the aspect ratio for image generation, influencing the dimensions of the output images.

inputs.name: batch_size
inputs.description: Specifies the number of samples to be processed in a single batch, affecting the node's execution efficiency.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: Influences the randomness involved in processing the prompts, such as in wildcard replacement or random syntax processing. It ensures reproducibility and consistency across different executions.

outputs.name: samples

outputs.name: positive_prompt_text_g

outputs.name: negative_prompt_text_g
outputs.description: The enhanced negative prompt text after processing and applying styles.

outputs.name: positive_style_text_l

outputs.name: negative_style_text_l

outputs.name: width

outputs.name: height

outputs.description: The width dimension for the refined samples.

outputs.name: refiner_height
