Range Float.description: The Range Float node generates a list of floating-point numbers within a specified range using a step value, then selects a specific number based on a seed value. This node is useful for creating sequences of numbers with precision and selecting an element from the sequence in a deterministic manner.

inputs.name: start
inputs.description: Defines the starting point of the range. It is crucial for determining the lower bound of the generated sequence.

inputs.name: end
inputs.description: Specifies the ending point of the range. It sets the upper limit for the sequence of numbers to be generated.

inputs.name: step
inputs.description: Determines the increment between each number in the range. This value affects the density and total count of numbers in the sequence.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: Used as a basis for selecting a specific number from the generated list. It ensures a deterministic selection process.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The floating-point number selected from the generated sequence.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The string representation of the selected floating-point number.

Range Integer.description: The RangeInteger node is designed to generate a list of integers within a specified range, using a step value derived from a seed. It then selects an integer from this list based on an offset calculated from the seed, providing a way to deterministically select a number within a range.

inputs.name: start
inputs.description: Specifies the starting point of the range. It is crucial for defining the lower bound of the generated list of numbers.

inputs.name: end
inputs.description: Defines the end point of the range, setting the upper limit for the list of integers to be generated.

inputs.name: step
inputs.description: Determines the interval between each number in the range. It is derived from the seed value, adding a layer of determinism to the selection process.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: Used as a basis for calculating the step value and the offset for selecting the final number. It introduces a deterministic element to the number selection.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: The integer selected from the generated list based on the seed-derived offset.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: A string representation of the selected integer, providing a textual format of the output.

Ratio Advanced.description: The `Ratio Advanced` node is designed to provide advanced functionalities for managing and selecting image ratios. It encompasses reading, updating, and utilizing predefined and custom ratio presets for image generation tasks, allowing for flexible image dimension specifications based on user input or predefined standards.

inputs.name: preset
inputs.description: Specifies the ratio preset to be used. If 'none' is selected, custom dimensions can be specified, allowing for greater flexibility in image generation.

inputs.name: swap_axis
inputs.description: Determines whether the width and height of the selected ratio should be swapped, enabling orientation changes without altering the ratio itself.

inputs.name: select_latent_ratio
inputs.description: Selects a specific ratio for the latent space dimensions, which can influence the aspect ratio of the generated image.

inputs.name: custom_latent_w
inputs.description: Allows for the specification of a custom width for the latent space, offering precise control over the generated image's dimensions.

inputs.name: custom_latent_h
inputs.description: Allows for the specification of a custom height for the latent space, offering precise control over the generated image's dimensions.

inputs.name: select_cte_ratio
inputs.description: Selects a specific ratio for constant tensor extension (CTE), which can affect the final image dimensions.

inputs.name: cte_w
inputs.description: Specifies a custom width for the constant tensor extension, providing flexibility in adjusting the image dimensions.

inputs.name: cte_h
inputs.description: Specifies a custom height for the constant tensor extension, providing flexibility in adjusting the image dimensions.

inputs.name: cte_mult
inputs.description: Applies a multiplier to the constant tensor extension dimensions, allowing for dynamic scaling of the image size.

inputs.name: cte_res
inputs.description: Specifies a resolution for the constant tensor extension, enabling precise control over the image quality and detail.

inputs.name: cte_fit_size
inputs.description: Adjusts the constant tensor extension dimensions to fit within a specified size, ensuring the generated image meets certain size constraints.

inputs.name: select_target_ratio
inputs.description: Selects a target ratio for the final image, influencing its aspect ratio and overall appearance.

inputs.name: target_w
inputs.description: Specifies a custom width for the target image, allowing for detailed control over its dimensions.

inputs.name: target_h
inputs.description: Specifies a custom height for the target image, allowing for detailed control over its dimensions.

inputs.name: target_mult
inputs.description: Applies a multiplier to the target image dimensions, facilitating dynamic adjustments to its size.

inputs.name: target_res
inputs.description: unknown

inputs.name: target_fit_size
inputs.description: unknown

inputs.name: crop_w
inputs.description: Specifies the width for cropping the image, allowing for precise control over the portion of the image to be used.

inputs.name: crop_h
inputs.description: Specifies the height for cropping the image, allowing for precise control over the portion of the image to be used.

inputs.name: use_preset_seed
inputs.description: Determines whether a preset seed should be used for generating images, ensuring consistency in image generation.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: Specifies the seed value to be used for image generation, allowing for reproducible results.

outputs.name: latent_w
outputs.description: The width of the latent space after processing, reflecting the dimensions used for image generation.

outputs.name: latent_h
outputs.description: The height of the latent space after processing, reflecting the dimensions used for image generation.

outputs.name: cte_w
outputs.description: The width of the constant tensor extension after processing, which can influence the final image dimensions.

outputs.name: cte_h
outputs.description: The height of the constant tensor extension after processing, which can influence the final image dimensions.

outputs.name: target_w
outputs.description: The width of the target image after processing, reflecting the final dimensions of the generated image.

outputs.name: target_h
outputs.description: The height of the target image after processing, reflecting the final dimensions of the generated image.

outputs.name: crop_w
outputs.description: The width used for cropping the image, reflecting the portion of the image that was selected for use.

outputs.name: crop_h
outputs.description: The height used for cropping the image, reflecting the portion of the image that was selected for use.

Resize Image for SDXL.description: The ResizeImageSDXL node is designed for resizing images specifically for the SDXL model, offering options for different upscale methods and cropping techniques to adjust the image dimensions as needed.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The 'image' parameter represents the image to be resized. It plays a crucial role in determining the final output by serving as the base for resizing operations.

inputs.name: upscale_method
inputs.description: The 'upscale_method' parameter allows the selection of a method for upscaling the image, affecting the quality and characteristics of the resized image.

inputs.name: crop
inputs.description: The 'crop' parameter specifies the cropping technique to be applied before or after resizing, influencing the portion of the image that is retained or discarded.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is a resized image, adjusted according to the specified upscale method and cropping technique.

Save Image If True.description: This node conditionally saves an image to disk based on a specified condition. It leverages a separate saving mechanism to store the image with optional metadata and a filename prefix if the condition is met.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image to potentially save. It is central to the node's operation as it determines what content is subject to conditional saving.

inputs.name: save_condition
inputs.description: A binary condition that dictates whether the image should be saved (1) or not (0). This condition is crucial for the node's selective saving functionality.

inputs.name: filename_prefix
inputs.description: An optional prefix for the saved filename, allowing for organized storage and easy retrieval of saved images.

Save Image With Prompt Data.description: This node is designed to save images along with associated prompt data and additional PNG metadata. It encapsulates the functionality to embed prompt information and other relevant metadata directly into the PNG files, facilitating a seamless integration of image content with descriptive data. The node aims to enhance the utility and interpretability of saved images by embedding contextual information, making it easier for users to understand and manage their image collections.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The 'images' parameter represents the collection of images to be saved. It is crucial for specifying the visual content that will be embedded with prompt data and additional metadata, serving as the primary input for the node's operation.

inputs.name: positive_prompt
inputs.description: The 'positive_prompt' parameter enables the inclusion of positive prompt information as part of the image's metadata, offering insights into the desired attributes or themes of the images.

inputs.name: negative_prompt
inputs.description: The 'negative_prompt' parameter allows for the inclusion of negative prompt information, specifying undesired attributes or themes to avoid in the images, enriching the contextual data.

inputs.name: filename_prefix
inputs.description: The 'filename_prefix' parameter allows users to specify a prefix for the filenames of the saved images. This aids in organizing and identifying images within a collection, providing a customizable naming convention that reflects the content or context of the images.

inputs.name: parameters
inputs.description: The 'parameters' parameter permits the inclusion of additional parameters as part of the image's metadata, further customizing the metadata content and enhancing the descriptive data of the images.

Save Images Mikey.description: This node is designed to facilitate the saving of images to disk, incorporating additional functionalities such as prefixing filenames and appending extra information to PNG files. It abstracts the complexities involved in file handling and metadata management, aiming to streamline the process of persisting images with contextual data.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The collection of images to be saved. This parameter is central to the node's operation, determining the primary content that will be persisted to disk.

inputs.name: sub_directory
inputs.description: Specifies the sub-directory within the output folder where the images will be saved, aiding in the organization of saved files.

inputs.name: filename_text_i
inputs.description: The part of the dynamic filename construction, contributing to a customizable naming scheme. This parameter allows for multiple filename texts to be specified, enhancing the flexibility in naming saved images.

inputs.name: filename_separator
inputs.description: A separator character or string used between different parts of the filename to ensure readability and structure.

inputs.name: timestamp
inputs.description: Indicates whether a timestamp should be included in the filename, providing a time-based identifier for the saved image.

inputs.name: counter_type
inputs.description: Defines the type of counter to be used in the filename, aiding in the creation of unique filenames for each saved image.

inputs.name: filename_text_i_pos
inputs.description: unknown

inputs.name: timestamp_pos
inputs.description: The position in the filename where the timestamp should be inserted, if applicable, to incorporate time-based identifiers.

inputs.name: timestamp_type
inputs.description: Specifies the format of the timestamp to be included in the filename, ensuring consistency in time-based identifiers.

inputs.name: counter_pos
inputs.description: The position in the filename where the counter should be inserted, facilitating the generation of unique filenames.

inputs.name: extra_metadata
inputs.description: Additional metadata that can be included with the image, enhancing the documentation and traceability of the saved file.

Save Images No Display.description: This node is designed to save images without displaying them in the UI, extending the functionality of its parent class to focus on backend image processing and storage.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The images to be saved; central to the node's operation as it determines the content to be stored.

inputs.name: sub_directory
inputs.description: Specifies the sub-directory path where images will be saved, influencing the organization of saved images.

inputs.name: filename_text_i
inputs.description: Part of the filename composition, contributing to a customizable naming convention for saved images. This represents a series of filename components (filename_text_1, filename_text_2, filename_text_3) allowing for extensive customization.

inputs.name: filename_separator
inputs.description: Defines the separator used between filename components, affecting the readability and structure of filenames.

inputs.name: timestamp
inputs.description: Timestamp information to be included in the filename, providing temporal context to the saved images.

inputs.name: counter_type
inputs.description: Determines the type of counter used in the filename, aiding in the unique identification of each saved image.

inputs.name: filename_text_i_pos
inputs.description: Positional information for the text components in the filename, influencing the naming order. This represents a series of positions (filename_text_1_pos, filename_text_2_pos, filename_text_3_pos) for each text component.

inputs.name: timestamp_pos
inputs.description: Specifies the position of the timestamp in the filename, affecting the overall naming convention.

inputs.name: timestamp_type
inputs.description: Indicates the format of the timestamp used in the filename, providing clarity on the temporal information's presentation.

inputs.name: counter_pos
inputs.description: Positional information for the counter in the filename, contributing to the unique identification of each image.

inputs.name: extra_metadata
inputs.description: Allows for the inclusion of extra metadata in the saved images, enriching the information associated with each file.

SaveMetaData.description: The SaveMetaData node is designed to save metadata information to a text file. It processes image metadata and additional information, such as prompts and extra PNG info, to generate a comprehensive metadata file that encapsulates various details about the image and its associated data.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image whose metadata is to be saved. This parameter is crucial as it determines the context and content of the metadata to be saved.

inputs.name: filename_prefix
inputs.description: A prefix for the filename under which the metadata will be saved. This allows for customizable naming conventions for the metadata files.

inputs.name: timestamp_prefix
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether to prepend a timestamp to the filename, aiding in organizing and sorting the metadata files.

inputs.name: counter
inputs.description: A boolean flag that determines whether a counter should be appended to the filename, useful for versioning or tracking multiple metadata files for the same image.

SD3TextConditioningWithOptionsOnePrompt.description: The SD3TextConditioningWithOptionsOnePrompt node is designed to enhance text prompts for image generation by applying style-based modifications and conditioning. It leverages specific styles to modify positive and negative prompts, integrates seed-based variations for style selection, and utilizes advanced text encoding techniques to refine the conditioning process for improved image generation outcomes.

inputs.name: positive_prompt
inputs.description: Represents the base positive prompt that will be modified according to the selected style and further processed to enhance its effectiveness in guiding the image generation process.

inputs.name: negative_prompt
inputs.description: Serves as the base negative prompt that undergoes style-based modifications and processing to refine its role in the image generation process.

inputs.name: clip
inputs.description: Specifies the CLIP model to be used for encoding the prompts, playing a crucial role in the conditioning process.

inputs.name: option_positive_clip_l
inputs.description: Option to apply specific CLIP model settings for the positive prompt's local features.

inputs.name: option_positive_clip_g
inputs.description: Option to apply specific CLIP model settings for the positive prompt's global features.

inputs.name: option_positive_t5xxl
inputs.description: Option to apply specific T5-XXL model settings for the positive prompt.

inputs.name: option_negative_clip_l
inputs.description: Option to apply specific CLIP model settings for the negative prompt's local features.

inputs.name: option_negative_clip_g
inputs.description: Option to apply specific CLIP model settings for the negative prompt's global features.

inputs.name: option_negative_t5xxl
inputs.description: Option to apply specific T5-XXL model settings for the negative prompt.

inputs.name: padding_character
inputs.description: Defines the character used for padding in the text encoding process, affecting the alignment and spacing within the encoded prompts.

outputs.name: positive_conditioning
outputs.description: The modified positive prompt, enhanced with style-based modifications and advanced encoding techniques for improved image generation.

outputs.name: negative_conditioning
outputs.description: The enhanced negative prompt, similarly modified with style-based adjustments and encoding to refine the image generation process.

SearchAndReplace.description: The SearchAndReplace node is designed to modify input text by searching for specific patterns and replacing them with new content, potentially utilizing additional information from JSON inputs to guide the replacement process. This node is part of a utility collection aimed at text manipulation, allowing for dynamic and context-sensitive alterations of text based on predefined rules or mappings.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The primary text input where search and replacement operations will be performed. It serves as the main content to be manipulated.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: A numerical input used to influence the randomness of certain operations within the node, ensuring reproducibility of results.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The modified text after search and replace operations have been applied.

Seed String.description: The Seed String node is designed to convert a numerical seed value into its string representation. This transformation facilitates the use of the seed in contexts where a string format is required, enhancing compatibility and ease of integration with various systems or processes.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: The seed parameter is a numerical value that serves as the input for conversion into a string. This seed is crucial for ensuring consistent results across different executions or for seeding random number generators in a predictable manner.

outputs.name: seed
outputs.description: The original numerical seed value, unchanged and passed through from the input.

outputs.name: seed_string
outputs.description: The string representation of the input seed, enabling its use in string-based contexts or systems.

SRFloatPromptInput.description: The SRFloatPromptInput node is designed for integrating floating-point values into a structured prompt system. It specifically handles the addition of floating-point input values to a prompt's metadata, facilitating dynamic content generation based on numerical input.

inputs.name: input_float
inputs.description: The primary floating-point value to be added to the prompt's metadata. It plays a crucial role in customizing the prompt content based on numerical input.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The same floating-point value that was input, indicating successful integration into the prompt.

SRIntPromptInput.description: The SRIntPromptInput node is designed to integrate an integer input into a structured prompt, enhancing it with specific numerical data. This node plays a crucial role in customizing prompts with integer values, thereby enabling more precise and context-aware generation processes.

inputs.name: input_int
inputs.description: The primary integer input required for the operation. It directly influences the customization of the prompt by adding a numerical value.

outputs.name: output_int
outputs.description: The integer input after being processed and integrated into the prompt, reflecting the customization applied.

SRStringPromptInput.description: The SRStringPromptInput node is designed to integrate string inputs into a prompt's structure, specifically targeting the enhancement of semantic resolution within the prompt. It focuses on accepting a string input and embedding it into a given prompt's context, thereby enriching the prompt's descriptive capacity and specificity.

inputs.name: input_str
inputs.description: The primary string input that is to be integrated into the prompt. This input is crucial for tailoring the prompt's content to specific requirements or contexts, thereby enhancing its relevance and effectiveness.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The modified prompt structure, now containing the integrated string input. This output reflects the enhanced descriptive capacity of the prompt, achieved through the incorporation of the specified string.

Style Conditioner Base Only.description: This node is designed to conditionally apply styling to a base input without the additional refinement layer, focusing on modifying the base attributes according to a specified style and strength. It abstracts the complexity of style application, ensuring that the base input is enhanced or altered in a manner consistent with the desired aesthetic or thematic direction.

inputs.name: style
inputs.description: Specifies the style to be applied. This affects the overall aesthetic or thematic direction of the base input.

inputs.name: strength
inputs.description: Determines the intensity of the style application, influencing how significantly the base input is altered.

inputs.name: positive_cond_base
inputs.description: The base positive conditioning to which the style will be applied, serving as the initial state before styling.

inputs.name: negative_cond_base
inputs.description: The base negative conditioning to which the style will be applied, complementing the positive conditioning in defining the initial styling state.

inputs.name: base_clip
inputs.description: The CLIP model used for encoding the style prompts, integral to the process of applying the specified style.

inputs.name: use_seed
inputs.description: Indicates whether a seed should be used to deterministically select a style from a predefined set, ensuring reproducibility.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: The seed value used for deterministic style selection when 'use_seed' is true, affecting the style choice.

outputs.name: base_pos_cond
outputs.description: The modified positive base conditioning after the style has been applied, reflecting the desired aesthetic changes.

outputs.name: base_neg_cond
outputs.description: The modified negative base conditioning after the style has been applied, complementing the positive conditioning in the styled output.

outputs.name: style_str
outputs.description: The style that was applied, providing a reference to the aesthetic or thematic direction chosen.

Style Conditioner.description: The StyleConditioner node is designed to apply specific stylistic adjustments to conditioning bases and refiners, leveraging a combination of predefined and dynamically generated style prompts. It utilizes seed-based selection for styles and performs encoding and averaging operations to blend the selected style with the existing conditioning, enabling nuanced control over the stylistic output.

inputs.name: style
inputs.description: Specifies the style to be applied. This can dynamically change the appearance or thematic elements of the output by adjusting the conditioning bases and refiners according to the selected style.

inputs.name: strength
inputs.description: Determines the intensity of the style application, affecting how strongly the selected style influences the conditioning bases and refiners.

inputs.name: positive_cond_base
inputs.description: The initial positive conditioning base to which the style adjustments will be applied.

inputs.name: negative_cond_base
inputs.description: The initial negative conditioning base to which the style adjustments will be applied.

inputs.name: positive_cond_refiner
inputs.description: The initial positive conditioning refiner to which the style adjustments will be applied.

inputs.name: negative_cond_refiner
inputs.description: The initial negative conditioning refiner to which the style adjustments will be applied.

inputs.name: base_clip
inputs.description: The CLIP model used for encoding the base conditioning.

inputs.name: refiner_clip
inputs.description: The CLIP model used for encoding the refiner conditioning.

inputs.name: use_seed
inputs.description: Indicates whether a seed should be used for selecting the style, enabling deterministic style selection.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: The seed value used for deterministic style selection when 'use_seed' is true.

outputs.name: base_pos_cond
outputs.description: Returns the updated positive conditioning base after style adjustments.

outputs.name: base_neg_cond
outputs.description: Returns the updated negative conditioning base after style adjustments.

outputs.name: refiner_pos_cond
outputs.description: Returns the updated positive conditioning refiner after style adjustments.

outputs.name: refiner_neg_cond
outputs.description: Returns the updated negative conditioning refiner after style adjustments.

outputs.name: style_str
outputs.description: Returns the string representation of the applied style.

Text2InputOr3rdOption.description: This node processes three input texts and, based on a condition, outputs either two of the original texts or duplicates one across both outputs. It allows for dynamic text manipulation and conditional output generation.

inputs.name: text_a
inputs.description: The first text input to be potentially modified and outputted. It serves as one of the primary inputs for conditional processing.

inputs.name: text_b
inputs.description: The second text input that may be modified and outputted, acting as another primary input for the node's conditional logic.

inputs.name: text_c
inputs.description: The third text input, which can replace the other two inputs based on the condition specified by 'use_text_c_for_both'.

inputs.name: use_text_c_for_both
inputs.description: A boolean flag determining whether 'text_c' should be used as the output for both 'text_a' and 'text_b', enabling conditional output behavior.

outputs.name: text_a
outputs.description: The modified version of 'text_a', or 'text_c' if the condition is met.

outputs.name: text_b
outputs.description: The modified version of 'text_b', or 'text_c' if the condition is met.

TextCombinations.description: The TextCombinations node is designed to generate a variety of text combinations based on predefined text inputs and operations. It allows for the dynamic mixing and matching of text elements to create new, composite strings according to specified operations, making it a versatile tool for text manipulation and generation.

inputs.name: text1
inputs.description: The first text input that can be dynamically combined with other text inputs according to the specified operation.

inputs.name: text2
inputs.description: The second text input that can be combined with the first text input and potentially others, depending on the operation defined.

inputs.name: operation
inputs.description: Defines the specific combination operation to be applied to the text inputs, determining how they are mixed and matched to generate the output.

inputs.name: delimiter
inputs.description: A string used to separate text elements in the output, allowing for customization of the output format.

inputs.name: use_seed
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether a seed should be used to generate deterministic combinations.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: An integer seed value used to ensure deterministic output when combining text inputs, if 'use_seed' is true.

outputs.name: output1
outputs.description: The first resulting string after applying the specified combination operation to the input texts.

outputs.name: output2
outputs.description: The second resulting string after applying the specified combination operation to the input texts.

TextCombinations3.description: This node is designed to generate a variety of text combinations based on predefined text inputs and operations. It allows for the dynamic creation of text outputs by applying specified operations to the input texts, potentially incorporating randomness through a seed value.

inputs.name: text1
inputs.description: The first text input for combination. It serves as a foundational element for generating text outputs.

inputs.name: text2
inputs.description: The second text input for combination. It complements text1 in generating diverse text outputs.

inputs.name: text3
inputs.description: The third text input for combination. It adds an additional layer of complexity and variation to the text outputs.

inputs.name: operation
inputs.description: Specifies the operation to be applied to the input texts, determining how they are combined into the final output.

inputs.name: delimiter
inputs.description: The delimiter used to separate text components in the final output.

inputs.name: use_seed
inputs.description: Determines whether a seed value is used to introduce randomness into the operation selection process.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: The seed value used for randomizing the operation selection, if enabled.

outputs.name: output1
outputs.description: The first generated text output based on the specified operation and inputs.

outputs.name: output2
outputs.description: The second generated text output, providing an additional variant based on the operation and inputs.

outputs.name: output3
outputs.description: The third generated text output, further expanding the range of possible combinations.

TextConcat.description: The TextConcat node is designed to merge multiple text inputs into a single string, offering the flexibility to specify a delimiter for the concatenation. This functionality is particularly useful for combining pieces of text in a customizable manner.

inputs.name: delimiter
inputs.description: Specifies the character or string used to separate the concatenated texts. Its presence allows for customizable spacing or formatting between the merged text inputs.

inputs.name: text1
inputs.description: Represents the first optional text input to be concatenated. If provided, it contributes to the final merged string.

inputs.name: text2
inputs.description: Represents the second optional text input to be concatenated. If provided, it contributes to the final merged string.

inputs.name: text3
inputs.description: Represents the third optional text input to be concatenated. If provided, it contributes to the final merged string.

inputs.name: text4
inputs.description: Represents the fourth optional text input to be concatenated. If provided, it contributes to the final merged string.

inputs.name: text5
inputs.description: Represents the fifth optional text input to be concatenated. If provided, it contributes to the final merged string.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The output is a single string that results from the concatenation of the provided text inputs, separated by the specified delimiter.

TextPadderMikey.description: The TextPadderMikey node is designed to adjust the length of a given text to a specified target length using either padding or repeating techniques. It allows for customization of the padding character, offering flexibility in text formatting for various applications.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The input text to be padded or repeated to reach the desired length. This parameter is central to the node's operation, determining the base content that will be manipulated.

inputs.name: length
inputs.description: Specifies the target length for the output text. This parameter directly influences the amount of padding or repetition applied to the input text.

inputs.name: technique
inputs.description: Determines the method used to extend the text to the desired length, either by padding with a character or repeating the text.

inputs.name: padding_character
inputs.description: The character used for padding when the 'pad' technique is selected. This allows for customization of the padding process.

outputs.name: padded_text
outputs.description: The resulting text after applying the specified padding or repeating technique to reach the desired length.

TextPreserve.description: The TextPreserve node is designed to manipulate and transform text inputs based on specific patterns and random choices, while preserving the original text for further use. It incorporates functionalities such as search and replace, wildcard text selection, and updating workflow states with modified text values.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The original text input that will be preserved and potentially modified through various text manipulation processes.

inputs.name: result_text
inputs.description: A modified version of the original text after applying search and replace operations and wildcard selections.

outputs.name: text
outputs.description: The final text output after all manipulations, including search and replace operations and wildcard text selections, have been applied.

Upscale Tile Calculator.description: This node is designed to calculate the dimensions of a tile based on the resolution specified, providing a way to adjust image tiles to a desired resolution. It abstracts the complexity of determining optimal tile dimensions for image processing tasks, facilitating the manipulation and analysis of image data.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image parameter represents the input image for which the tile dimensions are to be calculated. It plays a crucial role in determining the final tile width and height based on the specified tile resolution.

inputs.name: tile_resolution
inputs.description: The tile_resolution parameter specifies the desired resolution for the tile. It directly influences the calculation of the tile's width and height, ensuring that the output tile dimensions align with the specified resolution.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image, unchanged from the input.

outputs.name: tile_width
outputs.description: The calculated width of the tile based on the specified tile resolution.

outputs.name: tile_height
outputs.description: The calculated height of the tile based on the specified tile resolution.

Wildcard Processor.description: The Wildcard Processor node is designed to enhance text inputs by dynamically substituting placeholders with specified or random values. It leverages wildcard and random syntax processing to generate varied outputs based on the given seed, making it ideal for applications requiring text variation and customization.

inputs.name: prompt
inputs.description: The primary text input containing placeholders for dynamic substitution. It serves as the base for wildcard and random syntax processing, directly influencing the generated output.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: A numerical value used to initialize the random number generator, ensuring the reproducibility of text variations. It plays a crucial role in the deterministic transformation of the input text.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The processed text with wildcards and optional elements dynamically replaced, ready for further use or display.

WildcardAndLoraSyntaxProcessor.description: The WildcardAndLoraSyntaxProcessor node is designed to process text inputs by identifying and handling both wildcard and Lora syntax patterns. This dual functionality allows for the dynamic modification of text based on predefined patterns and the integration of Lora model adjustments directly within text inputs, facilitating a more flexible and powerful text manipulation and model interaction capability.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The 'model' parameter represents the model that may be adjusted based on Lora syntax within the input text, allowing for dynamic model manipulation.

inputs.name: clip
inputs.description: The 'clip' parameter represents the clip model that may be adjusted alongside the main model in response to Lora syntax within the input text, facilitating coordinated model adjustments.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The 'text' parameter is the primary input text that the node processes. It is crucial for the operation as it contains the wildcard and Lora syntax patterns that need to be identified and handled. The processing of this text enables the dynamic modification and model interaction based on the specified patterns.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: The 'seed' parameter is used to introduce a deterministic element in the processing of wildcard patterns, ensuring reproducibility of results across different runs with the same input.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The 'model' output is the potentially modified model after processing Lora syntax adjustments specified in the input text.

outputs.name: clip
outputs.description: The 'clip' output is the potentially modified clip model after processing Lora syntax adjustments specified in the input text.

outputs.name: text
outputs.description: The output 'text' is the modified version of the input text after the wildcard and Lora syntax patterns have been processed. This includes the application of dynamic modifications and model adjustments specified within the input text.

outputs.name: unprocessed_text
outputs.description: The 'unprocessed_text' output provides the original input text before any processing of wildcard or Lora syntax patterns, preserving the initial state for reference or further use.

WildcardOobaPrompt.description: The WildcardOobaPrompt node is designed to process input prompts by interpreting and replacing wildcard syntax and handling specific syntax for interacting with large language models (LLMs) through the OobaPrompt class. It aims to enhance the flexibility and expressiveness of prompts by allowing dynamic content insertion and custom processing for LLM requests.

inputs.name: input_prompt
inputs.description: The 'input_prompt' parameter is the initial input text that may contain wildcard syntax for dynamic content insertion and specific markers for LLM syntax processing. It plays a crucial role in determining the final output by guiding the node on how to transform the input prompt.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: The 'seed' parameter is used to initialize the random number generator, ensuring reproducibility in selections made during the wildcard and random word selection processes. It affects the node's execution by influencing the randomness of content insertion.

outputs.name: text
outputs.description: The output is a transformed version of the input prompt, with wildcard syntax and LLM markers processed and replaced according to the provided rules and parameters.

AutoNegativePrompt.description: The AutoNegativePrompt node is designed to automatically generate a negative prompt based on a given positive prompt and various parameters. It utilizes dynamic logic to adjust the negativity of the prompt, potentially enhancing it based on the input parameters and the specified base model. This functionality is aimed at creating prompts that can be used to guide or restrict generative models in producing content by specifying what should be avoided.

inputs.name: postive_prompt
inputs.description: unknown

inputs.name: base_negative
inputs.description: The base negative prompt to be enhanced or modified based on the other parameters. Acts as a foundational negative context.

inputs.name: enhancenegative
inputs.description: A boolean flag that, when enabled, enhances the base negative prompt by incorporating additional negative elements.

inputs.name: insanitylevel
inputs.description: Determines the level of randomness or 'insanity' in the generated negative prompt, affecting its variability and unpredictability.

inputs.name: base_model
inputs.description: Specifies the base model to influence the style and approach of the negative prompt generation, with options like 'SD1.5', 'SDXL', and 'Stable Cascade'.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: A seed value for random number generation, ensuring reproducibility of the generated negative prompt.

outputs.name: negative_prompt
outputs.description: The dynamically generated negative prompt, crafted based on the input positive prompt and other parameters.

CreatePromptVariant.description: The CreatePromptVariant node is designed to generate variations of a given text prompt, incorporating a level of randomness or 'insanity' to modify the original prompt in creative ways. It allows for the customization of the generated prompt based on specified parameters, such as the degree of variation and a seed for reproducibility.

inputs.name: prompt_input
inputs.description: The primary text input for which the variant is to be created. This serves as the base content that will be modified according to the other parameters.

inputs.name: insanitylevel
inputs.description: Determines the degree of variation from the original prompt. A higher value indicates a greater level of randomness and creativity in the generated prompt.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: A seed value for the random number generator, ensuring that the prompt variation can be reproduced if the same seed is used again.

outputs.name: prompt
outputs.description: The generated variant of the original text prompt, incorporating the specified level of variation.

OneButtonArtify.description: The OneButtonArtify node is designed to transform text prompts into art-inspired versions by incorporating artistic styles and elements. It allows users to specify an artist, the number of artists to influence the output, and the mode of artification, providing a creative and customizable approach to generating art-themed text prompts.

inputs.name: prompt
inputs.description: The main text input that will be transformed into an art-inspired version. It serves as the base content for artification.

inputs.name: artist
inputs.description: Specifies the artist or artistic style to apply to the prompt, allowing for a wide range of artistic influences on the output.

inputs.name: amount_of_artists
inputs.description: Determines how many artists' styles will influence the artified prompt, offering control over the diversity of artistic expression.

inputs.name: artify_mode
inputs.description: Defines the mode of artification, such as standard or other specified modes, influencing how the artistic transformation is applied.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: An optional parameter that sets the seed for random elements in the artification process, ensuring reproducibility of results.

outputs.name: artified_prompt
outputs.description: The result of the artification process, a text prompt transformed by specified artistic styles and elements.

OneButtonFlufferize.description: The OneButtonFlufferize node enhances text prompts by adding 'fluff'—additional words or phrases—to make them more elaborate or detailed. It allows customization of the fluff amount and can reverse the fluff polarity to potentially use antonyms or negative phrases, depending on the configuration.

inputs.name: prompt
inputs.description: The initial text prompt to be fluffed. This is the base content that will be elaborated upon.

inputs.name: amount_of_fluff
inputs.description: Specifies the degree of fluffiness to add to the prompt, which can be dynamic or a fixed range, influencing the verbosity of the output.

inputs.name: reverse_polarity
inputs.description: When enabled, reverses the fluff polarity to use potentially opposite or negative fluff, altering the tone of the prompt.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: A seed for the random number generator to ensure reproducibility of the fluff added to the prompt.

outputs.name: fluffed_prompt
outputs.description: The original prompt enhanced with additional fluff to increase its elaborateness or detail.

OneButtonPreset.description: The OneButtonPreset node is designed to streamline the process of applying predefined settings to generate prompts, incorporating elements like insanity level, subject, artist, and various subject subtypes. It simplifies the customization and generation of prompts by utilizing a set of predefined or user-defined presets.

inputs.name: OneButtonPreset
inputs.description: Specifies the selected preset to apply. This can be a predefined preset or a custom one defined by the user, influencing the overall theme and parameters of the generated prompt.

inputs.name: base_model
inputs.description: Defines the base model to be used for prompt generation, affecting the style and structure of the output.

inputs.name: prompt_enhancer
inputs.description: An optional modifier that applies additional transformations or enhancements to the prompt, further customizing the output.

inputs.name: preset_prefix
inputs.description: A prefix added to the prompt, allowing for further customization and refinement of the generated content.

inputs.name: preset_suffix
inputs.description: A suffix added to the prompt, used to append additional information or styling to the generated content.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: Determines the randomness seed for generating prompts, ensuring reproducibility of results when the same seed is used.

outputs.name: prompt
outputs.description: The generated prompt based on the applied preset, incorporating any specified customizations such as prefix, suffix, and enhancer.

OneButtonPrompt.description: The OneButtonPrompt node streamlines the creation and customization of prompts for image generation, offering a suite of options to tailor the prompt's subject, style, and complexity. It leverages a dynamic prompt building mechanism to generate prompts that can vary widely in theme and detail, accommodating a broad range of creative needs.

inputs.name: insanitylevel
inputs.description: Determines the level of creativity and randomness in the generated prompt, influencing its complexity and uniqueness.

inputs.name: artist
inputs.description: Selects artists to influence the style and aesthetic of the generated image, contributing to the prompt's thematic depth.

inputs.name: imagetype
inputs.description: Defines the type of image to be generated, such as digital art, painting, or concept art, guiding the visual style of the output.

inputs.name: imagemodechance
inputs.description: Controls the likelihood of selecting a special image mode for the prompt, adding an element of randomness to the image style.

inputs.name: subject
inputs.description: Specifies the main subject for the prompt, offering a base around which the prompt is constructed.

inputs.name: custom_subject
inputs.description: Allows for the specification of a custom subject around which the prompt will be built, providing a focused thematic direction.

inputs.name: custom_outfit
inputs.description: Specifies an outfit to be included in the prompt, adding detail to the character description.

inputs.name: prompt_prefix
inputs.description: Specifies a prefix to be added to the beginning of the prompt, allowing for further customization.

inputs.name: prompt_suffix
inputs.description: Specifies a suffix to be added to the end of the prompt, enabling additional tailoring of the prompt's theme.

inputs.name: humanoids_gender
inputs.description: Determines the gender of humanoid subjects in the prompt, allowing for more specific character depiction.

inputs.name: emojis
inputs.description: Enables or disables the inclusion of emojis in the prompt, affecting its tone and readability.

inputs.name: base_model
inputs.description: Chooses the base model for prompt generation, affecting the style and language of the prompt.

inputs.name: prompt_enhancer
inputs.description: Selects a prompt enhancer to modify the prompt's style or theme, offering more nuanced control over the generated output.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: Sets a seed for the random number generator, ensuring reproducibility of prompts when the same inputs are provided.

outputs.name: prompt
outputs.description: The primary generated prompt, ready for use in creative applications.

outputs.name: prompt_g
outputs.description: A variant of the generated prompt, offering an alternative perspective or theme.

outputs.name: prompt_l
outputs.description: Another variant of the generated prompt, providing additional creative options.

OneButtonSuperPrompt.description: The OneButtonSuperPrompt node is designed to generate enhanced prompts by integrating various styles and adjustments based on user-defined parameters such as insanity level and style preference. It aims to produce more creative and tailored prompts for specific needs, leveraging a combination of input parameters to influence the generation process.

inputs.name: prompt
inputs.description: The main text input from which the super prompt will be generated. It serves as the base content that will be enhanced according to the specified style and insanity level.

inputs.name: insanitylevel
inputs.description: Determines the degree of creativity or deviation from the original prompt, with higher values indicating more radical transformations.

inputs.name: superpromptstyle
inputs.description: Specifies the style or approach to be used in enhancing the prompt, allowing for customization of the output based on predefined styles.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: An optional parameter that sets the random seed for generating the prompt, ensuring reproducibility of results.

outputs.name: super_prompt
outputs.description: The enhanced prompt generated by the node, reflecting the applied styles and adjustments.

SavePromptToFile.description: The SavePromptToFile node is designed to save various components of a prompt, including positive and negative aspects, into a text file. It handles the creation of a unique filename based on the prompt content or a provided prefix, ensuring the saved file is easily identifiable and organized within a specified directory.

inputs.name: filename_prefix
inputs.description: An optional prefix for the filename, allowing for custom organization or identification of the file within the output directory.

inputs.name: positive_prompt
inputs.description: The main prompt text to be saved. It serves as the primary content for the file and influences the generation of the filename if no prefix is provided.

inputs.name: negative_prompt
inputs.description: The negative aspects of the prompt to be saved, providing a contrast or alternative perspective to the positive prompt.

inputs.name: prompt_g
inputs.description: An optional granular component of the prompt, saved additionally if provided.

inputs.name: prompt_l
inputs.description: Another optional granular component of the prompt, saved if present to add more context or detail.

PFG.description: The PFG node is designed to enhance the conditioning process in generative models by applying a learned transformation to the input conditioning vectors. It leverages a pre-trained model to compute features from an input image, which are then scaled and combined with the original conditioning vectors to produce modified conditioning vectors that better guide the generation process.

inputs.name: positive
inputs.description: A conditioning vector representing the desired attributes or content in the generated output. It plays a crucial role in guiding the generative model towards producing outputs that align with the specified positive conditions.

inputs.name: negative
inputs.description: A conditioning vector representing undesired attributes or content. It is used to steer the generative model away from generating outputs with these negative conditions.

inputs.name: pfg_scale
inputs.description: A scaling factor for the PFG feature vector, allowing for adjustment of its influence on the conditioning process. This parameter fine-tunes how strongly the PFG-modified features affect the final generated output.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image from which features are extracted using the PFG model. These features are then used to modify the conditioning vectors, enhancing the model's ability to generate desired outputs.

inputs.name: model_name
inputs.description: The name of the pre-trained PFG model to use for feature extraction. This allows for flexibility in choosing different models based on the specific requirements or characteristics of the input image.

outputs.name: conditioning
outputs.description: The modified conditioning vectors, both positive and negative, enhanced with features extracted from the input image to better guide the generative process.

Any Switch (rgthree).description: The Any Switch node is designed to select and output the first non-empty item from a set of optional inputs. It abstracts the complexity of handling various types of inputs by evaluating them to find the first one that is not considered 'empty' or 'none', making it versatile for different data types and scenarios.

inputs.name: any_i
inputs.description: Represents an optional input that can be of any type. The node sequentially evaluates these inputs, starting from the first, and selects the first non-empty one, directly affecting the output. This naming convention applies to all inputs from 'any_01' to 'any_05', indicating their order in the selection process.

outputs.description: Outputs the first non-empty input encountered among the optional inputs. This output is versatile, accommodating any data type provided to the node.

Context (rgthree).description: The Context (rgthree) node serves as the foundational context node, designed to be highly compatible with 1.5 applications and other context nodes. It focuses on converting input context parameters into a structured output that is optimized for most use cases, maintaining both forward and backward compatibility.

inputs.name: base_ctx
inputs.description: The base context to be converted or enhanced. It serves as the starting point for the conversion process, allowing for the integration or modification of additional context parameters.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: Specifies the model to be used in the context, allowing for customization and flexibility in processing.

inputs.name: clip
inputs.description: Defines the CLIP model to be incorporated into the context, enhancing the processing capabilities.

inputs.name: vae
inputs.description: Indicates the VAE model to be included in the context, contributing to the generation process.

inputs.name: positive
inputs.description: A positive conditioning factor to guide the generation towards desired outcomes.

inputs.name: negative
inputs.description: A negative conditioning factor to steer the generation away from undesired outcomes.

inputs.name: latent
inputs.description: Specifies the latent space representation to be used in the context, enabling advanced manipulation.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: Defines the images to be included in the context, allowing for visual data integration.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: Sets the seed for random number generation, ensuring reproducibility of results.

outputs.name: CONTEXT
outputs.description: The structured output context optimized for use in various applications.

outputs.name: MODEL
outputs.description: The model used within the context, reflecting the specified input.

outputs.name: CLIP
outputs.description: The CLIP model incorporated into the context, as specified in the input.

outputs.name: VAE
outputs.description: The VAE model included in the context, as per the input parameters.

outputs.name: POSITIVE
outputs.description: The positive conditioning factor applied in the context, guiding the generation process.

outputs.name: NEGATIVE
outputs.description: The negative conditioning factor used in the context to avoid undesired outcomes.

outputs.name: LATENT
outputs.description: The latent space representation utilized in the context for advanced manipulation.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: The images included in the context, integrating visual data.

outputs.name: SEED
outputs.description: The seed used for random number generation within the context, ensuring consistency.

Context Big (rgthree).description: The Context Big node serves as a comprehensive interface for managing context within a system, offering extensive flexibility by allowing all context fields to be used as both inputs and outputs. It ensures backward compatibility with other context nodes, facilitating seamless integration and interaction across different parts of the system.

inputs.name: base_ctx
inputs.description: Acts as the foundational context upon which additional context parameters can be layered, enabling the aggregation and modification of context data.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: Specifies the model to be used, contributing to the customization of the context based on the model's characteristics.

inputs.name: clip
inputs.description: Defines the CLIP model to be incorporated into the context, allowing for the integration of CLIP's capabilities.

inputs.name: vae
inputs.description: Indicates the VAE model to be included, facilitating the use of VAE features within the context.

inputs.name: positive
inputs.description: Sets positive conditioning for the context, enhancing the context's specificity towards desired outcomes.

inputs.name: negative
inputs.description: Establishes negative conditioning for the context, aiding in the exclusion of undesired elements from the outcomes.

inputs.name: latent
inputs.description: Provides latent vectors to be used, enriching the context with pre-defined latent space representations.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: Includes images in the context, allowing for the incorporation of visual data.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: Determines the seed for random number generation, ensuring reproducibility of results.

inputs.name: steps
inputs.description: Specifies the number of steps for the operation, defining the granularity of the process.

inputs.name: step_refiner
inputs.description: Sets the step refiner value, fine-tuning the operational steps for enhanced control.

inputs.name: cfg
inputs.description: Configures the CFG scale, adjusting the influence of conditioning on the generation process.

inputs.name: ckpt_name
inputs.description: Selects the checkpoint name from available options, customizing the context based on specific model checkpoints.

inputs.name: sampler
inputs.description: Chooses the sampler to be used, tailoring the sampling process to specific requirements.

inputs.name: scheduler
inputs.description: Picks the scheduler for the operation, optimizing the process flow according to the selected scheduling strategy.

inputs.name: clip_width
inputs.description: Sets the width for CLIP processing, adjusting the dimensions for CLIP model inputs.

inputs.name: clip_height
inputs.description: Defines the height for CLIP processing, customizing the size for CLIP model inputs.

inputs.name: text_pos_g
inputs.description: Provides global positive text conditioning, enhancing the context with global positive textual cues.

inputs.name: text_pos_l
inputs.description: Supplies local positive text conditioning, refining the context with local positive textual cues.

inputs.name: text_neg_g
inputs.description: Gives global negative text conditioning, improving the context by excluding global negative textual elements.

inputs.name: text_neg_l
inputs.description: Offers local negative text conditioning, polishing the context by avoiding local negative textual aspects.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: Includes a mask for selective processing, enabling targeted modifications within the context.

inputs.name: control_net
inputs.description: Incorporates a control network, extending the context's capabilities with additional control mechanisms.

outputs.name: CONTEXT
outputs.description: Returns the comprehensive context, encapsulating all specified context fields.

outputs.name: MODEL
outputs.description: Provides the model context, reflecting the specified model settings.

outputs.name: CLIP
outputs.description: Delivers the CLIP model context, indicating the integration of CLIP features.

outputs.name: VAE
outputs.description: Outputs the VAE model context, showcasing the inclusion of VAE characteristics.

outputs.name: POSITIVE
outputs.description: Yields the positive conditioning context, highlighting the desired elements emphasized.

outputs.name: NEGATIVE
outputs.description: Presents the negative conditioning context, detailing the elements to be excluded.

outputs.name: LATENT
outputs.description: Supplies the latent vector context, illustrating the latent space representations used.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: Offers the image context, showing the visual data incorporated.

outputs.name: SEED
outputs.description: Returns the seed value used, ensuring the reproducibility of the context.

outputs.name: STEPS
outputs.description: Provides the number of steps context, defining the process granularity.

outputs.name: STEP_REFINER
outputs.description: Delivers the step refiner context, fine-tuning the operational steps.

outputs.name: CFG
outputs.description: Outputs the CFG scale context, adjusting the conditioning influence.

outputs.name: CKPT_NAME
outputs.description: Presents the checkpoint name context, customizing based on specific model checkpoints.

outputs.name: SAMPLER
outputs.description: Supplies the sampler context, tailoring the sampling process.

outputs.name: SCHEDULER
outputs.description: Offers the scheduler context, optimizing the process flow.

outputs.name: CLIP_WIDTH
outputs.description: Returns the CLIP width context, adjusting the dimensions for inputs.

outputs.name: CLIP_HEIGHT
outputs.description: Provides the CLIP height context, customizing the size for inputs.

outputs.name: TEXT_POS_G
outputs.description: Delivers the global positive text context, enhancing with global positive cues.

outputs.name: TEXT_POS_L
outputs.description: Outputs the local positive text context, refining with local positive cues.

outputs.name: TEXT_NEG_G
outputs.description: Presents the global negative text context, improving by excluding global negative elements.

outputs.name: TEXT_NEG_L
outputs.description: Supplies the local negative text context, polishing by avoiding local negative aspects.

outputs.name: MASK
outputs.description: Offers the mask context, enabling targeted modifications.

outputs.name: CONTROL_NET
outputs.description: Returns the control network context, extending capabilities with additional control.

Context Merge (rgthree).description: The Context Merge node is designed to integrate multiple context inputs into a single, unified context output. It systematically merges the provided contexts, with later contexts having the ability to override the values of earlier ones, facilitating dynamic context management and updates.

inputs.name: ctx_i
inputs.description: unknown

outputs.name: CONTEXT

outputs.name: NEGATIVE

It intelligently combines the inputs, with later contexts overriding earlier ones where overlaps occur, ensuring a seamless integration of context data.

Context Switch (rgthree).description: The Context Switch (rgthree) node is designed to streamline context management by selecting the first non-empty context from a set of provided contexts. This functionality ensures efficient determination of an active context for subsequent operations, facilitating smoother transitions and management within various processing flows.

inputs.name: ctx_i
inputs.description: Serves as a generic placeholder for any of the contexts provided to the node. The node evaluates each context in sequence until it finds the first non-empty one, which is then selected for output. This approach allows for flexible and dynamic context switching based on the availability of content within the contexts.

outputs.name: CONTEXT
outputs.description: The comprehensive context output, encompassing various aspects like model configuration, image processing parameters, and conditioning information, among others, based on the first non-empty context found.

outputs.name: MODEL
outputs.description: Outputs model-related context information.

outputs.name: CLIP
outputs.description: Outputs CLIP model configuration context.

outputs.name: VAE
outputs.description: Outputs VAE model configuration context.

outputs.name: POSITIVE
outputs.description: Outputs positive conditioning context.

outputs.name: NEGATIVE
outputs.description: Outputs negative conditioning context.

outputs.name: LATENT
outputs.description: Outputs latent space configuration context.

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: Outputs image processing context.

outputs.name: SEED

Display Any (rgthree).description: The Display Any node is designed to display any type of data, handling various data formats and types gracefully. It attempts to serialize the input data into a JSON string for display, falling back to a simple string representation if serialization fails, thereby ensuring that any data can be visualized.

inputs.name: source
inputs.description: The 'source' parameter accepts any type of data, making this node highly versatile for displaying diverse data formats. It plays a crucial role in the node's ability to handle and visualize any input data, regardless of its complexity or type.

Display Int (rgthree).description: The Display Int node is designed to showcase integer values within the user interface. It serves as a straightforward mechanism for visually representing integer data, making it easier for users to interpret and understand numerical information.

inputs.name: input
inputs.description: This parameter represents the integer value to be displayed. It is essential for the node's operation as it determines the numerical data that will be visualized in the user interface.

Image Comparer (rgthree).description: This node provides a user interface for comparing two images, allowing for a side-by-side comparison to evaluate differences or similarities.

inputs.name: image_a
inputs.description: The primary image to be compared. It is a required input for the comparison process.

inputs.name: image_b
inputs.description: The secondary image to be compared against the primary image. This input is optional; if not provided, a second image from the 'image_a' batch can be used.

Image Inset Crop (rgthree).description: The Image Inset Crop node allows for the cropping of images based on specified inset values, which can be defined in either pixels or percentages. This functionality enables precise control over the cropping area, allowing users to adjust the visible portion of an image according to their needs.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image to be cropped. This input is essential for defining the source image on which the cropping operation will be performed.

inputs.name: measurement
inputs.description: Specifies the unit of measurement for the inset values (Pixels or Percentage). This determines how the inset values are interpreted and applied to the cropping operation.

inputs.name: left
inputs.description: The inset value from the left edge of the image. This defines how much of the left side of the image will be cropped.

inputs.name: right
inputs.description: The inset value from the right edge of the image. This defines how much of the right side of the image will be cropped.

inputs.name: top
inputs.description: The inset value from the top edge of the image. This defines how much of the top side of the image will be cropped.

inputs.name: bottom
inputs.description: The inset value from the bottom edge of the image. This defines how much of the bottom side of the image will be cropped.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The cropped image, adjusted according to the specified inset values.

KSampler Config (rgthree).description: The KSampler Config node in the rgthree context is designed to configure the sampling process for image generation, particularly focusing on the steps involved, refinement options, and the selection of samplers and schedulers. It abstracts the complexity of configuring various parameters for the sampling process, making it easier for users to customize their image generation pipeline.

inputs.name: steps_total
inputs.description: Specifies the total number of steps for the sampling process, allowing users to control the depth of the generation process.

inputs.name: refiner_step
inputs.description: Determines the step at which refinement should begin, enabling finer control over the image refinement process.

inputs.name: cfg
inputs.description: Controls the conditioning factor, influencing the guidance and quality of the generated images.

inputs.name: sampler_name
inputs.description: Selects the specific sampler to be used in the generation process, offering flexibility in choosing the sampling strategy.

inputs.name: scheduler
inputs.description: Chooses the scheduler for controlling the sampling process, allowing for different pacing and progression strategies.

outputs.name: STEPS
outputs.description: The total number of steps configured for the sampling process.

outputs.name: REFINER_STEP
outputs.description: The configured step at which refinement begins in the sampling process.

outputs.name: CFG
outputs.description: The conditioning factor set for guiding the image generation.

outputs.name: SAMPLER
outputs.description: The name of the sampler selected for the generation process.

outputs.name: SCHEDULER
outputs.description: The scheduler chosen to control the progression of the sampling process.

Lora Loader Stack (rgthree).description: The Lora Loader Stack (rgthree) node is designed to dynamically load multiple LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) modifications into a given model and clip, enhancing or altering their capabilities based on specified LoRA files and their associated strengths. It allows for the sequential application of up to four LoRA modifications, providing a flexible mechanism for model customization.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model parameter represents the neural network model to which LoRA modifications will be applied. It is crucial for defining the base architecture that will be enhanced or altered by the LoRA layers.

inputs.name: clip
inputs.description: The clip parameter signifies the CLIP model that will be adjusted using LoRA modifications. It plays a key role in specifying the target for LoRA enhancements alongside the primary model.

inputs.name: lora_i
inputs.description: Specifies a LoRA file to be applied to the model and clip. The choice of LoRA file directly influences the nature of the modification, allowing for targeted adjustments.

inputs.name: strength_i
inputs.description: Determines the intensity of the LoRA modification's impact on the model and clip, enabling fine-tuned control over the adaptation's effect.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The modified neural network model, now enhanced with up to four LoRA modifications as specified.

outputs.name: clip
outputs.description: The adjusted CLIP model, reflecting the cumulative effects of the applied LoRA modifications.

Power Lora Loader (rgthree).description: The Power Lora Loader node is designed to enhance models and clips by dynamically adding multiple Lora modifications. It offers a flexible interface for integrating Loras into existing structures, thereby extending their capabilities and performance.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The 'model' parameter represents the model to which Loras will be added. It is essential for defining the base structure that will be enhanced with additional features.

inputs.name: clip
inputs.description: The 'clip' parameter signifies the clip to be modified with Loras. It plays a crucial role in specifying the target for enhancements, ensuring the modifications are applied correctly.

outputs.name: MODEL
outputs.description: Returns the modified model with Loras applied, reflecting the enhancements made.

outputs.name: CLIP
outputs.description: Returns the enhanced clip with Loras integrated, showcasing the modifications.

Power Prompt (rgthree).description: The Power Prompt node is designed to process textual prompts, potentially enhancing them with additional context or modifications before further processing. It leverages utilities for handling specific text patterns and integrates with other components for text encoding, aiming to prepare the input for more sophisticated text-to-image or text-to-text applications.

inputs.name: prompt
inputs.description: The primary text input that the node processes. It may undergo various transformations or enhancements based on the node's logic and additional parameters provided.

inputs.name: opt_model
inputs.description: An optional parameter that allows for the selection of a specific model for processing the prompt, potentially influencing the outcome based on the model's characteristics.

inputs.name: opt_clip
inputs.description: An optional parameter that, if provided, allows for the encoding of the prompt alongside this parameter's value using a CLIP model. This can be used to generate a conditioning vector for further processing.

inputs.name: insert_lora
inputs.description: Permits the inclusion of a LORA (Locally Optimized Receptive Attention) adjustment to the prompt, which can modify the processing behavior based on the selected LORA's attributes.

inputs.name: insert_embedding
inputs.description: Allows for the insertion of a pre-defined embedding into the prompt, enhancing its context or specificity for subsequent processing.

inputs.name: insert_saved
inputs.description: Enables the inclusion of a saved prompt from a predefined list, potentially adding more depth or context to the primary prompt.

outputs.name: CONDITIONING
outputs.description: A conditioning vector generated from the prompt and optionally the 'opt_clip' parameter, using a CLIP model. This vector can be used for further processing in text-to-image or other generative tasks.

outputs.name: MODEL
outputs.description: The model selected for processing the prompt, if any, which can influence the final output.

outputs.name: CLIP
outputs.description: The CLIP model used for encoding the prompt, if specified, which can affect the conditioning vector generated.

outputs.name: TEXT
outputs.description: The processed or enhanced prompt, ready for further application or processing.

Power Prompt - Simple (rgthree).description: The Power Prompt - Simple node is designed to simplify the process of generating conditioning and text outputs based on a given prompt. It optionally incorporates CLIP embeddings and allows for the insertion of pre-saved prompts or embeddings, streamlining the creation of customized text inputs for further processing.

inputs.name: prompt
inputs.description: The primary text input for which conditioning and text outputs are generated. It serves as the base content for further modifications or enhancements.

inputs.name: opt_clip
inputs.description: An optional CLIP model input that, if provided, is used to generate a conditioning output based on the prompt, enhancing the relevance or specificity of the generated text.

inputs.name: insert_embedding
inputs.description: Allows for the insertion of a pre-saved embedding by name, enabling the customization of the prompt with specific, pre-defined characteristics.

inputs.name: insert_saved
inputs.description: Permits the inclusion of a pre-saved prompt by filename, facilitating the reuse of previously crafted prompts for new generations.

outputs.name: CONDITIONING
outputs.description: The conditioning output, generated based on the prompt and optionally enhanced by a CLIP model, which can be used for further processing or refinement.

outputs.name: TEXT
outputs.description: The original or modified prompt text, which can be used as input for subsequent operations or models.

SDXL Empty Latent Image (rgthree).description: This node is designed to generate an empty latent image based on specified dimensions and scale it according to a clip scale. It primarily serves as a foundational step in image generation processes, where the creation of an initial, blank latent space is required before further manipulations or additions.

inputs.name: dimensions
inputs.description: Specifies the dimensions of the latent image to be generated, offering a selection of predefined sizes with aspect ratios ranging from landscape to portrait and square. This parameter is crucial for determining the base size of the latent image.

inputs.name: clip_scale
inputs.description: Determines the scaling factor to be applied to the dimensions of the latent image, affecting the final size of the clip area. This parameter plays a significant role in adjusting the resolution of the generated image.

inputs.name: batch_size
inputs.description: Controls the number of latent images to generate in a single batch, allowing for efficient processing of multiple images simultaneously.

outputs.name: LATENT
outputs.description: The generated empty latent image.

outputs.name: CLIP_WIDTH
outputs.description: The width of the clip area after applying the clip scale to the original dimensions.

outputs.name: CLIP_HEIGHT
outputs.description: The height of the clip area after applying the clip scale to the original dimensions.

SDXL Power Prompt - Positive (rgthree).description: This node is designed for positive conditioning in text generation, utilizing advanced techniques such as Lora tags for enhanced customization and control over the generated content. It integrates with CLIPTextEncodeSDXL for semantic understanding and optimization of prompts.

inputs.name: prompt_g
inputs.description: The primary prompt for generation, supporting multiline input. It plays a crucial role in guiding the text generation process towards the desired positive outcome.
