inputs.description: The second audio file to be stitched. It follows the first audio file in the combined audio track.

inputs.name: silent_transition_seconds
inputs.description: The duration of silence to insert between the two audio files, allowing for a customizable pause or transition in the combined audio track.

outputs.name: stitched_audio
outputs.description: The resulting audio file after stitching the two input audio files, optionally separated by a silent transition.

SaltAudioTrebleBoost.description: This node enhances the treble frequencies of an audio file, allowing for a clearer and more pronounced high-end sound. It applies a high-pass filter at a specified cutoff frequency and then boosts the gain of frequencies above this threshold.

inputs.name: audio
inputs.description: The audio input to be processed for treble enhancement. It serves as the primary content for treble frequency boosting.

inputs.name: cutoff_freq
inputs.description: The cutoff frequency for the high-pass filter, determining the lowest frequency to be boosted in the treble enhancement process.

inputs.name: boost_dB
inputs.description: The amount of gain, in decibels, to apply to frequencies above the cutoff frequency, enhancing the treble portion of the audio.

outputs.name: audio
outputs.description: The processed audio with enhanced treble frequencies.

SaltAudioTrim.description: The SaltAudioTrim node is designed for trimming audio files to a specified start and end time, allowing for precise control over the segment of the audio that is of interest.

inputs.name: audio
inputs.description: The 'audio' parameter is the raw audio data that will be trimmed. It is essential for determining the segment of the audio file to be processed.

inputs.name: start_time_seconds
inputs.description: The 'start_time_seconds' parameter specifies the starting point of the audio segment to trim, measured in seconds from the beginning of the audio file. It plays a crucial role in defining the portion of the audio to retain.

inputs.name: end_time_seconds
inputs.description: The 'end_time_seconds' parameter defines the ending point of the audio segment to trim, measured in seconds. It is critical for delineating the end of the segment to be kept.

outputs.name: audio
outputs.description: The output 'audio' is the trimmed segment of the original audio file, processed according to the specified start and end times.

SaltAudioVisualizer.description: Provides a visual representation of audio data, enabling users to visualize the waveform or spectrum of audio clips. This can be particularly useful for analyzing the audio's structure, identifying specific parts, or simply for aesthetic visualization purposes.

inputs.name: audio
inputs.description: The audio data to be visualized. It is crucial for understanding the audio's structure and for generating its visual representation.

inputs.name: frame_rate
inputs.description: Defines the number of frames per second for the visualization, affecting the smoothness and detail of the output.

inputs.name: start_frame
inputs.description: Specifies the starting frame for the visualization, allowing for partial visualization of the audio clip.

inputs.name: end_frame
inputs.description: Determines the ending frame for the visualization, enabling users to focus on a specific segment of the audio clip.

SaltChangeAudioVolume.description: The node is designed to adjust the volume of an audio file. It modifies the volume level of the input audio data based on a specified decibel value, allowing for both amplification and attenuation.

inputs.name: audio
inputs.description: The raw audio data to be processed. This parameter is crucial as it serves as the input audio file whose volume is to be adjusted.

inputs.name: volume_decibals
inputs.description: The amount, in decibels, by which to increase or decrease the volume of the input audio. This parameter directly influences the loudness of the output audio.

outputs.name: audio
outputs.description: The modified audio data with the adjusted volume level.

SaltCLIPTextEncodeSequence.description: The SaltCLIPTextEncodeSequence node is designed for generating a sequence of conditioning data based on textual descriptions over a specified frame count. It leverages CLIP models to encode text into a format suitable for guiding generative models, with additional parameters to control the normalization and interpretation of token weights. This node is particularly useful for applications requiring dynamic content generation over time, such as animations or video content creation.

inputs.name: clip
inputs.description: The CLIP model used for text encoding. It plays a crucial role in converting textual descriptions into a format that can be understood by generative models.

inputs.name: token_normalization
inputs.description: Specifies the method for normalizing tokens, which can affect the encoding process and the resulting conditioning data. Options include none, mean, length, and length+mean, allowing for flexibility in handling token data.

inputs.name: weight_interpretation
inputs.description: Determines how weights are interpreted during the encoding process, with options like comfy, A1111, compel, and comfy++. This parameter influences the generation of conditioning data by adjusting the significance of different tokens.

inputs.name: frame_count
inputs.description: The number of frames for which conditioning data is generated. This parameter sets the length of the sequence, enabling the creation of dynamic content over time.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: Textual descriptions provided as input, which are encoded into conditioning data. Supports multiline input and dynamic prompts, allowing for detailed and varied content generation.

outputs.name: conditioning_sequence
outputs.description: The generated sequence of conditioning data, suitable for guiding generative models over the specified frame count.

outputs.name: frame_count
outputs.description: The number of frames for which conditioning data has been generated, confirming the length of the output sequence.

SaltConditioningSetMaskAndCombine.description: The SaltConditioningSetMaskAndCombine node is designed for advanced conditioning manipulation in audio-visual scheduling tasks. It combines conditioning schedules with masks, allowing for precise control over the application of conditions based on spatial or temporal criteria. This node facilitates the integration and coordination of multiple conditioning layers, enhancing the flexibility and specificity of audio-visual content generation.

inputs.name: positive_schedule_a
inputs.description: Represents the first set of positive conditionings to be scheduled and combined with a mask.

inputs.name: negative_schedule_a
inputs.description: Represents the first set of negative conditionings to be scheduled and combined with a mask.

inputs.name: positive_schedule_b
inputs.description: Represents the second set of positive conditionings to be scheduled and combined with a mask.

inputs.name: negative_schedule_b
inputs.description: Represents the second set of negative conditionings to be scheduled and combined with a mask.

inputs.name: mask_a
inputs.description: The mask to be applied to the first set of conditionings.

inputs.name: mask_b
inputs.description: The mask to be applied to the second set of conditionings.

inputs.name: mask_strengths_a
inputs.description: A list of strengths for each mask applied to the first set of conditionings, allowing for variable influence.

inputs.name: mask_strengths_b
inputs.description: A list of strengths for each mask applied to the second set of conditionings, allowing for variable influence.

inputs.name: set_cond_area
inputs.description: Determines whether the conditioning area is set to default or bounded by the mask.

outputs.name: conditioning
outputs.description: The combined and conditioned output for both sets of schedules, reflecting the applied masks and strengths.

SaltCyclicalSchedule.description: This node is designed to generate a cyclical schedule from a given list of schedule items. It allows for the repetition of a specified segment within the schedule list, optionally incorporating a ping-pong effect for a mirrored repetition pattern. The node aims to facilitate the creation of repetitive, cyclical patterns in scheduling tasks, enhancing flexibility and creativity in schedule design.

inputs.name: schedule_list
inputs.description: The list of schedule items to be processed. This list serves as the basis for generating the cyclical schedule, with specific segments being repeated according to the other parameters.

inputs.name: start_index
inputs.description: The starting index of the segment within the schedule list to be repeated. This determines the beginning of the pattern that will be cyclically replicated.

inputs.name: end_index
inputs.description: The ending index of the segment within the schedule list to be repeated. This marks the end of the pattern that will undergo cyclical replication.

inputs.name: repetitions
inputs.description: The number of times the specified segment is to be repeated in the cyclical schedule. This controls the length and repetition rate of the cyclical pattern.

inputs.name: ping_pong
inputs.description: A boolean flag that, when set to True, causes the repeated segment to be mirrored in a ping-pong fashion, enhancing the cyclical pattern with a reverse repetition.

outputs.name: schedule_list
outputs.description: The resulting cyclical schedule list, composed of the original schedule items arranged according to the specified cyclical pattern.

SaltFilmicTransitions.description: This node specializes in generating filmic transitions between two sets of images, offering a variety of modes such as swipes and circle expansions. It allows for the creation of smooth, visually appealing transitions with customizable frame counts and optional mask blur effects, enhancing the dynamic storytelling capabilities of image sequences.

inputs.name: images_a
inputs.description: The first set of images to transition from. These images serve as the starting point for the filmic transition effect.

inputs.name: images_b
inputs.description: The second set of images to transition to. These images serve as the destination for the filmic transition effect.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Specifies the type of transition effect to apply, such as swipe directions or circle expansions. This choice determines the visual style of the transition between the two image sets.

inputs.name: transition_frames
inputs.description: The number of frames to use for the transition, allowing control over the speed and smoothness of the effect.

inputs.name: mask_blur_schedule
inputs.description: An optional schedule for blurring the mask used in the transition, enabling dynamic blur effects throughout the transition process.

outputs.name: images
outputs.description: The resulting set of images after applying the filmic transition, combined into a single tensor.

SaltFloatScheduler.description: The SaltFloatScheduler node is designed for creating and managing float schedules, which are sequences of floating-point numbers that can be used to control various parameters over time. This node likely offers functionality to define, adjust, and iterate over these float schedules, providing a flexible tool for temporal parameter manipulation in audio-visual projects.

inputs.name: repeat_sequence_times
inputs.description: Specifies the number of times the sequence should be repeated, affecting the overall length and repetition pattern of the float schedule.

inputs.name: curves_mode
inputs.description: Determines the mode of curve application for the float schedule, influencing how the values interpolate or transition between points in the schedule.

inputs.name: use_perlin_tremors
inputs.description: Indicates whether Perlin noise-based tremors should be applied to the float schedule, adding a layer of complexity and variability to the schedule's progression.

inputs.name: tremor_scale
inputs.description: Sets the scale of the Perlin tremors, affecting the granularity and frequency of the noise applied to the float schedule.

inputs.name: tremor_octaves
inputs.description: Defines the number of octaves for the Perlin tremors, influencing the detail and layering of the noise effect on the float schedule.

inputs.name: tremor_persistence
inputs.description: Controls the persistence of the Perlin tremors, determining the amplitude's decay rate across octaves in the float schedule.

inputs.name: tremor_lacunarity
inputs.description: Specifies the lacunarity of the Perlin tremors, affecting the frequency growth per octave in the float schedule.

inputs.name: sequence
inputs.description: The sequence of values to be scheduled, serving as the base for the float schedule before any modifications or enhancements.

inputs.name: max_sequence_length
inputs.description: Limits the maximum length of the float schedule, ensuring that the sequence does not exceed a specified number of elements.

outputs.name: schedule_list
outputs.description: The resulting float schedule after applying the specified parameters and modifications, ready for use in controlling parameters over time.

outputs.name: schedule_length
outputs.description: The length of the generated float schedule, providing information on the total number of elements in the schedule.

SaltImageComposite.description: This node is designed for creating complex image compositions by blending multiple images together according to specified parameters and schedules. It enables the dynamic assembly of visual elements, allowing for the creation of rich, layered imagery that can be adjusted over time or in response to specific triggers.

inputs.name: images_a
inputs.description: Specifies the first set of images to be blended. It plays a crucial role in determining the base layer of the composition.

inputs.name: images_b
inputs.description: Specifies the second set of images to be blended with the first set. This layer is combined with the base layer according to the blending mode and other parameters.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Defines the blending mode to be used for combining the images. The choice of mode affects the visual outcome of the blend, offering various stylistic effects.

inputs.name: masks
inputs.description: Optional masks that can be applied to the images for selective blending, allowing for more controlled and intricate compositions.

inputs.name: blend_schedule
inputs.description: An optional schedule that defines how the blend ratio changes over time, enabling dynamic transitions between images.

outputs.name: images
outputs.description: The resulting images after blending, showcasing the combined visual elements from the input images.

SaltKeyframeMetrics.description: The SaltKeyframeMetrics node is designed to compute and visualize key metrics of a keyframe schedule, such as minimum, maximum, sum, average, absolute sum, and absolute average values, along with the duration of the schedule. It aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the schedule's characteristics through numerical analysis and graphical representation, facilitating the evaluation and adjustment of keyframe-based animations or effects.

inputs.name: schedule_list
inputs.description: The list of keyframe values to be analyzed. It is crucial for determining the metrics and visual representation of the schedule.

inputs.name: start_frame
inputs.description: The starting frame index for the analysis, allowing for partial evaluation of the schedule.

inputs.name: end_frame
inputs.description: The ending frame index for the analysis. If set to -1 or beyond the schedule list length, it defaults to the length of the schedule list.

inputs.name: frame_rate
inputs.description: The frame rate used to calculate the duration of the schedule, enhancing the accuracy of temporal metrics.

outputs.name: value_min
outputs.description: The minimum value among the keyframe values within the specified range.

outputs.name: value_max
outputs.description: The maximum value among the keyframe values within the specified range.

outputs.name: value_sum
outputs.description: The sum of all keyframe values within the specified range.

outputs.name: value_avg
outputs.description: The average of the keyframe values within the specified range.

outputs.name: abs_sum
outputs.description: The sum of the absolute values of the keyframe values within the specified range, providing insight into the overall activity level regardless of direction.

outputs.name: abs_avg
outputs.description: The average of the absolute values of the keyframe values within the specified range, offering a measure of the general intensity.

outputs.name: duration
outputs.description: The total duration of the specified range of keyframes, calculated based on the frame rate.

SaltKeyframeScheduler.description: The SaltKeyframeScheduler node is designed for generating a schedule based on keyframes, applying easing functions to interpolate between these keyframes over time. It allows for the customization of the schedule through various parameters, including the selection of easing modes and the adjustment of frame rates, to create dynamic and smooth transitions in animations or visualizations.

inputs.name: keyframe_schedule
inputs.description: Defines the sequence of keyframes to be scheduled. Each keyframe represents a significant point in the animation or visualization that the schedule aims to reach, serving as the foundation for the generated schedule.

inputs.name: easing_mode
inputs.description: Specifies the easing function to be applied between keyframes, determining the interpolation method and thus affecting the smoothness and dynamics of the transition.

inputs.name: end_frame
inputs.description: The last frame to be considered in the schedule, allowing for the specification of a custom range within the keyframe sequence.

inputs.name: ndigits
inputs.description: Determines the precision of the computed values in the schedule, affecting the granularity of the interpolation.

inputs.name: a
inputs.description: Custom variable 'a' that can be used for additional control over the scheduling, providing flexibility in the scheduling logic.

inputs.name: b
inputs.description: Custom variable 'b', similar to 'a', offers further customization options for the scheduling process, enhancing the node's versatility.

outputs.name: schedule_list
outputs.description: The resulting list of scheduled values, interpolated according to the specified easing mode and other parameters, ready for use in animations or visualizations.

SaltKeyframeSchedulerBFN.description: This node is designed for scheduling keyframes in a customizable manner, allowing for the application of easing modes and the inclusion of optional variables to fine-tune the animation process. It provides a flexible framework for generating animation schedules based on keyframe data, easing specifications, and additional parameters, facilitating the creation of dynamic and nuanced animations.

inputs.name: keyframe_schedule
inputs.description: Specifies the schedule of keyframes to be animated. It is crucial for defining the sequence and timing of the animation, impacting the overall flow and rhythm of the generated animation.

inputs.name: easing_mode
inputs.description: Determines the easing function to be applied to the keyframe animation, influencing the acceleration and deceleration of the animation between keyframes. This choice significantly affects the visual smoothness and dynamics of the animation.

inputs.name: end_frame
inputs.description: Optional parameter that specifies the last frame of the animation, allowing for the animation duration to be limited or extended as needed.

inputs.name: ndigits
inputs.description: Optional parameter that defines the precision of the computed keyframe values, enabling control over the granularity of the animation's timing.

inputs.name: a
inputs.description: An optional variable that can be used to introduce custom behavior or adjustments to the animation schedule, enhancing flexibility.

inputs.name: b
inputs.description: Another optional variable similar to 'a', providing additional capacity for custom modifications to the animation schedule.

inputs.name: c
inputs.description: An optional variable that can be introduced for further customization of the animation schedule.

inputs.name: d
inputs.description: Similar to 'c', this optional variable allows for additional adjustments to the animation schedule.

inputs.name: e
inputs.description: Provides further flexibility in customizing the animation schedule through this optional variable.

inputs.name: f
inputs.description: An optional variable for additional customization options within the animation schedule.

inputs.name: g
inputs.description: Allows for further adjustments and customization of the animation schedule.

inputs.name: h
inputs.description: An optional variable for extending the customization capabilities of the animation schedule.

outputs.name: schedule_list
outputs.description: The generated animation schedule, comprising keyframe timings and values adjusted according to the specified easing mode and optional parameters. This output is essential for implementing the planned animation.

SaltKeyframeVisualizer.description: The SaltKeyframeVisualizer node is designed to visualize the keyframe scheduling process, providing a graphical representation of keyframe values across frames. It calculates various metrics for the keyframes within a specified frame range and generates a visualization image that highlights these metrics, aiding in the analysis and adjustment of keyframe-based animations.

inputs.name: schedule_list
inputs.description: A list of keyframe values to be visualized. It is crucial for understanding the distribution and variation of keyframe values across the specified frame range, impacting the visualization's accuracy and detail.

inputs.name: start_frame
inputs.description: The starting frame number for the visualization. It defines the initial point of the frame range to be visualized, affecting the scope of the keyframe analysis.

inputs.name: end_frame
inputs.description: The ending frame number for the visualization. It marks the boundary of the frame range to be analyzed and visualized, determining the extent of the keyframe metrics calculation.

inputs.name: simulate_stereo
inputs.description: Indicates whether to simulate stereo visualization for the keyframes, adding a dimensional aspect to the analysis by mirroring keyframe values.

inputs.name: frame_rate
inputs.description: The frame rate used to calculate the duration of the keyframe sequence. It influences the time-based metrics and the overall temporal context of the visualization.

inputs.name: schedule_list_a
inputs.description: An alternative list of keyframe values, providing additional context or variations for visualization.

inputs.name: schedule_list_b
inputs.description: Another variation of keyframe values list, offering further insights or comparative analysis in the visualization.

inputs.name: schedule_list_c
inputs.description: A third variation of keyframe values list, allowing for a broader range of comparative visualization and analysis.

SaltKSamplerSequence.description: The SaltKSamplerSequence node is designed for advanced audio visualization and manipulation tasks, leveraging a sequence-based approach to sample, modify, and enhance audio data. It integrates complex scheduling, noise injection, and latent space interpolation techniques to produce high-quality audio outputs tailored to specific conditions or creative objectives.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: Specifies the model used for audio sampling, serving as the core engine driving the node's functionality.

inputs.name: seed_sequence
inputs.description: A sequence of seeds used to initialize the random number generator at different stages of the sampling process, ensuring variability and control over the output.

inputs.name: steps
inputs.description: Defines the number of steps to perform in the sampling process, affecting the granularity and quality of the audio output.

inputs.name: cfg
inputs.description: Controls the conditioning factor, influencing the strength of the conditioning on the generated audio.

inputs.name: sampler_name
inputs.description: Determines the specific sampling algorithm to use, impacting the texture and characteristics of the audio output.

inputs.name: scheduler
inputs.description: Selects the scheduling algorithm for controlling the sampling process, affecting the evolution of the audio over time.

inputs.name: denoise_start
inputs.description: Specifies the starting point of denoise strength, setting the initial condition for noise reduction in the audio.

inputs.name: denoise_sequence
inputs.description: A sequence of denoise values to apply at different stages of the sampling process, allowing for dynamic control over noise reduction.

inputs.name: positive_sequence
inputs.description: A sequence of positive conditioning factors to enhance certain aspects of the audio throughout the sampling process.

inputs.name: negative_sequence
inputs.description: A sequence of negative conditioning factors to suppress certain aspects of the audio throughout the sampling process.

inputs.name: use_latent_interpolation
inputs.description: Indicates whether latent space interpolation is used, enabling transitions between different audio states.

inputs.name: latent_interpolation_mode
inputs.description: Specifies the mode of latent space interpolation, affecting how transitions between audio states are handled.

inputs.name: latent_interp_strength_sequence
inputs.description: A sequence of strengths for latent space interpolation, controlling the intensity of transitions between audio states.

inputs.name: unsample_latents
inputs.description: Determines whether to perform unsampling on the latents, potentially enhancing the quality of the audio output.

inputs.name: inject_noise
inputs.description: Indicates whether noise is injected into the sampling process, adding texture and variability to the audio.

inputs.name: noise_strength_sequence
inputs.description: A sequence of noise strengths to apply at different stages of the sampling process, allowing for dynamic control over the texture of the audio.

inputs.name: latent_image
inputs.description: The latent image to be used or modified during the sampling process, serving as a basis for audio manipulation.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The final latent output, which is the result of the complex sampling and manipulation process, tailored to the specified conditions and creative objectives.

SaltLayerExtractor.description: The SaltLayerExtractor node is designed for extracting specific layer data from a sequence of animation layers based on a given index. It focuses on isolating zoom, x, and y values for a particular layer, facilitating the creation of detailed animation schedules for parallax motion effects.

inputs.name: float_layers
inputs.description: A list of animation layers, where each layer is represented as a sequence of frames with float values for zoom, x, and y positions. This input is crucial for determining the specific layer data to extract.

inputs.name: layer_index
inputs.description: An integer specifying the index of the layer to extract from the list of animation layers. This determines which layer's data is processed and extracted.

outputs.name: zoom_schedule_lsit
outputs.description: unknown

outputs.name: x_schedule_list
outputs.description: A list of x position values extracted from the specified layer, representing the horizontal movement schedule for animation.

outputs.name: y_schedule_list
outputs.description: A list of y position values extracted from the specified layer, representing the vertical movement schedule for animation.

SaltLayerScheduler.description: The SaltLayerScheduler node is designed for scheduling parallax motion effects in audio-visual presentations, enabling dynamic camera movements to enhance the visual storytelling experience.

inputs.name: frame_count
inputs.description: Specifies the total number of frames for the parallax motion effect, determining the duration of the animation.

inputs.name: zoom_speed
inputs.description: Controls the speed of zooming in or out, affecting the dynamic feel of the parallax motion.

inputs.name: pan_speed
inputs.description: Sets the speed of panning, influencing the smoothness and pace of horizontal movement.

inputs.name: pan_directions
inputs.description: Defines the directions for panning, allowing for customization of the motion path.

inputs.name: direction_change_frames
inputs.description: Determines the frames at which the direction of panning changes, enabling complex motion patterns.

inputs.name: tremor_scale
inputs.description: Adjusts the scale of tremor effects, adding a subtle dynamic to the visual presentation.

inputs.name: tremor_octaves
inputs.description: Modifies the complexity of the tremor effect through octaves, enhancing the visual texture.

inputs.name: tremor_persistence
inputs.description: Influences the persistence of tremor effects, affecting their visual impact over time.

inputs.name: tremor_lacunarity
inputs.description: Controls the gap between successive tremor effects, shaping the overall motion aesthetic.

inputs.name: direction_curve
inputs.description: Specifies the easing function for direction changes, smoothing transitions between movements.

inputs.name: start_x
inputs.description: Sets the initial X position for the motion, establishing the starting point of the animation.

inputs.name: start_y
inputs.description: Determines the initial Y position, marking the beginning of the vertical motion.

inputs.name: zoom_mode
inputs.description: Selects the zooming mode, offering various options for zoom dynamics.

inputs.name: layer_offsets
inputs.description: Defines offsets for different layers, creating depth in the parallax effect.

outputs.name: schedule_list
outputs.description: Outputs a list representing the scheduled parallax motion effects, detailing the sequence of camera movements and adjustments.

SaltListClamp.description: The SaltListClamp node is designed to adjust the values in a schedule list so that they fall within a specified minimum and maximum range. This process, known as clamping, ensures that all values in the list adhere to defined boundaries, enhancing the control over the data's range for further processing or visualization.

inputs.name: schedule_list
inputs.description: The list of numerical values to be clamped. It serves as the primary data input for the node, determining the values that will be adjusted to fall within the specified range.

inputs.name: min_value
inputs.description: The minimum allowable value in the clamped list. This parameter sets the lower boundary for the values, ensuring none fall below it.

inputs.name: max_value
inputs.description: The maximum allowable value in the clamped list. This parameter sets the upper boundary for the values, ensuring none exceed it.

outputs.name: schedule_list
outputs.description: The list of clamped values, adjusted to ensure that each element falls within the specified minimum and maximum range.

SaltListLinearInterpolation.description: The SaltListLinearInterpolation node is designed to perform linear interpolation between two lists of schedule values based on a specified interpolation factor. This node is essential for creating smooth transitions between different states or values in a schedule, allowing for the generation of intermediate states that blend elements from both input lists according to the interpolation factor.

inputs.name: schedule_list_a
inputs.description: The first list of schedule values to interpolate from. It serves as the starting point for the interpolation process.

inputs.name: schedule_list_b
inputs.description: The second list of schedule values to interpolate towards. It acts as the target endpoint for the interpolation process.

inputs.name: interpolation_factor
inputs.description: A floating-point value between 0.0 and 1.0 that determines the weight of the interpolation, influencing how much of each input list is reflected in the output.

outputs.name: schedule_list
outputs.description: The resulting list of interpolated schedule values, blending elements from both input lists according to the specified interpolation factor.

SaltListOperation.description: The SaltListOperation node is designed to perform specified numeric operations on schedule lists, enabling dynamic adjustments and manipulations of scheduling data. It abstracts the complexity of numeric list operations, providing a streamlined way to apply transformations like addition, subtraction, multiplication, or division to elements of scheduling lists.

inputs.name: operation
inputs.description: Specifies the type of numeric operation to apply to the elements of the primary and secondary lists. This determines how the lists are combined or modified, impacting the final scheduling outcome.

inputs.name: output_type
inputs.description: Determines the data type of the output list after the operation is applied, allowing for customization of the result's format.

inputs.name: schedule_list_a
inputs.description: The primary list of scheduled numeric values to be operated on. It serves as the base for applying operations in conjunction with another list or a single value, affecting the node's execution and the resulting list.

inputs.name: schedule_list_b
inputs.description: The secondary list of scheduled numeric values or a single numeric value to be used in the operation with the primary list. Its role is to modify or influence the outcome of the operation applied to the primary list, enhancing the flexibility in scheduling adjustments.

inputs.name: expression
inputs.description: A custom mathematical expression used for the 'custom_expression' operation, providing flexibility for complex operations beyond the predefined ones.

outputs.name: schedule_list
outputs.description: The resulting list after applying the specified operation to the input lists. It reflects the adjustments made to the scheduling data, showcasing the effect of the operation.

SaltLoadAudio.description: This node is designed to load audio files from a specified path, making them ready for further processing or analysis within the audio processing pipeline. It serves as the initial step in handling audio data, ensuring that audio files are properly loaded and available for subsequent operations such as editing, analysis, or conversion.

inputs.name: file_path
inputs.description: Specifies the path to the audio file that needs to be loaded. This is crucial for locating and accessing the audio data for processing.

inputs.name: start_seconds
inputs.description: Defines the starting point of the audio file in seconds from which the audio should be loaded. This allows for partial loading of audio files, facilitating operations that require only a segment of the audio.

inputs.name: manual_bpm
inputs.description: Allows for the manual specification of beats per minute (BPM) if known, which can be used for further processing or analysis. This is optional and used primarily when automatic BPM detection is not desired or needs to be overridden.

inputs.name: frame_rate
inputs.description: Sets the frame rate for the audio processing, affecting the temporal resolution of the loaded audio. This is crucial for ensuring compatibility with subsequent processing steps that may require a specific frame rate.

inputs.name: duration_seconds
inputs.description: Specifies the duration in seconds for which the audio should be loaded from the start_seconds point. This allows for loading only a specific portion of the audio file, useful in scenarios where the entire file is not needed.

outputs.name: audio
outputs.description: The loaded audio data, ready for further processing or analysis. This output is essential for any subsequent audio manipulation or analysis tasks.

outputs.name: bpm
outputs.description: The beats per minute (BPM) of the loaded audio, either detected automatically or set manually. This information is crucial for rhythm-based processing and analysis.

outputs.name: frame_rate
outputs.description: The frame rate at which the audio was processed. This information is important for ensuring that subsequent processing steps operate on data with consistent temporal resolution.

outputs.name: frame_count
outputs.description: The total number of frames in the loaded audio segment. This count is essential for operations that involve direct manipulation of audio frames.

SaltOPAC.description: The SaltOPAC node is designed for orchestrating complex scheduling tasks within audio-visual projects, specifically focusing on applying Perlin noise configurations to enhance the dynamic visual effects. It integrates various scheduling parameters such as zoom, angle, and translations along different axes, to create intricate motion and transformation effects in synchronization with audio or other triggers.

inputs.name: use_wiggle
inputs.description: Determines whether wiggle effects, based on Perlin noise, are applied to the visual elements, adding a dynamic, naturalistic motion.

inputs.name: frame_count
inputs.description: Specifies the number of frames for which the scheduling and effects are calculated, defining the duration of the visual sequence.

inputs.name: zoom_range
inputs.description: Defines the range of zoom values to be applied across frames, influencing the scale of visual elements over time.

inputs.name: zoom_tremor_scale
inputs.description: Adjusts the intensity of the zoom tremor effect, allowing for finer control over the zoom dynamics.

inputs.name: angle_range
inputs.description: Sets the range of angles for rotational effects, adding to the complexity of motion.

inputs.name: angle_tremor_scale
inputs.description: Controls the scale of angle tremors, affecting the subtlety or intensity of rotational movements.

inputs.name: trx_range
inputs.description: Determines the horizontal translation range, enabling lateral movement across frames.

inputs.name: trx_tremor_scale
inputs.description: Modifies the scale of horizontal translation tremors, impacting the smoothness or jitteriness of movement.

inputs.name: try_range
inputs.description: Specifies the vertical translation range, allowing for vertical movement adjustments.

inputs.name: try_tremor_scale
inputs.description: Adjusts the intensity of vertical translation tremors, affecting the vertical motion dynamics.

inputs.name: trz_range
inputs.description: Defines the depth translation range, influencing the perception of depth in the visual sequence.

inputs.name: trz_tremor_scale
inputs.description: Controls the scale of depth translation tremors, enhancing the depth dynamics.

inputs.name: rotx_range
inputs.description: Sets the range for rotation around the x-axis, contributing to the 3D rotation effects.

inputs.name: rotx_tremor_scale
inputs.description: Adjusts the intensity of x-axis rotation tremors, affecting the complexity of 3D rotational movements.

inputs.name: roty_range
inputs.description: Determines the range for rotation around the y-axis, adding another layer of 3D rotation.

inputs.name: roty_tremor_scale
inputs.description: Modifies the scale of y-axis rotation tremors, impacting the 3D rotational dynamics.

inputs.name: rotz_range
inputs.description: Specifies the range for rotation around the z-axis, completing the set of 3D rotational dynamics.

inputs.name: rotz_tremor_scale
inputs.description: Controls the intensity of z-axis rotation tremors, enhancing the 3D rotation effects.

inputs.name: opac_perlin_settings
inputs.description: This parameter allows for the customization of Perlin noise settings, which are crucial for generating naturalistic variations in the visual effects. By adjusting these settings, users can significantly influence the visual dynamics of the project.

outputs.name: zoom_schdule_list
outputs.description: unknown

outputs.name: angle_schdule_list
outputs.description: unknown

outputs.name: translation_x_schdule_list
outputs.description: unknown

outputs.name: translation_y_schdule_list
outputs.description: unknown

outputs.name: translation_z_schdule_list
outputs.description: unknown

outputs.name: rotation_3d_x_schdule_list
outputs.description: unknown

outputs.name: rotation_3d_y_schdule_list
outputs.description: unknown

outputs.name: rotation_3d_z_schdule_list
outputs.description: unknown

SaltOPACPerlinSettings.description: This node is designed for configuring Perlin noise parameters specifically for the OPAC visualization node. It allows for the dynamic adjustment of Perlin noise settings to influence visual effects based on audio or other inputs, enhancing the visual representation of data with more natural, organic variations.

inputs.name: zoom_octaves
inputs.description: Specifies the number of octaves for zoom-related Perlin noise, affecting the level of detail in the zoom effect.

inputs.name: zoom_persistence
inputs.description: Determines the persistence of zoom-related Perlin noise, influencing the smoothness of the zoom effect in the visualization.

inputs.name: zoom_lacunarity
inputs.description: Controls the lacunarity of zoom-related Perlin noise, affecting the granularity of the zoom effect.

inputs.name: zoom_repeat
inputs.description: Specifies the repeat interval for zoom-related Perlin noise, defining how often the noise pattern repeats.

inputs.name: angle_octaves
inputs.description: Specifies the number of octaves for angle-related Perlin noise, affecting the level of detail in the angle effect.

inputs.name: angle_persistence
inputs.description: Determines the persistence of angle-related Perlin noise, influencing the smoothness of the angle effect.

inputs.name: angle_lacunarity
inputs.description: Controls the lacunarity of angle-related Perlin noise, affecting the granularity of the angle effect.

inputs.name: angle_repeat
inputs.description: Specifies the repeat interval for angle-related Perlin noise, defining how often the noise pattern repeats.

inputs.name: trx_octaves
inputs.description: Specifies the number of octaves for translation-related Perlin noise along the x-axis, affecting the level of detail in the translation effect.

inputs.name: trx_persistence
inputs.description: Determines the persistence of translation-related Perlin noise along the x-axis, influencing the smoothness of the translation effect.

inputs.name: trx_lacunarity
inputs.description: Controls the lacunarity of translation-related Perlin noise along the x-axis, affecting the granularity of the translation effect.

inputs.name: trx_repeat
inputs.description: Specifies the repeat interval for translation-related Perlin noise along the x-axis, defining how often the noise pattern repeats.

inputs.name: try_octaves
inputs.description: Specifies the number of octaves for translation-related Perlin noise along the y-axis, affecting the level of detail in the translation effect.

inputs.name: try_persistence
inputs.description: Determines the persistence of translation-related Perlin noise along the y-axis, influencing the smoothness of the translation effect.

inputs.name: try_lacunarity
inputs.description: Controls the lacunarity of translation-related Perlin noise along the y-axis, affecting the granularity of the translation effect.

inputs.name: try_repeat
inputs.description: Specifies the repeat interval for translation-related Perlin noise along the y-axis, defining how often the noise pattern repeats.

inputs.name: trz_octaves
inputs.description: Specifies the number of octaves for translation-related Perlin noise along the z-axis, affecting the level of detail in the translation effect.

inputs.name: trz_persistence
inputs.description: Determines the persistence of translation-related Perlin noise along the z-axis, influencing the smoothness of the translation effect.

inputs.name: trz_lacunarity
inputs.description: Controls the lacunarity of translation-related Perlin noise along the z-axis, affecting the granularity of the translation effect.

inputs.name: trz_repeat
inputs.description: Specifies the repeat interval for translation-related Perlin noise along the z-axis, defining how often the noise pattern repeats.

inputs.name: rotx_octaves
inputs.description: Specifies the number of octaves for rotation-related Perlin noise around the x-axis, affecting the level of detail in the rotation effect.

inputs.name: rotx_persistence
inputs.description: Determines the persistence of rotation-related Perlin noise around the x-axis, influencing the smoothness of the rotation effect.

inputs.name: rotx_lacunarity
inputs.description: Controls the lacunarity of rotation-related Perlin noise around the x-axis, affecting the granularity of the rotation effect.

inputs.name: rotx_repeat
inputs.description: Specifies the repeat interval for rotation-related Perlin noise around the x-axis, defining how often the noise pattern repeats.

inputs.name: roty_octaves
inputs.description: Specifies the number of octaves for rotation-related Perlin noise around the y-axis, affecting the level of detail in the rotation effect.

inputs.name: roty_persistence
inputs.description: Determines the persistence of rotation-related Perlin noise around the y-axis, influencing the smoothness of the rotation effect.

inputs.name: roty_lacunarity
inputs.description: Controls the lacunarity of rotation-related Perlin noise around the y-axis, affecting the granularity of the rotation effect.

inputs.name: roty_repeat
inputs.description: Specifies the repeat interval for rotation-related Perlin noise around the y-axis, defining how often the noise pattern repeats.

inputs.name: rotz_octaves
inputs.description: Specifies the number of octaves for rotation-related Perlin noise around the z-axis, affecting the level of detail in the rotation effect.

inputs.name: rotz_persistence
inputs.description: Determines the persistence of rotation-related Perlin noise around the z-axis, influencing the smoothness of the rotation effect.

inputs.name: rotz_lacunarity
inputs.description: Controls the lacunarity of rotation-related Perlin noise around the z-axis, affecting the granularity of the rotation effect.

inputs.name: rotz_repeat
inputs.description: Specifies the repeat interval for rotation-related Perlin noise around the z-axis, defining how often the noise pattern repeats.

outputs.name: opac_perlin_settings
outputs.description: The modified schedule list after applying Perlin noise and optional easing curves, ready for use in OPAC visualization.

SaltParallaxMotion.description: The SaltParallaxMotion node is designed to generate a schedule for parallax motion parameters, enabling dynamic visual effects in audio-visual presentations. It leverages Perlin noise and various movement modes to create complex, organic motion patterns that enhance the depth and immersion of visual content.

inputs.name: zoom_preset
inputs.description: Specifies the zoom behavior for the parallax motion, allowing selection from predefined options or custom settings to tailor the visual zoom effect.

inputs.name: horizontal_pan_preset
inputs.description: Determines the horizontal pan direction and behavior, offering a range of predefined or custom options to control the horizontal movement.

inputs.name: vertical_pan_preset
inputs.description: Defines the vertical pan direction and behavior, with options for predefined or custom settings to manage the vertical movement.

inputs.name: custom_x_min
inputs.description: The minimum custom horizontal position, enabling precise control over the horizontal aspect of the parallax motion.

inputs.name: custom_x_max
inputs.description: The maximum custom horizontal position, allowing for detailed customization of the horizontal movement extent.

inputs.name: custom_y_min
inputs.description: The minimum custom vertical position, facilitating fine-tuned control over the vertical aspect of the parallax motion.

inputs.name: custom_y_max
inputs.description: The maximum custom vertical position, enabling detailed adjustment of the vertical movement range.

inputs.name: custom_z_min
inputs.description: The minimum custom depth position, providing control over the depth aspect of the parallax motion.

inputs.name: custom_z_max
inputs.description: The maximum custom depth position, allowing for precise depth customization in the parallax effect.

inputs.name: parallax_intensity
inputs.description: Determines the intensity of the parallax effect, influencing how much the background moves relative to the foreground to create a sense of depth.

inputs.name: zoom_intensity
inputs.description: Controls the intensity of the zoom effect, adjusting how much the zoom changes between the foreground and background layers to enhance the parallax effect.

outputs.name: front_x_min
outputs.description: The minimum X position for the front layer, part of the calculated parallax motion parameters.

outputs.name: front_x_max
outputs.description: The maximum X position for the front layer, part of the calculated parallax motion parameters.

outputs.name: front_y_min
outputs.description: The minimum Y position for the front layer, part of the calculated parallax motion parameters.

outputs.name: front_y_max
outputs.description: The maximum Y position for the front layer, part of the calculated parallax motion parameters.

outputs.name: front_z_min
outputs.description: The minimum Z position for the front layer, indicating the depth of zoom at the start of the parallax motion.

outputs.name: front_z_max
outputs.description: The maximum Z position for the front layer, indicating the depth of zoom at the end of the parallax motion.

outputs.name: back_x_min
outputs.description: The minimum X position for the back layer, calculated to create a differential motion effect with the front layer.

outputs.name: back_x_max
outputs.description: The maximum X position for the back layer, calculated to create a differential motion effect with the front layer.

outputs.name: back_y_min
outputs.description: The minimum Y position for the back layer, calculated to enhance the depth effect in the parallax motion.

outputs.name: back_y_max
outputs.description: The maximum Y position for the back layer, calculated to enhance the depth effect in the parallax motion.

outputs.name: back_z_min
outputs.description: The minimum Z position for the back layer, kept constant to maintain a consistent background depth throughout the parallax motion.

outputs.name: back_z_max
outputs.description: The maximum Z position for the back layer, kept constant to maintain a consistent background depth throughout the parallax motion.

SaltSaveAudio.description: The SaltSaveAudio node is designed for saving audio content to a file in various formats. It allows specifying the filename prefix and the audio format, supporting a range of common audio file types. This functionality is essential for audio processing workflows that require the output to be stored persistently.

inputs.name: audio
inputs.description: The raw audio data to be saved. This is the primary content that the node operates on, determining the actual audio that will be written to the file.

inputs.name: filename_prefix
inputs.description: A prefix for the filename under which the audio will be saved. This allows for easy identification and organization of saved audio files.

inputs.name: format
inputs.description: The format in which the audio should be saved. This node supports saving in 'wav', 'mp3', and 'flac' formats, affecting the compatibility and quality of the saved audio file.

SaltSchedule2ExecSchedule.description: This node is designed to transform a schedule list into an iterative execution list, facilitating the conversion of a sequence of elements for iterative processing.

inputs.name: list_input
inputs.description: The input list to be converted for iterative execution. It plays a crucial role in determining the structure and content of the output list.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The transformed list, now suitable for iterative execution, maintaining the original list's structure but enabling a different mode of processing.

SaltScheduleConverter.description: The SaltScheduleConverter node is designed to transform schedule lists into formats compatible with various modules by converting list elements into floats or integers. This ensures interoperability with modules that require specific numeric types, facilitating seamless integration and data manipulation within scheduling contexts.

inputs.name: schedule_list
inputs.description: The 'schedule_list' parameter is a list of numeric values representing a schedule. It is essential for the conversion process, as it undergoes transformation into floats or integers, depending on the context, to ensure compatibility with other modules.

outputs.name: floats
outputs.description: A list of floats, representing the original schedule list without modification.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: A duplicate of the 'floats' list, serving as a redundant output for compatibility purposes.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: A list of integers, derived from rounding the values of the original schedule list, to accommodate modules requiring integer inputs.

SaltScheduledBinaryComparison.description: This node performs scheduled binary comparisons on a batch of images, applying a dynamic thresholding technique that can optionally incorporate a margin of error (epsilon) to determine the binary outcome. It is designed to process images in batches, adjusting the comparison threshold per image based on a provided schedule, thereby enabling complex, time-varying binary image transformations.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The batch of images to be processed. This parameter is crucial for defining the input data on which the binary comparison and thresholding operations will be performed.

inputs.name: comparison_schedule
inputs.description: A schedule of comparison threshold values to be applied to each image in the batch. This parameter allows for dynamic adjustment of the thresholding criteria over the batch.

inputs.name: epsilon_schedule
inputs.description: An optional schedule of epsilon values providing a margin of error for the comparison, enabling a more flexible thresholding operation.

inputs.name: use_epsilon
inputs.description: A flag to determine whether the epsilon margin of error should be used in the comparison, offering a toggle between strict and flexible thresholding.

outputs.name: images
outputs.description: The resulting batch of images after applying the scheduled binary comparison and thresholding operations, represented as binary outcomes.

SaltScheduledImageAdjust.description: This node is designed for batch processing of images, allowing for scheduled adjustments to various image attributes such as brightness, contrast, saturation, sharpness, gaussian blur, and edge enhancement. It enables the dynamic modification of these attributes over a sequence of images, facilitating complex visual effects and enhancements in an automated manner.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The collection of images to be adjusted. This parameter is central to the node's operation, as it determines the base content that will be modified according to the specified schedules.

inputs.name: masks
inputs.description: Optional masks that can be applied to the images for selective adjustment. This allows for more precise control over which areas of the images are affected by the scheduled adjustments.

inputs.name: brightness_schedule
inputs.description: A schedule dictating the brightness adjustments over time. This enables dynamic changes to the brightness of the images, enhancing visual storytelling or compensating for lighting variations.

inputs.name: contrast_schedule
inputs.description: A schedule for adjusting the contrast of the images. This can be used to emphasize texture and depth, or to create a specific mood by altering the visual intensity of the images.

inputs.name: saturation_schedule
inputs.description: Defines how the color saturation of the images will change over time. This is useful for creating vivid or muted color effects in a sequence of images.

inputs.name: sharpness_schedule
inputs.description: A schedule for modifying the sharpness of the images, allowing for the enhancement or softening of details within the images.

inputs.name: gaussian_blur_schedule
inputs.description: Determines the intensity of gaussian blur applied to the images over time, useful for creating depth of field effects or focusing attention on specific elements.

inputs.name: edge_enhance_schedule
inputs.description: A schedule for the application of edge enhancement, which can be used to accentuate edges and details within the images.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: unknown

SaltScheduledImageDisplacement.description: This node applies a scheduled displacement to a batch of images based on provided amplitude and angle schedules. It utilizes a displacement layer to modify each image in the batch according to the specified schedules, allowing for dynamic image transformations over time.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The batch of images to be displaced. This input is crucial for determining the base content that will undergo displacement.

inputs.name: displacement_images
inputs.description: Images used to determine the pattern or direction of displacement for each image in the batch.

inputs.name: amplitude_schedule
inputs.description: A schedule dictating the amplitude of displacement over time. If not provided or too short, a default value is used.

inputs.name: angle_schedule
inputs.description: A schedule dictating the angle of displacement over time. If not provided or too short, a default value is used.

outputs.name: images
outputs.description: The batch of images after applying the scheduled displacement transformations.

SaltScheduledPerlinPowerFractalNoise.description: This node is designed to generate complex, visually appealing noise patterns by leveraging the Perlin noise algorithm. It intricately schedules and modifies Perlin noise parameters over time or across frames to produce dynamic, fractal-based noise textures that can be used for a variety of visual effects in audio visualization or graphical applications.

inputs.name: batch_size
inputs.description: Specifies the number of noise patterns to generate in a single batch, allowing for efficient bulk processing of noise textures.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Determines the width of the generated noise texture, defining the horizontal resolution of the output pattern.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Sets the height of the generated noise texture, establishing the vertical resolution of the output pattern.

inputs.name: scale_schedule
inputs.description: A schedule of scale values to apply to the noise generation process, enabling dynamic control over the zoom level of the noise textures across different frames or instances.

inputs.name: octaves_schedule
inputs.description: Controls the level of detail in the noise texture by specifying a schedule for the number of octaves to use, affecting the complexity and richness of the generated patterns.

inputs.name: persistence_schedule
inputs.description: Adjusts the amplitude of each octave in the noise texture according to a predefined schedule, influencing the contrast between high and low-frequency details.

inputs.name: lacunarity_schedule
inputs.description: Defines a schedule for the lacunarity parameter, which affects the gap between successive octaves in the noise texture, thereby influencing its overall roughness and texture.

inputs.name: exponent_schedule
inputs.description: Specifies a schedule for the exponent values applied to the noise, allowing for fine-tuned adjustments to the intensity and distribution of the noise texture.

inputs.name: seed_schedule
inputs.description: A sequence of seed values to initialize the noise generation process, ensuring variability and uniqueness across different noise textures.

inputs.name: clamp_min_schedule
inputs.description: Sets a schedule for the minimum clamping value, defining the lower bound for the noise texture values to ensure they stay within a desired range.

inputs.name: clamp_max_schedule
inputs.description: Determines a schedule for the maximum clamping value, setting the upper limit for the noise texture values to maintain control over the output intensity.

inputs.name: device
inputs.description: Specifies the computing device (CPU or GPU) on which the noise generation process will be executed, affecting performance and efficiency.

outputs.name: images
outputs.description: The generated noise images as a tensor, ready for further processing or visualization in various applications.

outputs.name: batch_size
outputs.description: The number of noise textures generated, corresponding to the input batch size, facilitating batch processing and management.

SaltScheduledShapeTransformation.description: This node is designed for applying scheduled transformations to shapes over a sequence of frames. It enables dynamic adjustments of shape properties such as size, position, and rotation according to predefined schedules, facilitating complex animations and visual effects.

inputs.name: max_frames
inputs.description: Specifies the total number of frames for the shape transformation sequence, dictating the duration of the animation.

inputs.name: image_width
inputs.description: Defines the width of the output image frame.

inputs.name: image_height
inputs.description: Defines the height of the output image frame.

inputs.name: initial_width
inputs.description: Sets the initial width of the shape before transformation begins.

inputs.name: initial_height
inputs.description: Sets the initial height of the shape before transformation begins.

inputs.name: initial_x_coord
inputs.description: Determines the initial x-coordinate position of the shape.

inputs.name: initial_y_coord
inputs.description: Determines the initial y-coordinate position of the shape.

inputs.name: initial_rotation
inputs.description: Sets the initial rotation angle of the shape, in degrees.

inputs.name: shape_mode
inputs.description: Specifies the mode of the shape to be transformed, affecting how the shape is interpreted and manipulated.

inputs.name: shape
inputs.description: Optional. Provides the shape object to be transformed if not using a predefined shape mode.

inputs.name: width_schedule
inputs.description: A schedule list defining the width transformation of the shape across the specified frames.

inputs.name: height_schedule
inputs.description: A schedule list defining the height transformation of the shape across the specified frames.

inputs.name: x_schedule
inputs.description: A schedule list defining the x-coordinate position transformation of the shape across the specified frames.

inputs.name: y_schedule
inputs.description: A schedule list defining the y-coordinate position transformation of the shape across the specified frames.

inputs.name: rotation_schedule
inputs.description: A schedule list defining the rotation angle transformation of the shape across the specified frames.

outputs.name: images
outputs.description: The output images resulting from the applied scheduled shape transformations, showcasing the dynamic changes in shape properties over the sequence of frames.

SaltScheduledVoronoiNoise.description: This node is designed to generate visual noise patterns based on the Voronoi diagram algorithm, with the ability to schedule various parameters over time. It allows for dynamic creation of complex, aesthetically pleasing visual textures that can be customized and animated according to specific schedules for scale, detail, randomness, and more.

inputs.name: batch_size
inputs.description: Specifies the number of noise patterns to generate in one execution. It affects the output's scale and can be used to create multiple instances of noise patterns simultaneously.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Determines the width of the generated noise pattern. It directly influences the spatial resolution of the output texture.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Sets the height of the generated noise pattern, affecting the spatial resolution of the output texture similarly to width.

inputs.name: distance_metric
inputs.description: Chooses the method for calculating distances in the Voronoi diagram, affecting the visual characteristics of the noise pattern.

inputs.name: x_schedule
inputs.description: A schedule for the x-axis positions over time, allowing for dynamic changes in the noise pattern's horizontal distribution.

inputs.name: y_schedule
inputs.description: A schedule for the y-axis positions over time, enabling dynamic alterations in the vertical distribution of the noise pattern.

inputs.name: scale_schedule
inputs.description: Controls the scale of the noise pattern over time, enabling zoom in/out effects.

inputs.name: detail_schedule
inputs.description: Adjusts the level of detail in the noise pattern over time, affecting its complexity and texture.

inputs.name: randomness_schedule
inputs.description: Modifies the randomness factor of the noise pattern over time, influencing its unpredictability and variation.

inputs.name: seed_schedule
inputs.description: Schedules the seed values used for noise generation, allowing for controlled variations in the pattern.

inputs.name: device
inputs.description: Specifies the computing device (CPU/GPU) on which the noise generation is executed, affecting performance.

outputs.name: images
outputs.description: The generated noise patterns as a batch of images, ready for further processing or visualization.

outputs.name: batch_size
outputs.description: The number of generated noise patterns, confirming the input batch size was processed as requested.

SaltScheduleListExponentialFade.description: This node applies an exponential fade effect to a schedule list based on the specified fade type and strength, optionally starting from a given index. It's designed to modify the intensity or presence of elements in a schedule over time, creating smooth transitions either into, out of, or both into and out of a sequence of values.

inputs.name: schedule_list
inputs.description: The list of values to apply the exponential fade effect to. It represents the sequence of elements whose intensity will be modified over time.

inputs.name: fade_type
inputs.description: Specifies the type of fade to apply: 'in' for a gradual increase, 'out' for a gradual decrease, or 'in-and-out' for an increase followed by a decrease.

inputs.name: strength
inputs.description: Determines the curve's steepness of the fade effect. Higher values result in a steeper curve.

inputs.name: start_index
inputs.description: The index in the schedule list from which to start applying the fade effect. Allows for partial application of the fade.

outputs.name: schedule_list
outputs.description: The modified schedule list after applying the exponential fade effect, with values adjusted according to the specified fade type and strength.

SaltScheduleMerge.description: The SaltScheduleMerge node is designed to combine two schedule lists into a single list, effectively appending the second list to the end of the first. This functionality is useful in scenarios where sequential scheduling tasks need to be merged for streamlined processing or analysis.

inputs.name: schedule_list_a
inputs.description: Represents the first list of scheduled items to be merged. It serves as the initial part of the combined schedule list.

inputs.name: schedule_list_b
inputs.description: Represents the second list of scheduled items to be appended to the end of the first list, completing the merged schedule list.

outputs.name: schedule_list
outputs.description: The combined list resulting from appending the second schedule list to the first, providing a unified sequence of scheduled items.

SaltScheduleRandomValues.description: This node is designed to generate a list of random values within a specified range. It allows for the creation of random schedules by specifying a count of values to generate, along with minimum and maximum values. An option to force the generated values to be integers is also provided, enhancing its flexibility for various scheduling and sequencing tasks.

inputs.name: count
inputs.description: Specifies the number of random values to generate. It determines the length of the resulting schedule list.

inputs.name: min_value
inputs.description: The minimum value that can be generated. This sets the lower bound for the random values in the schedule list.

inputs.name: max_value
inputs.description: The maximum value that can be generated. This sets the upper bound for the random values in the schedule list.

inputs.name: force_integer
inputs.description: A boolean flag that, when set to true, forces all generated values to be integers, providing control over the numerical type of the schedule list.

outputs.name: schedule_list
outputs.description: The list of randomly generated values, adhering to the specified minimum and maximum values and count. It can consist of either floating-point numbers or integers, depending on the 'force_integer' flag.

SaltScheduleSmoothing.description: Provides a method to smooth a given schedule list by applying a smoothing factor to each element, effectively filtering out rapid changes and creating a more gradual transition between values.

inputs.name: schedule_list
inputs.description: The list of schedule values to be smoothed. This list represents a sequence of numerical values that will undergo smoothing to reduce abrupt changes.

inputs.name: smoothing_factor
inputs.description: A factor determining the degree of smoothing applied to the schedule list. A higher value results in a smoother transition between schedule values.

outputs.name: schedule_list
outputs.description: The smoothed list of schedule values, where each value has been adjusted according to the smoothing factor to create a gradual transition.

SaltScheduleSplit.description: This node is designed to divide a given schedule list into two parts based on a specified index, facilitating the manipulation of schedule sequences by separating them into distinct segments.

inputs.name: schedule_list
inputs.description: The list of scheduled items to be split. This parameter is crucial for determining the point of division within the schedule.

inputs.name: split_index
inputs.description: The index at which the schedule list is to be split. This index determines the boundary between the two resulting lists, playing a key role in the segmentation process.

outputs.name: schedule_list_a
outputs.description: The first part of the schedule list, containing all items before the split index.

outputs.name: schedule_list_b
outputs.description: The second part of the schedule list, containing all items from the split index onwards.

SaltScheduleVariance.description: This node applies a combination of noise-based tremors and easing functions to a schedule list to create varied animation frames. It allows for the dynamic adjustment of animation parameters over time, enhancing visual effects with perlin noise and optional curve adjustments.

inputs.name: schedule_list
inputs.description: The list of values representing the schedule to be varied. It serves as the base for applying noise and curve adjustments, directly influencing the visual dynamics of the animation.

inputs.name: curves_mode
inputs.description: Specifies the type of easing function to apply to the schedule list, offering a method to smoothly transition between values.

inputs.name: use_perlin_tremors
inputs.description: A flag to enable or disable the application of perlin noise-based tremors to the schedule list, adding a layer of dynamic variation.

inputs.name: tremor_scale
inputs.description: Determines the intensity of the noise-based tremors applied to the schedule list, affecting the degree of variation.

inputs.name: octaves
inputs.description: Controls the number of layers of noise to combine for generating tremors, impacting the complexity of the resulting variation.

inputs.name: persistence
inputs.description: Affects the amplitude of each octave in the noise function, influencing the smoothness of the tremors.

inputs.name: lacunarity
inputs.description: Determines the frequency of each octave in the noise function, affecting the detail of the tremors.

outputs.name: schedule_list
outputs.description: The modified schedule list after applying noise-based tremors and optional curve adjustments, ready for use in animating visual elements.

SaltThresholdSchedule.description: This node applies a threshold to a schedule list, modifying each value based on a specified fade type and strength, starting from an optional index. It's designed to create dynamic adjustments in scheduling sequences, allowing for the implementation of fade-in, fade-out, or both effects to enhance the temporal dynamics of a schedule.

inputs.name: float_schedule
inputs.description: The list of schedule values to be modified. It serves as the base for applying the threshold adjustments, determining the sequence of values that will undergo fading effects.

inputs.name: max_frames
inputs.description: Specifies the maximum number of frames for the schedule, defining the temporal limit for the application of the threshold.

inputs.name: output_mode
inputs.description: Determines the format of the output schedule list, allowing for different representations such as 'prompt_schedule', 'float_list', 'int_list', or 'raw'.

inputs.name: schedule_values
inputs.description: A string representing scheduled values in a JSON format, which are used to generate the sequence with applied thresholds.

outputs.name: value_schedule_list
outputs.description: The modified schedule list after applying the specified threshold, showcasing the dynamic adjustments made to the original sequence.

SaltDisplayAny.description: The SaltDisplayAny node is designed to universally display any type of input data, converting it into a human-readable format or indicating if the data type cannot be displayed. It supports a wide range of data types, including basic types like strings and numbers, complex data structures like dictionaries and lists, and even PyTorch tensors, making it a versatile utility for debugging and data visualization.

inputs.name: input_value
inputs.description: Represents the data to be displayed. It can be of any type, making this node highly versatile in handling various kinds of input for visualization or debugging purposes.

outputs.name: output
outputs.description: The output is a human-readable representation of the input data or a message indicating that the data type cannot be displayed.

ClassifyObject.description: The ClassifyObject node is designed to classify images into categories based on a given taxonomy and a multimodal model. It leverages an image URL and a taxonomy description to generate a category name for the image, utilizing a large language model capable of understanding both text and image inputs.

inputs.name: image_url
inputs.description: The URL of the image to be classified. It serves as a direct link to the image that the model will analyze to determine its category.

inputs.name: taxonomy
inputs.description: A string representing the taxonomy against which the image will be classified. This taxonomy guides the model in understanding the possible categories and their hierarchy.

inputs.name: llm
inputs.description: A configuration object for the large language model (LLM) used in the classification. It includes the model details and API key necessary for multimodal understanding.

outputs.name: category_name
outputs.description: The name of the category into which the image has been classified, based on the provided taxonomy and analyzed by the multimodal model.

ClusterGroup.description: The ClusterGroup node is designed for clustering a set of features into groups based on their similarity. It utilizes dimensionality reduction techniques followed by a clustering algorithm to categorize the data into clusters, and generates visualizations to represent the clustering and distribution of data points.

inputs.name: features
inputs.description: A collection of features to be clustered. These features are the basis for the dimensionality reduction and subsequent clustering process.

inputs.name: n_components
inputs.description: The number of dimensions to reduce the feature space to before clustering. This parameter influences the granularity of the clustering process.

inputs.name: min_cluster_size
inputs.description: The minimum size of clusters to be formed. This parameter helps in controlling the sensitivity of the clustering algorithm to small clusters.

inputs.name: max_cluster_size
inputs.description: The maximum size of clusters to be allowed. This parameter sets an upper limit on cluster sizes, preventing overly large clusters.

outputs.name: labels
outputs.description: The labels assigned to each data point indicating the cluster it belongs to.

outputs.name: clustering_img
outputs.description: A visualization of the clustered data points, with different colors representing different clusters.

outputs.name: distribution_img
outputs.description: A bar plot showing the distribution of data points across the top-level categories or clusters.

CreateTaxonomy.description: The CreateTaxonomy node is designed to automate the process of updating and generating a new taxonomy based on provided product descriptions and updates. It leverages a language model to suggest modifications to an existing taxonomy or create a new one, aiming to enhance the organization and categorization of products within a marketplace.

inputs.name: path_to_descriptions
inputs.description: Specifies the file path to the product descriptions, which are used as input for generating or updating the taxonomy.

inputs.name: updates
inputs.description: Indicates the number of updates to be applied to the taxonomy during the generation process.

inputs.name: batch_size
inputs.description: Determines the number of product descriptions processed in each batch for taxonomy generation or update.

inputs.name: update_rate
inputs.description: Specifies the frequency at which the taxonomy is updated based on the provided product descriptions.

inputs.name: fix_request
inputs.description: A template for the request to fix issues in the taxonomy, used by the language model to suggest specific changes.

inputs.name: prompt
inputs.description: A template for the prompt used by the language model to categorize products and suggest taxonomy updates.

inputs.name: llm
inputs.description: The language model used for generating taxonomy suggestions and updates.

inputs.name: path_to_taxonomy
inputs.description: Optional. Specifies the file path to the existing taxonomy, which can be updated or used as a reference for generating a new taxonomy.

outputs.name: taxonomy
outputs.description: The updated or newly generated taxonomy as a result of the node's execution.

outputs.name: old_taxonomy
outputs.description: The original taxonomy before any updates were applied, used for comparison or rollback purposes.
