LLMImageTextReader.description: The LLMImageTextReader node is designed to read and process images, extracting text and additional information based on user-defined parameters. It leverages underlying image processing and text extraction technologies to facilitate the analysis and interpretation of image content.

inputs.name: path
inputs.description: Specifies the file path of the image to be processed. This is a crucial parameter as it determines the source image for text extraction and further processing.

inputs.name: parse_text
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether text should be extracted from the image. This affects whether the node will perform text parsing operations on the image.

inputs.name: extra_info
inputs.description: A string containing extra information in JSON format that can be used to provide additional context or instructions for processing the image.

outputs.name: documents
outputs.description: The output is a document containing the results of the image processing and text extraction, structured in a format that can be further analyzed or displayed.

LLMImageVisionLLMReader.description: The LLMImageVisionLLMReader node is designed to read and process image files, leveraging large language models (LLMs) to interpret and extract information from visual content. It aims to bridge the gap between visual data and textual analysis, enabling a deeper understanding of images through the lens of LLMs.

inputs.name: path
inputs.description: Specifies the file path to the image to be processed. It is a crucial parameter as it determines the source of the visual data the node will analyze.

inputs.name: extra_info
inputs.description: Provides additional, optional information in a string format that can be used to influence the processing of the image. This could include settings or parameters specific to the task at hand.

outputs.name: documents
outputs.description: Returns the processed data as documents, encapsulating the insights extracted from the image by the LLM.

LLMInputToDocuments.description: This node is designed to convert various types of input data into a standardized document format, facilitating their processing and analysis in language models. It supports a wide range of input types, including dictionaries, lists, and primitive data types like strings, integers, and floats, and transforms them into a structured document format with optional metadata.

inputs.name: input_data
inputs.description: The primary input for the node, accepting a wide variety of data types including dictionaries, lists, strings, integers, and floats. This flexibility allows for the processing of diverse data forms into a standardized document format.

inputs.name: extra_info
inputs.description: Optional metadata in JSON string format that can be attached to the generated documents, providing additional context or information.

inputs.name: concat_input
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether multiple input items should be concatenated into a single document.

inputs.name: resize_images
inputs.description: A boolean flag that determines whether images within the input data should be resized according to specified maximum dimensions.

inputs.name: max_image_width
inputs.description: The maximum width to which images in the input data can be resized, enhancing uniformity and processing efficiency.

inputs.name: max_image_height
inputs.description: The maximum height to which images in the input data can be resized, ensuring consistency across processed documents.

outputs.name: documents
outputs.description: The output of the node, consisting of standardized documents formatted from the input data, potentially including resized images and attached metadata.

LLMIPYNBReader.description: The LLMIPYNBReader node specializes in reading and interpreting IPYNB (Jupyter Notebook) files, transforming them into a format suitable for further processing or analysis within the llama_index ecosystem. It leverages the structure and content of IPYNB files to extract documentation or data, facilitating integration with llama_index's document management capabilities.

inputs.name: path
inputs.description: Specifies the filesystem path to the IPYNB file to be read. This path is essential for locating and accessing the file for processing.

inputs.name: extra_info
inputs.description: Provides additional, optional information in a string format that can be used to influence the reading process or handle specific requirements for processing the IPYNB file.

outputs.name: documents
outputs.description: The processed data from the IPYNB file, formatted as a document suitable for use within the llama_index ecosystem.

LLMJinaScrape.description: The LLMJinaScrape node is designed to fetch and process web content from a specified URL using the Jina AI service. It handles HTTP requests, manages potential errors, and formats the response into a structured document, facilitating the integration of web data into further processing pipelines.

inputs.name: url
inputs.description: The URL to be scraped. This parameter is crucial for defining the target web page from which the content is to be fetched, directly influencing the node's output.

outputs.name: result
outputs.description: The raw text content retrieved from the specified URL, serving as a direct representation of the web page's content.

outputs.name: documents
outputs.description: A structured document containing the scraped web content along with additional metadata, such as the source and Jina AI URLs, enhancing data context and utility.

LLMJsonComposer.description: The LLMJsonComposer node is designed to generate valid JSON objects from given text inputs by leveraging a language model. It processes textual data along with a set of classifiers and optional directions to compose JSON structures that encapsulate the provided information accurately and coherently.

inputs.name: llm_model
inputs.description: Specifies the language model to be used for generating the JSON object, playing a crucial role in interpreting the input text and classifiers to produce the desired output.

inputs.name: text_input
inputs.description: The primary textual data from which the JSON object will be composed, serving as the base content for the generation process.

inputs.name: classifier_list
inputs.description: A comma-separated list of classifiers that guide the JSON composition by categorizing the input text, influencing the structure and content of the generated JSON.

inputs.name: extra_directions
inputs.description: Optional additional instructions for the language model to follow when composing the JSON, allowing for more tailored and specific outputs.

outputs.name: json_output
outputs.description: The generated JSON object as a string, representing a structured and valid JSON format of the input text and classifiers.

LLMJSONQueryEngine.description: This node is designed to process queries against JSON data using a language model, enabling the extraction of information or execution of tasks based on a JSON schema and data. It leverages a JSON query engine to interpret and respond to queries, making it suitable for applications requiring dynamic data interpretation or manipulation.

inputs.name: llm_model
inputs.description: Specifies the language model to be used for processing queries. This model is crucial for understanding and generating responses based on the JSON data and schema provided.

inputs.name: json_data
inputs.description: The actual JSON data on which queries will be executed. This data is parsed according to the provided JSON schema.

inputs.name: json_schema
inputs.description: Defines the structure of the JSON data to be queried. This schema guides the query engine in interpreting the data correctly.

inputs.name: prompt
inputs.description: The query or command to be executed against the JSON data. This prompt drives the interaction with the data.

inputs.name: human_readable
inputs.description: A flag indicating whether the response should be synthesized for human readability. This affects how the query results are presented.

inputs.name: optional_service_context
inputs.description: An optional context that can be provided to customize the service's behavior or processing environment.

outputs.name: result
outputs.description: The direct response from the query execution, containing the information or results extracted from the JSON data.

outputs.name: json_path
outputs.description: Additional data about the query execution, including paths within the JSON data that were accessed to generate the response.

LLMJsonRepair.description: The LLMJsonRepair node is designed to correct malformed JSON strings using a language model. It takes a potentially incorrect JSON input and optional directions, and outputs a repaired version of the JSON, ensuring data integrity and proper formatting.

inputs.name: llm_model
inputs.description: Specifies the language model to use for repairing the JSON. It is crucial for interpreting the input and generating the corrected output.

inputs.name: text_input
inputs.description: The malformed JSON string that needs to be repaired. This input is essential for the node to understand what needs fixing.

inputs.name: extra_directions
inputs.description: Optional additional instructions for the language model to follow during the repair process, allowing for more tailored corrections.

outputs.name: json_output
outputs.description: The repaired JSON string, corrected for syntax and formatting errors to ensure validity.

LLMKSamplerTool.description: This node is designed to facilitate the generation of language models by providing a toolkit for sampling. It abstracts the complexities involved in sampling processes, making it easier to generate language models with specific characteristics or based on certain criteria.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: Specifies the model to be used for sampling, setting the foundation for the generation process.

inputs.name: clip
inputs.description: Specifies the CLIP model to be used alongside the main model for enhanced conditioning.

inputs.name: vae
inputs.description: Specifies the VAE model to be used in the generation process, contributing to the visual aspects of the generated model.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Defines the width of the generated images, affecting the dimensions of the output.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Defines the height of the generated images, affecting the dimensions of the output.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: Determines the randomness seed for sampling, ensuring reproducibility of results.

inputs.name: steps
inputs.description: Defines the number of steps to perform in the sampling process, affecting the detail and quality of the generated model.

inputs.name: cfg
inputs.description: Controls the conditioning factor, influencing the variance and creativity of the generated output.

inputs.name: sampler_name
inputs.description: Selects the specific sampling algorithm to use, tailoring the generation process to specific needs.

inputs.name: scheduler
inputs.description: Chooses the scheduler for controlling the sampling process, further customizing the output.

inputs.name: denoise
inputs.description: Adjusts the level of denoising applied during the sampling process, affecting the clarity of the generated model.

inputs.name: optional_control_net
inputs.description: Optionally specifies a ControlNet model for additional control over the generation process.

inputs.name: optional_control_image
inputs.description: Optionally includes a control image to guide the visual aspects of the generated model.

inputs.name: optional_latent_image
inputs.description: Optionally incorporates a latent image to influence the visual aspects of the generated model.

inputs.name: cn_strength
inputs.description: Specifies the strength of the ControlNet's influence on the generation process.

inputs.name: cn_start_percent
inputs.description: Defines the starting point of the ControlNet's influence in terms of the generation process's progress percentage.

inputs.name: cn_end_percent
inputs.description: Defines the ending point of the ControlNet's influence in terms of the generation process's progress percentage.

outputs.name: tool
outputs.description: Outputs the tool encapsulating the result of the sampling process, designed for generating language models.

LLMLlamaCPPModel.description: The LLMLlamaCPPModel node is designed to load and initialize LlamaCPP models, incorporating an embedding model alongside. It facilitates the integration of LlamaCPP models into larger workflows by providing a streamlined mechanism for model loading, including setting up necessary configurations and embedding models for enhanced functionality.

inputs.name: model_name
inputs.description: Specifies the name of the LlamaCPP model to be loaded. This parameter is crucial for identifying the correct model file and initializing the LlamaCPP model accordingly.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: Returns a dictionary containing the loaded LlamaCPP model, its name, the associated embedding model, and the embedding model's name. This output is essential for subsequent processing or analysis steps in the workflow.

LLMLLaVANextImageEvaluator.description: This node is designed to evaluate images using the LLaVA Next V1 model, providing detailed assessments and generating keywords, lists, and documents based on the image content. It aims to facilitate a deeper understanding and categorization of images through advanced image analysis techniques.

inputs.name: lnv1_model
inputs.description: Specifies the LLaVA Next V1 model to be used for image evaluation, determining the analytical capabilities and accuracy of the assessment.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The images to be evaluated, serving as the primary input for analysis and categorization by the node.

inputs.name: max_tokens
inputs.description: Defines the maximum number of tokens to be used in the evaluation, affecting the depth and detail of the analysis.

inputs.name: prompt_format
inputs.description: Determines the format of the prompt used in the evaluation, guiding the model's analysis and output generation.

inputs.name: prompt
inputs.description: The specific prompt to guide the evaluation, directly influencing the focus and nature of the analysis.

outputs.name: strings
outputs.description: A string representation of the evaluation results, providing a concise summary or keywords.

outputs.name: list
outputs.description: A list of structured data or keywords extracted from the image, offering detailed insights.

outputs.name: documents
outputs.description: Generated documents that encapsulate the evaluation findings, providing comprehensive details and context.

LLMLLaVANextModelLoader.description: This node is designed to load and initialize the LLAVA Next V1 model with optional quantization and flash attention features for optimized performance.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: Specifies the model identifier for the LLAVA Next V1 model to be loaded. This allows for flexibility in choosing different model versions or configurations.

inputs.name: device
inputs.description: Determines the computing device ('cuda' or 'cpu') on which the model will be loaded, enabling hardware-specific optimizations.

inputs.name: use_bitsandbytes_quantize
inputs.description: Enables or disables quantization using the bitsandbytes library for the model, potentially improving performance with a slight trade-off in accuracy.

outputs.name: lnv1_model
outputs.description: Returns the loaded LLAVA Next V1 model, ready for evaluation or further processing.

LLMMarkdownComposer.description: The LLMMarkdownComposer node is designed to transform input text into well-structured Markdown documents. It leverages a language model to interpret and format the given text according to specified classifiers and additional directions, ensuring the output adheres to Markdown syntax while incorporating all provided data.

inputs.name: llm_model
inputs.description: Specifies the language model to use for generating the Markdown document. It plays a crucial role in understanding the input text and formatting it according to Markdown syntax.

inputs.name: text_input
inputs.description: The primary text input that will be transformed into a Markdown document. This text serves as the base content for the Markdown generation process.

inputs.name: classifier_list
inputs.description: A comma-separated list of classifiers that guide the language model in structuring the Markdown document. These classifiers help in categorizing and formatting the input text appropriately.

inputs.name: extra_directions
inputs.description: Additional instructions for the language model to follow when generating the Markdown document. These directions can include specific formatting requests or content structuring guidelines.

outputs.name: markdown_output
outputs.description: The generated Markdown document, structured and formatted according to the input specifications and additional directions.

LLMMarkdownReader.description: The LLMMarkdownReader node is designed to read and process Markdown documentation files, such as GitHub READMEs, converting them into a structured document format suitable for further analysis or processing. This functionality facilitates the integration of Markdown content into data pipelines, enabling automated content extraction and transformation.

inputs.name: path
inputs.description: Specifies the file system path to the Markdown file to be read. This parameter is essential for locating and accessing the file for processing.

inputs.name: extra_info
inputs.description: Provides additional, optional information that can be used to influence the reading process. This could include metadata or configuration options in a JSON string format.

outputs.name: documents
outputs.description: Returns a structured document representation of the input Markdown file, ready for further processing or analysis.

LLMMarkdownRepair.description: The node is designed to repair malformed Markdown text, ensuring it is transformed into valid, well-structured Markdown without omitting any data. It leverages a language model to analyze and correct the input text based on given instructions.

inputs.name: llm_model
inputs.description: Specifies the language model to use for repairing the Markdown. It plays a crucial role in understanding and fixing the malformed Markdown based on the provided prompt.

inputs.name: text_input
inputs.description: The malformed Markdown text that needs to be repaired. This input is critical as it provides the content that the node will work on to produce valid Markdown.

inputs.name: extra_directions
inputs.description: Optional additional instructions for the language model to follow when repairing the Markdown. This can guide the repair process more precisely according to specific requirements.

outputs.name: markdown_output
outputs.description: The repaired Markdown text, which is the result of the language model's processing of the input text and any extra directions provided.

LLMMboxReader.description: The LLMMboxReader node specializes in reading email files and converting them into a structured document format, leveraging the capabilities of the llama_index Document model. It is designed to facilitate the processing and analysis of email data by transforming mbox files into a more accessible and analyzable form.

inputs.name: path
inputs.description: Specifies the filesystem path to the mbox file to be read. This path is essential for locating and accessing the file for processing.

inputs.name: extra_info
inputs.description: Provides additional, optional information in a string format that can be used to influence the reading process or handle specific requirements for processing the mbox file.

outputs.name: documents
outputs.description: Returns the processed email data from the mbox file as a structured document, ready for further analysis or manipulation.

LLMMistralAI.description: The LLMMistralAI node is designed to interface with the MistralAI API, allowing users to load and interact with various pre-trained language models provided by MistralAI. It facilitates the integration of advanced natural language processing capabilities into applications by leveraging the power of large language models.

inputs.name: model_name
inputs.description: Specifies the name of the MistralAI model to be loaded. This parameter is crucial for determining which specific pre-trained model is utilized for processing, affecting the node's behavior and the nature of its output.

inputs.name: api_key
inputs.description: The API key required for authenticating with the MistralAI service. This parameter is essential for enabling access to the MistralAI models, ensuring secure and authorized use of the API.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The output includes the loaded MistralAI model along with an embedding model, providing the necessary components for further natural language processing tasks.

LLMMultiModalImageEvaluation.description: This node is designed to evaluate images based on a given query using a specified LLM model. It processes image paths or documents, loads the images, and sends them to the LLM model along with the query for evaluation, providing a text-based assessment of the images.

inputs.name: llm_model
inputs.description: The LLM model used for evaluating the images. It is crucial for performing the evaluation as it processes the images and the query to generate the evaluation result.

inputs.name: image_documents
inputs.description: A list of image documents to be evaluated. These documents are processed and evaluated by the LLM model in conjunction with the query.

inputs.name: llm_message
inputs.description: The query or message to be evaluated by the LLM model. This message guides the evaluation process of the images.

inputs.name: max_tokens
inputs.description: The maximum number of tokens to be generated by the LLM model during the evaluation. It limits the length of the evaluation result.

outputs.name: response
outputs.description: The evaluation result text from the LLM model, providing a text-based assessment of the images.

LLMMultiModalImageEvaluationTool.description: This node specializes in evaluating images based on specific queries using a language model. It processes image paths or documents, loads the images, and sends them to the language model along with the query for comprehensive evaluation. The node is designed to integrate multimodal inputs (text and images) for generating detailed assessments or responses, making it a critical component for applications requiring nuanced understanding and interaction with visual content.

inputs.name: llm_model
inputs.description: The language model used for evaluating the images in conjunction with the provided query. It's essential for interpreting the visual content and generating relevant responses.

inputs.name: name
inputs.description: A unique identifier for the evaluation tool. This parameter is crucial for distinguishing between different instances or uses of the evaluation tool.

inputs.name: description
inputs.description: A detailed description of the evaluation tool's purpose and functionality. This parameter helps to provide context and expectations for the tool's output.

inputs.name: image_documents
inputs.description: A list of image documents to be evaluated. This parameter enables the node to directly process pre-loaded images for evaluation, facilitating more flexible and efficient handling of visual content.

inputs.name: max_tokens
inputs.description: The maximum number of tokens to be generated by the language model in the response. It controls the verbosity and detail level of the evaluation output.

outputs.name: evaluator_tool
outputs.description: The output from the node providing an evaluation or response based on the input query and images. It represents the node's capability to assess and interpret visual content through the language model.

LLMOpenAIModel.description: The LLMOpenAIModel node is designed to interface with OpenAI's language models, facilitating the loading and utilization of these models for various language processing tasks. It abstracts the complexities involved in interacting with OpenAI's API, providing a streamlined way to leverage their advanced natural language understanding and generation capabilities.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: Specifies the name of the OpenAI model to be loaded. This parameter is crucial for determining which specific language model is utilized for processing, affecting the node's behavior and the quality of its outputs.

inputs.name: api_key
inputs.description: The API key required to authenticate with OpenAI's services. This key enables the node to access OpenAI's language models, making it essential for the operation of the node.

inputs.name: embedding_model
inputs.description: Defines the model used for embedding purposes, which is part of OpenAI's suite. This parameter influences how text inputs are converted into embeddings, affecting tasks such as similarity searches or contextual analysis.

inputs.name: multimodal
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether the multimodal capabilities of the model should be enabled. This affects whether the model can process and understand inputs that include both text and other modalities, such as images.

outputs.name: llm_model
outputs.description: The loaded language model from OpenAI, ready for language processing tasks.

outputs.name: embed_model_only
outputs.description: The embedding model loaded alongside the main language model, used for generating embeddings from text inputs.

LLMOpenAIModelOpts.description: The LLMOpenAIModelOpts node is designed to configure and customize the options for language models and their embedding counterparts. It allows for the adjustment of various parameters such as temperature, retries, and embedding dimensions, enabling fine-tuning of the model's behavior and performance.

inputs.name: llm_model
inputs.description: The 'llm_model' parameter is a dictionary containing the language model and embedding model to be configured. It is crucial for specifying the models whose options are to be set, affecting the overall execution and results of the node.

inputs.name: model_temperature
inputs.description: Specifies the temperature setting for the language model, influencing its creativity and randomness.

inputs.name: model_max_tokens
inputs.description: Defines the maximum number of tokens the language model can generate, affecting the length of the output.

inputs.name: model_api_max_retries
inputs.description: Determines the number of times the API will retry a request in case of failure, ensuring reliability.

inputs.name: model_api_timeout
inputs.description: Sets the timeout duration for API requests, impacting the response time.

inputs.name: model_reuse_anyscale_client
inputs.description: Indicates whether to reuse the Anyscale client across requests, optimizing resource usage.

inputs.name: multimodal_max_new_tokens
inputs.description: Specifies the maximum number of new tokens for multimodal inputs, affecting the output length.

inputs.name: multimodal_image_detail
inputs.description: Determines the level of detail for images in multimodal inputs, influencing the model's focus.

inputs.name: embed_batch_size
inputs.description: Sets the batch size for embedding model operations, affecting performance and resource utilization.

inputs.name: embed_dimensions
inputs.description: Specifies the dimensionality of the embeddings, influencing the detail level of the generated embeddings.

inputs.name: embed_api_max_retries
inputs.description: Determines the number of times the embedding API will retry in case of failure, ensuring reliability.

inputs.name: embed_api_timeout
inputs.description: Sets the timeout duration for embedding API requests, impacting the response time.

inputs.name: embed_reuse_anyscale_client
inputs.description: Indicates whether to reuse the Anyscale client for embedding operations, optimizing resource usage.

inputs.name: model_additional_kwargs
inputs.description: Allows for the specification of additional keyword arguments for the model, enabling further customization.

inputs.name: embed_additional_kwargs
inputs.description: Allows for the specification of additional keyword arguments for the embedding model, enabling further customization.

inputs.name: model_system_prompt
inputs.description: unknown

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The 'model' output is a dictionary reflecting the updated configurations of the language model and embedding model. It encapsulates the adjustments made to the models' options, influencing their operational characteristics and output.

LLMPagedCSVReader.description: The LLMPagedCSVReader node specializes in reading CSV files and converting them into a structured document format with paging capabilities. It allows for efficient handling and processing of large CSV files by segmenting them into manageable pages.

inputs.name: path
inputs.description: Specifies the file path of the CSV file to be read. This is essential for locating and accessing the file for reading.

inputs.name: encoding
inputs.description: Defines the character encoding of the CSV file, such as UTF-8, to ensure correct interpretation of text.

inputs.name: delimiter
inputs.description: Sets the character used to separate columns in the CSV file, typically a comma (,).

inputs.name: quotechar
inputs.description: Indicates the character used to wrap text containing the delimiter, commonly a double quote (").

inputs.name: extra_info
inputs.description: Allows for the inclusion of additional, optional information that may be relevant for processing the CSV file.

outputs.name: documents
outputs.description: Returns a structured document format that represents the content of the CSV file, segmented into pages for easier handling.

LLMPandasCSVReader.description: The LLMPandasCSVReader node specializes in reading CSV files and transforming them into llama_index Documents, incorporating additional configuration options for joining rows and columns. This node enhances the flexibility in processing CSV data by allowing custom concatenation strategies, making it suitable for a wide range of data preparation tasks.

inputs.name: path
inputs.description: Specifies the file path to the CSV file to be read, serving as the primary data source for the node. The path's validity directly impacts the node's ability to access and process the specified CSV file.

inputs.name: concat_rows
inputs.description: Determines whether rows should be concatenated during the reading process, affecting how data is aggregated and presented in the output Documents. This option allows for tailored data structuring to meet specific analysis needs.

inputs.name: col_joiner
inputs.description: Specifies the string to be used for joining column values when concatenating rows, influencing the format and readability of the concatenated data. This parameter enables precise control over the data's presentation.

inputs.name: row_joiner
inputs.description: Specifies the string to be used for joining row values, impacting the structure and organization of the output Documents. This allows for customized data formatting, enhancing the node's adaptability to various data analysis scenarios.

inputs.name: extra_info
inputs.description: Allows for the inclusion of additional, user-defined information to be processed along with the CSV data. This parameter can enrich the output Documents with context or metadata, thereby increasing the node's utility in complex data processing tasks.

outputs.name: documents
outputs.description: Outputs the processed data as llama_index Documents, ready for further processing or analysis. The structure and content of these Documents are shaped by the input parameters, enabling tailored data preparation.

LLMParquetDatasetSearcher.description: The LLMParquetDatasetSearcher node is designed to efficiently search and filter data within Parquet files based on specified search terms, exclusion criteria, and length constraints. It leverages parallel processing to enhance search performance and incorporates relevancy scoring to prioritize results, making it a powerful tool for extracting and analyzing specific segments of large datasets.

inputs.name: file_type
inputs.description: Specifies the type of file to be searched. This parameter determines the appropriate reader to use for the file, supporting formats such as parquet, text, json, yaml, csv, and excel.

inputs.name: path_or_url
inputs.description: The path to the file or URL to be searched. It is the starting point for the search operation, allowing the node to access and process the specified file.

inputs.name: search_term
inputs.description: Defines the search terms used to filter the dataset. These terms are crucial for identifying relevant data segments within the file.

inputs.name: exclude_terms
inputs.description: Terms to be excluded from the search results, refining the search by removing irrelevant or undesired data segments.

inputs.name: columns
inputs.description: Specifies the columns to be included in the search. By default, all columns are included ('*'), but this can be customized to target specific columns.

inputs.name: case_sensitive
inputs.description: Determines whether the search should be case sensitive, affecting how search terms are matched against the dataset.

inputs.name: max_results
inputs.description: The maximum number of search results to return, allowing control over the volume of data retrieved.

inputs.name: term_relevancy_threshold
inputs.description: The threshold for term relevancy scoring, used to prioritize results based on their relevance to the search terms.

inputs.name: use_relevancy
inputs.description: Indicates whether relevancy scoring should be used to prioritize search results, enhancing the search's focus on the most relevant segments.

inputs.name: min_length
inputs.description: The minimum length of the data segments to be included in the search results, enabling the exclusion of too-short segments.

inputs.name: max_length
inputs.description: The maximum length of the data segments to be considered in the search results, preventing overly long segments from being included.

inputs.name: max_dynamic_retries
inputs.description: The maximum number of retries with dynamic search terms if no results are found, enhancing the chance of retrieving relevant data.

inputs.name: clean_content
inputs.description: Specifies whether the content should be cleaned, removing unnecessary or irrelevant information from the search results.

inputs.name: excel_sheet_position
inputs.description: For Excel files, specifies the sheet to be searched by its position, allowing targeted searches within multi-sheet documents.

inputs.name: recache
inputs.description: Indicates whether the file should be recached, potentially updating the cached version with the latest content.

inputs.name: condense_documents
inputs.description: Determines whether documents should be condensed, potentially merging similar documents to reduce redundancy.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: A seed value for random operations, ensuring reproducibility of the search results under the same conditions.

outputs.name: results
outputs.description: The primary search results, containing data segments that match the search criteria.

outputs.name: results_list
outputs.description: A list of search results, potentially including additional metadata or context about the matches.

outputs.name: documents
outputs.description: A collection of documents derived from the search results, formatted for further processing or analysis.

LLMPDFReader.description: The LLMPDFReader node is designed to read PDF files and convert them into a llama_index Document format, excluding embedded images. This functionality enables the extraction and processing of text data from PDF documents for further analysis or manipulation.

inputs.name: path
inputs.description: Specifies the file system path to the PDF file to be read. It is essential for locating and accessing the file for processing.

inputs.name: extra_info
inputs.description: Provides additional, optional information in a string format that can be used to influence the reading process or handle specific requirements.

outputs.name: documents
outputs.description: Returns the content of the PDF file as a llama_index Document, facilitating further data manipulation or analysis.

LLMPostProcessDocuments.description: This node is designed to refine and filter a collection of documents based on specified keywords. It allows for the inclusion of documents containing certain required keywords while excluding those with specified unwanted keywords, effectively tailoring the document set to more closely match user-defined criteria.

inputs.name: document
inputs.description: Represents the collection of documents to be processed. It is the primary data upon which the node operates, determining which documents are retained based on the presence or absence of specified keywords.

inputs.name: required_keywords
inputs.description: A comma-separated list of keywords that must be present in a document for it to be included in the output. This parameter enables the filtering of documents to those that are relevant to specific criteria.

inputs.name: exclude_keywords
inputs.description: A comma-separated list of keywords that, if present in a document, will result in its exclusion from the output. This parameter helps in removing documents that contain undesired content.

outputs.name: documents
outputs.description: The filtered collection of documents, which have been processed to include only those matching the required keywords and exclude those with any of the excluded keywords.

LLMPptxReader.description: The LLMPptxReader node is designed to read Microsoft PowerPoint (PPTX) files and convert them into a format that can be processed by llama_index, potentially including the interpretation of images within the documents.

inputs.name: path
inputs.description: Specifies the file path to the PowerPoint (PPTX) file to be read. This is essential for locating and accessing the file for processing.

inputs.name: extra_info
inputs.description: Provides additional information or instructions in a string format, which can be used to influence how the document is read or processed.

outputs.name: documents
outputs.description: Outputs the content of the PowerPoint file as a document in a format compatible with llama_index.

LLMPyMuPDFReader.description: The LLMPyMuPDFReader node is designed to read PDF files and convert them into a llama_index Document format, leveraging the PyMuPDF library for efficient processing. This node facilitates the extraction of text and potentially metadata from PDF documents, making them accessible for further analysis or processing within the llama_index ecosystem.

inputs.name: path
inputs.description: Specifies the file path to the PDF document to be read. This path is essential for locating and accessing the file for processing.

inputs.name: metadata
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether metadata should be extracted from the PDF document alongside the text. This option allows for more comprehensive document analysis by including additional information.

inputs.name: extra_info
inputs.description: A string containing extra configuration or information in JSON format, which can be used to customize the reading process. This parameter allows for flexible adaptation to specific requirements.

outputs.name: documents
outputs.description: The output is a Document object containing the extracted text (and optionally metadata) from the PDF file, ready for integration into the llama_index ecosystem.

LLMQueryEngine.description: The LLMQueryEngine node is designed to facilitate querying large language models (LLMs) by assembling and sending structured queries based on user input and predefined message components. It abstracts the complexity of interacting with LLMs, enabling users to obtain responses to queries efficiently.

inputs.name: llm_model
inputs.description: Specifies the large language model to be used for the query, including any necessary model configurations.

inputs.name: llm_index
inputs.description: Represents the index or interface through which the query will be executed, potentially encapsulating specific querying mechanisms or optimizations.

inputs.name: query
inputs.description: The user's query input, which will be included in the final assembled query sent to the LLM.

inputs.name: llm_message
inputs.description: A list of pre-defined messages or prompts that can be included in the query to guide the LLM's response generation.

outputs.name: results
outputs.description: The output from the LLM in response to the assembled query.

LLMQueryEngineAdv.description: The LLMQueryEngineAdv node is designed to leverage language models for advanced querying capabilities. It constructs a comprehensive query from user inputs and messages, utilizes an embedding model for query expansion, and employs a vector index retriever with post-processing for similarity-based filtering. This node aims to provide precise and relevant responses by integrating language understanding and retrieval technologies.

inputs.name: llm_model
inputs.description: The language model and optional embedding model used for query expansion and understanding. It's crucial for interpreting the query and retrieving relevant information.

inputs.name: llm_index
inputs.description: The index used for retrieving query results based on vector similarity. Essential for the node's ability to find the most relevant responses.

inputs.name: query
inputs.description: The user's query, which is combined with other messages to form the complete query input. It plays a key role in directing the search and retrieval process.

inputs.name: llm_message
inputs.description: A list of messages that can be included in the query construction. These messages add context and detail to the query, enhancing its comprehensiveness.

inputs.name: top_k
inputs.description: Specifies the number of top similar results to retrieve. It determines the breadth of the search results.

inputs.name: similarity_cutoff
inputs.description: The similarity threshold for filtering results. Only results with a similarity score above this cutoff are considered relevant.

outputs.name: results
outputs.description: The retrieved and processed query response, which is expected to be relevant and precise based on the input query and similarity criteria.

LLMQueryEngineAsTool.description: This node encapsulates a query engine as a tool, enabling the execution of queries against a document to extract or generate information based on the input question. It is designed to facilitate communication with documents by analyzing their content and providing relevant answers.

inputs.name: name
inputs.description: Specifies the name of the tool, used for identification and display purposes.

inputs.name: description
inputs.description: Provides a detailed description of the tool's functionality and its intended use case.

inputs.name: llm_index
inputs.description: Identifies the language model index to be used for querying, enabling the tool to access the appropriate resources for information retrieval.

outputs.name: query_tool
outputs.description: Returns a tool configured to perform queries, encapsulating the query engine functionality within a callable interface.

LLMRegexCreator.description: The LLMRegexCreator node is designed to generate regular expression (regex) patterns based on a given description and optional additional directions. It utilizes a language model to interpret the requirements and produce a well-formed regex pattern that accurately matches the specified criteria.

inputs.name: llm_model
inputs.description: Specifies the language model to use for generating the regex pattern. It is crucial for interpreting the description and extra directions to create the regex.

inputs.name: description
inputs.description: The primary description of the regex pattern to be created. This description is the basis for the regex generation, guiding the language model in crafting the pattern.

inputs.name: extra_directions
inputs.description: Optional additional instructions or constraints to guide the language model in generating the regex pattern. These directions can refine the output by providing more context or specific requirements.

outputs.name: regex_pattern
outputs.description: The generated regex pattern based on the provided description and optional extra directions.

LLMRegexRepair.description: The LLMRegexRepair node utilizes a language model to correct and improve regex patterns based on a given description of their intended functionality and any additional directions. It aims to transform potentially malformed or incorrect regex expressions into well-formed patterns that accurately match the specified criteria.

inputs.name: llm_model
inputs.description: Specifies the language model to use for repairing the regex pattern. It is crucial for interpreting the input pattern and generating the corrected version.

inputs.name: text_input
inputs.description: The potentially malformed or incorrect regex pattern that needs to be repaired. It serves as the primary input for the correction process.

inputs.name: description
inputs.description: A description of what the regex pattern is intended to match and how the current pattern fails to meet these criteria. This context helps guide the repair process.

inputs.name: extra_directions
inputs.description: Additional instructions or constraints to guide the language model in repairing the regex pattern. This can include specific formatting requirements or limitations.

outputs.name: repaired_regex_pattern
outputs.description: The corrected regex pattern, as generated by the language model. It reflects the intended functionality described in the input.

LLMRssReaderNode.description: The LLMRssReaderNode is designed to fetch and parse RSS feeds from provided URLs, converting the feed data into a structured document format. This node facilitates the aggregation of content from multiple RSS sources, streamlining the process of accessing and analyzing news or blog feeds programmatically.

inputs.name: url_i
inputs.description: The URL from which to read the RSS feed. This parameter is mandatory and initiates the RSS reading process. Up to four URLs can be provided, allowing for the aggregation of content from multiple sources.

outputs.name: documents
outputs.description: The structured document format output containing the aggregated content from the RSS feeds.

LLMRTFReader.description: The LLMRTFReader node specializes in reading RTF (Rich Text Format) files and converting them into a format suitable for further processing or analysis within the llama_index ecosystem. It leverages the capabilities of the RTFReader to parse and extract data from RTF files, facilitating the integration of rich text content into data pipelines.

inputs.name: path
inputs.description: Specifies the file path to the RTF document to be read. It is essential for locating and accessing the file for processing.

inputs.name: extra_info
inputs.description: Provides additional information or parameters in a string format that can be used to customize the reading process of the RTF file.

outputs.name: documents
outputs.description: The output is a document object that represents the parsed content of the RTF file, ready for further processing or analysis.

LLMSaltWebCrawler.description: The LLMSaltWebCrawler node is designed for web crawling and content extraction, tailored to efficiently navigate and retrieve information from websites. It leverages advanced parsing techniques to handle different content types (HTML, XML, JSON), assesses page relevance based on specified keywords, and manages link exploration depth and breadth with customizable parameters. This node is adept at extracting structured data from web pages, making it a valuable tool for web scraping, data mining, and content analysis tasks.

inputs.name: url
inputs.description: The URL to start the crawl from. It serves as the entry point for the web crawling process, determining the initial web page from which the crawler begins its operation.

inputs.name: urls
inputs.description: A list of URLs to be crawled. This allows for multiple entry points for the crawling process, enabling broader coverage of web content.

inputs.name: max_depth
inputs.description: Specifies the maximum depth of the crawl, controlling how deep the crawler can go into website links from the starting point.

inputs.name: max_links
inputs.description: The maximum number of links to follow from a single page. This parameter helps in controlling the breadth of the crawl, ensuring a focused and efficient web scraping process.

inputs.name: trim_line_breaks
inputs.description: Indicates whether to remove line breaks from the extracted content, which can help in cleaning and standardizing the text data.

inputs.name: verify_ssl
inputs.description: Determines whether to verify the SSL certificates of the websites being crawled. This can ensure the security of the web crawling process.

inputs.name: exclude_domains
inputs.description: A list of domains to exclude from the crawl. This helps in avoiding unwanted or irrelevant content by preventing the crawler from accessing specified domains.

inputs.name: keywords
inputs.description: Keywords to filter the content. Pages containing these keywords are considered relevant, allowing for targeted crawling based on content relevance.

inputs.name: relevant_links
inputs.description: Indicates whether to evaluate links for relevance based on the specified keywords. This helps in refining the crawl to include only links that are likely to contain relevant information.

inputs.name: relevant_page_content
inputs.description: Determines whether to evaluate page content for relevance. This allows for the exclusion of pages that do not contain any of the specified keywords, focusing the crawl on relevant content.

inputs.name: max_threads
inputs.description: The maximum number of threads to use for parallel crawling. This parameter enhances the efficiency of the crawling process by enabling concurrent fetching of web content.

inputs.name: use_jina
inputs.description: A flag indicating whether to use Jina for scraping. This enables the use of Jina's scraping capabilities, potentially improving the efficiency and effectiveness of content retrieval.

outputs.name: documents
outputs.description: A collection of documents representing the extracted web page details, including URLs, titles, texts, and links found on the pages. It encapsulates the data mined during the crawl, structured for easy access and analysis.

LLMScaleSERPSearch.description: This node is designed to leverage the capabilities of the ScaleSERP module to perform search operations, parsing the results into a structured format suitable for further analysis or integration into larger workflows. It abstracts the complexities of interacting with the ScaleSERP API, providing a streamlined interface for executing searches and handling the results.

inputs.name: api_key
inputs.description: The api_key is a required string input that represents the API key for accessing the ScaleSERP service. It is essential for authenticating and authorizing the search operation on the platform.

inputs.name: query
inputs.description: The query is a required string input that specifies the search terms or phrases. It is the primary determinant of the search operation's scope and relevance, directly influencing the results retrieved from the platform.

inputs.name: search_type
inputs.description: The search_type input allows users to specify the type of search to perform, such as 'news', 'scholar', 'places', or 'shopping', affecting the scope and nature of the search results.

inputs.name: location
inputs.description: The location input enables specifying the geographical location for the search, influencing the relevance of the search results to the specified area.

inputs.name: device
inputs.description: The device input specifies the type of device context for the search, such as 'desktop', 'mobile', or 'tablet', affecting the format and relevance of the search results.

inputs.name: mobile_type
inputs.description: The mobile_type input is relevant when the device is set to 'mobile', allowing further specification of the mobile device type for tailored search results.

inputs.name: tablet_type
inputs.description: The tablet_type input is relevant when the device is set to 'tablet', allowing further specification of the tablet device type for tailored search results.

outputs.name: documents
outputs.description: The documents output contains the structured search results, including relevant information parsed from the ScaleSERP platform, suitable for further analysis or integration.

outputs.name: results_dict
outputs.description: The results_dict output contains the raw JSON response from the ScaleSERP API, offering comprehensive access to all data retrieved during the search operation.

outputs.name: links_list
outputs.description: The links_list output includes the URLs of the search results, providing direct links to the sources of information retrieved during the search operation.

LLMSelectFromJSON.description: This node is designed to select specific data from a JSON input based on a given JSON path. It allows for the extraction of data by parsing the JSON structure and applying a JSONPath expression to identify and return the desired piece of data at a specified index.

inputs.name: json_input
inputs.description: The JSON string from which data is to be extracted. It serves as the primary data source for the operation.

inputs.name: json_path
inputs.description: A JSONPath expression specifying the path to the desired data within the JSON input. It determines the specific piece of data to be extracted.

inputs.name: match_index
inputs.description: The index of the match to return when multiple matches are found for the JSONPath expression. It controls which piece of data is selected when the path yields multiple results.

outputs.name: selection
outputs.description: The selected data from the JSON input as a JSON string. It represents the result of applying the JSONPath expression to the input.

LLMSemanticSplitterNodeParser.description: This node is designed to parse documents semantically using a specified language model for embeddings, optionally incorporating sentence splitting, metadata inclusion, and relationship analysis between sequential elements. It aims to enhance the understanding and structuring of text by leveraging deep learning models to identify and organize semantic components.

inputs.name: document
inputs.description: The primary text document to be parsed. It serves as the core input for semantic analysis and structuring.

inputs.name: llm_embed_model
inputs.description: The language model used for generating embeddings, which is crucial for the semantic parsing process.

inputs.name: buffer_size
inputs.description: Determines the size of the processing buffer, affecting the granularity of parsing and potentially the performance.

inputs.name: sentence_splitter
inputs.description: An optional model or method for splitting the document into sentences, enhancing the semantic parsing accuracy.

inputs.name: include_metadata
inputs.description: Flag to include metadata in the parsing process, enriching the semantic understanding of the document.

inputs.name: include_prev_next_rel
inputs.description: Flag to analyze and include the relationships between sequential elements, offering deeper insights into the document structure.

outputs.name: llm_node_parser
outputs.description: The result of the semantic parsing process, structured to reflect the semantic components and relationships identified within the document.

LLMSentenceSplitter.description: The LLMSentenceSplitter node is designed to segment text into smaller, manageable chunks based on specified size and overlap criteria. This functionality is crucial for processing large documents or texts in a way that makes them more amenable to detailed analysis or further processing steps.

inputs.name: chunk_size
inputs.description: Specifies the maximum size of each text chunk. It determines how large each segment of text will be, directly impacting the granularity of the splitting process.

inputs.name: chunk_overlap
inputs.description: Defines the number of characters that will overlap between consecutive text chunks. This overlap ensures continuity and context preservation across the segmented text.

outputs.name: llm_sentence_splitter
outputs.description: Produces an instance of a SentenceSplitter, configured with the provided chunk size and overlap, ready to be used for text segmentation.

LLMSentenceSplitterNodeCreator.description: This node is designed to split a given document into smaller, manageable nodes based on sentence boundaries. It utilizes customizable chunk sizes and overlaps to ensure comprehensive coverage and continuity across the document, facilitating further processing or analysis.

inputs.name: document
inputs.description: The primary text document to be split into smaller nodes. It serves as the foundational input for the node's operation, dictating the scope and granularity of the splitting process.

inputs.name: chunk_size
inputs.description: Specifies the maximum size of each chunk or node created from the document, allowing for control over the granularity of the splitting process.

inputs.name: chunk_overlap
inputs.description: Determines the amount of overlap between consecutive chunks or nodes, ensuring continuity and context preservation across splits.

outputs.name: llm_nodes
outputs.description: The output is a collection of smaller, sentence-based nodes derived from the original document, ready for further processing or analysis.

LLMServiceContextAdv.description: This node is designed to create an advanced service context for language model operations, incorporating various configurations and parameters to tailor the context to specific needs. It enables fine-tuning of the language model's behavior, including chunk size, overlap, context window, and output specifications, to optimize performance for complex tasks.

inputs.name: llm_model
inputs.description: Specifies the language model and its embedding model, serving as the foundation for creating the service context. It's crucial for defining the behavior and capabilities of the language model within the service context.

inputs.name: llm_embed_model
inputs.description: Determines the embedding model used alongside the language model, allowing for customization beyond the default setting.

inputs.name: llm_node_parser
inputs.description: Optional parser for processing language model nodes, providing additional flexibility in handling model outputs.

inputs.name: enable_chunk_overlap
inputs.description: Enables overlapping of chunks to ensure continuity and coherence in model outputs, particularly in segmented processing scenarios.

inputs.name: chunk_overlap
inputs.description: Specifies the overlap size between chunks, enhancing the model's ability to maintain context across segments.

inputs.name: enable_context_window
inputs.description: Activates a context window to limit the scope of the model's attention, focusing its analysis and generation on a specified range.

inputs.name: context_window
inputs.description: Sets the size of the context window, controlling the amount of text the model considers for each operation.

inputs.name: enable_num_output
inputs.description: Allows setting a limit on the number of outputs the model generates, useful for controlling output volume and detail.

inputs.name: num_output
inputs.description: Determines the maximum number of outputs produced by the model, offering control over the model's verbosity.

inputs.name: enable_chunk_size_limit
inputs.description: Permits the imposition of a maximum chunk size, potentially reducing memory demands and processing time.

inputs.name: chunk_size_limit
inputs.description: Defines the maximum allowable chunk size, ensuring that processing demands remain within manageable limits.

outputs.name: llm_context
outputs.description: The advanced service context created, encapsulating all specified configurations and parameters to customize the language model's operation.

LLMServiceContextDefault.description: This node is designed to generate a service context for language model operations, encapsulating the necessary configurations and settings to facilitate interaction with language models.

inputs.name: llm_model
inputs.description: Specifies the language model and its embedding model to be used, dictating the operational context for subsequent language processing tasks.

outputs.name: llm_context
outputs.description: Provides the generated service context, enabling tailored interactions with the specified language model.

LLMSimpleWebPageReader.description: The LLMSimpleWebPageReader node is designed to fetch and process web pages from specified URLs, converting them into a document format. It supports reading from multiple URLs, with the option to convert HTML content to text, facilitating the extraction of useful information from web pages.

inputs.name: url_i
inputs.description: The primary URL from which the web page will be read. This is a mandatory parameter to initiate the reading process. The index 'i' indicates that multiple URLs can be specified, allowing for the reading of multiple web pages in a single operation.

inputs.name: html_to_text
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether to convert HTML content to plain text, enhancing readability and processing of the web page content.

outputs.name: documents
outputs.description: The processed documents obtained from the web pages, ready for further analysis or storage.

LLMSimpleWebPageReaderAdv.description: The LLMSimpleWebPageReaderAdv node is designed to fetch and process web pages from a list of URLs, converting them into a structured document format. It optionally converts HTML content to text, facilitating the extraction of readable content from web pages for further analysis or processing.

inputs.name: urls
inputs.description: A list of URLs from which web pages will be fetched. This parameter is essential for the node's operation as it defines the sources of the web content to be processed.

inputs.name: html_to_text
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether the HTML content should be converted to plain text. This affects how the web page content is processed and presented in the output document.

outputs.name: documents
outputs.description: The processed web page content, structured as documents. This output is useful for downstream text analysis or content management tasks.

LLMSummaryIndex.description: The LLMSummaryIndex node is designed to create a summary index from a collection of documents using a specified language model embedding. It processes each document to handle metadata and text, applying sentence splitting as part of its transformation steps, and then constructs an index that can be used for summarizing or retrieving information from the documents.

inputs.name: llm_model
inputs.description: The language model and its embedding model used for generating document summaries. It's crucial for determining the embedding strategy for the documents.

inputs.name: document
inputs.description: A list of documents to be indexed. Each document's text and metadata are processed for indexing.

inputs.name: optional_llm_context
inputs.description: Optional context provided to the language model during the indexing process. It can be used to tailor the embedding process to specific requirements or contexts.

outputs.name: llm_index
outputs.description: The summary index created from the documents, ready for use in summarization or information retrieval tasks.

LLMTavilyResearch.description: This node is designed to leverage the capabilities of the Tavily Research model, focusing on advanced language understanding and generation tasks. It aims to provide deep insights and analyses, potentially enhancing various applications with sophisticated language processing features.

inputs.name: tavily_api_key
inputs.description: Specifies the API key required to access the Tavily Research model, essential for authenticating and enabling the node's operations.

inputs.name: search_query
inputs.description: The query input for conducting searches, serving as the basis for retrieving relevant information and insights.

inputs.name: search_depth
inputs.description: Determines the depth of the search, affecting the comprehensiveness of the results obtained.

inputs.name: max_results
inputs.description: Limits the number of results returned, allowing for control over the volume of data processed.

inputs.name: include_answer
inputs.description: A flag to include direct answers within the search results, enhancing the utility of the output.

inputs.name: include_raw_content
inputs.description: A flag to include the raw content of the search results, providing access to unprocessed data.

inputs.name: include_domains
inputs.description: Specifies domains to be included in the search results, focusing the search on specific sources.

inputs.name: exclude_domains
inputs.description: Specifies domains to be excluded from the search results, refining the scope of the search.

inputs.name: keep_looking_limit
inputs.description: Sets a limit on the number of times the search will attempt to find more results beyond the initial set, affecting the thoroughness of the search.

outputs.name: documents
outputs.description: A collection of documents retrieved as a result of the search, providing structured insights.

outputs.name: urls
outputs.description: A list of URLs corresponding to the documents found, offering direct links to the source material.

LLMTrafilaturaWebReader.description: The LLMTrafilaturaWebReader node is designed to extract content from web pages using the Trafilatura library. It accepts up to four URLs as input and returns the extracted content as documents, facilitating the processing of web-based information for further analysis or consumption.

inputs.name: url_i
inputs.description: unknown

outputs.name: documents
outputs.description: The extracted content from the specified web pages, returned as documents for easy integration into downstream processes.

LLMTrafilaturaWebReaderAdv.description: The LLMTrafilaturaWebReaderAdv node is designed to extract content from web pages provided as a list of URLs. It validates the URLs and uses the Trafilatura library to efficiently scrape and process web content, returning it in a structured document format.

inputs.name: urls
inputs.description: A list of URLs from which the content is to be extracted. This parameter is essential for the node's operation as it defines the sources of the web content to be processed.

outputs.name: documents
outputs.description: The structured content extracted from the provided web pages, returned as documents.

LLMTreeIndex.description: The LLMTreeIndex node is designed to construct an index structure from a set of language model nodes, facilitating efficient querying and retrieval of information. It supports customization of the indexing process through parameters that control the depth and breadth of the tree, as well as the option to include additional context for more nuanced indexing.

inputs.name: llm_model
inputs.description: Specifies the language model to be used for indexing, serving as the foundation for constructing the tree index.

inputs.name: llm_nodes
inputs.description: Defines the set of nodes to be indexed, representing the data structure that the tree index will organize and make searchable.

inputs.name: service_context
inputs.description: Optional context provided to tailor the indexing process to specific service requirements, enhancing the relevance of the index.

inputs.name: num_children
inputs.description: Determines the maximum number of child nodes each node in the tree can have, influencing the tree's breadth.

inputs.name: build_tree
inputs.description: Flag to control whether the tree structure should be constructed, allowing for flexibility in how the index is generated.

outputs.name: llm_index
outputs.description: The resulting index structure, optimized for efficient querying and retrieval within the specified language model context.

LLMUnstructuredReader.description: The LLMUnstructuredReader node is designed to read and process unstructured files, converting them into a format suitable for indexing and further analysis by the llama_index system. It supports a variety of file types, making it a versatile tool for ingesting raw data into structured document formats.

inputs.name: path
inputs.description: Specifies the file path to the unstructured file that needs to be read. It is crucial for locating and accessing the file for processing.

inputs.name: split_documents
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether the input file should be split into multiple documents based on certain criteria. This affects how the data is segmented and structured.

inputs.name: extra_info
inputs.description: An optional string containing additional information or parameters in JSON format that can be used to customize the reading process.

outputs.name: documents
outputs.description: The processed data from the unstructured file, structured as a document or a list of documents, ready for indexing and analysis.

LLMVectorStoreIndex.description: This node is designed to create and manage a vector store index for language models, facilitating efficient storage, retrieval, and manipulation of vectorized representations of text data. It abstracts the complexities involved in handling large-scale vector data, optimizing for performance and scalability.

inputs.name: llm_model
inputs.description: Specifies the language model to be used for generating vector representations. It is crucial for determining the embedding model that will vectorize the text data.

inputs.name: document
inputs.description: The text document or a collection of documents to be indexed. This input is essential for generating the vector representations that will be stored in the index.

inputs.name: optional_llm_context
inputs.description: An optional context parameter that can be used to provide additional information or settings to the language model during the indexing process.

outputs.name: llm_index
outputs.description: The generated vector store index, which can be used for subsequent retrieval and manipulation of the vectorized text data.

LLMVectorStoreIndexAdv.description: The LLMVectorStoreIndexAdv node is designed for advanced vector storage indexing within a language model framework. It extends the capabilities of standard vector indexing by incorporating additional features or optimizations tailored for complex language processing tasks. This node is pivotal for enhancing the efficiency and accuracy of retrieving and managing vectorized representations of text data in large-scale language models.

inputs.name: llm_model
inputs.description: Specifies the language model to be used for indexing, serving as the core component for generating vector representations of text.

inputs.name: document
inputs.description: The text document to be indexed, which is processed to generate its vector representation.

inputs.name: chunk_size
inputs.description: Defines the size of text chunks for processing, allowing for customization of indexing granularity.

inputs.name: chunk_overlap
inputs.description: Determines the overlap between consecutive text chunks to ensure continuity in the indexing process.

inputs.name: optional_llm_context
inputs.description: Provides additional context from a language model to enhance the indexing accuracy.

outputs.name: llm_index
outputs.description: The result of the indexing process, representing the vectorized form of the input document.

LLMVideoAudioReader.description: The LLMVideoAudioReader node specializes in reading multimedia files, specifically Mp3 and Mp4 formats, and extracting audio transcripts to create a structured document. This process enables the integration of multimedia content into text-based data analysis and processing workflows.

inputs.name: path
inputs.description: Specifies the file path to the Mp3 or Mp4 file to be processed. This path is essential for locating and accessing the file for transcript extraction.

inputs.name: extra_info
inputs.description: Provides additional, optional information that can be used to influence the processing of the multimedia file. This could include parameters for audio processing or metadata to be included in the output document.

outputs.name: documents
outputs.description: The output is a structured document containing the extracted audio transcript from the input multimedia file. This document is ready for further processing or analysis.

LLMXMLReader.description: The LLMXMLReader node specializes in reading XML files and converting them into a format suitable for further processing or analysis within the llama_index ecosystem. It leverages the XMLReader base to parse XML documents, enriching them with optional additional information if provided.

inputs.name: path
inputs.description: Specifies the filesystem path to the XML file to be read. This is a crucial input as it determines the source document for processing.

inputs.name: extra_info
inputs.description: Allows for the inclusion of additional, user-defined information that can be utilized during the reading process, offering a way to pass extra context or directives.

outputs.name: documents
outputs.description: Outputs the processed document in a format that is compatible with the llama_index ecosystem, ready for further analysis or manipulation.

LLMYamlComposer.description: The LLMYamlComposer node is designed to generate YAML documents from given text inputs, utilizing specified classifiers and any additional directions provided. It abstracts the complexity of YAML composition, leveraging language models to ensure the output is correctly formatted and comprehensive.

inputs.name: llm_model
inputs.description: Specifies the language model to use for generating the YAML document. It plays a crucial role in interpreting the input text and classifiers to produce a well-structured YAML output.

inputs.name: text_input
inputs.description: The primary text input from which the YAML document will be generated. This input forms the basis of the content that will be structured into YAML format.

inputs.name: classifier_list
inputs.description: A comma-separated list of classifiers that guide the language model in structuring the input text into a YAML document. These classifiers help in categorizing and organizing the data more effectively.

inputs.name: extra_directions
inputs.description: Additional instructions to further guide the language model in generating the YAML document. This allows for more tailored and specific YAML outputs.

outputs.name: yaml_output
outputs.description: The generated YAML document, structured and formatted based on the input text, classifiers, and any additional directions provided.

LLMYamlRepair.description: The LLMYamlRepair node is designed to inspect and correct malformed YAML content, ensuring its validity and proper formatting without data loss, guided by optional additional directions.

inputs.name: llm_model
inputs.description: Specifies the language model to use for repairing the YAML, central to interpreting and correcting the malformed input.

inputs.name: text_input
inputs.description: The malformed YAML content to be repaired, serving as the primary input for analysis and correction.

inputs.name: extra_directions
inputs.description: Optional instructions to guide the repair process, allowing for customization of the repair strategy.

outputs.name: yaml_output
outputs.description: The corrected and valid YAML content, resulting from the repair process.

SaltExportCaptions.description: The `SaltExportCaptions` node is designed for exporting pairs of images and their corresponding captions to a specified folder. It ensures that each image is saved alongside its caption in a text file, facilitating organized storage and retrieval of visual-textual data.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: A list of images to be exported. Each image is processed and saved in the specified folder along with its caption.

inputs.name: captions
inputs.description: A list of text captions corresponding to the images. Each caption is saved in a text file named after its image.

inputs.name: folder
inputs.description: The name of the folder where the images and captions will be exported. If the folder does not exist, it will be created.

SendMessage.description: The SendMessage node facilitates communication between agents by allowing one agent to send a message to another. It abstracts the complexities of agent interaction, ensuring messages are delivered and processed correctly.

inputs.name: recipient
inputs.description: Specifies the agent receiving the message. It plays a crucial role in determining the message's destination.

inputs.name: sender
inputs.description: Identifies the agent sending the message. It is essential for tracking the source of the message and for potential reply mechanisms.

inputs.name: message
inputs.description: Contains the text of the message being sent. This parameter is vital for the communication process, allowing agents to exchange information.

outputs.name: recipient
outputs.description: The recipient agent, potentially modified after receiving the message.

outputs.name: sender
outputs.description: The sender agent, potentially modified after sending the message.

SimpleChat.description: SimpleChat facilitates one-on-one chat simulations between two conversable agents, allowing for the initiation of dialogues, the application of summary methods to chat histories, and the option to clear or maintain chat history for subsequent interactions. It abstracts the complexities of chat initiation and management, providing a straightforward interface for simulating realistic chat interactions.

inputs.name: initiator
inputs.description: Represents the initiating conversable agent in the chat, setting the stage for the dialogue's commencement.

inputs.name: recipient
inputs.description: Denotes the recipient conversable agent, who responds to the initiator's messages, completing the two-way communication setup.

inputs.name: summary_method
inputs.description: Specifies the method used to summarize the chat history, impacting the way the conversation's essence is captured and presented.

inputs.name: clear_history
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether to clear the chat history before starting a new chat session, affecting the continuity of conversations.

inputs.name: init_message
inputs.description: The initial message to start the chat with, setting the tone and context for the ensuing dialogue.

inputs.name: max_turns
inputs.description: Limits the number of turns the chat can take, controlling the conversation's length and flow.

outputs.name: chat_history
