outputs.description: The output is a collection of images with the background removed. Each image in the collection has been processed to isolate the foreground elements.

Image Remove Background (Alpha).description: This node specializes in removing the background from images, utilizing various techniques to distinguish between foreground and background elements. It offers flexibility in handling different scenarios through parameters like mode, threshold, and smoothing, aiming to produce images with transparent backgrounds or altered backgrounds according to the specified requirements.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The input image or images to process. This parameter is crucial as it serves as the base for background removal operations, determining the node's execution path and the quality of the output.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Specifies the operation mode, such as removing the background or altering it. This parameter influences the approach taken for processing the image, affecting the outcome significantly.

inputs.name: threshold
inputs.description: A value used to differentiate between the background and foreground, playing a key role in determining which parts of the image are retained or removed.

inputs.name: threshold_tolerance
inputs.description: Defines the tolerance level for the threshold, allowing for finer control over the differentiation between background and foreground. This parameter helps in adjusting the sensitivity of the background removal process.

outputs.name: images
outputs.description: The processed image or images with the background removed or altered, depending on the mode and parameters used. This output is essential for applications requiring images with transparent or customized backgrounds.

Image Remove Color.description: The node is designed to selectively remove a specific color from an image, replacing it with another color. It operates by comparing each pixel's color to the target color within a defined threshold, effectively filtering out the target color and substituting it with a predefined replacement color. This functionality is useful for tasks such as background removal or color correction in images.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image from which a specific color is to be removed. It serves as the primary data for the node's operation, determining the visual content that will undergo color removal and replacement.

inputs.name: target_red
inputs.description: Specifies the red component of the target color to be removed from the image. It determines the red value of the color that the node will seek to filter out.

inputs.name: target_green
inputs.description: Specifies the green component of the target color to be removed from the image. It determines the green value of the color that the node will seek to filter out.

inputs.name: target_blue
inputs.description: Specifies the blue component of the target color to be removed from the image. It determines the blue value of the color that the node will seek to filter out.

inputs.name: replace_red
inputs.description: Specifies the red component of the replacement color. This color will fill the areas where the target color has been removed.

inputs.name: replace_green
inputs.description: Specifies the green component of the replacement color. This color will fill the areas where the target color has been removed.

inputs.name: replace_blue
inputs.description: Specifies the blue component of the replacement color. This color will fill the areas where the target color has been removed.

inputs.name: clip_threshold
inputs.description: Defines the sensitivity of the color comparison, determining how closely a pixel's color must match the target color to be replaced. A lower threshold means a stricter match is required, while a higher threshold allows for more variation in the colors that are considered a match.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image after the specified color has been removed and replaced with the replacement color. This image reflects the changes made during the color removal process, showcasing the effect of the target color's substitution.

Image Resize.description: The Image Resize node is designed to modify the dimensions of an input image according to specified parameters. It supports various resizing modes, including scaling, rescaling, and cropping, to accommodate different image processing needs. This node can also apply supersampling for higher quality resizing and adjust the image size to meet specific width and height requirements, making it versatile for a range of image manipulation tasks.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be resized. This image undergoes transformations based on the specified mode and parameters, affecting the final output dimensions and quality.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Specifies the resizing mode, such as 'scale', 'rescale', or a cropping method. This determines how the image dimensions are adjusted.

inputs.name: supersample
inputs.description: Indicates whether supersampling should be applied to the image for higher quality resizing.

inputs.name: resampling
inputs.description: The resampling filter used during resizing, such as 'bicubic' or 'lanczos', affecting the quality of the resized image.

inputs.name: rescale_factor
inputs.description: The scaling factor used when the mode is set to 'rescale', determining how much the image dimensions are increased or decreased.

inputs.name: resize_width
inputs.description: The target width of the image after resizing. It ensures the final width is a multiple of 8 for optimal processing.

inputs.name: resize_height
inputs.description: The target height of the image after resizing. It ensures the final height is a multiple of 8 for optimal processing.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The resized version of the input image, adjusted according to the specified parameters and mode.

Image Rotate Hue.description: This node is designed to adjust the hue of an image by applying a specified hue shift within a valid range. It ensures the hue shift stays within acceptable bounds and applies the shift to each pixel, effectively rotating the hue of the entire image.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to which the hue rotation will be applied. This image is transformed to ensure compatibility with the hue rotation process.

inputs.name: hue_shift
inputs.description: The degree of hue shift to apply to the image, constrained within a specified range to ensure valid hue rotation.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image with the applied hue rotation, reflecting the specified hue shift across all pixels.

Image Rotate.description: The Image Rotate node is designed to rotate a batch of images to a specified angle, with options for different rotation modes and sampling methods. It ensures that rotations are constrained within a 360-degree range and supports adjustments to the rotation angle for more precise control. This node caters to both internal and external rotation modes, offering flexibility in how images are transformed.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: A batch of images to be rotated. This parameter is crucial as it provides the raw visual data that the node will process and transform according to the specified rotation parameters.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Specifies the rotation mode, either 'internal' for direct rotation or an alternative mode that involves transposing the image. This affects how the image is rotated and transformed.

inputs.name: rotation
inputs.description: The angle in degrees to rotate the images. This parameter directly influences the final orientation of the processed images.

inputs.name: sampler
inputs.description: Defines the sampling method used during rotation, such as 'nearest', 'bicubic', or 'bilinear'. This affects the quality and appearance of the rotated images.

outputs.name: images
outputs.description: The batch of rotated images, returned as a tensor. This output represents the transformed visual data after applying the specified rotation and sampling methods.

Image Save.description: The `Image Save` node is designed for saving a collection of images to a specified directory, with options for naming, formatting, and additional metadata. It provides flexibility in how images are stored, including support for history tracking and embedding workflow information within the saved files.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: A collection of images to be saved. This parameter is central to the node's operation, determining the content that will be stored on disk.

inputs.name: output_path
inputs.description: The directory where the images will be saved. It allows for organizing saved images in a structured manner.

inputs.name: filename_prefix
inputs.description: A prefix added to the filenames of saved images, aiding in their identification and categorization.

inputs.name: filename_delimiter
inputs.description: The delimiter used between the filename prefix and the numbering in the saved file names, aiding in file organization and readability.

inputs.name: filename_number_padding
inputs.description: The number of digits to use for numbering files, ensuring consistent filename lengths and facilitating sorting.

inputs.name: filename_number_start
inputs.description: The starting number for filename numbering, enabling sequential organization of saved images.

inputs.name: extension
inputs.description: The file format in which the images will be saved, such as PNG or JPEG, affecting the image's quality and compatibility.

inputs.name: quality
inputs.description: The quality setting for saved images, applicable to formats like JPEG. It influences the balance between file size and image fidelity.

inputs.name: lossless_webp
inputs.description: A flag indicating whether to save images in the WebP format with lossless compression, optimizing for image quality preservation.

inputs.name: overwrite_mode
inputs.description: Controls how the node handles existing files with the same name, allowing for overwriting, skipping, or generating unique names.

inputs.name: show_history
inputs.description: A flag to display the saving history of images, providing insights into the node's operation over time.

inputs.name: show_history_by_prefix
inputs.description: Determines whether to group and display image saving history by filename prefix, aiding in the review of related images.

inputs.name: embed_workflow
inputs.description: A flag to embed workflow information within saved images, linking them to their generation context.

inputs.name: show_previews
inputs.description: Enables the display of image previews during the saving process, offering immediate visual feedback.

Image Seamless Texture.description: The node is designed to transform an input image into a seamless texture. It can optionally tile the texture across a specified number of tiles, blending the edges to ensure the texture can be repeated without visible seams. This functionality is particularly useful for creating backgrounds or textures that need to be repeated across larger surfaces without noticeable discontinuities.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The images to be transformed into seamless textures. This input is crucial as it directly influences the texture's final appearance and seamless quality.

inputs.name: blending
inputs.description: Determines the degree of blending at the edges of the texture, affecting how seamlessly the texture tiles. A higher value results in more blending, making the seams less noticeable.

inputs.name: tiled
inputs.description: A boolean indicating whether the texture should be tiled. If true, the texture is repeated across the specified number of tiles, enhancing the seamless effect.

inputs.name: tiles
inputs.description: Specifies the number of tiles the texture is divided into, both horizontally and vertically. This parameter is only relevant if tiling is enabled and directly affects the texture's repetitiveness and seamless nature.

outputs.name: images
outputs.description: The resulting seamless texture, which can be tiled across surfaces without visible seams. This output is essential for applications requiring repetitive background textures or materials.

Image Select Channel.description: This node is designed to isolate and extract a specific color channel (red, green, or blue) from an input image, converting the selected channel into a greyscale image that is then recombined into a three-channel image where all channels are the same, effectively filtering the image through the lens of the selected color channel.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed. It is the primary data on which the channel selection operation is performed.

inputs.name: channel
inputs.description: Specifies the color channel ('red', 'green', or 'blue') to isolate from the input image. This selection determines which channel of the image will be extracted and processed.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is an image where the selected color channel has been isolated and converted into a greyscale image, then recombined into a three-channel image.

Image Select Color.description: This node is designed to filter and highlight pixels within a specified color range in an image. It allows users to select a color by specifying RGB values and a variance, then creates a new image highlighting only those pixels that fall within the defined color range. This functionality is useful for tasks such as color-based segmentation or identifying objects of a specific color within an image.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed. The node will highlight pixels within the specified color range of this image.

inputs.name: red
inputs.description: The red component of the target color. This value, along with the specified variance, defines the range of red values to be highlighted in the image.

inputs.name: green
inputs.description: The green component of the target color. This value, along with the specified variance, defines the range of green values to be highlighted in the image.

inputs.name: blue
inputs.description: The blue component of the target color. This value, along with the specified variance, defines the range of blue values to be highlighted in the image.

inputs.name: variance
inputs.description: The allowed variance from the specified RGB values. This defines the tolerance for what is considered a match to the target color, allowing for slight variations.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image where only pixels within the specified color range are highlighted. Pixels outside this range are set to black, focusing attention on the selected color.

Image Shadows and Highlights.description: This node is designed to adjust the shadows and highlights within an image, enhancing its visual quality by modifying the intensity of its darker and lighter areas. It leverages advanced image processing techniques to isolate and manipulate these regions, offering a refined control over the image's contrast and overall appearance.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be processed. This image will undergo adjustments to its shadows and highlights based on the specified thresholds and factors, significantly altering its visual dynamics.

inputs.name: shadow_threshold
inputs.description: Defines the intensity threshold below which pixels are considered shadows. Adjusting this value allows for more precise control over which areas of the image are darkened.

inputs.name: shadow_factor
inputs.description: Determines the degree to which the shadows in the image are darkened or lightened. A higher factor increases the intensity of the shadows.

inputs.name: shadow_smoothing
inputs.description: Applies a smoothing effect to the shadow regions, reducing harsh edges and creating a more natural transition.

inputs.name: highlight_threshold
inputs.description: Defines the intensity threshold above which pixels are considered highlights. Adjusting this value allows for more precise control over which areas of the image are brightened.

inputs.name: highlight_factor
inputs.description: Determines the degree to which the highlights in the image are brightened or dimmed. A higher factor increases the intensity of the highlights.

inputs.name: highlight_smoothing
inputs.description: Applies a smoothing effect to the highlight regions, reducing harsh edges and creating a more natural transition.

inputs.name: simplify_isolation
inputs.description: Controls the simplification of the isolation process for shadows and highlights, potentially improving performance at the cost of precision.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The processed image with adjusted shadows and highlights, reflecting the specified modifications to enhance visual quality.

outputs.name: shadow_map
outputs.description: A tensor representing the isolated shadows within the original image, adjusted according to the specified parameters.

outputs.name: highlight_map
outputs.description: A tensor representing the isolated highlights within the original image, adjusted according to the specified parameters.

Image Size to Number.description: This node is designed to convert the dimensions of an image into numerical values, providing both integer and floating-point representations of the image's width and height.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image for which the width and height are to be determined and converted into numerical values.

outputs.name: width_num
outputs.description: The width of the image as a numerical value.

outputs.name: height_num
outputs.description: The height of the image as a numerical value.

outputs.name: width_float
outputs.description: The width of the image represented as a floating-point number.

outputs.name: height_float
outputs.description: The height of the image represented as a floating-point number.

outputs.name: width_int
outputs.description: The width of the image represented as an integer.

outputs.name: height_int
outputs.description: The height of the image represented as an integer.

Image SSAO (Ambient Occlusion).description: This node specializes in enhancing the realism of images by simulating the way light interacts with objects in a scene, particularly in areas where objects block ambient light, creating soft shadows known as ambient occlusion. It processes images and depth information to add depth and dimensionality, improving visual quality and realism.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: A collection of images to be processed for ambient occlusion effects. These images serve as the base for the occlusion calculations, determining where shadows and highlights are added to enhance depth and realism.

inputs.name: depth_images
inputs.description: Corresponding depth images for each image in the 'images' list. These depth maps are crucial for calculating how light interacts with the objects in the scene, influencing the generation of ambient occlusion effects.

inputs.name: strength
inputs.description: Controls the intensity of the ambient occlusion effect. Higher values result in more pronounced shadows, adding greater depth and contrast to the scene.

inputs.name: radius
inputs.description: Determines the spread of the ambient occlusion effect. A larger radius simulates a softer, more diffuse shadow, contributing to a more natural and realistic appearance.

inputs.name: ao_blur
inputs.description: Applies a Gaussian blur to the ambient occlusion effect, softening the shadows and blending them more seamlessly into the image.

inputs.name: specular_threshold
inputs.description: Sets the threshold for specular highlights. This parameter helps in distinguishing between surfaces that are directly lit and those that are not, affecting the application of ambient occlusion.

inputs.name: enable_specular_masking
inputs.description: A boolean flag that, when enabled, applies a mask to the specular highlights, preventing ambient occlusion from affecting highly reflective surfaces. This adds to the realism by ensuring that shiny surfaces retain their characteristic brightness.

inputs.name: tile_size
inputs.description: Determines the processing mode based on its value, affecting the quality and speed of the ambient occlusion effect generation. Smaller values lead to higher quality but slower processing.

outputs.name: composited_images
outputs.description: The final images with the ambient occlusion effect applied, showcasing enhanced depth and realism.

outputs.name: ssao_images
outputs.description: The generated ambient occlusion maps, indicating where shadows have been added to the scene.

outputs.name: specular_mask_images
outputs.description: Specular masks generated during the process, used to preserve the brightness of reflective surfaces by excluding them from the ambient occlusion effect.

Image SSDO (Direct Occlusion).description: This node is designed to simulate the effect of direct occlusion in images, enhancing the realism of 3D scenes by calculating how objects block light sources. It processes a set of images along with their depth information to generate occlusion effects, which can be adjusted for strength, radius, and specular highlights, optionally incorporating colored occlusion for added visual depth.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: A collection of images on which to perform direct occlusion. These images serve as the base for calculating how light interacts with objects, directly affecting the visual outcome of the occlusion effect.

inputs.name: depth_images
inputs.description: Corresponding depth information for each image, used to determine the spatial relationships between objects in the scene. This depth data is crucial for accurately simulating how objects block or allow light to pass, influencing the occlusion effect.

inputs.name: strength
inputs.description: Controls the intensity of the occlusion effect, allowing for fine-tuning of how pronounced the occlusion appears in the final image.

inputs.name: radius
inputs.description: Determines the size of the area around objects affected by occlusion, impacting the softness and spread of shadows.

inputs.name: specular_threshold
inputs.description: Sets the threshold for specular highlights, enabling the simulation of shiny surfaces where light is more likely to reflect.

inputs.name: colored_occlusion
inputs.description: When enabled, applies color to the occlusion effect, adding a layer of visual complexity and realism to the scene.

outputs.name: composited_images
outputs.description: The final images with direct occlusion applied, showcasing enhanced depth and realism through the simulation of light blocking effects.

outputs.name: ssdo_images
outputs.description: The calculated occlusion effects for each image, which can be used for further analysis or processing.

outputs.name: ssdo_image_masks
outputs.description: Masks indicating the areas of each image affected by occlusion, useful for understanding the spatial distribution of the effect.

outputs.name: light_source_image_masks
outputs.description: Identified light sources in the images, which are crucial for accurately simulating the occlusion effect.

Image Stitch.description: The Image Stitch node is designed to seamlessly combine two images together along a specified edge (top, left, bottom, right) with an option for feathering to blend the images smoothly. This node is part of the WAS Suite's image transformation capabilities, enabling creative and technical image manipulation.

inputs.name: image_a
inputs.description: The first image to be stitched. It serves as the base image to which the second image will be stitched.

inputs.name: image_b
inputs.description: The second image to be stitched to the first image. The stitching process combines this image with the first image along a specified edge.

inputs.name: stitch
inputs.description: Specifies the edge along which the second image will be stitched to the first image. Options include 'top', 'left', 'bottom', and 'right'.

inputs.name: feathering
inputs.description: Determines the amount of feathering applied to the edge where the images are stitched together, allowing for a smoother transition between the two images.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The resulting image after stitching the two input images together along the specified edge with optional feathering.

Image Style Filter.description: This node applies a specific style filter to an image, transforming its appearance to match a chosen aesthetic or visual theme. It leverages the capabilities of the Pilgram library to achieve various stylistic effects, offering a way to creatively alter the visual characteristics of images.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image to which the style filter will be applied. It serves as the primary input for the transformation process, determining the base upon which the style filter operates.

inputs.name: style
inputs.description: The specific style to be applied to the image. This parameter defines the aesthetic or visual theme that the image will be transformed to match, playing a crucial role in the style filtering process.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The transformed image with the applied style filter. This output reflects the visual changes made to the original image, showcasing the new stylistic appearance.

Image Threshold.description: The Image Threshold node is designed to process images by applying a thresholding technique, converting them into binary images based on a specified threshold value. This operation is fundamental in image processing tasks where distinguishing between foreground and background is necessary.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The 'image' parameter represents the input image to be thresholded. It plays a crucial role in the thresholding process as the source on which the threshold will be applied.

inputs.name: threshold
inputs.description: The 'threshold' parameter determines the cutoff value for converting the grayscale image into a binary image. It directly influences the outcome of the thresholding process by specifying the intensity level at which pixels are classified as either foreground or background.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is a binary image where pixels are either set to the maximum value (representing the foreground) or zero (representing the background), based on the applied threshold.

Image Tiled.description: This node is designed to process an image by dividing it into a specified number of smaller, equally-sized tiles. It aims to facilitate image analysis or manipulation tasks that benefit from focusing on smaller sections of an image at a time.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be tiled. This parameter is crucial as it determines the source image that will be divided into smaller tiles.

inputs.name: num_tiles
inputs.description: Specifies the number of tiles the input image should be divided into. This parameter directly influences the granularity of the tiling process, affecting both the number and size of the resulting tiles.

outputs.name: IMAGES
outputs.description: The output is a collection of smaller, equally-sized tiles derived from the input image. These tiles can be individually analyzed or manipulated further.

Image to Latent Mask.description: This node is designed to convert an image into a latent mask representation, facilitating the manipulation and analysis of images in a latent space. It abstracts the complexities of image processing and latent space conversion, providing a streamlined approach to working with image data in advanced computational contexts.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The 'images' parameter represents the input images to be converted into a latent mask. This conversion is crucial for enabling further operations in the latent space, such as blending or compositing with other latent representations.

inputs.name: channel
inputs.description: The 'channel' parameter specifies the color channel ('red', 'green', 'blue', 'alpha') of the input image to be used in the mask creation process. This selection can significantly influence the resulting latent mask by highlighting specific features or areas of interest.

outputs.name: MASKS
outputs.description: The output is a collection of masks derived from the specified image channels. These masks can be utilized in various image manipulation and analysis tasks within a latent space framework.

Image to Noise.description: This node transforms an input image into a noise pattern, incorporating various adjustments to simulate different noise effects. It leverages parameters such as color quantization, brightness modification, and optional gaussian blurring to produce a customized noise visualization. The node facilitates the creation of noise-based visual effects or textures from images, offering a range of customization options to achieve the desired noise pattern.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: Represents the collection of input images to be transformed into noise patterns, serving as the foundation for the noise effect application.

inputs.name: num_colors
inputs.description: Specifies the number of colors to quantize the input image to, affecting the color depth of the noise pattern.

inputs.name: black_mix
inputs.description: Determines the intensity of black pixels mixed into the noise pattern, influencing the pattern's darkness.

inputs.name: gaussian_mix
inputs.description: Controls the level of Gaussian blur applied to the noise pattern, affecting its softness.

inputs.name: brightness
inputs.description: Adjusts the brightness of the noise pattern, modifying its overall lightness.

inputs.name: output_mode
inputs.description: Specifies the format of the output, either as a batch of images or a list, affecting the structure of the returned noise patterns.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: Sets the seed for random number generation, ensuring reproducibility of the noise pattern.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image transformed into a noise pattern, showcasing the applied noise effect.

Image to Seed.description: This node transforms a collection of images into a corresponding set of numerical seeds. It serves as a bridge between visual content and numerical representations, enabling further processing or analysis based on these derived seeds.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The collection of images to be transformed into seeds. This input is crucial for generating a numerical representation that encapsulates the essence of the visual content.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: A list of integers, each representing a seed derived from the corresponding input image. These seeds serve as numerical representations of the images, facilitating further computational tasks.

Image Transpose.description: The Image Overlay node is designed to overlay one image onto another with specified dimensions, location, rotation, and feathering options. It enables complex image composition tasks, allowing for precise control over how images are combined and manipulated.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The 'image' parameter represents the base image onto which the overlay will be applied. It is fundamental in defining the canvas for the transformation.

inputs.name: image_overlay
inputs.description: The 'image_overlay' parameter specifies the image to be overlaid on the base image. This image will undergo transformations and be composited onto the base image.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Specifies the width of the overlay image after resizing, playing a critical role in how the overlay fits onto the base image.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Specifies the height of the overlay image after resizing, crucial for adjusting the overlay's fit on the base image.

inputs.name: X
inputs.description: The X coordinate for the top-left corner of the overlay image on the base image, determining the overlay's horizontal placement.

inputs.name: Y
inputs.description: The Y coordinate for the top-left corner of the overlay image on the base image, determining the overlay's vertical placement.

inputs.name: rotation
inputs.description: Defines the rotation angle of the overlay image, allowing for dynamic orientation adjustments.

inputs.name: feathering
inputs.description: Specifies the feathering radius for the overlay edges, enabling smooth transitions between the overlay and the base image.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output 'image' parameter contains the composited image after applying the specified transformations and overlay operations.

Image Voronoi Noise Filter.description: This node generates a Voronoi noise pattern on an image, leveraging parameters such as density and modulator to influence the visual complexity and style of the noise. It's designed to create visually appealing or useful noise patterns for various applications in image processing and graphics.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Specifies the width of the output image. It determines the horizontal dimension of the generated noise pattern.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Specifies the height of the output image. It affects the vertical dimension of the generated noise pattern.

inputs.name: density
inputs.description: Controls the density of the Voronoi cells in the noise pattern, affecting the overall complexity and appearance of the noise.

inputs.name: modulator
inputs.description: Adjusts the modulation of the noise pattern, allowing for finer control over the visual characteristics of the generated noise.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: Sets the seed for the noise generation algorithm, ensuring reproducibility of the noise patterns.

inputs.name: flat
inputs.description: Determines whether the noise pattern should have a flat appearance, affecting the visual depth of the noise.

inputs.name: RGB_output
inputs.description: Specifies whether the output image should be in RGB color mode, influencing the color information of the generated noise pattern.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The generated image with the Voronoi noise pattern applied. It showcases the visual effects of the input parameters on the noise generation.

Images to Linear.description: The node is designed to convert a batch of images to a linear (grayscale) color space. It processes each image in the input batch, converting it from its original color space to grayscale, and then concatenates the results into a single tensor. This operation is useful for tasks that require uniformity in color space across multiple images, such as certain types of image analysis or preprocessing steps before feeding images into a machine learning model.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The 'images' parameter represents a batch of images that the node will convert to grayscale. This conversion is crucial for tasks that benefit from or require image data in a linear color space, simplifying further processing or analysis.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is a tensor containing the batch of images converted to grayscale. This uniform linear color space is beneficial for various image processing and analysis tasks.

Images to RGB.description: This node is designed to convert a collection of images to the RGB color space, ensuring consistency in color representation across multiple images. It caters to scenarios where images may come in various color formats, standardizing them to RGB for uniform processing or display.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: The collection of images to be converted to the RGB color space. This input is crucial for ensuring that all images undergo a consistent color space transformation, facilitating uniform color representation.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The transformed images, now standardized in the RGB color space, ready for further processing or display.

Inset Image Bounds.description: This node is designed to adjust the boundaries of an image by applying insets, effectively shrinking the image's visible area by specified amounts from each edge. It's useful for creating margins or focusing on central parts of an image without resizing.

inputs.name: image_bounds
inputs.description: Specifies the original boundaries of the image to be inset. It's crucial for determining the new, inset boundaries based on the provided inset values.

inputs.name: inset_left
inputs.description: Defines the amount by which the left boundary of the image is to be inset, reducing the visible width from the left side.

inputs.name: inset_right
inputs.description: Defines the amount by which the right boundary of the image is to be inset, reducing the visible width from the right side.

inputs.name: inset_top
inputs.description: Defines the amount by which the top boundary of the image is to be inset, reducing the visible height from the top.

inputs.name: inset_bottom
inputs.description: Defines the amount by which the bottom boundary of the image is to be inset, reducing the visible height from the bottom.

outputs.name: image_bounds
outputs.description: The new, inset image boundaries after applying the specified insets to each side of the original boundaries.

Integer place counter.description: This node is designed to calculate the number of places in an integer, effectively determining its length. It abstracts the process of converting an integer to a string to count its characters, providing a straightforward way to assess the magnitude of an integer.

inputs.name: int_input
inputs.description: Specifies the integer whose places are to be counted. This input is crucial for determining the length of the integer, which directly influences the node's output.

outputs.name: INT_PLACES
outputs.description: Represents the number of places in the input integer. This output is significant as it quantifies the length of the integer, offering insight into its magnitude.

KSampler (WAS).description: The KSampler node is designed for advanced sampling in generative models, allowing for the customization of the sampling process through various parameters. It integrates with the broader WAS Suite to provide a flexible and powerful tool for generating and manipulating latent representations.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The generative model used for sampling. It's crucial for defining the behavior and output of the sampling process.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: A seed value to ensure reproducibility of the sampling results. It influences the randomness of the generated samples.

inputs.name: steps
inputs.description: The number of steps to perform in the sampling process, affecting the detail and quality of the generated samples.

inputs.name: cfg
inputs.description: A configuration parameter that adjusts the sampling process, allowing for fine-tuning of the generation.

inputs.name: sampler_name
inputs.description: Specifies the particular sampler to use, enabling the selection of different sampling strategies.

inputs.name: scheduler
inputs.description: Determines the scheduling algorithm for the sampling process, impacting how samples evolve over time.

inputs.name: positive
inputs.description: Positive conditioning to guide the sampling towards desired attributes.

inputs.name: negative
inputs.description: Negative conditioning to steer the sampling away from certain attributes.

inputs.name: latent_image
inputs.description: An optional latent image to start the sampling from, allowing for modifications or enhancements of existing images.

inputs.name: denoise
inputs.description: Controls the denoising level in the sampling process, affecting the clarity and sharpness of the generated samples.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The output latent representation generated by the sampling process, which can be further used or transformed.

KSampler Cycle.description: The KSampler Cycle node is designed to perform iterative sampling cycles using a specified sampling strategy. It leverages advanced sampling techniques to generate or modify latent images, incorporating various conditioning and noise parameters to guide the generation process. This node is part of a suite aimed at enhancing image generation capabilities through sophisticated sampling algorithms.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: Specifies the model to be used for sampling, playing a crucial role in determining the quality and characteristics of the generated images.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: The seed parameter ensures reproducibility of the sampling process by initializing the random number generator to a specific state.

inputs.name: steps
inputs.description: Defines the number of steps to be taken in the sampling process, affecting the detail and quality of the generated images.

inputs.name: cfg
inputs.description: Controls the conditioning factor in the sampling process, influencing how strongly the positive and negative conditioning affect the generated images.

inputs.name: sampler_name
inputs.description: Determines the specific sampling algorithm to be used, allowing for customization of the sampling process.

inputs.name: scheduler
inputs.description: Specifies the scheduler to manage the sampling steps, enabling fine-tuning of the sampling dynamics.

inputs.name: positive
inputs.description: Positive conditioning terms to guide the sampling towards desired attributes or features in the generated images.

inputs.name: negative
inputs.description: Negative conditioning terms to steer the sampling away from certain attributes or features, refining the generation process.

inputs.name: latent_image
inputs.description: The initial latent image to be modified or used as a basis for generation in the sampling cycle.

inputs.name: tiled_vae
inputs.description: Enables or disables the use of tiled VAE, affecting the texture and detail of the generated images.

inputs.name: latent_upscale
inputs.description: Specifies the method used for upscaling the latent image, influencing the resolution and quality.

inputs.name: upscale_factor
inputs.description: Determines the factor by which the latent image is upscaled, directly impacting its resolution.

inputs.name: upscale_cycles
inputs.description: Defines the number of cycles for upscaling, affecting the final image quality through iterative refinement.

inputs.name: starting_denoise
inputs.description: Sets the initial denoise level for the sampling process, influencing the clarity of the generated images from the start.

inputs.name: cycle_denoise
inputs.description: Adjusts the denoise level for each cycle, allowing for dynamic control over image clarity throughout the sampling process.

inputs.name: scale_denoise
inputs.description: Enables or disables denoise scaling, affecting the denoise level based on the image scale.

inputs.name: scale_sampling
inputs.description: Determines the sampling method used during scaling, impacting the texture and detail of the upscaled image.

inputs.name: vae
inputs.description: Specifies the VAE model used in the process, crucial for the generation and manipulation of latent images.

inputs.name: secondary_model
inputs.description: Optional secondary model for enhanced sampling or effects, providing additional customization.

inputs.name: secondary_start_cycle
inputs.description: Defines the cycle at which the secondary model begins to be applied, allowing for staged sampling processes.

inputs.name: upscale_model
inputs.description: Specifies the model used for upscaling, impacting the quality and method of image enlargement.

inputs.name: processor_model
inputs.description: Optional processor model for additional image processing or effects during the sampling cycle.

inputs.name: pos_additive
inputs.description: Additional positive conditioning terms, enhancing the guidance towards desired features.

inputs.name: neg_additive
inputs.description: Additional negative conditioning terms, refining the avoidance of certain features.

inputs.name: pos_add_mode
inputs.description: Determines how the additional positive conditioning is applied, affecting its influence on the generation process.

inputs.name: pos_add_strength
inputs.description: Sets the strength of the additional positive conditioning, controlling its impact on the generated images.

inputs.name: pos_add_strength_scaling
inputs.description: Adjusts the scaling of positive conditioning strength, allowing for dynamic influence based on other factors.

inputs.name: pos_add_strength_cutoff
inputs.description: Defines a cutoff for positive conditioning strength, limiting its maximum impact.

inputs.name: neg_add_mode
inputs.description: Determines how the additional negative conditioning is applied, affecting its influence on the generation process.

inputs.name: neg_add_strength
inputs.description: Sets the strength of the additional negative conditioning, controlling its impact on the generated images.

inputs.name: neg_add_strength_scaling
inputs.description: Adjusts the scaling of negative conditioning strength, allowing for dynamic influence based on other factors.

inputs.name: neg_add_strength_cutoff
inputs.description: Defines a cutoff for negative conditioning strength, limiting its maximum impact.

inputs.name: sharpen_strength
inputs.description: Adjusts the strength of image sharpening applied after sampling, affecting image clarity and detail.

inputs.name: sharpen_radius
inputs.description: Determines the radius of the sharpening effect, influencing the extent of detail enhancement.

inputs.name: steps_scaling
inputs.description: Enables or disables scaling of the number of steps based on certain conditions, affecting the sampling process duration.

inputs.name: steps_control
inputs.description: Specifies the control mechanism for dynamically adjusting the number of sampling steps.

inputs.name: steps_scaling_value
inputs.description: Sets the value for scaling the number of steps, directly impacting the sampling process duration.

inputs.name: steps_cutoff
inputs.description: Defines a cutoff for the number of steps, limiting the maximum duration of the sampling process.

inputs.name: denoise_cutoff
inputs.description: Sets a cutoff for denoise level, limiting the maximum amount of denoising applied to the generated images.

outputs.name: latent(s)
outputs.description: unknown

Latent Batch.description: This node is designed to merge two sets of latent representations into a single batch, potentially resizing one set to match the dimensions of the other before concatenation. It plays a crucial role in operations that require combining or comparing different sets of latent data.

inputs.name: latent_a
inputs.description: The first set of latent samples to be batched. It is crucial as it sets the base dimensions for the output batch if resizing is needed.

inputs.name: latent_b
inputs.description: The second set of latent samples to be batched. This set may be resized to match the dimensions of the first set before concatenation.

inputs.name: latent_c
inputs.description: An optional third set of latent samples that can be included in the batch. Similar to the other inputs, it may be resized to ensure consistency in dimensions.

inputs.name: latent_d
inputs.description: An optional fourth set of latent samples for inclusion in the batch. It may also be resized for dimensional consistency with the other sets.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The combined set of latent samples from all input sets, potentially with some sets resized to match others' dimensions.

Latent Input Switch.description: The WAS_Latent_Input_Switch node is designed to toggle between two latent inputs based on a boolean condition, effectively allowing for conditional selection of latent representations.

inputs.name: latent_a
inputs.description: The first latent input to consider for selection. It plays a crucial role in determining the output based on the boolean condition.

inputs.name: latent_b
inputs.description: The second latent input to consider for selection. This input provides an alternative choice for the output, contingent on the boolean condition.

inputs.name: boolean
inputs.description: A boolean flag that determines which latent input (latent_a or latent_b) is selected for output. This parameter is essential for controlling the flow of data based on conditional logic.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The selected latent input based on the boolean condition. This output facilitates conditional logic in processing latent representations.

Latent Noise Injection.description: The Latent Noise Injection node is designed to augment latent representations with stochastic noise. This process can introduce variability and potentially enhance the generative qualities of models by injecting controlled noise into the latent space.

inputs.name: samples
inputs.description: The 'samples' parameter represents the latent representations to which noise will be added. Injecting noise into these samples can help in exploring variations in the generated outputs.

inputs.name: noise_std
inputs.description: The 'noise_std' parameter controls the standard deviation of the noise to be injected, allowing for fine-tuning of the noise intensity for different effects on the latent samples.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The output is a modified version of the input latent samples, now augmented with noise according to the specified standard deviation.

Latent Size to Number.description: The Latent Size to Number node is designed to extract the width and height dimensions of tensors within a given set of samples and convert these dimensions into various numerical formats. It serves the purpose of providing a detailed breakdown of tensor sizes, facilitating operations that require specific dimensional data.

inputs.name: samples
inputs.description: The 'samples' parameter is expected to contain tensors from which the width and height dimensions are to be extracted. This parameter is crucial for the node's operation as it directly influences the output by determining the dimensions to be analyzed and converted.

outputs.name: tensor_w_num
outputs.description: Represents the width of the first tensor in the samples, provided in multiple numerical formats.

outputs.name: tensor_h_num
outputs.description: Represents the height of the first tensor in the samples, provided in multiple numerical formats.

Latent Upscale by Factor (WAS).description: This node specializes in upscaling latent images by a specified factor, utilizing various interpolation methods to enhance the resolution while maintaining the integrity of the original image. It provides flexibility in scaling and alignment options to cater to different upscaling needs.

inputs.name: samples
inputs.description: The latent images to be upscaled. This input is crucial as it determines the base content that will undergo the upscaling process.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Specifies the interpolation method to be used for upscaling, offering options like 'area', 'bicubic', 'bilinear', and 'nearest'. This choice affects the quality and characteristics of the upscaled image.

inputs.name: factor
inputs.description: The scaling factor by which the latent images will be upscaled. A positive float that directly influences the final size of the upscaled images.

inputs.name: align
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether to align corners in certain interpolation modes, affecting the upscaling precision and outcome.

outputs.name: latent
outputs.description: The upscaled latent images, enhanced in resolution according to the specified factor and interpolation method.

Load Cache.description: The 'Load Cache' node is designed to load cached data from specified file paths. It supports loading of latent representations, images, and conditioning data, ensuring efficient reuse of previously computed or stored information. This node is essential for optimizing performance and resource utilization by avoiding redundant computations.

inputs.name: latent_path
inputs.description: Specifies the file path for the latent representation cache. If the file exists, it is loaded; otherwise, an error message is displayed. Providing a valid path allows the node to retrieve and utilize pre-computed latent representations, streamlining the workflow by bypassing the need for re-computation.

inputs.name: image_path
inputs.description: Specifies the file path for the image cache. If the file exists, it is loaded; otherwise, a message is displayed. By loading an existing image from cache, this input enables the node to efficiently reuse visual data, facilitating quicker iterations and resource conservation.

inputs.name: conditioning_path
inputs.description: Specifies the file path for the conditioning data cache. If the file exists, it is loaded; otherwise, an error message is displayed. This input is crucial for accessing pre-defined conditioning data, which can significantly impact the generation process by providing necessary context or constraints.

outputs.name: LATENT
outputs.description: unknown

outputs.name: IMAGE
outputs.description: unknown

outputs.name: CONDITIONING
outputs.description: unknown

Load Image Batch.description: The Load Image Batch node is designed to aggregate multiple images into a single batch tensor. It dynamically combines input images based on provided parameters, facilitating operations that require batch processing of images.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Specifies the loading mode, which can be single or multiple images, affecting how images are aggregated into the batch.

inputs.name: index
inputs.description: Determines the starting index for image loading, enabling partial or staggered batch processing.

inputs.name: label
inputs.description: Assigns a label to the loaded batch, useful for identification and tracking purposes.

inputs.name: path
inputs.description: Specifies the directory path where images are located, serving as the source for batch loading.

inputs.name: pattern
inputs.description: Defines the pattern used to match filenames within the specified path, allowing for selective loading of images.

inputs.name: allow_RGBA_output
inputs.description: Controls whether RGBA images are allowed in the output batch, accommodating images with transparency.

inputs.name: filename_text_extension
inputs.description: Determines whether the filename extension is included in the output, affecting the representation of image names.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The aggregated batch of images, represented as a tensor, ready for further processing or analysis.

outputs.name: filename_text
outputs.description: The text representation of filenames included in the batch, useful for tracking and identification of individual images.

Load Lora.description: The Load Lora node is designed to dynamically enhance the capabilities of machine learning models by applying LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) adjustments. It allows for the fine-tuning of model and clip parameters through the application of pre-trained LoRA adjustments, thereby enabling more precise control over the model's behavior and outputs without the need for extensive retraining.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The original machine learning model to which LoRA adjustments will be applied. It serves as the foundation for the enhancement process.

inputs.name: clip
inputs.description: The clip parameter works alongside the model to receive LoRA adjustments, allowing for a coordinated enhancement of both components.

inputs.name: lora_name
inputs.description: The name of the LoRA adjustment file to be applied. This parameter specifies which pre-trained LoRA adjustments are to be used for enhancing the model and clip.

inputs.name: strength_model
inputs.description: Determines the intensity of the LoRA adjustments applied to the model. It allows for fine-tuning the impact of LoRA on the model's behavior.

inputs.name: strength_clip
inputs.description: Specifies the intensity of the LoRA adjustments applied to the clip parameter, enabling precise control over its enhancement.

outputs.name: MODEL
outputs.description: The enhanced version of the model after the application of LoRA adjustments, reflecting the improved capabilities and fine-tuning achieved.

outputs.name: CLIP
outputs.description: The enhanced version of the clip parameter after the application of LoRA adjustments, showcasing the precise control and improvement.

outputs.name: NAME_STRING
outputs.description: The name of the LoRA adjustment applied, providing a reference to the specific enhancements made.

Load Text File.description: This node is designed to load text from a specified file, processing the text to exclude lines starting with specific characters and handling file path validations. It supports loading the entire file content or specific lines based on the mode selected, and maintains a history of loaded files and their respective lines for efficient data retrieval and manipulation.

inputs.name: file_path
inputs.description: The path to the text file to be loaded. It is crucial for locating and accessing the file's content.

inputs.name: dictionary_name
inputs.description: An optional name for the dictionary key under which the loaded text lines will be stored. It defaults to the filename but can be customized.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The output includes the processed text line(s).

outputs.name: dict
outputs.description: A dictionary mapping the dictionary name to the list of processed lines.

Logic Boolean Primitive.description: The Logic Boolean Primitive node is designed to process a single boolean input and return it unchanged. This node serves as a fundamental building block in logical operations, allowing for the straightforward handling and passing of boolean values within a logic-based workflow.

inputs.name: boolean
inputs.description: The boolean input to be processed. This parameter is crucial as it directly determines the output of the node, effectively making the node act as a pass-through for the boolean value.

outputs.name: boolean
outputs.description: The unchanged boolean input. This output is significant as it allows the boolean value to be used directly in subsequent logical operations or conditions.

Logic Boolean.description: The Logic Boolean node is designed to process boolean inputs, performing basic logical operations or conversions based on the specified function. It abstracts the complexity of boolean logic into simple, reusable components that can be integrated into larger workflows, facilitating decision-making processes and data flow control.

inputs.name: boolean_number
inputs.description: The boolean_number input parameter is crucial for determining the operation's outcome, serving as the primary data upon which logical operations or conversions are performed. Its value directly influences the node's execution and results.

outputs.name: number
outputs.description: The number output represents the numerical result of the logical operation or conversion performed, encapsulating the outcome in a numerical format.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: The int output provides an integer representation of the logical operation or conversion result, further specifying the numerical outcome.

Logic Comparison AND.description: The Logic Comparison AND node performs a logical AND operation on two boolean inputs, returning the result of this operation as a boolean output. This node is part of the WAS Suite/Logic category and is designed to facilitate logical operations within workflows, enabling conditional logic and decision-making based on boolean values.

inputs.name: boolean_a
inputs.description: The first boolean input for the AND operation. Its value significantly influences the outcome, as the operation requires both inputs to be true for a true result.

inputs.name: boolean_b
inputs.description: The second boolean input for the AND operation. Together with boolean_a, it determines the result of the AND operation, which is true only if both inputs are true.

outputs.name: boolean
outputs.description: The boolean result of the logical AND operation between boolean_a and boolean_b.

Logic Comparison OR.description: This node performs a logical OR operation on two boolean inputs, returning true if at least one of the inputs is true, and false otherwise. It abstracts the basic logical OR functionality into a node for use within logical operations or decision-making processes.

inputs.name: boolean_a
inputs.description: The first boolean input for the OR operation. Its value influences the result by potentially making the overall result true if it is true.

inputs.name: boolean_b
inputs.description: The second boolean input for the OR operation. Similar to the first input, its true value can make the overall result true, contributing to the logical OR condition.

outputs.name: boolean
outputs.description: The result of the logical OR operation, indicating whether at least one of the inputs is true.

Logic Comparison XOR.description: This node performs an exclusive logical XOR operation on two boolean inputs, returning true if exactly one of the inputs is true, and false otherwise. It abstracts the concept of non-equivalence or exclusive disjunction in boolean logic, providing a straightforward way to compare two boolean values for exclusivity.

inputs.name: boolean_a
inputs.description: The first boolean value to compare. It plays a crucial role in determining the result of the XOR operation by its exclusivity with the second boolean value.

inputs.name: boolean_b
inputs.description: The second boolean value to compare. It is essential in the XOR operation, working in conjunction with the first boolean value to determine exclusivity.

outputs.name: boolean
outputs.description: The result of the XOR operation, indicating whether exactly one of the input boolean values is true.

Logic NOT.description: The node performs a logical NOT operation on a given boolean input, effectively inverting its value. It's a fundamental component in logical operations, allowing for the negation of boolean conditions.

inputs.name: boolean
inputs.description: The boolean input to be negated. This parameter determines the boolean value that will be inverted by the logical NOT operation.

outputs.name: boolean
outputs.description: The inverted boolean value of the input. If the input is True, the output will be False, and vice versa.

Lora Input Switch.description: The WAS_Lora_Input_Switch node is designed to selectively switch between two sets of model and CLIP inputs based on a boolean condition. It facilitates dynamic input selection for further processing or model application.

inputs.name: model_a
inputs.description: The first model input option. This model is selected if the boolean condition is true.

inputs.name: clip_a
inputs.description: The first CLIP input option. This CLIP is selected if the boolean condition is true.

inputs.name: model_b
inputs.description: The second model input option. This model is selected if the boolean condition is false.

inputs.name: clip_b
inputs.description: The second CLIP input option. This CLIP is selected if the boolean condition is false.

inputs.name: boolean
inputs.description: A boolean condition that determines which set of inputs (model_a and clip_a or model_b and clip_b) is selected.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The selected model based on the boolean condition.

outputs.name: clip
outputs.description: The selected CLIP based on the boolean condition.

Lora Loader.description: The LoraLoader node is designed to dynamically load and apply LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) adjustments to given models and CLIP instances, enhancing their capabilities or altering their behavior based on specified LoRA parameters and strengths.

inputs.name: model
inputs.description: The model to which the LoRA adjustments will be applied. It's crucial for defining the base architecture that will be enhanced or modified.

inputs.name: clip
inputs.description: The CLIP instance to which the LoRA adjustments will be applied, allowing for modifications in its behavior or performance.

inputs.name: lora_name
inputs.description: The name of the LoRA file containing the adjustments to be applied. It determines the specific LoRA modifications that will be loaded and applied.

inputs.name: strength_model
inputs.description: Defines the intensity of the LoRA adjustments applied to the model. It influences how significantly the model's behavior is altered.

inputs.name: strength_clip
inputs.description: Defines the intensity of the LoRA adjustments applied to the CLIP instance. It influences how significantly the CLIP's behavior is altered.

outputs.name: MODEL
outputs.description: The model with applied LoRA adjustments, reflecting enhanced or altered capabilities.

outputs.name: CLIP
outputs.description: The CLIP instance with applied LoRA adjustments, reflecting modifications in behavior or performance.

outputs.name: NAME_STRING
outputs.description: The name of the LoRA file applied, providing a reference to the specific adjustments made.

Mask Arbitrary Region.description: This node is designed to process image masks by applying an arbitrary region masking technique. It adjusts the regions within the masks based on specified size and threshold parameters, effectively altering the mask's focus or coverage area.

inputs.name: masks
inputs.description: The input masks to be processed. These masks are adjusted to focus on arbitrary regions based on the given size and threshold.

inputs.name: size
inputs.description: Specifies the size of the region to focus on within each mask. It influences the scale of the region being highlighted or suppressed.

inputs.name: threshold
inputs.description: Determines the intensity threshold for selecting which parts of the mask to include in the arbitrary region. It affects the mask's detail level and the region's prominence.

outputs.name: MASKS
outputs.description: The processed masks with arbitrary regions applied, reflecting the specified size and threshold adjustments.

Mask Batch to Mask.description: This node is designed to extract a single mask from a batch of masks based on a specified batch number. It facilitates the selection and isolation of a specific mask from a collection, enabling focused operations on a singular mask element within a broader batch context.

inputs.name: masks
inputs.description: The collection of masks from which a single mask is to be extracted. It plays a crucial role in determining the specific mask to isolate based on the batch number.

inputs.name: batch_number
inputs.description: Specifies the index of the mask to be extracted from the batch. It determines which mask is isolated and returned as the output.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The single mask extracted from the specified batch position. It represents the isolated mask element for further processing or analysis.

Mask Batch.description: The Mask Batch node is designed to aggregate individual mask tensors into a single batched tensor. This node is essential for operations that require batch processing of masks, such as applying transformations or models to multiple masks simultaneously. It ensures that all input masks are combined into a unified batch format, adding a channel dimension for compatibility with subsequent processing steps.

inputs.name: masks_a
inputs.description: Represents one of the individual mask tensors to be batched together. It is a crucial component for the node's operation, contributing to the aggregated batched tensor for further processing.

inputs.name: masks_b
inputs.description: Represents another individual mask tensor to be included in the batch. It is essential for compiling multiple masks into a single batch for processing.

inputs.name: masks_c
inputs.description: An optional mask tensor that can be included in the batch. It adds flexibility to the batching process by allowing for additional masks.

inputs.name: masks_d
inputs.description: Another optional mask tensor that can be included in the batch, further enhancing the node's capability to process multiple masks simultaneously.

outputs.name: masks
outputs.description: The output represents the aggregated batch of mask tensors, now in a format that is compatible with further processing steps.

Mask Ceiling Region.description: This node specializes in identifying and isolating the ceiling regions within given mask images. It leverages specific image processing techniques to discern and extract the ceiling areas, making it a valuable tool for tasks requiring focused analysis or manipulation of ceiling elements in images.

inputs.name: masks
inputs.description: The input masks represent the images from which the ceiling regions are to be extracted. These masks are crucial for the node's operation as they serve as the basis for identifying and isolating ceiling areas.

outputs.name: MASKS
outputs.description: The output is a tensor of masks specifically highlighting the ceiling regions within the original input images. This allows for targeted analysis or manipulation of these areas.

Mask Crop Dominant Region.description: This node is designed to identify and extract the dominant region from a given set of masks, applying a specified padding around the cropped area. It leverages image processing techniques to focus on the most significant part of the image, enhancing the relevance of the extracted region.

inputs.name: masks
inputs.description: The input masks from which the dominant region is to be cropped. It plays a crucial role in determining the area of interest within the image.

inputs.name: padding
inputs.description: Specifies the padding to be applied around the cropped dominant region, allowing for adjustable margins around the extracted area.

outputs.name: MASKS
outputs.description: The output consists of the cropped dominant regions from the input masks, potentially with applied padding.

Mask Crop Minority Region.description: This node focuses on isolating and cropping the smallest detected region within a given mask, applying optional padding to the cropped area. It leverages image processing techniques to identify minority regions in masks, enhancing the focus on less prominent features by cropping around them.

inputs.name: masks
inputs.description: The input masks on which the minority region cropping operation is to be performed. This parameter is crucial for determining the specific area to be isolated and cropped, directly influencing the output based on the mask's content.

inputs.name: padding
inputs.description: An optional parameter that specifies the amount of padding to add around the cropped minority region. This affects the final size of the cropped area, allowing for adjustments in the focus area's boundary.

outputs.name: MASKS
outputs.description: The output is a tensor representing the cropped minority region of the input mask, potentially with added padding. This tensor highlights the least prominent area within the original mask, focusing on details that might otherwise be overlooked.

Mask Crop Region.description: The node focuses on cropping a specified region from a given mask, based on the region type (dominant or minority) and an optional padding. It aims to extract and highlight specific areas within masks, enhancing the focus on regions of interest.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The mask input represents the image mask from which a specific region is to be cropped. It plays a crucial role in determining the area of interest for cropping.

inputs.name: padding
inputs.description: Padding specifies the additional space to be added around the cropped region. It allows for more flexibility in the size of the output region, potentially including more context around the targeted area.

inputs.name: region_type
inputs.description: The region type determines whether the dominant or minority region within the mask is to be cropped. This choice directs the cropping process towards areas of major or minor presence, respectively.

outputs.name: cropped_mask
outputs.description: The cropped mask is the result of the cropping operation, containing the specified region of interest from the original mask.

outputs.name: crop_data
outputs.description: Crop data provides detailed information about the dimensions and coordinates of the cropped region, facilitating further processing or analysis.

outputs.name: top_int
outputs.description: The top boundary coordinate of the cropped region.

outputs.name: left_int
outputs.description: The left boundary coordinate of the cropped region.

outputs.name: right_int
outputs.description: The right boundary coordinate of the cropped region.

outputs.name: bottom_int
outputs.description: The bottom boundary coordinate of the cropped region.

outputs.name: width_int
outputs.description: The width of the cropped region.

outputs.name: height_int
outputs.description: The height of the cropped region.

Mask Dilate Region.description: This node is designed to dilate regions within given masks, effectively expanding the areas of interest. It utilizes iterations to control the extent of dilation, allowing for precise adjustments to the mask's features.

inputs.name: masks
inputs.description: The input masks to be dilated. This parameter is crucial for defining the areas within the image that will undergo dilation.

inputs.name: iterations
inputs.description: Specifies the number of times the dilation operation is applied, directly influencing the degree of expansion for the mask's regions.

outputs.name: MASKS
outputs.description: The output consists of dilated masks, where the specified regions have been expanded according to the number of iterations.

Mask Dominant Region.description: This node is designed to identify and isolate the dominant region within a given set of masks based on a specified threshold. It effectively filters out less significant areas, focusing on the most prominent region as determined by pixel intensity and area size.

inputs.name: masks
inputs.description: The input masks on which the dominant region detection is to be performed. This parameter is crucial for identifying the area of interest within the provided images.

inputs.name: threshold
inputs.description: A value that determines the cutoff intensity for considering a region as dominant. It plays a key role in distinguishing between the significant and insignificant areas within the masks.

outputs.name: MASKS
outputs.description: The output consists of masks with the dominant region highlighted, effectively isolating the most significant area from the rest of the image.

Mask Erode Region.description: The node is designed to perform erosion on specified mask regions, effectively shrinking the mask areas based on the number of iterations specified. This operation is useful for refining mask boundaries or reducing noise in mask regions.

inputs.name: masks
inputs.description: The input masks to be eroded. This parameter is crucial for determining the regions within the image that will undergo the erosion process.

inputs.name: iterations
inputs.description: Specifies the number of times the erosion operation is applied to the mask regions. A higher number of iterations results in more pronounced erosion.

outputs.name: MASKS
outputs.description: The eroded mask regions as a result of applying the erosion operation specified by the iterations parameter.

Mask Fill Holes.description: This node is designed to fill in the regions of a mask where there are holes, effectively creating a more solid and continuous mask area. It operates on mask inputs, applying a filling operation to ensure that any gaps or holes within the mask are filled, enhancing the mask's integrity for further image processing tasks.

inputs.name: masks
inputs.description: The 'masks' input represents the mask or masks to be filled. It is crucial for determining which areas of the image need to be processed to fill in the gaps or holes, directly influencing the node's output by specifying the target regions for the fill operation.

outputs.name: MASKS
outputs.description: The output 'MASKS' consists of the processed masks with filled regions, providing a more continuous and solid mask area for subsequent image manipulation or analysis tasks.

Mask Floor Region.description: The Mask Floor Region node is designed to process input masks and apply a specific floor region masking operation. This operation identifies and isolates the floor regions within the given masks, transforming them into a format suitable for further analysis or processing.

inputs.name: masks
inputs.description: The 'masks' parameter represents the input masks on which the floor region detection and isolation will be performed. It is crucial for identifying the specific areas within the images that correspond to floor regions.

outputs.name: MASKS
outputs.description: The output is a tensor containing the processed masks with the floor regions isolated, ready for further analysis or processing.

Mask Gaussian Region.description: This node applies a Gaussian blur to specified regions within given masks, effectively smoothing the edges and transitions within the mask areas. It's designed to create softer, more natural-looking mask boundaries by utilizing a Gaussian filter.

inputs.name: masks
inputs.description: The input masks to which the Gaussian blur will be applied. These masks define the regions that will be smoothed.

inputs.name: radius
inputs.description: Defines the radius of the Gaussian blur. A larger radius results in a smoother, more blurred mask region.

outputs.name: MASKS
outputs.description: The output masks after applying the Gaussian blur to the specified regions. These masks will have smoother transitions and edges.

Mask Invert.description: The Mask Invert node is designed to invert the values of a given mask, effectively flipping the masked and unmasked regions. This operation is commonly used in image processing and computer vision tasks to reverse the areas of interest in a mask.

inputs.name: masks
inputs.description: The input mask to be inverted. This mask serves as the primary data for inversion, determining the areas that will be flipped in the output.

outputs.name: MASKS
outputs.description: The inverted mask, where the originally masked regions are now unmasked and vice versa, suitable for further processing or visualization.

Mask Minority Region.description: The Mask Minority Region node is designed to identify and process the minority regions within given mask images, applying a threshold to distinguish between major and minor areas. This functionality is crucial for tasks requiring focus on less dominant features within images, such as isolating specific objects or areas that occupy a smaller portion of the visual space.

inputs.name: masks
inputs.description: The 'masks' parameter represents the input mask images on which the minority region identification and processing will be performed. It is essential for determining the areas to be isolated based on their dominance within the image.

inputs.name: threshold
inputs.description: The 'threshold' parameter sets the boundary for distinguishing between majority and minority regions within the mask images. It plays a critical role in defining which areas are considered minor and thus subject to further processing.

outputs.name: MASKS
