outputs.description: The output is a tensor representing the processed mask images, where the minority regions have been isolated and emphasized, ready for further analysis or manipulation.

Mask Paste Region.description: The node is designed to paste a specified region within an image mask, allowing for precise manipulation and modification of mask areas. It focuses on enhancing or altering the mask's characteristics by integrating selected regions, thereby facilitating targeted adjustments in image processing tasks.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: The 'mask' parameter represents the primary image mask to be processed. It is essential for identifying the area within which the pasting operation will be executed, directly influencing the node's execution and the resulting modified mask.

inputs.name: crop_mask
inputs.description: The 'crop_mask' parameter specifies the mask of the region to be pasted into the primary mask. It defines the shape and area of the region being integrated into the 'mask' parameter.

inputs.name: crop_data
inputs.description: Optional parameter providing additional data related to the crop, such as its position or size. It can influence how the 'crop_mask' is integrated into the 'mask'.

inputs.name: crop_blending
inputs.description: Specifies the blending level between the 'mask' and 'crop_mask' during the pasting operation. A higher value results in smoother blending.

inputs.name: crop_sharpening
inputs.description: Determines the level of sharpening applied to the 'crop_mask' before it is pasted onto the 'mask'. This can enhance the clarity of the pasted region.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: This output represents the modified image mask after the pasting operation has been applied. It encapsulates the alterations made to the original mask, showcasing the region that has been pasted as per the specified parameters.

Mask Smooth Region.description: This node applies a smoothing operation to the specified regions within the input masks, utilizing a specified sigma value to control the smoothness level. It's designed to refine mask edges, making them less jagged and more visually appealing.

inputs.name: masks
inputs.description: The input masks to be smoothed. This parameter is crucial for determining which areas of the image will undergo the smoothing process.

inputs.name: sigma
inputs.description: A parameter controlling the smoothness level of the mask's edges. Higher values result in smoother edges.

outputs.name: MASKS
outputs.description: The smoothed masks, with refined edges for improved visual quality.

Mask Threshold Region.description: This node applies a thresholding operation to a given mask or set of masks, effectively segmenting the image into regions based on specified black and white threshold values. It aims to isolate and highlight areas within the masks that fall within the defined threshold range, enhancing the distinction between different regions.

inputs.name: masks
inputs.description: The masks to be thresholded. This parameter is crucial for determining which areas of the image are to be isolated based on the threshold values, directly influencing the node's output.

inputs.name: black_threshold
inputs.description: The lower bound for the thresholding operation. Pixels with values below this threshold are set to black, contributing to the segmentation of the mask.

inputs.name: white_threshold
inputs.description: The upper bound for the thresholding operation. Pixels with values above this threshold are set to white, further refining the segmentation of the mask.

outputs.name: MASKS
outputs.description: The result of the thresholding operation, a tensor representing the segmented regions within the original masks.

Masks Add.description: The node is designed to perform addition operations on mask data, effectively combining or layering two masks together. It supports handling masks with different dimensions by adjusting their shapes before performing the addition, ensuring compatibility and flexibility in mask manipulation.

inputs.name: masks_a
inputs.description: Represents the first set of masks to be added. Its role is crucial as it serves as one of the two primary inputs for the addition operation, directly influencing the outcome.

inputs.name: masks_b
inputs.description: Represents the second set of masks to be added alongside `masks_a`. It plays a vital role in the addition operation, contributing to the final combined mask result.

outputs.name: MASKS
outputs.description: The result of adding two sets of masks, which could be used for further image processing or analysis tasks.

Masks Combine Batch.description: This node is designed to combine multiple mask tensors into a single mask tensor by summing them up. It ensures that the resulting mask values are clamped between 0 and 1, maintaining the integrity of mask data.

inputs.name: masks
inputs.description: The 'masks' input consists of a batch of mask tensors to be combined. It plays a crucial role in the node's operation by providing the raw data that will be processed into a single, unified mask.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The output is a single mask tensor that represents the combined effect of the input masks, with values clamped between 0 and 1.

Masks Combine Regions.description: The node is designed to merge or combine multiple mask regions into a single cohesive mask. This process is essential for applications requiring unified mask representations from segmented or individually processed mask regions.

inputs.name: mask_a
inputs.description: The 'mask_a' parameter represents one of the individual mask regions to be combined. It is a crucial part of the input set for generating a unified mask.

inputs.name: mask_b
inputs.description: The 'mask_b' parameter is another individual mask region that contributes to the creation of a unified mask. It is essential for the combination process.

inputs.name: mask_c
inputs.description: The 'mask_c' parameter is an optional mask region that can be included in the combination process to contribute to the unified mask.

inputs.name: mask_d
inputs.description: The 'mask_d' parameter is an optional mask region that can be included in the combination process to contribute to the unified mask.

inputs.name: mask_e
inputs.description: The 'mask_e' parameter is an optional mask region that can be included in the combination process to contribute to the unified mask.

inputs.name: mask_f
inputs.description: The 'mask_f' parameter is an optional mask region that can be included in the combination process to contribute to the unified mask.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The 'mask' output represents the unified mask generated by combining the input mask regions. It is significant for downstream tasks that require a single, comprehensive mask representation.

Masks Subtract.description: The node is designed to perform subtraction between two sets of masks, effectively removing parts of one mask using another. This operation is useful in image processing tasks where specific areas of interest need to be isolated or removed from an image mask.

inputs.name: masks_a
inputs.description: Represents the first set of masks to be used in the subtraction operation. It plays a crucial role in determining the areas to be retained.

inputs.name: masks_b
inputs.description: Represents the second set of masks to be subtracted from the first set. It determines the areas to be removed from the resulting mask.

outputs.name: MASKS
outputs.description: The resulting mask after subtracting 'masks_b' from 'masks_a', containing only the areas present in 'masks_a' but not in 'masks_b'.

MiDaS Depth Approximation.description: This node utilizes the MiDaS model to approximate depth maps from input images. It supports different MiDaS models and offers options for CPU or GPU execution, depth map inversion, and depth map normalization. The node is designed to enhance image processing tasks by providing detailed depth information, which can be crucial for various applications such as 3D reconstruction, augmented reality, and scene understanding.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image tensor for which the depth map will be approximated. This tensor is crucial for generating the depth information that can be used for further image processing or analysis tasks.

inputs.name: use_cpu
inputs.description: A flag to determine whether to use the CPU or GPU for processing. This affects the execution speed and efficiency, especially for large images or batches of images.

inputs.name: midas_type
inputs.description: Specifies the type of MiDaS model to be used for depth approximation. Different models may offer varying levels of detail and accuracy.

inputs.name: invert_depth
inputs.description: A flag to invert the depth map. This can be useful for certain visualization or processing tasks where the inverse depth representation is preferred.

inputs.name: midas_model
inputs.description: Optional parameter to specify a pre-loaded MiDaS model and its associated transform. This allows for flexibility in using custom or pre-trained MiDaS models.

outputs.name: images
outputs.description: The output depth map tensor, providing a per-pixel depth estimation for the input image. This depth information is valuable for understanding the spatial arrangement of objects in the scene.

MiDaS Mask Image.description: The node 'MiDaS Mask Image' utilizes the MiDaS model to separate the background and foreground of an image by approximating its depth. This process involves converting the input image into a format suitable for the model, applying the MiDaS model to estimate depth, and then using this depth information to create a mask that distinguishes between the foreground and background elements of the image.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image tensor that the MiDaS model will process to approximate depth and generate a mask separating the background from the foreground.

inputs.name: use_cpu
inputs.description: A flag indicating whether to use the CPU instead of a GPU for running the MiDaS model, which may be necessary based on the available hardware.

inputs.name: midas_model
inputs.description: Specifies the version of the MiDaS model to use for depth approximation, affecting the precision and performance of the mask generation.

inputs.name: remove
inputs.description: Determines whether the foreground or background should be removed based on the depth estimation.

inputs.name: threshold
inputs.description: A flag indicating whether to apply thresholding to the depth mask to further refine the separation between foreground and background.

inputs.name: threshold_low
inputs.description: The lower bound for thresholding the depth mask, enhancing the mask's focus on relevant depth regions.

inputs.name: threshold_mid
inputs.description: The mid-point for thresholding the depth mask, used in conjunction with the low and high values to adjust the mask's sensitivity.

inputs.name: threshold_high
inputs.description: The upper bound for thresholding the depth mask, limiting the mask's sensitivity to distant depth regions.

inputs.name: smoothing
inputs.description: The amount of Gaussian blur to apply to the depth mask for smoothing edges and transitions.

inputs.name: background_red
inputs.description: The red component of the background color, used when removing the background or foreground based on depth.

inputs.name: background_green
inputs.description: The green component of the background color, used in conjunction with red and blue to define the background color.

inputs.name: background_blue
inputs.description: The blue component of the background color, completing the RGB specification for the background color.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output image with either the foreground or background removed, based on the depth estimation and specified parameters.

MiDaS Model Loader.description: The MiDaS Model Loader node is designed to load and prepare the MiDaS model for depth estimation tasks. It handles the installation of necessary dependencies, model selection based on input, and the application of appropriate transformations for input images.

inputs.name: midas_model
inputs.description: Specifies the version of the MiDaS model to be loaded. The choice of model affects the depth estimation accuracy and performance.

outputs.name: midas_model
outputs.description: Returns the loaded MiDaS model and the transformation function required for preparing input images for depth estimation.

Model Input Switch.description: The WAS_Model_Input_Switch node is designed to dynamically select between two model inputs based on a boolean condition. This functionality allows for flexible control flow within a pipeline, enabling the conditional execution of model-based operations.

inputs.name: model_a
inputs.description: Represents the first model input option. This parameter plays a crucial role in determining the output based on the boolean condition.

inputs.name: model_b
inputs.description: Represents the second model input option. It serves as an alternative to the first model input, with its selection dependent on the boolean condition.

inputs.name: boolean
inputs.description: A boolean flag that determines which model input (model_a or model_b) to pass through as the output. This parameter is essential for controlling the switch behavior.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: The selected model input based on the boolean condition. This output facilitates conditional model selection within a workflow.

Number Counter.description: The node is designed to perform various numerical operations such as incrementing, decrementing, and adjusting numbers within specified ranges, based on a unique identifier and mode of operation. It abstracts the complexity of numerical manipulations, providing a flexible tool for numerical adjustments in sequences or cycles.

inputs.name: number_type
inputs.description: Specifies the type of number to be manipulated, either as an integer or a float, affecting the precision and nature of the operation.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Determines the operation to be performed on the number, such as incrementing, decrementing, or adjusting to a stop value, defining the behavior of the numerical adjustment.

inputs.name: start
inputs.description: The starting value for the operation, serving as the base number from which adjustments are made.

inputs.name: stop
inputs.description: The target value for operations that adjust to a stop, setting a limit for the adjustment.

inputs.name: step
inputs.description: The increment or decrement step size, dictating the magnitude of each adjustment.

inputs.name: reset_bool
inputs.description: A flag to reset the counter to the start value, enabling reinitialization of the operation.

outputs.name: number
outputs.description: The resulting number after the operation, reflecting the adjustment made.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The resulting number in float format after the operation.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: The resulting number in integer format after the operation.

Number Input Condition.description: This node performs a variety of comparison operations between two numbers, such as checking if one is greater than, less than, equal to, or not equal to the other, among others. It can return either the result of the comparison as a boolean value or one of the input numbers based on the comparison result.

inputs.name: number_a
inputs.description: The first number to be compared. It plays a central role in the comparison operations, serving as the basis for determining the outcome of the comparison.

inputs.name: number_b
inputs.description: The second number to be compared. It is used in conjunction with 'number_a' to perform the comparison operation.

inputs.name: return_boolean
inputs.description: Determines whether the node returns a boolean result of the comparison or one of the input numbers based on the comparison result.

inputs.name: comparison
inputs.description: Specifies the type of comparison to be performed between 'number_a' and 'number_b'.

outputs.name: number
outputs.description: The outcome of the comparison operation, which can be either a boolean value or one of the input numbers, depending on the 'return_boolean' parameter.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The floating-point representation of the comparison result.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: The integer representation of the comparison result.

Number Input Switch.description: The Number Input Switch node provides a mechanism to select between two numerical inputs based on a boolean condition. It is designed to facilitate conditional logic within data flows, allowing for dynamic selection of input values.

inputs.name: number_a
inputs.description: Represents the first numerical input option for the switch. Its value is considered if the boolean condition is true.

inputs.name: number_b
inputs.description: Represents the second numerical input option for the switch. Its value is considered if the boolean condition is false.

inputs.name: boolean
inputs.description: A boolean flag that determines which of the two numerical inputs (number_a or number_b) is selected for output.

outputs.name: number
outputs.description: The original number selected based on the boolean condition.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The float representation of the selected number.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: The integer representation of the selected number.

Number Multiple Of.description: The `Number Multiple Of` node is designed to determine if a given number is a multiple of another specified number, and if not, it adjusts the number to the next multiple. This functionality is essential in scenarios where alignment to specific numerical intervals is required.

inputs.name: number
inputs.description: The `number` parameter represents the value to be checked against the specified multiple. It plays a crucial role in determining whether the number is already a multiple or needs adjustment.

inputs.name: multiple
inputs.description: The `multiple` parameter specifies the base value that the `number` parameter is checked against to determine if it is a multiple. This parameter influences the calculation of the next closest multiple if necessary.

outputs.name: number
outputs.description: The output is either the original number if it is a multiple of the specified `multiple` parameter, or the next closest multiple. It provides a way to ensure numbers align with specific intervals.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The output is either the original number if it is a multiple of the specified `multiple` parameter, or the next closest multiple, represented as a float.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: The output is either the original number if it is a multiple of the specified `multiple` parameter, or the next closest multiple, represented as an integer.

Number Operation.description: The `Number Operation` node performs a variety of mathematical operations on two input numbers, including basic arithmetic (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, etc.), comparison operations (greater than, less than, equals, etc.), and specific checks (divisibility, odd/even, prime). It abstracts complex conditional logic into simple, configurable operations, facilitating mathematical computations and comparisons within workflows.

inputs.name: number_a
inputs.description: The first number involved in the operation. It serves as the primary operand for arithmetic operations or the base for comparison and specific checks.

inputs.name: number_b
inputs.description: The second number involved in the operation. It acts as the secondary operand for arithmetic operations or the comparator for comparison and specific checks.

inputs.name: operation
inputs.description: Specifies the mathematical operation to perform on `number_a` and `number_b`. This includes a wide range of arithmetic, comparison, and specific checks.

outputs.name: number
outputs.description: The primary outcome of the specified operation on the input numbers, potentially in its original data type.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The outcome of the operation represented as a floating-point number, providing precision for division operations.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: The outcome of the operation converted into an integer, suitable for operations resulting in whole numbers.

Number PI.description: The Number PI node provides the mathematical constant pi, offering a straightforward way to access this fundamental value within numerical computations and simulations.

outputs.name: number
outputs.description: Returns the mathematical constant pi as a floating-point number.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: Returns the mathematical constant pi, ensuring compatibility with operations requiring float data types.

Number to Float.description: This node is designed to convert a given number into its floating-point representation. It abstracts the process of type conversion, ensuring that numerical inputs are seamlessly transformed into floats, facilitating operations that require floating-point precision.

inputs.name: number
inputs.description: The 'number' input is the numerical value that is to be converted into a floating-point representation. This input is crucial as it directly influences the output by determining the exact floating-point value that will be produced.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The output is the floating-point representation of the input number. This is significant for operations or calculations that require floating-point precision.

Number to Int.description: The node 'Number_To_Int' is designed to convert a given number into its integer representation. It abstracts the process of type conversion, ensuring that any input number, regardless of its original format, is transformed into an integer.

inputs.name: number
inputs.description: The 'number' parameter accepts any numerical value, serving as the input that will be converted into an integer. This parameter is crucial for the node's operation as it directly influences the output by determining the integer value to be produced.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: The output is the integer representation of the input number. This conversion is significant for operations or contexts where an integer value is required, ensuring compatibility and correctness.

Number to Seed.description: This node converts a given number into a seed value, facilitating operations that require a seed for randomization or procedural generation.

inputs.name: number
inputs.description: The number to be converted into a seed. This input is crucial as it directly determines the output seed value.

outputs.name: seed
outputs.description: The seed value derived from the input number. This output is significant for operations requiring a seed for randomization or procedural generation.

Number to String.description: The node converts a numerical input into its string representation, facilitating operations that require the input in textual form.

inputs.name: number
inputs.description: The numerical input to be converted into a string. This parameter is crucial for the conversion process, determining the textual output.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The string representation of the numerical input.

Number to Text.description: The 'Number to Text' node is designed to convert numerical inputs into their textual representation, facilitating the integration of numerical data into text-based workflows or interfaces.

inputs.name: number
inputs.description: The 'number' input accepts a numerical value that will be converted into its textual representation. This conversion allows for the seamless incorporation of numerical data into text-based formats.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The output is the textual representation of the input number, enabling its use in text-based applications or for display purposes.

Prompt Multiple Styles Selector.description: This node is designed to select and concatenate multiple style prompts from a predefined set, allowing for the generation of complex and nuanced text prompts based on user-selected styles.

inputs.name: style1
inputs.description: The first style to be included in the prompt generation. Its selection influences the overall theme and direction of the generated prompt.

inputs.name: style2
inputs.description: The second style to be included, further refining and adding to the theme initiated by the first style.

inputs.name: style3
inputs.description: The third style selection, adding another layer of nuance to the prompt generation.

inputs.name: style4
inputs.description: The fourth and final style choice, completing the composition of the prompt with its unique characteristics.

outputs.name: positive_string
outputs.description: The concatenated positive prompt generated from the selected styles.

outputs.name: negative_string
outputs.description: The concatenated negative prompt generated from the selected styles, used for refining the generation process.

Prompt Styles Selector.description: This node is designed to select and load specific styles for prompts from a predefined list. It allows for the dynamic customization of text generation by applying different stylistic templates, enhancing the versatility and creativity of text outputs.

inputs.name: style
inputs.description: The 'style' parameter specifies the stylistic template to be applied to the text generation process. It plays a crucial role in determining the thematic and stylistic direction of the generated text, thereby affecting the overall output.

outputs.name: positive_string
outputs.description: The 'positive_string' output represents the main prompt text associated with the selected style, which is used to guide the text generation process in a positive direction.

outputs.name: negative_string
outputs.description: The 'negative_string' output represents the negative prompt text associated with the selected style, which is used to steer the text generation process away from certain themes or concepts.

Random Number.description: This node generates random numbers based on specified parameters, including the type of number (integer, float, or boolean), and the range within which the number should fall. It allows for the generation of random numbers with a seed to ensure reproducibility.

inputs.name: number_type
inputs.description: Specifies the type of number to generate, which can be an integer, float, or boolean. This affects the method used for generating the random number.

inputs.name: minimum
inputs.description: The minimum value in the range from which the random number will be generated.

inputs.name: maximum
inputs.description: The maximum value in the range from which the random number will be generated.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: A seed value to ensure the reproducibility of the random number generation.

outputs.name: number
outputs.description: The generated random number.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The generated random number represented as a float.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: The generated random number rounded to the nearest integer.

SAM Image Mask.description: This node applies the SAM (Segment Anything Model) to an input image, generating a mask based on specified points and labels. It leverages a SAM model and parameters to perform segmentation, producing both a modified image and a corresponding mask.

inputs.name: sam_model
inputs.description: The SAM model to be used for image segmentation. It plays a crucial role in determining the accuracy and quality of the segmentation output.

inputs.name: sam_parameters
inputs.description: A dictionary containing parameters such as points and labels for the SAM model to use during segmentation. These parameters guide the model in identifying and segmenting the relevant parts of the image.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The input image to be segmented. This image is processed and modified by the SAM model based on the provided parameters.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The modified image after applying the SAM model and segmentation process.

outputs.name: mask
outputs.description: The generated mask corresponding to the segmented parts of the input image.

SAM Model Loader.description: The SAM Model Loader node is designed to facilitate the loading of SAM (Segment Anything Model) models, specifically tailored for image segmentation tasks. It supports loading different sizes of the SAM model, including ViT-H, ViT-L, and ViT-B, by downloading the model if it's not already present locally and then initializing it for use.

inputs.name: model_size
inputs.description: Specifies the size of the SAM model to be loaded. The size can be 'ViT-H', 'ViT-L', or 'ViT-B', each corresponding to a different configuration of the model, affecting its performance and accuracy.

outputs.name: sam_model
outputs.description: The loaded SAM model, ready for use in image segmentation tasks. It is initialized based on the specified model size and can be directly utilized for processing images.

SAM Parameters Combine.description: This node combines the parameters of two SAM (Spatial Attention Model) operations, effectively merging their points and labels into a single set. It's designed to facilitate the application of multiple SAM operations on a single image or dataset by consolidating their parameters for streamlined processing.

inputs.name: sam_parameters_a
inputs.description: The first set of SAM parameters to be combined. It includes points and labels that specify regions of interest and their corresponding labels in an image.

inputs.name: sam_parameters_b
inputs.description: The second set of SAM parameters to be combined. Similar to the first, it includes points and labels for regions of interest in an image.

outputs.name: sam_parameters
outputs.description: The combined SAM parameters, including points and labels from both input sets, ready for use in subsequent SAM operations.

SAM Parameters.description: The SAM Parameters node is designed to generate and manage parameters for segmentation and masking operations within the WAS Suite's Image/Masking category. It abstracts the complexity of parameter configuration, allowing users to specify points and labels for segmentation tasks.

inputs.name: points
inputs.description: Defines the coordinates for segmentation points in a string format, which are crucial for determining the areas of interest within an image.

inputs.name: labels
inputs.description: Specifies the labels associated with each point, playing a key role in the segmentation process by categorizing different regions of interest.

outputs.name: sam_parameters
outputs.description: A structured set of parameters including points and labels, ready for use in segmentation and masking operations.

Samples Passthrough (Stat System).description: This node is designed to pass through sample data without modification, primarily serving as a placeholder or intermediary within a statistical analysis or processing pipeline. Its main function is to facilitate the flow of data between nodes in a system that requires the preservation of sample integrity for further analysis or processing.

inputs.name: samples
inputs.description: The 'samples' parameter represents the data that will be passed through the node without alteration. It is crucial for maintaining the integrity and continuity of data across different stages of a processing pipeline.

outputs.name: samples
outputs.description: The output of this node is identical to its input, ensuring that the sample data is preserved without any modifications for subsequent processing or analysis.

Save Text File.description: This node is designed to save a given text to a file, handling path and filename generation with customizable options. It ensures the creation of the specified path if it doesn't exist, validates the text content, and updates a history of saved text files.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The text content to be saved. It's crucial as it determines the content of the created text file.

inputs.name: path
inputs.description: The destination path where the text file will be saved. The node supports token parsing for dynamic path generation.

inputs.name: filename_prefix
inputs.description: An optional prefix for the filename, supporting token parsing for dynamic generation.

inputs.name: filename_delimiter
inputs.description: A delimiter used in the filename to separate different parts, such as the prefix from the generated number.

inputs.name: filename_number_padding
inputs.description: Determines the padding for the numerical part of the filename, ensuring a consistent filename format.

Seed.description: The WAS_Seed node initializes a seed value for random number generation, providing a foundation for deterministic outcomes in processes that involve randomness.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: Specifies the initial seed value for random number generation. It's crucial for ensuring reproducibility of random processes by initializing the random number generator with a known state.

outputs.name: seed
outputs.description: Returns the initialized seed value, allowing it to be used in subsequent random number generation processes.

outputs.name: number
outputs.description: Outputs the seed value as a generic number, facilitating its use in contexts where a specific number type is not required.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: Provides the seed value as a floating-point number, enabling its application in scenarios that require decimal precision.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: Delivers the seed value explicitly as an integer, ensuring compatibility with operations that necessitate integer inputs.

String to Text.description: The String to Text node is designed to convert string data into a text format suitable for further processing or display. This node plays a crucial role in data preparation and transformation, ensuring that string inputs are correctly formatted as text for compatibility with subsequent nodes or operations within a workflow.

inputs.name: string
inputs.description: The string input parameter represents the raw string data that needs to be converted into text format. This parameter is essential for the node's operation as it directly influences the output text, ensuring that the input string is properly formatted and ready for further processing.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The string output parameter represents the converted text format of the input string. This output is crucial for downstream processing or display purposes, ensuring that the data is in the correct format for further use.

Tensor Batch to Image.description: This node is designed to convert a batch of tensor images into a single tensor image based on a specified index. It facilitates the selection of a specific image from a batch for further processing or visualization.

inputs.name: images_batch
inputs.description: A batch of images represented as tensors. This input is crucial for selecting a specific image from the batch for conversion.

inputs.name: batch_image_number
inputs.description: The index of the image within the batch to be converted into a tensor image. This parameter determines which image from the batch is selected for output.

outputs.name: image
outputs.description: The output is a single tensor image selected from the input batch based on the specified index.

Text Add Token by Input.description: This node facilitates the addition of custom tokens to a text processing context, allowing for dynamic content manipulation. It supports specifying a token name and value, and optionally printing the current set of tokens for verification or debugging purposes.

inputs.name: token_name
inputs.description: The name of the token to be added. It is crucial for identifying the token within the text processing context.

inputs.name: token_value
inputs.description: The value associated with the token name. This value is substituted in place of the token name during text processing.

inputs.name: print_current_tokens
inputs.description: A flag to indicate whether the current list of tokens should be printed. Useful for debugging or verification.

Text Add Tokens.description: This node is designed to add custom tokens and their corresponding values to a text processing system, optionally printing the current set of tokens for verification or debugging purposes.

inputs.name: tokens
inputs.description: Specifies the tokens and their values to be added, formatted as a string where each token and its value are separated by a colon. This allows for dynamic customization of token-based text processing.

inputs.name: print_current_tokens
inputs.description: A flag to indicate whether the current set of custom tokens should be printed, aiding in debugging or verification of the tokens currently in use.

Text Compare.description: The Text Compare node is designed to compare two text strings, evaluating their similarity or difference based on a specified mode and tolerance level. It abstractly measures how closely the texts match or diverge, providing a boolean result, a numerical score, and a comparison text as outputs.

inputs.name: text_a
inputs.description: The first text string to be compared. Its content is crucial for the comparison process, influencing the outcome of the similarity or difference evaluation.

inputs.name: text_b
inputs.description: The second text string to be compared against the first. The comparison results are directly affected by its content, playing a key role in determining the similarity or difference.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Specifies the mode of comparison: 'similarity' to evaluate how similar the texts are, or 'difference' to assess how they diverge. This choice dictates the nature of the comparison.

inputs.name: tolerance
inputs.description: A threshold value that defines the level of tolerance for differences between the texts. It influences the sensitivity of the comparison, affecting the similarity or difference score.

outputs.name: TEXT_A_PASS
outputs.description: The text string from 'text_a' that is evaluated in the comparison process.

outputs.name: TEXT_B_PASS
outputs.description: The text string from 'text_b' that is evaluated in the comparison process.

outputs.name: BOOLEAN
outputs.description: A boolean value indicating whether the texts are considered similar or different according to the specified mode and tolerance.

outputs.name: SCORE_NUMBER
outputs.description: A numerical score representing the degree of similarity or difference between the two text strings.

outputs.name: COMPARISON_TEXT
outputs.description: A text output providing detailed comparison results or insights.

Text Concatenate.description: The Text Concatenate node is designed to merge multiple text inputs into a single string, using a specified delimiter. It offers the option to clean up whitespace, ensuring that the concatenated result is tidy and adheres to the desired formatting.

inputs.name: delimiter
inputs.description: Specifies the character or string used to separate each text input in the concatenated result. It plays a crucial role in defining the structure and readability of the output.

inputs.name: clean_whitespace
inputs.description: Determines whether leading and trailing whitespace should be removed from each text input before concatenation, ensuring a clean and consistent output format. This parameter should be provided as a boolean value.

inputs.name: text_a
inputs.description: Accepts a text input as a string. This input is one of the strings to be concatenated, allowing for dynamic and flexible text merging.

inputs.name: text_b
inputs.description: Accepts a text input as a string. This input is one of the strings to be concatenated, allowing for dynamic and flexible text merging.

inputs.name: text_c
inputs.description: Accepts a text input as a string. This input is one of the strings to be concatenated, allowing for dynamic and flexible text merging.

inputs.name: text_d
inputs.description: Accepts a text input as a string. This input is one of the strings to be concatenated, allowing for dynamic and flexible text merging.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The final string resulting from the concatenation of all provided text inputs, formatted according to the specified delimiter and whitespace cleaning settings.

Text Contains.description: The `WAS_Text_Contains` node checks if a given substring is present within a specified text string, offering an option to ignore case sensitivity.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The primary text string in which the search for the substring will be conducted.

inputs.name: sub_text
inputs.description: The substring to search for within the primary text string.

inputs.name: case_insensitive
inputs.description: A boolean flag indicating whether the search should ignore case sensitivity.

outputs.name: boolean
outputs.description: A boolean indicating whether the substring was found within the primary text string.

Text Dictionary Convert.description: This node is designed to convert a string representation of a dictionary into an actual dictionary object. It is particularly useful in scenarios where dictionary data is received in text format and needs to be programmatically manipulated or accessed.

inputs.name: dictionary_text
inputs.description: The string representation of a dictionary that needs to be converted into a dictionary object. This parameter is crucial for the node's operation as it directly influences the conversion process.

outputs.name: dict
outputs.description: The converted dictionary object, allowing for programmatic access and manipulation of the data initially provided in string format.

Text Dictionary Get.description: This node retrieves a value associated with a specified key from a given dictionary. If the key does not exist, it returns a default value, allowing for flexible and error-tolerant data retrieval.

inputs.name: dictionary
inputs.description: The dictionary from which a value is to be retrieved. It is central to the node's operation, determining the source of data.

inputs.name: key
inputs.description: The key for which the value is sought in the dictionary. It specifies the exact data point to be retrieved.

inputs.name: default_value
inputs.description: An optional default value to return if the specified key is not found in the dictionary. This parameter enhances the node's flexibility and error tolerance.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The value retrieved from the dictionary based on the specified key, or the default value if the key is not found. It encapsulates the result of the data retrieval operation.

Text Dictionary Keys.description: This node extracts the keys from a given dictionary, providing a straightforward way to identify all the unique identifiers within a dictionary structure.

inputs.name: dictionary
inputs.description: The dictionary from which keys are to be extracted. It is essential for identifying the unique identifiers within the provided dictionary structure.

outputs.name: list
outputs.description: A list of keys extracted from the provided dictionary.

Text Dictionary New.description: This node is designed to create a new dictionary from a given string representation of a dictionary. It focuses on converting textual representations of dictionaries into actual dictionary objects, enabling further manipulation or usage within the flow.

inputs.name: key_i
inputs.description: unknown

inputs.name: value_i
inputs.description: unknown

outputs.name: dict
outputs.description: The output is a dictionary object created from the input string representation. This allows for the dynamic creation and utilization of dictionaries within the workflow.

Text Dictionary To Text.description: This node is designed to convert a dictionary into a text representation, facilitating the visualization or further processing of dictionary data in a textual format.

inputs.name: dictionary
inputs.description: The dictionary to be converted into text. This parameter is crucial as it provides the data structure that will be transformed into a textual representation.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The textual representation of the input dictionary, enabling easy reading or processing of the dictionary's contents.

Text Dictionary Update.description: This node is designed to merge multiple dictionaries into a single dictionary, allowing for the combination of key-value pairs from each input dictionary. It's particularly useful in scenarios where consolidating data from various sources into a unified format is required.

inputs.name: dictionary_a
inputs.description: The primary dictionary to be updated. Acts as the base for the merge operation.

inputs.name: dictionary_b
inputs.description: The second dictionary whose key-value pairs are added to the primary dictionary.

inputs.name: dictionary_c
inputs.description: An optional third dictionary to merge. Its key-value pairs are added to the resulting dictionary if provided.

inputs.name: dictionary_d
inputs.description: An optional fourth dictionary to merge. Its key-value pairs are added to the resulting dictionary if provided.

outputs.name: dict
outputs.description: The resulting dictionary after merging the input dictionaries. Contains the combined key-value pairs from all provided dictionaries.

Text File History Loader.description: The Text File History Loader node is designed to read and process text files, filtering out comments and empty lines, and maintaining a history of processed files. It aims to provide a streamlined way to load and manipulate text data for further processing or analysis.

inputs.name: file
inputs.description: Specifies the path to the text file to be processed. It plays a crucial role in determining the source of the text data for the node.

inputs.name: dictionary_name
inputs.description: Defines the key under which the processed lines will be stored in the output dictionary. This allows for customizable naming based on either the filename or a user-defined string.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: Returns the processed text as a single string with lines joined by newline characters, excluding comments and empty lines.

outputs.name: dict
outputs.description: Provides a dictionary where the key is defined by `dictionary_name` and the value is a list of processed lines from the text file.

Text Find and Replace by Dictionary.description: This node performs a search and replace operation on a given text using a dictionary. It identifies specific terms within the text, marked by a customizable replacement key, and replaces them with random selections from lists associated with those terms in the dictionary. The operation can be influenced by a seed for reproducible randomness.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The input text to be processed. It serves as the base content for search and replace operations.

inputs.name: dictionary
inputs.description: A dictionary where keys represent terms to be replaced in the text, and values are lists of possible replacements.

inputs.name: replacement_key
inputs.description: A string used to mark the beginning and end of terms in the text that should be replaced. It helps in identifying the exact terms to be replaced.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: An integer used to seed the random number generator for reproducible randomness in the selection of replacements.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The modified text after search and replace operations have been performed, with specific terms replaced by random selections from the dictionary.

Text Find and Replace Input.description: This node is designed to perform a search and replace operation on a given text. It searches for specified substrings within the input text and replaces them with a provided replacement string, effectively modifying the original text based on the user's criteria.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The text in which the search and replace operation will be performed. It serves as the primary content for modification.

inputs.name: find
inputs.description: The substring to be searched for within the input text. This parameter dictates what part of the text is targeted for replacement.

inputs.name: replace
inputs.description: The string that will replace occurrences of the 'find' substring within the input text. It defines the new content that will substitute the targeted parts.

outputs.name: result_text
outputs.description: The modified text after the search and replace operation has been applied.

outputs.name: replacement_count_number
outputs.description: The total number of replacements made during the operation, represented as a number.

outputs.name: replacement_count_float
outputs.description: The total number of replacements made, represented as a float.

outputs.name: replacement_count_int
outputs.description: The total number of replacements made, represented as an integer.

Text Find and Replace.description: This node provides functionality for searching and replacing specified substrings within a given text. It allows users to dynamically alter text content by finding occurrences of a specified pattern and replacing them with a new string, which can be useful for text preprocessing, data cleaning, or content transformation tasks.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The text in which to search and replace substrings. It serves as the primary content for manipulation, where specified patterns will be identified and replaced.

inputs.name: find
inputs.description: The substring to find within the input text. This parameter defines the pattern that will be searched for replacement.

inputs.name: replace
inputs.description: The new substring that will replace each occurrence of the 'find' pattern in the input text. It defines the content that will be inserted in place of the identified patterns.

outputs.name: result_text
outputs.description: The modified text after all occurrences of the 'find' pattern have been replaced with the 'replace' string.

outputs.name: replacement_count_number
outputs.description: The total number of replacements made within the text.

outputs.name: replacement_count_float
outputs.description: The total number of replacements made within the text, represented as a float.

outputs.name: replacement_count_int
outputs.description: The total number of replacements made within the text, represented as an integer.

Text Input Switch.description: The Text Input Switch node is designed to selectively output one of two text inputs based on a boolean condition. It serves as a logical switch within text processing workflows, enabling conditional text flow and decision-making.

inputs.name: text_a
inputs.description: The first text input option. This input, along with 'text_b', forms the pair between which the node chooses based on the boolean condition.

inputs.name: text_b
inputs.description: The second text input option. Together with 'text_a', it provides the alternative text input for the node to select from, contingent on the boolean condition.

inputs.name: boolean
inputs.description: A boolean input that determines which text input ('text_a' or 'text_b') is passed through as the output. True will pass 'text_a', and False will pass 'text_b'.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: Outputs the selected text input based on the boolean condition, effectively allowing conditional text routing within a workflow.

Text List Concatenate.description: The node is designed to concatenate multiple lists into a single list. It processes optional lists provided as inputs and merges them in a sorted order, creating a unified list that combines all elements.

inputs.name: list_a
inputs.description: Represents the first optional list to be concatenated. It plays a role in the overall merging process by contributing its elements to the final merged list.

inputs.name: list_b
inputs.description: Represents the second optional list to be concatenated. It contributes its elements to the final merged list, enhancing the overall content.

inputs.name: list_c
inputs.description: Represents the third optional list to be concatenated. Its elements are added to the final merged list, enriching the combined output.

inputs.name: list_d
inputs.description: Represents the fourth optional list to be concatenated. It adds its elements to the final merged list, completing the aggregation of content.

outputs.name: list
outputs.description: The output is a single list that contains all elements from the input lists, merged in a sorted order.

Text List to Text.description: The node is designed to concatenate a list of text strings into a single text string, using a specified delimiter. It can handle special cases, such as converting a literal newline delimiter into an actual newline character, to facilitate various text formatting needs.

inputs.name: delimiter
inputs.description: Specifies the string that will be used to separate each text item in the list. A special case is handled where a literal '\n' is converted to an actual newline character, allowing for multi-line text generation.

inputs.name: text_list
inputs.description: The list of text strings to be concatenated. This input is crucial for the node's functionality, as it directly influences the composition and structure of the final merged text output, enabling a wide range of text processing and formatting applications.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The resulting single text string formed by concatenating the input list of text strings, separated by the specified delimiter.

Text List.description: The node is designed to aggregate multiple string inputs into a single list, allowing for flexible text data collection and manipulation.

inputs.name: text_a
inputs.description: A string input that can be optionally provided to be included in the output list.

inputs.name: text_b
inputs.description: A string input that can be optionally provided to be included in the output list.

inputs.name: text_c
inputs.description: A string input that can be optionally provided to be included in the output list.

inputs.name: text_d
inputs.description: A string input that can be optionally provided to be included in the output list.

inputs.name: text_e
inputs.description: A string input that can be optionally provided to be included in the output list.

inputs.name: text_f
inputs.description: A string input that can be optionally provided to be included in the output list.

inputs.name: text_g
inputs.description: A string input that can be optionally provided to be included in the output list.

outputs.name: list
outputs.description: The output is a list of strings aggregated from the provided inputs.

Text Load Line From File.description: This node is designed to load a specific line or the next line from a text file based on the provided mode. It supports automatic sequential reading, reading by index, and handling multiline text inputs. The node integrates with a database for tracking read positions and file paths, facilitating efficient text batch processing.

inputs.name: file_path
inputs.description: Specifies the path to the text file from which a line will be loaded. It's essential for locating and accessing the file's content. The path influences which file is accessed for reading, directly affecting the text that is loaded and processed.

inputs.name: dictionary_name
inputs.description: Defines the name of the dictionary key under which the loaded lines will be stored. This can be customized or set to the default, which is the filename. The choice of dictionary name impacts how the loaded text is referenced and utilized in subsequent operations, allowing for organized storage and retrieval.

inputs.name: label
inputs.description: A label used for tracking the reading position in the file across multiple invocations, enabling sequential reading in 'automatic' mode. This label is crucial for maintaining continuity in text processing, ensuring that each invocation reads from the correct position in the file.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Determines the method of line selection: 'automatic' for sequential reading, 'index' for specific line access, or handling 'multiline_text' directly. The mode selection dictates how the text is accessed and loaded, influencing the node's behavior and the outcome of the text loading process.

inputs.name: index
inputs.description: When mode is set to 'index', this specifies the exact line number to be read from the file. This parameter is key in pinpointing a specific line for retrieval, directly determining which line of text is loaded when the 'index' mode is chosen.

inputs.name: multiline_text
inputs.description: Allows direct input of text content, bypassing file reading, and supports line selection based on the mode and index. This input provides an alternative way to supply text, offering flexibility in handling text data without relying on file access. It affects the node's execution by enabling direct manipulation of text content.

outputs.name: line_text
outputs.description: The specific line of text loaded from the file or the multiline text input, based on the selection mode.

outputs.name: dictionary
outputs.description: A dictionary containing the loaded lines under a specified key, useful for further processing or analysis.

Text Multiline.description: The Text Multiline node is designed to process multiline text inputs, removing lines that start with a hash '#' (commonly used for comments) and concatenating the remaining lines into a single string. This node aims to clean and prepare text data by eliminating unwanted lines and comments, making it suitable for further text processing or analysis.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The 'text' parameter takes a multiline string input, which is then processed to remove lines starting with '#' and concatenate the remaining text. This preprocessing step is crucial for cleaning the input text, making it ready for further analysis or processing.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The output is a single string that has been cleaned of lines starting with '#', with all remaining lines concatenated together. This cleaned text is ready for further processing or analysis.

Text Parse A1111 Embeddings.description: This node is designed to parse and replace specific text patterns with corresponding embeddings names, facilitating the integration of pre-defined embeddings into text inputs. It scans the text for known embeddings identifiers and substitutes them with a standardized format, enhancing the text's compatibility with further processing steps that utilize these embeddings.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The input text to be scanned for known embeddings patterns. This parameter is crucial as it determines the content that will be processed and potentially transformed by replacing identified patterns with their corresponding embeddings names.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The processed text with specific patterns replaced by their corresponding embeddings names, ready for further processing or analysis.

Text Parse Noodle Soup Prompts.description: This node is designed to parse and transform text inputs using Noodle Soup Prompts (NSP) or wildcard patterns. It dynamically replaces specified placeholders or wildcards in the input text with random selections from a predefined set of terms or patterns, allowing for the generation of varied and contextually relevant text outputs.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Specifies the parsing mode: either 'Noodle Soup Prompts' for NSP-based parsing or 'Wildcards' for wildcard pattern replacement. This choice determines the method of text transformation.

inputs.name: noodle_key
inputs.description: The delimiter used to identify NSP terms or wildcard patterns within the input text. It serves as a marker for the start and end of placeholders to be replaced.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: A seed value for the random number generator, ensuring reproducibility of the text transformation process by controlling the randomness of selections.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The input text to be parsed and transformed according to the specified mode and patterns.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The transformed text output, with NSP terms or wildcard patterns replaced according to the specified mode and selections.

Text Parse Tokens.description: The node is designed to parse and replace tokens within a given text. It utilizes a custom token parsing mechanism to identify and substitute predefined tokens with their corresponding values, facilitating dynamic text manipulation.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The input text to be parsed for tokens. This parameter is crucial as it provides the content within which tokens are to be identified and replaced, directly influencing the node's output.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The output is the text after token parsing and replacement. This reflects the transformed text with all predefined tokens substituted with their corresponding values.

Text Random Line.description: This node selects a random line from a given text based on a seed value. It allows for the randomization of text selection, providing a simple yet effective method for introducing variability into text processing workflows.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The input text from which a line will be randomly selected. This parameter is crucial for determining the pool of possible lines to choose from.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: A seed value to ensure the reproducibility of the random selection. This parameter influences the randomness, allowing for consistent results across different executions.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The randomly selected line from the input text. This output provides a single, randomly chosen line, offering a simple way to introduce randomness into text-based operations.

Text Random Prompt.description: This node generates a random prompt based on a given search seed by querying the Lexica.art API. It abstracts the complexity of fetching and selecting random art-related prompts, providing a streamlined way to inspire creative outputs.

inputs.name: search_seed
inputs.description: The search seed is a string that guides the generation of the random prompt. It influences the thematic direction of the resulting prompt, making the node's output somewhat predictable and tailored.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The output is a text prompt derived from randomly selected art-related images fetched from the Lexica.art API. It serves as a creative seed for further artistic or textual generation.

Text Shuffle.description: The `Text Shuffle` node is designed to randomly shuffle the segments of a given text string based on a specified separator. This functionality allows for the creation of varied and unpredictable text sequences, which can be useful in data augmentation, testing, or creating randomized outputs for creative purposes.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The `text` parameter is the input text string to be shuffled. The shuffling process rearranges the segments of this text, creating a new, randomized sequence.

inputs.name: separator
inputs.description: The `separator` parameter defines the character or string that delimits the segments of the input text to be shuffled. This allows for flexible segmentation based on the specific needs of the text being processed.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: The `seed` parameter sets the seed for the random number generator, ensuring reproducibility of the shuffle operation. This is useful for maintaining consistency across different runs or experiments.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The output is a new text string with its segments shuffled in a random order, based on the specified separator.

Text String Truncate.description: This node is designed to truncate a given string or multiple strings to a specified length, with options to truncate from the beginning or end, and by characters or words. It provides flexibility in text manipulation, allowing for precise control over the content length and format.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The primary text string to be truncated. This parameter is essential for defining the content that needs adjustment in length.

inputs.name: truncate_by
inputs.description: Specifies the unit of truncation, either by characters or words, influencing how the text is shortened.

inputs.name: truncate_from
inputs.description: Determines the direction from which the text will be truncated, either from the beginning or the end.

inputs.name: truncate_to
inputs.description: Defines the length to which the text should be truncated. This can be a positive or negative integer, affecting the truncation behavior.

inputs.name: text_b
inputs.description: An optional second text string to be truncated, allowing for simultaneous processing of multiple texts.

inputs.name: text_c
inputs.description: An optional third text string to be truncated, further extending the node's capability to handle multiple texts at once.

inputs.name: text_d
inputs.description: An optional fourth text string to be truncated, enabling the node to process up to four texts concurrently.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The truncated versions of the input texts, adjusted according to the specified parameters. Each output represents a text string that has been truncated based on the provided criteria.

Text String.description: The `WAS_Text_String` node is designed to process and manipulate text strings, allowing for the parsing and optional combination of up to four separate text inputs into parsed text outputs. This node is part of the WAS Suite's text manipulation toolkit, focusing on the transformation and interpretation of textual data.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The primary text input for processing. It undergoes token parsing to transform the text based on predefined tokens.

inputs.name: text_b
inputs.description: An optional secondary text input for processing alongside the primary text. It also undergoes token parsing.

inputs.name: text_c
inputs.description: An optional third text input for processing. Similar to the other inputs, it is parsed for tokens.

inputs.name: text_d
inputs.description: An optional fourth text input for processing. It undergoes token parsing like the other inputs.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The processed versions of the primary and optional text inputs after token parsing, returned as separate outputs.

Text to Conditioning.description: The 'Text to Conditioning' node is designed to convert textual input into a conditioning format suitable for further processing or generation tasks. It leverages an encoding mechanism to transform the input text and associated CLIP model information into a structured conditioning output.

inputs.name: clip
inputs.description: The 'clip' parameter represents the CLIP model information required for encoding the text. It plays a crucial role in the text-to-conditioning conversion process, influencing the encoding outcome.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The 'text' parameter is the textual input that needs to be converted into a conditioning format. Its content directly affects the resulting conditioning output, making it a key component of the node's functionality.

outputs.name: conditioning
outputs.description: The output is a conditioning format derived from the encoded text and CLIP model information, ready for use in subsequent processing or generation tasks.

Text to Console.description: The 'Text to Console' node is designed for debugging purposes, allowing users to output text to the console with an optional label for easier identification. It serves as a simple yet effective tool for displaying text information during the development and testing of workflows.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The 'text' parameter is the primary content to be displayed on the console. It plays a crucial role in conveying information or data that needs to be debugged or reviewed.

inputs.name: label
inputs.description: The 'label' parameter allows for an optional categorization or identification of the text output. It enhances readability and organization of console outputs, especially when multiple texts are printed.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: Returns the original text that was input, facilitating potential further use or processing in subsequent nodes.

Text to Number.description: The 'Text to Number' node is designed to convert textual representations of numbers into their numerical form. This node is essential for processing and interpreting text-based data that includes numerical information, facilitating the transition from textual to numerical analysis.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The 'text' parameter accepts a string representation of a number, which can be either an integer or a floating-point number. This parameter is crucial for the node's operation as it determines the numerical value that will be extracted and converted.

outputs.name: number
outputs.description: The output is the numerical representation of the input text, provided as either an integer or a floating-point number, depending on the format of the input text.

Text to String.description: The `WAS_Text_To_String` node is designed to process and transform input text through token parsing, enabling the manipulation and formatting of text data. It supports multiple text inputs, allowing for the flexible handling and transformation of text strings.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The primary text input to be processed and transformed. It serves as the main source of textual data for the node.

outputs.name: string
outputs.description: The processed and transformed version of the primary text input.

True Random.org Number Generator.description: This node interfaces with the RANDOM.ORG API to generate true random numbers based on atmospheric noise. It allows for the generation of integers within a specified range, ensuring randomness through external entropy sources.

inputs.name: api_key
inputs.description: The API key for accessing RANDOM.ORG's services. It's essential for authentication and utilizing the API to generate random numbers.

inputs.name: minimum
inputs.description: The lower bound of the range within which random numbers are generated. It defines the smallest possible value of the generated numbers.

inputs.name: maximum
inputs.description: The upper bound of the range within which random numbers are generated. It defines the largest possible value of the generated numbers.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Determines the mode of number generation, offering flexibility in how randomness is applied.

outputs.name: number
outputs.description: The generated random number as an integer.

outputs.name: float
outputs.description: The generated random number as a float.

outputs.name: int
outputs.description: The generated random number, explicitly indicating it's an integer for clarity.

unCLIP Checkpoint Loader.description: The unCLIP Checkpoint Loader node is designed for loading checkpoints specifically tailored for the unCLIP model. It facilitates the retrieval and initialization of model components such as the CLIP model, VAE, and CLIP vision, ensuring they are correctly configured and ready for use in various applications.

inputs.name: ckpt_name
inputs.description: The 'ckpt_name' parameter specifies the name of the checkpoint to be loaded. It is crucial for identifying the correct file within the 'checkpoints' directory, enabling the node to fetch and load the model's state.

outputs.name: MODEL
outputs.description: Represents the loaded model, ready for further processing or inference.

outputs.name: CLIP
outputs.description: The CLIP component of the loaded checkpoint, prepared for text and image understanding tasks.

outputs.name: VAE
outputs.description: The VAE (Variational Autoencoder) component, useful for generative tasks.

outputs.name: CLIP_VISION
outputs.description: The CLIP vision component, optimized for visual understanding tasks.

outputs.name: NAME_STRING
outputs.description: The name of the checkpoint, extracted from the 'ckpt_name' parameter, providing a string identifier for the loaded checkpoint.

Upscale Model Loader.description: This node is designed to load and prepare upscale models for use, ensuring they are in the correct state for upscaling tasks. It handles the intricacies of loading model state dictionaries and adjusting them if necessary, streamlining the process of getting models ready for image enhancement operations.

inputs.name: model_name
inputs.description: Specifies the name of the upscale model to be loaded. This name is used to locate the model file within a predefined directory structure, facilitating the retrieval and loading of the model for upscaling purposes.

outputs.name: UPSCALE_MODEL
outputs.description: The loaded and prepared upscale model, ready for use in upscaling tasks. This output facilitates the enhancement of images by providing a model that has been properly configured and evaluated.

outputs.name: MODEL_NAME_TEXT
outputs.description: The name of the loaded upscale model, provided as text. This output is useful for identifying or referencing the model that has been loaded and prepared for use.

Upscale Model Switch.description: This node facilitates the dynamic selection between two upscale models based on a boolean condition, enabling the choice of an appropriate model for image upscaling within a workflow. It exemplifies conditional logic in model selection, optimizing the upscaling process for varying requirements.

inputs.name: upscale_model_a
inputs.description: Specifies the first upscale model option for enhancing image resolution, playing a pivotal role in the conditional selection process.

inputs.name: upscale_model_b
inputs.description: Defines the second upscale model option, offering an alternative for conditional selection based on the boolean input, thus affecting the upscaling outcome.

inputs.name: boolean
inputs.description: A boolean condition that determines which upscale model (A or B) is selected for the upscaling process, directly influencing the node's execution path and the quality of the output image.

outputs.name: upscale_model
outputs.description: The selected upscale model based on the boolean condition, ready for use in the image upscaling process.

VAE Input Switch.description: This node is designed to switch between two VAE (Variational Autoencoder) models based on a boolean condition. It facilitates dynamic model selection within workflows, enabling conditional logic to dictate the choice of VAE model for subsequent operations.

inputs.name: vae_a
inputs.description: The first VAE model option for the switch. This model is selected if the boolean condition is true.

inputs.name: vae_b
inputs.description: The second VAE model option for the switch. This model is chosen if the boolean condition is false.

inputs.name: boolean
inputs.description: A boolean condition that determines which VAE model (vae_a or vae_b) is selected for output. True selects vae_a, and false selects vae_b.

outputs.name: vae
outputs.description: The selected VAE model based on the boolean condition. This output can then be used in subsequent nodes that require a VAE model.

Video Dump Frames.description: This node is designed to extract frames from a video file and save them as individual image files in a specified output directory. It leverages ffmpeg for frame extraction, providing options for naming conventions, output formats, and handling of video paths through token parsing. The node emphasizes flexibility in output customization and ensures compatibility with various video formats through ffmpeg integration.

inputs.name: video_path
inputs.description: Specifies the path to the video file from which frames will be extracted. This path is crucial as it determines the source video for frame dumping.

inputs.name: output_path
inputs.description: Defines the destination directory where the extracted frames will be saved as image files. It supports token parsing for dynamic path resolution.

inputs.name: prefix
inputs.description: A prefix added to the filename of each extracted frame, allowing for customizable naming conventions.

inputs.name: filenumber_digits
inputs.description: Specifies the number of digits to use for the frame numbering in the filenames, allowing for uniform filename lengths.

inputs.name: extension
inputs.description: Determines the file format (e.g., png, jpg) of the extracted frames, enabling output format customization.

outputs.name: output_path
outputs.description: Returns the absolute path to the directory where the extracted frames have been saved.

outputs.name: processed_count
outputs.description: Indicates the number of frames successfully extracted and saved from the video.

Write to GIF.description: The 'Write to GIF' node specializes in creating and editing GIF animations from images. It can generate new GIFs from single images, append images to existing GIFs with transition effects, and adjust animation parameters such as frame duration and looping behavior. This node is designed to enhance visual content by enabling dynamic image transitions and preserving the continuity of animations.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image to be written into a GIF. This can be a new image for creating a GIF or an additional frame to be appended to an existing GIF animation. It plays a crucial role in determining the visual content of the GIF.

inputs.name: transition_frames
inputs.description: Specifies the number of frames to be used for transitions between images in the GIF, affecting the smoothness and duration of the animation.

inputs.name: image_delay_ms
inputs.description: The delay in milliseconds before transitioning to the next image, influencing the pacing of the GIF animation.

inputs.name: duration_ms
inputs.description: The duration in milliseconds for each frame in the GIF, determining how long each image is displayed.

inputs.name: loops
inputs.description: The number of times the GIF animation will loop, with 0 indicating infinite looping. This affects the replayability of the GIF.

inputs.name: max_size
inputs.description: The maximum size of the images in the GIF, ensuring that the GIF does not exceed a certain dimension for compatibility and performance reasons.

inputs.name: output_path
inputs.description: The directory path where the GIF is to be saved. It specifies the location where the output animation is stored.

inputs.name: filename
inputs.description: The name of the file for the output GIF, determining the filename under which the GIF will be saved.

outputs.name: image_pass
outputs.description: The original image or the last frame added to the GIF, indicating the final visual state of the GIF animation.

outputs.name: filepath_text
outputs.description: The full file path of the saved or edited GIF, providing a reference to the location of the GIF file.

outputs.name: filename_text
outputs.description: The name of the GIF file, offering a simple identifier for the generated or modified GIF animation.
